Must have lunch too, the seafood noodles has the freshest abalone and soup ever.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is just beside the Manjang Cave, so I recommended a short 1hr stopover if you are heading to the cave.  Avoid the maze park on rainy days as the ground gets really muddy when it rains.

It's the first stop in our itinerary & we went to the Ssanyong cave where there are also lava tubes. It's not as big  as Manjang cave & it's better lighted. There's also a folk village in this park, a flower & bonsai garden & lots of lava stones formed into different figures. A bird sanctuary is also here.

It's a nice stop in general but also when you visit the nearby Manjanggul Cave Lava Tube. The whole maze property is very well maintained and nicely done, a great place for a picknick. The maze itself isn't that difficult and with the map really easy. Some fun for the young as well as the older ones. I also found out how useful a drone can be - to exit a maze easily :)

It's a hedge maze straight out of the movies, except with nothing popping up to scare you. It is only the hedge.  It takes about 20 minutes to find your way out and costs 3,300 for an adult. It's 500m down the road from Manjanggul cave, so if you're going to the cave you could stop by, but not worth the trip otherwise.
It's a cave, so it's dark and humid.  I learnt something new about lava cave though.  Worth the stop if you're around and have time.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It was raining and our driver decided to start with this attraction first. Although before getting into the caves, we got a bit wet, but once inside we lost track of the rain. This is a lava cave and quite different from the usual limestone caves. The only problem is that we have to backtrack all the way out. When we came out, the rain has stopped and the sun was out. Just Nice.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

I was looking forward to this attraction more than any other on Jeju and it didn't disappoint.  I wouldn't rate as #1 (more   touristy   than expected) but worth the stop.  If you can move past the gift stores selling trinkets, cheezy signage, animals in tiny cages and crowds, the attractions within the park are quite beautiful.  I especially liked the lava caves and the bonsai garden.  Those two areas alone were worth the stop.  If you have time, just past the park entrance is a stunning beach area.  Great for photos and possibly a toe dipped into the waters.

I can't make of this place. It has plants, caves, a folk village and greenhouses. Yet none of the attractions was really top rate. I would give it a miss and visit attractions with more focus on any one of the above.

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

Form by lava stalagmites and a long lava tube tunnels. It was cooling inside the tunnel . Stone pillars and stalactites are widely spread and the tunnels shows off the cave?s topographical features.   Stone Turtle   is especially eye-catching.
big enough & diff topic in park. you could see the flower, bird, cave etc,,,,not too crowded when i visited, good place for spending time

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

Visited this park on my way back from Manjanggul Caves. There were a lot of cats there as it seems the owner is pretty fond of them. They provided me with the map but could finish in about 8 minutes without using it. Nothing thrilling about the place though and one can skip it if short of time..
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.
very cool. a cave that was chilling yet interesting always cool to have a look into the past as it is.

This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

This lava tube is different from a cave. it is as big as the new york subway in headroom and width. runs for 7 over km but tourist are allowed to see over 1 km in a safe environment. The ground is most and uneven in some locations so wear comfortable hiking shoes. Entrance is very reasonable for this UNESCO world heritage site!
This is not a cave that was slowly worn away.  It is a tube that was created in a speck of time.  The unique conditions needed to make a lava tube of this size and length is pretty impressive.

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.
The Manjanggul Cave was a nice outing for my family and I. Very dark and wet and long but was interesting to read the facts along the way. Would definitely visit again.
The cave is very cool and seems to go on forever.  There are informative photos with descriptions along the way so you know what it is you are looking at.

Rented a scooter for 4 hours and went around the entire island. Renting is easy- just go to one of the places right next to the ferry docks. You have to go to the cliffs and the black sand beach below them. Cross the beach to the rocks where they have the boat then go inside the cave. Walk all the way to the left and go out the small opening- this place have practically no other tourists. Then if it's low tide- climb to the right to the small opening into another cave but this is a lot cooler!

Not a bad way to fill in a couple of hours. The cave floor is very uneven as you are walking on solidified lava be sure to wear comfy shoes. Also can be quite damp so if you don't want to have water dripping on you maybe take an umbrella. Lots of information provided throughout the walk in several languages to keep you engaged also
Nice attraction that suitable for all. Must walk all the way in order to see the main tube. Nice temperature inside the cave. Wear a cover walking shoe!

Nature is amazing and the lava tubes at manjang is worth seeing. The walk is about 1km in and same way out. Wear good shoes. Walk is not as tiring as climbing up other steep sites in jeju. Educational Signs in English are available. A bit chilly in autumn in the caves.

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)
My 10-year old and I had a great fun at the maze.  The maze layout is challenging.  The garden  is beautiful and well-maintained.  It is worth going and it is near to the Manjang cave anyway.

Manjang Cave is made of lava formation or lava tube as it is called. We walked about 1-2 km stretch of it only as not the whole tube was opened for tourist visitation.It is cold and dark. it is one of the longest lava tube in the world but it just is not my cup of tea. No  remorse on going into it but just was not awe blown away with it either. Go if you are a nature lover. skip if you are looking for awesome scenery to capture picture moments

KRW 2k for adults. Worth the 2km to and fro walk and all information panels in the cave have english. Not suitable for very old and very young. A lot of un even steps and walkways and high steps sometimes. Dark. Wear good tracking shoes.

Just below the Sanbangsan cave  by the Yongmeori coast here is a replica of Hamel ship from the 1600. A dutch sailor who sank on the coast on its way to Japan. I guess he liked the coast  he stays in Korea for 13 years before returning to write his memoire.Very basic site attraction with activities on the side for kids and food stalls  there is not much. It is just an addition to the other visit around I guess.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안

review: It's a Lava cave about 1 km. The walkway was very hard to walk because it's a lava rock. And it's wet because of the rain. It's OK. I didn't feel woww. If you have a free time you can go there.

It was a 2km walk (1km each way) and it is not easy to walk in low light and on uneven ground. Suggest to make bring your own led light especially if with old folks. It was interesting to see how this cave was formed by lava.

It is soooo dark in the cave. You couldn?t see the formations or well anything except the puddles of water. I have been to other caves before and they had dramatic lighting that shows off the details. We walked about half way and turned back as it was the same thing the whole way through. It does get a little chilly down there. It was our least favorite thing we did on Jeju.

It is actually quite nice the cave was very well developed; it has proper lighting and the pathway had been established. The statues were a bit unclear though but it were quite attractive. The folk village was good. The bird park was also nice with ostrich and peacock. I did not go to the rest of the attractions as 1 hour visit was not enough to cover all

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

I went on a group tour around Korea last year and one of my highlights was seeing the lava tubes at Jeju. You might think a cave is just a dark place with little to no visual interest but this Unesco site is really cool because you're actually inside a tunnel formed by volcano pressure. There are lights that guide your way and handlebars so you don't slip. If you're into nature and on this island it's a must see because there are some extraordinary natural feats you observe and experience first hand as you explore these tunnels. It's very interactive.

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

I loved this cave! 2 km in and out. It was a very educational trip as you'll get explanations about what you see along the way. It's dark and wet and there's water dripping from the ceiling so bring a cap and good boots to avoid slipping. Don't wear a long skirt as it will get wet. A bit hard to take pictures though because of the lighting :/ But the ending and the way it was presented with the lighted walkway at the end was great!

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.

Had a high expectation about this place since it always comes up on your google search when it comes to Jeju Island. It's just like a big cave and that's it. It's beautiful? Yes. Is it amazing? Not really. You can walk inside the cave and not seeing that much (just a stone of course)
Didn't expect the lava cave to be that long. But it was an interesting experience. Wear waterproof non-slip shoes as the floor is always wet.

Could have spent half a day here. Gardens were beautiful. The lava caves were nice to walk through to break up the heat! Interesting animals throughout.  Ran out of time and missed seeing the water gardens.  Great way to spend a day outside. Especially enjoyed the bonsai garden.

A walk through this cave took us back to the times with the images of the lava cave and dry rocks just like in the dinosaur films. The cave is kept just the same as it always is so the paths are rough and make it more adventurous.

A long way to reach the other end. The road was slippery and uneven. The place was dark and the only light source was tiny statues with lamps along the cave. The temperature inside was 11-18째C and well maintained throughout the year. If you are interested in geology you should probably check in here but it was quite mesmerizing for non geologist as well

A  unique cave with 70 cm lava stalagmites and lava tube tunnel . Lighted with dim lights. Floor rocky and slippery but manageable  with comfortable shoes . A kilometer long but takes about 20-25 minutes one way . The Lava  formed at the end is a beautiful one worth seeing.

While this is  just of the roadway, it?s fairly free of visitors.   The path goes alongside running water (or not - depending on rainfall).    There was about a 30m section where the path ended and we had to walk from rock to rock before the path restarted.    On the other side was a cave - Rock Shade Residence - which olden people used as shelter.   Entire area is a beautiful evergreen valley, well worth a visit.

While it is not spectacular like other caves around the world that are open to tourists, they are worth visiting due to their geographical nature.They are easy for families to visit, no bending over or crawling necessary.The temperature inside stays around 16-18c all year round. It is always damp, and most areas are dimly lit.

Went there after visiting the Manjanggul caves, fairly close by. Not necessarily a tourist attraction, but if you're looking to spend an hour or two in a nice forest away from all the coach visitors, this is a great spot. All we saw were Koreans out for a Sunday walk. There is a circuit path through the forest, all level, well maintained, took us maybe an hour to complete. Totally relaxing and peaceful.

Went here with a tour package bought from Klook. Entering caves experience feels great however, for it requires like 30 minutes walk to the Lava Coloum and you have to walk back (there is no other way out) so you need to make sure to wear comfortable shoes because the floor is uneven.

We went to this cave as friends want to visit even it was not on my bucket list. It was impressive to see volcanic layers and massive path inside. We walked down all way to the end i.e. 1 km away and walk back again. Personally, I don't find it interesting.

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.
We went here right as we landed, it was a fun way to get moving after sitting on the plane for a couple of hours.  Really enjoyed this cave experience.

We visited the cave on the way back to Udo (very easy to do both of these in one day. Very interesting and well explained. It would probably be a good idea to bring a jacket because the temperature in the cave is significantly lower than on the outside. However, it's still really cool to see and think about the implications of the event that made the cave in the overall of Jeju. Very good for kids although it can be a bit slippery inside too.

We visited on a very wet day so it was good to be inside even if the inside was the lava cave.  The lighting is very low in the cave and the floor, made by lava flow is very uneven so close attention needs to be made to where you are going. Its one kilometre each way to the end of the public bit and you miss quite a bit watching where the feet go so not to fall over.mAn interesting place to visit but take a torch!

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.
We saw birds, ostrich, peacocks and various bonsai trees. You need at least 2 to 3 hrs to enjoy the place. There is also a cave with paved walkways.

We originally did not schedule this visit as we have already seen Mulu Caves in Sarawak-East Malaysia.  But our hotel (TGG) told us that this is a very different cave (lava tubes).   The cost is not high at KRW2,000 and if you are already going to Seongsan Ilchbong, might as well make a visit.  We did not regret the visit.  It is really interesting to see how the lava flowing from Mt. Halla makes its way underground and forming the cave.  It is huge so you can see the magnitude of the lava flow.  Be sure to wear sturdy shoes as the ground is rather rocky and wet and you will need to walk carefully so that you won't fall.  I am amazed on how some ladies worn high heels!  It is also dim and cool so you must bring a jacket with you.  It is also a UNESCO site so definitely worth visiting.

We drove there and parking is free. The whole experience will take about less than 2hours? About 45mins to walk all the way inside to the end of the cave and another 45mins out. So remember to empty your bladder before entering. There is no loo inside the cave.The cave is cold. About 15 degree celcius? Luckily there is no wind. The ground is made up of rocky bits, and the place is constantly damped and slippery. So wear a light jacket and confortable shoes.Although there are lights in the cave, they are pretty dimmed. Not brightly lit. We used the torchlight function in our phones to further assist us to see the rocky ground. It is not unusual to carry a small portable torchlight if you want. Im not a person who likes cave, but well.. it is an experience i guess.
was there in March, temp in the cave is alot colder than outside. not much to see as the walkway is poorly light.

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This was fun. it only took about an hour to go all the way through. there is a 2,000W charge. its chilly inside so if you bring the kids, pack their jackets. Its solid lava so it is not as colorful or full of stalagtytes as other natural caves but being in a lava tube is a unique experience and this one is really big. enjoy!

This place is interesting only in concept - because it's one of the longest lava tunnels in the world.  But in reality, you climb down a hole and then walk for about a kilometer in what looks like a dirt tunnel made for a subway train with virtually northing to look at.  Then you arrive at a lava column which is far from impressive.  There are numerous amazing caves in the world such as the ones in Ha Long bay.  We are very unimpressed.

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This is one of the attraction in Jeju that nice to visit! The cave made by volcano lava. When we went there it's rain, so along the way inside the cave wet and dirty! Inside the cave quite slippery and dark. Overall I like this place! We manage to go to the deepest point and come out within 1.30 hr.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

The temperature drops dramatically after you descend 15 stairs into the cave entrance.  There was a cloud that had formed at the entrance due to the humidity which was really cool to see.  Walked about a km to the end where there is a lava column - a frozen in time dripping of lava from above.  Fascinating walk, lots of people (some in heels which I wouldn't recommend).  Really beautiful way to spend an hour or so.  Especially when it is super hot and humid outdoors!

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The silvery field of   grass   or   weed   is amazing if you come at the right season. Definitely a great photo taking opportunity. You can also catch the Halla mountain in the backdrop. Romantic and almost magical if not for the crowd. The place is getting more popular as words spread.The crater itself is not much to see but could be interesting if the leaves turn red or yellow. Visited here while on the way to the Manjanggul Cave

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.
The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The Manjang Cave was one of the   must-dos   in my itinerary. I can only say it was somewhat a disappointment. It was not quite as spectacular as I have thought it would be. I was with my mum and dad both 60. My mum did not take the walk well and headed back halfway. My dad stayed behind to do some photo-taking, Here's the bottomline:- If you have never ever been in a lava cave before - go for it!- If you are traveling with young children / older folks / people with bad knees and weak ankles - give this a miss. The initial flight of stairs can be quite a walk. The floor of the cave can be wet and uneven- If you have been to lava caves before and if you do not have a mental benchmark - go for it if you have time- If you have seen the most wondrous lava caves and already formed expectations - skip it... more than likely this might underperform

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The lava cave which need you to walk about one km in and walk back the same distance. You can walk with/ without a torchlight as there are lights in the cave as well, wear jacket as it's quite cooling in the cave. Better wear sport shoes since walkway is wet and slippery and uneven too. Overall its a nice attraction to visit :)

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The Cave was very different to other caves I have been to. It was like a Subway train tunnel. You can way approx 1 km of the reported 7km+ lava tube tunnel. Did have much of the usual Stalagmite and stalactite and crystal formations. The Lava tracks /grooves where interesting to me. But I was not a   Wow   experience.

The cave is really nice, and amazing as it was created by the lava tunnel, thus the floor is the original ground where the lava froze. The journey is 1km one way, butnthe cave is lit, so you dont need torchlight or guide inside. There's interactive exhibitions too inside about the structure of the cave that was created by lava, unlike any other limestone cave.

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Not suitable for old folks, because is full with rocks.. Better prepare a torch light or you handphone torch light. Inside very dark. The lights not that bright enough. Prevent any injury. Walking distance to the end about 1km, one way. Winter season, very fresh air inside the cave.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.

Nevertheless, people always recommend us to visit this cave when we're in Jeju. what we found is around 2km long cave with cold temperature all the way. if you quite a fan for geology and similar, this cave is exactly for you.the 'main' attraction is located at the very end of the cave. nothing more , nothing less...come if you have free time.. but not suitable for older people due to steep stair and slippery.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and it is a designated as a natural monument.Not an easy walk as lots of even walkway,  slippery and dark. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surrounding and was cooling as you walk. You will be able to see the trace of the lava that flow through the cave. I saw some who rush all their way in and out.With young children do note of their safety, for older people who having legs problem do not try. Partly, you need to walk down the stairs which is not easy and when you finished you need to walk up again.We really enjoyed the nature of this cave.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.
It's a lava cave, national herritage. Nothing special in there, it was dark and only rocks along the way. You need to be careful because the floor was wet and slippery.

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was cool to see the lava patterns, but I don't think one needs to go beyond 70 meters.  It is dark and the ground is not level in the cave, so my caution to you is to watch your step.  A lady from my tour group had sprained her ankle while we were in there.  It is easy to just look up and sideways, but if you don't want your trip marred with pain and discomfort, watch your step.  It is very interesting, informative, and very cool to see how this little island was formed.

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was a rainy morning that my friend and I visited this cave. We were greeted with a flight of stairs entering the cave. The temperature in the cave was so much lower, approximately 10 degrees celsius. It was dark and slippery too. The further we walked in, the colder it gets. The pathways are actual lava that hardened over the years therefore, it was not a smooth walk. A lot of locals enjoyed their walk, some strolling while youngsters brisk walk, talking and laughing along the way, making the whole cave not too scary. It was a nice morning walk looking through the structure left behind by the once active volcano forming rocks, mini wells naturally. The work of nature. Beautiful!

It was a hot day so felt great to get away from the  heat and descend into the cave. It felt about 10 degrees colder so be prepared with a light jacket. As with all caves, this has rocky wet floors that are very treacherous for those without proper track shoes. Very interesting signboards with geographical  information about the formation of lava caves too.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.

In this cave, you're allowed to walk about one kilometer in the lava tube where you'll find a lot of variation in the formation and environment. It's a lot of space in one of the tubes (the other one was closed off during our visit). In the tube, there has been several different lava levels and different factors, creating unique patterns on the walls, floor and ceiling. It's recommended to bring something warm down the cave, since it's a bit chilly.Along the way, there is several signs about detail information (both in Korean and English) about the different shapes and things in the cave.

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you like cave, do not miss out.my partner pick this one as a highlight in Korea. It's very huge cave.only open 1/3 ish though, you can walk on actual lava stones all the way.* MUST bring jacket or something to warm you up and wear proper shoes. its quite cool inside and wet.

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

If you are looking for a remote island off the coast of Jeju then this might not be for you. However, if you are after an island that is a short ferry ride away and has many activities to offer then this is it! Udo is beautiful, and attracts many tourists especially in the summer time. You can rent a bicycle for the day at about 10,000-12,000W, or rent an electronic bike/scooter thing (with an international drivers license). Caves, mountains, as well as many beaches to explore. Stay the weekend on Udo or ride the ferry back to Seongsan, you'll have a great time :).

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites, this is not a place. If there were, we probably missed them. It?s a dark underground cave and very interesting to see the lava flows. You can see imprints of such flows on the actual ground you?re walking on. It?s a bit nippy, so if you are prone to being cold, may want to take a light sweater. There is no bathroom in the tunnel (which my son figured out trying to get out halfway in the tunnel/cave. He had to run back the way we came to find one.) It?s interesting. I just wished that there were more lights in the tunnels so one can appreciate it more. Uneven ground due to the lava flows, as expected. 2000W/$1.75 to get in, half for kids.If you've never been into one of these types of caves, you should.  If you have, maybe worth skipping.

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was not sure what to expect when we went to Hallim Park, but we really enjoyed it. It's a really nice walk, with flowers, statues waterfalls, caves and animals. It's nice to get away from the city noises if you have been on the mainland for a while. It's not a place you can spend an entire day, and for us was a bit of a trek to get there so make sure you plan your day to only be there a couple of hours.

I was hoping to see how magnificient the lava is in one of the widest lava tube before going into the Manjang Cave. It is quite disappointing to realise that the cave is not entirely illuminated. The lighting is minimal in the cave which made walking and lava observation really difficult. I was going with my mum of around 60 years old, it is really difficult for her to see clearly in the tunnel. And the fact that you have to walk for  ~1 km into the tunnel and then the same way back is not entiring pleasing. When I was walking down the tunnel, I always thought   there will be better illumination/rocks in the next turn  . However, it was quite disappointing that this happens only at the end of the tunnel where you saw an illuminated lava pillar. I would recommend you to go to other caves if you want to see the lava clearly.

I really liked this cave, or lava tube as it's also called. I was hoping for more stalagmites and such but the lack thereof doesn't bring down the points due to it's massive size and length. There are also signs along the way with information about the   tube   in different languages. I really recommend giing to this place when you go to Jeju!!

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

Heard there are several entrance, but only one is open to public. The cave has been fitted with a pathway that takes away the hard work of walking on rocky surface for you. It is still quite deep though and will be challenging for anyone with lower fitness level. The tube is lit along the way and it is quite cold. If you've visited a natural cave before, this cave might be less interesting.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Definitely worth a visit, even if you only have a few hours to spare. This attraction my husband and I completed in just over an hour, there is no audio guide but there are informative signs throughout the cave. You return to the start of the cave the same way you came in, so take your time reading the signs but if you are tight on time you can read some of it on the way back. Being a natural cave/tube the floor of the cave is pretty rocky, must wear comfortable shoes. If you are driving around Jeju, and using the rental GPS, the telephone number to type into the gps system is: 7834818

Could not expect that it is so huge, need a lot of time to visit all the places. So many different plants, birds, even caves. The whole way is well organized, u just need to follow arrows to see everything step by step.There are several cultures and climates that you can see in bigger size than just normal botanical garden. Jeju culture is represented there a lot as well, so will not regret about missing local features.

Chose to visit this attraction because it is UNESCO world heritage site. I and my kids went into the cave, make our way to the lava column, took some photos, then u-turn to make our way out. Nothing to see unless you are a geological fan. It is OK, just another   for the experience   trip.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Arrived around 4pm and bought 4 tickets...2,000?? for adults and 1,000?? for children. That's about $5-6 USD. It was 90 degrees outside but cool and refreshing inside. At the start it was 50F and got colder as we got deeper. If you get cold easily, you should bring a light jacket. I would wear shoes because it's a bit wet and rocky but I saw many people walk through with sandals and slippers. It's about a 25 minutes one way. It is pretty well lit for a  tunnel/cave. There's no climbing or steep terrain except for the way down but there are handrails. You will enjoy the experience. It's informative as well.
Approximately 2km walk all the way in then back out. Cooling inside the cave. If I were to go again, I would bring a torch so I can take better pictures and videos inside.

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

After being in the cave, this is a good way to warm your body under the sun (well, at least during this season).So, it took 10 minutes to work out the right direction with the map, then we tried without the map and again it was ten minutes, then we left our 5 years old daughter to find the way out...still 10 minutes.I cannot define it challenging but fun for sure and super-rewarding to see your kid beaming with light every time she play the bell!Definitely worth combining cave and maze!

After all the hype about Manjanggul Cave, our expectations were high but were disappointed. Nothing spectacular to see unless you are interested in the stones that you will walk on in the dim, damp cave. You will come out the same way you went in.

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.
