Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

We reached the cave 45 minutes before closing hour and had to walk really fast in order to reach the end of the cave to see the Lava tubes. Many friends told us it's a must visit in jeju.  But my Cousin and I were disappointed as we felt it's nothing fascinating. Better time could be spent in other attractions such as the sunrise peak and Teddy bear museum.

We loved the park and spent about three hours. The cherry blossom and canola fields were the best as they were in full bloom. My little one loved the bird park and we even spotted a few peacocks roaming free in the park. The tulips were pretty but nothing extraordinary. We did not explore the caves and the hits.

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It?s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.

This place is just great! I love Hallim Park especially the caves! they are so mystical!! the parks has most of the natural attractions. The park is huge and you may need to spend hours in it to enjoy everything that they offer. It was so relaxing and very nice.

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

One of the highlights of my visit in Jeju - there's about a 1km walk in the cave which allows you to explore the after effects of lava tubes at your own pace; very interesting and spectacular. Would advise to bring additional clothing and comfortable covered shoes as the temperature is quite cooling with moist grounds. We used flashlights from our iPhones at a few points where it gets very dark; this helps us to better see the route ahead or for looking at details of the lava tubes.  Spent about an hour at this location. A must in your itinerary!
Long dark cooling walk. Only a small section of the cave was opened. Amazing sight. The entire walk will take more than 1 hour

Long cave path that has been carved out by lava flows.  Its just basically a walk thru the cave and back.  Paths are not paved and can be treacherous at times.  Wear good walking shoes.  Bring a tripod if you want to take some nice pics inside the cave.  Fairly dark in spaces.  The walk should take about 1.5 hours.

It was hot at the cave entrance at 32 degrees.  There is notice at entrance on temperature drop to 10 degrees as we continued the walk.  It is a 1 hour to and fro walk along the dark and slippery caveт囹. Good for those who like trekking.

Great place for nature lovers to soak in multi themes and explore the Hyeopjae & Ssangyong caves in one location for admission price of KRW10000. Park is wheelchair friendly and is a great place for friends and family to spend a few hours together. The park does not feel overly crowded as it is spread over 80 acres. Visitors still enjoy tranquil surroundings even though the park is crowded.
Good place to explore for 1-2 hours. Be prepared to walk. Bring a waterproof jacket and good walking shoes with good grip as it's wet inside the cave
Estimate to spend 2 hours. wear good shoes and jacket. The cave is quite cold and wet. Uneven roads and required to walk on few staircase too. but overall experience is great.

You could easily do 4-5 hours or even a day trip at Hallim Park. The first part of the gardens is uninspired, but persevere and head to the lava caves, tulip garden (late March/early April), bonsai gardens and beyond.
Working hours from 8AM (or 9?) till 5PM.Spend 2-3-4 hours there, many flowers (in season), animals, folk village inside, two interesting caves. Just nice! :)
went part of Yeha east tour. Spent 1 hour hiking deep inside the caves. Beautiful, damp and enjoyable.

Weather was not perfect, but the park was still well worth the visit, the walk through the caves is really fun too. Give yourself at least 2 hours there, we budgeted for one and no where near long enough

We were there about an hour before closing so there weren't many people in the cave. It's pretty dark and wet in the cave. The floor is also uneven. I must say that it's quite an awesome cave (different from the ones I've seen in NZ, USA & Switzerland) though I can imagine that it would be quite boring if there was no one to explain to you the different features of the cave.If you don't have a local guide with you and are not a Geography fan, you might want to give this a skip. But if you are into caves/rocks/Geography, I think you'd love it!

We went here mainly to see the cave network formed by Mt. Halla's eruption. It was really cool, literally. The temperature was about 17degrees so it was a nice rest from the 34 outside. There are about 3 sections to all the caves....It was very quiet when we went so not many people about which was nice, but it does get a bit hot walking around all the gardens as we went in the summer. We probably only stayed for an hour or two.

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We spent around 2-3 hours in Hallim Park, and didn't regret it. The flowers and the botanical garden were beautiful, the cave and the water area were also very interesting. Very good opportunities to take photos. As we went in April, we got to enjoy the countless cherry blossoms! My personal highlight was the 300-year old bonsai in the bonsai area. If you're in the area, this is definitely worth a visit. There are several restrooms inside the park, as well as spots where you can buy food at a reasonable price.

We hired Mr Kim Si Nam's service for a day, touring the Eastern route of Jeju island (Woljeongri beach, Seongeup Folk Village, Manjanggul Cave, Seopikoji, Seongsan Ilchulbong and Noksan-ro). Tour was stated to be 8-9 hours but we ran a little overtime and Mr Kim was kind not to charge extra. Throughout the journey from one attraction to another, he explained the history behind them even though his command of English is rather limited and took many gorgeous photos for us. We are indeed thankful to have met him and will definitely hire his services again when we return to Jeju.Mr Kim, thank you for taking such good care of us. We miss the beautiful Jeju island!

We arrived in late autumn nearing winter so there were not many flowers on display. We still managed to see chrysanthemum in various colours!! We also managed to spot the peacocks and ostriches. There's a small enclosure for kids (and adults) to see the various birds they have there. We also visited the 2 caves within Hallim Park. There's also a big bonsai area in the park.The park is huge, so allocate about 2 hours to visit everything!

Was skeptical at first. But the park turns out to be pretty nice.  With amazing bonzai (some over 300 years old), flowers, lava caves and even peacocks!  We were lucky that we visited during cherry blossoms season, so it was an added bonus.  Only caution is don't go there hungry.  Food there is terrible and expensive.  Much better to eat elsewhere then visit the park for a good 3-4 hours.

This place is huge, with lots of plants, flowers, caves to see. Though it may not be extra especial since it felt so artificial, it is still a cool place to visit. Stroll and take lots of pictures with friends or family. Don't join the tour because they only allow 1-1.5 hours and you'll end up just walking and not really appreciating the things that you will see.

This park has it all - Plants, bonsai, trees, birds, ostriches, stone sculptures, lava caves, folk houses. However, it is really big so you might need to have more than 3 hours to finish the entire park.

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.

This Hallim Park is a big area with the palm tree, tulips, cherry blossom, etc.  They also have some cave and near to the sea.  They have Historical Story since 1971 if you see the website.  We need to have 2-3 hours i think to go arround.  When i visit here last week, we still can see the tulips.

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)
There are lots of things to see here, we spend 2 hours here. Beautiful trees, caves, stones, small waterfall. It is all about nature and traditional korea living.
The park has birds area , flowers area, caverns with lots of other attractions probably you need 4 hour to see it all.We like the caverns more than anything else

The grounds are amazing and beautiful. Different times of year you can see beautiful blooms like azaleas, hydrangeas, bougainvillea, etc. It?s definitely worth some time to see the natural beauty of the flora. The animal enclosures are very disappointing, because as a true natural park, you would expect better conditions for the animals. The caves are a good break from the sun and heat. They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

The cave takes about an hour, nice walk. Wear sensible shoes as the floor is not even and take a small jacket as it gets colder the further in you go. It was an interesting walk and we got to see bats at the end.

Spent approximately 5 hours walking in the park. The park is sub divided into different sectors with different themes. Didn?t go to all the different sectors because some didn?t appeal to us. What I found nice and interesting were;1. The Caves2. Cultural Village3. The Bonsai & Stone Garden4. Seasonal Section - Ume FlowersWhat I didn?t like;1. Birds and reptiles in captivity2. Wild Flowers Garden - area seems to be poorly maintained. I didn?t get to see anything except grass and weedsBe prepared to walk and walk so if walking is not your thing then u better reconsider. Limited restaurants on site, so it?s best if u bring your own food and drinks.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

Only 1km of the 7.5km lava tube is open to the public, but I highly recommend coming! Expect to spend about an hour admiring the beauty of this natural volcanic formation!While we were there, it had rained the night before and was still drizzling slightly, so the ground was damp. Good to wear proper shoes with good grip (we were thankful for our boots) as the ground is a rather uneven terrain and can be slippery when wet. It's also rather dimly lit, with some lighting inside to guide your path and highlight specific features found in the cave.Even though there is only one entry/ exit point, there is much to see (if you're into geology/ geography/ nature lover, otherwise it'll just look like the same dark cavernous backdrop) as you loop back to the exit point.
Once you enter the cave and start to walk inside the cave, you will get a good amount of knowledge about the cave and how it is form. Very educational and quite a good 1 hour walk inside the cave.

Manjanggul cave is world historic place of volcanic lava formation! The cave path is very unsmooth with bumpy small rock patches and wet so we had to walk steps by steps very slowly to the end! All along to the main attraction, there are small lamps and lamppost to guide us along.Took us one and a half hours to reach the main attraction of lava formation.We spent a few minutes taking some picture there and proceeded back out of the cave.I think I won't be going there again because I'm not interested in geography.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

It's an incredible lava cave! We spent half day in this sight seeing and my daughters loved! (2 teenagers) It's very difficult to do sight seeing in Jeju without a rental car! We took almost an hour to arrive there, and the same to come back!!

It?s about an hour?s drive from the airport. Entrance is KRW11,000 for one adult.  The tulips and cherry blossoms were in full bloom. So lovely!  A surprise was the caves. It?s so cool!  Really worth the visit.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.

I say this one should not be missed, just because there are not a lot of lava tubes that exist and are easily accessible! The whole journey from the mouth of the cave to the lava column, and back, can be done in an hour. Walking thru the varying sizes of the tube, some areas narrow and some really big with high ceilings, is a spectacular experience! The largest lava column in the world, towards the end of the permissible distance, is a little underwhelming. Still, overall a great visit. Highly recommended when in Jeju.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place

First, do not get lost, second prepare to spend at least 3 hours here. If you don't like nature, this is not a place for u. It's like all nature in one. There's cave inside which is to be the only cave that has limestone and lava.

First time in a cave, so I really enjoyed the experience and learning about the history of the formation of the cave and Jeju island itself. Its a UNESCO site also, which gives the site a more special reason to visit. Be careful as the surface can be slippery, but in general the walk can take about over an hour.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.
Drove to this national park as planned, the park are well organised with the different type of flowers and cactus, caves tunnels, animals and birds. My family spend almost 3 hours in this huge park.

Dark cave, chilly, dripping water and uneven steps were all I felt for one hour journey in and u-turn out of the cave. Not much to see really unless you are acompanied by an expert or archelogist who can make rock and mud come alive and tell stories. I have been to few caves over the world and find this least interesting and dull.
Cave is big and long, take around 1 hour to come and back. Nothing much to see and it's dark so it's hard to take photo. Average compare to other caves

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.
Beautiful, clean and very well maintained. It has great collection of plants, cactus etc. Beautiful cave and water garden too. Should allocate 3 hours time to enjoy this place.

At first we didn't plan to visit the Cave as we had a tight schedule with so many other outdoor choices. Then I read something about the tube formed from volcanic lava activities so it is very unique compared to other limestone caves formed from soluble rocks.Overal the tube looked very smooth as you can imagine the hot lava flowing to make the tube. There are educational signs here and there to suggest you to look at the lava flow marks, the lava shelf marks and many others.I must say it was an eye opening hour and we learnt something new and be opened minded that it was not just another cave with so many stalagmites and stalactites that looked like different shapes in those unnatural colorful spotlights in some other countries.

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.
We highly enjoyed visiting the Songaksan and its temples especially the one within a cave after climbing some stairs up!

Is a UNESCO. There is a temple at the bottom of the mountain. And there is a Buddha sitting in the cave in the mountain. U have to climb few hundreds stairs up to reach the cave is about 394m height. My doggy was sick during my trip in jeju. So I pray to the Buddha at the temple and 1 day after I prayed my doggy has some improvements. He was sick for almost a week with the white blood cells keep increasing and to the stage that doctor suspected it might be blood cancer. Now he has all recovered. I?셫 so thankful. 瓦숅뿴佯숃퓲??겣謠뚨쉪 ?솋?뤌

A lovely puppy greets you at the start of the walk! You walk past a lovely stone house on the left and the dry riverbed on the right. They have well built stairs to the falls. At this time of year there are no falls - due to lack of rain  however there is a lovely pond at the bottom and the ability to climb down the rock's and close to the water. A lovely place to sit and contemplate! Don't recommend kissing the kissing cave...a blarney stone it's not haha!

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

This is a UNESCO site and I find it quite awesome, how Mother Nature made these underground caves. Do note that you'll have to climb steep stairs up and down to the caves, so I wouldn't recommend the elderly folks to go in. Do bring along a jacket as it can get chilly down in the caves. Also bring along a torch and have good anti-slip walking shoes as it can be a little wet and slippery.

There are statues of the Future Buddha, Maitreya; Bodhisattva of Compassion,? an outdoor huge Golden statue of Buddha, hundreds of miniature green Buddhas.? If you climb up the 471 steps, you will reach a cave with a statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion. The tears that she constantly cries for all the pain of this   ocean of suffering   world collects in pools up the stairs below the altar.? Visitors drink it and make prayers before it. If you drink 3 sips of the water, you will enjoy longevity in good health. Great temple to visit.

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

Be prepared to climb back up after going down the steps. Will need proper shoes as the floor is uneven, and does have small puddles of water  here and there.It was a nice walk in the cave, and getting a better understanding of nature involving volcanic lava flow.

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.
This UNESCO cave is well worth it. It's a long walk through the black lava cave but fascinating. Leave plenty of time if you are a slow walker because of uneven surfaces.

These caves are quite common all around the island  and this one is a well maintained and easily accessible example. Be aware though that if its been raining the day before you are likely to be dripped upon  but it's tolerable. Also  depending on the time of year  you will probably want to wrap up warm as it can be quite fesh inside.

The temperature in the cave is at least 5 to 10C lower so please bring a jacket and wear proper shoes when going in. The entrance fee is cheap at 2K each for an adult.There are many locals visiting during the weekends so it's recommended you visit during weekdays if possible.The cave is dark and wet so we spent more time watching the floor as opposed to the cave.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.

reach here after Manjanggul cave as sunny & good weather. it has some cats near around all of them were sleepy or lazily style. before went inside the maze. it has a small garden with some flowers. and the maze actually not to difficult or complex but good for take rest when you finished the game. it has shelter & you could buy a cold drink at there. ok to try if you got time.

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.

One can take a slow walk inside the cave and enjoy the art form by mother nature. It maybe one in a life time to walk on cool off lava where the surface is not smooth but rather come in difference shapes.
No trip to jeju should be without a visit to this amazing cave. Comfortable walk inside the cave as long as one has suitable shoes.  Take the time to enjoy this cave. Last entry should be at 5:10 pm.

Me and my friends really enjoyed our time around the Sanbanggulsa temple and really enjoyed the serenity and tranquillity it provided. The location within the mountain itself is breath taking and it really does give this temple a unique look compared to other temples. The stream that runs down into the cave is incredible and this place allows you to connect with your spiritual side.
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.

It was my first time walking through a lava cave which was an enjoyable experience. I appreciated the natural formation of the tubes and to think that lava once flowed through was exciting. Others might think it's just a cave and the first few meters is the same throughout which is fair enough but I loved it.

It is a nice place to visit. We have stayed there for the whole afternoon. Driving around the green tea field with a car having bibibah for lunch nice visit to the Cave Cafe and enjoying an exciting journey on the Zipline! I will try to visit there again in the spring time so as to collect the tea leaves.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

I visited in the past many caves but this is the first time for a lava cave. It is not so beautiful and interesting as a natural cave but it is something new for me. Three stars only because it is not the best place I ever visited but it is interesting.The entrance is really cheap and the cave is long 1 Km so the visit is really fast.
Had a really good time walking around the park. The gardens are beautiful and the lava caves are cool too! Worth a visit if you're passing by.

Going into the cave when it?s blazing hot outside is actually not a bad idea. It was 11degree inside the cave as you walked 1km to see the famous lava columns. Just need to be careful walking as the grounds are mostly uneven and sometimes can be slippery.

First time visiting a lava cave. It was nice and enjoyable as a couple hiking in the cave. There isnt much and just an experience and a place to spend some time. Go only if you have extra time on your hands.
Extensive botanical gardens which include some caves. Well worth a visit to explore. Allow plenty of time.

Cool nice underground cave cafe ... paid about KWR4000 each pax entrance to the cafe and have a choice of 1 hot or drink or green tea ice cream with that ticket.The green tea ice cream is the best I ever tasted in Korea the green tea latte as well.Cool quiet environment..As for the other attraction outside the cafe there are some miniature world famous buldings near to the green tea field. But they looks run down  which is left untaken care of for sometime.Green tea field is a little small scale  not so impressive as those in Boseung.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: Caves are pretty common but first time walking through a lava tube. It is quite a walk (close to 2kms) to the end where the lava poured in (column like structure) but worth the walk. The cave is rather chilly & wet with uneven surfaces. Do come prepared. Decent lighting throughout however can get rather dark. Maybe a small torchlight or glow stick so you can enjoy it more.
You can see there so well cared garden. There is also many different snakes, birds, turtles etc. The caves and botanic garden makes me happy too. Take time and relax. Eeva A

Whether you love nature or not, I strongly recommend visiting this cave. There is so much to learn on how the lava tube was formed and it provides you with a unique experience that is unforgettable. Do wear proper covered shoes as you will be walking on rocks almost the entire time and some parts might be slippery.

When we arrived in jeju it was raining so we needed to do something that was more indoor.  We drove out to the cave.  The entrance fee is cheap at 2000 won per person.  Then you walk down some steps and enter the lava tube.  It is really dark down there and the floor can be slippery.  I think we spent most of our time looking down at where to walk rather than looking around.  You walk 1km to the end and there is a rock formation.  Nothing too special.  Then you turn around and walk back.  Overall it is a nice cool 2km walk, perfect to escape the heat of jeju.  Just watch where you walk
Went to the cave, only walk for about 1-2 hrs as this is a short cave. see stone structure cause by volcano eruption. only go if you like nature. Can visit the maze park at the same time.

We were with a tour group so we did not see all the attractions, and our time was limited the ones we did experience were interesting, caves & botanical spirit gardens were worth the trip.  I really liked the stones - fascinating.

We went to this maze which was just beside the Manjang Caves. Weather was terribly cold with hail and rain and strong winds. Still 6 of us (2 adults and 4 kids) braved all that. It was great fun though we got lost a few times. There are many cats in the vicinity, kept by the people who man the place. Poor cats, all huddled up in the cold.

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We loved walking through Halla Park. The paths are organized and cultured so beautifully. Every turn brings new surprises. There are bonsai trees galore, rock formations, fountains, and green spaces the lure you in. The caves are small, but fascinating. The birds here are delightful, from parakeets to peacocks and ostriches. We would definitely come back and have a picnic here in the springtime.

We love exploring caves, and we've been to quite a few worldwide. However, Manjanggul isn't really one of the best. The problem is, there isn't much special,. By the time you walk in half a kilometre, what you see becomes a little unchanging. Not bad for a short visit however. Tips: 1. It is a long walk and can be slippery. Wear comfortable shoes with grippy soles.2. A small torch may be useful

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

We have visited many caves in various countries. More or less they are quite similar. Dark, quiet, mysterious, cold, etc.As with every cave, it's not well litted & its quite dark in certain sections of the cave. Being a natural formation, the ground is usually uneven. Particularly for this cave , the unevenness is very bad. And rocky in certain parts. We spent the most of the time in the cave focussing on the rough/uneven ground rather than the place - in order not to slip or fall. One can easily slip or fall on the widespread/rocky uneveness here & darkness if you looked up rather than down ;& get sprained ankles or worse injuries if you fall.Do not recommend children, elderly or physically disadvantaged people to visit this cave or any caves.Frankly, we were not keen to see yet another cave but since it was part of our paid day tour, why waste it?

We had a great time walking thru the lava tubes, talking about how they were formed and all the science behind this ecosystem.  Our friends ask if we recommend it and we do, but you need you to understand its a cave/lava tube and NOT a theme park style attraction.

We came on a drizzling day. The crater is certainly big, and the walk was nice despite the rain. But it wasn't as impressive or memorable as other Jeu attractions like the Manjanggul Cave or Seongsan Ilchulbong. If you're right on time, this place is possibly skippable.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!

This park has 9 different areas to visit, including a cave region, a bonsai section and a traditional Korean village.  This will take some time to see all of this, but is well worth the visit.  It is on the west side of the island, and near some nice beaches.
This location is nearby Manjanggul cave so if you have time specially have a kids, suggest you can visit, inside have some of Kids facilities and one more thing, there have a lot of FAT FAT Cat.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is not a cave, this is a lava tube so do not expect what you see in caves.  The tube is huge in size.  From the entrance you are able to walk 1km.  At the end you can see the remains of where lava had gone up and out of the tube.  It is not very impressive.  The tube itself is a large tunnel like structure.  There is not much to see and the lighting is a bit insipid.  The good thing is that the entrance fee is only like $2 so you don't need to worry about wasting money.  I am glad I visited but I would have been happy to have just walked down into the tube about 5 minutes, turned around and left.  Walking to the end of the open area is unnecessary and a bit of wasting time.  Spend about 10 minutes and its enough.

This is a park for all seasons. It is beautiful any time of the year. We were there in autumn and although the colours were not significant yet, there were plenty of flowers to please any nature lover. The only set back is the cave. It can be quite wet inside and one has to be careful.

This is a good location you should spend time to visit, nice and you can see some different kind of cave, some of the cave have spotlight follow so amazing. friendly reminder, please wear a shoes instead of slipper or sandals because the floor very wet.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

There is nothing much to see except of the cave. But if you spend time to read and understand the formation of the cave. Its quite educational for me.You will be more enjoyed if you slows down your steps and admiring the unique walls in the cave. Instead just walk, walk and walk until the end and took picture of the end of the cave then went back.

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

Stay in touch with nature and culture with this big park. Take time to appreciate the caves and read about the stories. I especially like the bonsai park. During spring, make sure to check out the rape seed canola flower beds and the cherry blossom trees on bloom.

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

Not cheap entrance fee however there are lots of things to see.Even if you don't have much time, do not miss out their caves especially in hot days as it's so nice and cool inside. :)tiny little things to see everywhere and exotic animals as well.

Mind your step! The cave is long, dark and slippery. This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience.The price is reasonable. A number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing.

Make sure to bring a jacket with you to the cave if you get cold, there is about a 10C temperature difference from outside to inside. So if you visit in Summer, it's a great break from the heat and humidity. It's about a kilometer walk, so give yourself plenty of time. Overall,a. Great attraction for all those visiting the island!!

Located next to Manjanggul Cave (a must-visit site), this park is great to let loose your inner child. If you have plenty of time and want to challenge yourself, go in without using the map! Remember to ring the bell when you have navigated through successfully and don't forget to collect all 6 stamps in the maze!

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

It's my favourite place in Jeju! It's not just an island as we thought it would be! Rmb to bring along your international license if you are planning to ride any motorised vehicles. We biked around the island which in my opinion allows you to see more attractions. Do time checks regularly as the ferry leaves at around 5pm, note that the timings given on the booklet is not accurate. Had the best Jakk Pong (seafood noodles) on this island near the cave! (just follow the smell) try the peanut ice cream! its better than the hallabong one.

It's more like a zoo combined with a synthetic garden. What attracted me were the cave's and they were disappointing as well, I've been to much nicer and impressive Caves, these are just hollow space under ground. Waste of time in my opinion, there are much better and natural sights in Jeju.

It was a 1km walk in and 1km out again. The lights were pretty dim unless there are signboards. The path inside is quite rocky with puddles of water here and there. Spent most of time watching out for puddles of water and where to walk instead of enjoying the lava cave. The cave was colder than outside, so might have to prepare a thin jacket.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

If you're in the area I'd pop in but don't make a special trip - It's nice seeing all the old huts and how they used to live but once you've seen one set of huts they are all pretty similar. i think they have some events on sometimes as there is a stage, but when we were there, there was just four girls playing drums and no one was watching them. Oh and they randomly have some ostriches - didn't figure out why but they were pretty cool!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

I went their with my wife. I didn't find the place as interesting and exciting as other people claimed. My recommendation, unless you are a geologist this place has nothing substantial to offer. Take a warm cloth and comfortable shoes when you visit this place. The temperature in the cave is low(you feel cool even in summer) and the floor is wet and a little bit slippery.A person can have knowledge about lava tubes but personally I felt unsatisfied. The cave is very dark for anyone to figure out things inside. Information boards inside give information about the site. If a visitor has enough time to visit, you can drop by this place. But, if your schedule is tight you can skip this place.

I went in a hot summer day so I can't judge. It has different plants, animals, folk village and cave. If you interest in these things you might like it. I went there because I have free time to spend but I think if the weather is better it will be different

I was on my wear the Toms until they literally fall off my feet, and this definitely got them about there. If you do anything before going to this cave, make sure you have the right waterproof, grippy-ish shoes for the job. But really, this was cool, literally.  I managed to be hot and sweaty almost everywhere we went while on the island, but in the cave he temp drops to a comfortable 50something degrees. Just glorious! Is it worth the walk? I'm not sure. It was nice enough, and definitely cool to say I have been inside a cave at least once. So I guess I would put this on the itinerary if you are visiting the island for he first time. Would I go again? Likely not, I think once was enough!

I found the volcanic caves here interesting but apart from that it was just another botanic garden. We went when the rapeseed and cherry blossoms were in bloom which was very pretty and a good photo opportunity. However, the same flowers are everywhere in Jeju at that time of year and don't cost anything to take a photo.

Having visited other caves in Vietnam and Australia, I was expecting a more developed tourist spot. The visit is essentially a 2km walk under low-light and chilly conditions. Most of the place is wet and somewhat slippery. I will not recommend it unless you have spare time in Jeju

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Hallim Park is located at the West part of Jeju island, approximately 20 minutes drive from Jeju City. The park is pretty large as it has a wide range of gardens (cactus, bird park, flowers) and it also has a couple of lava caverns. The park does not have spectacular sites but it is a great and cozy place to spend time especially for families. Do wear comfortable shoes.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.
Great for the caves. Do not miss them even if you've seen Manjanngul ( unless you have a real shortage of time, then choose M only for lava tubes, but the ones here are limestone meets lava.

For those visiting this cave expecting amazing cave formations you may be disappointed. On Jeju island all caves are more accurately defined as lava tubes. These vestiges from Jeju's volcanic origins are strange, dark, and geological wonders.Tips for visitors, expect Manjang Cave to be cold, dark, and rough surfaces to walk on. NO sandals or high heels! Hiking boots are a far better option. If you come into the lava tube expecting glittering cave formations you may not have a great time. However, if you want to explore a truly rare geological wonder, take this journey into the darkness to enjoy a unique experience.

First time to see a lava tube. It was not the most impressive thing to see but it was such an eye opener for me! Learned a lot about this amazing geological formation. Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! Bring a layer!

caves, bonsai trees, birds, nice gardens, restaurant in traditional style, and very well maintained area, the owner really has a passion to gardening and pride for his homeland. worth to visit at anytime, in summer you can also enjoy magic sandy beaches on the other side of the park

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

As for the places we visited, we loved the Manjanggul Cave, Sunrise peak and the foot bath class at the Herbal park. The maze and folk village were ok. I probably would prefer to exchange one of those two for more time at the Woljeong beach.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

Again, freezing of winter time and slippery step stone has discourage our tour leader to let us go any further getting inside the cave furthermore. up to the point we stand inside there, nothing special.Hard to explain accept you are cave adventurer... tourists ? it is a No No No

after taking a few geology classes as an adult, it was exciting to see the lava tubes. Would recommend taking a glow stick or a small flash light if prone to having a hard time seeing in the dark. Plus, the glow sticks added some fun to the darkness.  Slightly cold like most caves, bring a sweatshirt is a good idea. This offered something to do when it is raining and could  be a great break from the sun if traveling in the summer time.
A very long cave made from lava tube. Cold and dark, no bat dung smell though  as claimed. Kids having good time despite being city boys. Good new experience for us

A cave system that can get in easily just by walking down the step.according to the tour guide, this special cave is cold during summer and warm during winter. By the time i go is summer, it is real chill inside the cave

Went for a stroll after visiting Hanna Mountain. The cactus conservatory was impressive and we rounded up that part of Hallim Park with a thirst quenching cactus drink.  Similarly the cool walk into the lava cave, and the connecting limestone cave was particularly enjoyable, taking shelter from the melting sun. Highlight of this trip was feeding of birds inside a bird house.   We purchased their food at the vending machine.  Having them eating out of one's palm brought back fond memories of childhood.

Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. But dont be under the impression that it will be hot in there. It is very cold inside and be prepared with the winter clothing and a trekking shoes. It was a long walk and a nice experiences. A must visit cave.

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

It's supposed to be one of the seven winders of nature but not exactly my kind of travel destination. It's amazing for the sheer length of the cave (7km) although you are only allowed to go to the first km. We only managed to go 300 m since there wss not much to see except for molten rocks along the cave. There was not much to sustain interest in going further inside the cave so we decided to just go back. At least it was cool inside although the path was wet but nit muddy. Wear comfortable and non slippery shoes if you wish to see the cave.

I very much enjoyed Yakchunsa Temple. Its a new temple so dont expect old historical buildings but the atmosphere is very nice and  peaceful. And the setting is beautiful with palm trees a small pond a stream etc. My highlight was the small cave at the back of the temple. I was there alone and it was just magical.

Actually it is pretty cool to walk through a lave tube. It will take you back through history. The texture of the stone walls and the actual size of the cave is mind-boggling. If you come from an area that doesn't have volcanos it is a real educational experience.

We were able to easily find a cab in the parking lot, to take us back to our hotel. The cave itself was cool, temperature wise, so bring a jacket, even in the summer.  It is amazing to walk through.  Occasionally you get wet, your socks, if you step in an unfortunate wet spot or your hands, if you touch any of the walls.

We enjoyed this cave.  It's about 1 km to the end where the largest lava  pillar is located and then another 1 km back,  although the walk was relatively flat (no inclines) it was very uneven and slippery in places.  Wear shoes with good traction.  The cave is in a beautiful setting with many public toilets around.

Visited Manjaggul Cave because it was a UNESCO Natural site, like Seongsan Ichulbong.  Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

This place is a garden and there is cave and lot of birds, literally this place has everything. It is worth the visit, I like the cactus garden and the bird feeding area. I will definitely come back again with my family. I made a vblog during my trip, come and see if it is worth the visit.Search by title :#3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

Interesting cave, for someone who has stayed in a city for the whole of her life. We went in winter and what is interesting is that the cave is considered warm for winter. Be prepared for the long walk to and back and the path would be too rocky for strollers or wheelchairs

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

Can only walk about 1km of the cave as the other area is restricted, back and forth will take about 45mins. Inside of the cave is pretty cooling and nice to see such a natural occurring sight but I would say nothing much as the lighting inside is also pretty dark.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.
Visited many caves in different countries. this one was formed from flowing volcanic lava instead of the usual subterranean water hundreds of thousand of years ago.

Visited during Dec. The place is nice and cool. Do put on some thick coat or rain coat before there as there will be water dripping on your head. There is bat in the cave. Do not bring a stroller as the road inside the cave is very uneven. Do bring touch light along during your visit as the light inside the cave is not so bright.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water

The cave is cold and wet. It's not easy to walk on undulating floor filled with watery potholes. Certain section you have to bend your body as the ceiling is too low. The cave looks the same from the opening to the end.
Prepare umbrella or raincoat as water drips in the cave. It's amazing to see the rock formation and lava tubes. It's dark and the path is rocky and slippery so becareful.

Manjanggul Cave was a thoroughly interesting experience. The structure itself is awe inspiring and feels like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Be prepared for water droplets plopping on your head! It was a bit chilly when we visited as well.
Long lava tube and if you are into stones and caves you will find it interesting. Inside was cold and some water drops coming from ceiling. Once you reach the end that it just take a picture then go.

Less crowded than many other attractions somehow. A beautiful temple and big! Small cave behind temple worth checking out. Don't forget to drink of the water legend has it you will live a longer life!

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Make sure you carry rain coat or umbrella and have some warm clothese if you are not used to cold. The caves  has water dripping at place and its very cold even during the hot sun outside. We went there after noon and it was quite cold. Be careful while walking inside the cave and its slippery. Do read the story as you go through its. there is restaurant which server good korean food just outside the entrance which we felt was very good.
I don't like much the environment inside the cave. So much water dripped off and dark. Nothing much to see. I liked only the cooling temperature.

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction. We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water.
