Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

amazing trail in the woods like walking through a fairy tale! lots of glass ornaments, lighting,  this place is probably most beautiful and vibrant in the sun with all the reflections; we were there during a rain, but still very cute

After reading the reviews i was a bit reluctant about visiting the park but i am glad i did. I only wish i had more time to see everything, like all the small trails leading to the folk villages at the far back. This is not just for people who are history buffs, this park can be enjoyed by anyone who appreciates nature and quiet, peaceful walks. It is a windy area so be prepared if visiting in cool seasons. For only ~$5 this is a nice park to spend a few hours if you want to slow it down and be in nature.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

After hiking the Sunrise Peak, I was delighted by the fact that Jeongbang Waterfalls requires no rigorous hiking. We drove with our rental call and entered the phone number (7331530) into the GPS to get there. Parking is free. You just walk a short distance down a stairway and navigate through a few rocks to get closer to the waterfall. Overall, it is not difficult at all. The waterfall itself was so beautiful with the water flowing directly out to the ocean. If you've been to Yosemite, it kind of reminds me of the Vernal Falls/Mist trail without the heavy hiking up the steep steps. There were couples, seniors, and children sitting by the rocks enjoying the view. Of the three main waterfalls in the area, I would say Jeongbang is the best one.

Abu Oreum was a great easy hike.? Took about 45 minutes to get to the top, hike all the way around the crater, and get back down with a 5-year-old and 7-year-old walking.? There is a trail into the crater that we didn’t take.? The climb itself from the parking lot to the top is less than 10 minutes. Has beautiful views of the countryside around it and a very pleasant walk past some cows and a small forest. It was also very easy to find and park.

Absolutely hike Oedolgae, it's a beautiful coastal walk that is part of an Olle trail. You wind all around a part of the southern coast of Jeju, and can walk as long as you please. Lots of shops and restaurants along the way. The Jeju trails are my favorite attraction on Jeju, definitely walk one! And they're free!

A short but steep walk is rewarded with a spectacular view of the crater, ocean and the surrounding parts of the island. Very special to have the opportunity to visit such a special geological site. Informative signs along the trail help to educate visitors about the formation of the volcano.

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.
you have to walk 2km into the cave and it is cold! Nice feeling and nice view too~ bring your own umbrella as I went when raining.

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.
Wished they opened more of the cave for public viewing though! It was very well preserved and maintained. A really long walk to and fro. My favourite attraction in jeju by a mile.
Whenever you visit it is AMAZING ! Boarded walks in many places and rough climbing for the adventurous. Clamp-ons needed in the snow but trainers fine in summer. Views from there are wonderful :)

What a beautiful walk.  The walk up is on one side of the hill and the walk down is on another so there are fantastic views to be enjoyed.  It took me a half hour to go up the 180 meters and I am in good shape.  Take water and sunscreen.

Went there as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It is a great walk and views. Avoid if raining or cloudy. The walk to the top of what is known in English as Sunrise Peak is quite strenuous and involves a lot of stairs. There are rest stops along the way. There are no lifts. It can get quite windy so jackets are required. There is a town centre area at the base with restaurants and shops.

We were amazed by the hexagonal shaped columns of the cliff here. There are well-maintained boardwalks that one takes to the cliffside. We were there around sunset and the views out into the ocean is superb.

We went to hike here today and it was really fun. The air was clear and the view was beautiful. We didn't take the route to see the ponies  so our hike lasted about an hour. We walked around 5000 steps total. The stairs are well placed so it's easy to go up  and when we went there were only about ten-twenty people in total so it was quiet and lovely. Great place to hike before or after a nice meal to digest your food!

We went on the coastal walking path there The views are beautiful and the path is very easy to walk and enjoy a relaxing time. We were told in the spring there are flowers as well (We came in October).

We went on an afternoon after our stroll around museums. It was nice view. It's free.  A lot of tourist though... Visitors will be able to view by walking stairs. It was windy and cold when we went. Dress appropriately. Nothing else to see but the cliff itself.

We walked down to the water for a better view.  Parts of the trek were without steps or handrails and are not for the weak or unsteady.  Saw several women with heels fall when attempting to traverse the rocks.  The best part was the old women divers selling their fresh seafood!
We visited on a particularly beautiful day and took a nice walk to and on the bridge.? There are tours available from the nearby pier and the overall views are wonderful.

We took one walk here. Vertical rise of about 200m through nature. A couple of hours of hiking & stopping to view the plants & birds. Great view of the crater from the top. Worth the trek. Carry lots of water if it hot!

We stopped by Wolijeongri Beach for about 30 min. on the way to UDO; the water was very clear.  There were kids playing sand on the beach. The view was peaceful. We enjoyed our short walk along the beach. You can get some snacks and a good coffee from a caf챕 or a convenient store nearby. There is a restroom facility too.

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

We made a wrong turn and found this place by chance.? Amazing view. The bridge connects you to bird Birds Island. It's 1.2km walking path. Best to visit before the Sunset and you will be blown away with the views around this area. A good place to stroll and relax.

We hiked round the coastal route of the mountain in April and took an hour and a half to compete the hike which included stopping at various viewpoints to enjoy the beautiful coastal scenery and sunset.  Weather was good. We started at about 4pm and the place was peaceful with not many people.  We also flew a drone at one of the viewpoints.  The hiking path was well constructed and easy to walk.  You can also ride a horse there.

We headed down on a Wednesday around 11 am and its quite popular.  We wanted to Kayak in the glass bottom canoes however the wait was 3 hours.  We went ahead and walked around the area enjoying the view and finding beach glass (rounded glass made into 'gems' by the sea) from old glass net buoys.  We plan to go back in the next few days early in the AM to allow for a shorter wait time on the boats.  Very scenic area.

We finished the route #10 (17.5KM) in about 5 hours (we walked pretty slowly and took a lot of pictures). The whole experience was unforgettable. The magnificent view of the ocean on the left and mountain on the right was amazing. I thought it would be hard since I'm not that much used to walking for long hours but it didn't feel exhausting at all. Every sight was so gorgeous that I just didn't want to leave. I felt very fresh and relaxed after the walk. Even the tiredness after it was finished was worth all of those pretty shots I took and the healing. STRONGLY RECOMMEND!

We Enjoyed a leisure walk amidst the lovely silver grass swaying with the wind blowing :) reaching at the top ud be surprised to see swings  perched on top of the hill with piped in music. Love to just sit  there and enjoying the view and wind.the climb is not too hard as compared to other attractions.

Was quite doubtful if it is worth visiting after reading some of the reviews.  Went for it and it is quite worth a visit if you are interested in works of nature or with kids for education purpose.  The place isn't too difficult to walk if you are with the right shoes as the floor is wet and could be slippery.

Walking along the sides of the mountain next to the open sea was quite thrilling for us seniors to say the least.  We had to be careful of our steps in the uneven stone/rocks which were wet.  But it all paved for a good adventure with lovely views photo opportunity and a chance to take some great photos standing up on the rocks.  We enjoyed the visit.

Walk to the top is quite easy with good views.Don't miss the signpost to the women divers near the bottom on the way down.  They do a few shows a day and you don't have to pay extra to see it.Lot's of parking and eateries in the area
Walk to the highest mountain in Jeju. Then you can find a excellent view and enjoy the strong wind. Remember bring more water and some food. And keep clean for the natural environment.

Walk about 5 minutes from the parking lot to arrive at wide open grass field that showcases a cliff side view out to sea.There are tall columns of rock formation that are the site's main attraction.You can also peer down the cliff side walkways down to the waves crashing against the bottom of cliffs.Pathway consist of some stairs and portions just muddy... May be rectified as they were doing some renovation work on paving those sections.

Very pretty and not too taxing walk to add to any outings on Jeju. Our day was a little foggy but the view was still amazing with the Spring growth just starting to show. Lots of other attractions in the near vicinity makes it a good spot to include in a day out. The short but steep hike up to the 'temple in a cave' provides some lovely views on a good day and there are several other attractions at the base of the walk including the Big Golden Buddha temples tea shops the Dutch ship and rock walks. Enjoyable.
Very beautiful view from the top of the hill surrounding area is good for hiking a walking World heritage place can be crowded in high saison

Try to walk on the bridge and look back at the town  a great view with strong wind during our visit  we also saw some local people came for fishing in the island itself. Nearby area  there is a submarine tour which cost you around KRW100k ....worth a try.

Took a speedboat ride of krw10k for 15mins. Fun and thrilling with a quick stop for view of seagulls and black volcano stones. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver.Spectacular view even when you only walk 10mins from main entrance with free telescope. Didnt managed to climb to the peak. Reached there about 2pm.

To reach the place  need to walk along not properly paved route with long bushes  initially thought the guide had taken us to wrong place. Quiet place with nice coastal view. Unfortunately  we didn't manage to go to the church as there's sudden downpour  left us no choice but to end the visit. I saw horse carriage and shuttle bus service that can bring you around.

This was one of the most interesting things I visited in the cheesy Jeju Island. It's a piece of architecture. Everything is about meditation. The buildings are angled to frame Seongsan Ilchulbong volcano and they give you different perspectives of it. I found it very cool.The entrance fee was $5 but it is worth it. You have to walk from the parking lot to this area  it's about 10 to 15 minutes. The views are nice.

This was one of our favourite places from the list of to do activities in Jeju. It was really exciting to see such wonders of nature . These rock formations are few million year old and have column like shape. View of the blue water from the board walk is breathtaking. A must visit spot when you are in Jeju.

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.

This site explains everything one needs to know about the island's historical past.  It has a long walkway leading one through outdoor exhibit areas each section with attendants who can give information.  There also was a traditional musical performance available to view.  It was chilly when we were there so we left earlier than desired but if we had known there was a cafe in which to warm up and perhaps have lunch we could have made a day of it.  One perk of going in February was that the crowds were very very small here and at other locations.

This really worth a visit. I'm not good at hiking but its quite easy to walk up to the top. For those who have been hiking in China this is really nothing. The wooden stairs also in good condition. Great view from up here :) Also you can have some local snacks here.

This place is really good. You can see the cliff right beside the sea and it?s really safe to walk at the walk area. The view is really nice but there are a lot of stairs. So it?s kinda hard for old people and for family who use baby strollers.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: This place is one of the place that I wanted to visit in Jeju. I am glad that i did. I love the walk alongside  the field of tall flamegrass which bloom from Sep-Oct. The walk to the crater was nice and it was quite romantic. Though on the day of our visit it was raining  but nevertheless we enjoy and appreciate the beauty of this place. You can view the crater below and also the surrounding mountains. Will visit again when I come to Jeju next time.

This place is famous not only because of the movie but also the breath taking scenery here. You can access the place with great view here. Don't forget to walk further in to other side of the rock whereby the movie taken place. There is a small park in which you can have picnic and enjoy the scenery there.

This place is extremely beautifully especially during sunset. The rocks are carved by water to different shapes. Nice view of the ocean with a well maintained garden. It is 5 mins walk from international convention centre.

This place has great views  beautiful falls  and a cool folk tale about the nymphs or fairies that visit the falls. Not a particularly difficult walk  but if you have trouble with stairs  pace yourself. Only gave it 4 of 5  because the biggest and best falls are not always running. Best views require a visit after the rains. Definitely still a must do while in Jeju. Only need about 1-1.5 hours here.

THis Maze Park is located between Manjanggul Cave and Gimnyeongsagul Cave. It was designed by the world famous company and jeju National University. The Park contains a maze that has 7 view incorporated in it. and here are three skywalks called ?gureum dari? and an observatory. There are four ways to get through the maze from the entrance. We had funny and enjoyable time!
This is really amazing. I loved the view. The place is well taken care of. The walk is of moderate intensity. We had wonderful weather. Recommend this place

This is one of my wife's favourite walks. A lovely circular amble around the Songaksan peninsula mostly on boardwalks and steps. Lovely views of the unique geology of the cliffs. Can see pheasants cormorants peregrine falcons and occasionally dolphins if you're lucky. You can walk up to the summit which affords stunning views back to Sangbansan and Hallasan (clear day required). If you are that way inclined there's a Starbucks at the start/finish too.
This is a must-see on Jeju Island.  A walk along a set of stairs (not strenuous) provides many varied views of this area.  Look for the hexagonal columns of lava.

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.

This bridge connects Seogwipo Port to Birds Island and its design is inspired from the Jeju traditional log boat- Tewu.The best time to view this bridge is in the night. One can walk around the bridge and enjoy the scenery during the day and early evening.

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There isn't much there but it is a beautiful view and a nice walk along the coast.  Some of the fancier hotels with casinos are nearby.  It wasn't very busy when we went but I think during the summer peak season it would be a bit crowded.

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!
The Yakchunsa temple is very pretty and the sea view from the temple itself is gorgeous too. My family enjoyed walking around this temple very much.

The walk up the stairs is hard on knees but not specially challenging and can be done in 15-20mins. Make sure to be on top a bit before sunrise or otherwise gets quite packed with people and is hard to find a good spot to seat and see the sunrise. We got a somewhat cloudy morning so sunrise views were quite disappointing.

The walk to the crater is definitely worth the visit. Going up is fairly convenient as the stairs are not too steep. You should make it in about 30-40 minutes to the summit (normal speed and provided you skip the platforms from where you have a nice overview).

The walk started off beautifully with the canopy of the forest providing coolness against the heat of the day. It was an easy walk through this section and very pretty. Once you leave the canopy though the walk was extremely tough and hot. If you come prepared with lots of water and take regular breaks the views are well worth the effort. It does get pretty busy in sections so watch what you are doing. Stunning scenery is the reward for your efforts.
The views are stunning and its an easy climb/walk to the crater. Late afternoon there are possibly less tourists.
The view is magnificent! The haenyu women were modeerately fun to watch. Parking is atrocious! The walk to see the sights is rather difficult.
The rock does look like dragon but hard to capture the same through camera. There is walking path for people to enjoy the sea view with windy feel

The place is v nice and a walk in the green tea plantation is so comfy.. Cafe is small so buy take out and enjoy them in the garden as there are tables to sit ard and admire the view. Go up the top to enjoy the breeze and view..
The park has 2 parts..indoor and outdoor.It just like walking around a garden that full with glass sculpture. Nice view. Worth a visit.

The only (or so I'm told) waterfall that falls into the sea in Jeju Island.  Easy walk down stairs to the bottom of the falls.  Able to walk around on the rocks and view the falls.  Really gorgeous and totally worth the visit.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.

The mountain's peak itself was covered with fog signaled rain will soon came pouring. I did not hike the mountain as the weather is somewhat not on my side. Just walk along the canola field in front of the mountain and snap some photos. There are paid field if you want to take photo with better view costs around KRW1000. I walked down heading to Yongmeori Coast but ended up in a small snack shop called Mongma Reukabuden. The shop owner is very nice person. While I had my Cheese Octopus Bread with Hallabong Juice the rain started to pour down. It was just drizzling at first as I finish my last bite of the octopus bread the drizzles turned to somewhat heavy downpour. The shop owner's wife generously gave me a new raincoat that never been used. Though they were speaking in local Korean and all I could understood bits and pieces of what she tried to convey in her effort to tell me to have this raincoat with no charge. I was solo traveling and generous shown by strangers really moved me ?졼뀪 For that piece of raincoat I humbly thanks them!

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.
The crater itself wasn't much to see but it was a pleasant little walk and there are very good views of Mt Halla - the best we had during our stay on Jeju.
The crater is now full of trees and plants therefore looks like another mountain but I give it a rating of 5 for the fantastic views and park. Nice place to take a relaxing walk.
The crater is absolutely fantastic. Great view and best among Jeju sights. Very good track for walking around.

The cliffs are carved by the sea and you can walk the pillars of these cliffs all the way around the small outlet. Be careful not to slip and fall as it is very wet and very rocky. But the view and the scene and the smell of the sea are all worthwhile. There is also some small nearby attractions and food stalls
The beach is superb front of my hotel. Just walking 5 minutes.. a lot of restaurant here. The water is so cool and an amazing view. Not so crowded.

Temple is nice design and along our walk we found many tangerines tree which I believe during the spring season the temple view will be good. Since It's FOC do drop by if you have time. It's along the way to Teddy Bear Museum and Cheonjeyon Fall Yeomiji Botanical Garden

Started our hike as early as 5.30 am because we took only less than 5 minutes to walk from the guesthouse we stayed. So lucky to be able to have a perfect spot to stand and sit to enjoy our sunrise even though the place was very crowded. The view was spectacular and definitely worth the effort of hiking up to the peak!

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!

Sitting prominently on a hillside there is no missing this huge Temple and it is one of the largest in the East.There is a bit of steep walk from the carpark to the Temple complex and we rewarded ourselves with a drink from the spring well on one side of the grounds.Consisting of a main hall with a Deities sculptured side walls of Buddha a large bell a separate Pagoda Monks quarters and three or four floors upstairs that can be accessed by visitors. These floors have many donations of precious metal statues and from up here there are excellent views of the main hall.It is prudent not to use the main entry into the big hall as there are clear warnings in many languages not to so out of respect. Also shoes must be taken off before using the side entries on either side of the main doors. A group of hapless visitors ignored these signs and were promptly told off and hustled out to use the side doors.Money donations are accepted either for the upkeep of the Temple or for incense and candles.While we were there we had three or four Monks chanting and offering up to Buddha and it was very serene to hear it from upstairs while overlooking the main hall.The grounds are well maintained with a couple of restrooms around the complex a cafeteria and Temple stays are available too.Enjoy your visit!
should walk to the peak to see the amazing view of jeju island. sunny day is the best day to go so you can get clearer view.

Scenic views of surrounding landscape n grasslands.Panaromic views.Short walk to top - about 10 mins. 2 paths - steps or easier winding gradual footpath.One of the filming sites of Korean reality/variety show 2 days 1 night on KBS.

Really nice walk up some steps to a cave on the mountain with a Buddha inside for people to make offerings. There is a temple below with beautiful statues and stunning views of the sea. Worth the short hike up the stairs.

Really gorgeous view of the waterfall which flows right into the sea. A little bit challenging to go near it as you have to walk and hop on big rocks but you could still see it clearly just by standing near the stairs. Sat near to the waterfall and my shirt got slightly wet by the water splashes. Cold but refreshing. Do wear proper shoes if you intend to walk on the huge rocks to go near the waterfall.

Read mixed reviews about this place.However decided to go ahead to visit.Disappointed as it was very man made.The only thing that was natural was probably the short walk through the forest.Personal opinion would be that it?s not worth the visit for the price.
Pretty view and nice walk but nothing too spectacular.  My kids weren't too impressed.  There was a Korean drama filmed here that I guess was really popular.

Our driver drove us to the rest stop and from there we hiked about 30 minutes to the top. It had just rained so don't try it without solid walking shoes as it's easy to get a nasty fall. It was cloudy so we couldn't get a view of Jeju city but the feeling of being on top of the world was worth it!

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.
One of the UNESCO World Heritage site. Highly recommended to view its natural beauty.  The path is not easy to walk but it's worth the effort. Cold and wet!

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). The only down side is that the area as well as the park have limited street lights so you'll be needing a torchlight to walk either early in the morning or at night.

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. The sudden contraction of molten lava due to the cooling effect of water has resulted in these rocks splitting into polygonal columns and forming a coast of almost 2 km long.This attraction is worth the visit and can be reached directly by trekking from Cheonjeyeon falls or taking a bus and pass thru the garden (Jusangjeollidae Promenade) and then reach the cliff at the end.Walking around the garden would be relaxing and one should not miss it. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.

One can go for a hike or just sit near the shore and enjoy the view. Along the coastline one can see a number of manmade caves which stands as a testimony to the importance of Jeju Island during WWII. These caves built by the Japanese troops served as a place for storing the weapons.Though called as a mountain it is more like a hill as it is not steep and one can enjoy the walk up the peak.

Nothing spectacular in terms of size other than the water is running into the ocean. It was a nice walk to get there and the view is nice from the rocks along the sea.  Ladies selling fresh seafood on the rocks.

Nothing much to do over there. You will only walk walk walk to look at the view. With the cooling wind and nice view. I made me feel very relax and the walk is enjoyable. I think it is a must visit place if you have not been here before.

Not much to see or do except to take a few moments to take it the view and wind of Jeju. Many people (mostly Koreans) are seen walking along the beach picking shells or dipping their feet in the water. Not much sunbathers on this beach.

Nice quiet temple compound with a sea view. Place is rather big and is nice for a walk. One tends to feel peaceful there.We went there around late afternoon. Perhaps that?셲 the reason why there are not much people around. Just nice for us to explore the temple and do some photo taking.Worth a visit.
Nice place to walk and then eat at the Antoinette or seafood while enjoying the view.  There is also a nice hang bridge.

Nice little island to spend the day. If your a foreigner bring your passport with you to buy your ferry ticket.on the island itself you can walk around but by far the most popular way is to rent a bike. Pedal or electric powered that can seat 2 people.You will need a drivers license for the electric one though. Cute little beaches around and you can stop off and try some of the peanut ice cream which Udo is famous for. Also you can hike up to Udo lighthouse and get a good view from the top and see most of the island. A good way to spend a day

Nice hiking and walk for the great views. We managed to complete the hiking route round the mountain in about 2 hours.Also a good idea is to stop and walk slightly before the mountain as there are also nice scenery of the beach and sea.Beware that the buses out of the area are very irregular and it would be good to start the hike early in the morning and leave before noon as the buses seem to run more regularly early in the morning.We waited an hour for the bus out and gave up walking to the next town to get a cab.

Near to Hyeopjae Beach with breathtaking views. It was very cold in the winter by beach so make sure get yourself wrapped up and enjoy the views here. The water was shallow and nice enough for us to walk around on the rocks and saw many green seaweeds here too.  A must visit if you are in Jeju Island.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My friend and I enjoyed the hike up the stairs to the top and the view of Jejudo was worth the hike up. Took roughly 10-15 minutes to get up. There are rest stops on the way to the top. There are shops on the bottom if you need some energy before or after the walk :)

Mostly domestic tourists here. This hour-long hike offers both idyllic and dramatic views of the Songaksan volcanic craters and the open ocean. Walk on right till the end to make a complete loop journey so that you won't miss the breathtaking almost vertical volcanic crater wall rising up over the sea.

Moonlight is a great walking activity to do with your friends or family. It's pretty easy and the view is awesome. We walked on a golf felid for about 30min until arriving at a cliff with a great ocean view. Walking barefoot on the grass felt fresh and was pretty fun! After watching the sunset we head to watch a mini-concert just for us! this was the perfect getaway to feel relaxed again!
Might not be worth the $2 entry fee. If you walk behind the first ticket counter you get one of the best views of the falls. There's another ticket booth that they punch your ticket at.

Love the view here because of the lush greenery. You will also be able to see that there're people going some Kayaking. But it depends on the season as well. There's also cafes nearby and once you're done with the view you can also walk down along the coast towards the Yongdeum Rock (Rock that looks like a dragon). Definitely walkable distance With such lovely sea Breeze and beautiful greenery. Do make sure you wear a hat and sunglasses if you're going in summer though.

Looks like the Burj khalifa of Dubai but its just much smaller and in fact not a hotel but a bridge. Going across the bridge you will be on a small island to walk which will take around 45 min. Great for a scenic walk close to the city. You will also have a good view to the sea and of the diving women of Jeju.
Just a view of the crater. Nothing much to do in the area good thing they have ice cream that you can take while walking..

I've not been up a volcano before and the view is worth itIt's really not that high though if you get any exercise... Just 200m of climb... Remember you are climbing a volcano and not a building so it is a little strenuous !Shame you cannot walk around a little more At the top ... And I couldn't see Hallasan on this particular day..

Its still raining in Jeju when we arrived here. No regret walking in the rain and climbing the stairs when the view welcomed u so wonderfully beautiful. Spend at least 1 hr here to absord the view inside ur mind and take it home with you. Also try the grilled octo sold infront of the entrance. Yummy!

It's quite a tour to walk around and see everything in this theme park. The park has some huge dinosaur statues nice views it features a bird house a maze a small museum and some food vendors. It's a museum type very laid-back amusement park with nice scenery.
It's ok as a waterfall but nothing special. A pleasant and easy walk to it. You can also get a view of the falls from the park above.

It's an easy walk around the park to get some magnificent views.  The crater is deep with lush vegetation and is quite impressive.  The area is well maintained and pleasant to find a stop to sit and look out at the surroundings.  Probably 1 hour will do.
It's a great place with great view. The breeze bring peacefulness. You can walk around and enjoy surroundings as well. Nearby attraction is reachable by bus.

It?s a must visit place in Jeju. The time I went there was in Winter but surprisingly all trees along with the side walk bloomed so much. The walk in the forest and a big fall blew my stress away. Enjoy the view!

It was a very tiring hike up the mountain but the view was spectacular. I was not fully geared and use my running shoe which was a big mistake. Hiking boots are a must!  Kept twisting my ankles whenever I step on some huge rocks. I should have walked at a slower pace to enjoy the view but my focus at that time was to reach the top. Next time I will take it slowly and take more pictures. I hope they will have a cable car for people not fit anymore to hike. Experience was well worth it!

It takes a little effort climbing  up the peak but the fascinating view to Jeju from the top worth the climb. Do enjoy the view along the way & suggest to make an early morning trip to enjoy the stunning sunrise view from the top . There is haenyeo show beside the walking path which worth to explore how this great diving skill passing down the generation to women only divers can dive into the sea to pick up abalone & others sea produce without an oxygen tank
It needs some physical endurance to walk uphill to have a good view of sunrise or sunset. Many steps to climb so be prepare for it. It's absolute worth the climb as the scenic view is fantastic.
It is tiring but a nice walk up to the top. Nice view all round when at the top. Enjoy sometime up there before heading back where many good restaurants at the bottom.

It is the only freshwater fall that leads directly into the ocean (or something like that).  It is not a difficult hike down to the waterfall and the view is amazing. I was able to carry my two year old on my back and have my 4 year old walk down with us.  Really an amazing looking waterfall!

It is listed as a Unesco World Heritage and definetly a place to stop. Highway 1132 will bring you there and you cannot miss it. Be prepared that parking might not be easy and you may have to spend some time. The place is quite busy and many tourist buses are coming too. We had a cloudy day and it was very windy. Entrance fee is 2000 adult and 1000 child. Couple of shops at the entrance where you can buy each and everything. Please keep in mind that waste management is terrible as everywhere in Korea. If you buy something keep in mind that no any trash beans are available. The way up and down is quite crowded and loud. Obviously many tourists are rushing on top to get the selfies done to rush down again. The walk is definetly nothing for stroller or wheel chair. We went up slowly enjoying the view and getting some pictures. On top it is quite nice to look into the volvano and rest. Sure some pictures not to forget. But again very busy place and loud. Again our day was cloudy and windy but as long as it is not raining worth to visit the peak. So conclusion would be to visit the place very early.

It is a nice place for locals and tourists to relax and chill out as you can really enjoy the beauty of mother nature. We just chill and take some pics while trying out their local snack there. It is walking distance to Saeyeongyo Bridge so just stroll slwoly while enjoying the view and breeze =)
It is a beautiful place to visit in Autumn. This place offers a good walk around the crater with view of fall (flame grass?)

It a pleasant place to visit: Lots of visitors n cars maybe was a weekendThe walk is not too difficult  you will enjoy if you take it slowly n see the view from different angle n height Need food shoes n the slope is pretty steep n may need to hold the rope/railing at certain height Feel good n nice when reach the top

In five visits to South Korea in four years I have not come across a museum palace or historical building I did not like.They are all well-maintained offer good information in Englishoften have multilingual guides and free tours and are free or cheap to get in.The Jeju National Museum is no exception. Our hotel was about 4km away and we walked to and from there seeing many interesting sights on the way and eating lot of local food.I am an unabashed fan of the curating skills of the Koreans; they do a very good job.Here they provided a great overview from prehistoric to modern times offering interesting exhibits and information.There was also a special exhibition on Canopus a star of great significance to the people who lived here.Entry is free. There are buses from the city and taxi fares are reasonable. We like eating so we need to walk.

If you visit Jeju island dont forget to visit Jusabgjeolli Cliff. Rocks look like traditional greek pyramid shape and you can enjoy very beautiful view of south sea from well managed wooden walking zone around the cliff.

If you are near by or driving around the island this is definitely one of the places to check. It's not the place to stay longer than 2 hours since the place is small. I would recommend to get off the car and take a walk around the water enjoying the scenic view for about 1/2~an hour. My family were there in May when it was not too busy. There were only a few locals jogging and walking so we enjoyed the quiet peaceful and almost mystic moment there. The kayaks are no longer operating for the sake of environmental conservation. It definitely would have been amazing to have that clear water beneath when you paddle but I am glad that they've prohibited them. The place is amazing as it is. I would come back next time.
I would recommend to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and walk outside the park for better view of the bridge. Well built. Very clean beautiful park and falls.

I was on a group day tour so unfortunately didn't have as much time here. Walked through the museum very quickly ordered the ice cream and cake and quickly rushed to buy a few products at the shop. The view of the green tea fields provided a great photo op but was surprised to see 'beware of snake' signs walking through the garden fortunately didn't encounter any snakes though but they should take more precaution on this as I see a lot of small kids walking and running through the areas. There's an Innisfree house for buying the famous Korean brand cosmetic next door but quite frankly this was a bit disappointing for an Innisfree loyalist like me. The selections were limited compared to the shops in town all over Korea. One woman  in my tour group bought a bunch of products but was not offered any free samples which is common in other shops. I would suggest skipping this part and spend all the time in the O'Sulloc cafe and tea museum.

I was not expecting a lot when I drove into the car park but I was very pleasantly surprised with it visit. It only cost 2000 won entry and I spent about 1.25 hours.Firstly the guide will set up the video for you and it is pretty gruesome with the brutality of war shown. Then you walk through the exhibition area which has good information about the tunnel system and how Jeju was included in Imperial Japan's last stand at the end of the Pacific War plus weapons and memorabilia. All with English explanations. Then you walk up the hill and go into the tunnel system. When you come out you can follow the less used path and go to the top of the hill for good views.  Lastly there is a tank you can climb into just before you leave. Absolutelyrecommended for all ages.

I was here last week with my wife and we enjoyed the walk around this part of the coast. On a light drizzly morning the walk took on a determined bent but we were certainly not alone. There were loads of people when we were there. The backdrop is fairly dramatic looking and there is a small entrance fee. The view from the top at the carpark is quite beautiful too.

I visited Sanbangsan Mountain after walking along the coast at Yongmeori Beach. It's a walk which takes around 30 minutes to get to the top which is where you are allowed to reach. There is a really tall cave hole located on the top with a Buddha where people will do some offerings. The view is quite nice. You can certainly come here for a walk. Overall I will say it's an average spot.

I took my girlfriend here as she absolutely loves all things aquatic  especially shells  and she loves to go diving. A highlight of this museum is that the owner/operator collected all the exhibits herself  from oceans all around the world  and the museum represents literally a lifetime of work and passion for the sea.Taking that into consideration  if you love to dive  and love the sea  this place is simply amazing  my girlfriend was absolutely in awe  snapping picture after picture and commenting on the rarity and difficulty of finding she'll after shell in such amazing condition. The museum was an interesting oddity for myself  and I understand the reviews saying you could go through the whole thin g in 20-30 minutes  but for someone who is truly amazed by seashells  and the sea in general  you could easily spend more than an hour here (we were there somewhere around 2 hours) If you love seashells  an absolute must see  my girlfriend visibly lit up from the minute we walked in   all the way till we were back to our hotel in ?쒖＜??if you're not passionate about the shells  it's still worth a look at only 6$ (6 000?? per person. Some truly amazing art  especially if you consider it all came from the mind  hands  and worldwide dives of one very cool lady.

I read (other places) very bad reviews about the village. I was about to take it off the list. Im glad i didnt. Of course the place is not 100% original they have to keep renewing it in order to preserve as muchas they can. I loved it i even took pictures where my favorite Korean dramas where filmed!. Most of the areas are paved but it was great fo me since it made it easy to walk with the stroller.

I don't understand when I saw that people gave poor reviews for this place. Camellia Hill for me was nothing short of magic. Even in autumn when it wasn't supposed to be the peak season it was beautiful. You can take slow walks and just enjoy the relaxed feeling. It's made to be beautiful for every season and you can't deny it. I can imagine myself just being there reading a book or just sipping warm tea at the cafe. It's definitely well thought of.
i didn't go into the house but only walked along the path outside. the sea view is beautiful and you can plan to go with some other attractions nearby

I confess! We went there mainly for the dessert.We had fun taking some silly pics with the props provided at the enclosed viewing platform upstairs.  Then we joined the queue to the desserts. We tried the green tea roll cake (my favourite) the green tea mille crepe cake (my husband's favourite) the green tea ice cream & green tea frappe (my daughter's favourite). We liked it enough to go back for another round the next day.A short walk next door led us to Innisfree. Our daughter wanted to DIY soap but they were closing so we missed it.

Good spot for a quick photo very close to downtown jeju . You can walk from the middle of town very easily over the bridge and then round . Walk down do the photo and from the viewing area also a car park with toilet close by .

Good place to visit. We joined YEHA's East Course tour and this is one of the stops. A 20-25 mins walk up the slope to the tip of the peak. Nice to do this at end Nov where weather is cool. You can get a good view when you reach the top. You can visit Woman Drivers taking their dip at the base. There are many shops at the base where all buses and cars park.

Glad we went here. Quite busy on a Sunday but worth it. Great views of the formations and nice parks at either side to walk through or picnic in. Very reasonable admission and we took our dog in on a lead. Lots of stunning photographs to be taken. I would say it's a must see!

For me this is a must do as it is to me the main attraction for visiting Jeju island.Seongsan Iichulbong is one of the many UNESCO Heritage sites around the world.The name Seongsan Iichulbong also means Sunrise Peak. The view at the top is very scenic and breath taking. It takes about and hour to walk up and back to base. There were many local and foreign tourists climbing up to the top. Many people scrambling around to take photos.
For a short taste of the main national park on Jeju Eorimok is a  1 hour walk . Its easy and has a great view.
Flat walk and just a slight gradient to actual falls. Cheap entry at 2000 won per person.  Scenic views and not very busy at approx. 11.30am.
Family fun...there were views in every direction & everyone was friendly...a family allowed our daughter to walk their dog. The beautiful yellow flowers were everywhere. It was a nice little hike.

Everywhere was filled with silver grass. It was also a good walk from entrance to the hills with breathtaking view of the crater. Best place for photo opportunities. Perfect for those who love nature and fresh air.

Enjoy the breathtaking views of the ocean and impressive rock formation while walking along the coast. Very beautiful and unique scenery that is really beyond description. The beauty of nature is really awesome. One has to be there to experience it! Thanks to our guesthouse owner for recommending this place!
Easy walking course with great ocean view

Considered one of the ten best view points of Jeju this attraction is not to be missed One can enjoy this visit if you like to soak yourself or would like to find yourself among the clouds. On a foggy day one can easily miss the existence of this mountain.If you are visiting during winter or rainy season better to plan the visit during afternoon as one can have a magnificent view from the top without much clouds around.This mountain believed to be formed by the volcanic lava houses the Sanbang-gulsa Temple and the Bomunsa Temple.It also has other attractions as Golden Bhuddha Tea Shops etc. Once on the top one can see the ridge called the Dragon Head where a memorial has been built for Hendrick Hamel the first westerner who was the first to introduce Korea to the western world after his ship got wrecked. This mountain is believed to be used as a watch tower and smoke used to be sent out during the day or fire was lit during the night if any urgent message was needed to be conveyed.Climbing the steps would be a little tough for those who are not regular walkers and for the old.
Breathtaking! Enjoyed the walk and picturesque view. Really enjoyed the view. Entrance fee about 2000 won for adult and 1000 for kids

Breathtaking view of the surrounding landscape. A good way to discover by walking at leisure. There is so much to enjoy what the nature can offer right in front of you. The place is well kept and it deserve the UNESCO world heritage site. A must in your itinerary to Jeju. Only regret - could not climb as high to see the the peak of Halla due to time constraint.
Best time to visit us when tide is out and you can walk and climb amongst the lava rocks. Was a little surprised at the amount of litter on the beach. Great views and lovely color of water.

Before flying to Jeju-do (island) many of my friends suggested me to do a one day jeju tour that completes the island in one day. But I'm the type of person to enjoy my vacation slowly. Although the island is not that big I wanted to enjoy every bit and detail of the island. I choose to focus on one area at a time. Three months before my trip I researched top 5 beaches in Jeju. After researching I decided my hotel and location place where to spend my vacation. I choose Seogwipo end of Jeju.  The hotel I stayed in was Grand Mer Hotel. I stayed 3 nights there it was a new hotel and the best part was it was across the ocean. You can wake up to the view of the Jungmun beach. Which was listed top beach in Jeju. It's a little far out so you'll need to rent a car. Shopping and museums and hiking was 10 mins drive away. But the view was spectacular and my morning walk was so refreshing. If your ever in Seogwipo you have to try Hawaiian Shrimp restaurant which was 15 mins away from my hotel
Beautiful!! Had to walk up to see the whole view..its breathingtaking !!For those who appreciate nature..shld come.
Beach very nice with brown sand colored by volcanic rock.  Also can rent paddle boats and other water boats?  Great view overlooking the water on walking path over the water.
Awesome! to climb to the peak takes at least 1 hour in a walk and stop manner! nice view of the sea.

At first glance this place looks like a fun place but quickly becomes a waste of time.  The outdoor garden is the only place that is fun.  They have fun statues and great photo opportunities but as soon as you walk inside you will quickly become disappointed.  With the coupon entrance is about $12 and is not at all worth it.  If you come from a culture where sex is a taboo then maybe you will enjoy this place but anyone from a western culture will find it boring.  90% of the signage is only korean and not much else to see or do inside.  If it's a rainy day and you have nothing to do then maybe this could be an option but even then I would say pick something else.  This museum has gone through some changes over the years and you will notice that the more recent reviews are pretty low where as the older reviews are better.  It used to be a much better place than it is now~~

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

Arriving at the location we were welcome with the view of tea garden and a large glass with Ossuloc writing. The tour guide help us to take a photo in the tea garden. Then we walk into the Ossuloc museum where we can see various collections of tea sets from various countries. Then try green tea ice cream and various cakes. Oh yes they are selling various tea.

Around 10-15 mins walk to view the waterfalls. Easy to walk if you have elderly or kids with you. Water is clear and kids love the ducks around. Very near to my hotel in Jeju (EINS Hotel) which is around 5 mins drive away. Good for a short stop.
Amazing scenery and an absolutely peaceful place.  The walk up to the top is easy for such a fantastic view.  Go early at 9am to avoid the crowds.
A walking up a hill with edition of about eight hundred steps which give you a beautiful view on the eastern coast of the island. Areal nice chalenge.
A very scenic places and you must definitely plan this for your visit in Jeju. The view is so attractive but be prepared for some walking.
A nice walk to view the crater. Lovely scenes with reed plants called eoksae (flamegrass) swaying in the background. Special wonder of nature!
A nice walk to the top with spectacular views. Not too strenuous and well worth it. One of my favourite attractions in Jeju!
A great place to visit for fantastic coastal views of Jeju. The boardwalk was well constructed and easy for most people to walk. The women divers? shows are scheduled at 1.30 and 3 pm.

A great place to start off is the Women Divers exhibition center to see the old photos and explanation from the staff on the history of Women Divers. Than a slow walk up the peak for a great view ....  the wind was hallowing when we climb up and the local told us its a normal day ...   plenty of great eateries just a short walk from the entrance after the climb . A MUST visit .

A good place with nice view of the bridge and open sea. No entrance fees is required and is accessible via public transport and some walking is needed. Restaurants are available within the bridge area and other attractions such as submarine is located just right before the entrance into Saeyeongyo Bridge.

A compact park around a crater. Walk to the top and down the slope to various parts that can offer some quiet relaxation. The view is peaceful rather than spectacular but worth spending a couple of quiet hours.
You will have to walk a good while to get there. Worth the walk to see both falls. The bridge on our way was beautiful. Breathtaking view. We paid 2,500 won each. Which is under $5 for two people.

You can reach Ilchulbong by bus from the Intercity bus Terminal in Jeju-Si. It takes around 1h30 to reach it. You don't really care if it is an express or intercity bus you are taking, they more or less all go at the same speed... which is quite fast. You can't really miss the stop which is quite close to the crater. Dozens of buses parked in front of the mountain kind of spoil the nice atmosphere of the place but remember you are a tourist as well...  Left to the entrance, their is a nice small temple, worth the look. The climbing to the top is all made of wooden stairs and doesn't take too long (don't remember exactly, around 30 min). We did it with kids (youngest is 6) and she could do it easily. The view from the top is nice. It is a bit disappointing not to be allowed to walk around the crater. You can just see it from a platform. Before (or after) climbing, don't forget to take a look at the beach on the left of Ilchulbong specially between 13:00 and 15:00 when the old women divers are fishing.

You can climb up to the peak, you can climb down to the beach, or just walk around in between, & still have beautiful views. You could spend most of the day here. The women divers were not diving the day we were there.

Yes, the walk is steep and if you go for sunrise, you will be starting off in the dark, but it doesn't take long to reach the top (16-30 minutes for reasonably fit people). The most important thing is to watch the forecast beforehand to ensure a lovely sunrise. The views are outstanding. It can get quite crowded at the viewing   steps   at the top, so get there early to stake out your perfect viewing spot. The walk down will obviously be in much lighter conditions, affording some incredible views of the coastline and the little town of Seongsan. Early morning or during the day, any time would be a fantastic time take this short - but oh so worth it - hike.
