There is plenty of accommodation for all budgets in Seongsan at the foot of the mountain and bus 701 or 710 can take you directly there from Jeju City Bus Terminal. In April, 2016, the entrance fee cost 2000 Won for adults.

Worth a visit to capture the incredible sunrise and sunset views. Take a walk up and around the peak, listen to the waves crashing and feel the mighty wind sweeping.We were during winter. We were glad to be wearing enough to bear the chilly wind beating at us.
White sand, clear water. View of several islands. Family beach. Easy to get to, great to walk along the water's edge.

While we are attended an business meeting, after finishing all we went to visit some places. This place is very natural, but you need to walk a little bit to reach until the fountain.Keep some time for this place to explore and perhaps enjoy. Taking photos also can be very beautiful as it offers stunning views.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

When you said about Jeju, this Ilchubung will appear in the advertisement and you will know that is Jeju. But for sure, you will not able to snap a photo like in the adver since that only can be done if you take a photo from the helicopter and etc.For family, it is a bit tough if you bring small kids below 10 yrs old since you need to walk to the peak via stair and for adults people also a tiring activity but worth it since you can see the good view of the city and sea around that area. For photography also it will a nice thing to have.They said, the best thing during sunrise to be at the peak, but we are not make it during the sunrise so could not provide any comments on that. Also there is free show of diverwoman at the beach area just that area, they showing the activity of catching octopus with diving and selling the octopus to the audience. Most of the korea people eat it raw with Korean Sauce, i'm yet try the tast.Souvenir shop also available at the entrance of the Ilchubung peak.Thank You.

we've seen a few caves and this one is truly unique.  Its not loaded in formations such as stalagmites/stalagtites, but the lava shelves go on forever.  It literally takes over thirty minutes to walk from one end to the other at a decent clip.  Very humid inside, definately bring an umbrella or raincoat.  Also very chilly so if you are there in summer, the temperature change can be significant.  I brought a flashlight but you really don't need it as they do a great job in keeping you on the straight and narrow.  It really gives you a great understanding of what nature can do, well worth the detour to view

Went there without much training as I envisage that winter time is more pleasant to climb. We reached the base around 7.30am as we try to take the first bus. As we envisage there are snow, I have a pair of crampons bought before arriving in Jeju. Fortunately I did as the crampon sold at the shop is rather expensive. Then it was a relax 2 hours climb, I did not want to rush, but took time to appreciate the environments and snow. The crampons came in useful as you climb further up, it gets slippery. Good to have walking sticks too. At about the 1000+ meter stop, there is shop where you could buys hot noodles and drinks. I bought another set of crampons there as it is reasonable compared to the shop at the base of the mountain.After a short rest, the final climb to the top. Here there is a series of steps and staircase that leads to the top. At some point it was rather steep so have to climb up slowly, catching my breaths as the higher altitude and cold tends to slow you down. There is a timing to get down from the mountain per regulations, hence the need to get to the top early to enjoy the view and triumph. Finally reaching the top, was rewarded with a gorgeous scenery. It was kind of crowded and there was a queue of climbers taking turns to take picture with the summit monument.  After taking lots of pictures, hiking down was relatively easily, reaching the base in half the time. Took the bus back to town to enjoy a beer and fried chickens. A trip not to be missed.

Went there to catch sunrise, but was disappointed. Couldn't see the sun peek out over the horizon as it was cloudy.Went at about 5+ in the morning, it was freezing with the winds blowing. Its autumn. Be prepared to bring your thick windproof parkas and scarves. The walk up to the peak is about 30 minutes. For someone who doesn't exercise, I must say its quite a challenge going up. Take your time. Once up there, the view is gorgeous. Take lots of pictures.From Seogwipo-shi, we drove about 1 hour to get there. So do plan your time correctly to catch the sunrise.

Went there in early autumn, the crater is covered with silver grass field, view is breathtaking especially during sunset, drop dead gorgeous!Suggest to wear comfortable shoes as you are expected to walk on some manmade rocky pathway. Parking is free and plenty of parking lots available. Entrance ticket is 6000 won for adult, kinda pricey given the area isn't big, but if you've never been there, it's totally worth visiting especially in autumn!

Went there by bus using the 201 bus line, it will stop you to the 'entrance' (basically the highway) which is a long far walk into the actual entrance. There's a small bus stop where you can take another bus in (slow) but taxis will frequent the highway entrance looking for customers. The cave itself its a magnificent sight to behold..it's huge! Not sure about all the negative reviews about it poorly lit and all, because the place is actually adequately lit (to fit the ambiance of a cave, no artificial colored disco lights) and concrete steps are placed everywhere in the tunnel to prevent accidental missteps. The ground is naturally uneven, you can't expect marbled tiles here. It can get quite cold and wet at 10-13deg, so bring a light jacket and proper walking shoes. Overall it's quite an experience, you can tell your friends that you've been in the underbelly of a volcano!

Well-known by Korean tourists to Jeju as a filming location for the very popular drama   Daejangguem  , Oedolgae is perhaps the most scenic volcanic rock formation on the island. The area is more of a viewpoint attraction, you walk the beautiful coastline only so far. Most visitors spend 30-60 minutes visiting the site, cameras are usually busy. If you're visiting Jeju during the summer, it is probably best to visit Oedolgae in the morning before it gets too busy. Jeju is full of dramatic coastline, this is one of the most picturesque locations.

Well, its certainly not the Giant's Causeway, but still quite an impressive natural rock formation.  We were at the convention centre and found ourselves with a few hours spare one afternoon so it was a no-brainer to stroll down to the coast and view this rare feature.  Fairly busy, then then so is the GC.   Comfortable walkways and great views.  Certainly something to fill your trip to that part of the world with.
Weather was nice but windy and after a short (subjective!) walk on the steps up, we were rewarded with beautiful view of the sea and surrounding area. Worth a trip there.

We woke up at 3am for this and didn't regret it. It was really quite awesome. We drove in the wee hours of the morning for 1.5 hrs to get there, before hiking up for about 40mins to get to the viewing deck where there are seats to see the sunrise. To best enjoy this, be well prepared and equipped for the journey. We slept early at about 9pm the previous night because we knew we had to wake up at 3am. Prepare bread for breakfast on the road because you will need the energy for the hike. Wear proper walking shoes to make it easier to climb up. Remember to check the sunrise timing the night before, set your gps early and accurately if you are driving. If you need help with Korean gps or not sure if you got the right place, always ask your hotel or hostel host to help you set it right the night before. Charge and prep your cameras, go early to get a good spot, because you are going to get some really awesome sights of the sunrise at this spot. Definitely go for this if you are in Jeju. Not to be missed for the world!

We were there waiting for the submarine tour and decided to walk over the bridge to kill time, it's actually quite a plesant one with nice view to surrounding area. I think it might be worth a visit if you happened to be around there.

We were staying in the Lotte Hotel Jeju and it was not too far to walk to this sight from our hotel.The view is a nice one, probably not as impressive as the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but interesting nonetheless.Definitely worth a visit for the coastal scenery but doesn't occupy much time.

We were lucky: at the moment of our visit there was this Seashell Festival: a lot of seafood and music close to the ferry terminal. It takes only 15m to get there by boat and to walk up the hill is +/- 40min walk. you got a wonderful view over both sides of the island. There's even a little outdoor museum about lighthouses :-). Besides this festival, I think it's worth a visit and you can do a tour around Udo (or U-do) on a bike: rental service is at 50meters of the ferry terminal.

We were fortunate to catch a not-as-crowded ferry at around 2plus and stayed till 530pm and got back around 6pm. Ferry ride takes around 15mins but get up early and start walking towards the exit if u don't want to be Squashed w the main crowd! Upon arrival on the island, we decided to take the bus tour (costs 5000KRW/pax) which stops at 2 locations- the lighthouse peak as well as the beach.I must say Udo is very very windy so make sure u gear up and tie your hair if necessary!Hiking up to the lighthouse took us around 15mins up(lots of stairs, but after that it's v scenic). We had a good view of the whole island, despite being drizzly throughout the day. Dennis Cafe is really nice, cozy and affordable peanut ice cream as compared to the crowded 'Running man' ice cream shop which wasn't actually good. If I could go back, I would definitely bring my international driving license and rent an E bike!

We were cruising the Far East and stopped at Jeju. The cheapest excursion was $120 per person. $240 for the two of us. Instead we walked around Jeju a little then hailed a cab. He took us all over the island doing all the same things for $100. Personal service. Stayed. As long as we wanted. Left when we were ready. One of the many ways weve seen the world much cheaper than most. 73 countries and territories so far. The village is interesting. 100 huts. Some occupied. And a black pig. A guy will tell you about a tea they sell that if it tastes salty or sweet will diagnose your ailments. We passed. Not sure how many people read my reviews. If you hit ?helpful?,  I?ll get an email and they always encourage me to write more :)

We went up in 20 minutes and down in 15,  we are quite fit,  all age groups going up and even people in flip flops!) I would recommend you time your visit so that you get to see the women divers (13:30 and 15:00) either before or after your walk.  If I went there for just the walk I would have been disappointed,  the photos you see are of course ariel views and a walk up doesn't give you that view,  having said that the coastal views from above are nice.  It was raining when we went but it was still do-able.  We took bus 701 (runs every 20 mins 3300 wan per person each way) from seogwipo and back.  It stops at Seongsan-ri office,  ticket booth is a couple of minutes walk away.

we went up by erimok, was the slightly shorter course but scenery was still fantastic towards the top. took us 3.3hours to reach the 1700m resting point which sells korean cup noodles at only 1500+won (ard there). this is not the peak, if you like to challenge yourself further, will have to walk for another 3-4 hours to the peak. So if you really decide to go to the peak, then just use the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa course, its shorter.We were lucky to meet some locals who advise us to walk down by yeongsil. And apparently yeongsil has the most scenic view out of all the courses. Only thing is that its full of stairs... so dont advice ascending by yeongsil. We could see ppl giving up halfway on our way down yeongsil. One more problem abt yeongsil for those who dont drive is that the bus stops 2km away from the main entrance (20mins BRISK walk) and its quite steep on most parts. Or else you can actually catch a taxi from the bus stop, should be a 5mins journey.

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)

We went to three or four different beaches on the island and this one hands down is the best. We didn't swim as it was in September already but spent a couple of hours strolling on the boardwalk. There are plenty of eateries across the street from the beach and some were on the beach side as well. The view was fantastic and definitely worth a visit. Also, parking was quite easy as well. We stopped for coffee (of course) and sweets at the nice coffee shop right on the beach before leaving and sitting there drinking coffee and watching sunset was a real treat.

we went to this place, but we didn't went up the park/hill/rock, as it will require lots of walking, which we didn't want to do :)you will still be able to have an impressive view at the entrance, and amazed by this natural creation. you can see the people walking up to the peak, enjoy the strong wind, as it is located by the sea, do a little shopping around the entrance area, or even find a nice cafe that is facing the spot to enjoy a hot coffee!

We went to see waterfall at 12PM, there were loads of people, nevertheless view was stunning, waterfall is huge. I'd say better go in day time as when sun is starting to set you'd get weird shadows on your pics and it just won't be the same. Bear in mind you'll have to walk on huge rocks so it's not very safe for toddlers and those carrying their babies, not suitable for those with walking difficulties. Better wear sports clothes which would cover legs in case you fall, to prevent scratches or whatever other injuries. It says no swimming but we took off our shoes and walked in shallow water. It was cold but fun. We also sat on rocks in close proximity to waterfall and splashes from it made us quite wet. But it was spectacular. Such a unique place! Tickets are 1,000 for 16-24 year olds, they require ID. For adults it's 2,000.

We went to Marado Island by taking a 1 h-long ferry from Jeju Island (Daejung-Eup, Hamo ri). The ferry was nice and the could stand in either deck to enjoy the scenic view of the ocean. When you approach the island you could see the beauty of volcanic layers that forms the island and the interface of volcanic rocks and ocean was amazing. Walking is the best way to enjoy the island and you may spend nearly 3 h in the island. There are a couple of restaurants, a beautiful buddha temple, a church etc. A nice half-day trip. Highly recommended.

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

We went there for sunrise, which was a short drive from our hotel. It's green, refreshing and pleasant for the view of its surroundings. The view of the city and ocean from the top is ?も?breathtaking?р?р?. It was quite crowded with Koreans and tourists. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surroundings.

We went in fall and took the Youngsil pathway. There are about 4-5 different ways to hike up. I thought ours was supposed to be an easier one, but Id say it is like walking up the stairs endlessly. Once you get high up enough, you have a fantanstic view, and in fall, it is all red and yellow leaved. It's absolutely gorgeous and worth the hike. The way up and down is also very much enjoyable. But there is quite a bit of people, so if you are slow, make space for others coming behind you.

We walked up to the top to enjoy the breathtaking views. I felt that this was a mountain instead of a hill. It was really worth the trip to the top. The history of the area too makes visiting the area worthwhile, so many great views from both high up and down at ground level.

We walked to this Waterfall from our hotel (Days Hotel Jeju Seogwipo Ocean). Though it was scheduled to open at 9am, it open only at 11am as the rain the day before cause some flooding. Easy access to the Falls but needs to be careful walking on the rocks. I sprained my little toe doing this. View of the cliff and ocean is great!

We visited Udo Island in October 2016 and took the hop on hop off bus and got off at the first stop to climb up to the peak where the lighthouse was.  The climb took about an hour and though there were steps and a well travelled path, it still required some physical effort. There were hardly any trees and you would be well advised to wear a hat and sun block. Wear comfortable walking/hiking shoes and bring plenty of drinking water.  We climbed to the peak on a hot sunny day and had to stop a few times before we reached the lighthouse. The view was worth our effort.  Then we climbed down to the surrounding park, which was basically grassland with minimal trees and hardly any shelter. There were lots of other tourists.  We saw some horses grazing here and could see across to the mainland and sunrise peak as well as parts of Udo below.  This is the most enjoyable part of UDO for us and highly recommended.

We visited the Jungmun Golf Club for doing the Moon Light Walking Tour. We went there to warm up for the Jeju Olle Walking Festival. The view was awesome and it was a nice experience to walk there during sunset. At the end, they prepare a concert for all the participants there.

We visited on a sunny day, a nice change from the rain from the day before.At the entrance, you have the choice to walk around the short & free pathway by the sea or you could pay an entrance fee to hike up to the top of Seongsan for a birds eye view. We opted for the hike up.I wasn't very fit so it took me a couple of stops before I got up eventually..but the view was worth it. If you go earlier, you could catch the performance by the Haenyeo down by the shore at the bottom of Seongsan. Sadly, we did not manage to catch the performance.

We visited Jongbang waterfall (諛⑺) during our stay in Seogwipo. It's very conveniently located and easy to find. Entry fee is just 2000. There's very short hike (~130 steps) to get to the waterfall. It's a small-ish waterfall and don't expect it to be Niagara Falls kind of but the view is nice. Once you get down the stairs there are rocks that you can walk over to get to the bottom of the Falls, take some nice pictures and feel the water droplets. I wouldn't say it's THE things to do in Jeju island but if you happen to be staying in Seogwipo or driving by, it's worth a visit. It takes less than an hour and can be visited with kids...and if you happen to go here try some orange juice or chocolates!!

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We visited here as part of of our cruise ship day tour of the island. This is a very pretty place with amazing photo opportunities throughout. We purchased one of our favorite souvenirs from a kiosk selling genuine Jeju produced hats. We enjoyed the gardens and the walk over the bridge with the amazing views of the gorge and waterfalls. Be aware that the VERY long walk down to the   close-up   of the waterfalls is rather taxing and may not be worth the effort. Overall, a great experience!

We took bus no 100 from seogwipo city to the last bus stop. Walk up the road to the next bus stop and got on the intercity bus no 701. Got off at the beach overlooking seongsan illchubong. Plenty of spots for great pics here. Walked all the way to the entrance and up. Manageable. Highly recommend wearing good comfortable shoes. The climb up was not as bad as I thought it would be. The view from the bottom was quite intimidating at first  though. Many restaurants with reasonable prices to stop for lunch after the climb. Overall, good place to visit.

We took bus 701 from Jeju city... it only took 1hr 30mins when we were told it would take 2hrs which was a pleasant surprise. The walk up is (unsurprisingly) hard because of all the steep and often uneven steps. I would suggest going in the morning or late afternoon when it's not so hot because in the heat it was tough! People say it takes 20 mins which I would say is accurate but of course depends on your fitness levels. It was so worth it though, the views are incredible. They have an amphitheater like viewing platform I guess for those wanting to see sunset/sunrise. And you go down a different way so no clashing with people coming up. It can get quite busy though!

We took a walk along the Shores of the rock.. It sure beats jux standing at the top of the observertory and takin pictures! The views are once again spectacular, no complaints.. The walk was not terrible although but I'd warn you to be careful and pick proper shoes coz they can get slippery from the crashing waves! Along the walk you'll see ahjummas selling fresh seafood catches. Try it if you have time!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance (I have attached the photo) and you can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We alighted and headed to the dark brown beach along Seongsan. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore where to can pick clams and walkway with dry cuttlefish along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum as we reached Jongdal Elementary school at 5.30 pm. Noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market to Jongdal Elementary school (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier. We decide to go back as it was late by bus 701 back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal from Jongdal Elementary school  as we noted that the bus will take about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.

We stayed at Clouds Pool and Spa Hotel which is 1km away so we could reach there at 5am to do the climb. It is fairly an easy climb aided by a lot of stairs. We had breakfast at Paris Baguette which is opposite the mountain. They open at 5am. We had peaceful breakfast as we were the only couple there. The top of the peak offers beautiful panorama view of the green grass crater, sea view skyline and the other side is the Jeju city bird?s eye view.  Air is fresh and very windy on the peak (I thought I could fly away). There were only 3 persons on the peak when we arrived. We could stay there for about half an hour to enjoy the scenery and the peace. The female divers abalone catching activities happen at 1.30pm or 3.30pm below the mountain. It?s another steep way down from carpark infront of Seongsan Mountain. From my hotel room, I could see people walking up to the mountains all day and evening. It?s definitely a must visit when you come to Jeju!

We spent the day driving around the island, stopping off different places that sounded interesting and this was one of our stops!  GORGEOUS scenery but could be frustrating when packed with people.  No getting off the boardwalk so your view is the same as everyone else.  Fun little walk and exploration, especially for those with little kids.  The boardwalk helps keep young ones corralled!

We spent over 2 hours here just admiring the view and enjoying a very leisurely walk up and down Seongsan Ilchulbong. We didn't arrive until just before 9am but already it was packed with lots of tourist buses. If you want to miss the crowds then you definitely have to go at the crack of dawn. Having said that, we weren't too bothered by the tour groups as they would come and go in waves pretty quickly due to their limited time at the location. We sometimes had at least 5 minutes all to ourselves at the top to enjoy the view in peace.Wear comfy shoes!

We really enjoyed our visit. Great view over the ocean. The temple cave was very different. The main temple was beautiful with brilliant colors. We were told that it was built around 1970. Lots of photographic opportunities.We took the bus from Jungman (Bus 282, 202 or 32) and got off at the Jungman High School stop. We walked back towards the Stone Garden and took a right and then a left. Easy walk from the bus stop.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

we hired a taxi driver for day-trip, it's just located nearby Eco Land Theme Park & Mini Land Theme Park.we visited on late april, so not much to see. not even green farmbut still a great view to have fun with it. good experience to have a nice walk.

We hiked up Seongsan Ilchulbong  to watch the sunrise. It's a 20-40 minute walk to the summit where there is a spectacular view of the dormant volcano, a beautiful view of the sunrise even on a cloudy day and numerous other spectacular views.  There is a large platform at the summit so even though there were at 100 others, there was plenty of room. On your way down, you can visit the adjacent lagoon where there are pearl diving demonstrations and enjoy some additional views.  There is also a very nice Buddhist Temple near the parking lot at the base of Seongsan Ilchulbong.The walkway has steps going up and there is a separate route going down.Tips:  (1) Wear good walking shoes.  Some of the walkway is jagged volcanic rock, and the steps could get slippery if wet. (2) Bring a camera.--

We hiked to the top of the volcano. The walk was pretty easy but long. Lots of information signs make it really easy to manage. The first part is in the wood, which means no view but shadows. The last quarter of the ascension is out of the woods but was really crowded what made the walk boring.The volcano is nice, but i think it may be overrated dut to the fact that it is the highest mountain of Korea.Anyway, it is a must do if you go to Jeju

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do). The Sangumburi entrance fee is expensive if not in season to see the wheat fields at their peak and the changing leaves of fall, I think it was 11,000won or $11. I recommend going to Chefline Park if you are seeing this April 2018. Entrance if free there and but no volcanic crater. We went here and there was construction going on and the wheat fields had been cut down. They should charge less when construction is going on and the field has been cut. The walk around the park only takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. There are some nice views and the crater is cool.

We had only a metre of visibility when we went, it was cold, rainy and foggy. My review probably doesn’t do it justice, we were just super unlucky that day. Don’t visit on a rainy day. There is however a restaurant with an exhibition on top and there is a restroom too. We didn’t even bother with the walk as it looked gloomy and we couldn’t see much.

We had a tour inside a golf club and since it's a huge land, it actually takes time to go back and forth. So I recommend it for people who enjoy walking especially in such a beautiful place. At the end of the tour, we had a mini-concert organized by them and they were signing us a live song which made me goosebumps because it was like in a movie where you enjoy the ocean view, nature, and good music with the best company.

We found the reviews here very useful for preparing ourselves for the ascent so I'm contributing my own, hoping that others will find it equally helpful!   I'd say that it's a simple ascent for those already used to hill walks and there's no way one can lose the path, as it's between ropes or handrails all the way.  The path surface is mainly made of railway sleeper type large wooden beams and rocks which provide good terrain when dry.  However, for our descent it was raining and slippery and we were constantly bracing ourselves for a slip caused by the crowds - beware those with spikey walking poles! - descending more quickly than we were!  Our ascent to the peak took a leisurely 3 1/4 hours so we were delighted, although we weren't rewarded with any views but the sense of achievement and relief was great!  Our descent took 3 3/4 hours and sometimes my pace felt a little faster than comfortable, as had to concentrate so hard on each footstep placing. It looked as if some sections of the path near the summit have been replaced fairly recently, as we found it to be in good condition and not like the experience of other reviewers - and that was a relief!  I'm very glad that I wore my walking boots to protect my ankles, as the rocks are uneven and a few are slightly unstable.  So, short, if you're fit and used to hill-walking, you have nothing to fear but if you're not usually very active, then give yourself a plan B e.g. opting for the side-path to Sara Oreum if you realise, by the junction with the path off to that (round trip 40mins) that you're struggling.  That would mean that you'd still have the great satisfaction of a spectacular view from Korea's highest mountain but without the stress of having had to climb - and descend! - the 1200 metres from the bus stop to the peak!  Make sure you have enough layers of clothes and a good hat and gloves for the summit and descent, as, at this time of year, you'll definitely need them.  Oh, and if you're looking at the frequent posts with figures on alongside the path and which start with a '1' at the bottom which then progress to '2' etc, the peak is '36'.  Hoping you find this as helpful as we found other reviews!

We didn't take the 3-hour journey but rather followed our tour guide on shorter route (approx 45 mins one way) to the top of another similar peak. It was bright and sunny with cold breeze which made a perfect day for hiking and photo taking. It's mainly   country view   from the top where green fields and moutains cover majority of your sight. You can also see the beach and sea far away with planes taking off and landing at Jeju airport. Overall, it's a nice outdoor walk and a place to chill out after a hectic journey.

We did this on a rainy day just before a typhoon hit. It was perfect conditions as it meant a lot less people were walking around. The falls are all beautiful, the bridge is picturesque and  made for great views. The walkways are very well signposted and there is a lot of information about. You are not allowed to swim there which is important to know when taking kids, it is a real shame as there were many potential swimming holes!

We did this hike by end of March 2014. The first part is indeed a kind of forest walk. Half way we were indeed surprised to see some snow on the hills and later on lots of snow on the path, Since we did not have those clampons it was pretty tough. At the 2nd shelter we did indeed buy those clampons whereafter the hike was more easy to do. The view from top was not that good due to the upcoming mist. We were amazed though to see so many RAVENS waiting for food.

We did the Yeongsil Hike - having stumbled upon a sign for the 500 Buddha's Disciples.  We had no idea what to expect and went into it fairly blind.  Loved the hike!  A pretty walk, but it didn't take an excessive amount of time.  Not all that strenuous either.  We had a very pretty view, although it was a bit hazy.  I would've liked to have spent more time hiking around the National Park, but that just wasn't in our schedule.

We did the sunrise peak climb as part of our tour of Jeju with Yeha bus tours - it wasnt at sunrise, but it was pretty pleasant nevertheless.We started off by watching the women divers at the bottom of the cliff. After this, it is an easy 20 - 25 minute climb up - with gorgeous views over the sea and island. Unfortunately, part of the peak was fenced off because of some maintenance work . We had a nice  walk down, enjoying the views .Tips:There are clean restrooms midway down.Try the peanut and orange ice cream at the base of the cliff - oth are yummy.

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water. Most people were using walking poles as well, which became extremely frustrating as they tended to block the paths. The only people I saw fall were using these poles, they really are not required.It would be difficult to do this track in the rain, as it would get quite slippery in places. My advice would be to go early to avoid the majority of the crowds - the car park fills with tour buses by mid-morning. We started at 0700 and it was still relatively busy then. You need to be at the last rest station by 1230 to be able to continue to the summit and leave the summit by 1430.Overall - I wouldn't do it again, but if you had a free day on Jeju, it's a good way to burn off a few calories.

We can to Jeju island for a couple of days just for this park! You have different paths to get up to the top! We decided to take the easier one to get up and than the harder one to come back! (In the end it was a good decisions) the nature is incredible and is very peaceful! On top, if you are lucky and have clear wether, the view is outstanding! If you want to do the hard way, is important to have good shoes as you walk over rocks and stones!

We came here for the sunset view, because that was the recommendation for this place. But we were disappointed.We reached Jeju via plane around 1pm and went to Hallim park (5min walk to Hyeopjae beach) after check in. After a walk around Hallim park we walk to Hyeopjae Beach for sunset watching. The weather is just nice, no rain, not too hot. The sand beach was covered with plastic material (?), I guess so tourist can walk on it. There was few garbage lying around the beach and it was a bit crowded with people, both local and tourists. The sunset view is not that nice.Again, to be fair, we come from the tropic. The Bornean sunset is probably the best sunset. So for people from the tropics, you can skip this place if you want to. But if you have nothing to do in Jeju, I guess you can come here to relax, after a walk at Hallim Park.To go here: Take bus #710 bound for Hyeopjae beach (or Hallim Park if you want to go there first. It's just 5min walk to Hyeopjae beach).

We came here as part of a tour from Hong Kong and no one else went to climb up to the top, but me and my boyfriend did. It's about a 30 minute walk - you can take it slowly and take photos along the way, but it can be a bit steep. However, the views are great (on a clear day) and you get a good workout (after sitting on a bus for so long). The ascent/descent paths are clearly marked and separated, so it's quite well organised and the path/fence is very well maintained. At the top, you can overlook the big crater, which is now overgrown with lots of lush grass and trees - quite beautiful. You can also overlook the water and the town below etc. The way down has lots of stairs, so watch out if you have bad knees.

Watching sunrise from the sea is amazing experience. You don't have to climb up too high, still can see the downtown below. And the way down is such a relax with beautiful view. Just 5 minutes walk from the bus stop and very near from Seopjikoji
Was it worth the view? It was windy and a bit of a walk ...but was it worth the view? Nope! Our tour coach took us there. One has to use a lot of imagination to   see   a dragon's head!

Walking up the stairs is tiring but once at the top, you can see the craters which are filled with greenness of plants... View the surroundings from top is superb! Good for nature lovers yet those that do not want to hike the hill...At the seaside below the hill, you can enjoy seafood fresh fr the sea!

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html

Walked to the bridge as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel seogwipo). It's a nice bridge and you can walk across it to saeyong island, where you can have a short hike around the island. Nice views during the hike where you can see the ocean and three different islands. It's also near Cheonjiyeon waterfall.

Walked over from our hotel to the waterfalls and enjoyed the view.  Absolutely gorgeous. As a group, we enjoyed climbing up and down stones to get closer to the falls for pictures or over to see the fishermen (and women) slightly further away from the falls.
Walk up to the peak & you'll never regret...Healing by nature. Can see beautiful view of Jeju.Though a bit tiring to walk up to peak, you'll be amazingly surprised.Will come again soon!

Visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on a rainy and cloudy day. It was very busy, even with the bad weather.You can walk up via the stairs to the top of the volcano. With nice weather I am sure the views are great. When the top is in the clouds as today, I suggest you visit the house of the Jeju woman. Pretty sure you will be impressed by the skills of these older ladies. A must visit when in Jeju Island and having nice weather.

Visited during Jan, weather is cooling and is just nice for walking up to the peak. It takes some energy and time to get to the top, it wasn?t too difficult as there are many places you can stop and rest before you continue to the top. Very nice view, should take some time to enjoy the area instead of rushing to the next destination.

Very worthwhile museum to visit on Jeju.  Gives an in depth view into Haenyeo culture, female free divers who gather shell fish.  Since the culture of the Haenyeo is beginning to die out, the museum is an important way to keep the knowledge alive.  Movie and exhibits, with beautiful walks through the village and surrounding farm fields.
Very unique waterfall by the sea. walk up close and feel the water spray across your face, while the sea waves lap your feet below. great view and refreshing experience.
Very peaceful and beautiful place. Loved walking around and seeing all the beautiful bonsais, scenic view, beautiful waterfall and fishes. Would definitely love to visit again <3

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.

very close to segwipo city and easy access makes its must visit place if you are in segwipo city. The place is famous due to a korean drama., they have place the cut of the main character of the drama at the point it was shot. You take your pics there. there are 3 view points and is easily accessible (around 250m walk)

Udo- we went early, were there before 9am. Spent roughly 3 hours on the key spots.1. Ferry to Udo- Our jumbo taxi driver drove us over. Needed to fill out all personal details plus showing our passports when purchasing tickets. Return trip for 5 of us plus driver plus jumbo taxi return was KRW70,000. No queues, not crowded. We went there on 2 Jun 2017 Friday. Just a 15-min ride, need to leave the car diring the trip. Have a good view of Sunrise Peak from the ferry.2. Peak- For a good view of Jeju and Udo, walk up to the peak. Be alert that the track along the coastline uphill is not an easy one for people who don't exercise a lot.  Useful to have hiking stick with you for this short track.3. Geommeollae Beach- Absolutely gorgeous scenery.  A must go place. That's where the famous peanut icecream shops are. There are two.  We tried one and it tasted well.4. Beaches- We went to two. Unforgettable colour and tranquility.  Must go as well.

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say   Udo  . The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the   old fashioned   bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Took bus 781 from City Hall in Jeju City about 30-40min bus ride for 1300KRW. Had some breakfast at the Seongpanak bus station (base camp), got a bottle of water and a snickers then started the hike. Read that it would take 8-9 hours roundtrip, got to the top in less than 3, a very slow and steady rising hike firstly through the forest and later up the mountain. Stunning views from about 1800m and up, saw some water also in the crater, quite crowded at the summit. Ate my chocolate bar, took a selfie and started walking down. Total time return trip to the bus station was 6 hours. Best tip is to not pause at the middle camp which you must reach before 12:00 if you want to get to the peak, but instead just walk on to the top and have some lunch or break up there, you will then skip most of the crowd, try to head back down before 13:00, as you need to leave the peak before 13:30 it does get crowded on the descent and will just increase your time spent by waiting for slow groups.The views are spectacular, do recommend, no fees.

Took bus 701 from Seogwipo (around 1hr20mins) to Seongsan IIchulbong entrance station. The bus doesn't exactly stop at the entrance, but you can see the crater from the station. Just walk towards it. A big innisfree building is where the entrance is. The wind was pretty strong on the day that I went, so it was a good thing I brought my windbreaker. I suppose on less windy days, it's not that cold as many were in shorts and t-shirt. ie, they weren't prepared for the wind and were shivering. It is a relatively easy hike up, proper steps and handrails (many elderly made it up there slowly, taking multiple breaks on the way). But if you are fit, half an hour should be sufficient for you to reach the top. For this short hike, the view is totally worth it.

To get the best view you have to walk down steps to water level, then across a   flattened   stone area to a tent where a local vendor sells things.  Go just past the tent for the best view.  Best on a clear day with blue sky and water in the background.  Plan 30 minutes max.
To Enjoy the scenery, atmosphere we should climb up within the path.  To climb up it takes about 30-45 minutes if we walk slowly.  You can enjoy the Clean Air here.  The View will be very nice.

To be honest, I didn't expect much at first, but when I started walking up the stairs, OMG! I was really awed by the clear blue sky, silver grasses, wind, everything! The view of the crater was just   so-so   to me but the view of the other side with the silver grasses was just way too amazing! I would say, it's not something that's so special that you must go to see no matter what but still, it's something that you won't be able to see everyday or everywhere. First of all, you must go at the correct timing. I went during mid-October, the view was magnificent! You can even see Hallasan from afar (check out my photo). Thereafter, you can walk through a small road where you literally being surrounded by silver grasses. That's a perfect place to take photos as well (photo attached).This can be a romantic place, or it can also be a peaceful place where you go to relax your mind and to see something different.

To be blunt, I couldn't see the dragon's head in the Dragon Head Rock, and I'm not alone. Apparently a portion of the formation fell off during a heavy storm long ago, so perhaps it was once more impressive. Currently, it has become iconic for a rather tired trend in Korean tourism. Pointing at the sky and finding clouds that look like other things is childlike. Officially naming rocks and then designating them as   important cultural artifacts   in order to manufacturer tourism is crass. In much the same way that the Korean government has become intimately involved in generating the so-called   Korean Wave   of K-pop and Korean television dramas, there is a constant rush to capitalize on landmarks, events, and experiences that will help distinguish Korea in general and Jeju specifically in the competitive marketplace of global cultural value. This push to invent cultural significance is monopolized by a predominately male class of older Korean bureaucrats who have capitalized on Confucian values in order to override younger, better ideas, fueling their own, often tedious marketing concepts despite the existence of far better and substantive materials from which to draw inspiration. Take for instance Jeju's rich history of folklore and deities. Sure, you can dawdle about with stories of a dragon stealing jade or herbs of immortality from Halla Mountain and being shot by a celestial arrow as punishment, turning it to stone; but the fact is there are literally hundreds of far better stories that have some basis in local lore rather than the distinctly artificial details surrounding the Dragon's Head Rock. If you're interested, look for books on the subject, some of which were written by expatriates in an attempt to save this rich heritage from being slowly whitewashed away by modern fabrications. A book called   Spirits: Jeju Island's Shamanic Shrines   by Joey Rositano comes immediately to mind. Or you can go to any number of local beaches and walk along paths where every 20 yards or so you can read a plaque that tells you what a large stone vaguely resembles if you squint hard and suspend your disbelief.    That said, there's nothing wrong with taking a nice stroll along the seaside in this part of town if you only have a short amount of time to spend and you need to get to the airport soon. There are some passable restaurants along the way, a couple of good caf챕s, and some great views of the ocean. However, make no mistake - this is an authorized conduit for tourists and as such you will be subject to a conveyor belt of people on the same walk, as well as an abundance of stores whose sole purpose is to extract money from you by selling tawdry bits of plastic.

This waterfall is not very big as compare to other but the view is breath-taking as the water falls into the edge of the cliff at the sea front. One can feel the mist of the water fall spraying onto the face as one walk closer to the cliff of the water fall. However, be very careful while walking on the rock towards the waterfall as the rock gets more slippery as one get nearer to the waterfall. But it is definitely worth the risk and the slow walk as the pictures that comes out from the shot is gorgeous!

This was the most fascinating and beautiful experience during my two week stay in South Korea. The long, winding path to get to the coastline to see the Women Divers Show is gorgeous from beginning to end. The mist hovering over the black volcanic sand was unlike anything I have ever seen. I never wanted to leave. The hike up to Sunrise Peak was sweaty but worth it. The long, windy path to get the the top of the peak is fairly easy to walk and offers many wonderful views along the way. The fog was too dense to see anything from the very top, but I'm still glad I did it. This was such an amazing part of my trip; one of my most fond travel memories ever.

This was the last stop on Day 2 of our South Korea Tour after four previous destinations. By that time we had walked and walked and walked so much that we barely made it to the fork in the path that leads either to the top of the volcano or down to the sea shore. We took the path down  to the shoreline and waited until we got enough energy to climb back up.Whichever way you choose the views are literally breathtaking LOL. Wear shoes sensible for hiking. Sometimes the paths are rocky and steep. Also wear layered clothing as the effort of the climb up/down will cause you to sweat and the wind will cool you off very quickly. A windbreaker is useful. Always bring a cane style umbrella. Even if you don't need shelter from rain or sun, you can always use it to steady you on your hike.Take a lot of photos and keep your trash to yourself. Trash disposal bins are rare.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This was rated as one of the top 3 to visit in Jeju so we actually stayed at the nearby Airstay Hamdeok Hotel.  It  was very nice.  The beach is clean and had pristine waters and black rocks.  The sand was fine and felt good to walk on with your bare feet.  There were some really nice picturesque views so we took a ton of photos. There was a connected path to a hill and it allowed for some decent small hikes.  We went in March so the flowers on the hill were blooming with yellow and purple colors.  There were also some white flower blossoms coming out from the trees. With the ocean or the city views in the background from the hill, it allowed for some very unique photos for your memories.  After the little hike, we played around in the water on the beach and it was nice because it was low tide and you could hang out in one of the exposed sand bars. It was very pretty and relaxing. Definitely a must see if you're in Jeju!

This was our second trip to Udo.   We were riding around Jeju Island by bicycle so decided to explore the island on foot.   The weather was very hot and exposed (Summer), so you really need a big hat.    The island is quite unique, we walked up through the middle of the island and enjoyed the barren landscape.   We came across a Buddhist temple and met the lone monk there who chatted and gave us cups of coffee and tea.  He also introduced us to his friends - a haenyeo and visiting Butoh dancer who we interviewed for our website.   We briefly visited the beaches which were nice but crowded.  The unique landscape and interesting people was the best thing about Udo.

This was one of the highlights of my trip. In autumn there is a sea of pampas grass swaying in the breeze on the slopes of this volcanic crater. If you walk up a little you get an amazing view of Halla Mountain and it makes for some great photos.  We went early in the morning and it was amazingly quiet - we could just hear the rustling grass.As we were leaving tour groups started coming in so could be nicer if you beat the rush.Entrance is 6,000 won which is a little expensive on Korean terms for a small attraction like this, but I thought it was well worth it.

this was one of  the most memorable places i visited in jeju. the coast was not an easy walk through, there were 2 entrances/exits for the coast. we took the one with large rocks we had to climb down through. (would recommend taking the other entrance which was behind a large ship) it was scary and there were a lot of sea roaches scurrying around. the VIEW AND WALK around the coast was worth everything though. the coast right infront of sabangsan mountain was filled with canola flowers.

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This was a nice walk up to the top. There's a lot of stairs, but it's not nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. We went in Oct on a fairly sunny day (temp was probably in low-mid 20's) and you definitely want some water and sunscreen with you. I'd recommend going when it's more cloudy, if you can. There are a couple little shops along the way to the top (the first few levels of stairs, not all the way along) where you can also purchase water, and there is some tasty Jeju orange ice cream for sale too. The views are pretty, as is the temple, and it wasn't too busy when we were there in the middle of the afternoon.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This was a great stop for us, and even the kids enjoyed it.  It was refreshing in the summer.  The walk was not bad at all, and the view was just beautiful.  It's nice to just pause and think about how those rocks were created.  There were a handful of people so it took some time to get a nice spot to take a photo without people in the background.  I can't imagine how much harder it is when the weather is better.  It's still a must-see when in Jeju.

This temple is on the side of Sanbangsan (san means mountain). The mountain is very impressive. The scenery here is spectacular. I highly recommend buying a ticket for not just the temple but also the beach. (Keep in mind that the beach area closes at either 5:30 or 6:00pm depending on the day.)The walk up to the Buddha was nice with great views of the beach as you climbed. But bring bug spray!! I walked away from here with about 12 mosquito bites, because I forgot to put on my spray until I got to the top.After visiting the temple, leave yourself at least 45 minutes to explore the beach. It will take 10 minutes to walk down (and 15 to walk up - the uphill is always worse!). You can walk out along the coastline, and it's very cool. Important note: getting a taxi FROM here is VERY difficult. We were there near closing time, so no one was being dropped off once it was time for us to leave. Luckily for us, a Korean couple noticed our trouble and offered to call a taxi for us. Without them, we might still be there!

This site consists of a large network of staircases that you climb to see a crater as well as a beach where the woman divers do a demonstration.The walk up the stairs is very long. It is not impossible and there are many places to take breaks without holding up the line. The spot is very busy so there will be an unbroken line of people going up and down. I would suggest taking water with you. The view from the top is quite nice. Allow 1 hour to do the climb at a leisurely pace.At the beach the woman divers do demonstrations on a set schedule. Check the times when you arrive. They will suit up for the dive, sing a song and then go into the water looking for seafood. When we were there a lady came back with an octopus. It does not take long for them to find something so it is worth it to wait to see the catch.There are bathrooms and snack shops there as well.

This place is the signature sightseeing here. So every tourists would be here. It's crowd with people. There're many shops, kiosk, snack bar and food shops at the front of the sightseeing. So there are large space for parking. You need to buy ticket to get in there. Once you get ticket, you walk straight on the walk way till you see the junction. There's the highlight signage for photo shooting. And you need to choose either way to go. If you go to the right, you need to walk up to the hill and you will see the good view from there. The way to go up the mountain is fine, not too rough. But not recommend during rainy day.If you go to the left, you will see fisherman Village, sea sand sun and fresh seafood from local people. The highlight is the lady from the village dive deep into sea to get the seafood stuffs.

This place is massive! Truly a great venue to walk around. While it was closed the day I was there  I walked around the entire stadium and was impressed with everything outside of it. I went to the   Maze   next door and took the hot air balloon ride which gave me a great view of INSIDE the stadium! This place is gorgeous!

This place is easily accessible by bus. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about more than an hour to get to Seongsan Ilchulbong. After you get off at Ilchulbong entrance station, walk right into the small alley and continue straight until the end to the Main Street, you will see sign leading to Ilchulbong. It was a nice hike but a lot of stairs. The view is beautiful up at the top. There are plenty rest stop along the way so no need to worry. When you come down, you can go to the beach where you?ll find the house of women divers. There are performances at certain time slot but since I visited in the winter, there was none. They also sell fresh seafood where you can have right at the restaurant. It was quite expensive but It?s fresh and also to support the women divers.

This pedestrian bridge leads you to a small island where you can take a walk for around 30 minutes. There is not much to see on the island itself but I will say the view is quite nice. I visited around sunset time but it was a bit gloomy that day so we didn't get to see a nice sunset. There were many mosquitoes when we walked around so beware when you visit during Summer. Otherwise, this is a nice place to spend your time.
