This island took us almost 2.5 hrs to reach. We used public transport from our hotel to reach the intercity bus terminal and changed busses to the harbor. The bus ride took almost 1.5hrs but was very scenic. At the harbor, we filled out the boarding form and stood in queue for the ferry ticket. The ferry ride was 20min to the island and the ride was interesting with the sea gulls catching food thrown by other passengers. On reaching the Island, we took the hop on hop off bus .... red and got off on the 1st stop - for the light house. There we took the motor boat ride around the cliff edge. The guide was speaking in Korean so we couldn't understand much but enjoyed the view. We have a nice lunch of buttered spicy shrimps there and peanut ice cream. Then took the bus to stop 2 where we walked around the rocks and the smaller light house.  We saw both the white and red sand beaches. All in all a good day spend.

This is the largest waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea, and one of the only ones that is not fenced up at the bottom. Usually, when you visit waterfalls, it's always staring at it from a distance, where a viewing platform has been built. This is different, you get to walk ALL THE WAY to below that waterfall, and if you are open to wading through knee deep water, go touch that waterfall.The spray of water is refreshing, and the scenery rocks. You'll feel one with nature.

this is the easiest waterfall among all in jeju in terms of access.we walked for about 15 minutes before reaching the waterfall.however,to reach the waters,u have to go through slippery rocks-definitely not for kids or elderly.wear comfortable walking shoes.however,the view from the upper part of the waterfall(before descending down the many stairs) was already breathtaking.there were also foodstalls selling snacks-we had the ice cream and the grilled squid.super delicious.do try it.oh and don't forget the orange juice (hallabong).the freshest i have ever tasted.good snack,superb juice to wash it down,beautiful scenery-i could not ask for more.do visit if you are in jeju.preferably early morning before the crowd.

This is the climb for the unfit too. It is relatively easy compared to Hallasan or Elephant Mountain in Taipei (not even half as difficult) and the views all the way up and down is amazing. We did the sunrise climb as we stayed overnight at Illchubong Hotel. From the hotel, it is about 20mins walk to the base - we had a car. There are many public buses that come to this spot. If you have 4of you, you can cheaply get a taxi to the spot for the morning climb.At the top, we did not see the amazing postcard view (aerial view?). If you wanted to take the sunrise with the illchubong Seongsan, you actually do not have to climb up the mountain. There is a huge area to view it as you drive up the highway.There are public buses to the entrance/ base of the mountain. There are 2 women divers performance which we missed due to the timing. It's 11 and 1 or 3pm. You can probably go to Udo island and be back for the late performance.Highly recommended to visit.

This is sunrise peak at Jeju island you should to add in your travel list. Before go to Seongsan pls check the sunrise time. You will see a very fantastic view point here. Anaway, pls prepare your cloths for strong windy and cold. Along the walking platform the view is beautiful also. Do not miss it.

This is one of my favorite places in Jeju.? Walking up the steps to the temple you experience one enlightenment after the next.? The temple and the grounds are in immaculate condition, and clearly there is a lot of love and respect which goes into every section.? This is a wonderful hour or two to spend as you are wandering around the island - take your time, don't rush it, enjoy both the temple and its attractions, and the stunning views toward the ocean and the rest of the island.? BTW, this is not an easy stroll up the hill, but not that taxing either - if you have elders, perhaps you settle for mid-way.? if you're young - do the entire journey, you'll never know when you'll be back.

This is my favourite one of the three waterfalls i visited in Jeju! (April 2018)This place consist of three level waterfalls. The first level you will only see the waterfall if it has rained enough and the waterlevel is high enough to create the waterfall. The second one is the biggest of the three levels. It can be seen from two places. First is by the staircase and upclose. The second one is going over the bridge and after that (stone) stairs up on your rightside after crossing over the bridge. You can get a great view for the 2nd waterfall!The third and last level is the furtherst and the smallest one of all. If you are not fit enough or you can't walk very well, I advise to skip this one as there are a lot of stairs to go down and up afterwards.The first 2 levels are good enough to get a great view out of the place.

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a real gem. You can enter for free and walk around, have a picnic and enjoy nature and the views. If you hike to the top of the hill you can see the whole city and the ocean and on the other side the mountain
This is a place with a great view, you just need to walk a few minutes to get there from the enterance. There was some people that sell raw seafood snacks if you want to try.

This is a nice place to have some scenic shot. The natural volcanic formation is indeed unique. The walk from the carpark to the scenic view is just a short 10 Min slow stroll. There are amble carpark but there are many tourists too. If you don?t stay at the cliff to absorb the nature then the entire place can be done in just 45mins. So if you are here, don?t rush so that you can enjoy the wind and listen the waves hitting into the cliff!

This is a nice park with a lot of different flower and tree species. It's worth a visit and also a good opportunity to have a walk. You can climb on top of the hill to have a 360 degrees view (there is also a small cemetery there, not easy to find : take the most  peripheral path). Even in autumn it is colorful !

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This is a great little island for relaxing! Be sure to rent a bicycle in order to explore everything, as walking would take most of the day. There are a few nice cafes and restaurants along the coast, but mostly, I recommend buying yourself a can of Cass beer and sitting near the sea to enjoy the views.

This hike will make a great day trip. Make sure to leave early as you're likely to spend a couple of hours on the mountain, either walking/climbing or admiring the view. Wear proper hiking boots/shoes and layers of clothes. Bring sufficient water. Toilets are very clean.

This bridge in Seogwipo harbour goes across to a small island which takes about 20 minutes to walk around.? It is a nice place to go at sunset, there are nice views and many birds in the trees.? Also nearby are the Cheoniyeon waterfalls, and a few shops and cafes.

This beach, East of Jeju city, on the North coast, is a real gem. Our favourite part is the smaller bay to the East of the main beach. You can rent a static caravan right on the beach there, with an unbeatable, uninterrupted view of the sea. Great snorkelling around the rocks to the right and you can walk up the small oreum further to the right. The main beach has a good eatery that sells Western food and Stella Artois!

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

This beach is adjecent to GeumNeung Beach - you can walk between them. Hallim Park is also next to it - all are walkable from each other. There are plenty of shops and umbrella rentals, etc. Camping is avaiable at the next door beach. Some areas are not for swimming due to strong currents. Lovely view of a nearby island. You can take the 202 bus from the 5 day market near the airport. Takes about an hour.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

This attraction is much smaller then the other similar sounding spot - Cheonjeyeon. There is just one waterfall here and its q quick short walk to the view point. Like all other spots, swimming is not allowed here as well. Good for a quick visit before visiting the Saeyeongyo Bridge.

There's parking place but there's a fee to pay around 2000 won for my rented Kia Sportage   , Entrance fee was 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for youth . We walked around the park nearby the stairs leading to view the cliff from here .

There were sooo many people  and the view was also not that great. I couldn't even take a proper picture. First i wasn't even sure if this is the right place, because it didn't look like the pictures i saw online.Go there if you want to have a walk at the cost (2000 won admission fee) and en passant you can look at the cliffs.Going there by bus is not really convenient. The bus station is a bit far and the bus comes about every hour (timetable not reliable).By the way this kind of view you can also have at the Phoenix island (near ilchulbong).

There were a lot carter in jeju island, one of them is sangamburi.We went there by rent a car, from our hotel around 1 hour. The place is calm and nature. With mountain view, savana and trees all around.If you like nature, this place is one of your choice. One of korean movie was made there.When we entered the place, there's a garden, walked inside there's line of trees, in the middle, there's savana.Going further, you will find mountain view.
There is no harm to walk and hike to see the view of coastline and ocean.? The temple is not grand or manificent.? It is hard to hike to the budda in the cave, but you can try.

There are wonderful views from the peak here, and the walk up is pleasant enough.  I just hope that the loudspeakers blasting explanations (in various languages) are removed in the future.  They really spoil the atmosphere and convey the same information that can be conveyed on a sign.Admission is 2000 won.

There are 3 memorial towers, one of Kim Man Duk, civil uprising volunteers, and one of patriot at the end of Joseon dynasty. There is Kim Man Duk's grave stone, original one which moved here because of road construction in its original place. This is located in Sara-bong(hill) park. It is very low hi,, but you can enjoy beautiful sunrise on the top of hill. Even day time, I could enjoy nice view toward Jeju international port. I recommend walk around the hill first then visit Mochungsa afterwards, The Sarabong walk path is part of Olle #18. There are many locals who work out here. You can feel like a local!

The western name for this is Sunrise Peak, and it is an extinct volcano. The walk/hike to the top rim is quite tiring and the last 50 metres is quite steep.  Having said this, there are good steps/stairs all the way up and even older people can make it with a little effort.  The views from the top make the trip very worthwhile.

The waterfalls was nice and a real up close look was possible as the access allowed visitors to go all the way to the base of the waterfall. I like the views just before sunset, as there are haneyeo serving sashimi on the rocks nearby, giving it an additional local touch.In addition, the kids liked the fun and adventure of walking on the rocks up to the waterfall.

The waterfall is in walking distance from the center of Seogwipo, even if there are a fee steps to get to the waterfall it's worth the visit!The view is fantastic, and the vapour coming from the waterfall is refreshing (especially in summer).Beware just of the last few meters because are on rocks, and sometimes slippery.

The walk up was easy but definitely gets you sweating, even on a cool day.  The weather was not on our side when we went up and it was cloudy at the top.  We still had good views on the way up and down.

The walk up the mountain provided beautiful views!  The mild spring weather and breeze allowed for an easier ascend for a   not so in shape   person. Did not go for sunrise but pretty regardless. Easy to locate parking lot and shops near by to accept your money;).

The walk up sunrise mountain was  windy and relatively easy. Steps all the way up with many spots for you to rest and take in the beautiful view. Don't miss out on this mountain if you are going to Jeju. Entrance fee is 2000W. They charge for everything here, waterfalls and parks all have an entrance fee.

The village has preservations from time past. It made for a pleasant morning walk through the village.It's used much for filming of historical period dramas. One gets to see, close up, relative size et al, a little of what life was like 100 years ago.I enjoyed the bright golden sunshine, flowering trees and the beautiful voice of our guide who sang 2 folk songs whilst using a wine jar as an instrument.We also viewed the daily life of the women divers . Amazing people who adapted so well to the harsh realities of their world.
the view was great!  we climbed our way up to the top and when you looked across, it is just like a endless sea boundary view. the wind was relatively strong but stilll it is worth the walk

the view of the waterfall is great! however, many will get closer to the waterfall by walking through the very rocky area from the stairway. kids and elderly need to be careful and also to secure your belongings, if things were to drop into the rocks, may be hard to retrieve. ensure you wear proper footwear!

The view is so nice! It's a place where the sunrise and sunset look stunning. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. I enjoyed the walk, fresh air and most of all the view. This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. Visited September 2014

The trip up and down the 1.95km tall mountain took me the entire day but experience and view was really worth it. It would have been better if I had been properly equipped as I was in normal walking shoes and a small bottle of water while everyone else had their trekking shoes and stick with them which made going up and down more quickly and safe. There are alot of routes but not all the routes will lead you to the peak. Spoke to a few people on my way up and they shared that this is most tedious route as its the longest. There is only one way up and down which makes trekking easy for solo traveller like me.It'd be good if you can bring some food and lots of water with you where you can picnic with many korean families when you reach the peak. Do prepare to start early as you will have to reach a certain checkpoint before they allow you to continue your way up the peak. It was a heartwarming experience for me when all the korean people who walked past me would encourage me to press on and they would share they food around at the peak. Korean families usually do this as a family activity where the grandmother, grandfather, parents and kids would climb leisurely. If a grandparent can do it, so can you. Thats all :)

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The sun was shining though not really hot this time (last time 9 years ago was rainy).  I wasn't sure how far up I wanted to climb but started off with the family anyway.  Personally I preferred slopes to stairs.  I saw these signs which showed the distance to the peak (caldera): 274m, 180m, etc. I almost decided to turn back because I thought I would be late if I continued to the top when suddenly I reached the top.   Turned out that those were distance markers and not altitude markers.  The view at the top was really good.  The grass in the crater was lush green.  No steam here.  The walk back down was very manageable, and had some good photo spots.  Towards the bottom, the vast patches of perfect green grass were really pretty.

The stand-alone rock wasn't as impressive as say the Twelve Apostles in Melbourne, but it was nice to walk and take in the sights in the area.If you are a fan of Korean drama serial, Da Changjin (鸚㏝룝), you'll see that they filmed some scenes here (marked by some cut-out boards)On the way out, we saw a store selling black or red volcanic rocks (plus drinks and a really yummy grape ice bar). These rocks float cos of the air trapped in the holes. We bought some home as souvenirs to remember Jeju.I'll recommend taking a walk in the area. The views were great and it was most enjoyable.

The sorroundings are definitely better than the rock itself: nice little Korean hut, beautiful bridge. But the place is bigger than we thought and because of so many tourists and buses easy to find! To watch the waves and the ocean was also nice to see. Good to see if you are close by or want to walk around the coast! We walked there from the city centre, although it was raining, and enjoyed the view from the ocean!

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The place shows very nice rock formation, although it was eroded after so many years. It was still awesome. Nice view with a boardwalk to the observation point. We were lucky and saw some Haenyeo diving there. They could really hold their breath.

The park covers a vast area. One has to decide how far you wish to explore and watch your time. A map is given at the ticket counter and we did not expect it to be so big. We went according to the numbered stops. The view was spectacular for some parts of the park that we spent so much time on taking pictures. We tried to move quicker however, in the end, we did not even complete Course 1 (there are 3 different routes). It was enjoyable for some walk & laughter. There are scripts on stones to tell you about the legendary story of this stone park. You may decide, whether you want to keep walking and cover the whole park (I am not sure whether this is even possible in a day) or would you just want to have a feel of this peaceful and beautiful park.

The Moon Light Walking Tour at Jungmun Golf Club was pleasant and relaxing. The walking tour started and end at the same golf course with optimum safety rules for ongoing corona-19 spreading. The distance was shorter than expected, about 1.5 km which took only about 30 min. Walking was fun due to the group of new friends. During the walking, the sunset was very beautiful. Also, the scenery of the ocean view seen from the golf course was amazing. After walking for 30 minutes, we enjoyed an evening

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don?t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

The island was teeming with dragonflies and it felt like something out of a Disney film. At any rate, if you are in the area visiting the nearby waterfall, or going on a boat or submarine trip, it is a lovely walk with spectacular views all round.I wouldn't suggest going here specifically, but if you are nearby..... it's worth a look.

The hike up takes about 30 mins depending on your fitness level and speed. It is pretty easy climb up the steps and boardwalk. It was drizzling when we were there. Nevertheless, the surrounding view on top was nice. At eye level, the crater wasn't obvious as it looked more like a downhill slope. It would be great if a an observation tower is built to have an aerial view of the crater.Entrance ticket 2000 won. Suggest you relief yourself just before the entrance as there isn't any toilet facilities at the peak.
The GPS lead us to a wrong car park and that's a 20mom walk to the cliff, when there's another carpark just a few minutes away from the cliff. View is aweson but very crowded in the afternoon.

The ferry to Udo island is fairly close to the Seongsan Ilchulbong peak, close to a 15 mins walk. The ferry ride is 15 mins only, and you get to see some amazing views all through. In the island, there are many beautiful beaches and cafes. We rented bikes (do remember to ask them for a map if you do!), and rode all around the island. A complete round on the ocean road took like 3+ hours, but was loads of fun. Cos we could stop by at beaches to relax, or cafes for a quick bite or drink. We took lots of incredible pictures. A perfect day spent in gorgeous weather!

The entrance was about $6. Loads of tour buses and families.  The view of the crater is great but there are so many people that I found it very unpleasant to visit.  You can't go into the crater, but only walk around the rim on a wide fenced path with noisy kids and tour groups. Not peaceful.  If you go, I would suggest very early.

The dragon head lava rock was indeed a sight to behold, jutting out of the cliffs. That is if you could catch a glimpse of it amongst hordes of tourists jostling for a vantage point to capture it on their phones, with selfie sticks flailing about.Being only the dragon head, it was quite a pint size cliff, and there was only a tiny area /platform from which to view it.To make the most of our drive there, we walked several meters down a stepped path quite close to the waters and enjoyed our moments there on the rocks.

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

The Cliffs are an amazing volcanic rock formation on Jeju Island. It is an easy bus ride from one of the hotels. Get off at the Convention Center and walk about 500m to the park area. You can expect the viewing areas to be very crowded, full of people taking their time with photos. Look closely for the cylindrical formations. Very cool geology.

The cliff is located on the southern side of Jeju Island in the township of Seogwipo. A well-laid stair-way/boardwalk has been constructed for visitors to view and appreciate the natural rock formations of hexagonal lave tubes. These make great photo shots when framed with overhanging pine trees, crashing waves, clear blue skies and setting sun. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry and hordes of tourists, especially students on excursion. What an incredible place to spend an hour or two!

The cherry blomsson at its carpark in April 18 was wonderful - one long row of beautiful sakura trees.Do not expect to see much inside (basically you walk 5 min into the park and you saw crater on your side. It will not look like crater, only valley). Rather it is the 360 degree view of the horizon that counts. The air is fresh and the mood will be lifted when you can see very far into the horizon dotted with mountains. It really look like you are in Europe or NZ. Go there for sunset as there will be no shelter from the sun above your head.

The bridge itself is a landmark of Seogwipo, which leads to a small island that offers a short 20-25 mins walk. Not the most exotic part of the city, but nice indeed. My favourite place here however are rocks on the edge of the island, which is off the track, but if you are careful while walking out to the rocks (they are pretty flat and not dangerous at all), it is the best place to relax and enjoy the sea and view.

Take your time and enjoy the views. After rain, the waterfall is very pretty and worth the walk from the car parking area. Vendors sell drinks and traditional snacks at various spots and there are many photo spots.

Sunrise was at 5:58AM April 19th, 2018. We woke up ans started walking to the crater at 5:15 AM and had ample time to get up and witness what may be the only Unesco protected sunrise. We walked from the Co-op City Hotel and took about 10-15 minutes to get to the start of the path. It took another 20 minutes to climb to the lip of the crater. It can be challenging for some  but is is fine for anyone of average active health.Breathtaking views.

Sunrise is at 615 am . The entrance fee is free if you arrive before 7 am . Free Car park to the viewing points a short  8-10 minutes walk away , very doable and you get one of the most memorable sunrise sights . A most do except the getting there so early in the morning is hard .

Summary: You have to go here if you're on Jeju. But what can I add to the many reviews already here?The signs to the women's diving show are very clear. From the ticket office, just follow the signs down to the beach to the left of the peak. If the only way to make the show is to sacrifice something else on your itinerary, I wouldn't do it. But it was pretty cool if you happen to be there at the right time. You see the divers actually catch live octopus right in front of you.I recommend taking a snack up to the top and enjoying it there. There are plenty of places to sit down at the top and relax before you head back down. Also, definitely take at least one bottle of water if it's a hot day. You might even want two.If you plan to catch a taxi from this site to somewhere else, you'll have to walk just a little ways. We asked a taxi driver who was waiting on another family where we could get a taxi, and he told us where to walk. We had to wait about 10-15 minutes for one to show up that didn't already have people in it, but they always drive by eventually.
Stunning view, especially the beaches. I've chosen to walk around Udo to enjoy every inch of this nice little island. Took me about 5.5 hours (with photo taking) to walk around the island by foot.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Some of the reviews say it's a quick photo spot and that's all, but if you walk up the street just a little way, there's another path down where you can get some great pictures.  The main photo spot is kind of small and crowded, but this other area isn't, and you can still see the rock and more surrounding formations.I didn't really see the dragon, but it depends on your impression of what a dragon should look like.  This is definitely an Asian dragon, not a European one. :-)

Solo traveling in Jeju Island is not that scary:) Koreans living nearby this tourist spot can speak English. So I am not worried about it.It was raining that day when I reach the place. Nevertheless, still can see the view at the top.The wind blowing my hair together with the greenery grasses and leaves of trees surrounding the peak.The place is accessible by public buses so I don't have difficulty in reaching this site. Though you have to walk a few distance to reach the entrance gate.There are educational boards installed for all the tourists to read and understand the history of it.It's worth visiting this place. Entrance fee is also cheap:)I visited Unesco World Heritage!

So we saw great reviews and some great pictures online. Thought this was a must see place. To be fair, the island has some real potential to be fantastic, however it was a hot August day, it was getting very crowded.Highlights:- some really nice sights to take in and you can tour the whole island in about 4hrs (including stops along the way)- one let we went for a walk and ran into some people camping. Very pleasant and offered us coffee. We hadn?t encountered too many people willing to go out of their way, so was a nice touch. - took a high speed boat ride around the cliff that looks like the cow laying down (hence the name cow island). That was great and worth the 30k KRW for two adults.Low points:- way too much garbage around. Just about every beautiful sight is ruined by plastic bottles and litter. - a lot of areas were closed like it was low season (or maybe we were just early in the day)- lots people standing around endlessly. Got a little frustrating at times. Advice if you do go:- we took the bus. It was good, but we were on a bus schedule. If I did it again, I would have rented a small electric vehicle (which needs an international driving license to rent). Not sure if the cost, but they looked fun and you control your own timeline then.

Skip this and head for Dodubong Peak, especially if you're on the Jeju Golden Bus day tour. This place is unremarkable and is honestly one of the dirtiest parts of the area; I attempted to have my photo taken and a rat scurried out from between the rocks. If you walk up the road (away from the site) about a half mile, maybe less, the photo ops are much nicer. The area near Dodubong Peak is also nicer and you can see great views of of Jeju from the summit.

Since there is not much to see in Jeju City, I liked this the most. The rock itself looks nice, so if you happen to be in Jeju City and have free time, it worth to check and enjoy the view on the rocky seaside. easy to get here from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal, just take local bus #17, and tell the driver   Yongduam   he will show the right bus stop. From there only 5 mins walk. It is just a rock, so don't expect much, but it's good trip for 20-30mins. Before going to the rock, you should definitely check the bus schedule back to the city center (bus timetable is displayed not on the bus stop, but on the shopwindow just nearby where no one would ever search), as there's 1-2 bus in every hour.

Set out from the M-Stay Hotel for this attraction, and well worth the walk!  I think it is a bit better than the highly-enjoyable Cheonjiyeon Falls, with a wider view and a spectacular drop into the adjacent ocean.  Found this site to be more open and therefore afford a bit more solitary viewing than its aforementioned neighbor, though if you have trouble doing stairs than this site would pose a far greater challenge than Cheonjiyeon; here, you have to walk down steps to get to the falls, while the latter affords parking and access from the base of the falls.

Seongsan Ilchulbong or sunrise peak is one of the most visited spots in Jeju. We took a public bus here from port after visiting Udo Island. Lucky it is near the port as it was already late afternoon when we reached here.  The parking lot was crowded with tour coaches and and you could see the crowd climbing up and down the peak.  There was a well laid path which was fairly wide with steps leading up and separate steps leading down.  Certain parts had narrower steps and you have to slow down. Although the peak was not very high, you still need to stop now and then to catch your breath as the steps were quite steep. As usual, wear good walking shoes and stay hydrated. The views from the top were awesome and if you come before dawn, you can catch a beautiful sunrise here.  After climbing to the Udo lighthouse earlier, it was tiring to climb this peak as well but we managed.  There are platforms and steps to sit on at the top to rest and relax. By the time we got a public bus back to Jeju city, it was already getting dark.  You need to pay a small fee to climb up.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is very beautiful, but one thing our tour guide didn't mention was the difficulty of the walk up. You walk up a path and as the terrain gets steeper, the path turns into a bunch of stairs that you have to climb. If you are not physically able, this might be a difficult destination, but if you are able to reach the top the view is worth it.Here you can also see the haenyeos or Jeju women divers and learn a little bit about their history.For those of you who want to be one with nature and enjoy a good hike, I recommend this place.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the best view I have ever seen in my entire life. The place is an epitome of beauty and calmness despite being flocked by tourists. It is very worthy of your time, effort and energy. Trek it to experience and see its beauty. There are plenty of activities being offered on site such as horse back riding, see a Jeju woman diver and even a tour around the area through boat. We were very interested with the boat ride unfortunately we did not have the luxury of time. if given the chance to go back to Jeju I will surely comeback here and try the boat ride as well as other activities offered. Moreover, the site has plenty of coffee shops and cafes around the area. There are also stalls selling Korean street food. It has huge parking area so get ready to walk from the parking area to the site. This site entails a lot of walking but because of its beauty and being windy you can never feel fatigue.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of Jejudo's famous icon.  I'm so glad i was able to climb this famous icon on one sunny mid day. When you reach this attraction, you will see so many shops for souvenirs and food just before the entrance and there is even a Starbucks nearby. Upon entering, you will see a ridge where you can go horseback riding or just do some leisurely walk.  The climb going up was quite a challenge for me but because of the magnificent and awesome views on the way up, i was able to make it to the top. At the middle part of the climb, there is a stall ( the only one there) selling some refreshments and souvenirs.  There is a resting area nearby to enjoy some refreshing drinks before you continue your climb.  Upon reaching the top, i enjoyed the cool breeze and the awesome view of the dried crater covered with grass.  Sharp  rocks around the crater makes it looks like a giant crown.  Coming down was a lot easier as there is a wooden stairs provided and the steps are even, not like the going up where the stone steps are uneven.  i would recommend this attraction to the physically fit only.  When you go down, you might be able to catch their scheduled show of divers and there are also boat rentals.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seongsan Ilchulbing / Sunrise Peak ε뷴낡 , is a wonderful place for sunrise & sunset !? Yes it is. But I came here during 3pm ~ manage to walk up to the peak within 40mins ~ Although I do not have time to stay until sunset but I feel satisfy with the view of Jeju ; cooling weather and beauty of Spring.

Sangumburi Crater is our 1st stop after we got a rental car.It's 40 mins drive from Jeju city.Entrance fee cost KRW6,000. There are several small souvenir & coffee shops.It quite unfortunate for us because that day is raining. We're freezing because of the cold weather.We didn't prepare any umbrella or raincoat. So from the parking to the entrance, we soak under the rain.Thankfully the souvenir shop inside sell raincoat with the cost of KRW4,000.From the entrance, you have to hike up to the crater.The path up to the crater was breathtakingly beautiful.What makes this place looks so gorgeous is because of the vast flame grass field along the way to the crater.Sadly, when we arrive at the top, we couldn't see the crater at all.It was cloudy all over.  However we still enjoy the view.The walk down is as beautiful as it was on the way up.

Sanbangsan (?곕갑?? isn't a really big mountain but it has an interesting and distinguishable shape. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo by bus which stops conveniently right in front of the mountain.There is a nice temple at the base of the mountain called Sanbanggulsa (?곕갑援댁궗) with a huge golden Buddha a wonderful view of the town below and the ocean and an army of miniature mint-coloured Buddhas (I think). All make for great photos. Further up the mountain (you can climb up a long flight of stairs) is a small temple in a cave with an even better view of the town below. Worth visiting if you have made it this far. There is also an interesting story about a monk who hid in the cave during a violent time (can't exactly remember details). Down below south of the street in front of the mountain is a really really nice coastal walk with impressive cliffs that have been ocean and wind-swept into wonderful formations. This place is called   Yongmeori Coast   and also makes for great picture. (Worth knowing that the coast closes during heavy rain for safety reasons.)(Also of interest in the area to some is Hamel's Ship (a replica/museum of an old Dutch ship that landed on Jeju ages ago and the story of the Dutchman that was held captive in the island) and horseback riding (though it's only in a circle). Could be good for kids though these two are the least attractive for me personally.)

Reminder: do check this place out , esp during sunning days. We got the chance to walk through the hiking track around it at 5PM and its just breath taking, later we found out it's the no.1 to do on jeju!You get a million dollar view of the ocean and the mountain and you probably have seen something like this in New Zealand or South africa but not in Asia. Very stunning !

Remember to wear sunscreen, we went on a sunny day and I got a few shades darker walking to the top. Get ready for lots of stairs and a thigh workout, I was a sweaty mess by the time I reached the top, but let me tell you the views were worth it! Gorgeous!

Recommended to visit in Jeju, it maybe a funny or plain looking on the pictures but you will be amazed when you are there. Amazing rock formation and how the sea waves hit the rocks is the highlight here. Still, prepare for the crowd, we traveled here around May 2016 Summer season but rainy on that day, thought of less crowd because of that but still very crowded place. Good thing the location doesn't require long walks or hiking thus everyone can enjoy the view.
Really nice view when you get on top of the mountain, expect 40 minutes walk up and down. There will be a photo spots on your track.
Really like the walk to the top, nice view, unfortunately it was a bit too crowded for me. Go early on the morning if you want to avoid the crowd

Quite long caves, but we do enjoy walking through it until the end of the caves. It was cold inside, feels like we are walking inside a room with air-conditioner. Lols. My friend do enjoy reading all those facts and information on the formations, and I find it quites helpful for those who are interested in geology thing. Maybe.It is quite large caves too. For those who are on tight budgets like us, you can take a bus and walk 2km to the caves. Not tiring at all as the view is very nice.

positives: truly beautiful and amazing views of nature scenery and the waterfalls. also, one can take a leisurely stroll in the attached garden park. entry fee was only 2000 won.negatives: there was a bit of a crowd the day we visited, although it was still manageable. the entrance to the falls could be tricky to find if you planning to go there on foot from Seogipwo town. DO NOT follow google maps as it will only point you to the exact geographical location of the falls. You should walk down along taepyeong road until you see the bridge and the sea. cross the bridge and you will see a big carpark. the ticket office will be on the right side, near 7-11

Please stay around, check the sunrise time and go early. It?s took me 30 minutes to get up to the top. The climb is not easy, I took few breaks before reaching the top. I?m glad that I made it on time for the sunrise.It?s one of the best sunrise I?ve ever witnessed. And, the sea of clouds made me heaven! The picture doesn?t do the view justice. Trust me, you have to experience it by yourself! For your reference, I stayed at Seongsan Sunrise Hotel which is walking distance to Seongsan Ilchibong and Gwangchiji beach. It?s also short distance to Seopjikoji and Udo by cab. Public bus in Jeju is very convenient. You can take bus from Jeju Airport to Seongsan Ilchibong stop without transit.

Pleasant hike with young children, remember your water it was very hot on a mid august afternoon. Not too difficult a walk a few steps but enough photo shots to break it up for the kids. The view from the to is excellent out over the crater , to udo and remember to look at the pyroclastic cones behind you on the mainland. Don't forget the temple at the bottom in the car park worth a look.

People who visiting Jeju island is to see its nature (except those to Casino), Hallasan is a must go to me.  Together with the family, we opted for the route of Yeongsil (shorter though not to the top and unable to see the crater), where we could easily accessed by self driving from Seogwipo city.  Along the hiking, we experienced the sub tropical environment in the bottom, then a much cooler environment after 1.5km of steep uphill.  The view is great though not fantastic, we spotted few wild deers having grass in the mountain.  The first 2-3 km was quite steep but mostly on boardwalk and constructed staircases, the last 1-2 km was rather flat.We ended in the point with toilet and food supply and then back down on the same route, due to the last section was closed.  An interesting hiking day to experience different climate, weather condition, meet locals, spot the wild animal, and do physical exercise.

Overlooking the cliff from the viewing platforms, the formation is indeed unique and a beauty. Walk along the surrounding path, we get to see the different angle of the cliff and the formation.However, you can omit the park. It is just an added attraction due to the price paid for the entrance.

Our family went there after watching sunrise in nearby beach, where we could shot sunrise with Seongsan on the background.  It took about 30 mins for us to climb up to the top by the rather steep staircase, the higher we walked, we saw the full picture of the tombolo and its neigbour.  Up to the top, which is a narrow path and watching performs, we saw the view of the 'crater  , cliffs and the ocean.  As we arrived early, there were not many people, we enjoy the quiet and time to camera, but when we walked down, we saw the full load of coach, and group of tourist.

One of the best stops we made in Jeju. This rock formation is pretty cool and the stop is more worth it since it's a good hour's worth of walking and snapping photos (as opposed to a number of the really touristy places where it's just one kodak moment).Check the tides. The rock formation that people walk on are really close to the water, so if the tides are high, it gets slippery. Actually, some parts are slippery as it is.You have two options: going counter-clockwise, which ends up being an upward movement OR going clockwise, a downward movement.  The views are nice-ish both ways (personally the counter-clockwise views were nicer). More than that though, going counter-clockwise is a lot easier as the steps are easier to deal with moving up. Many of the people coming down were cursing the steep rocks and were tired even before it began for them. Might not recommend this if walking is difficult for you as climbing and hoping around is a must. Little children were around and they seemed to be enjoying themselves, but none of them were younger than 3 years of age.No bathrooms once you enter the formations, but ladies will sell you food and drink (mostly alcohol) if you're interested in a seaside meal.

One of the best beaches in Jeju, we loved this place for its cobalt colored crystal clear water and fine white sand and the view of Mount Hallasan.Our kids enjoyed playing in water and collecting seashells, while we enjoyed walking along the shore.Food stalls, shops, umbrella rentals are available.

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area

On a hot day, between breaks in a storm, my girlfriend and I came here for a nice walk with a great view at the top, where we met a very friendly Korean chap who told us stories of his life. Would definitely recommend as a close place to get to from the city.

Okay so we went to the address given by Tripadvisor, and to our astonishment it was just a small garden behind a hotel. The only reason I can think why it was set to that address - is perhaps there's free parking? Dont give up if you're there! Because the actual site is only about 800m further down. There's a walking path (goes uphill from the hotel garden) along the coast, so simply walk along that and forgo the stone garden (needs an entry fee). The actual cliff site is open to public and free for viewing..Path is quite family-friendly.

Of course as many reviews state, it was pretty busy. It was a simple walk down stairs. The steps were even, there is a handrail and spots to stop if you need to.Once you reach the bottom you can sit on the step and admire the falls. Equally, if you are happy to step over rocks you can get closer to the falls. My 6 and 10 yr old did it with ease. The walk up is easy enough but the exit steps vary a little in size. Nothing hard though. Nice little half an hour outing.

Nothing much really. The walk up the lighthouse was nice in terms of view but disappointing as you can't reach the lighthouse as shown in the brochure. You can find equally nice beaches in Jeju-do, so don't waste time and money to go Udo.
Nice view while walking along the way to the top, view of the sea and mountains, cold wind gets to blow away all worries and agony. Enjoying walk up the mountain, it is a place where you must visit.

My view is totally different from the rest of reviews on trip advisor.I actually wonder if I had went to the right place. I was expecting a entrance fee, but we were free to walk around the hotel gardens for 10-15mins till we reach the edge where u get a clear view of the coastal line and jungmum cliffs are.This jungmum cliff is supposingly behind a hotel garden, so if ur GPS brings u to an hotel like my 2 GPS (provided by car rental company), apple map and google map did then I got the right place.I saw some cliffs, strong sea waves smashing against it....... Eh huh???? There were 2 other couples (one from HK, another from China), all of us was having the same reaction... This is it????? .Was quite a waste of time especially after I drove round and round for almost 2 hrs looking for it, didn't knew it was behind a hotel garden.

My number 2 favourite place in Jeju after Oedolgae. The rock formation of the cliff on this volcanic island is really fascinating! Before going, do make sure it's low tide time because it will be closed during high tide as it will be too dangerous. We also saw some women (should be women sea divers) who were selling fresh sea produce to those who want to eat them fresh and raw there. From there too, we could get a clear view of Sanbang Mountain which is just nearby. There's also a ship there and you can read about the history of how the ship ended up there. Be careful as you walk along the coast as sometimes you might be shocked by the sudden strong waves that come hitting towards the coast. I saw someone who was so shocked that she nearly dropped her mobile phone into the sea. Overall, it's one of the must go places in Jeju.

My kids request for it & quite excited at 1st. The excitement last for the 1st train ride & once we got off the 1st station & need to walk nearly 1km the kids mood just went sour. Then it becomes a more sour when you need to wait for the next train & need to fight for a seat. They're several trains runs every 15-20m if i'm not mistaken. If you missed one you need to wait till the next train. There is no ticket system while waiting for the train & one must grab the seats. So for me with a 2 kids & a baby it was just very hard. Luckily we stayed at the far front of the track station. We managed to get the train & never get off till the end of the station. We went during end of spring. Nothing much to see. Some flowers & i think it will be a great view during summer. Pro's : A great way to relax while enjoying the ride. Con's : You need to walk a lot. The truth is the train tracks was just goes around the same land. 1st come 1st serve basic when taking on the trains. Not stroller friendly.  Tip's : If you have a tight schedule, just stay on the train. Don't go off.

My husband and I walked here from Jeju-si (not recommended, unless you just really like to walk) so it's not far from the big hotel district. It's free to get in, but is mostly just trees and bushes, the wildflower garden was completely bare, of course, we didn't really come at the right time for that anyway. Follow the signs for   Green Shower   and you'll go up a pretty steep climb (especially for us in our flip-flops) to a nice view of the city and the ocean beyond. There's a nice lily-pad pond and a nice green   lawn   for anyone wanting a place to sit in nature. Although, the entire island of Jeju is about nature, so this wasn't a must-see for us. Just behind the Arboretum (on the left as you drive out and behind a group of concrete apartment buildings) is the ＿?由쇱?? Buddhist Temple. It has a really gorgeous campus and nice view of the city and sea, as well. If you got to the Arboretum, take the time to visit the temple, too.

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My husband and I had an absolutely fabulous day pheasant hunting at the Daeyoo Hunting Preserve on Jeju Island in South Korea and then an excellent meal of (our) pheasant sashimi roast pheasant etc. washed down with wine at their excellent pheasant restaurant! Daeyooland also has lovely gardens a charming helpful staff and great coffee!We hunted with a guide and his trusty dog walking for miles thru the beautiful countryside... and my husband did get us a pheasant! We also got to shoot skeet (and they have ATVing as well). My husband had hunted on Jeju many years ago when he was in the US Army and stationed in Korea and I wanted to take him   home   and go hunting with him- and tourists can hunt at Daeyooland! As their website is only in Korean our concierge at the JW Marriott in Seoul (an EXCELLENT hotel which I've also reviewed) was kind enough to help make the arrangements for us. We flew to Jeju Island for the day went hunting and then walked around downtown Jeju going to museums and some of the historic markets (there are 22!) buying and eating those famous Jeju oranges! Then we flew back to Seoul in the evening having had  a GREAT day!

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My family walked from our hotel to the top of Ilchulbong and down. From the entrance, the mountain(?) looked formidable and it looked to be a painful hike, but it turned out to be rather a short hike. I wish I had taken more time on the way up and enjoyed the views more. On the way down, we saw a restaurant by the rocky shore.  I believe this is where mermaids do their demonstrations and sell raw oyster dishes.  I wanted to go down but my 10 & 12 yr olds won't have it.  So I missed out.         The guy who took the tickets at the entrance surprising had a good nack for taking pictures.  If he is not too busy, ask him to take your group photo.         After the hike, we went to a bakery just by the entrance.  From the second floor, we had a nice view of the Ilchulbong and enjoyed cup of coffee with various breads.  The owner was very kind and let us wait out the rain in the store.

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Most of Udo island except the attractions are rural farms. We went to Udo island with a few local Koreans from jeju island. We took a 15mins ferry. I was surprised that there are no seats on the ferry, people sit on the floor instead, korean style. Interesting experience. As I went with locals, I thought they would know the way. No! They didn't and we walked 1h around the island before reaching the peak. It was beautiful. The grass was green n the sea view was nice. Though it was really windy. And thus very cold even though it was summer. Be sure to wear enough clothes.

Might not be very tall at 1950m but it's no walk in the park. The best part though is that the path is clear and generally easy to walk especially when there are planks. Otherwise walking on volcanic rock and boulders are not so comfortable for the feet. Great views at the top and as we went in spring, flowers are in bloom.

Make sure to go when the day is clear, there are a lot of tourists during the peak times so keep that in mind as it could affect your views with all the group selfie stick shots. I highly suggest going off on the little paths around they all have views and are just lovely. If you bring a mini packed meal it's just spectacular for a picnic. It's very close to the falls and the botanical gardens and you can honestly walk (if you have good comfy shoes)This is a must see natural wonder!

Magnificent view formed by molten lava.View is nice when high tide, crowded during noon, so try to reach there early to avoid crowd.Discount for youth (need to show passport)There is also a pampas grass field, situated at your right side once enter the booth of Jusangjeoli cliff parking lot, can walk in the field if you have no time to visit Saebyeol Oreum
Lovely place with great seaview, but beware if you bring kids or elderly as the stone walk are not too easy.

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Liked: The view, the walk.Disliked: Many tour buses spend time here which means the place was full of (literally) thousands of Chinese tourists. It was really hard to relax and enjoy the tranquility when you are in a constant scrum with many loud tourists yelling at each other in tonal dialects.

Like other traveller's review, this is not a place that worth the effort to purposely come by to visit. As it is really just a peace of rock that stood by the sea... It seems more attractive when the spot light is on at night.We dropby this place when we are on the way back to Yeha Guesthouse, surprisingly lots of tour buses stopping by! And you need to walk all the way down the staircase to have a better view of the rock, so old folks with knee problem would suggest to skip this sight seeing point.We couldn't identify which portion is the 'dragon head' until we over heard a tour guide's explanation to their guests @@

Less than 15 min walking, the waterfall was beautiful, and there?s food photo spot where everyone line up when u get to the waterfall. In my opinion, the admission fee was little too much for the quick walk and waterfall view. But good to visit once!

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

Its snowing when I visited this area. A short walk to the top will reveal a nice scenery covered with snow and a crater below. The nice view around actually overshadow the crater itself! Good place to play some snow throwing too. Its suitable for kids or even elderly as the climbing is very gradual, I would say its more like a nice walk. You will be able to see some tall grass on both side of the walk, which according to locals, was used as a roof cover. It is good to hold the weight of snow on some old buildings.

Its really easy to reach this attraction. Parking is free however you are required to pay a minimal fee in order to view this waterfall. Walking on the stairs is easy but if you do wish to get close to the waterfall , a good pair of shoes with good grip is required as you have to walk on the slippery stone/rock. There are some women selling fresh seafood by the waterfall.

It's quite a walk going up this crater but there are 2 ways to get there. One is gradually, using concrete stairs or the otther one is by the plain path.Anyway, it's not that high and the view up there more than compensates the effort. Also, we get to see fields of Pampas grasses along thw way which is very beautiful

It's an okay, nothing to be exaggerated. However, enjoying the walk towards the fall with serene and scenic view is very relaxing. During spring, strolling under the cherry blossoms trees and get to enjoy some local live band music show with people get to move their body to the grooves! Once you got out of the fall, several merchandise shops selling local snacks and merchandise. There are also arrays of local food store nearby serving varies pick of seafood.
