I went to the nearest restaurant near the merchandise store with red signboard. Food potion is huge and price is reasonable. It was really fresh and tasty! I stayed in the Choi Hostel around the area, so it's quite a walk and hike on the way back, what's with full bloated tummy. BTW, I only ate 2 dishes alone :P
It's a nice walk to the waterfall, but from land I suspect the view is not as nice as from sea. Consider doing the boat cruise of the area to give a better perspective.

It's a mountain. A very beautiful mountain. If you visit here, then you MUST climb to the top of this mountain. Tired? Don't be. Because there are STAIRS to the top. All you have to prepare, is a will, drink, hat then just walk to the top. The view is sooooo Amazing!! You'll paid off all of your sweat up there.

It's a lot of stairs and little walking to get to the top, but it's worth it with great views and a wonderful sea breeze. On one side you have views of the crater, on the other of Jeju island. There are lots of other tourists (mostly local) going up and down so be prepared for some level of crowds. There was abundant parking when we visited. There are also plenty of food stalls at the bottom along with bathrooms. On the way up, there are lots of benches, rest areas, and viewing platforms. We saw people of all ages - really old to really young doing the climb. If you're in town and you have a couple hours to spare, we'd recommend it!

It's a beautiful view, worth the climb even though we didn't manage to see sun rise due to the cloudy day but the view is pretty. Have to walk up and be there before 5.30am. Depending on your fitness level, it can take 20-40 mins to climb the peak.

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.

It was very meaningful to spend 3 days to join the Jeju Olle walking festival in November, 2018. One route per day not only an physical exercise and challenge to myself but also a good opportunity to meet friends or make new friends there. No one push you to walk faster but we could take pictures, enjoyed nice views and landscapes on each route. Local food for lunchs were delicious. What a beautiful island, good for gathering and good for vacation. I love Jeju. It was my third time participating Jeju Olle Festival. Different experience every time.

It was really pretty and there are horses which you can ride at the bottom. Climbing up includes of climbing up many flights of steep stairs which might be difficult for the elderly or the unfit(like me). It takes about 50 mins to go up and down. The view on top was nice but when i was there, there were some construction works on going and they chased us away if we were to stand at the peak to take pictures. Imagine climbing up all the way to the top just to get chased away. Not a gd feeling.At the bottom near to the sea, there is also the performance of the women divers at 1.30pm and 3.30pm. It was interesting to watch even though we were flooded by many china tourist. Be careful when walking on the rocks as it can be very slippery. There was also a small pile of shells that you can choose from and to bring home. You can also buy the seafood caught by the women divers and enjoy them at the cafe just beside.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

It was nice to enjoy 15-20 minutes here. Expect to compete for photo taking opportunities. 2000 won/ticket, walk down a few flights of wooden stairs, and climb over some big slippery rocks to get the best vantage point for viewing. Can feel the spray from across the pool. Accessible by bus 281 from Jeju city.

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.
It was enjoyable to walk through this botanical garden,? but I have seen better. It was great fun to go up to the top of the tower for a 360 degree view of the area.

It was at the end of Hamdeok beach. It is not too high and easy to walk. I loved the view from the hill and you can see hallasan from seoubong. If you are staying around Hamdeok beach, seoubong is a great place to see sunrise or sunset. I loved it!

It was amazing!This is the worth place to go. The entrance fee is very cheap just 2000 won and the transportation arround 3300 won.Then Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak will gives unique view that you will never see in another place. It is very easy to go here, just take a bus from Jeju intercity Terminal or Seogwipo Intercity terminal then stop on Seongsan Ilchulbong  Entrance, Just walk for 10 minute from the bus stop to the ticket booth.

It was a short walk from the entrance to get to the actual Jeongbang waterfall site, but was a grand sight to behold - you get to see the ocean from the waterfall! I also like that you could make your way closer to the waterfall by stepping on the big rocks around it.Between Jeongbang and Cheonjiyeon, my vote goes to the former. For the latter, the walk from the entrance was longer, the view was not as fantastic, and you can't get nearer to the waterfall even if you wanted to.

It was a short range climb, about 20mins (if you walk fast), about 40mins (if you take frequent rest along the way).. It is quite steep and tiring.The view from the top is really superb! The sea is really wonderful.

It was a rainy and windy day when we went there, we were told the spot does not open daily and not all the time due to the weather and tidal timeWhen we went it was low tide, but super slippery and windy due to the rain. But amazing walk. There are some people selling fresh seafood, abalone sashimi from raw/ fresh, serving Korean alcohol.  Another type of experience. We walked half way, we had our umbrella but I almost got   flew away   since it is too windy.  But totally worth the walk, since you can catch the wave so closely, and the view is awesome.
It was a cold, sunny day, but the landscape in this area was just awesome!  There is a boardwalk lookout point where different landscapes could be viewed on each end.  Definitely worth checking out!

It takes about 8 hours total to get to the top and back down again. Do it on a clear day and you won't regret it, incredible views of the entire island, all the way to the coast and beyond. A fairly easy walk with lots of steps and sturdy path, it only gets somewhat difficult at the top. If you have any injuries, I wouldn't attempt it, but if you're moderately fit, it will be no problem. A must!

It offers one of the best view in Jeju. It is free to go, no need to book, super easy to walk. I was lucky with weather this time and was able to see hallasan from here! I cannot describe how amazing it was.  It is breathtaking and good to visit anytime of days. Many people came for sunset and sunrise. It is definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju. Be prepare for strong wind and amazing view. Recommend going during fall

it looks like a dragon, I guess. good views of the ocean. It's more of a tour bus place where people come, take pictures and go. But if you walk a bit up the hill from here, you come to a nice Buddhist temple.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.

It is a nice walk up to the top, windy.From the top we do have a nice view, wide view with many hills. Nothing special about the plants or vegetation. The entrance fee of KRW6,000 is a bit high when this is all you see.
it is a long walk up to the top of this peak, but the views are remarkable.  Bring water and be prepared to make the long climb.  Parking is difficult so go early or take a tour bus.
Is a relaxation place. We visited in early Feb, still it cover with snow. Beautiful snow view. Take a some relaxing slow walk to enjoy the cooling feel of the nature.

Innisfree Jeju House can be got to by taking a bus to the O'Sulloc tea museum stop. The tea museum is a very short walk away from Innisfree Jeju House.The place is quiet and peaceful, save for the calming music they play and the chatter of tourists and other visitors, but that wasn't too bad when I was there. There's an area devoted to DIY lessons/sessions where one can try making their own soap. There's a few pretty exhibits where one can smell various scents or read a little about the Innisfree brand and its products. There's a store area, with a few products that are exclusive to Innisfree Jeju House. And there's a cafe with various light food, drink and dessert options.Outside, there are tables and benches that overlook a nice view of the tea plantation, which you can go and take pictures in. Rows upon rows of tea leaves and a few windmills. It's all very pretty and is probably the biggest selling point of the whole compound containing both Innisfree Jeju House and the nearby tea museum. It's really very pretty.I enjoyed my time there, but if Innisfree products are not for you, or if you're the thrill-seeking type, perhaps you should skip this place.

Initially, we were only planning on staying here for a few minutes to take some pictures because the reviews were so mediocre. We rented a car and drove to the entrance our GPS took us to (FYI if you rent a car and don't read Korean, make sure you get a GPS with it, Google maps/Apple maps/etc doesn't work in Korea, only Naver). I think it was some kind kind of back entrance, off the road, because no buses or anything were parked there. There wasn't even really a parking lot. When we walked through the village, to the other side, we saw the big parking lot and all the cheesy buildings and shops and stuff. But from the back side, it was just lots of nice little houses (some I think still had people living there) and pretty, walled-off yards. We were there in the morning and the are we were in had almost no one around, except for a few Chinese ladies who had decided to leave their tour and were having fun (we saw them rejoin with their tour later, so I didn't pull that out of thin air, lol). The main front entrance area is way more touristy and that's probably all people getting off the bus see, hence the bad reviews. If you keep walking through the whole town and take your time (if you can), it's actually pretty and peaceful. I think we spent a couple hours here.
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.

In order to reach the waterfall, you need to walk down many stairs and using the same way back. But worth it as the view is beautiful as it directly flows to the ocean. But be careful since the area is rocky.

In my journey, I went to the Hallasan National Park at Jeju. Here is a good place to walk with family, since here has a wide stretch of land at the foot of hill, you can just walk around the hill. Children can play in a nature place with good air. All the building and transport are so far away, you must feel relax and do not want to leave.If you are younger and want to see more view, I really suggest that you must walk to the peak by stairs, but you must have enough energy, because it is really tired. Take water and some food are necessary. After that, you can see a good view at the peak, just like stand on the cloud.Finally, I suggest that you will climb at evening because of the sunset is very beautiful. Also the weather is better to climb the hill.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

If you one got time for 1 of the 3 waterfall in Seogwipo, you should choose this waterfall. View is spectacular, need to walk down the stairs to view the waterfall. and some actually walk very close to the waterfall by walk on the big rocks to get some nice photo. Plenty of parking space available, youth below 25 years get some discount for the entrance ticket (do bring along your passport). suggest to spend 1 hour there.
If you have time to visit while you are in Jeju City, Yongdu-am offers a nice walk and photo op. Yong pond is also within walking distance and had some very picturesque views.

If you have been to Giants Causeway in Northern Ireland,  you will want to stop here too. Same hexagonal basalt columns that are only found in a few places around the world. It's a quick visit as you view from a platform and walkway.  Entry is only 2000 KRW. Even the people in our group who have not been to Giants Causeway enjoyed it.

If you have a tight schedule and cannot afford a whole day climbing the Hallasan Mountain, or some of your group physically can't do Hallanshan, this is a good option, because it is closer to other sight seeing places so you don't need a whole day, also because it is a much easier climb compared to Hallasan.The day we visited this was not crowded at all because everybody went to Udo Island on the opposite, after a two day close of the ferry service due to weather. If there was a helicopter service i(not sure), it must be very spectacular from an aerial view.  From the ground level,  if you didn't see the photo from the Internet, nor post cards, you probably don't realize it is a flat volcanic crater.Anyway, it would be quite a nice walk close by other sightseeing places, but might look more impressive from opposite Udo, or from a plane or helicopter

If you go there just to see the Lonely Rock, you may feel somewhat underwhelmed. However, there is a nice walk along the coast. When I was there, it was sunny and breezy. I really enjoyed the walk, the beautiful coastal view, the clear water and the fresh air. I wasn't disappointed at all.
If you enjoy walk , is fine. Good view, so natural . Specially the air & wind. Fresh and clean. Family and friends can snap a good photo for remember.

If staying in or visitng Seogwipo, this is a must. It's no Niagra Falls, but the quality-to-price ratio of this georgeous waterfall is difficult to overstate, as it costs only 2000 won (less than 2USD). A short walk down several staircases, passing shops along the way, will lead you to a stoney beach and the nearby waterfall. You're free to get as close as you wish, but, as many other reviewers have pointed out, the myst created by the falls makes the rocks slippery. So, wear shoes with decent treading and proceed with caution!

I?ve visited this place with my GF. Definitely a date spot! Although some families also go with kids, from my point of view, not a family thing... but I might me wrong!It?s cold! Very cold! Wet and definitely slippery! Be prepared! But definitely amazing! 1km walk in and 1 km return walk out cane be done in quite 30 mins or so.Perfect if you go only once in your life! A must do if you are in Jeju. I guess...

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

I went Thursday morning with my girlfriend and it was quiet enough. Nice walk, but be prepared for stairs and bring water! The bridge you can cross is exquisite and crazily steep (so be careful in the winter). The views are outstanding on a clear day.I really enjoyed this site; the wooden walkways, the history behind the irrigation channels and of course the waterfalls really kept my interest.Would recommend!Shane & Jill

I went there early morning on a sunny day - perfect for photo-taking. The wonderful view of the sea from the walk down was just a prelude to the beauty that was to come later. I was delighted to see that little rainbow at the bottom! If you're more gutsy (and have a good sense of balance), you can make your way nearer to the waterfall to feel the cool mist and enjoy the grandeur and the surrounding scenery. Not a sight to be missed!!

I went early in the morning before the admission desk was opened and saw many walking up with torchlights. I went again in the afternoon and this time there was an admission charge and wad very crowded. There are restrooms at the foot of the rock and another on the way up. The toughest part would be the starting and it gets easier soon. It is a short walk up so pace yourself. The views and wind at the top was amazing. On the way down, look out for the diver women show which is at 1pm & 3.30pm. Look out for the rock resembling an eagle beak and the korean ironman

I wasn't expecting to have to walk up this thing, but I guess that should have been obvious to me. It was a hot and panting walk, but it was not that long. It was a sunny day, which made for great views, but not for a cool walk. I had JUST MISSED the show with the women divers, I guess it is at 1:30 and 3:00 daily. Nice panorama at the top, the view is certainly impressive.One other thing I liked a lot about this is that it is a fairly touristy area, which meant that most restaurants I passed had pictures and/or English on the menu outside and inside the restaurant, making it easier to order food,

I was very excited to visit Jeju; and this probably one of the most accessible place by Bus. There's actually public transport to this place (Yongduam Rock) from my accommodation. However, when I reached this place , i was busy looking for this legendary dragon head rock. Much to my disappointment, the rock doesn't seem to look like dragon head, you must really view it from the other side with your imagination.However, in order to reach to the other side, you need to climb all the way down the stairs, Not recommended for elderly. And if you notice carefully, you will spot alot of cockroach crawling around the rock, that totally freak me out!! Very big turn off if you spot the cockroach.the period I went was very crowded, probably around 5-6pm, This timing was quite a good timing for me, as I manage to catch a sunset. The sunset there was relatively awesome with the endless view of sea. If you can walk all the way down to those seafood stores, whereby you can enjoy fresh seafood hot pot + splendid view of sunset & sea!

I was thinking of skipping this attraction in favour of the natural attractions. Due to bad weather I visited this place on a whim but I enjoyed it better than expected. The building itself is quite pretty like a big greenhouse. The floral arrangement and landscaping is tasteful although not as good as Gardens by the Bay in Singapore. There are pretty sculptures dispersed through the compound. There are many different gardens to explore. We visited the indoor gardens first followed by taking the lift up to the top floor for a view of Seogwipo and lastly took the train for the outside gardens. It was too cold and windy to walk outside. There was some confusion about where to buy train tickets, the driver helped to walk to the counter and buy our tickets. Spring is probably a good time to visit since many flowers are in bloom. It would be good if they can stop the vandalism of the trees by the Koreans, many of them scratched their names on the branches.

I walked 40 minutes from Jungan Rotary to this place. The ticket is 2000 won. When I was there, it was in the afternoon 4-5 PM, there were so many tourists. So it's difficult to get a good shot. I find there's nothing special about these waterfalls, back home I've seen bigger and higher than here. I visited this place because it was close to my guesthouse and I was also curious about it. I don't see people swimming on it. What I like about this is the view of the sea, I was sitting between those big rocks towards the sea and waiting for the sun to set. It was a good experience for enjoying the sunset with having a natural background sound from the waterfalls.

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I think the word   museum   throws off this visit.  I expected to see many more interesting displays and films about tea but there is really just one room with some tea sets a few interesting facts and how Jeju tea is the best as the soil climate and underground water makes growing tea in Jeju at its optimal.  This so called museum is more of a flagship store where you can purchase tea and tea related items have a snack at the cafe/bakery that specializes in green tea ice cream and cake rolls and in a separate building building called   innis free   you can make natural soaps and enjoy Korean slushy ice in a cafe there as well and a store.  There are tea making classes but you must make a reservation to attend.  The grounds are nice and you can walk around the tea fields and go to the rooftop and get an amazing view of the surroundings.  The museum is free but for a true tea fanatic you may be disappointed as there are no samples or a big variety of tea products to choose from for purchase.

I stayed at Ojo Haenyo Guesthouse area, hopped on a taxi to get to the port to Udo. The port is actually very near but I chose not to walk there. Paid less than KRW4000 for the taxi, cheap indeed.Bought a return ticket at less than KRW6000, ran towards the ferry that was about to leave for Udo, and in less than 30 minutes, we reached beautiful Udo. In case you're wondering, the ferry ride is too short to get motion-sickness :pIt rained during my short trip to this island so I didn't rent a bicycle. Instead, I got on the hop-on hop-off bus, the ticket was about KRW5000 or so. Super cheap. But the driver/tourist guide spoke only in Korean. But no worries, I did enjoy the tour.I managed to walk up to the lighthouse, had the famous peanut ice-cream overlooking a gorgeous view of the beach and a cliff, I also went to one of the beaches there. Udo is as gorgeous as Jeju. There are nice cafes with free wifis. Street food, local food, souvenirs; Udo is small but it has everything for visitors. Do wear good walking shoes, bring a ponco with you, and get on the last ferry if you can as this island is beautiful!!

I spent few hours at the museum, I had jet lag  because of 6 hours difference in my biological hour, & it is near Hana Hotel where I stayed. It is a nice walk to the museum. I thought it is a happy place, because most of the visitors were happy especially those with children. I took my time looking at the museum & the shop. I enjoyed my time. The museum have stairs & elevator. I took lunch at the resturant , it is fast food, with reasonable price.Bathrooms at each level & they are clean. The view from outside the resturant is nice & relaxing, & the outside garden is beautiful.I watched the Elvis show,it is nice & professional work. I think to enjoy & appreciate the museum you have to spend few hours, not a quick visit.I thought it is a delightful happy place.

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

I really loved this place. The view before climbing and the view from up is just great!If you want to go for a short hike this is the place for you! The walk up is about 15 -30 minutes, if I remember well. But it is worth the walk up!

I read Trip Advisor to avoid wasting time or money. The reviews of this museum had warned me away. Unfortunately due to rainy weather we were a bit stuck for options of things to do and I ignored y own research to give it a go. Sonetimes that works out. This time it didn't.Prettt expensive ticket at 36,000KrW for a museum we walked through in 10 minutes.Our kids are usually easily entertained and even they were disappointed with the museum. If the entry price wasn't so steep for what was on offer, we might have felt more poitive about the experience.

I must have chosen a very good day to visit Seongsan Ilchubong. When I arrived, there were practically a few dozens sightseeing buses there, tourists as well as students for school outing. The whole place, paths walking up the hill and down to the seashore, on the hill top, everywhere! was FULL of people walking, talking, taking pictures?§?o there as early as you can if you want to enjoy the view in a much relaxed way.

I love nature and if you do too this is a must visit if you are in jeju. A Unesco site and a new seven wonder, the view from the top is worth the climb. Depending on individual it can take up to 30 minutes to climb but take your time and enjoy the crisp air and the beautiful view of jeju. Also walk to the sea to buy life seafood caught by the locals

I love hallasan so much, this is definetly the camp, although it was winter when we got there, but really its very beautifull .... I cant imagine , hallasan when spring ... For get in here, there is bus station 15 minutes walk from the foothills, but dont know exactly the number of the bus, because we hire rental car for only 20.000 won !!! Its amazing right ?? But sadly hallasan didnt have any restaurant or proper rest area for us to enjoy the view, or it because the winter season, i dont know ...

I like the view of the nature that surrounds this beautiful sunrise peak. The lush grass and the crashing waves against the cliff. The walkway was well built. What I didnt like was that as we had to start the climb quite early, it was pitch black and I was afraid of the darkness. So be sure to bring a torch and a jacket as it was raining and windy when I went in the morning.

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.

I had requested Tripadvisor to add this as an attractive as it was along the Jeju City Tour bus route. We decided at the last minute to get off at 'Sarabong Peak' as we wanted to see the lighthouse. However, we had a 10 or 15 minute uphill walk to reach the lighthouse during a cold December day but the view more than made up for the inconvenience. We only stayed for half an hour as we wanted to catch the bus back to town as it was already getting dark.

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I had no idea that there were going to be stiff hills/stairs to go top of the place. I was expecting kinda easy, but it was bit harder than I expected. Going to the top was a little tiring, but the view you get to see is magnificent. Make sure to have a bottle of water on the way! About 20-25 min of walking, and less than 20 to go back down. Would go again!

I enjoyed this place even more than Jusangeolli, maybe because there were less people, or maybe because the view was just so serene.  It was a nice walk through some trees before getting to the viewing spot.  We went in the afternoon so the sun was just perfectly positioned.  I got some nice photos of this place, especially including the trees on top of the cliff to the right of the rock.  You can't miss seeing this place, even for just a few minutes.
I enjoyed the walk, fresh air and most of all the view, it's crowded during the summer but otherwise a lovely place to visit.

I definitely recommend this place altough it's popular among tourists. Anyway, the view on the top is absolutely amazing and for me walking on the top wasn't too hard. It was very windy but sunny day (and I burned my nose) so I recommend to remember the sun lotion! Or if it's cold and windy to wear warm clothes. On the top there were many places to sit and take a brake. The journey down was also lovely because of amazing views. Before you start to walk to up remember to go to toilet and eat something (there are toilets and food in the same area). If you haven't used to walk lot of stairs it can be quite challenge but it is definitely worth of it.

I could see coming here to relax a little, the view of the crater was nice enough but not like it was a whoa moment attraction. I might go bak though, there were some lovely picturesque spots and the pampas grasses were quite nice. An easy walk up of, so good for those of you (like me) who aren't p for the massive hike up the other big crater by the women divers museum.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

Hiking Mt. Halla was on my bucket list for a long time and finally i did it. There is a time restriction and you cannot enter the gate before 6:00 am during the winter time. You have to pass 'Jindalaebat Shelter' before 12:00 pm to continuously hike up to the summit. The park keeper will not let up pass the gate of Jindalaebat if you arrive after the noon. It took about 2 or 3 hours to get to Jindalaebat from Seongpanak gate, and another 2 or 3 hours to get to the summit. It took me 4 hours to get to the Baekrokdam, and took another 5 hours to get down to Gwaneumsa temple. I highly recommend to hike from Seongpanak because it is easier to walk and you are too tired to look around. Then, walk down to Gwaneumsa direction which has a really good view and nature. (Gwaneumsa route is shorter, but definitely harder...super stiff)You will see many people lining up to take a photo with a monument, and I didn't understand why people want to take a photo with just a rock. I learned that you will get a certification of Mt. Hallasan hiking if you show the picture with the monument. All you need to do is go to the ticket office, pay 1,000 KRW and show the picture. I've seen many people hiking with sneakers, but I recommend wearing hiking boots since you have to walk on rocks for 8~9 hours. I heard that you need to be luck to see the summit because Hallasan is always foggy and cloudy. I was lucky and weather was just amazing!! I also heard that it is slightly easier to hike when it snows. There are buses that you can use and I strongly recommend hiking Mt. Halla!!!!!!!

Hike to the peak for a wonderful view, Jeju island is blessed wit so many nature attraction & Seongsan IIchulbong is one of it, did not get to see the women divers performance as the wave was very strong during our visit but we manage to see live women divers at other place the next day. Walk around and enjoy the nature.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hamdeok can be reached from airport by bus or taxi in 30 minutes. There are many hotels, convenient stores and restaurants in that area so We can get accommodation easily.We were staying at Ramada Hamdeok, about 1 km walking distance from the beach. Strolling at sunset time was very enjoyable. Nice weather, nice view, not too crowded. Just fine.We were hanging out until dinner time, took barbecued seafoods at outdoor table by the beach. To order the food and communicate need extra effort because we can only speak english, but the Resto staff can speak mandarin well. The food was good, drinking some soju and babunja make us warm...

Hallsan is the highest mountain in Korea. You will have to hike up 1200m.  It is tiresome but it is not very tough, you can take your time. The time estimations indicated in the panels along the way are overestimated (specially if you have some hiking experience).Hiking up this mountain is like being on a highway with a lot of very noisy companions. It is packed, you will most likely be queuing up the mountain if you go in summer.If you are looking for a communion with nature, this is not the place. The hike up is almost entirely man-made, you will be walking up on wooden stairs and on wooden paths. Once you reach the top, it is so packed that you can barely enjoy. Views are excellent though.As you go up, there is a small path to the left to go to another lake. I will recommend this on your way down. Much much quieter as most tourists just want to go to the top.

Had a port of call in Jeju. The cruise offered a number of shore excursions. Instead, we took the free shuttle into town. It dropped us off right by the underground mall (half block past it)We walked around a bit then hailed a taxi. He agreed to a fixed price of $100 USD to take us to the folk village, then to sunset peak. (The cruise was $119 per person so we saved $138)We climbed to the top. It was strenuous but with frequent stops we made it. It?s like 59 stories. At the to you get a great view of the town and the sea. You also can look down into the volcano (and see a grassy crater)A million photos later we came down. We then went and saw the women diver demonstration. That was fun. They sang for a while then went fishing. While we were there, one of the ladies caught an octopus. I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Great Views, Must Go, Wear to walking shoes, Not Baby friendly for Strollers as you will have to climb a lots of stairs. If you have child?s on stroller make sure you carry Baby Pouches/Bags for carrying the baby. Drink the Tap Water - Very Springy & Natural.

Great view of the rare animal cliff which is 20 meters height and surrounded by the beautiful islands. Hundreds of visitors went there to have a look of the amazing animal rock. The stone seemed independent and I like the fact that it is normal, nothing inorganic. The shape of Oedolgae formed by the daily erosion of wave and the weathering process. There is a small path in which it can walk along the edges of the island. In which I discovered that the venue was filmed by one of the most famous Korean drama - Dae Jang Geum. I was in love with the drama when I was young, I took tens of photos with the place that Jang Geum have been to.So, if you are I fan of Dae Jang Geum or you would like to see different shapes of stone, you are highly recommended to go there to have a look at the charming sea view.

Gosh...this place is awesome... Its very well maintained and comfy for those people walking inside and enjoy the lava tube nature. Recommend to wear shoes or comfy sandal as it sometimes wet inside. Not just the view, but also there are boards for explaining the things we see inside. Love it!

Gorgeous view of the ocean and surrounds, but extremely crowded in summer. You should be moderately fit to make it up the steep stairway here. Tip: walk on along the main coastal road to the east of to get an alternative view of this World Heritage site.
Good walk up to the top, windy & cooling during autumn (Nov 16). Enjoy a breathtaking view & good for nature lover. Great place to relax your mind.

Good for a walk as it is easy walking with limited stairs and if the weather is good, the peace surrounding the ocean views is rewarding. Can be very busy with tourists and if the weather is windy or wet, then find another place to visit. Some small markets? around the area to visit.

God?s beauty with unique rock formations and the waves crashing. Short boardwalk to see the beauty. We bought a bag of oranges and explored a bit more on the side paths but it was so hot, we didn?t enjoy that part as much as cliff viewing.

From the bottom Seongsan Ilchulbong looks daunting, but once you get walking its relatively easy, with many well placed rest spots along the way. The views at each spot are pretty great - you can really appreciate the black sand beaches from there. Take some water with you!The top of the volcano is amazing - covered in a sea of green grass, it looks like it could easily be a set in a Jurassic Park movie. There is something so primal about the feeling up there. And despite the many other hikers you will find up there, its pretty easy to find a spot to sit and appreciate it for a bit!The entrance is 2000 won. Take some water, a camera and some coins for the scopes. Also, it gets really, really gusty up at the top and along the walkway to Ilchulbong beach, so try and avoid any flyway items of clothing.
Fresh air and beautiful scene of the sky, sea & rocks all together. Walk along the coastal path to take in the views from different angles. It is supposedly also the filming location of 鸚㏝룝.

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

For family with kids, this will be a nice to visit as there's a nice steam train ride which brings you around to many scenic areas within Eco Land. A nice break from all the nature views and long trekking walks.

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

First and foremost, bring good walking shoes. You will need to hike up the hill to have a good view. There are many stalls at the base of the hill, before you pay to go into the entrance. As this location is near the sea, it is rather windy. A windbreaker may be required depending the time of the year you are travelling.Lots of toilets around, so there's no worry about needing it.There are many tourists as well as locals visit this scenic spot. Bring you camera as well. Note: This location is open depending on weather.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Easy boardwalk to see the attraction.  If you follow right, you will see the Oedolgae rock.  We happened to be there at sunset, and the view was magnificent & romantic!  You can also follow the boardwalk to the left for more view points.

Early Morning walk is rather cold and its indeed extremely tiring to walk up the stairs to the top. But the view at the top is so beautiful, the sea water surrounding very crystal clear. Its a must go attraction.
Drive to the place is fantastic, walking up to the mountain takes upto 20 mts minimum. The panoramic view frm the top is mind boggling with blue tiled roof on one side of the mountain
Don't take any photos (even though it's tempting) until you reach the top, which is a short walk. The view gets better and better as you go up.
Did this as part of Olle walk 1-1. Great views from all around, nice piece of history and beautiful lighthouse which is always a bit romantic and mysterious, so perfect for couples i'd say. Loved it.

Considering that the other craters type views Seongsan Ilchulbang (Sunrise Peak) and Hallasan are a ways up, and the seaside formations such as the Yongmeori Coast a slippery path of jumping about, the Sam-Gumburi Crater is nice and leisurely. The one place that seemed wheelchair friendly.It was also less crowded compared to the Seongsan Illchulbang so we really got to enjoy the nice leisurely walk up the small hill to see this crater. If you're a faster walker, you could probably do the whole thing in less than an hour (needless to say, we lazy walkers, took a little more than an hour). If you wanted to just roam about, you could spend a lot more time as well (there are different paths, one that's all stairs, one that is like a ramp, etc.). Anyways, this was probably the only geological tourist attraction that was wheelchair friendly and even seemed to have a few out in the front for rental. The ramp would be a bit steep but at least do-able. A lot of the other sites had either a lot of stairs/walking or way too many people for the elderly or others with bad knees to maneuver well.  Perhaps that's why we saw a number of couples with strollers.That said, this place had one of the most pricy admissions costs that we encountered. It is privately owned or something. So, instead of the usual 1,000-2,000KRW per person, we paid 6,000KRW per person. We were told that the place is nicer during the reed season, but we enjoyed the crater all the same. We'd recommended it to anyone looking to do a Jeju geotourist site without all the hard work.

Coming from a country where temples are famous for their stunning decoration I did not expect much from temples in East Asian countries. But Yakchunsa Temple was beyond my expectations. The temple is stunningly decorated. The Buddha statues are absolutely beautiful. I recommend you walk up to the second floor where you will see countless mini gold Buddha in different poses on the wall to your left and you can enjoy the view of the main hall and the main Buddha from high up. There is a small building to the left of the main hall with 500   heroes  . I think they are important monks or something. At least that's what it says in Chinese characters. All 500 of them have different facial expressions and poses. Some are very comical. Do take a quick look inside. And don't forget to drink the water from the water fountain before you leave the temple. The water there is refreshingly sweet.

Came here during sunset time. The view is very beautiful and natural. Many tourist took photo over here. During your walking distance to Yongduam Rock, don?t buy any fruit from the first stores! Very rude and not friendly. Make sure those of you beware of them.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This columnar joint was located in South Jeju, and had beautiful sight. This place was good to enjoy view made by wave and sight and sound made by wave and cliff. I didn't expect this area, but there was excellent, And had walking road was good with exotic atmosphere. Very beatutiful place to me.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!
Breathtaking waterfalls, good walk with family and kids. Love the view, the air and walk. Kids enjoyed the walk too.

Breathtaking view when you reached the peak. Time taken from entrance to the peak ~60mins. You can get a chance to see woman diver show but too bad we did not get a chance for it due to time constraint. Tips: please wear comfortable shoes for walking, the stairs can be steep, and eat some food before that for good stamina.

Breathtaking view of Jeju at the Peak of Seongsang iichulbong. Is cooling while walking up the Peak during winter. But no regret and is worth to go up the Peak and see the huge crater. Is not difficult to walk up, there is properly staircase and path. Young children and elderly also can walk up. There are CCTV at some of the pitstop.
Blowholes were small as compared to New Zealand?s Pancake rocks. But view is beautiful, a small park outside with shops around. Many attractions like Teddy bear museum are just a walking distance.

Best for sunrise. There are well-built boardwalks up to the peak of the extinct volcano. Overran by nature but the shape of the crater is still visible. The view of Jeju from the peak of the mountain is amazing, never fails to disappoint.

Besides the short walk up to the Buddhist cave, there is a lovely temple and huge golden Buddha just up from the carpark. It does cost money to get in but being able to get up close to the Buddha was excellent. And there are nice views of the coast too.

Beautiful views of the coastline and the cliffs.Part of the walkway to the viewing platform was closed due to the recent typhoon, so a lot of visitors were gathered on the main viewing platform. The park itself was not very big, making it a pleasant, easy stroll.

Beautiful view from the cliff and surprising rock formations. Went on a rainy morning so we took our time and walked around a lot too. Snacks from the vendors near the front gate were tasty. The entry fee and parking was 8,000 KRW for a family of 5.
awesome view, loads of walking so be sure to be in your comfy shoes. loads of picture taking & as usual loads of tourists

Attended the 1st day of the 2014 Jeju Olle Walking Festival, infectious mood with music and performances at various parts of the scenic seaside trek during the full day walk. We climbed up the Dodu-bong, a short hill with a panaromic view of the route, planes taking off from the airport runway and the sea. While it was quite sunny, late afternoon the sea breezes can get quite chilly. However at the end of the trek there were performances and hot local food, so overall it was a satisfying Day 1 of the trek.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed Jeju Olle Route 6 from Chilshimni Poetry Park (to see the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top) to Oedolgae and happened to see this Hwangwooji coast (probably part of olle route 6) which was my favourite spot of the day. You will walk along Namseong-ro road and passed by 외돌개나라 Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online). I love the place bcos it was like a private pool and it is free. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.? After-which we head to Oedolgae.You can walk there and you do not need a car. Probably a 15 minutes walk from the main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Poong Gyung Hotel or Park sunshine hotel jeju is) and walk in to Namseong-ro road where? 외돌개나라 Hostel is.

As my country does have lotsa waterfall, this short walk for the scene just a ok to us.  Well, the difference is since we are tourist, so we visited the place. You can skip to pay the entrance fee if you are not keen on waterfall as it can be viewed and spotted before climb down for a nearer view of it.
An easy-to-reach attraction that provides not only a fantastic view of the city and port, but also leads you to the island which is worth the walk in of itself.
An absolute must while in Jeju. The walk up is stimulating rather than stressful and the morning views are wonderful. 5,000 won well spent.

Although there is not a lot to do here, it is a short walk from the parking to see this absolutely beautiful view!  If you take a few minutes to watch the water swirling around the cliffs it will mesmerize you, so pretty!

After climbing the stairs for the view of the lush, plant-filled centre of the crater, you should definitely walk along part of the black sand beach that arcs around to the ?glass house.? You?ll see some amazing views of Seongsan Ilchubon there, and your pictures won?t be filled with random tourists. There are also bits of sea glass scattered along the shore, shells, and if you walk down the beach far enough, a beautiful, large ledge of lava covered in green moss you can walk on and explore. It was really easy to get to the crater by bus from Jeju-si, and it only took about 75 minutes.

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.

Admission fee for adult is 2000won. You will be able to enjoy walking up to the peak and see the entire sea/ Mountain View. It will be good to wear covered shoes or sport shoes so it?s easier to go up the steps. Not only that, there?s a 대? performance available but I missed the timing. But the 대? will be at their store selling fresh seafood. It?s a good place for solo travellers :)After exploring ilchulbong, head over to ㅼ“대?吏 for some abalone porridge :D

According to the tour guide, she told us it will take 25 mins to reach the top. But we took more than that.  Never mind just walk slowly and take short break in between. Feeling wonderful when reach the top. The sea view is perfect. Front side u can see the houses. I love the Back side view.

A way to escape from daily hectic life. You can walk at your own pace and choose the route and scenery you like (coastal road, hiking). I completed Route 1, 1-1, 20, part of route 6 & 7. Just choose the route and follow the olle sign, relax and enjoy the view Olle wanna show you. Is quite safe, I am a girl and I walked alone.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A very long and tiring climb if you are not used to climbing. There's lots of people both locals and tourists climbing along so you will definitely be motivated to continue climbing. Tip: bring sunglasses, pack light, grab a snack and bring a bottle of water, most importantly wear comfortable sports shoes. Just climb slowly and take a break along the way as you need so that you are not overly tired out. If you are thinking of combining this attraction with other nature sites that require ample walking or climbing, do take note that this attraction may already be rather tiring... the view and wind at the top is worth it, in my opinion. You do not see the bird's eye view you see online but nonetheless you see the vast greenery and top down view of the scenery below.

A vast crater overgrown with a diversity of plants, it's especially unique in autumn when waves of silver grass unfold in front of you. Have a leisure walk up to the main viewing platform, you can embrace the incredible view of Mt. Halla. I'd say it's one of the best scenery of Jeju in autumn!

A total of 19.7 KM hikeThe walk in early spring will be having snow so be prepared.. Buy the show snow covers Crampons its a must , its a must , its a must , i went without and sliped dozens of times  and injured myself once.. its snowy on the last third.. I hiked manytimes before in different parts of the world i go with sports shoe.. this one deserves crampons.. and maybe walking sticks as well.. Its long and tiresome. . But fun.. the view is great from up .. but make sure its not foggyat the end if u show them a picture taken at the top they will give u a certificate for 1000 won.. its a certificate of achievement really after a long hike. . Its 4 hours up and 4 hours down..

A short 10 mins walk down down several flights of steps would lead u to the base of the fall. For the adventurous and nimble folks, you can navigate carefully across the rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. I was there on a crowded day and the task of leaping from rock to rock didn?t seem possible. It was still a nice view from the base. Do include this site in your itinerary. I think the volume of water was lesser since it was still winter when I visited.

A must visit. The view is really breathtaking and you will find the climb for 180m worth all the tired walk. We came here early morning, less tourist and the sunshine just suit the mood with windy weather.

a coastine with beautiful cliff and rock - the line and layer of the rock are ideal for photography or selfie.  Not difficult to walk but cautious for the waves, also there is open view over the outlying islands. I recommend people go to the end of the path which has a exeptional setup by the nature.

A climb with lots of stairs and lots of tourists. The place is crowded and with little shade. I recommend to come for either the sunset or if you are like me and cannot wake up in time, do this walk in the evening time, so it's not too sunny. The view is very nice and offer a wide vista of the greenery. After the walk, you can enjoy exploring the adjacent black sand beach.
A   walkable   mountain for elderly. Enjoyed the very good view at the top on the mountain. I'll be there if I go Jeju again. For sure
Wonderful waterfall with an easy walk down toward it.  The path is well marked and is usually quite busy.  Would definitely visit again

We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.
Well unless you are into rocks and nature you might not like this place. Plus we have to walk quite far just to get a bus going back to hotel.

We were staying in Seogwipo and had an extra day with nothing to do. So decided to book tickets from Klook on the day of visit. From Days Hotel in Seogwipo we would have to take two buses 201 and then 295?. The first bus is 1 hr 10-15 mins and much more frequent than the second bus which is a 5 mins ride or a 25 mins 2 km walk. Taxis are cheap starting fare of 2800 krw will get you to Aqua Planet from the 201 bus stop but they are a needle in a sack - hard to come by! Other countries??hard to reach facility ir tourist site may provide some form of free shuttle/transport but not here. Once you enter the main facility it would take you a long time to find the toilets - certainly not tourist friendly. Live shows are also all in Korean  albeit with English & Chinese subtitles. The size of this Aquarium is about one third or one quarter of the Okinawa one so we were seriously disappointed with its size and varieties of fishes available. Visit if you have a car or join a local tour or book a taxi. If using public transport like us think twice about going as its 3-4 hrs to and fro Seogwipo.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: We went here today for first time and love it?s it?s so beautiful and fun to walk around have good restaurants and coffee shop and good shop to buy thing make from jeju !! You can take bus or taxi too

We travelled here by bus and got completely soaking wet walking the 20 minutes from the main road to the cave. Unfortunately it wasn't worth the soaking! It was pretty boring and after 30 minutes walk up and down we were out in the ran again.I would only recommended visiting if you have a thing for geology or if you have a car and happen to be passing by.

We took the bus to get to this location and was dropped off at the bus stop.  There were no signs how to get to the destination so we went to the nearest hotel to inquire.  They pointed us the way and we forgot to ask how far it was.   We still did not find any signs how to get there but after walking 15-20 min found the entrance.  The scenery is beautiful and we took several pictures.

We took bus 600 from the World Cup Stadium. This bus is also the Airport Limousine. We got off at Jeju ICC and walked from there towards the sea. The geometrical volcanic rock formation simply took our breath away!  Who cut/shaped the rocks this way? A fantastic work of art created by the Master Craftsman. Another wonder of nature. We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths. We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

We self-drive to this museum. Like everyone else we ate the green tea cake ice cream and hot green tea latte for lunch it was delicious especially for green tea lovers. It was crowded with bus loads of tourists but the cafe staff was very efficient and served quickly. Bought Jeju tangerine tea after trying the sample. We also went to the innisfree shop to buy cosmetics. And took photos of the garden that has beautiful cherry blossoms at this time. Great soothing weather and we also walked across the road to the tea plantation. Enjoyed ourselves.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. Walking through this garden park is very peaceful and relaxing. There is a cool cave feature so you get to also go into caves. The captive birds are in small enclosures and the peacocks look like there tail feathers have been pulled. Also there is a white sand beach walk across the street after you are done the park. Taxi from Ramada Plaza was 26000 wan. Bus ride home was 3000 wan and took about an hour on the 702.

To arrive in jeju misterious road you can go by bus or private car. If you use private car you can try how misterious that road. If you go by bus you need to walk to arrive in jeju misterious road.

I got there by bus and walk less than 5 mins.Not only it has a variety of tea but also has its own tea plantation and a cafe. This temple wasn't very busy when we were here and it was very pleasant to walk around for awhile. We probably spent a couple hours walking around the grounds and taking pictures inside. You can go up three floors inside the temple the paper lanterns hang down from the ceiling fairly far and you can get some neat pictures with them if you go upstairs.

This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.

This pavilion is something to visit when you get dropped off in town by the bus from the cruise ship.  It takes a few minutes to walk around and take a few pics but I certainly wouldn't consider it a must see destination to go to.

This is so amazing beach to walking around and relax even 11 pm we still walk and feel so peaceful and good food and good clean bar I always stay here when ever come to jeju and you can take the bus anywhere you want to go around jeju it?s beautiful island and I am from Hawaii tham you know what I mean alright

This beach was very beautiful and relatively clean. Water was clear and not too cold fot September. Altough it was posted reccommend  not to swim bc season ended in august the water and weather was great. Bathrooms were close by (though toilet paper was out at the one on the beach). The water was easy to swim in with children as it was very shallow and not rough. Got busier toward aftwrnoon with tourist buses and crowds though.
