review: Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.
Love this beach, we went in winter, wind very strong and cold, most of them hide inside the mini bus but few of us walk around, taking photos, see the raw seaweed near the stone

Love the walk. Advisable to use a pair of good shoes as the ground can be slippery. Very dark and cold. Difficult to reach by bus. Usually there will be taxis at the nearest bustop. Advisable to take taxi there from the nearest bustop. After the experience, do take some time to sit at the nearest cafe. Should try the Orange Freeze!

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)

It's pretty difficult using public transportation in Jeju to getting around expect using car. But this one is ok because there is bus stop in the highway, but you need to take a taxi or walking 3km from bus stop to get this place

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was an impressive sight. If you wear appropriate shoes/trainers and get close to the waterfall, you can get a bit wet. But you have to be prepared to walk on big and, sometimes, round rocks. Tip: Get there early. It was our first stop and we were glad. As we were leaving (around 10am), buses full of tourists were arriving. It would have been quite impossible to take good pictures without getting someone's head in them because the staircase is not that wide.

It was along the way to Manjanggul Cave. As we had missed the bus 990 which could take us to the Cave, we had to walk the 2.5km way. About 1.4km's walk, we came to the Gimnyeong Maze Park. It was a fun place even for adults. We did not follow the map so that it would be exciting. Indeed it was, and the more lost we were, the more exciting it got.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It took me a long time to get there. All those folks with cars would have no problems. But I am on a budget, and I am bussing it all the way. I came here from the Seongsan Ilchulbong crater thing, and I took the 701 bus to the stop that said it was for the cave. Then I walked 2.5km to the cave. The cave was gloriously cold inside, as I was a hot sweaty mess by then (Korean people staring at the fat, sweaty American haah!). I took my time through the cave, it was nice and worth the trip for me, even though it took me almost 2 hours to get back after I was finished. I think you could take a cab for a reasonable price... but I am cheap.

It took about 10 minutes to travel on a ferry to visit Udo (thanks to G map)!I decided to walked around the coastline after lunch on arrival.An interesting island with some public arts and you wouldn?t stop taking photos!It worth spending some time walking around! (A number of transportation options are available, such as bike, e-bike and bus)!

It took a little over 2 hours by bus to get here. I feel conflicted with it, as a part of me liked the place but another part of me thought there was (yet again!) nothing special here. Plus the journey to get there was already exhausting so probably my feet were already asleep halfway into my walk.So only go if you can rent a car, it will take much less time to get here. All in all a relaxing place to take a stroll or read in.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town
In short, you will be walking/driving with chaotic buses, motor cycles, bicycles, walkers & rental cars in single lane. Terrible visit.

If you were to Seongsan Ilchulbong and to Manjang cave next, you can grab the taxi if there is no bus.. The fare is quite reasonable.Wouldnt expect that the cave would be that cold but it is as cold as Seoul during Spring time.. The lighting is very good. Though it is  a long walk to the end, it id worth it.. The deeper, the colder it is..

If you want to enjoy around two hours walking without difficulties in the middle of an amazing and dense  forest I highly recommend you to visit Bijarim. Considering the time needed for these trees (nutmeg yew, family of the Taxus) to grow and the fact that normally you can only find it as bushes into other species's forest this place is a unique jewel with many of the trees aging more that 500 or indeed 800 years. Beautiful and relaxing experience that I will keep forever in my memories as a lover of trees that I am.

I went to see lighthouse in shape of horse, one is in red and the other is in white. They are well made, attractive and iconic!I too a bus heading towards West, (bus#444, it has a stop at Jeju intercity bus terminal), you would need to walk to the lighthouses or you can get off at the stop of beach.The coast line is nice, airplanes are frequently flying over the sky as it?s so close to the airport!

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called   Orum   in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

I love this cave as it was calmy, a little bit wet but make you comfortable after a long walk from the bus stop. I had to walk 3km or more (I think) coz my legs felt so sore, but I love the walk inside the cave. If you take a public bus, don't finish up too late as you might miss the last bus.

I have spend a week on Jeju Island in September, and of my Highlights was Udo. I had time only for a day trip, and if I ever make it back to Jeju, my priority will be to spend at least one night there. Its such a lovely, small and relaxed place. From Seongsan its only 15 minutes to Udo by Ferry. There, you can take the local bus that runs along the island, you can rent small tuk-tuks / quad bikes / scooters or bicycles, you can join a tour (I think only in Korean) or you can walk (like I did, but then of course you dont get to cover the whole island).

I have been wanting to visit the Teddy Bear Museum for the longest time but did not get to visit the one in Seoul 2 years ago. So, when we decided to plan a 2D1N trip to Jeju, this attraction is in my itinerary list. It is not located conveniently near the city centre and about an hour's bus ride to go to the attraction. I was so excited when I saw the museum when the bus passed by and alighted with much excitement. We were greeted with a huge bear at the entrance and it was like entering a wonderland. We walked around admiring the displays, the history of teddy bears etc. We also visited the outdoor park right behind the museum which are meant for visitors only. It was a fruitful visit and did not fail my expectation though. Love all the bears on sale at the gift shop but couldn't bring them all back so only got to admire them when I was there. If you are visiting Jeju, do drop by this museum to bring back childhood memories.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I got the bus here from Jungmun - a couple of hours in total but it was worth it. Really good value, lots to look at, peaceful place to walk around, beautifully done and looked after. There weren't many other people there so it felt as if I had the place to myself. I had lunch in the restaurant and that was also good. Make sure you take your camera. Hugely recommended.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

I first saw this falls on the local map I received. I investigated and stopped there using the airport limousine bus route no 600. It is a short walk from the main road and when you get closer, the sound of the water guides to its location. The water falls over a short (50-100 m) cliff, but it is beautiful and ideal to take some nature pictures. It runs into the sea immediately and provides a picturesque scene.Be careful when you visit, since the railing on the sea side was broken and seems quite a safety hazard for me.This spot does provide you with the opportunity to take some awesome pictures.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Had an awesome day here last week, awesome place for walking and photography. It was so nice to get out of the city and see some of the countryside. I think this is one of the most rugged areas, my kinda style of image. I dropped business for a few days to come here and it was worth it. If you have the change, like hiking or are a photographer. Go!

Good to go if you have not been to a cave before. Be prepared to walk though. Into the cave and out takes about 50mins including taking photos and reading the signboards. If u r taking bus 701, stop at manjanggul stn n take a cab.it is only 1.7km so shld cost u 2800won. But taxi driver will ask for 4000won.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

From Seogwipo city, I took the bus number 202, stopped at Sanbanggulsa. It took me 1 hr to reach there. But the coast was closed due to the weather, but I still could walk around. Across it, there is a temple on a mountain, you can climb up there too if this attraction is closed.

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

Easy to get to, a small entry fee, then a short walk down, out and around a spectacular and unique geological area that is set on the edge of the island. Very picturesque and a great spot for photos, but it can get very busy depending on the time of the day. Worth a visit and a wander - places for picnics - however if the day is wet, an hour or two will be enough time.

Easily accessible via 15min ferry from Jeju Seongsanpo harbour, Udo is ideal for a short day trip or sorta those places in Korean dramas whereby couples miss the last ferry and have to wing it for the night). Anyways we made sure to check the ferry schedule. We had 2 hours and decided to walk instead of renting motorised vehicles (didn't have IDL), bicycles (too hot) or tourist hop-on-hop-off bus (too rushed). Other than tourists nearly running down pedestrians and into other vehicles, it's a nice place to explore & hike for nature lovers. Ferry return is a little pricey at ??8500 but should be ok if staying over. We tried the peanut icecream but didn't think it was that great. Basically vanilla soft serve with sprinkled peanuts. Perhaps the wrong shop.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.

review: Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

careful of when walking in the cave, very uneven and wet grounds. The cave is very far from the city, the public bus does not go direct and takes 45min with many stops in between. When arriving at the destination, its about 2.4km walk to the entrance of the cave. If you are lucky to get a taxi when u alight from the bus, they will charge u 4000won to drive u to the cave entrance to purchase your ticket to the cave

Being adults and have been busy over the years, we truly enjoyed walking 'lost' in the maze.  We reached the place quite late and we were trying to get out of the maze asap.  Enjoyed the cool weather to search for the exit.  Managed to ring the bell just before closing time.

Beautiful place to take a nice walk around the shore line. Can imagine it would get a bit busy in the summer, but it was empty when we visited as it was a snowy winter day which by all accounts added to the experience. Be careful though it can become a wee bit slippery when the rocks get wet.

Basicallu it's a small island, so we can walk / rent bicycle - motorcycle - small car / hop on bus to get around. Almost no activities. Just stop by here n there to take picture, buy ice cream, dine, etc. If you just want to relax and embrace the beautiful nature around, this is a good place. Our family rent bicycle 10.000 won per bicycle. It took us 4 hours to go around the island slowly.

Awesome cave! The ticket price was 2,000KRW.  The transportation is a bit tricky as the bus stop isn't that close to the caves (additional 2.5 km walk).  You can take a taxi from the bus stop (4,000 KRW one way).

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

Apart from walking 2.5km in the extreme summer heat from the bus stop outside (pls find alternative routes), the cave was unique and pretty interesting to see. Love the temperature inside to cool us down and be away from the heat too.

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

After visiting the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, we proceeded to head to the ferry terminal for Udo Island. We were surprised we couldn?t get a cab during winter. Hence, we ended up walking to the ferry terminal instead.Note you need to show your passport and fill up a boarding form in order to take the ferry, at 30 mins interval. We took the 1400hr ferry. A 2-way ferry ticket costs 8,500 won. Upon arriving the island, one has the option of renting an electric scooter, manual bicycle or take the bus. For us, we took the round island bus. Bus fare is 5,00 won, which you can hop in and out at any attraction stops.  We headed to Udo-bond Peak stop and hiked up. Unfortunately, it was drizzling the whole day. We spent about an hour before returning to the ferry terminal.I suggest you allocate an entire day for Udo island. If the weather is fine, it is worthwhile to stop by all the attractions, enjoy the beach and food there.

Absolutely stunning location. Great place to sit on the beach and relax while the waterfall sprays you! If you're travelling from Jeju City, make sure you ask for directions before you try and find this waterfall (there are no buses that take you directly there so you have to walk for 15 minutes). - Guess that isn't the waterfall's fault though!

A place to walk, relax, and connect with nature! The Spirited Garden is regarded as one of the world's most beautiful gardens. The entire garden was designed by one man, Mr. Sung, which is quite interesting. The Spirited Garden includes 7 smaller gardens. The Secret Garden, one of the seven small gardens, is a world-class location for business meetings and diverse performance. It has received several awards, including Korea Unique Venue, Green MICE Venue, Jeju Unique Venue, etc. This garden is an unmissable place for those who love nature!

A place not to miss if visit Jeju. Hello Kitty Island is not very big, to complete the whole place plus take photos it takes around 2hrs.The entrance fees was quite reasonable. Can take a short break at their cafe, their cakes are delicious. The public bus stop is very near the museum,just less than 3 mins walk. This place is also near to Alive Museum.

A nice stop on the yeha bus tour, a lot of tourists so it easily gets overcrowded as the observation platform is small. Nice walk nearby with a small park next to the ocean. Pentagonal and heptagonal rock formations from lava cooling down. Enjoyed it and do recommend if in the area!

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

You're given a map at the beginning but it's much more fun to try and find your way without it! We got there pretty early so it wasn't very crowded. It didn't take us very long to walk through it but it was definitely worth the stop.
Worth the walk to see the cave and also get photos of the ocean from the top. ? Be prepared for a few stairs to get to the top.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.

We paid our entrance fees and simply stayed on the top to get some good pictures. There were hordes of people down below so I don't recommend taking a long walk down and then back up just to get some pictures of other tourists.

We enjoyed a pleasant walk up the steps to the temple at the top and wandering around the lower temple. Enjoyed a tasty hotdog lunch from the sweetest woman at cafe next door (sunny house) and a delicious peanut ice cream too. Great morning visit before walking down to the beach.

We decide to go up the mountain on foot. It was a long way but worth it. The scene from the this mountain top is unforgetable and undeniably great. We could have stayed here all day seeing the nature changed if the weather weren?t cold. Walking the way up was exhausting but the fresh air and the sights we saw at different heights really cooled us down.
Visited Oldolgae on a stormy day.  Spectacular with waves crashing on the cliffs and strong wind blowing. Very close to Seogwipo town (5 minutes drive). Nice cliff top walk.

Two things to see here: 1) small dried up crater top that I didn't even notice after walked by. 2) a loop of man made path with silvergrass on both sides for photos. Quite crowded on my day of visit even silver grass is not uncommon in most park. Many locals come to catch the famous Korean TV series scenes for photos as the silver grass is in season.

This was our last stop in Jeju. We arrived right after sunset and were able to walk around the island and enjoy the beautiful nature area and then walk back over the bridge while it was lit up. Good activity for young children to just get out and run. Best of all it was free! There is also a free public restroom in the parking lot.

This spectacular waterfall is worth the visit. Parking is easy and there is a small fee to walk down to the bottom of the falls. The bottom is all rocks so it could be difficult to maneuver for some. At the top is a lovely art gallery and cafe.

This site is one of the most popular places in Jeju so be prepared for the crowds of Chinese tours.  The hiking course is all paved and has a lot of steps.  The site says it takes around 55 minutes round trip.  Of course this is just an approximation.  I found the course to be pretty easy and it only took me 15 minutes to reach the top of the crater.  At the top there is a large deck like area to sit and take a rest.  The walk down has some beautiful spots for pictures overlooking the island.  At the base there are a lot of different restaurants but they all offer the same food.  Not a lot of options
The weather wasn't the best. It rained on the way up and was very cloudy. Would have been great if the cloud had lifted. Still was an easy walk to the top and a must do.

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

Stopped here on the way to Segwipo from Jeju City. Had an incredible lunch at Innisfree House walked the gardens and then had dessert and tea at the tea museum. Highly suggest this site to anyone who enjoys serene landscapes and healthy/energizing food!

Perfectly symmetrical columns of rocks stack on top of one another. Must see for geology/volcanology students ( columns were cooled-down volcanic lava). Located within few minutes walk to the Changjeyoun Falls.

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.

Nice walk to the falls  but cost 2.00 per person to walk down to the falls. Very crowded with tourist. The actual walk to the falls was nicer than the actual falls itself. A nice stop if you're in the area  but not worth the drive just to see the falls.
Nice to stop over for lunch and have a walk along the river and at the beach but not suggest going there on purpose unless you want a ride on the raft

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

most important points1 start your climb early. as you must reach a certain point before noon and must start the decent by 14:30.2 take a bout 3-4 leters of water per person as there is no place to fill or buy anywhere on the climb (locals take tangerines as they are filled with liquid and sugars)we started at  the road 1131  entrance at about 08:30 and reached the midpoint at about 11:30 and then the top at 14:00large parts of the route are wood walks and steps but others are more difficult.when you reach the top make sure to take a picture of the tree with writing as proof so you can get a certificate when you reach the bottom (1000 WON)Enjoy your climb

Loved it the various marine lives attraction there. Personally I liked most is the underwater aquarium where we could walk beneath the swimming fishes. Also the collection of various jellyfish and octopus on display. Stunning.

review: Love this natural rock formations along the coastal beach walk ... definitely not your usual sandy beach ... lots of opportunities for great photosThere are ladies selling fresh seafood catches along the way ... we didn't have time to stop for that though ...
It's shorter distance in real than I thought. But definately an interesting place to stop by! I both walked and drived along the road!

It's been several years since we have been but I can't stop talking about this place. Definitely worth the stop weather it's for half the day or half an hour a walk around this place will not disappoint the outdoor enthusiast or even the person who likes a causal stroll around a park. There are many different things to check out. All around an amazing site.

It was low tide so the rocks were dry and there were lots of little pools.  It was fun to see little kids playing in the pool water for hours.  We were just there for a little time. Our teenagers had fun walking on top of the lava rocks along the beach.  Careful not to step on crabs. Beautiful serene beach.

It was fun to walk thru but for the food products  much of the time I had no idea what anything was. I especially liked the fresh fish vendors with the live fish  octopi  and shellfish in the tanks. Quite a lot of fresh produce and clothing for sale as well. If you haven't been to a Korean market  it's fun to spend maybe 1/2 hour going thru.

It is really great how many things you can see on Jeju for less than $3 a person. We did not climb to the top but went into the park to the left to see the cliffs and get a closer look. You only have to walk a little to see a lot. Ample parking and coffee shops nearby. It was so beautiful despite the crowd. It was rainy and windy. Raincoats are sold in the gift shop.

It is easy to find and has a few parking places. No entrance fee. Restroom availabe at the parking lot. You walk alonxg the coast line and dont forget your camera. It is a nice spot for taking pictures. Has couple of small shops for water and fuits. Its worth to stop. Not easy for whell chair and stroller.

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is 9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is  9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

Having arrived in Jeju eager to see as much as possible in a short time frame - the art work was top on my hit list. I stumbled across the website for the Museum of Contemporary Art and was very excited to go (as there are so many museums to choose from!)I would recommend a whole morning to visit Jeoji as there is more than just this Museum there. The first Gallery I went to showed a lovely exhibiton on the Sound of Nature this gallery was on the left hand side of the road and was a free two floor exhibition. I then walked along the road to the Museum of Contemporary Art on the right. The Museum had 4 big rooms of Art - all of which had a meaningful message behind the artist's work in both Korean and English! The receptionists were very helpful when directing me as to where to go and I finished my self-guided tour with a visit to the Art shop which was outside in the sculpture garden. A lovely morning well spent taking in the delights of Korean art.
Breathtaking scenery. Lovely walk up. Many stops to catch your breath and look around the amazing place. Absolutely worth the visit.

Be prepared to climb flights and flights of narrow stairs to get up to the top of this mountain (felt like a 40min walk up and a 30min walk down). It was really windy when we reached the top and very crowded with tourists.

An interesting museum with various glass sculptures including a large pyramid that you can walk through. Staff were kind enough to let us try glass blowing and have a few activities available - we made candles. Worth stopping for if you're in the area  but probably not worth a detour.

After I toke all photos then hurry up to the musuem and walked around. And I stopped at the bakery shop! You must to order Green Tea ice cream Green Tea Latte. Guide always cheer about Green Tea roll I think it is not delicious.
A visit to this folk village is like a walk through time. It was as if time stopped and all buildings there were from the time it was built. The audio explanation was really informative.

A popular tourist stop on Jeju Island. A lot of uphill walking is required and would be a problem for elderly folks or those with bad knees. However this is a really lovely location for scenic photos. The old ladies who dive for octupus and shellfish is a must visit as well though be aware of the very steep stairs up and downwards.

You have to climb up quite a bit of stairs to get to the top but it is surely worth it when you see the crater and the ocean beyond! We arrived at 3 o'clock and was unaware that the women fisherman show was also at three by the time we had climbed to the top and back down we were 45 minutes late :-(. Be sure to walk out to the lookout of Udo island, gorgeous!

You could actually walk out into the ocean among swirling seaweed and chase after schools of small fish (my favourite part). There are also small rock ponds for you to observe some sea creatures that were washed up by the waves. Plenty of families and couples with puppies and dogs were frolicking in the waters and having a picnic on the sand. Sand was so soft!   For more information and pictures on Jeju, visit my travel blog.https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

Went here on a hot summer afternoon and could immediately feel the drop in temperature when entering the natural reserve. The water is clean, clear and very tempting. unfortunately swimming is not allowed. Need to walk and climb stairs to reach all the 3 waterfalls, but each one was worth it. stop by near the bridge to take photos

We, a group of friends had visited this place last week. It was awesome! The journey to get there, parking and the walk up and back were all good. There is ample parking space and plenty of eateries that offers various types of snacks and cold drinks.The area is impeccably clean and the walking path was clear and safe. The steps may seem a little steep at certain points, but you will be well rewarded once you reach the top. The crater is a beautiful sight! Not surprising that it's the iconic image of Jeju which appears on Google. You need about an hour or so for the entire visit.

We walked to the peak of Hallan Mountain from Seongpanak. We used around 5hours to walk from a height of around 800m to 1950m. The top of Hallan Mountain is a small pond - Bakrokdam. After returning to Seongpanak, you can get the certificate to show that you have arrived to the peak of Hallan Mountain (fee: 1000won)

We visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on two separate days - the first was in the afternoon to see the women free-divers' performance (1pm/3pm) and the second was in the wee hours of the morning (5+am) to see the sunrise. The free-divers were all middle-aged women who looked old enough to be our mothers. Despite their age, it was amazing how they managed to hold their breath so long underwater to harvest the seafood which you could buy from them and eat on the spot (they'll prepare/cook it in whichever way you want). The way they sang prior to the dive and the way they chatted and swam out to sea together reminded us of the friendly grannies in our neighborhood enjoying a nice chit-chat over tea. To see the sunrise at the peak, we started our climb at 4+am (it helps to stay in a hotel within walking distance to Ilchulbong). It was pitch-dark and torchlight was a must. The climb was shorter than expected and we reached the top before 5am. Thankfully the sky was clear that morning and we managed to catch a beautiful sunrise (around 5:30am) that was nothing short of amazing.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We stopped off here after lunch and easily spent 3 hours walking the grounds.  And that was at a fairly quick pace.  The garden has 8 separate sections that provide a contrast.  The garden is very well kept.  So if you are into shrubbery, its not a bad place to spend a few hours

We spent more than an hour walking to and back from the beach. The place can get crowded and you can walk farther too but we stopped because of the huge waves. Nice photo location!The stairs can get quite challenging for older folks because it's uneven and slippery even, so have to be careful. There is also some distance of walking from the car park.

We need to rent a car (邕竊to get there. The driver said walking up there requiring 30 min, yet is quite easy to arrive the top. After reaching the top, you could enjoy the sunset of the seongsan city which is worth it !

We hiked up Hallasan the first weekend in March 2012.  We brought coats, hats, gloves and scarfs, however we were not prepared for the amount of snow on the mountain.  Check the conditions ahead of time and be sure to bring walking sticks and spikes for your boots.  My family hiked for awhile but stopped about 1km from the top after we were in more than two feet of snow and freezing.

We have no idea that such place exist until we drove along the Hallasan range from North to the southern part of the island. Spotted the beauty along the road, we saw a parking space opposite the 1100 Altitude Wetland, decided to stop and take a look. There is a 1-km boardwalk which we stroll along the peaceful woods and admire the trees, stones, frozen stream, mountain range. As it is winter, we could not spot any birds, or wildlife.However, we are pleased with a little surprise that we have added a new destination of the day to our itinerary.

Visited in Oct, very windy and cooling. Walked up to the hill top in 10mins. Very good experience and the tracks and steps were very nicely constructed. But the place is extremely crowded so photo taking was difficult. Worth the visit and the climb.

visited by family with 3 teenagers in a hot August day. It was really hot, humid day, and we climbed Seonsan Ilculdong around 3 o'clock. It is said that it took about 25 mins' walk to the top, but it was very hard to climb because of heat during hot August day. It is nice picture taking place.Do not bring little kids. It is not for the young children. I saw many children who just wear sandals climbed the all steps to the top, and they cried and were angry because of the heat and hard work. Actually, Seongsan Ilchulbong is nice picture taking place from far, but there is nothing spectacular on the top. It is better to climb Seoungsan Ilculbong in the spring or fall, not in the summer. Otherwise, it is good enough to look at it from the parking lot and take a walk around shore areas.

Udo is an island very close from Jeju-do. It's next to Seongsan-ilchul-bong, which is also famous. It takes about 15 minutes by boat from Seongsan port. You pay for entrance to the island with the boat fare. The usual course seems to be walking up the hill in Udo, Gummerlae, and checking out the lighthouse surrounded by lots of stones stacked on top of each other for wishes to come true. The weather was perfect when we went, very sunny :)

This would just take you 5 minutes of your time. Get out of the taxi and snap some pictures. No, it did not look like a dragon's head to me no matter how I pictured it. But oh well, I have been told I could do with more imagination. One of those things that you do to strike off another   to-go   in your itinerary. If you are keen, walk down the stairs - you will see vendors selling fresh octopus sashimi - worth a try!

This was the last stop on our vacation. Unfortunately it was also the only grey/cloudy/cold day. The island was still a must see for us. The ferry ticketing area can be very confusing, so be prepared if you don't know any Korean. We figured it out after about 5 minutes of standing around, staring in confusion. Once we reached the island, we rented an electric car (from Gulliver's Travels) with side-by-side seating for 占35,000 for 2.5 hours and cruised around the island following the path. The beaches were incredible. White sand, crystal clear water at the shore, turning into turquoise water a little farther out. Even with the grey sky, it still looked amazing. We didn't climb out to the lighthouse (if you climb to the top of Hallasan on your visit, you'll understand why. Ow.) but we got some great photos of it. Peanut ice cream is way overrated in my opinion, but it was still a must since we were on Udo! My husband got the hallabong ice cream. We liked that one more, but the stuff they put on it tastes like mashed up hallabong peel, so it was bitter and we just scraped it off. There is a restaurant that serves (I forget the name, I am guessing) Hallasan fried rice. They make it look like a volcano! We really wanted to go, but needed to catch the ferry back. Overall, if it had been warmer and the we could actually see the sun, it would have been much more enjoyable. We talk about going back and spending a night on the island so we have the time to walk around it, instead of having to drive/rent a bike.

This place was breathtaking! After getting a yummy octopus pancake we walked around the cliffs admiring the beauty and the ocean. We started on the west and ended on the east it was a beautiful, windy, gorgeous day! Great place to get fresh seafood from the lady fishermen too.

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. When i visit Jeju, i stayed in a hotel nearby, so i can see the sunrise from the top of seonsan Ilchulbong. To see the beautiful sunrise, i walk from my hotel at 4.30 am. You need to buy an entrance ticket to this place.You need to walk the stair path, uphill, and soon you arrive on top, you'll find so many people already setting up the camera to capture the sunrise. after enjoying the beautiful scene from top, on our way down, my eyes can't stop admiring the beauty scene of Jeju City. Everything is taking your breath away in this place.You also can ride a horse or watch the mermaid show (lady divers). If you want to buy some goods for your family from Jeju (orange, souvenirs, cake, snacks), you have to buy it in Jeju, because you can't find any of these goods in Seoul. If you want to give a second thought on it, your last chance to shop is in the Jeju International airport (price is the same everywhere in Jeju).This is a very highly recommended place to visit in Jeju Island!

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This is a very long beach along the south Jeju coast near the south-western end.  You can bike (there's trial, do segway, or a long walk) or drive and stop along places to take beautiful photos. At the end of the beach is Songacsan where you can hike for an hour or so - very easy.

This hill looks rather spectacular from a distance and the approach to its foot is thru a pretty green field. The pathway is well maintained and it's an easy hike up to the top, at only 180 meters. It's mostly a broad stairway to the top and makes for a pleasant evening walk. At the peak it would be a great place to watch the stars on a clear moonless night. Admission is free after   closing time   -- there's no gate.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

There is a stair to reach to top to this extinct volcano. It seems easy at first but you will need to be prepared to reach its top. They put places to sit through the course.Since I was there during summer time, I sweated a lot. But reaching the top pay all physical efforts!Then you can walked down in order to see (and get enjoyed by) the friendly ladies who dive! It was nice to see that they also served the seafood they've just captured! You need to see them because they are now just a few and how knows if there will be more of them in the future.Remember 1: the presentations of this ladies happen in specific times (I got their 13:30pm presentation, so I had to walk fast up and down the volcano in order to see them)Remember 2: you should pay a ticket to get inside the park.I truly recommend you to reach both the top of the volcano and see the women divers presentation.

There is a small fee to enter the area, I think around 2-3000W. Once you are inside the park, you can hang out on the paths, admiring the rolling green fields, or head up some few hundred stairs to the top of the little mountain and look at the crater. The little mountain was formed by a volcanic eruption a long time ago and around the rim of the crater there are 99 'peaks' which they call the crown. That's cool. I think that's cool.After you have taken an inappropriate amount of selfies you can head back down to a small beach area and watch traditional women divers...diving. There is also a small black stoned beach by the women divers which you can walk along and admire the beautiful black stone of the small mountain, which is Seongsan Ilchulbong.We travelled there by public transport and it wasn't difficult at all.

There are many waterfalls in Jeju, we decided to have a look at Cheonjiyeon. There is a large parking lot, eateries and a couple of souvenir shops, 7eleven etc when you arrive. To walk to the waterfall is about 10-15 min along a small tree lined river. Many tourists and tourists groups are visiting the waterfall so it will be quite crowded. The waterfall as such is nice, but not too tall or spectacular. everybody takes a few selfies and then heads back to the parking lot pretty much. If nearby it makes to stop by and visit but it is not worth a long journey just to see this waterfall.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.

The taxi driver was really kind to walk with us, but he didn't   warn   us of the difficulty level and duration of the climb! :) We had lots of beautiful photos taken, in between the rest stops, and finally reached the peak with real sense of accomplishment!
The short walk to the falls is nice, and the falls are pretty.  They are good for a quick stop, but not a must see if you don't have time here.

The lava tubes are very interesting and quite large - especially compared to those in other parts of the world. The only word of caution is to bring a raincoat and sneakers if it has been raining, as the water will trickle down through the rock and will drip considerably as you walk through. Definitely worth a stop.

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the   Big Three   on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.

The hike was awesome. Very scenic and nature at its best. There are a few different routes to the top. ( summit is out of bounds though) At the top, you can find a shelter with washroom and a small shop selling cup noodles. We drove there, so had to take the same route down. There are taxis waiting at the start points when we finished our walk(around noon time)

The hike to the end of the cave was not short, so be prepared to walk a few kms if you plan to visit this place. The cave itself was wet and cool, which is good if outside was hot. You get to see different formations and immerse yourself deep underground at the same time. So, the time was well spent here. Afterward, you can stop by the restaurant near the entrance and have some cheap Korean food.  The admission to the cave was very reasonable as it is a government owned attraction.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time???
