The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

The cave is very dimly lit. The floor was very uneven (we are not blaming.. it's the natural formation of the lava) and slippery. I could only look down to make sure that I am walking safely and properly. I had no time to stop and look up and admire the caves. The cave is also very dimly lit, which makes the walk more challenging. We decided to turn back after 20 mins.

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Seongsan Ilchulbong is the best location on the Eastern part of Jeju Island. It is definitely an awesome place. It might however best be enjoyed not from the top of the volcano itself, but by walking or driving around (or flying?). The reason is that when you get to the top of the volcano, the caldera isn't as impressive as the one on top of Hallasan mountain. I did visit it during the day, and I get that it's more stunning at sunrise. It's still very nice. What's also great to see, if you climb the volcano, is to look back, and look at Udo island or the heart of Jeju island, with the villages and Hallasan in the background. Definitely a must-do in Jeju.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. Toilets are unfortunately not clean, so you may want to bring some disinfectant lotion and/or toilet paper.The first part of the hike is easily accessible, the latter part less so. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!
please take ur time to climb up the hill , you will never regret. the journey is not easy .you will need to walk about 1hour  to reach the top .

People still live here!     There was no admission fee.   We drove right in and walked around.     Obviously, the biggest thing is the roofs which are replaced every year.     You still have the stone walls and the entry gate.     We saw several people who still live here but didn?t interact with any of them.    The village was a convenient stop on our way back from the eastern side of the island.     I wouldn?t make a special trip to see it but it?s certainly worth 20-30 minutes if it?s on your way.
nice walk to the top. you can see volcano crater on the top, pretty windy and sunny, make sure you bring sunglass and water, also jacket

Nice looking beach and lovely water, but don?t recommend if you want to swim. Lifeguards are over authoritarian and you?re only allowed in a 10x10 square with many other people (who have inflatables)! We had a pretty bad experience here where the lifeguards seemed to be picking on us for no reason. Also not allowed to sit/walk on certain parts of the beach. Overall poor experience only saved but spotted an octopus!

My son live and work teaching English  in Jeju , I spent 10 days with him in his apartment and this trip to  Seogwipo and the hike will always be in my heart.  We stayed in nearby hotel and woke up 4am started walking and climbing the steps to see the sunrise on the top and its all worth it .. Indeed Jeju has teh rightful name - the island of the Gods.

Must walk..hike to the top.  Worth to go..because the nice scenery. Not suitable for old people & wheelchair. Really a huge place. Actually is a die volcano. But really beautiful.. when you on top the hill. Definate you wont regret . But must have a good stamina. Certain hour, there is a woman diver show. Quite interesting.

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

It's just a 1km tunnel walk, feeling the chill a little.  Kind of dim, ground is uneven, therefore watching our steps took most of our focus, stopping occasionally for pictures taking. Nothing exceptionally awesome.
It's a serious walk, lot's of steps. Not sure I'd do it again. Limited refreshments at top - just Pot noodles.

It's a dramatic coastline, just like blocks of puzzles stacking on top of each other. It's a unique sight. The entrance fee is KRW2,000 and the overall walk is easy, takes maximum 15-20 mins including photography. The sea water is clear and you can actually see the formation from below.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

it is very easy and friendly track to reach the peak, but for me the beautiful things about Seongsan Illchulbong are scenery from everywhere. so, I made a little tour by walking by from beaches till Saepjikoji and to Udo island. Never get missed from sunrise to sunset, everything is beautiful. is not wrong to choose stay near the Hills, Goseong-ri is perfect village to stay.But, if you just a few time to visit is good to stopping by. My wife loves here in spring time, lots of canola and pretty flower in the green green grass.You will found starbucks, convenience market, and lots of food.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.
i'm afraid there is too much tourist even during the low season, i need to walk really fast for more tourist are coming and i don't even have time to really stop by and take a good look at the top

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.
If u expect very exciting, not really! But it's good to have a walk in a rainy day until it stops raining! Overall it's fine!

If there is nothing else you do go see this temple. It is a sprawling complex that goes all up to the base of the mountain. Along the way if you do hike all the way up to the top, there are signs to explain the legends behind the names of the places you walk and why there is a temple there. But even if you don't it is still an sight to see

I went there with my family members in a cloudy day. This place is composed with several parts of themes. Lake, play ground, short hiking with spa, and snack bars.My kids(9, 5yrs) really enjoyed the place with running, taking pictures, and eating.Even I visited in Jeju more than 10 times, this place is the most memorable place to visit. Because kids didn?t have any bother others.Additionally, there were packed with people and very noise when I waited for tour train. Then please be sure to keep you eyes on your kids. I visited there at the last of tour then I couldn't have enough time to hiking.However, I recommend you to take a walk at the picnic garden station (2nd stop).There are kids town and eco-land at Picnic garden station

I really feel sorry for those went earlier this year and totally missed the beauty of the silvery purple grass we have not seen elsewhere. It is such an easy walk so even you push baby strollers, or having a baby buggy, it shouldn't be too difficult. Anyway, you probably stop Sao many times on the way to take photos so it is not a tiring climb.There's only one small snack place at the bottom but a few nice wooden picnic booth for people to rest.  We saw some Korean families enjoying their homemade kimba at the top enjoying the scenery. I think it's a great family trip for about one to two hours depending on the age difference in your group.Selfie stick is quite useful here if you want to post in from too the unique grass.  Obviously don't dress in silver (autumn time).After this we went on another 20~30 min to the world's biggest nutmeg forest which is on the way to the east coast (5 Day Market and Haenyeo Women Diver Museum) to,follow in the afternoon.

I really did enjoy working my way through this maze. The entire area is beautifully put together and is the kind of place you just want to spend time in and enjoy. Unfortunately, uniqueness comes with a price. I thought nearly $5 per person was a little steep but it isn't every day you get to walk through a hedge maze. The maze itself is a lot of fun and is large enough to actually be a bit of a challenge. We met the owner and he is very friendly and interesting to talk to. I am glad we stopped here but, because of the price, I don't think I would do it again.

I live in a country with waterfalls and volcanoes, so Jeongbang wasn't as impressive for me. Maybe the hype kind of spoiled it, but it was really just a clear and pretty waterfall -- crawling with tourists. We were in and out in ten minutes or less because there was nothing to do except take a photo. It is worth a stop and look if you are passing through but don't expect too much.People with mobility issues -- there is a walk down some stairs to reach the base of the falls. The picture spots at the base are on a mound of loose, smooth boulders. I scuffed my boots here.

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I have heard people said the sunrise from the crater is magnificent. But, I have visited Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon and it was just awesome! Thanks to the wide green field surrounded by the dark blue sea and cover with the bright blue sky! It was so relaxing there hearing the wave sound and feel the wind blowing pass through me. Hiking to the top of the crater would be good too, but you may need at least 2 hours to walk around the area.

I came to this place at a rainy day, so I can't go until the top of the mountain, but I can saw, the scenery is very nice, with the sea under the mountain. I suggest you go there on the spring so ytou can walk to the top.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

Hotel was right across this market so I stopped here on my first night for dinner. I was amazed by the selection of street food stalls, fresh produce and desserts. Most of the signs were in Korean but just follow the crowd and where there's a long line you'll never go wrong! I got a taste of the rice with fried black pork plus some fried octopus in batter, which were both great. Bought some boxes of cheap chocolate as well. Areas of the market selling fresh fish and vegetables are wet though so beware when walking through.

Here really is a nice and beautiful place. Rent a bicycle to walk around the island during autumn is soooo good. Worth to visit it. I ate a sashimi bibimbap there, is fresh and yummy. 3 hours is not enough seriously, if you wanna go through the whole island, unless you ride your bicycle without stop, haha.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Great for kids and any others that like train ride.You will be taking a small train ride through beautiful natural forests. Some walking is require in between stations, but just have fun and enjoy what nature brings. Take pictures of mini lake... the water is clear, windmills, grassy fields, pirate ship and not to miss the last stop with beautiful tulips.

Great experience walking around and reading the story,  The owner had a lot of faith that he could change this area into something wonderful.  Glad we made the time to stop and check out the Bonsai's!
For me it's not a very special sight, though it's adventurous and interesting to walk down the stairs to the coast and see the   diving women   serving octopus, shells and abalone on the rock
even if you don't have time to walk up to the top, it's worth going just to take photos and have a try at the freshly caught seafood.

Eco land is a fun mix of train riding and nature walking.  You should be aware that some walking and waiting are required.  The train takes you through some forest area and fields that are properly much prettier later in the year.  We visited in February and the scenery from the train wasn't great, but still fun.  The train stops and you have to walk from the first station.  It is a nice stroll across a lake.  You can check out how windmills work, if you desire.  The second stop is a kids play area, which if you are travelling with young kids they will love.  There are slides and swings and miniature buildings.  It was hard to get our kids to leave.  There are some unpleasant aspects to the train, getting a seat can be a hassle after the first loading.  The seats are also two sided benches, so if you have someone behind you that is inconsiderate, it can be quite uncomfortable.  Nonetheless, we had a great visit and really enjoyed Eco land.

Don't talk, just feel yourself on the walk way to clim to the top. Open your eyes and record the scene to your soul. It will treat your mind, very well. Don't forget your water bottle. Be careful when taking your selfie.

don't forget to be early for this and as this is privately owned attraction, the entrance fees is KRW6000 instead of the government owned ones at KRW2000. Wear comfortable walking or hiking shoes as it is a bit of walking towards the crater. Good place for photographs at the top and be   lost   around the pampas green field for dramatic photographs.

Cruise stop. Jeju tour. On the way back we walked through both this and the underground mall. A million oranges and fish stores. Neat to be among the Jeju people going about their day. Try some of the food! But watch out for the guys DRIVING up and down the aisles on mopeds!I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Completely worth the early morning waking up to see the sunrise. It looks completely difference bathed in the early morning light than after the sun has arisen, so check when the sun rises and wake up early!Is it easy to climb up? My wife doesn't work out, and we took about 40 minutes to walk up the stairs, with occasional stops along the way. I do work out, and even I had to pause a little here and there - bring some water, you'll be glad you did. Otherwise, it's not really difficult, just takes a bit of stamina.

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.

Arrived in the morning parked easily, cost for parking at the entrance was 1800 WON and picked up a map.  Make sure you wear good shoes -- preferably with good ankle support and walking sticks.  The path is well layer out but does take some effort.  We did not get all the way to the top as it was closed due to a slide but it's nice walk.  Suggest an early start and bring water too.

Armed with a Jeju Travel Guide map for cruise tourists, on 9 October we walked in the short distance from the Mariner of the Seas to Dongmun Market and the adjoining Jungang underground shopping street.Wandering through both of these sites provides the contrasting opportunity to encounter local culture with its unique produce, sights and smells  as well as standard internationally branded shopping in a bazaar environment.As a short term tourist visitors we 'soaked up' what we saw and, of course, the market with its variety from fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and food stalls came out on top.It was a rewarding morning off the boat, very easy to undertake.

A lot of local produces. Came during winter - tangerines season. All stalls selling similar items. Plenty of snacks: octopus, deep fried dishes, dumplings. Hoping that there is more price tag/signage to better ease foreigners in purchase. Language barrier is still something that block me from enjoying this walk better.

A little bit hard and tired for people who don't exercise so much to climb up this height but worth it. Trust me, you can see almost of the island from the top of the mountain, feel the sea breeze and hear the wave sound. If you don't familiar with climbing mountain just try to go with the way down. There will be stair so you can walk easily. This way should be fit for handicap and elderly people too.

180m to the top but more then worth it in the end. Taking the hike up the steps was quite a workout, so I highly suggest, prepare to break a sweat. My favorite part was taking pictures on the way down, there are many great picture opportunities. One thing I recommend is to take the extra steps down to the ocean, take your shoes off and enjoy the cool refreshing water. It is well worth it after after walking down.

You can get right up to the falls even as it empties into the sea. Where sneaks that day because there are a lot of rocks. Be careful and take lots of pictures. A taxi or bike ride is preferable but you can easily walk to the entrance it is just out of the way of the town
Yes! From far away it looks like a gigant clam!. No touring was available when we where there  but we parked near by and walked close and took pictures. It is huge  it is worth seeing!

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)

well. this fashion street was near with my hotel & i've walked here quite many times in a week. not so special for me as i don't do shopping but i ate 2times in this street that was impressivefirst time i reached here at 1st day no any breakfast shop near around*(they are opened at 9-10am at least) quite hungry & finally i stepped in one of traditional shop that only served 3 types of food all was hangover soup ha. seem that for drunken. price not so expensive(but not cheap) and quite many stuffs. tasty but full. lady boss also quite nice although she can't well communicate with meanother times with fds that was in a quiet corridor seem quite expensive restaurant with old & korean deco. however price was acceptable & serve sausage stew. well we ate traditional sausage stew in korean style house(boss always walk out from his room & overall style was house instead of restaurant). he was quite concern do we know how to eat & taking care of our table. maybe it has no many tourist but only korean or japanese while we having dinner moment.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..

We went up at 6am in the morning to see the sunrise. With cold rainy weather the event was less romantic than expected but well worth and good fun for us. We went up with our 3yr old boy. The way up is very well prepared and suitable for children who like walking/climbing a bit. We carried out son partly and party he walked. Well Organised tourist attraction.Entrance fee is only W2000.Have fun!

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We visited this last for the day at Jungmun Resort since this opened till rather late (~8+pm). Last entry should be around 7pm since it would take you around 1 1/2 - 2 hours if you're gonna snap alot of the photos inside. If you are already inside Jungmun Resort and are travelling in groups you can take a cab to this place since it would not cost much and you can save the hassle of walking. The paintings inside are really cool and we had a fun time snapping photos away. Effects came out rather cool on the photos. There are several sections in the museum and each sections has its own theme. Definitely worth a visit and we really didn't regret it. Initially we intended to spend only 1 hour in the museum since we really rushing off to other places in the night. We ended up spending 2 hours there. So do equip yourself with a camera and of course have someone with you to take photos for you.

We took many amazing pictures here against the camellia flowers. The walkways around the park were arranged nicely so we spent a few hours here easily. Overall one of the best spots we visited in Jeju this is a place you definitely have to include in your travel plans!

We stumbled upon this place whilst walking about but didn't regret it.I would be careful if you are accompanying very young children or old people as the stairs are made of rock and quite difficult to negotiate. Our 5 year old made it ok but required assistance.A nice place to visit but not much in the way of a waterfall when we were there. Perhaps they take the water in during the day? (that was a joke by the way!)

We stumbled upon this market while walking around Jeju. It was very vibrant inside with many vendors selling their products. The vendors were very friendly and tried to speak English to us. Some even gave us samples of their products. We bought some local chocolates. It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend some time.

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Walk thru a corridor of two rows of Buddha leading you all the way to tis great big golden gwaneusmsa Buddha. This golden Buddha backdrop contains many small Lohan buddhas in rows....there is also a small temple for you to pray
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.

This was really a nice long walk. Will advise to wear good walking shoe. The route was easy to walk just that when the wind come you can feel the wind blowing at you. You have to walk all the way up and you will be able to see the nice surrounding. It was really nice and we really enjoyed it.

This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

This place is ok if you have some spare time and want a peaceful walk.As long as you don't meet any tours because they can me noisy.Its nothing special just trees and very little else.Not worth it if you have to come out of your way.

This place is considered clean for a local market. Mixture of raw fresh food and cooked food stores. We came here at around 10am and a number of cooked food stores are already open. Nice experience walking around and eating street food along the way. There are benches around for you to sit and have your food. Market closes at 8.30pm.
This park was a five minute walk from the beach and the perfect way to pass the afternoon. It's huge! Such a great deal for the ticket price.

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.

this is the only white sand blue water beach in Korea. So i was pretty excited to see it. Its quite shallow and you can easily play around. Its well maintained just like alll other beaches in korea. there is life guard always on duty. Careful while walking near the stones.
This is a nice waterfall to see going in to the sea. The walk down is all steps about 130 each way. The rocks at the bottom can be difficult to walk over.

This is a farm for Green Tea. First and foremost it is near the Glass park 5 mins drive away. So if you are planning to visit this place and have no budget constraints and have lots of time you can consider to spend 30mins at the glass park as well.The Tea farm sells tea (of course) and remember to try the green tea ice cream in the building. You can walk around the farm but be careful of the snakes. We seen one there.Nice place to visit whether alone in a group or with your family and kids.

This is a cool place to take the family. It fun and easy way to walk through mazes. With stream for kids to play in. A amusing part for me was U given a picture of maze so can solve easily. The inside exhibition is worth a walk through with more puzzles and games.

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!

This collection of old houses and replication of villages was fascinating. One could really understand the way of living in the old times when getting up close to the stone construction and thatched roofs and garden plots. This is a perfect walking area for anyone and especially families. As an added bonus the little restaurant on site was reasonable for local dishes.

The outlook has been dressed up and over designed. It looks like a candy house rather than a church. It is quite disappointed especially when you have been walking from a long way out there in order to move closer to it but it does not give you any romantic feeling at all.

The museum is only a short walk from the Hyatt Regency hotel where we were staying.We went there to keep our daughter occupied but to tell the truth we all enjoyed the place. I enjoyed the way the displayed were made up from events in history.The only spoiler was the noise from Chinese tourists!

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

The butterfly museum is interesting showcasing many species of insects but the information are all in Korean. Walk out of the building there is an outdoor park with a maze. The mirror maze is not to be missed the kids had so much fun finding their way out!

The best way to do U-Do Island is by car or scooter.  Rent a car prior to boarding the ferry and take it across OR walk on to the ferry and rent a scooter on the island.  Fantastic sights and places to eat.

That means during a sunny day you can see as far as the Halla mountain. And also the various geological formations around the sea. A nice hike which will take about 1.5 hours but you can just take a walk. By the way the area is often used as backdrop for TV shows including the Dae Jang-geum 鸚㏝빓餓?popular drama show.

Tea Plantations are not my favourite places and this is not a museum as such. But the way the Koreans have done this makes it into a relaxing afternoon experience. The cherry blossoms just came out when we visited. There were scores of Korean students on a field trip but that's OK. It's spacious enough for everyone. A short display of tea cups from around the world lines the entrance of the building. Then it's tea shopping and testing. Try the buckwheat tea! Lots of chinese speaking staff (as with everywhere else in Seoul). Here I tasted the best green tea ice cream and cake. A walk in the surrounding garden and compound is nice. There is a glass building next to the main one by Korean brand Innisfree. In it there are soap making activities a cafe and skin care shopping.

Spent a Sunday morning relaxing on this magnificent beach.  Its emerald coloured crystal clear water and fine white sand laced with shells that makes it glitter.  A magic location!Cannot wait for the moon to appear and make my summer complete.  Walk all the way round to Geumneung beach and enjoy the stroll on the white sand.

Small museum which showcases lots of green tea cups from around the world. As it was raining at the time of visit I spent more time indoors and at the cafe. As this is a tourist hotspot the cafe is always full and finding a table is quite a challenge (I was lucky though). I recommend ordering the green tea ice cream and the cold drip tea which is only sold at the Jeju outlet.Will probably visit again next time to see the green tea plantations which I missed out on.This museum is a stone's throw away from Innisfree Jeju House - barely 90 seconds walk which is worth a visit as well.

Rented a scooter for 4 hours and went around the entire island. Renting is easy- just go to one of the places right next to the ferry docks. You have to go to the cliffs and the black sand beach below them. Cross the beach to the rocks where they have the boat then go inside the cave. Walk all the way to the left and go out the small opening- this place have practically no other tourists. Then if it's low tide- climb to the right to the small opening into another cave but this is a lot cooler!
Really nice calming atmosphere and was not crowded with too many tourists. Beautiful estuary connecting to the ocean. Nice walkway with not too many steps running alongside the estuary.

Our hotel room overlooks this sea. Don't think there is a way to get down but the waterfront makes for a nice breezy walk. I suppose the reason for the decoration on the barrier is to make the walk interesting and photo worthy.
one of the smaller waterfalls of he two but very well kept. shades of water can be seen along with a wishing well and a few picture spots on the bridge and walk way

Okay if visitor is kind of tea lover. Like being here for shopping which is not that extraordinary or the must spot. Just okay for the museum zone and cafe easy and relaxing tea field or area to walk but not that wow anyway. For food and drinks good but for cake and desserts I personally feel soso. For the shop and products' variety are good. Free parking on site.
Not a must see if you are press for time. It was dark most of the way and you don?t get to see much. The star attraction is towards end of the 1km walk.

Not a bad way to fill in a couple of hours. The cave floor is very uneven as you are walking on solidified lava be sure to wear comfy shoes. Also can be quite damp so if you don't want to have water dripping on you maybe take an umbrella. Lots of information provided throughout the walk in several languages to keep you engaged also

Nice way to enjoy the history of korean lifestyle in the past and at the same time walk through some of the shooting locations of the popular K-dramas...great use of the massive landspace and attractive to both young and old...my little gal enjoyed feeding the goats and other lil animals in the village...

Nice to take pictures of the tea gardens/have a walk around. Buy their different flavours of tea that they have and they always change their goods. You can try out their caf챕 as well as go up to the observatory area on a higher floor. It is extremely crowded though.
Nice attraction that suitable for all. Must walk all the way in order to see the main tube. Nice temperature inside the cave. Wear a cover walking shoe!
Need only about 2 hours here.   Combination of botanical gardens and kids amusement park.  Pleasant way to take a walk through wooded areas on Jeju island

Nature is amazing and the lava tubes at manjang is worth seeing. The walk is about 1km in and same way out. Wear good shoes. Walk is not as tiring as climbing up other steep sites in jeju. Educational Signs in English are available. A bit chilly in autumn in the caves.

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)

My 10 yo daughter and I have really enjoyed seeing the waterfall. It was a quick 20 minute walk up a scenic paved path with some other small falls. It was definitely worth a visit. Cost couple won to get in. There are several shops right outside and along the way to buy souvenirs and snacks.

Many Korean villages are reproduced so as you walk you glimpse at the way of life from long ago.  Korean dramas are filmed here and we were able to watch filming.  You can try your hand at games arts and crafts as you wander through the various areas and there  is a free train for those who prefer to ride. The blooming flowers and trees made for beautiful pictures.  This was one of our favorite places we visited while in JeJu it should be on your list of places to go!

Manjang Cave is made of lava formation or lava tube as it is called. We walked about 1-2 km stretch of it only as not the whole tube was opened for tourist visitation.It is cold and dark. it is one of the longest lava tube in the world but it just is not my cup of tea. No  remorse on going into it but just was not awe blown away with it either. Go if you are a nature lover. skip if you are looking for awesome scenery to capture picture moments

Little walk down pathway along the cliff on the seaside.Something to see while in the area.May be difficult for elderly or those with weak walking abilities as walk to the waterfall from parking lot consist of lots of stairs and wet floors.

KRW 2k for adults. Worth the 2km to and fro walk and all information panels in the cave have english. Not suitable for very old and very young. A lot of un even steps and walkways and high steps sometimes. Dark. Wear good tracking shoes.

It's one street away from the seafood street and walking distance to the shopping street too. Quite a number of korean bbq & restaurant. We went in to one that's filled with locals and it turned out to be a wise choice.
It's a Lava cave about 1 km. The walkway was very hard to walk because it's a lava rock. And it's wet because of the rain. It's OK. I didn't feel woww. If you have a free time you can go there.
It's a great experience and see the way. It's not really that difficult to walk inside and it's spacious.
It;s a historical village where we can find the heritage of old Jeju's culture from the past. We're walking around to see closely the way jeju's origin people.

It was very crowded at O'Sulloc and a tad chaotic. As there were no seats and the queue for their desserts was very long we went to Innisfree which was a 2-minute walk away. It's a beautiful place. Parking was easy. If the main parking area is full there is a big open space across the road to park at. There were persons helping to redirect cars so it was not stressful at all.

It was pretty cold even in May at the beach due to the strong winds. No one was there to swim but still it's a beautiful place to snap pictures and nice cafes surrounding the beach to simply chill and relaxI do not if I was there too early b4 the cleaners or .. Anyway the beach line was littered with trash and full of seaweeds making the walk on the shoreline kinda displeasing.

It was a 2km walk (1km each way) and it is not easy to walk in low light and on uneven ground. Suggest to make bring your own led light especially if with old folks. It was interesting to see how this cave was formed by lava.
It looks nice when u stay far away to take photos! U need to buy tickets to get in and then keep walking! So I chose not to get in and just take a few photos outside

It is soooo dark in the cave. You couldn?t see the formations or well anything except the puddles of water. I have been to other caves before and they had dramatic lighting that shows off the details. We walked about half way and turned back as it was the same thing the whole way through. It does get a little chilly down there. It was our least favorite thing we did on Jeju.

Irion (magma) carved the small valley. This is the place where the magma carved the valley long long ago. The small valley meet the sea here. You can enjoy transparent canoe and see under water(not always).  Scenery is exotic.  It is also good for you to walk along here.

If you visit the waterfalls do not expect that the water is floating like crazy. They're  freeze!! But you could still find the great one on the second waterfall or the third one which will make you walk some meters away. but it was lovely seeing the nature in other country. This waterfalls is very clean!! and people respect the area. Salut for Jeju Island!!!

If you go for brands (local and international) this short street is probably the place to go to on this part of the island. The street is closed to traffic so you could spend a while walking in comfort. The street is on the way to dongmun market and the underground shopping centre. Along the way it also branches off into some kind of roofed shopping arcade which we did not visit.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

If anyways in Jeju you will most likely walk this street. It's rather boring. Has quite some restaurants which all seem to be mediocre (can't say for certain as we only tried one of them - which definitely was not a highlight of our trip) Head on to he southern part of the island to truly enjoy this beautiful island.

I wouldn't go out of my way to see it but it is fun walking through the place. There are still some shops and a small waterpark/spa that only opens fully in the summer. Very quiet almost ghost town type of feel. Go karts are near by to if your into that

I loved this cave! 2 km in and out. It was a very educational trip as you'll get explanations about what you see along the way. It's dark and wet and there's water dripping from the ceiling so bring a cap and good boots to avoid slipping. Don't wear a long skirt as it will get wet. A bit hard to take pictures though because of the lighting :/ But the ending and the way it was presented with the lighted walkway at the end was great!

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

Hydrangea season so that friends chose this rainy season reach jeju. that was not good travel season as too hot & rainy always. but Camellia hill getting quite many flowers & not too crowded as jeju has many place to have this flower show. the garden big enough & well organize. good for taking picture & walk around if you love flowers

Had a high expectation about this place since it always comes up on your google search when it comes to Jeju Island. It's just like a big cave and that's it. It's beautiful? Yes. Is it amazing? Not really. You can walk inside the cave and not seeing that much (just a stone of course)

Good chance to explore natureof lava tube..I shall recommend for walk alley to be build along the way inside the tube..its to hard to walk on the slippery rocks.Hence to put more highlight inside the tube..its too dark inside
First time seeing Koreans surfing was at this very beach. Very clean and serene beach. Buffet restaurant in the area too and nice walkway around the coast.

Down steep stairs and into the lava tubes.You can go in a long way or a little way.I enjoyed this unusual experience.I did not like the fact that it was wet and surface uneven so difficult even with good walking shoes.

Didn't have much time so decided to watch the woman diver show first at the shores of seongsan ilchulbong (otherwise known as Sunrise peak). Shows are 130pm and 3pm. Quite interesting but they didn't seem to collect many sea creatures during the show. So the diving is mainly drive for tourists' sake. Can also buy fresh sea food from the women divers and get the restaurant right there to cook it. Walked up half way after that to grab some photo shots.

Could have spent half a day here. Gardens were beautiful. The lava caves were nice to walk through to break up the heat! Interesting animals throughout.  Ran out of time and missed seeing the water gardens.  Great way to spend a day outside. Especially enjoyed the bonsai garden.

Came here looking for lunch. If u r not a fan of sashimi  stay away then. The market primarily sold fresh seafood for the purpose of making sashimi. Easy walking with lots of vendors selling a variety of food - primarily seafood. There was one stall that sold braised pork trotters and very popular. Do watch out for the myriad of vehicles though. The walking paths and the roads does seem too integrated  sometimes forgetting that u were walking on the road already.
Breathtaking waterfalls with crystal clear blue water.  The walk to the waterfalls takes you through a pathway surrounded by trees and shrubs.

Black sand beach with lots of rocks.  Didn't see much wildlife but there were tons of people there.  The water from the river is clear blue and gorgeous but cold.  There is a place where you can canoe up the river for a bit.  Side note the parking is awful.  Be prepared to park a bit away and then walk.

Black Pork Street was recommended to us by our Hotel when I asked about where is the best place to eat the famous Black Pork on the Island. We were quite disappointed as we walked down the street there were hustlers from each of the restaurants approaching you trying to sell you on their restaurant which we found odd. Almost every restaurant required you to buy two orders of Black Pork and my Wife had her heart set on kimchee stew. 3/4 of the way down the street we found a restaurant that didnt require two servings so we ate there. I excitedly took pictures of the pork to find out later that it it wasnt black pork. My advice is find a local and ask where they take their family to have Black Pork and you will truely be able to enjoy their Island delicacy.

Banglimwon is a large exhibition of plants. All the descriptions and signs are written in Korean maybe taking a pleisure walk was a good idea to us. We don’t think the tour guide want either being able to translate some thousands of plant names into Eng lish anyway. However this place is beautiful and worth to visit.

As an American when I think beach I think sand water sand castles a boardwalk and a place to grab a drink. This beach has the sand and water but that is absolutely it. Sand water then a huge hill. You have to have a car to get here. There is a parking lot a 1/4 to 1/2 mile away. At the lot there is some minor touristy things. Think about 5 minutes of time to see it all. You then walk down a steep road and are at the beach. The pros: one of the few spots on the south side with sand and not just boulders. There are bathrooms and a place to wash off. The cons: it's a beach and nothing else. Since our hotel is about 4 miles up the coast and right on the beach that is solid rock we will drive here for the kids. But this is certainly not a reason to come here.

As a resident of Jeju  I enjoy walking through this park every week. It is a great and safe place to take kids or walk dogs. There are two parts to the park: north of the road and south of the road. In the southern part  there are interesting ponds and pathways.I would not recommend this place to tourists only because there is so much else to see in Jeju Island that is far more impressive than this park. However  it is only a five minute walk from the city Center (Jungang Rotary) to the northern part so it is not far at all.

After visiting the lava tubes we got to try out the maze park.  A fun way to spend a half hour and the site of many k-dramas and korean commercials.  Romantic for a date and fun if you have kids.  We even got to ring the bell at the end!A fun excursion if you're walking to the lava tubes it's on the same road.

Across the street from the museum is a green tea patch where people can take touristy pictures and just walk around. The day I was there it was way too hot to even attempt to take photos. Inside the building isn't really a museum but a tea shop that has a lot of variations of teas. There's also a little cafe that serves hot and cold tea drinks along with simple snacks to have with you tea. Out back there is a walkway for people so that they can see the open landscape. There is also a Innisfree Jeju Island shop that has make-up and it was interesting to see some of the main ingredients in their skincare line out on display. The Innisfree shop also had it's own separate cafe with beverages and food.

According t the map the falls were 400m from my hotel - so tried to walk.  Reched the park above the falls easily but could not find a path down.  Turns out only way to access to to go 1km downstream and walk down to the car park and in the official entrance. From entrance it is a 500m walk back upstream to the falls. many people all queuing to take photos.On the way out saw a musical performance near the entrance.

A walk through this cave took us back to the times with the images of the lava cave and dry rocks just like in the dinosaur films. The cave is kept just the same as it always is so the paths are rough and make it more adventurous.

A beautiful scenic walk along the coast and the path was well taken care of. We walked to the right first and walked most of the path up until it started to inclined towards the end and then turned around and walked down the left path all the way to the parking lot. Definitely recommend walking both paths since you see different rock formations and the walk is not too difficult or long.

yongduam rock is near to the airport. You can visit here the day before you depart from Jeju island. It has beautiful walk alone the sea. The place is good for seeing the ocean from the peak. There is a dead rock here. Those who like to take pictures of the plane can take pictures of the plane which is on the way to airport. This place is one of the icons of Jeju city. So, must see it.

With total of 2km walk in the tunnel (2 ways), you will be able to see different types of volcanic stones with good explanation notes in multiple languages. Not suitable for old people as it is dark and the walkpath is not even (all natural). Spend 1 hour.

While this is  just of the roadway, it?s fairly free of visitors.   The path goes alongside running water (or not - depending on rainfall).    There was about a 30m section where the path ended and we had to walk from rock to rock before the path restarted.    On the other side was a cave - Rock Shade Residence - which olden people used as shelter.   Entire area is a beautiful evergreen valley, well worth a visit.

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) ! After you flood yrselves silly with pics, you can try the maze. Its interesting walking in and out and along the way you can look out for cats that are just chillin by the greenery. Overall a good experience especially for families !

When my group and I first went to this market I assumed it would be small like a on the side of the road market where they sell fruits, veggies, and jams. This market was that times ten and the market even had the kitchen sink. When we first walked through they had fresh picked flowers, potted plants, fresh spices, 15 different types of kimchi. As we walked around it wasnt just food and plants they had housewares to clothes even puppies, rabbits and chickens. then we realized that they even had a fish market. This market of cousre smelled of fish we consumers selling squid, shrimp, and tilapia. This market is such a good way to imerse oneself into a the korean culture on the island. This was one of the places on my wish list to see while my group and I were in Korea and it was much more than I expected and I am so glad I went.

what made this place interesting besides the dragon head was the locals selling their wares.  We also bought our first hallabong here.  I can tell you prices are pretty much the same all over for those hallabongs.  If you walk down there are a lot of ajjumas selling I think sea food, I did not walk all the way down since I did not have the right foot wear but it seemed like fresh sea food.It is a very touristy place, we just took a look few pictures and left.  Its one of those places we dont have to go see again once you seen it thats good enough.  But were are glad we did see it.  Again I would have walked down to the ocean side but opted not to might have been interesting, so make sure you have the right footwear, it is rocky and maybe a little wet.

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

Went there in the morning via taxi. Not many people. Admission: 2000 won each.There are flights of stairs to climb down when you first reach, so imagine the climb back up once you are done. To get nearer to the waterfall, you have walk over many many many rocks. Not recommended to go after rain as it will be super slippery. However, I love this waterfall more than Cheongjiyeon waterfall. It is nicer actually and you can get closer to the waterfall (of coz getting passed the obstacles of rocks).Love it actually but no way near magnificent.

Went there after visiting the Manjanggul caves, fairly close by. Not necessarily a tourist attraction, but if you're looking to spend an hour or two in a nice forest away from all the coach visitors, this is a great spot. All we saw were Koreans out for a Sunday walk. There is a circuit path through the forest, all level, well maintained, took us maybe an hour to complete. Totally relaxing and peaceful.

Went here with a tour package bought from Klook. Entering caves experience feels great however, for it requires like 30 minutes walk to the Lava Coloum and you have to walk back (there is no other way out) so you need to make sure to wear comfortable shoes because the floor is uneven.

We were a little disappointed after walking all the way down the hill at Sunrise Peak to see the women divers, only to find out that because of the holiday, they wouldn't be diving today.So as a consolation, our tour guide took us to the Haenyeo Museum.  This museum was dedicated to the Haenyeo women divers of Jeju and Japan.  It's a very nice museum with excellent displays, and you will learn a lot about the divers.I recommend seeing the video show before you start wandering around.

We went to this cave as friends want to visit even it was not on my bucket list. It was impressive to see volcanic layers and massive path inside. We walked down all way to the end i.e. 1 km away and walk back again. Personally, I don't find it interesting.

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went there because closest hotel, we driving to there and saw that is not to much visitor maybe was late evening, we try to going up, however in the middle of the path have 1 counter ask us to buy a ticket, we only want to walk around so we haven't paid and plan to leave, but we saw some of people can go up on the other way, actually is the same road but one for entrance and one for exit, you can go inside in the exit way but only have limited area you can visit. if you want to go up, you must need to paid

We walked over the bridge, it was very windy and we could feel the bridge moving a little which was quite scary but was really nice to get some air. The island was really peaceful and was a lovely walk around.
