Unfortunatly there was two children with their dad shouting all the way round, we could hear them from the other side of the island so we sat on a bench for a while to wait for them to leave. We went before sunset and saw the sun set, just be careful of mosquitoes at this time as we got bit loads while on the island.

We visited this place on a slightly gloomy day. This and the amazon green colours of the flora made it look like a mystic forest, something out of an animation. They say, walking among these nutmeg trees has healing properties, and eventhough I was sceptical at first, soon I could feel my nerves calming down. It felt like someone poured some sleeping powder on us. Oh and the smell! I've never felt such pungent yet clean fragrance in a forest before, it's truly unique. All those pretty colours and the distinctive smell of nutmeg and cinnamon trees makes this pathway a mesmerizing experience. The route takes at least 40 minutes-1 hour. There are some charming restaurants and coffee places before the entrance, and a huge parking lot. The whole are is beautiful.

We visited this area with kids ages 3-11. Easy paved walk through a beautiful scenic shaded walkway. The falls were breathtaking. We took our shoes off and soaked our feet at the end of stairs leading into the water. Ate an easy convenience store lunch when we returned to the parking lot before heading to our next destination of the day. 1,000won for kids, 2,000won for adults. Can?t beat the price.
We saw birds, ostrich, peacocks and various bonsai trees. You need at least 2 to 3 hrs to enjoy the place. There is also a cave with paved walkways.

We rent a bicycle and just cycling along the sea coast. It's very windy and we even spotted the hanyeo picking up the seaweed! If you visit the island at the right timing. U can see lots of canola flower! We saw partial here and there still very pretty. If you are being lazy, you can just rent the ATV bike (which most of the people do so). If you plan to have lunch there. Give yourself 4-5 hours to explore this island (take photo, had an ice cream etc etc). Note: we didn't walk all the way up to light house as it is already mid noon and we can see something similar @ seopjikoji so we let go this one :)

We originally did not schedule this visit as we have already seen Mulu Caves in Sarawak-East Malaysia.  But our hotel (TGG) told us that this is a very different cave (lava tubes).   The cost is not high at KRW2,000 and if you are already going to Seongsan Ilchbong, might as well make a visit.  We did not regret the visit.  It is really interesting to see how the lava flowing from Mt. Halla makes its way underground and forming the cave.  It is huge so you can see the magnitude of the lava flow.  Be sure to wear sturdy shoes as the ground is rather rocky and wet and you will need to walk carefully so that you won't fall.  I am amazed on how some ladies worn high heels!  It is also dim and cool so you must bring a jacket with you.  It is also a UNESCO site so definitely worth visiting.

We heard about the dragon head rock and we were brought there by our tour guide. Our guide warned us to use   a lot of imagination   when we see the rock otherwise we will not be able to see the   dragon  . Well she was right about that. Lots of tour agencies bring their groups there to see the rock and there are lots of little restaurants all the way along the walkway to entice the tourists. After a short walk from the carpark, there is a steep staircase you have to walk down to, in order to get to the spot to see the dragon head from the side. Even so, you're pretty far from the dragon head rock. And to me, it's clearly just a natural process where the rock gets eroded into a certain shape and in this case it's going there for this one rock only... which I wouldn't have if I were on a free and easy route.

We have never seen or heard of anything like this before. Probably its the only one in the world. The 1km walk each way, was full of facts about lava formations.We had wonderful time, and just loved what we saw & learned.

We had the best time at the 3D Alive Museum.  As you walk through there are pictures on the walls and floors that you pose in certain ways to make it appear the picture is   alive  .  You can be sky diving riding on a magic carpet in King Kongs grip etc.  We edited our pictures once home and they are wonderful!  Highly recommend this museum!!

We followed Trip Advisor's map and was brought to a small hotel garden area. We were iniatially confused but the hotel staff pointed the way to us. It wasn't very far already. We took our time walking, and to tell you the truth, I was glad we came the way we came. We found a way down to the rocky beach and climbed a little right to where the waves break. At that point the rocks aren't geometrical, just normal. Afters we walked thru a garden, which was a good distraction, and finally arrived at the cliffs. To my disappointment we can't actually go down to the rocks. And then there were a few shops selling fresh seafood, postcards, ice cream, mandarin oranges and to my surprise, some hallabong oranges. I got it pretty cheap too, compared to other places that I went after that

We drove up to this attraction easily via an English GPS. No prams or strollers are allowed in there because it's mostly stairways and lots of rocks. You'll need to navigate across some amount of rocks to take a nice picture with the waterfall. There're a couple of old ladies selling seafood with a small fire burning nearby - we didnt buy anything coz they don't speak English. Not a huge waterfall, but the kids love it (not of the waterfall, but the rock walking experience) - if you're not careful, you can easily sprain an ankle or even break some bones.

We drove there and parking is free. The whole experience will take about less than 2hours? About 45mins to walk all the way inside to the end of the cave and another 45mins out. So remember to empty your bladder before entering. There is no loo inside the cave.The cave is cold. About 15 degree celcius? Luckily there is no wind. The ground is made up of rocky bits, and the place is constantly damped and slippery. So wear a light jacket and confortable shoes.Although there are lights in the cave, they are pretty dimmed. Not brightly lit. We used the torchlight function in our phones to further assist us to see the rocky ground. It is not unusual to carry a small portable torchlight if you want. Im not a person who likes cave, but well.. it is an experience i guess.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

We book a tour on line from the cruise ship before we arrived at the port. The tour included a visit to Seongeup Folk Village.  There was an admission fee to the village.  There are several walkways around the village. The walkways are well maintained and there are no steps to climb.  There are exhibits our old building, farming and animals.  There are clean restrooms along the walkways.
was there in March, temp in the cave is alot colder than outside. not much to see as the walkway is poorly light.

Walking the Dongmun Market is an experience that a visitor should not miss.  The local market has variety of daily food of the islanders.  Seeing the fresh fishes, seafoods, and other meats displayed in various forms for consumption was an eye opener.  We would love to buy and try some of the food if the merchant package them in ready-to-eat size.  On this entrepreneurs way, the Japanese market achieve high mark in its idea.  Visitors would love to try local food even to pay at a premium.

Very pretty beach on a sunny day. The colour of the water is so beautiful. Nicely prep walkway all along the whole beach area. Lots of places for coffee and a quick lunch. We had dinner at a local eatery, the owner was nice and friendly.  He helped BBQ our black skin pork belly for us. So yummy with water Kimchi and beer.

Three interconnected mazes come with a map to make sure you won't get lost, other sights nearby including a lovely and scenic walk under beautiful trees. On my way through one of the mazes the sprinklers above came on and then you're walking through mist. A very straightforward sight that is an interesting experience.

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This was a nice little excursion from the main island. Gotta take a ferry which means you need to head over to Udo early and be prepared to come back in the early evening as the ferry schedule will dictate your movement. There used to be a nice coffee shop halfway up at the base of the stairs to the lighthouse exhibits (October 2013). They had the cutest dog too but they were closed when we went back in December 2013. We took our car on the ferry. But you can also walk onto the ferry and then rent mopeds or four wheelers once you get to Udo so you can get around. I was thankful for the GPS in the car though because the roads are very winding, narrow, confusing, and I don't think are marked with names.

This place is interesting only in concept - because it's one of the longest lava tunnels in the world.  But in reality, you climb down a hole and then walk for about a kilometer in what looks like a dirt tunnel made for a subway train with virtually northing to look at.  Then you arrive at a lava column which is far from impressive.  There are numerous amazing caves in the world such as the ones in Ha Long bay.  We are very unimpressed.

This place is AMAZING. I can't describe with words how incredible it was so I will upload pictures too. I visited this place during the Jeju Olle Walking Festival and it was my favorite place. I highly recommend to visit this place. If you can, do Route 10 of the Jeju Olle Walking and you would come across this place. Also, in that place you can found ladies who are fishing and preparing dishes right away. You can try raw fish from Jeju right there. We tried and it was delicious!

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This maze is fun and quite simple. And from what I've observed, it really tests a couple's relationship strength. ALong the way I see couples arguing on which way to go, I see couples helping each other out. It was a fun experience. Walk there from Manjanggul to get a 500won discount!

This is something different: a 2 km or so walk through an underground lava tube where molten lava has flowed several times over the centuries. A unique experience. Be prepared for a bit of a trek over uneven, rough ground, dodging puddles. It can be drippy and it's always cold so take a jacket. But it's good fun and just out of this world.

this is one of those strange Jeju adventures that's worth a quick check.  yes, just like they describe, it's a road which, when you walk down it, it feels like you're going up - and vice versus.  be careful, so you don't get hit by a car - but on your way to something else to do in Jeju, give it a go.  BTW, I  m sure kids won't get it - this is an adult thing, and I don't think I'd want my toddler walking down an active road.

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is an easy walk from the centre of Jeju city. It'a one of the main attractions along the seafront walkway which goes all the way from the port to the airport. You often see the famous Jeju ladies, dressed in their black wetsuits, diving for pearls without breathing equipment.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a neat little place to enjoy the ocean breeze and see a rocky area.You don't need much time here; about 15 minutes is adequate. Wear comfortable shoes as the surface is uneven. I'm sure you will enjoy he scenery here... You can combine it with a walk along the coast into town.  I stumbled across a nice bridge and gazebo area along the way, as I headed towards the downtown market.

This is a fun and interactive show that would be great for families with members of all ages.The VIP seats are more expensive, but you have the chance of being picked to participate in segments of the show. If this is not important to you, choose the regular seats as the theater is not very large anyway. You can get a 5,000 won discount if you reserve tickets through YEHA Tours. Then pick up the tickets on the day of the show.Instead of an intermission in the middle, a cast member does some interactive clapping and stomping with the audience.The City Hall downtown area is a 15-minute walk away from the theater. You can find restaurants and shops there.

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

This high peak volcano is worth going for climbing... We went with my friend early march, the path was still snowyall the way!  Better to bring some equipement although it is possible to rent shoes at the convenient store down there.We were in march in a very low touristic season so it was quite nice to hike under the frozen pine trees with a beautiful blue sky. I think in high season on weekend, it could be crowdy! As it is a volcano, the walk is really sportive, meaning 6-10% continously during 2h. Get the first plane area, bring some candy bar or fruit, water of course, you will be enjoy this break on the roof of south Korea :=)

This Hallasan Fried Rice is a must have, must Go, must try, if you are in Udo Island. It is available at the 'Pungwon' restaurant. It is about 20mins walking from the harbour. If you are driving, key in the Tel no. 7841894 in your GPS device.First you will have to order either Black pork or cuttlefish according to your preference. There is a minimum number of portions to order based on the number of pax. There were 4 of us and we order 2 Pork and 1 Cuttlefish. We will begin by BBQ the meat. Until we are about halfway through, you can order the rice from the staff. The staff will put aside some meat and start by cooking the rice. The whole idea of Hallasan Fried Rice is that the staff will tell you the story about Mount Hallasan and the islands nearby; all these while making the rice into the shape of a mountain. He will then pour in the egg mixture and meat and cheese... and after numerous of flipping the rice, it's done. Fret not if you don't understand Korean, they have Chinese staff who can do the story telling in Mandarin. The process of hearing about the story is very interesting coupled with the visual of the staff cooking the rice. Not to mention, it tastes damn good too!

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

There were many tour groups at the place and many people were walking on the road. Anyway, there was nothing exciting about the place. It is just a short (around 50 metres) stretch of road and things roll upslope instead of downslope. Give this a miss if you have not enough time.

There is walk along the  nice promenade to get to this rock. It is hard to make out the dragon in the rock but Asians love strangely shaped rocks. In my opinion it was not so spectacular but the walk along the promenade is very nice, over nice bridge and coffee shops along the way.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The waterfall is not too far from the entrance. Just take a short walk around 5-8 minutes and then you will find the waterfall. For young children, must assist by adults, because on the way to waterfall there are many big rock. The wind is so strong. The waterfall is special because it's located near beach.

The visit to the lava tube is interesting, but the way leading there is not good, and might definitely be dangerous under certain weather circunstances. Lightning is precarious and there are only few explanatory boards. definitely not adequate for people with walking restrictions of any kind

The temperature drops dramatically after you descend 15 stairs into the cave entrance.  There was a cloud that had formed at the entrance due to the humidity which was really cool to see.  Walked about a km to the end where there is a lava column - a frozen in time dripping of lava from above.  Fascinating walk, lots of people (some in heels which I wouldn't recommend).  Really beautiful way to spend an hour or so.  Especially when it is super hot and humid outdoors!

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

The place is very organised with well created pathways to see the rock formations. However, the place is really quite crowded and it is hard to take photos because of the amount of crowd there. Everyone was just walking along the path and there isn't much space to move around. That being said, it is still quite worth it to pay it a visit.

The place is usually crowded.  Make sure to wear good walking shoes to walk and climb, some drinking water to quench thirst along the way. Not suitable for elderly and people who are not keen in climbing. Otherwise, is worth to visit - it is a Unesco World Heritage site after all.  If you are not there to catch sunrise, any season is fine.

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.

The market is full of local appeal with fresh fruits, vegetables, and local snacks to seafood and various sundries. A great way to spend a few hours walking around, doing some souvenir shopping, and eating local treats. The market is full of warm and friendly people who are interested and appreciative of the tourist that venture to visit the attraction. I would recommend to any one who appreciates the local things about traveling.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The Manjang Cave was one of the   must-dos   in my itinerary. I can only say it was somewhat a disappointment. It was not quite as spectacular as I have thought it would be. I was with my mum and dad both 60. My mum did not take the walk well and headed back halfway. My dad stayed behind to do some photo-taking, Here's the bottomline:- If you have never ever been in a lava cave before - go for it!- If you are traveling with young children / older folks / people with bad knees and weak ankles - give this a miss. The initial flight of stairs can be quite a walk. The floor of the cave can be wet and uneven- If you have been to lava caves before and if you do not have a mental benchmark - go for it if you have time- If you have seen the most wondrous lava caves and already formed expectations - skip it... more than likely this might underperform

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The lava cave which need you to walk about one km in and walk back the same distance. You can walk with/ without a torchlight as there are lights in the cave as well, wear jacket as it's quite cooling in the cave. Better wear sport shoes since walkway is wet and slippery and uneven too. Overall its a nice attraction to visit :)

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The building looks a bit old. There re space for parking. Inside the castle, there's hello kitty tree at the middle for photo shooting. When you walk inside, there're few theme of hello kitty for photo shooting and walk up the stair to the 2nd floor you will see a few rooms theme of hello kitty including the kitty cafe which sell drinks,Desserts and cakes. The restroom also there. The price is not high. The restaurant decorated in cute seating with hello kitty design. On the way back on ground floor you need to pass the souvenir shop. The price is not cheap for stuffs but if you are hello kitty fan it may worth.

The bridge is beautiful to look at, and provides a nice walk to an island that provides more opportunity to stroll near the water.? Big tourist attraction, and if you prefer staying away from the crowds, you may not enjoy this.? Great picture taking venue, and it doesn't cost anything, except a little workout for your feet and legs.
The bears are adorable! It is also a 10 min walk from the cheonjeyeon waterfalls, alive museum and 3100w away from the cliffs!
Take the afternoon and walk around this beautiful park and zoo. All different kind of plants, trees, flowers, and animals, this park is way better than it seems. Don't miss it!

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Spent about 3 hours here one afternoon and was very happy with the overall visit. A full display of buildings, traditional way of life, farm areas, gardens and other typical tourist information, shops and food areas give the whole village a unique attraction for everyone. A little pricey in the shops, but as you walk through the areas you get a real sense of tranquility with the how things were. Very enjoyable and if you are there - make sure you visit.

Spend a couple hours here walking through the village and seeing traditional Korean way of life.  There isn?t much interaction with anything outside of the performance they have, which is 2-3 times a day and with the vendors.  They do offer horse back riding here and you can also have photos taken in a hanbok.
Spectacular waterfall! Definitely worth a visit. If you are staying in Tae Gong Gak Guesthouse, the waterfall is just a 10-15 minute walk away :)

Sangumburi crater is a designated Natural Monument touted as the world's only flatland crater. The car park entrance showcases several large rocks from the crater such as the volcanic bomb and lava tree mold. During the eruption, molten rock flew from the volcano into the air and cooled into many exotic shapes. The area near the crater also contain several traditional Jeju graves - wide, trapezoidal stone walls surrounding the burial mounds. Visitors can walk around the extinct volcano crater rim, peer into it but cannot venture inside the crater pit covered with lush vegetation. The hills and Hallasan surrounding the crater is a picture of serenity and rustic greenery. Sangumburi is especially popular in autumn when the slopes are covered in Jeju?s famous Eulalia. Crowds and couples will be lining up for photos among the tall plume-like, silver grass swaying in the breeze. At a quiet spot, listen to the whispers of the eulalia dancing against the blue sky to add a pensive mood to the autumn romance.  Note: KRW6000 entry fee is quite expensive. Closes at 6 pm, except Nov-Feb closing at 5 pm.

Rushed to watch the sunrise. Starts around 5am and everybody walk as fast as they can but once reach the stairway, mostly starts to b exhausted. Took some rest by snapping some pictures. Suddenly reached at 530am and already some crowd booked their best location for taking the sunrise. Anyway its a must do activity once you are in jeju island.

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street ? you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

Perhaps I've been in Asia too long, but I feel like a lot of these markets start to look, feel and smell the same. It was fun to walk through but I didn't feel like it had a whole lot to offer that felt special. If you're new to Asia, certainly worth a walk though I wouldn't go out of my way to come here.

Our family visited   Cheonjiyeon Falls   on June 8th, 2019. To get to the waterfall, you have to walk a lot. There were a lot of small markets that sold simple snacks, which was sweet, but the way to the waterfall was not worth it. Although the way to the waterfall was harsh, still the waterfall was beautiful. I recommend this waterfall to whom that likes walking. If your stamina is poor, you will be tired . I don't think the waterfall was worth walking a lot.

Our family really enjoyed this walk.? It was nice to see the lighthouse and islands around this area.? And when we were there, the brushes were full of beautiful spiders and webs.? Of course, they were far enough away to not bother you.? It was really cool to see.

Our children really wanted to spend time on the ocean. This was a great introduction to the power of the sea. Big waves. Rocky coast. Perfect for sea shell collecting, sand castle building, and glimpses of aquatic life. We managed to watch the Haenyo divers bobbing their way across Jungmun Beach and later walked the length of the beach to see their catch.

One of our favorite places! We practically ate at every stall! Best place to bargain for souvenirs plus a underground mall is just steps away....Nice place to walk around, food trip and people watch...

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Not suitable for old folks, because is full with rocks.. Better prepare a torch light or you handphone torch light. Inside very dark. The lights not that bright enough. Prevent any injury. Walking distance to the end about 1km, one way. Winter season, very fresh air inside the cave.

Not spectacular but unusual that it flows into the sea. You can walk across the rocks to get really close and many did for pictures. Be careful though. Some women selling freshly cut abalone, sea cucumber, snails - raw! Just 200m away from the base of the fall. Ticket is affordable at 2000 won even for foreigner which is the good part about most of the sights unlike some countries which cost double or more for foreigners.Don't see any restaurant so drive into the city seogwipo food street for plenty of choices.

No point come to this fall, not even if you are nearby. Not worth your time. I walked all the way in just to find out that The waterfall is so small. I don?t see how they made an attraction out of this.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.

My own experience was during dark, and I loved it. There was a spotlight highlighting the rock. Relax listening to the waves coming from the sea to the shore. On the way here I recommend walking through Yongyeon bridge.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

Massive ground. A full walk about will take 2hrs easily. Even though all the stones look similar after an hr, it's a very effective way to understand the folklores of Jeju. Cheap entrance fee of only 2K won.Some places near the museum are still under renovation when we were there.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and it is a designated as a natural monument.Not an easy walk as lots of even walkway,  slippery and dark. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surrounding and was cooling as you walk. You will be able to see the trace of the lava that flow through the cave. I saw some who rush all their way in and out.With young children do note of their safety, for older people who having legs problem do not try. Partly, you need to walk down the stairs which is not easy and when you finished you need to walk up again.We really enjoyed the nature of this cave.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Located an easy walk from the Seogwipo Harbor, these waterfalls and surrounding area are quite pretty, and certainly worth the easy, pleasant walk to see them. It was only 2,000 won to enter the are, and about a 5 minute walk to the actural waterfall. As someone who loves swimming in natural water, I was a little disappointed, because you can't really swim here. It was quite crowded (when I went in early August), so all my photos are full of other people. It wasn't necessarily a beautiful nature experience, so in that way a bit underwhelming, but again, worth a look.

Just makes you wonder nature creativity. Need to have camera able to take photo in low light.Note: Long walk, water dripping, uneven and dark pathway. However don't loose hope, beautiful @ end of tunnel. Worth the efforts.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

It's very near to Jeju city, within walking distance. It's nice walk strolling along the seaside to dragon head rock and even walk further from there. However this place is always full of tourist, and not easy to get a good picture of this attraction. Nevertheless the environment and surrounding is beautiful and relaxing and I was here during sunset and foggy evening, absolutely beautiful.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

It's good place for experience the local community which they will arrange the local guide whom live tin the village to give you the informations and details about the village including the history and culture. There's the translator for the local people since they are hardly speak other language besides Korean. They will explain the way they hand the wooden stick at the gate. The meaning of the stone statue. They will have to room the tell us their history and story. They will have a village walk so everyone can see and experiences their village including photo shooting. They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. The Omecha is sticky so need to mix with water for drinking and contain a lot of vitamins. The local guide will try to up sales their local products after tour such as Omecha and horse bone. They make the bone into small pills and they said its good for those whom need calcium or need recovery from injury and also good for the growth of young kid. They also sell dried squids which already mix with sauce before dried it. It's a good experience as the village is very unique. The house is only one floor and low ceiling since Jeju is very windy. The wall also made with the lava stone from the hallasan mountain.Avoid to go during rainy day even they provide the umbrella during the walk but it's not convenience at all.

It's deep and long and wet and cold but pretty amazing.  It's lit with pathways and only 1 way in and out.  It's about 1km long and you double back the same way you came.  It's pretty easy to access, saw a lot of seniors and children, there's about 20-40 stairs I guess to get you down. Not too many opportunities where you can walk actual lava tube.  Give it about 1 hour to do.

It's a new experience to us. It's great. Just walk inside the maze until you find the way. Maybe try and get help from your friends who have reached the tower. It's a great activity. Got some traditional games to play as well. There are lots of big fat cats at the ticketing counter. So cute, so fluffy.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It was very nice taking a walk along the beach of Udo, the sea is clean but unable to swim because of sharp rocks. We are happy that they keep this place just the same as it is, not making it into a tourism spot. And once again,  most of them cannot speak English, we couldn?t say any word to the locals and the tour guide was helpful all the way through.

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

It was really hot when we arrived so we did not go up the summit but explored the surrounding. You could walk to the left where you will come to several flights of steps leading down to the beach where the haenyeo or women free divers will perform their skills. If you do not fancy walking all the way down, just continue left as you will come to a cliff overseeing the Udo island. Another go to place in jeju. Understand that this island is form from volcanic eruptions much like jeju is as well. There are also lots of photo opportunities at the foot of the 180m+ mountain(?). Of course the usual F&B outlets are here as well. We also see some signage for horse riding but did not explore.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.
It was freezing in the tube! There were puddles of water everywhere so be careful when walking. The stones were interesting and do walk all the way in. You've already paid,so why not?

It was early afternoon & very sunny, & super hot during our visit. Coupled with the long walk & return climb up from the bottom, it was terrible in the heat.Perhaps if we had come in early morning or in spring climate, would probably have enjoyed it better.The Jeju Women Divers Performance was a disappointment. With due respect to this fantastic women, the show was too commercialised.Have read much about these tenacious women & was looking forward to something better than this.However, our guide arranged for us earlier to meet up with these women not far away in another area.Most are in their 70s & had been doing this job almost their whole lives. They are so fit even at this age.Certainly respect them.There are paid boat rides as well round the area & horse riding too.

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was a rainy morning that my friend and I visited this cave. We were greeted with a flight of stairs entering the cave. The temperature in the cave was so much lower, approximately 10 degrees celsius. It was dark and slippery too. The further we walked in, the colder it gets. The pathways are actual lava that hardened over the years therefore, it was not a smooth walk. A lot of locals enjoyed their walk, some strolling while youngsters brisk walk, talking and laughing along the way, making the whole cave not too scary. It was a nice morning walk looking through the structure left behind by the once active volcano forming rocks, mini wells naturally. The work of nature. Beautiful!

It was 15-min walking from our hotel, and admission was 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenages (up to age 24). You purchase at ticket box, but don't throw or put tickets away, as they check for them close to the entrance.  It was an easy walk, not too many steps down to the sea level.  Nice waterfall, where you can get close to it should you choose! If low tide, there is a pebble/sand pit area revealed, where you can get to by carefully climbing over some rocks...but could be slippery...so weigh the risk carefully!  However, pictures taken from this angle - with the waterfall as the backdrop - was breathtaking!

It smells so good as soon as you get off the car and pass the entrance. After a short walk, you get to the Forest.  It is also easily accessible for baby strollers as they put some straw mats alone the forest so the whole family can enjoy a wonderful walk in the forest.  Not sure if wheelchairs can roll easily on those mats though but I saw quite some baby strollers.We took a detour after Sangumburi crater (about 20 min away), and spent about an hour in the forest but didn't complete it. Then in another 20-30 min, we arrived at a Five Day Market, which is about 10 min from the Haeyeo (Women Divers) museum.So this was how we planned our route to and from the forest.

It is a pretty waterfall, though not as majestic as I thought but the walk to the waterfall was not too difficult anyway. It is possible to do the 3 waterfalls in Seogwipo in one day - Cheonjeyeon, Cheonjiyeon and Jeongbang.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.

It falls into the sea,  very unusual. Wear walking shoes if you're going there as there are uneven rocks leading to the fall. Saw several kids slipped & fell down. Painful indeed.  After purchasing the entrance ticket,  there's a walkway that leads you to the fall.  But the last 100m or so is uneven rocks surface.  It's nice to walk nearer to the fall so you can feel the mist.  Refreshing.

Interesting rock formation open for imagination. Otherwise the area has not much other sights. There is no ticket required, so you can see the popularity is not great. Anyway, nice forested area is good for a quiet walk.
Interesting place, walk in a lave tube & learn about formation along the way. it was very interesting experience. P/S Please wear shoe.

In this cave, you're allowed to walk about one kilometer in the lava tube where you'll find a lot of variation in the formation and environment. It's a lot of space in one of the tubes (the other one was closed off during our visit). In the tube, there has been several different lava levels and different factors, creating unique patterns on the walls, floor and ceiling. It's recommended to bring something warm down the cave, since it's a bit chilly.Along the way, there is several signs about detail information (both in Korean and English) about the different shapes and things in the cave.

In general, Jeongbang Falls is a nice looking waterfall that plunges into the blue ocean. Entry fee is low too at 2000 krw. However, this place is way, way too crowded with tourists. Chances of you getting 'photo bombed' is 100%, unless you risk your safety by walking over the rocks to the point near the waterfall like most tourists did. Hence, it is not recommended for travellers with walking difficulties.

I'm not usually impressed by holes in the ground, but this lava tube was a blast.  It's always cold, damp and a enjoyably creepy no matter how sunny it is above ground, and you will love it!  Plenty of great rock formations to see and a sense of what goblins might call home, but the main attraction walking in this huge tunnel that once screamed with magma.

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

If you love nature and taking walks, you'd enjoy this place. The smell is nice and the trees are impressive, but walking around for an hour looking at hundreds of the same trees doesn't excite me. It was nice and an okay way to kill an hour, but if it's between this and doing something else, choose the ladder.

If you like cave, do not miss out.my partner pick this one as a highlight in Korea. It's very huge cave.only open 1/3 ish though, you can walk on actual lava stones all the way.* MUST bring jacket or something to warm you up and wear proper shoes. its quite cool inside and wet.

If you go in the summer, be sure to take some water with you.  It's a 10-15 minute walk to  the falls and there's not much shade on the return route or actually at the falls.  Everyone tries to get as close as they can, which is fine, but there are several places to take beautiful pictures up on the platform/courtyard in front of the falls.  There are also two smaller falls that you don't see much unless you cross the bridge about halfway between the falls and the parking lot.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites, this is not a place. If there were, we probably missed them. It?s a dark underground cave and very interesting to see the lava flows. You can see imprints of such flows on the actual ground you?re walking on. It?s a bit nippy, so if you are prone to being cold, may want to take a light sweater. There is no bathroom in the tunnel (which my son figured out trying to get out halfway in the tunnel/cave. He had to run back the way we came to find one.) It?s interesting. I just wished that there were more lights in the tunnels so one can appreciate it more. Uneven ground due to the lava flows, as expected. 2000W/$1.75 to get in, half for kids.If you've never been into one of these types of caves, you should.  If you have, maybe worth skipping.

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was not sure what to expect when we went to Hallim Park, but we really enjoyed it. It's a really nice walk, with flowers, statues waterfalls, caves and animals. It's nice to get away from the city noises if you have been on the mainland for a while. It's not a place you can spend an entire day, and for us was a bit of a trek to get there so make sure you plan your day to only be there a couple of hours.

I was hoping to see how magnificient the lava is in one of the widest lava tube before going into the Manjang Cave. It is quite disappointing to realise that the cave is not entirely illuminated. The lighting is minimal in the cave which made walking and lava observation really difficult. I was going with my mum of around 60 years old, it is really difficult for her to see clearly in the tunnel. And the fact that you have to walk for  ~1 km into the tunnel and then the same way back is not entiring pleasing. When I was walking down the tunnel, I always thought   there will be better illumination/rocks in the next turn  . However, it was quite disappointing that this happens only at the end of the tunnel where you saw an illuminated lava pillar. I would recommend you to go to other caves if you want to see the lava clearly.

I walked Routes 6 and 7 on 23rd-24th Oct 2017. The distance was 15km and 18km respectively.The weather was perfect - sunshine and cool breezes. These 2 routes are reputed to be the more beautiful ones. There are a couple of picture-perfect waterfalls and breath-taking shorelines along the way. 2,000Won per entry is charged for the waterfall. Along the way are small fishing ports where one can get to taste local seafood. There are small cafe along the way too, where one can sit, relax and taking in the beautiful scenery. Coffee is +/-4,000won. As I was staying at the starting point, from the finishing point I took taxi back It costs about 8kWon. Oh yes, there are clean restrooms every 5km or so. Just a little minus point, the blue & red ribbon is not easy to be found in urban area. So try looking for the blue line on the tar road.

I think we paid KRW2,000 per adult for entry. Walked the lava tube where the temperature dropped by a few degrees. It was raining that day, so it was a good hideout from the downpour. The walk was rather long but many things to see along the way. Remember to wear good waking shoes tho! It can get slippery.

I saw this on a map that the tourist center at the Airport provided. It was within walking distance from Ocean Palace Hotel and was very nice with walkways, parking, souviniers, food, stores, all for W2,000!

I like to explore super markets in different cities and different countries. It's a good way to see what people are eating. Sometime when I have the courage, I will tried some of the local food. Dongmun Market is one of the popular traditional markets in Jeju. It is big, clean and colourful. They sell all kinds of stuff, like fruit, fresh or dry (some in gift boxes), vegetables, dry mushrooms, herbs, spices and fresh or dry sea food. There are some restaurants ready to serve you. They even sell clothing there. We walked around and took photos, but no one came to pressure us to buy stuff, I like that.Happy Travelling!

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I heard from the owner of our guesthouse that this place isn?t always open because of the tides and weather, so if you have the chance to go, take it. It?s an amazing rock formation, but unlike the ones that you can see at a distance, like Oedolgae and the Jungmun Daepo, you can actually walk on it. That rocks. It took us a while ? was it an hour? ? to walk along the perimeter of this massive rock. The terrain is not smooth ? think of desert sands except that the undulating surface is made of rock instead of sand, so wear study shoes that won?t split because of the damp. It looks like a movie set -- for an alien planet. Really, I didn?t know such a place existed on earth.If I were taking someone around Jeju, I?d recommend this place and I would definitely come back so we can exclaim together.Where: Seogwipo west coast

I checked out Samseonghyeol not even knowing what it was exactly but went anyway because it was close to my hotel and it was some sort of a cultural sight.  Upon entering I learned it was basically three unimpressive holes where three demi-gods supposedly emerged from.  While the main sight isn?t impressive, it was still a nice park to walk around in during spring with the cherry blossoms.  It?s definitely not a sight worth going out of your way to see unless you?re interested in Korean legends.
