I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

I always wanted to visit the Devils Postpile National Monument in California. It is a surprise to find Columnar basalt on the seashore of Jeju-do, South Korea. One can walk behind the Sailboat ladders to take a closer look at the Columnar basalt. If you have time, you can stroll along the park to enjoy the beautiful seashore.

Heard there are several entrance, but only one is open to public. The cave has been fitted with a pathway that takes away the hard work of walking on rocky surface for you. It is still quite deep though and will be challenging for anyone with lower fitness level. The tube is lit along the way and it is quite cold. If you've visited a natural cave before, this cave might be less interesting.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Half science, half art. A museum dedicated to the formation of the igneous rocks in the area, tectonic plate movements, volcanic eruptions, formation of lava tubes, and various methods of making craters. Extremely interesting!Then rock art. Lots of interesting rocks from around the island, arranged in a way that makes them just so fascinating.Budget a couple of hours here for a leisurely walk through these sections. Add a couple more hours to see the historical village section (which we didn?t go into as we had seen these elsewhere already).

For the last day of our Jejueco tour, the first attraction we visited in the morning was Jeongbang waterfall. Situated on a high cliff by the sea, Jeongbang waterfall is the only waterfall in Asia to fall into the sea. Admission fee is 2,000 won for individuals and 1,600 won per person if you are in a group of 10 or more.When we finally reached our destination, to actually get up-close to Jeongbang waterfall, we had to walk down some (more) steep steps and make our way over a field of rocks/boulders. It was a pretty slippery (and uneven) walk, so make sure you wear footwear with good grip. But the walk was worth it: the sight of the waterfall emptying itself right into the sea which makes it a pretty unique and amazing (since we don?t really have such waterfalls in Singapore).For more photos and our Jeongbang Waterfall experience, do check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jeongbang-waterfall.html :)

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!
Enjoyed the cool air, the lovely outdoor smell of nature and that it was not at all a long walk through the forest. Well tethered and constructed pathways.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

Cheonjeyeon Falls are very near to the Booyoung hotel and the ICC (International Convention Center), an easy 5 minutes walk takes you to the bottom of a very steep flight of wooden steps. If you chance to go up there (no English signs, and as far as I could judge, they do not mention the fall even in Korean) you will find the falls, only to climb down - and then up again. I found it very exhaustive. The falls had very little water, so were somewhat disappointing. Apparently there is an easier, but somewhat longer, way to get there from Booyoung, going to the Botanic Gardens along the main road.

Be sure to wear good shoes for the somewhat uneven - but not particularly slippery - walk and a raincoat for the dripping water.    There is only 1km of the lava tube which is open to tourists, so the entire walk is 2km roundtrip.   There are a number of informational plaques along the way as well as before you even enter.    There are restrooms and a restaurant by the parking lot.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini   jungle   that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.

As someone who loves walking on rocky surfaces (yes it does sound weird when I type it like that), I really enjoyed walking down to the base of the waterfall. You don't have to walk the rocky part to get you to the waterfall though - the steps from the carpark down to the base will take you close enough. Someone the rocks are slippery so be careful. Along the way I think there were haenyeon with their very freshly caught seafood. Loved this place; would come back in a heartbeat.

As it is UNESCO heritage site which I had planned to pay a visit. The temperature starts to drop slightly when you walk further in. There's low dim light installed along the walk however, the pathway full of small rocks, uneven ground and wet with little bit slippery. So might not be suitable for elderly or young kids. Wear comfortable shoes although i did see some ladies wear heels which i wondered how are they going to survive for the 2km walk. Worth visit if you are interested to know more on lava tube formation.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Arrived around 4pm and bought 4 tickets...2,000?? for adults and 1,000?? for children. That's about $5-6 USD. It was 90 degrees outside but cool and refreshing inside. At the start it was 50F and got colder as we got deeper. If you get cold easily, you should bring a light jacket. I would wear shoes because it's a bit wet and rocky but I saw many people walk through with sandals and slippers. It's about a 25 minutes one way. It is pretty well lit for a  tunnel/cave. There's no climbing or steep terrain except for the way down but there are handrails. You will enjoy the experience. It's informative as well.
Approximately 2km walk all the way in then back out. Cooling inside the cave. If I were to go again, I would bring a torch so I can take better pictures and videos inside.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

After all the hype about Manjanggul Cave, our expectations were high but were disappointed. Nothing spectacular to see unless you are interested in the stones that you will walk on in the dim, damp cave. You will come out the same way you went in.

A long lava tube with about 1km opened to public.  Very easy to walk as perfectly level all the way apart from the initial steps, and wide and spacious (up to 23m high and 18m wide). Lots of interesting volcanic geology, features, etc. Well worth visiting.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

- Jeju is also known for it's high quality green tea. And here O'Sulloc Tea Museum you can taste many green tea-flavored foods.- Though this place has a   Museum   on its name it's more like tea shop & garden observatory.- Good place for spending time and chat.- Various kinds of  flavored-tea-products are so attractive. you can smell them before you buyTIP:   Innisfree house  (cosmetics shop) is just 1-min away by it's walk.

You need to do light hike up to Udo-bong Peak to reach this lighthouse park. The park contains several lighthouse miniatures around the world. Went in May pre-summer and you may need to apply sunblock and proper hat to avoid sunburn. Scenery are marvelous if you walk around the island in one day. I arrived about 830am and leaved the island about 2.30pm. Toilet is available near the horse fieldIts a must do list if you visit Jeju Island and i wish to come again to try walk in winter.

Was recommended by the people at my resort to visit this place. Reason being it is very clean. I did not do too many hikes in Jeju and this was just one of the few I did. It was a small forest garden owned by a family and now looked after by the 2nd generation daughter.She gave us a brief intro in English of the forest. One that actually does not have soil and one that offers a different season from what it actually should be.Unfortunately we did not experience this difference in season while in the forest. But we just enjoyed walking around this small forest garden admiring the trees that have sprout out.A good walk if the true forest hike may be too much to bear
This was the first time we hiked in the snow. We had to wear crampons in order to walk on the snow. The ascent was manageable and we saw kids around 10yrs old climbing as well.

This is just like a paradise on earth! Super beautiful and totally worth visiting! Wear comfortable shoes and some cute clothes for the most beautiful pictures! The walk is around an hour long so prepare for a bit of a hike! The price is super cheap in comparison to what you get

Hello everyone! This is a must do if you are on Jeju Island. It is a TON of walking and I will not ever recommend doing it on a hot day in the middle of the day because there is very little shade. It is a hard walk up a lot of steps but some very beautiful scenery. If you do hike it bring water and some fuel bars. It won't take you very long unless you are out of shape but even then it is worth every pain to get there. Truly breathtaking.

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.

We did not hike it due to lack of time & the huge crowds of people was daunting. The parking lot was chaotic. If there is one major complaint I would make about South Korea it would be that the driving here is awful. The drivers, especially the younger ones are inconsiderate, extremely aggressive & quite dangerous. There is absolutely no consideration shown to pedestrians even in clearly marked crosswalks.

Jeju is famous for hiking and its Olle walking routes, chosen to hike in Hallasan National Park as part of our itinerary. My first hiking experience in oversea and it is an unforgettable experience I ever had. Fantastic !

Interesting hike down a rare lava tube. Remember to bring a jacket, as it can get pretty cold down there. Not the most beautiful save out there, but definitely worth the visit to see the various lava formations. Do wear proper walking shoes as the walking surface can be quite undulating.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.
Beautiful place to take a walk - 19km though !Paths designated well, lots of places photoworthy. With small crowd of hike crazy fans... and brides.

A spacious and calm park! Nice place to walk around if you love nature. Best thing is it is free of charge to visit and once you come in, you are surrounded by nature. Wear comfortable shoes if you want to hike to the upper areas too!

We bought some fresh ginseng, chilly flakes and also fresh gingko from the market (after tasting some that were steamed and sold as snacks), The gingko there is different from those that we get in MY (most imported from China). Once you enter the cave and start to walk inside the cave, you will get a good amount of knowledge about the cave and how it is form. Very educational and quite a good 1 hour walk inside the cave.

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Not so good as all is make of glass. All in korean, nothing much to see. walk out of the castle within 1 hour. (quite a waste of money, dun go unless really got a lot of spare time)

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Manjanggul cave is world historic place of volcanic lava formation! The cave path is very unsmooth with bumpy small rock patches and wet so we had to walk steps by steps very slowly to the end! Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos. It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot. I was staying in Booyoung hotel (next to the ICC - international Convention Center) and had a few hours to walk around. I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.

I thoroughly enjoyed the Castle. I got to try my hand at glass blowing  (I'm not very good) and found the detail in the pieces amazing. I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).

I am traveling with my 79 years old dad who has weak knees. When our driver brought us to yongmeori beach, we have no idea what we are in for. Because of my dad, we chose to enter the beach on the left entrance and exit by the right entrance which we heard is the opposite direction of what most people would do. From the entrance, we had to walk down a very steep stairs which led us directly onto the beach. Honestly, the walk down the stairs was a bit dangerous as there was no railing or any safety measures. Despite collecting entrance fee, there are no staff around if you need help. That said, the scenery was stunning. The natural formation of the rocks was beautiful and the water was clear. For a popular tourist destination, this is also one of the cleanest I have been. You don?t see any garbage around. I hope anyone who plans to visit, continue to keep this place clean. As we had to walk slowly, we completed one round of the beach in over an hour.

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

For 11000krw entry per person, we expected an eye opener and an attraction different than most. Upon entering, we can see from the number of glass exhibits on display that this place would've been a great place to visit for couples or families.Beautiful display with intricacies that you will need to understand to appreciate. The displays look quite challenging to maintain as there are so many glass objects that could be dulled due to weather conditions. Aside from that, we appreciated the effort it would've taken to create this glass wonderland and enjoyed it extremely. Even in the wintry snowy condition we were experiencing, although this is an outdoor exhibition, we enjoyed it!Would recommend 1-2 hours at a slow walk pace with many photo opportunities.

First time in a cave, so I really enjoyed the experience and learning about the history of the formation of the cave and Jeju island itself. Its a UNESCO site also, which gives the site a more special reason to visit. Be careful as the surface can be slippery, but in general the walk can take about over an hour.

Early at 9.00am we arrived and was chilly, wet and misty. For those having knee and walking problems don't attempt to go up as it is quite steep when coming down. It takes 45mins for those who are fit but give 1hour within your own limit.

Dongmun wet and dry market show lots of fish and seafood. One shop inside provides local korean food even Running man visited before. Jeji mandarin can be purchased by box. Small souvenirs are sold. If you want local experience, 2 to 3 hours walk can be arranged.

Carpark available. It was a lovely walk in the forest. Wear comfortable shoes and a light jacket. We went during autumn. I have sinus.. but minute we walked into the forest, my nose magically cleared up. The air was fresh and the sounds in the forest was beautiful. Wish i could record it. They have created a path to walk so its easy. No food allowed though. Took about an hour to walk.

Bijarim Forest is one of the most visited attractions in Gujwa area.  The forest area is quite small and walkable in about a half hour.  The fauna there isn?t anything out of the ordinary but the walk was pleasant especially in the hot weather when all of the path is in shaded areas.  I?m not sure why the forest gets so many visitors, especially with the 3000 won charge (which is probably necessary to control the number of visitors) as an area like this can be found in some public parks that are free.  Since there is really only one path, it?s impossible to avoid other tourists making it impossible to have a peaceful time.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Basically it is a place where you can hug, touch and take photos with the giant teddy bears around. The teddy bear there are based on novel idea, which they showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. They are very charming and creative but the place itself is not too big, it only take about 45 mins to 1 hour for the leisure walk. One thing is, if you go on peak season, Teseum will be very pack and hardly to take some nice photos, or maybe you have to wait for the photo session.
An decent park to spend 2-3hrs.Nothing great just decent.Lots of tourist thought, so don't expect a peaceful walk unless you go at odd hours.The park close at 6pm.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

Allow for at least 2.5 to 3 hours to walk around. There are a number if different areas, my favourite being the bonsai trees. The park is very well kept and very tranquil. There are a couple of places that sell snacks and one restaurant on site.

After paying for the tickets (2000 won per adult and 1000 won per child/youth), we walked about 5-10min to the waterfall. It was a therapeutic walk through the park to reach the waterfall. Recommend to stay about an hour here to take photos with the waterfall as the backdrop.

Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. A place to go if you want to relax and have a nice walk or if you are really interested in history and stones..

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.
A novel idea to showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. Very camera-friendly but it's not a big place. We had a leisure walk in here and comb the area in about an hour.
A nice break from the heat, it's nice and cool down there!You can walk 1km, I think we spent about an hour down there total.Really slippery, be careful!One of the coolest things I did in Jeju.

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.

We didn't seek to visit Mt. Songak -- our driver just brought us there. Not knowing what to do and since he didn?셳 speak a word of English we just consulted a map near the entrance and decided that the only thing to do there really was walk up to the crater. It's a genuine natural wonder. I?셫 glad we went there because the place was just so beautiful it was worth the effort of climbing. And believe me there was some effort. Unlike other Jeju-do mountains there were rough parts in this mountain without steps or any pavement. Some bits were steep too. If you have mobility issues forget the crater; just walk around. One Korean grandpa lost his footing and scraped his hand on the rocks ??we felt bad for him.There were horses that you can ride briefly for a little bit of money. They were cute and surrounded by fields of flowers. It was like a dream to be there looking at the sky the sea the fields and the horses. Would come back if I have the chance.

We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.
Walking along the coastal and climb up to the lighthouse is not a bad idea. Horse riding course nearby. Relaxing and enjoyed the cool wind blow .

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!
Short walk from the carpark but need to climb down stairs and walk on rocks to go near waterfall. Not suitable for stroller or wheelchair.
like a pretty chinese garden. easy to walk. carefully landscaped. no dangerous climbs required. tickets needed.

It's worth our climb n walk to the fall. Please wear warm enough to prevent same thing as us. I just wear a sweater and T-shirt inside yet the wind breeze can make you freeze. Worth the long walk and stairs taken to reach the destination.

I?ve visited many waterfalls during my travels but this one is unique as it is not located within a lagoon or by a river or along a forest but this is one that goes out to the ocean!! A unique experience for me :)Definitely no swimming here but you can actually walk up close to the foot of the waterfalls for pictures and such. Wear comfortable shoes as there is a significant amount of steps to climb up and down.

Best to arrive early to avoid the hordes of tourists. Wear comfy shoes because it is asteep climb up steps. Don?t bring your strollers. May not be a place to bring the older folk who might have trouble walking.
a unique nature architecture here. There are extreme tour there which is to walk and climb around the coast. It will close if weather is not good. Near to Sanbangsan

A lovely puppy greets you at the start of the walk! You walk past a lovely stone house on the left and the dry riverbed on the right. They have well built stairs to the falls. At this time of year there are no falls - due to lack of rain  however there is a lovely pond at the bottom and the ability to climb down the rock's and close to the water. A lovely place to sit and contemplate! Don't recommend kissing the kissing cave...a blarney stone it's not haha!
Wonderful place to visit when in Jeju island. That said, you must be ready to do lots of walking and climbing. Make sure you got the right attire.

We visited here during our cruise day trip of the island. This is a very scenic place with gorgeous architecture and the   spring of life  . WARNING: Do not drink from that spring unless you want to risk some messy   internal issues  . The walk involves some climbing but not too bad with no steps just a gradual walk up an inclined path. They offer a gift shop and snack bar as you enter and exit.

We took a walk up seongsan ilchulbong, to get a glimpse of the early morning sunrise.It didn?t disappoint.The walk was very easy to complete (we had a 7 & 4 year old with us).And not to be a cheapskate, but it?s totally free if you start your climb before 7am......after that time you have to purchase tickets.

Unlike Hallasan and Ilchulbong, the shape of the crater is not very obvious. Moreover, there are less climbing and walking involved here. The main attraction here is actually the field along the path to the observation point of the crater. Make sure your camera fully charged and enough memory because it is a good photography location.

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

This is quite possibly the most beautiful spot on the island-- definitely worth the small entrance fee (I think it was about 7000 won for my family of 5). There are some fairly serious steps to get down the cliff, and then to actually get close to the falls, it's necessary to climb across a bunch of small/medium rocks. Most people will have no problems with either, but for someone with knee or foot problems it could be an issue.The only thing I didn't love was that it was SO crowded. It was impossible to get a decent photo without someone walking into the frame, and several times we were actually shoved off of rocks as more and more people tried to crowd in. It would be great if they would limit the amount of people allowed down at one time.Other than that-- a great experience that we definitely won't forget.

This is a very accessible waterfall. Kudos to the local government for making it as easy as possible to enjoy the natural landmarks on the island. A flight of steps down and a very short walk brings you to the waterfall. There are large rocks to climb over and also a rocky flat   beach  . Young children will especially love climbing over the rocks and exploring the pools of flowing water. I have a sturdy 4 year old and a 5.5 year old and I think the waterfall impressed them less than the natural rocky playground they happily found themselves in. Do keep a very close eye on young children as the rocks are sharp edged and uneven, some even loose when you step on them.

This is a UNESCO site and I find it quite awesome, how Mother Nature made these underground caves. Do note that you'll have to climb steep stairs up and down to the caves, so I wouldn't recommend the elderly folks to go in. Do bring along a jacket as it can get chilly down in the caves. Also bring along a torch and have good anti-slip walking shoes as it can be a little wet and slippery.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

The weather was extremely good and the scene was nice.Only have 2 hrs to walk this time, will definitely climb up if i have a chance to go again.Recommended to go in the morning, less tourist and more fresh air.

Really enjoyed watching how the water flowed into the sea. Interesting. Pretty much that's all you can do with a Waterfall. Beware though, the steps to climb back up from the Waterfall are quite steep, so if you're traveling with elders and kids, be prepared to walk up.

One of the 3 major waterfalls in Jeju, the water falls from a height of around 22 meters and thus named Cheonjiyeon ? meaning Sky connected with Land. Though not as majestic as Cheonjeyeon , this water falls is as beautiful when it comes to its natural surroundings . A very well laid out path ensures one can enjoy the long walk from main entrance to the waterfalls. As there is not much climbing to do, tourists of all ages can visit this place.
No climbing of stairs required at this location, which was great! The walk in was rather scenic and cooling.
It was amazing to, after a very short walk down stairs, be able to walk/climb so close to these spectacular waterfalls. Just lovely, safe, accessible, great!

It costs a few thousand won to get into this attraction. BUT, I highly recommend that when you get to the area right before the ticket office, walk left instead of right. You'll be at a free beach with some very cool lava formations. My friend and I were able to climb the lava formations without a soul around. All of the tourists were at the paid location, so there was literally no one on the other beach (and it was a 1 minute walk from the main area. Why was noone there??)

I went earlier to see the Cheonjiyeon waterfall and must say this is a better one because you can actually get to dip your toes into the water. I paid 2000 won for an adult. Basically there are steep steps you need to walk down and then in order to get nearer to the waterfall you need to climb over big rocks. If you are with little children or older folk you might have a hard time. With the waterfall, you can wade right up to it if you are brave enough the stand the cold.

I found this waterfall a better experience than Cheonjiyeon Falls as you can go very close to the waterfall. Be prepared to walk down a lot of stairs and then climb over rocks to get close to the falls, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Don't bother paying for the museum close to the gate, it's a waste of time but only 500 Won if you want to.

I could not recognise how horrible the place has become since my second visit in 2009.  Not only was it very crowded, I was sad to see lots of garbage on the rocky beach below.  It was also not possible to enjoy a nice walk by the cliffside for those of us not out to climb the mountain.  I left after no more than 15 minutes to the utter surprise of my cab driver.It was a beautiful and serene place and the authorities should take steps to limit the number of visitors and do more to clean up the garbage.

I choose to stay near to the peak so it only took us 5 mins to walk here. We didn't managed to see the sunrise as the weather was a great challenge. It was extremely windy and cold in the morning. Thus we came here at noon time. When we reach the foot of the peak, I could see that the whole peak was full of people climbing either up or coming down. The entrance fee is cheap, it cost only 2000won. The scenery was really beautiful, it worth coming here to take a look at the natural beauty.

Climb down stairs to reach this waterfall but the place is hard to reach cause no ground at all, have to walk on different shapes and size of stone to reach the waterfall. Only need to spend about 15 minutes here will do. Natural scene than Cheonjiyeon Falls that with man made paths.

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

Be prepared to climb back up after going down the steps. Will need proper shoes as the floor is uneven, and does have small puddles of water  here and there.It was a nice walk in the cave, and getting a better understanding of nature involving volcanic lava flow.

At this place you need to walk, climb a little. Be very careful when climbing on and over rocks at the bottom of the fall to take pics. Some rocks are very slippery. You can see the water go straight into the ocean which is quite different to the other two waterfalls. It is a lovely sight!

amazing landscape. A nice spot to take beautiful pictures of tranquil waters with pitch black rocks and white sand. Walk right from the main entrance till the end, you will fine some nice restaurants and cheaper places to stay. From there you can climb the hill and get the whole picture of Hamdeok area.

You will enjoy this place depends on how u spend your time :1. Take photo in the tea garden & entrance2. Order you green tea/ green tea ice cream or drinks and bring it outside the cafe (depend on weather) 3.Walk around4. visit the innisfree museum & shop for some innisfree product.
Went there when it was above 30 degrees Celsius outside. Better get a jacket ready. It might be little chilly. It is a popular destination with lots of people walking at The same time.

Went during the summer and its still pretty cold down there. Its a good rainy day itinerary as its entirely underground. Be warned that it can get really cold when  its raining though. Advised to wear good shoes are you wont be walking on flat ground and its quite wet and slippery. Its pretty interesting to learn  of the formation of the lava tube and a must go if its your first time in Jeju.

We?re staying at the Lotte Hotel and this place is within walking distance.  First waterfall didn?t have any fall at this time due to a drought or off season maybe.  2nd fall was nice & it involved some walking down the stairs.  Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.
We weren't sure what to think until we got inside. Simply amazing. It was funny and silly and cute all at the same time. It's a walk through history as told by the Bears!

We were here as part of a Yeha Tour. Our guide took us around the village and pointed out some key elements of traditional KKorean living. The Village was small but well kept. We did not go into any of the houses and we did not meet any of the families. Nobody tried to sell us anything. We had free time to walk around and take pictures and then we had lunch on site just outside the gate.
We went to Hallim Park and decided to spend a little time on the beach as it's right next door. Nice place for some fresh air and a quiet walk

We went as we read many positive feed-backs from families and we were not disappointed. All our family enjoyed it to the last minute including also the garden outside and the cafeteria.My only strong suggestion would be to do it either in the morning or early afternoon (enter before 2.00pm) as when we were leaving (5pm) the crowd was definitely bigger than when we got in. We walked back to the main entrance to still have a look and by that time it would have been almost impossible to take a pic without being interrupted many times by 'passer-by'.

We stayed at Benikea Jungmun Hotelon not very far walking distance from this beach. In the early morning or late afternoon are especially the best time to enjoy the beach not very crowded during these times of the day. There's a special section for swimmers however it's not too small. There is a changing a showering  conveniently close it is just beside the beach so that made it easy to prepare and have a shower after the swim. An amazing beach!!

We arrived and were surrounded by Koreans dressed in proper hiking gear and walking sticks. The day wasn't too warm and we made it up to the summit in good time. It was lovely to relax at a beach afterwards though.

Was expecting to see beautiful blossoms of camellia flowers but was disappointed as the blooms were over at that time. I believe if you come at the right time it will be awesome. The only blooming flowers that we saw were in the greenhouses. Park is not small so there's quite a bit of walking to visit the various parts of the park. Would recommend to check on the bloom timing before visiting the park.
visited 3 more popular waterfalls in Jeju and this one is the best.  best visit time is summer so that you can enjoy the splash when you walk close.  Imagine it would be too chilly for winter though.

Very well managed green tea museum. They have a small museum to show the process of tea and how it has evolved over the years. Upon finishing the museum you can buy different green tea products from the shop. And there is also a cafe within the museum that sell excellent green tea ice cream and also green tea Swiss roll. If you have time you can walk further into the next building which is the innisfree shop within this building you will be able to make your own green tea soap under the supervision of the Innisfree staff. There is also a cafe that sell jam and cake in this building. Perfect to spend your afternoon in this place.

This waterfall is much smaller than Jeongbang Falls  and is worth spending the time walking to it if you're in the area. Beautiful clear blue water beneath  it would make a good swimming spot in hot weather!

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.
This UNESCO cave is well worth it. It's a long walk through the black lava cave but fascinating. Leave plenty of time if you are a slow walker because of uneven surfaces.

This temple and the grounds are very well maintained. Take off your shoes before you enter the temple. More than a tourist attraction people still come to pray meditate and present offerings. Be respectful and use indoor voices or be silent.Give yourself enough time to explore the entire area. There are walking paths around the temple where you can see for yourself the perfect Feng Shui.

This museum is EXTREMELY well put together.  It is not often in Korea where you will find proper English translations.  This place does not disappoint. There is a wealth of knowledge to be found here for those interested in the sad history Jeju people have had to endure.  ProTip:  Make sure you take time to explore the outside part (the lands and the memorial wall). ProTip:  You do not want to rush thru this.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to really walk around and read about the history.  The museum covers almost 6 years worth of events and details!

this is the place to go for food and shopping when at Seogwipo. The market is pretty huge to walk  see and experience the everyday routines of those worked there as well as the regular stream of tourists that makes the place crowded and noisy. if you stay around Seogwipo  chances is you will be there at least once or every evening for did or to pass time. take time to go around the entire interior with multiple lanes with as well as the outside shops. You might just find interesting things to see and get something you like.

This is such a beautiful place! Right next to the seaside the estuary is a great place to relax and take pictures. It?셲 very serene and great for visiting with family. It?셲 right next to a black sand beach where lots of people go to swim in the summertime. There is a cafe nearby called no. 183 that was very nice to relax after walking a bit. A must see when in jeju!

This is first time we experienced a visit to a Green Tea plantation. Walking between the rows & rows of beautifully layed out fragrant tea leaves was just great.The cafe sells nice Green Tea ice creams & cakes plus tea leaves products obviously.An Innisfree shop sells the famous Korean cosmetics plus a small cafe included.Certainly this is an attraction that should not be missed when in Jeju.

This is actually my second time here and this time without a guide as we go by car ourself. You need a guide to actually understand the history of these traditional houses. I went there around 3pm and the whole village seems like a ghost town. Very quiet. Only 2 families of tourist sighted. We took a nice walk around the village but our main reason for visiting is to eat the black pork meat cooked in spicy flavour. It was my best meal 11 years ago when I visited and best meal in Korea this time too.
This is a BIG park. There is a lots of nice scenery for photo shooting.  Do spent more time to walk around and train ride.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.
The maze is very fun to walk or run through.  We had a great time trying to navigate it.  I would definitely suggest trying to do it without the map.  That is part of the fun of it!

The initial part was fine. There are 3 routes within the park. Route 1 was ok. Route 2 was getting creepier as one approached further into the route. What they didn't tell you is that this is a graveyard from the ancient times and we were walking around the graves.

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.

One can take a slow walk inside the cave and enjoy the art form by mother nature. It maybe one in a life time to walk on cool off lava where the surface is not smooth but rather come in difference shapes.
No trip to jeju should be without a visit to this amazing cave. Comfortable walk inside the cave as long as one has suitable shoes.  Take the time to enjoy this cave. Last entry should be at 5:10 pm.

Just visited the market at 12 in the afternoon and felt quite underwhelmed. The market was quiet. There were stalls selling seafood  vegetables and fruits. The food alley wasn't very happening. Tracked down the ahjuma that sold hallabong pancakes  after biting into it  it tasted so so. After hunting for lunch we walked past the market again and noticed more people. Perhaps we visited at the wrong time.

It's wet and dark inside..we just walk and walk in dark sometimes we just talk about going back and not see what's in the end of the path. But somehow we reach the end..take a photo and then walk the same road to get out.

It was our first time riding a horse.Strict instructions were given not to make sudden noises when riding as the frightened horses will go crazy & will cause serious injury to riders.All handphones/sling bags are not allowed too.Each rider gets to choose a hat & were matched to horses according to height.The horses walked unguided on a short (about 5 mins) fenced circuit. About 100 metres near the finish point the horses suddenly start galloping slowly.It was not easy to balance oneself on a horse holding just 2 grips on the saddle while it was galloping. We were concerned for that moment if we will fall off & was also wondering what happened to the horse. This was probably the scary part of uncertainty.It was a good experience though it was a short ride. At least now we know how it was to ride a horse.

It was nice to see how people live in thatched roof in time before however after a while you kind of see the same stuff.  For those who watched Korean movies  you will be able to identify a few sets there.  I wish they would have more entertainers maybe dressed up in period costumes  walking  around.  Managed to catch a short drum performance which was entertaining.  There is a small Korean eatery which serves nice bimbimbap.

It was my first time walking through a lava cave which was an enjoyable experience. I appreciated the natural formation of the tubes and to think that lava once flowed through was exciting. Others might think it's just a cave and the first few meters is the same throughout which is fair enough but I loved it.

It is relatively easy to drive to this location with ample parking lots. You will have to purchase yr tickets first before venturing further as the next booth only inspects the ticket. you probably need about 10 to 15mins walk before you reached the waterfall.  Do take your time to admire the nature during yr walk.  You can take the other path when you leave the waterfall. I enjoyed that moment with my family.

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

It features Korean ancient village type of houses they stayed their work places their farms their lifestyle and others. It's a huge place so be prepared to walk a lot. The biggest draw here is the famous actress Lee her famous tv series was shot in one part of this village. It has a small exhibition house displaying things used in that tv series. Enjoy visiting this place if you are her fan otherwise you might just feel its just another garden. There was one thing interest me there were beams and beam holes in front of each village house by placing different number of beams it's actually telling others whether its widow's house or available or man at home. Be reminded it takes up a lot of the time for visiting this place may skip and visit other indoor museum.

Initial feeling of uncertainty and doubt was quickly dispelled as we progressed through the front gates of this beautifully set and immaculately well thought of garden. Never would one imagine that from the exterior we would find such a warm and charming display of timeless and ancient art of bonsai and many other arts of nature. Definetely a thumbs up for this walk through time.

Im pretty sure some dramas were filmed there but Im not sure which ones. It is a short walk around the the surroundings are filled with lallangs. It is beautiful but not worth to pay 6000 KRW unless you really love it. Go only if you have time to kill.

I walked along the garden path together with my best  friends during our trip to korea.each plant has their own story and some piece of advice regarding life that we can learnt from tree.The garden well kept and all the staff very friendly and can speak englishWe had a great time hereWe even get free tea.KamsahammidaⅠ

I visited this place because is part of the Route 10 of Jeju Olle Walking Festival. Walking here was the most refreshing feeling. Everywhere you look is beautiful and is hard to fight the temptation of taking pictures all the time. I wanted to enjoy the walk instead of taking pictures so I tried to don't use the phone that must. Still couldn't help it. So I will share some pictures too. I hope you have the chance to visit this place. Even better if you can do the full Route 10. Is long but is worth it. I came here during corona times and it was super safe. Max of 15 people per group and mandatory mask (and they give you one for free btw)

I initially wasn't too keen on visiting this attraction as it was a hot day and inside the village it looked even hotter but via peer pressure I went in.I ended up really enjoying myself and although all the houses look the same it was still a very nice walk and large enough that it keeps you occupied for sometime.If you're into Korean Drama's you would most likely really like this place along with killing some time.

Halla Mountain is the tallest mountain in South Korea and dominates Jeju Island.  It is an old shield volcano and is snow capped.  The part of the national park that we went walking in was swathed in fog the day that we were there.  The fog gave the national park an eerie ethereal feel as you never knew what interesting things would come up ahead.  Had a great time.
Had a really good time walking around the park. The gardens are beautiful and the lava caves are cool too! Worth a visit if you're passing by.

Good to visit this place if you have extra time in Jeju Island building was surrounded with green tea plantation and a small nice walking path connecting both O'Sulloc and Innisfree. It was good to have both closed by as it was a rainy day we went in March.O'Sulloc building has a very spacious cafe serving nice desserts and many selection tea from the counter bar. Green tea cream roll is a must if you happen to be there.The souviner section has so many to choose from. Parking and admission to this place is free.

Going into the cave when it?s blazing hot outside is actually not a bad idea. It was 11degree inside the cave as you walked 1km to see the famous lava columns. Just need to be careful walking as the grounds are mostly uneven and sometimes can be slippery.

Caves are pretty common but first time walking through a lava tube. It is quite a walk (close to 2kms) to the end where the lava poured in (column like structure) but worth the walk. The cave is rather chilly & wet with uneven surfaces. Do come prepared. Decent lighting throughout however can get rather dark. Maybe a small torchlight or glow stick so you can enjoy it more.
Be prepared to spend a lot of time here. And be prepared to walk.  Much to see. Fantastic bonzais that are over 100 years + older

At the entrance of the plaza there is tourist information center where you can get any info related to the area. From this plaza there are occasional festival from time to time this time I just went to see sunset on the ocean. Above the big waves sunset was pretty. There is long sea-side walk which leads to Dragon head rock.

At least Pyeoson Folk Village had more flowers and more greenery and smaller than this one sk you don't have to spend so much time walking around looking at basically the same hut in different locations.Not worth the exhorbitant entrance fee. I'd rather buy food with that money.

A very nice nature park with lots of flora and fauna. There is lots to see and do so do set aside more time to spend at this place. Do wear a pair of comfortable walking shoes and take lots of pictures!

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).

Whether you love nature or not, I strongly recommend visiting this cave. There is so much to learn on how the lava tube was formed and it provides you with a unique experience that is unforgettable. Do wear proper covered shoes as you will be walking on rocks almost the entire time and some parts might be slippery.

When we arrived in jeju it was raining so we needed to do something that was more indoor.  We drove out to the cave.  The entrance fee is cheap at 2000 won per person.  Then you walk down some steps and enter the lava tube.  It is really dark down there and the floor can be slippery.  I think we spent most of our time looking down at where to walk rather than looking around.  You walk 1km to the end and there is a rock formation.  Nothing too special.  Then you turn around and walk back.  Overall it is a nice cool 2km walk, perfect to escape the heat of jeju.  Just watch where you walk
Went to the cave, only walk for about 1-2 hrs as this is a short cave. see stone structure cause by volcano eruption. only go if you like nature. Can visit the maze park at the same time.

Well, comparing to Seogwipo Daily Olle Market, sashimi is cheaper here. The market is bigger and there are most stalls for the snacks. But majority of these stalls are not open until evening time.  It is short walking distance to the Black Pork Street.Ample parking nearby and there is also a multi storey parking which is among the most expensive parking I had in entire Jeju. 6000W.

We took the ferry to Udo Island. We went as walk ons with our tour guide. The ferry ride was short and easy. We were happy we had our guide with us because the weather was not very good that day and they were closing down the ferry service due to rough seas. We were glad she could translate this information for us.  We went over for a short visit and took the last ferry back to Jeju which was around noon. Because of the ferry schedule we did not have much time on Udo. We did go to 2 lookout spots. They were very pretty but the weather interfered. It would be a nice place on a sunny day, but there doesn't seem to be much to do on the island so plan on relaxing.

we took some interesting shots. cool place to spend some time outdoors, it's not too big and easy to walk around. definitely worth going there!! in fact, we thought this was pretty much the most interesting thing in Jeju

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We loved walking through Halla Park. The paths are organized and cultured so beautifully. Every turn brings new surprises. There are bonsai trees galore, rock formations, fountains, and green spaces the lure you in. The caves are small, but fascinating. The birds here are delightful, from parakeets to peacocks and ostriches. We would definitely come back and have a picnic here in the springtime.

We love exploring caves, and we've been to quite a few worldwide. However, Manjanggul isn't really one of the best. The problem is, there isn't much special,. By the time you walk in half a kilometre, what you see becomes a little unchanging. Not bad for a short visit however. Tips: 1. It is a long walk and can be slippery. Wear comfortable shoes with grippy soles.2. A small torch may be useful

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

We had a great time walking thru the lava tubes, talking about how they were formed and all the science behind this ecosystem.  Our friends ask if we recommend it and we do, but you need you to understand its a cave/lava tube and NOT a theme park style attraction.

We enjoy shopping underground. We were able walk from one end to another. Just remember where you enter. There is a number so you will not get lost.There were beauty products, children clothing, adult clothing, bags, shoes, restaurants, etc. They are not your designer stuff but cheap items. Since winter, they sell winter wear. We bought some face masks, cleanser for less than $10. We also bought bags for $15. The lady said made in korea so we think ok. The backpack is great cos very spacous. Good for traveling. Quality is just ok. Then at one exit near to the wet market, we found a shop called bang bang. It belongs to a friend of the korean actor who starred in the famous korean drama   my love from the star   we were able to buy simple T shirts, socks. They are less than $10. Socks about $3. We actually shop here 2 times when we were staying in ocean suites hotel. It was just 10 to 15 minutes walk to this underground shopping area.There are restaurants here too. We found a good korean restaurant here. It was good food and affordable.

We drove by after a visit to Hallim Park and couldn't resist this beautiful place.Totally unprepared for the beach, we went for a short walk around the area. The water was cool & clear. There were many tide pools for the kids to explore and catch crabs, little fishes & shrimp. The weather was perfect.The kids wished that they could stay there all day but we had to leave for another place.We would go back there again when we visit Jeju the next time.

We came on a drizzling day. The crater is certainly big, and the walk was nice despite the rain. But it wasn't as impressive or memorable as other Jeu attractions like the Manjanggul Cave or Seongsan Ilchulbong. If you're right on time, this place is possibly skippable.
Very easy and accessible walk. I wish I had more time to enjoy it, but since I got there about 30 minutes prior closing I had to rush.

Understand there are three courses here - 30 mins, 60 and 90. Basically it?s a very light forest with pine and a few other trees that I am not familiar with. You choose the course and just take your time to walk - the air is fresh, nobody speaks loudly. The path will meander through trees, laughing statues, water fountain, and more trees. Would definitely recommend coming this place for those who want to calm their nerves and leave the city behind. We took the 30 mins course and came out refreshed.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!

This place is perfect for culinary, searching for snack with cheaper price, and mall (called Jungang Shopping Mall). I find small authentic teokbokki stall here and seafood restaurant. It will a little quiet at night, so you can walks freely here. The market will be closed around 7 pm so come here before closing time.

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This place is big and we didn?t go through each inch of this place as both of us felt tired when came to this place. If you have time and the leg can support the walk, a good place to spend time with.

This market sells many products either fashionable clothes and branded cosmetics. There're many food shops available with reasonable place too. If you are seeking for sport shoes or toys.You can also find here. Some shops will give you the tax refund and some not.You need to check carefully. The famous cosmetic shops like ETUDE and skin food, some of famous items may not available. There're 11 gates which the even gate no. will locate on the right whereas the odd ones are on the left. It's not complicated and easy to walk. There's restroom available too.If you don't buy the well known brand, you will also find the local Korean cosmetic brand which is very cheap. I buy 12 hand creams with 10,000 won prize and can get the complimentary mask for 10 sheets. It's very good price. The souvenir shop also available here.I would also recommend to come as the choice of your shopping since it's not too crowded like duty free building and you don't need to buy a lot of same items in pack like duty free. As most of Korean cosmetics in duty free would be sold in pack of more than 2 pieces which sometimes you don't need that much.

This is your typically local market where you can get fresh product here.  I will NOT say this place offers the cheapest price but rather there are varieties for you to choose from.  The market has many entrance and each entrance leads to you to a particular section where they sell the same stuff ranging from clothes, fruits and to live seafood.  We picked up some Jeju tangerines and sweets here which were pretty good.  Discount?  Most shops are priced the same so its hard to get discount. Best time to come is about 2pm where there are lesser crowd.  Its also a short walk to the underground shopping mall so if you are here, do take the chance to visit the underground mall altogether.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge .
