At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won
This is something for children or adults who have not grown up! Spend your time as you wish, we just walked on...

This is not as well known as Udo and having visited Udo prior, I was equallly impressed with Gapado. I was there for the green barley festival but it was already mid May so the fields weren’t green. I think week 1-2 of April may be a better time to visit. It’s easy to walk around the island and you won’t need to rent bikes.

This is not a cave, this is a lava tube so do not expect what you see in caves.  The tube is huge in size.  From the entrance you are able to walk 1km.  At the end you can see the remains of where lava had gone up and out of the tube.  It is not very impressive.  The tube itself is a large tunnel like structure.  There is not much to see and the lighting is a bit insipid.  The good thing is that the entrance fee is only like $2 so you don't need to worry about wasting money.  I am glad I visited but I would have been happy to have just walked down into the tube about 5 minutes, turned around and left.  Walking to the end of the open area is unnecessary and a bit of wasting time.  Spend about 10 minutes and its enough.

this is  rare chance to walk down lava tubes and look at the odd shapes and formations caused by the molten rock. You can see different layers of lava that once flowed here and see how the laval squeezed through smaller passages.   Consider bringing an umbrella or a very light shell. It can be damp and sometimes water drips from the ceilings. Also, it's significantly cooler than outside.   All in all, a must.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

They call this place because it looks like dragon's head. There is walking area around that stones so you can see that from the right beneath. But at that time of we are there, path is closed due to bad waves.

There is nothing much to see except of the cave. But if you spend time to read and understand the formation of the cave. Its quite educational for me.You will be more enjoyed if you slows down your steps and admiring the unique walls in the cave. Instead just walk, walk and walk until the end and took picture of the end of the cave then went back.

The waterfall is not so large when we came, so we can walk up near to it to take some pictures. It is only a short walk down from the entrance, but be careful when walking on the stones as it can be very slippery and very crowded at times. The falls itself is very unique as it flows straight to the ocean and it cost only 2000 won to enter.

The professional photos are very well taken thus I was quite interested in this place before i go. But basically you will spend perhaps a good 20 to 25 mins walking from one end to another end seeing the same thing (unless you are very interested in rocks or stones) in very dark lighting.. and then another 20 to 25 mins back. I don't think its a bad place.. just not to my liking i guess. If you have time and a good camera and a tripod, you might take some very nice photos there lol

The park is big and have many to see, especially for people who don't know the culture of Jeju. It would be also good for family but since it requires lots of walks I wouldn't recommend elder people who can't walk for a long time. The weather of the day we went wasn't quite good, but the drizzle and fog made that place more mysterious which is quite special because we saw different type of scenery from those pictures you can find from the Internet.

The indoor gardens are very lovely especially the flower and cactus gardens. We were there on a sunny day in May and expected it to be hot inside. But these are not just greenhouses. They are greenhouses with air conditioning and so it was pleasantly cool and we took our time to walk around and admire the plants in comfort. The gardens are very well maintained without a leaf out of place. The arrangements are very pleasing and and these two gardens are simply beautiful. Go on a sunny day when the light and shadow creates a most charming effect.As for the outdoor gardens, the Italian one is very picturesque with a magnificent water feature. This is not so much a garden but nonetheless very attractive.Definitely worth a visit.

The grounds are HUGE! It felt like a nature forest walk, a geography and history field trip all rolled into one.I don't know if it's windy there all the time, but when we were there, it was freezing when the wind blew when we were in the shade.We had a tour guide who explained the various rock features and how/why people carved the stones for use in the past. But honestly, I was bored after awhile. This place had rocks/stones galore. Considering that there are so many other things to see/do in Jeju, I would give this place a miss.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

The best waterfall to visit! Don't waste time to other waterfall, this is the best one. I managed to see rainbow at the waterfall was simply amazing! Made the whole trip worthwhile! Just wear the right shoes there as there are some rocks to walk on before getting close to the waterfall

The best parts about this tour were the walk from the main road where you can admire the cherry blossom on both sides of the road and the newly opened Angel-In-Us coffee house. If not for the springtime cherry blossoms, there doesn't seem to be much else to see.

The beach is nice, clean and not too crowded but a bit small. Many hotels and villas are located along this beach. Therefore, if you want to be stick on it, just take one hotel here, normally just 5 minutes walking. A good place to relax and have romantic time.

The beach is conveniently a walking distance from Halim Park across the street. Pretty good size and a very shallow beach, good for children to play. It's kind of too crowded for me and the rent for the beach umbrella is somewhat expensive KW25,000. We did not spent too much time there.

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

So I read some idiot blog somewhere that said this place was apparently fun. What an idiot. NO. JUST NO.A bloody waste of 9000won is what this place is. It's extremely rundown. Smells like cat pee EVERYWHERE, especially all over the 1st floor. All the   studio sets   are not well maintained and look old and disgusting. What's worse... the moment you walk in, there's a set with a noose & wooden chair... IF you notice my photo, the tiles there are broken and the set is elevated.. imagine walking towards the noose only to have your feet sink into the the set, aka feeling like you're falling through the tiles. They have free clothes and hanbok for you to try and pose in. BUT... like everything else in this place... it's old and... i dont even know when any of the clothes were last washed. Remember, the whole place smells like cat pee. It's 2 floors of rundown studio sets... they even have signs saying   please leave your shoes on  .IF you're looking to waste time and 9000won/person, go ahead. Visit this place. Just remember my voice saying   I told you so   when you walk into a cat pee smelling rundown area of studio sets and leave disappointed.

Short walk to cross the bridge while having a good time to enjoy the scenery. Nice to take a good shot. One facing the ocean and open sea, while the other side facing the sea with the city as the background.

Second time here with another friend. More time this round to walk leisurely.As said in the title, no wow, OMG thing inside you'll find unless probably you are an geologist, etc. The most memorable is probably the experience of walking on very uneven, ripply hardened lava ground spotted with many puddles in near total darkness through low and tall ceiling of an underground tunnel.

Real value for money being able to see he best of Jeju in the short time we had on the island. Our tour guide, Jin, was excellent and walked us through the itinerary adding in stories about the history of the island and his own experiences. Highly recommended.

quite near with my hotel but seem that was commercial food street with not so many food shop. we walk around 2-3times & try to select reasonable & maybe good service also tasty one. finally, we selected one of only Korean & English spoken restaurant. lucky that was ok.
Probably not worth going there just to do this, but if you are going to the nearby falls or the submarine, then definitely make time to do this too. It is a pleasant, easy walk.

Perhaps it was the time of day we were here. We got here really early around 8am to start our road trip down the east side of Jeju Island. So nothing was open yet. We saw the dragon rock and even walked down the side of the small cliff to see the rock from a different angle. It was raining quite a bit on the morning we visited so the walk down was a little slippery. It was interesting to see the dragon rock formation and read about it's significance in Korean folklore. We had a photo with the mermaid there too. Unfortunately due to the time of day we visited nothing else was open, but from what we could tell there were mainly souvenir, fruit and convenient stores and stalls. Worth a visit if you have time, but essentially a nice looking rock

Our family visited the Cheonjiyeon Falls on the first day of our trip. We came out quite late, around 5 pm and we decided to come here as this was one of the attractions that were opened at that time. The admission fee was reasonably cheap. The area was not that big as I imagined, you walk from the entrance to the waterfall and then back. The waterfall is quite nice to look at and I'm pretty sure it might look more majestic if you come here at night. Even though I came on a cloudy and rainy day, it didn't ruin the mood much, it makes the waterfall more mysterious and I liked the atmosphere.
On sunny day, beautiful rainbow and  really blue sea you can see. you need to walk down some steps, but it is valuable experience to take time and effort.you don't want to miss it ^^

On a recent vacation in Jeju, I decided to check out the Ramada Plaza Jeju Casino. My visit was in the mid-afternoon, and there were only a handful of casino patrons inside this small casino.When you enter the casino, they ask for your ID, and then they make a photocopy of it. I do not believe that there is a legal requirement for them to photocopy your passport (or in my case, Korean residency card) for their permanent records. Frankly speaking, I was offended by this requirement. To check a visitor’s identification, yes; permanent photocopied record, no.I had the intention of playing some blackjack, but as soon as I saw that they use continuous shuffling machines, I walked out. It is impossible for a blackjack player to gain the tiniest of advantages when such machines are used. My recommendation to blackjack players: don’t waste your time going to this casino.
address: 제주 제주시 탑동로 66 라마다 프라자 제주호텔
입력주소: 제주 제주시 탑동로 66 라마다 프라자 제주호텔

review: My 6 year-old girl loves this place sooo much. We enjoyed walking around & taking photos of all the cute things. Too bad, we didn't have enough time for the activities like glass painting, glass blowing. (We spent around 30 mins walking around the place.)

Mazeland was both beautiful AND fun!  We got there close to closing so we didn't get to stay long, but the time we were there was awesome.  I got some awesome photos, and it was really fun to walk around in.  *HIghly recommended.

Make sure to bring a jacket with you to the cave if you get cold, there is about a 10C temperature difference from outside to inside. So if you visit in Summer, it's a great break from the heat and humidity. It's about a kilometer walk, so give yourself plenty of time. Overall,a. Great attraction for all those visiting the island!!

Jeju is well known by the haenyeo, or that we usually called it as woman divers. Since it was not a good time for diving like a haenyeo and it means that it was so difficult to find one of them when i visited Jeju, i decided to visit the museum. It's not so big, but shows completely how the haenyeo's life, their lives, and their historical stories. It shows not only the diving suit they wear since long time ago until nowadays but also their house, their foods, their tools, and everything. Your journey will be started by watching a video about history of haenyeo. Then you can walk through the dioramas to learn how haenyeo live and works.
It's relatively easy to find this place. We need to pay 2000 won for entrance fee. If you have more time, take another walk to the parking lot, there is also beautiful scenery.
Its quite a good time for walking in the lava tube. There are several announcement, so you can read and understand whats that.Its quite slippery, just be careful or hold ur friends hand (better).

It's more of a shopping place. The green tea ice-cream is quite blandand there's not much green tea taste.But the   saving grace   is the tea plantation . There are giant cupslots of flowers and is overall a photo taking place. We did not have enough time and did not visit the museum . There are interesting sample tea blands that you can smell with names like   Moon Walk   and   Jeju Green Tea  . Overall could be better. Might come again.
It's a beautiful park to stroll around in the spring time (that's when I visitors Jeju) and given the good weather condition, walking around is just refreshing and calming. A must visit place

It?s a place must visit in Jeju island. Air is so fresh and the walk is tranquil. When you walk through the forest and appreciate wat the Korean say that it is a place for meditation. There is a tap near the entrance, water is so refreshing. Trees in the forest have been there for hundred of years . It?s a treat to see some trees with autumn leaves. There are some Low walls with black stone formations which apparently is the volcanic rock from Jeju itself.. Would definitely come back here again to spend more time in the forest At the end of the walk they even have the vacuum facility to blow off the red soil from your shoes

It was felt like exercising when walking down to the see the waterfall. But just about ten steps down the stairs, the scene reveal the hidden stunning waterfall. So beautiful.  A dozen shoots were never felt enough to capture its beauty. I would recommend to spend a sufficient time just to enjoy the scenery.Please take be careful when walking in between stones near and around  the waterfalls. They are so slippery, so chose a flat surface stones as you walk? or not at all. A friend had her camera and mobile phone slipped down into water when she struggled to stand still on a stone. I was slightly more fortunate to be able to keep those gadgets of mine dry?. but not my shoes. While the water was refreshing, but I do not think you would like getting your shoes wet, particularly when you have only a pair for the whole Jeju island exploration. A wet trousers could spoil your whole day trip around the island.

It was a 1km walk in and 1km out again. The lights were pretty dim unless there are signboards. The path inside is quite rocky with puddles of water here and there. Spent most of time watching out for puddles of water and where to walk instead of enjoying the lava cave. The cave was colder than outside, so might have to prepare a thin jacket.

It is one of the few villages that still exist on Jeju with complete retention of the traditional houses. The villagers still live in these houses but with modernized technology. They no longer uses the open air toilets, rearing black pigs and using electricity for lights, television and wifi. This is also the village that Dae Chang Guem were filmed in the early 2000s. Interesting to walk in the village as if we have travelled the time back in the past.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

Interesting facts about the formation of the lava tube. Malaysia has no such thing so i was definitely eager to learn more and to experience it. Walking into the lava tube really exciting as i step on to the solid harden lava ...beautiful formation of harden lava, adores the lava pattern ... careful stepping onto the path as it is uneven and can be challenging to some ... just take your time walking in. As i adores nature, i really enjoy exploring the lava tube...as you go deeper into the tube it gets warmer than the windy cool air outside of the tube. Enjoy it, a must.

In order to reach this beautiful waterfall one has to endure walking for few minutes. We went there on April, it was the start of the spring season, yet it was windy so it was cold. For me the fall is just average, may be because I have seen more beautiful falls from the other countries. However, this is worth the walk and time. We manage to have beautiful photos near the falls and in the park.

in front of mt sanbangsan, this is a nice place to visit to see the great scenery and cliffs where you can take a walk along the coast around the cliffs with the interesting formations. When we were there, there is a sign that states the opening time (for entry to the coast) is from 3pm when the tide is low.

If you stay in Seogwipo, this is absolutely a nice walk and visit. We payed 4,000 won for two people for entrance, which is worth the small amount of money. The area is beautiful where you can see different trees, fishes and of course the waterfall. We were there around 12 in the daytime, and it was a little bit crowded by the waterfall (since everyone wanted to take a picture and the place is small), but there is a small place where you can sit and just watch the beautiful waterfall!

If it's your first time visit, definitely take the path to Oedolgae. If you have time, from the main entrance, take a left and it will take you along a path along the ocean. Go about 1/2 mi walk along the path and you'll see off on your right a smaller path. Take this and it will take you down to the ocean. Many locals take this down and it's a small watering hole where locals go to swim and fish. Once you get to the bottom, the navigation along the rocky formations can be challenging but very much worth it. It's not a beach but you're right next to the waves as they come in. It's absolutely beautiful. Just for context, I took my 8 year old daughter and 6 year old son. They had to be careful navigating, but was able to do so with adult supervision. Many others have come to appreciate this but they have been leaving their trash behind and it's quite saddening to see such a beautiful place littered with garbage. If you do go down, please respect the beauty and take your garbage with you.

I was sold! Though it was more like a replica of a village from many, many years ago, it felt like I walked back through time to an age where everything was bathed in tranquilityI got a glimpse of houses and possible lifestyle in ancient JejuIt gave me the impression of how rough life was back then but peaceful as it appearedThough visitors may have mixed opinions about this place, to me, it works

I was on my wear the Toms until they literally fall off my feet, and this definitely got them about there. If you do anything before going to this cave, make sure you have the right waterproof, grippy-ish shoes for the job. But really, this was cool, literally.  I managed to be hot and sweaty almost everywhere we went while on the island, but in the cave he temp drops to a comfortable 50something degrees. Just glorious! Is it worth the walk? I'm not sure. It was nice enough, and definitely cool to say I have been inside a cave at least once. So I guess I would put this on the itinerary if you are visiting the island for he first time. Would I go again? Likely not, I think once was enough!

I visited Jeju Glass Castle last winter. I went there twice while I stayed in Jeju for a week. The first time I visited, the weather was good and so my family walked around the museum with joy. We were very glad to be there. The second time, I was very thrilled to visit again, but unluckily, it was raining. Our family struggled to see the sculptures that were placed outside. I recommend that you go to Jeju Glass Castle when the weather is good.

I quite enjoyed this place. It takes a while to walk around so don't go if you are in a hurry. If you take your time there is plenty to see, ancient tombs, traditional housing/tools, stone statues, giant stone towers, etc. The museum was also good and I learnt a bit about volcanic rock formation that I hadn't seen before.

I love that this beach tends to to have many waves, and is located within walking distance of places to stay and eat. The water is warm and clear,and theres a fantastic BBQ place over the little bridge to the right of the beach. I've returned to this beach both times I've come to Jeju! The sand is fantastic!

I just don't get this place. The rock doesn't look like a dragon head.... does it?Maybe cos I went there on my own... but I just don't see the significance of this place. Why? It's a waste of time and effort. Not that it requires that much walking... But I'd conserve my energy and also my time on something other than this.So not worth the time and energy. To me, that is. Maybe there is more to this place... but I just don't see/get it.

Having visited other caves in Vietnam and Australia, I was expecting a more developed tourist spot. The visit is essentially a 2km walk under low-light and chilly conditions. Most of the place is wet and somewhat slippery. I will not recommend it unless you have spare time in Jeju

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.
Have your passport  and money for the Udo Ship ticket and you will take your glorious  time  on the Beach, in the cafes, just walking or riding around
Free admission, strong wind as it is at the coast. A volcanic activity aftermath feature, work of nature. Nice walk around the area but if in rush for time and not a Korea serial fan, you can skip

For those visiting this cave expecting amazing cave formations you may be disappointed. On Jeju island all caves are more accurately defined as lava tubes. These vestiges from Jeju's volcanic origins are strange, dark, and geological wonders.Tips for visitors, expect Manjang Cave to be cold, dark, and rough surfaces to walk on. NO sandals or high heels! Hiking boots are a far better option. If you come into the lava tube expecting glittering cave formations you may not have a great time. However, if you want to explore a truly rare geological wonder, take this journey into the darkness to enjoy a unique experience.

Figured I?d give it a walk through after getting sun burn the day before. Not crowded on a Sunday. Free parking. 10,000w entrance fee. The museum was a little hot and stuffy. The depictions of historical moments using bears was humorous at times. Most labels were in Korean with some English. Might be fun for small kids. The garden out back was nice extra touch to allow kids to run around and see more bears.

Dragon Head Rock (Yongdu-am) is worth a look just to say   been there, done that  !It's nothing fantastic but does live up to its name.As it is within walking distance of downtown make the effort if you have the time.Tour groups, especially in the morning, arrive by the coach load. So walking makes good sense!

Communication barrier is not a problem for us to shop here. Yes, they don't really speak English. But, we still had a good time to shop and bargain. If you want to shop korean fashion (but not the designer label or branded one), clothing, accessories, bags, cosmetic, skin care, this is the place. One place for everything so that you don't have to walk more. Innisfree, Nature Republic, The Saem, Skin Food, you name it. All are here.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.
At the time we reached here, the coast was closed due to bad weather condition. We just managed to walk arounf that area. It's located in front of Mt Sanbangsan.

Another great beach but this time with more cafes and restaurants right outside.  There's also a supermarket right to the left of the entrance.  There's a nice boardwalk to stroll, and kayaks to rent.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.
A very enjoyable place to walk around and watch the waves. If you have limited time on the island, it is definitely one of the places that's worth visiting and doesn't take up much time to see.

A cave system that can get in easily just by walking down the step.according to the tour guide, this special cave is cold during summer and warm during winter. By the time i go is summer, it is real chill inside the cave

World heritage Site. 13km long lava tube under Jeju Island. Formed by successive eruptions. The section that can be visited is about 1km long - first descending down two levels into the lava tube where the roof has collapsed and then walking up the tube under the mountain and ending at a lava pillar where the lave cascaded down from a parallel tube running above.  There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.

Walk around the mountain and you can see different rock formations.  The water is very clear (look at the picture as if there is no water) that you can see sea urchins. I advise you wear rubber shoes to be more comfortable walking through sharp rock formations.

This was not part of my original plans but I'm so glad this was suggested to me!!! The mountain is gorgeous along with the temples inside. If you walk further down the base of the mountain there are some different food places/cafes. ALSO  at the bottom of the mountain is Yongmeori cliffs!! I had no idea they were there. Such a pleasant surprise. I'm not sure why this place isn't more popular! Gorgeous.

Sangangsan Mountain provides a short walk up stairs to a Buddhist temple and shrine. Only 1000 krw to enter. Even my teenage boys enjoyed the walk and the visit to the shrine where we were encouraged by a local to drink from the sacred water for our good health and fortune.

It is a place to visit if you visit Jeju Island. In particular we recommend trekking around Songak Mountain. You will be able to enjoy the stunning scenery and strolls while gazing at the southernmost island of Mara Island in Korea. Trekking courses and benches for relaxation are well maintained and can be walked with men and women seniors and children because they are not difficult. You may meet horses grazing.

Went for a stroll after visiting Hanna Mountain. The cactus conservatory was impressive and we rounded up that part of Hallim Park with a thirst quenching cactus drink.  Similarly the cool walk into the lava cave, and the connecting limestone cave was particularly enjoyable, taking shelter from the melting sun. Highlight of this trip was feeding of birds inside a bird house.   We purchased their food at the vending machine.  Having them eating out of one's palm brought back fond memories of childhood.

Well, there has been near our place in Jeju and in our schedule. We could go by walk and bought Citrus fruit in the street, specialties of Island. The bridge leads to the road around the mountain. Can proceed to visit

Sea, isles, mountain,  good smell of exotic flowers, nice seashores' cafe, pitoresque pensions, and great rest area. JeJu Island has 19 Olle trekking roads however, Olle 7 is the most famous and it has the most beautiful scenery among them, if I may say it! This is the very beginning of Olle 7, it worth it to walk 16.4km(whole length of Olle 7) from this place. Strongly recommended.

Nice walk down to the falls. Well organized. The waterfall is not spectacular, just a stream of water coming down the mountain. 20 years ago the made electricity here, but the whole installation is gone now.

We couldn't walk further down due to the heavy rain. However it was still beautiful and amazing. You could go for a stroll with your family. I heard so many good things about this place. So I will definitely go back on a sunny day when I have a chance. :)

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. But dont be under the impression that it will be hot in there. It is very cold inside and be prepared with the winter clothing and a trekking shoes. It was a long walk and a nice experiences. A must visit cave.

This is a very nice stretch of beach easily accessible via several staircases from the main road or the Olle walking path located among the cliffs above the beach. This is perhaps the closest beach that you can leisurely walk to from any of the hotels in the Jungmun resort area. This is not a black sand beach but it makes up for it with the wide and clean beach and the great surf. There?셲 a direct staircase to the beach from the Hyatt regency back garden.
The walk towards and back from the fall is very well kept. Quite romantic with the trees around . The fall is not too big but there is a calm serene feeling looking at it .
The beach was nice enough. Very shallow waters. Lots os rocks around the beach. Lots of people. Except at 1am in the morning when I snuck back for a walk.
Spectacular experience whereby you got to walk one kilometer in and walk back the same distance. It is the longest lava tube in the world. Very interesting experience.

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Osulloc tea is known as one of the more famous and reliable brand in Jeju...most of the tea is expensive too. Thus it is not uncommon for travel agencies to include the Osulloc green tea museum into its itinerary. A walk around the museum shows you a little background of tea in particular. You can also be able to see tea cups from different countries on display. I tried the green tea ice cream and it was yummy. We were told that if we spend more than 30000 won we can get a tax refund at the airport. So we really spent more than 30000 won on tea :) I wandered alone out of the tea museum and saw Innisfree!!! They were conducting some soap making lesson when I walked in. The deco is very different from what I saw in the malls. And of course I ended up buying stuffs....some facial masks that I wasn't able to find in Singapore.

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

My wife was bowled over when she saw the poster of the actress in the famous Korean drama - Jewel In The Palace.  Walking through the grounds we were told that the drama was filmed on site and visited the villages and houses.  It brought back nostalgic memories of the show capping the highlight visiting the exhibits.  But if you are not a fan of the drama the village is still a good place to visit to get a good idea of the traditional Korean homes during the Joseon era.

Jeju National Museum is set almost in the middle of nowhere -- well it's beside an adult theme park but otherwise literally nowhere. Had a car so it wasn't tough to find but would be extremely tough using public transport.The museum and the garden that surrounds it is well sterile... for the lack of a better term. Beautiful but seems to lack any personality... it's quiet laid back and perfect for a long walk... but not much action.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.
Great walk around the crater with the long grass surrounding you. Great background for pictures and not a strenuous walk. Im sure it is also beautiful int he other seasons.

Actually it is pretty cool to walk through a lave tube. It will take you back through history. The texture of the stone walls and the actual size of the cave is mind-boggling. If you come from an area that doesn't have volcanos it is a real educational experience.

a nice place to visit. walk around the green tea farm to see the green tea trees visit the gallery to understand the background and history of tea buy the tea products at the retail shop enjoy the tea at the cafeteria. there is an Innisfree Cafe next door also which is a must visit place to enjoy the soap making process and enjoy the food and drink where I had the best yam drink I had ever tasted!

Yes, it's just an ordinary rock. But with the perfect backdrop of the ocean, blue skies and outlying islands this place is perfect to visit in the morning for a relaxing walk. You can even sample their famous orange fruit in season.

We were tired in the carpark and considered sleeping but decided to go in. So glad we did, walking through the garden was a deep feeling of peace and felt refreshed. Would definitely come back. A must do in Jeju Island!

We were able to easily find a cab in the parking lot, to take us back to our hotel. The cave itself was cool, temperature wise, so bring a jacket, even in the summer.  It is amazing to walk through.  Occasionally you get wet, your socks, if you step in an unfortunate wet spot or your hands, if you touch any of the walls.

We went to this beach during the day and kayaked and swam. It was a lot of fun! Then we went at night and it had a wonderful nightlife with restaurants and lights!  *I really recommend this beach!  It wasn't too crowded like the others, and there weren't too many black rocks, and no seaweed.  It was great to walk in the water at night too.  We're going back to this beach again this year!

We gave a 4 stars owing to its mysterious element.The 100m stretch of road appears to be uphill but it is actually and in fact downhill. This can be done by several experiments. E.g. pour water on the road, put a bottle of water and it will roll towards the   uphill  , walk or run backward along this road; you will feel the difference whether it's uphill or downhill.There are a few stalls selling food so you can eat and think how this is possible.

We enjoyed this cave.  It's about 1 km to the end where the largest lava  pillar is located and then another 1 km back,  although the walk was relatively flat (no inclines) it was very uneven and slippery in places.  Wear shoes with good traction.  The cave is in a beautiful setting with many public toilets around.

Walking 2km (to the end of the section open to the public, and back) in a lava tube is a cold, dark and wet affair, but it's a unique and educational experience. The floor is very uneven and there are many puddles to step around. There's not a whole lot to see, but every now and then, features of a lava tube are highlighted and explained. This is not for everyone but if you can appreciate that it's rare to get the chance to walk through a lava tube, go for it. Just be ready for the slightly challenging conditions

Visited Manjaggul Cave because it was a UNESCO Natural site, like Seongsan Ichulbong.  Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

Very educational walk through the lava tubes.  Be sure to bring a sweater and wear proper footgear (uneven ground).  If you are wearing any light coloured pants or shoes, be prepared to get them soiled alittle.  Basically its a   walk-to-the-end   and back type of attraction.  After the walk, you'll learn more about lava tubes and volcanic eruptions.

This place is an epitome of beauty, beautiful rock formation, beautiful sea, beautiful waves, beautiful clouds, it is amazingly beautiful. Here you enjoy both worlds of rock formation and beautiful sea. Definitely this place is super windy and you might get wet with huge waves hitting against the rock formation. The scenery of the place couple with the beautiful sound of waves for me makes any visit to Jeju complete. Be careful in walking and exploring place, there are areas that are slippery and rough.  If you are an instagram addict this place is the best for you. You can choose to have those lovely rock formation as background or the beautiful blue sea with the huge waves and or both the lovely rock formation and waves.

This is a massive lava tube that the public are allowed to visit and does give you a real sense of the magnitude of the volcanic activity that created this island. For that alone you should visit.It is a nice cool 1km walk to the end and then, of course, you have to come back.A good experience.
Really enjoyed the walk around the coastal, all the rock formation is awesome. We walked around from the shipwreck and back again to the same spot. If you love nature, this place is a must.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands. One of these was the Chilseongro Shopping Street. Fortunately, I had bookmarked Dongmun Market on Kakao map and it was a short walk from there. I had no plans to buy branded clothes (nor any clothes for that matter) so I ditched Chilseongro and headed to Dongmun.The Dongmun Market is a wet market, a traditional market. Pretty much everything in Jeju is available here?clothes, tangerines, chocolates, seafood, household items, food. The prices here were a lot lower than the chocolate stores and souvenir centers that our tour group operator brought us to.At Dongmun, you can haggle, especially if you buy plenty. I decided to buy chocolates to bring back home to our office staff. Since there were plenty of stalls selling chocolates, I compared prices first. I ended up buying from an elderly lady who offered the lowest price. I got more than 60 boxes and she gave me lots of freebies. There are stalls that had different types of food. Some even had live seafood available and they will cook it for you. I was too full to try out the local food, but I did miss having photos taken.There were a handful of stalls that sold kitsch souvenir items like keychains and magnets. There were two large stalls that had numerous items on display; their prices were high though. I ended up buying from the other stalls whose main items being sold were something else and just happened to have magnets and keychains on the side. Nevertheless, the prices at the souvenir shops in Seongsan IIchubong were lower; I wished I had bought there instead.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

It's actually just one short stretch of the road but interesting. The road gives you an impression that its going up hill instead it's actually going down the hill. The surrounding including the plants, trees, field and fencing are giving you that up hill impression. So when you switch off the vehicle engine that you are in, the vehicle will continue to move forward. Same goes to the test where they will show you by rolling a water bottle. Try walking backward and you can feel it. You might feel a bit disappointed as there is nothing else over there

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.

It was ur eyes who played trick! Discovered in the 70s, there are 4 such places in the whole of Jeju island. Your tour guide will reveal to you the   secret   of the road, so I won;t be here to soil your surprise. It's fun to try to walk backward (uphill) and fell more easier than downhill.
It was awesome to see, nevertheless you walk for 700m, turn around and walk back again. That makes a bit dull, especially when there is many tourists and you focus more on not bumping into someone

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

Interesting cave, for someone who has stayed in a city for the whole of her life. We went in winter and what is interesting is that the cave is considered warm for winter. Be prepared for the long walk to and back and the path would be too rocky for strollers or wheelchairs

If you love nature, this is a place you should visit. Nothing much to do , basically just walking and taking photos. But I personally love it ,because you can't find such a relaxing place back in a big city. It's good to visit during colder days.

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

Can only walk about 1km of the cave as the other area is restricted, back and forth will take about 45mins. Inside of the cave is pretty cooling and nice to see such a natural occurring sight but I would say nothing much as the lighting inside is also pretty dark.

At the back or Osulloc Tea Museum is Innisfree house. This is a much more peaceful place to have a drink and small eats but unfortunately, we were not aware hence and our drinks at the Osulloc. But we had another drink here just because it was peaceful and we needed the calm. Is cute that we walked the 30 steps from Osulloc to Innisfree we see a sign that there are snakes... we would think with the amount of crowd and noise, the snakes would have been gone. Lol This place is about clean eating and is peaceful. Some light shopping and not crowded at all.

As we booked for a tour package in Jeju ofcourse Mt. Hallasan will be on the list. Experiences the thin layer of snow on the park which is perfect for strolling, walk a couple of meters and go back. And yeah visit the museum to see some photo gallery. Its worth to see.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

A veey dark and long walk with informative description on different formation of rocks created after cooling of the lava. Interesting and educational, no exit @ the end of the walk so would have to take the same route back.
You can make-out the dragon head once you reach the shoreline. A short walk which gets a little difficult during the peak tourist season.

We visited in the peak of winter so there was very heavy snow fall.We came quiet under prepared in terms of walking gear so the walk to the crater was pretty difficult. I wouldn't recommend for elderly or anyone with mobility issues but this is from my experience with snow so can't comment on the difficulty during other seasons.

We came on Feb... It's sunny and so windy there when we came... But it's a worth to come... A long walking to the peak but got a great scenery when we arrived at the peak... Go down the cliff throught the stairs and you can see many Haenyeo selling abalones and they also can cook it for you after you pay it... Don't forget to bargain it... But you must speak in Korean because they cannot speak English lor... Hohohoh...

This is more like a nice park rather than a garden. They have beautiful walks among the trees and you can have tea and cakes in a small restaurant with the terrace seats looking out the wide green field. But the staff can?셳 speak English so there must be a tour guide to take you here.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: this is a great place and a must to visit. you have to walk to the peak to see the place. this place has been name the world 7 wonder of nature. its definitely live up to the name.

Just visited the falls today. There hasn't been enough rainfall for the 1st waterfall to happen so we saw a peaceful lake instead.There were wooden boardwalks around with quaint lamps. A peaceful and refreshing visit. Quite a few stairs but more manageable than Sunrise Peak.

It was nice to walk around the village and learn about their culture. If you are not travelling on a tour or travelling with a tour guide which you can't understand (for my case i am with Chinese Speaking tour when i don't understand) remember to borrow english speaking tour aid from the entrance then you will enjoy well.

If u do not object natural scenicThis place is the most value for money u must visit. Entrance fee is only 2000w for adults . easy walking path for child.the only deficit is the tour guide can only speak in korean. The most amazing wonder is the entrance fee includes a 25 minutes well filemed 4D movie
Fun walk through the lava tubes. We did this as part of an east side tour that included a beach and Sunrise Point and an English speaking guide

We sought out Saryeoni Forest thinking it would be a great place to escape the July heat.  We visited the section with nicely laid out boardwalks which was great for taking our baby on a stroller.  The scenery was picturesque and even during peak season, it didn?t feel crowded as the forest area is vast.  However, the humidity level was significantly higher as it felt like we were walking around wearing a plastic raincoat.

Udo feels like more of an island than Jeju itself, because it is much smaller and rural. You can hire a car, golf buggy, cycle or simply walk around this scenic little island. Very short and cheap ferry ride from Seongsan, so add this into your trip to Sunrise Peak.

This is my favorite place whenever I go to Jeju. You can walk up to the peak for forty minutes where you can see the East Sea of Jeju. From there, you can leave for Cow Islet on a cruise, another destination in Jeju. This place is famous for beautiful sunrises.

Not as touristy or crowded like Sunrise Peak. Walk to the crater was on the milder side, not too much steps.Leisurely romantic walk pass the fields of silver grass (graminee) which can only be seen late September to November. Some parts have swings for you to sit and enjoy the breeze. The crater was covered completely with vegetation and the nearby green hills was a picture of serenity and you feel removed from urban cityI wouldn't mind coming again. Near ticket area, there's a stall selling the sausage sticks that were flavorful and yummy.

Located on the beach, you must go down and walk on lava stones, it's a nice place, many people take photos in front of this waterfall that comes out from the massive right on the beach, this place is connected to story of a Chinese traveller speaking the elixir of eternal youth, he hoped to find it on Jeju

I went to Udo with a group of friends. It was really nice, we went around the island with rented bicycles (10.000 KRW for the afternoon). We swam in an incredibly clear water.I recommend going to Sunrise peak afterwards, walking along the coast gets you there in 15 min and seeing the sunset was an amazing experience.

clean sand, perfectly sloping beach, with sandbars at a convenient distance to provide interest -- it's not a beach for ocean swimming, but for relaxing and walking and building sand castles.  It is a relatively small area, though, so it might be crowded in peak periods.

A tiring long walk but well-worth the workout as you get to soak in the beautiful green slops of the peak, and the ocean blue waters below. Lots of photo opportunities, and you also get to see the jet ski in the waters below.
We walk around this dongmun market and bought a lot of local snacks and souvenirs. You may bargain the price with them.

This would be my fav market so far at Jeju. You can buy lots of local products and local delicacies to eat as well. The market was so packed with locals and tourists so you kinda need to walk slowly and try not to block the road. LOLThere are lots of exit / entrance here but rest assured that it is interconnected and you won't get lost. Most shops are selling the same products but if you really wish to buy then you need to scout for the best price!

There is a lot of food at this market. From snacks to proper meal. You can buy fresh fruits and souvenirs at this market too. The market is 5 mins walking distance from Artstay hotel. Sashimi is also available at this market.

The street food stalls at night were awesome in the market. However all the good one has long lines and slow moving as most of them are cooking in front of you. Not knowing which one is the best  we choose to join the crowd and stand in line with others and skipped the other with short lines. Parking is terrible even Google Maps shows many nearby parking lots. We tried two separate lots and both were full. Instead of waiting someone to pull out  I ended up parking on the side of nearby street and walked to the market.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

Not as big as the 5 day market but still provides an interesting insight into the daily food norms of the locals. It's sheltered so rainy days is not an issue though parking may be. There are a few local eateries inside but the one we went in insists we order one portion (they are big) per person. Rather than having to waste food we walked out.

Located 100m from Boo Young Hotel  you can just walk up. It;s a 5 level building slightly similar to HKCC in Wan Chai. There is a 7-11 convenient store but closes early. In house also a buffet restaurant  a bank and a Duty Free Supermarket where you have to pick up the perfumes  liquors and cigarettes at airport.

It's very much a market for locals but interesting to walk around. There are lots of colourful displays of fruit and vegetables. Dried fish stalls are also common  as are live shellfish and fish tanks where you can choose your purchase. It's a bit smelly in parts  particularly around the meat stalls.
It's fun to walk around in the market and see all the different things.A lot of fish and other thinfs out of the sea are available alibe or dried.Great atmosphare in there!

It's a pretty big local market but after awhile u realised it's repeating. Be adventurous I say and try the different local food and snacks despite the language barrier. The stall ajuma are really friendly.Parking is a bit challenging and don't forget to check out the Black Pork street nearby (10-15mins walk) for some nice BBQ.

It's a nice shopping street that is about 5 min walk from Dongmun Market and beside Jungang underground shopping place that is closed till August 2016. There is Tommy Hilfiger interesting souvenir store The Islander local designer and mid-range fashion shops shoes and stationery stores and cafes as well. Nearby at one end is the attraction Gwandeokjeong Pavilion. At the other end of the street there is also a black pork street.

We walked though the Dongmun market and found it quite enjoyable.  They have a huge selection of good,  especially seafood, veggies and fruit.   All looked very fresh and well presented.  There are also stands where you can purchase food items as well.  As it is covered it was a good rainy day activity.

We stayed in old jeju side and this fish market is located 5 minutes by walk to our hotel. A lot of souvenirs, local foods, dried fishes, seafoods and street foods. This place is a must visit and people are very hospitable

We had dinner at a resto in Blackpork street in Jejusi which locates opposite Dongmun market. The price was 14.000w/200gr (normal pork) and 18.000w/200gr (black pork). Our meal was so delicious, it costed nearly 40.000w for two of us. You are highly recommended to have a try with this once you visit Jeju, as black pork bbq is one of the island?s specialties. Near the Blackpork street is the shopping street and underground shopping area where you could have a walk after a heavy meal.

We enjoyed walking through the colorful Dongmun Jeju market but the prices were very high, especially when they see Westerners, Chinese or Japanese. We later spoke to our hotel and they said the price is almost doubled for foreigners. We had a simple raw seafood dinner for four and it costs each person USD$44.00. We had no liquor (beer, wine, etc). So enjoy the colorful scenery but if you want to eat there be ready to pay a high price.
walking in the local dongmun market, I was impressed with a lots of fresh fish shops. I can observe how local people work and enjoy their normal life.Seafood is fresh and at reasonable price!

This shop is located along Chilsung Fashion Street, just a short 5 min walk from Dongmun Market. There is a range of souvenirs that are affordable and not found at the typical tourist shops, e.g. scented candles, dolls, organic socks, brooches, postcards, handmade key chains of fabric horse, notebooks, tote bags and posters. The quality of products are better here.

This is a very big market with lots of local foods you can try while walking around. Prices are very reasonable too, and the people friendly and helpful, no pressure sales at all. Best market we've been to whilst travelling!

Our FIRST meal in JEJU and we were just spoilt for choices. This is traditional market and we had so much fun walking in the market.The large boxes of tangerines greets you at the entrance and as you explore further, you see endless rows of fresh seafood. We randomly selected some food and they tasted delicious!

Its a short street UG mall sells things you will find in normal shops in Jeju.  The catch here is that this place is not just underground BUT its air conditioned.  Its maintained very well with clean toilets.  We spent about 40 mins leisurely but didn't buy anything in the end.  I won't say its a must-go place but if you happened to be at Dongmun market, its a short walk to this place.
Interesting experience to walk around the local market, we are there early, not many stalls open yet and some preparing to open...

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

actually we yet to go inside the museum but just walk around the street of LeeJoongSeop. not bad. however, seem that not too direct related to art but flea market or street market with some handmade stuff. if finish Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market, go here together if you like to buy something.btw, it has an old cinemas but seem already closed. we saw a band to do some rehearsal. one of artist maybe

Wonderful beach in Jeju island. Very clear water. Amazing colors and good vibes all around. You can spend here one day to have relax and chill out. And If you want you can walk around. There are close to the beach a lot of restaurants and caf챕s

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.
We passed by just to get to Jeongbang waterfall. Nothing special but it is free entry. So no harm taking a walk and snapping some photos overlooking the sea.

Very popular tourist attraction (you know its popular when they have those cheesy fast speedboat tours on the water) but still worth the visit to see these unique shaped cliffs in the ocean if you are already in the area. Just a short simple walk along their boardwalk to see them so quite a short visit. Only 2000 Krw per adult to visit with kids under 4 free.

Very beautiful beach although one has to pay a large amount for a spot with an umbrella on the main beach. You can however walk just a bit further and find another beach. Beautiful beach with clear water. It can become crowded in summer over the weekends
Took cab from Seongsan Ilchulbong. Beautiful site for sea and waterfall. A bit crowded but worth it. About a 30 minute walk from hotel Little France.
This place show a 3 tier waterfall that you need to walk different place by follow the path. The 3rd tier a bit tough as very steep and staircases.

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.

This is a three tiered waterfall. To see all three you must walk a lot of staircases. It is much smaller than what I thought but where it is quite beautiful. If in Jeju I recommend a visit(if you love the nature).

This is a place suitable for kids and senior citizen. It is just a short walk from the entrance to the waterfall via a flat road. We make this place the last place on our itinerary (late evening) as this place close later than any then attractions in Seogwipo. Quite a romantic walk and we even met some couples doing their wedding photoshoot here.

there's nothing much to do. just walk a bit and you see waterfall right down to the sea. they said this is the only one in Asia. i did spend few minutes here. people who love nature and photography will love it here.
The waterfall is very close to the ticketing booth so there isn't a need to walk for a long distance to get to it. It is generally quite nice but not super impressive.
the waterfall is not huge but we can walk close to it. we saw 2 women selling raw seafood nearby which is a nice experience to have the sashimi near the sea.
The water fall was rather small but the good thing is we can walk on the big rocks path and take an up close pic without getting wet.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...
The park around the waterfall area was simple and not too long and tedious for a walk with your family. Waterfall was nice too for a photoshoot. Overall was great!

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

The cave is cold and wet. It's not easy to walk on undulating floor filled with watery potholes. Certain section you have to bend your body as the ceiling is too low. The cave looks the same from the opening to the end.
The beach was super pretty.. not a long walk.. Very clean.. it was amazing.. And the water was super clean which was really nice!! Love it!

The area around the waterfall is big. There are three different waterfall in the same area. You will need to walk a bit to get to the second and third tier waterfall. You can also go to the seonimyo bridge in the same area.

The answer is of course when there is no water. Even though it was raining  it wasn't raining enough to produce a waterfall. Still a pretty spot with a pleasant walk past orange blossom scented orchards.

The 1k walk is really interesting and had good info in english. It's much cooler as soon as you walk down the steps and raincoats are useful as there are water drops and wear comfortable shoes for the rocky and wet floor. Most of it is quite dark but you can still get good photos. Definitely worth the visit

Staying in Seogwipo we were lucky enough to be able to walk to these amazing waterfalls which fall into the sea.  We descended  down some wooden steps to the beach and clambered over rocks to get close to the falls.  There was a great atmosphere there with many tourists all happy to help take photos of each other with the falls behind.  Well worth a visit.

So didn't really plan where I wanna go but just walked. And I walked to this beach. There are signs to say no swimming after August but people were still swimming. The waters look nice and felt nice and 2 meters out and it's at chest level so watch out there.There's also surf school to teach surfers wannabes.Now the trip up though..... 300+ steps up to reach Lotte World and Shilla

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Nothing that fantastic unless you are the one driving. The road is also only approximately 150metres long. Difficult to feel the gravity on human body/walking. Test using a vehicle or can/bottle/water poured on the road. The better deviation is Black pork stall manned by samurai-looking chefs. Mouth-watering black pork BBQ. Nice ice ball dessert nearby as well.
Nice small beach. Clear water. We had sunny day so the beach and water together  was very beautiful. Have a walk there it improves your day.

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.

Its good place to get to know how Korean people lived on Jeju do island. There are houses of all kind of people like craftsmen usual habitants prisoners and etc. Also some photos of women divers from Jeju. Its probably better to use a guide since all information is in Korean and  there are several traditional korean games on the ground that need to be explained. There are several shops inside: some craftsmen shops like wooden crafts and caligraphy and also souvenirs and some local candy. We enjoyed our walk here. Its nice park that also got some ponds and small waterfalls. Its quite big one also. fee amount is 10000 krw per person.

Its definitely one of the most impressive waterfall I have been to. Its only a 5 mins walk from the parking lot and you see this strong waterfall. The water was nicely cool. I wish I had my bathing suit with me.  Its a small area.. we only spent like 30 mins there.

It's a short walk down to the waterfall. Very doable and not tiring. We went early in the morning after breakfast and the pictures turned out lovely.  Also saw real Hanyeo women actually diving tirelessly.

It's a nice waterfall and it falls right in the sea. There a little walk down the coast to reach the best spotit's super crowed and that makes it a unsustainable to us. There was a tent with some ladies that served you raw fish on the rocks. Nice one
It's a memorable sight as it is the only waterfall in Asia that flows directly to the sea. Just be extra careful when walking down the wet steps.
It`s worth to see the waterfall going straight to the sea. Have good shoes - you'll need to walk on stones to get close to it.
It?s a lovely walk down to the waterfall. The ladies were selling some food which we didn?t venture to try but noted some others did.

It was soooo good that we were so tired after all the photo-taking! It is a walk in to the museum but definitely manageable from the teddy bear museum or the waterfalls. Just ask around and can save cab fare.

It was a relaxing short walk to the falls. We went during the evening and it was quite touristy. It's a great site to take pictures before the waterfall if there isn't too much people. The entry was only 2000 won and there are shops and restaurants near the entrance
It is a wonderful sight to visit.  The only problem being smokers who don't adhere to the laws and smoke anywhere.  Other than that it was a wonderful experience and very easy walk to the waterfall
I'm very amazed by the 23m waterfall and it is just next to the ocean!! It's a bit difficult to walk on the rocks though but it's definitely worth the visit!

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Make sure you carry rain coat or umbrella and have some warm clothese if you are not used to cold. The caves  has water dripping at place and its very cold even during the hot sun outside. We went there after noon and it was quite cold. Be careful while walking inside the cave and its slippery. Do read the story as you go through its. there is restaurant which server good korean food just outside the entrance which we felt was very good.

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction.
