We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water. Walking through the cave was thrilling and filled with excitement. Round trip to and fro the cave took us about 1hr30mins. Would highly recomend to anyone visiting Jeju Island. Proper shoes are also recommended as it can be very slippery and slip and fall may happen. Kids and Older people may find this attraction tough and difficult to walk through.

Cool and refreshing. The rocks just at the foot of the waterfall are difficult to walk down. Not recommended for old people.I could not find the inscription which this waterfall is famous (go check out the history/story behind this)!

Came with my 80-year old dad and we had a slow walk along the uneven ground. Would recommend wearing waterproof as water drips fr the ceiling. It's is also a little chilly inside the tube (abt 8 degrees C) The place is also dim so some agility is needed to prevent slipping but it is generally safe. Just walk slowly. Overall it's an enjoyable experience as we marveled at the forces of nature that made the tube possible.
Beautiful beach very tranquil water is clean and unpolluted. If you just want a nice place to walk or rest this beach is for you.
About 5mins down the long flight of stairs and you get upclose with the waterfall. Helpful to come with proper shoes as you can walk closer the the waterfall on the rocks to get a good photo.

A popular hotspot and parking can be a problem. The waterfall is nice but not very spectacular. Can stand on the rocks bottom to catch a better glimpse of the waterfall but mind the slippery rocks. Wear a sport shoes with good traction or simply walked bare footed on the rocks.
A long walk although only 1km. Inside cave at low temperature and water keep dripping. Experience the nature of the lava cave formed since 20000-30000 years ago would be something not to miss.

A few dozen steps down to the open rocks at the base of the waterfall.  And then you are rewarded with a beautiful scene and welcoming and cooling mist.  If you have good balance you can walk on the rocks for some beautiful pic of the falls and the waves crashing on the rocks.  Gorgeous!
2000won per adult. A 3min walk down the stairs and you'll reach the waterfall. Love the weather and sun during autumn.

2000krw to get in.    Walk down stairs to get to a very rocky area with the waterfall coming down right next to the sea.  There was not a huge amount of water flowing down.     Some souvenir/food shops around.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: You have to walk a little distance from the car/coach park, but the path is flat and well paved.  The falls themselves were, however, disappointing with little water flowing.  I?m sure the falls would be more impressive after heavy rainfall.

Yeah, very nice for a waterfall that's in s decent-sized city. It's not Niagara by any means, but the walk through the gardens leading up to it are pleasant and it's very photogenic. Getting there early - pre 10am - is the best bet as the light is good for photos and the crowds are not as hectic.
Worth seeing, and I liked that it was within walking distance of our hotel. The beach area was really pretty although it is not a place to go if you want a beach and not a waterfall.

With a 2,000?? fee, this waterfall is well worth a visit! It's a short walk down from the parking lot - not hard to get to at all. You should, however, wear comfortable and supportive shoes because you need to balance on rocks in order to get close to the falls.

When we arrived we were a little surprised at the ticket price to enter. There was quite a lot of steps to get down, as we walked down you can see the waterfall. when we got down to the rocks by the waterfall there was tons of people it was so crowded. but the waterfall was very beautiful and was very nice how it was all open without any barriers keeping you from the waterfall.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

What I like about this waterfall is that you can either admire it from a distance or if you prefer, you can literally walk along the rocks and take a closeup shot right next to the falls. What a thrill.

We went on a very rainy day, so not many people.    Neither of us had any trouble with footing.   It was not slippery at all!     Huge level of water flow.    I can?t believe they found it necessary to have a no swimming sign as if anyone would even attempt it.   Maybe when the water flow was greatly reduced.    We only went to the 1st and 2nd falls.     Enjoyed them.   Entire walk for the 2 doesn?t take more than 30 minutes.   I imagine on a nice day there were be a large number of vendors at the end  but this day, there was no one out.

we visited this place with little or less expectation as many friends had said it too overrated but to our surprise is pretty awesome. Maybe because there was strong wind and rain the waves were very strong. The waves were hitting almost the observation point. We bought rain coat outside the cliff entrance for 2000wons (2$) and trust me its best decision we did. We were showered with water like anything as there was rain and wind. maybe in other season you dont need to worry aobut it. the phone number listed on site took to the parking lot the resort next to cliff, had to walk a bit to reach it but got to see the resort common area with some nice garden and statues!

We visited a total of 3 waterfalls (including Jeongbang Waterfall) for our recent trip to Jeju Island.  This was my favourite among the 3 waterfalls visited, as it was rather unique, flowing directly into the sea.  However, when we were there on a weekday afternoon, it was nice and quiet for only a few minutes, then a huge group of teenagers / students arrived and filled up the whole place.  It was too crowded and we had difficulty finding space to walk on the rocks and to take a good picture was nearly impossible.We would have stayed longer if it didn't get so crowded.

We enjoyed our walk to the falls and took great pictures.  It is a beautiful area that is a national cultural heritage. There is a sidewalk that takes you close to the falls.  The waterfall drops 23m into the sea, this is one of the 3 major falls on JeJu island.  Well maintained, very clean and well worth a visit!

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

very nice paintings on the walls inside the temple. peaceful and quiet at the compound. there are 3 levels to the temple and you can actually walk up to look around all 3 of the levels. it also has a nice garden behind. you can drink from the water at the 2   tanks   which is located one on each side of the temple.

Very good exercise, the longest route takes about 6 hrs if you walk fast (as it says 8 hrs) but u need to go in the morning so that u should return before dark.Lot of locals doing this but don't forget to bring water n packed lunch!

Too fascinating when seeing all the traits of massive lava flow in the cave, which is actually part of the lava tube. Must bring along a powerful torch if you want to enjoy from the ceiling to the ground. Relying just on the phone torch or the lights inside will hinder your enjoyment and appreciation of this natural masterpiece as you will be only focusing on your steps. Do walk the entire 1 km so you can see the big massive lava lumps which stretches from the ground to the ceiling. Water drippings and water patches are common, wear a cap and windbreaker will help. In fact the temperature inside is a few degrees lower than the outside

This was the only waterfall we visited in Jeju and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Unlike the others (according to what I read online), you can walk right up to the waterfall itself, although you'll need to brave the rocks to do it. Loved sitting here right by the edge of the water and just letting the spray wash all over me.

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

This is the 1st attraction we visited when we arrived at Jeju. Its near our hotel in Seogwipo.We saw a group of tough ladies, the Haenyeo, scuttling over the rocky beach. They were hunting for seafood hidden between the rocks.The waterfall was nearby, beautiful with strong steady stream of water gushing into the sea as it had been raining a lot recently.A lot of people around the area as it was an easy to reach attraction with a short walk down the stairs...

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).
This is a fun place to visit, as apart from the waterfalls you can walk around the area and see many different attractions.
This is a beautiful area. The breeze, sun, and walk were refreshing. The water was many colors of blue! Lots of people though!

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

This beach is a great place for tourists! Upon arriving there are lots of vendors with delicious food and things you might need for the beach (towels, hats, beach mats, swim suits, booze, etc). The main beach is usually very crowded (understandably). I like to go to the beach to the right, it's just a 5 minute walk on the sidewalk, clearly visible with a clear understanding it's leading to another beach. This part of the beach seems to be less crowded with all of the same benefits! Great place to relax, enjoy the sun, and swim in the water!

This beach is a good one.  The sand is soft and powdery and the clear water very gradually gets deep which allows us to comfortably walk unusually far into the ocean.  The other special characteristic is that there is a big change from low tide to high tide.  The high tide, which occurred around 10 pm when we were there, completely covers up a pretty large beach area.  It's pretty fascinating.  The food and drink shops near the beach were a bit of a letdown for us because they were overpriced.

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The waters were gentle and one saw more people in water than out there, although a selfie moment happening is never far in South Korea. Also great for a walk( into the village area, but please don't take photos without asking, off the coast as they share the coast with visitors freely and it is respectful to enter their space on their terms)

The Waterfall is very close to Seogwipo, within walkig distance.  It costs 2000eon adults to enter but you can get very close to the Waterfall.  There are even seafood being sold next to the cliffs so you can eat seafood, watch the sea and enjoy the waterfall.  We took a few pictures and then   left because the downside is that there are a lot of people.

The water is amazing. There are 3 waterfall spots and a beautiful bridge to see at this attraction. Highly recommended although the walk can be a pain, especially the last waterfall.The bridge is also quite a sight to behold. This is probably the best waterfall in Jeju.

The walk to the waterfall was nice although it is kind of man made. The natural sights at the side was beautiful nonetheless.However, the waterfall itself was just ok. It didn't seem like that's the focal point of this attraction but it was good enough for a trip there.

The walk to Cheonjiyeon Falls is quite easy and beautiful. The waterfall is quire charming as well. However, compared to Cheonjeyeon Falls (which is a 3 tiered waterfall attraction in Jeju not mentioned in TripAdvisor), Cheonjiyeon is still second best.

The place was hot and mosquito infested honestly due to the Aug weather. However if you have enough repellent with you, this is a good place to walk over, sit on the rocks, chill by the waterfall, feel the cold clear air and pose till you are tired.

The park is built for the waterfall. Was there during dusk, though there are sufficient lighting around. The waterfall is a tad disappointing, especially when you came from Jeongbang Waterfall. However it is suitable for people of all ages, the walk to the waterfall is very easy.
The natural waterfall in the raw form and walking in the rocks is fun. The surprise was a fresh Jeju orange juice nearby, the seller was honest and nice.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

The cave is very nice, different from all other sights in Jeju. It?s a short walk but the ground is wet inside and can be slippery, also a bit dark in certain places. Wear a hoodie as water drops from the cave roof. Not recommended for people with mobility issues.Once inside, the sight is beautiful, it?s an amazing work of nature.

Pretty waterfall. It?s easy to get to, a short walk brings you there. Unfortunately you aren?t able to get into the water. This waterfall is more accessible as compared to Jeongbang waterfall. So for older folk and young children, this might be more suitable. I prefer Jeongbang just because I get to play in the water. Admission is 2000 won for an adult.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

One of the real highlights for my visit to Jeju Island. It's absolutely fascinating and I've been to a few different caves before. It's different because it's a lava tube cave and there are a few different information boards in there to explain the different features which helped to understand how it was formed. It's very well and cold in there so bring a wet jacket and comfortable walking shoes (waterproof/ resistant if possible) with good traction. There is a small descent but other than that it's rather flat in there so most people should be able to do it, just watch out for the wet surface. If you go to Jeju, you must visit this cave.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Oh gosh!  This is definitely one of the must-sees of Jeju Island!A short 15min (mostly flat) loop, and you will be rewarded with babbling brooks and crystal clear waters overlooked by towering cliffs.  Best of all, this is off the beaten path, and there were virtually no tourists around.  Oh...the tranquility.Some parts of the walk involve jumping from rock to rock in the streams.  Not a problem generally (my kids found it fun), but if you have mobility issues, you may want to bear this in mind.We would like to thank Victor of Jejueco Suites for helping us discover this hidden jem.

Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.

Next door to the popular Hyeopjae Beach is the lesser known Geumneung Beach. Make sure you pack your snorkeling gear as it's teeming with all kinds of marine life. Like most of Jeju's North-side beaches, it's very shallow, which means you could easily walk for about a kilometre and the water hardly passes your middle as the tide's going out.
need to be careful walking on the rocks, the water is very clean n clear, a lot of tourist here so have to be 'skillful' to take photos and move about on the rocks.

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Just try to get past all the tourists and walk down to the waterfall, bring a rain proof jacket :) went in November and waterfall was relatively small, probably more awesome after period of heavy rain. Great selfies ;)

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.

Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest, walking through these wood is believed to enhance cardiovascular function and to prevent asthma and tuberculosis. This is the most famous forest on Jeju island and here you can taste mineral water that is thought to relieve muscle and gastrointestinal problem
It's not an easy feat, walk about 2 km round trip filled with stairs. There is a 2500 Won enterance fee. 3 waterfalls and a huge bridge

It's just a road, but if you want to make it interesting, do some experiment on it. Get out of your vehicle, and try walking down/up the road. Or test the road by pouring water/ walk inversely. We enjoyed it!

It's close to the main centre of Seogwipo, easy to find with street signs posted in English around the place, it only costs 2000 won to enter, and it's not only unique but a spectacular chance for photos. Do as the Koreans do, they sure do love a waterfall selfie.This and the nearby Cheonjiyeon Falls are two must-visit attractions in the area.I'm not sure if you can walk too close to the actual waterfall, or what the rules are for swimming in the waterfall pool, but on a hot and sunny day I seriously considered it.You do get a bit of spray from the waterfall, so keep that in mind when taking a photo so as not to get your camera too wet.
Its a nice beach, a bit small, lots of kids but nice. When we went the waves weren't very large, so didn't bother going in the water. But we walked around and there's a nice park nearby.

it was just a super long cave that is really cold, perfect when you are visiting during the hot summers. Wear comfortable shoes because you will be avoiding water puddles, trekking on uneven rocky floors. Its just a super long walk in and out.
It was an easy walk, lots of street vendors, waterfall was beautiful. Perfect weather in October! We spent 2 days in jeju and just about did it all.
it is Only waterfall in Asia falls directly to the ocean. Not that interesting, easy to walk down, a lot of kids and old people can visit.
It costs 2,000 to get in here and complete the walk to the waterfall. That works out to about 짙1.50 in U.K. pounds. Worth a visit

Interesting waterfalls with a park. Lighted up at night. We came by at 8pm.  The clear and deep water of Cheonjiyeon Falls is designated as Natural Monument No. 27 and is renowned as a habitat for Mutae eels. Take a walk around the beautiful park. You can also take photos with the props such as 'Summer', hearts etc.

Impressive sight withthewaterfall ending directly into the sea, walking down to the foot of the waterfall can be challenging with the rocks formation and without proper path, so don't wear heels!!!If you want to get near to the waterfall, be prepare for a shower of blessings

I?ve never been this near to the base of a waterfall before.  No railings, just the raw power of a thunderous fall.  And a rainbow!  The kids loved jumping from rock to rock.  This may be a little precarious on a wet day, but we were lucky with the weather during our visit.You do get some splashes.  So if you have very expensive camera equipment, you may want to protect it?  The walk up was a little tiring, but not overly so.Absolutely love it.  A must see!
I went to Manjang Cave. It  was really good place to see. It was very cold when we got in side and we can see you cave of Volcano, while you are walking the water drop down and very lively..

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.

I find it as an average, nothing special ... better to walk around outside the stone park,the surrounding is quite nice with traditional hall nice traditional look toilet (no hot water, water is icey cold) I came last month (early May)

I expected a longer walk for this, given that this is what Mother Nature had blessed us with, but this cave is only opened for the first 1km to the public. Still, it was an amazing sight (with the turtle-like rock formation and the various lava formations). Wear comfortably with a cap or hoodie as the cave will be chilly and the water will drip from above! Also, bring flash lights as it can get quite dark!

How they get the cars, coaches etc up the hill with the engine switched off is a bit of a mystery,I thought some kind of electro-magnetic set up under the road, then if that's the case when people poured water onto the middle of the road surface, why did the water go uphill and not downhill. Do not think it is an optical illusion as it certainly was a hill that went up and down, I walked it !.

Great beach. The water is really clear and nice blue color. The tide comes up and down during the day though. So from 11am~ until 5pm~ you can walk few hundred meters until you reach deep enough water. But besides that one minus it is a worth visiting beach!If you want some more information on what you can find on the island, you can check out this video: http://youtu.be/X2RwSnOMgYk?list=UUYEqXBrHobdnJF591_o-vcg

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

First thing we've noticed is how civilized this beach is - loads of restaurants, shops , cafes nearby. We were lucky enough to visit it in September, when holiday season is over for majority of Korean guys - so, it was not that crowded. Water was very clean and the only downside, that it was already a little bit cold. If you walk few hundred meters in a right hand direction from the main beach (towards the hill), you would see a camping ground with even smaller strip of sand - and we were absolutely alone there.

Falls is very beautiful.  You walk down 100 steps or so, then across big rocks to the bottom of the falls.  Wear tennis shoes or flip-flops for rock hopping!  Lots of water spray, and nice wading in the cool water as it runs across a few rocks to the ocean.
Enjoyed how easy it was to walk from parking lot down to the waterfall, ws not expecting such a short walk! A waterfall that goes into the ocean, two awesome things in one!

Come prepared and you'll love it, good walking boots and waterproof jacket. If you find it too cold or dump you can go in for a few metres, and go outside, but we kept going wanting to see what is at the end, and it was spectacular, with huge lava column in blue dim light.
Cliffs formed by flowing lava and water and wind form dramatic coastline of Jeju island, great place for photos, in sunny days nice walks, don't miss it

Clearly, going in early spring is not the best idea; water's still too cold for swimming but it was perfect to go walking barefoot in the fantastically clear water. It was pleasant to walk into random warm currents while chasing after fish in the shallow water. Our driver said it was the best beach on Jeju but he said that about Hallim Park too so I would not take his word for it.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .

Bring your jackets, better to be water proof! Cave temperature is around 10 plus degree or lower. Also ground is uneven so wear good shoes and walk slowly. But overall fascinating to see how geography works

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

Beautiful, according to our guide we hired he claims that the this is the only waterfall in South Korea that is sea side. The place is touch crowded and a bit of walk downhill from visitor location. Otherwise, totally worth the effort.
Beautiful waterfall. I walked to the area as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel in seogwipo). It's a huge waterfall, and a tourist attraction. The water is very clean.
Beautiful blue/green water  with white sand beach. We didn't get in the water since it was chilly, but it looks very shallow with some rocks.   Can park and walk along the beach shore.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

Anyone who can appreciate nature, especially geology, will love this. There are only about 5 countries in the world where you can go walk in a lava tube and South Korea is one of them.It's inexpensive to enter (2000won for those over 24, discounts for younger ages) and it is worth it.There are lights installed, but bring lights if you can. The ground is not paved and it's easy to trip. The cave also drips water, so there are puddles around. It was suuuuuper cold inside the cave in March-so cold that when we came outside to the 40 degree weather it felt like summer!!

A unique must-do in my books to go where lava has gone before.   It is also a cave, so it dark, a little chilly with the occasional water drop.  The cave is left largely in its raw form (which was great) but it also meant an uneven and potholed path which requires a great deal of care walking it.

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.

A really beautiful sight to behold! Its a short but steep walk down to the waterfall, with an entrance fee of 2000 won. You wont be able to get too up close and personal though - the waterfall   guards   get a little touchy if you get too close to the rocks that are wet.

A large colourful night club with large bar different seating areas and private booths and a water slide. Drinks the usual, but by sheer coincidence, being just 11.45pm when we came in, it was still my birthday by 15 mins and having my passport with me got a genuine full 75cl bottle of Johnny Walker Black Label Whisky !! Water and ice was also free but we had big beer chasers. The rest of the visit was fun but rather blurry. Just disappointed it didnt fill up, though it was mid-week.......

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It?s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn?t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.

1st falls was kinda disappointing cos there was no water coming down. Perhaps dry season? On the + side, the still water surface made excellent photo opp. After more staircases, we had the option to descend a long staircase to 2nd falls. Which we skipped and proceeded on. We crossed the bridge of the 7 nymphs - indeed an odd architecture with such a curved surface to near centre of bridge. Easiest is to walk in reverse to give the hamstrings some relief. Later on, there was a lookout point for 2nd falls. Yay. All done, we rewarded ourselves with icecream :)

We did the yeongsil walk and it was amazing. It was tough in parts of you are not used to hiking but walking all the kids and grandparents doing it lends you the stamina to keep going and gosh is it worth it. Some of the best scenery I have ever seen.
Visited on 17th October 2019.If you going with friend it would be great.A relax mini hiking walk along the breezy turquoise sea.It's a must go. Nice place to take photo too.

Wasn't planning to do any hiking, so just drove to Eorimok base station to experience the snow and took some photographs, as we came from a tropical country and never had any snow experience before. Turns out the drive up to the station is very beautiful with the snow covered trees along the road. The base station itself is also nice for a leisure walk especially for family with kids.

I have never seen anything like it. The walk was unbelievable! A must see and do in Seogwipo. Great for travellers who love nature, hiking (must wear comfortable shoes) and photography. Highly recommended.
I enjoyed it more than the group.  It's geared for those who are used to hiking.  Long lava tube - you don't have to walk the whole thing, but why not?  It is just 1 KM in and 1 KM out.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

This is highlight of my Jeju West Coast Trip; it's beautiful scenic walk; however its not an easy walk. My mother has difficulty to walk on this path and return to the entrance after 10 minutes walk. There are some woman divers selling abalone near the entrance and its quite fascinating to see them.I highly recommend to visit this attraction while you are in Jeju and its very close to Mount Sanbang where usually people visit for trekking.

The park was quiet when I visited. It was an easy walk with nice trees and scenery. It had a great calming effect on me. Love it. Just 5 minutes drive from the park is the Hanwha Resort Jeju which I went for a fantastic spa treatment. My afternoon was made perfect !

The Manjanggul Cave is splendid and provides an excellent Geology lessons on how the caves are formed over thousands of years. A must for cave lovers and nature lovers. The walk is relatively easy for elderly and young kids as well.

The footpaths were well-marked and easy to walk even for my 71-year-old mum. I enjoyed the walk and the fresh air. The only downside was there were a few noisy tourists around so it was not so calming an experience.

nice place to visit to see how nature works!!!....u can see how jeju was made thousands years ago.....beautiful cave!!!...but you must be fit to walk about 2km and walking in a slippery floor is not really easy in the dark....beautiful!!!!

I enjoyed walking through the park. It's was pretty. I didn't really like birds being caged though. Bonzai trees were fun and pretty cool. It's near one of the nicest beaches I ever been too.  It's an easy place to walk around with family.

Came with the cruise ship an easy walk up the park area. There are park gymnasium equipped area and a reflexology stoned path. There's a library and a museum around the vicinity. Nice to just walk around.

A pleasant walk among trees and nature. Many small flies hovering around at certain areas. A small cafe and convenience store near the entrance. An easy outing for elderly folks and a pleasant walk for families.
A must visit to this attraction . Entrance fee is 2000W . Short and easy walk to the cliffs . Expect to spend around 30-60minutes here if you want to take photos .

You need to bring jacket that day we went even if its summer still cold inside, wear rubber shoes easy for you to walk, though there's not much inside to see, young kids will not enjoy for sure they will just be tired walking very long cave.

We went up the Yeongsil side. Lots of parking cost was 1800 won. You drive about 2kms after paying.  Nice fairly easy walk. Still bits of remaining snow around. I could've done with putting my merino leggings on!  Still, forced me to walk faster!  Haha!

Walking through a lava tube is an incredible experience. You can see the flow of lava on the ground, the different historical depths of lava flow is visible on the wall due to the layers of layers, and other features such as the world?s largest lava column and lava rafts. Truly remarkable and easy to see why UNESCO regards this sight so highly.
Very easy to walk to. Eating places nearby. Very beautiful.  We had breakfast at Dunkin Doughnuts nearby. Cost is 2,000 won to see. Unique shopping near location.

this is the largert lava tube in the world (well, that we have found) and it's fascinating.  Really huge tube, interesting rock formations all through.  The walk is quite easy (a little uneven and damp, headlight recommended) and the informative signs are useful.  Not that expensive and well worth the trip.

This is one location where you do not have to worry about bad weather, actually I would recommend going here on a day with rain and wind since then you can actually experience the force of nature when the waves hit the cliffs.Easy access, parking (for a fee) and you can walk along the shore line on a board walk (sort of).

This forest has a nutmeg tree that is over 826 years old.  We enjoyed walking on the paths that weave through the forest.  Beautiful trees, flowers and lovely singing birds.  We saw a snake and loved the fresh smelling air.  There is a small store selling drinks and snacks and a small coffee shop.  No gift shop.  The paths are well maintained and very easy to walk on.

The place could get quite crowded, however, the rock formation was awesome, take a slow walk and enjoy the breeze. I visited this place with my mother, there are some stairs here and there, but it is an easy track, she doesn't have difficulty at all. Amazing Scenery

The museum has many airplanes on display and also an outdoor area where you can walk into the planes. ? Very well done, lots of information and displays. ? Hands on activities instructions are only in Korean, but easy to figure out. ? A steal for the 10,000 WON entrance fee.

Since the cave is managed by government, the ricket price is cheap. Just 2.000 won.It takes around 30 minutes in and 30 minutes out  of the cave. There we enough man-made lighting inside, and man-made path, so its easy to walk inside. Beautiful. Rare tourist attraction that might not exist in other places.
It was an okay park, easy and nice to walk around, the best part was the caves. Love exploring the caves!However, food choices are limited should one be hungry.
It is the first lava cave I visit, easy to walk in and the temperature is not too cold or too humid.
It is majestic by its dimension, inside temperature around 7 degree Celsius, easy to walk path, not slippery, must go destination

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.

Good sight seeing place and jungle trekking. Wear sport shoes for easy walking if you plan to walk   round the sea  . Weather was just nice for walking in April. Crossing the bridge and standing there watching the big sea was feeling awesome.
Cool scenic cliffs at the ocean, easy path to get to them, not a very long walk, highly recommend it.

A pretty long walk over some decent grounds and some stairs to get through the entire cave. Its a little chilly down there so bring some easy to shed clothing. Really a vast and large cave, not something you get to see very often elsewhere and for the small entry fee... you cant beat it.
You can find almost everything here from fresh seafood to local eateries to clothing stalls. Things may not be real cheap here but it's interesting to walk around.

Went around with a friend and the place is huge. I think we managed to walk from gate 8 to gate 4 before we realized we cane there looking to eat and ended up just window shopping because there?s lots to feast your eyes on. There?s mostly food and fresh produce and seafood and food products made from Jeju oranges.

Well is rather a unique Lava rock by the sea shore but to me it looks more like a Horse head. You may find people selling seafood by the side of the rock under simple canopy. Just be careful as you walk down to the sea because the rocks are hard .

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe.  There were many different types of tea for sale and all beautifully packaged.  Again thanks to the friend who asked us to help buy stuff for her we knew to get the green tea milk spread.  For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!
Very beautiful island and worth a full day to walk around. Nice ice cream but food there quite expensive.
The canoes were closed by 4 pm. I'm not sure if it was bc of the rain. So we just walked the grounds Boardwalk and skipped rocks at the black sand beach. There was live music and food places there.

It was very very very crowded with locals and tourists. The cafe food was alright but in my opinion too sweet. The green ice cream was aromatic but too creamy for my liking (after the green tea cake I had at Cafe Aewol de Monsant). The iced tea however was really good. It tasted like yuzu but then had a less sweeter and lighter taste. The place was filled with flowers and tea leaves and innisfree & innisfree cafe was within short walking distance (it?셲 connected). Good to come if you?셶e never been here before but probably won?셳 come for a second visit so soon.
It is interesting to walk around the shops and see the food and souvenirs they sell.The vendors are very friendly!
Cool falls near rocky coast.  Walk down into rocky coast and get sprayed by the falls.  There are women selling freshly caught seafood just near the fall. Great place to visit.
Came here just for the desserr and did not walk around in the area. So I can only comment on the food and it was great.Love all the cakes and ice cream here. The hallubong juice is so refreshing too.

The stacked cliffs of Yongmeori are beautiful! This was one of my favorite sites in Jeju. It's a very windy walk but in the summer, this provided respite from the humid heat. The rocks are uneven and bumpy, so it is a good idea to wear sturdy shoes.You have to pay a small fee but it's very much worth it. Along the walk, there are women selling raw seafood meals for 10,000 a pop. It's a very simple set-up: plastic stools and chairs, some garlic, gochujang, and soju if you wish.

Lovely peaceful spot , nice statue at the start then all the buddas on the walk up to the temple offset by the lanterns. The temple is nice take a good look at the food and painting but the golden Buddha at the side is worth a look. Nice cafe and shop on site well priced.

It is a quite tough for elderly to walk to the place in order to take great pictures (the usual spot that tourists will take pic). It is so windy and nice actually. You can see how the locals get the fresh seafood from the sea and consume it. Thou it is very fresh but I am not a fan of raw food hence, I pass! LOL
In a hurry up and go culture, it was nice to slow down and wind down walking through the gardens. Relax at the cafe and try the food.

I think that it's not as grand, but the stairs are well kept and in good shape. There's a lot of people and a lot of food too. Parking wasn't an issue for us.I've been twice, and maybe it wasn't anything special to me as I didn't get to go in the morning to watch the sunrise. But be prepared to walk up with a lot of people
Good to walk , and watch local food and ingridients...specially seafood, and souvenirs. Dont forget to pick up  ginseng to carry home.
Except for a few good and clear moments on the first afternoon, didn't get any clear day and was virtually rained in. But Seongsan was a nice little to walk around with some fabulous sea food places.

Did a soap-making session and had lunch at the Innisfree Jeju House. Building is well-lit and nice and open inside. Soap-making was a fun activity to do with our group, and I was able to make a custom souvenir to bring home. They had a selection of some products to purchase, but was small when comparing to the size of their stores. The lunch caf챕 had many options, and my super food salad was delicious. The caf챕 also offered many drinks and impressively decorated desserts. Directly outside are the tea fields that you can walk through and take pictures in.

Couldn't walk through the rock formation due to high tide when we visited that day around 11am , so we just took some picture with the lovely yellow color flowers for 1000 won per person entry , there's a horse ride nearby too with a old wooden ship , fresh seafood available, it was a good place to take pics .

Bring your own food or you can buy from the cafe nearby and sit by the stairs watching the locals fishing or enjoying the sea breeze. Beautiful red and white horse light-houses that stood out from far. We took a cab there and for return trip, just walked 5~10mins to grab a cab from the main road.
you will something is pulling you when you try to walk...real fun when you could get down and walk on the mysterious road
You need to pay 2000 won to do the beach walk . A rocky formation where people lay on flat stone to take sun. I guess it's up to you

You could park and walk to the falls. Entrance was 2000w. Opens at 0900 not crowded. You?re able to walk right up to the edge of the falls for great photos. Some available shops for souvenirs and snacks.

You can see the history of tea in Korea and world in general you can eat green tea ice cream and shop from a variety of products (face creams etc.) which are all made from green tea. There are tea farms outside also so that you can enjoy a short nice walk in these tea farms.
You can see a very beautiful scenery here including the crater. However we arrived on rainy day so the fog is thick and the crater is unseen. But we still happy walking around.

You can go underground and experience the cold temperatures close to 12 degrees.. its like walking through an igloo.. Cold air everywhere and some parts are wet due to the precipitation though the soil. Reminder to bring a jacket and good shoes as floor is slippery and area is dark! Very good experience!

Yongmeori is an excellent beauty but one has to walk along the coast during low tide to see its true beauty. The rock formation is unique n a city dweller like me walk each step with awe looking at the formations. I believe anyone who enjoys nature but is brought up in a concrete jungle will love this place.
Worthwhile to take 30 min in touring round and taking photos. Need to walk down a steep flight of around 50 stairs.
Worth a visit at least once. Pleasant walk round the folk village. Good collection. Could do better with more displays in English. But all in all thumbs-up for this place..
While there are numerous exhibits and really very well kept the visitors are few.  The signs are not that great and there is a lot of walking required.

When we were there they were having a special limited showing of the ancient art of making furniture jewelry boxes etc using shells.  The displays were beautiful and it was interesting to learn how involved the process is.  The museum was nice we went on a rainy day when we needed indoor activities.  The museum is laid out so you walk through different period of history.
Went there Sunday mid-morning. Car park was crowded with locals after /preparing for morning walk. Take a slow stroll to soak up nature's beauty. Boardwalk wide enough for wheelchair access.
Went on a rainy day but most importantly wear comfortable clothing and walking shoes that won't slip on rocks.. Also bring a sweater or wear long sleeve as it gets colder further inside.
Well maintained. It is basically a km long walk into a cave (which is created by lava). Some structures inside from the lava. But otherwise nothing interesting. It is cold in there so be prepared.

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.

We were mesmerized with the glass art. Such detailed work! The route made it easier to walk and enjoy all the glass art. Admission fee is 11 000 won. There were also one part of the park that showed glass palace  but we end up walking about 10minutes and no castle was in our sight  quite disappointed. P/S: you can find cute fridge magnet of jeju at the end of the souvenir shop. There were only 1 000 won for one. Very cheap for a fridge magnet I think.
We went to this after our Seopwipo Submarine tour.? Very relaxing to walk especially early in the morning or at night.

We went there with a tour group as part of a package.  It's basically a long walk in the park with a bunch of photo ops.If we had kids with us I would think it was OK.  But not for a couple of retired folks.
We went there on January so the weather is a bit cold. It's nice to walk around and learn more Korean Culture.

We went here in a sunny morning and took a glance for the natural six-edges poles. We enjoy the mild sea breeze together with stunning scenery here.There was a giant seashell in the entrance and you may sat inside to take a funny photo. You could also enjoy a short walk for Olle route here if you wish.

We walked through the Sex and Health Museum and took some crazy pictures!  It is a large museum with many different themed areas.  There is a sex education hall showing sexual positions differences in male and female pregnancy and more.  Other halls have sexual movies playing displays of sexual cultures from all over the world lifelike sex dolls and the craziest statues of things like a humongous penis.  Overall we enjoyed the museum had many good humored laughs and got some funny pictures.

We walked over the bridge to get to Cheonjeyeon Falls. I didn't think too much of it. When we were below the bridge level and I looked up  I was very pleasantly surprised by the beautiful dragon motifs on the side of the bridge.

We walked in at 5:30pm. The place was lit and was surprised by the size of the garden. Wouldn’t recommend it any earlier since you will not be able to enjoy all the lights...Must visit inside studio where a lot of sets are set up with the lights for DIY semi-professional photo shoot.The staff were very nice and offered to take photos for you.
We visited this place and you can see the explanation of the art works while walking to this museum. Can visit for children to see =)
we visited the museum which located just five minutes walking from Lotte Hotel. It is excellent place for a visit.

We stayed in a resort on walking distance from this beach. Especially early in the morning the waves are good. Quite a bunch of surf school offer lessons and boards for hire. There's a special section for swimmers however this is much too small.

We spent a half day here for a short walk. It was such a peaceful and relaxing place. You could see many coastal rocks and Udo. If you like  you could ride a horse to wander a while. You may also visit the lighthouse and the chapel nearby. This was one of must go tourist points in Jeju!
We really enjoyed this part of the weekend. I would even like to return. Superior glass art and plenty of outdoor walking through the facilities. Highly recommend this be on your short list.

We planned to see the crater with the mind of seeing the silver grass. We arrived at 1600 which was 2hrs from closing. It was quite quiet with most tourisg leaving the attraction. We entered after purchasing our tickets at 6000 won per person. It was a short walk before arriving at the silver grass.  It was really beautiful. We managed thi catch the sun set and the silver grass seemed to be glowing. Pictures were fantastic.
We loved walking throughout the cave and having the experience of walking on something that was once lava.  It is cheap and impressive.  Check out the worlds largest lava stack.

We learned a lots about how lava tube was formed and get to experience these natural phenomenon hands on. The kids thoroughly enjoyed the walk as well. Walking inside can be a bit tricky as it?s not flat and some part can be a wet and slippery. Overall a very educational trip for us.

We had heard about the tea plantation first on the television show Kimchi Chronicles on PBS (http://www.kimchichronicles.tv/). As an avid tea drinker I could hardly pass up the chance to check it out in person and it is amazing. We drank tea walked in the tea fields checked out the tea museum watched the roasting of tea bought tea tea soap tea lotion and tea ice cream. The museum and center are quite stunning and the drive out there interesting on some very well maintained roads. Don't miss this one if you are on Jeju Island.
We enjoyed walking until the end point.It is recommended during summer since inside the cave is cool ..

We engaged a Local private driver to bring us to Yongmeori Coast. He made a call to the Relevant Authority to check the weather and tide condition. Yongmeori Coast is situated beside Mt Sanbangsan.The car park was full that day and fortunately we found one lot. Our driver guided us the walking route to the coast.He was indeed a good private tour guide!We were immense into the nature and its beauty. He skilfully captured many memories into pics for us! This trip was my most memorable part in Jeju.

We discovered Jeju Mokgwan (the Governors historical admin center) when we drove past it then walked to it from our hotel. Of all the places we visited in Jeju City it was our favorite. Most of the signage included English translations of how Jeju-do was run in the past. The buildings are well restored pieces of art. Very relaxing.  There were also ancient games for children. The venue seemed to be set up mostly for locals for who this venue is free. Foreigners enter for a nominal fee.If you found this rating beneficial please click the helpful button.

We came with high hopes of being awed by beautiful camellia Flowers but left disappointed. There was really nothing much except the blooming flowers in the greenhouses. Maybe it was the timing of our visit but we felt cheated. Be prepared to walk a bit to visit the various parts of the park. I will not recommend this park.

We arrived early morning but a crowd had already built up with a school trip group from Seoul. All the rides were prebooked and the earliest rides available was after 2pm that day. We took a walk on the boardwalk alongside and that was nice too.
Walking through the lava tubes is just an amazing experience.  It is surreal and beautiful to see what millennia of lava flow has created.  One of the best places to see on Jeju Island.

Visited this amazing cave recently with the kids. Aged between 7-13 years old. We all enjoyed it. Remember to bring along a jacket as the cave can be quite cold. It?s about 11 degree Celsius. Wear a pair of good shoes too as the walking surface is uneven and wet.
Visited the park when it was raining. Still very enjoyable and there is some sort a mini bird park in there. Very interesting and relaxing walk through the park.

Very cool place to take some nice pics.If you leave the area where you have to pay and walk torwards east you will have different coast lines where you can acces the lava rocks and walk around on them and as well take some pics they look like you landed on mars.

Unfortunately  I cannot say that this place is worth visiting. The surrounding area and sites (Sanbangsan and the temple  Yongmeori Coast) are worth the visit though  and I speculate that this is the only reason the museum has survived.The ship museum itself provides information about the Dutch sailor who landed on Jeju and was held captive and against his will for several years by Koreans (not sure why this is a source of pride as it seems to be made out). The story itself could be quite interesting  but to be honest  I would rather read about it in a well-written book than in a tacky and very cheesy museum using broken English. Children might enjoy walking through the ship replica so I suppose it could be worth visiting if you also visited the other nearby sites.I personally would never recommend this place to anyone.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안

The temple is extremely new as it was built only in 1990s. The outlook was grand and the temple architectural style was reminiscent of the early Korean Joseon Dynasty.  Buddhism in Jeju is unique with its own characteristics and distinctive feature. Unlike the main stream counterpart in mainland Korea Jeju's Buddhism accepts combines and adapt to the local characteristics to form an integrated form of its own. The native folks were staunch followers of Shamanistic beliefs pray to stone deities and attend to superstitious rituals but Buddhism in Jeju embodied the local belief in her Buddhist temples. Behind the Shamanistic gods idols stood the compassionate and tolerant statue of Buddha. Jeju is famous for her natural environment and Jeju's Buddhism takes a natural path towards enlightenment. In fact the repressive Joeson Dynasty suppressed Buddhism but this Buddhist temple incorporated the beauty of the Joseon temple architectural style with Buddhism worship. The compassionate hands of the Buddha practiced acceptance and non-hatred non violence in pursuit of the emancipation of the human soul. I observed that the Buddha statues in the prayer hall were magnificently golden and the grand prayer hall with a height of 28 m was reputed to be the largest in Asia. The ambience here was tranquil and serene. It was a place most suitable for meditation and prayer. I walked around the temple and felt the calmness and peacefulness in the air. From a distance I could hear the dim chanting of the Buddhist prayer. Historically this lovely island of Jeju had suffered tremendously under the repressive hands of the Mongol Empire and also during the Japanese tyrannical rule. But the island survived with the most scenic and gorgeous natural wonders of the world and may this temple bring continual peace to this natural place!.

Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Walking on the Olle is nice--a great pilgrimage for healing. If you really want to know about the unique history of Jeju and the Korean Peninsula however you must visit this museum. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The highlight of this museum is its peace garden. This huge garden made me pray for peace in the Korean peninsula.

The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. A fun and interesting maze to walk through. The map is a definitely must have or it will be challenging.

2000 won fee and well wooden path for tourist. Wind can be very strong since at the open sea and you can imagine the conditions in bad weather. If you like geography this is very interesting. Otherwise still a good place for some photo and walk in the south of the island.

You can walk around under the shade of thick netmeg trees. Also, you can enjoy basking in the woods. The oldest tree is about eight hundred and fifty years old.
You can walk along the shore and admire the nature artist who created wonderful coastline and statue made from stone. It's very scenic, photogenic and good exercise for your body.

You can find all kinds of teddy bears in the museum and the   cosplay  is simply amazing. I was impressed by how creative they are. There is a garden behind the museum for which you can have a short walk with a couple of photos.
You can enjoy a cool breeze and a walk around the yongduam area. The dragon head is not that interesting but since it's free admission, why not? We spent about 20 minutes walking around the area.

Yes, it's just a cave. Nothing much there besides a long, large, cool and dark cave with uneven walking path. The walk path is uneven and wet. Please wear good walking shoes and that will be good if you have flashlight. I will not recon to bring kids or old folks to this attraction. I saw only 1 security camera at the entrance but none in the cave and no workers in the cave. So, if someone injured or any emergency help, I guess no one can help you except other tourist.

Whilst attending a conference at the ICC Jeju I took a walk to see this larva rock cliff. It's fabulous and well worth seeing if you are on Jeju. Must admit, the boat trip to see the cliffs up close looked really good.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. Although the path throught the three sections of the cave are shorter, you can see much more. Go to Halim Park and skip Manjang Cave.

While the Crater is interesting and as is usual presented well, by Korean standards the prices are excessive.There are many more things to see on Jeju for free (or a minimal charge) that I can't understand why this was so expensive.The grounds are attractive and the path well made.However it was not possible to get really close to the crater and I would have liked to walk the rim.I wouldn't bother including it on your itinerary, unless you are a fan of the drama that is shot there.
Well worth the walk.Words are not enough to explain the beauty, the sounds of thunder and the vision

Well worth the visit, especially if geology is your interest.Plenty of stairs in and out of the cave so not too advisable for elderly, or families with babies/ toddlers. (though i did bring both!) Being a lava tube, the flooring can be uneven and slippery within the cave so wear proper footwear.It will be cold and dimly lit down in the lava tube, so bring your sweaters if chill is a concern.The walk long to and fro the end, so be prepared.After the first half to the end, it can get boring for some especially the kids. That said it is still a unique experience for many.

We were very excited to visit Manjanggul Cave, and it did not disappoint.It is quite a large cave, and if you walk slowly and look around at the cave carefully, you can see the changes of the lava formation colours and shapes.Make sure you walk the entire length to check out the lava tube, I mean - when will you get another chance? Also make sure you wear comfortable shoes, as my recommendation of walking slowly is not just to check out the different sections, it also means you won't trip, as the ground is pretty uneven and the cave is quite dimly lit!

We were up early and looking for something that was also open early and found Halla Arboretum. Right in Jeju City and east to get to yet plenty of space, beautiful paths and forests to walk through. Great morning activity with early rising kids ans it?s free.

We were at Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon before we went to Manjanggul. It was a god decision as it was a brief respite from the scorching sun.That aside, this place is itself a gem. Well maintained and interesting facts have their own boards for the visitors to read. Light jacket is highly recommended if you don't like cool places. Temperature is similar to if you blast your AC unit in your room. Very nice. Wear good shoes. Slippers and heels / platforms not recommended although we saw several girls wore them. You'll be walking on solidified lava. Hence, the walking surface is very unkind to ill-equipped feet. :).Overall, very good experience.
We went with friends who had kids and everyone enjoyed walking around the buildings, statues and garden.

We went to the Jungmun Golf Club to have a Moonlight Walking Tour as part of the preparation for the 2020 Jeju Olle Walking Festival. This place is worth a visit as the rock and the surrounding area is lovely. The foot path was well-designed, making the walk enjoyable.

This is the longest lava tube in the world.  It's 7kms long and only 1km is open to the public.  It's rather spectacular to be in it, to appreciate the wonders of Nature.
