For me, it's a been there, done that experience.  Enough said!

This is the first UNESCO world heritage that we visited in Korea. Walking distance about 1km, so be prepared to wear the comfort shoe. Some area a bit dark so be careful. Overall nice experience to visit this nature cave.

This is one of the longest lava tubes in the world and a World Heritage Site. You are able to walk for about 1km and return. We enjoyed the walk, especially as it was so hot outside and nice and cool inside.

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn?t find some key sights.

this is a very good island in jeju, just about 10min from the pier to there and meanwhile you can see many seagulls follow the boat, just for asking the snack in your hand~the island is a good place for a walk, or you can rent a bike, motorbike or electric car(these 2 types needa an international car license) just nearby the pier.and please remember to bring your passport to there cos you needa show your passport when you buy the boat ticket.

This is a seriously big lava tube. In fact, as lava tubes go I think it's one of the biggest. Definitely a whopper! The whole thing is almost 8km long, but the section open to the public is just 1km. You descend steps and walk along the dimly lit tube. There are some things to look at like lava 'rafts' (lumps of lava that have floated along) and lava stalactites (lumps of lava that have dripped from the ceiling) and at the end a lava column (where lava has poured in through a hole in the ceiling and formed a column). In short, it's lava-ly!

This is a real village with households living inside, opposite from folk villages built in museums. In fact, the people live there are mainly the haenyeo (women divers) - there is a museum for them in the east coast of Jeju. There is no entrance fee, so the village depends on the sale of souvenirs, basically the blueberries fermented drink and the organic skin creams. A volunteer will assist you to walk around the town, which is very helpful. A site note is that it is often used as a movie set, for example for the movie entitled Dae Jang Gum.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.
This is a huge park and we go around by trains. Not much to see other than natural scenes, but good to walk around. Access is not convenient, you need cars.

This ancient historical & cultural village was meant to show its rich origin & history. Therefore, it was left intentionally in its original state ie old, rundown & unmodernised. Living in an ultra modern city, it was a very humbling experience for us to be able to witness what living conditions were like in those days.It is a very small village, so obviously there aren't much to see or photos to take. There were big portraits of the 2 lead casts of the famous Korean drama   A Jewel of the Palace,   filmed in 2003. This drama probably spark off the K-Wave phenomena worldwide. Maybe this was one of the filming sites.The resident guide gave us a walk & run up of the place. After which, we went to a small hut where she was explaining the honey & other products of this village.Sampling of honey was given. She did not hard sell nor push anyone to buy. It was the visitors' own free will if to buy.Many in our group (including us) bought the honey because they loved it & not because they were scammed or hard-sold.

This ?Unesco? lava grot is quite nice. You can walk a kilometer underground in a dark cave with lots of information panels in English and Korean/Hangul. The Floor is uneven and the temperature is ten degrees Celsius. We did not expect something special, but overal it was a nice experience with a rewarding pilar at the end of the walk.

There is only 1 main maze park that separate into left and right wing. However, the maze park is not as big as expected. You will need to walk through the park and follow your   six sense   in order to reached the destination and ring the bell to prove that you have walk out from the maze. ;)

There is a train servicing in the theme park that will drop the visitors to every station and allow them to walk around and take photo. As of the name   Eco   the theme park is closed to the mother of nature which basically full with plants and trees. Besides, highly recommend the lavender ice cream in the lavender and rose garden station.

There is a cafe at level 2 and a small gift shop selling Hallabong items after walking through their tangerines greenhouse. There is also a small museum where kids could learn about tangerines but they are mostly in Korean.Outside  the korean fans dedicated a small hectre of tangerine plantation to G-Dragon. There is even a Kwon Jiyong Tree. But since we were there in late March  the weather was still pretty chilly  so the leaves are not growing yet.You could ask the reception where it is  its just nearby. However do try asking them as   G-Dragon   forest. i tried saying as   GD    but they dont really get it. Lol.

There are many beautiful walks along this southern side of Jeju and this is another one. As it was so hot when we visited, our driver took us to a swimming hole among the rocks, down some steep steps at the opposite end of the walk to Oedolgae itself. Our families loved this very much.

There are beautiful indoor and outdoor displays of blown glass in a variety of formats.  The indoor display includes masterpieces, many by the Italian master, Signoretto.  The outdoor displays make for a great walk about through a beautiful park-like area.

The visit to Bijarim Forest is a relaxing visit with a closer touch to the nature, feeling calm and peace. The trees looks aged and birds chirping, soft wind blowing. There are many locals walking or jogging in the forest during my visit. I would love to revisit it again if I visit Jeju again.
The texture of the cave and the formation were very interesting and unique. The walk into the cave was a bit tedious due to the uneven ground. Otherwise, had a great outing.

The rocks surrounded by the island have different size and have eroded for years. But the most interesting thing is that rocks are eroded into different levels of cylinders, so it is worth to spend a couple of minutes there taking photos and have a look. Moreover, there are paths for visitors to walk around the edges of the island to have different look of the rocks. It is the margin of Jeju, so when the wave flaps the cliffs, it creates a huge noise. At first, I thought it was something like weapons exposed, my heart pumped faster than normal. After I recognize it is only the wave hits the cliffs, I can clearly experience that how the level of power that the nature can be. It was an unforgettable experience.So, if you have an iPhone which contains the program of Live Photo, try to open it before you take photos. It is because you can record the energetic movement of wave in your photo.
The place is nice and well maintained, it was a bit cold down there so i would suggest a light sweater and comfy shoes as the floor was uneven with lava stone and made it hard to walk
The place defitinely not suitable for elder people. Is too long walk for them and the long stair case. However, is an amazing place to visit.

The park is a unique in the sense that it is dedicated to stones in Jeju culture. Lots of statues, pavilion with the history of volcanic activity, some traditional houses, old sculptures, big and small. Large space, a lot of walking.

The museum was ok, computers and computer games are not my kind of thing but it was interactive so really kept me engaged.The keyboard-shaped waffles in the cafe with four side sauces/cream/ice-cream in the cafe in the basement are awesome. Go for them!Walkable from Nohyung Lotte Mart.

The main part of this beach is full of kids and you will need to pay to sit on the beach...(there are table services). Also, the area is restricted. You can only go to a certain area. Instead, if you go to another part, which is 10mins by walk, you can enjoy more and free to sit... This beach does not have many waves.

The floor is uneven and the lighting is dim, not for those with walking issues. Nice place to see the strange wall formation due to lava. Only 1 km and mostly even.  The tourists can be a bit noisy, hope the bats in the other parts are not too disturbed

The dragon head rock is a good place to visit, if your wanting to stay close to jeju si. It doesnt take long to look at the rock and there are many tourists but the costal road is a nice relaxing walk.
The cliff is amazing with a nice park to walk around. After the stroll, we visited to ICC duty free shop for shopping.
The cave is dark and cold especially nearing winter. If you are into cave exploration, then be sure to bring along a flashlight to brighten up. Be careful walking in the cave.

the cave is 1 km long you walk mostly in dark.not too.kuch to seeat the end there is a pillar but if you have been to.caves in the world before, it's not as fascinating as you see on the pictures not a real must

The cave has a number of formations throughout and there are information boards explaining what they re, and the English is good. The cave was a cool 13 degrees when I went down but outside was 34 so it was a welcome temperature.The steps down are a little deep so if you have vertigo or need help walking, it could be a little tough. It is wet under foot, I walked in flipflops and it was ok, but if you are a bit unsure of your footing, wear trainers. The cave is lit well  but some lights shine up into your eyes, which I found incredibly annoying, as it ruined my night vision. There are some areas with wooden bridges over the areas very difficult to walk on, so you aren't constantly in need of watching your footing.Worth a visit, as it it is not something you will see in many other places. I have been twice now, and it seems much more tourist friendly now.

The cave floor is uneven combined with inadequate lighting makes the winter walk very uncomfortable and after some distance, we gave up. Our youngsters were bored as the couldn't see the cave's beautiful features. Rather disappointed.

The beach itself could do with some TLC from the council.   There is a lot of debris which washes up daily onto the beach and along the coastal walk. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.

Straight from the hotel looking something to eat and just found out that our hotel is quite near to Black Pork Street just 15 minutes walking distance. Randomly choose one restaurant to have late lunch. Since the special here is black pork so I order 2 portion. The black pork was really good! It was more tender than the usual pork, the price also okay.

Stayed by Hyeopjae beach two nights, wish we stayed longer.Lovely place with a real local feeling, many caf챕s and restaurants around.Large and free car park.Don?t miss the beer battered chicken with beer by the walk down to the beach, opposite to the foot cleaning bath

Seemed this is a set-up village with less than 5 residents. Walking around this village, I don't even find any children running around the village. Saw only one sample black pig in the sty. At the end of the walk around, we were escorted to a small hut to listen to the sales talk on their tea, wine, horse bone products. Can treat this place as a tourist trap or a toilet breaks.
Really nice for walking. Quiet, peaceful and quaint place. It is good place to rest from cities and people.

Really nice dinner at decent prices.I can't say which resturant is the best because I didn't try them all, but it's sure a nice area for dinner and BBQ Pork.There are also some 'smaller' restaurants round the cornerk (just 2 mins walk off the main black pork street signage.Was recommended by a local sales girl as we were making a purchase for some beauti products.One of the best dinner we had in Jeju at a decent 25,000Won. Can't be cheaper for what we were served.
Plenty to see here including traditional houses, a museum and plenty of... stones. Nothing special but a nice place to enjoy a walk.

PLAYKPOP, Must visit place in Jeju island.You can enjoy K-POP star?s concert such as GD, BIGBANG, AOA, PSY and more everyday, also can experience exciting date with G-dragon only at PLAYKPOP! PLAY KPOP is a future-oriented digital theme park where both children and adults can enjoy singing and dancing like a true star. You can also buy the STAR GOODS and jeju souvenirs at PLAYKPOP SHOP! There're many kinds of VR experience. The seat type of Jeju travel, urban pursuit and full-body walking VR,such as Mystery jungle, dark mage, haunted house.

Place kinda small, outdated. You will probably like the outdoor more than the indoor. You would walk through glass sculptures illuminated at night. So recommended to visit at night. There is a workshop where they will help you to make your own glass work. It is also a great chance to learn glass work.

Place for everyone who like caves, volcanos or geology. The cave is long, but the one kilometre available for tourists is enough. There are many interesting lava formations, described in English. Beside that the cave is just beautiful. The temperature inside is around 10째C, humidity close to 100%. If you are not very fond of caves, stones or walking, probably you should skip it. :-)

Personally, this is my least favourite falls in Jeju.  Nothing special about it except that it is a fall that flows directly to the sea.  The walk down the steps to the falls are fine but I do not recommend walking on the rocks to be nearer to the rocks.  Kids and senior citizens should not attempt that is it is rather dangerous.  You can still see and take photo of the fall from a further distance.  Not worth injury during your holidays!

Perfect for couples to take a romantic walk through the woods. Be sure to take the shortcut if you just want to get to the end of it quickly and see the oldest tree around, or if you're a romantic be sure to take the long route and walk hand in hand with your beloved. Enjoyed the refreshing walk and highly recommended.

One of the best UNESCO place. Worth it to come here and visit this place. We spent approximately 50minutes here included walking and taking photos. The addmission fees is ??2,000 per person still affordable for me and the rate still the same as we went here last year. The parking space were spacious with numerous parking units available for visitors. Gentle reminder, please be cautious on your steps as some of the areas are quite dark and jacket is a must to wear to enter this lava tube place.
Nothing too spectacular, but it's a nice walk along the coast. Restaurants nearby for dinner and a drink. If you're in the area, check it out!

Not many such places are open to public visit, so I will say this is something interesting to explore if you visit Jeju. Temperature is lower than outside, so do bring a jacket or wear long sleeves if you are scare of cold. Physical mobility is required as there are steep steps to walk down to the entrance and paths are uneven.There is a restaurant and convenient store on site. We had lunch at the restaurant after the visit. Pretty decent Korean meals. Have translation app ready if you do not read Korean as menu is in Korean .

No ! Not again another Fall ! But this one worth the peaceful walk in a nice park and by a small river. If you pass by, go there. You have to see the harbour with small fishing boats. I liked this even better.
nicely labelled signs to explain the lava tubereally awesome to see the marks left by nature it's about a slow walk of about an hr, wear good shoes and a jacket as it gets cold
Nice walk around to see different carvings of stones which we took lots of picture with. Not spectacular, but nice to see. There is a small entrance fee.
Nice walk along the shore and take a few photos near the airport, tourist information, gift shops and casino.

Nice place to visit. U walk into the tunnel until its very derp end almost 1km in..... Then finally at the end of the tunnel u will get to see the light and the only stalagmite in the entire cave.... Lights in the caves are sufficient but not bright enough. The thing is, we thought the wet floors would be slippery but surprisingly thruout our entire walk into and out of the cave, there was absolutely no spot thatvwas slippery, thanks to the natural grooves on the ground which may have been created by the lava flow hundreds of years ago. Nice to explore, but obviously not for those who are claustrophobic.

Nice place to have a relaxing walk with lots of trees and plants. If you are there try to visit the herbal cafe with the ostrich and peacocks just beside it, it was very nice having a cup of tea there.

Nice place to go for a walk through the fields. The   museum   itself is not much and very little in English. The tea shop is OK with great but expensive green tea ice cream.The best bit is the other   Innisfree   shop and coffee shop in the grounds. Nice range of teas and coffees and interesting snacks. Inside and outside seating available. There are also stations in the shop to shape and   flavour   soap - if you buy the $15 kit that is. instructions on the supplied Ipad in several different languages.

Never been to lava cave before..it's fascinating..the colour led lighting makes the cave more beautifull..to reach the end of a cave you had to walk for about 1km..maybe because it's rain outside,the temperature inside the cave is more colder..you should wear a long shirt and a long pants..

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.

My family was recommended by our (Nam Yang Taxi) driver cum guide to this   must visit   place which was not in our initial planned itinerary. We are so glad to visit this captivating cliff by the beautiful blue sea!! It was a breezy cosy walk enjoying the marvelous scenery and shoreline natural volcanic black stone. It wasn't difficult for my parent (just walk at own comfort pace) especially for my dad whom was aided/help by our taxi driver/guide whenever required. This is our most loved sightseeing venue among others. Indeed a   must-see   attraction!!
Must visit.  Remember to bring a light jacket with comfort and non slip shoes.  It is about 40 mins walking, but worth it.

Manjanggul is a nature creation which 1km of it is opened for visitors to walk through. However majestic it is, if you are not a keen learner of geography or stones and cave, this walk would be boring for you. If you are there in Jeju for a short trip, I would recommend you to skip this instead.

Manjanggul Cave came to me as a surprise. To walk in a lava tube is an enchanting experience. There are steep stairs and long walk so be prepared. Don't bring heavy bags. Wear jacket because its cold inside the cave. Bring good camera. As you enter the cave, you will see the limestone that looks like lava flow (see picture attached). The path is dim that completes the enchanting atmosphere. By the end of the road, you can see the lava column.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world. It is one of the UNESCO heritage. There's a good 1km walk from the entrance of the cave til you get to the end of the tunnel to sight the beautiful stalactites.  The tunnel is of course much longer than that however access is only allowed up to the 1km mark. The path is dark, chilly,  rocky and slippery. Please wear good shoes and bring a jumper and mini torchlight if you wish.

Manjang cave in overall was really nice expierence, but we got a bit cold.When outside is more than 30 degrees, and you go downstairs, it's a bit...cool.And wet as well.But I won't whine about it, because the expierence you get there is more important!We were walking really slowly taking pictures of everything (if you don't have a good camera, pictures won't bet any good ://)They have diferent color lights and it makes cave more visitor-friendly.Only thing is that there is really crowded...Even though we went there on a weekday.So be prepared to see a lot of people there as well.
Love this beach! Sand was soft and the sea was beautiful. We walked to the extreme left and it was peaceful, quiet and secluded.

Love love love. Everything was beautiful. If you like just seeing different glass art works this is the place for you. It was between $11-12 for entry but of the   museums   in korea  this one is my favorite (lived in korea for 4 years). The jungle walk through that starts with some dinosaurs is kind of long but very gorgeous

Love Hallim Park! My expectation was a quick walk around an outdoor park, but it was so much more! Easily taking an entire day if you want it to, you can meander through under ground lava tubes, fruit orchards, small animal zoos, bonsai tree forests, etc.! Highly recommended.

Korea can feel very touristy and materialistic. Udo is the antidote to this. A beautiful, small island... with stone fences and perfectly kept fields of rye. Cute cafes and stone beaches. You can walk all over or cycle or drive your own rickshaw. Picturesque and less changed by tourism. I wished I had spend 2-3 days here instead of Jeju.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.
Just another cave. Cold and damp, dark and wet. However, it is one of the Unesco heritage site. Hence you should pay a visit. Just walk in 1km and another 1km out.

Jeju's teddy bear museum is one of the most iconic destinations. I first heard about it from watching the show Goong years ago, and decided I had to visit it if I ever went to Jeju island. It was a small museum, but nonetheless i'm glad I paid a visit. The museum is a short walk from The Shilla Jeju  , which is where we stayed.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.

Jeju Glass Castle is the famous place at Jeju. When I first went inside, I just like walk in an unreal place. Since the entire thing is made by glass. You can see glass everywhere, such as the flowers, the trees and the artworks.One of the special things in this castle is an artwork that calls ?a moment of musical concert?, this artwork show that the moment of a band that is performing. The entire performers have different emotion and music instruments. It is very hard to do this, because each performer?s face is smaller than a coin.Here also have some funny place, such as Glass labyrinth and distorting mirror. Be careful, maybe you will lose in the labyrinth, or become a fat boy/girl in the distorting mirror.Finally, I suggest that you need to be very careful in this castle, if not you will break the glass.

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

I've never been in a lava tube before, but it was a lot like a cave. The formations inside are pretty interesting and the park does a good job lighting them colorfully. It was a nice walk. However, it is very touristy and if you've been to bigger caves in other parts of the world it's just cool, not extremely impressive.
It's where the locals go to shop. Fun walking around seeing what is being offered and mingling with the locals. I never realized there were so many varieties of the Korean classic, Kimchi.
It's quite a long walk to the end and return but I enjoy myself. wear suitable shoes, its rocky, wet and limited light source.
its just a bridge but over the other side is a nice little island you can go for a walk around,very touristy area.

Its definitely a worthwhile trip to make and just walking through the Lava Tube is quite an experience.  It is not everyday one has the opportunity to walk through and see the various formations, the caves formed, columns, the different textures formed, etc.One needs to be relatively fit to do the walk with comfortable shoes as the location tends to be wet. Elderly should have a walking stick which will help and carry a torchlight.  Its a few degrees lower underground.

it's definitely a unique place to visit but you should wear proper shoes as the 2km walk to and from the entrance has lots of rocky areas...the cave was dark,cold and wet but worth the visit if it's part of your tour.
It's definitely a different weather from the above, pls bring along jacket if you enter. The attraction is really worth for a kilometre walk.
its better to discover the place in summer, but enjoyed the cold and excitement, walking around feels better

It's a nice place for a stroll, especially in the late afternoon or early evening, that's when the bridge will be lighted up. The bridge leads to Saeseum island where you can walk around it and enjoy the scenery

It's a nice bridge, and takes you across to the little island on the other side. Not really a lot to see apart from passing through the quaint port and adjacent coastline. Would suit you if you just wanted to go out for a relaxing walk along a peaceful area.

It's a natural wonder.  Amazing how lava can create a tunnel as large as this. Must visit when in Jeju.  Wear a pair of walking shoes and an autumn jacket as temperature falls to around 15 inside the tube. It'll take you at least 30 minutes to walk 1km in and then another 30 minutes out.  So,  it's pretty chilly if you are without a jacket. Floor is wet therefore walk carefully & enjoy the unusual sights especially the walls & ceiling of the tube. Walk until the end as there's a lava column in there, the only one.
It's 1km walk.You can learn about geographical things about caves as you walk by.It is colder than outside, you should bring clothes with you.
It?s like a Learning journey, pretty cold 8 degree) and dark in the cave.Just need to follow the pavement and keep walking to the end of the cave.
It will be a good place to visit for educational purposes. Nice to be walking in a lava tube. Not a must go attraction but if you have children, it will be good to bring them there.

It was raining when we reached the place. From the parking area, you will see this beautiful crater. As we are slowly walking up the slope, the wind was too strong for us to walk further up.Decided not to go up, but must had to take a few photographs of this beautiful place with the wind, rain and waves.On Normal day, there is also diving show by the famous Sea Women - Haenyeo. Mostly are 50 and above who dive for a living.Try to plan the visit during normal weather.

It was around a 20 minute walk into the cave and another 20 minutes going out... Path was dark and wet, so you must be careful walking inside the cave... It was a good experience with a little workout.

It was an interesting experience to walk through the 1km long tunnel if you enjoy understanding and seeing the various structures and rock formations formed from the lava flow. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!
It was a chilly walk up the slopes but a must-visit place on your list if u do go to Jeju island.We had many lovely photos taken there, that we brought home and i look at them a lot.

It is really long cave. Pls wear sensible shoes and high heels are NO NO there.I think it is nice for the first 15 min but after 15min it all looks the same. So unless you really knows you rocks well, or else it will be just a walking trip
It is just a long, dark, unending walk in a tunnel and nothing to see.Just a nice temperature inside. Don't bother and not suitable for older people...

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

It is a dood place to walk, think, and stare.....  Many people  come with families & friends Children have a lot of pace to play. One can  have a lunch  at the restaurant. It is a  great beautiful park   within Jeju Si.
Intriguing to see teddy bear in different sizes, shapes and costumes! Enjoyed our walk in the garden as well!

In my opinion, there are two world heritage sites that visitors to Jeju must visit. One is Manjanggul Cave and the other one is Seongsan Illchubong. Manjanggul Cave is unique as it was formed by lava movement thousands of years ago. It provides an insight into Jeju's geographical structure. The temperature in the cave could be chilly, so bring a jacket along. Visitors to the cave usually walked for about 2 km to reach the end, where photos with a large stalactite pillar could be taken. Other features in the cave include lava formations that look like elephant feet, turtles and book shelves.

I'm from Hawaii, but this cave was very impressive, not to mention a welcome reprieve from the heat and humidity!Walking on wet lava rock is not for the faint-of-heart, so wear a good pair of tennis shoes that can provide some traction, because it is slippery!

If you love nature and have never seen any volcanic formation before, it would be worth the visit. Personally,  i enjoyed walking inside the cave and having a look at the volcanic formation.  It's like you can almost imagine how the lava flowed inside the tunnel a few thousand years ago :) i was in awe of how powerful mother nature can be. It was quite cold inside. Wear layers and proper shoes.  Can be quite slippery as well.

If you like quirky and somewhat kitschy glass sculptures, you?ll love this place. If not it?s not worth the relatively high ticket price. It?s a nice outdoor area and some lovely walks. It?ll be also fun for kids I guess. But it was a bit too much kitsch for my liking.
If you have not experience going into a lava tube, you have to try Manjanggul Cave. A nice 30 mins walk inside the tube, and you will find a beautiful Manjang-gul at the end of the tube.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.
if you go by walk don't bother to go there, you can't notice anything apart from cars driving very slow

If you are interested in caves at all, this one is unique.  Easily accessible, this horizontal lava tube demonstrates the vocanic processes happening over 100,000 years ago.  Cool, wet and accessible with helpful descriptions in multiple languages and little anthropromorphizing of geological shapes.  A quick visit taught us a lot....and our 7 and 10 year old kids enjoyed the walk.  Modest fee.

if you are a nature lover like me, you should not miss this while you are in Jeju. Be ready to walk for 1 km and get prepared to experience some cold with dark which gives you an awesome feeling to enjoy the cave more.
If weather is beautiful, it is a lovely walk around the crater. Although volcanic is inactive, the green growth in it is still lovely. windy.
I'd recommend you to go at night since it is much nicer with variety of lights.Also, you can walk around tiny island and it takes about 20 min or less.

I would highly recommend this place for an extremely hot or wet day.  Being covered and large enough, it was an enjoyable walk.  There was adequate lighting and enough fellow tourists not to make the cave walk too scary.  Despite the unevenness of the terrain - they are dried lava and so quite uneven, most people would be able to walk comfortably.It's certainly a nice change from limestone caves although some people may miss seeing amazing rock formations like the stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves.  In fact, I was not overly impressed with the gigantic lava mass on display at the end of the walk.  For me, the enjoyable walk was good enough.

I went there with my 7 others female friends. We just walk around and take photos. This park is suitable for family with young children. There is a lot of things that u can do such as take train, picnic and eco friendly.

I was staying at the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun and decided to go for an out door walk to enjoy the beautiful weather. I was walking along the coastline and it eventually lead me to this attraction. Although it is wonderful to see these unique rock formation, this attraction is rather small.

I was looking forward to seeing the traditional/indigenous village but after a quick walk around we were marched into a hut ...after a brief introduction about this ancient village,then the hard sell began. Impressive products made from horse bones & horse oil - with almost magical values! No, I didn't buy anything.This is not a living village. I could only sight tour operators.

I was expecting an obvious large crater but when I saw it, it was rather underwhelming. It was filled with trees and the fact that it was a crater was very unobvious. Nonetheless, the scenery justified the short upslope walk to the crater.

I was excited to see the Manjanggul Lava Tubes up close and personal, but I was rather disappointed after my visit..The Caves were poorly lit and without using a flashlight, one can barely see the markings on the rocks. The ground is very uneven and understandably so. However, for older people, children and people prone to ankle injuries, the lighting does not allow one to see where one is walking and injury can can easily occur.

I visited this place on October 23 2020 on my trip to Jeju Island. It was marbelous! So beautiful everywhere! Spirited Garden in Jeju is a beautiful place to relax, walk through and contemplate. It also has a healing buffet with healthy, tasty and pleasant meals for visitors. Contemplating the garden, I got inspiration and relax feeling. In the papers they say that the Spirited Garden is a symbol of Korean spirit: pioneer spirit and progressiveness, perseverance, and ceaseless endeavor.
I tried walking and rolling in car to feel the effects of such claims... no luck, felt cheated... at least the kids had fun.

I think it really depends on what kind of traveler u are. Some people might find it boring, some people might find it cool. I love it. I've never been in a cave nor a lava tunnel so for me it was a new and exciting experience. The cave is huge, wet and super duper cold, colder than outside in fact and lit up enough to see where you're walking. It's nice to see and feel how hardened lava looks and feels like. Walking into Manjanggul's huge cave feels like a scene from Prometheus.. Awesome!

I saw one picture in instagram and decided to go Jeju olle train route 8. Actually, Route 8 is restricted, but you will see everyone just walk into. It is called 'Gaetkkak Columnar Jointing (媛二쇱?\由щ?)' It is better to wear comfortable shoes since you have to walk on rocks, but you better dress nice if you want to have a good picture. I saw many girls dressed up and walked on the rocks which looked extremely tiring but worth it. You might need to line up to take a photo, and I also waited to take a photo at specific spot. Now I have really cool pictures ;)

I really enjoyed my visit here. I've never visit a volcanic cave before but its an very cool place (literally!). The temperature in the cave is much cooler than outside, although be careful, because they keep it quite dark so it can be difficult to walk on without good shoes.

I haven't been anywhere else in the world where there has been the option to walk a couple of kms through a volcanic cave. The experience is quite surreal. From 30+ degrees on the outside you soon plummet down to perhaps 10-15 degrees, damp and dark. The rock formations are stunning and they've done a good job to keep it natural without too much human interference.Bring sensible shoes.

I have a deep love and appreciation for the artist Lee Jung Seob. The museum itself? and the neighboring art-walk is a great tribute to the artist, but the exhibition itself does not do the artist that much justice. They have a great selection of his smaller works from the earlier periods but they do not house his bigger, dynamic paintings that he is known for. This visit would be a great place to take the family as the entrance fee is very manageable. The museum offers a closer look at the artists' context and life story rather than a display of his most prominent works. In short, a brilliant artist but not the best exhibition space/display method.

I find walking in this lava cave is interesting as it is so cool inside and surprisingly there is no bad smell as it is rather wet. The cave produces it's on air conditioning as the temperature inside is around 15-17 Celsius. Some areas are well lighted and some are not, proper walking shoes are needed as there are many uneven areas along the path provided. Good experience for the ones who loves outdoor!

I find this cave beautiful as it is made by nature. It is just 1km long, it is good for a short trip. The place is cold, that's why Koreans go here in the summer. If you get bored easily, this place is not for you as the cave doesn't have a variety of rock formations.Furthermore, if you do not like to walk in rocky paths, you may not appreciate this. This place is dimly lit to preserve the cave, so you have to be careful. Overall, a good place to visit if you appreciate nature.

I bought a ticket which included access to all 3 museum buildings for 16 000 won. The museums are within walking distance of one another. A map as well as an audio guide is available. The   abandoned   buildings gave it an eerie feel that I thoroughly enjoyed. I was surprised around every corner and turn - the whole experience felt very dreamlike. I loved it.

I am really amazed and really love walking inside the forest you will feel delighted very clean and green trees, smells good and you can relax and breath well. Bijarim Forest-Is a group of about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old. They are 7-14m in height and 50-110cm in diameter. This is the largest nutmeg tree forest in the world. In the middle of the forest is an 800-year-old tree, called ?Ancestor tree of the Bija trees.

I am interested in world heritage and Manjang Cave is included in sites of Jeju's world heritage so I went there. I had never walked inside a cave before, so it was an interesting experience. And I appreciate the carving in the walls and the shapes of rocks that were formed by volcanic activities.The temperature inside the cave is colder than the temperature outside, so it's better to bring a jacket.

Hmm... Where to start?Well, Jeju Island, being volcanic in nature, must really have places like this!Honestly saying, it wasn't something so jaw-dropping and spectacular!Just more like a place with rock formations due to the cooling of lava!The trek inside isn't hard and what I really liked was that it was chilly while we did it!It was a nice sidetrip nonetheless if you like walking and if you like all these geo stuff!If you're in Jeju, maybe you can give it a try

History of traditional Korean Tea and a brief introduction to tea in general. You'll have a chance to walk about the surrounding tea garden. Also a chance to saviour a variety of green tea and cakes. Catered for tourist it's not exactly a place for sipping cuppa and reflecting on   Zen   but it's green tea for what it's worth to appreciate.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.

Had a mixture of nice gardens, some birds and lava caves. When I entered and started walking, it did not sem like much, but then impressed me as I went on. So enjoyed it quite a bit, was a good pleasant walk. Worthwhile if you go to Jeju.
Great place to enjoy walking and see different species of plants, trees, we enjoy palms, something special, very quiet place
Great beach for walking, swimming and relaxing. Volleyball tournament there once a year :) Many great places to eat and stay in the area.
Good news about this place is that other than the entrance steps which as quit steep, the rest of the 1-2 KM walk is actually not too bad.
Get some fresh air and enjoy the walk here. The suspension bridge is just aroud the corner, cute little bar over looks it for when you have earnt a sit down

Fortunate we are able to catch the cheery blossom even during mid April. Nice place to walk around, similar to The Garden of Morning Calm. There is a beach across the park, very nice walk and beautiful scenery. Bring your jacket if you are going during early spring, ITS COLD!

For those who are interested in geology as my family is, this is a fascinating, and not too difficult, walk through a lava tube created by the molten lava. Worth a visit and the entrance fee is extremely cheap. UNESCO heritage.

for me there is nothing special about this cave. the only thing we can do is just walking straight through the cave almost 1km (cmiww). and after we arrive to the end of the tunnel , we just see a small stage and some pic as i remembered. if you traveling with child , pls be carefull when you step the floor. because its really slipper..
Footbridge is of interesting architecture and good photo opp, walk across to the small island and trek around it (about 30 min) to see the sceneries around.
Floor of cave dark, wet and uneven. Bring torch and must be able to walk on wet slippery uneven ground to enjoy this national heritage site.
Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.Lots of walking.Will definitely revisit, loved it loved it loved it.Visited in Summer of 2015

Entrance was KRW15,000 which was extremely expensive for the show. There are simply not the facilities here to walk with the number of visitors and the parking is extremely limited so you have to park on the main road and walk quite some distance to reach it.? Expect no support from staff in any language except korean.

Entrance fee 5,000 won and free for senior and disable as this place is not wheelchair friendly. Thank God my aunt could walk a little so those part that cannot be pushed on wheels.... she had to walk slowly..
Drove here with a driver and walk around the park with family in a chilly weather, not too cold yet not hot. A very memorable moment and good place to have a fresh breathe of air!

Despite the heat, its very cooling inside the cave. Took a walk and I find that it was smaller than what I expected. Path is quite rocky and its good to wear proper shoes instead of sandals or slippers. It can be quite slippery too. Its good to visit but if you are tight on your schedule I think you can give it a miss :)

Certainly my first experience entering a natural geological occurrence like this one. A nice walk on a seasoned path, although some parts were slippery, it was safe for most people. Senior citizens must take extra care as the uneven path were dimly lit. Here were many features to be amazed by and the information centre gave visitors a better understanding of the geological occurrence. Worthy visit.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) I visited there for watching Teddy's parody, because I've visited Teddy museum in Sokcho formerly. According to my expectation, there was funny Teddy doll describing person, event and fairy tale. Walking through the flow, I smile at funny doll. Good to visit once, but I will not visit one more becasue of high price and unchanged exhibits.

But too overcrowded by visitors even at September! :)Possible to rent bicycle or scooter (electric or usual) or quadro-unit and make your trip around the island (but you need actual international driver license with correct category!).It's big enough for walkers.Very small and narrow road all around island - be very, very, very careful as main part of drivers are young people with very little experience of driving and winds in their heads (sorry, but true!) :)
Brought my 7 yr old girl here and it was a good educational walk and eye opener for her. It's wet and cool inside, and unsuitable for wheelchair or stroller.

Bijarim Forest holds about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old and is supposedly the largest nutmeg grove in the world. A 813 years old   Ancestor tree of Bijia tree  , also dubbed the   New Millennium Nutmeg   (#0001 tree) sits in the middle of the forest. Local residents hope the spiritual power of this noble tree will bring happiness, prosperity, and health to all in the coming millennium.The trees emit phytoncide, said to strengthen one's immunity system and enhances natural healing of the human body. Japanese and Koreans advocate forest bathing, aka shinrin-yoku or 汝役 and sanlimyok ??곕┝ respectively.  Essentially this is a short, leisurely visit to absorb the forest atmosphere and was developed in Japan during the 1980s as part of preventive health care and healing.  So do walk slowly, breathe deeply, open all your senses in the revitalising woods to calm, rejuvenate and restore your body.  Truly pleasant stroll for nature lovers and family outing.Note: Despite its charm, Bijarim Forest is more popular with locals than foreign tourists due to public transportation and lack of awareness. Cover this place as part of  Manjanggul caves/Sangumburi crater tour. The woods can get mud-logged after rainfall.

Beautiful authentic cave that gives you an idea about the magma power. I visited with my dad, but teenagers, couples with small children and elders. There are stairs and very variable ground so it is not recommendable for those who have trouble walking.
Beautiful   Stone Grandpa   displays in multiple setting. A nice walk around the park and also learn about the local culture and history.
Be prepared to walk a lot. Stores selling similar items tend to cluster together. Traffic and parking can be a harrowing experience. From what we observed at the taxi queue, it can be a long wait.
Awesome! 2 km total by walking, cold place inside, we are so amazed by how the nature creates it. When you come in rainy season please be careful with your steps. Not recomended for the elder.

At first, going through the green house,? we were a little disappointed until we walked the grounds outside.? The French? and Roman gardens were absolutely beautiful.? It was so peaceful and relaxing.

As there are not much railings inside the cave to guide the tourists while walking and steps are uneven, make sure to wear comfortable walking shoes. It is beautiful and a must visit when in Jeju. I joined a tour for this visit as it is quite far from where I stayed. Tourist spots in Jeju are not close to each other and I didnt quite see a lot of public transport the in the area.
An interesting walk underground in a 1 km long cave. Some people would find fascinating, others might get abit claustrophobic.Very cheap, about 90 pence per person. Beautiful grounds on the outside.

An amazing cave; one of nature's wonder!  Must wear a good pair of walking shoes, and be prepared to walk some distance. Enjoy the strange and mysterious dark tunnels. Dimly lit, but well kept with small platforms and bridges, this UNESCO heritage site is one selling point selling for Jeju! Worth paying a visit.

Amazing cave carved by molten lava moving underground with many interesting features, however, you need to be prepaired for dim lighting, uneven floor with many tripping hazards as well as uneven steps/stairs.  Not suitable for young children or older folks who have trouble with sight or walking.
About 40min drive from jeju it was a park with about 5 areas. Not bad but not amazing. Weather needs to be good or else don't bother. A few good photo's, a few short walks .... it's ok.
About 40 min taxi from the airport. The cave is a must see if you visit Jeju. Walk inside the cave, beutiful lighting. Amazing.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.
A wonderful place to visit a regular place to visit whether for a walk along the shore to relax or to camp out for the weekend in summer,it is really just great!

A very wide (23m), high (18m) and long cave (7+ km) one can walk along by yourself (about 1km is open to the public). The temperature inside is perfect, when there is a heatwave outside (which was the case in August 2016). It is doable with a small kid, however you can't bring a stroller as the surface is too uneven in the cave. Also bring solid shoes, it is slippery. Some visiters had flipflops or even some kind of high heals - truly not recommended.
A train ride that takes you from sight to sight, there is a gorgeous lake walk and a pretty garden, but sights are very simple and straightforward. Not a must-see.

A terrific site that is well maintained and well explained. Points of interest are marked in 3 languages including English. Come prepared with proper footwear. Tourists are walking on uneven flooring. Also this tunnel can be damp.  Photographing is not permitted, but plenty of visitors were using their cell phones.

A short walk to these falls - low ticket price at the entrance and then about 100 steps down to the base of the falls - quite rocky and need to watch the step - fortunately we went on a day without many tourists. Could feel the refreshing cool spray, nice when in the sunshineI love the fact there?s no littering here - helps maintain the natural state
A pretty rock to look at and the surrounding area is also very pleasant to walk around. It's best to get there early to avoid the crowds and heat in summer, but definitely worth a visit.

A pretty large castle with grounds littered with many colourful glass decorations of animals etc. If you take a walk into the garden, you will also find colourful glass figurines of insects and animals nicely arranged in the park to create a fairy-tale like experience for the kids.

A nice park where you can walk up easily to see the crater. The crater is long dried up with vegetation growing and on my visit, there was a excavation truck at the bottom working! Wonder how the truck and worker get down there.Recommend to all age group.
A nice panorama, 'enchanted forest' atmosphere, but very many people. Also be prepared for quite a bit of a walk.
A nice evening walk at sunset.There were many locals lying down on the benches, playing loud music.? Although it lacked tranquility, we found it interesting to observe local customs.

A lava tube showing the flow of lava and various natural formation such as the lava shelves or columns. Inside the cave is chilly (around 11c when outside is around 25c), dark, wet and slippery. Bring your jacket and sturdy shoe for this visit. Heels is a definite no no. Forget about your camera (too dark for photo taking) and just enjoy the brisk walk. To and fro takes you around 45mins-1hr.

A cute and cuddly experience at the Teddy Bear museum, this place is for kids and adults alike. It has an impressive collection of impressionistic teddy bears, from the 19th century to the major icons of today; a teddy bear version of Madame Tussaud's. Then there is a peaceful garden walk which is also adorned with teddy bear statues. The gift shop is irresistible, too.
1st visit in the cave tube. Really fascinated cold, dark, wet cave. The ground is uneven so walk with caution. It's good to walk in a group for safety.
1km in, 1km out... really amazing walking through world's largest lava column! We get to imagine we are the lava flowing through!!

Sanbangsan Mountain is a wonderful bell-shaped huge body of lava situated nearby the ocean. At few places it stretches into the ocean where majestic rock structures can be seen. Almost vertical cliffs with columnar joints at this mountain are impressive. This mountain is visible from almost everywhere in the southwest plains of Jeju. Also the legend associated with this mountain is very interesting. According to the legend it was plucked out from the Hallasan Mountain peak by the angry Emperor when he got hit by a misfired arrow that was shot to white deer. Interestingly it is said that the circumferences of the Sanbangsan Mountain and the crater at Hallasan are of similar size. The Jeju Olle Trail Route 10 is connected to this mountain by stairs. A Buddha temple huge Buddha statue and the caves on this mountain are very beautiful.  This mountain along with nearby Yongmeori Coast are highly recommended especially to those who love coastal cliffs and interesting rock formations.

Good place to visit for experiencing the lava tube. But.... Pease please please prepare a good walking shoes if you were to visit this place. You'll need to walk on rough and uneven surface and the trail is pretty long. Not recommend to bring kids and elderly to visit this attraction.

Arrived an hour and a half before closing. The trails starts with a relatively step decent and the walk thru the lava tube is a 1km walk in and 1 km walk back. The lava tube cave is spectacular. Signs were available to help us learn about the the lava tube. An easy walk but need to be careful on certain section of the party as we were walking on wet lava rock. Well worth the drive there!!!

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

Went today - very clear day. Reminded me of Falcor from the Never Ending Story. Hahahha!  We took the southern trail to the lookout. Was a great place to stop and see the local female divers gather fresh mussels, clams, abalone, squid and sea cucumbers. They quickly set up shop with a few kids stools and rock formations (ready made table top). They brought out a few bottles of soju (I think they hid it in the ocean to keep it cool. Luv the grapefruit flava) and they were ready for customers.  Freshest seafood I've ever tasted- Anthony Bordain would've been proud.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We walked to Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff for almost 30 minutes from Cheonjeyeon waterfall. it was worth it. We can witnessed the picturesque landscape of the nature. We had to pay 2,000KRW for the admission free. Easy access to the lavatory. Easy trail for walking.

We hiked the Eorimok (up) and Yeongsil (down) trails. *If you're hiking in winter, you definitely need crampons.*These trails were stunning. On the Eorimok, we experienced surreal forest setting shrouded in misty clouds and stunning landscapes. At the top of the trail, there's a great place to snag some cup Ramen and Choco-pies. Bring a few cheons and you'll be fine. Two-thirds of this trail was in the forest and the last third was along a large plain created by a lava field. Expect to be amazed by vast skies.The Yeongsil trail was just as satisfying. There are sheer drops and exposed cliff faces. Most of this trail was composed of wooden stairs. If you're planning to bus in and out, make sure you start early. The buses fill up fast and the last bus back to Jeju-si from Yeongsil runs at 16:15 during the winter (until March). Also, if you're not exhausted, the walk to the bus stop from the trail is not too far (maybe 2km at max). Don't waste you money on shuttle service.

To be honest, it?s quite dark and your attention will be used on minding your steps rather than looking up. Rocky slippery trails and it?s 2km in total, in and out the same way. Worth a visit once as its not often you get to trek in a lava cave. Would recommend warmer clothes and proper footwear.

This is enormous highly worthwhile visiting. While I've visited caves around the world this is the first time I've seen lava tubes. They are huge you could drive a semi trailer through most of them. Defiantly worth seeing just for this aspect.It's quite wet on the floor of the cave, while you won't get wet, there are puddles of water. The ground is extremely uneven in places so good footwear is essential.There is heaps of signage in English on how they were formed.Highly worthwhile.

The whole trail takes about 45 mins to an hour to complete. It was truly interesting to be inside a lava tube and during the walk, there were informational signs to explain parts of the tubes! The UNESCO Lava Tube. Beautiful in the tube. Can get to see the trail of lava movement,  the moulden formation. It is common to visit caves, but a lava tube, is rare.

The Park is quite a distance away from other major sights but it is different in that the star attraction are those   grandfather stone sculptures  .Be prepared for lots of walking on easy trails.  There are small pebbles everywhere so do watch the kids and carefully navigate those wheelchairs and baby strollers.The underground museum near next to the water reservoir/water sculpture is definitely for those interested in geology. The lava tube was pretty impressive and interesting. The trails in the lava tube revealed how the lava flows and form. Please visit this place only if you really love and in great passion to help preserve the nature. This attraction requires reservation as it only allow 400 hikers daily. While you can only look from the outlook points at Sangumburi 掠긷訝 and Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone 掠길ε뷴낡, this activity is an authentic encounter inside the crater, with the geological formation, vegetation and traits of lava activities

On Jeju Island's Halla Mountain--at 1,950 meters, South Korea's tallest-- can be found Korea’s highest paved roadway, known as 1100 Meter Road or the 1100 Highland Rest Area.? There, you can take a self-paced nature hike on an elevated wooden walkway through a “volcanic” wetland; with its many lava rocks, trees and wildflowers, this place has an otherworldly beauty that you and your camera will love.? You’ll likely see lots of ravens, magpies and maybe some roe deer (be sure to stay alert for them along the highway if you are driving). Across the road, there’s a colorful cafe and shop, offering local beverage favorites and snacks, as well as souvenirs.? (They carry a good selection of galot clothing, made locally using persimmon-dyed fabrics.)? From the cafe’s observation deck, enjoy a perfect view of some of Halla’s most famous landmarks, including Yeongsil Folding Screen Rocks and the 500 Generals Rocks.This area takes on a very different character with each season, and locals often drive up to see the magnificent ice formations that form on the trees and rocks in the winter and spring, when Halla’s higher-elevation trails may be closed to hikers.? But it’s also a good choice for visitors who have limited time to climb, even when the higher trails are open, because it is possible to experience these incredible scenes at the 1100 Meter Road area.Not only is this a beautiful area, these days the 1100 Meter Highland is part of the Jeju Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO and World Natural Heritage Site.A couple of points:? this attraction is actually located on Highway 1139, which will also take you past Eorimok, Yeongshil and Mysterious Road. You can drive or take an intercity-bus from either the Jeju City (north) or Jungman Resort area (south) side.? If you take a taxi, you should make a roundtrip reservation, allowing 1-2 hours there.? It’s a good idea to take at least a light jacket, even on a summer day, and for late fall to late spring, have a heavier coat, gloves and even a hat.? And don’t forget your shades and skin protection; even in winter, the sunlight can be strong on Hallasan.

My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

Lava tubes are different all over - so these have their own special yet similar features. The overall experience was well worth it and I certainly recommend the visit. The trail is reasonable well developed with stairs down into the tubes. Though basically light, I thought the selected illuminations added to the features and overall feel of the caves. It is not overly spectacular in showing off the various formations and features, but it still gives a good view of the tube walls. Be careful of the path as it does have rough spots and puddles. Moist, cool and over 2 kms of walking, I enjoyed the visit, although not the most impressive caves I have visited.

Jeju Olle Trail is completely round the island broken up into 21 different routes.In total we walked about 13km, about 3.5 to 4 hours time taken. Photography time included.We started our walk from Hyatt Jeju along the Jungmun Beach (we did Route 8 going eastwards) heading towards the Daepo Pego (port) and ended our walk at the Yakcheon Temple.Ensure that you look out for arrows (blue&orange) along the ground and olle trail ribbons (blue & orange as well) tying on trees along the way. Terrain is very varied, from easy tarmac lanes to quite difficult lava rocks along the bays. Suggest you wear proper walking shoes. Bring along your own water & snacks. There are a few restrooms along the way. If you are staying around Jungmun resort area (many hotels there), take airport bus limousine no 600 to go back to your hotel. Its about 1000 Korean Won per person.Overall is an interesting walk because you will see village, seaside, port & temple along the way. This is one of the very popular walk in Jeju, so its like a   must walk   walk.. We just did a short segment of the Olle Trail & apparently other segments are even more interesting.. Check out some photos for illustration.

It's quite exciting to walk down the huge lava tube and imagine the flow of lava melting its way to the ocean. You see the striped walls indicating different levels of the flow, each stripe has a bit different color. Glossy lava sinters, black, dark red and orange. It was once the most beautiful street in Korea. As a German that comes from the countryside it was just a regular forest with a small hiking trail. Nothing real special about. I was a little disappointed.If you're in a hurry, don't visit the Bijarim Forest but rather the Lava tunnel which is close by!

It was a rather short trip ( 1 hour) , but it was worth it. For adults 2000 won and until 24years only 1000 won. If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:?
