Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I hiked to the top today.  I had decided not to do this but at breakfast this morning a gal from Korea highly suggested I go, so I did. I took the Seongpanak trail up and back. I got there a little after 10 and was told that it was a bit late to make it to the top so I went out very quickly so I would make it to the Check station by 1 PM. If you get there after that time they won?t let you up to the top. I made it and got to the top. At 2:30 they make everyone come down. I came down slowly and at the end I was all by myself walking those trails as it got darker. I didn?t get down until about 7 PM. Because I was in such a hurry to get up it took me much more time to come down than it did to go up. As I was walking down a deer jumped right in front of me And then jumped away. I brought two bottles of water and lunch. That was perfect for me. There are restrooms on the way up but not at the top. They are outhouses. I do not have hiking shoes with me, just my slip on sketchers, so my feet are still sore from walking on those lava rocks with these shoes. This is also the reason it took me so long to get down, my feet were really sore At that point and I had to rest them during the descent. There is a Monorail track next to the trail. Today I saw them taking down some people who couldn?t make it down on that.
Hiking on Lava, Seriously. :)Watch for snakes. I saw two of them on the trail. As you climb up the weather becomes colder and colder so have proper clothing.

Great experience being in the caves, reading the explanation on the formation of the stalactites, lava lines and reason for the uneven heights at certain lengths of the cave. There are summarised English translation on the explanation boards which makes it easier to understand what we are looking at. Trail wise, the ground is made up of flat rocks with some shallow water holes. Wearing comfortable cover shoes would help. We saw some families with young children, about 6 years and above and they could run about on their own, so I would think this would be OK for families who want to bring their kids alone. Overall a good experience and good change from seeing the land attractions. At 2000KRW for an adult ticket, it is definitely reasonable and worth your every cent.

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

Very interesting sight with polygonal rock columns from cooled lava. There was a platform for viewing and a thrilling jet ride and sailboat rides. We probably spent only at most 15minutes there. An easy and quick climb.
This was part of our Yeha bus tour - South Course - and it is a beautiful cliff formed by lava.  Such beautiful views!!
This is a must-see on Jeju Island.  A walk along a set of stairs (not strenuous) provides many varied views of this area.  Look for the hexagonal columns of lava.
The rocks are beauty made by nature. It is formed by lava flows but the shapes will leave you to wonder on how it is formed. There will be some steps to climb up to view the cliff.

Place where you can consider one of the exercise from steps and all the way to the end to view the nature of Lava.You can learn about the Manjanggul Cave as there's information along the way. Cool weather as we went during the winter. Not sure if you go during any other season.Must come as you might not get it from your own country.

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. The sudden contraction of molten lava due to the cooling effect of water has resulted in these rocks splitting into polygonal columns and forming a coast of almost 2 km long.This attraction is worth the visit and can be reached directly by trekking from Cheonjeyeon falls or taking a bus and pass thru the garden (Jusangjeollidae Promenade) and then reach the cliff at the end.Walking around the garden would be relaxing and one should not miss it. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

I am 6 years old and when I first got to sunrise peak it was really tall and big. I thought I couldn't climb it but I did. My mummy wanted to quit but I wouldn't let her. The best bit was we saw a shop that sold water and I bought juice. It was halfway up so mummy didn't need to carry water after all. I wish it wasn't such a cloudy day but the view was still cool. I saw a telescope to see everything. Me and my Brother had a fight over the telescope and mummy and daddy got mad. When we got to the top daddy said it was a crater but I did not see any lava so I think he was lying. The end. Finished.
Good views. UNESCO site.Natural volcanic history n lava tubes.Lighted direction arrows on footpath was useful.

Considered one of the ten best view points of Jeju this attraction is not to be missed One can enjoy this visit if you like to soak yourself or would like to find yourself among the clouds. On a foggy day one can easily miss the existence of this mountain.If you are visiting during winter or rainy season better to plan the visit during afternoon as one can have a magnificent view from the top without much clouds around.This mountain believed to be formed by the volcanic lava houses the Sanbang-gulsa Temple and the Bomunsa Temple.It also has other attractions as Golden Bhuddha Tea Shops etc. Once on the top one can see the ridge called the Dragon Head where a memorial has been built for Hendrick Hamel the first westerner who was the first to introduce Korea to the western world after his ship got wrecked. This mountain is believed to be used as a watch tower and smoke used to be sent out during the day or fire was lit during the night if any urgent message was needed to be conveyed.Climbing the steps would be a little tough for those who are not regular walkers and for the old.
Best time to visit us when tide is out and you can walk and climb amongst the lava rocks. Was a little surprised at the amount of litter on the beach. Great views and lovely color of water.
Beautiful cave with lava rock sides. Hard to take beautiful pictures but amazing views. Specially the end of the 1km hike inside the lava tube.
A must go place as you can see how the lava formed meeting the sea. Be prepared for strong wind but spectacular view

A good place especially for first-timers or those who are interested to see lava formations. Really gorgeous view when the sea hit those rocks. Nothing much to see so don't really have to spend much time here.
A beautiful spot of commanding good view of the sea and the rocks of special shape lava formed on cooling.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

we've seen a few caves and this one is truly unique.  Its not loaded in formations such as stalagmites/stalagtites, but the lava shelves go on forever.  It literally takes over thirty minutes to walk from one end to the other at a decent clip.  Very humid inside, definately bring an umbrella or raincoat.  Also very chilly so if you are there in summer, the temperature change can be significant.  I brought a flashlight but you really don't need it as they do a great job in keeping you on the straight and narrow.  It really gives you a great understanding of what nature can do, well worth the detour to view

We found ourselves frequenting this beach during our stay in Jeju. The water is turquoise and semi-transparent with beautiful contrasting lava rocks lining the coast. Also, there is a view of an island. Note: there are few bars and/or beach cafes.

We entered this park with great expectations - the gardens themselves are great, the bonsai area stands out as superb, and the Lava Caves offer some welcome respite from the heat.Everything in the garden was destroyed by the horrific and unacceptable conditions of the birds and other animals.  There was a smallish section with parrots, a few other birds, a monkey in a tiny cage and a few other small furry creatures.  It was filthy, some of the animals had no water, the temperature must have been 35 degrees.  There was one small animal that was clearly suffering greatly (in one of the cages with no water). I emptied the contents of my water bottle into it's water bowl, and reported its condition to a member of staff - who did nothing.We went on to see peacocks and ostriches, yes in slightly larger enclosures, but with no shade, no vegetation, and 13 peacocks in a tiny cage.  The birds were in obvious distress with obsessive grooming and clear skin infections.I've travelled all over the world, and been to many places like this and never, from the poorest, to the richest countries, have I seen animals kept in these conditions. I rarely, if ever, write reviews, but I am so angry at the conditions here, that it's important to be aware.The gardens are immaculate, the conditions of the animals are disgraceful, and should be an embarresment to whoever runs this organisation.Do not visit!
Viewing of lavas in the cave was interesting.  But having been to other caves in other countries, like the Postjna Cave ins Slovenia, this place is rather boring.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

took our family of 3 about 11hrs round trip. it can be done in 9 if you ha e the right gear and move fast. its gradual grade, so its not strenuous but the terrian is terrible. it is 85percent big rocky jagged lava chunks. if you are prone to ankle injury, this hike is not for u. you have to watch your feetthe whole time  which is fine since there is no view until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. so all in all i do not really recommend this hike unless you have lots of time in Jeju and you really wanna say you climbed Koreas highest peak.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This park includes a variety of sights including two lava tubes, an aviary that includes a variety of peacocks, ostriches etc, a small traditional village, strange little rock people sculptures, and a very impressive botanical garden with outdoor sections around a pond and several green houses.   Some strange combinations in the outdoor section with large palms mixed up with various types of cacti and other random mixes of fabulous plant specimens from all over the world.  The greenhouse plants seem a bit more organized by regions or types (e.g., large cactus collection in one greenhouse; palms in another), with live animals interspersed between the plants (impressive boa and python collection, also some special turtles, and lizards such as nile monitors, iguanas, etc.).  In between plant viewing, I enjoyed a nice cool cactus juice relaxing in the herb bar.

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This cave is actually a volcanic Lava tube, not limestone cave. So don't expect to see amazing things like what you see in Guilin and Yunan.Same as reviewer ggkoh, I visited there after a day of persistent rain. The cave is wet, filled with small pool of water here and there. The floor bed is rocky and uneven. So be equipped with a jacket comes with hood (or raincoat) and a good pair of track shoes.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don?t need to linger. It?s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.
The view is breathtaking, a must see and must go location in my opinion. You will be amazed how lava can turn into such a beautiful scenary.

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The dragon head lava rock was indeed a sight to behold, jutting out of the cliffs. That is if you could catch a glimpse of it amongst hordes of tourists jostling for a vantage point to capture it on their phones, with selfie sticks flailing about.Being only the dragon head, it was quite a pint size cliff, and there was only a tiny area /platform from which to view it.To make the most of our drive there, we walked several meters down a stepped path quite close to the waters and enjoyed our moments there on the rocks.

Perhaps there was some misunderstanding on my part, but it seems that it is no longer possible to watch the sunrise from the peak, as the ticket office information says that it only opens at 7.30am (sunrise is around 7am in November). The views during a day climb is still good, though mostly of Seongsan. As compared to the views from the peak, I found the beach at the foot of the peak (along the downward route) more interesting, with the lava formations and rock pools. Try and catch the haenyeo (female divers) in action if you can!Also, try to visit either very early or very late in the day - the crowds in between are huge (from the top, I counted at least a dozen tour buses in the parking lot).

Nice views, nice place to take pictures, not a lot of beach front to relax or swim. Most of the area people relax and sunbath are away from the beach since most of the coast has lava rock. Fun place for kids to find stuff in the rocks.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Magnificent view formed by molten lava.View is nice when high tide, crowded during noon, so try to reach there early to avoid crowd.Discount for youth (need to show passport)There is also a pampas grass field, situated at your right side once enter the booth of Jusangjeoli cliff parking lot, can walk in the field if you have no time to visit Saebyeol Oreum

Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

Jusangjeolli Cliff, designated as a natural monument of Jeju Island, is the largest columnar-jointed lava in South Korea. It was formed due to the sudden cooling of lava from the Hallasan Mountain, which erupted into the sea of Jungmun, thousands of years ago. Witnessed a picturesque view of the sea and the cliff. I recommend not wearing any hat or cap when you visit Jusangjeolli Cliff as the wind is strong there.

It was kind of windy when I had my visit at Yeongmori cliff. At first, I thought it was another ordinary rock formation viewing after taking a few steps from the entrance...I was about to back out from the trek thinking I can see much of these in the Philippines, but as soon as my tour guide led me to the farther side of the cliff, I started to appreciate how unique the lava rock formation  was.  The best view to take a picture maybe is to include Mt, Sanbang in the back draft. You may also climb a few steps to the top or catch a good timing for huge strike of waves by the rocks.  Wear appropriate shoes as the pathways are always slippery and wet.

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

I would echo an earlier review that said that you should not bother with this if you have done any caving or similar - this is aimed at casual visitors not experts. It is a gentle wander in a cool cave that is appropriately lit, reasonably level and there is enough English signage to explain what you need to know. It is the fact that this was a lava tunnel that is not interesting and the signs do explain how the lava flowed, melted and cut down and through from other tunnels. 1) Wear sensible shoes.2) If it has been raining it can drip a lot inside though on our visit I did not think so.3) Some might feel it is cold - I did not

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Gosh...this place is awesome... Its very well maintained and comfy for those people walking inside and enjoy the lava tube nature. Recommend to wear shoes or comfy sandal as it sometimes wet inside. Not just the view, but also there are boards for explaining the things we see inside. Love it!

After climbing the stairs for the view of the lush, plant-filled centre of the crater, you should definitely walk along part of the black sand beach that arcs around to the ?glass house.? You?ll see some amazing views of Seongsan Ilchubon there, and your pictures won?t be filled with random tourists. There are also bits of sea glass scattered along the shore, shells, and if you walk down the beach far enough, a beautiful, large ledge of lava covered in green moss you can walk on and explore. It was really easy to get to the crater by bus from Jeju-si, and it only took about 75 minutes.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html
absolutely beautiful cliffs, great views of lava cliffs. a must see for anyone traveling to Jeju Island!only quirk is the small shops selling touristy things.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.
You pass the Maze Park when you head towards the Lava Cave. My mum and I went to the park after the cave on our way back up to the main road to catch the bus. It was a fun way to kill some time.

This was part of our Yeha Bus Tour and I am really glad it was one of our stops as one of our daughters is a tea lover.  She got some lava cake and a coffee and it was enjoyable just watching her.  It was very busy and we did have to be patient for a table so just keep that in mind.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This beach is less clustered by tourist and easily accessible. Take the 702 for an hour from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal and arrive at the entrance.  There are several food options and convenience stores.  The lava rocks are also pretty cool.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

So dont get this place confused with maze land.  This one is near the lava cave.  Here it has one maze only.  It would have been fun and peaceful but then 3 buses of middle school children arrived and all hell broke out.  Very hars to walk around it when a bunch of kids are running past you.  But the maze owners also have a bunch of cats that were super friendly.

first advise don't travel juju alone ... tour and tour buses become a necessity ... as i was travelling by public bus it took almost more then an hour to reach there .... was already a bit tired by the time we reached ... After going in was a bit excited at how beautiful the place is .... but its so huge that we got bored watching trees after trees at such heat ..... exciting part was the lava cave.... where it was also coooollll.... there are many places to take pictures .... a very good picnic spot .... will enjoy with family

Well it's a big cave and you are surrounded by lava rocks- which are basically... Rocks.So if you like caves or rocks you will love this!It was very quiet.. Just a few people walked past us... Very different from Ichulbong..You don't need walking shoes or even a torch really, but do care where you walk..It is about 2km from the main road if you take a bus that drops you off on the main road.. Taxis often wait in the main road and charge 4000 one way to the caves..I think entry to the caves was just 1500..The Maze garden is a few hundred metres away too but I didn't go

We were staying in the Seogwipo area (near the International Convention Center), so it took us about an hour by bus to get to the Stone Park. It was interesting, with some unususal lava formations, but the drizzling rain didn't help in enjoying the scenery. The   museum   is OK, but nothing spectacular. When you (if) select a sunny day!

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took a nice walk through the nutmeg forest, took us about an hour to finish the circuit. It isn't easy to get to if you don't have a car though-we took a taxi from manjangul lava caves, but found it very hard to get back, since there were no taxis or regular buses. Thankfully some helpful Koreans helped call a taxi for us.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We didn't have great weather when we were on the island so couldn't climb the mountain. This was an alternative activity and glad we did it as it was really interesting. Make sure you go all the way to the end as you don't want to miss the lava flow. The ground is slippy in places and not suitable for small children, strollers or wheelchairs. If you're using public transport get the bus 900. Not the 701 as we did! The 701 has a stop called 'Manjamggul Cave entrance' but it's 2km walk away from the entrance!!

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

Visited the cave as a part of a bus tour. We entered through the 2nd section and were given 40 mins to walk to end of the cave and back. Grounds are uneven and slippery due to water dripping from the ceiling, hence proper shoes are necessary. The lighting was quite dim and there were only a couple of descriptions along the way. I didn't come out with a full appreciation of the lava cave. The cave wasn't very spectacular but it's worth a visit if you are in the area.

Udo is simply beautiful. You should rent either a bike or a moped once you arrive. You can easily circle the whole island with stops in a couple hours. The enclosed beaches, volcanic rocks, crystal clear water, and very green landscape is exquisite.The road is not really crowded even during the busy summer months. I really enjoyed Udo Island, but then again what major natural location in Jeju-do disappoints? Whether you visit the lava tube caves, craters, dramatic coastline, waterfalls, nearby islands, beaches, mountains, and forests, Jeju-do is a natural paradise.

Udo is a small island just off Jeju island and is a 15min ferry ride. Once you are there you can hike, hire a bike or get on a round island hop-on hop-off bus which are quite frequent.The island is a lava plateu but some beaches have golden sand or white coral sand.The island is lush and green and is apparently very fertile.As it is touristy, prices can be high but it is definitely worth a visit if it is a good day.Give yourself plenty of time.

Transportation: There are several buses that make stops at this destination, but just like everything in Jeju, rental car is the recommended mode of travel. Food: the lava tubes does have a restaurant colocated but I did not eat. There are also some snacks you can purchase here but you are not allowed to bring them down into the lava tubes. Attraction: The scale of the lava tube really surprised me. We descended roughly 30 feet into the lava tube after we purchased our tickets ($4 pp). The stairs were slippery, so be cautious when descending. Don?t worry if you have claustrophobia, The tube is about 25ft across and 20 feet high! There are no tour guides, so you won?t have anybody explaining the history or the geology of the tubes, but there are educational signs posted about every 100 feet. There was also a great museum on sit I recommend visiting prior to going into the lava tubes. Great place to visit, and it took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

This was a very interesting Lava Tube cave.  There were signs in English as well as various other languages describing what you were looking at.  The signs were informative.  The cave is cool, so I recommend a zippered sweatshirt or windbreaker.  Also, the floor of the cave is uneven, so you definitely want to have good walking shoes.  I was just fine wearing old jogging shoes.  We went as part of a guided tour - I would have liked to spend just a little more time there, but that's how it goes on bus tours...  There may be more beautiful caves, but overall, it was the nicest cave I've been in - very nice Lava Tube - you will enjoy it.

This was a part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - and felt it was worth seeing.  It is a lava tunnel/cave, which makes it kind of unique.  Visitors are limited to how far you can explore, which is fine as you do need to watch carefully where you walk - it is a lava tube and the floor is very uneven.  It is known for   Stone Turtle   because it is shaped like Jeju island.  Be sure to have a light jacket.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

These lava columns are a must to visit when staying on Jeju.  They are basalt hexagonal columns similar to The Giants Causeway in Ireland, though not as big.  We got the bus to the Conference Centre and walked through to the entrance.  They were amazing and were our favourite sight on the island, although you can't actually get down to them and walk on them.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!

Quite a small cave.  Different coz it's a lava tube.  Go if u have time.  Needs about 1-2 hours.  Bus stops outside at main road which is half an hour's walk to the entrance.  Try to get a taxi to take u to the entrance.  Otherwise, skip this.

Pretty unique place, well worth to visit! Dress up well as it doesn't seem chilling down there at first, but if you walk until the very end, then back, it may take an hour. Also, getting there not that easy:take #701 from jeju city intercity bus termal to the bus stop named   Entrance to the Manjanggul Lava Tubes  . This is quite far from the entrace though, and the bus #990 supposed to go there is extremely rare, so not much chance except to take a taxi (it should not cost more than 3000 won/ride).

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

I've visited many caves but by far this is the first lava tube that I have experienced. It is interesting to know the science and geography behind this magnificent tube. However, only 1 km deep into the tube is open to tourists. You can take a public bus directly from the Jeju bus station if you opt to travel on a budget. The bus fare is less than KRW 2000 compared to very pricey tours with taxi. The bus ride is only slightly more than an hour away from Jeju City.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for   you silly tourist   sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. You can get here from Jeju bus terminal using the 701 bus (3,000 KRW). There is a stop for it about 40 mins in. It's near Manjangul cave (6,000 KRW taxi) so worth combining it with a trip with that.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.
