The trail we took was Seongpanak trail, which is the easiest one. It was early of the fall season. Leaves started turning into different colors, chilling, not so cold, sunny and very enjoyable.We just finished 1500m of height and ate a noodle in a shelter. Then, we turned back (blaming non-stop walking in the previous days :D) and took a quick turn in a shortstop in Saraoseum (beautiful lake, nice view of the mountain).Overall, really enjoy it! Will try it again one day.P/S: it is a natural place so not clean bathroom. A very natural way of toiletry but I really don't like it but can't blame!!

I am a resident of the Seattle metropolitan area so I have to compare it to the Chihuly Garden and Glass museum.  The Jeju Glass Castle is very different in concept as it also focuses on small to medium sized glass items.  Conversely, Chihuly Garden and Glass focuses on large scale items produced by Chihuly in small quantities.  That's not to say it was disappointing, but it wasn't that impressive in the sheer quality of the items.  However, you do get a very large variety of glass items from throughout the world so it does make it up in quantity.  Unlike the Chihuly museum, the glass castle is a very large complex.I did notice the museum seemed a little run down in a few areas - it really did seem it needs some upgrades to its infrastructure.  However, there is a maze, nicely manicured gardens, glass shoes, and a large variety of other takes on glass items.  There is also a nice trail to walk that showcases certain glass items as well.Perhaps the most interesting part of the museum is near the entrance.  You'll find a glass making room there with windows you can look through to see glass artisans at work.  It was quite interesting to see these people create glass items by sculpting it, putting it in the oven, and more.

Hiked up to the summit via the Seongpanak trail. A 35 minute ride on the 5.16 bus from the Jeju main bus terminal drops you off right at the entrance to the trail. Great hike up. Took me a little under 4 hours including a 30 minute detour which breaks off from the trail to go see the Saraureom. This trail is mostly wooden steps. Both the Saraoreum and summit crater lake were dry, but still beautiful. I do not recommend relying on the   store   at the Jinderaebal shelter. They do have hot water if you want to bring your own instant noodle mix. Bring your own food and be prepared to bag your garbage and carry it. walked down via the Gwaneumsa trail which is a bit shorter. I defenitely recommend this since the trail also has a different type of scenery, including a beautiful bridge crossing. Not sure if there is a bus back to the city from the bottom of the Gwaneumsa trail, but by the time I made it down (3 hours) I was ready to take a taxi, one of many which are available which cost me 15,000 Won (about $ 15) back to the city. Certainly worth it. Overall, a beautiful and amazing experience.One last recommendation would be NOT to attempt this hike with less than proper hiking shoes.

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

First of all, this place is huge.Formed through volcanic activity which resulted in 46 'small volcanoes' in the park itself. From what i saw, they ain't 'small'!There are a few entrances and trails. I took the Eulrimok Trail. It was pretty easy as compared to other mountains i hiked. First third, about 2.4km is quite difficult. Lots of stones and steps. Then it gradually became easier. The view is definitely awesome the moment you clear the forest area.There is a reststop at about 5km. Be sure to bring your own food. There is no cafe or shop there. The locals actually even cooked their own ramyeon by bringing them and hot water too. Some used the army-styled ration. There are no trash cans. You have to bring your trash back.You can take a public bus to this trail (gotta walk in opposite the bus stop. A good almoat 2km gentle upslope).Only bus 240 brings hikers here. You might want to check.Reminder, it is super cold in winter.

Before going there please be sure you are in a good physical condition because climbing up takes big efforts. In case you stay in Seogwipo city, it is better to start climbing to the top by Eorimok trail because it is shorter, and go down by Yeongsil trail. During thⓒ trip the the Halla mountain you have a chance to meet a deer, enjoy fascinating view from the top and beautiful nature. To get to Eorimok trail entrance get bus No. 714 (if I am not wrong) from Jungnum (Seogwipo).

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

As unexperienced hikers, we did the 9,6 km Seongpanak trail and it took us around 9 hours to finish the trail back and forth (breaks included). The view at the top of the mountain is stunning and very rewarding. The hike itself is not very scenic as you walk in a forest for almost 90% of the time (which is beautiful and relaxing though). We were quite exhausted at the end of the day, but it was all well worth it. To memorize this day, we decided to buy a certificate (which can be bought for 1000 won at the Seongpanak trail entrance).

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

A relatively easy hike going up Yeongsil trail (lots of climbing). Note that if you're taking the bus, you still need to do a pre-hike of 2.5km going up the mountain after you get off the bus stop. In my opinion, this was harder than the actual hike going up, but it was good preparation. There's also a cafe near the actual entrance. You can buy food here right before going up the trail.The cutoff time for Yeongsil trail is 2pm during the summer, but I would advise you to come early. The hike itself can be done in 1.5 hours, but with picture-taking, it can take as long as 3 hours (and the view at the top is gorgeous in many places!).Wear good hiking shoes. I've seen people wear regular sneakers (and even a guy with leather shoes -- what was he thinking?!), but I swear your feet will hurt if your shoe even manages to survive. Both Yeongsil and Eorimok trails have unpaved trails with unforgiving rocks. Hiking sticks would also help with the descent if you have weak knees.It's safe to hike solo (even for females) during popular days, so you're sure to hike with other people. It's also best to go down where most people are going if you started late (most people drive, so they go down the same trail they went up).In case of emergencies though, you can call their emergency number. (There's mobile coverage for most, if not all, of the trail). Take note of the location posts every few hundred meters. In case you get injured, there's this small train which can take you down, but you have to wait quite a while.

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014.  Glass is a common item we use daily.  But there in the Glass castle, they have made beauty out of something ordinary to something beautiful, works of art actually.  However, many tourists were not aware that there is a trail going round the Castle where you can see more sculptures placed along the trail.  A prominent signpost placed at the entrance to the trail will be helpful.  i am glad my friends and I didn't miss this trail.  To make sure it is not slippery during rainny season, the managements have placed gunny sacks along the trail.  This helps greatly for many of us.So if you are in Jeju, don't miss Jejeu Glass Castle.

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.

You want free entrance? Then go to this place and plunge into warm sea water in a cold weather.You will love the view and be amazed how the nature formed these rocks.The place is not so crowded by the time I visited this place.Going solo into this place. I met a kind Ajussi who lives in Jeju. He guided me to reach the top of the rock formation. He always come to this place to see dolphins and observe sunset.

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.

Went to visit this attraction even though I saw some negative reviews as I have planned some attractions based on region and this is some thing that I think the kids would love to visit.Entrance fee is pricey at $5k won as there is practicably nothing much to see and do inside. After buying the tickets  the staff would give the adults coffee and kids chocolates. The display were very old  like it has been there for 3 or 4 decades and we felt uneasy as it looks dirty. There is a kitchen whereby apprentice showcase their skils on chocolate making. Wanted to buy some chocolates since we are there. But they dont seemed to be interested as the minimum sale item cost about $39k for a box of chocolates. Not worth my moneh and thus left empty handed. Adults ans children were disappointed.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내

review: We went there in the morning. 2000krw for the entrance fee. Nice scenery view. Watch out for slippery rocks if you wanna take photos.

We need to pay for the entrance fees but it is not that pricey and worth it. You need to take a few stairs to finally reached the waterfall area. The view is very sceneric and worth to take a picture on every angle of it. A must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

Took a speedboat ride of krw10k for 15mins. Fun and thrilling with a quick stop for view of seagulls and black volcano stones. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver.Spectacular view even when you only walk 10mins from main entrance with free telescope. Didnt managed to climb to the peak. Reached there about 2pm.

This was one of the most interesting things I visited in the cheesy Jeju Island. It's a piece of architecture. Everything is about meditation. The buildings are angled to frame Seongsan Ilchulbong volcano and they give you different perspectives of it. I found it very cool.The entrance fee was $5 but it is worth it. You have to walk from the parking lot to this area  it's about 10 to 15 minutes. The views are nice.

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.

THis Maze Park is located between Manjanggul Cave and Gimnyeongsagul Cave. It was designed by the world famous company and jeju National University. The Park contains a maze that has 7 view incorporated in it. and here are three skywalks called ?gureum dari? and an observatory. There are four ways to get through the maze from the entrance. We had funny and enjoyable time!

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!

There are places in Jeju that convince you that you made the right decision to go there -- they're just really beautiful. Oedolgae is one of those places. It's just a photo spot that will take about 15 minutes of your time. The rock formation is interesting and the place is just lovely in a natural way. I gave this a 4/5 because it's not difficult to get there from the entrance of the park -- no steep mountains and such to climb in order to see the view.There's not much to do here -- just check it out and move on.
The water fall easy to find from central seogwipo very beautiful view from entrance And easy going down to the sea to see the waterfallCan find some lady divers sell fresh seafood

The view and scenery is good.The stairs are slippery so better watch your steps.Some stalls located at the entrance.I tried their famous Jeju fruit...taste like Mandarin orange (costs5000won-for about10pcs)

The tea caf챕 and museum were extremely crowded so we headed for the Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a delightful oasis of calm comprising an organic food caf챕 a large space for making your own soap and a smallish retail space dedicated to bath and arotherapy products as well as a small selection of exclusive souvenirs.  We had the house special bingsoo (the Korean ice kachang) and it was so refreshing.  Not only was the shaven ice powdery soft the red beans were tasty the selection of healthy nuts crunchy and various Korean rice cakes both soft and crispy were delicious - all in a great dessert.  Being starved of clean fresh air for a while during the haze season back in Singapore it was very refreshing to sit outside enjoying the cool clean air and view the miles of tea bushes.We were so entranced by the place that we returned for lunch the next day.  I had the rice balls with soba & oden soup while my sis had a mini hot dog with the same soup.  We then proceeded to relax with a cup of coffee.  What utter bliss!Besides enjoying the F&B we picked up body scrub facial wash and some soft drinking bottles.  The staff was friendly and fluent enough in English which made our buying experience very smooth indeed.  We will definitely return when we are next in Jeju.

The Sanbanggulsa Temple is located SSW of Mt. Hallasan directly at the coast. It is a very unique and colourful temple which reminds us more on the temple in Taiwan as in Korea mainland. The temple is located just below Mt. Sanbang. We had our junior with us but with older kids it is probably a nice tour on top including the temple. The view from the temple is very nice and gorgeous. Probably from top of Mt. Sanbang even better. The area is quiet and peaceful.? Except the opposite place where noisy? Korean caterwaul being played at a swing boat. The place is not reachable for stroller and wheel chair. Parking place available. Entrance fee is negligible for parking and temple access. It is definitely worth to stop and to spend some time. Religious people are probably also allowed to pray i guess. Doors are open.

Sunrise Peak. Sunset PeakWe travelled as part of a tour and on arriving were given the usual coach departure time. 1hour in this instance! Not sure of the entrance fee as it was included in our tourNot hanging around we set off immediately for the top with several good rests in between. The pathway is steep in places but in good order with plenty of resting/passing places. Separate paths up and down. Quite a climb but well worth it. Half way up is a little stall/shop for soft drinks and snacks (they have to manhandle everything up!)Once at the top there are plenty of viewing spots. Really worth the climb. We witnessed a superb sunset over the island and took some wonderful photosOn the path down there is a WC.We made the round journey just about in time with 15mins at the peak and a wander around the cliff edge on the way downFrom what I?ve heard the sunset is equally as breathtaking as the sunrise but not as crowded. Sunset was at approx 7.30 and on the way down the path is fairly well lit

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

read reviews on this place and thought should visit and ee all the hype. To start of with there is an entrance fee of 12000 KW its not worth it for the exhibits and it was all in Korean so really didn't get it at all. Anyways since I was already there just make the most of it. nothing so special so you can give this a miss if you have spare time enjoy the beach view is much better than wasting time here.

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). The only down side is that the area as well as the park have limited street lights so you'll be needing a torchlight to walk either early in the morning or at night.

Nothing much here unless you wanna do kayaking. No doubt the view is nice but the visit only took us less than 10mins cos we are not doing kayaking. Entrance is free. You can drop by if you have extra times to kill.
Not bad for visiting the entrance ticket fees is 12000won per person . Inside have a lot of things to view for sex and health...
Nice view here but too windy and cold for us who comes from tropical country..but we enjoy out trip here.. We eat at the korean restaurant who serve abalone poridge just the front of entrance..
Nice place to view all sorts of native Camellia. Entrance fee is cheap around 5000-6000krw.It's a good place for couples basking in the sun and enjoying the flowers at the same time.

My review is a little late but it's better late than never. We've visited this place when I was four months pregnant and I was able to hike up to the summit. This place is serene. It's breathtaking to see the wonderful view when you've reach the top. The kids love the lush greens at the hilly part of this place. It's very well-maintained. There are souvenir shops located at the entrance of the park.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Its still raining in Jeju when we arrived here. No regret walking in the rain and climbing the stairs when the view welcomed u so wonderfully beautiful. Spend at least 1 hr here to absord the view inside ur mind and take it home with you. Also try the grilled octo sold infront of the entrance. Yummy!
It only take a 1 hour to 1 1/2 hour to top of the Mt. but view is awesome. They close aroud 6:00 pm. entrance fee is 2000 won per person.

It is listed as a Unesco World Heritage and definetly a place to stop. Highway 1132 will bring you there and you cannot miss it. Be prepared that parking might not be easy and you may have to spend some time. The place is quite busy and many tourist buses are coming too. We had a cloudy day and it was very windy. Entrance fee is 2000 adult and 1000 child. Couple of shops at the entrance where you can buy each and everything. Please keep in mind that waste management is terrible as everywhere in Korea. If you buy something keep in mind that no any trash beans are available. The way up and down is quite crowded and loud. Obviously many tourists are rushing on top to get the selfies done to rush down again. The walk is definetly nothing for stroller or wheel chair. We went up slowly enjoying the view and getting some pictures. On top it is quite nice to look into the volvano and rest. Sure some pictures not to forget. But again very busy place and loud. Again our day was cloudy and windy but as long as it is not raining worth to visit the peak. So conclusion would be to visit the place very early.

I was here last week with my wife and we enjoyed the walk around this part of the coast. On a light drizzly morning the walk took on a determined bent but we were certainly not alone. There were loads of people when we were there. The backdrop is fairly dramatic looking and there is a small entrance fee. The view from the top at the carpark is quite beautiful too.

I was a little worried after reading some reviews but after going i am pleasantly surprised.  The entrance fee is a little high at 11000 won for an adult and if i had kids i might be worried they would get bored.  Seems perfect for couples and people who like taking pictures.  If you take your time and dont rush you can do the whole place in am hour.  Lots to look at.  Worth a stop.  Bonus...if your name is yoori you get free entrance and a free gift

Herb hill located a bit far from town and we having bit hard time searching for the right place. If happen to drive there by urself just key in Herb Dongsan navigation will lead the way. The journey from Seogwipo to this place it's approximately 40mins. There's two different entrance fees charges which is day entry or night entry the charges is 3k differences. Day entry - 9am - 530pm (9000won per person) Night entry - 530pm onwards (12000won per person) Before you get into this lovely place  they you hand you a map of this place which stated 15 Mark points. The park is really good for photography  remember to get ur tripod with you if you travel alone or just couple. =) come in at day time go back at night time so you have two different view of pic. We arrive at 3pm but we told the lady that we wish to stay until 8pm. and they need us to paid 12000 per person. But I personally think that you can pay the day entry price and stay till late night becos no one is checking the ticket when going out from the park. (At least no one check mine ticket although I paid 12000  so your own risk ya. Just a small tips)

Have to climb down the stairs with 3 kids. Very challenging task & we need slowly go down the stairs. It?s not that far. But the view & surrounding is worth it. The waterfall falls right into the sea. And i must say it is among the amazing sight in Jeju Island. You need to be very patience to get a good angle & picture. Need to get as close as possible & i think it?s worth it. Pro's : Amazing waterfall (can take good picture)Con's : Crowded & need to make sure nobody in front of you (to take a good Picture).By the way you need to Pay for entrance.

Everywhere was filled with silver grass. It was also a good walk from entrance to the hills with breathtaking view of the crater. Best place for photo opportunities. Perfect for those who love nature and fresh air.

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.

Calling this place a museum is absolute fraud. The entrance fee is 3000 won which is returned to you in the form of a coupon for the cafe or gift shop - both of which are insanely overpriced. The 'displays' are ridiculous - chocolate gold coins  chocolate Easter eggs  Guylian seashell-shaped chocolates  posters of the film 'Chocolat ' a statue of Willy Wonka. It's almost as if the museum is teasing the West for its chocolate traditions - if it can even be called that. There is really nothing of interest in this museum. There is  however  a pretty nice view of the ocean to the rear of the museum.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This beach's wave and view was beautiful and many people enjoyed swimmng and surfing in this beach. I enjoyed this beach's view in high place that's good. Some raw fish restaurant was operating at the entrance of beach. Though there was not big but beautiful beach.

C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) This temple was not famous in Jeju area but there was very good temple and had good seaview. There was not traditional temple shape and magnificent. Becasue there was not many people it was good to me with quietness and enjoying reserve. Recommenable place I think. No entrance fee.
Breathtaking! Enjoyed the walk and picturesque view. Really enjoyed the view. Entrance fee about 2000 won for adult and 1000 for kids
Be sure to witness the sunrise view. Its worth the climb to the top.entrance fee is 2000won. Wear comfortable shoes preferably sneakers

At first glance this place looks like a fun place but quickly becomes a waste of time.  The outdoor garden is the only place that is fun.  They have fun statues and great photo opportunities but as soon as you walk inside you will quickly become disappointed.  With the coupon entrance is about $12 and is not at all worth it.  If you come from a culture where sex is a taboo then maybe you will enjoy this place but anyone from a western culture will find it boring.  90% of the signage is only korean and not much else to see or do inside.  If it's a rainy day and you have nothing to do then maybe this could be an option but even then I would say pick something else.  This museum has gone through some changes over the years and you will notice that the more recent reviews are pretty low where as the older reviews are better.  It used to be a much better place than it is now~~

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.
A must visit when you come to Jeju. Great ocean views. Its quite a drive from the city around 2 hours but its worth the experience and super views . Entrance fee : 2000 KW

A great place to start off is the Women Divers exhibition center to see the old photos and explanation from the staff on the history of Women Divers. Than a slow walk up the peak for a great view ....  the wind was hallowing when we climb up and the local told us its a normal day ...   plenty of great eateries just a short walk from the entrance after the climb . A MUST visit .

A good place with nice view of the bridge and open sea. No entrance fees is required and is accessible via public transport and some walking is needed. Restaurants are available within the bridge area and other attractions such as submarine is located just right before the entrance into Saeyeongyo Bridge.

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.? Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!? It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

You can reach Ilchulbong by bus from the Intercity bus Terminal in Jeju-Si. It takes around 1h30 to reach it. You don't really care if it is an express or intercity bus you are taking, they more or less all go at the same speed... which is quite fast. You can't really miss the stop which is quite close to the crater. Dozens of buses parked in front of the mountain kind of spoil the nice atmosphere of the place but remember you are a tourist as well...  Left to the entrance, their is a nice small temple, worth the look. The climbing to the top is all made of wooden stairs and doesn't take too long (don't remember exactly, around 30 min). We did it with kids (youngest is 6) and she could do it easily. The view from the top is nice. It is a bit disappointing not to be allowed to walk around the crater. You can just see it from a platform. Before (or after) climbing, don't forget to take a look at the beach on the left of Ilchulbong specially between 13:00 and 15:00 when the old women divers are fishing.

Yes, the walk is steep and if you go for sunrise, you will be starting off in the dark, but it doesn't take long to reach the top (16-30 minutes for reasonably fit people). The most important thing is to watch the forecast beforehand to ensure a lovely sunrise. The views are outstanding. It can get quite crowded at the viewing   steps   at the top, so get there early to stake out your perfect viewing spot. The walk down will obviously be in much lighter conditions, affording some incredible views of the coastline and the little town of Seongsan. Early morning or during the day, any time would be a fantastic time take this short - but oh so worth it - hike. There is plenty of accommodation for all budgets in Seongsan at the foot of the mountain and bus 701 or 710 can take you directly there from Jeju City Bus Terminal. In April, 2016, the entrance fee cost 2000 Won for adults.

Yeomiji, located in JoongMoon sightseeing complex, is one of the most impressive place in my memory. - Entrance ticket fee is under 10USD, which is quite reasonable. - Area is divided by its own theme like tropical, Japan, Korea ... - Why don't you order a cup of coffee(or ice cream) and take a rest at the center of greenhouse garden- Observatory has nice view. but it is easily get crowded.Tip: you'd better to go CheonJeYeon waterfall(천제연폭포) after here. that place also has beautiful natural scenery :)

When you visit Jungmun Resort, don't forget to visit Jungmun-Daepo Coast (Jusangjeolli Cliff). The location is near the ICC and the Seaes Hotel & Resort. For KRW 2000 entrance fee, you get great view and it is perfect location for taking photos! It is said that the best time to visit here is during sunset.

When you said about Jeju, this Ilchubung will appear in the advertisement and you will know that is Jeju. But for sure, you will not able to snap a photo like in the adver since that only can be done if you take a photo from the helicopter and etc.For family, it is a bit tough if you bring small kids below 10 yrs old since you need to walk to the peak via stair and for adults people also a tiring activity but worth it since you can see the good view of the city and sea around that area. For photography also it will a nice thing to have.They said, the best thing during sunrise to be at the peak, but we are not make it during the sunrise so could not provide any comments on that. Also there is free show of diverwoman at the beach area just that area, they showing the activity of catching octopus with diving and selling the octopus to the audience. Most of the korea people eat it raw with Korean Sauce, i'm yet try the tast.Souvenir shop also available at the entrance of the Ilchubung peak.Thank You.

Went there in early autumn, the crater is covered with silver grass field, view is breathtaking especially during sunset, drop dead gorgeous!Suggest to wear comfortable shoes as you are expected to walk on some manmade rocky pathway. Parking is free and plenty of parking lots available. Entrance ticket is 6000 won for adult, kinda pricey given the area isn't big, but if you've never been there, it's totally worth visiting especially in autumn!

Went there by bus using the 201 bus line, it will stop you to the 'entrance' (basically the highway) which is a long far walk into the actual entrance. There's a small bus stop where you can take another bus in (slow) but taxis will frequent the highway entrance looking for customers. The cave itself its a magnificent sight to behold..it's huge! Not sure about all the negative reviews about it poorly lit and all, because the place is actually adequately lit (to fit the ambiance of a cave, no artificial colored disco lights) and concrete steps are placed everywhere in the tunnel to prevent accidental missteps. The ground is naturally uneven, you can't expect marbled tiles here. It can get quite cold and wet at 10-13deg, so bring a light jacket and proper walking shoes. Overall it's quite an experience, you can tell your friends that you've been in the underbelly of a volcano!

We were there at around 10 am and there were already many tourists and tourist buses. At the entrance before we climbed to the peak, I found out why it was one of the most popular tourist spots in Jeju. The view was breathtaking. At some spots, we could see Udo. Despite the flocking of tourists (majority were foreigners including us) and the time of the day we reached there, the view was so stunning nevertheless. The flight of stairs was nothing compared to the view we witnessed.

we went up by erimok, was the slightly shorter course but scenery was still fantastic towards the top. took us 3.3hours to reach the 1700m resting point which sells korean cup noodles at only 1500+won (ard there). this is not the peak, if you like to challenge yourself further, will have to walk for another 3-4 hours to the peak. So if you really decide to go to the peak, then just use the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa course, its shorter.We were lucky to meet some locals who advise us to walk down by yeongsil. And apparently yeongsil has the most scenic view out of all the courses. Only thing is that its full of stairs... so dont advice ascending by yeongsil. We could see ppl giving up halfway on our way down yeongsil. One more problem abt yeongsil for those who dont drive is that the bus stops 2km away from the main entrance (20mins BRISK walk) and its quite steep on most parts. Or else you can actually catch a taxi from the bus stop, should be a 5mins journey.

we went to this place, but we didn't went up the park/hill/rock, as it will require lots of walking, which we didn't want to do :)you will still be able to have an impressive view at the entrance, and amazed by this natural creation. you can see the people walking up to the peak, enjoy the strong wind, as it is located by the sea, do a little shopping around the entrance area, or even find a nice cafe that is facing the spot to enjoy a hot coffee!

We went there directly from the airport via bus (because it was too early for us to check in at our booked hotel).  At the place, the lockers were not available, unfortunately, and we cannot leave our bags somewhere. So we had to carry our things up to see the Seongsan Ilchulbong. We did not attempt to climb up to the peak due to our heavy bags. Instead, we opted to see the observatory at the side of the mountain (it was free... the side going to the peak has an entrance fee) and has a nice view of the sea and the mountain. Can even go down to the sea shore if you like (we didn't). The view from the observatory was breathtaking vast ocean, blue sky and cool green mountain. Will definitely go back someday to see the peak! Also, we tried the Hallabong softcone (ice cream) just near the entrance road to the place, and it was so delicious!!

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited on a sunny day, a nice change from the rain from the day before.At the entrance, you have the choice to walk around the short & free pathway by the sea or you could pay an entrance fee to hike up to the top of Seongsan for a birds eye view. We opted for the hike up.I wasn't very fit so it took me a couple of stops before I got up eventually..but the view was worth it. If you go earlier, you could catch the performance by the Haenyeo down by the shore at the bottom of Seongsan. Sadly, we did not manage to catch the performance.

We took bus no 100 from seogwipo city to the last bus stop. Walk up the road to the next bus stop and got on the intercity bus no 701. Got off at the beach overlooking seongsan illchubong. Plenty of spots for great pics here. Walked all the way to the entrance and up. Manageable. Highly recommend wearing good comfortable shoes. The climb up was not as bad as I thought it would be. The view from the bottom was quite intimidating at first  though. Many restaurants with reasonable prices to stop for lunch after the climb. Overall, good place to visit.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance (I have attached the photo) and you can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We alighted and headed to the dark brown beach along Seongsan. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore where to can pick clams and walkway with dry cuttlefish along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum as we reached Jongdal Elementary school at 5.30 pm. Noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market to Jongdal Elementary school (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier. We decide to go back as it was late by bus 701 back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal from Jongdal Elementary school  as we noted that the bus will take about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

We hiked this in December in the snow.  We started from the Yeongsil entrance, and just went up to the Shelter as we started pretty late.  The hike is tough for those who are out of shape but perfectly doable for regular hikers.  It took us about 2 hours up and about 1.5 hours down - the snow making it much slower than we would normally take (and more scenic, but very slippery in places).I would recommend good hiking shoes as the rocks are tough and slippery in places - I saw some people wearing what I would consider to be bedroom slippers and they were really struggling!  Those mini-crampons were also a godsend in the snow (the shop at the bottom sells them).Great views on the way up and from the top.  As we had a car, we had to go back the way we came but next time we will come when the plants are green and do a loop hike.  Can't wait.

We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do). The Sangumburi entrance fee is expensive if not in season to see the wheat fields at their peak and the changing leaves of fall, I think it was 11,000won or $11. I recommend going to Chefline Park if you are seeing this April 2018. Entrance if free there and but no volcanic crater. We went here and there was construction going on and the wheat fields had been cut down. They should charge less when construction is going on and the field has been cut. The walk around the park only takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. There are some nice views and the crater is cool.

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

Was recommended to visit this crater by our driver cum guide. Initially we wasn't too keen from the view of main entrance but we were stunned by the beautiful silver grass surrounding after entering. Climbing slowly is possible thou pathway can be slight steep. My parent did it at their own pace and there was a little hut & mini playground at the top for a rest. Along the way up, silver grasses are fully bloom and it views are fascinating with mountains seen faraway (like a natural backdrop). It's a sight not to be missed and understood only occur during autumn into winter period!! Thanks to our taxi driver Mr Lee Hong Min for the great recommendations.

Was lucky to have been here as it was free for the entrance. Usually per entry would cost 2000 won but it was a holiday. The scenery and view is amazing up top. The view of the crater is nice but the view 180 degrees around is way better. You will see the town which you stopped at and the immense coastline around. Would highly recommend if you can catch the sunrise however it is quite a journey away from the Jeju city which means you have to time your travel right. Visiting during normal hours will still give you the breath taking view. Just a catch, you would have to hike. If you are fit enough, it should take you 15 to 20 mins up top. Can be pretty steep so take your time and rest along the way.

Visited this museum with my kids.  There were hundreds of Teddy bears displayed over 3 floors. We saw Teddy bears in all sizes,  different era and occasions, celebrity characters dress up, themes etc.   Kids were excited to watch the free performance theatre with teddy bears dressed up as Elvis and his supporting singers singing. Every floor has different group of bears on display.   Entrance also allowed visitors to venture out to the back garden which boosted more Teddy bear statues.   Garden was well maintained and worth a visit.  Near the main entrance,  it also had a 2 storey high wooden Teddy bear which is a real attraction for the kids. The entry ticket is not cheap,  unless you are a real Teddy bear fan,  in my view,  it is not a must see destination.

Visited May 2016, season of summer but the day we visited it was a bit of rainy thus our tour guide told us to explore it before the rain totally pours as the place will be foggy means the view will be blocked. The view is nice, I traveled with my pregnant wife so we didn't went to the top as I assume you need to take that hundred or more steps to reach the top. Also, for the reason of not giving a perfect rating, the place is very crowded, though there is an entrance fee but no control of the number of tourist going inside. Its too many that we didn't enjoy much thinking that we visit it in off season, rainy weather, and even just wandering on the lower ground still crowded (refer to my picture that I took just in the entrance part only).

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Took bus 701 from Seogwipo (around 1hr20mins) to Seongsan IIchulbong entrance station. The bus doesn't exactly stop at the entrance, but you can see the crater from the station. Just walk towards it. A big innisfree building is where the entrance is. The wind was pretty strong on the day that I went, so it was a good thing I brought my windbreaker. I suppose on less windy days, it's not that cold as many were in shorts and t-shirt. ie, they weren't prepared for the wind and were shivering. It is a relatively easy hike up, proper steps and handrails (many elderly made it up there slowly, taking multiple breaks on the way). But if you are fit, half an hour should be sufficient for you to reach the top. For this short hike, the view is totally worth it.

this was simply superb. you need to buy a ticket for the visit and get to the bottom of it although i personally thought that the views were much better from the entrance up top. Empties into the ocean, what a view

This was one of the highlights of my trip. In autumn there is a sea of pampas grass swaying in the breeze on the slopes of this volcanic crater. If you walk up a little you get an amazing view of Halla Mountain and it makes for some great photos.  We went early in the morning and it was amazingly quiet - we could just hear the rustling grass.As we were leaving tour groups started coming in so could be nicer if you beat the rush.Entrance is 6,000 won which is a little expensive on Korean terms for a small attraction like this, but I thought it was well worth it.

this was one of  the most memorable places i visited in jeju. the coast was not an easy walk through, there were 2 entrances/exits for the coast. we took the one with large rocks we had to climb down through. (would recommend taking the other entrance which was behind a large ship) it was scary and there were a lot of sea roaches scurrying around. the VIEW AND WALK around the coast was worth everything though. the coast right infront of sabangsan mountain was filled with canola flowers.

This was an attraction I did not plan. But was in the area and decided to do. I did enjoy the climb. They have different levels of intensity and with this views are included. You can take stairs all the way to the top or you can slowly climb. Once up there the view was amazing. If you take a different way down you can even take pictures at a mini park with swings. They also had refreshments at the entrance and a small gift shop with over priced items. Definitely a must if in the area, but not necessarily worth to go out of your way to fit this place in. As its further away from other attractions and buses here can be difficult.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This place is just WOW. The views, the nature, the sea, everything. Even when it is a bit rainy or foggy, it is still a great experience. They do not let you in with any sort of snacks or food other than water, just so you know. You must try the raw seafood that the   mermaids   catch every morning. It is located at the bottom near the entrance. That is, if you like raw seafood. There is plenty of parking and there is even a Starbucks near by and other restaurants.

This place is easily accessible by bus. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about more than an hour to get to Seongsan Ilchulbong. After you get off at Ilchulbong entrance station, walk right into the small alley and continue straight until the end to the Main Street, you will see sign leading to Ilchulbong. It was a nice hike but a lot of stairs. The view is beautiful up at the top. There are plenty rest stop along the way so no need to worry. When you come down, you can go to the beach where you?ll find the house of women divers. There are performances at certain time slot but since I visited in the winter, there was none. They also sell fresh seafood where you can have right at the restaurant. It was quite expensive but It?s fresh and also to support the women divers.

This place is caused by volcanic activity, specially beautiful on October full of Flame Grass. Entrance fee is quite expensive, but you can enjoy beautiful views ,can see volcanic cones in other place even Seongsan Ilchulbong when it's sunny.

This park is on the mountain above the Jeju main ship port.The way up can be done with a car, then the entrance to the park is near the large white lighthouse with a great view over the coastline.you'll have their wide green areas. good for to chilling out but can be skip after the lighthouse.

This is the climb for the unfit too. It is relatively easy compared to Hallasan or Elephant Mountain in Taipei (not even half as difficult) and the views all the way up and down is amazing. We did the sunrise climb as we stayed overnight at Illchubong Hotel. From the hotel, it is about 20mins walk to the base - we had a car. There are many public buses that come to this spot. If you have 4of you, you can cheaply get a taxi to the spot for the morning climb.At the top, we did not see the amazing postcard view (aerial view?). If you wanted to take the sunrise with the illchubong Seongsan, you actually do not have to climb up the mountain. There is a huge area to view it as you drive up the highway.There are public buses to the entrance/ base of the mountain. There are 2 women divers performance which we missed due to the timing. It's 11 and 1 or 3pm. You can probably go to Udo island and be back for the late performance.Highly recommended to visit.

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This is a beautiful volcanic crater well worth visiting. It doesn?t take too long to reach the top from the entrance (despite the sometimes steep stairs). The views are magnificent as you ascend, from the summit, as well as when you descend. Plus there are various volcanic rock formations that you can appreciate along the way, both ascending and descending (the two paths are different). The crater is full of trees and grass of a very unique shade of green (I?ve seen this shade of green only in the vegetation of other extinct volcanic craters such as the ones in Tanzania). There are platforms to sit on at the summit from where you can appreciate the view. After descending, make sure to visit the cove where you can meet the Haenyeo or the traditional fisher women of Jejudo. The way to the cove is clearly marked with signboards and it?s only a couple of staircases down to the beach. The Haenyeo put up a performance twice a day, which is very touristy but interesting nevertheless. You can buy all kinds of fresh seafood from them and ask them to prepare it for you to eat at the restaurant. But it?s mostly eaten raw / semi-raw with various sauces and the typical side dishes. The sea weed is particularly good, which you get as a side dish. There is unfortunately no English menu. If you don?t want to eat raw seafood, after picking your seafood portion at the entrance, take it to the counter inside the restaurant and ask that it be stir-fried (?pokkum? in Korean). Beware that even when it?s stir-fried, it?ll still be more on the raw side than the fried side. The black sand beach in the cove is also a treat. If you look closely and attentively, you?ll find all sorts of marine life among the rocks, in the pools and on the sides of the mini cliffs facing the beach.

This crater was a 40 mins drive from our hotel, its absolutely worth the trip. It offer one of the best view among the rest of the jeju major attraction.The climb up to the crater was relatively easy and relaxing which was suitable for all ages, entrance fees to the crater was 9000 won which was reasonable for the stunning view which the crater offered.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

There's parking place but there's a fee to pay around 2000 won for my rented Kia Sportage   , Entrance fee was 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for youth . We walked around the park nearby the stairs leading to view the cliff from here .
