The Yeomiji Botanical Garden is easy to find and has parking places available. Entrance is not so pricy. The place is easier to enter with stroller or wheel chair. The glass house is quite big and divided into flower/aquatic/cactus/jungle and tropical fruits garden. The outdoor garden is also spacious but we did not go there. Not many people have visited the place. Consequently it was quiet and empty. The garden is very beautiful, interesting and green. It has also a lot of plants and trees but the wow effect is definitely missing.? On top of the glass house is also a view point with elevator connection. Finally I have seen much better botanical gardens.

The walk up sunrise mountain was  windy and relatively easy. Steps all the way up with many spots for you to rest and take in the beautiful view. Don't miss out on this mountain if you are going to Jeju. Entrance fee is 2000W. They charge for everything here, waterfalls and parks all have an entrance fee.

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The period I went was very windy, the surrounding was very refreshing with patches of green. Very relaxing, peaceful  and is a good place for photography. A typical k-drama filming location for kfans to visit! Once you reach the highest point, you will see endless of   green    and can even spot mountains that is far away. You can actually relax and enjoy this view by sitting at this cute wooden swing. Very nice place which you probably won't want to miss it.However, to visit this place, you need an entrance fee of  6,000won, But if you booked a experience tour driver with your own group of friends, he can help you bargain it to a even cheaper price which is like 3,000won per person! So, afterall, it was pretty worth it for both the price and this exquisite experience! Recommended to rent a car there, inaccessible by public transport!

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.? There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).? In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.? If art is your thing, then definitely go.? Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don?t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

The hike up takes about 30 mins depending on your fitness level and speed. It is pretty easy climb up the steps and boardwalk. It was drizzling when we were there. Nevertheless, the surrounding view on top was nice. At eye level, the crater wasn't obvious as it looked more like a downhill slope. It would be great if a an observation tower is built to have an aerial view of the crater.Entrance ticket 2000 won. Suggest you relief yourself just before the entrance as there isn't any toilet facilities at the peak.

The hike id quite steep, but only takes about 25 minutes if you take a few breaks. Entrance is 占2,000. The path is all wooden and carved rock stairs. It's a great view! We came here right before Chuseok and stayed on the beach across from Seongsan. We wanted to watch the sunrise over the cone, but the sun was behind the cone from where we were. Make sure you hike the mountain or go to the park to watch the sunrise!

The entrance was about $6. Loads of tour buses and families.  The view of the crater is great but there are so many people that I found it very unpleasant to visit.  You can't go into the crater, but only walk around the rim on a wide fenced path with noisy kids and tour groups. Not peaceful.  If you go, I would suggest very early.

The actual Hyeopjae beach, at the north end of town can get very crowded, but is close to the cafes on the main street. Personally we prefer the Geunmung beach end which is to the south, just past the Hallim park entrance.Both beaches are stunning with turquoise water and great views out to the island. The beaches shelve very gently which makes them great for kids. Geunmung particularly is awesome for the kids as it has little bays and rock pools too.

Sunrise is at 615 am . The entrance fee is free if you arrive before 7 am . Free Car park to the viewing points a short  8-10 minutes walk away , very doable and you get one of the most memorable sunrise sights . A most do except the getting there so early in the morning is hard .

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Solo traveling in Jeju Island is not that scary:) Koreans living nearby this tourist spot can speak English. So I am not worried about it.It was raining that day when I reach the place. Nevertheless, still can see the view at the top.The wind blowing my hair together with the greenery grasses and leaves of trees surrounding the peak.The place is accessible by public buses so I don't have difficulty in reaching this site. Though you have to walk a few distance to reach the entrance gate.There are educational boards installed for all the tourists to read and understand the history of it.It's worth visiting this place. Entrance fee is also cheap:)I visited Unesco World Heritage!

Seongsan Sunrise Peak is one of the seven wonders of Nature, a Unesco Heritage sight not to missed while in Jeju. From the peak, you see the remains of an erupted volcano.From the entrance, you can see the green mountain  view. From one angle you can see rock of the mountain going all the way to the sea. All in all an awesome sight. All of these accompanied by strong wind from the sea that is a trademark of Jeju. The park has two main path, one that leads to the peak and another that leads to the sea. There is also a show featuring the diving women of Jeju. By the way, there is also a place where you can see Jeju Horses, smaller than usual horses.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of Jejudo's famous icon.  I'm so glad i was able to climb this famous icon on one sunny mid day. When you reach this attraction, you will see so many shops for souvenirs and food just before the entrance and there is even a Starbucks nearby. Upon entering, you will see a ridge where you can go horseback riding or just do some leisurely walk.  The climb going up was quite a challenge for me but because of the magnificent and awesome views on the way up, i was able to make it to the top. At the middle part of the climb, there is a stall ( the only one there) selling some refreshments and souvenirs.  There is a resting area nearby to enjoy some refreshing drinks before you continue your climb.  Upon reaching the top, i enjoyed the cool breeze and the awesome view of the dried crater covered with grass.  Sharp  rocks around the crater makes it looks like a giant crown.  Coming down was a lot easier as there is a wooden stairs provided and the steps are even, not like the going up where the stone steps are uneven.  i would recommend this attraction to the physically fit only.  When you go down, you might be able to catch their scheduled show of divers and there are also boat rentals.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is certainly the top scenic spot in Jeju island. It?s basically a crater formed from volcanic eruptions, so it?s definitely has geological phenomena associated on top of being scenic. We drove from Jeju city to Seongsan for about an hour. There?s ample parking spots and entry fee is only 2000 KRW. Hiking involves climbing lot of stairs and takes about an hour to the top. We had a 2 year old with us and we could easily pick her and go to the top. I recommend carrying water and small snack items for energy. View from the top is very beautiful and obviously you see the crater when you reach the top. I think it?s top 3 spots to visit in Jeju Island and definitely a must if the weather is nice. Bonus if you during sunrise or sunset!! There are coffee shops (starbucks, McDonald, Paris Baguette etc.) and some local souvenir shop at the entrance. Enjoy

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seongsan ilchubong has a very nice view on top of the mountain or even before u climb. Everywhere is so beautiful. Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. Ilchubong means sunrise mountain. Normally people are there to watch sunrise. But we were there in the evening about 4pm. The view is nice too. There are performance of haenyeo (dive women) at beach near the mountain everyday at 1:30pm and 3pm. We missed the time. I was so regretted. The parking area is spacious. We had our dinner at a seafood restaurant near the mountain. Reasonable price with superb ingredients. Crabs, prawns, squids and 5 live abalone and other seafoods with only 100,000 won for 4 persons, we eat till very very full and satisfied (100,000 won is 3 persons portion). The boss of the restaurant is also very friendly.

Sangumburi Crater is our 1st stop after we got a rental car.It's 40 mins drive from Jeju city.Entrance fee cost KRW6,000. There are several small souvenir & coffee shops.It quite unfortunate for us because that day is raining. We're freezing because of the cold weather.We didn't prepare any umbrella or raincoat. So from the parking to the entrance, we soak under the rain.Thankfully the souvenir shop inside sell raincoat with the cost of KRW4,000.From the entrance, you have to hike up to the crater.The path up to the crater was breathtakingly beautiful.What makes this place looks so gorgeous is because of the vast flame grass field along the way to the crater.Sadly, when we arrive at the top, we couldn't see the crater at all.It was cloudy all over.  However we still enjoy the view.The walk down is as beautiful as it was on the way up.
Really nice waterfalls. Awesome view of the beach from the top. Entrance is just 2,000 KRW with 50% discount for military.

positives: truly beautiful and amazing views of nature scenery and the waterfalls. also, one can take a leisurely stroll in the attached garden park. entry fee was only 2000 won.negatives: there was a bit of a crowd the day we visited, although it was still manageable. the entrance to the falls could be tricky to find if you planning to go there on foot from Seogipwo town. Overlooking the cliff from the viewing platforms, the formation is indeed unique and a beauty. Walk along the surrounding path, we get to see the different angle of the cliff and the formation.However, you can omit the park. It is just an added attraction due to the price paid for the entrance.

Need more than 2 hrs here to enjoy the scenery and also street food at the entrance.  Be prepared to climb alot and travel light so you can enjoy the views. If you are driving, may need to park some place far off as the carpark can be crowded. Advisable to have a meal before hiking up and down.
natural cliff formation like steps, very much similar to giant causeway in belfast. good ocean view, cheap entrance ticket. a vert worthwhile visit

My view is totally different from the rest of reviews on trip advisor.I actually wonder if I had went to the right place. My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My family walked from our hotel to the top of Ilchulbong and down. From the entrance, the mountain(?) looked formidable and it looked to be a painful hike, but it turned out to be rather a short hike. I wish I had taken more time on the way up and enjoyed the views more. On the way down, we saw a restaurant by the rocky shore.  I believe this is where mermaids do their demonstrations and sell raw oyster dishes.  I wanted to go down but my 10 & 12 yr olds won't have it.  So I missed out.         The guy who took the tickets at the entrance surprising had a good nack for taking pictures.  If he is not too busy, ask him to take your group photo.         After the hike, we went to a bakery just by the entrance.  From the second floor, we had a nice view of the Ilchulbong and enjoyed cup of coffee with various breads.  The owner was very kind and let us wait out the rain in the store.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Kids may enjoy posing with Cinderella's carriage & shoe collection and running around the grounds.  As I was not however, although a few glass sculptures were interesting, I did not think it was worth the time or effort (& of course the entrance fee) to go.  Agree with the comments of previous reviewers who rated   poor  .  The  fish lunch I had at the restaurant next door however, was enjoyable. On the plus side, the place is wheelchair accessible.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).
Just a normal bridge like many others,it's kind of relaxing with a seaview..as it has no entrance fee, it's no harm to come to this place since it is near to where I was staying.

I've visited Seongsan Ilchulbong 11 years ago and this is my 2nd visit. Why? Because this place is so beautiful. The climb is really worth it. I took about 30 minutes to reach the peak. View of the peak and below are lovely. As the path to the peak involve stairs, be careful as it can get pushy (there are just so many tourist there). Entrance fee is 2,000 won per adult. Parking area is large but you will find yourself searching for an empty lot if you come late.

Its worth it to climb up there. such a beautiful and breath taking view from the top. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. entrance fee is just 2000krw per person. we actually drove there from our pension. many parking space. other than climbing the peak, you can also catch a Haenyo Diver Women performance at the bottom of mountain right beside it. its amazing to watch those elderly women  holding their breath for several minutes without any oxygen mask! overall its awesome! for those muslims, there's fast food restaurant Lotteria for you to grab your lunch or dinner since they have shrimp burger available. its located on your left when exit the car park area.

It's a must visit. We decided not to go for the sunrise as the weather forecast rain and we went for the normal trekking up the peak at 730am. Thank god we did not went for the sunrise as it was very cloudy but rain was later the day.It took us 30mins to get to the peak and another 30mins to get down. We do stop a few times to gasp for breath as we both are non-routine exerciser. No toilet available on the way up the peak, so just do what you need to do right after the entrance.Suggest to do your trekking as early as possible before the tour group arrives if you can force yourself out from the bed.As soon as we reached the ground, it was flooded with tour group and it will definitely block your view if you want to take photographs at the peak if you enter the same time as them.Tips: it is very windy n chilling at the foot of the peak but by the time you made it to the top, you are sweaty n warm. (I travel in May, around 18degree at that point of time)

It will take about 30 to 40 minutes to hike up the mountain which involves lots of stairs. View is superb, especially during sunrise because you will be facing east. There are quite a number of shops and restaurants down there, perfect for breakfast after morning hike. Spacious carparks. p/s: I read somewhere that there will be entrance fees (KRW2000-3000). However when we went there, the ticket booth was closed, perhaps because we went there at dawn.

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.

It was kind of windy when I had my visit at Yeongmori cliff. At first, I thought it was another ordinary rock formation viewing after taking a few steps from the entrance...I was about to back out from the trek thinking I can see much of these in the Philippines, but as soon as my tour guide led me to the farther side of the cliff, I started to appreciate how unique the lava rock formation  was.  The best view to take a picture maybe is to include Mt, Sanbang in the back draft. You may also climb a few steps to the top or catch a good timing for huge strike of waves by the rocks.  Wear appropriate shoes as the pathways are always slippery and wet.

It was amazing!This is the worth place to go. The entrance fee is very cheap just 2000 won and the transportation arround 3300 won.Then Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak will gives unique view that you will never see in another place. It is very easy to go here, just take a bus from Jeju intercity Terminal or Seogwipo Intercity terminal then stop on Seongsan Ilchulbong  Entrance, Just walk for 10 minute from the bus stop to the ticket booth.

It was a short walk from the entrance to get to the actual Jeongbang waterfall site, but was a grand sight to behold - you get to see the ocean from the waterfall! I also like that you could make your way closer to the waterfall by stepping on the big rocks around it.Between Jeongbang and Cheonjiyeon, my vote goes to the former. For the latter, the walk from the entrance was longer, the view was not as fantastic, and you can't get nearer to the waterfall even if you wanted to.

It is known as the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the ocean. The view is breathtaking, the most beautiful waterfall I have seen so far. Definitely worth the visit. The entrance ticket is 2,000 KRW, it is only 1,000 KRW for teenager.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.

It is a nice walk up to the top, windy.From the top we do have a nice view, wide view with many hills. Nothing special about the plants or vegetation. The entrance fee of KRW6,000 is a bit high when this is all you see.

Interesting way they hide it from free view, but a  nice drop and fall into the ocean.  Careful clambering over the cobbles and boulders to get your shot.  Looks like local vendors selling raw oysters of sashimi down by the shore.  Other souvenir shops align the entrance and exit.

Initially, we were only planning on staying here for a few minutes to take some pictures because the reviews were so mediocre. We rented a car and drove to the entrance our GPS took us to (FYI if you rent a car and don't read Korean, make sure you get a GPS with it, Google maps/Apple maps/etc doesn't work in Korea, only Naver). I think it was some kind kind of back entrance, off the road, because no buses or anything were parked there. There wasn't even really a parking lot. When we walked through the village, to the other side, we saw the big parking lot and all the cheesy buildings and shops and stuff. But from the back side, it was just lots of nice little houses (some I think still had people living there) and pretty, walled-off yards. We were there in the morning and the are we were in had almost no one around, except for a few Chinese ladies who had decided to leave their tour and were having fun (we saw them rejoin with their tour later, so I didn't pull that out of thin air, lol). The main front entrance area is way more touristy and that's probably all people getting off the bus see, hence the bad reviews. If you keep walking through the whole town and take your time (if you can), it's actually pretty and peaceful. I think we spent a couple hours here.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

If you're into nature, love moderate hiking and stairs climbing, love to see sea and city thru the bird eye view, taking plenty of photos of nature formations and also selfies (or wefies), then wjy don't you go to Seongsan Ilchubong, Jeju Island, South Korea. Designated as Unesco World Heritage site, this mountain is one the best place that you can hike and feels the wind blows your hair or maybe yourself too. The combination of flat lands and also the hike to the peak gives you an unforgetable memories. With each steps you take to climb to the peak, you will encounter several break spots or photo viewing for you to stops and take photos. Half way thru to the peak, you can see the entire city below you and starting to see the seas too. Hike to the peak, you can the see majestic view of the Seongsan Ilchubong itself. To your front is wide sea and the flat land (heard that it's actually a death volcano, correct me if i'm wrong) and to your behind is the view of the city and their surrounding. Don't forget to take photo at the peak's signboard. The formation of the clouds and the sun may give you the awe moments to you, especially when it reflects to the sea surfaces. When you go down from the peak, try to look at your right. You may see people going down to feels the sea water. Mind you, sometimes the wind blows a bit strong.  You need to pay for entrance and you don't like to hike to the peak, the ground is enough for you. Me and my friend, went there on Nov'15. Do try to enjoy nature at their best.

If you want to see a waterfall without the hassle of hiking a long way, go for this one. Just a little stairways descend from the entrance and voil - you'll be greeted by this pretty view of water flowing freely to the sea of Jeju.

If you one got time for 1 of the 3 waterfall in Seogwipo, you should choose this waterfall. View is spectacular, need to walk down the stairs to view the waterfall. and some actually walk very close to the waterfall by walk on the big rocks to get some nice photo. Plenty of parking space available, youth below 25 years get some discount for the entrance ticket (do bring along your passport). suggest to spend 1 hour there.

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I start my trekking 8.00AM at Gwanneumsa entrance and reach the summit around 12.30 and down to Seongpanak at 3.00PMPros : Magnificent various views(uphill), very easy downhillCons : No Hallasan view during uphillat this period, The weather is not so cold and the snow is still thick but robes and signs are intact. Good equipment is needed

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

I am used of the garden by the bay in Singapore which is great, so I went there just to depend some time and expecting something just .. so so.I was actually wrong. The garden is nice, outside as inside. The round shape with all kid of plants, the elevator to go on the top and enjoy a great view, the type of gardens outside (japanese, coreen, italien, french...).Sometimes a lack of maintenance but.. definetely a nice place. Entrance is about 7usd for adults. A little train can bring you around but I didnt use it and.. not sure it is free.

I admit that i lack of exercise, i keep thinking of giving up after completing 20% of the total course(at the entrance, there is a signboard saying that the whole course just needed 50 min). It is very tiring so please be prepared. Anyhow, it took me 80 min to complete the course. The view at the top is nice, i guess if you come for sunrise, it will be very impressive. Not suitable for those who are physically weak.

Hexagonal shaped rock formations jutting out of the ocean that reminds me of the kryptonite crystals I once saw in an early Superman movie. Unusual and definitely 1 of the places to see if you are in Jeju. Entrance is KRW2000, 50% off if you are below 24 ? foreign ID accepted. Unfortunately, since the best view is only through a series of stairs which ends at a platform, weekend crowds in bus loads can be a nuisance for that desired background photos effect or even a selfie. And I was continuously concern about the strength of the viewing platform to hold so many people at any one time. I got there in a rented car and discovered fields of canola flowers up front for good picture taking.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Getting to the crater was after a 20 minutes steep climb upwards via a rocky road made up of bumpy rocks. The steps got smaller, higher and steeper as you move higher up the crater. The view was amazing as you climb, and was breathtaking when you get to the top. The timing of the sunrise varies daily but the top may get a little crowded, so it?s advisable to climb up a little earlier to secure a good position. The way down was via another route, but this time, with proper stairway. It leads to another cliff of the just at the side of the bottom of the crater. You can either take the stairs down the cliff to the bottom where it?s closer to the seashore or you may go up the cliff and then make your way back to the entrance.

From the bottom Seongsan Ilchulbong looks daunting, but once you get walking its relatively easy, with many well placed rest spots along the way. The views at each spot are pretty great - you can really appreciate the black sand beaches from there. Take some water with you!The top of the volcano is amazing - covered in a sea of green grass, it looks like it could easily be a set in a Jurassic Park movie. There is something so primal about the feeling up there. And despite the many other hikers you will find up there, its pretty easy to find a spot to sit and appreciate it for a bit!The entrance is 2000 won. Take some water, a camera and some coins for the scopes. Also, it gets really, really gusty up at the top and along the walkway to Ilchulbong beach, so try and avoid any flyway items of clothing.

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

First and foremost, bring good walking shoes. You will need to hike up the hill to have a good view. There are many stalls at the base of the hill, before you pay to go into the entrance. As this location is near the sea, it is rather windy. A windbreaker may be required depending the time of the year you are travelling.Lots of toilets around, so there's no worry about needing it.There are many tourists as well as locals visit this scenic spot. Bring you camera as well. Note: This location is open depending on weather.

Excellent view especially at sunrise. Hiking was good for a beginner level. Many places to stop and take a rest if needed. If not an experienced hiker, it takes maybe 40 minutes to get up to the top. No entrance fee if you go super early. Lots of lovely places around to grab coffee or some food after you hike down as well. I would do this again in a heartbeat!

Excellent view and atmosphere! A long steep (with stairs) and challenging climb up the inactive volcanic island mountain that earns you good exercise and satisfaction! You can already enjoy the picturesque surroundings at the foot of the mountain with different views and you can buy some souvenir there and also enjoy a short horse ride (not free of course). If you are there on a sunny day, do buy some popsicle or ice-cream to go up.   There are entrance fees for the entrance as well. However, it is well worth it once you reached the top. It is fantastic to be on top looking down to the inactive volcano crater and enjoy the view of the sea that looks like touching the sky. You can literally feel like you are touching the sky too! The best time to go there will be during sunrise! Don't forget to take a selfie with the mountain height indicator board to boast your achievements! Oh, and just right before you reach the top, please take a look at the back downhill at the interesting look of the city below and take a selfie and also take some nice selfie around you.     On the way down, there is the fishing village where the you can enjoy the seafood while watching the women divers catch clamps and oyster. There are some fiexed timing but I have already forgotten the timing.    Seongsan Ilchulbong is indeed a must visit destination everytime you arrive in Jeju!
Entrance fee costed me 4 000 krw. Reachable by bus. The view inside of the cave is very intriguing and fascinating. For me, it is worth it to visit.

Disclaimer: this review is written by my better half since I?m obviously not part of the Hello Kitty! target audience.Omg! Everything is in pink! Look at the displays! They are sooooo cuteeeeee! I want to take photos with everything! I?m an adult in Kittyland! Omg, the cafe is so nice! I don?t wanna leaveeeeeeeeee......Back to the lesser half: if you are a guy, just pay the entrance fee and make the Girlfriend/Wife/kids happy. They will love you even more when you cough up for the overpriced merchandise. Seriously, I?ve never seen the Wife happier, not even on our wedding day.

Came early at 5.15 am. Reached the peak at about 5.35 am but there was no sunrise. Maybe because it was a bit cloudy due to the rain? The view however was still spectacular. I am a solo traveller and was worried about being the only person there early in the morning but nope, a lot of people including locals were there. The path was not too dark and it was a fair hike up. A few areas to stop by if you ever needed some rest. If you come in the morning for the hike, you do not have to pay any entrance fees which is actually necessary during the day (2000W).Oh the woman divers show. It was really a ?show? and then, they were off to the sea. I didn?t wait until they were back though. You need to pay the general entrance fee to Seongsan Ilchulbong of 2000W to gain access to the area of the woman diver.So basically I came here twice - once for the morning hike and the other one for the woman?s diver show.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This temple's shape was unique and located in cave. The way to this tempe was about 15 minutes in uphill stairs and had good view. Though it was hard to temple, but after climbing there was good, and could drink mineral water. Sometimes there was no climbing because of bad weather. There was another temple at the entrance of way to this temple, that temple was good and beautiful sculpture. Good place to enjoy temple and view.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Bring along a lot of water before climbing. There is few cafe that open very early at the counter ticket area, for you to have anything if you feel hungry before climbing, but just for snacking. The entrance fee is 2k Won, if im not mistake. The view was great along the way from bottom to top. After half-way through, there is a checkpoint with nice scenery of the city and ocean during dawn, which is so beautiful. Better to take picture during that time of your climbing if you climb to see the sunrise, because when you get down, it is another daylight scenery. If you are not fit enough or dont have that much stamina, don't worry, it is still okay for you to climb, you just need a strong will to arrive at the peak and keep on going. As the view from top is worth the sweat!For you to see sunrise, its better for you to be down at the entrance as early as you can, during my time, I already there by 530am, the gate open at 6am as far as I can remember. If you climb slow and steady, it will take you about an hour to climb to the peak. Just keep in mind, if there is a lot of clouds, you might not be able to see the sunrise. So check your weather before you go.

Breathtaking view when you reached the peak. Time taken from entrance to the peak ~60mins. You can get a chance to see woman diver show but too bad we did not get a chance for it due to time constraint. Tips: please wear comfortable shoes for walking, the stairs can be steep, and eat some food before that for good stamina.
Beautiful place with an amazing view...managed to get here just before the sun goes down, lucky me..really enjoyed the moment(priceless!!)Entrance fee = freeParking fee = 1000 won

At east spot of Jeju. Takes about 1.5 hour bus ride from the intercity bus terminal. Free entrance. Although the peak is only 180 metres, it's still challenging to climb because of the steepness. Very beautiful view along the way. The ocean and the mountain are all visible. Highly recommend.

As my country does have lotsa waterfall, this short walk for the scene just a ok to us.  Well, the difference is since we are tourist, so we visited the place. You can skip to pay the entrance fee if you are not keen on waterfall as it can be viewed and spotted before climb down for a nearer view of it.

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.
Another in the city waterfall which means that if you are staying in Seogwipo, you must go to see this fall. Entrance is 2000 won which is justified. Beautiful views.

After my Manjanggul Cave   expedition   and since the park is just along the way back, I took the chance to see what's the place could offer. I paid KW 2800 for an entrance (I have read reviews that some paid more than the cost, maybe the cost vary by seasons, not really sure). The maze can be finished roughly 10-15 mins, yet completed the maze roughly 30 mins hahaha. I just enjoyed messing around. Didn't really paid attention to the map and it's goal to ring the bell. The maze is good for family to enjoy.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.

A must do in Jeju. We hired a taxi driver to take us and it was 2000won a person to enter. We wanted to go for sunrise but there was an extra fee to hire them that early. (If you want to rent a car, make sure you have an international license - it's about 1.5hr from Jeju city) The hike really isn't too bad. It is an incline, and yes there are lots of stairs, but it is do-able. There were plenty of elderly hiking up and lots of places to stop. Beautiful view from up top. Entrance also allows you to go down to the beach and see the women divers and eat fresh catch.

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.
2000 won entrance fees for adults, but really gorgeous waterfall, nice views. Worth a visit, much more so than Cheonjiyeon Falls :)

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

We took the bus to get to this location and was dropped off at the bus stop.  There were no signs how to get to the destination so we went to the nearest hotel to inquire.  They pointed us the way and we forgot to ask how far it was.   We still did not find any signs how to get there but after walking 15-20 min found the entrance.  The scenery is beautiful and we took several pictures.

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

This small island with a unique history and is classified as a national recreation area.  It  is accessbile by a low cost ferry from  Seongsan which includes the entrance fee to the area.  Bus tours and ATV rentals are available.  The island has many small farms and peanuts are a major crop.

This is one of the best waterfalls in Jeju. Easily accessible from Seaogwipo city by taxi or bus from E Mart. Entrance will charged ?? 5000 or $5. This is the only waterfall in Asia that falls to the ocean.

This beach is less clustered by tourist and easily accessible. Take the 702 for an hour from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal and arrive at the entrance.  There are several food options and convenience stores.  The lava rocks are also pretty cool.

The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. The entrance fees is 2000 won and there are 3 levels of teddy bears exhibition and the ground floor is where all sorts of teddy bears are being sold. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

Suitable for anyone who can walk without aid as there were steep stairs leading in/out of cave. Floors were uneven as can be expected. We entered just after the rain so the place was literally dripping from the ceiling. One way in and out from the same entrance. Midpoint (the deepest part of the cave) was a formation that was supposedly the highlight. Lighting was sufficient to find your way around but not for taking pictures unless you are equipt with an SLR and a tripod. My 10yr old couldn't wait to get out as he was rather bored. No thanks to his father(me) who was busy taking pictures with long exposure :-)

Soesokkak is a great place to visit if you are in Jeju-do. From Seogwipo area take bus 110 and get off at Hyodon Middle School. It takes another 20 minutes of walking passing by orange farms. No entrance fees is required but if you want to try the transparent kayak or the traditional hand-pulled raft you will need to buy tickets at the counter situated on your right side before you reach the estuary. The clear green blue water is mesmerizing and definitely a great place to visit. Stop-by for a bottle of fresh orange juice to quench your thirst or a cone of ice-cream to complete the trip.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

Jeju World Cup Stadium is certainly worth stopping by if you are in the area. It looks superb from the outside and can be seen from a distance as you come down the hill from Seogwipo.Main entrance is open allowing you to walk in and spend some time in the stands for free. Tickets for Jeju United games are reasonably priced  and only attended up a small number of fans meaning they are up for grabs if you happen to time your visit in the K-League Classic season.Lots of busses pass by including the Airport Limo service (stop just in front) so pay a visit if you're a football fan or just want to see one of the 2002 World Cup's venues

I visited this place in January 2018. I traveled alone so I decided not to get into the theme park. I just take pictures in front of the entrance but I feel that this theme park is very exciting. I'd love to play when I come again in the future. Access to this place is accessible by bus/taxi. This place is still not crowded by tourists probably because this place has just opened and many tourists don't really know the whereabouts of this place.

Huge crowds. Same food stuff / restaurant items as if you were visiting a cafe in Busan. Perhaps there were one or two special items but probably not worth going specially for afternoon tea / food.Outdoor tea plantations were good can take photos to mock up a scene of you on a remote tea farm.Many tours and crowded. Had to park at an alternative lot 10 minutes from the entrance

Hello went there on a family trip with our small kids on children's day. Overall ok not so crowed as expected nice park and arrangement. However here some points which should be improved:1. Ticket price is 39.000 KRW for adult and 29.000 KRW which is too high for what is offered (still construction ongoing). Price should be reduced during construction time to attract more tourist. There should be family tickets with reduced price. 2. Bump Tube Car in New Oscar World. Its not mentioned on the map/guide and even worst its not free! You have to pay extra 5.000 KRW for adult (any maybe even more for kids) but nobody explained to you nothing was mentioned on a board. When you think you can take the tube car the staff ask for your ticket. So you wait 15 min then have to buy a ticket and line up again. Poor communication and every parents were very angry but had to pay because their child already lined up and wanted to take trip tube car. Very clever from the management. Why there is a need to pay for this attraction it should be included in entrance fee as this is already very high.  3.
