Helium balloon price is 13.000 KRW which is already 1/3 of entrance fee which is too expensive for a simply balloon. Should be less than 9.000 KRW at least. 4. The worst all the food where sold out in Food Court. Can happen but all food? We asked to call the other cafeteria and ask what kind of food they still have. They still had one food where we had to run to get it. We also asked what will happen if there is no food but the staff could not answer. Later we had to eat at the snack corner where as along cue and you had ti wait 20 min to get something. 5. Shuttle bus frequency to parking lot F shall be at least doubled currently one but and you have to wait again in the cue for 15 min. 6. Before you decide to go there with your kids you should check witch attractions your child can take. There are some restrictions on children's height (good due for safety reasons). Sorry the park might be nice.

Excellent visit to this world heritage site. It is easy to get to by bus and the signage also guides you toward the entrance. It is unexpectedly cheap and there are lots of things to do and see. There are also many restaurants to choose from in the area.

Entrance in Apr is FREE! My family had a pleasant time taking a bus 701 from Intercity Bus Terminal for 50mins and walked in 2km to Manjanggul cave.The cave was quiet and wasn't too crowded at the time we gone in. Just be prepared that it's rlly cold (around 5-10deg).
A must. Breath taking and unique. Wear the right shoes.  Take bus 201 from bus terminal and alight at the cave bus stop. Walk for 2km and you will reach the cave.  Entrance fee is won2000

You want to know about volcanoes? This is the place. The museum is interactive and informative. And not to mention it houses some of the most beautiful natural volcanic sculptures around. There are three courses to follow in order to see what the park has to offer - taking things at a leisurely pace, this can easily take 3 hours to complete. It is well worth it though - with the some of the paths in course two taking on an enchanted forest appeal. The entrance is 5000 won, and you can get to the park on the Jeju City Tour Bus. The stops are just outside the park. A good poncho will serve better during rainy weather than an umbrella here, as there are parts of the course with low lying foliage (and the wind can be a little ferocious at times too).

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

What a waste of money! Very disappointing especially given the very high entrance fee (6K). The crater is just a hole in the ground covered with trees and a 1.2 km walk is a loop around grass patch and small forest on one side (next to a busy road, so you can hear the traffic). If you have never left a city before you might like it (like, you get to walk on a grass for a moment, not on a concrete sidewalk, UNBELIEVABLE NATURE EXPERIENCE, right?). Just save your money, for 6K you can have a nice lunch, not 30 minutes grass walk.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We went on a cloudy day and the driver drove us all the way to the entrance at Yeongsil.  Having a hot afternoon the day before, we thought it would be warmer thN the day before as we Han to walk uphill. The driver saw us in our thin layer, offered me a rain and wind breaker and a pair of gloves. I reluctantly accepted them out of courtesy but later genuinely thanked him after four hours.On a windy and cloudy October morning, the temperature actually dropped as we ascended. Two hours later it got even much colder with strong gusts, as we approached near to split of the main road to either continue uphil to the top, or to go downhill to the other parking lot. I had to use my gloves and another layer there. My husband regretted not bring his hat on a cloudy day to protect his cold ears (anyway later I found his nose sunburnt even on a cloudy day)We used our walking sticks and wore our hiking shoes, which I found very helpful. We saw some people who really had difficulty completing the loop.  I suggest tourists first decide whether you physically can complete the four hour trip (adults) to the other parking lot. If not, better discuss with your driver (if using one) to meet in the starting point, or decide where to park your car, if not taking the bus.Pack your bag reasonably and don't take any unnecessary items. Some snacks are helpful though as there are no snack bar at all. I suggest also try to bring your garbage downhill as I don't think there will be regular cleaner everyday up/downhill for hours'hike.

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

we stayed 3 nights in a hotel right near Black pork street, and it is rather close to Dongmun market, so we came here every afternoon when we finished our trip to famous attractions around the island. Lot of local eateries you can try, lot of candy/chocolate and mandarin shops those are specialties of Jeju that you can bring back home as gifts. From the Jeju bus terminal you can access here by bus #100 (takes around 10-15mins). bus stop is Dongmun rotary, right beside the entrance gate of the market.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We didn't have great weather when we were on the island so couldn't climb the mountain. This was an alternative activity and glad we did it as it was really interesting. Make sure you go all the way to the end as you don't want to miss the lava flow. The ground is slippy in places and not suitable for small children, strollers or wheelchairs. If you're using public transport get the bus 900. Not the 701 as we did! The 701 has a stop called 'Manjamggul Cave entrance' but it's 2km walk away from the entrance!!

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

We could not come here to enjoy the famous sunrise, but we had the chance to see the sunset from the top. AMAZING! If you come with bus #701, you should get off at the bus stop called   Entrance to the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak  . from there, the entrance is only two blocks away. Climbing up to the top is takes around 20 mins. NOTE --> If you would not take your luggage or bag with you to the top, but leave the in the number coded lockers downstairs, don't forget to check the opening hours of the luggage store!!! When we were there it closed at 6 pm, we got there only 4 mins past 6, and despite the place was still open, the lockers could not be opened anymore even with the right codes after 6 pm. We had to call the emergency number shown on the locker side, to unlock it for us and retrieve our bags.

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Very well maintained and beautifully laid out area around the falls. Only costs a couple of AUD to go in and wander round the tree lined river. Plenty of lucky charms around for your wishes too. Very popular with tourists, I expect it can get very busy. Recommend the Angel caf챕 near entrance coffee ok and great free wifi. Also take a walk past the fishing boats with there large glass squid lights and over the nearby bridge on to the island.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

This was an exciting attraction. It takes about 1 hour to get to the end of the tube and back. The closer you get to the end the colder it gets. Also pe prepared to get a little wet, as there are drops of water falling from the top. You wont need an umbrella or anything like that. Getting here is tricky. As I was waiting for the bus to get here (990) I found a taxi and got him to take me for $4,000 won. This saved me a lot of time. It might have been too much but it saved me time, since the bus comes by every 45 minutes or so. There are restaurants at the entrance, they over charge for water so make sure you are prepared if you like to drink water. Definitely an amazing experience and a must do in the area.

This was a great beach and was easy to get to with a bus station right on the corner. Entrance was lined with a variety of vendors and there was a supermarket, well stocked in case you forgot something. There were many stores and restaurants nearby to quench your post-swim hunger. The beach was quite nice, water felt great and overall was pretty clean. The shower/bathroom area wasn't that good, but we didn't expect it to be.

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This place exceeded my expectations, it is definitely a highlight of Jeju, it is perfectly organized to be a journey itself. We spent around 3 hours walking around ( it has 3 different routes well explained in the map) and simply feeling the nature was already healing. The entrance is 6.000 Korean won per person. They have drinking fountains and toilets inside. You can reach it by bus!

These lava columns are a must to visit when staying on Jeju.  They are basalt hexagonal columns similar to The Giants Causeway in Ireland, though not as big.  We got the bus to the Conference Centre and walked through to the entrance.  They were amazing and were our favourite sight on the island, although you can't actually get down to them and walk on them.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

The maze is closely located to Manjanggul cave.The entrance fee is KRW3,300. The entrance is fill of cute cats.The maze is constructed by high and neatly-trimmed bush walls.It is not too large.There is an observation decks/bridge. From here you can clearly see path.As we're running out of time, we use the map to solve the maze.It took us 8 min to ring the victory bell.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The beautif beach is lined with numerous hotels and restaurants. There are also activities like kayaking available. Do go there early at least before 10am to avoid the crowd.Easily accessible by public bus, it stops right in front of the beach entrance.

Street markets are the same wherever you go, only the locality and design might change, so if you are looking for something unique this is not the place.I enjoy wandering through markets throughout the world, watching the locals go about their daily business and interact with each other. Also to see what the local delicacies are like.There are several entrances, with the street food stalls being close to entrances 1 and 2.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!

Since I am fan of Kitty White, I visited this place. Love the place so much, Kitty so cuteeee... But could be nicer if we can see the bathroom of Hello Kitty house (not only peek the picture from the door). Unfortunately the staffs not so helpful. There were only two staffs in entrance (one in ticket booth one who check the ticket). After I finished all, I went to front to ask what bus I should take to go back to Seogwipo. The one who were checking ticket asked me to ask the ticket booth girl, so I queued about 5 minutes. Then when I asked the ticket booth girl, she called the ticket checker girl to tell me the what bus should I take. All she said was   Go to across, bus number I don't know.   Hufffttttt!!!!

Quite a small cave.  Different coz it's a lava tube.  Go if u have time.  Needs about 1-2 hours.  Bus stops outside at main road which is half an hour's walk to the entrance.  Try to get a taxi to take u to the entrance.  Otherwise, skip this.

Pretty unique place, well worth to visit! Dress up well as it doesn't seem chilling down there at first, but if you walk until the very end, then back, it may take an hour. Also, getting there not that easy:take #701 from jeju city intercity bus termal to the bus stop named   Entrance to the Manjanggul Lava Tubes  . This is quite far from the entrace though, and the bus #990 supposed to go there is extremely rare, so not much chance except to take a taxi (it should not cost more than 3000 won/ride).

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Of all the waterfalls we visited, which included all the major ones, this waterfall takes the cake. How to get there:It is easy to reach, a quick walk from anywhere in Seogwipo to the shore. Taxi's help.Once you get there you pay entrance and climb down the steps to the beach.What we liked:Waterfall falling into the sea.Nice way to cool down in the summer heat (water spraying everywhere, cold sea water).Busy, but not too busy.There are much appreciated ice creams and cold drinks at the top of the stairs.What we didn't like:The idea that we looked as silly as everyone else with our selfie stick. Would we recommend others to go?Yes

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

Iho Taewoo Beach 댄명고대? is the closest beach to Jeju-si (city) and is closed to airport too, one can look down from the plane of the two very special red and white horse-shaped lighthouses when it almost reach Jeju Airport. Beach are sandy white and swallow water that are safe to swim. It is open for public and no admission charges except if is Jeju Iho Taewoo Festival.Visitors are welcomed to camp at the camping site. Facilities like charging room and shower room with locker are available too, is chargeable.There is two entrance to Iho Taewoo Beach, one is closer to the sandy beach and camping site located in the pine forest but less parking space. The other one is close to the horse-shaped lighthouses with huge free parking space and food trucks selling food and beverage. Here you can cycling and photographing. The two white and red horse-shaped lighthouse is famous for sunset photographing, it is best to be there around 5-6pm for the best sunset moment. Iho Taewoo Festival is around Jul-Aug every year. Local and tourist will be coming to witness the happening festival and event like boat ricing, fishing competition and many more fun activities. It will be a long day event.If you are driving, key in 728-3393.If you are taking public transport, take green bus 7,17 or 60 or blue bus 36

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. In the cruise ship, we could find seats. A 15 min ride and we were greeted by several e-scooters and shop houses. Here, you could settle for lunch. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Do be careful for safety sake. Returning from Udo Island was amazing : we could not find a bus stop that for the same bus number  supposed to bring us back to Seoqwipo! Nevertheless, luckily we had alternative plan ! we took a bus that brought us to Gimpo Airport. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. This DIY by public transport comes in cheap!This trip you need a whole day.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I never been to such places before so i have no reference to compare it to. I think it was worth the entrance fee, a bit hard to get there with the buses. You pay the fee for inside baths that are separated by male and females, where most of the people are naked. You pick a small locker room for your shoes and with the same key you can open a bigger locker for the fest of your belongings. You should shower before getting in the tubs and must pay to use the outdoor tubs, where both man and women can use(not naked). Try to follow the instructions in english of how to use the baths, for how long and in what order and it will be worth it. They also have massages, sleeping rooms, lounges, vibrating chairs, small restaurant ...

I have been wanting to visit the Teddy Bear Museum for the longest time but did not get to visit the one in Seoul 2 years ago. So, when we decided to plan a 2D1N trip to Jeju, this attraction is in my itinerary list. It is not located conveniently near the city centre and about an hour's bus ride to go to the attraction. I was so excited when I saw the museum when the bus passed by and alighted with much excitement. We were greeted with a huge bear at the entrance and it was like entering a wonderland. We walked around admiring the displays, the history of teddy bears etc. We also visited the outdoor park right behind the museum which are meant for visitors only. It was a fruitful visit and did not fail my expectation though. Love all the bears on sale at the gift shop but couldn't bring them all back so only got to admire them when I was there. If you are visiting Jeju, do drop by this museum to bring back childhood memories.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I happened to notice a separate entrance desk that had pictures of SCUBA divers on it. I asked an attendant nearby in simple English sentences if they had any SCUBA diving and how much was it? It was only 119000 KWon and they happened to have availability right away! I've dove in other aquariums but this was the cheapest and didn't even require a reservation on a busy day! Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids. They loved it!I still had to pay the separate entrance fee for the aquarium (about $40 but I received a 20% off coupon at the airport) but it was worth it. The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Would definitely go back.Note: A lot of the aquarium features the image of a whale shark. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I got to visit this museum as part of an inclusive tour so I can't comment on the value of the entrance fee, but I loved this museum.  I haven't laughed so much in ages.  I am not sure if it is meant to be so delightfully funny!  It is famous in S Korea for a TV series   about a Princess that was filmed there.What you get is several galleries of teddy bears dressed up as historical figures, famous art works, and scenes from history or of S Korean culture.  There are several large bears around the place suitable for having your photo with eg Charlie Chaplin, Michael Jackson.  Outside there are several bears enjoying the gardens again suitable for being photographed with.  There is a cafe and a gift shop.  The cafe was closed when we visited late afternoon. There is a short running show of an automaton Elvis-Bear again hilarious!  I would definitely go back.  This museum is located in the Jungmun resort area on the Bus Route 600.  Get off at PlayKpop stop - its just next door.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

From Seogwipo , we took bus 201 and it dropped us off at the entrance. The mountain is just so beautiful to look at. It?s a very easy hike, just 25 minutes to the peak. Bring some water . Drones are not allowed.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

Fairly small place for a hefty KRW10,000 entrance fee; the most expensive Jeju attraction. Features 2 galleries of teddy bears from various countries and themes and a teddy souvenir shop.  Will appeal to ladies, children and couples keen on photo snaps with huggable teddies, especially the human-sized ones at the corner of each floor and in the gift shop. Be prepared to jostle with crowds on a busy day.  There is a 5 minute T-Elvis performance held at every 15 minute interval in the Elvis Presley theatre.  Can skip if you're not a teddy lover or been here before as exhibits hardly change.

Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

careful of when walking in the cave, very uneven and wet grounds. The cave is very far from the city, the public bus does not go direct and takes 45min with many stops in between. When arriving at the destination, its about 2.4km walk to the entrance of the cave. If you are lucky to get a taxi when u alight from the bus, they will charge u 4000won to drive u to the cave entrance to purchase your ticket to the cave

As with everything on Jeju, this is built for tourists. The cave itself is interesting but understand there is nothing but this one section of one cave that you can access. This is not in the least bit adventurous - the cave is lit well all along its length. It's the kindergarten of caves but if you haven't been in a lava tube before then it may be for you. Beware that if you take the bus to the caves, you still have 2.5 km on foot to the cave entrance, though you can flag a cab down if one happens past.  Overall ok, but don't expect to be blown away.

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Although it takes about an hour by bus from Seogwipo hiking up this volcanic peak was one of the highlights of our trip to Jeju.  The hike only takes about an hour round trip, if you go at 1pm or 3 pm they have a women diver's show.  Cost about 2,000 won each and there's many food vendors at the entrance of the park.

A place not to miss if visit Jeju. Hello Kitty Island is not very big, to complete the whole place plus take photos it takes around 2hrs.The entrance fees was quite reasonable. Can take a short break at their cafe, their cakes are delicious. The public bus stop is very near the museum,just less than 3 mins walk. This place is also near to Alive Museum.

A group of 22 of us went to South Korea from 13 - 20 April 2014.  We visited Ecoland Theme Park after our flight from Jeju Island. If you have seern Disneyland  in California, you wil;l; have some idea of what to expect from Ecoland.  However, when we were there, there was this tulip festival.  So we got to see tulips of various colours in a number of places, particularly  near the entrance. Overall, the theme park is an exciting place to visit.  I have one grouse to make.  We lined up like everyone else for the safari park ride on the bus.  Guess what? Instead of our turn to get on the bus, the ushers pushed us aside and gave some other tourists (locals I think) preference to get onto the bus.  In all my life, I have never been humiliated this way.  Come on South Korea, especially Ecoland.  You are developed country.  Civilsed society don't treat tourists to your country like that. There were not  many animals in the park.  Safari Park Indonesia beats you flat.  I like tthough the bus driver got the bears to stand to get food thrown to them.

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

We paid our entrance fees and simply stayed on the top to get some good pictures. There were hordes of people down below so I don't recommend taking a long walk down and then back up just to get some pictures of other tourists.

We paid for our tickets and got past the entrance when it started pouring. We waited it out for maybe an hour or more  but it didn't stop  only got harder. The lady at the ice cream shop must have felt sorry for us because she gave us chairs to sit on while we waited and even some free chocolates. We asked the ticket counter if we can get a refund since we didn't actually see anything except for the sign  but unfortunately they said no. It seemed like it would have a been a great place if we actually got to go past the front hahaha! At least they made a lot of money selling umbrellas that day.

Waterfall is easily accessible from seogwipo town and surrounded by lovely parks. Entrance fee is 2000 krw but no one was collecting fares when I was there. There is a stairway down to water fall but you can see it from the top easily. Nothing spectacular if you have seen other water falls.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.

review: The temple is very impressive and is worth stopping at for an hour if you're passing the general area - that said I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to visit.No charge for entrance but a donation box on entry/exit.
The sunset at Oedolgae was beautiful. It was free parking and free entrance to go in. You can go down to the sea level but we chose to be seated at the top where we can see the skyline.

The aqua show was really the only thing we really enjoyed but it was too long and very crowd. This place is definitely on top list but very overpriced when it comes to entrance fee. Our family two adults paid entrance so if you have several children over the age of 3 it will cost lots of money and honestly not worth it. It was at the time we visited very crowded and long queues. We had for example wait 30 min in line to order food. It was raining heavily that day so maybe that caused it but to sum up nice visit but not worth it

review: Nearby the lava cave so we stopped by. The size of maze is smaller than expected but good enough for young kids. There's plenty of cats outside the maze entrance which my girl loves.

most important points1 start your climb early. as you must reach a certain point before noon and must start the decent by 14:30.2 take a bout 3-4 leters of water per person as there is no place to fill or buy anywhere on the climb (locals take tangerines as they are filled with liquid and sugars)we started at  the road 1131  entrance at about 08:30 and reached the midpoint at about 11:30 and then the top at 14:00large parts of the route are wood walks and steps but others are more difficult.when you reach the top make sure to take a picture of the tree with writing as proof so you can get a certificate when you reach the bottom (1000 WON)Enjoy your climb

It was winter when we came so most of the trees at the entrance were naked. But people were doing their warm ups for the climb to the crater with the lake. It's the highest peak in Korea so it takes about 4 hours to get to the top. It was advised to bring a packed lunch. I recommend climbing during the spring though. More trees and flowers to look at during the climb. The park is a UNESCO heritage site so it is definitely well maintained. They also have a building that shows the different eco systems that can be found in the park. Not only is it for the physically inclined people but the smart minds as well.

It takes entrance fee to enter the museum  but that's okay as there are three venues in total. With lots of different appearances bears  such as dressing up like students and wedding. The most memorial teddy bear is the president Obama  it is similar to the real Obama but in bear form. The top floor of the second venue is about wedding and relationships between lovers  so it is a great place for lovers to take pictures and have memories with the teddy bear couples. Although I am not a teddy bear fan  I took lots of photos in that first two venues. And in the third venue  bears are for sell  so please remember not to photo bears in the third venue as it is subjected to copy right. Finally  my father bought me a bear which I think is the cutest as a present of graduation. It takes about 40k-80k unequally per bear  but I think it is valuable as all bears are made in Jeju.So  if you think you don't have any way to spend your money  you can go to this teddy bear museum and buy your favorite bear as an emblem of stepping on Jeju.

It is easy to find and has a few parking places. No entrance fee. Restroom availabe at the parking lot. You walk alonxg the coast line and dont forget your camera. It is a nice spot for taking pictures. Has couple of small shops for water and fuits. Its worth to stop. Not easy for whell chair and stroller.

Given the trials and tribulations faced by the Dutch crew all those centuries ago  I did find it irritating that the top deck of the boat was closed because the wind had risen to a slight breeze. I am unsure what sort of risk or danger the owners were trying to mitigate against  as I am sure the bridge would have been perfectly sate and noone was going to be blown overboard by a tiny puff of air. The display inside the boat tells an interesting story. The Covid temperature readers at the entrance were causing the staff member a bit of trouble (and they are inaccurate) and we almost got the impression that it was our fault for being foreign humans unable to work broken temperature readers. Hamel would have given up trying.
