We finally found this street on our second attempt. Google map failed to function well in Korea, don't know why. Maps.me as suggested by other blogger was good for car travellers. It is not stable for pedestrians. Anyway, it's just opposite the jeju dongmun traditional market, cross the main road and the street is at the inner side. You may show the entrance arch to shop keepers nearby, they will indicate the direction. To me, the black pork is not anything spectacular, just common bbq as can be found elsewhere. I am not a food critic, hence I couldn't actually tell the difference. You can try any of the restaurants in this street. I guess they are the same. Enjoy!

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is for the female Merchant who saved people in Jeju island 17,18 Century, Joseon dynasty. Very carefully and beautifully made. However, it is limited for 3rd floor. 2nd floor is for kids' experience museum. 1st floor is for some special exposition from time to time. It is FREE, worth to visit for an hour. It is located near by Jeju coastal international port and Dongmun traditional market. Actually from this market, exit/entrance #3, it is just 500 m away. In those times, people in Jeju island could not get out of the island, however, since she saved whole population in the island, The King Jungjo wanted to give a awards but she refused. Instead, she asked him she would love to visit the peninsular once, and wanted to travel in Diamond mountain(located in North Korea now). So she could get the chance to meet the King and travel inland. Under the Patriarchal system, it must be very hard for her to work as a merchant, but became the most rich person in Jeju, then when there was big famine, she released whole rice and food for free to Jeju people. Any way, it was great fun to enjoy each section from her birth to death. All explanation are in English and in Korean both.

This huge place has many shops and stalls selling household items, fish and seafood.   And there is also the food street selling all kinds of local food.   Just be careful and remember which gate/entrance you enter or else you may find yourself lost and spend time trying to find your way out.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The waterfall is not too far from the entrance. Just take a short walk around 5-8 minutes and then you will find the waterfall. For young children, must assist by adults, because on the way to waterfall there are many big rock. The wind is so strong. The waterfall is special because it's located near beach.

The temperature drops dramatically after you descend 15 stairs into the cave entrance.  There was a cloud that had formed at the entrance due to the humidity which was really cool to see.  Walked about a km to the end where there is a lava column - a frozen in time dripping of lava from above.  Fascinating walk, lots of people (some in heels which I wouldn't recommend).  Really beautiful way to spend an hour or so.  Especially when it is super hot and humid outdoors!
The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.
Since when did it became samsung ? The place spelling is wrong.! Anyway.. Nice to visit, entrance fee for adults 2500krw only and nearby is the folklore and natural history museum.

Sangumburi crater is a designated Natural Monument touted as the world's only flatland crater. The car park entrance showcases several large rocks from the crater such as the volcanic bomb and lava tree mold. During the eruption, molten rock flew from the volcano into the air and cooled into many exotic shapes. The area near the crater also contain several traditional Jeju graves - wide, trapezoidal stone walls surrounding the burial mounds. Visitors can walk around the extinct volcano crater rim, peer into it but cannot venture inside the crater pit covered with lush vegetation. The hills and Hallasan surrounding the crater is a picture of serenity and rustic greenery. Sangumburi is especially popular in autumn when the slopes are covered in Jeju?s famous Eulalia. Crowds and couples will be lining up for photos among the tall plume-like, silver grass swaying in the breeze. At a quiet spot, listen to the whispers of the eulalia dancing against the blue sky to add a pensive mood to the autumn romance.  Note: KRW6000 entry fee is quite expensive. Closes at 6 pm, except Nov-Feb closing at 5 pm.

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Our guide brought us here to understand the striking cultural lifestyle of the local folks of Jeju.  The unique and exquisite architectural design of the `primitive'' huts and cottages of the natives was impressive. The pair of well carved and exotic Jeju deities statues that were made from volcanic lava stood spiritually on guard at the entrance. The sculptures matched harmoniously with the decorative Kimchi clay vases left unattended in the manicured lush green lawn compound displaying a special cultural taste that reminded me of the unique Hindu traditions on the island of Bali. I always think that it is the vibrancy and dynamism of the native folk culture that made certain attractions so special. The unique Alisan native lifestyle in Taiwan is just remarkably outstanding and different from that of the Maori in New Zealand and again, distinctively unique from the Dayaks longhouse traditions. It is thus a pleasure and a must thing to do to visit a folk village in Jeju to look at how the culture of the natives and how it is being preserved here.  We were introduced to a guide speaker who showed us the many agricultural tools used by the local natives but the real commercialized promotion began when we were `lured' into a room with seats and the speaker started marketing a type of drinks made from `Wuweiji' traditional herb that grew in abundance in Jeju and is believed to strengthen and invigorates the mind and body. It looks like another `tourist trap' and on the pretext of going to the toilet, I escaped the aggressiveness of the marketing talk. I wandered around the cottage compound admiring the foliage and the surrounding native architectural designs until my group of friends came out from the promotion. One of my group members was anxious to purchase the `elixir' drinks to enhance her youthfulness and she shared the drinks with the rest in the group.   I came out from the cottage and saw there were many similar cottages around the village and there were many sales talk going on in the other cottages. The admission to this folk village was free but I am not sure if my guide earned any commission from the purchase of the herbal bottled drinks by my friend.Except for the commercialized promotion, it is interesting to visit a folk village in Jeju.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

on reaching the car park ., Go and grab a J - Shape ice cream before you buy the entrance ticket to this Unesco Sights . To those who is not so fit you will be able to rest on the way uphills with the friendly stools provided at different stage of the climb upwards . Wonderful Sight await you on reaching the peak and you will want to catch up on your breadth as you soak in the sights . Never to be missed !!

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

Massive ground. A full walk about will take 2hrs easily. Even though all the stones look similar after an hr, it's a very effective way to understand the folklores of Jeju. Cheap entrance fee of only 2K won.Some places near the museum are still under renovation when we were there.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Lots of fun! Dozens of tame affectionate kitties greet you at the entrance. Cute kittens too! There is a toddler playground with toddler-sized shops play kitchens, jungle gym, rope course, teeter totter? al kid sized. Plenty of great spots for selfies of all kinds. The maze is very tall and take a good 15 minutes at full sprint to wind through and capture stamps on the way to ringing the bell. If you are feeling silly or have small a children with you, this is the spot!

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was 15-min walking from our hotel, and admission was 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenages (up to age 24). You purchase at ticket box, but don't throw or put tickets away, as they check for them close to the entrance.  It was an easy walk, not too many steps down to the sea level.  Nice waterfall, where you can get close to it should you choose! If low tide, there is a pebble/sand pit area revealed, where you can get to by carefully climbing over some rocks...but could be slippery...so weigh the risk carefully!  However, pictures taken from this angle - with the waterfall as the backdrop - was breathtaking!

It smells so good as soon as you get off the car and pass the entrance. After a short walk, you get to the Forest.  It is also easily accessible for baby strollers as they put some straw mats alone the forest so the whole family can enjoy a wonderful walk in the forest.  Not sure if wheelchairs can roll easily on those mats though but I saw quite some baby strollers.We took a detour after Sangumburi crater (about 20 min away), and spent about an hour in the forest but didn't complete it. Then in another 20-30 min, we arrived at a Five Day Market, which is about 10 min from the Haeyeo (Women Divers) museum.So this was how we planned our route to and from the forest.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

It falls into the sea,  very unusual. Wear walking shoes if you're going there as there are uneven rocks leading to the fall. Saw several kids slipped & fell down. Painful indeed.  After purchasing the entrance ticket,  there's a walkway that leads you to the fall.  But the last 100m or so is uneven rocks surface.  It's nice to walk nearer to the fall so you can feel the mist.  Refreshing.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I had always wanted to go to a maze park, and finally I did in jeju :) it was a small maze but enough to make us excited to find our way out. The entrance fee is 33,000 won for adult. In front of the entrance, there were lots of cats and quite tame too.

Heard there are several entrance, but only one is open to public. The cave has been fitted with a pathway that takes away the hard work of walking on rocky surface for you. It is still quite deep though and will be challenging for anyone with lower fitness level. The tube is lit along the way and it is quite cold. If you've visited a natural cave before, this cave might be less interesting.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Having just climbed Hallasan the day before, we decided to just take some pics from the ticket office entrance and treat ourselves to icecream on a hot late morning - delish. Many a shot has been taken, looking up to the falls, but did anyone ever wonder about its source? And so, on our way out, I peeked over a stone wall and sure enough, Jeongbang Falls as it drops over into the ocean. Click2. I like to think I'm the first to snap this. Ha2.

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

Finally we met a Filipino tourist guide here in Seongeup Village. She can speak english very well but of course we used our native tounge/language so she was able to explain to us very well the history of the village and Jeju as well. It's only from her where we learned that the famous Jeju Black Pig used to eat human poop/dung (but that was circa 1940's or earlier).  We also learned from Grace (name of the Filipino guide there) that Korean women, during the early years, were the one who work for the family while the husbands only stay at home. Sad to hear that. =/ We also learned about the history of Stone Grandfather Harabong as well as the various symbolisms used in Jeju.When in Seongeup, make sure to try their Omija, an herbal drink made out of fermented berries. It can help cure acne, headache, kidney problems and good for diabetics. Kinda pricey but worth a shot. They also have other herbal medicines which you can try. As we all know, Koreans, especially their ancestors, are used to taking medicinal plants so I guess they are really credible enough when they say that this or that plant is effective for healing ailments. Google the benefits of OMIJA.By the way, this is also the place where the famous Koreanovela Dae Jangeum (Jewel in the Palace) was filmed.If you happen to visit Seongeup Village, ask for Grace as a guide. You will definitely learn a lot. And oh, we get to check out old korean houses as well. ^_^NOTE: I think there are many communities within Seongeup village but ask your guide to specifically drop you off at the community where Grace is. No entrance fee as well.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Do this! I hiked to the peak with my sister and i'd say both of us are average when it comes to our fitness level. We took the  Seongpanak route, up and down and it took us 6.5 hours. When we got to the peak it was really chilly, so be wise and pack a light windbreaker/jersey. It's a beautiful hike through the mossy trees. Be prepared for too many stairs to count and hundreds of Asians taking selfies. You can buy yourself Kimbap at the start of the hike to fuel yourself or to eat as a much needed snack at the peak. There is one or two bathroom points on the way and a place to refill your water bottle. Entrance is free

Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.? The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.? The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.? The calm music playing enhanced the experience.? The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.? Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

Wow, wow, if you love to hike, this is awesome. Tons of steps. As I came up on the entrance I was expecting Khaleesi to come around the bend with the Dothraki horde. With the rain coming down I felt like I was in another world. It is a hike with lots of stairs about 180 meters but so worth it, dry or wet (with caution). I did it wet and no regrets.

We went sometime March so the weather was a bit cold and the wind was strong since the mountain is near the ocean. Suggest to wear something warm and put on comfortable shoes for the hike. There are also cafes (Starbucks, etc.) and shops (Faceshop, local souvenir shops, etc.) by the entrance.

Was really excited when going up the crater as this place is one of the UNESCO heritage site. Upon reaching the entrance was a really beautiful place as it was well maintained. The hike is gradual, suitable for kids and elderly.However upon reaching the peak, it just looks like a patch of green field on the crater, nothing impressive at all. I guess it's just for the experience.

It is a great place for families, whether you are just playing in the snow or hiking there. We intended to hike a bit, but we didn't have clampons on, we only did that for about 10 mins. On descend, we found out that they can be bought at the convenience store at the entrance. Otherwise, it would  have been a great place to hike

Went there with my other half but we didn't do a race. Spent about half an hour there to figure out the maze. its actually pretty obvious from the mini map they gave you but we took on the challenge of not using the map at all. Recommended to do a race and first to the bell tower wins! Its a little pricey for just half and hour of fun though. Paid about 4-5k won each. Cat lovers will love it there as they have free roaming cats around the entrance :)

We first went to this museum 7 years ago and wanted to visit this place again hoping there is some new attraction.  Sadly nothing has changed and lesser crowd.  Entrance fee is not cheap and I don't think its really worth to go unless you love teddy bear. We are out by 1 hour and kids wasn't very excited with the same display.

This is a pretty big park that has a little bit of everything from history folklore and stones.  I had to convince my friends to check it out and only won when i told them it was like 15 minutes from where we were staying.  However they both were quiet happy with the decision since it was empty and just a lovely walk through nature with some great smells.  Even the trash cans are made out od stone pits.  I thought we would only go for like 30 minutes but ended up being there for an hour and a half.  Other bonus is that for the month of may there is no entrance fee!

The village is huge explaining about the cultures of jeju folks. Plenty of photo shooting corners beautiful flowers farm.There is also a shop renting korean traditional clothes (hanbok renting) where you can wear the clothes and walk around the village for photo shooting. the price is reasonable (comparable to those hanbok renting shop in jeju city)estimate to spend 3 hours there.youth and kids got discount for the entrance fee (do bring passport along)is a must visit spot if you come to jeju.

The parking is free . Entrance fee was 2000W per Pax. You first descend about 5 minutes to a blue pond with the first waterfall . Beautiful and stunning . Then you proceed to the second waterfall about 10 walk . There was a third waterfall but it was about 40 minutes walk so we decided not to do that one . A five minute walk brought us to a bridge  which would bring you to another route . Overall expect to spend between 1-2 hours here .

The aquarium is spacious.  You can see a lot of sea animals no matter how hot cold or rainy the outdoor is.  Taking a leaflet at the entrance is a must because the show time is up-dated.  It is so funny to see the penguins line up to eat food and jump up the stairs.  The otters are also interesting when you see them playing through the tunnels and on the swinging bed.  The 'stars' of the aquarium can be seen at the theatre which is attractive and interesting. My family stayed there for more than three hours.  The soft toys sold there are in good quality and my daughter bought a penguin as a souvenir.  There are food shops for people to enjoy but we didn't try any.

review: The aquarium is good and English-friendly (so you know what you're looking at). The show at the end is aimed at kids and solely in Korean but as it's mostly visual that's not a problem. Families can definitely spend a fun few hours here. However the admission fee is excessive (40900 won for adults at time of writing) especially when most of the other main attractions in Jeju are either free entry or priced around 2000 won. I think this one ticket cost me more than all other entrance fees during my 5 day visit to the island combined. If you aren't visiting with children I suggest giving it a miss.
