입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Out of our surprise no entrance fees needed when you visit Jeju Folk museum. There was a guide that told us about their culture and was a nice experience for us and even the kids. The village was small but a nice encounter. An hour is more than enough.

Our son LOVED it here and has been asking to go back daily since we left. It could use a few more things to do  but you can easily spend a good few hours here  especially if your children are familiar with the animation. Everything seemed very safe and well organized. We didn't pay extra money to go into the play area  but it sounded like kids were having a blast in there too. No idea why adults have to pay entrance though.... as theres nothing for adults to really do and the only reason they are entering is to go with their children. Many play parks around Korea offer free entry for adults  it's a shame here doesn't follow suit. Also  the kids play room with the balls and lego blocks is a little lacking..... our son still loved it  but it could use a few more items to build/play with etc

Love Land is the place i visit and having so much fun in jeju! entrance fee w9000 per person but seriously worth it cos place is huge with indoor and outdoor. outdoor with all the sex pose statues very embarrassing while walking around the park. but i really do enjoy! its cute and some sexual knowledge >///< visit during January spend about 2 hours plus in the park. i believe can be more but due to weather is super cold we couldn't stand the windy cold we left right after round the whole park. basically is 80% outdoor and 10% indoor + 10% indoor souvenir shop.

It's fun about this place. Entrance fees 12 000 won per person. There's is a show every hour about 15mins each show. But one thing need to highlight is  the explanation are all in Korean words. So for foreigner like us may have difficulties on understand the instructions on the activities. But so far I very enjoy. Is good for indoor visit especially during raining day.

It was hot at the cave entrance at 32 degrees.  There is notice at entrance on temperature drop to 10 degrees as we continued the walk.  It is a 1 hour to and fro walk along the dark and slippery caveт囹. Good for those who like trekking.

It is located at the nearest to the entrance of the district. Although I have also been to some similar 4D museum in Thailand before it is still big and fun to visit this museum! We spent around 2 hours taking photos and is quite fun!

In Jeju  we had the opportunity to visit the Jeju Art Museum & Glass Castle  which is a theme park featuring an exhibition hall  garden and models made entirely of glass. One must spent at least two hours or more to walk around the indoor and outdoor areas. Nearby the entrance  there is a display ?쏥lass Worldwide??and the countries that produced glass are mentioned here - China  Italy  Czech Republic  Arab and Japan. Once you step indoor  a large glass beanstalk from the fairytale ?쏪ack & the Beanstalk??will greet visitors.The world's largest all-glass labyrinth  glass ball  glass diamond  a glass stonewall  mirror lake and a glass bridge are found in the model parks here. In one part of the outdoor theme park are Cinderella's glass slippers and a glass carriage. One will be held in awe at the marvellous pieces of art  all made entirely out of glass! Truly an eye opening experience!

If you visit Jeju especially Seogwipo you don't want to miss to visit here. With entrance ticket KRW 9000 you can see and take photos of many art galleries in 3D. It's a fun experience. So many photos you could take in this big museum it's too bad that I only spent about 2 hours in here because I didn't have much time then. I suggest to visit this museum in the morning and prepare to spend 3-4 hours in here. I visited here at noon and it's a bit crowded with people.

If you just wan to spend for few hours while waiting for your flight. Here the good place. Entrance 8000KRW.  A small area block up for your big luggage you will have locker for your shoe. Once you enter inside you will find a long locker to store your belonging. It can fit in a small backpack.  Take a spa relax and rejuvenate before go for rest room. There are a lot ppl go there for overnight stay even it is weekday perhaps just their culture. The living hall area and sleep place rather to say it's hot I will say is steaming. If you kind of person can't stay for hot this might not be a good place to sleep for you unless you are very tired. You can take blanket from the counter you pay for your entrance fee. Where the pillow just look it from any empty room

I visited this place since my hotel is directly opposite it and I had an hour to spare before my flight home. This is the former central government office from 1392 to 1910. The compound consists of 7 buildings with signages in English. It was quiet and peaceful there as I met less than 10 visitors during my visit. Entrance fee is 1500 won. Toilet facilities available.Tip:  One can wear the traditional costume and take photos with 2 figurines for free. It is unmanned just help yourself. It is located at the left corner of the entrance building.

Great for experiencing traditional Korean Culture. I recommend around 2~3 hours there. It's quite big and there's a lot to see and experience. We went there during the first weeks of October and it was very green and lush. I think in summer and spring it's gonna be even more pretty. Different types of Korean housing and different lifestyle (farmer student worker etc.) are portrayed very well and the tools they used are there to see. There is also a convenience store near the entrance which doesn't work with cash.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

this beautiful mountain is located in the east side of island , from centre of jeju to mountain is around more than an hour . entrance ticket is 2 dollar and your journey will start from bottom of mountain , korean made easy stairs which really don't bother u that much . i visited mountain on evening so like sunrise which is famous , sunset can be too . this is a must so go n enjoy it .

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!

The theme is good and it is very funny and interesting. Although we arrived the entrance at 18:00, we were able to complete the adventure within half an hour. Highly recommend for you especially with kids.

Taxi took us here as part of a few hours tour.  It's a pretty waterfall, but I thought Cheonjiyeon Falls was more impressive with 3 layers so if you are nearby, it's worth going, however, if you only have time to go to one, I'd choose the latter :).  Both have small entrance fees per person.

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. Spend 3 hours there.Suggest to go for a toilet break before going thru the entrance.Bring baby carriers, cause the road is uneven. Have to be extra careful especially going with kids.There are 2 entrance. (follow the counter clock wise direction, where the entrance is situated behind the huge ship)Enjoy the scenery, watchout for the waves too.Their is a canola flower field where you can take some instagram photos too (need to pay to enter)

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Jeju Glass Castle is a must see museum. It has outdoor which can be seen with in 2 hours & indoor as well. There are a lot of glass shapes. This museum is good for people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. The entrance ticket is little bit expensive.

It?s about an hour?s drive from the airport. Entrance is KRW11,000 for one adult.  The tulips and cherry blossoms were in full bloom. So lovely!  A surprise was the caves. It?s so cool!  Really worth the visit.

I saw all 3 waterfalls near Seogwipo and I liked this one most. It is an only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean (sea). It is really big and it gets pretty crowded, so if you want to enjoy it without a lot of people taking photos go in the morning. There are opening hours and small entrance fee, so check it before going. Really nice  and big waterfall worth visiting.

I found this museum really interesting. I knew a little about Hanyeo beforehand but this gave me a much more detailed understanding. The exhibits (consisting of genuine Haenyeo clothing, tools and equipment alongside dioramas, videos and various documents) are well laid out and the accompanying explanations and labels almost all have high-quality English translations. I read every word and it took me a little under 2 hours to complete my visit, which considering the entrance fee is only 1100 won is excellent value for money. Recommended, especially if you are already on the east side of the island.

I am traveling with my 79 years old dad who has weak knees. When our driver brought us to yongmeori beach, we have no idea what we are in for. Because of my dad, we chose to enter the beach on the left entrance and exit by the right entrance which we heard is the opposite direction of what most people would do. From the entrance, we had to walk down a very steep stairs which led us directly onto the beach. Honestly, the walk down the stairs was a bit dangerous as there was no railing or any safety measures. Despite collecting entrance fee, there are no staff around if you need help. That said, the scenery was stunning. The natural formation of the rocks was beautiful and the water was clear. For a popular tourist destination, this is also one of the cleanest I have been. You don?t see any garbage around. I hope anyone who plans to visit, continue to keep this place clean. As we had to walk slowly, we completed one round of the beach in over an hour.

Fun for children to climb over the big stones. Our child (3) was a bit small but enjoy it nevertheless. Beautiful scenery over the cost. Entrance only W2000, nearby the small city centre. Nice visit and takes just an hour to do this. We rapidly visited before checking in to our hotel.

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.

Bring your swimming gear along, it has a sea swimming pool during low tides, basically daytime. Seeing ppl drives and swimming. There is life-jacket rental available for snorkelling. No entrance ticket required. But the carpark attendance charged us W2K which seem only W1K per hour. No proper carpark control. See ppl park along road side.

We didn't seek to visit Mt. Songak -- our driver just brought us there. Not knowing what to do and since he didn?셳 speak a word of English we just consulted a map near the entrance and decided that the only thing to do there really was walk up to the crater. It's a genuine natural wonder. I?셫 glad we went there because the place was just so beautiful it was worth the effort of climbing. And believe me there was some effort. Unlike other Jeju-do mountains there were rough parts in this mountain without steps or any pavement. Some bits were steep too. If you have mobility issues forget the crater; just walk around. One Korean grandpa lost his footing and scraped his hand on the rocks ??we felt bad for him.There were horses that you can ride briefly for a little bit of money. They were cute and surrounded by fields of flowers. It was like a dream to be there looking at the sky the sea the fields and the horses. Would come back if I have the chance.

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!

It is easy to access the fall for those who dislike climbing steps.  It was only a short distance from the entrance via some steps.  Nice feeling to get up close and personal to the fall however just gotta beware of wet ones which at times can be slippery.  Smaller rocks tend to move when you are stepping on them so be careful.

i have visited the Seongsan in Udo. I think Seongsan is a must go place because it has average difficultiy to climb up (108m). It's named as one of the new 7 wonder natural places. reasonable entrance fee applied.

We saw many people taking photos around the waterfall. It's not the tallest nor grandest waterfall so I'm not sure what's the fuss about.Entrance fee is only 2K/pax. It's a short climb back up from the waterfall, ie very suitable for family and elderly.The rocks around the waterfall are rather pointed so please watch out while taking your selfies.

This place was one of the highlights in my jeju trip and it did not disappoint me. Seongsan area are small and stroll-able with mostly seafood restaurants. I stayed in a guesthouse that's literally right at the entrance of the peak. So took me fifteen minutes from getting up to reaching the peak. The stairs was not for the fainted heart and Or who has knee problems. If you think the stairs may concern you, come little early and really take your time there are a few platforms you can stip while climbing up.

This is quite possibly the most beautiful spot on the island-- definitely worth the small entrance fee (I think it was about 7000 won for my family of 5). There are some fairly serious steps to get down the cliff, and then to actually get close to the falls, it's necessary to climb across a bunch of small/medium rocks. Most people will have no problems with either, but for someone with knee or foot problems it could be an issue.The only thing I didn't love was that it was SO crowded. It was impossible to get a decent photo without someone walking into the frame, and several times we were actually shoved off of rocks as more and more people tried to crowd in. It would be great if they would limit the amount of people allowed down at one time.Other than that-- a great experience that we definitely won't forget.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

One of the 3 major waterfalls in Jeju, the water falls from a height of around 22 meters and thus named Cheonjiyeon ? meaning Sky connected with Land. Though not as majestic as Cheonjeyeon , this water falls is as beautiful when it comes to its natural surroundings . A very well laid out path ensures one can enjoy the long walk from main entrance to the waterfalls. As there is not much climbing to do, tourists of all ages can visit this place.

Is worth going if u have young kids and a husband/wife who enjoyed looking at vintage cars instead of young woman (:p). My kids enjoyed driving the cars and they were issued a license with photo after the 10mins ride. Although they say no phototaking but trust me, phototaking opportunity are plenty once u r out of their sight. Read that there's an outdoor area where we can feed the deer. Unfortunately it was raining shortly after we were there. Hence didn't manage to do there. This place is very near to the ossulloc green tea museum. Easy to swing over after the visit to ossulloc. But beware to check weather. There's a unsheltered slope uphill from the entrance area (remb to bring enough umbrella for whole family in case it rains). My hubby only brought 1 from the car hence he needs to go bk to the car and climb uphill again just to pass us the ponchos and umbrellas). :P
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

I choose to stay near to the peak so it only took us 5 mins to walk here. We didn't managed to see the sunrise as the weather was a great challenge. It was extremely windy and cold in the morning. Thus we came here at noon time. When we reach the foot of the peak, I could see that the whole peak was full of people climbing either up or coming down. The entrance fee is cheap, it cost only 2000won. The scenery was really beautiful, it worth coming here to take a look at the natural beauty.

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls consists of 3 waterfalls. Such a nice turquoise water. There is an entrance fee to enter this place. Make sure you have some energy because you need to climb stairs to reach each point. There is a bridge called 'Seonimgyo Bridge', meaning 7 nymphs as there has an arch carved on the side. This place open from 8am to 6pm. We came here late in the evening in a rainy day but the admin staff were so nice to allowed us to enter but with time restrictions.

amazing landscape. A nice spot to take beautiful pictures of tranquil waters with pitch black rocks and white sand. Walk right from the main entrance till the end, you will fine some nice restaurants and cheaper places to stay. From there you can climb the hill and get the whole picture of Hamdeok area.

You will enjoy this place depends on how u spend your time :1. Take photo in the tea garden & entrance2. Order you green tea/ green tea ice cream or drinks and bring it outside the cafe (depend on weather) 3.Walk around4. visit the innisfree museum & shop for some innisfree product.

When we came around this time there were abundant hydrangeas and a few other types of flowers. Unfortunately it can be very crowded especially where the lanes are small and everyone is fighting to take a picture there.The entrance fee is quite expensive too which os 8000??for an adult. All in all only go there if you enjoy looking at flowers.

What is offered at the Glass Museum does not justify its 9 000 won entrance fee.There is a garden with glass flowers  glass birds  and other ornaments. The displays are dull and although they probably took a lot of time and effort to make  the whole place seems like something that would have been more interesting 15 years ago.

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !

We went as we read many positive feed-backs from families and we were not disappointed. All our family enjoyed it to the last minute including also the garden outside and the cafeteria.My only strong suggestion would be to do it either in the morning or early afternoon (enter before 2.00pm) as when we were leaving (5pm) the crowd was definitely bigger than when we got in. We walked back to the main entrance to still have a look and by that time it would have been almost impossible to take a pic without being interrupted many times by 'passer-by'.

We regretted going to this place. The entrance fee is 5 000 won and they give you a 3 000 coupon to use when you buy their products. There is nothing to see except display of chocolates from different countries which is available at a supermarket. Really it is a waste of money and waste of time.

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

This was the only waterfall we visited on Jeju island. It was worth the visit although somehow not terribly exciting for me. I think it would be  nicer in  the summer time when you can put your feet in the water. There is a small entrance fee.

This is not a bias assessment. I would be glad if the establishment owner would take in advise from visitor feedback. This is my first time to rate an establishment with such a low rating. It is a total rip-off as entrance fee is collected before cafe and store. There nothing impressive with the collection and exhibit area is extremely small. There is another fees impose for DIY chocolate making session. No educational value  no entertainment value. I would not recommend it to anyone.
The water is very clean n clear.  Can see the fish clearly. Can drop by if have extra time. The entrance fee is 2000w for adult

The temperature in the cave is at least 5 to 10C lower so please bring a jacket and wear proper shoes when going in. The entrance fee is cheap at 2K each for an adult.There are many locals visiting during the weekends so it's recommended you visit during weekdays if possible.The cave is dark and wet so we spent more time watching the floor as opposed to the cave.

The overall theme was a good one cause you get to see the various famous landmarks in a fraction of its size. We went on a day where there wasn't many people so thats a good thing cause we can take our time with the photographs. The entrance fee was the most expensive among all the entrance fee standing at 20000 won for 3 people (2 adult 1 student) but it was pretty fun despite the shabby appearances.

The overall theme was a good one  cause you get to see the various famous landmarks in a fraction of its size. We went on a day where there wasn't many people  so thats a good thing  cause we can take our time with the photographs. The entrance fee was the most expensive among all the entrance fee  standing at 20 000 won for 3 people (2 adult  1 student)  but it was pretty fun despite the shabby appearances.

The land is big with many miniatures but I get tired of the figures real quickly. However there are some interesting photo worthy displays. Go if you have time to spare or if you are going with kids. Entrance fee is 8000won.

The entrance is an orange frame which juts our of the ground so it will be really hard to miss. But If you go for flashy shopping centre then this place is not for you. There?s a lot on sale if you take the time to browse through. Unfortunately I am the type who goes for flashy shopping centre so we just came in and breeze through.

Tea plantation near the city center with a tea museum containing a few old tes pots (you will probably have wider assortment in a flea market). I will probably enjoy visiting an actual farm with fruit trees and greenhouses planted to vegetables than spending time at the tea plantation. There is no entrance fee but there is also no tour guide or someone or something to explain what there is to see.

Only one of the passengers is allowed to row. No explanation of what is going on. My gf was upset she didn?셳 get to row. The staffs were very rushing. Did not give enough time for you to think. Everything from finding entrance to the activities and safety was very poorly organised. Plus unbelievably rude staffs made me speechless. I would never recommend to go here for a kayaking. I do think the staffs need to be educated better.
Not worth the entrance fee and time spent at the park. Unless you really have no other attraction sites to visit.

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

If you have seen any miniature park before then this park will be boring for you. But if you have time remaining for the day then you can see this place. The entrance ticket is expensive if you are not a solo traveler.  Eco land Stone park and Sangumburi Crater are near this place.  I have been to a miniature park in Shenzhen city of China so this park was borning for me.

I visited in the past many caves but this is the first time for a lava cave. It is not so beautiful and interesting as a natural cave but it is something new for me. Three stars only because it is not the best place I ever visited but it is interesting.The entrance is really cheap and the cave is long 1 Km so the visit is really fast.

Horse ridding for kids and teens not me!! Hahaha seen REAL horses in life that the adult one is almost as tall as me OMG can't imagine if it goes rampage that jumps up with the back legs how tall will it be and do feedings of the pony that the mouth open so bigPS - they do not have much food selling at this area but there is a small booth nearby the main entrance a convenience store near to the horse race trackBtw 1st time in life I seen real horse races can feel the wind and a the bet-ers  shouting their gambling numbers of the horse toooooo many people down there

Cool nice underground cave cafe ... paid about KWR4000 each pax entrance to the cafe and have a choice of 1 hot or drink or green tea ice cream with that ticket.The green tea ice cream is the best I ever tasted in Korea the green tea latte as well.Cool quiet environment..As for the other attraction outside the cafe there are some miniature world famous buldings near to the green tea field. But they looks run down  which is left untaken care of for sometime.Green tea field is a little small scale  not so impressive as those in Boseung.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: At the entrance of the plaza there is tourist information center where you can get any info related to the area. From this plaza there are occasional festival from time to time this time I just went to see sunset on the ocean. Above the big waves sunset was pretty. There is long sea-side walk which leads to Dragon head rock.

At least Pyeoson Folk Village had more flowers and more greenery and smaller than this one sk you don't have to spend so much time walking around looking at basically the same hut in different locations.Not worth the exhorbitant entrance fee. I'd rather buy food with that money.

Without considering visitors could visit and shop at this museum, they charged the highest entrance fee among all other natural sites we visited in Jeju. If it were not for the kids, it was certainly not worthwhile to pay 4 times the entrance fees to other UNESCO sites.

When we arrived in jeju it was raining so we needed to do something that was more indoor.  We drove out to the cave.  The entrance fee is cheap at 2000 won per person.  Then you walk down some steps and enter the lava tube.  It is really dark down there and the floor can be slippery.  I think we spent most of our time looking down at where to walk rather than looking around.  You walk 1km to the end and there is a rock formation.  Nothing too special.  Then you turn around and walk back.  Overall it is a nice cool 2km walk, perfect to escape the heat of jeju.  Just watch where you walk

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

This waterfall is easily accessible in south Jeju Island with spacious parking lot at entrance.  Entrance fee is 2000 won, reasonable and worth a visit.  We arrived around 4:50pm and was just in time to watch the sun set there.  If you want to get closer to the waterfall, be prepared to get a slightly wet but it?s a great experience.

This market is worth your time with the various street food (inside the market) , wet market and souvenirs to look at. If you could do by the evening, I think they have a designated spot (close to one of the entrances) for modern street food.

This is your typically local market where you can get fresh product here.  I will NOT say this place offers the cheapest price but rather there are varieties for you to choose from.  The market has many entrance and each entrance leads to you to a particular section where they sell the same stuff ranging from clothes, fruits and to live seafood.  We picked up some Jeju tangerines and sweets here which were pretty good.  Discount?  Most shops are priced the same so its hard to get discount. Best time to come is about 2pm where there are lesser crowd.  Its also a short walk to the underground shopping mall so if you are here, do take the chance to visit the underground mall altogether.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is not a cave, this is a lava tube so do not expect what you see in caves.  The tube is huge in size.  From the entrance you are able to walk 1km.  At the end you can see the remains of where lava had gone up and out of the tube.  It is not very impressive.  The tube itself is a large tunnel like structure.  There is not much to see and the lighting is a bit insipid.  The good thing is that the entrance fee is only like $2 so you don't need to worry about wasting money.  I am glad I visited but I would have been happy to have just walked down into the tube about 5 minutes, turned around and left.  Walking to the end of the open area is unnecessary and a bit of wasting time.  Spend about 10 minutes and its enough.

The waterfall is not so large when we came, so we can walk up near to it to take some pictures. It is only a short walk down from the entrance, but be careful when walking on the stones as it can be very slippery and very crowded at times. The falls itself is very unique as it flows straight to the ocean and it cost only 2000 won to enter.

The park is a it run down and not well maintained. Although the park is big, but there is nothing really big and great. There was a signboard (even on the brochure) stating there is white peacock but we see none. Flowers are dying (perhaps it's because of winter starting soon?) Feel a bit disappointed. I would advice you to plan this in your itinerary if you really have a lot of time as it take quite sometime to go to this park and entrance fees is not cheap.
The park has a lot to offer, needs quite some time to fully explore everything.They offer strollers for kids/babies at the entrance (We brought our own though).

The museum was very very hard to find. The employees were rude and unpleasant. The glass   art   is just a pile of glorified junk. I regeret wasting my time there with my boyfriend. The entrance fee is a joke  please Do NOT go there

The lack of literature on the Seongeup Folk village was compensated by the cheerful caretaker who gave informative, colourful and refreshing description of their well preserved ancient village.The village revealed a period of time when peace and security were prevailing, and privacy was highly respected. No one would enter the village when the two horizontal portable poles placed across the main entrance were not removed.Visitors would learn about the social structure of the days gone by, when men were out-numbered by women, when men stayed home and were pampered, while the women became the   work-horses   of the family.  Apart from becoming skilled divers, many womenfolk had to travel long distance daily, carrying heavy loads of water supply or agricultural products back to their homes.One would be surprised to learn that rudimentary recycling system was already being practiced. The caretaker must be congratulated for so cleverly circumvented the description the   grand father   stone status, which was in the shape of a male organ.  She described the statue as a god that offered protection against the demons, and promoted fertility for the living.
The entrance was a bit expensive but since we had the time we went for it, saw lots of colorful flowers and trees, they also had a souvenir shop and lots of benches around the park for resting.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

Our family visited the Cheonjiyeon Falls on the first day of our trip. We came out quite late, around 5 pm and we decided to come here as this was one of the attractions that were opened at that time. The admission fee was reasonably cheap. The area was not that big as I imagined, you walk from the entrance to the waterfall and then back. The waterfall is quite nice to look at and I'm pretty sure it might look more majestic if you come here at night. Even though I came on a cloudy and rainy day, it didn't ruin the mood much, it makes the waterfall more mysterious and I liked the atmosphere.

Not cheap entrance fee however there are lots of things to see.Even if you don't have much time, do not miss out their caves especially in hot days as it's so nice and cool inside. :)tiny little things to see everywhere and exotic animals as well.
It's relatively easy to find this place. We need to pay 2000 won for entrance fee. If you have more time, take another walk to the parking lot, there is also beautiful scenery.

It?s a place must visit in Jeju island. Air is so fresh and the walk is tranquil. When you walk through the forest and appreciate wat the Korean say that it is a place for meditation. There is a tap near the entrance, water is so refreshing. Trees in the forest have been there for hundred of years . It?s a treat to see some trees with autumn leaves. There are some Low walls with black stone formations which apparently is the volcanic rock from Jeju itself.. Would definitely come back here again to spend more time in the forest At the end of the walk they even have the vacuum facility to blow off the red soil from your shoes

If you stay in Seogwipo, this is absolutely a nice walk and visit. We payed 4,000 won for two people for entrance, which is worth the small amount of money. The area is beautiful where you can see different trees, fishes and of course the waterfall. We were there around 12 in the daytime, and it was a little bit crowded by the waterfall (since everyone wanted to take a picture and the place is small), but there is a small place where you can sit and just watch the beautiful waterfall!

If you are not a fan of BB, don't bother to go. Literally waste your entrance fee, if you want to get the gift, the gift shop is just rite at the entrance, no entrance fee requiredI think going to the GD Caf챕 is better than this KPop Museum. And the Teddy Bear museum next door worth 10 times more. I am not a huge fan of BB  but definitiely I know many KPOP stars.

If this place was in Europe I am sure the entrance fee would be double or triple, and it would have a giant shop at the end. This place is full of hard to believe facts, artsy stuff and little experiments. To be honest, I would really like to see a little shop at the and, so that I could send a postcard or add a pencil to my collection if not buying a few sciencey gifts. Definitely spare some time for this place, you will enjoy!

If it's your first time visit, definitely take the path to Oedolgae. If you have time, from the main entrance, take a left and it will take you along a path along the ocean. Go about 1/2 mi walk along the path and you'll see off on your right a smaller path. Take this and it will take you down to the ocean. Many locals take this down and it's a small watering hole where locals go to swim and fish. Once you get to the bottom, the navigation along the rocky formations can be challenging but very much worth it. It's not a beach but you're right next to the waves as they come in. It's absolutely beautiful. Just for context, I took my 8 year old daughter and 6 year old son. They had to be careful navigating, but was able to do so with adult supervision. Many others have come to appreciate this but they have been leaving their trash behind and it's quite saddening to see such a beautiful place littered with garbage. If you do go down, please respect the beauty and take your garbage with you.

I still enjoyed checking out the bear museum but I must say that the entrance fee is too much and unreasonable considering the bear museum is not that big.You can visit this place in less than 30 minutes because nothing much to see, they have small collection.This is just across the road from Ripleys Believe it or Not Museum. You better skip bear museum and just spend more time in Ripleys as it is more collection of interesting items and reasonable entrance price.

I learnt a lot about the brave women divers of Jeju by visiting this museum. I had hired a driver/tour guide for sightseeing in Jeju Island and got to visit some of my ?must see? attractions that were not close to my hotel. My tour guide was good so I had a great time. We visited this museum as part of our itinerary for the day, and I was glad we did. The museum charges a small entrance fee. I got to see a very interesting video about the history and lives of the women divers. There also a lot of painting, sculptures that is centered on the lives of these brave women. The museum is small but I liked it a lot. I came out more knowledgeable about the women and Jeju Island as a whole.

I have to say it was nothing special for me. The good news is that the museum is located in the jungmun complex, where other interesting attractions available, like trickart museum, jusangjeoli cliff, pacific land, etc. So if you have time, why not visit it as the entrance fee is not that expensive. But it's not a must visit attraction in my opinion

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

First time to see a lava tube. It was not the most impressive thing to see but it was such an eye opener for me! Learned a lot about this amazing geological formation. Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! Bring a layer!

Figured I?d give it a walk through after getting sun burn the day before. Not crowded on a Sunday. Free parking. 10,000w entrance fee. The museum was a little hot and stuffy. The depictions of historical moments using bears was humorous at times. Most labels were in Korean with some English. Might be fun for small kids. The garden out back was nice extra touch to allow kids to run around and see more bears.

Entrance fee is affordable even for budget travellers like us :) Furthermore, the adorable Teddy Bear collections are many times worth the price. We really enjoyed our time there.They also have Teddy's Forest with fountain and pond.I love this museum!  <3 <3 <3

At the entrance of the village, the town mayor greets us. It?s a very small town. But this guy speaks good English, easily understandable, proceeds to his narrative of the village, it?s culture and history. Very informative and entertaining as he interjects jokes from time to time that find application in our daily lives. At the end of the tour, he will try to sell you tea concentrate (which really tastes good, just did not buy because of luggage space management) and a beauty product, horse oil cream, which if we look at his face, would seem to be doing a good job. His skin is very firm despite his old age. My friend was convinced to buy one because of his skin. Short visit but worth every minute

As its name, here is an idea to visit for Teddy Bear lovers and who interested in. Many zone that's quite interesting such as the first Winnie the Pooh, world's all time classic paintings x Teddy Bear, characters bear like Michael Jackson or Audrey Hepburn from Breakfast at Tiffany, and Steve Jobs. Entrance fees isn't cheap but still OK. For the exhibition of Bear dolls is good but for the shop, just soso nothing attractive.Parking available. Good for friends and family.

Another great beach but this time with more cafes and restaurants right outside.  There's also a supermarket right to the left of the entrance.  There's a nice boardwalk to stroll, and kayaks to rent.

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the   mini car   or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

Entrance fee cost KRW10000. We got 10% discount after show the discount voucher. No need to print just show the picture from mobile phone will do.There are more than 100 houses in this place.Among them are Mountain Village Hill Country Village Fishing Village & Shamanism Village.With the traditional houses complete with the small plantation and livestock it feel like we was teleported back to the 1890s.Everything here looks and feels so authentic.There are also various folk games which include jegi skipping rope swing etc.The village is a place various dramas and films are made.There are 13 set places built for dramas inluding Jewel in the Palace The Slave Hunters Merchant Kim Man Deok Tamna the Island etc.There are signs to show exactly where each one was filmed.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

There is a big signage in Korean at the entrance next to the ticketing booth which we didn't apprehend  but the window of the ticketing booth was blocked with wood and when we moved to the back of the premises  we found back doors not closed and things which seemed to be exhibits were scattered on the backyard.

I and my family visited this place in late June 2015. One of the main reason we wanted to go there was because of the whale shark. Unfortunately the whale shark was no longer there. There was a notice in the entrance saying it was released back to the ocean. There was nothing noted about the whale shark release in the company web site before. If there was a notice in the company web site I would probably not going there. The aquarium is not very big compared to other aquariums that I visited before. But the admission fee is quite expensive IMHO compared to other aquariums I visited before.One thing I want to mention that you could take a good picture of Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak from outside the aquarium. Will I go there again? Probably not unless they bring back the whale shark.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: The indoor gardens are great when the big rains come.? Went back the next day and enjoyed the outdoor gardens as well.? Unfortunately, there is a person screaming via a loudspeaker at the entrance, which spoils what could be a peaceful, serene experience.

My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

Most of famous travellers places are not free of charge but this place has no entrance fee :) I visited here in winter and fortunately there weren't many people so I was able to enjoy this forest path pretty much. Calm, beautiful and very peaceful place even thou trees were not that green. You don't need to wear athletic stuffs but sneakers are essential.One thing you need to be reminded is there aren't any trash boxes and they must be taken back with you.

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.

It is one of many museums in Jeju, and it's dedicated to Teddy bears. It is full of its history with all the teddy bears from all over the world. All of the ancient teddy bears is well preserved but with relatively minimal background story. Some of the information are written only in Korean, so there isn't many interactive attraction here. There is also an open garden with a few sculptures on it, a Lotteria restaurant and of course the store. The merchandise there is quite expensive and we didn't buy anything. The entrance fee when we came there is 8000 won, a little bit expensive, but quite worth it.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

Visited in golden weekend so expected crowded with tourist and local. This place is big and nice. Environment is clean just not so tourist friendly cos the staffs barely speak English. review: It was nice to walk around the village and learn about their culture. If you are not travelling on a tour or travelling with a tour guide which you can't understand (for my case i am with Chinese Speaking tour when i don't understand) remember to borrow english speaking tour aid from the entrance then you will enjoy well.

The cone-dome architecture is interesting, the roofs of different gardens within culminates to a peak into the center of the compound and u can take a lift up to catch a 360 panoramic glimpse of the surroundings (see pic). However, adult tix are at 9000krw per person which is not cheap for what u get within. The place has lots of potential but not that well-maintained as the place looks very weathered on the whole. There is a garden dedicated to tropical fruits but those are mostly common fruits for southeast Asians like us. There were only chrysanthemums at the entrance even though it's supposed to be in-season. Parking is easy though, and free, like most places of interests at Jeju. Overall, this place is more suitable for the elders and for people dropping by to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and Seonimgyo Bridge, which is just next door. Otherwise, my 2c worth - it'll be fine to spend your money elsewhere.

Knowns also as Sunrise Peak. We went there on afternoon as we did not know this place  can see beautiful sunrise. Must visit place when you in Jeju Island. Worthwhile hiking by stairs about 45 minutes. This wonderful craters formed from volcanic eruption l00,000 years ago. Entrance Ticket KRW2000. Twice a day can see women divers go to the sea and singing before catch their seafood such as abalone, sea urchin, etc. Overthere you can ride pony horses

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.

Very disappointing. There were a few panels in the entrance hall that had information about chocolate and very poorly kept display boxes  but everything was only in Korean. Downstairs  you can see chocolate packages from different countries  but mostly ordinary products that can be bought in Korean supermarkets. No effort was given to make a proper display with special chocolates. Plus  some chocolates were mislabeled under the wrong countries. There was a station where chocolates in bags could be squeezed into molds. I was not able to participate because the staff panicked when they saw a non-Korean face  despite the fact that I spoke Korean to them. Do yourself a favor and go in the convenience store across the road - there is a better display of chocolate there.

This would be my fav market so far at Jeju. You can buy lots of local products and local delicacies to eat as well. The market was so packed with locals and tourists so you kinda need to walk slowly and try not to block the road. LOLThere are lots of exit / entrance here but rest assured that it is interconnected and you won't get lost. Most shops are selling the same products but if you really wish to buy then you need to scout for the best price!

A market worth a visit if you are in Jeju.
Very near the Dongmun market, just like any ordinary underground shopping center. Nothing new, nothing different. Many entrances and exits too.

Our FIRST meal in JEJU and we were just spoilt for choices. Is  a must visit to this market. Parking spot is very hidden. Lots of street food, souvenirs, tangerines, chocolate, fresh fish availables. (near to entrance 4)Lots of people buying chocolates from the stall located at the intersection between entrance 3 and entrance 7. (probably the biggest stall and cheapest?)

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

As the name implies, this street is a street of restaurants & dining. This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.

This is a place suitable for kids and senior citizen. It is just a short walk from the entrance to the waterfall via a flat road. We make this place the last place on our itinerary (late evening) as this place close later than any then attractions in Seogwipo. Quite a romantic walk and we even met some couples doing their wedding photoshoot here.

The temple is super huge and well decorated. There are three layers the first layer is for the believers to worship the Buddha. Second floor is a place where you can talk to the Buddhist monks about your difficulties you faced in your life and have their spiritual purification. Of course some ?쁤oodwill??you have to forgive to this temple I saw one of the believer distribute a considerable fortune to that temple that believer must treats Buddha sincerely. The scenery was nice. The driver told me it is the largest waterfall feature in Jeju area.  Lots of tourists when we visited.  The rocks were quite slippery and could be dangerous for young kids and elderly.  Overall a nice place to visit even if you only have 30mins to spare.  The entrance fee was cheap.

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.

It was a relaxing short walk to the falls. We went during the evening and it was quite touristy. It's a great site to take pictures before the waterfall if there isn't too much people. The entry was only 2000 won and there are shops and restaurants near the entrance

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Beautiful waterfall near the ocean. The water is icy cold. You can't swim in all the waterfall in jeju. Too bad as the weather very hot and I really wish can dip inside here to cool down my body. Entrance fee of 2000won.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

we visited this place with little or less expectation as many friends had said it too overrated but to our surprise is pretty awesome. Maybe because there was strong wind and rain the waves were very strong. The waves were hitting almost the observation point. We bought rain coat outside the cliff entrance for 2000wons (2$) and trust me its best decision we did. We were showered with water like anything as there was rain and wind. maybe in other season you dont need to worry aobut it. the phone number listed on site took to the parking lot the resort next to cliff, had to walk a bit to reach it but got to see the resort common area with some nice garden and statues!

We came here after the Manjungal caves. The maze is challenging enough and took us about 35min to solve, but it was fun and worth the entrance price. It was a hot day so take a bottle of water with you to stay hydrated. Also, whilst in the maze we noticed some pretty large spider webs with some fairly big spiders, so careful of those. All in all, its a great family activity. There's also some lovely cats in the park that are friendly and you can pet them.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The waterfall is beautiful, it gave me the urge to jump in it under the hot sun. There is a entrance charge for that. For those who are from places like Malaysia, Philippines where surrounded with beautiful waterfalls, you might don't feel like spending money just to see this waterfall.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000\ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.
The park has different areas including water garden, bird garden, bonsai garden, cave and folk village... Overall, the garden is very nice, huge but the entrance ticket is a bit bit bit pricey.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.
overly touristy entrance, path to waterfall messy. sight nothing special- at least in gloomy weather

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Ofcourse is a nice waterfal but i think it was a little overrated. Like everyplace att Jeju you have to pay a small entrance fee (2000 won) and then its just what it is, a waterfall. For sure you can take some nice pictures but thats it.

Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.

Nice wiev, cold water. Not that big but worth going in hot summer days. Easy to reach, wide car parking. Entrance fee than stairs to reach sea level. Fun for kids, if you dare:...... get into the water!!!

Just one waterfall, not much of a sight to behold. However, it's the only touristy waterfall that doesn't have stairs, so if you have knee problems, this is waterfall to see. On the plus side, the souvenir store near the entrance has good merchandise at good prices. They had nice hats on sale when I was there.

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

I was excited to go see the Manjanggul caves, and had an image in my mind that unfortunately didn't fit what I saw. The whole experience is pretty cool, the floor is uneven, dodging water droplets becomes a game, the lava flow marks are beautiful, but lack of light, lack of stalactite formations, and a lot of areas that are fenced off let me down slightly. However, cheap entrance, and the atmosphere is actually quite lovely. If you get the chance to go, try and do it.

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

Entrance fee is 2000 won which is not that bad but again, the waterfalls are not that big. There are other falls on Jeju with greater magnitude you should consider instead unless you stay in Seogwipo as this is literally just on the outskirts of the city.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

A really beautiful sight to behold! Its a short but steep walk down to the waterfall, with an entrance fee of 2000 won. You wont be able to get too up close and personal though - the waterfall   guards   get a little touchy if you get too close to the rocks that are wet.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.
Went here with our two sons (8M and 4Y) and it was very interesting and a bit cold.Cheap entrance fee being in Jeju.Easy to park and restaurant in front was OK.

A pleasant walk among trees and nature. Many small flies hovering around at certain areas. A small cafe and convenience store near the entrance. An easy outing for elderly folks and a pleasant walk for families.
A must visit to this attraction . Entrance fee is 2000W . Short and easy walk to the cliffs . Expect to spend around 30-60minutes here if you want to take photos .

The museum has many airplanes on display and also an outdoor area where you can walk into the planes. ? Very well done, lots of information and displays. ? Hands on activities instructions are only in Korean, but easy to figure out. ? A steal for the 10,000 WON entrance fee.
Quite pretty and relatively easy to get to. Granted you have to go down some steps to get to the falls. Entrance fees are KRW2,000 per person.
Part of Hallim Park. Your entrance fee to the park grants access to this site. Nothing special, but already included, so check it out. Easy to go thru, even for the older less mobile people.
It's very scenic and a good location for photography, it's near to town and easy to reach. The entrance fees is affordable

You could park and walk to the falls. Entrance was 2000w. Opens at 0900 not crowded. You?re able to walk right up to the edge of the falls for great photos. Some available shops for souvenirs and snacks.

We went here in a sunny morning and took a glance for the natural six-edges poles. We enjoy the mild sea breeze together with stunning scenery here.There was a giant seashell in the entrance and you may sat inside to take a funny photo.
