This place is expensive and very small.  You can walk around the whole garden in about 5-10 minutes.  We were expecting a much larger place based on the entrance costs.  Kids were not impressed and thought it was not worth it.

This is a natural cave and you have to walk down a stair at the entrance. It is dark inside the cave and be aware of your step as the stone on the floor are not plain. Better bring a jacket with you as the temperature inside is around 10-degree celsius only.

Entrance fee is around 9000 krw per person but you can spend a good 40mins to 1hr in the museum walking around and taking photos. Very good place to visit. Not too sure how accessible it is by public transport as I booked a driver for the day.

Place is very clean and beautiful. No thrash bins around so do bring extra plastic bag to throw your unwanted things or drinks in it. It is a long walk up to the entrance. Choose the path wisely. Not advisable for those with joint pain and old injuries.

People say if you want to know about the place you must understand the culture. So this place are all about it. They show the history of their lives the culture the utilities the household etc. A large place to walk to reach at each point but worth the knowledge. You have to pay the entrance fee just before entrance gate and they will provide you with the map/pamphlet according to your language.
Luckily no need to pay for entrance fee. Go only if you like tea. Can take a nice walk outdoor other than that nothing much.

It was raining when we arrived and spent a fun afternoon at this museum posing with the different paintings photos and displays. Unfortunately the rain prevented us from taking photos with the various outdoor displays. Wheelchairs are available for loan and help make the experience more enjoyable for my mom who has difficulty walking. Entrance fee is KRW9000 per person. The Alive Museum covers a wider area and has more/different displays than the Trickeye Museum in Seoul.
Bring your jacket: is super cold as walking into cave. Entrance fee is KRW 2000. Wear sport shoes: cave floor is slippy.

An interesting outing to learn about volcanic activity and how the lava tube was formed. Not suitable for elderly visitors with the dim and uneven terrain. Many information board to explain unusual structures. Educational. Some wooden boardwalk in certain areas. The stairs at the entrance leading into the tube can be steep and slippery.

Yes, it's just a cave. Nothing much there besides a long, large, cool and dark cave with uneven walking path. The walk path is uneven and wet. Please wear good walking shoes and that will be good if you have flashlight. I will not recon to bring kids or old folks to this attraction. I saw only 1 security camera at the entrance but none in the cave and no workers in the cave. So, if someone injured or any emergency help, I guess no one can help you except other tourist.
We went there with a tour so we didn't wait at entrance. Very pleasant walk, and small train ride, but gets a bit crowded.

We brought our 3 young kids and two elderly mothers to the Manjanggul Cave in late Nov, and it was quite an experience descending into the dark and cold cavern.  It was lit sufficiently to walk, though some areas could be a little dark and wet.  The kids sure had fun, until it got a little boring for them after 500 metres. The entrance fee was reasonable, not expensive.

Very cool trip and 2km walk underground in the lava tube. Largest in the world. It is dark, cool and damp. The walking surface is cooled lava, so I'd recommend appropriate footwear. The lighting is respectful for the nature of the cave and energy efficient. Plenty of photo opportunities, for the low entrance price I was very pleased!!I wouldn't recommend any strollers or children who are learning to walk unless you plan to carry them the entire cave visit.

Too dark to actually take any nice photos inside. The paths are quite moist and therefore slippery, so have to take extra care when walking. The scariest part was the path down from the entrance as it was pretty steep, so have to be careful of your footing.

This Underground Shopping Mall is again beside one of the walking street.  It also has many entrance/exit.  Basically, the shops are selling more for women and not for youngsters. It really make use of the space on the island, and place to hide during down pour.

This spot is one of the UNESCO Heritage places, however to enjoy its beauty you?d need to visit it on a sunny day. Unlikely, it was raining heavily and was foggy when I was there. Despite that, I enjoyed the trip and the place itself, besides it was fo free if you walk around. (you?d only pay for the entrance if you want to go up to the extinct volcano crater). Landscape was amazing and loked kind of alien. Eventually, I found this spot beautiful in any weather conditions.

This is a real village with households living inside, opposite from folk villages built in museums. In fact, the people live there are mainly the haenyeo (women divers) - there is a museum for them in the east coast of Jeju. There is no entrance fee, so the village depends on the sale of souvenirs, basically the blueberries fermented drink and the organic skin creams. A volunteer will assist you to walk around the town, which is very helpful. A site note is that it is often used as a movie set, for example for the movie entitled Dae Jang Gum.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.

Not many such places are open to public visit, so I will say this is something interesting to explore if you visit Jeju. Temperature is lower than outside, so do bring a jacket or wear long sleeves if you are scare of cold. Physical mobility is required as there are steep steps to walk down to the entrance and paths are uneven.There is a restaurant and convenient store on site. We had lunch at the restaurant after the visit. Pretty decent Korean meals. Have translation app ready if you do not read Korean as menu is in Korean .
Nice walk around to see different carvings of stones which we took lots of picture with. Not spectacular, but nice to see. There is a small entrance fee.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world. It is one of the UNESCO heritage. There's a good 1km walk from the entrance of the cave til you get to the end of the tunnel to sight the beautiful stalactites.  The tunnel is of course much longer than that however access is only allowed up to the 1km mark. The path is dark, chilly,  rocky and slippery. Please wear good shoes and bring a jumper and mini torchlight if you wish.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.

it's definitely a unique place to visit but you should wear proper shoes as the 2km walk to and from the entrance has lots of rocky areas...the cave was dark,cold and wet but worth the visit if it's part of your tour.

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

I have a deep love and appreciation for the artist Lee Jung Seob. The museum itself? and the neighboring art-walk is a great tribute to the artist, but the exhibition itself does not do the artist that much justice. They have a great selection of his smaller works from the earlier periods but they do not house his bigger, dynamic paintings that he is known for. This visit would be a great place to take the family as the entrance fee is very manageable. The museum offers a closer look at the artists' context and life story rather than a display of his most prominent works. In short, a brilliant artist but not the best exhibition space/display method.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.
Good news about this place is that other than the entrance steps which as quit steep, the rest of the 1-2 KM walk is actually not too bad.

For those who are interested in geology as my family is, this is a fascinating, and not too difficult, walk through a lava tube created by the molten lava. Worth a visit and the entrance fee is extremely cheap. UNESCO heritage.

Entrance was KRW15,000 which was extremely expensive for the show. There are simply not the facilities here to walk with the number of visitors and the parking is extremely limited so you have to park on the main road and walk quite some distance to reach it.? Expect no support from staff in any language except korean.

Entrance fee 5,000 won and free for senior and disable as this place is not wheelchair friendly. Thank God my aunt could walk a little so those part that cannot be pushed on wheels.... she had to walk slowly..

A short walk to these falls - low ticket price at the entrance and then about 100 steps down to the base of the falls - quite rocky and need to watch the step - fortunately we went on a day without many tourists. Could feel the refreshing cool spray, nice when in the sunshineI love the fact there?s no littering here - helps maintain the natural state

This is a great place to go inside the city to get some quality exercise. The trails are in great shape and the views are magical.Going for a walk is easy and fun. Finding a parking spot is a little more challenging. This is inside the city so it is a very popular spot. Great for the whole family.

The temple is located on olle 8 trail and there is a bus that takes you directly there from Seogwipo (bus 140).At the entrance someone might aak you to give 10 000 won to buy a bag of rice but you dont need to pay ... You can make a small donation instead. They alow you to take photos inside this temple (which is rare in Korea).  Outside is a small souvenir store where you can get cheap postcards and even a bowl of cooked ramen (not cup!) for 3000 won.

Jeju stone park was not part of the regular sightseeing itineraries and do we opted for a customized private tour to visit Jeju stone park. Requires atleast 3 to 4 hours if you want to walk along the trails to cover entire area. A visit inside the museum to understand the volcanic activities and formations will help in understanding the nature of the island better. Good to go with a local guide. Interesting statues and rock formations

It's well preserved but not good for people with disability. Inside is quite dark and has uneven flooring. Nothing to complain as it is made by nature and they also provided some trail/even flooring to follow.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. The Gwamneumba trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre.. And not to mention the fattest and most active flies inside and outside the cubicle..We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa. Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved. Yes it is a mountain, and I hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan which did not put me through the physical pain without much reward that hallasan did. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope!Enjoy!

We took the Seongpanak trail for both ascend and descend, took us a whooping 9 hours! Please wear a good pair of shoes as the trail is rocky, that explains why we couldn't run up and down afraid of slipping and fall. Parking is very limited there, we reached at 8am and parked at the roadside because there weren't any parking left inside. Beware of the time as you would need to reach the last rest house at 12.30PM in order to continue your hike to the summit. Great view at the summit but it was very crowded. Overall, it wasn't a very difficult climb but it'll take you a whole day.

The whole trail takes about 45 mins to an hour to complete. It was truly interesting to be inside a lava tube and during the walk, there were informational signs to explain parts of the tubes! I would recommend bringing a hoodie and water proof shoes as it is very wet and slippery inside :) The dampness will make you feel cool even in the summer.

The temperature inside the cave is between 13 and 16 degrees celsius despite outside summer weather. Hence it is good if you can bring along a sweater or jacket. Also bring something to protect your head from the cold cave droplets. Overall, it is a wonderful experience to explore this amazing cave. Look for the iconic turtle rock as well as the large column rock at the end of your 1km trail.

The marker for Routes 13, 14 and 14-1 are located in one spot. We got confused at first that we ended up completing abour 2-3km of Trail 14 until we got to another marker that we realized we were following the wrong path. We went back to the spot and started looking for the 14-1 trail. We spent the first half of the day doing Trail 14.When we headed to Trail 14-1 which was the intial plan, it was past noon already so the sun was up and it was hot (we did the trail on a summer day). It was a cool experience because the trail will bring you to the peak where you get a great 360 degree view of Jeju! It will take you inside a forest. You might even meet some horses along the way. By the time you'll get to the midpoint, which is the Osulloc Museum, you will realize how much you miss civilization and strangers. The trail will connect you to nature. You'll even find yourself in a dense forest! There are a lot of blue/orange ribbons so you won't be lost. This trail taught me to simply trust and find the blue/orange ribbons and enjoy/embrace nature wherever the trail (or life in general) may take you. Haha. This is definitely off the beaten path but it makes your Jeju tour even more special and truly your own. I would want to do more of the Olleh Trails in the future :)

Please visit this place only if you really love and in great passion to help preserve the nature. This attraction requires reservation as it only allow 400 hikers daily. There are 10 sessions and 3 different trails, a one-hr one, a 2.5-hr and a 3.5-hr one. All hikers will be lead by a center guide. Though the guide speaks only Korean and knows only limited English, there are signage and descriptions on each special location.We joined the first session and started at 9. We were required to arrive at least 10 minutes before 9, then bought the ticket (2000 won each) and showed the tickets to the Information Desk. Then we were given a badge which we needed to put on all the time and returned to the Desk after the hike. No food, including candies and gums, are allowed. Only water, without colours or tastes, is allowed to bring into the site. There is a water machine inside the Information Desk.The   Gotjawal   forests, grow in the center of the Geomunoreum crater, are very dense and luxuriant. While you can only look from the outlook points at Sangumburi 掠긷訝 and Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone 掠길ε뷴낡, this activity is an authentic encounter inside the crater, with the geological formation, vegetation and traits of lava activities

My husband and I visited Jeju last November.Mt. Halla was out of the picture on this trip ( supposed to be ) bec. I am not an adventurous person and I thought I will not have energy to climb this mountain, but after learning that it is a world natural heritage park I finally gave it a go. I was afraid at the beginning of the trail but as we climb further, higher and steeper I was in Awe! I was literally inside the mountain. Plus it  was autumn at that time and the color of the surrounding was just beautiful, it seems so peaceful all you could hear was the chirping birds, gushing winds. It was tiring but i must i was worth it so sad that we didn't reach the summit bec we started a little late. But if i could go back I will strive to reach the peak, but I was still happy though because I've seen the best Autumn inside the mountain..It is really is the Climb!

My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

If you stayed in Seogwipo, just go to the bus terminal and ask the local there or to the tourist information inside the terminal which bus route to get in.The trip from Seogwipo take about 1 hour and 40 minutes with little traffic and several bus stops.On arrival you will see right away the remarkable Seongsan rocky mountain, really beautiful.The admission is only 4.000 Won for two people.You can easily climb to get to the top as the trail is well maintained with a good step stairs and get a good pictures while you?re on your way up. If you?re lucky, you may catch the women diver show and there?s a trail down to the rocky beachside to ride a boat.

If you are there and have no place to visit, perhaps you may want to waste and hour or 2 to walk into the cave. There is no special attraction inside the cave that will give you a WOW factor. By end of the trail, you would just like saying...err...thats it? Its cold in winter and the floor are wet with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Its dark too.

I enjoyed snorkeling at the place. Inside the water is not that colorful as some famous snorkeling spot around the world, but you will see very attractive black rocks and ecosystems only seen at Jeju Island. Also there is a nice trail following the coast with great view. Though you are not going to swim, it is still good to visit.

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

Wow... just wow. I certainly didn't expect that. Yakchunsa isn't considered one of the must-go in Jeju so I didn't expect all that much especially given that you have to take a small road to go there. But once I arrived I was in awe. The complex is big colorful and the main pagoda-like multi-floor temple is massive and beautiful. What's even better is that the inside is at least as good as the outside view. There are three floors each with its own atmosphere and ornaments (murals candlelights wooden structures...). Take some time to go outside towards the sea to get the full perspective of the temple complex.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

Went to visit this attraction even though I saw some negative reviews as I have planned some attractions based on region and this is some thing that I think the kids would love to visit.Entrance fee is pricey at $5k won as there is practicably nothing much to see and do inside. After buying the tickets  the staff would give the adults coffee and kids chocolates. The display were very old  like it has been there for 3 or 4 decades and we felt uneasy as it looks dirty. There is a kitchen whereby apprentice showcase their skils on chocolate making. Wanted to buy some chocolates since we are there. But they dont seemed to be interested as the minimum sale item cost about $39k for a box of chocolates. Not worth my moneh and thus left empty handed. Adults ans children were disappointed.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내

review: We came to this museum based on the previous reviews and came away extremely disappointed. The displays are very average and there's really not too much to see inside the display hall. The tunnel with the dioramas (which looked to be the most interesting one) was locked while we were there. There were no signs to indicate why it was closed or when it would re-open.The other tunnels were OK but once you've seen one tunnel you've seen them all - and the fairy lighting in the tunnels did seem a little out of place considering their history. There is a lot of painful history in this area but the museum fails to capture and relay it.It would have been better to see more of the human history alluded to in the video display in the other displays.Note that a lot of the pictures for this Trip Advisor listing may not actually be of this museum - we were quite confused trying to find it based on these pictures and they make it seem a lot grander than it really is.Overall wouldn't recommend and wouldn't go back.

We came on a foggy and rainy day so we didn't had a great view like other did.  Nonetheless we enjoyed ourselves with the tea and cakes even though there isn't any WOW to those matcha cakes we ordered.  Beside the restaurant there isn't much to see inside other than tea tasting and tea goods.

This stadium had an awesome design. I wouldn't travel far to see it but it was on the way so I popped it. I couldn't go inside so viewed from behind the gate. I can imagine watching a game their would be great

This place was surprisingly fun! It was cooling inside and we enjoyed the view inside. Really cool place. Only went there cos' Running Man did and it turned out to be one of the more interesting places we visited in Korea. Definitely go to this place if you are in Jeju!

This place is worth visiting given it's nice environment and a lots of things to do. Food:  I highly recommend the green tea icecream and cake at the O'Sulloc tea museum which appears to be the focus of most visitors.  But I also want to take some time to remind you that there's another little gem inside the organic cafe of Innisfree that's also within the complex--DON'T MISS OUT THE TANGERINE SHAVED ICE! It comes in a big original size that can be sufficiently shared among 3 persons or there's a mini version if you only want a taste of it.  It's not cheap but worth trying because they use Jeju Tangerine which tasted somewhat more intense and flavourful.  Drinks:  They have free tea-demo which you can try their teas.  They also sell a selection of other drinks like tea latte.  Most of them tasted and smelled spectacular.  The teabags are also wrapped individually so they make good souvenirs as well. Soap making:  If you go early do try making your own soap at the Innisfree house it's a fun experience and make good souvenirs.View and/or pictures:  The environment around and within the museum is a great place for pictures with the open tea-farm and the delicate glass buildings or the colourful interior of the Innisfree house.  There's also a viewing deck in the O'sulloc Tea Museum which you can access by taking a lift.  The view up there is pretty amazing.  Tip:  1. Go on a sunny day if you want to take great pictures in the tea-farm2. Go early if you are worried that they sell out the cakes.  The tangerine shaved ice wasn't available after 5.30pm so we went to visit again on the next day.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This is a beautiful destination. I would consider this a must do for all foreigners visiting Jeju Island. It reminded me of visiting an upmarket winery. There is a fabulous view from the tower over the tea fields fabulous art displayed inside and precious tea cups to look at the amazing smell & sight of seeing tea roasting and demonstrations. The outside had sculptures. The kids loved airy ambiance of the cafe & wolfed down the Green Tea Swiss Roll. I loved my dacquoise! Plenty of parking bathroom facilities Well Done!

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.
The view around the curch is really nice. I didn't go inside the church.The location near seongsan ilchubong.Make sure u visit two of them when u come to jeju

The road to this temple is a single carriage way and you drive carefully.  Parking is free. Before I reached the temple I can hear the chanting and is was so soothing. It would be great to have a audio or a translator/guide to explain more of this historical and majestic temple.  The sea view from the temple is stunning. Do check out the temple second floor.

The musuem is located next to the tea farm great view from the rooftopinside the musuem you can buy a range of different tea made in JEJU and evevn drink somethere is a restaurant inside where youi can eat an tea icecream or a tea cake anything which is made with tea!good for family and couple

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).
Not bad for visiting the entrance ticket fees is 12000won per person . Inside have a lot of things to view for sex and health...

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Maze park is an unique park than consists of two maze. You can play inside the maze and your friend can stand at the station to guide you. The view is nice and there is a mini museum for the maze. Try to spend more time in this park estimated 2hours.

Its still raining in Jeju when we arrived here. No regret walking in the rain and climbing the stairs when the view welcomed u so wonderfully beautiful. Every theme garden was in the peak of health and beauty.Allow several hours. Inside and outside gardens.Great view from the top of the tower.

Don?셳 t be confused. The museum of sex is further south near Seogwipo and NOT what is in the photos of this review. 12000won totally not worth entry to the museum. Beautiful cave with lava rock sides. Hard to take beautiful pictures but amazing views. Specially the end of the 1km hike inside the lava tube.

At first glance this place looks like a fun place but quickly becomes a waste of time.  The outdoor garden is the only place that is fun.  They have fun statues and great photo opportunities but as soon as you walk inside you will quickly become disappointed.  With the coupon entrance is about $12 and is not at all worth it.  If you come from a culture where sex is a taboo then maybe you will enjoy this place but anyone from a western culture will find it boring.  90% of the signage is only korean and not much else to see or do inside.  If it's a rainy day and you have nothing to do then maybe this could be an option but even then I would say pick something else.  This museum has gone through some changes over the years and you will notice that the more recent reviews are pretty low where as the older reviews are better.  It used to be a much better place than it is now~~
Zoned gardens, lovely to stroll about and inside the dome was quite unique. Also an excellent view from the top of the dome.

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.? Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!? It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

we've seen a few caves and this one is truly unique.  Its not loaded in formations such as stalagmites/stalagtites, but the lava shelves go on forever.  It literally takes over thirty minutes to walk from one end to the other at a decent clip.  Very humid inside, definately bring an umbrella or raincoat.  Also very chilly so if you are there in summer, the temperature change can be significant.  I brought a flashlight but you really don't need it as they do a great job in keeping you on the straight and narrow.  It really gives you a great understanding of what nature can do, well worth the detour to view
Went a day after heavy downpour. Cave was   dripping wet   so we had to wear raincoat. Could not enjoy the view inside as we had to concentrate on our steps on the uneven rocky path.

We had a tour inside a golf club and since it's a huge land, it actually takes time to go back and forth. So I recommend it for people who enjoy walking especially in such a beautiful place. At the end of the tour, we had a mini-concert organized by them and they were signing us a live song which made me goosebumps because it was like in a movie where you enjoy the ocean view, nature, and good music with the best company.

Visited May 2016, season of summer but the day we visited it was a bit of rainy thus our tour guide told us to explore it before the rain totally pours as the place will be foggy means the view will be blocked. Very interesting inside and out. The first floor is mostly modern about sexual preference health and rights but it is 95% in Korean. I would recommend to bring a Korean friend who doesn't mind translating if you are interested in that part. There was also a big wall of history at the very front which was all in Korean that would be worth translating. It wasn't very busy and some of the   hands on   things that would show examples were broken so I started with a mediocre impression. The bigger and more impressive part though is the number of historic sexual things they have on the second and third floor. Lots of artifacts about sex in Eastern cultures with some in Western cultures but a lot of things have their English translation. This part is much more impressive and interesting to look at. A lot of phallic objects and   traditional   pieces but it's historic and that is how people viewed sex in history. The more modern section is more modernly-styled and was a bit confusing (a lot of sex dolls...? kind of weird) and included more fetish stuff than I expected. Not much on queer and non-hetero there was a small section (in Korean) on the ground floor and then one very gray area display on the top floor but not a whole lot can be expected of Korea (where homosexuality is still viewed very negatively). Overall it was worth the price and was pretty interesting to look at. Having a translator or understanding Korean would make it more memorable.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This place is massive! Truly a great venue to walk around. While it was closed the day I was there  I walked around the entire stadium and was impressed with everything outside of it. I went to the   Maze   next door and took the hot air balloon ride which gave me a great view of INSIDE the stadium! This place is gorgeous!

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This is a beautiful volcanic crater well worth visiting. It doesn?t take too long to reach the top from the entrance (despite the sometimes steep stairs). The views are magnificent as you ascend, from the summit, as well as when you descend. Plus there are various volcanic rock formations that you can appreciate along the way, both ascending and descending (the two paths are different). The crater is full of trees and grass of a very unique shade of green (I?ve seen this shade of green only in the vegetation of other extinct volcanic craters such as the ones in Tanzania). There are platforms to sit on at the summit from where you can appreciate the view. After descending, make sure to visit the cove where you can meet the Haenyeo or the traditional fisher women of Jejudo. The way to the cove is clearly marked with signboards and it?s only a couple of staircases down to the beach. The Haenyeo put up a performance twice a day, which is very touristy but interesting nevertheless. You can buy all kinds of fresh seafood from them and ask them to prepare it for you to eat at the restaurant. But it?s mostly eaten raw / semi-raw with various sauces and the typical side dishes. The sea weed is particularly good, which you get as a side dish. There is unfortunately no English menu. If you don?t want to eat raw seafood, after picking your seafood portion at the entrance, take it to the counter inside the restaurant and ask that it be stir-fried (?pokkum? in Korean). Beware that even when it?s stir-fried, it?ll still be more on the raw side than the fried side. The black sand beach in the cove is also a treat. If you look closely and attentively, you?ll find all sorts of marine life among the rocks, in the pools and on the sides of the mini cliffs facing the beach.

There were a lot carter in jeju island, one of them is sangamburi.We went there by rent a car, from our hotel around 1 hour. The place is calm and nature. With mountain view, savana and trees all around.If you like nature, this place is one of your choice. One of korean movie was made there.When we entered the place, there's a garden, walked inside there's line of trees, in the middle, there's savana.Going further, you will find mountain view.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

The cherry blomsson at its carpark in April 18 was wonderful - one long row of beautiful sakura trees.Do not expect to see much inside (basically you walk 5 min into the park and you saw crater on your side. It will not look like crater, only valley). Rather it is the 360 degree view of the horizon that counts. The air is fresh and the mood will be lifted when you can see very far into the horizon dotted with mountains. It really look like you are in Europe or NZ. Go there for sunset as there will be no shelter from the sun above your head.

Sangumburi Crater is our 1st stop after we got a rental car.It's 40 mins drive from Jeju city.Entrance fee cost KRW6,000. There are several small souvenir & coffee shops.It quite unfortunate for us because that day is raining. We're freezing because of the cold weather.We didn't prepare any umbrella or raincoat.
