However we still enjoy the view.The walk down is as beautiful as it was on the way up.

Quite long caves, but we do enjoy walking through it until the end of the caves. It was cold inside, feels like we are walking inside a room with air-conditioner. Lols. My friend do enjoy reading all those facts and information on the formations, and I find it quites helpful for those who are interested in geology thing. Maybe.It is quite large caves too. For those who are on tight budgets like us, you can take a bus and walk 2km to the caves. Not tiring at all as the view is very nice.

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.

It is such a beautiful place to go! The scenery inside the cave is breathtaking and it is unbelievable for such a view. It is a bit cold and dark tho, but it has light installed along the pathway. A very nice place!

I wouldnt get out of my way to visit, but if you are in the area and enjoy gardens, you might want to visit.Outside, the japanese and korean gardens are lovely. The french and italian gardens are too kitschy for my taste. Inside, the water flower garden is especially nice. Make sure to take the elevator up to the   observation platform   -? if the weather is clear, you can get good views of Hallasan.

I would echo an earlier review that said that you should not bother with this if you have done any caving or similar - this is aimed at casual visitors not experts. It is a gentle wander in a cool cave that is appropriately lit, reasonably level and there is enough English signage to explain what you need to know. It is the fact that this was a lava tunnel that is not interesting and the signs do explain how the lava flowed, melted and cut down and through from other tunnels. 1) Wear sensible shoes.2) If it has been raining it can drip a lot inside though on our visit I did not think so.3) Some might feel it is cold - I did not

I wasn't expecting to have to walk up this thing, but I guess that should have been obvious to me. It was a hot and panting walk, but it was not that long. It was a sunny day, which made for great views, but not for a cool walk. I had JUST MISSED the show with the women divers, I guess it is at 1:30 and 3:00 daily. Nice panorama at the top, the view is certainly impressive.One other thing I liked a lot about this is that it is a fairly touristy area, which meant that most restaurants I passed had pictures and/or English on the menu outside and inside the restaurant, making it easier to order food,

I was very excited to visit after reading the reviews; while it was very nice, I left slightly dissapointed. Maybe we visited at the wrong time of year, but almost nothing was blooming outside. The different outdoor gardens were pretty, but I was expecting a lot more colorful displays.Inside was a bit more of what I expected (although again, not as many flowers as I thought there would be). The main area is air-conditioned, which is a HUGE relief from the heat outside (and some of the display rooms are pretty toasty, as well).? We were lucky to get a clear day, so the view from the top of the glass dome was fantastic.The garden is in a great location, with plenty of restaurants and other attractions nearby, and just a short drive from Pacificland and the beach. As a stand-alone, the garden may have been a bit of a let-down, but since we were able to spend a couple of hours here, get some lunch, and then head down to the beach for some waves, it ended up being a fun family day.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

I am used of the garden by the bay in Singapore which is great, so I went there just to depend some time and expecting something just .. so so.I was actually wrong. The garden is nice, outside as inside. The round shape with all kid of plants, the elevator to go on the top and enjoy a great view, the type of gardens outside (japanese, coreen, italien, french...).Sometimes a lack of maintenance but.. definetely a nice place. Entrance is about 7usd for adults. A little train can bring you around but I didnt use it and.. not sure it is free.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Gosh...this place is awesome... Its very well maintained and comfy for those people walking inside and enjoy the lava tube nature. Recommend to wear shoes or comfy sandal as it sometimes wet inside. Not just the view, but also there are boards for explaining the things we see inside. Love it!
Entrance fee costed me 4 000 krw. Reachable by bus. The view inside of the cave is very intriguing and fascinating. For me, it is worth it to visit.

Easy to travel to from either bus terminal (Jeju or Seogwipo). The hike is not daunting at all as it is primarily a flight of stairs and some inclined stones at the beginning. Entry fee is $2. No food is allowed inside so forget about having picnics. Provides a great view and the tuft is something special and best viewed in person , so do the short hike. Gets rather crowded but there are a number of places to eat at. I enjoyed it!

Coming from a country where temples are famous for their stunning decoration I did not expect much from temples in East Asian countries. But Yakchunsa Temple was beyond my expectations. The temple is stunningly decorated. The Buddha statues are absolutely beautiful. I recommend you walk up to the second floor where you will see countless mini gold Buddha in different poses on the wall to your left and you can enjoy the view of the main hall and the main Buddha from high up. There is a small building to the left of the main hall with 500   heroes  . I think they are important monks or something. At least that's what it says in Chinese characters. All 500 of them have different facial expressions and poses. Some are very comical. Do take a quick look inside. And don't forget to drink the water from the water fountain before you leave the temple. The water there is refreshingly sweet.
Amazing view of the city as well as of the nature inside the peak.- 20 to 40 min to go up- pack water- pack sport shoesPlenty of rest areas on the way, so you can take your time

Amazed by the view inside the cave. Overall distance travel back and forth takes 1 hour to complete, approximately 2km. Advised to wear comfortable shoes (rocky slippery floor) and jacket as it can be very cold inside the cave. Bring an umbrella if you need it as there?s water droplets from the top of cave.

We were quite frustrated when we arrived and see a crowd of people inside plus it is raining heavily on the day we arrived. Yet the tasty green tea crepe makes the whole trip worth it ! You can take bus 152 from new Jeju city.

We travelled to this market in October 2016 using the Jeju City tour bus. The inside of the market was well lighted and there were lots of fruits and local goods on display. Inside there was a branch alley which sold fish and other marine products. Across the market there was an open square with a small river and we saw some tourist police on horseback. The market was not as big as we expected but OK to visit and buy some fruits.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

We got the bus to this amazing temple which we found quite easily.  It was one of the most beautiful temples we visited in Korea and one of the few which you are actually allowed to go inside free of charge. There are many parts to this temple which is comprised of several buildings all really interesting and it is set in pretty gardens.  Well worth a visit.

Very beautiful and serene temple. there is also an option for temple stay here. it's tucked away from the hustle and bustle of city life so it will be a good retreat. There were prayers ongoing when we were there which was very relaxing to listen to. you can enter the temple through the side doors (not through the centre) make offerings of rice (you can get this at the counter inside) or donations. it may be a little difficult to get there by public transport. we hired a driver Mr Yang (+82 10-3639-7469) to help us get around - he was most helpful quite humorous and very easy to get along with even taking photos for us and giving short descriptions of the sights at the attractions.

This temple wasn't very busy when we were here and it was very pleasant to walk around for awhile. We probably spent a couple hours walking around the grounds and taking pictures inside. You can go up three floors inside the temple the paper lanterns hang down from the ceiling fairly far and you can get some neat pictures with them if you go upstairs.

This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

The admission fee for trickeye museum in Jeju is cheaper than other branch in Hongdae and Busan. I dont know if there's different inside the museum of every branch or not but the Jeju branch is relatively small. But its not too crowded so you can take the picture freely without long queue with other visitors.

Serene and peaceful temple with intricate designs and architecture inside. The main prayer hall was also well-kept and clean. It provides visitors a very nice and calming retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life.

In the front there is a bus stop. Along the road to the temple is full of orange tree. Big temple with beautiful decoration. Just feel silent and peaceful here. You can just go inside free of charge. I think this is the best temple in Jeju!

Despite being extremely busy (there was almost no space to move inside the building) the experience was still pleasant. There is a large assortment of teas to try and buy. The caf챕 is also worth a visit. Just make sure you grab a table before you order.

Be careful what you do. Just kidding  fret not for breaking anything. The biggest chance of you breaking anything here would be in the souvenir shop. A beautiful museum to go to  to see everything created out of glass pieces. How a simple  yet breakable piece of glass can turn into an artpiece which seems as strong as the pillars of a temple.I like the glass tulips best  a great number of them around this museum. It really shows Korea being a Tulip country  as I get to see these lovely  brightly coloured flowers everywhere. There's a little cafe in there which I thought was a very beautiful cafe  made out of glass. The table you use  the chairs you sit are all made out of glass  added with colour.Surprisingly  the thing you should be checking out is the stand alone toilets  one for female  the other for male. Yes  it's made of glass and from the inside  you can actually see through to the outside! Don't worry  your privacy is intact while answering nature's call  because it's tainted black from the outside and people cannot actually see anything inside! So don't be surprised to see people taking a look at their reflections and doing funny poses while you are doing your business in the toilet. Have a good laugh instead!

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

We went there on July 17, 2016. We asked the hotel front desk how to get there by public bus, 2 bus numbers to take to the destination. There are plenty of bus for the first leg, but the 2nd bus no. 990 there are only 2 or 3 available in a day and the next one for us like 2 hours away, so the few people/tourists that was there with us decided to walk to the destination for about 3 kilometers. When we got there sweaty and tired we pay the cheap fare of KW2,000 (mind you cheap attraction). The good thing is the cool breeze inside the cave, mind your steps because its wet and some puddle of waters in there. Many people in there, mostly Korean tourists. The few inside the dimly lighted cave is not impressive neither beautiful as I thought. When we got out at about 4:30 pm. we happened to catch the bus no. 990, to our surprise the bus driver told us to get out of the bus while he let the Korean passengers in. We asked why and he keep telling us taxi..taxi..taxi.. So apparently, he does not take foreigners to go to the next bus stop and forced us to take taxi, sure enough, a taxi driver in the area approached us. I felt so discriminated by the bus driver, we didn't even want to negotiate with the taxi driver (because, I believe they do this on purpose). We decided to walk back 3 km. to the next bus stop. It was a waste of almost a day of our time, definitely not recommended to visit this place, NOW I KNOW WHY IT'S CHEAP!

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We didn't spent much time here as we are rushing. Overall is a nice place to visit. You can rent a bike or motor cars to go around the island or take the bus tour. At first we planned to drive car inside the island. However, due to many vehicles in the island and to avoid traffic jam, they have set the rules that only local island cars can drive into Udo island. I forgot the timeline but it took around one year period. For those who plan to drive car enter the island you may need to further check on it. When purchased the ferry ticket, you are required to fill in the two forms. Please bring along your passport as well. The counter personnel not many can speak English where we feel a bit challenge. Overall, is a nice place to visit. And if possible do spare around one day to enjoy the environment here.

We could not have gotten to so many attractions on our own in one day, so great time taking the bus tour from Yeha.  Wish we had booked more days in Jeju to explore other parts of the island such as Seowipo.  The cave is 1km long and a nice attraction to check out, especially for families.  Cold inside!  Bring an extra layer...

Visiting Manjanggul Cave is one of the main reason I visited Jeju. I and my family were not disappointed at all. We visited during late June 2015. The cave is a little bit cooler inside even in a hot summer day so remember to bring a jacket especially for kids. There was rain before our visit so the cave inside was a little bit wet but we could go inside and visit. There is a steep stair in the beginning of the tunnel/cave so one must walk very carefully. After entering the cave, there is no more stair and on flat level mainly.The whole cave is well lit so you should be able to see inside without bringing your own flashlight torches. (You can still bring it if you want to see everything in detail!)Only 1km of the cave is accessible by visitors. You go inside and walk to the end of the tunnel and then walk back the same way you go in. I suggest you riding a taxi to this place since public bus is not easily accessible to this tourist spot. There is a bathroom outside the cave only. So if you need to go to bathroom, you have to go before entering the cave.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This place exceeded my expectations, it is definitely a highlight of Jeju, it is perfectly organized to be a journey itself. We spent around 3 hours walking around ( it has 3 different routes well explained in the map) and simply feeling the nature was already healing. The entrance is 6.000 Korean won per person. They have drinking fountains and toilets inside. You can reach it by bus!

This cave was decent but the caves in Jeju were much better. It was a nice get-away from the heat since the cave is nice and cool but when I went it was super busy so I was constantly wading through crowds while inside the cave. If you have  a chance to go, try in the off-season or go early in the day to avoid the crowds.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The cave is nice if you are natural lovers, weather becomes cold inside the cave around 13 degree celcius. It should takes around 1 or 2 hours to explore the cave. For people travelling by bus, i recommends to use kaokao map and naver at the same time to find bus route and english name of bus station to get off

quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

Of all the places we visited in Jeju via our taxi tour, this is what I would rank as #1 (see  http://www.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=1121529), with Sunrise Peak as #2.  This is a Buddhist temple set in a vast very pretty land.  Interesting Buddha statues ? very exotic particularly for those who have never been to a Buddhist temple.  Our taxi guide politely asked, I believe a caretaker, to see if we can actually go inside the temple.  We were allowed.  I?m not sure if it was early or this is not a traditional tourist place, since we only saw very few people (as compared to the other temple in Busan packed with too many people.)  Felt a little bit odd being a tourist spectator in a house of worship, but glad we did.  The landscaping and statutes in the area were very interesting.  So there's more to see other than the temple itself. I would recommend this place for sure.  Would go back again if have the chance.  Hopefully with less rain this time.  Free to visit.

Most of government tourist attraction charge 2.000 won, and the place are so beautiful because its natural. Halim is man made park. It's pretty. It takes around 1-2 hours inside. However the price is not value for money. A lot of other morreee beautiful park in Busan n Seoul that we can visit for free.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.
Love this beach, we went in winter, wind very strong and cold, most of them hide inside the mini bus but few of us walk around, taking photos, see the raw seaweed near the stone

It took me a long time to get there. All those folks with cars would have no problems. But I am on a budget, and I am bussing it all the way. I came here from the Seongsan Ilchulbong crater thing, and I took the 701 bus to the stop that said it was for the cave. Then I walked 2.5km to the cave. The cave was gloriously cold inside, as I was a hot sweaty mess by then (Korean people staring at the fat, sweaty American haah!). I took my time through the cave, it was nice and worth the trip for me, even though it took me almost 2 hours to get back after I was finished. I think you could take a cab for a reasonable price... but I am cheap.

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I never been to such places before so i have no reference to compare it to. I think it was worth the entrance fee, a bit hard to get there with the buses. You pay the fee for inside baths that are separated by male and females, where most of the people are naked. You pick a small locker room for your shoes and with the same key you can open a bigger locker for the fest of your belongings. You should shower before getting in the tubs and must pay to use the outdoor tubs, where both man and women can use(not naked). Try to follow the instructions in english of how to use the baths, for how long and in what order and it will be worth it. They also have massages, sleeping rooms, lounges, vibrating chairs, small restaurant ...

I love this cave as it was calmy, a little bit wet but make you comfortable after a long walk from the bus stop. I had to walk 3km or more (I think) coz my legs felt so sore, but I love the walk inside the cave. If you take a public bus, don't finish up too late as you might miss the last bus.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

Hallim park is quite big park and there are many things inside. Tickets 10,000won. Sightseeing times around 1 and half hours. On April has tulips festival in park. There's different flowers in each months. From bus terminal take bus no 702 (1 and half hours) for reach there. Hallim park fits with everyone.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Great place to relax and take shelter form harsh weather condition.It's very peaceful and quite beautiful, particularly on the inside. The temple is spacious and also has a little garden, with a lake and several tangerine trees.We got? there by taxi but you can also take bus 600 from Jeju International Airport (Bus Stop 1).

For everyone's information, Nanta theater in Jeju just moved to middle of nowhere, without bus lines nor taxi around. It became a spot only for group tourist.The performance was perfect. But after the performance, when we asked the theater staff for help. The two girls refused to call a taxi for us and asked us to take the bus which we later found out didn't exist. It was cold winter and I asked for permission to stay inside when I call for taxi, they insist we go out and lied to us about the bus.Luckily there's also a newly built Nanta hotel around. The hotel staff drove us to nearest town and helped us get a taxi.So, 5 star for Nanta hotel service and 0 for Nanta theatre staff.

Eco land has big landscape. Inside there are 4 trains station. A small train that drops people in all station, after reaching a station, people can look around and get into next train. One part is good for children, since there are kids house, kids coffee shop(miniature), fire station (miniature), bank(miniature), movie theatre(miniature) . This whole place is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park, Sangumburi Crater  and stone land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places. Usually if you taxi for using between 9 AM to 5 PM, you will have to pay 120,000 KRW.

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Bangju Church is a picturesque little church that?s unmissable on the way to Bonte Museum.  It?s the unique ark-shaped exterior along with the surrounding water that makes it photogenic and there isn?t much inside (which is off limits most of the time anyway).  Despite being a short stop, there were always a half dozen cars in the parking lot with people busy taking photos around the church.

As a part of our school's field trip program, we went to the one of the known attraction in Jeju-do which is the Jeju mysterious road. While inside of the bus, our tour guide asked the driver to turn the engine off. Our tour guide pointed out that even though the engine is turned off, the bus still continues to move   way up  . But in reality, our bus moved downwards. It was like an optical illusion. For me, this attraction is not that amazing, just a normal road. On a positive note, if you have a lot of time to spend in the island, give it a try and experience the illusion.

As a child I was a big Hello Kitty fan and thought it would be nice to visit this place, after seeing it at the airport. Getting here is really easy from the main bus terminal. I did not know what to expect when I got here. But when I got there I noticed it was $12,000 won to get in. But once you are inside there is nothing special about the place to be charging so much. Its just a bunch of halls with Hello Kitty pictures and some random facts. On the second floor there is a Cafe, that is also overpriced and over crowded. Almost impossible to get a good seat. Service is not great. They not only took forever to take my order, I was the only one in line, but also to give me what I had ordered. The gift shop is also an overpriced place with not a lot of options. Knowing what I know now I dont think I would have done this place.

Apart from walking 2.5km in the extreme summer heat from the bus stop outside (pls find alternative routes), the cave was unique and pretty interesting to see. Love the temperature inside to cool us down and be away from the heat too.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

we went on a rainy day & late (about 5pm) which they close at 7pm. many area closed due to our late entry but at least we got a 20% discount for the tickets. tulips are beautiful. the caves inside are nice too (good to get some shade from the rain). but pity I didn't manage to visit the cherry blossom garden because it was near to 7pm already which the cherry blossom garden is supposed to be the last stop.
We stop here on the way to the airport. It's quiet interesting experience when the car moves. Can't help laughing inside the car as the power is off but it still moves.

this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

There is nearly no advertisement for this museum in the city. I saw the sign at the traffic and wanted to give it a try. The building is so small that when i arrived I thought it will be a quick tiny event. But once you are inside you will be amazed by the beauty and the variety of seashells. Most of the explanations are in Korean but still nothing can stop you to enjoy this museum. At the roof  there is a giant shell  which you can go in and have a photo. There is also a small shop where you can buy gifts to your loved ones and something for yourself too.

Stop by Alive museum on the way to visit other places spend an hour inside the optical illusion museum and play kart outside.  Karing part is fun with the two seater. (Kids can sit next to parent) and it is 4 times faster than the ones in Disney.

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

Innisfree is a Korean cosmetics brand known for its natural ingredients sourced directly from Jeju in Korea...think of it as a Korean Body Shop. The Innisfree House in Jeju is a combined shop and cafe located inside the Osulloc Green Tea Museum complex. You can buy products and make your own soaps as well as sit and chill with some Korean and Western fusion drinks and cafe style food. Good stop for lunch or afternoon tea and to pick up souvenirs. Recommend spending only 1 hour (combined with the green tea plantation photo op)

In this museum you get to see the rows of tea plantation outside and if you head inside you get to enjoy the awesome tasting cakes and tea. Great stop over while visiting Jeju. It also has other tea made products like soap etc.

I have seen all the a lot of Aquariums in Asia and America. Comparatively this is not big as that with big shows but it makes use of its space and is a natural stop over from Seongsan sunrise peak. 10 minutes away. There are amphibians like exotic frogs iguana and Lizzard from all over the world Penguins and Pelikans Walrus seals and sealion. You can also sea them during feeding time.There is also a big aquarium with fishes sharps and stingrays. What I liked most were the small aquariums with exotic fish variety. It did not have whale shark which require big space and are usually in the wild. This I have seen in the open sea while swimming near it. Overall the place is cool although smaller by comparison but spacious inside. It is recommended because it is part of the it is on the way to or from Seongsan and educational especially for children.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Here was held the biggest event of the 2002 Korean and Japan Football World cup. The stadium blends in well with its surroundings  reminiscent of a small volcano in shape. The 6 pillars inside the ground represent the 6 continents.In rooms around the stadium  you can see memorabilia from the 2002 World Cup.Certainly worth a stop even if you're not a football fan.

Given the trials and tribulations faced by the Dutch crew all those centuries ago  I did find it irritating that the top deck of the boat was closed because the wind had risen to a slight breeze. I am unsure what sort of risk or danger the owners were trying to mitigate against  as I am sure the bridge would have been perfectly sate and noone was going to be blown overboard by a tiny puff of air. The display inside the boat tells an interesting story. The Covid temperature readers at the entrance were causing the staff member a bit of trouble (and they are inaccurate) and we almost got the impression that it was our fault for being foreign humans unable to work broken temperature readers. Hamel would have given up trying.
