review: Actually the road has a huge magnet inside well we do not know is it natural or human does it....still mysterious....but we had the sensation when the engine stopped the car is moving

What a fantastic place to visit, spectacular looking ,inside ,jungle,cacti,gardens under glass ,lift in the middle at the top you get to see all gardens outside you can explore,the beautifully Italian and French gardens are just so awesome,well worth a visit ,although yes extremely hot,lots of Aircon outside garden areas ,cafe to cool down .

Went in August, so it was really hot outside. Was so pleased to be welcomed by the cool temperature of the cave. It will take you about 2 hours to go in and back out with some stops to take pictures. Recommend everyone to wear proper shoes as the cave surface is really uneven since it used to be flowing lava coupled with low visibility of the cave. The floor is also wet, so advice to wear something non slippery. I wore normal slippers and i got my feet wet and dirty, no worries though, there's a place near the toilet specifically to clean you feet outside the cave.I saw some locals even wearing heels inside, not recommended, but i guess it's possible to come out unharmed.

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

There is a start point specified on the road. I stopped my car, put car to neutral and released the brakes - the car started to move slowly forward and up slope! From inside the car, the road is up slope, yet the car is like rolling down slope on neutral gear. Fascinating! A must try if you are self-driving.

There is a stair to reach to top to this extinct volcano. It seems easy at first but you will need to be prepared to reach its top. They put places to sit through the course.Since I was there during summer time, I sweated a lot. But reaching the top pay all physical efforts!Then you can walked down in order to see (and get enjoyed by) the friendly ladies who dive! It was nice to see that they also served the seafood they've just captured! You need to see them because they are now just a few and how knows if there will be more of them in the future.Remember 1: the presentations of this ladies happen in specific times (I got their 13:30pm presentation, so I had to walk fast up and down the volcano in order to see them)Remember 2: you should pay a ticket to get inside the park.I truly recommend you to reach both the top of the volcano and see the women divers presentation.

There is a small fee to enter the area, I think around 2-3000W. Once you are inside the park, you can hang out on the paths, admiring the rolling green fields, or head up some few hundred stairs to the top of the little mountain and look at the crater. The little mountain was formed by a volcanic eruption a long time ago and around the rim of the crater there are 99 'peaks' which they call the crown. That's cool. I think that's cool.After you have taken an inappropriate amount of selfies you can head back down to a small beach area and watch traditional women divers...diving. There is also a small black stoned beach by the women divers which you can walk along and admire the beautiful black stone of the small mountain, which is Seongsan Ilchulbong.We travelled there by public transport and it wasn't difficult at all.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time??? The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It was raining and our driver decided to start with this attraction first. Although before getting into the caves, we got a bit wet, but once inside we lost track of the rain. This is a lava cave and quite different from the usual limestone caves. The only problem is that we have to backtrack all the way out. When we came out, the rain has stopped and the sun was out. Just Nice.

It was Autumn, when I visited this place. I enjoy playing indoor coz its very cold outside. Upon entrance, I enjoyed already the music that u will listen to from generation to generariion, it was fun to guess them until u reached the dance floor whic you can see yourself dancing in the platform also, after that u will experience also, to sing and play some music instrument. Beside that corner, u can also have a chance to hear top 100 music alonh the way, u can play and take photo with all ur favorite k-pop star on the stage! While enjoying inside, they will give u a call if their hologram concert starts, everybody will run to watch this. The best part is to shop items, with our favorite k-pop star logo/dasigns. See you there!

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

Form by lava stalagmites and a long lava tube tunnels. It was cooling inside the tunnel . Stone pillars and stalactites are widely spread and the tunnels shows off the cave?s topographical features.   Stone Turtle   is especially eye-catching.

Bonte Museum was designed by Tadao Ando who designed scores of museums (including the Suntory Museum in Osaka) in Japan so the building itself is very photogenic.? The complex is divided into five galleries with one of them permanently housing two works by Yayoi Kusama, Pumpkin and the Infinity Mirrored Room (each visitor gets two minutes inside).? One gallery is dedicated to Tadao Ando’s meditation room while the rest of the? artwork inside rotates.? The other three galleries were pretty bland with one dedicated to Korean traditional crafts and the other two dedicated to temporary exhibitions.? Each gallery is relatively small with the entire museum taking a little over an hour to check out.? The spacious surrounding area is a nice spot to chill after checking out the art if the weather is nice and despite the steep admission, it was still a worthwhile stop.

We visited this last for the day at Jungmun Resort since this opened till rather late (~8+pm). Last entry should be around 7pm since it would take you around 1 1/2 - 2 hours if you're gonna snap alot of the photos inside. If you are already inside Jungmun Resort and are travelling in groups you can take a cab to this place since it would not cost much and you can save the hassle of walking. The paintings inside are really cool and we had a fun time snapping photos away. Effects came out rather cool on the photos. There are several sections in the museum and each sections has its own theme. Definitely worth a visit and we really didn't regret it. Initially we intended to spend only 1 hour in the museum since we really rushing off to other places in the night. We ended up spending 2 hours there. So do equip yourself with a camera and of course have someone with you to take photos for you.

We stumbled upon this market while walking around Jeju. It was very vibrant inside with many vendors selling their products. The vendors were very friendly and tried to speak English to us. Some even gave us samples of their products. We bought some local chocolates. It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend some time.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This is a well put together museum. It has all of the explanations in English. The museum includes an outside area as well as the inside. It covers the history of the island as well as the way of life of the islanders. There's a wildlife and fish exhibit.

This is a cool place to take the family. It fun and easy way to walk through mazes. With stream for kids to play in. A amusing part for me was U given a picture of maze so can solve easily. The inside exhibition is worth a walk through with more puzzles and games.

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

Rented a scooter for 4 hours and went around the entire island. Renting is easy- just go to one of the places right next to the ferry docks. You have to go to the cliffs and the black sand beach below them. Cross the beach to the rocks where they have the boat then go inside the cave. Walk all the way to the left and go out the small opening- this place have practically no other tourists. Then if it's low tide- climb to the right to the small opening into another cave but this is a lot cooler!

Perfect for a rainy day and this island has a ton of them!When we pulled up we weren't sure if it was the right way place. The exterior is huge! Doesn't look like a trick eye museum type of place. But once inside there is a ticket booth. It was 10000 won per adult and 7000 won for your children. It was well worth the price. Once inside you will see pictures that you interact with and take pictures from specific angles. With the right pose it looks like you are in the action. Took us about 1 hour to make our way through and we had a blast. Only down side is that if it is crowded people are waiting to take pictures and shoving infront of you.
Nice attraction that suitable for all. Must walk all the way in order to see the main tube. Nice temperature inside the cave. Wear a cover walking shoe!

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)

Jeju Beer Company is the biggest of the microbreweries in Jeju.  They are now the fourth biggest brewery in Korea even though the gap between the third brewery (Lotte) and the fourth is quite large.  Despite chagrin 12000 won for a brewery tour the slots filled up pretty quickly and we had to reserve well ahead of time.  The factory is a bit out of the way from the main road and in the middle of a rather stinky industrial area.  The pub area inside the factory is nicely decorated and a cool spot to enjoy a few drinks straight from the source even though not a lot of food is served.  The tour is well run but only includes one beer without any opportunity to taste more than one beer type.  They charge for everything like pens and coasters which I thought was a bit petty when people are driving out of the way to visit the brewery and paying a rather steep price for the tour.
It's a great experience and see the way. It's not really that difficult to walk inside and it's spacious.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

I went on a group tour around Korea last year and one of my highlights was seeing the lava tubes at Jeju. You might think a cave is just a dark place with little to no visual interest but this Unesco site is really cool because you're actually inside a tunnel formed by volcano pressure. There are lights that guide your way and handlebars so you don't slip. If you're into nature and on this island it's a must see because there are some extraordinary natural feats you observe and experience first hand as you explore these tunnels. It's very interactive.

I have visited half a dozen Buddhist temples in Korea and so far this is my favorite! This temple is simply gorgeous. We arrived just as the monks started ring the outside bell. We were greeted with open arms and encouraged to come inside the main temple building and to go upstairs to see it all. I have always been hesitant to venture into the temples to take pictures because I do not want to offend anyone but we were invited in to explore it was fantastic. so ornate. The three gold Buddhist statues were very large and beautiful. The monks where in the middle of chanting it was a mesmerizing experience so peaceful and relaxing. The grounds of the temple were just as lovely.

I had never seen dried lava before (other than when hiking hallasan which was only the day before) so I thought this was super cool. There are tons of informative signs along the way too. Oh and it's cool inside--not humid!

I didn't come to pray but to take pictures -- and this place did not disappoint. The carvings statues and paintings inside the massive temple were really beautiful. There was a dignity about the place; it was peaceful and solemn. We spent more time here than we planned (about 30 minutes) since we made our way down from the temple to the fields covered in canola flowers. There were paths to run in it! There were cherry blossoms and tangerines. It was a beautiful place and I would come back if I have the chance.

Had a high expectation about this place since it always comes up on your google search when it comes to Jeju Island. It's just like a big cave and that's it. It's beautiful? Yes. Is it amazing? Not really. You can walk inside the cave and not seeing that much (just a stone of course)
great place to go on a hot day as it is nice and cool inside and it is amazing to see how lava carved it's way through the rocks

Good chance to explore natureof lava tube..I shall recommend for walk alley to be build along the way inside the tube..its to hard to walk on the slippery rocks.Hence to put more highlight inside the tube..its too dark inside

Admission fee 12.000won per Person. Free parking. Coffee and souvenir shop inside.I would give 4 points but this museum has no information in english at all. Although they advertise the museum with ?쐀iggest sex museum in the world?? so in my opinion the translation of information in english is a must. The admission fee is way too overpriced for not understandig everything. They do translate in chinese.By the way the museum is more funny instead of ?쐓exy?? Would just go here with friends not with a date because some statues/pics etc kill every possible erotic moment. XD

Across the street from the museum is a green tea patch where people can take touristy pictures and just walk around. The day I was there it was way too hot to even attempt to take photos. Inside the building isn't really a museum but a tea shop that has a lot of variations of teas. There's also a little cafe that serves hot and cold tea drinks along with simple snacks to have with you tea. Out back there is a walkway for people so that they can see the open landscape. There is also a Innisfree Jeju Island shop that has make-up and it was interesting to see some of the main ingredients in their skincare line out on display. The Innisfree shop also had it's own separate cafe with beverages and food.

A long way to reach the other end. The road was slippery and uneven. The place was dark and the only light source was tiny statues with lamps along the cave. The temperature inside was 11-18째C and well maintained throughout the year. If you are interested in geology you should probably check in here but it was quite mesmerizing for non geologist as well

While it is not spectacular like other caves around the world that are open to tourists, they are worth visiting due to their geographical nature.They are easy for families to visit, no bending over or crawling necessary.The temperature inside stays around 16-18c all year round. It is always damp, and most areas are dimly lit.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

We went to this cave as friends want to visit even it was not on my bucket list. It was impressive to see volcanic layers and massive path inside. We walked down all way to the end i.e. 1 km away and walk back again. Personally, I don't find it interesting.

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went there because closest hotel, we driving to there and saw that is not to much visitor maybe was late evening, we try to going up, however in the middle of the path have 1 counter ask us to buy a ticket, we only want to walk around so we haven't paid and plan to leave, but we saw some of people can go up on the other way, actually is the same road but one for entrance and one for exit, you can go inside in the exit way but only have limited area you can visit. if you want to go up, you must need to paid

We visited the cave on the way back to Udo (very easy to do both of these in one day. Very interesting and well explained. It would probably be a good idea to bring a jacket because the temperature in the cave is significantly lower than on the outside. However, it's still really cool to see and think about the implications of the event that made the cave in the overall of Jeju. Very good for kids although it can be a bit slippery inside too.

We visited on a very wet day so it was good to be inside even if the inside was the lava cave.  The lighting is very low in the cave and the floor, made by lava flow is very uneven so close attention needs to be made to where you are going. Its one kilometre each way to the end of the public bit and you miss quite a bit watching where the feet go so not to fall over.mAn interesting place to visit but take a torch!

We drove there and parking is free. The whole experience will take about less than 2hours? About 45mins to walk all the way inside to the end of the cave and another 45mins out. So remember to empty your bladder before entering. There is no loo inside the cave.The cave is cold. About 15 degree celcius? Luckily there is no wind. The ground is made up of rocky bits, and the place is constantly damped and slippery. So wear a light jacket and confortable shoes.Although there are lights in the cave, they are pretty dimmed. Not brightly lit. We used the torchlight function in our phones to further assist us to see the rocky ground. It is not unusual to carry a small portable torchlight if you want. Im not a person who likes cave, but well.. it is an experience i guess.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

This was fun. it only took about an hour to go all the way through. there is a 2,000W charge. its chilly inside so if you bring the kids, pack their jackets. Its solid lava so it is not as colorful or full of stalagtytes as other natural caves but being in a lava tube is a unique experience and this one is really big. enjoy!

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This is one of the attraction in Jeju that nice to visit! The cave made by volcano lava. When we went there it's rain, so along the way inside the cave wet and dirty! Inside the cave quite slippery and dark. Overall I like this place! We manage to go to the deepest point and come out within 1.30 hr.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a lovely spot to visit. You can wander around the artists village enjoy the outdoor sculptures (kids will like the brightly coloured animals near the art shop/cafe) and then have a good look at the exhibitions inside.  There is a permanent one and a temporary one. The temporary one at present is about marine plastics and pollution. The work was really good especially the video work and created   man   by a young female Korean artist. Most impressive.The last Wednesday of the month entry is free but it's only 2000 won anyway I think. They have an English brochure and the lady at reception was very pleasant.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The cave is really nice, and amazing as it was created by the lava tunnel, thus the floor is the original ground where the lava froze. The journey is 1km one way, butnthe cave is lit, so you dont need torchlight or guide inside. There's interactive exhibitions too inside about the structure of the cave that was created by lava, unlike any other limestone cave.

The building looks a bit old. There re space for parking. Inside the castle, there's hello kitty tree at the middle for photo shooting. When you walk inside, there're few theme of hello kitty for photo shooting and walk up the stair to the 2nd floor you will see a few rooms theme of hello kitty including the kitty cafe which sell drinks,Desserts and cakes. The restroom also there. The price is not high. The restaurant decorated in cute seating with hello kitty design. On the way back on ground floor you need to pass the souvenir shop. The price is not cheap for stuffs but if you are hello kitty fan it may worth.

Sangumburi crater is a designated Natural Monument touted as the world's only flatland crater. The car park entrance showcases several large rocks from the crater such as the volcanic bomb and lava tree mold. During the eruption, molten rock flew from the volcano into the air and cooled into many exotic shapes. The area near the crater also contain several traditional Jeju graves - wide, trapezoidal stone walls surrounding the burial mounds. Visitors can walk around the extinct volcano crater rim, peer into it but cannot venture inside the crater pit covered with lush vegetation. The hills and Hallasan surrounding the crater is a picture of serenity and rustic greenery. Sangumburi is especially popular in autumn when the slopes are covered in Jeju?s famous Eulalia. Crowds and couples will be lining up for photos among the tall plume-like, silver grass swaying in the breeze. At a quiet spot, listen to the whispers of the eulalia dancing against the blue sky to add a pensive mood to the autumn romance.  Note: KRW6000 entry fee is quite expensive. Closes at 6 pm, except Nov-Feb closing at 5 pm.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Not suitable for old folks, because is full with rocks.. Better prepare a torch light or you handphone torch light. Inside very dark. The lights not that bright enough. Prevent any injury. Walking distance to the end about 1km, one way. Winter season, very fresh air inside the cave.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

It's a new experience to us. It's great. Just walk inside the maze until you find the way. Maybe try and get help from your friends who have reached the tower. It's a great activity. Got some traditional games to play as well. There are lots of big fat cats at the ticketing counter. So cute, so fluffy.
It's a bit dark here and u hardly can see your way, so u need to be careful when u go inside. Every lava section is quite different that makes it quite special and memorable.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

I'm a teddy bear lover, going this place is always my dream, but when i reach there, its really disappointing. The entry ticket is not cheap but inside is all the teddy bear display only. There is no interaction or anything that is special. Basically its just like entering a teddy bear soft toy shop. The souvenir shop also ridiculously expensive, one small teddy bear can easily cost u around USD 30. The small here is really small like a palm size teddy bear keychain. So if you really wanted to visit, once is enough.

If you love the nature, do not forget to visit this place. This lava tube stretches out to about 1km. Do watch out for your steps as it is quite dark inside, unnecessary to bring a torch light anyway.

If you like cave, do not miss out.my partner pick this one as a highlight in Korea. It's very huge cave.only open 1/3 ish though, you can walk on actual lava stones all the way.* MUST bring jacket or something to warm you up and wear proper shoes. its quite cool inside and wet.

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Arrived around 4pm and bought 4 tickets...2,000?? for adults and 1,000?? for children. That's about $5-6 USD. It was 90 degrees outside but cool and refreshing inside. At the start it was 50F and got colder as we got deeper. If you get cold easily, you should bring a light jacket. I would wear shoes because it's a bit wet and rocky but I saw many people walk through with sandals and slippers. It's about a 25 minutes one way. It is pretty well lit for a  tunnel/cave. There's no climbing or steep terrain except for the way down but there are handrails. You will enjoy the experience. It's informative as well.
Approximately 2km walk all the way in then back out. Cooling inside the cave. If I were to go again, I would bring a torch so I can take better pictures and videos inside.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

this is a place to take many trick photo. Some looks totally great on photo while perhap others may not. A lot of lying down pose is needed and we spend hours inside taking all kinds of photos. Had a lot of fun with my gals. But the location is a bit out of no where so be cautious if you gotten go in the evening and head out when night falls because the distance to walk out and the darkness is totally far and dark. Get the reception gal to help call for cab if needed. Oh ya we miss out those that are outdoors as the dark falls when we are done with the indoor photos.

There are quite a few of these in Jeju and Seoul. If you aren't the type to take photos at every painting then about an hour will be sufficient for the inside exhibits. It was raining so we didn't get to explore outdoors pity. The little Provence village at the end with the big stuffed dogs makes nice pictures too.

So much cuteness in one place. If you love teddy bears this is the place for you. And if you love Prince Hours (Goong) You will find the bears that they use on that korean drama displayed here. Place is located inside Jungmon Resort so it is pretty easy to find.

Personally I find this place to be one of the most undervalued sights in Jeju. Mokwana represents the historic administrative center in the oldest part of Jeju City. The place is not large yet has a lot to show with stories at every corner. It takes only about half an hour from the airport and it took us about an hour to get around once inside. They have nominal admission fee (~ 1.4USD) and it was worth. The only complaint is that some of the labels for exhibits were provided only in Korean.

Max 1 and half hour. The human figures in the park shows the erotic part of the human being in different sex positions but done in an very artistic fashion. There's also shops inside selling sex toys accessories. Try not to bring underage in not sure if they restrict.

Long cave path that has been carved out by lava flows.  Its just basically a walk thru the cave and back.  Paths are not paved and can be treacherous at times.  Wear good walking shoes.  Bring a tripod if you want to take some nice pics inside the cave.  Fairly dark in spaces.  The walk should take about 1.5 hours.

If you just wan to spend for few hours while waiting for your flight. Here the good place. Entrance 8000KRW.  A small area block up for your big luggage you will have locker for your shoe. Once you enter inside you will find a long locker to store your belonging. It can fit in a small backpack.  Take a spa relax and rejuvenate before go for rest room. There are a lot ppl go there for overnight stay even it is weekday perhaps just their culture. The living hall area and sleep place rather to say it's hot I will say is steaming. If you kind of person can't stay for hot this might not be a good place to sleep for you unless you are very tired. You can take blanket from the counter you pay for your entrance fee. Where the pillow just look it from any empty room

Green Tea museum is a garden where kids can run around parents can sit down for a tea and cakes.  Also have a cosmetic shop selling organic cosmetic inside the compound.Worth for a hour stay. Nice photo scenic place.
Good place to explore for 1-2 hours. Be prepared to walk. Bring a waterproof jacket and good walking shoes with good grip as it's wet inside the cave

For those going to Seoul Lotte world after visiting Jeju please note that there are some pictures available in Seoul Lotte world too. Having said that i still highly recommend you to visit this place. The photo is funny and your kids will surely love it. We spend around 2 hours inside taking all kinds of photo. The air-conditional place makes the stay more comfortable. There is an out-door venue but as it is still hot (9 sept) outside we have given it a miss.

Awesome Museum! Has everything for singles and couples who want to visit! It was only 20 minutes from the hotel and the taxi service was great! Spend about 2 hours with the gift shops mini museums inside and looking at the statues. It was raining however the staff was prepared for the rain and had rain coats available for 2000 won! I would definitely recommend!

A nice place to go for a couple of hours if you like animals and botany but in my opinion it was too expensive at 9000 Won per person. I think a fair price would be 6000 Won per person especially as the food and drink inside the park was extremely expensive.
Working hours from 8AM (or 9?) till 5PM.Spend 2-3-4 hours there, many flowers (in season), animals, folk village inside, two interesting caves. Just nice! :)
went part of Yeha east tour. Spent 1 hour hiking deep inside the caves. Beautiful, damp and enjoyable.

We spent around 2-3 hours in Hallim Park, and didn't regret it. The flowers and the botanical garden were beautiful, the cave and the water area were also very interesting. Very good opportunities to take photos. As we went in April, we got to enjoy the countless cherry blossoms! My personal highlight was the 300-year old bonsai in the bonsai area. If you're in the area, this is definitely worth a visit. There are several restrooms inside the park, as well as spots where you can buy food at a reasonable price.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

This is a great place for young children, with so many teddy bears to see and to play with. Even my husband and I were kept fully entertained. Inside you can see teddy bears in many different settings, all very cuddly and well presented. What I loved most is the outside area - I could spend hours just watching kids play, and it'll be great to have a picnic in the garden with all the nice surrounding, and with teddy bears of course.

This crater is unlike the others seen on the island because it didn't form much of a surrounding cone due to its quick explosion without spewing much lava around. It is the only such kind of volcano seen in Korea.Apart from the special crater, there are miscanthus (the purple reed) and eulalia in different seasons. Very leisure walk around.We spent an hour inside, including a nap under the tree on a wooden swing.

They are selling variety of products ranging from skin care, hair care, body care and even food and beverage. Their skin care products are popular in Korea and well known. Besides, if you have times try to buy a hand made soap pack and try to make the soap yourself. It might take time around 1 to 2 hours as there are 3 pieces of soap inside the pack. I would strongly recommend you to try this as this is only available in Jeju island not at other's innisfree branch.

The museum has a lot of teddy bears (e.g.   Goong   or   Princess hours   teddy bears, etc) well protected in a glass boxes. A total of 3 levels in the building, displaying different kind of teddys and you can buy some souvenirs from the ground level. At the grond level, there are also teddys which you can take picture with (e.g. Steve Jobs, Psy, etc).Outside the building, there are some other teddys which you can also take pictures with. It would be fun if you love teddys but if you are not, it would be quite boring. Nothing much you can do, other than taking pictures and buying souvenirs. However, it still worth a go if you are curious about the variety of teddy bears being displayed inside. The admission fee is around 8,000 won (if i didn't remember wrongly).

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.

Only 1km of the 7.5km lava tube is open to the public, but I highly recommend coming! Expect to spend about an hour admiring the beauty of this natural volcanic formation!While we were there, it had rained the night before and was still drizzling slightly, so the ground was damp. Good to wear proper shoes with good grip (we were thankful for our boots) as the ground is a rather uneven terrain and can be slippery when wet. It's also rather dimly lit, with some lighting inside to guide your path and highlight specific features found in the cave.Even though there is only one entry/ exit point, there is much to see (if you're into geology/ geography/ nature lover, otherwise it'll just look like the same dark cavernous backdrop) as you loop back to the exit point.
Once you enter the cave and start to walk inside the cave, you will get a good amount of knowledge about the cave and how it is form. Very educational and quite a good 1 hour walk inside the cave.

If you go to Jeju Island, this is a good place to go. There is a Kitty Cafe inside, it is the same as those in Seoul. Apart from the Cafe, there is also an souvenir shop, you can buy those limited edition products there. If you drive there, you may need to wait for the parking space during peak hours.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

First, do not get lost, second prepare to spend at least 3 hours here. If you don't like nature, this is not a place for u. It's like all nature in one. There's cave inside which is to be the only cave that has limestone and lava.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.

Dongmun wet and dry market show lots of fish and seafood. One shop inside provides local korean food even Running man visited before. Jeji mandarin can be purchased by box. Small souvenirs are sold. If you want local experience, 2 to 3 hours walk can be arranged.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.

It's worth our climb n walk to the fall. Please wear warm enough to prevent same thing as us. I just wear a sweater and T-shirt inside yet the wind breeze can make you freeze. Worth the long walk and stairs taken to reach the destination.

The sea woman's show and horse riding beach are all inside the park.Climb up takes 20 min. Then you are at the edge of the volcano.Must go place beautiful volcano peak.you can hear sea woman sing and eat their harvest. you can ride pony along the seashore.As you know, every scenery place cost 2,000.
We weren't sure what to think until we got inside. Simply amazing. It was funny and silly and cute all at the same time. It's a walk through history as told by the Bears!

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

These caves are quite common all around the island  and this one is a well maintained and easily accessible example. Be aware though that if its been raining the day before you are likely to be dripped upon  but it's tolerable. Also  depending on the time of year  you will probably want to wrap up warm as it can be quite fesh inside.

There are many glass exhibits in this park with indoor and outdoor sections. There is a myriad of colours once you step inside and it is sure to lift your mood. It is recommended for families and couples as there are many chances for memorable photos. You can try out glass blowing if you have the time and willing to pay.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.
romantic feeling but at the same time feeling creepy. So many cute bears inside please be prepared the cuteness of the bear..:)

reach here after Manjanggul cave as sunny & good weather. it has some cats near around all of them were sleepy or lazily style. before went inside the maze. it has a small garden with some flowers. and the maze actually not to difficult or complex but good for take rest when you finished the game. it has shelter & you could buy a cold drink at there. ok to try if you got time.

Personally I love this place very much.It's a good place to relaxing your mind.The place is huge yet I do find peace at every corner and section inside.You should come by yourself or with your family.I've been to couple of aqua place in several country and I think its worth it to spend time here.However don't waste your time with a cheesy diving show.I recommend you to go to nearby White House (actually Light House) rather than waiting for the diving show time. So I'll definitely come again!
