review: One can take a slow walk inside the cave and enjoy the art form by mother nature. It maybe one in a life time to walk on cool off lava where the surface is not smooth but rather come in difference shapes.
No trip to jeju should be without a visit to this amazing cave. Comfortable walk inside the cave as long as one has suitable shoes.  Take the time to enjoy this cave. Last entry should be at 5:10 pm.

It's wet and dark inside..we just walk and walk in dark sometimes we just talk about going back and not see what's in the end of the path. But somehow we reach the end..take a photo and then walk the same road to get out.

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

I initially wasn't too keen on visiting this attraction as it was a hot day and inside the village it looked even hotter but via peer pressure I went in.I ended up really enjoying myself and although all the houses look the same it was still a very nice walk and large enough that it keeps you occupied for sometime.If you're into Korean Drama's you would most likely really like this place along with killing some time.

Going into the cave when it?s blazing hot outside is actually not a bad idea. It was 11degree inside the cave as you walked 1km to see the famous lava columns. Just need to be careful walking as the grounds are mostly uneven and sometimes can be slippery.

Except if you're a soccer or stadium fanatic  I wouldn't make a huge detour to go there  but if you have some time and are in the vicinity  it can be interesting. The stadium itself isn't all that huge (35 000 seats)  but it's fairly modern and has a truly beautiful roof that looks like a canopy. There are things to do in the structure of the building (cinema  restaurants)  but make sure to actually get Inside the stadium  which you can do freely and was a pleasant surprise for me. I guess it would be nice to go there on a match day but I didn't have this opportunity.
A large variety of tea and tea sets. Nice litle store where they sell the tea's and set together. Too many groups and very crowded but interesting enough to spend a short time inside the tea museum.

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).

This market is worth your time with the various street food (inside the market) , wet market and souvenirs to look at. If you could do by the evening, I think they have a designated spot (close to one of the entrances) for modern street food.
This location is nearby Manjanggul cave so if you have time specially have a kids, suggest you can visit, inside have some of Kids facilities and one more thing, there have a lot of FAT FAT Cat.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

This is a park for all seasons. It is beautiful any time of the year. We were there in autumn and although the colours were not significant yet, there were plenty of flowers to please any nature lover. The only set back is the cave. It can be quite wet inside and one has to be careful.

This Eco Land is nice and Comfortable for doing Recreation.  Relaxing and Quiet Place to visit.  They also provide Train Inside the Park.   The Train come every 5-10 minutes Here we can decide which area we want to go.  There are area with Park, Lake, Holland Decoration.  There also a place that we can do Recreation with Family Complete with the children playgrond area.  They also have Garden with some Flowers, such as Lavender, Tulips, etc.  They also have Place to have some snack like coffee, churros, ice cream.  Enjoyable place to relax and need some time to enjoy all the area.  Good to Visit.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.

There are many many many uncountable (which may count but hei! not necessary man~) teddy bears inside and a lots of other animals dolls like brown bears, sheeps, monkeys, elephants, snakes, lions, tigers, etc. Me and my siblings are having a great photo time inside there. I feel lovely and joyful for all interior design which teddy bear had placed. Love this place much! Worth to visit once in lifetime.

The indoor gardens are very lovely especially the flower and cactus gardens. We were there on a sunny day in May and expected it to be hot inside. But these are not just greenhouses. They are greenhouses with air conditioning and so it was pleasantly cool and we took our time to walk around and admire the plants in comfort. The gardens are very well maintained without a leaf out of place. The arrangements are very pleasing and and these two gardens are simply beautiful. Go on a sunny day when the light and shadow creates a most charming effect.As for the outdoor gardens, the Italian one is very picturesque with a magnificent water feature. This is not so much a garden but nonetheless very attractive.Definitely worth a visit.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

Second time here with another friend. More time this round to walk leisurely.As said in the title, no wow, OMG thing inside you'll find unless probably you are an geologist, etc. The most memorable is probably the experience of walking on very uneven, ripply hardened lava ground spotted with many puddles in near total darkness through low and tall ceiling of an underground tunnel.

Overall  the glass museum was a good experience. Everyone ranging from my 4 year old to my 70 mother found something to   ohhh   and   ahhhhh   about. My little one especially liked going through the   forest   with the glass mushrooms  butterflies  and lanterns. I wished we had a bit more time to explored the shop as there was an artist on site who could paint your name inside a teeny glass globe.

On a recent vacation in Jeju, I decided to check out the Ramada Plaza Jeju Casino. My visit was in the mid-afternoon, and there were only a handful of casino patrons inside this small casino.When you enter the casino, they ask for your ID, and then they make a photocopy of it. I do not believe that there is a legal requirement for them to photocopy your passport (or in my case, Korean residency card) for their permanent records. Frankly speaking, I was offended by this requirement. To check a visitor’s identification, yes; permanent photocopied record, no.I had the intention of playing some blackjack, but as soon as I saw that they use continuous shuffling machines, I walked out. It is impossible for a blackjack player to gain the tiniest of advantages when such machines are used. My recommendation to blackjack players: don’t waste your time going to this casino.

review: Not cheap entrance fee however there are lots of things to see.Even if you don't have much time, do not miss out their caves especially in hot days as it's so nice and cool inside. :)tiny little things to see everywhere and exotic animals as well.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

Make sure to bring a jacket with you to the cave if you get cold, there is about a 10C temperature difference from outside to inside. So if you visit in Summer, it's a great break from the heat and humidity. It's about a kilometer walk, so give yourself plenty of time. Overall,a. Great attraction for all those visiting the island!!

I've never imagine that I could spend 3 hrs for a botanical garden and that will be not enough :)The garden is very well and smart planned! Such many things to? see inside and outside of main tower!2 hrs is an absolute minimal time to spend there! Some small shops with hand made decorations and one or two coffee shop are inside of main building.Possible to   rent   a small funny train for to travel around of territory - but in this case just not possible to see and feel every perfect corner of the external garden as the train is going by schedule and route.

It was a 1km walk in and 1km out again. The lights were pretty dim unless there are signboards. The path inside is quite rocky with puddles of water here and there. Spent most of time watching out for puddles of water and where to walk instead of enjoying the lava cave. The cave was colder than outside, so might have to prepare a thin jacket.

I would not call it a must see attraction, but go there if you have spare time. I really liked their collection of cacti and insectivorous plants. The glasshouse arrangement is really impressive. The tropical section had fruit-bearing mango trees which was a sight to behold (inside the glasshouse). The French garden, the Italian garden, etc are good for a stroll. Didn't find anything there specifically impressive.

I went their with my wife. I didn't find the place as interesting and exciting as other people claimed. My recommendation, unless you are a geologist this place has nothing substantial to offer. Take a warm cloth and comfortable shoes when you visit this place. The temperature in the cave is low(you feel cool even in summer) and the floor is wet and a little bit slippery.A person can have knowledge about lava tubes but personally I felt unsatisfied. The cave is very dark for anyone to figure out things inside. Information boards inside give information about the site. If a visitor has enough time to visit, you can drop by this place. But, if your schedule is tight you can skip this place.

I was on my wear the Toms until they literally fall off my feet, and this definitely got them about there. If you do anything before going to this cave, make sure you have the right waterproof, grippy-ish shoes for the job. But really, this was cool, literally.  I managed to be hot and sweaty almost everywhere we went while on the island, but in the cave he temp drops to a comfortable 50something degrees. Just glorious! Is it worth the walk? I'm not sure. It was nice enough, and definitely cool to say I have been inside a cave at least once. So I guess I would put this on the itinerary if you are visiting the island for he first time. Would I go again? Likely not, I think once was enough!

I visit the place with the tour I bought in Jeju city. The place is higher than expectation. There are several parts of the park including the real underground lava tube which is amazing. The folk village also decorated really nice. When I visit the place, it is about 5 degree c so theres not many flowers in that time. Theres also a small zoo inside as well!

I came here by chartered taxi, I got rate 130k KRW for 8 hrs use. Not sure how to come here with public transport though. For a first timer underground trip like me, it's quite interesting. The track is not very long, not suggested for Claustrophobic person (like my friend) as it's dark,wet and getting smaller inside. Suggested to bring a raincoat with you, if you forgot don't worry you can buy on convenience store in there.

Historic timeline of bears from all over the world. Endless phototaking of them in the exhibition. Feeling closer to bears after teh bear musuem ... :) Must go for bear loversHowever, if there were more life-size bears for photo taking will be fantastic. The bears were all inside the glass panels except for those on sale. The bears on sale were not very cheap.

First time to see a lava tube. It was not the most impressive thing to see but it was such an eye opener for me! Learned a lot about this amazing geological formation. Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! Bring a layer!

Ermm. I like this place. The houses are maintained like they used to be long time ago but people still live inside (watching tv) make the village so lively. The place is clean, well-protected and demonstrate Jeju culture.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

Again, freezing of winter time and slippery step stone has discourage our tour leader to let us go any further getting inside the cave furthermore. up to the point we stand inside there, nothing special.Hard to explain accept you are cave adventurer... tourists ? it is a No No No

A great museum in Jeju with all its collection of computers and video games. Pay around 8 USD and we can enjoy this museum along with playable exhibitions.Not only we can go back in time with old videogames and computers, we can even try to play the latest videogames (Xbox, Playstation etc) and just forget the time while you are inside!Basement is worth to visit if you really want to spend your day playing games.. quite a varsity of collection.Don't forget to try ordering the keyboard waffle... ^^

A cave system that can get in easily just by walking down the step.according to the tour guide, this special cave is cold during summer and warm during winter. By the time i go is summer, it is real chill inside the cave

This was not part of my original plans but I'm so glad this was suggested to me!!! The mountain is gorgeous along with the temples inside. If you walk further down the base of the mountain there are some different food places/cafes. ALSO  at the bottom of the mountain is Yongmeori cliffs!! I had no idea they were there. Such a pleasant surprise. I'm not sure why this place isn't more popular! Gorgeous.

Went for a stroll after visiting Hanna Mountain. The cactus conservatory was impressive and we rounded up that part of Hallim Park with a thirst quenching cactus drink.  Similarly the cool walk into the lava cave, and the connecting limestone cave was particularly enjoyable, taking shelter from the melting sun. Highlight of this trip was feeding of birds inside a bird house.   We purchased their food at the vending machine.  Having them eating out of one's palm brought back fond memories of childhood.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. But dont be under the impression that it will be hot in there. It is very cold inside and be prepared with the winter clothing and a trekking shoes. It was a long walk and a nice experiences. A must visit cave.

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

It's supposed to be one of the seven winders of nature but not exactly my kind of travel destination. It's amazing for the sheer length of the cave (7km) although you are only allowed to go to the first km. We only managed to go 300 m since there wss not much to see except for molten rocks along the cave. There was not much to sustain interest in going further inside the cave so we decided to just go back. At least it was cool inside although the path was wet but nit muddy. Wear comfortable and non slippery shoes if you wish to see the cave.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

It's a great and interesting place! When else can you just go through a   natural tunnel   made by lava? The whole place is very well maintained and clean. Price is inexpensive and there is also a small restaurant and shop. You may think of bringing a second shirt because inside the lava tube is it cold (12째C/54째F). Fun fact, there is no exit at the end of the tube, you have to go all the 1 km back again ;)

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

Can only walk about 1km of the cave as the other area is restricted, back and forth will take about 45mins. Inside of the cave is pretty cooling and nice to see such a natural occurring sight but I would say nothing much as the lighting inside is also pretty dark.
Be immersed inside this lava tube! It's cold and wet, so prepare sport shoes and a jacket. Length: 1 km which you have to do twice (to go and come back)

You need to present a copy of your identification before you are allowed into the range. At 35K Won it is not exactly the cheapest range in the world but it is cheaper than Seoul for sure.There are a variety of handguns to choose from and apart from the tacky advertisements on the wall it is actually quite a secure and well maintained range.Weapons are chained to the wall for safety and only the staff can tap you in or out. Good quality 3M earphones are used. There is also a selfie stick attached for you to take your pictures. Unfortunately the staff inside the range does not speak english (only the receptionist does basic english). However they do a pretty good job of demonstrating how to handle the weapon showing you on the screen where your shot have landed after each shot.After the shoot the receptionist will total up your score and pack your score sheet for you to bring it home as a souvenir. The hot tip is to book via Klook or Trazy and hunt for discounts instead of paying for the full price.Overall we enjoyed our shoot very much. Had it been cheaper we would definitely have another go.

There are a lot of food choices in the market  especially a lot of shops selling the Jeju oranges and Jeju orange juice. You can easily get souvenirs from the market. Most of the shop keepers can speak English/Mandarin. There is a free car park just 1 min on foot from the market  another one with charge right inside the market.

Not that easy to find foods for muslim  but if you are not strict the muslim-friendly will do for you if you ask around what theyre put inside.. i looked around the musling speaking person to guide me on this. This one kind Korean salesgirl helped me on this. ^^ so please dont be shy to ask around yaa..^^

My girlfriend and I went for fun. It literally is like a museum. They have a bunch of statues outside and inside there is a lot of information to explain themes relating to sex. There is two floors. The first floor is about different positions amongst a lot of other stuff. The whole first floor is almost exclusively written in Korean. Unless you can read Korean I would skip it. The second floor does have English. I would only go if both floors have English. It is not for non-Korean speakers.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

Small local old village. There are several old huts for tourist to visit.Shops sell honey, traditional juice and facial cream inside those houses.Sales are very helpful to show direction of road. They speak fluent Mandarin.

The Stadium is closed almost all the week long except when a match is there  no visits are allowed inside  may be because that was in winter. The nice thing is that you can picture it from outside inside in  and a nearby small shops community & large e-Market place to shop & eat in their food-court. Nice play ground area around to check & may be to practice for free  you can see the local folks play around with some apparatuses  and machines to fit up
The market consist of many raw seafood sellers  vegetables  till street food. The food inside were very tasty. Its a must try

Not as big as the 5 day market but still provides an interesting insight into the daily food norms of the locals. It's sheltered so rainy days is not an issue though parking may be. There are a few local eateries inside but the one we went in insists we order one portion (they are big) per person. Rather than having to waste food we walked out.

All the kudos to the marketing team which managed to paint this place as a touristic attraction. The surface of their parkings is bigger than the entire tea plantation. Inside you can buy any premium (overpriced) tea based products you can imagine. We went on Monday outside season and it was so crowded that I got the impression it was black Friday sales.

It is an ideal place to buy souveniors and see/taste the local food.  Rather clean even we went inside the fish and vegetable market.  Along we found few food stalls and restaurants to offer seafood, we were hesitated but decided to go for fish and cuttle fish sushimi in one with rather good environment, it's food and service were up to standard, price was not high compared to those in restaurant. One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave. On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.

Brought my 7 yr old girl here and it was a good educational walk and eye opener for her. It's wet and cool inside, and unsuitable for wheelchair or stroller.
Awesome! 2 km total by walking, cold place inside, we are so amazed by how the nature creates it. When you come in rainy season please be careful with your steps. Not recomended for the elder.

As there are not much railings inside the cave to guide the tourists while walking and steps are uneven, make sure to wear comfortable walking shoes. It is beautiful and a must visit when in Jeju. I joined a tour for this visit as it is quite far from where I stayed. Tourist spots in Jeju are not close to each other and I didnt quite see a lot of public transport the in the area.
About 40 min taxi from the airport. The cave is a must see if you visit Jeju. Walk inside the cave, beutiful lighting. Amazing.

A very wide (23m), high (18m) and long cave (7+ km) one can walk along by yourself (about 1km is open to the public). The temperature inside is perfect, when there is a heatwave outside (which was the case in August 2016). It is doable with a small kid, however you can't bring a stroller as the surface is too uneven in the cave. Also bring solid shoes, it is slippery. Some visiters had flipflops or even some kind of high heals - truly not recommended.

A lava tube showing the flow of lava and various natural formation such as the lava shelves or columns. Inside the cave is chilly (around 11c when outside is around 25c), dark, wet and slippery. Bring your jacket and sturdy shoe for this visit. Heels is a definite no no. Forget about your camera (too dark for photo taking) and just enjoy the brisk walk. To and fro takes you around 45mins-1hr.

We walked from our hotel located at the Arang Joeul Street to the Saeyeongyo bridge for almost 30 minutes. There were many locals visited and walking leisurely there. There many restaurants and the Seogwipo Submarine was located on the way there. You can see the beautiful ocean wave along the way to the bridge. The bridge connected to the Saesom island. The island was brighted by light and old korean song music at night. We visited the bridge twice in the evening to see the colourful light and daytime to observe the surrounding scenery. The trail to Cheonjiyeon waterfall can be found? on the way to the Saesom bridge. The entrance to the waterfall was after Chilsimnigyo bridge.
We took the Yeongsil trail. It is a well laid out path. Only challenge walking on rocks on some parts. Beautiful views. Very cold in the morning. Bring enough clothes.

We participated in the 2020 Moonlight Walking Tour and it was a really great experience! They prepared a music show and guided us through the whole trail without any issue. The view from the golf course is especially stunning!

We got so much help from the people to get here on the first day in Jeju. The view was really great and we felt released to enjoy the wind when walking through the trail. The horses and goats look so cozy around the trail.

Visited this beautiful temple while walking Olle Trail 8. Its pretty impressive with a nice location overlooking the south coast of Jeju. Easy to reach using airport limo 600. Busy place with many tourists so go early to avoid crowd to have a peaceful time to enjoy the temple. Souvenir stalls at the temple entrance.
Very close to the Ocean palace hotel. Easy walking trail. Worth a visit for people of all ages! Recommend to arrive early before the tour busses arrive.
The real beauty of Oedolgae is walking along Olleh Trail 7. You can start from the observatory for Oedolgae rock and walk along the coast to enjoy the scenery. It's also free of charge.

The parking is 1000w. Don?t stop right after the entrance keep driving or you?ll end up walking very far. The trail is well marked no chance of getting lost. I got there about 0900 and it wasn?t busy. When I was heading back to the entrance at 1200 it was getting very crowded. The ?peak? wasn?t much of a peak. It was a flat staging area with the rock slab marking the elevation. There is a trail that leads off left of the seating area and one behind the rock slab. I followed it about 1 hour before I decided to turn back. I wasn?t sure where the path led and my car was at one end. Beautiful but easy hike. Little to no shade to wear sunscreen or hats.

The park is very big so wear comfy hiking shoes!  We only saw 1 wild deer after walking the whole trail. There are however deer in captive just after the entrance. Not a bad place if you have the time and effort.

Songaksan Mountain is another highly impressive place that I have visited in Jeju. It is a volcanic mountain with several craters. It is said that there are 99 small volcanic peaks besides two major craters in which the largest one is 500 m wide and 80 m deep and still covered with black volcanic soil. The walking route follows the perimeter of a volcanic mountain which allows the hikers to observe amazingly gorgeous vertical cliffs around the mountain. The walking trails at the top of these cliffs along the perimeter of the crater is just spectacular. Since the mountain lies at the edge of the southwesternmost corner of the mainland the visitors can see a wide view of the open sea at both northwest and northeast sides. The view of the Gapado and Marado islands on the northwest side and Hyeongjeseom Island and Sanbangsan Mountain on the northeast side are amazing from the observation platform.

My family and both of my grandmas said they felt like they gained 10 years more of their life after walking through this forest. The trails are excellent and there?s plenty to see for all ages. Definitely one of the prettiest sights of Jeju.

Lovely views from every corner. We were lucky that weather cooperated that day. Make sure that you take your time walking the several trails.  Some of them have a few steep steps but not impossible unless you have issues with your legs or balance.Great spot for picture talking. Highly recommended.

Lovely island with walking trail along the island.  Having to take bus from Jeju city for about 45 minutes and then ferry ride to the island.  It was of about an hour from the city at least.  A lot to see in the island and the flowers are lovely.  You could choose to take bicycle or motor bikes or driving around.
Located along Olle 7 (I believe) Oedolgae is a gorgeous coastline and certainly worth a visit! Spend the day walking the Olle trail and stopping for drinks and snacks along the way. Recommended!

It is stunning.  You can wear walking shoes or sandals to trek along the coastline. Most of the trail is paved with wooden boards.  This place offers many scenic sites for photos. The photos don't give this place its justice.  Have to see it in person to take it in.   There are small cafes along the trail offering refreshments and a place to sit.

If you like to visit beautiful scenery this should definitely be one of the places you go in Jeju. If you start near the beach it'll only take you a few minutes to see the best parts. If you're like me and you enjoy seeing a bit more you can walk for about 10-15 minutes along a boardwalk trail up the estuary. The trail (and river) are next to the road the whole time so it's a very easy walk. I'd probably recommend starting up the river a bit and walking to the beach that way the scenery gets nicer and nicer as you go.As for the kayaks I had no expectation of being able to go on one since the reviews all suggest you have to come early and wait for a long time. It was a pleasant surprise then that the kayaks were not operating. There were none to be seen anywhere. This was great because it meant there weren't too many people and the river looked serene with no one paddling around in it.If you're keen on doing the kayaks people have told me that they're stopped for good  and other people have told me that they're just stopped temporarily. I would recommend calling a tourist office or tour agency to find out the latest news.

Good place to visit for experiencing the lava tube. But.... Pease please please prepare a good walking shoes if you were to visit this place. You'll need to walk on rough and uneven surface and the trail is pretty long. Not recommend to bring kids and elderly to visit this attraction.

First obtain the Olle walking trails book from tourist information counter near the central bus station. From there you can ask for recommendations. I chose the scenic routes and it required walking up slopes which allowed paranomic view of scenery and also along the coastal area which was slippery due to rain. Some routes bring you directly to the beach whereby you can enjoy Jeju famous mandarin oranges and buy souvenirs such as their honeyed tea and famous chocolates! Do ask for discount like for all tourist attractions and at times the lady boss will throw in more pieces of the chocolate.You can also take partial route but check for the correct bus and you need to check which stop to alight. Unfortunately despite being a popular tourism attraction bus drivers can't communicate in English. Good luck if you encounter locals who can speak English.

Arrived an hour and a half before closing. The trails starts with a relatively step decent and the walk thru the lava tube is a 1km walk in and 1 km walk back. The lava tube cave is spectacular. Signs were available to help us learn about the the lava tube. An easy walk but need to be careful on certain section of the party as we were walking on wet lava rock. Well worth the drive there!!!
An excellent walking area with beautiful views and interesting seascapes.Trails were accessible and facilities were clean and pleasant.

A wonderful way to enjoy beautiful Udo is actually by walking the Olle Trail 1-1. There's a total of 26 trails totaling 425kms round Jeju. Website jejuolle.org. Distance is 11.2km which covers the major places on the island. Trail starts & finishes at Cheonjin-hang(port) where you arrive by ferry from Seongsan Harbour. Its a relatively easy & flat trail taking 3-4hrs. Only slight challenge is Udo Peak. There is a century old lighthouse at the peak with a Lighthouse Park with miniature lighthouses in Korea & around the world as you make you descent. Need to watch out for scooters & buses while walking.
A short walk from the parking lot to see Oedolgae rock. Keep walking along the trail to get more views of the rock from different angles.

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long? It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

We went up the Gwaneumsa Trail and down Seongpanak and thought it was a great route. Seongpanak has much better views that are easier to see while walking down, otherwise your back is facing the beauty on the way up. Both trails are majority rock. Meaning, nearly the entire hike is trying to find rocks to climb up/down. There are some wood paths, bridges, and stairs, but mostly rock which is hard on the arches of your feet. I used regular Adidas sneakers which worked, however the bottom of my feet began to ache on the way down. On the way up Gwaneumsa, we couldn't refill our water at all, then at the top - NOTHING! It wasn't until 2 km down Seongpanak (6 hours after we began the hike) that there was free water access. Nothing was sold on this hike, even though I read about ramen and drinks being sold. I was DYING for water. Bring tons!!! At Gwaneumsa there is a store to purchase beverages and 2 servings of gimbap for 3,000 won, as well as walking sticks for 20,000. I didn't use one but many did and it seemed to help balancing on all the rocks. I began the hike at 7:00am and was down by 3:45 - this included a half an hour break at the top and 2 min stop at each base camp (there were about 4 or so on each route.) I'm not an experienced hiker at all and really doubted my ability to do this, but it IS manageable! Today I can't walk but it was totally worth it.PS - for those interested, drones are NOT allowed to be flown at the top however there was absolutely no indication of this in English anywhere.

We walked up Yeongsil and down Eriomok. Would definitely recommend getting a taxi right up to the start of the trail if you want to start walking straight away. As other mentioned, it is a long, winding up hill 2.5 km walk from the bus stop. It cost us 30,000 won in a taxi from the other side of Seogwipo. The walk up was beautiful and the rest area with bathrooms at the top was  a surprise. We brought all our own food and drinks and didn?t see anywhere selling, which we enjoyed at the top. The walk down was equally lovely although the hard bit lasted longer so we were glad we did it on the way down. A short 10 minute walk from the base of Erimok are the bus stop going to Jeju City or Seogwipo. All in all it was a lovely hike and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Took us about 6 hours including numerous stops here and there and a 30 minute lunch break.

We walked to Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff for almost 30 minutes from Cheonjeyeon waterfall. it was worth it. We can witnessed the picturesque landscape of the nature. We had to pay 2,000KRW for the admission free. Easy access to the lavatory. Easy trail for walking.

We visited this place while walking the Olle trail route 10 and its great view and fresh seafood were very pleasing and I strongly recommend it. Definitely great to snap some fantastic photos while enjoying the rocky beach. The whole place was very clean and I just really enjoyed my time there chilling and staring at the ocean and volcanic cliffs. It took about 30min to walk the whole path but if you want to take everything in, chill and take some pictures 1 hour and more would be perfect.

We visited Mount Halla National Park yesterday, Aug 25th, and it was an excellent experience and great views!It is very easy to get there by the 740 bus from Jeju Bus terminal, now here is the tricky part.. there are several entrances and trails. All of them are intense hiking. Use comfortable shoes, take lots of water and snacks.. there is nothing to buy up until the very top, which is noodle soup, water and chocolates......We took the Eorimok trail to go up to Witsae Shelter and took the Yeongsil trail to return down and my recommendation is:Take Yeongsil train, the view is by far much better than the one from Eorimok trail.In order to get there:Take 740 bus and get down on Yeongsil ticket office (@45m) and from there take a taxi to the main entrance (there is a taxi that goes up and down all the time and charges 5000). Please take the taxi, otherwise you will end up walking uphill for @2km. Once at the entrance... just follow the signs to Witse Shelter. Take lots of pictures along the way!Again ... it is uphill .. from @900m to @1750m, with lots of stairs and rock trails on both trails. Up and down in @5 hours is an ok time.Enjoy !!

We visited Hallasan National Park in mid December. We ascended via Gwaneumsa trail (8.7km) up to the peak and descended via the Seongpanak trail (9.6km). Gwaneumsa is shorter but more challenging on the way up, it is easier on the knees. We started at 07:30hr, which is the sunrise time. The initial hike was relatively flat, walking on uneven big rocks. There were signs throughout the trail, indicating where you are, distance and estimated time to the peak. Snow started to appear midway and we had to put on crampons on our boots. We took about 3 hours to reach the shelter and another 1 hour 45 minutes to reach the peak. Unfortunately, the weather was cloudy at the peak with low visibility. It was very windy and cold. We joined the queue to have photos taken at the iconic landmark.We started our descent at 12:45hr, arrived at the shelter at 15:15hr, had a short break before descending the remaining 4.1km. We took about 4 hours for the entire descent, exhausted by then.This is the first time my friend and I hiked in snow during winter. We took longer than expected as we were extra careful and also took many photos. Overall, it was a great first time experience hiking on snow.Tips for winter hiking:1. Start as early as possible so that you are not pressured to reach the shelter before 1200hr.2. Wear comfortable shoes, preferably water resistant or waterproof.3. Be extra careful when stepping on the big rocks during the initial trail. They are uneven and may twist your ankles. 4. Crampons are necessary, while trekking poles are optional.5. Wear layers of clothing so that you can add/remove when necessary.6. Wear beanie hat and neck covering to protect your ears/neck from the cold, especially at the peak.7. Bring your own food, snacks and water/energy drink. There are no food stalls nor toilet at the peak.8.Toilet facilities are only available at the shelters, hence relief yourself before proceeding.Hope you enjoyed the hike.

We took the Seongpanak trail since we wanted to go to the top.  Believe me it's not easy! It is 9.6 km long (one way) and there are signs all along stating how far you have come. But the path, well its not a path, extremely rocky and uneven. It gets difficult as you climb higher. You need to reach the last shelter before 1 pm (in summers) if you want to go to the top. But nobody tells you, until you reach there, that you have to start climbing down by 2.30 because they close it and you cannot view the crater if you reach after that.  I took us little more than 2 hours to climb the last stretch and we reached just on time. On the way back, we just stopped for a few mins and then we were completely alone! It was scary because it was getting dark and there was nobody at all. I don;t know whether it is safe after dark or not but I am sure it would be almost impossible to climb down after that. So please start early. I think the maintenance should be improved even if that means charging an entrance fee. The guy at the last shelter was closing at 4 pm and we had to request him for water on our way back. It took us more than 9 hours to complete the trek. Take lots and lots of water and some food also. Not for people with knee problems or not so active lifestyle. The view at the top was no doubt beautiful and you can see the volcano crater but you can also see the crater at Ilchulbong which is much easier. So, if you are going be ready for a challenge and reconsider your decision if you are not used to walking and hiking!

We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline. After the bridge, there was a short 20 minutes trail that brought you to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree celcius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up the the temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was). You do not need to rent a car. All these could be done by foot. We clocked about 25k steps walking around for that day.

We started at 8.30 at Yeongsil and exited at 1 pm from Eorimok . Lovely walking and climbing experience. Fresh air, lot of greenery, lot of birds. Just us and nature and fellow hikers. It was fun. Very exhausting but refreshing.One must have good pair of shoes. It has lot of rocky patches.Carry water and some snacks. Sunhat is must. The trail is well guided with sign boards and emergency numbers. It becomes windy on top so a jacket is useful.Must visit place.

We really enjoyed our hike up Hallasan.  From the tropical, palm-tree lined streets at the bottom to the barren, snow coated, rocky pathways at the top - at times it felt like we had wandered into Narnia.  After reading some of the previous reviews on this website and following a stern warning from the concierge at the Lotte Hotel, we almost opted out of our plan to take the more challenging Seongpanak trail to the peak and Gwaneumsa path back down.  In the end we decided to give it a go and turn around if it became too challenging.  For people who have hiked up mountains previously, the difficulty is actually fairly reasonable (mostly steps and handrails etc).  We did not have crampons, walking sticks or colourful walking gear like our Korean accomplices, yet somehow we made it to the top and back anyway.  It took us 3 hours up and 3 hours down (starting at 8am).  I suspect the time of year largely will determine the difficulty so check the weather on the mountain carefully before you go.  And avoid the toilets.  Trust me.

We made a side trip to this attraction and thanks to our guide, we were able to experience a very refreshing afternoon hike and enjoy the beautiful colors of autumn.  There is a walking trail and it's  an easy hike even to non-hikers. It was late October when we visit and i just love the foliage in this mountain.

We did the hike up the Summit via the 8.7km Gwaneumsa Trail and down via the 9.6km Seongpanak Trail. Though parts of the Trail are marked deceptively yellow and green (  easy  ), we couldn't feel our legs for 3 days thereafter. Very rocky/uneven terrain at most parts of the Trail - challenging without the aid of hiking poles. Good hiking boots is a definite must. Please note there is a specific cut-off time at each Trail checkpoint (which may differ depending on season) and also a specific cut-off time to descend from the Summit. Hence, it is recommended to start as early as possible. We started at 8am and completed around 7.30pm (which was getting really dark by then). Though tiring, the hike is still the highlight of our Jeju trip and memorable for many reasons. The feeling of walking above the clouds (at 1,950m) and having accomplished such a challenging hike is priceless.

We did the Gwaneumsa trail up Mount Hallasan to the peak and back is over 18 miles round trip, over 3500 feet of climbing and then descending it. But it's worth it. I offer only a few points of advice. It is tougher, 800m longer, but more scenic than the Seongpanak trail. To find the Gwanmeusa trail entrance parking lot, plug in the number for the Unesco Hallasa Gwaneumsa Office: +82-64-756-9950 (you only need the last 7 digits on Jeju GPS systems if driving).1) Be prepared with good hiking and walking shoes. We saw two shoes blow out, one about 2.5 hours in. The poor guy had to walk back. There is no rescue if this happens. Also, a girl's shoe blew out on the way down about 3/4 way down, it still nearly 1.5 hours to the end depending on how slow you go. I will discuss in #3 why good shoes are so important.2) Go early, and go slow if you are not in shape or do not do activities often. Hallasan is definitely attainable by nearly anyone but it is tough, very tough because of the steep steps. Unless you are in shape and do many physical activities all the time, I recommend starting at 6AM. You MUST be at Samgakbong shelter by 12:30PM otherwise they will turn you around. It is 3/4 way up the climb. From here it is another 2 hours to the peak of the Halla.3. The volcanic stone paths and the stairs will make your legs very very tired and your feet sore. I believe they made Gwanmeusa trail challenging with rocks on purpose. These are not small rocks, they are big ones that challenge each step. Walking sticks are highly recommended. The stones seem pretty and authentic until halfway up then they are tough. Then on the way down, each step seems like a sadistic joke played by the planners. Eventually you will be relieved to make it to the bottom to your car or bus.4. Be prepared for wind. We got lucky and it was warm the day we went... in fact low warm temperatures will seem even warmer due to humidity about 1/2 the time up the mountain and back. It is a little cooler and windier at the top. Wear light, polyester clothing in layers. long sleeve tech shirt, with light jacket and light rain cover. You should be OK. Gloves and hat or scarves during cooler time. Very light during summer due to heat and humidity.After you get down on Gwanmeusa trail, there is a small restaurant with Korean snacks like pajeon and gimbap, as well as a 7/11 next door. Drink some local mokkoli or soju with with the hot snacks/food! We had a great time. Only 20 minutes out Jeju City when there is no traffic. However with rush hour traffic, or busy time it takes about 45 minutes to get back into Jeju City.

We did Olle 8, 9, and 10 trails, they are free of charge. These trails are truly amazing, within easy reach by public bus. They are very well maintained, yet in a natural setting. The trail design is incredibly diverse, taking you through towns, homes, single track, beaches, forests, mountains, farms, and historical sites. There are enough toilet facilities and convenience stores along the way  for convenience. We barely saw other people on the trails, although we were there during midweek. The walking is easy to moderate, and the route is well marked. The scenery is breath-taking!!!

We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. However, we decided to walk back to our hotel as we were tire. Jeju Olle Route 14 ? 1If you love beaches, this is a must walk route (at least it was really breathe-taking for me). We stayed at Seowipo, we took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields (photo attached). You will see a beautiful beach 1st (Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down to Geumneung Beach later as it was part of olle route 14-1 (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up. In Summary, I always thought that you would need to rent a car around jeju. However, during my 4 days trip (even Hallasan was done using public transport ? can look at my post at tripadvisor), all our travelling was done throuh public transport. We were able to view those usual scenic places that ple usually go too! The good thing about walking was that we could stop at anytime we want to take picture or do something we did not plan for (Eg: watch how the local harvest shellfish). However, we were the kind that love to walk and could spend 7 hours walking. Therefore, we could travel in jeju with a budget using their public transport.

We decided to go up  the Eorimok Trail and then down the Yeongsil trail and then catch a taxi back to the Eorimok car park.    I had been told it was a gentle incline to the top (from where you can see the summit of Hallasan) but this is far from the truth unless you are super fit.    If you are like me and generally unfit, it is a steep climb (it's very well done with wooden steps but they are steep!) Towards the end of the trail as you near the cafe and rest area it does level out.   Fortunately there are lots of benches on the way up for frequent stops and it took us 3 hours to the top.  About 5km long?The Yeongsil trail is shorter - about 3.7km I believe - but quite tricky in some parts as the steps are a mixture of wood and rock and you have to watch your step going down.   The scenery is fantastic - especially on the Yeongsil trail - and if the azaleas had been out it would have been even more amazing.   The whole trip took us 5 hours and then the taxi ride took about 20 minutes and cost KRW 20,000.   At the time I said it was unlikely I would ever do this hike again but now I have recovered I think I would in the Autumn to see the colours and also maybe in May to see the azaleas.   Maybe next time we will try the other way round......  Tips - lots of water, snacks, walking poles might be useful. good walking boots and a coolish day.

We choose a day with the best weather forecast, during our visit to Jeju island, to take a walk to the peak of Hallasan. We choose west trail ? it doesn't lead to the peak, but is much shorter. It took us 3h to get to the highest point of the trail and 2h to get back to the next bus stop. Everything was very exotic, as we are used to hike in Alps or Carpathians. It is worth to remember, that the temperature drops about 1째C/200m, so it should be 10째C colder on the peak than on the sea level. And it was. More surprising was that there are no possibility to buy food or drink in the park. Fortunately we took lot of water and some fruits and sweets (old habit from   real   mountains). The trail was very   civilised   ?mostly steps, easy and very safe (however with ice or snow it's for sure not a pice of cake). More walking than climbing. Not so much people (May seems to be off season), but we were not alone. The view from the trail and the peak just beautiful. In my opinion it's worth to spent half a day on Jeju to see it.

We came here on 11 January 2015. We hiked up the Eorimok trail and came down on the Youngsil trail. According to the signs, the Eorimok trail are divided into three sections of differing difficulties - it begins difficult and gets easier as you hike up. I found the first half of Eorimok exhausting for a casual hiker because it is quite steep, and also slippery with snow. On the day it was also very foggy, resulting in low visibility. As we walked up to 1700m, we came across a store selling cup noodles. The cup noodles aren't very good and the environment of the eating area is poor; however, it is sensible to say that one shouldn't expect too much from a little mountain store. After eating you have to take the cabbage with you and bring it down to the mountain.Next, the Youngsil trail, which is THE BIGGEST NIGHTMARE. After walking for half an hour down we realised that most of the fences are covered in snow, meaning that we were walking in a mountain unfenced! Given the steep and slippery (snow) nature of the trail, it poses significant risks of fatal falls. In some situations we were (and also some other hikers) so scared that we had to sit down and slid slowly rather than walking. Sometimes it is so steep and slippery that it's not possible to stand up without tripping over, so we slid as though it's slippery dip. Make sure you wear crampon and bring trekking pole. Without them it is almost impossible to hike in Mt Halla in winter.

Want to do a bush walk with nice scenery ?  Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail in Hallasan National Park in Mt Halla will be a good choice when you visit Jeju Island in South Korea. Be sure to take a bush hat, sun screen lotion and bottles of water. Along the trails, there are a couple of water refill spots for refilling water from the mountain. The cheapest way is to take a bus No. 740 from the Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal if you stay at Jeju city.  Get off at the stop for the entrance to Eorimok Trail.
