In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

First and foremost, bring good walking shoes. You will need to hike up the hill to have a good view. There are many stalls at the base of the hill, before you pay to go into the entrance. As this location is near the sea, it is rather windy. A windbreaker may be required depending the time of the year you are travelling.Lots of toilets around, so there's no worry about needing it.There are many tourists as well as locals visit this scenic spot. Bring you camera as well. Note: This location is open depending on weather.
Drive to the place is fantastic, walking up to the mountain takes upto 20 mts minimum. The panoramic view frm the top is mind boggling with blue tiled roof on one side of the mountain

Considering that the other craters type views Seongsan Ilchulbang (Sunrise Peak) and Hallasan are a ways up, and the seaside formations such as the Yongmeori Coast a slippery path of jumping about, the Sam-Gumburi Crater is nice and leisurely. The one place that seemed wheelchair friendly.It was also less crowded compared to the Seongsan Illchulbang so we really got to enjoy the nice leisurely walk up the small hill to see this crater. If you're a faster walker, you could probably do the whole thing in less than an hour (needless to say, we lazy walkers, took a little more than an hour). If you wanted to just roam about, you could spend a lot more time as well (there are different paths, one that's all stairs, one that is like a ramp, etc.). Anyways, this was probably the only geological tourist attraction that was wheelchair friendly and even seemed to have a few out in the front for rental. The ramp would be a bit steep but at least do-able. A lot of the other sites had either a lot of stairs/walking or way too many people for the elderly or others with bad knees to maneuver well.  Perhaps that's why we saw a number of couples with strollers.That said, this place had one of the most pricy admissions costs that we encountered. It is privately owned or something. So, instead of the usual 1,000-2,000KRW per person, we paid 6,000KRW per person. We were told that the place is nicer during the reed season, but we enjoyed the crater all the same. We'd recommended it to anyone looking to do a Jeju geotourist site without all the hard work.

Came here during sunset time. The view is very beautiful and natural. Many tourist took photo over here. During your walking distance to Yongduam Rock, don?t buy any fruit from the first stores! Very rude and not friendly. Make sure those of you beware of them.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This columnar joint was located in South Jeju, and had beautiful sight. This place was good to enjoy view made by wave and sight and sound made by wave and cliff. I didn't expect this area, but there was excellent, And had walking road was good with exotic atmosphere. Very beatutiful place to me.

Breathtaking view when you reached the peak. Time taken from entrance to the peak ~60mins. You can get a chance to see woman diver show but too bad we did not get a chance for it due to time constraint. Tips: please wear comfortable shoes for walking, the stairs can be steep, and eat some food before that for good stamina.

Breathtaking view of Jeju at the Peak of Seongsang iichulbong. Is cooling while walking up the Peak during winter. But no regret and is worth to go up the Peak and see the huge crater. Is not difficult to walk up, there is properly staircase and path. Young children and elderly also can walk up. There are CCTV at some of the pitstop.
Blowholes were small as compared to New Zealand?s Pancake rocks. But view is beautiful, a small park outside with shops around. Many attractions like Teddy bear museum are just a walking distance.
awesome view, loads of walking so be sure to be in your comfy shoes. loads of picture taking & as usual loads of tourists

Attended the 1st day of the 2014 Jeju Olle Walking Festival, infectious mood with music and performances at various parts of the scenic seaside trek during the full day walk. We climbed up the Dodu-bong, a short hill with a panaromic view of the route, planes taking off from the airport runway and the sea. While it was quite sunny, late afternoon the sea breezes can get quite chilly. However at the end of the trek there were performances and hot local food, so overall it was a satisfying Day 1 of the trek.

Admission fee for adult is 2000won. You will be able to enjoy walking up to the peak and see the entire sea/ Mountain View. It will be good to wear covered shoes or sport shoes so it?s easier to go up the steps. Not only that, there?s a 대? performance available but I missed the timing. But the 대? will be at their store selling fresh seafood. It?s a good place for solo travellers :)After exploring ilchulbong, head over to ㅼ“대?吏 for some abalone porridge :D

A very long and tiring climb if you are not used to climbing. There's lots of people both locals and tourists climbing along so you will definitely be motivated to continue climbing. Tip: bring sunglasses, pack light, grab a snack and bring a bottle of water, most importantly wear comfortable sports shoes. Just climb slowly and take a break along the way as you need so that you are not overly tired out. If you are thinking of combining this attraction with other nature sites that require ample walking or climbing, do take note that this attraction may already be rather tiring... the view and wind at the top is worth it, in my opinion. You do not see the bird's eye view you see online but nonetheless you see the vast greenery and top down view of the scenery below.

A total of 19.7 KM hikeThe walk in early spring will be having snow so be prepared.. Buy the show snow covers Crampons its a must , its a must , its a must , i went without and sliped dozens of times  and injured myself once.. its snowy on the last third.. I hiked manytimes before in different parts of the world i go with sports shoe.. this one deserves crampons.. and maybe walking sticks as well.. Its long and tiresome. . But fun.. the view is great from up .. but make sure its not foggyat the end if u show them a picture taken at the top they will give u a certificate for 1000 won.. its a certificate of achievement really after a long hike. . Its 4 hours up and 4 hours down..

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

We travelled here by bus and got completely soaking wet walking the 20 minutes from the main road to the cave. Unfortunately it wasn't worth the soaking! It was pretty boring and after 30 minutes walk up and down we were out in the ran again.I would only recommended visiting if you have a thing for geology or if you have a car and happen to be passing by.

We took the bus to get to this location and was dropped off at the bus stop.  There were no signs how to get to the destination so we went to the nearest hotel to inquire.  They pointed us the way and we forgot to ask how far it was.   We still did not find any signs how to get there but after walking 15-20 min found the entrance.  The scenery is beautiful and we took several pictures.

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

Walking through this garden park is very peaceful and relaxing. There is a cool cave feature so you get to also go into caves. The captive birds are in small enclosures and the peacocks look like there tail feathers have been pulled. Also there is a white sand beach walk across the street after you are done the park. Taxi from Ramada Plaza was 26000 wan. Bus ride home was 3000 wan and took about an hour on the 702.
to define this place in one word serene. not many people at all walking distance from the bus stop with a few cafes around

This temple wasn't very busy when we were here and it was very pleasant to walk around for awhile. We probably spent a couple hours walking around the grounds and taking pictures inside. You can go up three floors inside the temple the paper lanterns hang down from the ceiling fairly far and you can get some neat pictures with them if you go upstairs.

This is so amazing beach to walking around and relax even 11 pm we still walk and feel so peaceful and good food and good clean bar I always stay here when ever come to jeju and you can take the bus anywhere you want to go around jeju it?s beautiful island and I am from Hawaii tham you know what I mean alright

This beach was very beautiful and relatively clean. Water was clear and not too cold fot September. Altough it was posted reccommend  not to swim bc season ended in august the water and weather was great. Bathrooms were close by (though toilet paper was out at the one on the beach). The water was easy to swim in with children as it was very shallow and not rough. Got busier toward aftwrnoon with tourist buses and crowds though. Nice also as there were restraunts and snacks within walking distance as well as showers. 2000 won for parking but was worth it.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

The cliffs are beautiful and wondrous. Be sure to go very early as there will be less visitors then. Once the tourist buses come and go it will be difficult to move around. You can get there by walking from Jeju International Convention Centre and going out the back door into the park and walk towards the left side of the park for about 10 minutes.

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!

Soesokkak is a great place to visit if you are in Jeju-do. From Seogwipo area take bus 110 and get off at Hyodon Middle School. It takes another 20 minutes of walking passing by orange farms. No entrance fees is required but if you want to try the transparent kayak or the traditional hand-pulled raft you will need to buy tickets at the counter situated on your right side before you reach the estuary. The clear green blue water is mesmerizing and definitely a great place to visit. Stop-by for a bottle of fresh orange juice to quench your thirst or a cone of ice-cream to complete the trip.

It is fun to watch others here - a great people watching place.  To see masses of tourists walking backwards on what is really a busy road is great for fun and photos.  Sit outside at one of the lpocak food places - order some beers and snacks and enjoy the quirky road.  Good for an hour or so including lunch.

I found about this temple while looking for things to do around the waterfalls. It's quite a drive from them and I'm not pretty sure if by bus it's possible to get there but since it was my first temple we drove there anyway. It's a nice big temple though some of its decorations seem to be amateur. Nevertheless it was a nice experience. It's not very crowded so that's also a bonus. I don't recommend this temple for people who are disabled or have a hard time walking since there's a fare amount of stairs till you get to the temple.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

we've been Udo island on the day 2 at Jeju Island after hiking to Sunrise Peak Seongsan Illchulbong. we going to the port by walking about 15 minutes from Illchulbong, and takes ferry only for 11.000W returns. the ferry takes 15 minutes to island and schedule every 10 minutes. We have only for 3 hours at the island before going back, so we chose to hiking Udo peak. takes 40 minutes - 1 hours to reach the peak, just follow the path. really recommend to going Udo island, very beautiful scenery of Seongsan Illchulbong and the cave.You also can rent a bike for around the island or motorbike if you have international license. Or shuttle bus.

Well it's a big cave and you are surrounded by lava rocks- which are basically... Rocks.So if you like caves or rocks you will love this!It was very quiet.. Just a few people walked past us... Very different from Ichulbong..You don't need walking shoes or even a torch really, but do care where you walk..It is about 2km from the main road if you take a bus that drops you off on the main road.. Taxis often wait in the main road and charge 4000 one way to the caves..I think entry to the caves was just 1500..The Maze garden is a few hundred metres away too but I didn't go

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We went on a cloudy day and the driver drove us all the way to the entrance at Yeongsil.  Having a hot afternoon the day before, we thought it would be warmer thN the day before as we Han to walk uphill. The driver saw us in our thin layer, offered me a rain and wind breaker and a pair of gloves. I reluctantly accepted them out of courtesy but later genuinely thanked him after four hours.On a windy and cloudy October morning, the temperature actually dropped as we ascended. Two hours later it got even much colder with strong gusts, as we approached near to split of the main road to either continue uphil to the top, or to go downhill to the other parking lot. I had to use my gloves and another layer there. My husband regretted not bring his hat on a cloudy day to protect his cold ears (anyway later I found his nose sunburnt even on a cloudy day)We used our walking sticks and wore our hiking shoes, which I found very helpful. We saw some people who really had difficulty completing the loop.  I suggest tourists first decide whether you physically can complete the four hour trip (adults) to the other parking lot. If not, better discuss with your driver (if using one) to meet in the starting point, or decide where to park your car, if not taking the bus.Pack your bag reasonably and don't take any unnecessary items. Some snacks are helpful though as there are no snack bar at all. I suggest also try to bring your garbage downhill as I don't think there will be regular cleaner everyday up/downhill for hours'hike.

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

We originally got the bus here to go to hallim park. we noticed this beautiful beach and decided to check it out. anyway we ended up staying here all day. Was so nice to be on such soft, yellow sand with clear waters. There was quite a few families with young children which was nice to see all the children playing. Unfortunately there was a digger truck digging the sand while we were there for a few hours and a man kept blowing his whistle at everyone walking near the truck. if it wasnt for this it would have been excellent. Theres shops and restaurants close by and toilet blocks that provide flowing water to wash off but this is cut off around 5 or 6 pm. Sunset here was amazing.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to get off the bus on the way to Jeju city and walking towards the sea it looked like a really quiet place... When we arrived on the beach front we were pleasantly surprised by all the quaint little cafes that dotted the shoreline. There's a surf school on the beach and parasols everywhere. It is a smaller beach, but clear and shallow water. You are not short for choice for lunch or snacks. We had a lovely day!

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Very cute little island, great for 1 day trip.  It's too big to do it by walking, but you can rent scooter (only with international driving license), bicycle or to take hop in hop out bus. There are 2 kinds of busses: one that makes only 4 stops (3000 KRW) and another that goes all around the island (5000 KRW). I think the one that makes only 4stops is good enough, as the rest you can do by walking. We took the hop in hop off bus for 5000 KRW, but we used it only 3 times, the rest we walked around. Enjoy your time there!

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.

This was an interesting experience. I am usually ok in small spaces and felt this would be a great thing to do. But once I was in the middle of the first maze I felt a little uneasy. They provide a map and the maze itself is pretty easy to do. You also hear people walking around, but just something about the possibility of making a wrong turn made me not want to do the second and third maze. But there are really cool towers and a museum where you can take amazing pictures. the museum is free, they have trick art and a puzzle art. Getting here was a little bit difficult. Ask around your previous destination at the bus stop perhaps some people are willing to share taxi with you. Since the bus that goes around this area takes almost 45 minutes. And once you get to your destination you sometimes still have to walk a while to get to where you want to.

This was a very interesting Lava Tube cave.  There were signs in English as well as various other languages describing what you were looking at.  The signs were informative.  The cave is cool, so I recommend a zippered sweatshirt or windbreaker.  Also, the floor of the cave is uneven, so you definitely want to have good walking shoes.  I was just fine wearing old jogging shoes.  We went as part of a guided tour - I would have liked to spend just a little more time there, but that's how it goes on bus tours...  There may be more beautiful caves, but overall, it was the nicest cave I've been in - very nice Lava Tube - you will enjoy it.

This place exceeded my expectations, it is definitely a highlight of Jeju, it is perfectly organized to be a journey itself. We spent around 3 hours walking around ( it has 3 different routes well explained in the map) and simply feeling the nature was already healing. The entrance is 6.000 Korean won per person. They have drinking fountains and toilets inside. You can reach it by bus!

The world's largest nutmeg forest can be found on Jeju Island, South Korea.  A beautiful, old growth forest with a gigantic nutmeg tree as the central attraction, this forest offers quiet beauty to stroll through in a relaxed and rejuvenating atmosphere. The smell of nutmeg is distinct immediately upon entering.  Parts of the forest have beautiful red crushed stone walking paths and other parts have very well maintained wooden pathways.  To do the whole forest takes about 60 minutes at a comfortable pace.  Picture opportunities abound, and you'll likely be able to see wedding couples posing for their formal pictures amidst the beauty of the forest surroundings.  A great break from the hustle-bustle of other attractions, this forest offers the opportunity to enjoy nature in a very unique way.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

the pinky building and all kitty stuffs! Very interesting and nice place for pictures. they have cafe & shop for kitty stuffs, Kitty fans this is the place do not be missed. things slightly expensive because of   Sanrio   brand. but not so tourist friendly cos its not a walking distance from town, either by bus or taxi. We took bus to Kitty island (but missed one station cos we dont understand Korean language, we only stop the bus driver when we passed kitty island), for return in convenient we pick taxi (black color), cost us 60USD back to town (like 10mins distance only)

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The beach was almost empty when we went there. It was sunny, quiet and very nice. The beach is very shallow, so it requires like a hundred meters of walking to reach a place where a grown up guy's feet don't touch the sand anymore. It was the perfect beach for just walking around in the shallow water. I would absolutely go there again. We took a bus from Seogwipo (＿?洹?ъ), which took quite a while but they're not expensive. And the drivers are crazy so be prepared for a thrill ride!

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

Our plans to visit Hallasan were foiled by a typhoon the night before (we luckily still got to go, though), and we were all excited to do a nice hike. We came here probably 2 or 3 hours before the park closed (we did some other sightseeing instead of Hallasan, this happened to be close by), and the admission was free because the typhoon had caused some damage. Anyways, because of the typhoon and the time of day, the park wasn't very busy. It felt like we had the walking paths to ourselves most of the time (we chose one of the shorter routes because we didn't want to run out of time). It was a nice, easy, relaxing walk. It was also dead quiet except for the occasional group of ladies walking by with music playing on their phone's speaker. Oh and the crows going off every now and then, but that was kind of amusing since their call is funny to me (and different from North American crows). A good alternative if you can't go up some of the steeper stairs and stuff like in Hallasan. We got plenty of beautiful photos because the typhoon the night before gave all the woods a nice, moody atmosphere. If you like going for walks in the woods (even though these are all wooden paths), just being outdoors enjoying the fresh air, and you have enough time, this is worth a visit. If you are short on time and can only do one park or something, then make sure you try to at least go to Hallasan. I would definitely recommend this park over Hallasan though if you have any mobility issues, because the wooden paths are very easy to walk on and there doesn't seem to be a lot of uphill/stairs.

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

My sister and I went to Udo on a ferry ride after spending a couple of hours at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Because we did not want to go back at dawn, we limited our time to be on the island for about 2-3 hours.It is actually best recommended to spend half a day touring the island either on bus or motorbike. Since we did not have much time, we only walked to the nearby beach which was pretty deserted and that was the best part. Most of the tourist places in Jeju was crowded, but not Udo at the time we were there. The beach was beautiful with small stones and black rocks layering the sand. It was beautiful.There were plenty of cafes within walking distance but we chosed a bench facing the sea in front of a GS25 mart.I love the serenity the island offered. I just wish we had more time to go around the island.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

It's pretty difficult using public transportation in Jeju to getting around expect using car. But this one is ok because there is bus stop in the highway, but you need to take a taxi or walking 3km from bus stop to get this place

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It took about 10 minutes to travel on a ferry to visit Udo (thanks to G map)!I decided to walked around the coastline after lunch on arrival.An interesting island with some public arts and you wouldn?t stop taking photos!It worth spending some time walking around! (A number of transportation options are available, such as bike, e-bike and bus)!

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)
In short, you will be walking/driving with chaotic buses, motor cycles, bicycles, walkers & rental cars in single lane. Terrible visit.

If you want to enjoy around two hours walking without difficulties in the middle of an amazing and dense  forest I highly recommend you to visit Bijarim. Considering the time needed for these trees (nutmeg yew, family of the Taxus) to grow and the fact that normally you can only find it as bushes into other species's forest this place is a unique jewel with many of the trees aging more that 500 or indeed 800 years. Beautiful and relaxing experience that I will keep forever in my memories as a lover of trees that I am.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Had an awesome day here last week, awesome place for walking and photography. It was so nice to get out of the city and see some of the countryside. I think this is one of the most rugged areas, my kinda style of image. I dropped business for a few days to come here and it was worth it. If you have the change, like hiking or are a photographer. Go!

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

careful of when walking in the cave, very uneven and wet grounds. The cave is very far from the city, the public bus does not go direct and takes 45min with many stops in between. When arriving at the destination, its about 2.4km walk to the entrance of the cave. If you are lucky to get a taxi when u alight from the bus, they will charge u 4000won to drive u to the cave entrance to purchase your ticket to the cave

Being adults and have been busy over the years, we truly enjoyed walking 'lost' in the maze.  We reached the place quite late and we were trying to get out of the maze asap.  Enjoyed the cool weather to search for the exit.  Managed to ring the bell just before closing time.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

Apart from walking 2.5km in the extreme summer heat from the bus stop outside (pls find alternative routes), the cave was unique and pretty interesting to see. Love the temperature inside to cool us down and be away from the heat too.

After visiting the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, we proceeded to head to the ferry terminal for Udo Island. We were surprised we couldn?t get a cab during winter. Hence, we ended up walking to the ferry terminal instead.Note you need to show your passport and fill up a boarding form in order to take the ferry, at 30 mins interval. We took the 1400hr ferry. A 2-way ferry ticket costs 8,500 won. Upon arriving the island, one has the option of renting an electric scooter, manual bicycle or take the bus. For us, we took the round island bus. Bus fare is 5,00 won, which you can hop in and out at any attraction stops.  We headed to Udo-bond Peak stop and hiked up. Unfortunately, it was drizzling the whole day. We spent about an hour before returning to the ferry terminal.I suggest you allocate an entire day for Udo island. If the weather is fine, it is worthwhile to stop by all the attractions, enjoy the beach and food there.

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

We enjoyed a pleasant walk up the steps to the temple at the top and wandering around the lower temple. Enjoyed a tasty hotdog lunch from the sweetest woman at cafe next door (sunny house) and a delicious peanut ice cream too. Great morning visit before walking down to the beach.

We decide to go up the mountain on foot. It was a long way but worth it. The scene from the this mountain top is unforgetable and undeniably great. We could have stayed here all day seeing the nature changed if the weather weren?t cold. Walking the way up was exhausting but the fresh air and the sights we saw at different heights really cooled us down.

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

It was low tide so the rocks were dry and there were lots of little pools.  It was fun to see little kids playing in the pool water for hours.  We were just there for a little time. Our teenagers had fun walking on top of the lava rocks along the beach.  Careful not to step on crabs. Beautiful serene beach.

A popular tourist stop on Jeju Island. A lot of uphill walking is required and would be a problem for elderly folks or those with bad knees. However this is a really lovely location for scenic photos. The old ladies who dive for octupus and shellfish is a must visit as well though be aware of the very steep stairs up and downwards.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

We, a group of friends had visited this place last week. It was awesome! The journey to get there, parking and the walk up and back were all good. There is ample parking space and plenty of eateries that offers various types of snacks and cold drinks.The area is impeccably clean and the walking path was clear and safe. The steps may seem a little steep at certain points, but you will be well rewarded once you reach the top. The crater is a beautiful sight! Not surprising that it's the iconic image of Jeju which appears on Google. You need about an hour or so for the entire visit.

We visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on two separate days - the first was in the afternoon to see the women free-divers' performance (1pm/3pm) and the second was in the wee hours of the morning (5+am) to see the sunrise. The free-divers were all middle-aged women who looked old enough to be our mothers. Despite their age, it was amazing how they managed to hold their breath so long underwater to harvest the seafood which you could buy from them and eat on the spot (they'll prepare/cook it in whichever way you want). The way they sang prior to the dive and the way they chatted and swam out to sea together reminded us of the friendly grannies in our neighborhood enjoying a nice chit-chat over tea. To see the sunrise at the peak, we started our climb at 4+am (it helps to stay in a hotel within walking distance to Ilchulbong). It was pitch-dark and torchlight was a must. The climb was shorter than expected and we reached the top before 5am. Thankfully the sky was clear that morning and we managed to catch a beautiful sunrise (around 5:30am) that was nothing short of amazing.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We stopped off here after lunch and easily spent 3 hours walking the grounds.  And that was at a fairly quick pace.  The garden has 8 separate sections that provide a contrast.  The garden is very well kept.  So if you are into shrubbery, its not a bad place to spend a few hours

We spent more than an hour walking to and back from the beach. The place can get crowded and you can walk farther too but we stopped because of the huge waves. Nice photo location!The stairs can get quite challenging for older folks because it's uneven and slippery even, so have to be careful. There is also some distance of walking from the car park.

We need to rent a car (邕竊to get there. The driver said walking up there requiring 30 min, yet is quite easy to arrive the top. After reaching the top, you could enjoy the sunset of the seongsan city which is worth it !

We hiked up Hallasan the first weekend in March 2012.  We brought coats, hats, gloves and scarfs, however we were not prepared for the amount of snow on the mountain.  Check the conditions ahead of time and be sure to bring walking sticks and spikes for your boots.  My family hiked for awhile but stopped about 1km from the top after we were in more than two feet of snow and freezing.

Udo is an island very close from Jeju-do. It's next to Seongsan-ilchul-bong, which is also famous. It takes about 15 minutes by boat from Seongsan port. You pay for entrance to the island with the boat fare. The usual course seems to be walking up the hill in Udo, Gummerlae, and checking out the lighthouse surrounded by lots of stones stacked on top of each other for wishes to come true. The weather was perfect when we went, very sunny :)

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The cave is very dimly lit. The floor was very uneven (we are not blaming.. it's the natural formation of the lava) and slippery. I could only look down to make sure that I am walking safely and properly. I had no time to stop and look up and admire the caves. The cave is also very dimly lit, which makes the walk more challenging. We decided to turn back after 20 mins.

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Seongsan Ilchulbong is the best location on the Eastern part of Jeju Island. It is definitely an awesome place. It might however best be enjoyed not from the top of the volcano itself, but by walking or driving around (or flying?). The reason is that when you get to the top of the volcano, the caldera isn't as impressive as the one on top of Hallasan mountain. I did visit it during the day, and I get that it's more stunning at sunrise. It's still very nice. What's also great to see, if you climb the volcano, is to look back, and look at Udo island or the heart of Jeju island, with the villages and Hallasan in the background. Definitely a must-do in Jeju.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. Toilets are unfortunately not clean, so you may want to bring some disinfectant lotion and/or toilet paper.The first part of the hike is easily accessible, the latter part less so. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!

My son live and work teaching English  in Jeju , I spent 10 days with him in his apartment and this trip to  Seogwipo and the hike will always be in my heart.  We stayed in nearby hotel and woke up 4am started walking and climbing the steps to see the sunrise on the top and its all worth it .. Indeed Jeju has teh rightful name - the island of the Gods.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

it is very easy and friendly track to reach the peak, but for me the beautiful things about Seongsan Illchulbong are scenery from everywhere. so, I made a little tour by walking by from beaches till Saepjikoji and to Udo island. Never get missed from sunrise to sunset, everything is beautiful. is not wrong to choose stay near the Hills, Goseong-ri is perfect village to stay.But, if you just a few time to visit is good to stopping by. My wife loves here in spring time, lots of canola and pretty flower in the green green grass.You will found starbucks, convenience market, and lots of food.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

Hotel was right across this market so I stopped here on my first night for dinner. I was amazed by the selection of street food stalls, fresh produce and desserts. Most of the signs were in Korean but just follow the crowd and where there's a long line you'll never go wrong! I got a taste of the rice with fried black pork plus some fried octopus in batter, which were both great. Bought some boxes of cheap chocolate as well. Areas of the market selling fresh fish and vegetables are wet though so beware when walking through.

Great for kids and any others that like train ride.You will be taking a small train ride through beautiful natural forests. Some walking is require in between stations, but just have fun and enjoy what nature brings. Take pictures of mini lake... the water is clear, windmills, grassy fields, pirate ship and not to miss the last stop with beautiful tulips.
