I don't think its a bad place.. just not to my liking i guess. If you have time and a good camera and a tripod, you might take some very nice photos there lol

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

The beach is nice, clean and not too crowded but a bit small. Many hotels and villas are located along this beach. Therefore, if you want to be stick on it, just take one hotel here, normally just 5 minutes walking. A good place to relax and have romantic time.

The beach is conveniently a walking distance from Halim Park across the street. Pretty good size and a very shallow beach, good for children to play. It's kind of too crowded for me and the rent for the beach umbrella is somewhat expensive KW25,000. We did not spent too much time there.

So I read some idiot blog somewhere that said this place was apparently fun. What an idiot. NO. JUST NO.A bloody waste of 9000won is what this place is. It's extremely rundown. Smells like cat pee EVERYWHERE, especially all over the 1st floor. All the   studio sets   are not well maintained and look old and disgusting. What's worse... the moment you walk in, there's a set with a noose & wooden chair... IF you notice my photo, the tiles there are broken and the set is elevated.. imagine walking towards the noose only to have your feet sink into the the set, aka feeling like you're falling through the tiles. They have free clothes and hanbok for you to try and pose in. BUT... like everything else in this place... it's old and... i dont even know when any of the clothes were last washed. Remember, the whole place smells like cat pee. It's 2 floors of rundown studio sets... they even have signs saying   please leave your shoes on  .IF you're looking to waste time and 9000won/person, go ahead. Visit this place. Just remember my voice saying   I told you so   when you walk into a cat pee smelling rundown area of studio sets and leave disappointed.

Second time here with another friend. More time this round to walk leisurely.As said in the title, no wow, OMG thing inside you'll find unless probably you are an geologist, etc. The most memorable is probably the experience of walking on very uneven, ripply hardened lava ground spotted with many puddles in near total darkness through low and tall ceiling of an underground tunnel.

My 6 year-old girl loves this place sooo much. We enjoyed walking around & taking photos of all the cute things. Too bad, we didn't have enough time for the activities like glass painting, glass blowing. (We spent around 30 mins walking around the place.)
Its quite a good time for walking in the lava tube. There are several announcement, so you can read and understand whats that.Its quite slippery, just be careful or hold ur friends hand (better).
It's a beautiful park to stroll around in the spring time (that's when I visitors Jeju) and given the good weather condition, walking around is just refreshing and calming. A must visit place

It was felt like exercising when walking down to the see the waterfall. But just about ten steps down the stairs, the scene reveal the hidden stunning waterfall. So beautiful.  A dozen shoots were never felt enough to capture its beauty. I would recommend to spend a sufficient time just to enjoy the scenery.Please take be careful when walking in between stones near and around  the waterfalls. They are so slippery, so chose a flat surface stones as you walk? or not at all. A friend had her camera and mobile phone slipped down into water when she struggled to stand still on a stone. I was slightly more fortunate to be able to keep those gadgets of mine dry?. but not my shoes. While the water was refreshing, but I do not think you would like getting your shoes wet, particularly when you have only a pair for the whole Jeju island exploration. A wet trousers could spoil your whole day trip around the island.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

Interesting facts about the formation of the lava tube. Malaysia has no such thing so i was definitely eager to learn more and to experience it. Walking into the lava tube really exciting as i step on to the solid harden lava ...beautiful formation of harden lava, adores the lava pattern ... careful stepping onto the path as it is uneven and can be challenging to some ... just take your time walking in. As i adores nature, i really enjoy exploring the lava tube...as you go deeper into the tube it gets warmer than the windy cool air outside of the tube. Enjoy it, a must.

In order to reach this beautiful waterfall one has to endure walking for few minutes. We went there on April, it was the start of the spring season, yet it was windy so it was cold. For me the fall is just average, may be because I have seen more beautiful falls from the other countries. However, this is worth the walk and time. We manage to have beautiful photos near the falls and in the park.

I love that this beach tends to to have many waves, and is located within walking distance of places to stay and eat. The water is warm and clear,and theres a fantastic BBQ place over the little bridge to the right of the beach. I've returned to this beach both times I've come to Jeju! The sand is fantastic!

I just don't get this place. The rock doesn't look like a dragon head.... does it?Maybe cos I went there on my own... but I just don't see the significance of this place. Why? It's a waste of time and effort. Not that it requires that much walking... But I'd conserve my energy and also my time on something other than this.So not worth the time and energy. To me, that is. Maybe there is more to this place... but I just don't see/get it.

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.
Have your passport  and money for the Udo Ship ticket and you will take your glorious  time  on the Beach, in the cafes, just walking or riding around

Dragon Head Rock (Yongdu-am) is worth a look just to say   been there, done that  !It's nothing fantastic but does live up to its name.As it is within walking distance of downtown make the effort if you have the time.Tour groups, especially in the morning, arrive by the coach load. So walking makes good sense!

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

A cave system that can get in easily just by walking down the step.according to the tour guide, this special cave is cold during summer and warm during winter. By the time i go is summer, it is real chill inside the cave

World heritage Site. 13km long lava tube under Jeju Island. Formed by successive eruptions. The section that can be visited is about 1km long - first descending down two levels into the lava tube where the roof has collapsed and then walking up the tube under the mountain and ending at a lava pillar where the lave cascaded down from a parallel tube running above.  There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.

Walk around the mountain and you can see different rock formations.  The water is very clear (look at the picture as if there is no water) that you can see sea urchins. I advise you wear rubber shoes to be more comfortable walking through sharp rock formations.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. But dont be under the impression that it will be hot in there. It is very cold inside and be prepared with the winter clothing and a trekking shoes. It was a long walk and a nice experiences. A must visit cave.

This is a very nice stretch of beach easily accessible via several staircases from the main road or the Olle walking path located among the cliffs above the beach. This is perhaps the closest beach that you can leisurely walk to from any of the hotels in the Jungmun resort area. This is not a black sand beach but it makes up for it with the wide and clean beach and the great surf. There?셲 a direct staircase to the beach from the Hyatt regency back garden.

My wife was bowled over when she saw the poster of the actress in the famous Korean drama - Jewel In The Palace.  Walking through the grounds we were told that the drama was filmed on site and visited the villages and houses.  It brought back nostalgic memories of the show capping the highlight visiting the exhibits.  But if you are not a fan of the drama the village is still a good place to visit to get a good idea of the traditional Korean homes during the Joseon era.

We were tired in the carpark and considered sleeping but decided to go in. So glad we did, walking through the garden was a deep feeling of peace and felt refreshed. Would definitely come back. A must do in Jeju Island!

Walking 2km (to the end of the section open to the public, and back) in a lava tube is a cold, dark and wet affair, but it's a unique and educational experience. The floor is very uneven and there are many puddles to step around. There's not a whole lot to see, but every now and then, features of a lava tube are highlighted and explained. This is not for everyone but if you can appreciate that it's rare to get the chance to walk through a lava tube, go for it. Just be ready for the slightly challenging conditions

Visited Manjaggul Cave because it was a UNESCO Natural site, like Seongsan Ichulbong.  Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

This place is an epitome of beauty, beautiful rock formation, beautiful sea, beautiful waves, beautiful clouds, it is amazingly beautiful. Here you enjoy both worlds of rock formation and beautiful sea. Definitely this place is super windy and you might get wet with huge waves hitting against the rock formation. The scenery of the place couple with the beautiful sound of waves for me makes any visit to Jeju complete. Be careful in walking and exploring place, there are areas that are slippery and rough.  If you are an instagram addict this place is the best for you. You can choose to have those lovely rock formation as background or the beautiful blue sea with the huge waves and or both the lovely rock formation and waves.

It's actually just one short stretch of the road but interesting. The road gives you an impression that its going up hill instead it's actually going down the hill. The surrounding including the plants, trees, field and fencing are giving you that up hill impression. So when you switch off the vehicle engine that you are in, the vehicle will continue to move forward. Same goes to the test where they will show you by rolling a water bottle. Try walking backward and you can feel it. You might feel a bit disappointed as there is nothing else over there

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

If you love nature, this is a place you should visit. Nothing much to do , basically just walking and taking photos. But I personally love it ,because you can't find such a relaxing place back in a big city. It's good to visit during colder days.

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

We visited in the peak of winter so there was very heavy snow fall.We came quiet under prepared in terms of walking gear so the walk to the crater was pretty difficult. I wouldn't recommend for elderly or anyone with mobility issues but this is from my experience with snow so can't comment on the difficulty during other seasons.

We came on Feb... It's sunny and so windy there when we came... But it's a worth to come... A long walking to the peak but got a great scenery when we arrived at the peak... Go down the cliff throught the stairs and you can see many Haenyeo selling abalones and they also can cook it for you after you pay it... Don't forget to bargain it... But you must speak in Korean because they cannot speak English lor... Hohohoh...

If u do not object natural scenicThis place is the most value for money u must visit. Entrance fee is only 2000w for adults . easy walking path for child.the only deficit is the tour guide can only speak in korean. The most amazing wonder is the entrance fee includes a 25 minutes well filemed 4D movie

We sought out Saryeoni Forest thinking it would be a great place to escape the July heat.  We visited the section with nicely laid out boardwalks which was great for taking our baby on a stroller.  The scenery was picturesque and even during peak season, it didn?t feel crowded as the forest area is vast.  However, the humidity level was significantly higher as it felt like we were walking around wearing a plastic raincoat.

I went to Udo with a group of friends. It was really nice, we went around the island with rented bicycles (10.000 KRW for the afternoon). We swam in an incredibly clear water.I recommend going to Sunrise peak afterwards, walking along the coast gets you there in 15 min and seeing the sunset was an amazing experience.

clean sand, perfectly sloping beach, with sandbars at a convenient distance to provide interest -- it's not a beach for ocean swimming, but for relaxing and walking and building sand castles.  It is a relatively small area, though, so it might be crowded in peak periods.

There is a lot of food at this market. From snacks to proper meal. You can buy fresh fruits and souvenirs at this market too. The market is 5 mins walking distance from Artstay hotel. Sashimi is also available at this market.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

We enjoyed walking through the colorful Dongmun Jeju market but the prices were very high, especially when they see Westerners, Chinese or Japanese. We later spoke to our hotel and they said the price is almost doubled for foreigners. We had a simple raw seafood dinner for four and it costs each person USD$44.00. We had no liquor (beer, wine, etc). So enjoy the colorful scenery but if you want to eat there be ready to pay a high price.
walking in the local dongmun market, I was impressed with a lots of fresh fish shops. I can observe how local people work and enjoy their normal life.Seafood is fresh and at reasonable price!

This is a very big market with lots of local foods you can try while walking around. Prices are very reasonable too, and the people friendly and helpful, no pressure sales at all. Best market we've been to whilst travelling!

Our FIRST meal in JEJU and we were just spoilt for choices. This is traditional market and we had so much fun walking in the market.The large boxes of tangerines greets you at the entrance and as you explore further, you see endless rows of fresh seafood. We randomly selected some food and they tasted delicious!

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

Nothing that fantastic unless you are the one driving. The road is also only approximately 150metres long. Difficult to feel the gravity on human body/walking. Test using a vehicle or can/bottle/water poured on the road. The better deviation is Black pork stall manned by samurai-looking chefs. Mouth-watering black pork BBQ. Nice ice ball dessert nearby as well.

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.
It's a memorable sight as it is the only waterfall in Asia that flows directly to the sea. Just be extra careful when walking down the wet steps.

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Make sure you carry rain coat or umbrella and have some warm clothese if you are not used to cold. The caves  has water dripping at place and its very cold even during the hot sun outside. We went there after noon and it was quite cold. Be careful while walking inside the cave and its slippery. Do read the story as you go through its. there is restaurant which server good korean food just outside the entrance which we felt was very good.

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction. We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water. Walking through the cave was thrilling and filled with excitement. Round trip to and fro the cave took us about 1hr30mins. Would highly recomend to anyone visiting Jeju Island. Proper shoes are also recommended as it can be very slippery and slip and fall may happen. Kids and Older people may find this attraction tough and difficult to walk through.
Worth seeing, and I liked that it was within walking distance of our hotel. The beach area was really pretty although it is not a place to go if you want a beach and not a waterfall.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.
The natural waterfall in the raw form and walking in the rocks is fun. The surprise was a fresh Jeju orange juice nearby, the seller was honest and nice.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

One of the real highlights for my visit to Jeju Island. It's absolutely fascinating and I've been to a few different caves before. It's different because it's a lava tube cave and there are a few different information boards in there to explain the different features which helped to understand how it was formed. It's very well and cold in there so bring a wet jacket and comfortable walking shoes (waterproof/ resistant if possible) with good traction. There is a small descent but other than that it's rather flat in there so most people should be able to do it, just watch out for the wet surface. If you go to Jeju, you must visit this cave.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.
need to be careful walking on the rocks, the water is very clean n clear, a lot of tourist here so have to be 'skillful' to take photos and move about on the rocks.

Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest, walking through these wood is believed to enhance cardiovascular function and to prevent asthma and tuberculosis. This is the most famous forest on Jeju island and here you can taste mineral water that is thought to relieve muscle and gastrointestinal problem

It's just a road, but if you want to make it interesting, do some experiment on it. Get out of your vehicle, and try walking down/up the road. Or test the road by pouring water/ walk inversely. We enjoyed it!

Impressive sight withthewaterfall ending directly into the sea, walking down to the foot of the waterfall can be challenging with the rocks formation and without proper path, so don't wear heels!!!If you want to get near to the waterfall, be prepare for a shower of blessings
I went to Manjang Cave. It  was really good place to see. It was very cold when we got in side and we can see you cave of Volcano, while you are walking the water drop down and very lively..

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

Come prepared and you'll love it, good walking boots and waterproof jacket. If you find it too cold or dump you can go in for a few metres, and go outside, but we kept going wanting to see what is at the end, and it was spectacular, with huge lava column in blue dim light.

Clearly, going in early spring is not the best idea; water's still too cold for swimming but it was perfect to go walking barefoot in the fantastically clear water. It was pleasant to walk into random warm currents while chasing after fish in the shallow water. Our driver said it was the best beach on Jeju but he said that about Hallim Park too so I would not take his word for it.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

A unique must-do in my books to go where lava has gone before.   It is also a cave, so it dark, a little chilly with the occasional water drop.  The cave is left largely in its raw form (which was great) but it also meant an uneven and potholed path which requires a great deal of care walking it.

We did the yeongsil walk and it was amazing. It was tough in parts of you are not used to hiking but walking all the kids and grandparents doing it lends you the stamina to keep going and gosh is it worth it. Some of the best scenery I have ever seen.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. Unfortunately  I cannot say that this place is worth visiting. Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Walking on the Olle is nice--a great pilgrimage for healing. If you really want to know about the unique history of Jeju and the Korean Peninsula however you must visit this museum. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The highlight of this museum is its peace garden. This huge garden made me pray for peace in the Korean peninsula.

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.
Must visit.  Remember to bring a light jacket with comfort and non slip shoes.  It is about 40 mins walking, but worth it.

Manjang cave in overall was really nice expierence, but we got a bit cold.When outside is more than 30 degrees, and you go downstairs, it's a bit...cool.And wet as well.But I won't whine about it, because the expierence you get there is more important!We were walking really slowly taking pictures of everything (if you don't have a good camera, pictures won't bet any good ://)They have diferent color lights and it makes cave more visitor-friendly.Only thing is that there is really crowded...Even though we went there on a weekday.So be prepared to see a lot of people there as well.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.
It's where the locals go to shop. Fun walking around seeing what is being offered and mingling with the locals. I never realized there were so many varieties of the Korean classic, Kimchi.

Its definitely a worthwhile trip to make and just walking through the Lava Tube is quite an experience.  It is not everyday one has the opportunity to walk through and see the various formations, the caves formed, columns, the different textures formed, etc.One needs to be relatively fit to do the walk with comfortable shoes as the location tends to be wet. Elderly should have a walking stick which will help and carry a torchlight.  Its a few degrees lower underground.
its better to discover the place in summer, but enjoyed the cold and excitement, walking around feels better

It's a natural wonder.  Amazing how lava can create a tunnel as large as this. Must visit when in Jeju.  Wear a pair of walking shoes and an autumn jacket as temperature falls to around 15 inside the tube. It'll take you at least 30 minutes to walk 1km in and then another 30 minutes out.  So,  it's pretty chilly if you are without a jacket. Floor is wet therefore walk carefully & enjoy the unusual sights especially the walls & ceiling of the tube. Walk until the end as there's a lava column in there, the only one.
It?s like a Learning journey, pretty cold 8 degree) and dark in the cave.Just need to follow the pavement and keep walking to the end of the cave.
It will be a good place to visit for educational purposes. Nice to be walking in a lava tube. Not a must go attraction but if you have children, it will be good to bring them there.

It was raining when we reached the place. From the parking area, you will see this beautiful crater. As we are slowly walking up the slope, the wind was too strong for us to walk further up.Decided not to go up, but must had to take a few photographs of this beautiful place with the wind, rain and waves.On Normal day, there is also diving show by the famous Sea Women - Haenyeo. Mostly are 50 and above who dive for a living.Try to plan the visit during normal weather.

It was around a 20 minute walk into the cave and another 20 minutes going out... Path was dark and wet, so you must be careful walking inside the cave... It was a good experience with a little workout.

It was an interesting experience to walk through the 1km long tunnel if you enjoy understanding and seeing the various structures and rock formations formed from the lava flow. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!

It is really long cave. Pls wear sensible shoes and high heels are NO NO there.I think it is nice for the first 15 min but after 15min it all looks the same. So unless you really knows you rocks well, or else it will be just a walking trip

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

I'm from Hawaii, but this cave was very impressive, not to mention a welcome reprieve from the heat and humidity!Walking on wet lava rock is not for the faint-of-heart, so wear a good pair of tennis shoes that can provide some traction, because it is slippery!

If you love nature and have never seen any volcanic formation before, it would be worth the visit. Personally,  i enjoyed walking inside the cave and having a look at the volcanic formation.  It's like you can almost imagine how the lava flowed inside the tunnel a few thousand years ago :) i was in awe of how powerful mother nature can be. It was quite cold inside. Wear layers and proper shoes.  Can be quite slippery as well.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

I was staying at the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun and decided to go for an out door walk to enjoy the beautiful weather. I was walking along the coastline and it eventually lead me to this attraction. Although it is wonderful to see these unique rock formation, this attraction is rather small.

I was excited to see the Manjanggul Lava Tubes up close and personal, but I was rather disappointed after my visit..The Caves were poorly lit and without using a flashlight, one can barely see the markings on the rocks. The ground is very uneven and understandably so. However, for older people, children and people prone to ankle injuries, the lighting does not allow one to see where one is walking and injury can can easily occur.
I tried walking and rolling in car to feel the effects of such claims... no luck, felt cheated... at least the kids had fun.

I think it really depends on what kind of traveler u are. Some people might find it boring, some people might find it cool. I love it. I've never been in a cave nor a lava tunnel so for me it was a new and exciting experience. The cave is huge, wet and super duper cold, colder than outside in fact and lit up enough to see where you're walking. It's nice to see and feel how hardened lava looks and feels like. Walking into Manjanggul's huge cave feels like a scene from Prometheus.. Awesome!

I find walking in this lava cave is interesting as it is so cool inside and surprisingly there is no bad smell as it is rather wet. The cave produces it's on air conditioning as the temperature inside is around 15-17 Celsius. Some areas are well lighted and some are not, proper walking shoes are needed as there are many uneven areas along the path provided. Good experience for the ones who loves outdoor!

I bought a ticket which included access to all 3 museum buildings for 16 000 won. The museums are within walking distance of one another. A map as well as an audio guide is available. The   abandoned   buildings gave it an eerie feel that I thoroughly enjoyed. I was surprised around every corner and turn - the whole experience felt very dreamlike. I loved it.

I am really amazed and really love walking inside the forest you will feel delighted very clean and green trees, smells good and you can relax and breath well. Bijarim Forest-Is a group of about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old. They are 7-14m in height and 50-110cm in diameter. This is the largest nutmeg tree forest in the world. In the middle of the forest is an 800-year-old tree, called ?Ancestor tree of the Bija trees.

Hmm... Where to start?Well, Jeju Island, being volcanic in nature, must really have places like this!Honestly saying, it wasn't something so jaw-dropping and spectacular!Just more like a place with rock formations due to the cooling of lava!The trek inside isn't hard and what I really liked was that it was chilly while we did it!It was a nice sidetrip nonetheless if you like walking and if you like all these geo stuff!If you're in Jeju, maybe you can give it a try

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.

Had a mixture of nice gardens, some birds and lava caves. When I entered and started walking, it did not sem like much, but then impressed me as I went on. So enjoyed it quite a bit, was a good pleasant walk. Worthwhile if you go to Jeju.
Great place to enjoy walking and see different species of plants, trees, we enjoy palms, something special, very quiet place
Great beach for walking, swimming and relaxing. Volleyball tournament there once a year :) Many great places to eat and stay in the area.

for me there is nothing special about this cave. the only thing we can do is just walking straight through the cave almost 1km (cmiww). and after we arrive to the end of the tunnel , we just see a small stage and some pic as i remembered. if you traveling with child , pls be carefull when you step the floor. because its really slipper..
Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.Lots of walking.Will definitely revisit, loved it loved it loved it.Visited in Summer of 2015

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) I visited there for watching Teddy's parody, because I've visited Teddy museum in Sokcho formerly. According to my expectation, there was funny Teddy doll describing person, event and fairy tale. Walking through the flow, I smile at funny doll. Good to visit once, but I will not visit one more becasue of high price and unchanged exhibits.

Beautiful authentic cave that gives you an idea about the magma power. I visited with my dad, but teenagers, couples with small children and elders. There are stairs and very variable ground so it is not recommendable for those who have trouble walking.
Awesome! 2 km total by walking, cold place inside, we are so amazed by how the nature creates it. When you come in rainy season please be careful with your steps. Not recomended for the elder.

As there are not much railings inside the cave to guide the tourists while walking and steps are uneven, make sure to wear comfortable walking shoes. It is beautiful and a must visit when in Jeju. I joined a tour for this visit as it is quite far from where I stayed. Tourist spots in Jeju are not close to each other and I didnt quite see a lot of public transport the in the area.

An amazing cave; one of nature's wonder!  Must wear a good pair of walking shoes, and be prepared to walk some distance. Enjoy the strange and mysterious dark tunnels. Dimly lit, but well kept with small platforms and bridges, this UNESCO heritage site is one selling point selling for Jeju! Worth paying a visit.

Amazing cave carved by molten lava moving underground with many interesting features, however, you need to be prepaired for dim lighting, uneven floor with many tripping hazards as well as uneven steps/stairs.  Not suitable for young children or older folks who have trouble with sight or walking.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.

A terrific site that is well maintained and well explained. Points of interest are marked in 3 languages including English. Come prepared with proper footwear. Tourists are walking on uneven flooring. Also this tunnel can be damp.  Photographing is not permitted, but plenty of visitors were using their cell phones.
1km in, 1km out... really amazing walking through world's largest lava column! We get to imagine we are the lava flowing through!!

Woke up early hoping to catch the sunrise. We stayed at a pension just 5 min walk from the entrance to Seongsan ilchulbong. It was a wonderful experience to climb in the darkness of the predawn hour. We were surprised to see so many people waiting the start the climb when we reached?? it was raining the night before so the ground was rather slippery. Thankfully the rain had stopped when we started the climb. According to a local there are 500 steps to the peak. It's  doable though it does require a good amount stamina / more time (we were pressed as we wanted to catch the sunrise). The route is easy to follow - steps all the way; there're toilets along the trail too. It was cloudy on the day we climbed so the sunrise wasn't as we'd hoped but still spectacular regardless. On the way down we took a short detour down a flight of steps to a lagoon-like region where the haenyeon dive for seafood. The view there is spectacular especially before the tide rises in the morning. There is a restaurant that sells seafood caught by the haenyeon that was very yummy  we actually took some really nice pictures there. Would return in a heartbeat just for the refreshing climb!!

We went in winter with 2 young kids (6 & 8) and it was easy going but cold. Lots of locals ply this route and it?s 5km to the witsoreoum rest area where you can transfer to other trails or have a nice pit stop. Trekking poles and good shoes would be a good idea. The scenery is marvelous with very nice panaromic vistas all round

We went here as per the recommendation on Tripadvisor. We wanted to go to Udo island and then come to see the sunset on this peak.since the ferry to Udo was cancelled due to rough sea and strong winds we had to change our plan and come to peak right in the afternoon.Since it was overcast and cloudy weather we could hike easily to the top. the 360 view from top is breathtaking.hiking trails is good. You can see the black sand beach and also see the jeju fishing lady show.

We finally got a good clear day.Yesterday at Sunrise Mountain we had been in the clouds.  Some nice views down the coast. Not a terrible tough or long hike to get to the end of the trail with a small temple cave. Number of mostly coffee shops at the bottom and bathroom facilities.

We climbed to the top of Mt.  Hallasan via the seongpanak trail. We are in just above average shape and we had no issues getting to the top with not stops in 2hrs 40 mins. There are three rest areas along the way that you can stop at if you need a good break. The last 1.5k to the top is the real shocker. We did not do our homework and went up real early on the morning and it was so windy and cold we did not stay long at the top. It was cloudy at the top anyway so we were not able to see 20 feet off the mountain so we headed back down. There is little to no people climbing the mountain at 6am but I'm out way down there was more people ascending to the top. Overall it was a good trip but I recommend bringing a windbreaker and not starting until around 7 on a clear day.

tried the forest healing program last month during my visit to jeju island. Guided by forest therapist we have completed forest healing trail. I can say it really helps me relax the body by focusing on natural noises flowing water  chirping mountain birds  fresh forest air and those Phytoncide!!! oh it just smells so nice >.< we got to try the foot bath and aromatherapy too. the therapist said they also have body bathing tub and aqua line  but since we dont have many time.. maybe next time. Good place to relax your mind and escape from hustle and bustle city. i will try another program if i have chance to visit it again.

Took the longest trail to Mount Hallasan peak (Seongpanak Trail) - 9.6 km - but started a bit late and did not make the cut-off time at the Jindalrae shelter (7km). However it was a great walk and I visited the Saraoream peak on a side tril on the way back.  This was well worth it as there is great view and also a beautiful crater lake.  It is key that you start early and take enough water with you.  Also need good shoes. Although it was August - most of the trail is in the forest - so not so hot.
This park has a trail  insect specimens  pig show  petting zoo and several activities such as horse riding and tangerine picking.It is a good excursion place for everybody especially for family.

There are 7 trails that you can climbs the mountainBut there are 2trails  only to reach to the top.Since i took 4courses i will explain where i visited that is also most people goTo SummitTrails : If you want to go to the top there are 2trails Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa  trail. Normally people go up by Seongpanak and go down by Gwaneumsa since Gwaneumsa is more difficult to go upTaking time : round trip takes 9 to 10hours so you better start your day early otherwise they will stop you to go up in some area Especially Jindalrea shelter will close at 1230pm or 1pm which can be vary depends on seasonAlso on your way to Jindalrea shelter there is another short trail Sara oreum which is really beautiful and takes only 40min. so it is YOU MUST VISIT place unless you are not hurry by time.How to get to : from Jeju bus terminal there is a bus that ofpen goes every 15min and takes 30min For beautiful viewTrail : Yeonsil trail and Eorimok Trail People normally go up by Eorimok and go down by Yeongsil but for me the opposit is betterTaking time : round trip takes 5hours and easy to walk if you like climbingHow to get to : there is only one time every hour so you better check in the termimalEorimok takes 35min from terminal and Yeonsil is 2stops more from EorimokPersonally i prefer Eorimok and Yeongsil trails.Also i highly recommend you to have climbing shoes otherwise your feet will be beaton up by rocks and enough waterall trail has shelters that sell food and drink but you better bring your own water Even it rains it is another feeling climbing mountain very attractive to go with lots of fogI never thought it is good to climbs when raining but i liked it a lotHowever prepare a nylon raincoat  from jeju bus terminal since it is very windy Poly raincoat would be ripped It is double price from the entranceThis is the best montain among i have visited in Korea

There are 3 tiers of the waterfall but we only opt to go for 2 of the tiers as the 3 tier is a long walk down the trail and path. And we know we will have a long walk up which we are not inclined to do. The 1st tier and 2nd tier is not far from each other and really have a lot of good photo taking points for memory keep sake. The path is well guided with sign board and easy to walk. The most well worth place is the bridge as the design and color is really unique.

Place is good and interesting but an averagely.Nothing too special. I've been there at the end of season (September) - so trail was closed and not possible to rent a kayaks as well.Maybe in summertime it a bit more interesting but not sure :)

just a well maintained hill track. More like a plantation than a forest though we spotted a deer. Crowded with people going in a hurry to complete a formality. No great scenes on this trail.of course we did upto Sara Oreum only. May be the other difficult trails must be having better sceneries. If you want to go to summit better start early say by 8 am since there is no permission beyond the upper shelter after 12 noon. Not good for someone with weak knees. Avoid on rainly or cloudy days.

Jeju stone park was not part of the regular sightseeing itineraries and do we opted for a customized private tour to visit Jeju stone park. Requires atleast 3 to 4 hours if you want to walk along the trails to cover entire area. A visit inside the museum to understand the volcanic activities and formations will help in understanding the nature of the island better. Good to go with a local guide. Interesting statues and rock formations

It's well preserved but not good for people with disability. Inside is quite dark and has uneven flooring. Nothing to complain as it is made by nature and they also provided some trail/even flooring to follow.

It is a remote the only time we used a taxi instead of a bus in a week ay Jejudo. Glad we visited.  We were visiting the island to hike the Olle Trails and climb Mt Halla so this was a side trip.  We picked it because it seemed the most interesting attraction built for tourists and we agreed it was a good choice.
It is 1 km trail one way and nothing much. The ground is uneven so a good footwear is essential and can be a bit cool.

If you like to visit beautiful scenery this should definitely be one of the places you go in Jeju. If you start near the beach it'll only take you a few minutes to see the best parts. If you're like me and you enjoy seeing a bit more you can walk for about 10-15 minutes along a boardwalk trail up the estuary. The trail (and river) are next to the road the whole time so it's a very easy walk. I'd probably recommend starting up the river a bit and walking to the beach that way the scenery gets nicer and nicer as you go.As for the kayaks I had no expectation of being able to go on one since the reviews all suggest you have to come early and wait for a long time. It was a pleasant surprise then that the kayaks were not operating. There were none to be seen anywhere. This was great because it meant there weren't too many people and the river looked serene with no one paddling around in it.If you're keen on doing the kayaks people have told me that they're stopped for good  and other people have told me that they're just stopped temporarily. I would recommend calling a tourist office or tour agency to find out the latest news.

I have spent years reading about WW2 history so it's a sobering experience to walk the same places as the men and women who fought and died in that conflict. Altteureu Airfield was a WW2 Japanese airbase that sits in a strategic corner of Jeju Island  midway between China and Japan. In the 1930s bombing missions were launched from here to Shanghai  later it was a training base. There are 19 remaining concrete hardened shelters sized for a Zero fighter and Jeju has done a good job with preserving the site (even though most of it is active farmland)  adding a large parking lot and bathroom  and placards to explain the history and locate the structures. It's right on the Olle trail so there are many hikers passing through and it's easy to find from the shore road by car.

I go here every day to walk up the steep hill to the right of the beach for exercise.  It's the start of the No. 19 Olle Trail.  I usually always see bride and grooms having their photos taken on the beach and in the fields of rapeseed.  Views from the top of the hill are amazing.  Sometimes if there are horses around I'll pick grass and feed them in exchange for a little pat and nuzzle from them.  If you look carefully there are quite a few different flowers around.  If you pick a green rapeseed that hasn't yet flowered and peel the stalk you can eat the stalk.  It tastes like sweet brocalli.  The cherry blossoms are lovely there too if you happen to be there in early April.  The water is clear.  I like to feed and water some of the stray dogs.  It kills me that I can't give them a home.  They appreciate a bit of a cuddle too but you can see their priority is getting food.  There are some very good restaurants in Hamdeok as well.  Ive put a pic of one of the ones on the main street of Hamdeok. .its a local one that serves a set menu at lunch time and its very good.  The sunsets are spectacular.

Good scenery location for photo taking & trail walk. Area are clean and windy. They are free parking area that i just realized after finished my activity here and my rent car parked in the paying area! Paid 2000 won to old man already waiting next to my car as i went to toilet.

Good place to visit for experiencing the lava tube. But.... Pease please please prepare a good walking shoes if you were to visit this place. You'll need to walk on rough and uneven surface and the trail is pretty long. Not recommend to bring kids and elderly to visit this attraction.

Good for a walk at day or night time. At night look out for the hundreds of fishermen along the shore with multicoloured lights of their fishing floats. Stop at one of the numerous cafes along the trail

First obtain the Olle walking trails book from tourist information counter near the central bus station. From there you can ask for recommendations. I chose the scenic routes and it required walking up slopes which allowed paranomic view of scenery and also along the coastal area which was slippery due to rain. Some routes bring you directly to the beach whereby you can enjoy Jeju famous mandarin oranges and buy souvenirs such as their honeyed tea and famous chocolates! Do ask for discount like for all tourist attractions and at times the lady boss will throw in more pieces of the chocolate.You can also take partial route but check for the correct bus and you need to check which stop to alight. Unfortunately despite being a popular tourism attraction bus drivers can't communicate in English. Good luck if you encounter locals who can speak English.
Beautiful and serene forest trails . Very good view but the walk up is not easy especially in a rainy day
Another must see place in Jeju . Easy access from Seogwipo city. Olle trail around this avea is good to explore. This can be the most scenic place for sunset.
Another good place to visit in Jeju. Easy access from Seagwipo. Easy access from Seogwipo. Can go through the Olle trail and see this waterfall. No tickets required.
a beautiful location for a good view and some interesting plantlife. also a trail where one can go hiking.

Wow. Just wow. We're beginners climbing up Seongpanak trail (longest trail, 9.6km). I thought I was never going to make it! But the people going down were very encouraging. Try to go early, as the carpark will be full by 9. Entrance is free, but you have to pay for the parking. Take note - you gotta reach the peak by 1.30. They'll start chasing people down by then, because you don't want to get stuck up there in the dark (trek takes approximately 4.5 hours one way) Oh, the weather was really good; it was sunny and not a cloud to be seen. It gets pretty hot up there so wear sunscreen. The lake was quite dry though.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We went with our boys for a short hiking. Jeomul Oreum trail is shady and only takes 45min. There are few junctions at the top of the trail which might be confusing. The maps say one big round trail, ultimately it is the same way up and down. If you took the wrong trail, it will lead to 5km trail. Overall good and short trail for the kids.

We want to cover a few attractions in one day, thus, we chosen the shorter route up a part of Mount Hallasan (can't recall the name if the trail). Glad, we made the right choice, 1.3km up to 1,163m in about 45min, not really scenic until you reach the top. The trail is very well laid, easy to walk, good for beginners and not so fit. Up, enjoy the view, photo taking and down, all done in <2.5 hours.

We walked up the Gwanmeusan Trail, only 20 minutes from downtown Jeju-si. It took us, going slowly with lots of rests about 9.5 hours. Good hiking shoes required. We witnessed multiple shoe failures. You have to hike back down shoeless if your shoes rip apart and they will due to the volcanic rocks used on the rrail. The rocks are cute until they aren't. They are murder on the feet, ankles, knees, and legs on the way down.We went in April 20 and it was warm... only one water stop about 3/4 way up.18+ miles round trip. Please ask questions if you have concerns. It is quite breathtaking but a strenuous hike. Many turn back early. Must make it to the Samgakbong shelter by 12:30. No support on the trail.... 2 bathrooms though about 1/4 and 3/4 way up. Must start return hike by 2PM... still took us 4 hours to down due to strenuous terrain and infinite number of stairs.

We walked the Eorimok Trail and it is a well maintained trail with signage all along the way that keeps you informed about how far you have gone, how far you have to go and categorizes the slope into three levels of difficulty (red=steep; yellow=moderate slope; green=gentle slope). It took us 2 hours to get to the tea house (Nambyrok Junction) from the parking lot at the base.  Even though we didn't go to the summit, there are beautiful views all along the trail. While this isn't a mountain climbers kind of trail, it is the tallest mountain in South Korea. My legs were sore for a week afterwards and I am in good shape. Be advised:  About 2/3s of the trail has big trees and good shade; there is no water along the trail; there are emergency phones every several hundred meters; and there is a single track 5-10m off the trail that looks like it would be used for emergency evacuation.

We visited the National Park as well as Mt. Hallasan during our trip to Jeju-do. It is a beautiful park with average to good hiking trails. We took the long trail (Seongpanak, 9,6km) up to the summit, which took us 2,5 hours (i will take you much longer if you hike slowly and take breaks!). The view from the Summit was just stunning! Definately worth it! I'd advise anybody hiking this trail to wear boots or other firm shoes since the trail is very steep and rock at some parts. You also have to start early in the morning (~8am) since you have to reachthe second station until 1pm to be allowed to go to the summit. Geaneumsa trail is currently closed!

We visited Jeju only for Hallasan mountain! There are two ways on top, one easier and one harder! We took the easier to get on top and the harder to get back down! Once on top you will have a beautiful view over the national park and the island! Take some good shoes with you if you want to take the harder trail! The park is easy to reach by bus

We travelled from Seogwipo by bus to Jungmun Elementary school.  Thereafter, we were supposed to hop on another bus to the stop nearest to the entrance of Yeongsil Trail.  However, we did not read the bus schedule careful enough to notice the change in the schedule during winter.  The bus starts later and ends earlier during winter.  We ended sharing a cab with the other 2 tourists who happened to be there earlier than us and were heading to the same destination.  The guy who mended the convenient store near the bus stop was so nice that he helped us to call the taxi.   It was a blessing in disguise since the taxi actually sent us right to the door step of the Yeongsil Trail entrance in which otherwise, we would have to walk up for about 2 km to the starting point of the trail.  Should you travel with baggage, the park office (which I guess so) can keep them for you.  I?m not sure of the storage capacity or if lockers are available, or this is just an additional service provided for those who happen to travel there with their baggage.It took us slightly more than 3 hours to hike up to Witsoreum Shelter since we?re quite slow and took plenty of photos.  The Koreans took 2 hours only.  The wind was very strong, so do take care of your scarf or anything which is light.  Witsoreum Shelter is where you can opt to go back down with the same trail or by another trail, Eurimok Trail.  However, the other trail was closed on that day.There?s a canteen and restrooms at Witsoreum Shelter.  The canteen sells instant noodle and simple snacks.  After eating and disposing the residue of the noodle, you have to bring the trash back for disposal.  Plastic bag for keeping your trash is provided but I find it rather thin.  However, we brought some plastic bag along with us for this purpose as well since we had some snacks while hiking up.The fog was building up when we left at about 1:10 am.  It took us about an hour and 40 minutes to descend.  Overall, this was a good experience.  We were just on time to catch the last bus back to Jungmun Elementrary school (if I recall this destination correctly).

We took up this challenge in early April, just stepping into Spring. We took the bus from Jeju Express Bus Terminal, took about 40 minutes to reach the Eorimok bus stop. Before taking the bus though, we highly recommend to check with the Tourist Information Center just outside the bus terminal on the last returning bus. Thankfully we checked, the last bus in March period was 4.55pm at Eorimok. Summer periods probably have a later last bus back. This bus serves the Yeongsil trail entrance as well.There is still a ~20 mins walk along the road before reaching the entrance to the Eorimok trail. Impressive mountain views once you reach the park entrance.The Eorimok trail starts off deceptively tame for about 500m. Once you get the past the wooden bridge, the tough hike starts. For the next 2km, we experienced the toughest climb of the entire trail. Steep and large steps at times, with large, uneven rocks littering the way up. The view is mostly green at this point.Near the end of the first 2km, we started to see melting ice along the trail. Certain parts were still iced up; we had to climb on top of the ice to traverse. Due to the melt, it was quite slippery. A hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended, though we had not brought any for our trip.After 2km, the trail leveled off into a plateau, a welcome rest after a seemingly endless slog. Strong winds and rain pummeled us that day, but all the more made the challenging climb more exciting and enjoyable. The rest of the way to the Witse Oreum was of average difficulty, and the landscape was foggy and snowy/icy. We encountered many instances that we had to walk on the ice so be sure to be equipped with good shoes to reduce the chance of slipping on the ice.We finally reached the Witse Oreum after about 3 hours, and bought and slurped down the ramen and its soup, as well as a chocolate energy bar. They also carried stuff like crampons and plastic sheet raincoat (we bought it for the heat trapping characteristic rather than for shielding against rain, we foolishly did not expect snow and ice in April tbh :P).We originally wanted to go down via the Yeongsil trail which meets the Eorimok trail at the Witse Oreum, but a pair of local, seasoned hikers who turned back for Eorimok warned us that the Yeongsil trail is still mostly frozen over and is very difficult to traverse at this time. Due to the lack of proper equipment, we heeded their advice and went back down Eorimok instead.The trip down was much faster, but hurt our knees more due to the impact. Tread with care as the uneven terrain may cause slip and falls.The journey down took approximately an 1.5 hours.Overall it was really challenging but fun.Things to note:1. Take note of the last bus timing or you may have to hitch a ride back to town.2. And of course, cater buffer time to reach the bus stop, there is still a 20 min walk to it.3. Hiking gear, especially proper shoes and a hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended.4. Early April features unmelted snow in the terrain, wear proper clothing.5. The same bus goes to the Yeongsil trail, may want to try hiking that as well (on different days of course)6. The Eorimok is pretty challenging for a novice like myself, heard from locals that the Seongpanak trail on the Eastern side is more relaxing but longer.7.
