Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After nearly two years spent in Korea, I can quite easily say that Hallasan is the most beautiful place I've visited while here. Dramatic scenery, including sprawling vistas and interactive cloud-cover made this an exhilarating climb. Don't expect an easy journey! I took the   easiest   trail and it took us a good 5 hours to complete, and the hike up the mountain itself was via a crowded and steep staircase.The sheer variety of landscapes you experience as you climb up is really impressive. When you reach the mid-point, there's a rest stop where you can buy water, coffee and ramen noodles (oh, Korea!), but bring your own snacks because you'll probably be up there for a while.

A stunning view of the surrounding can be had on a clear day, but if the clouds are in then the view is not so good. A typical national park with beautiful surroundings to enjoy, trails, hikes and scenery. Not for the faint hearted and can be very tiring if fitness levels are an issue. Take plenty to drink and worth the climb once y ou get there!

A relatively easy hike going up Yeongsil trail (lots of climbing). Note that if you're taking the bus, you still need to do a pre-hike of 2.5km going up the mountain after you get off the bus stop. In my opinion, this was harder than the actual hike going up, but it was good preparation. There's also a cafe near the actual entrance. You can buy food here right before going up the trail.The cutoff time for Yeongsil trail is 2pm during the summer, but I would advise you to come early. The hike itself can be done in 1.5 hours, but with picture-taking, it can take as long as 3 hours (and the view at the top is gorgeous in many places!).Wear good hiking shoes. I've seen people wear regular sneakers (and even a guy with leather shoes -- what was he thinking?!), but I swear your feet will hurt if your shoe even manages to survive. Both Yeongsil and Eorimok trails have unpaved trails with unforgiving rocks. Hiking sticks would also help with the descent if you have weak knees.It's safe to hike solo (even for females) during popular days, so you're sure to hike with other people. It's also best to go down where most people are going if you started late (most people drive, so they go down the same trail they went up).In case of emergencies though, you can call their emergency number. (There's mobile coverage for most, if not all, of the trail). Take note of the location posts every few hundred meters. In case you get injured, there's this small train which can take you down, but you have to wait quite a while.

Wow... just wow. I certainly didn't expect that. Yakchunsa isn't considered one of the must-go in Jeju so I didn't expect all that much especially given that you have to take a small road to go there. But once I arrived I was in awe. The complex is big colorful and the main pagoda-like multi-floor temple is massive and beautiful. What's even better is that the inside is at least as good as the outside view. There are three floors each with its own atmosphere and ornaments (murals candlelights wooden structures...). Take some time to go outside towards the sea to get the full perspective of the temple complex.
Would not take up much time here as the viewing area is very limited and congested with travellers scouting the area to take a good spot & photo. Worth to visit.
Worth a quick stop but good luck trying to avoid others tourists interested in taking selfies and blocking the view!

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.
Who does not like teddy bears - bears everywhere; great views and of course - the essential shop! Good for children and families

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

When it is raining this is one of the place you should come you can just relax and have  some tea besides they sell variety of Tea which is very nice and good. They have a tester too where you can taste certain tea. There is a cafe too but mind you it's a long queing so I just skip it maybe because it is raining time so everyone go there. My favorite is the pack O'sullac Milk Tea it is so very nice. I should buy more of it. Next time will surely buy a lot of it.Besides the tea thing there is innisfree house beside it. you can make your own soap the organic cafe at the innisfree house is also nice too.So I recommmend you to come here whenever it is raining for indoor activity. even if it is not raining it is good for relaxing and enjoy the view of the tea trees.

What a beautiful walk.  The walk up is on one side of the hill and the walk down is on another so there are fantastic views to be enjoyed.  It took me a half hour to go up the 180 meters and I am in good shape.  Take water and sunscreen.
Well maintained and a good place to visit. View is phenomenal. There is some climbing to do so be prepared.
We were wondering near our hotel and found the falls it was a great way to spend afternoon.  Lots of stairs so wear good shoes...but every step is rewarded with a beautiful view ?

We were there in a bad timing when it was raining hard so we opted not to proceed for fear of slipping or whatnot but I have seen pretty good shots of the view from the peak. I heard the climb can be challenging too.

We visited on 23rd October. A misfortune happened at about 5.15pm when we were about to leave  our rented car could not start due to no battery. Our baby was temporarily locked in the car so a helpful bystander helped us to opened the door using manual lock and called the car rental company. After a long wait we gotten the staffs at the park to help.the 'gatekeepers' were friendly enough to let us stayed there while awaiting help to arrive. A thin tall lady staff without spectacles came to our help and called the car rental company as we could not understand the options given in Korean. She explained to us and reassured us in English fluently. She also took extra care to follow up and waited til a tow car to help to jump start the rented car. I think by that time her shift is over as few staffs waiting for her too. We are indeed thankful for her and the staffs on that day. Cocomong Ecopark does have a good commendable staff. thank you.Park wise games and design are well thought and worth the entry ticket. The slide down on tire is fun though it looked a bit scary but it is safe. Cafe has got a nice sea view.

We stopped by Wolijeongri Beach for about 30 min. on the way to UDO; the water was very clear.  There were kids playing sand on the beach. The view was peaceful. We enjoyed our short walk along the beach. You can get some snacks and a good coffee from a caf챕 or a convenient store nearby. There is a restroom facility too.

We made a wrong turn and found this place by chance.? Amazing view. The bridge connects you to bird Birds Island. It's 1.2km walking path. Best to visit before the Sunset and you will be blown away with the views around this area. A good place to stroll and relax.

We made a stop there for lunch as recommended by our B&B owner. There are now 2 coffee shops. We had lunch in the new one. The steamed bun with sausage was nice. The brunch set menu was a bit bland. The best thing in the brunch set is the homemade yoghurt with marmalade. We enjoyed the view while having lunch. Quite relaxing. More Korean day-trippers and foreigners. We had green tea ice cream from the old coffee shop afterwards. Really good green tea ice cream. Better than some that we had in Japan. If you want a quick lunch and want something non-local this is the place to go.

We hiked round the coastal route of the mountain in April and took an hour and a half to compete the hike which included stopping at various viewpoints to enjoy the beautiful coastal scenery and sunset.  Weather was good. We started at about 4pm and the place was peaceful with not many people.  We also flew a drone at one of the viewpoints.  The hiking path was well constructed and easy to walk.  You can also ride a horse there.

We drove to check this Estuary out and we werent disappointed at all.Love the scenic view especially when the Estuary meets the Ocean half way....u have to see it for yourself... Good place to chill and there are cafes to while some time away too...

We didn't bother with the museum itself. Not my thing.But the Sunday Brunch at the cafe is legendary.Smoothies come in cute glass jars with thick straws and are so full of chunks of fruit that you almost have to chew them as you drink.The brunch itself is a mix of odd elements that I wouldn't normally put together - but they work..... creamy butternut squash soup scrambled eggs mustard coated potato wedges plus a ham/cheese/vegetable panini with salad leaves and balsamic vinegar on the side. Really good food.We sat outside the weather was lovely. Great view of the tea field (part of the museum) and the road. If I come back to Jeju on a trip sometime I'll definitely return for Sunday brunch!

We didn?셳 spend much time here which was a pity but in any case there were too many tourists. Would be a better experience when less crowded. The buildings are stylish and there is a nice view of the tea gardens. You can try the tea and they explain the tea making process. The cafe looked good with desserts like green tea cake and ice cream but we didn?셳 try as the queue was too long. Nearby was the Innisfree building where many people were making handmade soap. There was also a cafe and exhibits of the different distilled essences of flowers and plants in Jeju.

We come here for the lighthouse where Korean drama Iris was filmed. The view is exceptional and didn't disappointed. One unexpected experience is we got to see the women divers. They caught bunch of sea urchins and see their male partners cut it. I wish we could taste it but seeing it is good enough.

We came on a foggy and rainy day so we didn't had a great view like other did.  Nonetheless we enjoyed ourselves with the tea and cakes even though there isn't any WOW to those matcha cakes we ordered.  Beside the restaurant there isn't much to see inside other than tea tasting and tea goods.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

Walking along the sides of the mountain next to the open sea was quite thrilling for us seniors to say the least.  We had to be careful of our steps in the uneven stone/rocks which were wet.  But it all paved for a good adventure with lovely views photo opportunity and a chance to take some great photos standing up on the rocks.  We enjoyed the visit.

Walk to the top is quite easy with good views.Don't miss the signpost to the women divers near the bottom on the way down.  They do a few shows a day and you don't have to pay extra to see it.Lot's of parking and eateries in the area

Viewpoint on the western end of Jeju Island.  Great place for sunset observation.  High on a cliff with good views all around.  There is a weather station here.Was here on a windy day - with field of swirling grass. To the north of the hill is a tail along the shore where it is possible to rent electric scooters.  There is also a small museum on the prehistoric settlement found in the area.

Very pretty and not too taxing walk to add to any outings on Jeju. Our day was a little foggy but the view was still amazing with the Spring growth just starting to show. Lots of other attractions in the near vicinity makes it a good spot to include in a day out. The short but steep hike up to the 'temple in a cave' provides some lovely views on a good day and there are several other attractions at the base of the walk including the Big Golden Buddha temples tea shops the Dutch ship and rock walks. Enjoyable.
very nice island. one can spent 2-3 days while roaming around the island. a very beautiful place with lot of good natural views of mountains.
Very beautiful view from the top of the hill surrounding area is good for hiking a walking World heritage place can be crowded in high saison
unesco world heritage !! When I went there it's snowing. very cold. But view was very very gooddddd. Mountain and sea were absolutely breath-taking. The stair was high. You should beware.

This waterfall is beautiful in that the water falls all the way to the rocks in the ocean unimpeded.  You have to scramble on rocks to get closer or you can remain on the landing at the bottom of the steps and get a pretty good view.
This tourist attraction has good view for photo. You can see the Jeju city landscape from here and the dragon head rock itself only the minor thing to see.

This really worth a visit. I'm not good at hiking but its quite easy to walk up to the top. For those who have been hiking in China this is really nothing. The wooden stairs also in good condition. Great view from up here :) Also you can have some local snacks here.

This place still exists as of April 2019. It's an amazing place for kids and they have so many toys and so much equipment. If your kids know about Tayo the little bus the place is magic and if they don't well it is still a pretty good kids play cafe. There's a cafe selling drinks and food. While as noted in the previous review the staffs English isn't good but is sufficient and they try to help. We have been to this Tayo cafe and some in Seoul as well. This one is much bigger and has more and better play equipment overall. It was also way less busy than the ones in Seoul and slightly cheaper @ 12k won per child and 3k won per adult compared to 15kw won per child and 5k won per adult in Seoul. Note: Visits are capped at 2 hours (or I'm sure the kids can play there all day)Tip: Ask the staff about riding the Tayo car ride as they are not always on but when you request a staff member will assist with it. Also the pork cutlet and rice were pretty decent for the kids (and adults) to eat.

This place is worth visiting given it's nice environment and a lots of things to do. Food:  I highly recommend the green tea icecream and cake at the O'Sulloc tea museum which appears to be the focus of most visitors.  But I also want to take some time to remind you that there's another little gem inside the organic cafe of Innisfree that's also within the complex--DON'T MISS OUT THE TANGERINE SHAVED ICE! It comes in a big original size that can be sufficiently shared among 3 persons or there's a mini version if you only want a taste of it.  It's not cheap but worth trying because they use Jeju Tangerine which tasted somewhat more intense and flavourful.  Drinks:  They have free tea-demo which you can try their teas.  They also sell a selection of other drinks like tea latte.  Most of them tasted and smelled spectacular.  The teabags are also wrapped individually so they make good souvenirs as well. Soap making:  If you go early do try making your own soap at the Innisfree house it's a fun experience and make good souvenirs.View and/or pictures:  The environment around and within the museum is a great place for pictures with the open tea-farm and the delicate glass buildings or the colourful interior of the Innisfree house.  There's also a viewing deck in the O'sulloc Tea Museum which you can access by taking a lift.  The view up there is pretty amazing.  Tip:  1. Go on a sunny day if you want to take great pictures in the tea-farm2. Go early if you are worried that they sell out the cakes.  The tangerine shaved ice wasn't available after 5.30pm so we went to visit again on the next day.

This place is very good. If you leave to this place then have to prepare ride licence.because if you rent to scooter then you can travel comfortably. This place have beach. very good view of beach.And if you come here then you should eat  Jjajangnodle. this food is very very  delicious.

This place is really good. You can see the cliff right beside the sea and it?s really safe to walk at the walk area. The view is really nice but there are a lot of stairs. So it?s kinda hard for old people and for family who use baby strollers.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. review: This peak offers a good view of the oreums and the sea but it did get very very crowded when we arrived there at about 9am. First time to Jeju? Must visit.

This museum features the history of tea in Jeju as well as you can view the tea plantation from the observation deck. You also can taste the green tea ice cream and cake at the cafe besides a good place to buy green tea. This area also features innisfree shop where you can make your own soap besides a lot of innisfree products on sale.

This is THE place if you crave green tea desserts!! Tried both the green tea soft ice cream and green tea roll cake with cream cheese...absolutely delightful! Small museum with history of tea culture lots of tea types for purchase...even green tea based chocolates and jam! The rooftop offers a good view of the surrounding areas! This is a fun place for the family !  To enjoy this place to the max you must not be shy about lying on the floor or doing funny expressions to pose to achieve the photo effect .  We had great fun as a family n have a good laugh as we review the photos taken.  There's also a outdoor sculpture park which we enjoyed doing funny pose with the sculpture ! We were there on a Sunday about 1030am there wasn't a crowd that allow us to have more time at each exhibit to pose without worrying on holding up others.Go n have fun !

There is a parking lot for self park and that was handy. Luckily we found a spot as someone was leaving. Hiked up to the top for fabulous views. Came back down and had lunch at a local place just down the road since the car was parked in the lot we didn't want to try parking somewhere else. The local place was very good. Definitely have to go to this tourist destination if you go to Jeju

The walk up the stairs is hard on knees but not specially challenging and can be done in 15-20mins. Make sure to be on top a bit before sunrise or otherwise gets quite packed with people and is hard to find a good spot to seat and see the sunrise. We got a somewhat cloudy morning so sunrise views were quite disappointing.
The view was great from the bottom and top.  It's a good upwards hike that makes your  heart pumping.  The stairs coming down made me had a vertigo.  It was worthwhile though.
The view of the row of natural stone is very good. The scenery around is also very beautiful. This place is worth a visit when you are in Jeju island.
The view of the green tea field is really wonderful. And there are good things to give your parents and friends as gifts.
The view is good but the climb is tiring in spring with the cold wind. You have to climb about 30 mins to make it to the top.
The view is amazing. And the green is calming and lush. A lot of good photo spots. There are restaurants and some street food in the area.

The view and scenery is good.The stairs are slippery so better watch your steps.Some stalls located at the entrance.I tried their famous Jeju fruit...taste like Mandarin orange (costs5000won-for about10pcs)

The place is good for picture taking but can be a good climb for people who are not very active. Great view from atop while you can experience Jeju women divers if you go to the shore. Many restaurants in the area as well for those who want to taste fresh seafood like abalones shrimp crabs squid shells etc.

The musuem is located next to the tea farm great view from the rooftopinside the musuem you can buy a range of different tea made in JEJU and evevn drink somethere is a restaurant inside where youi can eat an tea icecream or a tea cake anything which is made with tea!good for family and couple
The museum has nothing much in it it is more like a cafe with overcrowding issue. The tea plantation is of decent size and good view for photo spot.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.

The most memorable thing was rather on the ferry to Udo Island.The seagulls were hovering over those who had Calbee prawn crackers ready to feed them. They followed the ferry from Jeju all the way to Udo. That was a sight!Udo generally has good scenic views and interesting coral beach with clear blue waters.

The highest mountain in South Korea.  Several paths and some are easily accessible by public bus.  I chose the one to the summit up and down.  Clear sign and a small shop before going up the summit.  Good view.  Can get a certificate to the summit in the park office.

The drive from jeju airport area to aqua planet is around 1 hour 10 minutes passing by many small towns. The entry tickets were quite costly and I used klook to get some discounts with the tickets. Upon parking the rented car outside the vicinity of aqua planet then picked up a number from the machine next to the ticket counter. Waited for the number and redeemed my wristbands without much hassle. Kids under 3 can enter for free.There are plenty to see and we were in time to watch fish feeding a seal and dolphin show. Outside the facilities has really good view and many people were taking photos.Food in the food court was not too bad and similar like incheon airport have to be ordered and paid at the cashier counter and picked up from the individual sections when the device buzzes.Overall experience was great and worth every cent spent.

Recommended to visit when you go Jeju Island. The view is amazingly breathtaking. We booked for a private tour for 1 day and bring us to different tourist attractions and good foods as well.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Many steps to reach the grotto mid way up. Have to stop to rest many times but view is quite good. Also can make wishes and prayers as lots of altars for different things such as eternal love and to be blessed with a baby.

Looks like the Burj khalifa of Dubai but its just much smaller and in fact not a hotel but a bridge. Going across the bridge you will be on a small island to walk which will take around 45 min. Great for a scenic walk close to the city. You will also have a good view to the sea and of the diving women of Jeju.

Like most government run museums in Korea Jeju National Museum takes up some major square yardage despite having only about half hour worth of displays. just for trekking within 1hr view & overall environment not bad. also getting good view at the top. good for try it if you have time

It was great to visit the temple while it was decorated with thousands of colorful lanterns to commerate the birthday of Budda.  I don't know if the review would be as good if it was during the year.  A lovely temple that was made awesome because to the lanterns.

Hallasan the 2nd highest mountain in South Korea is a fantastic hiking place!! You can choose to hike from two different easy routes to enjoy different scenery. If this is your first hike after a long hiatus do be mindful that it's better to take the easy route. Cos at some points it's huge boulders that require some stamina to step up.Take the first bus from the bus interchange cos it's advisable for tourists to reach midpoint by noon so that you have adequate time to trek back and catch the last bus from the bus stop which is still 20 min from the start of trekking point. Alternatively there's taxi if you are a group or pair. There's only a hut at midpoint which sells cup noodles which is not cheap.  Thus advisable to bring along dry food and plenty of water for recovery. Along the way you would meet seasoned hikers and some are so friendly that they offer you a ginseng sweet if they see you resting.  There's a water point and the water taste so good! The viewing points offer such fantastic view and it's so breezy that we forgot ourselves!  Definitely a place to visit.
Good views. UNESCO site.Natural volcanic history n lava tubes.Lighted direction arrows on footpath was useful.
Good view. Very amazing tea recommended for people who love to drink tea. Have Great cafe to chill and relax. Varieties of place have museum cafe and tea plantation
Good view if you go on the day they don't have a heavy fog like me 555Please look for the weather forecast before you go.You have to pay 2000 KRW for a parking fee

Good spot for a quick photo very close to downtown jeju . You can walk from the middle of town very easily over the bridge and then round . Walk down do the photo and from the viewing area also a car park with toilet close by .

Good place to visit. We have visited the place in he beginning of July on rainy season. In spite of that we really enjoyed the view. There's a track with the same name follow it. Everywhere was filled with silver grass. It was also a good walk from entrance to the hills with breathtaking view of the crater. Best place for photo opportunities. Perfect for those who love nature and fresh air.

As noted by other reviewers there are indeed large crowds to beat on a weekend visit but the tea museum is definitely worth a visit. Good to note that here is English subtitling on most of the signs in the small museum. The biggest draw for me was the beautiful architecture of the building. Local volcanic stone is used in combination with brick glass and steel. The result is beautiful and the building has featured in quite a few design magazines for good reason.

Around 10-15 mins walk to view the waterfalls. Easy to walk if you have elderly or kids with you. Water is clear and kids love the ducks around. Very near to my hotel in Jeju (EINS Hotel) which is around 5 mins drive away. Good for a short stop.

Amazing views all the way up and at the top. If visiting in summer - better to visit in evening or early morning.  We climbed up twice - once at 5pm and then at 5.30 the next morning.  Both were excellent - with different sun position giving different light and shadows.  Both worth it.  Fee is 5000 won per person ( half price if child or youth under 24).  If you go before 7 in the morning - there is no charge.  When you come down make sure that you take the path around to the right - good views down to the small beach and also on the main peak
Am a nature buff and this one is just Loveㅿ A good few minutes hike and a foxy view atop awaits you.One must not miss this when in Jeju.

A good place. It is very near to jeju love land and it just looks like any other normal road but when you go there you will see the mystery of your car moving by itself without the external and engine force. Also there is a very scenic view around road. Had nice fun.

A good place with nice view of the bridge and open sea. No entrance fees is required and is accessible via public transport and some walking is needed. Restaurants are available within the bridge area and other attractions such as submarine is located just right before the entrance into Saeyeongyo Bridge.

A good place especially for first-timers or those who are interested to see lava formations. Really gorgeous view when the sea hit those rocks. Nothing much to see so don't really have to spend much time here.
A beautiful spot of commanding good view of the sea and the rocks of special shape lava formed on cooling.
You will need good shoes and ~20 min, and water, the rout is amazing, clean, safe and view is breathtaking, on the way back you can buy tangerine juice form the shops - delicious!
You will have to walk a good while to get there. Worth the walk to see both falls. The bridge on our way was beautiful. Breathtaking view. We paid 2,500 won each. Which is under $5 for two people.

Wouldn't really recommend this place as i don't find it very interesting. Think it's a very good idea (since Korean Dramas are so popular) but very bad execution. If you have the spare time, don't mind spending the money, you are nearby and you loveeeeee korean drama, maybe you can consider coming.. else, don't waste your time here.Full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/drama-world/

When you said about Jeju, this Ilchubung will appear in the advertisement and you will know that is Jeju. But for sure, you will not able to snap a photo like in the adver since that only can be done if you take a photo from the helicopter and etc.For family, it is a bit tough if you bring small kids below 10 yrs old since you need to walk to the peak via stair and for adults people also a tiring activity but worth it since you can see the good view of the city and sea around that area. For photography also it will a nice thing to have.They said, the best thing during sunrise to be at the peak, but we are not make it during the sunrise so could not provide any comments on that. Also there is free show of diverwoman at the beach area just that area, they showing the activity of catching octopus with diving and selling the octopus to the audience. Most of the korea people eat it raw with Korean Sauce, i'm yet try the tast.Souvenir shop also available at the entrance of the Ilchubung peak.Thank You.

When I went up in July 2014, it was cloudy and misty, so no views to be seen which was a pity a heck of a climb up, but even though knocking 66 years old I made it (my pulse settled down after less than 15 mins), so it wasn't that bad for the oldies, once again shame about the clouds/mist.Worth a visit, on a good day.I marked it down 'cause of the clouds.

Went there without much training as I envisage that winter time is more pleasant to climb. We reached the base around 7.30am as we try to take the first bus. As we envisage there are snow, I have a pair of crampons bought before arriving in Jeju. Fortunately I did as the crampon sold at the shop is rather expensive. Then it was a relax 2 hours climb, I did not want to rush, but took time to appreciate the environments and snow. The crampons came in useful as you climb further up, it gets slippery. Good to have walking sticks too. At about the 1000+ meter stop, there is shop where you could buys hot noodles and drinks. I bought another set of crampons there as it is reasonable compared to the shop at the base of the mountain.After a short rest, the final climb to the top. Here there is a series of steps and staircase that leads to the top. At some point it was rather steep so have to climb up slowly, catching my breaths as the higher altitude and cold tends to slow you down. There is a timing to get down from the mountain per regulations, hence the need to get to the top early to enjoy the view and triumph. Finally reaching the top, was rewarded with a gorgeous scenery. It was kind of crowded and there was a queue of climbers taking turns to take picture with the summit monument.  After taking lots of pictures, hiking down was relatively easily, reaching the base in half the time. Took the bus back to town to enjoy a beer and fried chickens. A trip not to be missed.

Went there because I heard it's a good place for silver grass view, and I was welcomed with a full mountain of beautiful silver grass! Wear comfortable shoes as the oreum is quite steep. Below the oreum are some food trucks selling snacks, good enough to fill your tummy after the steep hike. It might not be easy to locate this place, as the phone numbers I key in the GPS failed to bring me to the correct place. Finally able to find this place by searching for   Everis Golf & Resort   phone number, and managed to see   Saebyeol Oreum   at the highway signboard. Try searching for Everis resort if you can't locate saebyeol oreum, as they are just next to each other.

went there after breakfast and was a good time to start if you didn't care too much of sunrise view. Even though it was windy and chilly, got up to the top sweaty and hot. you see see pretty ckear view from the top; Udo island, the wind turbines in the east, Seopjikoji in the south.

Went in the morning. The view is breathtaking. Must visit. Korean artists love this place for a good reason. Featured in some korean shows as well. It's very pretty. Packed some sandwiches, lay a mat, have a breakfast and feel the breeze.

Well, it is a beach. With bus 101 roughly 15 minutes away from Jeju city.As far as I remember the beach feature something like a free gym and a few toilets.I did not see much of changing facilities, showers or lockers near the beach.In my view Hamdeok Beach is less good than the beaches in Busan.During my time in Hamdeok Beach I saw three surfers who practiced their skill.

We woke up at 3am for this and didn't regret it. It was really quite awesome. We drove in the wee hours of the morning for 1.5 hrs to get there, before hiking up for about 40mins to get to the viewing deck where there are seats to see the sunrise. To best enjoy this, be well prepared and equipped for the journey. We slept early at about 9pm the previous night because we knew we had to wake up at 3am. Prepare bread for breakfast on the road because you will need the energy for the hike. Wear proper walking shoes to make it easier to climb up. Remember to check the sunrise timing the night before, set your gps early and accurately if you are driving. If you need help with Korean gps or not sure if you got the right place, always ask your hotel or hostel host to help you set it right the night before. Charge and prep your cameras, go early to get a good spot, because you are going to get some really awesome sights of the sunrise at this spot. Definitely go for this if you are in Jeju. Not to be missed for the world!

We were lucky with the weather to visit the place, and it is important because during the rain it might not be so attractive.The nature is very beautiful, you will take good pictures for sure.We took a small electric car (for 2 people), but it was comparatively expensive for only 2,5 hours. It is possible to go around the island during that time but only without staying at all tourist points. Moreover, you cannot really enjoy the trip because of being in hurry.All Korean suggested to try peanut and mandarin ice-cream, that we did. Again the price was high, and mandarin one was so sweet that make us to put it in trash right away.People in the island are friendly, and even offer to pick us up to some places by car and shown the shortest way.Taking a boat to see caves was the best experience during the whole travel. For only 10 000 won you will have a lot of fun as the boat goes so fast, and definetly amazing view on the island.

We were fortunate to catch a not-as-crowded ferry at around 2plus and stayed till 530pm and got back around 6pm. Ferry ride takes around 15mins but get up early and start walking towards the exit if u don't want to be Squashed w the main crowd! Upon arrival on the island, we decided to take the bus tour (costs 5000KRW/pax) which stops at 2 locations- the lighthouse peak as well as the beach.I must say Udo is very very windy so make sure u gear up and tie your hair if necessary!Hiking up to the lighthouse took us around 15mins up(lots of stairs, but after that it's v scenic). We had a good view of the whole island, despite being drizzly throughout the day. Dennis Cafe is really nice, cozy and affordable peanut ice cream as compared to the crowded 'Running man' ice cream shop which wasn't actually good. If I could go back, I would definitely bring my international driving license and rent an E bike!

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We took bus no 100 from seogwipo city to the last bus stop. Walk up the road to the next bus stop and got on the intercity bus no 701. Got off at the beach overlooking seongsan illchubong. Plenty of spots for great pics here. Walked all the way to the entrance and up. Manageable. Highly recommend wearing good comfortable shoes. The climb up was not as bad as I thought it would be. The view from the bottom was quite intimidating at first  though. Many restaurants with reasonable prices to stop for lunch after the climb. Overall, good place to visit.

We took bus 182 early morning reached there around 7.30am and started to hike about 8am. It's good to bring hiking stick as there are lots of steps up, with a hiking stick it's easier to move up the rocky paths. It was very cold at the mountain so it's good to wear in layers and can remove the jackets if it gets too warm during the hike. We managed to reach Saraoreum shelter before 12pm where we ate and took a break before moving on to the summit. After 12pm no one is allowed to move on up to the summit from the shelter as it gets dark very early during winter time. We reached the summit just before 1.30pm. The ranger already chasing people to get down. It was very cold and windy at the top and it started to drizzle. So it's important to bring a raincoat too. I could'nt get a good view as it was very foggy and windy. We did'nt get some rest and started to descend. It took a long while to descend too as the path is very rocky and slippery. Lucky i have my hiking stick with me. Half way down it started to get dark we needed to use our handphones as touch light to guide us down the path. Very happy we are all able to reach the summit. It's a nice experience.

We stopped here on a whim to go zip lining which was pretty tame but a lovely way to view the green tea fields from above. The guides were good but very minimal English. We stopped and had some green tea ice cream at the cave cafe which is really unique. It's a true cave which gives you a break from the Jeju heat and humidity. The server here spoke English and was really nice even helping people take photos at the cave   photo spot.   We enjoyed the small tea museum too but would have appreciated translations for the exhibits. Overall a fun couple of hours.
