It is about an hour west of Seogwipo by bus which stops conveniently right in front of the mountain.There is a nice temple at the base of the mountain called Sanbanggulsa (?곕갑援댁궗) with a huge golden Buddha a wonderful view of the town below and the ocean and an army of miniature mint-coloured Buddhas (I think). All make for great photos. Further up the mountain (you can climb up a long flight of stairs) is a small temple in a cave with an even better view of the town below. Worth visiting if you have made it this far. There is also an interesting story about a monk who hid in the cave during a violent time (can't exactly remember details). Down below south of the street in front of the mountain is a really really nice coastal walk with impressive cliffs that have been ocean and wind-swept into wonderful formations. This place is called   Yongmeori Coast   and also makes for great picture. (Worth knowing that the coast closes during heavy rain for safety reasons.)(Also of interest in the area to some is Hamel's Ship (a replica/museum of an old Dutch ship that landed on Jeju ages ago and the story of the Dutchman that was held captive in the island) and horseback riding (though it's only in a circle). Could be good for kids though these two are the least attractive for me personally.)

Samchoon (Mr Kim Si-Nam), was our guide for a 2 day taxi tour in jeju! Samchoon was super friendly, considerate and warm hearted! Samchoon really felt more like family to us!Samchoon texted me 2 days before to confirm the time and location of pickup and asked about my itinerary and gave suggestions on the order of location we should visit first. Samchoon made sure we get the best experience we could have in jeju!Samchoon was very well prepared. In his taxi, he had prepared water, phone cable for charging, wet & dry tissues, umbrellas, raincoats and even torchlights for caves.First thing he told me was that we didn't have to worry about time and that we can take as much time at any location. He wouldn't rush or give us a time limit. So that we could enjoy every place to the fullest. Samchoon even said that he will not charge us extra even if we exceed 8 hours, he said that he would want us to enjoy and not feel rushed. Samchoo said he was a photographer in the past and actively helped to take beautiful pictures throughout the 2 day trip. He knew exactly where the spots to stand so that the pictures came out amazing!Samchoon was very accomdating to our changes in the itinerary he gave suggestions on alternatives. Samchoon knew that we like to take photos to so on the last day he brought us to see the sunset so that we could take nice pictures! True enough the sunset and view was breath taking! Samchoon is really familiar with all the places and routes and the rides between locations was really smooth and comfortable! Samchoon even has a 40 year accident free award!To Samchoon, A very big thank you for making our jeju trip so fun and enjoyable! Thanks for taking such good care of us! We will miss you and the beautiful Jeju island! Will definitely go back to look for him when in jeju!

Sabyeol Oreum definitely has lots to offer especially for tourists/foreigners. The stunning view from the top of the hill is obviously something worth to be explored, and the best part of it is that you don?t need to pay anything to experience such aesthetic view! It is a flexible place that offers different kind of experience depending on the seasons, and it does not take much of a hiker to climb it. Not only does it not take long to climb to the top, the paths are also significantly safe. Near the place, you can also see some horses without having to pay for it, and there are lots of places where you can take good pictures! If you are coming to Jeju, I believe it is a must visit place that you should consider in your itinerary!

Recommended to visit in Jeju, it maybe a funny or plain looking on the pictures but you will be amazed when you are there. Amazing rock formation and how the sea waves hit the rocks is the highlight here. Still, prepare for the crowd, we traveled here around May 2016 Summer season but rainy on that day, thought of less crowd because of that but still very crowded place. Good thing the location doesn't require long walks or hiking thus everyone can enjoy the view.
Really worth to win 'New 7 wonders of Nature' as the view there is amazing.  From a geographic perspective, its formation letting us know more about the nature.Little hiking is good for our trip!

Perhaps there was some misunderstanding on my part, but it seems that it is no longer possible to watch the sunrise from the peak, as the ticket office information says that it only opens at 7.30am (sunrise is around 7am in November). The views during a day climb is still good, though mostly of Seongsan. As compared to the views from the peak, I found the beach at the foot of the peak (along the downward route) more interesting, with the lava formations and rock pools. Try and catch the haenyeo (female divers) in action if you can!Also, try to visit either very early or very late in the day - the crowds in between are huge (from the top, I counted at least a dozen tour buses in the parking lot).

One of the top places to see in Jeju.  Great view of some craggy coastline.  The other reviews are pretty good and we experienced about the same - great place, but really crowded even though it was raining!  Again...people come in waves, just wait it out.  The wind was high and seas rough so it made pretty spectacular wave crashes.  On one side there was a consistent high wind and mist/spray coming at you, so watch your cameras!  There is a 1,000 W Parking fee on top of the 2,000 entrance fee.

One of the most visited Tourist attraction in Jeju, the Seongsan IIchulbong peak or the Sun rise peak was formed due to Volcanic eruption thousands of years ago. This peak has a huge cater in the middle surrounded by huge rocks making it look like a gigantic crown. In addition to this the other most sought-after attraction here is the old ladies diving deep into the water without oxygen masks to collect sea food. Twice a day a special show is conducted for the visitors.Though it was quite windy and cold when we visited, we were sweating a lot once on the top as we have to climb a lot of steps.Once on the top we were surrounded by the moving clouds, the experience which made us forget all the fatigue.We could not see the sunrise as it was quite cloudy when we visited, but as our guide informed, one can have a good view of the one during summer.At the base there are lot of eating joints which ensures everyone gets refreshed after a long trek.We thank our Jumbo taxi driver who shared the spare waterproof jerkins he had with him to wear when it started drizzling (Kin nam joon / +821046166650 / kimnj0424@naver.com)

One of the best stops we made in Jeju. This rock formation is pretty cool and the stop is more worth it since it's a good hour's worth of walking and snapping photos (as opposed to a number of the really touristy places where it's just one kodak moment).Check the tides. The rock formation that people walk on are really close to the water, so if the tides are high, it gets slippery. Actually, some parts are slippery as it is.You have two options: going counter-clockwise, which ends up being an upward movement OR going clockwise, a downward movement.  The views are nice-ish both ways (personally the counter-clockwise views were nicer). More than that though, going counter-clockwise is a lot easier as the steps are easier to deal with moving up. Many of the people coming down were cursing the steep rocks and were tired even before it began for them. Might not recommend this if walking is difficult for you as climbing and hoping around is a must. Little children were around and they seemed to be enjoying themselves, but none of them were younger than 3 years of age.No bathrooms once you enter the formations, but ladies will sell you food and drink (mostly alcohol) if you're interested in a seaside meal.

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area
Nice weather to hike in Feb, good view when surrounding area is all cover by snow. By quite slipping when going down the hill.
Nice View and good for health,Guys try going this place and you will feel the Fresh of Air at top of mountain.
natural cliff formation like steps, very much similar to giant causeway in belfast. good ocean view, cheap entrance ticket. a vert worthwhile visit

My mum and i took about one hour plus to reach the top. but not to worry if you aren't that physically fit, you can always take a break at seats along the way and enjoy the nice scenery. we went around sept therefore the weather is very good though we are sweated a lot too. However once you are up at the peak, you can enjoy the full panoramic view of the sea and the eastern coastline.A place not to be missed when you go Jeju

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My friend and I joined the East Coast one day tour - it’s meant to be a small group tour but only my friend and I joined today’s tour, so it was a private tour! Weather wasn’t nice today - it rained all day and was windy, but it was still a good trip after all. Beautiful scenery from the summit of the Seongsan Sunrise Peak - where you can have a view from above of the shore of the island. Our tour guide was June - a hiking expert with excellent knowledge of Korean culture and history. A memorable experience after all!

My first time to Korea focusing on Jeju and Seoul. Generally I would think the overall experience to South Korea is kind of over rated. I expected more based on the comments from friends, reviews by travellers and most importantly seeing it in Korean Dramas.Udo island is an exception, it gave me the best experience in the entire 8-day trip, except the weather wasn't too good on my day trip to Udo. Rented a bike to travel almost the entire island which i think is the best mode to explore remote areas without using too much energy.  Hopping up and down to take photos by the beach, colorful cafes, yellow canola fields, uphill and downhill.Unforgettable squid volcano rice was one of its kind and one of the most satisfactory meal in the entire trip.

My favourite one in Seogwipo, it may be not as large as Kpop Live in Seoul  but its still good one. With fifteen-thousand-won ticket you could experience the 4D media concert of Big Bang, GD, PSY...Remember to choose the showtime for concert because your ticket is available for max. 3 hours. Besides that you could experience over 31 attractions including be the star, meet the star, recording with star, make up and dancing with star. Its cool one when you could take pictures or singing with TOP, GD or PSY. There is also a section for Korean music history that you could help you have an overview of Korean music industry. Play Kpop will catch some of your moments and then you could download your photos and videos you take there by filling the ID ticket. Worth your money & well recommended!

My family walked from our hotel to the top of Ilchulbong and down. From the entrance, the mountain(?) looked formidable and it looked to be a painful hike, but it turned out to be rather a short hike. I wish I had taken more time on the way up and enjoyed the views more. On the way down, we saw a restaurant by the rocky shore.  I believe this is where mermaids do their demonstrations and sell raw oyster dishes.  I wanted to go down but my 10 & 12 yr olds won't have it.  So I missed out.         The guy who took the tickets at the entrance surprising had a good nack for taking pictures.  If he is not too busy, ask him to take your group photo.         After the hike, we went to a bakery just by the entrance.  From the second floor, we had a nice view of the Ilchulbong and enjoyed cup of coffee with various breads.  The owner was very kind and let us wait out the rain in the store.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Marado island is small island but it has amazing view. You can see the wide field, blue sea,and Jeju-representing rocks.You can borrow a bike and look around the island riding a bike. And there is also a good restaurants. They use Jeju local specialities.

Make sure to go when the day is clear, there are a lot of tourists during the peak times so keep that in mind as it could affect your views with all the group selfie stick shots. I highly suggest going off on the little paths around they all have views and are just lovely. If you bring a mini packed meal it's just spectacular for a picnic. It's very close to the falls and the botanical gardens and you can honestly walk (if you have good comfy shoes)This is a must see natural wonder!

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Less than 15 min walking, the waterfall was beautiful, and there?s food photo spot where everyone line up when u get to the waterfall. In my opinion, the admission fee was little too much for the quick walk and waterfall view. But good to visit once!

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Its snowing when I visited this area. A short walk to the top will reveal a nice scenery covered with snow and a crater below. The nice view around actually overshadow the crater itself! Good place to play some snow throwing too. Its suitable for kids or even elderly as the climbing is very gradual, I would say its more like a nice walk. You will be able to see some tall grass on both side of the walk, which according to locals, was used as a roof cover. It is good to hold the weight of snow on some old buildings.

Its really easy to reach this attraction. Parking is free however you are required to pay a minimal fee in order to view this waterfall. Walking on the stairs is easy but if you do wish to get close to the waterfall , a good pair of shoes with good grip is required as you have to walk on the slippery stone/rock. There are some women selling fresh seafood by the waterfall.
It's good to work out your legs, but if the view over the dull crater really is reward enough has everyone decide for himself.

It's good for photo taking as there are many cute bears all over. There are also good displays , but it is not entirely bears, as there are many other animals there too. The day we visited it, it was very foggy. Oh, and some teddies looked quite  old and worn.Overall, nothing much except photo taking. Hope this review was useful.

It's a beautiful waterfall. As described by another reviewer, there is a flight of stairs you have to descend to reach the waterfall. At the bottom of the stairs, you will have to carefully traverse across rocks if you want to get nearer to the waterfall to take a good photo with it in the background. Be sure to get good shoes to avoid injury as the rocks can be slippery. Not recommended for pregnant ladies or old folks, especially so when the rocks are wet from rain.
It's a beautiful place for you to admire the view and take IG photo. If you're good in photo shooting, you might be able to trick people that you're in Grand Canyon.

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.

It was very meaningful to spend 3 days to join the Jeju Olle walking festival in November, 2018. One route per day not only an physical exercise and challenge to myself but also a good opportunity to meet friends or make new friends there. No one push you to walk faster but we could take pictures, enjoyed nice views and landscapes on each route. Local food for lunchs were delicious. What a beautiful island, good for gathering and good for vacation. I love Jeju. It was my third time participating Jeju Olle Festival. Different experience every time.

It was raining when we went here. The steps were not at all slippery (they had rubber/metal bars at the end) Although it will be a long hard climb to the top of the mountain. If you started the climb up the mountain there is a different set of stairs going down. At the top of the mountain are set of seats, possibly a good view (it was raining) and a sign to commemorate your achievement. The place is also crowded with people. It is not suggestible for old people to go up the mountain but they could go through the sea. i would go back there again to see the wonderful view.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

It was kind of windy when I had my visit at Yeongmori cliff. At first, I thought it was another ordinary rock formation viewing after taking a few steps from the entrance...I was about to back out from the trek thinking I can see much of these in the Philippines, but as soon as my tour guide led me to the farther side of the cliff, I started to appreciate how unique the lava rock formation  was.  The best view to take a picture maybe is to include Mt, Sanbang in the back draft. You may also climb a few steps to the top or catch a good timing for huge strike of waves by the rocks.  Wear appropriate shoes as the pathways are always slippery and wet.

it was interesting to see these column-shape geological formations. The sea was calm when I visited so i did not get to see the waves getting on them. Nonetheless, the formations made really good photos.The sheer number of visitors on the small and narrow viewing platform could spoil your trip!

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.

It was a tiring climb to the peak. Good thing there are stairs to lead you to the top. The place can be crowded at time, but glad that there is only one way up and the other way down to guide the human traffic flow. At the peak, you are rewarded with the spectacular paranorma view of the towns nearby and of course the bowl-like crater. Worth to challenge yourself to the climb.

It was a nice, warm yet windy weather when I was there. The climb was easy and safe, really a good exercise. Along the way up, there're small gazebos with benches for people to rest and catch their breath. Whoever climbs up are always drenched with sweat but when reached to the peak, the view was really breathtaking. It was worth the climb.

It offers one of the best view in Jeju. It is free to go, no need to book, super easy to walk. I was lucky with weather this time and was able to see hallasan from here! I cannot describe how amazing it was.  It is breathtaking and good to visit anytime of days. Many people came for sunset and sunrise. It is definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju. Be prepare for strong wind and amazing view. Recommend going during fall

it looks like a dragon, I guess. good views of the ocean. It's more of a tour bus place where people come, take pictures and go. But if you walk a bit up the hill from here, you come to a nice Buddhist temple.

It is most satisfactory to complete our climb to the top to experience the cold air, sea breeze and overlooking at the mountains and sea below you.  The feeling is so good and the view is just simply awesome!  It's a great place not to be missed!

It is just like the cheap Chinese market in my hometown, with small stalls, no room to try things on and dirty floor. We were quite surprised when we got there, as the reviews of this place are rather good. Did not buy anything there. If you want some normal shopping in Jeju, go to any Emarket instead.
It is easily to reach from the downtown area.  Next to the Seobok Park, at the coastal rim.  You may enjoy a nice view on the coast-front.  Good for the family for fun.

It is a small island. we took the boat from Jeju. In a lobby full of Korean people, speak no English or Chinese. It was a bit challenge for me. ;) helpful enough, when I tried to talk to the ticket officer, she spoke a little Chinese. The boat took around 15 min. it is a pretty simple boat, with both people, and cars. with 30 min. time interval.Landing on Udo, we chose the red bus tour. 4 stops. the first stop is the best place I should say. Brilliant view! sea with sea wind. And there are some bars and restraunts where you could take a seat and rest.The rest of the 2-3 stops, are normal. On the bus, the driver were saying in Korean languange, which we do not understand at all. But we heard laugh from time to time, which we believe everyone else enjoyed the drivers speech.It is a good short stay. sun shine is strong, get prepare with some protections.
It is a naturally formed pool with sea water, good to go with swimming gear.  The view is good too.  Good for the teens and young people.

It is a good place to watch the whole seaside view and the horizon of the sea where the sky meets the sea. The view is breathtaking as you can see not only the sea view but the city view of Jeju island and the mountain in the background. However, one need to put in the effort and climb 45 minutes up to the mountain top in order to enjoy this view. And also hope for the best of luck that it is not a cloudy day.

Interesting volcano hike up to the crater ledge. Good views out over the coastline, even tho we had a rainy, cloudy day so didn't get the best of it! Quite steep steps and climbing at times. Exposed to wind too. We saw some of the Jeju women divers from the top just about to launch themselves into the sea. I am told it's VERY busy on new year's day when everyone goes up to welcome in the dawn.
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.

In short, a MUST GO when in Jeju-do. The beautiful breathtaking view of the ocean and on good days, clear view of Halasan mountain from the beach. We were there on 2nd Feb, and if it was not because of the freezing cold weather i would have jumped in the sea myself! Reaching U-do by ferry (15mins ride) and there are cute scooters for rent. We went with a travel agent, hence, we toured by bus. We went to two main places, one with a speedboat ride circling the island they claimed to look like a cow laying down and another by the beach of U-do. The water is of emerald in colour and dark blue  here is a picture for reference.

In my journey, I went to the Hallasan National Park at Jeju. Here is a good place to walk with family, since here has a wide stretch of land at the foot of hill, you can just walk around the hill. Children can play in a nature place with good air. All the building and transport are so far away, you must feel relax and do not want to leave.If you are younger and want to see more view, I really suggest that you must walk to the peak by stairs, but you must have enough energy, because it is really tired. Take water and some food are necessary. After that, you can see a good view at the peak, just like stand on the cloud.Finally, I suggest that you will climb at evening because of the sunset is very beautiful. Also the weather is better to climb the hill.

If you're unfit like me, please be mentally and physically prepared before embarking on this   hike  , 4-5 hours upwards, another 4-5 hours downwards. The view at the top is great but that highly depends on the weather. Don't be surprised to see many elderly Koreans in their 50s or 60s even at the peak. And oh yes, please bring along good hiking shoes for this trip, it will definitely help you a lot.

If you have a tight schedule and cannot afford a whole day climbing the Hallasan Mountain, or some of your group physically can't do Hallanshan, this is a good option, because it is closer to other sight seeing places so you don't need a whole day, also because it is a much easier climb compared to Hallasan.The day we visited this was not crowded at all because everybody went to Udo Island on the opposite, after a two day close of the ferry service due to weather. If there was a helicopter service i(not sure), it must be very spectacular from an aerial view.  From the ground level,  if you didn't see the photo from the Internet, nor post cards, you probably don't realize it is a flat volcanic crater.Anyway, it would be quite a nice walk close by other sightseeing places, but might look more impressive from opposite Udo, or from a plane or helicopter
If you enjoy walk , is fine. Good view, so natural . Specially the air & wind. Fresh and clean. Family and friends can snap a good photo for remember.

If the weather's bad come prepared.If the weather's good enjoy the views.Enjoyed my hike but it can be a bit of a highway at times dur to popularity.Cell phone tower on top of 2nd highest mtn was odd but hey, good coverage.

I wouldnt get out of my way to visit, but if you are in the area and enjoy gardens, you might want to visit.Outside, the japanese and korean gardens are lovely. The french and italian gardens are too kitschy for my taste. Inside, the water flower garden is especially nice. Make sure to take the elevator up to the   observation platform   -? if the weather is clear, you can get good views of Hallasan.

I went there early morning on a sunny day - perfect for photo-taking. The wonderful view of the sea from the walk down was just a prelude to the beauty that was to come later. I was delighted to see that little rainbow at the bottom! If you're more gutsy (and have a good sense of balance), you can make your way nearer to the waterfall to feel the cool mist and enjoy the grandeur and the surrounding scenery. Not a sight to be missed!!
I went during autumn but seams not many changes is leafs color at that time. love the view, flower garden, took tons of good photos.

I was very excited to visit Jeju; and this probably one of the most accessible place by Bus. There's actually public transport to this place (Yongduam Rock) from my accommodation. However, when I reached this place , i was busy looking for this legendary dragon head rock. Much to my disappointment, the rock doesn't seem to look like dragon head, you must really view it from the other side with your imagination.However, in order to reach to the other side, you need to climb all the way down the stairs, Not recommended for elderly. And if you notice carefully, you will spot alot of cockroach crawling around the rock, that totally freak me out!! Very big turn off if you spot the cockroach.the period I went was very crowded, probably around 5-6pm, This timing was quite a good timing for me, as I manage to catch a sunset. The sunset there was relatively awesome with the endless view of sea. If you can walk all the way down to those seafood stores, whereby you can enjoy fresh seafood hot pot + splendid view of sunset & sea!

I was thinking of skipping this attraction in favour of the natural attractions. Due to bad weather I visited this place on a whim but I enjoyed it better than expected. The building itself is quite pretty like a big greenhouse. The floral arrangement and landscaping is tasteful although not as good as Gardens by the Bay in Singapore. There are pretty sculptures dispersed through the compound. There are many different gardens to explore. We visited the indoor gardens first followed by taking the lift up to the top floor for a view of Seogwipo and lastly took the train for the outside gardens. It was too cold and windy to walk outside. There was some confusion about where to buy train tickets, the driver helped to walk to the counter and buy our tickets. Spring is probably a good time to visit since many flowers are in bloom. It would be good if they can stop the vandalism of the trees by the Koreans, many of them scratched their names on the branches.

I wanted to do this at sunrise but never woke up. So I went around 11h. Lots of tourists. It's all stairs to the top but not that hard. Takes 20 min in all. Beautiful view and scenery on top. There are some souvenirs and food shops at the bottom (Dunkin Donuts, Starbucks and cie).There is also a souvenir shop at half the moutain with beautiful engraved wood done by a woman there. I bought my most beautiful souvenir to her. She engraved Jeju, the date on it and wrapped it good for me. It's a short must do thing! You will get great pics there.

I walked 40 minutes from Jungan Rotary to this place. The ticket is 2000 won. When I was there, it was in the afternoon 4-5 PM, there were so many tourists. So it's difficult to get a good shot. I find there's nothing special about these waterfalls, back home I've seen bigger and higher than here. I visited this place because it was close to my guesthouse and I was also curious about it. I don't see people swimming on it. What I like about this is the view of the sea, I was sitting between those big rocks towards the sea and waiting for the sun to set. It was a good experience for enjoying the sunset with having a natural background sound from the waterfalls.

I visited 4 different beaches in Jeju. They all had their own charms but for popularity goes to Hyeopjae Beach becaue of good size and fantastic photogenic view. If you want calmer, smaller, less crowded and less windy beach, there is Kumnyoung beach right next to Hyeopjae beach. It is good for younger children to play. Hyeopjae beach was quite windy and cold. Of course Summer time would be different story. I was looking forward to riding transparent kayak but it was not operating in Apr. There was number on banner but no one answered.

I think I was deceived by the   Museum   term. If you expect an actual museum you'll be disappointed as the museum itself is really just one room. So I did feel like it was a bit of a scam... It's more of a premium flagship O'Sulloc store which sells tons of tea products and memorabilia. If you're into buying you'll have a good time but don't go there if you want to learn about tea or the history of tea. One redeeming quality of the place is that the building is nice and it has good views from the top.

I stayed at Ojo Haenyo Guesthouse area, hopped on a taxi to get to the port to Udo. The port is actually very near but I chose not to walk there. Paid less than KRW4000 for the taxi, cheap indeed.Bought a return ticket at less than KRW6000, ran towards the ferry that was about to leave for Udo, and in less than 30 minutes, we reached beautiful Udo. In case you're wondering, the ferry ride is too short to get motion-sickness :pIt rained during my short trip to this island so I didn't rent a bicycle. Instead, I got on the hop-on hop-off bus, the ticket was about KRW5000 or so. Super cheap. But the driver/tourist guide spoke only in Korean. But no worries, I did enjoy the tour.I managed to walk up to the lighthouse, had the famous peanut ice-cream overlooking a gorgeous view of the beach and a cliff, I also went to one of the beaches there. Udo is as gorgeous as Jeju. There are nice cafes with free wifis. Street food, local food, souvenirs; Udo is small but it has everything for visitors. Do wear good walking shoes, bring a ponco with you, and get on the last ferry if you can as this island is beautiful!!

I start my trekking 8.00AM at Gwanneumsa entrance and reach the summit around 12.30 and down to Seongpanak at 3.00PMPros : Magnificent various views(uphill), very easy downhillCons : No Hallasan view during uphillat this period, The weather is not so cold and the snow is still thick but robes and signs are intact. But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I read many negative review about this place from other travellers but for me, it was quite an interesting place with strange phenomena going on. My taxi driver brought me here on the way to Seongsan and he show me what is so mysterious about this road and it was indeed very strange. He stop the car at one end of the road and the car will automatically move up towards the slope (even when the car engine is not on). It was just an experience and one will not spend more than 10 minutes here. A good short trip before going to other places.

I must have chosen a very good day to visit Seongsan Ilchubong. When I arrived, there were practically a few dozens sightseeing buses there, tourists as well as students for school outing. The whole place, paths walking up the hill and down to the seashore, on the hill top, everywhere! was FULL of people walking, talking, taking pictures?§?o there as early as you can if you want to enjoy the view in a much relaxed way.

I might not have came at the right time to enjoy the view which was why I might not have enjoyed it that much? I arrived about 1 and the sun was so hot. Paid 5000 for entry ticket and climb to the TOP. The view was good but I felt not worth the sweat and effort haha. But upon making the way down, it is a must to go see the female divers who dive without any equipment to catch seafood like octopus. Their show time is at 3pm. Make sure to watch it.
I mean, its a decent bridge if you've got time to kill and want a good view, but I wouldn't go out of your way to see it.

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.

I found this to be the best attraction in Jeju. It really is a lot of stairs, so if you are not good in health condition, this might be very tiresome. But there are rest points a long the way, so you can take your time. There are little shops and restaurants around after you finish your hike. Beautiful views to take pictures both going up and down.

I could see coming here to relax a little, the view of the crater was nice enough but not like it was a whoa moment attraction. I might go bak though, there were some lovely picturesque spots and the pampas grasses were quite nice. An easy walk up of, so good for those of you (like me) who aren't p for the massive hike up the other big crater by the women divers museum.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.
I am thinking of driving up the mountain, where would be a good pit-stop to enjoy some view with snow?

I am not really good at hiking, but this is doable. In less than an hour, you can reach the top for magnificent views of the coastline. Too bad we missed the sunrise, but this hike is still worthwhile.

How often do you see hexagonal columns along the coastline? This is the place.We were there at about 6:30pm when they were almost closing. They close at 7pm. Although it was quite a rush, we managed to enjoy and soak in the scenery.The observation deck provides very good view of the columns. Be sure to read how the columns came about. It will make the views that much more interesting and meaningful.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Hiking Mt. Halla was on my bucket list for a long time and finally i did it. There is a time restriction and you cannot enter the gate before 6:00 am during the winter time. You have to pass 'Jindalaebat Shelter' before 12:00 pm to continuously hike up to the summit. The park keeper will not let up pass the gate of Jindalaebat if you arrive after the noon. It took about 2 or 3 hours to get to Jindalaebat from Seongpanak gate, and another 2 or 3 hours to get to the summit. It took me 4 hours to get to the Baekrokdam, and took another 5 hours to get down to Gwaneumsa temple. I highly recommend to hike from Seongpanak because it is easier to walk and you are too tired to look around. Then, walk down to Gwaneumsa direction which has a really good view and nature. (Gwaneumsa route is shorter, but definitely harder...super stiff)You will see many people lining up to take a photo with a monument, and I didn't understand why people want to take a photo with just a rock. I learned that you will get a certification of Mt. Hallasan hiking if you show the picture with the monument. All you need to do is go to the ticket office, pay 1,000 KRW and show the picture. I've seen many people hiking with sneakers, but I recommend wearing hiking boots since you have to walk on rocks for 8~9 hours. I heard that you need to be luck to see the summit because Hallasan is always foggy and cloudy. I was lucky and weather was just amazing!! I also heard that it is slightly easier to hike when it snows. There are buses that you can use and I strongly recommend hiking Mt. Halla!!!!!!!

Hexagonal shaped rock formations jutting out of the ocean that reminds me of the kryptonite crystals I once saw in an early Superman movie. Unusual and definitely 1 of the places to see if you are in Jeju. Entrance is KRW2000, 50% off if you are below 24 ? foreign ID accepted. Unfortunately, since the best view is only through a series of stairs which ends at a platform, weekend crowds in bus loads can be a nuisance for that desired background photos effect or even a selfie. And I was continuously concern about the strength of the viewing platform to hold so many people at any one time. I got there in a rented car and discovered fields of canola flowers up front for good picture taking.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hamdeok can be reached from airport by bus or taxi in 30 minutes. There are many hotels, convenient stores and restaurants in that area so We can get accommodation easily.We were staying at Ramada Hamdeok, about 1 km walking distance from the beach. Strolling at sunset time was very enjoyable. Nice weather, nice view, not too crowded. Just fine.We were hanging out until dinner time, took barbecued seafoods at outdoor table by the beach. To order the food and communicate need extra effort because we can only speak english, but the Resto staff can speak mandarin well. The food was good, drinking some soju and babunja make us warm...

Hamdeok beach is just so beautiful. It offers you black rocks, white sand, and breathtaking views. It was our first destination for the day after we landed in Jeju. I found the beach quite peaceful and calm. It is very near to Hallim park. Just took us about 2 mins to reach the park by a car. I wish we could spend some more time at the beach but we had to rush to our next destination. Good place to stop by and click some nice pics. Good luck!!! :)

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.
Good walk up to the top, windy & cooling during autumn (Nov 16). Enjoy a breathtaking view & good for nature lover. Great place to relax your mind.

Good for an afternoon, you can learn lots about the women and how they shaped/ built Jeju. There are dioramas, videos, clothing throughout the history. I learnt a lot. Worth a view if you are in the area.

Good for a walk as it is easy walking with limited stairs and if the weather is good, the peace surrounding the ocean views is rewarding. Can be very busy with tourists and if the weather is windy or wet, then find another place to visit. Some small markets? around the area to visit.

Getting to the crater was after a 20 minutes steep climb upwards via a rocky road made up of bumpy rocks. The steps got smaller, higher and steeper as you move higher up the crater. The view was amazing as you climb, and was breathtaking when you get to the top. The timing of the sunrise varies daily but the top may get a little crowded, so it?s advisable to climb up a little earlier to secure a good position. The way down was via another route, but this time, with proper stairway. It leads to another cliff of the just at the side of the bottom of the crater. You can either take the stairs down the cliff to the bottom where it?s closer to the seashore or you may go up the cliff and then make your way back to the entrance.

For those who are not really into long hikes and yet still want a good panaromic view of Jeju?s surroundings, this is the place. There are also live performances apparently involving the female divers but we missed the timing.

First and foremost, bring good walking shoes. You will need to hike up the hill to have a good view. There are many stalls at the base of the hill, before you pay to go into the entrance. As this location is near the sea, it is rather windy. A windbreaker may be required depending the time of the year you are travelling.Lots of toilets around, so there's no worry about needing it.There are many tourists as well as locals visit this scenic spot. Bring you camera as well. Note: This location is open depending on weather.

Ferry ride from seongsan port was 11,000 W for 2 people and only took about 15 minutes.  There's a really good review by katja below, so I won't go in depth.  If you don't have a lot of time, take a scooter or ATV.  We had a lot of fun cruising around this island on ATV!!   As soon as you get off the ferry there are two places to rent from - ATV was 20,000 W for 2 hours; Scooter was 10,000 W for 2 hours.  If you stop several places you'll be pushing 2 hours but can definitely get it done.  Can be a little difficult navigating if you cannot speak or read Korean.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Excellent view especially at sunrise. Hiking was good for a beginner level. Many places to stop and take a rest if needed. If not an experienced hiker, it takes maybe 40 minutes to get up to the top. No entrance fee if you go super early. Lots of lovely places around to grab coffee or some food after you hike down as well. I would do this again in a heartbeat!

Excellent view and atmosphere! A long steep (with stairs) and challenging climb up the inactive volcanic island mountain that earns you good exercise and satisfaction! You can already enjoy the picturesque surroundings at the foot of the mountain with different views and you can buy some souvenir there and also enjoy a short horse ride (not free of course). If you are there on a sunny day, do buy some popsicle or ice-cream to go up.   There are entrance fees for the entrance as well. However, it is well worth it once you reached the top. It is fantastic to be on top looking down to the inactive volcano crater and enjoy the view of the sea that looks like touching the sky. You can literally feel like you are touching the sky too! The best time to go there will be during sunrise! Don't forget to take a selfie with the mountain height indicator board to boast your achievements! Oh, and just right before you reach the top, please take a look at the back downhill at the interesting look of the city below and take a selfie and also take some nice selfie around you.     On the way down, there is the fishing village where the you can enjoy the seafood while watching the women divers catch clamps and oyster. There are some fiexed timing but I have already forgotten the timing.    Seongsan Ilchulbong is indeed a must visit destination everytime you arrive in Jeju!

review: The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.
Overall..this museum is good if we go with family due to my visit this time is for business tour..so just enjoy take photo and buy some souvenir for my kids.

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.
