There are plenty of bus for the first leg, but the 2nd bus no. 990 there are only 2 or 3 available in a day and the next one for us like 2 hours away, so the few people/tourists that was there with us decided to walk to the destination for about 3 kilometers. When we got there sweaty and tired we pay the cheap fare of KW2,000 (mind you cheap attraction). The good thing is the cool breeze inside the cave, mind your steps because its wet and some puddle of waters in there. Many people in there, mostly Korean tourists. The few inside the dimly lighted cave is not impressive neither beautiful as I thought. When we got out at about 4:30 pm. we happened to catch the bus no. 990, to our surprise the bus driver told us to get out of the bus while he let the Korean passengers in. We asked why and he keep telling us taxi..taxi..taxi.. So apparently, he does not take foreigners to go to the next bus stop and forced us to take taxi, sure enough, a taxi driver in the area approached us. I felt so discriminated by the bus driver, we didn't even want to negotiate with the taxi driver (because, I believe they do this on purpose). We decided to walk back 3 km. to the next bus stop. It was a waste of almost a day of our time, definitely not recommended to visit this place, NOW I KNOW WHY IT'S CHEAP!

We went there after a typhoon so beach was a little mixed up. It was a bit too windy for comfortable swimming, but all in all the cafes around the place and the atmosphere on the beach were good. And it was easy to get there from jeju city with buses. We visited in the beginning of October and it was still warm enough for just relaxing on the beach.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre. We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000\ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

We walked past Yongdu-am rock when we were trying to find the jimjilbang that we were staying at for the night. If we had made any effort to go and see it I would have been bummed but since it was in passing it was interesting in its own manner. I can understand how it looks like a dragon and you don't need TOO much of an imagination to be able to see it but unless your interested in folklore/'the dragon' means anything to you, you won't be overly excited/impressed.If it didn't have reams of tourists and tour buses or the tourist shops all around it Im not sure I would have even stopped to take a picture.(the ladies working in the tour information centre right outside of this area speak good english and are very kind and helpful if you need directions)

we tried to take bus and ferry ourselves to visit Udo. The weather on that day was very good, there were a lot of geographical scenes in Udo, beaches were beautiful, besides taking bus for seeing the whole island, take a walk along the seaside was also very good.  eating seafood in a famous restaurant, also tried the famous peanut ice cream of this island.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took a relaxing stroll through a beautiful forest Bijraim Nutmeg Forest. The shade of the forest is perfect for a hot summer day. It's a beautiful small forest, but getting there was a bit time-consuming, involving a bus ride from Jeju City and some brief hitch-hiking. (We were to take a second bus, but we waited so long that decided to hitch a ride instead.) However, from Bijraim, there is a bus that takes you directly to the popular Manjanggul, so it's a good idea to visit both in the same day.

We took a cab from Ramada Plaza for 30,000 wan. It took about half an hour. The bus home 710 was great and took an hour. 3000 wan. The island was good fun. We cycled the island stopping along the way to see things. The elder diving women were really cool. Sad to see the garbage around from the sea :( Udo is in such a highly populated area of the world garbage is a big problem. It makes me want to really try to become green at home in Canada.

We read how good the pork belly was and from what we read, recommendations were to go to  Hwaro Hyang instead of Dumbedon. We arrived, dropped our bags, took a taxi to get there to make sure we experience what everyone is raving about. Hwaro Hyang was not too crowded and we easily got a table. The server explained that we should get the set for a couple to be able to taste a good sample of the cuts and some abalone. That we did. We got the platter, he dropped it on the hot plate and that was the last time our server came to our table. We saw how he was going around to all the other tables, turning their food over, cutting it up. Finally, we saw this lady who was serving another table and we flagged her down to see who might help us. She had to yell and call/force a young person to help us. I?ll chalk it to a language barrier issue as they were busily chatting with the rest of the customers. Finally the boy cut up our food, and we had to help ourselves and towards the end, the lady came back to turn off our hot plate. The experience would have been enhanced if we had known how to pair the condiments. We didn?t want to offend anyone so we watched as they showed the other tables how to eat the food and just mimicked them. They even did the lettuce wraps for some tables to show them how the side dishes are rolled. So moral of the story, unless you?re local or can speak with them conversationally, prepare to be ignored and just watching to see how others do it.

We reached the ferry terminal at 11am and waited for a short while for the ferry. The ferry depart quite frequently so there is no worry for that. As mentioned by other people, you will need to bring your passport to purchase a ticket. If you intend to rent a motorised vehicle in Udo, you will need to bring along your international driving permit. We rented a covered motorised scooter for 3h at KRW40,000. The scooter has doors and can seat 2 people. It took us less than 2.5h to cover the whole island, we even took 45min lunch break in between. The entire island is around 17km, so if you intend to make stopovers for photo taking, renting for 2h will be good enough. Just follow the coastline and you won't get lost. I highly recommend travellers to opt for the motorised scooter for a relaxing trip around Udo island. It will take you just half day. There are not many cars on the road but there are many scooters and bicycles which share the same path. There are many tourists and they might not observe the driving rules very well, so do be careful when driving on the roads. However, if you intend to see some of the other sights on Udo, they are not accessible for these transportation as you will need to take a separate ferry to go there. There seems to be many people taking the shuttle bus in Udo, so I don't really recommend people to do so if you have an international driving permit.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We felt peacefulness in this place even if it is next to a main road. The entry fee is only 1000 won and clean facilities.From Seogwipo bus station take bus 700 for 1500 won each way.The building in the Korean style are well maintain and the climb all the way to the grotto is a good exercise. The golden Buddha sit up there under the dripping mountain. People collect the water for? believe of power, may be like Christian for Easter water..Well! Each are different, Friday for the Jews, Saturday the Muslim, Sunday the Christians, everyday for Buddhas...

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.
Very good place,beautifull,amazing,you won't say sorry if you come here.easy to find it,bus stop in front of temple.

Very easy to go from Jeju city.. We took a bus and the time is less than 30mins for sure... Beside osulloc so good to visit both places same time.Did not try the soap making as the place is pretty small and it was pack then.. We ate at the cafe. Pretty layout, the ice is so so.. The food is nice thou.. The food is IG ready anytime, worth to make a trip there..

Very cute little island, great for 1 day trip.  It's too big to do it by walking, but you can rent scooter (only with international driving license), bicycle or to take hop in hop out bus. There are 2 kinds of busses: one that makes only 4 stops (3000 KRW) and another that goes all around the island (5000 KRW). I think the one that makes only 4stops is good enough, as the rest you can do by walking. We took the hop in hop off bus for 5000 KRW, but we used it only 3 times, the rest we walked around. Enjoy your time there!

Udo was the best place in my jeju visit. although the weather was very hot, but its windy too. My hat even blow off by the wind. The sea and sand were just too beautiful. its really a relaxing place when seeing the green grasses dancing all over in front of you. Besides, the zha jiang mian was really tasted good. it costed 8000won. the peanut icecream was famous too, 3000won. We sent a whole morning there. In the island, we can take bus, rent bicycle or scooter.

Udo was formed by an volcanic eruption in the 12th century. We took the ferry boat then signed up for a on/off bus tour and it was worthwhile. The bus stopped at 6 different locations to include three beaches (black sand, gold sand and white sand), near the large volcanic mountain that is the hump that makes up Udo (you can walk up  to the top but given the limited visibility, we  didn't), the Udo Museum (free if you are taking the on/off bus), and Biyang-dong (a small island off of Udo). Because of the weather we did not swim at the beaches but the other attractions were worthwhile, especially Biyang-dong. We were told that because of the rain there weren't the crowds that you normally have on Udo. There are plenty of good restaurants as well. If the weather had permitted, we would have rented bicycles and  ridden around the island (apx 14 KM). I would plan for just over a half day.Costs: Ferry apx 10,000 won per person round tripBus tour: apx 6,000 won per per person (one complete circuit)

Udo was beautiful but our Korean two (2) hour tour wasn't sufficient. Apparently taxi's are hard to come by on this SMALL island. We would have liked to eaten elsewhere besides the port but our Volcano Rice & Pork resto was equally fun & good, near the bus drop off & Keith Harding mural. Hard to miss... enjoy

Udo is a small island just off Jeju island and is a 15min ferry ride. Once you are there you can hike, hire a bike or get on a round island hop-on hop-off bus which are quite frequent.The island is a lava plateu but some beaches have golden sand or white coral sand.The island is lush and green and is apparently very fertile.As it is touristy, prices can be high but it is definitely worth a visit if it is a good day.Give yourself plenty of time.

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

Tour companies love this tourist trap because it add a good few lines to their tourist brochure while being totally costless for them and wasteful for us.If you can, ask your guide to just pass this, getting back to the hotel staring at your ceiling is better than this.My guide made it worse since he was totally excited of this place, yet when I get there, even before we stop, I look outside the bus to the row of trees and can see the reason behind   the mystery road   and I was   hmmm...lame, can we just move on  . But the guide insist that we spend our expensive time on this thing and my group members want to agree with him.And since I already see the row of tree and how the optic illusion would work, the optic illusion (which is weak) dissipates for me. Ask your guide to go somewhere else.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

To get to this island, one has to fill in a form and pay for the fees. All is convenient and easy peasy. Then, the ferry ride is quick. We opted for a bus tour. The tour was in Korean and we couldn't understand a thing but considering it is one of the easiest method to get around the island,we just go along with it. We would like to ride one of those adorable scooters but we don't own an international license. Overall a good experience.

This was a very interesting Lava Tube cave.  There were signs in English as well as various other languages describing what you were looking at.  The signs were informative.  The cave is cool, so I recommend a zippered sweatshirt or windbreaker.  Also, the floor of the cave is uneven, so you definitely want to have good walking shoes.  I was just fine wearing old jogging shoes.  We went as part of a guided tour - I would have liked to spend just a little more time there, but that's how it goes on bus tours...  There may be more beautiful caves, but overall, it was the nicest cave I've been in - very nice Lava Tube - you will enjoy it.

This was a great beach and was easy to get to with a bus station right on the corner. Entrance was lined with a variety of vendors and there was a supermarket, well stocked in case you forgot something. There were many stores and restaurants nearby to quench your post-swim hunger. The beach was quite nice, water felt great and overall was pretty clean. The shower/bathroom area wasn't that good, but we didn't expect it to be.

This road is interesting! When we are about to reach the site, the driver turned off the engine, and yet the bus is moving upwards!! Amazing!We even went down the bus to try running backward on the road, and one can feel like you are being pulled from the back. Also, we try by pouring water onto the road itself, which is a good test.And yes, the food stall along the road is more interesting.

This road is have trick optical, whick look like up hill but actually down hill. All the bus and car turn off their engine in the down, but the car n bus can move to the top of the road like climb without machine, but that acttualy just optical trick. Many place like this in the world, but Jeju goverment use that as a attraction, very good idea.

This place will be good for nature lovers and those who are in Jeju to relax and get away from busy city life. It only takes 1hour to cover the area at a slow pace. You may get a chance to see autumn foliage here from mid to late Nov as there are quite a number of maple trees in the forest. (Note: Autumn is mild in Jeju, while northern parts of Korea are having colourful autumn foliage, we hardly see any colourful trees in Jeju till we came to Bijarim forest)

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.
This is a lovely waterfall, but try to avoid the peak season otherwise it's a bit busy.  Beautiful how the water flows right next to the sea.  Good for a paddle as well.

There are 3 mazes in this park which you are encouraged to try all of them. There were buses of students visiting the maze land when we were there. the kids were good in the mazes and we simply followed them to get out of the mazes. There are also a 'tower' where the teachers made sure the kids don't get into accidents while playing in the mazes. Pretty amazing and fun to spend some time there. But will not return again as we have completed all 3 mazes. Unless, they expand and created a few more, then will consider visiting again the next time I go Jeju.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The trip ti Mt Halla is great and do not miss it. Youu really should start early, and it takes a little less than recommended times, about one hour less if you walk clow but continuously.We walked three 15, 30 and 55, two males - my son and me and one female accompanied us.We traveled by bus from Seogwipo, busses go every 15-30 minutes since early morning to Seongpanak - busstop.Back we walked to Gwaneumsa and there is no direct bus connection, but take a taxi (for 5 thous WON) or walk about 5 km. We finaly shared taxi with very kind Korean directly to Seogwipo, thank again to the kind man. It was good and exhausting and we slept nicely after all. The next day we were ready to walk again. Unfortunatelly was very cloudy and walked upon clouds finally, however it was June, it was not too hot. There are two springs along the way - one up and nexd on the way down. Recommended to every who travels with teenagers:) Normal hiking shoes like trainers were OK, dont worry.

The market is 60% local 40% tailored to tourist, hence depending on what you are after you can choose the part that suits your expectation.It is the local fresh meat , fish and vegetable market--fresh goodies are sold at a very reasonable price and exceptional quality. The touristic part is nice also-- lot of old aunties promoting the snacks, personally i dont think that's the most authentic souvenir so we decided to go to the pottery shop and ending up buying soup copper pot and stone pot back (though it's heavy) as it did remind us a lot more about the trip.The fresh snack stands are very busy and people are elbow to elbows. Food was yum but probably you don't wonna spend more than 2 hours there. Btw, there is a night food market outside after 5 pm and it's worth grabbing a snack or two.

The main attraction of the beach is the inclusion of a somewhat historic public bath.  As it was November and no one was using the public baths, I was able to get into the public baths for a look.  Don't worry, you're not missing out on much as the public baths were not very impressive in size or scope.  I can imagine these public baths would be very busy in the summer when the weather is more appropriate.The beach itself is good - there is plenty of sand so I could imagine people swimming in the sea near the beach in the summer.  However, there are some rocks there as well for people to walk around.All in all, it's a typical beach - nothing to write home about.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The island is windy. Quite convenient to go around as there's shuttle bus with blue and red route that bring you around the island. The bus driver will narrate in Korean to explain the places, although we don't understand but is a fun trip to go along with mostly korean. The field grows full of canola flowers (yellow), very beautiful. Also, with nice cliff with plunging waves, good place to take pictures. The water is clear blue at the beach. Unfortunately, we only planned for half day trip so we can only complete the blue route. So, best to plan for a day as it probably takes you full day to admire the scenery.

The hot springs have a good reputation and are very popular amongst Koreans. There is a large indoor area, separated of course for male and female, and then an outdoor area with 4 small pools the size of a hot tub and one larger lap pool which has cold spring water. Out of the 4 smaller pools 3 have hot water, 1 has cold water.The overall condition of the outdoor pools is quite shocking actually and I was surprised. In Korea almost everything is well maintained and in good condition, at these hot springs the paint coating came off at the pools, the pool furniture was old and falling apart, just very surprised to see it in this poor condition. It was busy nevertheless. There is a mix of couples and families, kids running around, people talking loudly, so it is not really serene and peaceful as a hot spring should be. The bathing experience was good, very relaxing, no doubt, but the overall experience was mediocre.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The beach is beautiful on a sunny day - calm, clean, safe and relaxing. Suitable for couples or family with seniors/kids. We got there by bus no. 10 from the city. Very convenient with good facilities. You pay a small fee to shower otherwise the usual toilets are available if you just want to have a change of clothes. If it rains there are plenty of cafes to take shelter at.We spent a few hours at the beach in the afternoon and had a seafood banquet for dinner at one of the many restaurants close by during sunset.

The beach has beautiful, clear emerald waters (the pictures doesn?t do the place justice as its much better experienced in person), and a really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries. We got there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. Near the beach there are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice. Easy to hail a taxi there too for those who wants to travel to their next location  by cab. Parking lots available too for those who are driving.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

The beach has beautiful, clear  waters, and really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries and tea.We went there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. There are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice near the beach . Easy to get a taxi there too. Parking lots are available too.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Stone park is a must see one. It has big outdoor. There are a lot of big stone shapes. This park is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park and Eco land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places.

So we went to Hallasan but didn't have much time, so we've decided to do the yeongsil train until the shelter and then go back the other way (eorekon? Haha). It was about 2hours each ways so 4 hours total. The mountain is free but to get there it's either a bus from Jeju city hall or a taxi (about 27.000 won - 25???). You have to be there before 12:00 pm otherwise it's closed. Really good activity, winter time so there was snow, pretty cool!!But wear good shoes and some coat because it's super windy there !I recommend it 100 times.

Seriously, this rock simply had a good marketing team that created a story and a good image of this rock.. Bus visually you can find so much more interesting rocks in any other place of the Jeju island

Really great to see and well maintained. Wonderful visit. Went on a rainy day and it was still a pleasant experience. The bus to the cave is very slow and infrequent so you either have to walk or take an expensive taxi which is inconvenient, but otherwise very good

quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.

Pretty much everything in Jeju is available here. Within the city, easily accessible via car, taxi, bus. There's the traditional market, seafood market, fruits & veggies, night market (6pm onwards). However the zones seem kinda grey cos clothes shop can be next to fish shop, snack shop next to shoe shop, you get the picture. We bought some dried seafood, snacks, fruits. Then popped over to the underground mall. Good place for those wanting to shop and see everything in 1 spot.

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.
Pretty good stuff for an accessible waterfall. The surrounds are pleasant, it's cheap to get in, but it's  busy in the summer months.

Our plans to visit Hallasan were foiled by a typhoon the night before (we luckily still got to go, though), and we were all excited to do a nice hike. We came here probably 2 or 3 hours before the park closed (we did some other sightseeing instead of Hallasan, this happened to be close by), and the admission was free because the typhoon had caused some damage. Anyways, because of the typhoon and the time of day, the park wasn't very busy. It felt like we had the walking paths to ourselves most of the time (we chose one of the shorter routes because we didn't want to run out of time). It was a nice, easy, relaxing walk. It was also dead quiet except for the occasional group of ladies walking by with music playing on their phone's speaker. Oh and the crows going off every now and then, but that was kind of amusing since their call is funny to me (and different from North American crows). A good alternative if you can't go up some of the steeper stairs and stuff like in Hallasan. We got plenty of beautiful photos because the typhoon the night before gave all the woods a nice, moody atmosphere. If you like going for walks in the woods (even though these are all wooden paths), just being outdoors enjoying the fresh air, and you have enough time, this is worth a visit. If you are short on time and can only do one park or something, then make sure you try to at least go to Hallasan. I would definitely recommend this park over Hallasan though if you have any mobility issues, because the wooden paths are very easy to walk on and there doesn't seem to be a lot of uphill/stairs.

One of the many very interesting sites in Jeju Island.  These women would dive for 2 minutes at a time to harvest food from the ocean bottom, using no tanks or other equipment.  They were the only known groups of women who resisted during the Japanese occupation.  Also good access by bus.  Easy to get there by bike, depending on where you are staying on the Island. NIce bike paths, though often are covered with the drying sea weed that the old women still harvest from the rocks. There is also a very small Buddhist temple with a Quan Yin statue in front, about a half mile to the west along the coast.

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Love the walk. Advisable to use a pair of good shoes as the ground can be slippery. Very dark and cold. Difficult to reach by bus. Usually there will be taxis at the nearest bustop. Advisable to take taxi there from the nearest bustop. After the experience, do take some time to sit at the nearest cafe. Should try the Orange Freeze!

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

It?s a very big place.. there are a cave, garden, mang kind of birds, trees ans flowers.. i think it is a good place to visit in jeju.. you can see many things here.. but it is difficult to find a bus to here and the bus is not ontime..

It was an impressive sight. If you wear appropriate shoes/trainers and get close to the waterfall, you can get a bit wet. But you have to be prepared to walk on big and, sometimes, round rocks. Tip: Get there early. It was our first stop and we were glad. As we were leaving (around 10am), buses full of tourists were arriving. It would have been quite impossible to take good pictures without getting someone's head in them because the staircase is not that wide.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

It is located just beside O'Sulloc Tea Museum. To get there, just take bus no.755 from any bus stop bound for Pyonghwa-ro global education and alight at O'Sulloc Tea Museum station.They sell cosmetics, skin care products, stationaries, D.I.Y soap, etc..There are also cafe which sells bingsu, beverages and food. Tried the 珥덉퐫荑좏궎?먯씠?? (choco cookie shake), it costs 6000 won and tastes good but I think the portion is a little small (for me). Nice to visit if you are visiting O'Sulloc Tea Museum since it is just beside it. There is a big tea farm beside Innisfree Jejuhouse.. you can take some pics there, but it was raining when i visited the place so i didn't manage to take a lot of pictures.

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

If you were to Seongsan Ilchulbong and to Manjang cave next, you can grab the taxi if there is no bus.. The fare is quite reasonable.Wouldnt expect that the cave would be that cold but it is as cold as Seoul during Spring time.. The lighting is very good. Though it is  a long walk to the end, it id worth it.. The deeper, the colder it is..

If you are travelling with small kids, i suggest to drive a car into the island. (They allow car to enter the island if having kids below 6 years old), really regret that we park our car at the multi storey parking, with all the high hope to rent a electric scooter (the one with 3 wheels)The electric scooter is strictly for 2 person only (they dont allow 2 adult + 1 baby too)Only those with Class A international license allow to rent the electric scooter (i am a Class B international license holder (allowed to drive car only)If you plan to travel the island by bus, it will waste lots of time on queueing and waiting for the bus. The bus driver will not explain any tourist spot in english, so you will have a hard time to decide which is the good spot to get down from the bus.Overall the island has nothing special with we are not allow to ride the electric scooter and generally the island is too crowded with tourist.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. There's also an outdoor gardens with bear exhibits, fountain and lake and a blooming grapefruit tree. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. Get your tickets cheaper via taobao, the China online shopping site. They have almost 50% discount for foreigners, which we tapped on. Just need to print our confirmation and entry was a breeze. Also, this place is accessible via a bus from Jeju intercity bus terminal. Stop at jungmun resort. Nearby are alive musuem, yeomiji botanical gardens and cheonjiyeon waterfalls, good for a self planned one day trip.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called   Orum   in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I got the bus here from Jungmun - a couple of hours in total but it was worth it. Really good value, lots to look at, peaceful place to walk around, beautifully done and looked after. There weren't many other people there so it felt as if I had the place to myself. I had lunch in the restaurant and that was also good. Make sure you take your camera. Hugely recommended.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Good to go if you have not been to a cave before. Be prepared to walk though. Into the cave and out takes about 50mins including taking photos and reading the signboards. If u r taking bus 701, stop at manjanggul stn n take a cab.it is only 1.7km so shld cost u 2800won. But taxi driver will ask for 4000won.
good facility,many store and warm when winter season its the best place for shopping at Jeju.nearby to dongmun market and its easy to go by bus

Good experience, but not so special as there are some other place in my home country that seems similar to it. We are on a group tour, upon reaching the road our driver stopped the engine, the bus continued running, the tourguide did some explanation, something about magnetic features of the area, if you will look around its just like an ordinary road.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

For the ones who believe they are in good shape:Why struggle, why do it the hard way? because it is much more scenic and maybe only one tenth of climbers going that way. Taxi from town to starting point (approx 20 min) was 11.000 won on taximeter from my hotel in Nohyung-dong (near the int. airport) or take the bus but only on sat and sundays). Bus stop at Seongpanak when you come down from the mountain on the road. Check schedule and bus no. Taxi back 20.000 won (not on meter..)This is by far the most important place to look before you set out. THE WEATHER! http://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Hallasan/forecasts/1950 I wouldn't call my self an experienced climber but I did it in 3h10min up and 2h down. This is in a pace where I overtook and was not overtaken, and very short breaks, maybe only 2 min in total 5 times. The track is changes between rocks or stairs, I think it's well kept. Two toilet stations up and two down. None at the top. Bring 3-4L of liquids minimum, no passport nor entry is needed for the mountain (aug 2013). A windbreaker for the summit can be nice to have. The weather can change every minute so rain is likely. I did it in old worn-out runners. Bring food and nutrition - no shops. Good luck and enjoy

For people who loves green tea, can check out the variety of green tea products they have; it's nice to 'chill-out' at the yard with hot beverage in hand.It will be good for the kids to try out their self made soap and they felt very good with their artwork. However, if you would to make your purchase at Innisfree, please do note that they DO NOT give out any free samples or gifts for your purchases (even thou I've purchased about KRW500,000 worth of products) unlike those in Seoul or Busan, they are very generous with their samples and gifts with purchase.

Eco land has big landscape. Inside there are 4 trains station. A small train that drops people in all station, after reaching a station, people can look around and get into next train. One part is good for children, since there are kids house, kids coffee shop(miniature), fire station (miniature), bank(miniature), movie theatre(miniature) . This whole place is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park, Sangumburi Crater  and stone land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places. Usually if you taxi for using between 9 AM to 5 PM, you will have to pay 120,000 KRW.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.

review: Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

Basicallu it's a small island, so we can walk / rent bicycle - motorcycle - small car / hop on bus to get around. Almost no activities. Just stop by here n there to take picture, buy ice cream, dine, etc. If you just want to relax and embrace the beautiful nature around, this is a good place. Our family rent bicycle 10.000 won per bicycle. It took us 4 hours to go around the island slowly.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

As a child I was a big Hello Kitty fan and thought it would be nice to visit this place, after seeing it at the airport. Getting here is really easy from the main bus terminal. I did not know what to expect when I got here. But when I got there I noticed it was $12,000 won to get in. But once you are inside there is nothing special about the place to be charging so much. Its just a bunch of halls with Hello Kitty pictures and some random facts. On the second floor there is a Cafe, that is also overpriced and over crowded. Almost impossible to get a good seat. Service is not great. They not only took forever to take my order, I was the only one in line, but also to give me what I had ordered. The gift shop is also an overpriced place with not a lot of options. Knowing what I know now I dont think I would have done this place.

Although we went in the evening when some stalls are closed the place is quite vibrant nonetheless. If you hire a taxi for the day ask the driver to drop you off here. We kind of regretted we didn't as the taxi we hired went overtime and we were a bit tired. We took a bus at 1200 won from Jeju City (500) and it was a long and crowded trip as it had to pass through the airport first. Definitely worth a visit. Nothing much to buy other then tangerines (sold in bags of about 12 to 13) and jeju orange chocolates which you can find in Seoul. You can see the live seafood such as abalone, octopus, fishes etc. Also enjoy food such as gimbap, oden, tteoboki, fried stuff, blood sausages etc. There is also a stall selling orange jam filled cookie in the shape of the stone grandfather. Tastes good when eaten warm.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

we went on a rainy day & late (about 5pm) which they close at 7pm. many area closed due to our late entry but at least we got a 20% discount for the tickets. tulips are beautiful. the caves inside are nice too (good to get some shade from the rain). but pity I didn't manage to visit the cherry blossom garden because it was near to 7pm already which the cherry blossom garden is supposed to be the last stop.

We stopped by this place mainly to try tea but ended up buying so many gifts for our friends and families. Tea cosmetics and other souvenirs are pretty good here. Don't forget to check out the tea farm on the opposite site.

We paid our entrance fees and simply stayed on the top to get some good pictures. There were hordes of people down below so I don't recommend taking a long walk down and then back up just to get some pictures of other tourists.

We enjoy the visit. The place looks magical. We couple enjoy it and so thus our young adult kid and 9 year kid. Each of the stop is worth the visit. There are coffee shop and snacks in each of the stop.The best stop is the last stop wherein there are so many beautiful flowers fully landscape and so good to take pictures. We visited autumn. The place is clean the restrooms are clean. I love their coffee its worth the visit.

We didn't have to pay for admission so I guess it's a relaxing place to stop over a drink as there is Nothing much to see. we bought some tea leaves and cookies as gifts. The green tea cookies is good!

We are glad that we have our wonderful tour guide was with us thus we were able to gain better understanding n knowledge about the green tea n it's plantation.The museum itself actually showcase the different type of green tea products (including facial products) so it's a shopping paradise for some.  There are free sampling of the green tea however we like the cafe most. Though a little pricey but the green tea yogurt ice cream n also the green tea milk ice cream is yummy (it has strong green tea taste).As it was crowded when we were there the cafe seemed to be under stocked for the crowd.  A friend managed to get herself green tea macaron n said it taste superb.A good stop over for some retail therapy n tea break n photo taking.

This was our last stop in Jeju. We arrived right after sunset and were able to walk around the island and enjoy the beautiful nature area and then walk back over the bridge while it was lit up. Good activity for young children to just get out and run. Best of all it was free! There is also a free public restroom in the parking lot.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.
