review: this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

This is a very beautiful location and in a good location. You can visit here for any length of time that you would like. It is great for a quick stop on the way to other attractions on the south side of the island. Don't miss this one. Even if you have many other things to do there is time to put this on the list.

There is nothing much here at the museum but the green tea ice cream and the green tea cake roll are fabulous! The green tea cake roll sold out in a very short period of time! We reached there at around noon time and we were so lucky that we took the second last roll! I guess the cake roll is pretty popular among the locals too as we saw a lot of locals stopping by at the cafe. I saw an O'Sulloc Cafe at Myeongdong too. We went in the morning and there were still quite a few of green tea cake rolls there. I wanted to get a cake roll the night before I flew back to Singapore (in order to maintain the freshness) but the staff told us that it has been sold out! The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. Other than food you can go all the way to the third floor to take some photos. Personally I feel that the scenery outside of the building is much more nicer. There's a big park right in front of the tea museum there are people who lie down and chill on the grass. There's tea plantation located opposite of the tea museum. We are allowed to wander around there for more pretty photos.

There is a long steep path in order to reach the lighthouse on top. But that shouldn't be a problem as the scenery along the road is empowering your feet to work. In the middle of the path  there is a candy house like building. But unfortunately  it was reconstructing at that moment. So  I bought a chocolate ice cream beside the reconstruction to settle my unhappiness. The ice cream tastes unexpectedly good  it is rich in chocolate and smooth when I put it into my mouth. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the lighthouse  we took several pictures there  but no one is perfectly taken because of strong wind  our hair flowing like crazy  so we didn't spend much time on the lighthouse.We took about 30 minutes there and didn't have a chance to visit the building at that time  so I strongly recommend you to go there at autumn or spring and plan more than half an hour if you are deciding to visit there.

There are lockers for you to keep your bags in. You have to change and shower in the gender-designated shower areas before you put your spa outfits (shorts and a shirt) on and head to the sauna area (where both men and women are). Try the steam and sauna rooms for a good sweat (you can bring your phones in if you want to listen to music). Be prepared for crowds of tourist though as this seems to be a popular stop for large tour groups.

the sun came up around 630am when I was there.. start hiking 430am got a good seat (rought 50minutes to reach the top).. it start getting crowded when is near 630am... the top is under contruction to extent the seatings.
The green tea ice cream is good and I enjoyed the hallabong O tea ice that the top not cream but ice cream. Delicious. A good place to shop for authentic tea in Jeju .

The attraction consists of a tea museum a cafe and a tea field. If you have been to Seoul you will notice that there are other O'Sulloc Tea houses in Seoul minus the tea field. We had the green tea ice cream here and it was good but pricey. The tea field itself was great for photos but it is not all that different from other tea fields you see across Asia. I don't think this is a must-see attraction but it is great as a pit stop if you are passing through the area.

Since it is October it is a bit too cool to swim but there were some people in the water.  The beach was empty.  The temperature was only around 24 but it t was a beautiful day.  There are a lot of places to grab a coffee or have a meal.  Good place to stop off on a round the island drive!

Our first time in Shinhwa World theme park visit in December 2017. One must come with the understanding that the theme park is not yet fully developed but it has some nice rides and you can spend a few hours there . My kids had a wonderful time . Since it is new  the park is not crowded. We had lunch at the food court and it was good Korean food . We were initially disappointed when the rides were suspended due to the snow. However the rides were resumed quickly after the snow stopped. We happened to have met the theme park Manager Mr Mason Kang when we ran into communication difficulty with one of the staff attending to the ride . He was very kind to explain to us that the rides would resume soon after they dry the area . His professionalism impressed us .  Our theme park experience was a great one . My kids tried the ice skating ring within the theme park compound . Everything is new and clean . We will come again ! They are going to have a Water theme park probably year after .

Nicely done up place very organise. Good stop for green tea ice cream and cake. Good range of tea pots and cups displayed. Well written history of tea drinking in Korea.Good for photo takings.Free sampling of tea and explanation (although mostly in Korean).
Nearby the lava cave so we stopped by. The size of maze is smaller than expected but good enough for young kids. There's plenty of cats outside the maze entrance which my girl loves.

Majority of tourists are fascinated by this mysterious road as all drivers will put it on neutral gear and you find the car moving to everyone's delight.A short stop is given and you can have a good photo shoot of it and its surrounding sights.

Made a quick stop here and found it mostly overrated and not that special. There were an abundance of tourists around. One thing I did enjoy is the green tea ice-cream. Also taste tested the Jeju mandarin flavoured tea which you can buy from the gift/tea shop. Overall a good place to stop at for a quick break if you are on the way to other attractions around the island.

I've heard there are just two countries in the world now with women divers like Jeju. It is  historical and a good museum to think about different things you may not really have chance to even imagine in practical city life. I wouldn't say a must go destination but definitely a stop by if you are near by.

It's a good stop if you're in the area. I get the feeling there's much more to do around but it was raining. Anyways it's cheap and easy to access. It's also right in the city so ot won't require you to travel far. Really nice spot for photos.

It was so close to being excellent reason I did not rate it as excellent is because the 3D movie was closed due to covid so obviously could not comment on that. Only other thing to add was the animal enclosure at the top of the park was rather smelly and did need a good clean out however the parrot/parakeet aviary section was amazing and very clean. The park is excellent value and you could spend the whole day here with the kids providing that you bring a packed lunch.

It was pouring and we needed something to do.  Jeju has a lot of museums and this was our first stop.  As a person who studies sexual health I found the museum average.  Why?First the museum does a good job at giving a lot of different perspectives. Covering things like marriage history  homosexuality  maturity sti masturbation  bdsm etc. They have displays installations artefacts video and some interactivity. The biggest problem is that all the information is written in Korean. So it was impossible to actually learn. I would have liked to read all the information that was presented. Also the price was expensive 12000 won was a lot for what you got.If the information was in English I could see me giving 4 stars.

Innisfree is a Korean cosmetics brand known for its natural ingredients sourced directly from Jeju in Korea...think of it as a Korean Body Shop. The Innisfree House in Jeju is a combined shop and cafe located inside the Osulloc Green Tea Museum complex. You can buy products and make your own soaps as well as sit and chill with some Korean and Western fusion drinks and cafe style food. Good stop for lunch or afternoon tea and to pick up souvenirs. Recommend spending only 1 hour (combined with the green tea plantation photo op)

I'm traveling with a tour group and I think we stopped by this place because it's close to the O'sulloc Tea Museum. I'm not a fan of glass art and I feel that the glass art shown here were not that amazing.Another thing is that there's a lot of outdoor exhibition  so it is not a good place to visit if it's raining.

If you've never been to one of these grab a camera and have a good time.  We had a couple of hours to spend so we thought we'd stop by not knowing what it was.  We were surprised at the good time we had. We took lots of great corny pictures and were entertained. These will make for some fun memories.  Definitely worth the stop.

If you love green tea it's nice to stop by and have their desserts here. We ordered the ice cream the cake roll and they latte. Innisfree store is also at this faciity where you can buy their products too. Good stop for shopping a green tea snack!

If you like green tea I strongly recommend stopping by here... Their tea is really good... BEWARE... they are really expensive. Also for sampling one scoop of green tea ice cream - approx $8; one slice of green tea pastry - approx $9... one small bag of lower grade green tea - approx $25.
Green tea latte green tea ice-cream and green tea rolls are delicious! There is also an Innisfree Shop behind the Tea Museum a good place to stop over on rainy day!
Great fish and oranges.... on weekends there is a lively food court . Clean and . We like markets so we think it?s a good stop in Jeju colorful
Good trekking course in great nature. But no confusion that there is only one way to see the lake on the top called Baekrokdam.
Good easy hike and once you reach the top you get to see more of Jeju. April is a good month to visit as there are less tourists and perfect weather

First of all I had to say I was somewhat attracted by their logo of a whale shark on it.  But only to find out that there was actually no whale shark in the aquarium anymore.  I have been to a number of aquariums in Asia including Singapore Okinawa and Osaka but this one on Jeju island is probably the least impressive.  Nonetheless the aquarium is literally 5 minute drive from Seobjikoji so if you have the time might be a good stopover point.

Being the stupid American I am I learned very quickly that this place was a miniature replica of famous monuments and buildings throughout the world. It was a fun place to stroll around. It's a good site for a few photos. Good place to stop by for an hour or less... Any more would be a waist of time.
average place for just a quick pit stop. lovin' the cold n breezy weather. a good place to visit for sight seeing and taking pictures. hassle with many tourists.

A good short stop to see a waterfall. There is a few steep steps so not recommended if u are bring a baby or toddler. The waterfall is not extremely fanciful though.  There are some old ladies trying to sell the usual seafood.
A 20-minute easy climb to the top awards you with good scenery.  Remember to visit the the free women diver show 130pm and 3pm.

Yep, there are a lot of stairs here. It honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting it to be, seeing as how stairs are my natural enemy. You will probably be tired when you get to the top, but little kids and elderly people are doing it, so it's not crazy. It's over a lot faster than it feels like it's going to be as you're ascending. We were there in the late afternoon, and it was a little crowded, but not too much trouble. Most people move along at a pretty good pace and don't stand in the way too much when taking pictures. It's worth the climb and you'll get some good pictures out of it if the weather permits. Even if you think you are unable to go up to the top, it's worth coming out here just for the landscape.

When I reached the top, I could  see a crater that I had not seen in any other climbs and felt very special! I felt like I was in a huge nature. The weather was not good on the day I went, but if I go on a fine day, I think I can take a very nice picture. Went to Hallim Park on the end of September 2015, its a good thing we came at Autumn because the weather was not hot and not too cold either. The leaves were turning orange - just like in the movies. There are several flower parks in the Hallim park, such as flowers park; cactus park; bonsai park; stone cave; bird park; and folk village - where we can stop by for lunch. This place is suitable for families travelling with old ones, since the scenery is beautiful for photo-shoots.

We, a group of friends had visited this place last week. It was awesome! The journey to get there, parking and the walk up and back were all good. There is ample parking space and plenty of eateries that offers various types of snacks and cold drinks.The area is impeccably clean and the walking path was clear and safe. The steps may seem a little steep at certain points, but you will be well rewarded once you reach the top. The crater is a beautiful sight! Not surprising that it's the iconic image of Jeju which appears on Google. You need about an hour or so for the entire visit.

We visited Woljeongri Beach as a rest stop while driving just to have some ice cream.  Even though the weather wasn?t particularly good in the midst of the monsoon season, the beach still looked amazing with turquoise water.  You can go pretty far out and the water remains shallow although we didn?t go in as the water was a bit cold.  There isn?t a lot of parking available nearby but plenty of decent restaurants and cafes nearby.
We visited this 1100 when we cross from jeju to seogipo and it was good to see the beautiful nature. Because of time issue, we couldn't visit on top of Mt hanla.

We joined Yeha Tour and this is one of the stops. Good information, humor house owner. Do not buy the house oil which cost 40000 won. It is similar to Guerisson 9-complex which costs less than US$20 when you buy from lotte duty free Jeju

We had lunch at this restaurant as it came highly recommended and we had heard that it was on the Michelin list of restaurants of 2011. We got there just as it opened which was a good thing as it filled out quite quickly. We later found out that reservations are highly recommended if you plan to go there for dinner. We got the mixed set for 2 and it was a lot of food for the price. The pork was very good, obviously very fresh. The side dishes were also top-notch. Service was quick and efficient and very friendly. It was a little hard to find as a number of streets around the area were being repaired when we were there but it was totally worth it.

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

We did a back to back sunset/sunrise hike. Sunset was great because it wasn't hot and it was really nice and breezy up there after 20 minutes of stomping up stairs. You get to see the sunset on one side of the peak while you see the moon rise over the crater at the top. Pretty awesome. There is a water/coffee stand about halfway up in case you forget water, but the it wasn't open when we hiked it in the morning (big fail). We camped on the beach nearby, not the greatest...Garbage EVERYWHERE! Not just your typical beach garbage (cups, bags, broken plastic boxes) but long fluorescent light bulbs, peices of boats, clothing... The water had lots of debris in it and despite the sweltering heat, we just couldn't get ourselves to wade past the trash into the deeper areas so we left for Udo Island instead. It was also pretty tricky finding a good spot to post our tent. The tide comes up REALLY high there and the garbageless, flat tide-safe spots are pretty much non existant. Pretty uncomfortable night/morning, but at least we didn't have to get up until 5am to hike the peak. There are washrooms in the village which is about 10 min from the beach, but bring a flashnight cause the lights and water turns off at night.

Visited in Oct, very windy and cooling. Walked up to the hill top in 10mins. Very good experience and the tracks and steps were very nicely constructed. But the place is extremely crowded so photo taking was difficult. Worth the visit and the climb.

visited by family with 3 teenagers in a hot August day. It was really hot, humid day, and we climbed Seonsan Ilculdong around 3 o'clock. It is said that it took about 25 mins' walk to the top, but it was very hard to climb because of heat during hot August day. It is nice picture taking place.Do not bring little kids. It is not for the young children. I saw many children who just wear sandals climbed the all steps to the top, and they cried and were angry because of the heat and hard work. Actually, Seongsan Ilchulbong is nice picture taking place from far, but there is nothing spectacular on the top. It is better to climb Seoungsan Ilculbong in the spring or fall, not in the summer. Otherwise, it is good enough to look at it from the parking lot and take a walk around shore areas.

Visited 4 times during my one year assignment in Jeju. Udo Island is very beautiful and peaceful. Rent a bike to tour around the island will definitely bring you fresh air and excitement. Stopped by at any cafe to try their peanut ice cream from udo! Really nice! I give average for their hallasan fried rice, it?s good to try but the taste is just normal. Udo has a very nice beaches around and good for photo:) recommend to go when you visit jeju.
Very good hike, gorgeous scenery but this does not go up to the crater! Be warned only the Gwaneuma and Seongpanak go to the top!

This was the last stop of our tour so the sun was setting by the time we got there. I recommend coming in the morning for good pictures. It was quite solemn, cold, and eerie because it was just the tour guide of the village, our tour guide, and the rest of our group in the area. The assigned tour guide had very interesting insights on the place and the rest of Jeju culture. She also sold us some products that the folks of the village made. The berry honey is definitely worth buying.

This was one of our stops in our taxi tour for that day.This is a small place showing the traditional homes of that area a long time ago.  It?s free. An English speaking guide will tour you around.  Some interesting facts, like two separate doors (one bigger for the male I think.) They will offer you a drink made of honey and some fermentation of some berries.  It?s like juice but with some tart aftertaste.  Taste good though that we spent I think $40.00 for a bottle.  In hindsight, maybe a bit too much considering it?s not an alcoholic drink (tongue in cheek).  But while drinking that juice at home, it sure brings in mind our visit to Jeju.  While there we saw a black pig with a small companion rat.  Well seems the rat was hovering near the pig pen.  Interesting place and the guide did tell some interesting stories and tidbits! (Can be done in half an hour).

This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. When i visit Jeju, i stayed in a hotel nearby, so i can see the sunrise from the top of seonsan Ilchulbong. To see the beautiful sunrise, i walk from my hotel at 4.30 am. You need to buy an entrance ticket to this place.You need to walk the stair path, uphill, and soon you arrive on top, you'll find so many people already setting up the camera to capture the sunrise. after enjoying the beautiful scene from top, on our way down, my eyes can't stop admiring the beauty scene of Jeju City. Everything is taking your breath away in this place.You also can ride a horse or watch the mermaid show (lady divers). If you want to buy some goods for your family from Jeju (orange, souvenirs, cake, snacks), you have to buy it in Jeju, because you can't find any of these goods in Seoul. If you want to give a second thought on it, your last chance to shop is in the Jeju International airport (price is the same everywhere in Jeju).This is a very highly recommended place to visit in Jeju Island!

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This could be an amazing place to visit provided you have good weather and great friends. Scootering around the tiny island can be fun if you stop off at the beaches, swim along the way and explore the caves and tunnels by the black sand beach. Definitely keep an eye out for the giant burger restaurant and the peanut Makgeolli stand (留嫄몃━, it's alcoholic rice wine!), both are delicious! Don't over-hype it or expect too much, just go to have fun and you'll be happy you went.

There's no variety at all, looks like... Only the exoensive overrated oranges of Jeju. don't get me wrong, they are good, but I would NEVER pay so much money for fruit! Yes, fruit is REALLY expensive in Korea, but 50k is over the top... So: Harabongs, the other oranges in sweets like tartlets and chocolates, black pork jobal, seafood, souvinirs and fruit. That's what you can buy in the market. It was nice to see and the taste some stuff, but i wouldn't visit there again

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The waterfall is rather small, but it is almost in the middle of a city. When you arrive you will be on top of the cliff in which Jeongbang flows off of. Located near Seogwipo city, Jeongbang Waterfall is 23 meters high and is very close to the sea. This is why people tell that the water falls directly into the ocean. A legend says that servant of Emperor Jin of China, called as Seo Bul, sent to the area in order to search the magical herb of eternal youth in Mount Halla. People interested in seafood can taste fresh abalone sashimi with garlic slices & hot pepper paste as dipping. It is offered by ajummas, who collect them directly at this spot. Don쨈t forget to wear good shoes to avoid becoming a casualty.

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.
The short walk to the falls is nice, and the falls are pretty.  They are good for a quick stop, but not a must see if you don't have time here.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The park is well manicured and you can take great pictures of scenery with fences. There are swings near the top where you can enjoy the breeze while taking in the scenery of the surrounding lands and mountains.  You can also see the bottom of the   green crater   from the top.This is one of the more expensive natural attractions in Jeju (KRW6,000) but I feel it's a good place to relax and worth a visit.

The only waterfall in Jeju that drains directly into the ocean is worth stopping by for around half an hour. Ample parking space, free admission, good accessibility and the ability to get quite close to the waterfall even if it isn't that tall.

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the   Big Three   on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.

The hike to the end of the cave was not short, so be prepared to walk a few kms if you plan to visit this place. The cave itself was wet and cool, which is good if outside was hot. You get to see different formations and immerse yourself deep underground at the same time. So, the time was well spent here. Afterward, you can stop by the restaurant near the entrance and have some cheap Korean food.  The admission to the cave was very reasonable as it is a government owned attraction.

The Botanical gardens is set up in to different gardens and a large doom/ indoor area set up into zones. The plants on show were very nice but I have seen a lot better. This could be because of the South Korea climate. Look at the surface and it's well kept then you notice dirty water in the ponds. What I did enjoy was watching some of the workers weed some of the areas they are so methodical. As we were part of a day tour this was just one of our many stops and our time was limited. Perhaps I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have such a tight schedule. I would rate this attraction as Good but there isn't a good rating and average would do it a disjustice. I thought the entrance fee to be very high considering the country it's in. You don't pay much more to go in Kew Gardens, London's Botanical garden that can actually take you days to get round.

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Pretty much boring, probably one will only get really excited if the person is a hardcore teddy bear fan .. Else it's really just a   oh ya I've been there.. Full stop    kinda trip.. Was lucky I went during the children days weekend so quite a good no of attractions were free.. Else I will probably feel $ wasted on this

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.

Only works in one direction. Good pit stop bathroom is next to it. It was cool. 5-10 minutes. Pretty area. Cute, fun, short and quick. If you just want to try something different and free, this might be a little fun if you are already in the area south west-ish  of jeju city.

One of Jeju Island attraction, the rock formations that looks more like a horse head to me. Well, legendary it was a head of a dragon. We stop by for a photo stop on our way to airport.A good nice photographing platform for visitor to take picture. There is a stairway leading down to the rocky beach, down there you can see many locals selling fresh seafood.  It is not a wheelchair friendly place. Be there before sunset otherwise you will not able to take a clear photo.

My daughter and I went to this place because my daughter very fond of Hello Kitty. The exhibition room quite good, but we really disappointed when we saw the park on the rooftop... It was not much to see and the Hello Kitty statue at the center of this park very dirty. Ticket price for this place quite high either.

Must walk..hike to the top.  Worth to go..because the nice scenery. Not suitable for old people & wheelchair. Really a huge place. Actually is a die volcano. But really beautiful.. when you on top the hill. Definate you wont regret . But must have a good stamina. Certain hour, there is a woman diver show. Quite interesting.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

It's a 100m road whereby majority of the tourists are fascinated by this mysterious road. All the drivers will put it on neutral gear on the   starting point   and you find the car moving up but the road looks like incline. A short stop is given and you can have a good photo shoot over there. Most of the tour guide will tell you the truth behind this mysterious road and you will realise that    Things really cannot be judge by it's appearance.   Beside the Mysterious Road, there are a few stall selling some snacks. You must go to the first stall which is near to the ending point of the mysterious road, and try their strawberries. It's the most fresh strawberry i have ever seen and eat! It's a must to try.

It was the best decision to travel around the beautiful island of Jeju with Jeju Taxi Tour Samchoon Kim! He brought us to all the places in our itinerary that we intended to visit and he even checked the weather prior to that so that we would not be caught in the rain. The whole trip was very comfortable and it was not in a rush. We took our time to see and soaked in all the goodness of Jeju! Samchoon Kim is also very kind and polite, I remembered one of the day he stopped by a morning market and ran down coming back with 6 freshly made Bungeo ppang (a Korean dessert) for us. That act really warm our hearts =) Not to forget, he also always offered to snap pictures for us so we do not need a selfie stick! Thank you for being a great tour guide and driver!

It was a good experience for me family with 2 children as they enjoyed ut the most. Weather as a bit chilly even during autumn, so bring extra layers with you so that you can get confortable. The train ride at the start of the trip really feels like the highlight of the trip, although you can board the train on and off later to get from one garden to another. There are 5 stops for you to stroll around, toilets, cafes and other facilities are available and very much well taken care off. We had a great time all in all. Highly recommended to friends and families.

It rained almost nonstop on our trip to Jeju so we visited a lot of museums we probably would normally have not. The hologram concert is the major attraction in Play Kpop and it was good fun. The rest? Meh. The entry ticket is 15 000 won which is rather expensive since most museums on the island just cost a few thousand won. On top of that, a lot of the other attractions (like photo booths) cost extra. Kpop history was interesting enough, but most of the other stuff was quite boring.

it is very easy and friendly track to reach the peak, but for me the beautiful things about Seongsan Illchulbong are scenery from everywhere. so, I made a little tour by walking by from beaches till Saepjikoji and to Udo island. Never get missed from sunrise to sunset, everything is beautiful. is not wrong to choose stay near the Hills, Goseong-ri is perfect village to stay.But, if you just a few time to visit is good to stopping by. My wife loves here in spring time, lots of canola and pretty flower in the green green grass.You will found starbucks, convenience market, and lots of food.

In my opinion the best way to go around the island is a bicycle. About 16km. Took us 4h to make it, with stop in every single possible place, including a lunch brake, rest on a beach, etc. Most interesting for us were diving women, we had a chance to see at work in few places. Probably the island is crowded in a season. In May we had good time and enjoy the trip very much.

I'm not a big fan of Hello Kitty (my friend does), but it was fun to stroll around the place. It was filled with Hello Kitty goodness in pink and such a nice place to take pictures. There are so many rooms to be visited, and they even have a rooftop garden! Some of item showcased are very interactive and enjoyable. I believe it's worth the visit as every adult has their own inner-child side. Unravel your younger side out, and you'll enjoy the place lot more than you think. Recommended for families. Make sure to visit their cafe that serves nice choco drink (approx. KRW4000) & the gift shop!Admission fee for adult: approx. KRW10800++
i'm afraid there is too much tourist even during the low season, i need to walk really fast for more tourist are coming and i don't even have time to really stop by and take a good look at the top
If u expect very exciting, not really! But it's good to have a walk in a rainy day until it stops raining! Overall it's fine!

I started off by lowering my expectations for this tourist stop.  The building is a little outdated from the outside and I wasn't sure how good it could be.  The whole family was pleasantly surprised.  We learned about the fun character and her family and friends.  Everything was well done and there was more to the museum than expected.  My daughter and son both had smiles from ear to ear, making for a great day.

I love this place so much. Everyone can easily climb this mountain because they provide stairs which is well built, not too steep and not slippery. Although it made me tired to climb to the top but the scenery up there is very beautiful. I took so many photographs. The combination of land and sea scenery is very good.There is also many souvenir shops and food stall on the rest area with cheap souvenirs which is a good place to buy jeju souvenirs.Must visit.

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I hiked for 14 hours (amateur hiker) because I'm slow and also have not been doing any exercise for years... It was raining and windy quarterway through. Then it was sunny on the hike back. Since it was misty at the peak, so I didn't see the lake. Go prepared with water and food. Two bottles of water to last you to the top. When you come down, refill water at portable water spot. When I said food, like actual kimbap, bento or even cup noodles. In fact, bring all three. If one of the guy I bumped into did not give me his kimbap, I'd have starved for sure cause all I brought was three bananas and protein bar. Some people even offered me mini chocolate bars and tangerines. Bring isotonic drink if you want to. Bring Hiking stick(s) if you're uncoordinated like me. Bring windbreaker for sure and make sure it's waterproof. Get a good hiking shoes tha can grip because I slipped a lot on the way down. Because of my lack of preparation, I've suffered for sure coupled with my lack of exercise lol. So really, go prepared. And if you're like me with determination, and don't mind 14 hours hike, please go early like 5am. Though they do have transportation to bring you down should you really need it. I just missed it...

I have heard people said the sunrise from the crater is magnificent. But, I have visited Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon and it was just awesome! Thanks to the wide green field surrounded by the dark blue sea and cover with the bright blue sky! It was so relaxing there hearing the wave sound and feel the wind blowing pass through me. Hiking to the top of the crater would be good too, but you may need at least 2 hours to walk around the area.

Here really is a nice and beautiful place. Rent a bicycle to walk around the island during autumn is soooo good. Worth to visit it. I ate a sashimi bibimbap there, is fresh and yummy. 3 hours is not enough seriously, if you wanna go through the whole island, unless you ride your bicycle without stop, haha.

For us it was a bit of a disappointment that we would need international driver's licence to rent 50-125cc scooter/motorbikes/small car like vehicles on the island. So it is a good thing that they have the electronic scooters, which don't require the licence. They are way cooler to cruise around the island with.It was a clear sunny day, and we spent 2 hours driving around the island, stopping every now and then to enjoy the scenery. There are a few places to visit on the tour so no need to rush around the place. Be sure to make it to the last boat back to the mainland in time (for us it was 5:30pm, but people kept coming there late so it left just before 6pm). From the boat we were able to enjoy the setting sun, which was a great finish for the trip. The boat ride there and back was reasonably priced, and the scooters we got were 25,000KRW for 2 hours. We went there a bit late so the only minus was that the place available for us was with no insurance for the scooters. Still, if you visit Jeju and have extra time on the east side of the island, be sure to visit udo!

Entrance fee is 10,000KRW.I visited during Spring and the place is so beautiful with flowers all around! Daisy, roses, lavender are everywhere. It's so breathtaking!The place is divided into 3 parts, and they take you to these places via train. The train will stopped at each stop and you can get down to visit and explore the places and get on to the next trip of train to get to next destination.Their ice cream is good too! Tasty and fresh! Worth trying.Good place to enjoy beautiful scenery. The air is so fresh and you could really enjoy your time here.We visited this place for like 2 hours.

don't forget to be early for this and as this is privately owned attraction, the entrance fees is KRW6000 instead of the government owned ones at KRW2000. Wear comfortable walking or hiking shoes as it is a bit of walking towards the crater. Good place for photographs at the top and be   lost   around the pampas green field for dramatic photographs.

Dived back to those nostalgic childhood moments when teddy bears once played as friends in your life. This Teddy Bear Museum has a wide array of collection of teddy bears, dressed beautifully in different costumes. The most popular bear will probably be the one dressed in Louis Vuitton clothes.What particularly caught my attention was the exhibition which actually used famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa, and the Teddy Bear was dressed to depict her. A creative way to carry out this exhibition. However, those expect to see a wide range of   depiction  .Overall, I felt that this was only an average stop-over, but will be good for families traveling with their young children. There's a souvenir shop on site too, where I'll be expecting young children to be bugging their parents to get them a teddy bear each!

Cheonjiyeon Falls is a peaceful stop for those that want some refreshing time. Unofrtunatelly swimming is not allowed here. Good for a quick visit before visiting the Saeyeongyo Bridge. The nature also is astonishing, a glimpse of tropical nature in Jeju.
Cheap and good quality food.The restaurant I went serves seafood soup and marinated raw yummy crab as side dish. Unlimited TOP up. With just 2 serving of pork about 24,000 won
big enough & diff topic in park. you could see the flower, bird, cave etc,,,,not too crowded when i visited, good place for spending time

As part of the tour, we had a short stop at dragon head rock, where you can see the head of a dragon naturally carved on a big rock. There is also a small mermaid sculptured on a rock for photo opportunity. This is more of a photo stop. Jeju as an island attraction have plenty of rock formation, volcanic rocks, and shoreline with plenty of rock. Again like all part of Jeju, the place has good breeze and quite comfortable.

Arrived in the morning parked easily, cost for parking at the entrance was 1800 WON and picked up a map.  Make sure you wear good shoes -- preferably with good ankle support and walking sticks.  The path is well layer out but does take some effort.  We did not get all the way to the top as it was closed due to a slide but it's nice walk.  Suggest an early start and bring water too.

Well i get there by accident - really - i didnt plan to visit this park but good thing happened. I had so much fun back there. All labyrinths(maze) are great adventure. Just try to get lost and find way between tries without any map of maze! :P. Tickets are bit expensive but still it worth to go especially if you have kids! Well for grow ups it is also fun ( but make it harder- dont use  map)

We wwnt here because it was on the way to the airport.  It isnt really special but a good place to pick up some last minute souvenirs like chocolates and jeju oranges.  We looked around for 15 minutes then headed off because most of the venders were all selling the same items
We were lucky that the lady of the house was both detail and funny when explaing about the old jeju ways. A good place to visit and get to know abit of the culture.

We went up at 6am in the morning to see the sunrise. With cold rainy weather the event was less romantic than expected but well worth and good fun for us. We went up with our 3yr old boy. The way up is very well prepared and suitable for children who like walking/climbing a bit. We carried out son partly and party he walked. Well Organised tourist attraction.Entrance fee is only W2000.Have fun!

We went there on our way back after a day of sightseeing. It is good to just drive pass that stretch. But not worth if it is not on the way. You could just spend a brief less than 5mins there while staying in the car.

We spent the night at a Pension at the base so it was easy to get to to catch the sunrise. From the base we could already see people making their way up. We were prepared to spend at least 40 mins to climb the stairs but surprisingly we got there within 20 mins. I would not say it was a breeze as we (and most people there) were panting and had a good sweat. Regardless of your fitness level just go at your pace with comfortable shoes and attire - the beautiful sunrise against the ocean is definitely worth it (unless it's bad weather)

We rented a car. We reached the Tea Museum just after 12 noon. The car park was already full and we had to park by the side road. The museum is more of an exhibition of tea cups with write-ups on a brief history of tea and the origins of the Osulloc tea. Easy reading for a morning activity. There is a tea merchandise section and a cafe.We ordered the green tea ice-cream and black tea ice-cream. Both were good. The tea was very intense on both the ice cream. The green tea roll was just passable for us. Drop by if you are on the way. I think at certain times of the day there maybe some demonstration on tea but nothing was written in English so not sure of the timing.

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

Was very crowded the day/time we were there.  There's a tiny museum which leads to shop and cafe.At the cafe we had the trio of  green tea cake/roll smoothie and ice cream which were very good.Then we headed next door to the Innisfree Jeju house.A nice way to spend a couple of hours.  There's a couple of very uncrowded O'sulloc cafes in Seoul too.

Very well manicured plantations and garden areas. Museum is professional and store was well laid out with all their delicious teas with samples in bottles for customers to smell.Limited parking space though. Could see people parking by the sides of roads all over the vicinity.Cashier staff was very helpful combining our global tax refund receipts when we made two purchases separately.Ice cream was good. Cream roll would prefer it like a Swiss roll where cream is well spread around the roll. Current style has too much dry cake at the sides.Beautiful packaging as always.
Very cute themepark to while away a good 1-2 hours. Good for summer when it's too hot outside. The rooms are separated into various different themes. Particularly good for silly selfies!!

This was really a nice long walk. Will advise to wear good walking shoe. The route was easy to walk just that when the wind come you can feel the wind blowing at you. You have to walk all the way up and you will be able to see the nice surrounding. It was really nice and we really enjoyed it.

this place offers audio guided tour which we loaned kind of gotten lost along the way and didnt really follow the sequence. there are many interesting places to see but more of less are quite similar with regard to the houses and all the area is big and spaced out. it will be great if there are a little more resting areas/bench along the road for visitors to rest along the way. better wayfinding would be good as well.

This is an excellent play place for teenagers. If you are a child 120 cm and under you must go with an adult. I recommend that if you’re really tall or big you might not want to go because this place has narrow tunnels. I almost got stuck in one of the hammock tunnels... haha.We saw this place on a pamphlet we got from the airport and really wanted to go right away and it was totally worth going.Remember to wear something comfortable because you’ll be moving around a lot so clothing with shenanigans hanging off from it probably won’t be a good idea. Or excessive jewelry. The price was 12000 per person for the Maze ep.3 and the Level 2 (harder level with timer) was around 5000?? But as a package it was 16000 per person. We had so much fun here!

The water park is ok. It would have been way better if you didn't have to pay extra for swim vests and extra for sun beds. So practically paying entrance fee doesn't mean you go and have fun. You are forced to spend good amount of money to have a good time.

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.
Thank you for visiting the Aquaplanet JEJU. I'm glad you had a good time with your daughter. We will reflect your suggestion. Be happy always.

Rent a bicycle or ATV to enjoy the scenery here. In spring rape flowers are all over the island. The cliff by the sea are amazingly nice. Good place to go with your love ones if two of you want a short getaway by yourselves.

Past by Wolijeongri beach on my way to other attractions. The beach is very beautiful. Good to spend 15 mins of your time there to take some nice shots.

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.
Our guide June gave us a detailed explanation of all the places we went to. She was also helpful in many ways and answered our queries. She even recommended a good dinner place for us!

Okay if visitor is kind of tea lover. Like being here for shopping which is not that extraordinary or the must spot. For the shop and products' variety are good. Free parking on site.

Nice to take pictures of the tea gardens/have a walk around. Buy their different flavours of tea that they have and they always change their goods. You can try out their caf챕 as well as go up to the observatory area on a higher floor. It is extremely crowded though.

Nature is amazing and the lava tubes at manjang is worth seeing. The walk is about 1km in and same way out. Wear good shoes. Walk is not as tiring as climbing up other steep sites in jeju. Educational Signs in English are available. A bit chilly in autumn in the caves.

My wife wanted to visit this place since the last time we came.  This place is ideal for kids and couples.  Lots of history and old bears on display.  Good way to pass some time.   Located close to other museums...

My husband and I were visiting Jeju mid-August. A week before our trip I searched online for a dive experience and found Good Dive. My husband and I live in China and had no way of contacting the center by phone so good thing they had an email address on tripadvisor. I emailed…

Magpie Brewery is a great place to have some decent western food and high quality craft beer. Their Baltic Porter is particularly good as is their Kolsch. You probably need a  car to get to the place or a taxi which will cost you \10000 to \15000 each way depending which part of Jeju City you are in.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

KRW 2k for adults. Worth the 2km to and fro walk and all information panels in the cave have english. Not suitable for very old and very young. A lot of un even steps and walkways and high steps sometimes. Dark. Wear good tracking shoes.

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

Irion (magma) carved the small valley. This is the place where the magma carved the valley long long ago. The small valley meet the sea here. You can enjoy transparent canoe and see under water(not always).  Scenery is exotic.  It is also good for you to walk along here.

In this place you will learn history of Jeju Island people. The houses how they lived what they did in daily activity and their natural products. It's always good to know traditional knowledge from around the world. Don't forget to take pictures! :)

If you want ride transparent kayak you have to do reservation. Sea and water is so clean transparent kayak is quite good experience. Water bicycles was good too but little bit harder to ride than kayak. Without reservation we can ride waterbycles. Anyway beautiful sightseeing and place.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

i was excited to visit this park. unfortunately the park did not meet expectation. most of the models look fake  poorly maintained. maybe this park suitable for school kids to introduce them to the famous architecture. i really hope they do something to make sure visitors enjoy this miniature theme park. anyways  the concept is good. but not the models.

I loved this cave! 2 km in and out. It was a very educational trip as you'll get explanations about what you see along the way. It's dark and wet and there's water dripping from the ceiling so bring a cap and good boots to avoid slipping. Don't wear a long skirt as it will get wet. A bit hard to take pictures though because of the lighting :/ But the ending and the way it was presented with the lighted walkway at the end was great!

I love open-water swimming and just plain jumping off rocks. This spot is ideal for both and is also a good way of interacting with locals. you don't even need to speak Korean to get along with folks here!

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) !
