When my group and I first went to this market I assumed it would be small like a on the side of the road market where they sell fruits, veggies, and jams. This market was that times ten and the market even had the kitchen sink. When we first walked through they had fresh picked flowers, potted plants, fresh spices, 15 different types of kimchi. As we walked around it wasnt just food and plants they had housewares to clothes even puppies, rabbits and chickens. then we realized that they even had a fish market. This market of cousre smelled of fish we consumers selling squid, shrimp, and tilapia. This market is such a good way to imerse oneself into a the korean culture on the island. This was one of the places on my wish list to see while my group and I were in Korea and it was much more than I expected and I am so glad I went.

What WERE they thinking of! The   museum   is a few glass cases with examples of bars/boxes of chocolates. The   factory   is a table where you can buy cooking chocolate and make your own. The only good news is that your (HUGE) entrance fee is refunded in the way of a coupon to use at the (VERY OVERPRICED) chocolate shop. There is NOTHING here. It's AWFUL.Buy your choccies in the supermarket and give this place a wide berth.

what made this place interesting besides the dragon head was the locals selling their wares.  We also bought our first hallabong here.  I can tell you prices are pretty much the same all over for those hallabongs.  If you walk down there are a lot of ajjumas selling I think sea food, I did not walk all the way down since I did not have the right foot wear but it seemed like fresh sea food.It is a very touristy place, we just took a look few pictures and left.  Its one of those places we dont have to go see again once you seen it thats good enough.  But were are glad we did see it.  Again I would have walked down to the ocean side but opted not to might have been interesting, so make sure you have the right footwear, it is rocky and maybe a little wet.

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

Went up and down seongpanak. Went with my parents who are in their early 50s. The way up gets a little tough after the 12:30 point. We started at 6:30 and got to that area by 11:00. On the way down gets very boring. Bring lots of water and wear shoes. You'll see old Korean people wearing stuff you'd wear to summit some crazy mountain but just good shoes with good grip (not converse) will be good for the hike. Of course hiking boots would help. Things to bring: hand sanitizer, water, sunscreen, gatorade/pocari sweat if it's very hot. Bring some food and bags for trash as you have to take it all with you. Overall probably 4/5 experience but nice to experience with family. Probably not good for young kids - people with health problems die each year per locals.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

Wear your sport shoes, warm jacket, bring light snacks, a bottle of water, and of course..a determination. Dont forget camera as you will blown away by the scenery from the peak. Early morning is a good time to climb

We went to this folks village on tour. For me, this village is very nice and i learn a lot of their culture. For example, as a Chinese, we celebrate Chinese New Year. The elderly will give red packets to us as a sign of good fortune. Everything comes in red during Chinese New Year. But in Korea, they will use White packets and everything comes in Black and White during Chinese New Year. This is because in old era of Korea, when they have wars, the man will be wearing white colour war costume and when they come back to their own house, their clothes is full of Red Colour Blood, that's the reason why they thinks that Red Colour is not a fortunate colour to them. More and more stories you can learn from this place, especially from the statue, you can see usually man is eating always and woman is the one who always do everything. That's their culture. This place is really worth a visit, and by the way, we are not being brought to those shop which sells local specialty. Hence, i felt that this place is nice to visit and nice place to take photos.

We went to the one at T 724-0228, mainly after the ferry landed and we were hungry, 'tween lunch and dinner parking wS available out front.  Staff were a little underworked so we go the full service treatment, good thing not tips expected (?);  we had the less fatty pork neck.  Served with a nice crab soup and nangymun noodles as a dessert.  Can't seem to get away from grilled fatty pork in Korea, have they heard of lean tenderloin here? Marinated  Pork skin was also served,

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

We went here straight away. Had some street foods,some of them so good ,some of them so spicy!!!But quite huge market so look around first then try some foods.so many sea foods,veges,fruits and Korean foods.One thing... normal streets has bins but when I been 4-5 markets dose not have bins..I wonder... How or where these peoples throw away the rubbish...

We visited the cave on the way back to Udo (very easy to do both of these in one day. Very interesting and well explained. It would probably be a good idea to bring a jacket because the temperature in the cave is significantly lower than on the outside. However, it's still really cool to see and think about the implications of the event that made the cave in the overall of Jeju. Very good for kids although it can be a bit slippery inside too.

We visited Seongeup Folk Villagein end Jan 2018, it?s snowing during our visit. There is a lady tour guide that speak English assign to us. She did it well and we enjoy the visit. The building in village are unique. We were there on the good timing where snows make the area really beautiful. You also can buy some of the products they sell over there, anyway is optional.

We visited on a very wet day so it was good to be inside even if the inside was the lava cave.  The lighting is very low in the cave and the floor, made by lava flow is very uneven so close attention needs to be made to where you are going. Its one kilometre each way to the end of the public bit and you miss quite a bit watching where the feet go so not to fall over.mAn interesting place to visit but take a torch!

We travelled long way only to be told a short story on how the village people survive previously before we were presented their expensive products. The guide told us the quality is good but we were not told elsewhere the price of the products are 50% cheaper. They said their horse oil treat allergies. I bought, used but it didn't get any way better.

We followed Trip Advisor's map and was brought to a small hotel garden area. We were iniatially confused but the hotel staff pointed the way to us. It wasn't very far already. We took our time walking, and to tell you the truth, I was glad we came the way we came. We found a way down to the rocky beach and climbed a little right to where the waves break. At that point the rocks aren't geometrical, just normal. Afters we walked thru a garden, which was a good distraction, and finally arrived at the cliffs. To my disappointment we can't actually go down to the rocks. And then there were a few shops selling fresh seafood, postcards, ice cream, mandarin oranges and to my surprise, some hallabong oranges. I got it pretty cheap too, compared to other places that I went after that

We finally found this street on our second attempt. Google map failed to function well in Korea, don't know why. Maps.me as suggested by other blogger was good for car travellers. It is not stable for pedestrians. Anyway, it's just opposite the jeju dongmun traditional market, cross the main road and the street is at the inner side. You may show the entrance arch to shop keepers nearby, they will indicate the direction. To me, the black pork is not anything spectacular, just common bbq as can be found elsewhere. I am not a food critic, hence I couldn't actually tell the difference. You can try any of the restaurants in this street. I guess they are the same. Enjoy!

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We decided to include this in our tour after feeling a bit tired from all the hiking up mountains and paths. It's an easy couple of hours, especially if you have kids, whom seemed to be entertained with every variation of dressed up bear. There is also an extensive gift shop, with, you've guessed it, lots of bears and cuddlies. The prices aren't exactly cheap, but the quality seemed good. It's a good way to slow the pace down if you are in need of a rest.. Nice afternoon out.

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

This place is a definite must see on my list. The market is huge and includes shops that sell about everything you can imagine (clothes, kitchen appliances, souvenirs, meat, fish, ice cream, pancakes, desserts, traditional street food, oranges, oranges and more oranges). The fruit is expensive, but that's normal for Korea. The street food is cheap and absolutely delicious. It is definitely a good way to kill a couple hours and try some of Jeju's famous treats.

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This market was near our hotel so we came by here a few times in the evenings (and a couple times in the day time). Mostly because we were trying to find this fried chicken restaurant that never seemed to be open and we kept going back to try to find it. Don't come here expecting a night market extravaganza like other parts of Asia. This is more strictly a   market   market, though there are lots of restaurants that have take-out. There are a few street food stalls, so you can get your fix in a couple spots. Definitely make sure you try the orange juice from one of the sellers here, Jeju has amazing oranges (and tangerines). There are some souvenir type places here, but nothing special. We bought some of the chocolates because they were dirt cheap and wanted to try them, but when we got home and ate them they were just waxy and artificial tatsing (you'll see which chocolates I mean when you get there. EVERY souvenir seller has them. Even in the airport). We bought some dried mandarins from the same vendor, and they were pretty good. We also bought a bunch of oranges to bring around with us as snacks while we were driving. If you've been to markets in Asia before, this will be nothing special. But if you're looking for something to do, it's probably worth visit - wouldn't go out of my way for it though.

This market is really big, there is fish market, street food corner and the souvenir shops corners where you can buy jeju chocolates,... Anyways, I'm addicted to the street food corners here. The food marrket is at the gate 8. There are so many kind of street food with good price.

This is something different: a 2 km or so walk through an underground lava tube where molten lava has flowed several times over the centuries. A unique experience. Be prepared for a bit of a trek over uneven, rough ground, dodging puddles. It can be drippy and it's always cold so take a jacket. But it's good fun and just out of this world.

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

This is an underground shopping center which is just around the corner of Orange Tree  Cafe & Hotel. This is just the normal shopping center which you would see in most of the subways thru out Seoul, however, the good thing about this underground shopping mall is that each of the exits leads to different streets which has more shops....eg. Uniqlo, ABC Mart, Daiso, and also various cafes.....and also to the Dongmun Market and also to the Black Pork Street.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a lovely spot to visit. You can wander around the artists village enjoy the outdoor sculptures (kids will like the brightly coloured animals near the art shop/cafe) and then have a good look at the exhibitions inside.  There is a permanent one and a temporary one. The temporary one at present is about marine plastics and pollution. The work was really good especially the video work and created   man   by a young female Korean artist. Most impressive.The last Wednesday of the month entry is free but it's only 2000 won anyway I think. They have an English brochure and the lady at reception was very pleasant.

This is a lived-in Village.  Locals are still living their lives as how they used to live centuries ago.  That being said, modernity started to encroach into the lives here with satellite dishes being placed outside their residences and that villagers explained that theft & burglary are starting to become a nuisance, most possibly caused by tourists that came to their village.  Here, you got to learn about sustainability measures that were used before and we have to ask ourselves why such tradition isn't continuing.  That being said, there are certain customs that are gone for good measures such as the black pigs that are raised there.  In the olden days, the pigs would be fed faeces by humans and then, their meat would be consumed by humans (recycling)!  Anyhow, this is only applicable if you are genuinely curious about Jeju way of life, which is VERY different from the mainland.

This is a facility that houses multiple attractions  and they are all basically geared toward separating the tourist from his or her money. Notwithstanding this  our family had a great time spending a couple of hours here. The main attraction appears to be the indoor cart racing track. It's not cheap  around KRW 40 000 for a package that includes 10 minutes on the track and a ticket to the   unique objects   museum. We actually found the items in the museum quite entertaining - objects that trick your eye  weird inventions. The go cart driving was a bit disconcerting (no helmets  no apparent real concern for safety) but in the end it was fun. I was glad I was on the track with just another father-son pair. On the way out  my kid bought carrots for horses that were in a corral  and the guy there was nice enough to take my kid around a lap on the horse (again  no safety gear). My kid was fine but I was glad when both the go cart ride and the horseride finished without any problems.If you are desperate to kill a couple of ours and the weather is bad  this may be a good place to go with tweens or teens. They also offered a   Survival Game   attraction which looked like it was done with laser-tag type guns (not paintball).

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

This is a beautiful waterfall that empties directly into the sea. Once at the bottom the mist was very refreshing on a hot day. There are places where kids can wade but I'd recommend water shoes. I saw an adult sandal get swept into the sea. I brought my two kids (age 8 and 4). At the bottom of the stairs there were some very big rocks that were difficult for my 4 year old to navigate, had to carry him part of the way. My 8 year old did just fine. We didn't have water shoes and even though they had fun, they would have been a lot more comfortable with better foot protection. Good site, family friendly with some caution due to big rocks/slippery, not good for toddlers or smaller.

This Hallasan Fried Rice is a must have, must Go, must try, if you are in Udo Island. It is available at the 'Pungwon' restaurant. It is about 20mins walking from the harbour. If you are driving, key in the Tel no. 7841894 in your GPS device.First you will have to order either Black pork or cuttlefish according to your preference. There is a minimum number of portions to order based on the number of pax. There were 4 of us and we order 2 Pork and 1 Cuttlefish. We will begin by BBQ the meat. Until we are about halfway through, you can order the rice from the staff. The staff will put aside some meat and start by cooking the rice. The whole idea of Hallasan Fried Rice is that the staff will tell you the story about Mount Hallasan and the islands nearby; all these while making the rice into the shape of a mountain. He will then pour in the egg mixture and meat and cheese... and after numerous of flipping the rice, it's done. Fret not if you don't understand Korean, they have Chinese staff who can do the story telling in Mandarin. The process of hearing about the story is very interesting coupled with the visual of the staff cooking the rice. Not to mention, it tastes damn good too!

This folk village which has a collection of 600 years old thatched roof houses built using the volcanic basalt rocks and passed on from one generation to another, showcases the unique culture of Jeju Island. The stone statue of Harubang called the grandfather of Jeju and worshipped as the protector of this island can be seen in front of almost all the huts.This village is still inhabited by the locals and one can see them practicing their traditional rituals including rearing of the Black Pigs.By the way ,Jeju is famous for its Black Pork dishes.There are also sites for holding special rituals like praying God for good luck and health, place where breast feeding women pray for lack of milk etc.Our Guide cum Driver Mr Kim Nam Joon (+82-10-4616-6650) not only took us around the village but also ensured we had a good time.

There is a place for hand-made soap. If you buy a pack of raw material for making soap, you are able to sit down and design your own soap right away. The package is ~15,000 won which includes the material of making 3 pieces of soap and the final product wrapping stuff as well. It is a very good experience for ladies apart from shopping.

The visit to the lava tube is interesting, but the way leading there is not good, and might definitely be dangerous under certain weather circunstances. Lightning is precarious and there are only few explanatory boards. definitely not adequate for people with walking restrictions of any kind

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

The place is usually crowded.  Make sure to wear good walking shoes to walk and climb, some drinking water to quench thirst along the way. Not suitable for elderly and people who are not keen in climbing. Otherwise, is worth to visit - it is a Unesco World Heritage site after all.  If you are not there to catch sunrise, any season is fine.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The concept of the Innisfree Jeju House is nice. Good brand extension. However, don't expect great bargains on cosmetics. As a matter of fact, the range is limited. Best to buy from Seoul or other major cities. The cafe is a nice place to rest with some interesting food choices. However, it's always crowded and thus the ambience is not too conducive for a nice tea session. Overall, it's a nice short introduction to the use of tea in Innisfree product range.
The black pork was really good. I love BBQ pork belly, but the black pork was a tad different -in a good way. It had more flavor and was more tender. I would go here again to eat!

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

Small island - the main road that goes around the island is around 13,8 km. A good way to explore is to rent a vehicle - electric scooter, electric motor cycle, electric bike, or bike - and go as you like. But all the electric is required international driving license.

Seongeup Folk Village of Jeju Island is the place that the past resident live in. The tour guide told us this place can keep well mostly because of the government. The government funds the residents to live here, let them to keep the old building and the culture well. When there have visitor like us, the resident will become a tour guide or shop assistant. It is a good way to spread the culture. Because the residents must know more about the culture than other tour guides. They will show the old tools and teach you how to use it, it is funny and you must be proud of their wisdom.If you like to watch the episode that comes from Korea. You must go here, because most of the building had appeared in the episode, such as ?Dae Janggeum?, if you are lucky, you will see the actor here.

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Not spectacular but unusual that it flows into the sea. You can walk across the rocks to get really close and many did for pictures. Be careful though. Some women selling freshly cut abalone, sea cucumber, snails - raw! Just 200m away from the base of the fall. Ticket is affordable at 2000 won even for foreigner which is the good part about most of the sights unlike some countries which cost double or more for foreigners.Don't see any restaurant so drive into the city seogwipo food street for plenty of choices.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.

Maybe we expected too much of the beach but it we didn't enjoyed this beach too well. We hoped for a large beach where you can swim and relax and maybe some small shops/cafe쨈s around to buy some drinks/food. We spent 25 hours and it was enough since it didn't reach our expectations. We stayed at Seogwipo and took the taxi to Jungmun for around 13000 won one-way. The beach is nice/OK but its crowded (July 2018) and the beach is too small. You can't swim because of the waves and only a small area where you can stay. The rest of the beach is for surfing. You can rent two sun beds and one parasol for 40000 Won (only cash) and other services on the beach (that we did not use). The good thing that it is a GS25-store (or 7/11 store don't quite remember) so you can buy drinks and small food. Near the beach there is a small   restaurant   but we didn't it looks so nice to eat there. There's also a restroom available and a parking lot. If you want to relax on the beach I would not recommend this beach. You might skip this beach and try to find another one. If you are in this area/Jungmun maybe its more preferable to stay at a resort.For families with kids; I think this beach would suit very well.

Lots of steps but there are plenty of places to rest along the way. Probably prettier to visit in Spring or Fall. It was a cold, gray and windy day, though the sun did come thru a little.  The Haenyeo, lady divers performance at 13:30 and 15:00 is very good and we enjoyed eating some of their very fresh catch! Easy to get to by public transportation but takes a long time. Easier if you have a car.

Lots of fun! Dozens of tame affectionate kitties greet you at the entrance. Cute kittens too! There is a toddler playground with toddler-sized shops play kitchens, jungle gym, rope course, teeter totter? al kid sized. Plenty of great spots for selfies of all kinds. The maze is very tall and take a good 15 minutes at full sprint to wind through and capture stamps on the way to ringing the bell. If you are feeling silly or have small a children with you, this is the spot!
Just a rock in the sea. Good for a few pictures, but it is difficult to take a proper picture as it is always crowded.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

It's very near to Jeju city, within walking distance. It's nice walk strolling along the seaside to dragon head rock and even walk further from there. However this place is always full of tourist, and not easy to get a good picture of this attraction. Nevertheless the environment and surrounding is beautiful and relaxing and I was here during sunset and foggy evening, absolutely beautiful.

It's good place for experience the local community which they will arrange the local guide whom live tin the village to give you the informations and details about the village including the history and culture. There's the translator for the local people since they are hardly speak other language besides Korean. They will explain the way they hand the wooden stick at the gate. The meaning of the stone statue. They will have to room the tell us their history and story. They will have a village walk so everyone can see and experiences their village including photo shooting. They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. The Omecha is sticky so need to mix with water for drinking and contain a lot of vitamins. The local guide will try to up sales their local products after tour such as Omecha and horse bone. They make the bone into small pills and they said its good for those whom need calcium or need recovery from injury and also good for the growth of young kid. They also sell dried squids which already mix with sauce before dried it. It's a good experience as the village is very unique. The house is only one floor and low ceiling since Jeju is very windy. The wall also made with the lava stone from the hallasan mountain.Avoid to go during rainy day even they provide the umbrella during the walk but it's not convenience at all.

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

It was interesting but not too mysterious.  It's just a trick of the eye because of the surroundings.  Anyway, it was a fun little detour and makes for good videos/pictures to show my students back in the States.

It smells so good as soon as you get off the car and pass the entrance. After a short walk, you get to the Forest.  It is also easily accessible for baby strollers as they put some straw mats alone the forest so the whole family can enjoy a wonderful walk in the forest.  Not sure if wheelchairs can roll easily on those mats though but I saw quite some baby strollers.We took a detour after Sangumburi crater (about 20 min away), and spent about an hour in the forest but didn't complete it. Then in another 20-30 min, we arrived at a Five Day Market, which is about 10 min from the Haeyeo (Women Divers) museum.So this was how we planned our route to and from the forest.

It is one of the best place in the world where you can watch sunrise. Even you have to wake up early, have a tiring stair climb and difficult to get clear whether even in summer ; if you ever go to Jeju island, here is one of a place where you must go. On the way Good scenery to enjoy also. In return don't miss the chance of fisherwomen's diving coast and have great breakfast with fresh seafood in the    haenyeo jib    .

It is an old village that show us the homes for the people of Jeju in the past few hundred years. We have been guided through the village by a lady, who speaks very good Chinese's Mandarin. After the tour, they try to sell their products. Some of those are quite expensive. The thing that made us a little unhappy is   I think they have been trying too hard to make us buy something   so we end-up to select the cheapest product but then it became worst when the price was 10X different from what was being offered. It was already nicely packed and we did not want to make her unhappy so we just swipe the card.Anyway, it could be a communication error but both of us are Chinese and heard the same thing. It is a nice place but just be a little careful when you purchase those items.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.

Interesting rock formation open for imagination. Otherwise the area has not much other sights. There is no ticket required, so you can see the popularity is not great. Anyway, nice forested area is good for a quiet walk.

If you've read my post about my 14 hours hike, you'd understand why I didn't go up this peak lol. Anyway, I strolled around the area and had dinner so it's still nice to watch the sceneries around it. If you're sick of Korean food, there's McDonald's, Starbucks and Dunkin' Donuts. Not to mention a fish and chips shop (on the two-way main road) , but I'm not sure if it's good. If you're not sick of Korean facial and body products shopping, Innisfree and Nature Republic are around there.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was on tour with my parents thus the title. The art itself is pretty good. You have different artists interpreting sex in different ways. Just like a typical museum with labels this has one too. Don't miss out on reading what their art are called. It's pretty hilarious. There's a shop where you can buy   stuff   as well. The whole place is open to 18 year olds and above only.

I think we paid KRW2,000 per adult for entry. Walked the lava tube where the temperature dropped by a few degrees. It was raining that day, so it was a good hideout from the downpour. The walk was rather long but many things to see along the way. Remember to wear good waking shoes tho! It can get slippery.

I like to explore super markets in different cities and different countries. It's a good way to see what people are eating. Sometime when I have the courage, I will tried some of the local food. Dongmun Market is one of the popular traditional markets in Jeju. It is big, clean and colourful. They sell all kinds of stuff, like fruit, fresh or dry (some in gift boxes), vegetables, dry mushrooms, herbs, spices and fresh or dry sea food. There are some restaurants ready to serve you. They even sell clothing there. We walked around and took photos, but no one came to pressure us to buy stuff, I like that.Happy Travelling!
I could just sit here for a couple of hours enjoying the scenery and it's beauty. It was windy in October but very calming and relaxing. A good place to   re-charge   and be away from the city life.

Here is much more the beauty of the man made. The Bonsai garden made in an Arboretum which otherwise would've been an entirely sandy/rocky area. A good place to stroll completely away from the coastline. But given that Jeju's primary attractions are natural, spend time here only after seeing the real natural stunners.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Had a lovely half-day here. The island is small, but has beautiful beaches, and a tall hill. We rented a scooter and had a slow day driving around, seeing the sights and having our snacks.I'd say it's a fairly good place to take it easy and go at your own place to be close to nature, but not so close that a cafe by the sea isn't too far away.Visited in early November.

For the last day of our Jejueco tour, the first attraction we visited in the morning was Jeongbang waterfall. Situated on a high cliff by the sea, Jeongbang waterfall is the only waterfall in Asia to fall into the sea. Admission fee is 2,000 won for individuals and 1,600 won per person if you are in a group of 10 or more.When we finally reached our destination, to actually get up-close to Jeongbang waterfall, we had to walk down some (more) steep steps and make our way over a field of rocks/boulders. It was a pretty slippery (and uneven) walk, so make sure you wear footwear with good grip. But the walk was worth it: the sight of the waterfall emptying itself right into the sea which makes it a pretty unique and amazing (since we don?t really have such waterfalls in Singapore).For more photos and our Jeongbang Waterfall experience, do check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jeongbang-waterfall.html :)

Finally we met a Filipino tourist guide here in Seongeup Village. She can speak english very well but of course we used our native tounge/language so she was able to explain to us very well the history of the village and Jeju as well. It's only from her where we learned that the famous Jeju Black Pig used to eat human poop/dung (but that was circa 1940's or earlier).  We also learned from Grace (name of the Filipino guide there) that Korean women, during the early years, were the one who work for the family while the husbands only stay at home. Sad to hear that. =/ We also learned about the history of Stone Grandfather Harabong as well as the various symbolisms used in Jeju.When in Seongeup, make sure to try their Omija, an herbal drink made out of fermented berries. It can help cure acne, headache, kidney problems and good for diabetics. Kinda pricey but worth a shot. They also have other herbal medicines which you can try. As we all know, Koreans, especially their ancestors, are used to taking medicinal plants so I guess they are really credible enough when they say that this or that plant is effective for healing ailments. Google the benefits of OMIJA.By the way, this is also the place where the famous Koreanovela Dae Jangeum (Jewel in the Palace) was filmed.If you happen to visit Seongeup Village, ask for Grace as a guide. You will definitely learn a lot. And oh, we get to check out old korean houses as well. ^_^NOTE: I think there are many communities within Seongeup village but ask your guide to specifically drop you off at the community where Grace is. No entrance fee as well.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

Before we arrive, the tour guide told us the story of the dragon and how the mark of the dragon landed create all the cracks on ground. At night with spot lights, it added some mysteries of the legend and when we climb all the way down hill at the dragon head,. it complete the story itself. A good trip full of imagination

Be sure to wear good shoes for the somewhat uneven - but not particularly slippery - walk and a raincoat for the dripping water.    There is only 1km of the lava tube which is open to tourists, so the entire walk is 2km roundtrip.   There are a number of informational plaques along the way as well as before you even enter.    There are restrooms and a restaurant by the parking lot.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. As a bear lover, I enjoy this museum & appreciate all the hard work put into each & individual presentation & its theme. Be warn that its really for the young & young at heart. My only regret is that I missed the outdoor cafe. Didnt realised after I exited & look down thru the windows. Must have missed the signages? Overall , a good way to spend 1-2 hours

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .
Although the weather wasn't perfect for a visit this afternoon, however, it hasn't spoiled a positive impression. Lots of tourists anyways, and it leaves a good feeling of connectedness with nature.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first. After being in the cave, this is a good way to warm your body under the sun (well, at least during this season).So, it took 10 minutes to work out the right direction with the map, then we tried without the map and again it was ten minutes, then we left our 5 years old daughter to find the way out...still 10 minutes.I cannot define it challenging but fun for sure and super-rewarding to see your kid beaming with light every time she play the bell!Definitely worth combining cave and maze!

- Jeju is also known for it's high quality green tea. Was recommended by the people at my resort to visit this place. Reason being it is very clean. I did not do too many hikes in Jeju and this was just one of the few I did. Is a quaint place with some very good drinks and desserts. But the crowd is overwhelming. I would skip this place altogether if I visit Jeju next. Sunrise Peak is the nickname - I was sadly not able to see the sunrise because the weather, but it was still a beautiful lookout. The hike isn't too bad - I did have to catch my breath a few times because some parts are steep, but it was worth it. The path is lit, so you don't need a flashlight. Get there early because the good seats will be taken!The ferry to Udo Island is also close to here. You can find a path outside the town that leads to the ferry terminal. The path also provides great picture taking for Seongsan.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

I came here after a hike up Hallasan and boy the hassle of trying to find it was so worth it. The pork bbq we had (don't know the name of the restaurant) was amazing, anyone who has had Korean bbq before knows how good it is, don't miss this place.
For hikers this place was the good spot, but for some who doesn't like hiking you can still take pictures specially during winter and experience the snow.

We were brought there by our guide and had no idea what the place was about. We spent over an hour there and had a great time . You need to go there armed with a sense of humor a handphone with a good camera setting  and the ability to use the camera and it?셲 functions for the best results . I would certainly recommend this to anyone with young children  young adults and not so young adults who are young at heart!

We went there in 2017 and spent several hours going through the facility. It was one of the highlights of the trip. I strongly recommend it for families and even couples. It provides some lighter entertainment which is good for all age groups. Price is nominal.

we visited two parks in Jeju. Hallim and Spirited Garden. ticket price was almost the same for both but Hallim was by far much better and bigger with good design and a lot of different and amazing trees and some birds too. It is really a must visit for Jeju visitors to spend around two hours enjoying the park.
We liked the place and very well keptWe spent a good three hours here and had snacks coffee and icecream (twice...) All good. easy to park too

We just visited the chocolate museum as a family and it was a bit of a let down. The tickets were 6000 for adults (tickets for children in elementary I think were 4500?) and they gave us free Americano. There really wasn't that much to see  and the place smelled funny. I think if you?셱e really interested in learning about the past of cacao and chocolate in Korea then this might be a fun place to visit  but if you don't have much interest in that  it might be a waste of money.However they do offer chocolate making classes every hour for little kids under 13. So there were a lot of children there when we went. Might be a fun place to visit with children :)They also sell chocolate  and we tried a sample and it was pretty good and rich in quality. We also bought 3 bars of 70% cacao for 30 000. The original price was 36 000  but with the entree ticket you get a 6 000 discount.

review: We have took a lot of photos and it amazed us a lot!! must go!!It will take up a good 1 - 1.5 hours to go around the whole museum.

we have been to a number of such markets in korea/japan  and this was nothing new. the usual stalls selling food  produce  vegetables  dried foods  household items  textiles  souvenirs  etc.this market seemed to be pretty much smaller too only a couple of rows. couldnt see spending more than an hour here. good thing was that we didnt get harassed by stall owners every stall we walk past and the prices seemed reasonable too. bought snacks and small souvenirs here. also  it wasnt that crowded compared to some other markets

We arrived at 10am and the place was delightfully empty. The downside was that there was no glassblowing display. However  the walks  the gardens and the exhibits are all interesting and enjoyable. Families of all ages can spend a good hour here.

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It?s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.

This venue offers quite a few exhibits for photo moment. Kids will surely like his place. The place can be done in an hour time unless you spend time explaining to the kids what each exhibit is about. The gift shop offer a good range of teddy bear to buy as a gift.

This place was AWESOME!!! Do yourself a favor though -- stay at the resort that is immediately there. We didn't and regretted it for 4 straight days ... This beach is really good and we spent 6-8 hours there a day!

The aquarium is spacious.  You can see a lot of sea animals no matter how hot cold or rainy the outdoor is.  Taking a leaflet at the entrance is a must because the show time is up-dated.  It is so funny to see the penguins line up to eat food and jump up the stairs.  The otters are also interesting when you see them playing through the tunnels and on the swinging bed.  The 'stars' of the aquarium can be seen at the theatre which is attractive and interesting. My family stayed there for more than three hours.  The soft toys sold there are in good quality and my daughter bought a penguin as a souvenir.  There are food shops for people to enjoy but we didn't try any.

review: The aquarium is good and English-friendly (so you know what you're looking at). The show at the end is aimed at kids and solely in Korean but as it's mostly visual that's not a problem. Families can definitely spend a fun few hours here. However the admission fee is excessive (40900 won for adults at time of writing) especially when most of the other main attractions in Jeju are either free entry or priced around 2000 won. I think this one ticket cost me more than all other entrance fees during my 5 day visit to the island combined. If you aren't visiting with children I suggest giving it a miss.
