review: Teady bear musuem in Jeji island is another touris spot for bear lover. 2 hours walk in the museum is a good walking tour whr en travel in Jeji.
Spent two hours hear on a rainy day. Great fun and lots of good photos. Even though quite full pf people still able to see the attractions and get good photos.

Our son LOVED it here and has been asking to go back daily since we left. It could use a few more things to do  but you can easily spend a good few hours here  especially if your children are familiar with the animation. Everything seemed very safe and well organized. We didn't pay extra money to go into the play area  but it sounded like kids were having a blast in there too. No idea why adults have to pay entrance though.... as theres nothing for adults to really do and the only reason they are entering is to go with their children. Many play parks around Korea offer free entry for adults  it's a shame here doesn't follow suit. Also  the kids play room with the balls and lego blocks is a little lacking..... our son still loved it  but it could use a few more items to build/play with etc

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

Lots of historical houses. I would suggest getting the audio guide if you haven't seen these types of asian history areas before.However saying 'museum' doesn't do the place justice as it's a vast expanse of space that will take a few hours to walk through if you listen/read all the info descriptions.Good for photos

Long cave path that has been carved out by lava flows.  Its just basically a walk thru the cave and back.  Paths are not paved and can be treacherous at times.  Wear good walking shoes.  Bring a tripod if you want to take some nice pics inside the cave.  Fairly dark in spaces.  The walk should take about 1.5 hours.

Jeju Folk Village is an outdoor museum that places various houses in Jeju during late 1800s. It's a good place to bring your family to learn about the lifestyle in Jeju back then. It is located nearby Seopjikoji hence it can be included in your itinerary if you're visiting nearby.However if you're into adventure or a crowded place like a city you would not want to visit this museum. For me I enjoyed learning hence my short visit to the museum an hour before its closing time was a pleasant one.
It's good to learn the history of the island but I spent like an hour listen to the guide try to sell a horse bone. Not recommend this place at all.

It's fun about this place. Entrance fees 12 000 won per person. There's is a show every hour about 15mins each show. But one thing need to highlight is  the explanation are all in Korean words. So for foreigner like us may have difficulties on understand the instructions on the activities. But so far I very enjoy. Is good for indoor visit especially during raining day.

It was so quiet when we arrived.  We weren't even sure if it was opened until someone greeted us.  We spend an hour here watching a indoor 3-d movie and had someone guided us within the garden.  Its good to know there is a 'fantasy' in which the people believe in Jeju Island.  I wondered what the three men were thinking when three beautiful were presented to them as I cant help to smile when I hear is them laughing in the 3d movie.

It was my first time ever to any of the ALIVE series and honestly it wasn't fantastic but I could be bias cause I hate crowded attractions and people hog and does not wait for their turn. My recommendation is to go during off peak season with at least a group of 3 as some of the displays can fit in a couple. I guess it will be more fun as well. Condition of displays are pretty good and one could easily spend at least 1.5 hours in there. There is also an outdoor park which features more abstract art which is pretty interesting. Overall worth the money? I'll say it's alright but it will be a place that I'll visit once.

It was hot at the cave entrance at 32 degrees.  There is notice at entrance on temperature drop to 10 degrees as we continued the walk.  It is a 1 hour to and fro walk along the dark and slippery caveт囹. Good for those who like trekking.
It is a very different museum mostly for kids but me and my wife visit d because we were in the vicinity but turned out to be pretty good for the 10000 k we spent for an hour.

Incredible work of art it was a great place to visit. The number of pictures were beyond my expectation; need more than 1 hour to see all exhibitions. Need a good camera for good quality. Sometimes need flash to get a brighter picture. ??0000 only.

If you're a bit kinky and you like art this is the place for you. About 100 different sculptures in all size with amazing details. This site will make you laugh and smile no matter how serious you are. Good attraction for about 2 houres.

If you just wan to spend for few hours while waiting for your flight. Here the good place. Entrance 8000KRW.  A small area block up for your big luggage you will have locker for your shoe. Once you enter inside you will find a long locker to store your belonging. It can fit in a small backpack.  Take a spa relax and rejuvenate before go for rest room. There are a lot ppl go there for overnight stay even it is weekday perhaps just their culture. The living hall area and sleep place rather to say it's hot I will say is steaming. If you kind of person can't stay for hot this might not be a good place to sleep for you unless you are very tired. You can take blanket from the counter you pay for your entrance fee. Where the pillow just look it from any empty room

I was here in September right before a typhoon hit Jeju. It was raining after dinner and there was nowhere to go. We decided to visit this attraction and spend a good 2 hours right up to closing - taking many fun and hilarious pictures. It is the largest of such attraction I've visited. Unfortunately there were no taxis by the time we left and we have to walk back to our hotel in nearby Jungmun.

I visited here on November 2018 when blossom flower season was gone and winter hadn't came yet. Even though I missed the best scene the weather and landscape were too beautiful. The park is not too big with many corners are designed for taking selfie. I think spending around 1-2 hours here is a good choice. I also recommend you to bring some foods and drinks then you can sit for a while and enjoy the environment.

I think the museum is open until 11 pm so this could be one of the things to do on a slow evening if you are near Seogwipo. Lot of interesting 3d art sorta stuff and if you are in a group or with kids and are into taking pictures it's worth it. Prices are ok and you can spend a good 2 hours in the museum. Overall though I would say it's nothing THAT great so better manage your expectations.

I think the best part is the mini train ride where you actually drive the train yoursel with the kids sit at the back. My kid like train ride  that's why I think it's worth a visit and rate this place very good. Otherwise you can have chance to visit some of the world most famous architecture in an hour.
I rented a motobike and rode all around the island in 2 hours. This Island is a gem. Don't miss it. The ferry price was very cheap and you can have good korean foods on the Island.
I really and strongly recommend you to visit this market. Lots of food and other hand made goods are there. You will enjoy about 3 hours af hanging and buying things there

Hi got Mr Kim as our tour guide for a day at Jeju. He came to hotel half an hour earlier than the designated time. He bring us to eat pork noodles before we start our tour. He is very accommodative with our request. Especially is a raining day and he still being us to outdoor tour site. If you are in Jeju for a tour pls get Kim. He able to speak little English and little Chinese. But for a Korean is consider very good.

Good place to see all the monuments in one time.It takes around 1 hour and half to visit all the park and the price is 9 000Krw for one adult.Some monuments needs some refresh work but the others are in a good state.
Good place to explore for 1-2 hours. Be prepared to walk. Bring a waterproof jacket and good walking shoes with good grip as it's wet inside the cave
Good experience and a cooling walk underground. I was expecting something more and was disappointed when reached the end. Took about an hour.

Except a receptionist  very good place.I strongly recommend this place.Museum  Korean mandarin cookies making  foot bath  a large botanical garden  picking Korean mandarins.You can stay just a hour  but You'd better use more time.It's not free  but absolutely not expensive.
Estimate to spend 2 hours. wear good shoes and jacket. The cave is quite cold and wet. Uneven roads and required to walk on few staircase too. but overall experience is great.
Crowded with tourists during lunch hours. We had a green tea cakes amd icecream. They are wonderful. Service staff speaks good command of English. Highly recommended.

Come here once and you don't need to travel the world. Here you'll find minis of dozens of world wide land marks  a short and relatively small attraction that can be conquered in under an hour. Good fun and very charming.

Bring your camera as many 3D pictures that bring you into the scene. Good for photo taking and each picture show location of where to take.  If you really serious taking each photo 2 hours will be spent over there. It also situates close to hotels cluster walking distance from major hotels.

Bored?  Run out of things to do for the evening?  this is good for about an hour's worth of entertainment.  Visit with low expectations and your experience will be improved.As others have stated the statues are redundant and some are just kind of creepy (fat lady in her panty with a skinny undersized man).  The high note are the dioramas depicting different sexual acts.Not only do they look accurate but they also look very cute.

A wonderful hour of Korean/Mongolian drama with beautiful horses and very talented Mongolian riders.Had a chance to pet and feed the horses before the show.Great acrobatics.Would be good for all ages.
A good place to spend 1-2 hours. The green tea plantation area was well-maintained. Great green tea latte. I thought they should offer sampling of various merchandise.

A beautiful island and it was nice to travel around in an ATV along the coastline although 2.5 hours wasn't quite enough after taking a break at a cafe. It might be a good idea to stay overnight at Udo too.
Worth it, Super good! Done in about an hour and with young children. Eye opening and interesting geography lesson. UNESCO 3 Star site.

When we have a summer vacation in Jeju, it was one of must see.  If you want to visit, visit when it is magic hour (golden hour). The sky makes perfect blue color. It was very good place especially for children. They had experience in making necklace with glass. The sculptures in the Glass Castle were beautiful.  Visit with children. It is good place for children.

We were looking for a good place to shop and buy souvenirs and we found this place in Jungang area. Lot of cheap items from clothes, bags, shoes and beauty products.Tips:- GPS: 752-8776- There is a public parking in front of Jeju Bank along Ohyeon-gil. 3-4 hours cost us 3700Krw.- Jejumok Gwana is just on the West exit (exit 11). You might want to drop by if you got time.- There are Korean food in the middle section. Cheap but taste good.

We spent may be half an hour here and had a good time. The maze is very pretty and you don't see mazes made from trees in the US any more, so this was a treat. The mazes were not difficult, but can be confusing. The admission was quite reasonable, so I do recommend this place if your family is into mazes. Oh, there were a lot of cats roaming the ground and made good subjects for photos.

We spent around 2-3 hours in Hallim Park, and didn't regret it. The flowers and the botanical garden were beautiful, the cave and the water area were also very interesting. Very good opportunities to take photos. As we went in April, we got to enjoy the countless cherry blossoms! My personal highlight was the 300-year old bonsai in the bonsai area. If you're in the area, this is definitely worth a visit. There are several restrooms inside the park, as well as spots where you can buy food at a reasonable price.

We hired Mr Kim Si Nam's service for a day, touring the Eastern route of Jeju island (Woljeongri beach, Seongeup Folk Village, Manjanggul Cave, Seopikoji, Seongsan Ilchulbong and Noksan-ro). Tour was stated to be 8-9 hours but we ran a little overtime and Mr Kim was kind not to charge extra. Throughout the journey from one attraction to another, he explained the history behind them even though his command of English is rather limited and took many gorgeous photos for us. We are indeed thankful to have met him and will definitely hire his services again when we return to Jeju.Mr Kim, thank you for taking such good care of us. We miss the beautiful Jeju island!

We hired bicycles at a shop adjacent the pier and cycled around the whole island. Along country roods, there were many scenic spots, mostly adjacent to the sea,  where we could take pictures. Besides, there were many cafes and kiosks where we could dine and rest.  Cycling around the island in a relaxing pace took about 3 to 4 hours. It was a very good experience.

Was skeptical at first. But the park turns out to be pretty nice.  With amazing bonzai (some over 300 years old), flowers, lava caves and even peacocks!  We were lucky that we visited during cherry blossoms season, so it was an added bonus.  Only caution is don't go there hungry.  Food there is terrible and expensive.  Much better to eat elsewhere then visit the park for a good 3-4 hours.
To do after Hallasan hiking. Very good place to feel relax and quiet for one hour! In case you feel hungry, go to the hotel next to it they have a grocery!

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!
This park is bigger, big to occupy few hours. The upkeep is not as good as many other parks in Korea.

This market sells many goods. I would recommend it for buying souvenirs from Jeju, like chocolate crunch and chocolate. There were also shoes and clothes for sale but not so fashionable. There are many shops selling dry and wet goods, mandarin oranges and other Jeju products. It is really large and you can spend quite a few hours there. Good for wet weather as it is covered.

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

The theme is good and it is very funny and interesting. Although we arrived the entrance at 18:00, we were able to complete the adventure within half an hour. Highly recommend for you especially with kids.
The park is quite big and there are many interesting stuff to see. There's a bonsai garden, a small hanok village, bird park etc. It's quite an interesting place where you can spend a good 2 hour.

The market is huge, we were walking for about an hour and still not sure if we cover even half the market. There?s fresh seafood cured seafood, Korean pastries, clothes, kimchi ingredients, etc etc etc. Good photo opportunities here as well. Or just come here to soak in the local atmosphere.

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The grounds are amazing and beautiful. Different times of year you can see beautiful blooms like azaleas, hydrangeas, bougainvillea, etc. It?s definitely worth some time to see the natural beauty of the flora. The animal enclosures are very disappointing, because as a true natural park, you would expect better conditions for the animals. The caves are a good break from the sun and heat. They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

The course I went to is Seongpanak course. This place is the most comfortable of the various courses. And many beautiful scenery unfolds, which varies from season to season. The course here is good enough to climb, even if you are young or older. You can climb the mountain very flat, just over the slightly steep staircase course in the middle. You can think of the round-trip time for about four hours.

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

Only 1km of the 7.5km lava tube is open to the public, but I highly recommend coming! Expect to spend about an hour admiring the beauty of this natural volcanic formation!While we were there, it had rained the night before and was still drizzling slightly, so the ground was damp. Good to wear proper shoes with good grip (we were thankful for our boots) as the ground is a rather uneven terrain and can be slippery when wet. It's also rather dimly lit, with some lighting inside to guide your path and highlight specific features found in the cave.Even though there is only one entry/ exit point, there is much to see (if you're into geology/ geography/ nature lover, otherwise it'll just look like the same dark cavernous backdrop) as you loop back to the exit point.
Once you enter the cave and start to walk inside the cave, you will get a good amount of knowledge about the cave and how it is form. Very educational and quite a good 1 hour walk inside the cave.
Not so good as all is make of glass. All in korean, nothing much to see. walk out of the castle within 1 hour. (quite a waste of money, dun go unless really got a lot of spare time)

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. Spend 3 hours there.Suggest to go for a toilet break before going thru the entrance.Bring baby carriers, cause the road is uneven. Have to be extra careful especially going with kids.There are 2 entrance. (follow the counter clock wise direction, where the entrance is situated behind the huge ship)Enjoy the scenery, watchout for the waves too.Their is a canola flower field where you can take some instagram photos too (need to pay to enter)
Long, impressive and well maintained. It has good English explanations. Surly worth  the visit. About 1.5 hours all in all

Know this place from   Princess Hours   drama, and i love this museum. A lot unique diorama. This place is so Instagram-able, there is a lot beautiful spot to take a picture. And also, they know how to treat a very old teddy, good job!

Jeju Glass Castle is a must see museum. It has outdoor which can be seen with in 2 hours & indoor as well. There are a lot of glass shapes. This museum is good for people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. The entrance ticket is little bit expensive.
It was a good place to bring the girlfriend and rent a scooter for a 2 hour, romantic, oceanside drive.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

If you go to Jeju Island, this is a good place to go. There is a Kitty Cafe inside, it is the same as those in Seoul. Apart from the Cafe, there is also an souvenir shop, you can buy those limited edition products there. If you drive there, you may need to wait for the parking space during peak hours.
I would recommend others to spend an hour or so in this site. Spend good time with wife strolling the path and of course, took some beautiful pictures.

I was planning on going up gwaneumsa and coming down seongpanak but seongpanak is closed until 31st Jul, 18 so I came down the the same. It took me about 3.5 hr to climb up, and 3 hrs to come down. Together with my lunch breaks, I finished the entire round trip in a little over 7 hours. Unfortunately, it was  really misty when I was at the summit, so, i didn't get to see the crater lake. I highly recommend bringing a pair of trekking poles and good hiking shoes.

I thoroughly enjoyed the Castle. I got to try my hand at glass blowing  (I'm not very good) and found the detail in the pieces amazing. You can wander around at leisure, take as long as you like (I was there for 2 hours). There's a short 500m walk at the back you should do if able, there's all sorts of surprising pieces hidden in the woods.

I think it was unfortunate that it rained the day we went. The grounds were muddy. The kids were having fun. The adults were grumpy. Thankfully, we were prepared with umbrellas and raincoats. Still, the kids' shoes got all muddy and we had other places to go to after this. So, not the most pleasant of experiences. But to be fair, the maze is challenging enough to provide good fun for about an hour or so.

I stumbled upon this area by coincidence, I had not made any plans yet that day so I decided to visit the waterfalls. My decision was a good one! The colours of the water, lake and waterfall are amazing. There were some people but it was not too crowdy, I could easily take pictures and just wonder around, which is what I did for a few hours.

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.

Having just visited the newly opened Teddy Bear Museum in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China (by the same group), this original museum in Jeju was a little underwhelming, even for a solid teddy bear fan like me. Unlike those in Chengdu, I didn't appreciate the fact that all teddies in Jeju were enclosed in glass cases. Impossible to take a decent pic with them!There was a good collection of antique bears. Great for a collector like myself. Also there was the supposedly most expensive teddy bears in the world. The LV bear and the diamond bear.For sale of their Elvis bears I believe, there was a small theater on the second floor showing 4 mins Elvis teddy concert every quarter of the hour. Perhaps I went at a later hour (5pm), I was the only one in the theater. Appreciate that the museum is opened till 8pm in the evening, so it's great as a quick destination pre or post dinner, if you are staying or hanging around the Jungmum Resort Area. The museum was located right next to Lotte Hotel. There was a Lotteria on the ground floor but it was closed during my visit. An attractive and well stocked teddy store on the ground floor too, unlike its sad and sparse Chengdu cousin. Happy that there were some collector grade Korean handmade teddies for sale. Their house brand   so-called   limited edition replica made-in-China white Alfred bear (real limited edition would come with serial numbers) came in a nice copycat Steiff look alike gift box and a photo with a Korean prince. At only USD 35, it's great as a souvenir/gift!I like the outdoor park area. Great for kids to run around. Overall not a very big place. Whole place would take about an hour.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.
Had a few hours before catching flight, chose this beach because of location, but turns out it was a good choice. the rocks, and clear water was something you do not see in the US

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

A good place to go if you love Teddy Bear. For us, I had a good time having some history lessons with my 8 year old daughter. There's a display of historical events using Teddy Bears as characters, eg, opening of disney land, WW2, man landing on moon, return of Hong Kong to China in 1997 etc. the place isn't very big. spending 1 hour here would be sufficient. make sure you take photos with PSY as Teddy Bear, or Steve Jobs as Teddy Bear! There are 12 characters in total.
A good place to check out unique volcanic rock formations. A very popular place with local and Chinese tourists. Still, it is worth the hour we spent here.

Went past the falls as we were looking for the tourist info office so decided to have a look. As it had been fairly dry the falls were not very spectacular and though it claims to be the only one in Asia that falls directly into the ocean I am pretty sure Duden falls in Turkey are in Asia and fall into the ocean. Some stairs take you down to the falls - they seem less lengthy when you are climbing back up which is a good thing and we rewarded ourselves with some ice cream!!
We didn't like it at all. There was pretty much no water falling out of the water falls. You climb very steep stairs and get very tired. The bridge is good for a few nice clicks though.
I went there at night and there was this huge spotlight shining on the rock itself. Not a good place for the elderly people as climbing up and down that narrow staircase is a hassle.
a unique nature architecture here. There are extreme tour there which is to walk and climb around the coast. It will close if weather is not good. Near to Sanbangsan
We go to Hyeopjae beach whenever in Jeju, lovely sand, good safe swimming, great rocks to climb over, the grandkids love it

Unlike Hallasan and Ilchulbong, the shape of the crater is not very obvious. Moreover, there are less climbing and walking involved here. The main attraction here is actually the field along the path to the observation point of the crater. Make sure your camera fully charged and enough memory because it is a good photography location.

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

This is a UNESCO site and I find it quite awesome, how Mother Nature made these underground caves. Do note that you'll have to climb steep stairs up and down to the caves, so I wouldn't recommend the elderly folks to go in. Do bring along a jacket as it can get chilly down in the caves. Also bring along a torch and have good anti-slip walking shoes as it can be a little wet and slippery.

There are statues of the Future Buddha, Maitreya; Bodhisattva of Compassion,? an outdoor huge Golden statue of Buddha, hundreds of miniature green Buddhas.? If you climb up the 471 steps, you will reach a cave with a statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion. The tears that she constantly cries for all the pain of this   ocean of suffering   world collects in pools up the stairs below the altar.? Visitors drink it and make prayers before it. If you drink 3 sips of the water, you will enjoy longevity in good health. Great temple to visit.

The weather was extremely good and the scene was nice.Only have 2 hrs to walk this time, will definitely climb up if i have a chance to go again.Recommended to go in the morning, less tourist and more fresh air.

The temple is at the foot of the Sambang mountain, where you have a choice to scale 400 steps to the mid point of the mountain to see another goddess statue there. A good 30 mins climb up and down at a casual pace with photo opportunities of the scenery.

The place is so great. The geopark is one of UNESCO heritage world. We must climb at about 500 stairs to reach the peak. In a good weather, you can go there early in the morning to see the sunrise. The combination of mountain and beach (with the black sand) is so beautiful. You can also see the performance of woman diver there and buy live seafood.
Sunrise peak another UNESCO,drizzling while we climb the peak. Crowded even the weather wasn't good. Descending is nice.
Such a great waterfall in Jeju island, it's good to be able to take photo with this Mother Nature. You will not be regret to climb down and up to the waterfall. A place that must visit.

Our 70 year old tour guide could climb these rocks to get here. The Grand Canyon of Jeju. Whilst it was breathtaking, I couldn?t help but constantly call out to the kids to be careful of the slippery rocks. There are life rings hanging on the cliffs but let?s be realistic. With currents that strong, if you fell into the water, the current would crash you straight into the rocks. We went early morning when the tide was out but could feel the tide level rising. Our guide wanted to go further as he said it was more spectacular.Make sure you go with good gripped sneakers and a jacket. You are on the edge of the ocean after all.
just climbing up in darkness is an experience by itself. wear good shoes, warm clothes, water and some munchies. take your time coming down and enjoy the scenic beauty.

It's a nice place to take some nice photos with the teddies.  Lots of them there huge ones as well.  The most I've seen in one single location. Good effort. You can touch them,  hug them,  even climb over them.  Our children had a fun time.

It was very good and origin. I though I'd given up before I even start, but the quite,the white of the snow amazed me, I kept moving head. Lost of local people climb on the last day of 2014. and I have to say is they climbed so fast,we were passed by many followers.

If you want to see sunrise, please go to Seongsan Ilchulbong: It's very beautiful place. You should wake up in the early morning. It'll take 20 mins to climb in the peak. And you can experience excellent atmosphere there. You can take lots of picture because of its beauty. Good luck to you, hope you can see sunrise in the Seongsan Ilchubong

I found this waterfall a better experience than Cheonjiyeon Falls as you can go very close to the waterfall. Be prepared to walk down a lot of stairs and then climb over rocks to get close to the falls, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Don't bother paying for the museum close to the gate, it's a waste of time but only 500 Won if you want to.

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

Worth spending the money and time to have a good laugh. Even the kids were laughing loudly. Not much talking but many actions. They speak good English so not a problem to understand.I was even being selected to go on the stage to perform with them!! Unforgettable!

Went there in the morning. Was windy but filled with tourists. They have some photo locations that will look good on a photo graph.not a place you can stay for long but a good place to drop by if u have some spare time.

Went during the summer and its still pretty cold down there. Its a good rainy day itinerary as its entirely underground. Be warned that it can get really cold when  its raining though. Advised to wear good shoes are you wont be walking on flat ground and its quite wet and slippery. Its pretty interesting to learn  of the formation of the lava tube and a must go if its your first time in Jeju.

Well worth the small trek down.  Do a little rock/boulder hopping to the base and you can get a nice spray.  If you catch this waterfall during the rainy season or after a good rain it will be much more powerful.  Take the time to visit this place...maybe a little crowded but plenty of space to find your own spot.

Well if an already successful huge company invest in something new it can't go too wrong. I expected this place to be more authentic but what we got was a commercialized sugar-coated tea plantation experience. Nonetheless the place is very professional of course the quality is great and both the tea and desserts are yummy. The surroundings are beautiful the air is fresh and the scent of the plantation is amazing. It's a safe choice if you prefer a guaranteed good time over something unexpected and little bit more unique. It's a sophisticated modern place that reminds me more of a spa than a tea house. Regardless you can buy good quality tea here and some other gifts that comes in beautiful packages. All in all we had a good time!

We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!
We had good time playing in this maze. It is well-maintained the owner/ caretaker is accommodating and they also have several cats who will welcome and waiting to be cuddled.
We had fun at this maze park! Seemed easy but not! My son and I had a good time trying to figure the maze out! Kids will definitely enjoy! Lovely place for good exercise too!

We had a very good time discovering the different houses that corresponded to different areas of the island and different social statuses. The re-enactement was excellent. Very relaxing stroll beautiful landscaping.

We had a great night out with TeamK's pub crawl! The bars we went to were really fun and we met lots of local Koreans and Foreigners living on the island! Having the pub crawl sticker was great fun and allowed us to talk with other travellers easily! Thank you to TeamK for the good times!!

We did only this folk village with my family and friends. This recreated the feeling of living a long time ago in korea it communicates well the differences of different backgrounds. We did not hire the audio guide and we had two korean speakers with us who were able to read everything. It was fabulous for my kids to see and touch most of the displays plenty to keep them occupied. We saw a dance and others getting photos taken in wedding costumes and a Korean Drama being filmed. Overall the experience was a good cultural morning out. We did not eat there as we were meeting friends for lunch but it looked very traditional
we believe you made also good memories at this time visit ^^

We arrived and were surrounded by Koreans dressed in proper hiking gear and walking sticks. The day wasn't too warm and we made it up to the summit in good time. It was lovely to relax at a beach afterwards though.

Very rocky do be sure to wear appropriate shoes. Lots of great angles to take photos without having lots of other tourists in the shot. Go around dinner or lunch time as they have some local women selling freshly prepared seafood (I'm a vegetarian and didn't try it but looked good).
Unexpected place. Really huge. Good for family visit. Fun time with the kids. You may need to spend the whole day in the area.

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...

This waterfall is much smaller than Jeongbang Falls  and is worth spending the time walking to it if you're in the area. Beautiful clear blue water beneath  it would make a good swimming spot in hot weather!

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.

This was actually my 2nd 3D museum that I'd been too. While it had different structures and art pieces it's also bigger than the 'trick eye museum' in Hongdae Seoul. This could be good or bad:Good: there's obviously more photo opportunities more of a day out and worth more for your moneyBad: you need to be in the mood to have lots of photos taken turns out multiple photo taking can actually be draining!Don't get me wrong though we had a great time! There's also a go-kart track round the back which you can use for extra money.

This is where physics takes over. Let the fun takes over. What you see don't really make sense until the guide explains it to you. All in natural surroundings and in good time. Don't forget to try out the street food there while you are at it. Made my day. Cheers again!

This is more of a shop and cafe than a museum. The museum part is just a few display cabinets that leads to a cafe with goods displayed for sale. The tea plantation across the street is a flat moderately sized area that pales in comparison to the vast rolling and picturesque tea plantation of cameron highlands.This attraction is not worth the time unless one is a tea-lover.
This is a good place to spend some time. I really love the Obama bear. It looks so cute! and also the ones with Korean traditional clothes. Joanna is really obsessed wtih teddy bears!!

There wasn't much to look and read (all in Korean) but caring and friendly staff made our day.For one of the most visited city or area for foreign tourists  it's hard to believe that the most of the places do not have English speaking staff.We were having hard time finding good place to go and dine  recommendations by the staff at the Chocolate Land were very very helpful. Also  the chocolates we purchased with his help turned out very good.If you are in Jung Moon tour sector  need a little break for a free coffee (it's free with a coupon you get when you pay an admission) and some help from an English and Chinese speaking staffs.

The overall theme was a good one cause you get to see the various famous landmarks in a fraction of its size. We went on a day where there wasn't many people so thats a good thing cause we can take our time with the photographs. The entrance fee was the most expensive among all the entrance fee standing at 20000 won for 3 people (2 adult 1 student) but it was pretty fun despite the shabby appearances.

The overall theme was a good one  cause you get to see the various famous landmarks in a fraction of its size. We went on a day where there wasn't many people  so thats a good thing  cause we can take our time with the photographs. The entrance fee was the most expensive among all the entrance fee  standing at 20 000 won for 3 people (2 adult  1 student)  but it was pretty fun despite the shabby appearances.

The Lee Jung-Seob Street near the museum is where more time can be spent (than the Lee Jung-Seob Museum) with some good restaurants and cafes lining the street that is decorated with art influenced by him or replicas of his work. Visitors can also take a look at his old home located on this street.

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.

The cafe is pretty good with green tea drinks of all kind and dessert! We tried the green tea ice cream which was really good. However almost EVERYONE comes here so it will take some time to find a table. Be patient and enjoy the outdoor fields. I personally thought the outdoor fields had more to see than the so called museum. They also have a variety of green tea for you to buy as souvenirs too. Really easy to find with a huge free parking lot.
The aquarium is nice the show was good.I just wish there was more of the animal involvement but my daughter and I had a good time though.

review: The aquarium is good and the penguins and sharks are worth watching. Huge collection of marine life you cant miss...The show seemed to be a bit dragging. Before the sealion and dolphin show there was a 'good pirate bad pirate ' show which for me was a bit boring. Dolphin show also wasted time showing videos. But towards last 5 mins it was good.

review: The ?Dragon Hair? rock location is near Jeju airport and a good recommendation if you are trying to burn some time prior to departing Jeju. The location has spacious parking and allows visitors easy access to the actual rock.

That was amazing. I used to be student in SKorea. And it was my best memorable trip in that time. Its a little expensive specially for students. We were around 30 persons and our hotels was really good smin services and the price. I really recommend u to travel Jeju once go to SK.
thank you so much for your decision to visit our museum on another day. and also we are very happy to hear you had a good time at our museum. thanks again and have a nice day ^^
thank you so much for visiting and also a good comment. please let me know instagram id of yours. i will follow you and i will post our museum's news sometimes. have a nice day ^^

Some of the mini structures in the land look like not taken good care for a long time and  most of the painting had faded. If you are travelling with kids and have extra time can go for a short visit .
simple & peaceful environment. not too crowded & good for taking time for scrolling. staff also professional & nice with good communication.
Seri World is a super basic theme park. To me  the only thing fun to do was ride the Go Karts  which was a good time  but expensive and pretty small. I wouldn't return.

Second time at O Sulloc and the grounds are beautiful and offers nice picture opportunities and a relaxing vibe. Spent a good amount of time at Innisfree House where you can buy packages of soap and customise them for friends. Good activity to engage the kids and also make gifts for friends :) Green tea ice cream was good and the tea leaves smelled really good as well.
scenic and windy. crowds were in the hundreds so it can get squeezy. good place to go for pictures if u have the time

Reminds me of kenyas hells gate. The place is a sight to behold. Be carefull to put on comfy shoes that have great treads and grips so that you dont slip on the sometimes slippery rocks. Also find out about tides. If its high tides then definately you will be soaked by action of water on your feet. Good place though. I recommend finnishing it with a horse ride by the ajoshi at the exit for man won and a cold jeju tangerine juice.

reach here after Manjanggul cave as sunny & good weather. it has some cats near around all of them were sleepy or lazily style. before went inside the maze. it has a small garden with some flowers. and the maze actually not to difficult or complex but good for take rest when you finished the game. it has shelter & you could buy a cold drink at there. ok to try if you got time.

Personally I love this place very much.It's a good place to relaxing your mind.The place is huge yet I do find peace at every corner and section inside.You should come by yourself or with your family.I've been to couple of aqua place in several country and I think its worth it to spend time here.However don't waste your time with a cheesy diving show.I recommend you to go to nearby White House (actually Light House) rather than waiting for the diving show time. So I'll definitely come again!

review: Other beaches such as Geumneng or Hyupjae are shallow and no waves so it is good for family with little kids. Otherwise Jungmun Saekdal beach is deep and has quite waves. If you are not a good swimmer you should have a tube or life jacket here. My kids are all teenagers and all good swimmers. They complained about other beaches: they are for toddlers not for thembut they had really good time in Jungmun Saekdal beach. Water are super clear and cool for good swim during hot summer days.

Open air museum that hosts a plethora of weird statues that are lewd and sometimes bizarre. It is really more of a photo-taking venue than one that is educational. Even so I felt embarrassed posting any of the photos I took here on Facebook as some of the sculptures were just too sexually explicit. Great if you are going with a group of good friends for a good laugh. Don't go if you are easily offended by sexual content.
Nice place  for young kids  is best. Not really good for adults but it was cute......will try water park next time.

My family had lots of fun posing for pictures in this place. However you need patience and the right angle to capture a good photo. We were amazed by the result of the photos taken  it looked so rich and real! Take your time to enjoy this place.
My daughter enjoyed reading and seeing unusual and interesting facts. We had a good time at the museum.
Jeju Folk Museum - I found the museum little overbearing but all in all the collection was good for the time.

I've been to Jeju twice. The first time I saw the Nanta show the second time I saw this one. And it's a good show. It's held in the local university which is conveniently close to the downtown of the northern part of the island. The show is creative and entertaining. It's just not quite as good as Nanta (although I believe it is cheaper?)

It's pretty went on May around 3pm. So cloudy and cold because of the light rain. But must visit. School students trip also arrived at the same time. Got to taste free hot green tea. Long lines at the cafe but worth trying. Yes must try the cake and ice cream. Very nice. Got to make own postcards at innisfree museum for souvenirs. If you're good at photography i mean insta moments the pictures will be very great for that!
It's good to know Haenyeo history from this museum. The museum is quite nice but my main concern is not history. If you have spare time in Jeju then drop by here is not a bad idea.

It was our first time riding a horse.Strict instructions were given not to make sudden noises when riding as the frightened horses will go crazy & will cause serious injury to riders.All handphones/sling bags are not allowed too.Each rider gets to choose a hat & were matched to horses according to height.The horses walked unguided on a short (about 5 mins) fenced circuit. About 100 metres near the finish point the horses suddenly start galloping slowly.It was not easy to balance oneself on a horse holding just 2 grips on the saddle while it was galloping. We were concerned for that moment if we will fall off & was also wondering what happened to the horse. This was probably the scary part of uncertainty.It was a good experience though it was a short ride. At least now we know how it was to ride a horse.
It was nice try and not that amazing.Time is short.Price is 25 and 35 thousands won.Good not crowded
It is a bit dangerous to watch the rock but good to visit shortly if you have no time before your flight bacause it is near airport.
I would't bring anyone there at all.  It's really a waste of time for adults and teens.  Maybe it may be good for small kids.
I wish i can bring home all the teddy bear back home but unfortunately i cant... so sad... Keep up the good job as this is the 2nd time i came here

i went here in heavy rain. not much to see. but im having good time here with my friends. there are a lot of stones sculpture here. and also theres a museum regarding jeju.the museum tell us about types of stone. and the jeju itself formed by the volcanic activity happened before this.

I visited Jeju Folk Village on my last day of my trio to Jeju. Jeju Folk Village is a place where the traditional culture of Jeju and the history of the Korean language since the 1890s the late Joseon Period Dinasty are well preserved in their original state. You can experience Folks Customs Life Folk games Crafts and Traditional Folk events. I recommend to visit if you have time. Last day of the trip can be perfect because you can relax and go back home with a good feeling.
I used to go here as a child all the time and it left me with so many good memories. I recommend checking it out if you have young children with you!

review: Dec 2019 My husband and I (in our 40s) went on a free & easy to Jeju Island in Dec 2019 and engaged Mr Kim Choong Kun for 4 days from 14th to 17th. We touch base with him via what's app and listed the activities & food we wished to try and places of interest we wished to visit prior to our travelling. He could text in English converse in Mandarin & English. He planned our itinerary in an organised manner which ensured travelling time efficiency. He did such a good job in planning our itinerary that we could visit so many places of interest plus completing all our intended activities such as horse riding shooting Go karting and catching a NANTA show. Mr Kim not only drives us to destinations he was knowledgable and could enlighten us with historic information to the various places of interest. This was a big bonus to us as he served as a good tour guide and doubled up in helping us take photographs. He brought us to places for meals which are patronised by locals (not touristy places) for instance we had a yummy authentic ginseng chicken soup pork knuckles sashimi and other Korean local dishes. If you are willing he is able to join in for meals and personally we liked the arrangement as he was able to communicate on our behalf when placing ordersand even suggested to us which food goes well with which sauces. His sensitivity and personality made dining together very comfortable. He is patient and accommodating to our preferences and needs. He is friendly and we enjoyed conversations with him along our rides. He is also sensitive hence for travellers who are introverts I am sure he is able to gauge his involvement in conversations accordingly. He definitely made our stay in Jeju enjoyable and memorable. These are his info/ contact: Mr Kim Choong Kun Taxi licence plate: 2984 +82-10-63425688 Highly recommended. Good Value.

There are several lanes organized according to the wet market section, fruits and vegetables, packaged goodies to take home, food stalls and dry goods such as clothes. The clothes are of Korean origin of good quality and reasonable price, i.e. a dress for 12,000 kw. In a small stall we tried the Korean fried chicken with hot sweet sour glazing and it was very delicious. The fruit section was a good photo spot with its stalls abound with tangerines. Overall one can see how the vendors, locals and non-locals interact to reflect one aspect of Jeju life.  Very interesting, indeed!

Jeju is well known by the haenyeo, or that we usually called it as woman divers. It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was quite quiet when we were there and we only saw a few people except for a group on a guided tour at the end. Such a shame there are not more visitors but good for those who made the effort. Recommended visit in Jeju!

Innisfree Jeju House is just next to O'Sulloc Tea Museum, so is great to visit both the places. Innisfree is just one floor in a glass house.Besides selling Innisfree products like facial care, there is also many other things to explore.There is a big space for soap making area, visitor can purchase a bag of soap making set at the counter, and do it at the available place. The staff will guide you on the soap making. A self making post card corner for visitor to bring back (free but with limited, per card per person).Nice cozy clean comfortable cafe. Don't forget to try the black pork hot dog. It is so delicious. I bought a soap making set for my son to enjoy the art work, while I enjoy my facial product shopping. My husband and mother where having a good time at the cafe.

In previous trips to Seoul, i had passed by the theatre in Myeongdong many times but never thought of seeing the show.Then a friend who saw it recommended it highly.And I'm glad I did.It was very entertaining and tge skills on show were awesome. I would not call it a must see attraction, but go there if you have spare time. I really liked their collection of cacti and insectivorous plants. The glasshouse arrangement is really impressive. The tropical section had fruit-bearing mango trees which was a sight to behold (inside the glasshouse). The French garden, the Italian garden, etc are good for a stroll. Didn't find anything there specifically impressive.
