hello folks looking for a driver. Mr Ann is who i recommend. he is friendly with decent english. His english is optimal for getting by. Not only that but his charges are very affordable. He has many clean and nice taxis with fresh air . He is able to take 2 to 10 or more people. Having worked as a tour guide for 10 years or more with a huge diversity of customers from all over, he is genuinely a good guide. He drives fast but safe recommends cheap and good quality food.  He taught us lots of korean jeju culture too. With him as my guide 2 days in jeju wasnt enough. overall like what many others said he not only proactively takes many pictures for us but also brings us to as many places as possible, giving us alone time too. He brought us to eat black pork, tea museum, folk village, mount hallasang, glass museum, trick eye museum, love museum, the maze place, a beach, udo island, and many many other scenic places that you can take good shots.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Guide is good explaining about the village and oldtime Jeju. We came here by chartered car, not really sure how to come here by public transport. For me this place not very special, it's just different with typical hanok house that you ever see in Seoul or Jeonju.

Good show for young and old. No need any knowledge of Korean. Theater is located in the middle of nowhere so make sure you have your meals before going. There is a convenient shop (GS25) in the hotel nearby but limited food selection. There is also a restaurant within the hotel but only opens at 7pm (our show was 8pm) when we were there. Be punctual, the show starts on time.

Going to the Jeju Folk Village is like taking a trip back in time.  I can only imagine how hardy the people of Jeju were in order to survive.  You can see replicas of ancient houses, learn about the different social classes...even play dress up....my mom dressed up as a queen of the Joseon Dynasty and I dressed up as a kisaeng (not fun with my big feet) and we got our pictures taken and had a good laugh.  For those of you who have watched Dae Jang Geum, the folk village is not to be missed.

Go only if you have time or your kids want to go. There are 2 maze outlet in Jeju. As per the hotel, this one is the bigger one. 3 interconnecting mazes. Went in winter, it was cold and drizzling, didn't enjoy it. It's good if you are with a group of friends. Paid $27,000 won for 4 person after discount. We had a discount coupon from the hotel. We drove there, just key in the telephone number of the place into the GPS. Nothing really much. Can skip if you have better things to do.
Friendly and knowledgeable driver Mr Kim who can speak mandarin. Good service and enjoyable time in jeju! Anyone looking a man drain speaking driver, try Mr. Kim @ +82-10-7402-6878.

For a first timer visiting this place as tourist, i can say that this place gives you the choices you need to bring back home. You need to do some haggling of price. Some of the salespersons are quite persistent. They would do the 'extra mile' to make you buy their merchandise. 3rd floor gift section also has good variety of choices. I ended up spending more than W100,000 there. No regrets !

Expected the place to be bigger. Only reason we went here was to kill some time before heading to the airport. Could have gone to the Ripley's museum instead which was just across the road. As expected, lots of teddy bears in the museum. Only interesting part was the history section. They had teddy bears from as old as 1905 on display. The bears were still kept in good condition.
Easy to find by driving. Good scenery. Not far from the airport. If you are waiting for hotel check in like me, it's good idea to visit and have a good time. We had seafood with abalone lunch nearby.

Dragon Head Rock (Yongdu-am) is worth a look just to say   been there, done that  !It's nothing fantastic but does live up to its name.As it is within walking distance of downtown make the effort if you have the time.Tour groups, especially in the morning, arrive by the coach load. So walking makes good sense!

Communication barrier is not a problem for us to shop here. Yes, they don't really speak English. But, we still had a good time to shop and bargain. If you want to shop korean fashion (but not the designer label or branded one), clothing, accessories, bags, cosmetic, skin care, this is the place. One place for everything so that you don't have to walk more. Innisfree, Nature Republic, The Saem, Skin Food, you name it. All are here.

Cold lave tunnel at 12.4 degrees Celsius. Very educational and good for hiking.Entire tunnel is 7.4km, only 1km (the middle section) is opened to public.My 2nd time visiting, still very amazed with all these rock formation.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) This museum was meaningful museum of Jeju's anti-Japanese. This museum's outside had monument, square and sculpture about anti-Japanese. The museum was not bigger than I think, but there was operating about 10 years, and had meaningful exhibits. That's good to visit bright attraction in Jeju, but I think this meaningful attraction was good to visit sometimes.

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) The museum's theme was various and unique. Maybe there was like   Guinness Book  . The exhibits was good and arouse my interest, but the price was higher than I think. There was good place to spend killing time and need to increase contents.

Because of the location in the north part of the island, Hamdeok beach is the calmest beach ever that you can find. It is good for you to earn how to swim because it does not so much wave. Best time to visit: Fall (summer is too hot in Korea)

At the entrance of the village, the town mayor greets us. It?s a very small town. But this guy speaks good English, easily understandable, proceeds to his narrative of the village, it?s culture and history. Very informative and entertaining as he interjects jokes from time to time that find application in our daily lives. At the end of the tour, he will try to sell you tea concentrate (which really tastes good, just did not buy because of luggage space management) and a beauty product, horse oil cream, which if we look at his face, would seem to be doing a good job. His skin is very firm despite his old age. My friend was convinced to buy one because of his skin. Short visit but worth every minute

As its name, here is an idea to visit for Teddy Bear lovers and who interested in. Many zone that's quite interesting such as the first Winnie the Pooh, world's all time classic paintings x Teddy Bear, characters bear like Michael Jackson or Audrey Hepburn from Breakfast at Tiffany, and Steve Jobs. Entrance fees isn't cheap but still OK. For the exhibition of Bear dolls is good but for the shop, just soso nothing attractive.Parking available. Good for friends and family.

after taking a few geology classes as an adult, it was exciting to see the lava tubes. Would recommend taking a glow stick or a small flash light if prone to having a hard time seeing in the dark. Plus, the glow sticks added some fun to the darkness.  Slightly cold like most caves, bring a sweatshirt is a good idea. This offered something to do when it is raining and could  be a great break from the sun if traveling in the summer time.
A very long cave made from lava tube. Cold and dark, no bat dung smell though  as claimed. Kids having good time despite being city boys. Good new experience for us
4 Floors of a journey in time from the 70s to the very much today technology.Experience interactive games and tasks, good for age 9+
You can find this at the Sanbangsan Mountain area. It's a really good rock formation brought by years and years of the sea waves slapping those great rock walls.

World heritage Site. 13km long lava tube under Jeju Island. Formed by successive eruptions. The section that can be visited is about 1km long - first descending down two levels into the lava tube where the roof has collapsed and then walking up the tube under the mountain and ending at a lava pillar where the lave cascaded down from a parallel tube running above.  There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.

Sangangsan Mountain provides a short walk up stairs to a Buddhist temple and shrine. Only 1000 krw to enter. Even my teenage boys enjoyed the walk and the visit to the shrine where we were encouraged by a local to drink from the sacred water for our good health and fortune.

The first impression and experience was good. After a while, everything else looked the same. The same sea, mountains and stones, albeit in a different formation. There are beach bikes for rent, which I think will be fun but we didn't enjoy that because we had hired a taxi for the Jeju trip.

Sea, isles, mountain,  good smell of exotic flowers, nice seashores' cafe, pitoresque pensions, and great rest area. JeJu Island has 19 Olle trekking roads however, Olle 7 is the most famous and it has the most beautiful scenery among them, if I may say it! This is the very beginning of Olle 7, it worth it to walk 16.4km(whole length of Olle 7) from this place. Strongly recommended.

I'm from Vietnam and the guide people speak vietnamese too although she come from Korea. And the village is very good, it tell about the people in Jeju is very poor, because woman have to take water in the mountain.

I went trekking in Hallasan on 4 July 2016. The weather was not so good that day, sunny in the city but rainy, windy and very foggy in the mountains. It's better to do the trekking in Autumn. Avoid rainy and foggy days.
You should have a look at this place  look good as your background photo  it is pretty loud when it works.

We got a very nice tour from a local resident who spoke fairly good English.  It was very interesting to see how the huts were designed and the durability of the thatch roofs.  There was a sales pitch to buy some locally made tea and other products (which were very expensive) but no one bought anything.  You would think that they would figure out international tourists wouldn't be buying any kind of drinks to bring back home.

We couldn't walk further down due to the heavy rain. However it was still beautiful and amazing. You could go for a stroll with your family. I heard so many good things about this place. So I will definitely go back on a sunny day when I have a chance. :)
There's really nothing much to see for a museum but the cafe is good for a tea break and the green tea plantation is a nice backdrop for photo taking if the weather is good

There are so much to see in this museum. The whole day is enough to spend here if you want to read and appreciate all the displays. Good collections. I learned a lot from this museum. I regret doing four museum tours in one day for we had to rush this one. I would love to go back here.

The usual suspects (green tea roll matcha soft serve etc) are good of course but I also had a delicious cup of Houjicha Latte. It was perfect for a cool spring day sitting out in the O'sulloc back garden. Definitely deserves a repeat order.The O'sulloc shop here has many varieties of tea as well as skincare. Bought a pack of jeju green tea bags - when I opened the packet a most delicious aroma of roasted tea leaves greeted me.

People generally come here for the green tea and buying tea products. It's the best green tea I've tasted in the whole of Korea. And triumphs Malaysia's also. Their cakes dessert are just so good and you have tons of tea products to choose fromThose who like to see tea plantation can also come here to take pictures otherwise just sit back relax and enjoy green tea

My wife was bowled over when she saw the poster of the actress in the famous Korean drama - Jewel In The Palace.  Walking through the grounds we were told that the drama was filmed on site and visited the villages and houses.  It brought back nostalgic memories of the show capping the highlight visiting the exhibits.  But if you are not a fan of the drama the village is still a good place to visit to get a good idea of the traditional Korean homes during the Joseon era.

My wife and I visited this road last year during our 4 days tour of Jeju. It was a good experience but once is enough. Jeju is a really wonderful island to visit and we will definitely come back in the future

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

It was raining when we visited this museum. Many tourists frequent this place too. They have lots of tea products. They have a resto with variety of tea juices and goodies. Try to visit their tea plantation at the back.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.

I and my family visited this place in late June 2015. One of the main reason we wanted to go there was because of the whale shark. Unfortunately the whale shark was no longer there. There was a notice in the entrance saying it was released back to the ocean. There was nothing noted about the whale shark release in the company web site before. If there was a notice in the company web site I would probably not going there. The aquarium is not very big compared to other aquariums that I visited before. But the admission fee is quite expensive IMHO compared to other aquariums I visited before.One thing I want to mention that you could take a good picture of Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak from outside the aquarium. Will I go there again? Probably not unless they bring back the whale shark.

review: Had the green tea cake and latte both were fantastic. Bought some tea also and they are unique and taste good. Nice place to read a book while enjoying the greenery. Will be back!

We enjoyed this cave.  It's about 1 km to the end where the largest lava  pillar is located and then another 1 km back,  although the walk was relatively flat (no inclines) it was very uneven and slippery in places.  Wear shoes with good traction.  The cave is in a beautiful setting with many public toilets around.

This is a massive lava tube that the public are allowed to visit and does give you a real sense of the magnitude of the volcanic activity that created this island. For that alone you should visit.It is a nice cool 1km walk to the end and then, of course, you have to come back.A good experience.

Really cool volcanic flowlines and terrain.  Bring a rain jacket with a hood or umbrella and decent shoes.  Although I saw a woman in heels, but wouldn't suggest it. ouch.Take flash off your camera and use tripod for good pics.Does not take long at all to get at end and back.

Our guide is June. On the first day, she’s a bit late on the pick up, then we have to go back to her place because she forgot her document for the trip which is unprofessional. Then as we started the tour on the car, she just silence which is weird for me, because normally a good tour guide will start speaking & add so much to a traveller's understanding about the landmark , history & culture of the country. But thats not happening on both of these tour. Even when i asked her some questions, she seems hesitate when answering. Later i found out that some of her answer about Jeju actually is wrong. This shown how she doesnt have much knowledge about the Island. It’s a shame because for being a tour guide ,thats one of the important skill to have.

My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

It's good for what it is.  Some people have been calling this place a glass museum - it's not.  It's a theme park for glass.  I say theme park, but if you're thinking rides then you're wrong.  What they do have is lots of things made out of glass to see.  It's pretty and often colourful.  My female partner enjoyed it more than I did, and there's nothing there that would make me want to go back.  I think children might get a little bored by the place, although girls would probably enjoy it more.  As far as adults are concerned, if you think it sounds like a place you'd enjoy, then you probably would.  But if you think it sounds kinda boring then you wouldn't enjoy it.

It is interesting to see this authentic folk village that is the only one that still exist in Korea with people living there. Our Chinese guide allocated to us was good and she explained everything to us on their culture and how this village is sustaining. There wasn't so much of pressure that she pushes us to buy the products as she explains that she is just doing her job to explain but if we decide not to buy, that's totally fine too. We tried the products and we like it and bought some. It maybe a little pricey but she mentioned that the proceeds go back to these villagers too. It was a happy sale to me. No pressure.

If you love nature, this is a place you should visit. Nothing much to do , basically just walking and taking photos. But I personally love it ,because you can't find such a relaxing place back in a big city. It's good to visit during colder days.

I guessed many have mentioned that this was a typical market and I do not think they were wrong. However, it really depends the reason for your visit. If you are here to try cheap and good raw and fresh seafood (eg: raw fish slices for 10000won only), OR to try a variety of local food (eg: Sundae aka blood sausage, traditional fishcake stick, Kimbap, fresh Jeju orange juices, different types of kimchi, korean rice cakes, croquette, Tteokbokki, hotba, Modeumjeon - where they eat during new year and jeons, OR to purchase souvenirs and snacks for your family and friends then you are at the right place! It was also cheaper to purchase dried goods like ikan bilis and kelp in the market than supermarkets.We were at Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market before coming to this market and we found that stalls that sell Jeju's souvenirs and local snacks such as Jeju crunch chocolate were cheaper in this market. The shop owners also gave us a handful of other snacks to try after our purchase in hope that we would be back for more. In Summary, this was a good place to try many local food at a smaller amount and a place to purchase affordable snacks for gift at a cheaper price.

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

For most tourist spots, warm and clear weather are the best, but I did visit the cliffs on a stormy day, and it might have been even better. The cliffs are nice, but what truly made this an amazing experience was the stormy weather. The sea was agitated and waves were breaking on the on the cliffs, making for a truly dynamic and wild sight. The only drawback is that the cliffs do not go on and on (only for a couple of hundred meters) and there are few good vantage points. So the scale is not overwhelming.

Every stuff you want to eat can be found here. The Sea Food are really fresh and have no idea of the price but saw many locals buying ..,  must be good.  The cooked pig leg was a really good and went back the next day to buy again. Really enjoy eating the stuff selling in small food stall.  And the fruits are so sweet &  reasonable price too.

did not really go down to the beach as it was raining and need to pay to see the 'dragon head'. there's a small shipwreck museum which is good rainy day activity, nice for a free museum. like the yellow canola flower field at the parking area with sanbangsan at background. didn't went up sanbangsan due weather as well.

Although these lava-stone houses with the thatched roofs held on by handmade ropes are a part of Jeju's past, they are still very much occupied today.  You can see the kimchi jars and old-style gates along with satellite dishes attached out back.  This is very much a low-key place, gradual and picturesque...good photo ops and a study in contrasts.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

You need to present a copy of your identification before you are allowed into the range. At 35K Won it is not exactly the cheapest range in the world but it is cheaper than Seoul for sure.There are a variety of handguns to choose from and apart from the tacky advertisements on the wall it is actually quite a secure and well maintained range.Weapons are chained to the wall for safety and only the staff can tap you in or out. Good quality 3M earphones are used. There is also a selfie stick attached for you to take your pictures. Unfortunately the staff inside the range does not speak english (only the receptionist does basic english). However they do a pretty good job of demonstrating how to handle the weapon showing you on the screen where your shot have landed after each shot.After the shoot the receptionist will total up your score and pack your score sheet for you to bring it home as a souvenir. The hot tip is to book via Klook or Trazy and hunt for discounts instead of paying for the full price.Overall we enjoyed our shoot very much. Had it been cheaper we would definitely have another go.

We were in Jeju during a thypoon event and looking for indoor activities. This was one of them and to be honest we probably would have sought out a brewery regardless of the weather. The tour was in Korean which we found out on arrival. It would have been nice to have been told that when we booked by email and before we travelled out to the brewery. However after the tour the guide apologised and informed us that there needs to be 5 or more English speakers in the tour to do it in English which was fair enough. They then also gave us an unreleased Belgian Quadrupel to thank us. More importantly the beer was good and the pizza tasty.

Visited in golden weekend so expected crowded with tourist and local. This place is big and nice. Environment is clean just not so tourist friendly cos the staffs barely speak English. But it?셲 doesn?셳 spoil our mood of visit cos I love ocean. This is a really good place to visit. Entrance is bit expensive compare others tourist attractions museum. It?셲 cover with 2 shows.  I got my discount ticket online via KLOOK. If visit on the day without buy online cost 39800won per person.

review: This is a very expensive museum that is not worth visiting.  Although they have a lot of antique teddy bear and nice gallery but most of the explaination are in korea that make us difficult to understand their history.  The staff are not good in speaking English or Chinese.  The only good things is their surrounding scenery are nice for photographer to take photo.

I have tried green tea ice cream cake and ice blended. It is tasty and good. However the dining area a bit small and when I came here there's are pack of people. The staffs unable to speak in English but they are nice.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We visited May 2016, rainy weather but still open. The staff or local tour guide are very helpful that they provide umbrella that we can use around the folk village. Take note, the staff tour guide we met don't speak much of English, good thing we have our own private tour guide that help on translation. Appreciate the staff for her patience because even though all of her explanations need to be translated, I felt like she didn't skip any detail that we need to know. My favorite part when she showed us those black pig that is famous for their BBQ. Also, the drink that they offer is good that we end up buying one.

This place was soo dope! Take note that it was so nice to visit this place around sunrise so it was a good decision that we stay near the sunrise peak! Our airbnb owner was driving us to the sunrise peak 30 minutes before the sunrise. As a beginner, the track was good and a nice hiking for us. Definitely a must visit when you stay at Jeju Island. Note that, bring your hiking shoes and hiking outfit! If you come in the morning, you cant see the woman diver show or take a boat around, but it was nice!
The driver (mr.Kang) is really really helpful and polite. He's very good at driving, helped us to buy the ticket, and took some pictures. He also speaks and understands english very well.

The admission is free of charge and they have volunteer guides in the village to show you around, explain the history of the village. Volunteer guides can speak either english or chinese. Can try some special local products in this village which claimed to be good for health.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is the most eastern part of Jeju Island and has the same terrain as Punchball. When you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, you can see the beautiful sea and clear sky endlessly, and when you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with a cool breeze, you feel good. Also, there are many tourist attractions nearby, so it is convenient to move around. In addition, there are many restaurants that cook braised kingtail fish and roast caught in Jeju, and there are many unique and delicious restaurants around. I recommend that you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with your family at least once.

Not happy with the service (bad attitude- one of the waitress who took the order for us) Ordered the volcano cake and latte set. She didn?셳 understand what we wanted to order even though she speak good english, therefore I let know the cake set number on the menu instead of the cake?셲 name after she said ??she doesn?셳 understand ?? But she gave us a pissed face cause she had to look the menu( which only took 2 second, with no other customers queuing behind and before us)

Mr Kim is a very friendly and experience driver who can speak some english and some mandarin. He recommended a good foods to us and we enjoyed it a lot, also very helpful in finding answer for our questions. Good service and hope

Most people or tour guides will recommend you to go there for the seafood. However, the stall owners cannot speak other languages. The ones who do speak Chinese are too touristy. Those that sell abalone don't sell fish and vice versa. Better to go to a good restaurant for a taste of seafood stew. Fruits are ok. The good mandarin oranges are sold in boxes. I see locals buying boxes of oranges.

If you need a good work out, this forest in Jeju is worth paying a visit. The autumn 10C air is perfect, although the leaves were only starting to blend with the sun, you can imagine the shades of red, orange and yellow if it's at its peak!  The old nutmeg trees provided good photo opportunities for those with a passion for nature.

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.

Excellent experience. Good Diver was able to hook me up with an American speaking   buddy  . She was very helpful and even though it was 2 years since my certification she helped me thru the process and was very patient on my dives.

Even in peak season Sehwa Beach didn?t have nearly as many visitors as some of the more popular northeast Jeju beaches mainly because most of it is covered in volcanic rocks.  We actually weren?t even sure it was a beach at first.  We did see a handful of people in the water who had sidestepped all the volcanic rocks but most seemed happy taking photos standing on the rocks.  Cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores line the beach and all were good spots to admire the nice scenery of the beach.  For actually going in the water, the other popular beaches are more popular for that reason.
Went there to browse around local market and foods. Ended up eating lots of local food fare and buying goodies at good bargain. Would recommend a visit there

We visited for the night market. Nearby there is a multi storey public parking. The first stall butter fried rice with spicy pork is truly delicious and their orange juice (hallabong) freshly made is very nice though it is slightly expensive than the other stores. But it is freshly blend thus I love it and it taste good. Others stall look okay for me.

Visited in the evening.  It is a local market selling Jeju specialities as well as a wet market section selling the fresh & live seafood.  Good to visit if you are into shopping for foods and want jeju local foods and street food.
This is not a very big market but there are lots of authentic Korean food here for you to choose. It?s a good place to experience the local fare.Recommended place to go if you are in Jeju.

The street food stalls at night were awesome in the market. However all the good one has long lines and slow moving as most of them are cooking in front of you. Not knowing which one is the best  we choose to join the crowd and stand in line with others and skipped the other with short lines. Parking is terrible even Google Maps shows many nearby parking lots. We tried two separate lots and both were full. Instead of waiting someone to pull out  I ended up parking on the side of nearby street and walked to the market.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

Same array of goods being sold throughout the market. Oranges and local produce were plentiful in the market. Didn?t notice any significant stalls that sold anything exceptional. Tried a stall that sold stirred fried black pork but it only turned out average. I Guess it?s still a doable place to visit just to immerse in the local culture.

Located next to dongmun and jungang underground market so you can combine all three in one go. Not much to see and shop. You will probably eat in dongmun. We took dinner at the end of the street in a Japanese restaurant and was really good food. Jeju has a small population and do not really expect much shopping I could not find a memory card for my camera :-(
Good place to visit to explore traditional Korean Market. Here you can get wide variety of goodies including souvenirs  food items  even live tunas.

We walked though the Dongmun market and found it quite enjoyable.  They have a huge selection of good,  especially seafood, veggies and fruit.   All looked very fresh and well presented.  There are also stands where you can purchase food items as well.  As it is covered it was a good rainy day activity.
Unique setting near the sea-shore. The water flow was good, take tangerine from market outside the falls and enjoy water sprinkling out of the falls.

Unfortunately we visited in the morning and a lot of the stalls were just opening up.  I was surprised as a lot of the markets in Asia open at the crack of dawn.  There are a large number of stalls selling a large variety of goods, some at fairly good prices.  It was a dull day so it was nice to be indoors.

This is an authentic market which embodies local life on the island. It has so much to offer... There is an entire section devoted to the economy of the elderly, selling their goods and calling sweet encouragements to passerbys. There are regional fruits and veggies, artisan crafters, cloth and clothing sellers, seafood and fresh meats, animals, and a multitude of food trucks/stalls.This is the ideal market for immersing yourself in Jeju and Korean culture. It's open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27thPictured: a pressure cooker used for puffing rice and corn, cooking beans, etc...

This is a traditional wet as well as dry market. Goods are clearly segregated into their respective categories, eg, fruit, vegetables, poultry and seafood so customers can find what they need easily. Quite crowded on a weekday afternoon and there is a festive mood around the place. I was tempted to buy all the fresh produce like strawberries, tangerines and persimmons but they were expensive and I could only eat a limited amount.
This is a traditional Korean market selling wide variety of items including food, souvenirs and live seafood. Good to try some street food here.
Not expensive. Just like any other market area, where u can buy seafood and groceries, dry goodies and their famous tangerines ;)

Lots of variety here from plants, pulses, clothing, fruit and veges and fish and local street food.  The prices aren't cheap as you would expect in a market but that's the same all over Korea.  A good variety is why you would go there.
It is one of the good markets to see around. Very neatly maintained and you can find various types of seafood, pickles and fruits.

It is an ideal place to buy souveniors and see/taste the local food.  Rather clean even we went inside the fish and vegetable market.  Along we found few food stalls and restaurants to offer seafood, we were hesitated but decided to go for fish and cuttle fish sushimi in one with rather good environment, it's food and service were up to standard, price was not high compared to those in restaurant.  Interested to see local Kimchi, fish, fruits, herds, snacks from the stores

Every kind of locally caught fish and produce can be found in the Dongmun Market, as well as some imported items.  Don't miss out on getting a box of mandarins or Hallabong oranges.  Try the kiwifruit, too.  It's also a good place to sample Jeju's   street food   made by local vendors.  You can find all sorts of clothes and many household gadgets, accessories, rain shoes, Korean quilts, souvenirs...you name it, it's most likely in the market.  You can visit Dongmun during the day or at night.  Nearby, you can also see Sanjicheon Square, where local performers can also be found playing, singing or dancing for tips.  Some local seniors and maybe a few homeless persons frequent the area, adding to its   color.    The square is by a small tidal inlet, and features a quaint railing with traditional Korean characters on the railing.  Do check it out!

Dongmun market is a must visit in Jeju. Its a market where you can get almost any local products here. In the AM, there are plenty of shops selling dry food supplies, fruits, seafood, local snacks and few small restaurants. At night, you can grab some local food here at the stalls. Prices at the stalls are quite standard, ranging from KRW1000. We tried few food here which was good.

Crowded with a good mix of locals and tourists; jostling along for something.But the items on offer are common, with lots of seasonal clothing on display. Snacks are plentiful, so you have lots of choice. It's an interesting market, with old hands working at street food corners.

Basically a market place that sells the usual basic seafood and fruits. Practically all the fruit stalls sell the same things; mango, Jeju mandarin orange, peaches, etc. Do try the peaches if they are in season. They are huge, soft and fragrant.A lot of stalls are selling the same Jeju chocolate, mandarin or Hallabong tea & jam, etc.There are several stores that sell street food like oden, teokbokki, sundae, etc. In fact there is one particular stall that seems to be very famous due to the Korean variety show 'Running Man'. There is a long queue by 5pm; with people waiting to get a table to try all their Korean snack food. The teokbokki, sundae and fried fritters are really good.Do try the Jeju orange ice cream on a stick if you come across them. They are really nice and fragrant; especially on a warm day.

A traditional market situated in Jeju City that gives you a real and authentic taste of the local lifestyle in Jeju. It sells a wide range of local produce and goods. Buy all your local souvenirs such as hallabong orange, jeju chocolates and snacks here! The shopkeepers will toss in freebies (they call it   service  ) as well! It is near the black pork street which is also worth the visit.

*Firstly, don't go here. Instead, go to the 5 Day Market (誘쇱ㅼ쇱 Minsok O-il Jang) in Jeju-si. It is open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27th.*As for Dongmun, the best part is the 몃 (Hoddeok). Along one of the side alleys are these beautiful grandmas (癒몃 Halmeoni) who sell fried rice pastries filled with cinnamon, brown sugar, and nuts (Hoddeok). This is some of the best I've had in Korea. SO delicious. There are three of these stalls in this alley. The best, and oldest one, is furthest inside the market.The bad: vendors are rude and over priced. Their goods are not the highest quality and they know that the tourists don't know how to find better quality.
You need to pay 2000 Korean dollars to have a sight of this waterfalls. It's not a lot of money so it's good

Wonderful beach in Jeju island. Very clear water. Amazing colors and good vibes all around. You can spend here one day to have relax and chill out. And If you want you can walk around. There are close to the beach a lot of restaurants and caf챕s

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.
This place is easily accessable and great place to take good photographs.  The sound of the waterfall and the breeze of the wind gives us a calm mind.
The water fall was rather small but the good thing is we can walk on the big rocks path and take an up close pic without getting wet.

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

The 1k walk is really interesting and had good info in english. It's much cooler as soon as you walk down the steps and raincoats are useful as there are water drops and wear comfortable shoes for the rocky and wet floor. Most of it is quite dark but you can still get good photos. Definitely worth the visit
Spent several afternoons here. When you have nice sunny weather for the day the beach is a good place for young kids - the water is calm and clear. Highly recommended.
Really nice beach with a lot of restaurants near by.The water was really clear and the beach was clean so good for snorkeling and swimming.

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Nearby the waterfall is a free campground. We liked it enough to stay three nights while visiting Seongwipo and Hallasan. The campground is a good size. The waterfall is refreshing to swim in. This place is worth checking out.

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill

Its good place to get to know how Korean people lived on Jeju do island. There are houses of all kind of people like craftsmen usual habitants prisoners and etc. Also some photos of women divers from Jeju. Its probably better to use a guide since all information is in Korean and  there are several traditional korean games on the ground that need to be explained. There are several shops inside: some craftsmen shops like wooden crafts and caligraphy and also souvenirs and some local candy. We enjoyed our walk here. Its nice park that also got some ponds and small waterfalls. Its quite big one also. fee amount is 10000 krw per person.
It`s worth to see the waterfall going straight to the sea. Have good shoes - you'll need to walk on stones to get close to it.

It was soooo good that we were so tired after all the photo-taking! It is a walk in to the museum but definitely manageable from the teddy bear museum or the waterfalls. Just ask around and can save cab fare.
It sets you with AWE where you could see the waterfall meeting the sea.  You could experience the good ion in the air and listening to the music of the sea.

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Make sure you carry rain coat or umbrella and have some warm clothese if you are not used to cold. The caves  has water dripping at place and its very cold even during the hot sun outside. We went there after noon and it was quite cold. Be careful while walking inside the cave and its slippery. Do read the story as you go through its. there is restaurant which server good korean food just outside the entrance which we felt was very good.

I took the PADI Open water diving course with Good Diver. I am contend with the service they provided and thinking of getting my Advanced Openwater diver license with Gooddiver next month. It was an amazing experience. I felt comfortable during the whole course and could enjoy my first diving experience 100%. All the instructors were so patient that they made sure I was fully ready to descend and start the journey. I am so looking forward to diving again!

I took the PADI Open Water Diver course at Good Diver. Fast response on requests taken care of reservations and formalities everyday pick up nice dinner great English Instructors (even some German ;-)) and above all great diving at different sites! I seen waterfalls of over 70m so a 20m one is not so impressive but they did a really good job at making a nice park around it.

I am 6 years old. And I like to swim. It was very cold and cool. The water was kind of yucky. Plastic and rubbish. It looked like it was good for sand castles but daddy forgot to bring the bucket and spade for sand castles. Some waves were big and at first I was scared but then I learned to jump the waves. The surfers were clumsy because whenever there's big waves the surfers fall off. There were a lot of surfers. Mummy's Favourite bit was eating the shells on the rocks with the old aunties. The shells looked like snails and they moved and I thought they are disgusting! My Brother and me really really like Swimming. The end. That's all.
Good photo opportunity. Visit during high tide to see majestic falls flowing into the ocean.Visit during rainy season to see more water crashing down.
About 5mins down the long flight of stairs and you get upclose with the waterfall. Helpful to come with proper shoes as you can walk closer the the waterfall on the rocks to get a good photo.
a rare waterfall that falls directly into the ocean its a sight to behold. can go quite near the falls for a good picture.

A popular hotspot and parking can be a problem. The waterfall is nice but not very spectacular. Can stand on the rocks bottom to catch a better glimpse of the waterfall but mind the slippery rocks. Wear a sport shoes with good traction or simply walked bare footed on the rocks.

A few dozen steps down to the open rocks at the base of the waterfall.  And then you are rewarded with a beautiful scene and welcoming and cooling mist.  If you have good balance you can walk on the rocks for some beautiful pic of the falls and the waves crashing on the rocks.  Gorgeous!

yes we took that long but it was definitely a highlight of our trip...start early, 630 to 7am would be good... as it was nov, we ended trekking the last part in the dark... a torchlight would be a good idea...there's a shelter 3/4 up that sells water and instant noodles...still some snacks as you trek might be a good idea

Yeah, very nice for a waterfall that's in s decent-sized city. It's not Niagara by any means, but the walk through the gardens leading up to it are pleasant and it's very photogenic. Getting there early - pre 10am - is the best bet as the light is good for photos and the crowds are not as hectic.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.
We went in July end and found this waterfall good.It was loud,nice place to get some snaps. scenic beauty is good.Recommended for family.

We visited a total of 3 waterfalls (including Jeongbang Waterfall) for our recent trip to Jeju Island.  This was my favourite among the 3 waterfalls visited, as it was rather unique, flowing directly into the sea.  However, when we were there on a weekday afternoon, it was nice and quiet for only a few minutes, then a huge group of teenagers / students arrived and filled up the whole place.  It was too crowded and we had difficulty finding space to walk on the rocks and to take a good picture was nearly impossible.We would have stayed longer if it didn't get so crowded.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

Very good exercise, the longest route takes about 6 hrs if you walk fast (as it says 8 hrs) but u need to go in the morning so that u should return before dark.Lot of locals doing this but don't forget to bring water n packed lunch!

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

This beach is a good one.  The sand is soft and powdery and the clear water very gradually gets deep which allows us to comfortably walk unusually far into the ocean.  The other special characteristic is that there is a big change from low tide to high tide.  The high tide, which occurred around 10 pm when we were there, completely covers up a pretty large beach area.  It's pretty fascinating.  The food and drink shops near the beach were a bit of a letdown for us because they were overpriced.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The wind blows hard in this area (as the wind turbines might hint at). But the water is beautiful, the sand is white and the rock formations around are really special. It gets crowded but not as crowded as some others on the island. I have seen better beaches for sure, but here in Jeju this one is probably as good as it gets.

The walk to the waterfall was nice although it is kind of man made. The natural sights at the side was beautiful nonetheless.However, the waterfall itself was just ok. It didn't seem like that's the focal point of this attraction but it was good enough for a trip there.

The place was hot and mosquito infested honestly due to the Aug weather. However if you have enough repellent with you, this is a good place to walk over, sit on the rocks, chill by the waterfall, feel the cold clear air and pose till you are tired.

The park is nice and had a good size. There are a variety of different sections and when you add it all up it gives a good mini summary of Jeju - with the caves, stone park, waterfall, historical aspects, flower garden, and bird park. If you have only 2-3 days in Jeju this should be a must on the itinerary.

The building is attached to the   jeju tourism   board (or something like that). It costs about 4 or 5 000 won to get in  then handed a coupon for a discount at the cafe or any of the products. The children enjoyed it as they got to make chocolate for 10 000 which included a take home mold. The museum isn't much to look at but just enough to make your mouth water. It is close enough to all the other activities in the area  if traveling with kids  this is a good   trade off   point to let them have some fun.

The beach was fine and no rocks, but a lot of seaweed. The water was clear and very shallow, so it's good for kids, but I was a bit bored since I like to play in the waves.I think they should clean the beach more often since I found too much trash around

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

One of the real highlights for my visit to Jeju Island. It's absolutely fascinating and I've been to a few different caves before. It's different because it's a lava tube cave and there are a few different information boards in there to explain the different features which helped to understand how it was formed. It's very well and cold in there so bring a wet jacket and comfortable walking shoes (waterproof/ resistant if possible) with good traction. There is a small descent but other than that it's rather flat in there so most people should be able to do it, just watch out for the wet surface. If you go to Jeju, you must visit this cave.
One of the most beautiful waterfalls in Jeju! I didn't ecpect it to be so nice! Definitely worth spending 45 minutes there. Good spot for photoes, too.
Nothing compared to other famous waterfalls around the world. Nothing about heritage. So I am here only because I am on Jeju.After this, decided to skip other waterfalls. But good for some exercise.

My friend took me here because he said it was beautiful. Indeed, a waterfall next to the ocean is as picturesque as it gets. We took some dope pictures and dip our feet into the cool and refreshing water when I saw my FIRST EVER DOUBLE RAINBOW. Life is good haha

Just one waterfall, not much of a sight to behold. However, it's the only touristy waterfall that doesn't have stairs, so if you have knee problems, this is waterfall to see. On the plus side, the souvenir store near the entrance has good merchandise at good prices. They had nice hats on sale when I was there.

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

It is a good experience to be there and see how mystery the road was. We were with our kind tour guide that gave us an experiment to test the road. Pour water and see where it flows, true enough it was a mystery (still need not to be solved).
I went to Manjang Cave. It  was really good place to see. It was very cold when we got in side and we can see you cave of Volcano, while you are walking the water drop down and very lively..
I was expecting a bigger waterfall but was disappointed with what I've seen.However, it's still a good place to visit to see nature in its own wonder.

I think, this is really good waterfall. To see a water fall just beside of the sea is not usual... yes, very unusual. And it was good to see... A little bit high waterfall. 2,000 won for adult... If you enter it in another path, you don't need to pay. There is ticket checkpoint but the worker there didn't check.

i like this waterfall that connect to the beach but i dont understand why they have to take entry fee for that because its really close to car park.other than that, all good. beautiful and huge waterfall cool you down.

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. A good thing we visited this Dragon Head Coast while doing the west coast route.The canola flowers site is a paid visitor spot (should be around KRW2K each adult). There is a Viking ride @ the base for the young ones to try. You can see many interesting lines and grains on the side of the rocks' walls. You get to see women divers selling fresh seafoods along the coast, youngest are already in their 50s and oldest are in their 70s (still diving)...they are simply amazing.

Come prepared and you'll love it, good walking boots and waterproof jacket. If you find it too cold or dump you can go in for a few metres, and go outside, but we kept going wanting to see what is at the end, and it was spectacular, with huge lava column in blue dim light.

Can't resist going there every night as it's near to my hostel. Kinda good place for dinner for solo traveller as most of the restaurant serving food for more than 2 persons. You can get local food, fusion, western, sashimi, fresh fish, pork knuckles, fresh fruits and vegetables. Price range around kw2000 to kw10,000 per dish. Now you can get hallabong orange everywhere. Sweet and seedless. Yummmm love it when it's cool. After dinner can catch the water show nearby at 8pm every night except Monday.

Bring your jackets, better to be water proof! Cave temperature is around 10 plus degree or lower. Also ground is uneven so wear good shoes and walk slowly. But overall fascinating to see how geography works

Blue color of beach water. Very good.  We visited there late July. The color of beach was amazing. We enjoyed swimming. Also the sunray was very strong to enjoy sun tenning. We are food a little far from here, because restaurants near beach was expensive. Also there are good places to nearby beach ; Hyeopjae cave, botanical garden, tracking beach, etc.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

Because Jeju is a volcanic island, it doesn?t have too many beaches relative to its 300 km of coastline.  Hamdeok Beach is one of the closest beaches to Jeju City.  It?s also one of the most picturesque in Jeju making it quite crowded when it?s warm enough to go into the water.  Unfortunately when we went there were a lot of seaweed washed up on the sand.  Despite the crowd, the parking lot was quite large and there is a good selection of cafes and restaurants nearby making it a decent visit even if you don?t go into the water.

Beautiful scene to be seen. Very natural. 20,000 stones of different verities. Natural as traditional village houses in India. Toilet facilities are everywhere. Very clean. Dogs and cats are not allowed.Water fountain is there. very good place for peace, health and meditation.Thanks.

Beautiful beach, many people during summer but still acceptable. Very good for children because the water is very shallow. The only thing i didn't like ia that i couldn't even cool down in the water because it was so hot, like in a bath tub.There is no sunlounger, so if you want to tan, you need a mat.

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc
A crowded place to visit during the summer but a lovely waterfall with clean amenities for visitors. Very family friendly, reasonable prices on tourist goods.
Good place to visit in Juju for nature lovers. should go for hiking here to get close to nature and understand how J eju island is made of

The lava tube is different from other lime stone or erupted caves I seen before, this one is very big and the its formation and feature is fantastic.  Try to avoid the high crowd and prepare jacket, poncho and hiking shoes.  We took good camera and tripok to take picture.

Definitely a special cave. As it is a lava tube, the floor is also made of solid lava, aka uneven flooring. Bring good hiking boots as it takes at least 40 minutes to reach the end. Advice to use a tripod for good photos.
A UNESCO Heritage site, but basically an underground hole. Make sure you wear good hiking shoes+you may get wet.

Larger than anticipated with lots of interactive displays.  Bring a camera and be willing to be funny in a crowded space.  The indoor attractions were bettrr than the outdoor ones.  There is a coffee and snack bar with a lounge in the middle that made a very nice break point.  Easy to get to and staff was nice and helpful.  Staff spoke pretty good english and even called a cab for us.

It was not easy to find out where exactly it was but tried on good luck with the location google maps advised (trust google maps :-) )and it was worth it - really a hidden Temple. It must be visible from the roads but not sure

I heard about Udo Island from a few of the other ladies I was traveling with. They had seen pictures and couldn't wait to visit. I tagged a long for some good fashion outdoor fun. We rented bikes for the afternoon and took a ride around the island. The weather was perfect and we were able to see some great scenery. We visited a couple of the beach places and were able to take incredible pictures. We took a ferry ride over and it was amazing. Getting tickets and filling out paper work to take the ferry was incredibly easy and everyone was very helpful on the island. We were able to eat some great seafood and awesome ice-cream. Great spot to visit!

Easy access using public transportation and I remind you to bring a good camera and prepare yourself with extraordinary pose and don't be shy to act silly even lots of people will watching you. But don't worry they will do the same. Alive museum in Jeju is waaaaay bigger than in Seoul and the paintings are more interesting.
Our guide June is very informative on Jeju, and we had a wonderful trip to the southern part of Jeju. She is friendly and easy-going , and took good care of us and the kid.
It's very scenic and a good location for photography, it's near to town and easy to reach. The entrance fees is affordable

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.

Good sight seeing place and jungle trekking. Wear sport shoes for easy walking if you plan to walk   round the sea  . Weather was just nice for walking in April. Crossing the bridge and standing there watching the big sea was feeling awesome.

Drove to Udo island on a self-drive trip and took ferry from Seongsan pier in the morning. It was easy driving in Udo island - it was a tiny island and there weren't many tourists around. While strolling up Udo-bong, saw a group of physically challenged students brought to Udo-bong by their teachers. A very heart warming sight. There isn't anything much to do yet if you are interested in exploring the nature (like I do), it is a good place to spend a morning just feeling the nature.

There has a long line up food area even they only have simple menu. The food is good. Must try their mandarin drink. Lot of different kind of tea you can pick. I bought it for gift and its little bit pricey.

The green tea flavour food collection is greatCan take a close look of green tea fieldA good place for souvenir as there are wide range of tea collection However it is not suggested to go on rainy day

The folk village was quite large with some interesting buildings but everything looked samey after a while. I was hoping to see a variety of performances on the stage but it was only a few songs sung by a group of women - charming enough but not what we were expecting. The foodie street also didn't have alot of stalls open though we did buy some cactus taffy which tasted like treacle and raisins and lasted us most of our trip in SK. One good thing was the interactive bits such as the old games children used to play. Having been in folk villages in other countries where there were people in traditional costumes showcasing different crafts and activity the Jeju one was a little disappointing.

the facilities are excellent  very spacious  and comfortable. staff great. out on it own with little to attract you and but great facility. not sure who supplied the food first night plenty to eat second night they ran out. end of our evenings there was no where to book/order a cab so thank goodness the BooYung hotel assisted.
Small but with good food and soap crafts
Park is a little small but has some fun rides. Very clean and new. Great staff. Good food (except for pizza).
It's a good place to learn about how the well-known O'Sulloc Tea is manufactured. Great place great food. It's near to Innisfree Cafe as well.

It was very very very crowded with locals and tourists. The cafe food was alright but in my opinion too sweet. Highly recommended to come during sunrise and/or sunset - absolutely gorgeous scenery and wonderful air. Also has a lot of good food and convenience stores in the area. Only downside is that it can get quite crowded.

Hallam Park is one of the best botanical gardens we?ve visited. The paths are clearly posted and friendly to foreign visitors that don?t read Korean. We loved it. The restaurant at the entrance is only a good choice if you like Korean food. The barbecue spot inside might be a better choice for western visitors.

great icecream and the cakes are pretty good too but seats inside the cafe are very limited due to the crowds and long queue to purchase the food adds to the delay.families with young kid may want to avoid bringing in stroller in as it extremely crowded inside

Good place to enjoy aquarium.  Sea animals.  My children enjoyed this place very much. It was perfect place for children for me and wife it was a little plain. Dragon shape rock. The rock will bring you good fortune. It is also famous for fishing site. The lighted rock is also beautiful at night. Make a wish and the rock help you. Regardless of the legend you can enjoy the beautiful scenery.  Omegi ddeok (cake) is also good food to try.
Amazing beach the mount and amazing women diver.Good fresh air and many kind of traditional street food

A good place if you love tea.They have a tea plantation that you have access to and take pictures. Not bad but when we went it was pretty hot. So we opt out of that. The museum itself was alright. It has the teacups from around the world.On the ground floor itself you have the cafe as well. The cafe sells ice cream the roll and other light food. A very good place to escape the heat.Innisfree Jeju House is just next door as they are run by the same Group.

깁?躍?? provides seafood for people to enjoy the delicious elements of the freshness and beautyness of it throughout eating. Windy Island15 minute taking ship from Sungsan dock to Woo-do, it?s really convenience to visit there.The road were well maintained and there were variety of vehicles could I used.Before I got there, I heard that the peanut jam is famous and ice-cream made by peanut is good.
