review: On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.
This museum is in a remote location but it's quite easy to find. We totally enjoyed visit.  The exhibitions are very impressive.  Its a relatively small museum but it's the highlight of my day.
The museum has really cool exhibits and they were beautiful to see. It's easy to relax and forget about the outside world.

The place is quite far from the main town but it's worth it if you are a fan for green tea. There's a simple exhibition on history of green tea. Then there's the O'Sulloc shop and cafe which is full of green tea products and food. The green tea latte green tea ice cream and the green tea log cake are the 3 things must try in the cafe. The only bad thing is that the cafe is a bit too crowded and noisy to enjoy such nice tea.

It's a tea museum but there's very little exhibits so I was a little disappointed.However there's lush green fields of tea leaves to take photos with there's a Innisfree boutique store here and the food at the Ossuloc Cafe is really worth a try!
While there are numerous exhibits and really very well kept the visitors are few.  The signs are not that great and there is a lot of walking required.

The building itself is pretty cool  when we were there the tall grass was in in its full glory and towered over either side of the path into the building. We were given discounted admission because one of the exhibits inside was temporarily closed. It's interesting to walk around inside a bit (there are some nice clean bathrooms in there too) and see the several art exhibits inside. It's very peaceful and relaxing inside the building.

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.
Jeju April 3rd Peace Park  - really a peaceful place to visit. Walk through the small exhibitions to understand it better.

Great scenic spot with narrow shelf or rock at the base of cliffs which were part of an old volcano.  We visited on a day of high wind and rough seas and the site was closed as the path was too dangerous.  was able to visit the climate exhibition centre and see the model of the Dutch Ship De Sperwer  wrecked hundreds of years ago.  Also took the walk up the hill to the beacon tower.
This was worth the entry fee. There is a nice walking tour of the   museum  . It was interesting to see all the glass displays in the forest. We really enjoyed the walk through the exhibits

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

I have a deep love and appreciation for the artist Lee Jung Seob. The museum itself? and the neighboring art-walk is a great tribute to the artist, but the exhibition itself does not do the artist that much justice. They have a great selection of his smaller works from the earlier periods but they do not house his bigger, dynamic paintings that he is known for. This visit would be a great place to take the family as the entrance fee is very manageable. The museum offers a closer look at the artists' context and life story rather than a display of his most prominent works. In short, a brilliant artist but not the best exhibition space/display method.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) I visited there for watching Teddy's parody, because I've visited Teddy museum in Sokcho formerly. According to my expectation, there was funny Teddy doll describing person, event and fairy tale. Walking through the flow, I smile at funny doll. Good to visit once, but I will not visit one more becasue of high price and unchanged exhibits.

We hiked the Eorimok (up) and Yeongsil (down) trails. *If you're hiking in winter, you definitely need crampons.*These trails were stunning. On the Eorimok, we experienced surreal forest setting shrouded in misty clouds and stunning landscapes. At the top of the trail, there's a great place to snag some cup Ramen and Choco-pies. Bring a few cheons and you'll be fine. Two-thirds of this trail was in the forest and the last third was along a large plain created by a lava field. Expect to be amazed by vast skies.The Yeongsil trail was just as satisfying. There are sheer drops and exposed cliff faces. Most of this trail was composed of wooden stairs. If you're planning to bus in and out, make sure you start early. The buses fill up fast and the last bus back to Jeju-si from Yeongsil runs at 16:15 during the winter (until March). Also, if you're not exhausted, the walk to the bus stop from the trail is not too far (maybe 2km at max). Don't waste you money on shuttle service.

We followed the Seongpanak Trail to reach the top. It is hard to say that there is a   road   in many parts of the walk, merely some volcano rocks placed irregularly on the ground :) Although we were exhausted when we reach the top, we were amazed by the great view from there, which was a good return for all the efforts we made.

Jeju Island is indeed a unique island with so many gorgeous scenery, i had a great time travelling there in Winter, a low season with lesser tourist gives a different experience from visiting it in busy Summer. I have seen pictures about Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff (?ъ＜ⓒ\由) and was amazed by the neat shapes of hexagon stone pillars formed by volcanic lava, i totally recommend tourist to spend time walking around the nicely design olle trail in the beautiful, as well as to visit Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff during your trip in Seogwipo or Chungmun area. you don't have to plan for a long stay, a good two hours should be more than enough, as it was just a viewing spot rather than you can actually walk-in and visit. Don't worry about the transport, bus services are available (in fact it is very convenient to reach most of the travel spot around Jeju island), just drop by Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and walk about 15 minutes to the park entrance, bus drivers in Jeju are very friendly and can basic communication woudn't be a concern. there is a entrance fees of 2000won in the park.there are steps to walk down to have a clearer view, description board with picture will explain how the hexagons shapes are formed, you can take amazing pictures and enjoy the sea view too.speaking of the weather, i have quite an experience, it was sunshine at first while i was taking the bus, and soon it become heavy downpour and even snow flakes begin to attack me during my walking! i think an umbrella or raincoat is necessary for either bright sunshine or unexpected rain. i gotta say, Jeju Island's weather is unpredictable! although this is not a spot to actually feel and touch the pillars, it can be quite boring to certain people who expected more attraction, but seeing the amazing cliff, the neat pillars, it was totally worth it to witness it by your own eyes, even the finest artist surrender to this piece of art, isn't it?

It was with much endurance for me to walk up the mountain. It took me approx 4hours to complete the trail. It amaze me to see many kids trekking together with their parents. U can drive all the way up and trek from 1280m. This trail led u up yo 1700m. It's very popular trail and many people trekked together. It motivate us to trek together. Up the trail there is a small house that sell ramen cup noodle, chocolate and drinks etc. Overall good experience.

I am a resident of the Seattle metropolitan area so I have to compare it to the Chihuly Garden and Glass museum.  The Jeju Glass Castle is very different in concept as it also focuses on small to medium sized glass items.  Conversely, Chihuly Garden and Glass focuses on large scale items produced by Chihuly in small quantities.  That's not to say it was disappointing, but it wasn't that impressive in the sheer quality of the items.  However, you do get a very large variety of glass items from throughout the world so it does make it up in quantity.  Unlike the Chihuly museum, the glass castle is a very large complex.I did notice the museum seemed a little run down in a few areas - it really did seem it needs some upgrades to its infrastructure.  However, there is a maze, nicely manicured gardens, glass shoes, and a large variety of other takes on glass items.  There is also a nice trail to walk that showcases certain glass items as well.Perhaps the most interesting part of the museum is near the entrance.  You'll find a glass making room there with windows you can look through to see glass artisans at work.  It was quite interesting to see these people create glass items by sculpting it, putting it in the oven, and more.

This place is massive! Truly a great venue to walk around. While it was closed the day I was there  I walked around the entire stadium and was impressed with everything outside of it. This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.
The view is breathtaking, a must see and must go location in my opinion. You will be amazed how lava can turn into such a beautiful scenary.

Recommended to visit in Jeju, it maybe a funny or plain looking on the pictures but you will be amazed when you are there. Ok ok, to be honest...most of my rating is because of the seemingly endless cats that were here. If you are planning to visit the Hello Kitty Island, beware: there is a specific audience that his place caters to; it is not recommended for everyone. There is also a room that narrates the history of how Sanrio characters came about.  There is a Hello Kitty Caf챕 at the 2nd floor. On the 3rd floor, there is an auditorium that plays a Hello Kitty-themed show. Outside is an open-air Hello Kitty-themed miniature garden maze. The view of the landscape from here is wonderful. I read reviews/blogs about what & where and the most economical way to explore east of Jeju in a day. One of the blogs I read mentioned about Udo on her trip (you may look for theLostWanderer's blog-Jeju in 3 days for more detailed trip in Jeju). I just love this islet. I rented a manual bicycle to get around for KW 5000 for 2hrs, yet you can rent at KW 10000 for 3hrs to the entire day. Well for my time is constrain, & travelling on a budget & also wanted to keep myself fit as a preparation for Mt Hallasan hike, gladly I did. Other than bicycle, you can rent an e-bike, ATV, and a scooter. The tranquility & scenery that the place could offer is magnificent. Shouldn't let this islet slip from your list once in Jeju.I took bus #701 after I visited Manjanggul Cave & Gimnyeong maze park (same bus stop where I alighted for the cave) & alight at Seongsan Habour. At the port, I paid KW 5500 (to & fro) for I'm going back the same day to the main Island of Jeju.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.
i am lucky to visit udo on a sunny day. we are amazed by the unbeatable view and superb environment. spent a relaxing day in udo.if you go to jeju, you MUST go to udo!

Amazed by the view inside the cave. Overall distance travel back and forth takes 1 hour to complete, approximately 2km. Advised to wear comfortable shoes (rocky slippery floor) and jacket as it can be very cold inside the cave. Bring an umbrella if you need it as there?s water droplets from the top of cave.

Along with Go Carts and a hot air balloon ride, the Maze Park has enough to keep everyone busy and happy! The Maze is fun to watch people navigate from the hot air balloon. A great view of World Cup Stadium too!! This was a fun day!

After some hiking (which was hard for me as I didn't really exercise), you can see a small museum on top to explain how light house works, interactive equipments for you to feel more relevant with the light house. After my Manjanggul Cave   expedition   and since the park is just along the way back, I took the chance to see what's the place could offer.
