The maze is good for family to enjoy.
You pass the Maze Park when you head towards the Lava Cave. My mum and I went to the park after the cave on our way back up to the main road to catch the bus. It was a fun way to kill some time.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

So dont get this place confused with maze land.  This one is near the lava cave.  Here it has one maze only.  It would have been fun and peaceful but then 3 buses of middle school children arrived and all hell broke out.  Very hars to walk around it when a bunch of kids are running past you.  But the maze owners also have a bunch of cats that were super friendly.
I took a bus tour on Udo. The beaches on Udo are light blue in colour - really amazed me! Would definitely like to go again in summer!

Well it's a big cave and you are surrounded by lava rocks- which are basically... Rocks.So if you like caves or rocks you will love this!It was very quiet.. Just a few people walked past us... Very different from Ichulbong..You don't need walking shoes or even a torch really, but do care where you walk..It is about 2km from the main road if you take a bus that drops you off on the main road.. Taxis often wait in the main road and charge 4000 one way to the caves..I think entry to the caves was just 1500..The Maze garden is a few hundred metres away too but I didn't go

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We planned this for the kids but the adults had fun too. When we arrived, we bought the tickets while the kids were busy with the numerous cats around the area. It turns out that this is also a place for cat lovers, this place is a mini cat world too. You can get cat food from the ticket counter to feed the cats.In the maze, the kids formed a team and raced with us, the parents. Each team had to find the stamps hidden around the maze and stamp on the paper given. First team to collect all 6 stamps and ring the bell to exit the maze wins.Upon exiting the maze, as we passed thru the ticket counter again, the lady manning the counter asked us to visit the gift shop to claim a free postcard.

We chance upon this on our drive from Seogwipo to Hyeopjae.  The pink building is big and visible from the highway. They should have repainted it as it looks washout and faded pink. But once I step in, it?s totally new! Infact it is even newer than Sanrio Puroland which I visited in Tokyo and bigger than there! I am a true blue HK fan since 40 years ago. Once HK fan steps in, I am sure you will be transformed to a little princess at heart and you?ll be so excited again! There are a lot of Instagram worthy area to take photos. As others pointed out, it has a section that talks about the evolution of HK from 1970s till now.  There are HK rooms, dining room, bus, living room, wardrobe, dressing room etc. Even the toilets are so pretty! Level 2 offers some purikura area, a restaurant and some other HK displays.  There is a 3D dancing room too. On the 3rd floor, there is a open air rooftop HK small maze. On level 1, you go through the souvenirs shop to exit and a notice states that once u exit, u can?t go in again. So it?s best that u buy yr souvenirs when u are ready to leave. I swear I could stay there for 3 hours but as my husband is with me, it only took us about 1.5 hrs to complete our visit. Overall this place is small and not much for non Kitty fans. For us Kitty fans, it is definitely a must visit.

This was an interesting experience. I am usually ok in small spaces and felt this would be a great thing to do. But once I was in the middle of the first maze I felt a little uneasy. They provide a map and the maze itself is pretty easy to do. You also hear people walking around, but just something about the possibility of making a wrong turn made me not want to do the second and third maze. But there are really cool towers and a museum where you can take amazing pictures. the museum is free, they have trick art and a puzzle art. Getting here was a little bit difficult. Ask around your previous destination at the bus stop perhaps some people are willing to share taxi with you. Since the bus that goes around this area takes almost 45 minutes. And once you get to your destination you sometimes still have to walk a while to get to where you want to.

There are 3 mazes in this park which you are encouraged to try all of them. There were buses of students visiting the maze land when we were there. the kids were good in the mazes and we simply followed them to get out of the mazes. There are also a 'tower' where the teachers made sure the kids don't get into accidents while playing in the mazes. Pretty amazing and fun to spend some time there. But will not return again as we have completed all 3 mazes. Unless, they expand and created a few more, then will consider visiting again the next time I go Jeju.

The maze is closely located to Manjanggul cave.The entrance fee is KRW3,300. The entrance is fill of cute cats.The maze is constructed by high and neatly-trimmed bush walls.It is not too large.There is an observation decks/bridge. From here you can clearly see path.As we're running out of time, we use the map to solve the maze.It took us 8 min to ring the victory bell.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Really enjoyable walk through the dark and luminous cave created by the eruption of Halla. It will take a decent time and is right next to a maze filled with cats!Unfortunately there isn't convenient bus transport as you have to walk about 30 minutes from the bus stop but if you're relatively fit, it will be no problem (aside from your friends nagging you how long till you get there).
Quite fun. If go with group and play games, will be more fun.Took direct bus#260 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal. Journey 1 hour 5 min.Alight Maze Nusuem Bustop and walk to Maze Land about 5 min.

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

My family was holiday in Jeju on 12 Dec 2011.  One of the tourists spots where we visited is the Mysterious road.  It really amazed us after we had seen in our own eyes and sitting in the car.  The driver took us to place near to our our hotel Ocean Suite Hotel.  He then switched off the engine of the car and of course, there is a spot where there is a sign show   start here  .  There it goes the moment he let off his brake, 5 of us including the driver were siting in the car and the car just move up the a slight steep slove (about 5 degrees) and the distance it travelled is about 50m.  After that he U turn and took us to the same spot where we can witnessed other cars, including buses and coaches also did the same thing.  What a wonderful and awesome sight I have seen.  So when you are in Jeju, please do not miss this.

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

It was along the way to Manjanggul Cave. As we had missed the bus 990 which could take us to the Cave, we had to walk the 2.5km way. About 1.4km's walk, we came to the Gimnyeong Maze Park. It was a fun place even for adults. We did not follow the map so that it would be exciting. Indeed it was, and the more lost we were, the more exciting it got.

Interesting road... My bus was shifted to neutral gear and went up th hill by itself....Had saw this before in Taiwan and china... It was actually an optical illusion .. Nonetheless quite amaze by it. Other than this generally speaking the attraction has no depth... Can go if visiting some other attraction in the area, but not worth it if travelling long distance for it .

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

Had a lot fun going through this maze. Don't use the map because it will spoil the experience. We kept on running into the other tourists that had the same look on their faces because we couldnt find the exit. But you could tell they were also having fun no translation needed. Took us about 45 minutes to finish the maze. Only problem was getting there. The nearest bus stop is a bit far and taxis are few and far in between.We took a cab going to the bus stop and planned on splitting the cab fare with other tourists. Turns out the driver wasnt using the meter and asked us to pay 2000 won each. We didn't argue too much with the driver because we were trying to catch the bus plus he didnt speak English. Just be careful because this might also happen to you. This was the only bad experience we had in Jeju (the cab ride, not the maze).

Being adults and have been busy over the years, we truly enjoyed walking 'lost' in the maze.  We reached the place quite late and we were trying to get out of the maze asap.  Enjoyed the cool weather to search for the exit.  Managed to ring the bell just before closing time.

As I rented a car to explore Jeju (highly recommended), we came here a couple of times to enjoy the experience putting the gear at N position and realizing how the car went up the hill.We also tried on the road with a can of beer that also was rolling hill up apparently. It is maybe an optical illusion but when you are there it looks clearly and without any doubt that cars and things go up the road. The kids were amazed and really enjoyed as we also did.Try to avoid the afternoons, as most of the guided tours are here at that time with many buses horning in hurry to repeat the experience several times and many pedestrians around. In the morning the day after it was almost empty !

This is our last stop for the day trip so we can't spend too much time at there. There are totally 3 mazes and we went through 2 big mazes and last one without knowing it. Is fun if go with a group of friends. Abit boring for the elderly people.

There is nearly no advertisement for this museum in the city. I saw the sign at the traffic and wanted to give it a try. The building is so small that when i arrived I thought it will be a quick tiny event. But once you are inside you will be amazed by the beauty and the variety of seashells. Most of the explanations are in Korean but still nothing can stop you to enjoy this museum. At the roof  there is a giant shell  which you can go in and have a photo. There is also a small shop where you can buy gifts to your loved ones and something for yourself too.

The scenery was very beautiful. But it was very windy in winter. Choose your clothing wisely.You will need to hike to reach the top or you can also go to the beach by climbing down the stairs to buy some squid or oyster. They say that you can watch traditional diver at the beach. But it wasnt there when i arrive (I will be very amazed if there is a diver in that chilly winter)
The only waterfall in Jeju that e water flows into the ocean. U can go very close to it & feel e cool Breeze. Was so amazed to c rainbow too! Worth stopping by.
Nearby the lava cave so we stopped by. The size of maze is smaller than expected but good enough for young kids. There's plenty of cats outside the maze entrance which my girl loves.

Wear sunscreen because this maze can take quite awhile to conquer!  I wouldn't advise trying to complete it during the middle of the day when there will be very little shade, because it can be quite hot while you are in the direct sunlight.There are restrooms, free parking, a small convenience store style snack shop, and a small picnic area under the trees near the parking area.  A fun stop.

We where on the way to the Love Park, then suddenly our driver passed it by some 20 metres. He stopped the car with the 5 of us in it, we were facing up hill, he turned of the engine, took the handbrake off, put the car in neutral and I kid you not we rolled UP the hill???I am told it's obvious its an optical illusion but amazed us!! It's free by the way, it's just a normal road

We start our journey from Hotel Fine at 5 am in the morning and manage to arrived there at 6 am. Please bear in mind that you are required to climb a high numbers of stairs so at least make sure you had a breakfast first. The effort of climbing the numerous stairs is really worth it as once you reached the top, the scenery are breathtaking and amazed me on each second I blink my eyes. This is a must visit place when you are at Jeju.

There are 3 different mazes you'll get to go through. It's tricky and fun at the same time. Once you've solved the last one, take time to go to the top of the main building and see the vista from there! At the end of the maze, you might need refreshment so there are drinks and ice cream available! Definitely a fun place to go to!

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is just beside the Manjang Cave, so I recommended a short 1hr stopover if you are heading to the cave.  Avoid the maze park on rainy days as the ground gets really muddy when it rains.

It's a nice stop in general but also when you visit the nearby Manjanggul Cave Lava Tube. The whole maze property is very well maintained and nicely done, a great place for a picknick. The maze itself isn't that difficult and with the map really easy. Some fun for the young as well as the older ones. I also found out how useful a drone can be - to exit a maze easily :)

It's a hedge maze straight out of the movies, except with nothing popping up to scare you. It is only the hedge.  It takes about 20 minutes to find your way out and costs 3,300 for an adult. It's 500m down the road from Manjanggul cave, so if you're going to the cave you could stop by, but not worth the trip otherwise.

I really did enjoy working my way through this maze. The entire area is beautifully put together and is the kind of place you just want to spend time in and enjoy. Unfortunately, uniqueness comes with a price. I thought nearly $5 per person was a little steep but it isn't every day you get to walk through a hedge maze. The maze itself is a lot of fun and is large enough to actually be a bit of a challenge. We met the owner and he is very friendly and interesting to talk to. I am glad we stopped here but, because of the price, I don't think I would do it again.

Hotel was right across this market so I stopped here on my first night for dinner. I was amazed by the selection of street food stalls, fresh produce and desserts. Most of the signs were in Korean but just follow the crowd and where there's a long line you'll never go wrong! I got a taste of the rice with fried black pork plus some fried octopus in batter, which were both great. Bought some boxes of cheap chocolate as well. Areas of the market selling fresh fish and vegetables are wet though so beware when walking through.

Didn't think there was anything special about this as compared to other jeju attractions. Mainly a maze which could be completed in an hour, then u ring the bell at the top before making your way out. The kids would probably like that, I saw quite a number of teenagers and families with young children.

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..

Well i get there by accident - really - i didnt plan to visit this park but good thing happened. I had so much fun back there. All labyrinths(maze) are great adventure. Just try to get lost and find way between tries without any map of maze! :P. Tickets are bit expensive but still it worth to go especially if you have kids! Well for grow ups it is also fun ( but make it harder- dont use  map)

Very interesting maze. First 2 are fairly easy but the 3rd one gets a little tricky. Water mist kept getting in the way as you try to navigate so it gets a little more complicated. The kids and adults had a fun time. Should do it without the maps given so you just have to rely on sense of direction.

This was a great way to spend an hour!  It would have been more fun had I been able to navigate alone.  My friend was not interested in using the map and just wanted to finish for the photo op as quickly as possible.  We did go back into the maze to each of the six stations and stamped our cards.

This is an excellent play place for teenagers. If you are a child 120 cm and under you must go with an adult. I recommend that if you’re really tall or big you might not want to go because this place has narrow tunnels. I almost got stuck in one of the hammock tunnels... haha.We saw this place on a pamphlet we got from the airport and really wanted to go right away and it was totally worth going.Remember to wear something comfortable because you’ll be moving around a lot so clothing with shenanigans hanging off from it probably won’t be a good idea. Or excessive jewelry. The price was 12000 per person for the Maze ep.3 and the Level 2 (harder level with timer) was around 5000?? But as a package it was 16000 per person. We had so much fun here!

This is a cool place to take the family. It fun and easy way to walk through mazes. With stream for kids to play in. A amusing part for me was U given a picture of maze so can solve easily. The inside exhibition is worth a walk through with more puzzles and games.
There are three connected mazes.  You can go through one or all.  A great way to spend a few hours.  There is also a museum/exhibit maze in the building.

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

The butterfly museum is interesting showcasing many species of insects but the information are all in Korean. Walk out of the building there is an outdoor park with a maze. The mirror maze is not to be missed the kids had so much fun finding their way out!

Quite interesting maze. It took us a bit more time than expected to find the way out and it was funny. If you plan to take a brake in this area I would certainly recommend spend about hour to play in the maze.

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)
My 10-year old and I had a great fun at the maze.  The maze layout is challenging.  The garden  is beautiful and well-maintained.  It is worth going and it is near to the Manjang cave anyway.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.
It was relatively easy to find this place from the highway we took. It boast a simple and beautiful maze. It wouldn't take more than 15 mins to complete it. Definitely a place to visit!

It was a butterfly and insects theme park. Entry fee 9500 won. It doesn't display real butterflies and insects I think. There were just fake but they really did a great job by setting up for the exhibition. I really adored their creativeness to potray various human activities and historic scene by using insects and butterflies. The miniature were really nice. If you are expecting to see some real butterflies flying around you wouldn't see one :(We also went to mirror maze. This was superrr awesome! The maze was small but it really did made us feel excited to find our way out. Beware not to bump to those mirrors hehe.
It is interesting of the maze and provide bonding time with family when try to explore our way out of the maze.

I have always wanted to visit a maze.  This one was lots of fun.  Just when we thought we found our way out  we were at a dead end.  The Korean people who were actually at the end were up on the platform laughing at us and cheered when we arrived. No translation was needed.

Fun...but not ONE that you would go all out to do it. Some of us manage to complete and ring the bell in 30mins other do got lost if not good at reading maps. The maze is lacking in maintenance. The checkpoints do not correspond with the maps and the chops has no inks disappointing the children. If you are a cat lover it is a interesting place. We visit the maze on the way to Manjanggul Lava Tube.

After visiting the lava tubes we got to try out the maze park.  A fun way to spend a half hour and the site of many k-dramas and korean commercials.  Romantic for a date and fun if you have kids.  We even got to ring the bell at the end!A fun excursion if you're walking to the lava tubes it's on the same road.
2 giant mazes for you to try find your way out of it. One of the maze is of short trees and the other is of stone.

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) ! After you flood yrselves silly with pics, you can try the maze. Its interesting walking in and out and along the way you can look out for cats that are just chillin by the greenery. Overall a good experience especially for families !

We went with 3 children (aged 5,7 and 10) and two seniors, and they enjoyed the maze park. It was a smaller maze park compared to maze land, so it's not too difficult for kids. We spilt into two groups, one group managed to find out way out and rang the bell in 5 mins, while the other got lost in the maze and required rescue.  We spent about an hour or so, going through the maze thrice, and it was a fun experience.
We visited the maze after Manjanggol Lava Tubes, which is just less than 1 km away. It fun for the kids. We managed to get out within 10 minutes :)

We originally did not schedule this visit as we have already seen Mulu Caves in Sarawak-East Malaysia.  But our hotel (TGG) told us that this is a very different cave (lava tubes).   The cost is not high at KRW2,000 and if you are already going to Seongsan Ilchbong, might as well make a visit.  We did not regret the visit.  It is really interesting to see how the lava flowing from Mt. Halla makes its way underground and forming the cave.  It is huge so you can see the magnitude of the lava flow.  Be sure to wear sturdy shoes as the ground is rather rocky and wet and you will need to walk carefully so that you won't fall.  I am amazed on how some ladies worn high heels!  It is also dim and cool so you must bring a jacket with you.  It is also a UNESCO site so definitely worth visiting.

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

Three interconnected mazes come with a map to make sure you won't get lost, other sights nearby including a lovely and scenic walk under beautiful trees. On my way through one of the mazes the sprinklers above came on and then you're walking through mist. A very straightforward sight that is an interesting experience.

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This maze is fun and quite simple. And from what I've observed, it really tests a couple's relationship strength. ALong the way I see couples arguing on which way to go, I see couples helping each other out. It was a fun experience. Walk there from Manjanggul to get a 500won discount!

This is not really part of our tour in Jeju but since I researched on how to enjoy the tour with 30+ friends, I chanced upon this garden maze near Manjanggul lava tubes site (as in 500m away only).I really recommend this to friends and families who'd like to solve a mystery together and have fun doing it. The price in finishing the maze is a banner and the right to be the first to ring the bell.Please try the ice cream at the exit. You'll enjoy it after an exhilirating yet fun game (30 minutes estimated)

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

There are two main mazes: trees and stone and it is fun to find your way out. Unfortunately, it took us shorter than usual as we did not loose our way. We were able to find directions by referring to the map. Will be a great fun for family with kids.

There are 3 levels for the visitors to try. The first one is the easiest before you are engaged in a more challenging maze. It is fun if you have 2 groups of children/ people visiting this place. Not only that they can help their group members to find their way, the competition between the 2 groups makes it more exciting. Finally, the 3rd maze is the most difficult but you will have no problem. There is a clue/ help (you will see, it is a secret here) when you really need it. I think, the children managed all 3 maze puzzles in 1 hour.

The maze park is suitable for photo-shoots, the beautiful alley filled with green-leaves and also stone-walls. There are 3 maze available in this place. The first one is the easiest one, round shaped, and we can have a shortcut just by going to the side way. The side way also makes us easier to travel through the second maze. The third maze is the hardest, where it doesn't have a shortcut, and we have to go through the map by ourselves. Interesting if we are travelling with our little ones. On my last trip here at the end of September 2015, it was raining so bad, the wind was also very strong. So avoid to come here when the weather forecast predicts the weather to be raining.

Lots of fun! Dozens of tame affectionate kitties greet you at the entrance. Cute kittens too! There is a toddler playground with toddler-sized shops play kitchens, jungle gym, rope course, teeter totter? al kid sized. Plenty of great spots for selfies of all kinds. The maze is very tall and take a good 15 minutes at full sprint to wind through and capture stamps on the way to ringing the bell. If you are feeling silly or have small a children with you, this is the spot!

Looking for something different when touring through Jeju? Then this is a nice alternative. Manicured gardens with stunning hydrangeas abound in this most peaceful setting. Taking about 30-40 minutes to complete, it's an enjoyable time to try and navigate through the maze without a GPS! There's a shop (there's always a shop!) compete with souvenirs, drinks and ice creams - and there's a quite spot to sit and soak up the peaceful atmosphere. Enjoy!

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. However, the grass/plant at the maze seem not well taken care as you can see a lot of holes along the plant fences of the maze.

It's a new experience to us. It's great. Just walk inside the maze until you find the way. Maybe try and get help from your friends who have reached the tower. It's a great activity. Got some traditional games to play as well. There are lots of big fat cats at the ticketing counter. So cute, so fluffy.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

If you love Alice in Wonderland you will love Maze Land.  The mazes are fun to explore and make you feel like a kid again. Also, the statue garden and rose garden are worth a look.  A really fun, unique way to spend a day on Jeju.

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.

I had always wanted to go to a maze park, and finally I did in jeju :) it was a small maze but enough to make us excited to find our way out. The entrance fee is 33,000 won for adult. In front of the entrance, there were lots of cats and quite tame too.
Have fun getting lost in the maze! We didn't get lost because we got someone to lead the way for us! But if he didn't lead,I think must take ard an hour to find the exit!
Had a great time to find my way out of the maze!!! The owner of this place, has cats family! They are friendly cats of black and white fur with spots!

Get lost in the mazes and have fun exploring your way out. Great for everyone. This is the maze park featured by the Running Man. There are 3 mazes in this park, two with grassy walls which is for beginner and intermediate maze solver. The longest stone maze measures about 5.3km in length and it is for the advance players. If you get lost, you can get stuck there for more than an hour.

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..

After being in the cave, this is a good way to warm your body under the sun (well, at least during this season).So, it took 10 minutes to work out the right direction with the map, then we tried without the map and again it was ten minutes, then we left our 5 years old daughter to find the way out...still 10 minutes.I cannot define it challenging but fun for sure and super-rewarding to see your kid beaming with light every time she play the bell!Definitely worth combining cave and maze!

2 maze garden which worth to explore, test your capability to overcome the obstacle in finding your way out. There is 2 giant mazes within the park come with easy & challenging route to explore. RM has make this place popular

Went there with my other half but we didn't do a race. Spent about half an hour there to figure out the maze. its actually pretty obvious from the mini map they gave you but we took on the challenge of not using the map at all. Recommended to do a race and first to the bell tower wins! Its a little pricey for just half and hour of fun though. Paid about 4-5k won each. Cat lovers will love it there as they have free roaming cats around the entrance :)
We were told by our guide that it takes at least half an hour to complete the maze. It was a piece of cake for us as we only took 12 minutes to walked out of the maze.
We have took a lot of photos and it amazed us a lot!! must go!!It will take up a good 1 - 1.5 hours to go around the whole museum.

This is a very lovely maze park with a beautiful garden! We absolutely enjoyed the hour we spent here. The garden is well kept and we were given little bags of cat food to feed the 40 cats scattered throughout the garden.

can spend a couple of hours reading the many Greek myths and learn about the many names which you have heard of often.  Do the 3 quizes at the end to see if you have missed anything (or you already knew about it much).  The Trckeye Museum is at the same place and there is also a mini- maze to keep the family and children occupied.
Amazing maze. You could either stuck for 1hour or complete it in 15minutes like me. Cute and adorable cats. Beautiful flowers and scenery. Admission is quite pricey.
Worth a visit if you've got nothing to do for a few hours,loads of cats running around,just a garden mazes nothing special

We thought the kids might be excited by the maze but they were quickly bored by the turning and it started to drizzle.  Hide in the main building and left before an hour.  I think its 30,000W for 2 adults and 2 kids, not that cheap.  Not a cup of tea for everyone I guess.

We spent may be half an hour here and had a good time. The maze is very pretty and you don't see mazes made from trees in the US any more, so this was a treat. The mazes were not difficult, but can be confusing. The admission was quite reasonable, so I do recommend this place if your family is into mazes. Oh, there were a lot of cats roaming the ground and made good subjects for photos.

We didn't know what we could do with that one hour before sunset, so we decided to relive our childhood by going to this maze park. We completed the maze in slightly less than an hour. But boyfriend wanted to have some more fun by collecting all the ink stamps at various points in the maze, so he attempted the maze again and he got himself lost in the park while I waited for him at the elevated finishing point. It was fun. For children, if they managed to collect all the stamps, they will give a small gift from the park. We got a KimYoung Maze Park pen although we are not children :x The lady was nice. haha :)

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.
Spent an hour in this place as it is our last spot for the day. We completed all three mazes, the last one is tougher while the rest are quite easy to navigate.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

I visited in maze park last week with my family. The park is not big but you can enjoy the maze enough. It took about 1 hour to find exit for me but other people took 30~40 minutes. I recommend not to use map for more fun. You can also see the beautiful flowers and meet lots of cats. If you could find Dr. Dustin who made the park, ask him to take a picture together. He like that :).

I think it was unfortunate that it rained the day we went. The grounds were muddy. The kids were having fun. The adults were grumpy. Thankfully, we were prepared with umbrellas and raincoats. Still, the kids' shoes got all muddy and we had other places to go to after this. So, not the most pleasant of experiences. But to be fair, the maze is challenging enough to provide good fun for about an hour or so.

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.
Had a lot of fun here with my friends. I think there were 3 total mazes? Probably could spend like 3 hours here, but we just ran the mazes real quick before heading to the airport.

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

It was very good and origin. I though I'd given up before I even start, but the quite,the white of the snow amazed me, I kept moving head. Lost of local people climb on the last day of 2014. and I have to say is they climbed so fast,we were passed by many followers.

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

We like this maze a lot as it's not that easy as you can think of. Several times we went to an dead end and travel around similar corners!! Some kids running around to be the first ringing the bell at the finish point. It's a place full of laughter and we enjoyed it very much!!
We had good time playing in this maze. It is well-maintained the owner/ caretaker is accommodating and they also have several cats who will welcome and waiting to be cuddled.
We had fun at this maze park! Seemed easy but not! My son and I had a good time trying to figure the maze out! Kids will definitely enjoy! Lovely place for good exercise too!

This is the place where Running Man shooting happened previously. Nice place to spend some time but it will be time consuming.Didn't manage to play the maze. But I'm like facade of the design of this park. And it is chilling too!
The maze is very fun to walk or run through.  We had a great time trying to navigate it.  I would definitely suggest trying to do it without the map.  That is part of the fun of it!

reach here after Manjanggul cave as sunny & good weather. it has some cats near around all of them were sleepy or lazily style. before went inside the maze. it has a small garden with some flowers. and the maze actually not to difficult or complex but good for take rest when you finished the game. it has shelter & you could buy a cold drink at there. ok to try if you got time.

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.

My friend had completed the maze shorter time by instinct and not following the map.  Me and my partner collected all the marking stamp but takes a longer time to end.  But it was a great fun. Worth visit!

My family had lots of fun posing for pictures in this place. However you need patience and the right angle to capture a good photo. We were amazed by the result of the photos taken  it looked so rich and real! Take your time to enjoy this place.
It?s a once in a lifetime opportunity to visit this maze considering it is the world?s longest. Young and old alike will enjoy the adventure it brings.
It has a great green tea maze we spend a lovely time reaching the end of the maze and the smell of the green tea its all over the place
A small but well built maze for family activities. Probably great for family outings or just to let the time flies. Can skip this if you are on a tight schedule.

When you see the symmetry of the cliff, you will be amazed.  The columns that have been created by Mother Nature are a sight to behold.  If you're looking for one of a kind sights, this is one of them.  There is an admission fee, but it's negligible.  From pictures I've seen when the surf is up, that might be a more awesome time to visit.

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html
Went to the cave, only walk for about 1-2 hrs as this is a short cave. see stone structure cause by volcano eruption. only go if you like nature. Can visit the maze park at the same time.

We went to this maze which was just beside the Manjang Caves. Weather was terribly cold with hail and rain and strong winds. Still 6 of us (2 adults and 4 kids) braved all that. It was great fun though we got lost a few times. There are many cats in the vicinity, kept by the people who man the place. Poor cats, all huddled up in the cold.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.
the maze is not that big, a few turns here and there & u can practically memorize the route already. nevertheless, quite challenging for first timer like me. ^^

Second time visiting the maze. The kids loved the maze as did the adults. We broke up into single groups to try to time each other on who can get through the maze the fastest. this would only work on a non-crowded day! Ran through the maze a few times to beat each other's time and then broke into groups (kids vs adults) to see who could get through the fastest. Great time in the fall, as it is a reminder of the corn mazes in the states.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

Mazeland was both beautiful AND fun!  We got there close to closing so we didn't get to stay long, but the time we were there was awesome.  I got some awesome photos, and it was really fun to walk around in.  *HIghly recommended.

Located next to Manjanggul Cave (a must-visit site), this park is great to let loose your inner child. If you have plenty of time and want to challenge yourself, go in without using the map! Remember to ring the bell when you have navigated through successfully and don't forget to collect all 6 stamps in the maze!

I think this maze is one of the bigger maze land made famous by the   running man   Korean reality show. It's comprise by 3 mazes and I kind of enjoyed the the first or wind maze. If you're pressed for time and wants the easier path, take the 2 outer routes .

I like to visit sites like that this because it gives you a flavor of how folks lived in the olden times before electricity and indoor piping.  They have houses made with stones and have their toilets outside  using the   pig system  .Meaning pigs eat the waste.  There are still people living in the area and i am just amazed how far technology and evolution we have gone through.  I cannot imagine living in this environment especially the cold of the winter

I hope you had good time in Jeju Island. Unfortunately, I think you didn't visit Kimnyoung Maze Park. Because, we have only one maze and no museum. Seems like you had visit Mazeland. Anyhow thanks to visit Jeju and hope to see you next time when you visit Jeju again! :)

hello folks looking for a driver. Mr Ann is who i recommend. he is friendly with decent english. His english is optimal for getting by. Not only that but his charges are very affordable. He has many clean and nice taxis with fresh air . He is able to take 2 to 10 or more people. Having worked as a tour guide for 10 years or more with a huge diversity of customers from all over, he is genuinely a good guide. He drives fast but safe recommends cheap and good quality food.  He taught us lots of korean jeju culture too. With him as my guide 2 days in jeju wasnt enough. overall like what many others said he not only proactively takes many pictures for us but also brings us to as many places as possible, giving us alone time too. He brought us to eat black pork, tea museum, folk village, mount hallasang, glass museum, trick eye museum, love museum, the maze place, a beach, udo island, and many many other scenic places that you can take good shots. Go only if you have time or your kids want to go. There are 2 maze outlet in Jeju. As per the hotel, this one is the bigger one. 3 interconnecting mazes. Went in winter, it was cold and drizzling, didn't enjoy it. It's good if you are with a group of friends. Paid $27,000 won for 4 person after discount. We had a discount coupon from the hotel. We drove there, just key in the telephone number of the place into the GPS. Nothing really much. Can skip if you have better things to do.

Fun and exciting. Go through once without the map and get lost. Then try the second time with the map. Finally, the challenge starts. Go individual or in teams. Shouting and screaming and laughter will fill up the maze.

Experience狩狩狩Price狩狩狩The Glass Castle is highly recommended for glass artefacts enthusiasts, so definitely not recommended for families with children. Extremely boring except for the mirror maze, an extremely small maze reminiscent of the one at the Trick Eye Museum. Only if you're trying to kill time or collect false eyes as a hobby.
Don't think other country still have this kind of maze land garden.  If you have time and want to check your capability to overcome the difficulties, you may try...

Did it once with the SO, and then a second time as a race against each other. I saw a group of guys doing the maze with money on the line, if you want to make it more interesting.Also, there are loads of cats near the ticket office, if you're into that.

Cold lave tunnel at 12.4 degrees Celsius. Very educational and good for hiking.Entire tunnel is 7.4km, only 1km (the middle section) is opened to public.My 2nd time visiting, still very amazed with all these rock formation.

By the time we reached the Jungmun Daepo cliff, it's already 4.50 pm! 40 minutes to closing time! We hurried to buy tickets and rushed in! We're amazed to met with awesome lava volcanic rocks naturally forming into octagonal shapes and in poles like! Scenery there are beautiful too! We quickly took pictures as we went along every scenic spots.Then time to go out and even outside are some man made decorations of big shell and fishes too! On the whole, it's a nice place!

As for the places we visited, we loved the Manjanggul Cave, Sunrise peak and the foot bath class at the Herbal park. The maze and folk village were ok. I probably would prefer to exchange one of those two for more time at the Woljeong beach.
A maze which is A-maze-ing. Lol, is okay, go there if you have free time, will be definitely better than the horrendous show with animals/dolphins that we saw before that.

The are lots of nice background for picture - taking here. It is made area per area. Lots of youngsters also come to this place. The maze itself is nice to try. But be careful is you are with kids. They might get lost. The parking is huge.

I dont know about gravity or earth magnetic thing..but when our taxi driver did the experiment by taking off his car key and free his gear...the car move backward and it was against the gravity...amazed

Our visit to this village was an amazing experience! We learned a lot about the history Jeju, specifically their culture and traditions. Jeju is known for its black pig pork and we were given the chance to see one at the backyard of one the old house in the village. Plus our hosts were very entertaining and discuss to us the unique heritage of Jeju. The traditional role of husband and wife, music played, beliefs, practices and their livelihood. Moreover, we were lucky because the house we visited was the location of the famous Jewel in the Palace. We were amazed with their stone structures. We took photos in almost every corner of the village. Everything there was just amazingly beautiful. The old houses, tress, the souvenirs stores being in house in the traditional homes, the government offices, the pavement, etc, everything was mesmerizing. The people are very kind, approachable and welcoming.

What amazed us when we visited the market was the market was very organised and clean. The fish was swimming in the drainage under the bench. There were many sashimi restaurants and local food restaurant. The sellers (ahjuma and ahjeoshi) greeted us very well which made us felt very welcome. We bought the orange (halabong) fruit  juice and key chain souvenirs.

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!
Only waterfall in asia which falls in ocean.i was amazed.must must see.very high falling.entry fee 2000 won
Is just a short road to be amazed.  Not worth to travel so far.  Saw people trying to roll water bottle on the road and ignoring oncoming cars.
I'm very amazed by the 23m waterfall and it is just next to the ocean!! It's a bit difficult to walk on the rocks though but it's definitely worth the visit!
I more amazed by the crystal clear water than the rock formation. Suggest to give it a pass and head on to other attractions.

We came here after the Manjungal caves. The maze is challenging enough and took us about 35min to solve, but it was fun and worth the entrance price. It was a hot day so take a bottle of water with you to stay hydrated. Also, whilst in the maze we noticed some pretty large spider webs with some fairly big spiders, so careful of those. All in all, its a great family activity. There's also some lovely cats in the park that are friendly and you can pet them.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Sanbangsan Mountain is a wonderful bell-shaped huge body of lava situated nearby the ocean. At few places it stretches into the ocean where majestic rock structures can be seen. Also the legend associated with this mountain is very interesting. According to the legend it was plucked out from the Hallasan Mountain peak by the angry Emperor when he got hit by a misfired arrow that was shot to white deer. Interestingly it is said that the circumferences of the Sanbangsan Mountain and the crater at Hallasan are of similar size. The Jeju Olle Trail Route 10 is connected to this mountain by stairs. Halla-san is the highest mountain in South Korea and the middle of Jeju Island.  There are two trails that go to the summit of the mountain.  There are a few other trails on Halla-san but they don't go to the top.  It is about 9KM from one side of the mountain to the top and about 10 KM on the other trail to the top.  There are water sources on the mountain so you don't need to carry much drinking water.  It took me between 2 to 2.5 hours to reach the summit and about the same time to go back to where I had parked my car.  The trail is fairly rocky and vertical.  On a clear day you can see all of Jeju Island and the sea below from the summit.  There is also a small pond in the middle of the summit of the dormant volcano that is Halla-san.

Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

Went on a day hike up and down the Seongpanak trail! It was a gorgeous day, about 18C and I couldn't have asked for better weather. It took about 10 hours round trip. Started around 8:30am and made it down by 6:30pm. Luckily the sun didn't go down until 7:15ish so I had plenty of light to guide me.Now, I am not a hiker by any means and this was one of the toughest hikes I've been on. To be honest, it wasn't because the trails were all that difficult - it was actually quite pleasant through the woods and there were 2 rest stops along the way. The first stop is basically a bathroom break and the 2nd had some food available before heading up the last (somewhat steeper) trail to the lake up top. Oh, by   food   I mean some cup ramen and snacks. They also sold water and sports drinks. It would be helpful for you to bring food of your own. They also have no garbage cans so you need to carry and dispose of your own trash once you get back down.The reason why this trail was difficult for me was because I simply wasn't ready for a 20km hike! By the last 5km of the descent, I felt my feet and legs were going to fall off or give in to becoming jelly due to all the stairs and rocks. Make sure you have proper shoes! All in all, I'm glad I did this hike - it was worth it when I got to the top and was able to experience amazing views and clean air. And the flowers!! It was simply beautiful. Just expect to have sore calves for a few days following :)

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance.
