Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hamdeok Beach is really splendid! Clear aquamarine water, super fine sand, mountain in the  background.... the view is to die for! You will find beautiful volcanic rocks all around the area. There's a bridge that stretches out into the sea that gives you an even more fantastic view. A must visit if you are in Jeju!

Hamdeok beach is just so beautiful. It offers you black rocks, white sand, and breathtaking views. It was our first destination for the day after we landed in Jeju. I found the beach quite peaceful and calm. It is very near to Hallim park. Just took us about 2 mins to reach the park by a car. I wish we could spend some more time at the beach but we had to rush to our next destination. Good place to stop by and click some nice pics. Good luck!!! :)

Great view of the rare animal cliff which is 20 meters height and surrounded by the beautiful islands. Hundreds of visitors went there to have a look of the amazing animal rock. The stone seemed independent and I like the fact that it is normal, nothing inorganic. The shape of Oedolgae formed by the daily erosion of wave and the weathering process. There is a small path in which it can walk along the edges of the island. In which I discovered that the venue was filmed by one of the most famous Korean drama - Dae Jang Geum. I was in love with the drama when I was young, I took tens of photos with the place that Jang Geum have been to.So, if you are I fan of Dae Jang Geum or you would like to see different shapes of stone, you are highly recommended to go there to have a look at the charming sea view.

Great view of the coastline. Some uniquely formed rocks. Lots of people. Great spots for photography. Stalls for local snacks. I guess the above summed up what to expect at this place.For me, the   Dragon Head Rock   wasn't the main attraction, it is just something to label this place for tourists to drop by for photography. However, if he rocks weren't there, the authorities may lack a tagline to draw crowds.  The view of the coastline here was amazing, facing a beautiful and rough seas with nature to your left and modern residential buildings to your far right.

God?s beauty with unique rock formations and the waves crashing. Short boardwalk to see the beauty. We bought a bag of oranges and explored a bit more on the side paths but it was so hot, we didn?t enjoy that part as much as cliff viewing.

Getting to the crater was after a 20 minutes steep climb upwards via a rocky road made up of bumpy rocks. The steps got smaller, higher and steeper as you move higher up the crater. The view was amazing as you climb, and was breathtaking when you get to the top. The timing of the sunrise varies daily but the top may get a little crowded, so it?s advisable to climb up a little earlier to secure a good position. The way down was via another route, but this time, with proper stairway. It leads to another cliff of the just at the side of the bottom of the crater. You can either take the stairs down the cliff to the bottom where it?s closer to the seashore or you may go up the cliff and then make your way back to the entrance.
Fresh air and beautiful scene of the sky, sea & rocks all together. Walk along the coastal path to take in the views from different angles. It is supposedly also the filming location of 鸚㏝룝.

Easy boardwalk to see the attraction.  If you follow right, you will see the Oedolgae rock.  We happened to be there at sunset, and the view was magnificent & romantic!  You can also follow the boardwalk to the left for more view points.
Didn't expect to see such a good view there, the rock , island, and sea makes perfect scenario. Definitely a spot to visit if visiting Jeju!

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.

Created by winds and waves over thousands of years, the rock is formed resembling a dragon's head. Close by is the dragon pond Yongyeon, where the sea meets fresh water. The pond is flanked by 8 rock walls that resemble folding screens and has a stunning view.

Came here during sunset time. The view is very beautiful and natural. Many tourist took photo over here. During your walking distance to Yongduam Rock, don?t buy any fruit from the first stores! Very rude and not friendly. Make sure those of you beware of them.

Breathtaking views all the way to the peak and the weather was great. The hike was definitely worth it, not as strenuous as it looks. It'll all be worth it when you reach the peak!For those whom don't fancy the hike, there are women divers who demonstrate their skills without oxygen tanks at the rocks below!!
Blowholes were small as compared to New Zealand?s Pancake rocks. But view is beautiful, a small park outside with shops around. Many attractions like Teddy bear museum are just a walking distance.

Beautiful weather with wonderful scenic view. Took a bit of time getting to the side of the waterfall due to uneven rocks surrounding it after going down the stair for about 10 mins. Once you get past that, have a great time snapping away and find your best angles  though you have to take turns with other tourists who are doing the exact same thing. Snap away!

Beautiful view from the cliff and surprising rock formations. Went on a rainy morning so we took our time and walked around a lot too. Snacks from the vendors near the front gate were tasty. The entry fee and parking was 8,000 KRW for a family of 5.

Beautiful scenery at the top with breathtaking surrounding views of Jeju. Well maintained stairs, although uneven at first because they use the volcanic rocks, Many resting places as you go up. There is a lady at the top who explains the origins of the peak in English, which was a pleasant surprise. Large carpark area, fast food stores and souvenir shops.
Amazing view , the unique of natural for the cliff rock. Must not miss during visited Jeju island. Highly recommended visited during sunny day.

Amazed by the view inside the cave. Overall distance travel back and forth takes 1 hour to complete, approximately 2km. Advised to wear comfortable shoes (rocky slippery floor) and jacket as it can be very cold inside the cave. Bring an umbrella if you need it as there?s water droplets from the top of cave.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A short 10 mins walk down down several flights of steps would lead u to the base of the fall. For the adventurous and nimble folks, you can navigate carefully across the rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. I was there on a crowded day and the task of leaping from rock to rock didn?t seem possible. It was still a nice view from the base. Do include this site in your itinerary. I think the volume of water was lesser since it was still winter when I visited.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

a coastine with beautiful cliff and rock - the line and layer of the rock are ideal for photography or selfie.  Not difficult to walk but cautious for the waves, also there is open view over the outlying islands. I recommend people go to the end of the path which has a exeptional setup by the nature.
Well unless you are into rocks and nature you might not like this place. Plus we have to walk quite far just to get a bus going back to hotel.

We took bus 600 from the World Cup Stadium. This bus is also the Airport Limousine. We got off at Jeju ICC and walked from there towards the sea. The geometrical volcanic rock formation simply took our breath away!  Who cut/shaped the rocks this way? A fantastic work of art created by the Master Craftsman. Another wonder of nature. The geometrical shapes were amazing! This is - must-visit site!

Unique geographical nature reserve called Gotjawal is Jeju local language stands for forest(怨?Got) and thorn bushs on rock(?먯솃;jawal). The area is kept 10-15 degrees celsius throughout the year making Summer cool and Winter warm where tropical Northern hemisphere plants and frigid Southern hemisphere plants can coexist.There are four main Gotjawal terrain in Jeju Island this is the one in the South-West area. They also have a guided tour around this Gotjawal forest which you can explore the area with it's own story. The thing is they only have Korean tour so far so you might want to speak Korean or request them to open up an English tour.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This was our last station before we heading to airport to catch our flight to Busan. You will be able to see the rock that look like a dragon head. Overall this place what you see was the rock. It was near to the sea and lots of people too.

This was of our Yeha bus tour - South Course and this was a beautiful stop.  You can take steps down to the waterfall for some great photo opportunities.  There are some really large rocks that you walk and stand on.

This spot looks like it exists purely for the 15-20 tour buses that were there when we visited as its pretty much a rock with a different shape that you can see in the picture. Save your time and your parking fee and check out the world heritage listed rocks formations around the island otherwise you will need just 1 min here to take a photo and be off again

This is one of the stops on the Jeju City tour bus route.  We arrived here in the evening and this was our last stop before returning to Jeju main bus terminal via the airport.  There were plenty of tourists at this small tourist site. The rock resembled a dragon head. It is just a photo stop but you can also stroll around and relax here as it is beside the sea and is breezy.

This beach is less clustered by tourist and easily accessible. Take the 702 for an hour from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal and arrive at the entrance.  There are several food options and convenience stores.  The lava rocks are also pretty cool.

The place was accessible by bus from the Jeju city!I arrived the rock before 12pm and going around the rock to take photos!The color and shape of rock is some how unique!If you have time you may want to come and take a look!

Small area but you can see clear waters around the rocks formed from the volcano. Do visit if you have time. I imagine it would be amazing to catch the sunset here but am unable to do so because of time constraints.Easily accessible by bus no. 462 from Jeju Bus Terminal.
If you take the steps down to the rocks you will see some ladies peddling fresh sashimi seafood with soju. Location is very popular with tour buses so be prepared for crowds

I live just down the road from O'Sulloc and pass it on a nearly daily basis it's always busy always!.I have visited once get past standing next to a tea plant and a big tea pot and your pretty much done there is a collection of crockery and quite a nice cafe you need to like green tea though...It takes about half an hour to see and do everything.

Can be extremely busy during summer but the beach is beautiful.  Can rent umbrellas to lie under or just bake in the sun.  Some rocky areas in the water but you can navigate around them to enjoy the blue sea.

Well it's a big cave and you are surrounded by lava rocks- which are basically... Rocks.So if you like caves or rocks you will love this!It was very quiet.. Just a few people walked past us... Very different from Ichulbong..You don't need walking shoes or even a torch really, but do care where you walk..It is about 2km from the main road if you take a bus that drops you off on the main road.. Taxis often wait in the main road and charge 4000 one way to the caves..I think entry to the caves was just 1500..The Maze garden is a few hundred metres away too but I didn't go

We walked past Yongdu-am rock when we were trying to find the jimjilbang that we were staying at for the night. If we had made any effort to go and see it I would have been bummed but since it was in passing it was interesting in its own manner. I can understand how it looks like a dragon and you don't need TOO much of an imagination to be able to see it but unless your interested in folklore/'the dragon' means anything to you, you won't be overly excited/impressed.If it didn't have reams of tourists and tour buses or the tourist shops all around it Im not sure I would have even stopped to take a picture.(the ladies working in the tour information centre right outside of this area speak good english and are very kind and helpful if you need directions)

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We traveled here by public transport. The bus stop turned out to be quite a bit away from the cave itself, but we were lucky enough to get a lift from a friendly lady. The cave itself is nice, with lights everywhere. It's not a long walk through, nor is it a difficult one. I would recommend wearing shoes, rather than sandals or flipflops, as the rocky surface isn't easy in the low light. Also recommend a jacket/vest because it gets cold and drops fall from the ceiling.

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

We must have been very lucky, because there was almost no one else around the day we went and we were there in the middle of the afternoon. We were there in October, so maybe it's less busy (but we were there during Chinese Golden Week, so I dunno?). It's definitely worth checking out if you enjoy unique and interesting rock formations.

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

Udo is simply beautiful. You should rent either a bike or a moped once you arrive. You can easily circle the whole island with stops in a couple hours. The enclosed beaches, volcanic rocks, crystal clear water, and very green landscape is exquisite.The road is not really crowded even during the busy summer months. I really enjoyed Udo Island, but then again what major natural location in Jeju-do disappoints? Whether you visit the lava tube caves, craters, dramatic coastline, waterfalls, nearby islands, beaches, mountains, and forests, Jeju-do is a natural paradise.

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.
This place is amazing, the rock formations are beautiful but be prepare for some hordes of tourists when buses arrive. We were lucky and saw some Haenyeos diving out of the beach in the complex.

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!
This Dragon head shaped rock formation is near the airport, and hence favourite of many bus group tours. Can take pictures with the frequent airplanes flying pass by at low altitudes.

The waterfall is said to be the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the sea - although it seems to fall into a cove, not directly into the ocean.  The spot is very touristy and busy, but is a nice waterfall in itself.  You can paddle in the water to cool off and kids love playing on the rocks.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The main attraction of the beach is the inclusion of a somewhat historic public bath.  As it was November and no one was using the public baths, I was able to get into the public baths for a look.  Don't worry, you're not missing out on much as the public baths were not very impressive in size or scope.  I can imagine these public baths would be very busy in the summer when the weather is more appropriate.The beach itself is good - there is plenty of sand so I could imagine people swimming in the sea near the beach in the summer.  However, there are some rocks there as well for people to walk around.All in all, it's a typical beach - nothing to write home about.

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

Spent the day here after going to to the Tuff Cone. I like how they have a lot of business by the beach and how the main beach is enclosed like a cove.  You have either the option to pay to sit under an umbrella, I believe it was 20,000 KRW for all day or you can just go find a shaded area to sit by the rocks.  We chose to latter as you wouldn?t be in the sun and didn?t have to spend the 20,000 KRW.  The water is beautiful and clear, there are plenty of lifeguards at the beach, and it?s a family oriented beach.

Seriously, this rock simply had a good marketing team that created a story and a good image of this rock.. Bus visually you can find so much more interesting rocks in any other place of the Jeju island

Really....it is just another rock with a legend.  It seems that everyone turns into rock while waiting for someone....story line is always the same.  If you are a big fan of Korean drama - Daejeonggeum, then this is the place for you.  A lot of tourist stops here....maybe becos it has no admissions fees.  Try and come early in the morning as the tour buses start coming in late morning.

part of the rock was eroded. it appeared more like a rabbit instead of dragon head. Suggest to go to Heopjae beach which is 5 minutes walk or next to Halim Park. It is overwhelming with crystal clear sea water fine sandy beach, and unique volcanic rock formation within your reach.  It is free and really worth going. The intercity bus will stop right in front of the seaside.

Our kids (7&10) enjoyed the rock climbing, surf and sand...not to mention the modestly price ferry ride.  We attempted to rent a motorized vehicle but there were no rentals for four people...maximum people limit per vehicle was two and one of us did not have a driver's license...so we took the modestly priced bus trip.  Note that a home-country drivers license will not work.  once we figured out the system (no English speakers found on the island of Jeju.), it worked to see most of the island.  The peanut ice cream was all variations of soft-serve...low quality ice cream.  There were enough snack shops for coffee or short orders.  Okay for a day trip.

One of the many very interesting sites in Jeju Island.  These women would dive for 2 minutes at a time to harvest food from the ocean bottom, using no tanks or other equipment.  They were the only known groups of women who resisted during the Japanese occupation.  Also good access by bus.  Easy to get there by bike, depending on where you are staying on the Island. NIce bike paths, though often are covered with the drying sea weed that the old women still harvest from the rocks. There is also a very small Buddhist temple with a Quan Yin statue in front, about a half mile to the west along the coast.

My sister and I went to Udo on a ferry ride after spending a couple of hours at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Because we did not want to go back at dawn, we limited our time to be on the island for about 2-3 hours.It is actually best recommended to spend half a day touring the island either on bus or motorbike. Since we did not have much time, we only walked to the nearby beach which was pretty deserted and that was the best part. Most of the tourist places in Jeju was crowded, but not Udo at the time we were there. The beach was beautiful with small stones and black rocks layering the sand. It was beautiful.There were plenty of cafes within walking distance but we chosed a bench facing the sea in front of a GS25 mart.I love the serenity the island offered. I just wish we had more time to go around the island.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Just a rock formation that looks more like a bunny than a dragon.  Nothing much.  FOC entry but if you're driving, parking is paid when you exit the carpark.  Payment is to an attendant.  Highly touristy area and can be quite packed when the tour buses arrive.  This attraction is open 24hrs.

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was an impressive sight. If you wear appropriate shoes/trainers and get close to the waterfall, you can get a bit wet. But you have to be prepared to walk on big and, sometimes, round rocks. Tip: Get there early. It was our first stop and we were glad. As we were leaving (around 10am), buses full of tourists were arriving. It would have been quite impossible to take good pictures without getting someone's head in them because the staircase is not that wide.

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town

If you have seen any of the large dramatic water falls around the world then you will be disappointed by this tiny cascade. Barely 60/70 ft tall and about 20/25 ft wide. A small stream tumbles directly into the ocean. The tourist brochures make this more dramatic than what it actually is. Have uploaded pictures of the falls from the top (from the platform adjacent to the ticketing office and entry barriers) and from the bridge over the stream just before it tumbles down. Would give you some idea of the size.But having said all of that, this a pleasant enough area. Pay Won 2000 for entry (entry hours 8am - 6pm/7pm, depending on summer/winter) and leisurely climb down about 60 odd feet i.e. equivalent of climbing down about 6 stories. You will arrive at a rocky area. Clambering over about 1/5th mile (300 odd mts) of large rocks to where the water falls, isn't for the aged like me! But it would be nice to get to the water's edge if you can.Not a bad idea to carry sandwiches and beer and sit on the rocks, moments of peace and quiet, isolated from bustling Segwipo all around.You wouldn't miss anything if you haven't been here. But it would be a shame to miss it if you are on Jeju.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for   you silly tourist   sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. You can get here from Jeju bus terminal using the 701 bus (3,000 KRW). There is a stop for it about 40 mins in. It's near Manjangul cave (6,000 KRW taxi) so worth combining it with a trip with that.

I have no idea why Chinese and Korean tourists flock here by the busload.  I just don't get it.  And personally, I don't see a dragon.However, the surrounding areas are truly beautiful. I love the little park and the coastline is spectacular.  Just don't go hoping to be wowed by....a rock.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

For the ones who believe they are in good shape:Why struggle, why do it the hard way? because it is much more scenic and maybe only one tenth of climbers going that way. Taxi from town to starting point (approx 20 min) was 11.000 won on taximeter from my hotel in Nohyung-dong (near the int. airport) or take the bus but only on sat and sundays). Bus stop at Seongpanak when you come down from the mountain on the road. Check schedule and bus no. Taxi back 20.000 won (not on meter..)This is by far the most important place to look before you set out. THE WEATHER! http://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Hallasan/forecasts/1950 I wouldn't call my self an experienced climber but I did it in 3h10min up and 2h down. This is in a pace where I overtook and was not overtaken, and very short breaks, maybe only 2 min in total 5 times. The track is changes between rocks or stairs, I think it's well kept. Two toilet stations up and two down. None at the top. Bring 3-4L of liquids minimum, no passport nor entry is needed for the mountain (aug 2013). A windbreaker for the summit can be nice to have. The weather can change every minute so rain is likely. I did it in old worn-out runners. Bring food and nutrition - no shops. Good luck and enjoy

Decided to skip driving for the day, and took a taxi to Yongduam Rock. It is really cheap if you flag one from Nohyeong-dong area, the fare will only cost around 5000 korean won. There is a little community near the attraction selling food, fruits and all sorts of beverages to shield you from the chilly winter gale. Heading back to the city (Nohyeong-dong area) is a breeze as well, just take a bus back and it will only cost you 1000 korean won. Explore the neighbourhood around Yongduam and explore local sights and sounds. *Thumbs up*
Cool Place, great mountain rock formation. Ilchulbong Peak is an hour travel via InterCity Bus #701 from Jeju City Hall cost around 2,050won. There are eateries and souvenir shops nearby.

Beautiful small island - green hills, lava rocks and small beaches. It's about one hour and a half by bus from Jeju-city to Seongsan ferry terminal (final stop) and 10 minutes by ferry.  We rented ATV to get around the island. The weather changed quickly and suddenly we found ourselves in the middle of the storm. We had a lot of fun riding ATVs through the heavy rain and felt like we are true rangers.  It was too cold to go swimming and by such a weather we couldn't explore the shore caves. So we skip it for the next time.

Beautiful place to take a nice walk around the shore line. Can imagine it would get a bit busy in the summer, but it was empty when we visited as it was a snowy winter day which by all accounts added to the experience. Be careful though it can become a wee bit slippery when the rocks get wet.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

A nice stop on the yeha bus tour, a lot of tourists so it easily gets overcrowded as the observation platform is small. Nice walk nearby with a small park next to the ocean. Pentagonal and heptagonal rock formations from lava cooling down. Enjoyed it and do recommend if in the area!

A local has fulfilled himself a dream. He moved ground to this place and built this park with areas for Bonsai, azalees, palm trees, a natural lava tunnel, traditional houses, strangely formed lava rocks etc.The stop here is part of  a bus tour tio the Western part of the Island.

What a beautiful day to see such a spectacular setting.  This site is a wonder of nature where hexagonal rock pillars stand on top of each other like giant stairs.  I would love to come back in the winter period and see the waves crash over these rocks.What a beautiful day to see such a spectacular setting.  This site is a wonder of nature where hexagonal rock pillars stand on top of each other like giant stairs.  I would love to come back in the winter period and see the waves crash over these rocks
we could not go to the top due to falling rocks on the road. the road was closed due to wind and rain but its beautiful to see the mountain even from the foot hill..its nice place to visit

This spectacular waterfall is worth the visit. Parking is easy and there is a small fee to walk down to the bottom of the falls. The bottom is all rocks so it could be difficult to maneuver for some. At the top is a lovely art gallery and cafe.
Stopped by this beach after visiting Hallim Park. The sand is soft and the water is turquoise-y. But I have seen better beaches. The unique feature to me is the volcanic rock by the beaches.

Perfectly symmetrical columns of rocks stack on top of one another. Must see for geology/volcanology students ( columns were cooled-down volcanic lava). Located within few minutes walk to the Changjeyoun Falls.
Nice location and pretty rock formations down to the sea but not a lot else to see. Give yourself 15-20 minutes tops to see it unless you want to go on the Kayaks.

Love this natural rock formations along the coastal beach walk ... definitely not your usual sandy beach ... lots of opportunities for great photosThere are ladies selling fresh seafood catches along the way ... we didn't have time to stop for that though ...

It was low tide so the rocks were dry and there were lots of little pools.  It was fun to see little kids playing in the pool water for hours.  We were just there for a little time. Our teenagers had fun walking on top of the lava rocks along the beach.  Careful not to step on crabs. Beautiful serene beach.

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is 9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is  9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

Hike this 19.2km return path *9.6km one way on a rainy and cloudy day is definitely an unforgettable experience. Rocky paths have turn into flowing streams. Took  9 hours non stop to reach the peak and return. Thick fog on the peak most of the time and only manage to get a glance at the lake. Great sense of achievement when reaching the top
accessible and you can stop anytime and take pictures but it's quite difficult to get closer as the rocks are quite sharp

You could actually walk out into the ocean among swirling seaweed and chase after schools of small fish (my favourite part). There are also small rock ponds for you to observe some sea creatures that were washed up by the waves. Plenty of families and couples with puppies and dogs were frolicking in the waters and having a picnic on the sand. Sand was so soft!   For more information and pictures on Jeju, visit my travel blog.https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

Well, it was just a rock, nothing special as we come from a place full of strangely-shaped rocks and mountains (Guilin)! We tried the alive octopus at the restaurant near the rock, it was FUN!!! The shop owner caught and cut the octopus into small pieces. The poor thing was still stuck on the plate while we tried to get it into our mouth.  Tasted great with some mustard and soybean sauce!

We were attracted by the promise from the literature that this was the only waterfall in Asia with 'debouches' into the ocean. Hmmm, you almost get the impression from above that some channel engineering has helped this along. Anyway, Wikipedia tells me that this claim is not quite correct. Anyway, we arrived as then had to purchase entry tickets. The stressed out man next to the ticket gate then seemed to think that we have not purchased the correct amount of tickets. We had. It was all the more puzzling because he was only 2 feet from where we bought the tickets. Maybe he was so bored he was asleep at the wheel. Or maybe it was because we were foreigners. Anyway, once that nonsense was resolved we headed down the steps, only to be stopped half-way down at yer another ticket check! Ridiculous, three check for a 1000-or-so won entry ticket. We thought we must be in for something very special. Alas not. Said waterfall falls a few score metres, generates a modest amount of spray and attracts thousands of people taking selfies of themselves and said insipid attraction. There are some older folk selling ghastly looking octopus slices by the rocks - poor animals (the octopus that is). We were not stopped for more ticket checks on the way out, thankfully. I suggest you just look at the photo on the web and go and do something more interesting instead.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

Udo Island, a small volcanic island 10 minutes by ferry from Jeju Island. A day out on this island can be a bore to those who have no affinity to the outdoors, particularly that of the sea.But if you love the care-free life of roaming from one sandy beach to another rocky one. In between with lots of coastal features to be awed by, then this is the little paradise on earth.Udo is an island which allows you to go the entire distance around the coastal roads, in under 4 hours, including stops for pictures, strolls, ice-cream, desserts and of course a whole host of meals.  There are rugged, rocky coastlines and little stretches of sandy beaches with emerald waters.Getting from point to point on the island is very easy, either on bicycles, rental motorbikes and scooters. Mainlainders can ferry in their car for their own pleasure. We rented a motor-scooter for 25, 000 Won for just over 4 hours. The rental is for 2 hours (Won 25000)

Udo is a mini-Jeju, with traditional elements such as stone walls, farms, female divers and ocean cliffs all compressed into a much more manageable area. I rented a bicycle with a basket from an old ahjussi for 4000krw (3 hours). His stall, or rather tent, was located just at the ferry terminal. There are shops across the street that rent out bicycles, scooters and motorcycles.Cycling around Udo was a breeze. It was mainly flat terrain with some gentle slopes here and there. You will ride past white sandy beaches, rocky pools, farms, stone walls, female divers, cute puppies and cafes. Remember to grab some peanut ice cream, the island?s specialty.For more information and pictures on Udo, visit my travel blog https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

This is just another roadside attraction that many people visiting Jeju stop by to see only because it is in the city proper. It is just a rock that could appear to look like any number of different animals.If your tour guide takes you out of your way to see this then you need a new tour guide because this rock is typical of any of the millions of rocks you run into along the seashore in Jeju.There are a lot of interesting things to see and fun places to go in Jeju but, this isn't one of them.

The rock itself isn't very impressive. Yes, it looks like a dragon and you can take pictures but that isn't the only thing you can do there. If you go down the steps and cross a quite rocky and unstable path (be careful), there are some fishermen who sell fresh seafood like octopus, oysters, and sea cucumber. You can eat them fresh and raw. Food adventurers will definitely love the place. There's a stall near the toilets where they grill the catch too.

The lava tubes are very interesting and quite large - especially compared to those in other parts of the world. The only word of caution is to bring a raincoat and sneakers if it has been raining, as the water will trickle down through the rock and will drip considerably as you walk through. Definitely worth a stop.

The Dragon Head Rock was rather disappointing since the shape was difficult to visualize as a dragon head no matter which ever way we looked at it.  However for a brief stop, it is worthwhile for first time visitors.

The dragon head rock makes for an interesting photo souvenir. It is a nice place to visit, but probably would not count as one of the must-see places in Korea. Shops selling grilled octopus and other snacks line the route to the attraction, but the food is nothing spectacular as well. Allocate 30 minutes for the place.

So, one might think that this is a great place to see artifacts or historic pieces, but as far as we saw, everything was a replica. To include the replica lava tube entrances. Sigh. They couldn't even be bothered to completely thatch a straw hut- they had concrete roofs with thatch done at the top and edges. They do have quite the array of carefully placed rocks and replica stone statues, but seeing as how none of it was real (the whole thing was built on the site of a landfill) there are more real things to go do on Jeju. The price is cheap. Spend it looking at the columnar basalt on the beach. At least that is real.

Rent bikes and escape the tour groups, and you can stop where you like. We found Udo was quieter than the rest of Jeju Island. There are plenty of coffee shops, small eateries and ice cream places. Things to see include lighthouses and beaches - but there is a huge amount of litter around the rocks and headlands.  Peanuts are grown on the island and there was a peanut festival at the ferry terminal when we visited.

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.

One of Jeju Island attraction, the rock formations that looks more like a horse head to me. Well, legendary it was a head of a dragon. We stop by for a photo stop on our way to airport.A good nice photographing platform for visitor to take picture. There is a stairway leading down to the rocky beach, down there you can see many locals selling fresh seafood.  It is not a wheelchair friendly place. Be there before sunset otherwise you will not able to take a clear photo.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Jeongbang Waterfall was near our guesthouse and it was the first stop of our trip to the east of Jeju. You can climb through the rocks and take a photo in the middle the small pond, in front of the waterfall. The water spray catches the light and acts as a prism to scatter the light into rainbows..pretty

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It takes about 6 hrs for hiking up and go back. The way back is rock path half of the way, so quite tough for me. But it's worth to hiking up. The scenery on the top is breathtaking and unique. I visited there on late May, which there were still some pink azalea blooming and it was very beautiful.Please beware of the weather and strong wind on the top.I'd rate it for No.1 attraction site to visit in Jeju-do.

It takes 10 min tops to actually enjoy the rock.  Its unique and pretty but that's all folks!  You have to pay for parking (500 won every 30 min) and believe me, it doesn't even take that long to see all there is to see.  We had extra time before rental car needed to be returned so we stopped.  But I wouldn't have otherwise gone out of my way to see this rock formation.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

For us - it was a last 'must see' on Jeju Island.  Our tour books featured it as a top site, so we went.  We didn't have much time, and it worked (since it's near the airport) for a quick stop off.  I didn't hate it - it was crowded though.  Lots of tour groups, teens, etc.  There were several shops nearby that were handy for our last bit of shopping.  You don't need to spend a lot of time here, but the rock formation is neat and the myth behind it is interesting.
For me it's not a very special sight, though it's adventurous and interesting to walk down the stairs to the coast and see the   diving women   serving octopus, shells and abalone on the rock

As part of the tour, we had a short stop at dragon head rock, where you can see the head of a dragon naturally carved on a big rock. There is also a small mermaid sculptured on a rock for photo opportunity. This is more of a photo stop. Jeju as an island attraction have plenty of rock formation, volcanic rocks, and shoreline with plenty of rock. Again like all part of Jeju, the place has good breeze and quite comfortable.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.

You can get right up to the falls even as it empties into the sea. Where sneaks that day because there are a lot of rocks. Be careful and take lots of pictures. A taxi or bike ride is preferable but you can easily walk to the entrance it is just out of the way of the town

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.

We stumbled upon this place whilst walking about but didn't regret it.I would be careful if you are accompanying very young children or old people as the stairs are made of rock and quite difficult to negotiate. Our 5 year old made it ok but required assistance.A nice place to visit but not much in the way of a waterfall when we were there. Perhaps they take the water in during the day? (that was a joke by the way!)

This was seriously one of the coolest things I've ever seen. The waves crashing against the rocks was incredible. I went on a rainy day and that didn't take away from how amazing it was. Since it was rainy it wasn't that crowded. I stayed longer than many people though. I just couldn't believe it. Stay longer if you want. Definitely try to see this in Jeju.

This natural attraction isn't that remarkable (rock that looks like a dragon) but it would have been nice except it is PACKED with tourists. It is way too crowded for my liking and most photos taken will include a bunch of other random tourists in it as well. My boyfriend and I were far more interested in the little food stalls set up around this tourist attraction - as you can try some local snacks. We came here as a part of a tour from Hong Kong.
This is a nice waterfall to see going in to the sea. The walk down is all steps about 130 each way. The rocks at the bottom can be difficult to walk over.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!
rock formation. nothing particularly special about it. visit if along the way or have time to do so.

Rented a scooter for 4 hours and went around the entire island. Renting is easy- just go to one of the places right next to the ferry docks. You have to go to the cliffs and the black sand beach below them. Cross the beach to the rocks where they have the boat then go inside the cave. Walk all the way to the left and go out the small opening- this place have practically no other tourists. Then if it's low tide- climb to the right to the small opening into another cave but this is a lot cooler!

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

Nice park and a great way to know about the history of the island.amazing grand sight of the rock formations.Rocks & stones everywhere. Beautiful landscape. There are nice traditional houses in the park.
Nice magma formations but not realy a dragon head.Many tourists are around the rock so easy to find.If you're anyway around there worth a look but you don't have to come extra for this rock...
It's a Lava cave about 1 km. The walkway was very hard to walk because it's a lava rock. And it's wet because of the rain. It's OK. I didn't feel woww. If you have a free time you can go there.

I love open-water swimming and just plain jumping off rocks. This spot is ideal for both and is also a good way of interacting with locals. you don't even need to speak Korean to get along with folks here!

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.
great place to go on a hot day as it is nice and cool inside and it is amazing to see how lava carved it's way through the rocks

Good chance to explore natureof lava tube..I shall recommend for walk alley to be build along the way inside the tube..its to hard to walk on the slippery rocks.Hence to put more highlight inside the tube..its too dark inside

Black sand beach with lots of rocks.  Didn't see much wildlife but there were tons of people there.  The water from the river is clear blue and gorgeous but cold.  There is a place where you can canoe up the river for a bit.  Side note the parking is awful.  Be prepared to park a bit away and then walk.

As an American when I think beach I think sand water sand castles a boardwalk and a place to grab a drink. This beach has the sand and water but that is absolutely it. Sand water then a huge hill. You have to have a car to get here. There is a parking lot a 1/4 to 1/2 mile away. At the lot there is some minor touristy things. Think about 5 minutes of time to see it all. You then walk down a steep road and are at the beach. The pros: one of the few spots on the south side with sand and not just boulders. There are bathrooms and a place to wash off. The cons: it's a beach and nothing else. Since our hotel is about 4 miles up the coast and right on the beach that is solid rock we will drive here for the kids. But this is certainly not a reason to come here.
all over the island you can see beautiful coast line with clear waters and rocky pathway. is just the island natural built

A walk through this cave took us back to the times with the images of the lava cave and dry rocks just like in the dinosaur films. The cave is kept just the same as it always is so the paths are rough and make it more adventurous.

A beautiful scenic walk along the coast and the path was well taken care of. We walked to the right first and walked most of the path up until it started to inclined towards the end and then turned around and walked down the left path all the way to the parking lot. Definitely recommend walking both paths since you see different rock formations and the walk is not too difficult or long.

A  unique cave with 70 cm lava stalagmites and lava tube tunnel . Lighted with dim lights. Floor rocky and slippery but manageable  with comfortable shoes . A kilometer long but takes about 20-25 minutes one way . The Lava  formed at the end is a beautiful one worth seeing.

yongduam rock is near to the airport. You can visit here the day before you depart from Jeju island. It has beautiful walk alone the sea. The place is good for seeing the ocean from the peak. There is a dead rock here. Those who like to take pictures of the plane can take pictures of the plane which is on the way to airport. This place is one of the icons of Jeju city. So, must see it.

Yongduam (meaning dragon head rock) is probably the most overrated sight in all of Jeju.  It was a favorite photo spot for honeymooners a few decades ago and it?s mind boggling why.  It is just a dragon head shaped rock and there are so many more impressive coastal scenery on the island.  If it wasn?t for our last stamping station being located near it, no way we would?ve gone out of the way to see it.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever.
