We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.
tough climb to take pictures at the waterfall because of the rocks and uneven ground. but the sight is well worth it.

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!
The place is well kept and there was a lovely souvenir shop on site. There is not much to see in this part of Jeju so climbing up this rock was definitely an uplifting experience.
Short walk from the carpark but need to climb down stairs and walk on rocks to go near waterfall. Not suitable for stroller or wheelchair.

It is easy to access the fall for those who dislike climbing steps.  It was only a short distance from the entrance via some steps.  Nice feeling to get up close and personal to the fall however just gotta beware of wet ones which at times can be slippery.  Smaller rocks tend to move when you are stepping on them so be careful.
I went there at night and there was this huge spotlight shining on the rock itself. Not a good place for the elderly people as climbing up and down that narrow staircase is a hassle.

How many places can you see that?  And be accessible.  It's very pretty I think maybe 20m tall.  There's plenty of stairs and rocks to climb but it's worth the extra effort. Our 10 yr old loved getting sprayed by the mist.  It's near the town and easy to get to worth the$4 admission.

A lovely puppy greets you at the start of the walk! You walk past a lovely stone house on the left and the dry riverbed on the right. They have well built stairs to the falls. At this time of year there are no falls - due to lack of rain  however there is a lovely pond at the bottom and the ability to climb down the rock's and close to the water. A lovely place to sit and contemplate! Don't recommend kissing the kissing cave...a blarney stone it's not haha!

We saw many people taking photos around the waterfall. It's not the tallest nor grandest waterfall so I'm not sure what's the fuss about.Entrance fee is only 2K/pax. It's a short climb back up from the waterfall, ie very suitable for family and elderly.The rocks around the waterfall are rather pointed so please watch out while taking your selfies.

We had a wonderful time, enjoying the beautiful rock formations.  Great place to take pretty photos.  The climb down on the rocky rocks can be a challenge but the reward is well worth it.  Some ahjumas are selling their catch of fresh seafood too.  Place may be closed if it is high tide.
We go to Hyeopjae beach whenever in Jeju, lovely sand, good safe swimming, great rocks to climb over, the grandkids love it

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.

This is quite possibly the most beautiful spot on the island-- definitely worth the small entrance fee (I think it was about 7000 won for my family of 5). There are some fairly serious steps to get down the cliff, and then to actually get close to the falls, it's necessary to climb across a bunch of small/medium rocks. Most people will have no problems with either, but for someone with knee or foot problems it could be an issue.The only thing I didn't love was that it was SO crowded. It was impossible to get a decent photo without someone walking into the frame, and several times we were actually shoved off of rocks as more and more people tried to crowd in. It would be great if they would limit the amount of people allowed down at one time.Other than that-- a great experience that we definitely won't forget.

This is a very accessible waterfall. Kudos to the local government for making it as easy as possible to enjoy the natural landmarks on the island. A flight of steps down and a very short walk brings you to the waterfall. There are large rocks to climb over and also a rocky flat   beach  . Young children will especially love climbing over the rocks and exploring the pools of flowing water. I have a sturdy 4 year old and a 5.5 year old and I think the waterfall impressed them less than the natural rocky playground they happily found themselves in. Do keep a very close eye on young children as the rocks are sharp edged and uneven, some even loose when you step on them.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

The unique thing about this waterfall is it's by the sea. Do wear proper shoes as you would have to climb down stairs and rocks if you want a closer look at the falls. Like most attractions in Jeju, it was awfully crowded. Ap, one doesn't really get a chance to sit and enjoy the falls, which is a pity.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

Our family spent much effort taking a nice family picture near this waterfall - and it turned out GREAT!! Hahaha... Nice place to go, for the sight, the EXERCISE!!But it can get quite crowded though. Older folks may find it hard to climb on the uneven rocks but they can get near enough for picture with the waterfall at the background. To get REAL near to the waterfall, leave it to the young ones!

Our 70 year old tour guide could climb these rocks to get here. The Grand Canyon of Jeju. Whilst it was breathtaking, I couldn?t help but constantly call out to the kids to be careful of the slippery rocks. There are life rings hanging on the cliffs but let?s be realistic. With currents that strong, if you fell into the water, the current would crash you straight into the rocks. We went early morning when the tide was out but could feel the tide level rising. Our guide wanted to go further as he said it was more spectacular.Make sure you go with good gripped sneakers and a jacket. You are on the edge of the ocean after all.

I've never been able to go up so close to a waterfall that flows directly into the sea. You'll need to climb over rocks to go up near to the falls. I loved being so near the waterfall and the sea at the same time!If you only have time to see 1 waterfall on Jeju island, go to this one. Cheonjiyeon & Cheonjeyeon waterfalls were quite unimpressive in my opinion.

Island best explored by driving, ATV or bike rental. Ferry across from mainland Jeju also carries vehicles. Road kinda narrow so one need to be careful, I blew a tyre when my right wheel rammed into a rock or kerb :-(  Lots of climbing if you really wanna explore in-depth. Many small eateries on the island. Very scenic island with lots of photo opportunity. Be wary of last ferry back or you would be stuck there overnight

If you're one for waterfalls, this shouldn't be missed as our guide told us that this is the only waterfall that falls directly into the sea. We caught rainbows quite a couple of times which made the scenery that more beautiful. You can also climb up onto the rocks to get nearer to the falls and snap loads of pictures!

If you only see one waterfall in Jeju, I would see this one. It is beautiful how it goes into the see. We visited it during a taxi tour along with Cheonjiyeon Falls. They are very close to each other so there is no need to see just one but if you are short on time I would go to Jeongbang. For 2000 won each it is a bargin. Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet and can climb over rocks in, if you want to get close to the waterfall.

I went earlier to see the Cheonjiyeon waterfall and must say this is a better one because you can actually get to dip your toes into the water. I paid 2000 won for an adult. Basically there are steep steps you need to walk down and then in order to get nearer to the waterfall you need to climb over big rocks. If you are with little children or older folk you might have a hard time. With the waterfall, you can wade right up to it if you are brave enough the stand the cold.

I found this waterfall a better experience than Cheonjiyeon Falls as you can go very close to the waterfall. Be prepared to walk down a lot of stairs and then climb over rocks to get close to the falls, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Don't bother paying for the museum close to the gate, it's a waste of time but only 500 Won if you want to.

I could not recognise how horrible the place has become since my second visit in 2009.  Not only was it very crowded, I was sad to see lots of garbage on the rocky beach below.  It was also not possible to enjoy a nice walk by the cliffside for those of us not out to climb the mountain.  I left after no more than 15 minutes to the utter surprise of my cab driver.It was a beautiful and serene place and the authorities should take steps to limit the number of visitors and do more to clean up the garbage.
Easy climb down to see the waterfall. If you are adventurous, go navigate across the rocks for better photos angles and also for a challenge. A simple waterfall for photo ops and a light stroll.

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

At this place you need to walk, climb a little. Be very careful when climbing on and over rocks at the bottom of the fall to take pics. Some rocks are very slippery. You can see the water go straight into the ocean which is quite different to the other two waterfalls. It is a lovely sight!

amazing landscape. A nice spot to take beautiful pictures of tranquil waters with pitch black rocks and white sand. Walk right from the main entrance till the end, you will fine some nice restaurants and cheaper places to stay. From there you can climb the hill and get the whole picture of Hamdeok area.

Well worth the small trek down.  Do a little rock/boulder hopping to the base and you can get a nice spray.  If you catch this waterfall during the rainy season or after a good rain it will be much more powerful.  Take the time to visit this place...maybe a little crowded but plenty of space to find your own spot.

Very rocky do be sure to wear appropriate shoes. Lots of great angles to take photos without having lots of other tourists in the shot. Go around dinner or lunch time as they have some local women selling freshly prepared seafood (I'm a vegetarian and didn't try it but looked good).

This rock formation was spotted on the eastern side of Jeju island. I was lucky enough to see this attraction having not spotted one a long time ago.The water present in these area is crystal clear where you can see different fishes swimming in the ocean breeze.

This is no Caribbean beach so don't expect warm turquoise waters and endless stretches of fine white sand. Considering the area however it is a decent beach and worth checking out if you are in the area. It is located within the Jungmun Resort complex in Seogwipo but there is no charge so anyone can visit.Here's what to expect: yellow/orange rough sand with lots of bits of shell; water that gets deep quite quickly; STRONG undertow on stormy days. The resort restricts people from swimming during certain months (wintertime I think) because of the risk of undertow.  I mention the last point because the beach is actually quite beautiful to watch on a windy day as the waves crash into the volcanic rock.Quite often on weekends foreigners gather to play rounds of volleyball.There are spots to get food near the beach and in the resort but be ready for sky-high prices.
The rock formations near the water are absolutely remarkable. I recommend taking the time to visit if you are on Jeju Island.

The ?Dragon Hair? rock location is near Jeju airport and a good recommendation if you are trying to burn some time prior to departing Jeju. The location has spacious parking and allows visitors easy access to the actual rock.

Reminds me of kenyas hells gate. The place is a sight to behold. Be carefull to put on comfy shoes that have great treads and grips so that you dont slip on the sometimes slippery rocks. Also find out about tides. If its high tides then definately you will be soaked by action of water on your feet. Good place though. I recommend finnishing it with a horse ride by the ajoshi at the exit for man won and a cold jeju tangerine juice.
Not so spectecular after you have seen all the beautiful scenery in Jeju. A quick visit is alright if you have the time. Just a rock formation.
It's a rock that kind of likes a dragon head. There really wasn't much else. Skip it if you you don't have time. Not worth battling the crowds to take a picture.
It was crowded with some tour groups and there was really not special about this. It is just some rocks with one of them looking like a dragon head. Give this a miss unless you have too much time.
It is just a rock that looks like a dragon's head but only if you are looking at it from up close. I wouldn't recommend spending lots of time here.
It is a bit dangerous to watch the rock but good to visit shortly if you have no time before your flight bacause it is near airport.

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

I went here a couple of times during my stay on Jeju Island. I loved the Innisfree shop where you could buy packs of soap that you then made with either green tea tangerine or volcanic rock ash. It was so cool and they made lovely souvenirs for when I came home. Also the green tea roll cake there is delicious! And the gardens are great for taking photos. 10/10 would recommend.

Experience狩狩狩狩狩Time worth狩狩狩狩狩Good for photos狩狩狩狩狩The Dragon Head rock was formed through volcanic activity and the surrounding beach is covered in a thick layer of volcanic ash and rock. The whole area is beautiful and great for taking photos though not worth visiting again as it's more of a love at first sight thing
Enjoyed extra time here because the rushing water sounds were so relaxing. You can hang out on the rocks quite close to the falls.

At the entrance of the plaza there is tourist information center where you can get any info related to the area. From this plaza there are occasional festival from time to time this time I just went to see sunset on the ocean. Above the big waves sunset was pretty. There is long sea-side walk which leads to Dragon head rock.
A small rock formed around many rocks. It is near the city and black pork street. Good time to visit is sunset or sunrise time.
Wifi so fast here, I can video call with my mother in Indonesia. Many snacks sellers here. Sunset is best time to going yongduam rock. The air is very cool

Whether you love nature or not, I strongly recommend visiting this cave. There is so much to learn on how the lava tube was formed and it provides you with a unique experience that is unforgettable. Do wear proper covered shoes as you will be walking on rocks almost the entire time and some parts might be slippery.

When we arrived in jeju it was raining so we needed to do something that was more indoor.  We drove out to the cave.  The entrance fee is cheap at 2000 won per person.  Then you walk down some steps and enter the lava tube.  It is really dark down there and the floor can be slippery.  I think we spent most of our time looking down at where to walk rather than looking around.  You walk 1km to the end and there is a rock formation.  Nothing too special.  Then you turn around and walk back.  Overall it is a nice cool 2km walk, perfect to escape the heat of jeju.  Just watch where you walk

We loved walking through Halla Park. The paths are organized and cultured so beautifully. Every turn brings new surprises. There are bonsai trees galore, rock formations, fountains, and green spaces the lure you in. The caves are small, but fascinating. The birds here are delightful, from parakeets to peacocks and ostriches. We would definitely come back and have a picnic here in the springtime.

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

We have visited many caves in various countries. More or less they are quite similar. Dark, quiet, mysterious, cold, etc.As with every cave, it's not well litted & its quite dark in certain sections of the cave. Being a natural formation, the ground is usually uneven. Particularly for this cave , the unevenness is very bad. And rocky in certain parts. We spent the most of the time in the cave focussing on the rough/uneven ground rather than the place - in order not to slip or fall. One can easily slip or fall on the widespread/rocky uneveness here & darkness if you looked up rather than down ;& get sprained ankles or worse injuries if you fall.Do not recommend children, elderly or physically disadvantaged people to visit this cave or any caves.Frankly, we were not keen to see yet another cave but since it was part of our paid day tour, why waste it?

We enjoyed the experience of transversing the rocks to get to the falls. It can be a challenge though with young children. The feel of water vapour sweeping through your face and sitting close to the falls was great. I can't compare it with the other nearby falls as we didn't have time to visit those but we were satisfied with this fall. While heading out, there are a few hawkers selling stuff and bought boxes of Jeju chocolates and biscuits at really good price.

This small rock which located next to beach is famous maybe because of many chines visitors , Highly recommended to not waste your precious time to going there , if u want to eat local food nearby there maybe is not bad idea to visit here otherwise don't .

this place is free and located nearby airport. it won't take too much time also, spend around 1hrs here.Sometimes u can see the airplanes landed as the background..kinda cool..the dragon-shaped rock is visible if u take picture with the right angle, otherwise it's just an ordinary rock.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is one of the must see in Jeju. The most beautiful rocky beach in Jeju. Hamel ship (copy) is on beachside. You can check some pics on TripAdvisor. Spring season is high season.  Summer season is also high season, but check if typhoon is near. Check the typhoon, you cannot go close beach if there is typhoon. It is not normal beach, waves carved this beach for long time, hundreds of thousands of years.

this is  rare chance to walk down lava tubes and look at the odd shapes and formations caused by the molten rock. You can see different layers of lava that once flowed here and see how the laval squeezed through smaller passages.   Consider bringing an umbrella or a very light shell. It can be damp and sometimes water drips from the ceilings. Also, it's significantly cooler than outside.   All in all, a must.

The professional photos are very well taken thus I was quite interested in this place before i go. But basically you will spend perhaps a good 20 to 25 mins walking from one end to another end seeing the same thing (unless you are very interested in rocks or stones) in very dark lighting.. and then another 20 to 25 mins back. I don't think its a bad place.. just not to my liking i guess. If you have time and a good camera and a tripod, you might take some very nice photos there lol

The grounds are HUGE! It felt like a nature forest walk, a geography and history field trip all rolled into one.I don't know if it's windy there all the time, but when we were there, it was freezing when the wind blew when we were in the shade.We had a tour guide who explained the various rock features and how/why people carved the stones for use in the past. But honestly, I was bored after awhile. This place had rocks/stones galore. Considering that there are so many other things to see/do in Jeju, I would give this place a miss.

The dragon head rock is in North part of Jeju, close to the airport. It is a rock that looks like a dragon head on the coast. The Seogwipo coast line like the Jusanjeolli Cliff or the Odelgae Rock are much more interesting than this. However, if you do not have time to visit the Jungmun/Seogwipo area, this is an alternative to see the rocky coastline. The sunset here is nice, but the place is packed with tourists fighting to get photos, so it's not all that romantic. I think a beach sunset at a more remote beach on the West side would be nicer and a calmer experience.
the destination is built by legend about dragon who fall from the earth, as tourist object not much to see. it's nature rock, beach and on autum the weather is nice. no need much time

The cliffs are a real sight to visit. You can see the nice natural rock formations, and the beautiful blue sea in the background. A really beautiful and peaceful place which we were told transform itself during the different seasons. There is a 'resident' painter who is there the whole year round and he captures the beauty of the place in all seasons and during different times of the day.

The best waterfall to visit! Don't waste time to other waterfall, this is the best one. I managed to see rainbow at the waterfall was simply amazing! Made the whole trip worthwhile! Just wear the right shoes there as there are some rocks to walk on before getting close to the waterfall

Perhaps it was the time of day we were here. We got here really early around 8am to start our road trip down the east side of Jeju Island. So nothing was open yet. We saw the dragon rock and even walked down the side of the small cliff to see the rock from a different angle. It was raining quite a bit on the morning we visited so the walk down was a little slippery. It was interesting to see the dragon rock formation and read about it's significance in Korean folklore. We had a photo with the mermaid there too. Unfortunately due to the time of day we visited nothing else was open, but from what we could tell there were mainly souvenir, fruit and convenient stores and stalls. Worth a visit if you have time, but essentially a nice looking rock

One of the benefits of being an island is all the beaches. One of the drawbacks is that beaches usually draw tourists, and where there are tourists, the shallow villainy of tourist industries inevitably follows. Sehwa has not yet been targeted for development. As of this writing, the long, open expanse of Sehwa beach is still a beach in its rawest form. When the tide goes out, the volcanic rock formations nearer to the road are exposed, leaving tidal pools to explore, thriving with an over abundance of flora and fauna. The beach at low tide is enormous, and rarely crowded. There are no lifeguards. No music. No lights. Just a beautiful beach, minor waves, clean sand, and decent swimming. When the tide comes in, you can continue swimming, or you can visit some of the restaurants in the area that cater to the locals rather than skimp for the tourists. I had some shabu shabu (??\대＿?) very near Sehwa which was like a kick to the pleasure center of my brain.  Sometimes there's even a local crafts market right next to Sehwa beach, but you have to get lucky to catch it.   Basically, Sehwa is a beach that is still Jeju. It's part of a local community, part of a local ecosystem, as yet only mildly disturbed by ideas of profitability or development.
Nothing special. For me, it wasted our time. Its a rock with a shape of dragon. The ice-cream shop nearby is nice.
Nice to visit...but do not spent too much time in this area.  There are a lot of nice places in Jeju.  Please note, Dragon Head Rock near sea with strong wind.

Mind your step! The cave is long, dark and slippery. This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience.The price is reasonable. A number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing.
Just a rock but  if ur imagination is working overtime , you can see the   dragon head  . Many group of tourists see the place. Its near the seaside restaurants of which we find very expensive food.

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

It's a nice looking waterfall that falls directly into the ocean which is great but there are literally hundreds of people here at a time. The rocks are not particularly dangerous by themselves but add a huge crowd of tourists and school kids to the mix and it's a little risky. I think the fact that it was the scene of a Korean drama tv show may be part of the reason for it's popularity. The ladies selling seafood on the rocks so affectionately mentioned by others are not genuine haenyon, they just sell seafood at exorbitant prices. Buy your lunch elsewhere.

It?s a place must visit in Jeju island. Air is so fresh and the walk is tranquil. When you walk through the forest and appreciate wat the Korean say that it is a place for meditation. There is a tap near the entrance, water is so refreshing. Trees in the forest have been there for hundred of years . It?s a treat to see some trees with autumn leaves. There are some Low walls with black stone formations which apparently is the volcanic rock from Jeju itself.. Would definitely come back here again to spend more time in the forest At the end of the walk they even have the vacuum facility to blow off the red soil from your shoes

It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was quite quiet when we were there and we only saw a few people except for a group on a guided tour at the end. Such a shame there are not more visitors but good for those who made the effort. Recommended visit in Jeju!

It was a 1km walk in and 1km out again. The lights were pretty dim unless there are signboards. The path inside is quite rocky with puddles of water here and there. Spent most of time watching out for puddles of water and where to walk instead of enjoying the lava cave. The cave was colder than outside, so might have to prepare a thin jacket.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

If you're in the area I'd pop in but don't make a special trip - It's nice seeing all the old huts and how they used to live but once you've seen one set of huts they are all pretty similar. i think they have some events on sometimes as there is a stage, but when we were there, there was just four girls playing drums and no one was watching them. Oh and they randomly have some ostriches - didn't figure out why but they were pretty cool!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

If it's your first time visit, definitely take the path to Oedolgae. If you have time, from the main entrance, take a left and it will take you along a path along the ocean. Go about 1/2 mi walk along the path and you'll see off on your right a smaller path. Take this and it will take you down to the ocean. Many locals take this down and it's a small watering hole where locals go to swim and fish. Once you get to the bottom, the navigation along the rocky formations can be challenging but very much worth it. It's not a beach but you're right next to the waves as they come in. It's absolutely beautiful. Just for context, I took my 8 year old daughter and 6 year old son. They had to be careful navigating, but was able to do so with adult supervision. Many others have come to appreciate this but they have been leaving their trash behind and it's quite saddening to see such a beautiful place littered with garbage. If you do go down, please respect the beauty and take your garbage with you.

I quite enjoyed this place. It takes a while to walk around so don't go if you are in a hurry. If you take your time there is plenty to see, ancient tombs, traditional housing/tools, stone statues, giant stone towers, etc. The museum was also good and I learnt a bit about volcanic rock formation that I hadn't seen before.

I just don't get this place. The rock doesn't look like a dragon head.... does it?Maybe cos I went there on my own... but I just don't see the significance of this place. Why? It's a waste of time and effort. Not that it requires that much walking... But I'd conserve my energy and also my time on something other than this.So not worth the time and energy. To me, that is. Maybe there is more to this place... but I just don't see/get it.

i feel i am lucky cos my hotel just nearby Yongduam Rock.the story behind is very attractive but won't give you a surprise when you really at there.The scale of Yongduam Rock is smaller than you think, but if you love to take picture with infinity sea or amazing sea wave, this place is a good place to go.finally, there are lot of restaurants around there, can have a good time after visit there.

I also went to Cheonjiyeon Falls, but this one was incredible. I found Cheonjiyeon Falls pretty, but it didn't feel special. This waterfall is loud. You can definitely feel the power. You can feel the mist and it is just awesome. The rocks are also really fun to play around on. I spent most of my time sitting by the ocean watched the waves crash on the rocks. It was really beautiful. While it is just a waterfall, there is more to do around this one than snap a photo. I definitely recommend this one.

Getting close to the waterfalls looks easier than it seems. However, that adds to the thrill of getting nearer to mother nature. It is tricky manuvering around the wet, slippery & sometimes unstable rocks & boulders in cold weather. Many a times, you find yourself balancing precariously on the boulders or have your feet stuck between the rocks as you slip or slide from the smooth rocks. You will also find visitors around you lending you a hand to help you get back on your feet. Such spontaneous camaraderie !  For the young & agile, it is fun watching them jumping from rock to rock, like Tarzan in action.  It is a thrilling on the rocks experience not to be missed !  And you get rewarded by the beautiful sight & sound of a great waterfall!

Dragon Head Rock (Yongdu-am) is worth a look just to say   been there, done that  !It's nothing fantastic but does live up to its name.As it is within walking distance of downtown make the effort if you have the time.Tour groups, especially in the morning, arrive by the coach load. So walking makes good sense!

Cold lave tunnel at 12.4 degrees Celsius. Very educational and good for hiking.Entire tunnel is 7.4km, only 1km (the middle section) is opened to public.My 2nd time visiting, still very amazed with all these rock formation.

By the time we reached the Jungmun Daepo cliff, it's already 4.50 pm! 40 minutes to closing time! We hurried to buy tickets and rushed in! We're amazed to met with awesome lava volcanic rocks naturally forming into octagonal shapes and in poles like! Scenery there are beautiful too! We quickly took pictures as we went along every scenic spots.Then time to go out and even outside are some man made decorations of big shell and fishes too! On the whole, it's a nice place!

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.
You must go!The road from the mountain to the sea is thrilling. The rocks the beach the mountain the environment all worth I went there at the end of the day around 18 h and regret for being late
You can find this at the Sanbangsan Mountain area. It's a really good rock formation brought by years and years of the sea waves slapping those great rock walls.

Walk around the mountain and you can see different rock formations.  The water is very clear (look at the picture as if there is no water) that you can see sea urchins. I advise you wear rubber shoes to be more comfortable walking through sharp rock formations.

It is a volcanic rock formation in the form of a dragon?s head, created by strong winds and waves over thousands of years. However, legend has it that a dragon stealing precious jade from Mt. Halla was shot down by an arrow from the mountain deity. When he fell down on Yongduam, his body immediately sank into the ocean and his head rapidly froze looking at the sky. Another legend has it that a white horse dreamt of being a dragon and ascending to the sky. On his ascent, he was caught by a soldier and froze into the rock. While admiring the dragon?s head, one can see how the black rocks contrast with the emerald blue ocean.

Very Nice place to understand and enjoy Jeju in South Korea. There is old story that a women had been waited for her husband who was fisherman.  She became the rock statue(Oeidolgae) because her husband couldn't come back home while fishing sunk by windstorm.  Also another point of sightseeing is beautiful beach with rocks. There is beach of rocks in this region.   You may see pics in TripAdvisor.  Atlas Dream.
The beach was nice enough. Very shallow waters. Lots os rocks around the beach. Lots of people. Except at 1am in the morning when I snuck back for a walk.

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

It's supposed to be one of the seven winders of nature but not exactly my kind of travel destination. It's amazing for the sheer length of the cave (7km) although you are only allowed to go to the first km. We only managed to go 300 m since there wss not much to see except for molten rocks along the cave. There was not much to sustain interest in going further inside the cave so we decided to just go back. At least it was cool inside although the path was wet but nit muddy. Wear comfortable and non slippery shoes if you wish to see the cave.

Yes, it's just an ordinary rock. But with the perfect backdrop of the ocean, blue skies and outlying islands this place is perfect to visit in the morning for a relaxing walk. You can even sample their famous orange fruit in season.

Went there to watch sunrise with Sunrise Peak background and foreground with water and rock.? The beach is large and we could find a spot without disturbance of others.? However, there is no official car park space.

We went to this beach during the day and kayaked and swam. It was a lot of fun! Then we went at night and it had a wonderful nightlife with restaurants and lights!  *I really recommend this beach!  It wasn't too crowded like the others, and there weren't too many black rocks, and no seaweed.  It was great to walk in the water at night too.  We're going back to this beach again this year!

We only went here to escape from the unrelenting rain, but were glad we went. They've resisted the temptation to over-commercialise or trivialise, so only minimal lighting, natural rock footpath underfoot, no intrusive commentary or redundant health and safety notices. All that allows you just to take in the majesty of the space and lava formations in the hushed atmosphere, reminiscent of a great cathedral. 1km from start to finish then 1km back.
Was terribly rainy on the day we visited, but managed to get our picture with the dragon rock formation in the background.  Was a fun trek to get to the location.

Unique pattern of rocks made of lava. You could take great pictures of the nature from anywhere here. Great background for any photo types - selfies, family photos, etc. all seniors (65+) are free with a valid identification!

This place is an epitome of beauty, beautiful rock formation, beautiful sea, beautiful waves, beautiful clouds, it is amazingly beautiful. Here you enjoy both worlds of rock formation and beautiful sea. Definitely this place is super windy and you might get wet with huge waves hitting against the rock formation. The scenery of the place couple with the beautiful sound of waves for me makes any visit to Jeju complete. Be careful in walking and exploring place, there are areas that are slippery and rough.  If you are an instagram addict this place is the best for you. You can choose to have those lovely rock formation as background or the beautiful blue sea with the huge waves and or both the lovely rock formation and waves.

This island is not in your usual tourist-package because you really need 1 day to cover the whole quaint island. But it is worth it. The whole place had lots of walls made up of volcanic rocks, making it look almost Irish. And the scenery around the island is just quite breath-taking. We drove and put the car in the ferry as well. Only complaint is that instructions were all in Korean at the ticket office, so hard to figure out what to do. Also, what would happen if one misses the last ferry back to the main island???
Really enjoyed the walk around the coastal, all the rock formation is awesome. We walked around from the shipwreck and back again to the same spot. If you love nature, this place is a must.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

Interesting cave, for someone who has stayed in a city for the whole of her life. We went in winter and what is interesting is that the cave is considered warm for winter. Be prepared for the long walk to and back and the path would be too rocky for strollers or wheelchairs
I am not sure I will tell others that this is a MUST GO place.  We spent 5 mins taking few photos of the rock, enjoyed the breeze before going back into the car.

Also known as Jusangjeolli (Jisatgae Rocks). Be warned though, it can get very crowded with local tourists and foreign tour groups. When we were there, we found it hard to get a picture without someone else appearing in the background, despite the light drizzle.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

A veey dark and long walk with informative description on different formation of rocks created after cooling of the lava. Interesting and educational, no exit @ the end of the walk so would have to take the same route back.

Even in peak season Sehwa Beach didn?t have nearly as many visitors as some of the more popular northeast Jeju beaches mainly because most of it is covered in volcanic rocks.  We actually weren?t even sure it was a beach at first.  We did see a handful of people in the water who had sidestepped all the volcanic rocks but most seemed happy taking photos standing on the rocks.  Cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores line the beach and all were good spots to admire the nice scenery of the beach.  For actually going in the water, the other popular beaches are more popular for that reason.

The Jeju City 5-day traditional market is a place to visit if you happened to be in Jeju on the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of the month. It is the biggest and oldest among the other 5-day markets. The place is big and the locals sell wares ranging from fishes, livestocks, clothings, hats, crockery, flowers, agricultural produce, local food stuffs, etc. The place is noisy and colorful, crowded and they add excitement to your visit. It is    When in Jeju, do as the local folks do  .

We visited with our 4 kids and it was a hit with them.  Pretty waterfall and you are able to get pretty close to it with the mist from the waterfall hitting you.  A couple of our kids crossed the river and played on the rocks on the other side.  Was worth the visit.
This would have to be the most overrated tourist attraction Basic waterfall with 2streams of water  onto rocks below. Cost 2000 per adultDon't bother
This is a great beach with the most beautiful water on Jeju. The waters are crystal clear and the color is picturesque. The lava rocks add to the beauty of this place.
The water fall was rather small but the good thing is we can walk on the big rocks path and take an up close pic without getting wet.

The scenery was nice. The driver told me it is the largest waterfall feature in Jeju area.  Lots of tourists when we visited.  The rocks were quite slippery and could be dangerous for young kids and elderly.  Overall a nice place to visit even if you only have 30mins to spare.  The entrance fee was cheap.

The ocean waves against the beautiful volcanic rocks are just so amazing. The island is gorgeous and so much to see and do. We enjoyed going further down the beach to go into the water as well. The pineapple & tangerines are awesome.

The 1k walk is really interesting and had good info in english. It's much cooler as soon as you walk down the steps and raincoats are useful as there are water drops and wear comfortable shoes for the rocky and wet floor. Most of it is quite dark but you can still get good photos. Definitely worth the visit

Staying in Seogwipo we were lucky enough to be able to walk to these amazing waterfalls which fall into the sea.  We descended  down some wooden steps to the beach and clambered over rocks to get close to the falls.  There was a great atmosphere there with many tourists all happy to help take photos of each other with the falls behind.  Well worth a visit.

Spent a day swimming in fresh water. Fresh sweet river water mixing with warm salty seaNo umbrella for renting. Black rocks and sandYou can rent canoas. Next to big nice black sand beach only for serfers.
Prepare umbrella or raincoat as water drips in the cave. It's amazing to see the rock formation and lava tubes. It's dark and the path is rocky and slippery so becareful.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill
It's so beautiful here and there are different type of boat for you to enjoy while seeing at the historical rocks clear water.

It's a nice waterfall and it falls right in the sea. There a little walk down the coast to reach the best spotit's super crowed and that makes it a unsustainable to us. There was a tent with some ladies that served you raw fish on the rocks. Nice one
I'm very amazed by the 23m waterfall and it is just next to the ocean!! It's a bit difficult to walk on the rocks though but it's definitely worth the visit!
I more amazed by the crystal clear water than the rock formation. Suggest to give it a pass and head on to other attractions.

I am 6 years old. And I like to swim. It was very cold and cool. The water was kind of yucky. Plastic and rubbish. It looked like it was good for sand castles but daddy forgot to bring the bucket and spade for sand castles. Some waves were big and at first I was scared but then I learned to jump the waves. The surfers were clumsy because whenever there's big waves the surfers fall off. There were a lot of surfers. Mummy's Favourite bit was eating the shells on the rocks with the old aunties. The shells looked like snails and they moved and I thought they are disgusting! My Brother and me really really like Swimming. The end. That's all.

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction. We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water. Walking through the cave was thrilling and filled with excitement. Round trip to and fro the cave took us about 1hr30mins. Would highly recomend to anyone visiting Jeju Island. Proper shoes are also recommended as it can be very slippery and slip and fall may happen. Kids and Older people may find this attraction tough and difficult to walk through.

Cool and refreshing. The rocks just at the foot of the waterfall are difficult to walk down. Not recommended for old people.I could not find the inscription which this waterfall is famous (go check out the history/story behind this)!
About 5mins down the long flight of stairs and you get upclose with the waterfall. Helpful to come with proper shoes as you can walk closer the the waterfall on the rocks to get a good photo.

A popular hotspot and parking can be a problem. The waterfall is nice but not very spectacular. Can stand on the rocks bottom to catch a better glimpse of the waterfall but mind the slippery rocks. Wear a sport shoes with good traction or simply walked bare footed on the rocks.

A few dozen steps down to the open rocks at the base of the waterfall.  And then you are rewarded with a beautiful scene and welcoming and cooling mist.  If you have good balance you can walk on the rocks for some beautiful pic of the falls and the waves crashing on the rocks.  Gorgeous!

2000krw to get in.    Walk down stairs to get to a very rocky area with the waterfall coming down right next to the sea.  There was not a huge amount of water flowing down.     Some souvenir/food shops around.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

You need to purchase a ticket at 2000won each and then take 130 steps down a flight of stairs to get to the waterfall. Comfortable shoes are recommended if you want to get closer to the waterfall. It is advisable to use your feet to check for the stability of the rocks before stepping on them as there were some loose and moving ones amongst the pile of rocks. The rocks nearer to the waterfall are wet so be careful if you want to get even closer to the fall. The waves crashing on the shore are also rather strong, so be more cautious if you?re moving nearer towards the shore.
Would recommend to all visitors of Jeju. Nice atmosphere, clean beach, blue water, and great scenery. A little rocky in the water but overall it was peaceful!

With a 2,000?? fee, this waterfall is well worth a visit! It's a short walk down from the parking lot - not hard to get to at all. You should, however, wear comfortable and supportive shoes because you need to balance on rocks in order to get close to the falls.

When we arrived we were a little surprised at the ticket price to enter. There was quite a lot of steps to get down, as we walked down you can see the waterfall. when we got down to the rocks by the waterfall there was tons of people it was so crowded. but the waterfall was very beautiful and was very nice how it was all open without any barriers keeping you from the waterfall.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

What I like about this waterfall is that you can either admire it from a distance or if you prefer, you can literally walk along the rocks and take a closeup shot right next to the falls. What a thrill.

We visited on a particularly windy day which made it unfit for swimming. However, the landscape itself was great to look at, especially the black volcanic rock contrasting with the white sand and turquoise waters. I'm sure this beach would be stunning in better weather.

We visited a total of 3 waterfalls (including Jeongbang Waterfall) for our recent trip to Jeju Island.  This was my favourite among the 3 waterfalls visited, as it was rather unique, flowing directly into the sea.  However, when we were there on a weekday afternoon, it was nice and quiet for only a few minutes, then a huge group of teenagers / students arrived and filled up the whole place.  It was too crowded and we had difficulty finding space to walk on the rocks and to take a good picture was nearly impossible.We would have stayed longer if it didn't get so crowded.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

Visited this place which is really a lava tube rather than a cave.  It is about 1 kilometer from end-to-end.  Inside the tube you can see different rock formations created by the lava flow, among them the turtle-shaped rock at 600-meter mark.  It is cool inside the tube and water is dripping everywhere.  It is recommended that you wear appropriate footwear while taking this tour as it could really be slippery and some areas are not so well-lit.  Maybe this is intentional to give the place a more realistic feel.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

This was the only waterfall we visited in Jeju and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Unlike the others (according to what I read online), you can walk right up to the waterfall itself, although you'll need to brave the rocks to do it. Loved sitting here right by the edge of the water and just letting the spray wash all over me.

This was my 3rd waterfall visit in Jeju and my favourite, probably because the waterfall goes directly to the sea. Also, we saw some haenyeo (female divers) there and they were selling fresh sashmi seafood on the rocks next to the sea. It was definitely a very unique eating experience!

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

This is, so far, the best waterfall I have ever been. You need to go down from a lot of big rocks to go near the falls. That is what makes it exciting. Wear comfortable shoes and I recommend to wear pants.

This is the 1st attraction we visited when we arrived at Jeju. Its near our hotel in Seogwipo.We saw a group of tough ladies, the Haenyeo, scuttling over the rocky beach. They were hunting for seafood hidden between the rocks.The waterfall was nearby, beautiful with strong steady stream of water gushing into the sea as it had been raining a lot recently.A lot of people around the area as it was an easy to reach attraction with a short walk down the stairs...

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The wind blows hard in this area (as the wind turbines might hint at). But the water is beautiful, the sand is white and the rock formations around are really special. It gets crowded but not as crowded as some others on the island. I have seen better beaches for sure, but here in Jeju this one is probably as good as it gets.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000\ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.

The place was hot and mosquito infested honestly due to the Aug weather. However if you have enough repellent with you, this is a good place to walk over, sit on the rocks, chill by the waterfall, feel the cold clear air and pose till you are tired.
The natural waterfall in the raw form and walking in the rocks is fun. The surprise was a fresh Jeju orange juice nearby, the seller was honest and nice.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

The beach was fine and no rocks, but a lot of seaweed. The water was clear and very shallow, so it's good for kids, but I was a bit bored since I like to play in the waves.I think they should clean the beach more often since I found too much trash around

Out of the 3, this is the most dangerous but also the most fascinating, mostly due to the old lady divers at the bottom selling freshly caught seafood. So fresh you can taste the salt. Waterfall is beautiful on it's own, the trek down is pretty steep but easy. Only concern is once you're nearby the waterfall you have to hop onto the rocks to get closer, which can be pretty dangerous for the elderly, kids or those who are not sure footed.A must see if you're into waterfalls.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

Oh gosh!  This is definitely one of the must-sees of Jeju Island!A short 15min (mostly flat) loop, and you will be rewarded with babbling brooks and crystal clear waters overlooked by towering cliffs.  Best of all, this is off the beaten path, and there were virtually no tourists around.  Oh...the tranquility.Some parts of the walk involve jumping from rock to rock in the streams.  Not a problem generally (my kids found it fun), but if you have mobility issues, you may want to bear this in mind.We would like to thank Victor of Jejueco Suites for helping us discover this hidden jem.

Never been to a beach where the sand had a huge net over it. But then I'd never been to a beach in Korea. We werent too upset because we kept our shoes clean for the museum we visited next. The only sunbathers were foreigners, everyone else waded in the water almost fully clothed or stood on the lava rock taking selfies. It's pretty and there are places to grab lunch or an ice cream.
need to be careful walking on the rocks, the water is very clean n clear, a lot of tourist here so have to be 'skillful' to take photos and move about on the rocks.

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

It's a waterfall that goes directly to the see. Not many like that so you should visited it at least once. The road after the stairs was rocky, so you have to be careful. There's a woman diver, so there' s some people that ate her catch near the waterfall.

it was just a super long cave that is really cold, perfect when you are visiting during the hot summers. Wear comfortable shoes because you will be avoiding water puddles, trekking on uneven rocky floors. Its just a super long walk in and out.
It is an average beach, nothing special. The water wasn?t warm.  There is a lot of sand, not just rocks as in some areas of Jeju.

Impressive sight withthewaterfall ending directly into the sea, walking down to the foot of the waterfall can be challenging with the rocks formation and without proper path, so don't wear heels!!!If you want to get near to the waterfall, be prepare for a shower of blessings

If you are traveling to the south side of Jeju island, you must come see this cliff surrounded by emerald waters and roaring waves.Truly awesome. You will be even more surprised when you get home by the amazing photos you took. Don't focus on people shots, get the amazing rocks and waves instead! Don't worry about the apparent crowds around you, you will definitely be able to take some fantastic pictures without them.

I?ve never been this near to the base of a waterfall before.  No railings, just the raw power of a thunderous fall.  And a rainbow!  The kids loved jumping from rock to rock.  This may be a little precarious on a wet day, but we were lucky with the weather during our visit.You do get some splashes.  So if you have very expensive camera equipment, you may want to protect it?  The walk up was a little tiring, but not overly so.Absolutely love it.  A must see!

I was lucky to be here on a fairly sunny day, and saw the beach show its beautiful turquoise colour. Thanks to the shallow white sand bed which stretches very far out, under the sun, the water glistened and sparkled. The lava rock added the character of the whole scenery. It?s very photogenic and well worth a visit. Do not mind the industrial surrounding, it won?t interrupt your pictures.

I expected a longer walk for this, given that this is what Mother Nature had blessed us with, but this cave is only opened for the first 1km to the public. Still, it was an amazing sight (with the turtle-like rock formation and the various lava formations). Wear comfortably with a cap or hoodie as the cave will be chilly and the water will drip from above! Also, bring flash lights as it can get quite dark!

Falls is very beautiful.  You walk down 100 steps or so, then across big rocks to the bottom of the falls.  Wear tennis shoes or flip-flops for rock hopping!  Lots of water spray, and nice wading in the cool water as it runs across a few rocks to the ocean.

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. A good thing we visited this Dragon Head Coast while doing the west coast route.The canola flowers site is a paid visitor spot (should be around KRW2K each adult). There is a Viking ride @ the base for the young ones to try. You can see many interesting lines and grains on the side of the rocks' walls. You get to see women divers selling fresh seafoods along the coast, youngest are already in their 50s and oldest are in their 70s (still diving)...they are simply amazing.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .

Black rock, golden sand, turquoise waters, green fields. Such a colourful island, easy to cycle around. The contrast of the simple life of haenyo and farmers with those vacationing was also felt strongly.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.
Beautiful blue/green water  with white sand beach. We didn't get in the water since it was chilly, but it looks very shallow with some rocks.   Can park and walk along the beach shore.

Although the waterfall itself was very beautiful to see we only stayed for a few minutes if that there was a lot of people there taking pictures and sitting on the rocks once there, there wasn't much stuff to do. But on the bright side it was really nice to see.

A waterfall which falls right into the ocean, one of its kind and unique. Suitable even in rainy weather but take caution on the slippery rocks leading down to base of waterfall. The best of the 3 famous waterfalls around Seogwipo

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.
