We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

We must have been very lucky, because there was almost no one else around the day we went and we were there in the middle of the afternoon. We were there in October, so maybe it's less busy (but we were there during Chinese Golden Week, so I dunno?). It's definitely worth checking out if you enjoy unique and interesting rock formations.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

We decided to visit this   Green tea Museum   because it was a rainy day but could not find much of a direction - there was a mention of the tea stone experience but no further information.  We ended up going to the busy restaurant through a small 'museum' and ended up 'enjoying the $9 green tea'.  On the fields across from the museum there are kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures for photo opportunities.
This place is amazing, the rock formations are beautiful but be prepare for some hordes of tourists when buses arrive. We were lucky and saw some Haenyeos diving out of the beach in the complex.

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!
This Dragon head shaped rock formation is near the airport, and hence favourite of many bus group tours. Can take pictures with the frequent airplanes flying pass by at low altitudes.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

The cave and formation is very unique. Must go and it's not expensive. Only 2000 won per adultAs for transportation, we took bus 701 and waiting for bus 990. Note that bus 990 is not very frequent and be prepared to walk 2.5km. It's quite a pleasant walk though. So take note.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!

part of the rock was eroded. it appeared more like a rabbit instead of dragon head. Suggest to go to Heopjae beach which is 5 minutes walk or next to Halim Park. It is overwhelming with crystal clear sea water fine sandy beach, and unique volcanic rock formation within your reach.  It is free and really worth going. The intercity bus will stop right in front of the seaside.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Just a rock formation that looks more like a bunny than a dragon.  Nothing much.  FOC entry but if you're driving, parking is paid when you exit the carpark.  Payment is to an attendant.  Highly touristy area and can be quite packed when the tour buses arrive.  This attraction is open 24hrs.

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

Jin, our guide is very helpful and speaks English well enough to give us information about the places we visited. The bus was comfortable. Since it was a small group, we managed to follow the schedule.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I went here on Friday 31.05.2019. The front desk staff were very helpful, the museum is really easy as there's arrows on the floor directing you where to go. There is loads of information in English, it's easy to follow and very informative. The island has some really sad history, for anyone interested in history, and the impact of splitting Korea, this is a must do. The information does not make easy reading, but you will never forget this story, and it's an important one to remember. The gardens have lots of memorials, and outside is a nice space.It's not a pop in memorial/museum, it's bigger than expected. I'd recommend 2.5 hours to do the museum and outside. Unfortunately I had to rush as I got there late in the day and wish I'd had more time, but I'm pleased I went, and got most stuff done. It's accessible by bus. The museum closes at 6, last entry 5, but I'd suggest you get there no later than 3.30pm to do it properly.For clarity, this is the 4.3 peace park on the east side of the island, as there is one on the west side with a similar name, I've no idea what that one is like.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

For everyone's information, Nanta theater in Jeju just moved to middle of nowhere, without bus lines nor taxi around. It became a spot only for group tourist.The performance was perfect. But after the performance, when we asked the theater staff for help. The two girls refused to call a taxi for us and asked us to take the bus which we later found out didn't exist. It was cold winter and I asked for permission to stay inside when I call for taxi, they insist we go out and lied to us about the bus.Luckily there's also a newly built Nanta hotel around. The hotel staff drove us to nearest town and helped us get a taxi.So, 5 star for Nanta hotel service and 0 for Nanta theatre staff.
Cool Place, great mountain rock formation. Ilchulbong Peak is an hour travel via InterCity Bus #701 from Jeju City Hall cost around 2,050won. There are eateries and souvenir shops nearby.

A nice stop on the yeha bus tour, a lot of tourists so it easily gets overcrowded as the observation platform is small. Nice walk nearby with a small park next to the ocean. Pentagonal and heptagonal rock formations from lava cooling down. Enjoyed it and do recommend if in the area!

A great museum that is easily accessible.  A bus stop is located a block from the museum.  The ticket price is 1,100KRW during time of visit and well worth it.  The front desk also showed a special screening for me of the information video.  The exhibit is brilliant - informative, visual and interactive.  There's a observatory that oversees the water and the Sehwa area and a play area for small children.

this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

The cliff is formed from lava flow. Hexagonal basalt columns like those in Ireland. It is interesting if you have not seen this kind of formation. It will be interesting if you could visit during high tide and high waves as the crashing waves may reach all the way to the top.

Spectacular geological formations and scenery.  It really is quite unique. It's easily accessible and there's a nice small park around the top.  There's a path that can take you to the portion of the shore which is nice and not many people go to.  Jeju let's nature take center stage and they do a nice job getting you access.
Nice location and pretty rock formations down to the sea but not a lot else to see. Give yourself 15-20 minutes tops to see it unless you want to go on the Kayaks.

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

Love this natural rock formations along the coastal beach walk ... definitely not your usual sandy beach ... lots of opportunities for great photosThere are ladies selling fresh seafood catches along the way ... we didn't have time to stop for that though ...

It was pouring and we needed something to do.  Jeju has a lot of museums and this was our first stop.  As a person who studies sexual health I found the museum average.  Why?First the museum does a good job at giving a lot of different perspectives. Covering things like marriage history  homosexuality  maturity sti masturbation  bdsm etc. They have displays installations artefacts video and some interactivity. The biggest problem is that all the information is written in Korean. So it was impossible to actually learn. I would have liked to read all the information that was presented. Also the price was expensive 12000 won was a lot for what you got.If the information was in English I could see me giving 4 stars.

You could actually walk out into the ocean among swirling seaweed and chase after schools of small fish (my favourite part). There are also small rock ponds for you to observe some sea creatures that were washed up by the waves. Plenty of families and couples with puppies and dogs were frolicking in the waters and having a picnic on the sand. Sand was so soft!   For more information and pictures on Jeju, visit my travel blog.https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

We joined Yeha Tour and this is one of the stops. Good information, humor house owner. Do not buy the house oil which cost 40000 won. It is similar to Guerisson 9-complex which costs less than US$20 when you buy from lotte duty free Jeju

We hired a taxi for the day but this wasn't one of the place we wanted to go. The driver, Charles Cho, unilaterally decided we should stop at Sangumburi anyway. We're glad he did. We've been to Kintamani in Bali, but this crater is smaller and within a more scenic and lonely area. The surrounding mountains and farmland are serenely beautiful. One of the attractions here is a patch of tall reeds, but at this time of the year, they have not sprouted yet.The crater itself is supposedly valuable because of the unique plants and animals there, but for us casual visitors, it's a nice, green geographical feature.There are remains of tombs there, but no information on them.

Udo is a mini-Jeju, with traditional elements such as stone walls, farms, female divers and ocean cliffs all compressed into a much more manageable area. I rented a bicycle with a basket from an old ahjussi for 4000krw (3 hours). His stall, or rather tent, was located just at the ferry terminal. There are shops across the street that rent out bicycles, scooters and motorcycles.Cycling around Udo was a breeze. It was mainly flat terrain with some gentle slopes here and there. You will ride past white sandy beaches, rocky pools, farms, stone walls, female divers, cute puppies and cafes. Remember to grab some peanut ice cream, the island?s specialty.For more information and pictures on Udo, visit my travel blog https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

this mysterious road is so famous so many tourists stop by and in awe.. as for us, We didn't understand anything...we tried to ask someone to explain the 'special' thing about this road, but still, we didn't get it..those who wanna visit, please spare around 30mins to find information on the internet about this place ... otherwise,, it'll be a waste of time...

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

The hike to the end of the cave was not short, so be prepared to walk a few kms if you plan to visit this place. The cave itself was wet and cool, which is good if outside was hot. You get to see different formations and immerse yourself deep underground at the same time. So, the time was well spent here. Afterward, you can stop by the restaurant near the entrance and have some cheap Korean food.  The admission to the cave was very reasonable as it is a government owned attraction.

The cave is very dimly lit. The floor was very uneven (we are not blaming.. it's the natural formation of the lava) and slippery. I could only look down to make sure that I am walking safely and properly. I had no time to stop and look up and admire the caves. The cave is also very dimly lit, which makes the walk more challenging. We decided to turn back after 20 mins.

One of Jeju Island attraction, the rock formations that looks more like a horse head to me. Well, legendary it was a head of a dragon. We stop by for a photo stop on our way to airport.A good nice photographing platform for visitor to take picture. There is a stairway leading down to the rocky beach, down there you can see many locals selling fresh seafood.  It is not a wheelchair friendly place. Be there before sunset otherwise you will not able to take a clear photo.

It's a dramatic coastline, just like blocks of puzzles stacking on top of each other. It's a unique sight. The entrance fee is KRW2,000 and the overall walk is easy, takes maximum 15-20 mins including photography. The sea water is clear and you can actually see the formation from below.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It takes 10 min tops to actually enjoy the rock.  Its unique and pretty but that's all folks!  You have to pay for parking (500 won every 30 min) and believe me, it doesn't even take that long to see all there is to see.  We had extra time before rental car needed to be returned so we stopped.  But I wouldn't have otherwise gone out of my way to see this rock formation.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

It is interesting because people actually live there in the old style.  The physical village wasn't much different from other villages you can stop at.  Even though some other places were created for tourist, at least the villagers acted happy and were willing to share some information.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

For us - it was a last 'must see' on Jeju Island.  Our tour books featured it as a top site, so we went.  We didn't have much time, and it worked (since it's near the airport) for a quick stop off.  I didn't hate it - it was crowded though.  Lots of tour groups, teens, etc.  There were several shops nearby that were handy for our last bit of shopping.  You don't need to spend a lot of time here, but the rock formation is neat and the myth behind it is interesting.

because it is a volcano, it is not too steep. You do need to get to certain points by certain times to be able to reach the top due to the sunset (so this changes throughout the year). You can get an information booklet at the airport.

As part of the tour, we had a short stop at dragon head rock, where you can see the head of a dragon naturally carved on a big rock. There is also a small mermaid sculptured on a rock for photo opportunity. This is more of a photo stop. Jeju as an island attraction have plenty of rock formation, volcanic rocks, and shoreline with plenty of rock. Again like all part of Jeju, the place has good breeze and quite comfortable.

We went to the memorial hall to see the exhibition on Kim Manduk after we visited a recreation of her travellers' in that is about 150m away.I have always admired Korea's efforts to recreate buildings and scenes fron the past that are both infirmative and interesting.The exhibit at the hall added to what we had learnt at the inn.What comes across from the information cards and exhibits was a woman dedicated to the service of others.Profit was never her main motive. Nor self-aggrandizement.We need more people like her today.

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.
This was a disappointing visit. There was not much in the way of information and it seemed like a gimmick if anything. Many buildings were under renovation.

This place were providing some information about teas making and how korean history about tea production and cultures. They also provide a cafe that served tea of course and some tempting Deli. If you visit the place on winter it actually perfect to spent time to get warm up and stuff your stomach. On Summer or Spring would be great for afternoon tea or take away for your picnic basket. And once more as this place is all about teas there is cosmetic and some supplies product made from tea essence. You could also find some fun activities at the creation counter at the third building near the tea plantation. Come and have look!!
This is a great place to visit on your way to somewhere. Worth about 30 mins of your schedule. See the formation and learn how they are formed.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!
This attraction is located minutes drive away from Jungmun Beach. Slow down your pace as you admire this amazing natural cliff formation.

The butterfly museum is interesting showcasing many species of insects but the information are all in Korean. Walk out of the building there is an outdoor park with a maze. The mirror maze is not to be missed the kids had so much fun finding their way out!

That means during a sunny day you can see as far as the Halla mountain. And also the various geological formations around the sea. A nice hike which will take about 1.5 hours but you can just take a walk. By the way the area is often used as backdrop for TV shows including the Dae Jang-geum 鸚㏝빓餓?popular drama show.
Take your time to read the information plaques along the way to fully appreciate the geological aspects of this unique place.

Spent a few hours at the museum along with many many others! Small building with some good information but crowds crammed the shop which leads into the cafe. This caused overcrowding and did not make for the most enjoyable afternoon. Outdoors area is worth wandering through and the gardens and fields are worth looking at. The Innisfree Jeju House across the way is probably more interesting.
rock formation. nothing particularly special about it. visit if along the way or have time to do so.

Pro: nice place as you will get free explanation of jeju. We were able to get first hand information about the traits of jeju woman and good history background of jeju.Cons: you will be exposed to v. long sales talk of made in jeju products. quite expensive and I was sitting through the talk half way i decided to leave.

Not a bad way to fill in a couple of hours. The cave floor is very uneven as you are walking on solidified lava be sure to wear comfy shoes. Also can be quite damp so if you don't want to have water dripping on you maybe take an umbrella. Lots of information provided throughout the walk in several languages to keep you engaged also

Nice park and a great way to know about the history of the island.amazing grand sight of the rock formations.Rocks & stones everywhere. Beautiful landscape. There are nice traditional houses in the park.
Nice magma formations but not realy a dragon head.Many tourists are around the rock so easy to find.If you're anyway around there worth a look but you don't have to come extra for this rock...

Manjang Cave is made of lava formation or lava tube as it is called. We walked about 1-2 km stretch of it only as not the whole tube was opened for tourist visitation.It is cold and dark. it is one of the longest lava tube in the world but it just is not my cup of tea. No  remorse on going into it but just was not awe blown away with it either. Go if you are a nature lover. skip if you are looking for awesome scenery to capture picture moments

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

KRW 2k for adults. Worth the 2km to and fro walk and all information panels in the cave have english. Not suitable for very old and very young. A lot of un even steps and walkways and high steps sometimes. Dark. Wear good tracking shoes.

It is soooo dark in the cave. You couldn?t see the formations or well anything except the puddles of water. I have been to other caves before and they had dramatic lighting that shows off the details. We walked about half way and turned back as it was the same thing the whole way through. It does get a little chilly down there. It was our least favorite thing we did on Jeju.

If you are a fan of green tea you should pass by here if it's on the way of where you are going. The museum itself doesn't offer too much information. There is a green tea field and they serve green tea green tea drinks green tea ice cream and all things related to green tea (ok maybe not all but you know what I mean). My time here was not too bad just too many tourists and it may be hard for you to find a seat. There is an innisfree shop right next to the museum and there are some limited products you can find there.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.
I love its ancient. But it's difficult to find rightway and information about that folk village. It doesnt have exactly guide to explore this place

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

Admission fee 12.000won per Person. Free parking. Coffee and souvenir shop inside.I would give 4 points but this museum has no information in english at all. Although they advertise the museum with ?쐀iggest sex museum in the world?? so in my opinion the translation of information in english is a must. The admission fee is way too overpriced for not understandig everything. They do translate in chinese.By the way the museum is more funny instead of ?쐓exy?? Would just go here with friends not with a date because some statues/pics etc kill every possible erotic moment. XD

A beautiful scenic walk along the coast and the path was well taken care of. We walked to the right first and walked most of the path up until it started to inclined towards the end and then turned around and walked down the left path all the way to the parking lot. Definitely recommend walking both paths since you see different rock formations and the walk is not too difficult or long.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

We went as a couple  not expecting much  but this place was really fun! Lots of little experiments to do with electricity  plasma  light. The   tesla coil music orchestra   was impressive... or did I just got high on the ozone? Even the arcade games upstairs were great.We ended up staying for more than 2 hours and left only because they were closing down.I only wish they put more effort into the English information/displays. There are little English summaries  but the Korean version always looked way more exhaustive.There also an   organic salad bar   and a black pork restaurant at the facility  but we didn't have time to visit.

We have never seen or heard of anything like this before. Probably its the only one in the world. The 1km walk each way, was full of facts about lava formations.We had wonderful time, and just loved what we saw & learned.

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This lava tube is huge.  The part open to the public is a bit over half a mile in although the entire system is much larger.  The natural formations are fascinating and beautiful in their own way.  The place is   other worldly   and so different from life on the surface. Be aware that there are many steps (some steep) down and up.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

The place is very organised with well created pathways to see the rock formations. However, the place is really quite crowded and it is hard to take photos because of the amount of crowd there. Everyone was just walking along the path and there isn't much space to move around. That being said, it is still quite worth it to pay it a visit.

The place is small. According to the guide (a man who lives there), that is his house passed down to him by his ancestors. He speaks English and some of our Malay language (impressive). It was very compact with the history of the island, culture, food, the roles of men/ women in Jeju, architecture, etc. He was a fun man with a lively way of presenting the information. I think it was excellent. Listening to him is like reading a small introductory chapter about Jeju. There was no fee collected, I appreciate that. However, at the end of the visit, he showed us some local products which we happily bought (the tea) because the children like it.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The Cave was very different to other caves I have been to. It was like a Subway train tunnel. You can way approx 1 km of the reported 7km+ lava tube tunnel. Did have much of the usual Stalagmite and stalactite and crystal formations. The Lava tracks /grooves where interesting to me. But I was not a   Wow   experience.

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Spent about 3 hours here one afternoon and was very happy with the overall visit. A full display of buildings, traditional way of life, farm areas, gardens and other typical tourist information, shops and food areas give the whole village a unique attraction for everyone. A little pricey in the shops, but as you walk through the areas you get a real sense of tranquility with the how things were. Very enjoyable and if you are there - make sure you visit.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street ? you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

Jungmun Daepo is the spot where the iconic columnar joint rock formations can be seen. There?s not much to do here, except take a few pictures from a distance, but it?s worth seeing if you?re in the area anyway. I can?t say much about it because there?s not much to say. except that you should allot about 15 minutes in total (including the time to get in an out).Further down the coast is Jungmun beach. I went here in March, so there wasn?t much to do when it?s 10 degrees Celsius. I imagine on a hot day it would be fun to swim here. The beach is pretty ? sand is slightly coarse but clean and lovely since it?s golden in color. The slope from the parking area/restaurants to the beach is pretty steep. I don?t know if it?s safe for people with mobility issues.One downer: I didn?t like the seafood restaurants playing loud, outdated music when we got there ? I think it would be a pain to eat here if you have to listen to that. Someone has to tell the tourism board about this.Where: Seogwipo west coast

It's good place for experience the local community which they will arrange the local guide whom live tin the village to give you the informations and details about the village including the history and culture. There's the translator for the local people since they are hardly speak other language besides Korean. They will explain the way they hand the wooden stick at the gate. The meaning of the stone statue. They will have to room the tell us their history and story. They will have a village walk so everyone can see and experiences their village including photo shooting. They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. The Omecha is sticky so need to mix with water for drinking and contain a lot of vitamins. The local guide will try to up sales their local products after tour such as Omecha and horse bone. They make the bone into small pills and they said its good for those whom need calcium or need recovery from injury and also good for the growth of young kid. They also sell dried squids which already mix with sauce before dried it. It's a good experience as the village is very unique. The house is only one floor and low ceiling since Jeju is very windy. The wall also made with the lava stone from the hallasan mountain.Avoid to go during rainy day even they provide the umbrella during the walk but it's not convenience at all.
It's an unusual formation, I'll give it that, but really I don't see why it's a tourist attraction. It's something I planned on missing, but stumbled upon anyway.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was a hot day so felt great to get away from the  heat and descend into the cave. It felt about 10 degrees colder so be prepared with a light jacket. As with all caves, this has rocky wet floors that are very treacherous for those without proper track shoes. Very interesting signboards with geographical  information about the formation of lava caves too.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

Interesting rock formation open for imagination. Otherwise the area has not much other sights. There is no ticket required, so you can see the popularity is not great. Anyway, nice forested area is good for a quiet walk.
Interesting place, walk in a lave tube & learn about formation along the way. it was very interesting experience. P/S Please wear shoe.

In this cave, you're allowed to walk about one kilometer in the lava tube where you'll find a lot of variation in the formation and environment. It's a lot of space in one of the tubes (the other one was closed off during our visit). In the tube, there has been several different lava levels and different factors, creating unique patterns on the walls, floor and ceiling. It's recommended to bring something warm down the cave, since it's a bit chilly.Along the way, there is several signs about detail information (both in Korean and English) about the different shapes and things in the cave.

I'm not usually impressed by holes in the ground, but this lava tube was a blast.  It's always cold, damp and a enjoyably creepy no matter how sunny it is above ground, and you will love it!  Plenty of great rock formations to see and a sense of what goblins might call home, but the main attraction walking in this huge tunnel that once screamed with magma.

If we had known that the rock formation was disappointing, we wouldn't have taken the effort to get lost on our way there! We went there at night, and all we saw were a few spotlights shining upon a small piece of rock jutting out of the land mass - there are other wayyyy better ways to spend your limited time in Jeju. Seriously! Don't bother please.

I really liked this cave, or lava tube as it's also called. I was hoping for more stalagmites and such but the lack thereof doesn't bring down the points due to it's massive size and length. There are also signs along the way with information about the   tube   in different languages. I really recommend giing to this place when you go to Jeju!!

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit.
