review: My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

It was supposed to be sunny day according to forecast but the rain started the night before and it just won't stop. I was about to give up the plan but my friend insist on going and we ended up on top of the mountain :) it was rather a different experience hiking under the rain. The only disappointment was the fog on top which basically cover the beautiful view of the lake.

It was a very tiring hike up the mountain but the view was spectacular. I was not fully geared and use my running shoe which was a big mistake. Hiking boots are a must!  Kept twisting my ankles whenever I step on some huge rocks. I should have walked at a slower pace to enjoy the view but my focus at that time was to reach the top. Next time I will take it slowly and take more pictures. I hope they will have a cable car for people not fit anymore to hike. Experience was well worth it!

It took us 30 mins to climb up. Was very windy at the start but the heat from the climb took over. Lol. Managed to catch the sunrise. Everyone cheered when the sun peeked out. Bring some breakfast and hot drinks in a flask to enjoy. Yes there were PRCs talking very loudly disrupting the peace. I tot they banned PRCs to Jeju? Oh wells.Climbing down was a chilly experience but u get a really nice view of jeju going down. Lots of photo ops.

It is my first time seeing a waterfall by the sea... The view was spectacular! Experience the breeze of the sea combined with the breeze from the waterfall. The majestic waterfall is already quite impressive itself...

If you want to buy or get your fix of osulloc green tea goodies you don?셳 really need to come all the way to Jeju. Shopping in seoul for osulloc goods is a better option. Aside from the view and the shop nothing else to do here. I?셫 not sure why they even call this a museum. I wish they have a proper green tea tour as part of their program. I don?셳 mind spending for a quality experience.

If you are interested in green tea this is a good place for you to know about green tea in South Korea.  There are demonstrations on how to make a cup of good green tea if you like it you can buy the tea leaves back home and make it yourself.  There is also a small cafe where you can enjoy their green tea cake and ice-cream sitting in the cafe you will have a view of the tea field.  Quite an enjoyable experience.
Hope we could go back here in different seasons because of the view and experienced that we had. Train ride was awesome. Alot at least 4 hrs.for the instagram photos ;-)

Fields of green tea leaves greeted us at our next destination - O'Sulloc Tea Museum (?ㅼ꽕濡앺떚裕ㅼ???. It was a sight to behold and similar to the tea plantations that you can find at Cameron Highlands (Malaysia) sans the slopes - rows upon rows of green leafy segregated sections. After a couple of touristy photos we headed into the museum.Apparently the 'o' in O'Sulloc has a dual meaning: to appreciate and enjoy and also stands for the the origin of Sulloc (tea). The O'Sulloc Tea Museum (?ㅼ꽕濡앺떚裕ㅼ??? first opened in September 2001 and since than visitors can enjoy unique o?셲ulloc teas and the unique views of the nearby green tea fields and the surrounding landscape. After hanging out a bit at the museum we were brought to the souvenir corner where there all sort of teas: flower tea barley tea tangerine tea etc... There was even free sampling of of their tangerine tea which was a good marketing tactic since I bought myself a packet. The tea was really fragrant (full of tangerine!). There is also a cafe nearby but I didn't get to try it.For more about my experience and photos please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/osulloc-tea-museum-and-plantation.html

Experience狩狩狩狩狩Highlly recommendedWonderful for taking pictures and lovely views. Highly recommended for couples on honeymoons and hikers wanting a picturesque view while hiking and climbing all the way up

Enjoy the breathtaking views of the ocean and impressive rock formation while walking along the coast. Very beautiful and unique scenery that is really beyond description. The beauty of nature is really awesome. One has to be there to experience it! Thanks to our guesthouse owner for recommending this place!

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.

Been there twice already but can't get enough of this place! I love nature and I love tea so it is a perfect place for me to heal as I can enjoy gorgeous scenery and have a cup of the best tea. You can take a tea class as we did and it was the most unforgettable experience there! I have learned so many things and I had the best view while making tea.
A must visit when you come to Jeju. Great ocean views. Its quite a drive from the city around 2 hours but its worth the experience and super views . Entrance fee : 2000 KW

A 2-hour30mn climbing experience that you will not forget. I went to Hallasan during winter time and the snow makes the mountain even more beautiful !! I was impressioned that there were a few people climbing (maybe because it was winter time). This means you can take your time and enjoy the amazing view

While it is not the only waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea as many think (I've seen them both in Indonesia and Philippines), it is definitely a cool waterfall to see and they are relatively rare. I would definitely recommend seeing this waterfall first if you're planning to check out all of the waterfalls on Jeju. It is very accessible and a great viewing experience.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

When you come to Jeju, you have to go to the lovely island of Udo. It is very touristy, but it still has much to offer and so many lovely views. The Udo icecream experience from the bluffs to the kind people, interesting black sand beaches, breath taking views, suje burger (in ho ho ho restaurant, even the ferry ride is an experience... grab some beers and enjoy the ride. We ferried over our rental (??26,000) for two pax to a grand total of ??37,000; it's ??5,500 a piece for a single passenger on the ferry roundtrip. They have little buggies for rent there as well, they are the real danger for anyone driving on Udo. But its an overall lovely little place and be prepared to go full selfie mode there because every view is amazimg.

Went there by bus using the 201 bus line, it will stop you to the 'entrance' (basically the highway) which is a long far walk into the actual entrance. There's a small bus stop where you can take another bus in (slow) but taxis will frequent the highway entrance looking for customers. The cave itself its a magnificent sight to behold..it's huge! Not sure about all the negative reviews about it poorly lit and all, because the place is actually adequately lit (to fit the ambiance of a cave, no artificial colored disco lights) and concrete steps are placed everywhere in the tunnel to prevent accidental missteps. The ground is naturally uneven, you can't expect marbled tiles here. It can get quite cold and wet at 10-13deg, so bring a light jacket and proper walking shoes. Overall it's quite an experience, you can tell your friends that you've been in the underbelly of a volcano!

Well, I think in fact if you go up the pathway at the right it's easier. But in fact you are supposed to go up on the left side and come down on the right. In any case, if you are able, it's quite an experience going up and should try it the tough way! It's beautiful throughout, up you'll have a magnificent view.

We were lucky with the weather to visit the place, and it is important because during the rain it might not be so attractive.The nature is very beautiful, you will take good pictures for sure.We took a small electric car (for 2 people), but it was comparatively expensive for only 2,5 hours. It is possible to go around the island during that time but only without staying at all tourist points. Moreover, you cannot really enjoy the trip because of being in hurry.All Korean suggested to try peanut and mandarin ice-cream, that we did. Again the price was high, and mandarin one was so sweet that make us to put it in trash right away.People in the island are friendly, and even offer to pick us up to some places by car and shown the shortest way.Taking a boat to see caves was the best experience during the whole travel. For only 10 000 won you will have a lot of fun as the boat goes so fast, and definetly amazing view on the island.

We were lucky because when we went, there weren't a lot of tourist going up. Otherwise, it will be even more tiring as everyone will have to accommodate each other's pace. A lot of stairs to deal with but when you're at the top, it is worth the effort. We took about 20 mins (I think), stopping occasionally to take pictures of the scenic view down below. If you're tired, don't worry as there are enough benches on the way up to rest to regain your energy, if it comes to that. It is manageable overall.On our way down, we went to the black sand beach. Spent about 40 mins there, soaking in the view from another angle. If you want the full experience, you can take the boat out with the lady divers (Hanyeo) and see them in action. Alternatively, very fresh seafood is available for your palate should you want to try. From the sea, to the chopping board and straight to your plate (raw) and that's how they eat it. We didn't do that. Can't find the courage to do so. Lol. If the heat really got to you, after the climb down, go to one of the coffee places (Angel-in-us or Starbucks) to cool down before you go elsewhere. Be prepared to sweat buckets!!!

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

We visited the Jungmun Golf Club for doing the Moon Light Walking Tour. We went there to warm up for the Jeju Olle Walking Festival. The view was awesome and it was a nice experience to walk there during sunset. At the end, they prepare a concert for all the participants there.

We visited here as part of of our cruise ship day tour of the island. This is a very pretty place with amazing photo opportunities throughout. We purchased one of our favorite souvenirs from a kiosk selling genuine Jeju produced hats. We enjoyed the gardens and the walk over the bridge with the amazing views of the gorge and waterfalls. Be aware that the VERY long walk down to the   close-up   of the waterfalls is rather taxing and may not be worth the effort. Overall, a great experience!

We took bus 182 early morning reached there around 7.30am and started to hike about 8am. It's good to bring hiking stick as there are lots of steps up, with a hiking stick it's easier to move up the rocky paths. It was very cold at the mountain so it's good to wear in layers and can remove the jackets if it gets too warm during the hike. We managed to reach Saraoreum shelter before 12pm where we ate and took a break before moving on to the summit. After 12pm no one is allowed to move on up to the summit from the shelter as it gets dark very early during winter time. We reached the summit just before 1.30pm. The ranger already chasing people to get down. It was very cold and windy at the top and it started to drizzle. So it's important to bring a raincoat too. I could'nt get a good view as it was very foggy and windy. We did'nt get some rest and started to descend. It took a long while to descend too as the path is very rocky and slippery. Lucky i have my hiking stick with me. Half way down it started to get dark we needed to use our handphones as touch light to guide us down the path. Very happy we are all able to reach the summit. It's a nice experience.

We read some of the other reviews and went to HWARO HYANG: 27, Gwandeok-ro 15-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do. We recieved a very warm welcome and great service.  The food was so awesome.  It was fun watching it being cooked in front of us - a Korean thing.  Cool atmosphere. Thank you for a great experience and lovely night out.

We love the story around the Innisfree Jeju House. It's organic and farm to table supply chain and mission is admirable. We had the the diver's special bento and it was delicious. My wife had the blue colored tea ade and I had fresh carrot juice and all of it was great. The have beautiful cakes in the shape of Halla mountain and tiramisu with delicate flower designs. The prices are in the higher end but well worth the refined quality and experience for those who like this sort of thing. My wife loved the purity of the food and calm views of the tea plantation.They also have products for sale as well as a tea extract exhibit. They have fun hands on tea soap making as well you can purchase and do there. Or they have other ones you can purchase and take home to do. Great place to calm down, re-energize, and enjoy.

we hired a taxi driver for day-trip, it's just located nearby Eco Land Theme Park & Mini Land Theme Park.we visited on late april, so not much to see. not even green farmbut still a great view to have fun with it. good experience to have a nice walk.

We hiked up on a cloudy day. I really recommend choosing the day for hiking according to the weather forecast. The hike itself and the views and people on the path made it an unforgettable experience, but after like 2,5 hours of hiking on a really quick pace we made it to the top and couldn't see anything. The crater was filled with mist and it was so windy that staying up there would have been quite uncomfortable. It doesn't necessarily take 4,5hours to get up and 4,5 hours to get down, if you don't stop every two hundred meters. But make sure to get to the last milestone (the place to take a break and buy ramen) in time to be able to start the climb to the top.I can only imagine what the trip and the scenery would be like on a clear sunny day.

We found the reviews here very useful for preparing ourselves for the ascent so I'm contributing my own, hoping that others will find it equally helpful!   I'd say that it's a simple ascent for those already used to hill walks and there's no way one can lose the path, as it's between ropes or handrails all the way.  The path surface is mainly made of railway sleeper type large wooden beams and rocks which provide good terrain when dry.  However, for our descent it was raining and slippery and we were constantly bracing ourselves for a slip caused by the crowds - beware those with spikey walking poles! - descending more quickly than we were!  Our ascent to the peak took a leisurely 3 1/4 hours so we were delighted, although we weren't rewarded with any views but the sense of achievement and relief was great!  Our descent took 3 3/4 hours and sometimes my pace felt a little faster than comfortable, as had to concentrate so hard on each footstep placing. It looked as if some sections of the path near the summit have been replaced fairly recently, as we found it to be in good condition and not like the experience of other reviewers - and that was a relief!  I'm very glad that I wore my walking boots to protect my ankles, as the rocks are uneven and a few are slightly unstable.  So, short, if you're fit and used to hill-walking, you have nothing to fear but if you're not usually very active, then give yourself a plan B e.g. opting for the side-path to Sara Oreum if you realise, by the junction with the path off to that (round trip 40mins) that you're struggling.  That would mean that you'd still have the great satisfaction of a spectacular view from Korea's highest mountain but without the stress of having had to climb - and descend! - the 1200 metres from the bus stop to the peak!  Make sure you have enough layers of clothes and a good hat and gloves for the summit and descent, as, at this time of year, you'll definitely need them.  Oh, and if you're looking at the frequent posts with figures on alongside the path and which start with a '1' at the bottom which then progress to '2' etc, the peak is '36'.  Hoping you find this as helpful as we found other reviews!

Watching the sunrise at Seongsan Ilchulbong was definitely the highlight of my stay at Jeju. We had reserved a hotel right next to the attraction (Hotel Aroha), which was a very wise decision as all we had to do at 5 am in the morning was to get up, get ready and get going. There were hardly any people when we had started our ascent roughly 45 mins to an hour before sunrise. The hike itself is ~30 mins or less, but it can be a bit tiring because of the steep steps. We stopped a few times to catch our breaths and also interact with the locals. We had close to 10 mins before the sunrise by the time we were at the peak. The view from the sunrise is gorgeous, and even amidst so many people around you, it is still not chaotic but calm and serene. We stayed at the top for over 2 hours, taking pictures, resting, and even listening to some folk music being played by local artists. Great experience overall!The descent isn't tiring, so we took our time taking pictures and taking in the gorgeous views. At the base, we had freshly squeezed orange juice from Jeju oranges, which are again a must try!

Watching sunrise from the sea is amazing experience. You don't have to climb up too high, still can see the downtown below. And the way down is such a relax with beautiful view. Just 5 minutes walk from the bus stop and very near from Seopjikoji

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html
Very unique waterfall by the sea. walk up close and feel the water spray across your face, while the sea waves lap your feet below. great view and refreshing experience.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Udo is a beautiful island by itself but due to the time constrain we had, we didn't had time to digest the beaches and scenic views. We had always wanted to rent an ATV there and even applied for international driving license as advised by many reviewers, however, we were greatly disappointed as the rental places only rent ATV to holders of Korean driving license. IDL are not accepted so don't waste money to apply for one. We rented electric bike in the end but had a dispute with the rental store nearest to the udo habour. One of our electric bike tyre went burst as the tyres were already old and the store owner wanted us to pay. We had an disagreement as the tyres when rented to us were already worn out. I must attribute to miscommunication as the people at udo are not conversant in English nor mandarin. We beared half the cost only after calling udo police to mediate the situation. But not much help from the police who told us to   go home  . Quite a memorable experience for us though.

Took eight to nine hours to complete the hike via the gentler route. View at the top is really amazing you'll get to see a beautiful crater lake which sadly we're not allowed to go further down to. Terrain is mad crazy so make sure you're in good footwear made for hiking. Bring plenty of foot, water and a deep heat in case your aches/injuries act up (which most likely will). Be prepared as this hike will definitely take a toll on your legs which will hurt for days after the hike. Update boards can be seen along the way, the terrain is labelled and broken down into easy, normal and difficult segment. BUT, DO NOT BE FOOLED! The normal terrain is just as tough as the difficult terrain. Big boulder of rocks which are freakinggggg steeeeep! Trekking poles will definitely come in useful! If you intend to hike here, be prepared for an arduous journey, smelly puke-inducing restrooms at the two pitstops all in return for a spectacular view at the peak. A really good once in a lifetime experience, no regrets but I will defo not do it again. hahaha

To be blunt, I couldn't see the dragon's head in the Dragon Head Rock, and I'm not alone. Apparently a portion of the formation fell off during a heavy storm long ago, so perhaps it was once more impressive. Currently, it has become iconic for a rather tired trend in Korean tourism. Pointing at the sky and finding clouds that look like other things is childlike. Officially naming rocks and then designating them as   important cultural artifacts   in order to manufacturer tourism is crass. In much the same way that the Korean government has become intimately involved in generating the so-called   Korean Wave   of K-pop and Korean television dramas, there is a constant rush to capitalize on landmarks, events, and experiences that will help distinguish Korea in general and Jeju specifically in the competitive marketplace of global cultural value. This push to invent cultural significance is monopolized by a predominately male class of older Korean bureaucrats who have capitalized on Confucian values in order to override younger, better ideas, fueling their own, often tedious marketing concepts despite the existence of far better and substantive materials from which to draw inspiration. Take for instance Jeju's rich history of folklore and deities. Sure, you can dawdle about with stories of a dragon stealing jade or herbs of immortality from Halla Mountain and being shot by a celestial arrow as punishment, turning it to stone; but the fact is there are literally hundreds of far better stories that have some basis in local lore rather than the distinctly artificial details surrounding the Dragon's Head Rock. If you're interested, look for books on the subject, some of which were written by expatriates in an attempt to save this rich heritage from being slowly whitewashed away by modern fabrications. A book called   Spirits: Jeju Island's Shamanic Shrines   by Joey Rositano comes immediately to mind. Or you can go to any number of local beaches and walk along paths where every 20 yards or so you can read a plaque that tells you what a large stone vaguely resembles if you squint hard and suspend your disbelief.    That said, there's nothing wrong with taking a nice stroll along the seaside in this part of town if you only have a short amount of time to spend and you need to get to the airport soon. There are some passable restaurants along the way, a couple of good caf챕s, and some great views of the ocean. However, make no mistake - this is an authorized conduit for tourists and as such you will be subject to a conveyor belt of people on the same walk, as well as an abundance of stores whose sole purpose is to extract money from you by selling tawdry bits of plastic.

This was the most fascinating and beautiful experience during my two week stay in South Korea. The long, winding path to get to the coastline to see the Women Divers Show is gorgeous from beginning to end. The mist hovering over the black volcanic sand was unlike anything I have ever seen. I never wanted to leave. The hike up to Sunrise Peak was sweaty but worth it. The long, windy path to get the the top of the peak is fairly easy to walk and offers many wonderful views along the way. The fog was too dense to see anything from the very top, but I'm still glad I did it. This was such an amazing part of my trip; one of my most fond travel memories ever.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This was one tiring experience, since it was freezing cold back in December.I am not sure if hiking in boots is a good idea, but hey who said that you can't hike in slippery boots? This was honestly worth a thousand words.Watching the sun set into the the buildings was such a beautiful experience. When i stood right on top with the cold breeze slapping my face, admiring the view and the nature, i felt like time has stopped and that feeling was quite amazing. That feeling was everything. I fell in love with that place.

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This place is just WOW. The views, the nature, the sea, everything. Even when it is a bit rainy or foggy, it is still a great experience. They do not let you in with any sort of snacks or food other than water, just so you know. You must try the raw seafood that the   mermaids   catch every morning. It is located at the bottom near the entrance. That is, if you like raw seafood. There is plenty of parking and there is even a Starbucks near by and other restaurants.

This place is just a little hike for most. It does have about 300 steps up, but they are set up for a nice pace. Great views up and down, but not much to the crater itself. During morning this place can be very crowded. Visiting later in the day allows you to experience everything more quickly with less crowds. Lots of places to eat in the nearby area. Recommend you dedicate 40-60min for your visit.

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe.
