At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This is one of my favorite places in Jeju.? Walking up the steps to the temple you experience one enlightenment after the next.? The temple and the grounds are in immaculate condition, and clearly there is a lot of love and respect which goes into every section.? This is a wonderful hour or two to spend as you are wandering around the island - take your time, don't rush it, enjoy both the temple and its attractions, and the stunning views toward the ocean and the rest of the island.? BTW, this is not an easy stroll up the hill, but not that taxing either - if you have elders, perhaps you settle for mid-way.? if you're young - do the entire journey, you'll never know when you'll be back.

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

There were bears of every color and design imaginable: there was an Elvis bear, Marilyn bear, Mona Lisa bear, Chinese bears, countryside bears and even Goong (the Korean drama) bears! It really was a bear wonderland. The only problem was that the commentary was all in Korean, it would have been better if there was English translation as well. The other problem was that most of the exhibits were housed in glass cases which made taking photos challenging as the reflections were very prominent. Besides viewing the bears, there is an in-store souvenir shop that has all sorts of bear items (e.g. keychains, stuffed bears, bags etc...). But if you love bears, than it should be worth a visit.For more on my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/an-impromptu-visit-to-teddy-bear-museum.html

There was no sun in a June afternoon, the temperature was pleasant and the air was clear. I climbed up to the top to view the crater which is covered by lush green.  The climb was pleasant along with the gorgeous views.  The views on the way up were lovely, there were many places for great photo op. I appreciated the views from the top, views to the city and views to the sea without interruptions. It was one of the most memorable experiences I recorded in Jeju.

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

The trip up and down the 1.95km tall mountain took me the entire day but experience and view was really worth it. It would have been better if I had been properly equipped as I was in normal walking shoes and a small bottle of water while everyone else had their trekking shoes and stick with them which made going up and down more quickly and safe. There are alot of routes but not all the routes will lead you to the peak. Spoke to a few people on my way up and they shared that this is most tedious route as its the longest. There is only one way up and down which makes trekking easy for solo traveller like me.It'd be good if you can bring some food and lots of water with you where you can picnic with many korean families when you reach the peak. Do prepare to start early as you will have to reach a certain checkpoint before they allow you to continue your way up the peak. It was a heartwarming experience for me when all the korean people who walked past me would encourage me to press on and they would share they food around at the peak. Korean families usually do this as a family activity where the grandmother, grandfather, parents and kids would climb leisurely. If a grandparent can do it, so can you. Thats all :)

The ticket office was still not opened, cold and windy and we could not find the signs. We just follow 2 guys, there were more people coming along but not in tourist buses. So going this early is best to avoid the hordes of tourists we saw after we had our sunrise view and breakfast. It is steps all the way but it goes up and up and up and up ... bring your gloves windproof type!The crater is in front of you and then the sea and in the horizon, the egg yolk getting cook and rising up into the sky. Cloudy and initially disappointed but we waited and finally it emerged from behind the clouds and the rays and appearance became much more dramatic!One of the best sunrise I have experienced!

The Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak has 2 main attractions. The first is obviously the climb to the peak itself. The second is the Woman Divers at the black sand beach at the bottom. We spent about 3 hours here and it was just barely enough. The climb is actually not that bad for the physically fit. The steps are steady and most are stone paved or have wooden stairs. There were quite a few elderly ladies/gents climbing too. Rest areas with benches are plentiful, so there really is no reason why you would not try for the top if you have the time. :-) Two thirds of the way up, you will see a big resting area with a marvelous view of the city below. Once you are up at the peak, you will also be able to see the city view AND into the crater. The climb back down is very safe with well made wooden staircases. Regarding the Woman Diver show at the bottom, I found the show to be a little underwhelming and a bit too touristy. However, it was still an interesting experience to see divers selling fresh seafood off the beach. If you have limited time, I would recommend that you focus on the hike/view, and just spend a couple of minutes to browse through the woman diver area. I think the Seongsan Iichulbong is a must-see in Jeju.

The place was filled with cars, buses and people at about 10.30am when we were there but we had no difficulty finding a parking lot. We were too lazy to wake up early to watch the sunrise which should be spectacular. Signs were well posted as to the route to climb up. It was a tiring climb but we were rewarded with spectacular view of the surrounding. After getting down from the peak, we headed towards the shore where Haenyo woman divers sell their catch of the day. To get there, it was another flight of stairs up and down but again it was an experience to be near the shore and watching people eating raw stuff.
The place is very scenic, enjoyed the blue ocean view and hexagonal stones makes it a different experience.

The period I went was very windy, the surrounding was very refreshing with patches of green. Very relaxing, peaceful  and is a good place for photography. A typical k-drama filming location for kfans to visit! Once you reach the highest point, you will see endless of   green    and can even spot mountains that is far away. You can actually relax and enjoy this view by sitting at this cute wooden swing. Very nice place which you probably won't want to miss it.However, to visit this place, you need an entrance fee of  6,000won, But if you booked a experience tour driver with your own group of friends, he can help you bargain it to a even cheaper price which is like 3,000won per person! So, afterall, it was pretty worth it for both the price and this exquisite experience! Recommended to rent a car there, inaccessible by public transport!
The hike was tiring as I've never hiked before. But it's worth the experience, the view and the wind!

The experience was exactly like what I read from reviews and so I'll just focus on key things.-If for youngsters,  no issues.-For people not used to visiting caves-*wear shoes that don't slip*bring a torch if darkness is a concern *wear a light jacket- there are unexpected water drops, huge temperature difference with outside -Using mobile phones, not easy to take good photos. What you see is better than what is captured by phones. Online photos look so much better than what we saw.-Flowers outside the cave are lovely. Good photo taking spots.

Take a boat is convenient from Jeju to Udo (we were driving , the boat is able to carry the car) only 30 minutes boat, then arrive at Udo. We drive along the coste road, stopped by the hill, it is a 30 mins climbing, once reach the top you can have a overview of this Island  We literally turned around the island by car. Tried sea food abalone and some shellfish. It was very good experience. We star at 11.30am boat to Udo and finished at 4pm to take boat back to Jeju main land. It can be a 3-4 hours visit.

Since their official website is unclear about opening hours in June, I called the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline and was informed that the museum was indeed open late under summer hours. So after spending 45 minutes in and 30,000+ ?? on a taxi to visit the area with my girlfriend, who absolutely loves teddy bears, we arrived at 6:10pm. With doors still open and people still inside, we were told the museum closed at 6pm. After asking politely to let us enter the gallery and   No, no, no   being the only response, I asked the non-English speaking employee for management and soon they found someone who spoke English. I calmly explained the situation and again asked for an exception, that we were only here for a day, it would be doing us a great favor and that we would finish with the other guests and not prevent them from going home late. We were again met   No, no, no   To her credit, the English speaking manager(?) did include a   sorry   with her   no's   and did genuinely want to know how I received wrong information about their hours (and yes,if I can find a way to review the Korea Travel Hotline, they too will receive a poor rating). But ultimately, we were turned away. The only positive I could take from this experience is that, from what we could see from the lobby, the gallery looked small and over-rated. So I guess we saved ourselves the 20,000?? entrance fee.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the places to be visited in Jeju island, it has three kinds of beautiful views: the sea, the mountains and the meadow.No need to climb or hike the mountains to enjoy the view, just stay at the flat ground and see the surroundings and feel the wind ... it also a pleasant experience.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the best view I have ever seen in my entire life. The place is an epitome of beauty and calmness despite being flocked by tourists. It is very worthy of your time, effort and energy. Trek it to experience and see its beauty. There are plenty of activities being offered on site such as horse back riding, see a Jeju woman diver and even a tour around the area through boat. We were very interested with the boat ride unfortunately we did not have the luxury of time. if given the chance to go back to Jeju I will surely comeback here and try the boat ride as well as other activities offered. Moreover, the site has plenty of coffee shops and cafes around the area. There are also stalls selling Korean street food. It has huge parking area so get ready to walk from the parking area to the site. This site entails a lot of walking but because of its beauty and being windy you can never feel fatigue.

Samchoon (Mr Kim Si-Nam), was our guide for a 2 day taxi tour in jeju! Samchoon was super friendly, considerate and warm hearted! Samchoon really felt more like family to us!Samchoon texted me 2 days before to confirm the time and location of pickup and asked about my itinerary and gave suggestions on the order of location we should visit first. Samchoon made sure we get the best experience we could have in jeju!Samchoon was very well prepared. In his taxi, he had prepared water, phone cable for charging, wet & dry tissues, umbrellas, raincoats and even torchlights for caves.First thing he told me was that we didn't have to worry about time and that we can take as much time at any location. He wouldn't rush or give us a time limit. So that we could enjoy every place to the fullest. Samchoon even said that he will not charge us extra even if we exceed 8 hours, he said that he would want us to enjoy and not feel rushed. Samchoo said he was a photographer in the past and actively helped to take beautiful pictures throughout the 2 day trip. He knew exactly where the spots to stand so that the pictures came out amazing!Samchoon was very accomdating to our changes in the itinerary he gave suggestions on alternatives. Samchoon knew that we like to take photos to so on the last day he brought us to see the sunset so that we could take nice pictures! True enough the sunset and view was breath taking! Samchoon is really familiar with all the places and routes and the rides between locations was really smooth and comfortable! Samchoon even has a 40 year accident free award!To Samchoon, A very big thank you for making our jeju trip so fun and enjoyable! Thanks for taking such good care of us! We will miss you and the beautiful Jeju island! Will definitely go back to look for him when in jeju!

Sabyeol Oreum definitely has lots to offer especially for tourists/foreigners. The stunning view from the top of the hill is obviously something worth to be explored, and the best part of it is that you don?t need to pay anything to experience such aesthetic view! It is a flexible place that offers different kind of experience depending on the seasons, and it does not take much of a hiker to climb it. Not only does it not take long to climb to the top, the paths are also significantly safe. Near the place, you can also see some horses without having to pay for it, and there are lots of places where you can take good pictures! If you are coming to Jeju, I believe it is a must visit place that you should consider in your itinerary!

Reading some previous reviews for this place, I was rather puzzled how this place could be rated 3 or more stars by others. It has a number of different glass creations presented in a museum-like setting. Quite a few of these items were from Italy, Venetian glass. There are a lot nicer ones in Venice. Also, they have quite limited displays and very few look special to us. We managed to see all displays in about 20 minutes! Overall, we were completely underwhelmed by this place. If you are interested taking photos, there are opportunities for some nice photos. For others, there is nothing to learn and experience anything new here. There are other nicer museums or sights to see in Jeju, so this can be safely avoided.
Quite an experience! This is one of the harder courses, takes less time and its said to offer one of the best views of Hallasan. But note that this route doesn't go to the summit.

Please stay around, check the sunrise time and go early. It?s took me 30 minutes to get up to the top. The climb is not easy, I took few breaks before reaching the top. I?m glad that I made it on time for the sunrise.It?s one of the best sunrise I?ve ever witnessed. And, the sea of clouds made me heaven! The picture doesn?t do the view justice. Trust me, you have to experience it by yourself! For your reference, I stayed at Seongsan Sunrise Hotel which is walking distance to Seongsan Ilchibong and Gwangchiji beach. It?s also short distance to Seopjikoji and Udo by cab. Public bus in Jeju is very convenient. You can take bus from Jeju Airport to Seongsan Ilchibong stop without transit.

People who visiting Jeju island is to see its nature (except those to Casino), Hallasan is a must go to me.  Together with the family, we opted for the route of Yeongsil (shorter though not to the top and unable to see the crater), where we could easily accessed by self driving from Seogwipo city.  Along the hiking, we experienced the sub tropical environment in the bottom, then a much cooler environment after 1.5km of steep uphill.  The view is great though not fantastic, we spotted few wild deers having grass in the mountain.  The first 2-3 km was quite steep but mostly on boardwalk and constructed staircases, the last 1-2 km was rather flat.We ended in the point with toilet and food supply and then back down on the same route, due to the last section was closed.  An interesting hiking day to experience different climate, weather condition, meet locals, spot the wild animal, and do physical exercise.

Our visit was in the second week of September recently. It's quite an experience for both of us who are above 55yrs of age but nevertheless, we managed to reach the top! The view is so exhilarating and beautiful! Spend time taking photos and enjoy the cool breeze! You will not regret it even though the next day our calf muscles were sore!

One of the top places to see in Jeju.  Great view of some craggy coastline.  The other reviews are pretty good and we experienced about the same - great place, but really crowded even though it was raining!  Again...people come in waves, just wait it out.  The wind was high and seas rough so it made pretty spectacular wave crashes.  On one side there was a consistent high wind and mist/spray coming at you, so watch your cameras!  There is a 1,000 W Parking fee on top of the 2,000 entrance fee.

One of the most visited Tourist attraction in Jeju, the Seongsan IIchulbong peak or the Sun rise peak was formed due to Volcanic eruption thousands of years ago. This peak has a huge cater in the middle surrounded by huge rocks making it look like a gigantic crown. In addition to this the other most sought-after attraction here is the old ladies diving deep into the water without oxygen masks to collect sea food. Twice a day a special show is conducted for the visitors.Though it was quite windy and cold when we visited, we were sweating a lot once on the top as we have to climb a lot of steps.Once on the top we were surrounded by the moving clouds, the experience which made us forget all the fatigue.We could not see the sunrise as it was quite cloudy when we visited, but as our guide informed, one can have a good view of the one during summer.At the base there are lot of eating joints which ensures everyone gets refreshed after a long trek.We thank our Jumbo taxi driver who shared the spare waterproof jerkins he had with him to wear when it started drizzling (Kin nam joon / +821046166650 / kimnj0424@naver.com)

Okay judging by the other reviewers, I must have been there on a great day. The water was crystal clear and the experience was amazing. There is a convenient store located right on the beach for all your necessities (i.e. beer etc) and convenient ice cream and restaurants. While it was a little far away from where I was staying, it was an unforgettable experience and was my favorite part of my trip to Jeju.

Not just a temple, but amazing views of the coast and water. The temples are free to enter and offer an amazing experience. A must see if in this area. Plenty of drinks, food, views and restrooms. Only con is the steps are not very friendly. We have a 3, 7 and 8 year old. 3 year old needed carried.

My wife and I were rather underprepared for this hike. And the terrain is not for someone who had never trekked before.Nevertheless, taking it to summit on the 3rd day of November was an interesting experience. From temperate zone to the frosted summit, the temperature and views changed dramatically. Thumbs up!

My friend and I joined the East Coast one day tour - it’s meant to be a small group tour but only my friend and I joined today’s tour, so it was a private tour! Weather wasn’t nice today - it rained all day and was windy, but it was still a good trip after all. Beautiful scenery from the summit of the Seongsan Sunrise Peak - where you can have a view from above of the shore of the island. Our tour guide was June - a hiking expert with excellent knowledge of Korean culture and history. A memorable experience after all!

My first time to Korea focusing on Jeju and Seoul. Generally I would think the overall experience to South Korea is kind of over rated. I expected more based on the comments from friends, reviews by travellers and most importantly seeing it in Korean Dramas.Udo island is an exception, it gave me the best experience in the entire 8-day trip, except the weather wasn't too good on my day trip to Udo. Rented a bike to travel almost the entire island which i think is the best mode to explore remote areas without using too much energy.  Hopping up and down to take photos by the beach, colorful cafes, yellow canola fields, uphill and downhill.Unforgettable squid volcano rice was one of its kind and one of the most satisfactory meal in the entire trip.

My favourite one in Seogwipo, it may be not as large as Kpop Live in Seoul  but its still good one. With fifteen-thousand-won ticket you could experience the 4D media concert of Big Bang, GD, PSY...Remember to choose the showtime for concert because your ticket is available for max. 3 hours. Besides that you could experience over 31 attractions including be the star, meet the star, recording with star, make up and dancing with star. Its cool one when you could take pictures or singing with TOP, GD or PSY. There is also a section for Korean music history that you could help you have an overview of Korean music industry. Play Kpop will catch some of your moments and then you could download your photos and videos you take there by filling the ID ticket. Worth your money & well recommended!

My 4 year old found the road very fascinating and he kept mentioning mysterious road throughout the day. It was probably just an average experience for adults but if you are travelling with the little ones, it may be worthwhile to spend some time to bring your kids to view this road.

Most of Udo island except the attractions are rural farms. We went to Udo island with a few local Koreans from jeju island. We took a 15mins ferry. I was surprised that there are no seats on the ferry, people sit on the floor instead, korean style. Interesting experience. As I went with locals, I thought they would know the way. No! They didn't and we walked 1h around the island before reaching the peak. It was beautiful. The grass was green n the sea view was nice. Though it was really windy. And thus very cold even though it was summer. Be sure to wear enough clothes.

Located next to   Loveland   this museum is small modern place with beautiful outdoor features such as a reflecting pool sculptures and a small surrounding forest. There was a little bit of everything from an exhibit about a famous national artist who lived for decades on Jeju to an interesting video and poetry collaboration of Korean rappers talking about social issues. The upstairs is currently showcasing drawings and sculptures made by Korean schoolchildren in a surprisingly cheeky cheerful exhibit. Much of the museum was in English but others were only in Korean. The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Living in a country where there is no chance the snow will fall, we are so excited to experience snow even though by that time it is nearly end of March. The view is amazing, though I cannot go for the hike as I went there with my mom. Will definitely go again and bring my hiking partner next time.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

It was very meaningful to spend 3 days to join the Jeju Olle walking festival in November, 2018. One route per day not only an physical exercise and challenge to myself but also a good opportunity to meet friends or make new friends there. No one push you to walk faster but we could take pictures, enjoyed nice views and landscapes on each route. Local food for lunchs were delicious. What a beautiful island, good for gathering and good for vacation. I love Jeju. It was my third time participating Jeju Olle Festival. Different experience every time.

It was nice experience when suddenly u find these kinds of roads... Some kind of mysterious nature behaviour that able to control your vehicles to suddenly runs on its own... Probably kind of magnetic field...Well, u can also enjoy a small view of grassfield and view restaurants around... I took a nice picture here with my travel friends, used a large stone (its carved with korean words) as background... Interesting experience... ;)

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.

It was a very windy and rainy day... we could not climb to the summit but the experience was trilling! Recommended for trekking amateurs and pros! There are many coffee shops around the routes but bring your own food, comfortable clothing and decent equipment. It's totally equipped with stairs and view points but safety is always first!

It was a rainy day when we went to this beach after visiting the Hallim park, end of october. It was however a very nice experience, the sand is white and contrast nicely with the black rocks that you can see at low tide. The view on the island makes the picture even nicer.

It was a rainy and windy day when we went there, we were told the spot does not open daily and not all the time due to the weather and tidal timeWhen we went it was low tide, but super slippery and windy due to the rain. But amazing walk. There are some people selling fresh seafood, abalone sashimi from raw/ fresh, serving Korean alcohol.  Another type of experience. We walked half way, we had our umbrella but I almost got   flew away   since it is too windy.  But totally worth the walk, since you can catch the wave so closely, and the view is awesome.

It takes quite awhile trekking down the stairs to catch the view of the waterfall which flows to the ocean. There are some   halmoni   selling fresh raw abalones, sea cucumbers, sea potatoes and blanched octopus at the side of the waterfall. It's a great experience to enjoy the seafood with a bottle of soju while enjoying the view of the waterfall and ocean while feeling the sea breeze dancing around your face^^~

It takes 1.5 hours from Jeju Intercity bus station to Seongsan IIchulbong, by bus 701. After 30 mins drive, you can see the blue sky and green sea outside of the windows. The admin fee is 200 0 KR but the great view is worth of it. You can see large grass ground and hike to the top. If there is sunshine, no doubt you can have wonderful pictures and experience even with a phone camera.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is most satisfactory to complete our climb to the top to experience the cold air, sea breeze and overlooking at the mountains and sea below you.  The feeling is so good and the view is just simply awesome!  It's a great place not to be missed!

It is an attraction for people to take photos of the special ?Dragon? like stone with the endless sea. That stone is 100% organic and experience years of erosions to form today?s ?Dragon? appearance. You can spend a couple of minutes with that ?Dragon? and spend another few minutes buying and enjoying the traditional outdoor cuisines. If you are interested in buying souvenirs like key chains or the ?Dragon? like badges, there is a shop for you to go shopping. Even though the viewpoint just for people to take a photo, there would always be many tourists standing in front of the best position for taking photos, so if there are many tour groups at the moment, you really have to spend time on waiting for just a photo. So, if you don?t mind the feel of crowded or if you get plenty of time, you are recommended as it is a special attraction in Jeju. It is nearby the international airport of Jeju so you can go there at the time you arrived or before you leave Jeju.

It absolutely great experience! The view is absolutely beautiful from the top. You have to experience it yourself. Keep your stamina full charge because you have hike to the top. The ticket is 2,000 won.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

I'm always fascinated with natural wonders so visiting this place amuses me. For a more meaningful experience, try climbing the peak (only takes less than an hour). The pathway is safe since there are stairs that you can climb to but it gets steeper as it nears the peak so make sure you wear comfortable shoes. Choose a clear day for the climb because when it is foggy (like mine), you can't see the crater once you reach the peak. It's quite windy here (since it's near the sea) so make sure your skin is covered to fight off the cold. Even if you don't attempt the peak, the view is still great and you can take a lot of beautiful photos here.Do not buy here, especially beauty products as they are more expensive. Buy in the downtown area for cheaper prices.

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

I went with my boyfriend and his dad. We had our cab driver take us there at 6am from our hostel. It took us about 12hrs round trip. I'm not a experienced hiker, so it took a loooonnnngggg time because of me. View is EXCELLENT from the peak. You can see the entire Jeju-do. Hallasan is a stony mountain, so if you can, bring a pair of hiking sticks to help you, and wear hiking shoes. The rocks are pointy, and not all of them are easy to step on.

I was on my way to another destination when I saw this place. I caught the 700 bus that runs around the outside of Jeju island for a cost of around $2, and wondered why so many people were getting on and off at this stop, so on my way back I got off. It ended up being my highlight of the day.It was a lovely sunny day with a few hundred people climbing up, and with ramps and steps all the way it was easy. I got to the top in about half an hour if not less. The views from the top were probably the best I experienced for my whole trip in Jeju, and that includes the view I saw from top of Mt Hallasan.At only 2000 won entry, it's a must-do when visitng Jeju, and there's lots of restaurants at the bottom.

I walked 40 minutes from Jungan Rotary to this place. The ticket is 2000 won. When I was there, it was in the afternoon 4-5 PM, there were so many tourists. So it's difficult to get a good shot. I find there's nothing special about these waterfalls, back home I've seen bigger and higher than here. I visited this place because it was close to my guesthouse and I was also curious about it. I don't see people swimming on it. What I like about this is the view of the sea, I was sitting between those big rocks towards the sea and waiting for the sun to set. It was a good experience for enjoying the sunset with having a natural background sound from the waterfalls.

I think the best time to climb here is during Spring, went during Winter and couldn't see much except for nice view. It's quite high up, so make sure you're a bit fit to climb the stairs.I personally didn't go up to see the sunrise but I've heard it's an amazing experience. Do give it a shot but you did have to be there by 6am

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I read Trip Advisor to avoid wasting time or money. The reviews of this museum had warned me away. Unfortunately due to rainy weather we were a bit stuck for options of things to do and I ignored y own research to give it a go. Sonetimes that works out. This time it didn't.Prettt expensive ticket at 36,000KrW for a museum we walked through in 10 minutes.Our kids are usually easily entertained and even they were disappointed with the museum. If the entry price wasn't so steep for what was on offer, we might have felt more poitive about the experience.

I read many negative review about this place from other travellers but for me, it was quite an interesting place with strange phenomena going on. My taxi driver brought me here on the way to Seongsan and he show me what is so mysterious about this road and it was indeed very strange. He stop the car at one end of the road and the car will automatically move up towards the slope (even when the car engine is not on). It was just an experience and one will not spend more than 10 minutes here. A good short trip before going to other places.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

I don't find this a really exciting place. Like what the other reviewers had said, this is what you will experience: Turn off the car engine and the car still continue to move   uphill  ... 10mins and it's over.

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I am really suprised this place has only few reviews here  it is one of the best things I got to do in Jeju  if you are afraid it's gonna be boring then let me tell you it's not  it's truely a   healing   experience  you leave phone and gadgets at the enterance and you just follow the guide and get far from everything and allow yourself to just rest  well you have to like nature to enjoy this experience for sure. Our guide was unforgettable.

I am not an early morning riser. However, since this place is one of the most recommended place to visit in Jeju, my friends and I decided to wake up super early to watch the sunrise. The stairs to get to the peak were steep, I had to stop to catch my breath a few times before reaching the peak. It was worth it though, the sunrise view was so pretty, and actually one of my best experiences in Jeju.
Hidden place. Even local people don't know much about it.this place has great, dramatic view and some time you can go over rocky small islet. it's really enjoyable experience!!.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hallsan is the highest mountain in Korea. You will have to hike up 1200m.  It is tiresome but it is not very tough, you can take your time. The time estimations indicated in the panels along the way are overestimated (specially if you have some hiking experience).Hiking up this mountain is like being on a highway with a lot of very noisy companions. It is packed, you will most likely be queuing up the mountain if you go in summer.If you are looking for a communion with nature, this is not the place. The hike up is almost entirely man-made, you will be walking up on wooden stairs and on wooden paths. Once you reach the top, it is so packed that you can barely enjoy. Views are excellent though.As you go up, there is a small path to the left to go to another lake. I will recommend this on your way down. Much much quieter as most tourists just want to go to the top.
great experience, tiring when climbing up, but glad to see the sunrise and feeling the cool sea breeze. magnificent view, must visit

Going to Seongsan Ilchulbong and climbing to the top to see the crater is on every  Jeju Island   To Do   list, but the best kept secret is down the mountain on the other side. In a gorgeous alcove, a handful of Jeju Haenyeo (women divers of Jeju) serves freshly caught mollusks in between diving and offering prayers of safety and a bountiful harvest. Some of these women are in their 80s and it is a very moving thing to experience. There are two shows daily 1:30 pm and 3:30 pm. It's free, although I suggest supporting these dynamic women by having some Makgeolli and a snack. The view is spectacular and so is the company.

From our recent experience and what our driver/guide told us:(1) rental cars: totally not allowed in busy summer. We visited in October so his car was allowed to take us onto the island, and still it was very crowded with the scooters and the bus, after a two day closure due to the wind(2) bring your passports (or other ID): although we had a rental car and were not going to rent any scooter, we were still asked for the passports before we boarded the ferry(3) when you plan your itinerary, if Udo is a must for your trip, be ready to make flexible rearrangements due to weather. We had to change our hiking in Hallashan due to a two day closure of the ferry service because of the wind. Check your weather forecasts as you get close to your Udo visit. If you plan to stay there overnight, also ask for cancellation or delay policy.(4) snacks not to be missed: peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine (although I should say it's a snack!) peanuts are local on Udo Island(5) reserve a whole day or most of the day if you want to fully enjoy Udo.  Even we had a car, we found it quite rush with some time wasted on the traffic (and it was only October, not the busy summer!)(6) romantic?? The reviews below were quite right about the beep,beep, beep.......of the scooters and the bus so I guess if you really want a Romantic Udo, it's better to stay overnight and after all the day visitors are gone, I think you should be able to enjoy a serene starry sky (but we didn't stay I could only imagine....)Enjoy Udo!

First, we went to see the woman diver show. It appears to occur twice per day, at 1.30pm and 3pm if I remember correctly. They were singing, then entered into the water. I found their catch more interesting than their swimming. Afterwards, we climbed the   mountain   (small but cute is the motto). The view over the volcanic crater and the island is amazing, even despite the rainy weather that we experienced. The ascend is a bit physically challenging.

Excellent view especially at sunrise. Hiking was good for a beginner level. Many places to stop and take a rest if needed. If not an experienced hiker, it takes maybe 40 minutes to get up to the top. No entrance fee if you go super early. Lots of lovely places around to grab coffee or some food after you hike down as well. I would do this again in a heartbeat!

During winter time, it is surely different experience when you hike up. The view is totally different from summer. Can see icy plant. So beautiful that we wont forget. It might take about 45min to hike up if you are in good shape during winter time as it is not easy to hike up because of cold air.

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.

Climbing up the iconic Seongsan Ilchulbong, by all means, is not an easy climbHowever, with the refreshing Jeju breeze, the beautiful landscape, and with a little thirst for excitement, it gets you going!The peak! though as you may predict how it would look like to be in the middle of the crater, the wind was so cool and refreshing and the view of Jeju, while going to the sides, makes the climb all worth it!Just too bad there wont be climbs at night to see glittering Jeju but seeing that it's no easy trek, I think it's understandableI am so thankful for the chance to see the sunrise and Jeju from the top!It was a breathtaking experience to see and not to mention, good exercise too!If you head over to Jeju, never miss this iconic place!To me, this is the overall representation of what Jeju has to offer!A promise of fun, beautiful and laidback adventure :)Another side of a Korean holiday experience
Brought my baby (14 months old) along , climbed the stairs together,  nice view, very good experience, awesome !

Book the jeju tour under Rakso travel from the Phillipines. Visited mt halla on dec.31,2015. We were lucky as snow during the week was scant but during our visit, snow is falling and everything transformed to a magical sight.This is the first time my children saw snow falling. However, i noticed that the falling snow are not flakes but more like 'dippin dots' unlike the one i experienced in switzerland.Nevertheless, the moment and the view were enchanting!. Highly recommended!!.

Been there during last autumn. This place is also known as Sunrise Peak. To reach the peak, you need to ascend 600 steps. The 1st 400 over steps seems easy but be more careful after that as the steps become steeper and more rugged. Also mind the autumn chilly strong wind which can blow your bags off (personal experience). Get there to the top for the panoramic view of the peak. Also, if you are in time, you can also watch the pearl diver women in action.

Based on a Malaysian blogger's review, we went over to one of the shops there to savour this renown dish.It was a BAD experience, the black pork sold there tough like wild boar and did not have any distinct tastes.Later on when we met some locals, they advise that locals don't eat there, only tourist who are attracted by the hype of the place.Fortunately, there are many other shops around Jeju City which served better Black Pork., In fact, we had a very good one at Halla Pork Restaurant in nearby Sehwa-ri.

Also known as the   Island of the Gods   and being marketed as the   Hawaii of Korea  . They said going to this volcanic island (also favorite destination for honeymooners) is like going back in time. From the top, it offers scintillating views from coast to coast including naturally sculpted cliffs. It's an uphill battle to Mt. Halla made more so with hordes of tourists who come your way. Once up there, it's euphoria. Visited last Sep-12 during   Experience Hyundai   Trip.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.

You need to see it once as an experience.There was not much to do except sit in the bus and watch the bus slowly moving upwards (looks like it). There is a stopover by the side of the road that sells food and snacks.

What a quirky little place to visit! Just wish I had got my international drivers license before we left Australia though because then I would have been able to drive one of the fun little 3-wheel vehicles to get around the island. A short ferry trip from Jeju Island and then a bus trip around showed us the sights. A must-do is to get off the bus at the first stop and explore the 2 caves down on the beach - stunning and quite a spiritual experience. Absolutely loved our visit to this little island!

We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)
We visited this stretch of the road and experienced the slope of the road. The driver stopped the engine and switched to neutral. To our big surprise the bus picked up speed and rolled downhill.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.
We had a great time. Beautiful sites and refreshing experiences. Highly recommend this tour instead of a large bus tour. More time for interaction and conversation. Thanks Jin!

This is located in the southwest quadrant of the island and can be a chore to get to without a car. The highlight of the building is the tea drinking experience that you need to make a reservation for(I'm pretty sure) that is entirely in Korean though so bear that in mind. There are tea fields in different directions for quite a ways the ones next to the museum are setup for visitors and picture but the further away fields aren't meant for tourists. We arrived around 10:30 and it wasnt busy at all but when we were getting ready to leave at 12:30 it was quite full.

The last time I went to a similar place with during my childhood days. Visiting aqua planet in jeju again is a good experience. The whole place isn't all that big but there is plenty of sea marine life to see and a Enormous fish take. This place can give u a kind of relaxing atmosphere. At the end there is a performance where u can rest your weary legs. Good place to be If you have a busy trip before you came to jeju. A little break for a change. Overall I enjoy the trip here and will revisit again with my love ones if ever given the chance.
