review: Really was a wonderful walk and experience. The path is well maintained and easy to find. We took the bus there and it is convenient and easy. Take a jacket as the forest can get a little cold
Not a place where you can experience nature. Next to busy road and parking place. Still pretty good compared to other beaches in Jeju.
Like - the experience and seeing a tour bus driver standing up and showing his passengers that he did not do anything will letting the bus roll uphill. Dislike - nothing.
It was quite a cool experience to feel the bus that we were in moving up the hill with the engine off.

It was a fun visit to the Mysterious Road in Jeju Island. Buses and cars that passes the road will turn off their engines and experience going uphill on a downward-looking slope. Apparently there are a few of these kind of roads around the world. Worth a short stop just to be puzzled for a few mins.

I visited on a tour from Yeha Bus Tours. It was such an awesome experience that I would have never seen if it wasn't for being part of that tour. The buildings were really neat and the restaurant was delicious. I was there on a rainy day but it was still pleasant. The mist contributed to the mysterious and dreamy vibe that this place had. I recommend carrying a small umbrella. I needed it throughout my 2 week stay in South Korea.

I found about this temple while looking for things to do around the waterfalls. It's quite a drive from them and I'm not pretty sure if by bus it's possible to get there but since it was my first temple we drove there anyway. It's a nice big temple though some of its decorations seem to be amateur. Nevertheless it was a nice experience. It's not very crowded so that's also a bonus. I don't recommend this temple for people who are disabled or have a hard time walking since there's a fare amount of stairs till you get to the temple.
Heard about this road from our tour guide. We experience it in a bus. The driver stop the bus n turn of the engine...the bus will drive itself. Pretty cool experience

Experience狩狩狩狩Time worth狩狩狩This attraction is basically a road. Just a road. With mysterious powers. Go there yourself to see if it's really that great because when we went to the mysterious road the bus driver switched off the engine and the bus continued moving along the road without any power. Mysterious. Aha. I don't know what's so fun about this road but I'll just give it a 4狩 rating

Despite being extremely busy (there was almost no space to move inside the building) the experience was still pleasant. There is a large assortment of teas to try and buy. The caf챕 is also worth a visit. Just make sure you grab a table before you order.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

What's interesting is that you really, actually get to see cars/buses with their engines obviously off, rolling up the slope. Expect to see a number of tour buses. Some tour guides will demonstrate the mysteriousness of the road even further by pouring water on the ground. The water will flow upwards. 10mins is enough time to spend here. Recommended to visit once for the experience.

What is so mysterious about this road is that vehicles can still move upslope with the engine switched off. We had the engine of the bus switched off and experienced it first hand what it felt like. The bus was first moving at a very slow speed but it started to gear up towards the end of the road. We then got off the bus to watch other vehicle move on the road. It was quite an interesting sight. Somewhere nearby, I even saw a stand giving out free Christian literature. Lots of snacks available. My first time trying the milk. At first, I thought it was some yoghurt drink or a big bottle of Yakult. Tried the one with black cap and realised that it's banana milk. I never like flavoured milk but this taste nice.More pictures available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html

What a waste of money! Very disappointing especially given the very high entrance fee (6K). The crater is just a hole in the ground covered with trees and a 1.2 km walk is a loop around grass patch and small forest on one side (next to a busy road, so you can hear the traffic). If you have never left a city before you might like it (like, you get to walk on a grass for a moment, not on a concrete sidewalk, UNBELIEVABLE NATURE EXPERIENCE, right?). Just save your money, for 6K you can have a nice lunch, not 30 minutes grass walk.

What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

Went there twice. Once on a rainy day and on a sunny day. Do not go on rainy days! We went on the bus tour which told us that English tour will be provided but the guide spoke korean throughout instead. Bus tour took us to a few attractions which were pretty scenic and impressive. However, the wind was too strong and it was freaking cold. Always have a poncho/raincoat prepared in case of rain! Went on a sunny day the next day and rented the ATV for 15,000 won for an hour. Managed to explore and rode the ATV round half of the island. Fantastic experience, would definitely recommend it and do it again! Also, try the peanut ice cream!

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We took a taxi to this road. The driver spoke limited English but it was sufficient for us to understand the explanation: when the vehicle gear is put to N on what seemed to be an up-slope, the vehicle rolls forward (it should have rowed backward instead)When we alighted the cab, we stood there longer to examine all the passing vehicles: mainly tour buses experimenting the same concept. You can hear their engines turned off and you will see the buses rolling   forward   on the up-slope. It was an intriguing experience but will be even better if you drive and experience it yourself. Other than the road itself, you may consider alighting and try out the two street food stores there.. or have a walk around the area, we saw herd of cattles grazing just beside the road too.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We read how good the pork belly was and from what we read, recommendations were to go to  Hwaro Hyang instead of Dumbedon. We arrived, dropped our bags, took a taxi to get there to make sure we experience what everyone is raving about. Hwaro Hyang was not too crowded and we easily got a table. The server explained that we should get the set for a couple to be able to taste a good sample of the cuts and some abalone. That we did. We got the platter, he dropped it on the hot plate and that was the last time our server came to our table. We saw how he was going around to all the other tables, turning their food over, cutting it up. Finally, we saw this lady who was serving another table and we flagged her down to see who might help us. She had to yell and call/force a young person to help us. I?ll chalk it to a language barrier issue as they were busily chatting with the rest of the customers. Finally the boy cut up our food, and we had to help ourselves and towards the end, the lady came back to turn off our hot plate. The experience would have been enhanced if we had known how to pair the condiments. We didn?t want to offend anyone so we watched as they showed the other tables how to eat the food and just mimicked them. They even did the lettuce wraps for some tables to show them how the side dishes are rolled. So moral of the story, unless you?re local or can speak with them conversationally, prepare to be ignored and just watching to see how others do it.

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We did this as part of Yeha bus tour - South Course - we were in the back of the bus, so it was really hard for us to see, but apparently, you put your vehicle in neutral and it rolls the opposite of what you would expect.  I'm sure the experience would be better in a car.

We decided to visit this   Green tea Museum   because it was a rainy day but could not find much of a direction - there was a mention of the tea stone experience but no further information.  We ended up going to the busy restaurant through a small 'museum' and ended up 'enjoying the $9 green tea'.  On the fields across from the museum there are kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures for photo opportunities.

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Udo or ?Cow Island? lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing ??5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It?s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

To get to this island, one has to fill in a form and pay for the fees. All is convenient and easy peasy. Then, the ferry ride is quick. We opted for a bus tour. The tour was in Korean and we couldn't understand a thing but considering it is one of the easiest method to get around the island,we just go along with it. We would like to ride one of those adorable scooters but we don't own an international license. Overall a good experience.

This was an interesting experience. I am usually ok in small spaces and felt this would be a great thing to do. But once I was in the middle of the first maze I felt a little uneasy. They provide a map and the maze itself is pretty easy to do. You also hear people walking around, but just something about the possibility of making a wrong turn made me not want to do the second and third maze. But there are really cool towers and a museum where you can take amazing pictures. the museum is free, they have trick art and a puzzle art. Getting here was a little bit difficult. Ask around your previous destination at the bus stop perhaps some people are willing to share taxi with you. Since the bus that goes around this area takes almost 45 minutes. And once you get to your destination you sometimes still have to walk a while to get to where you want to.

This was an exciting attraction. It takes about 1 hour to get to the end of the tube and back. The closer you get to the end the colder it gets. Also pe prepared to get a little wet, as there are drops of water falling from the top. You wont need an umbrella or anything like that. Getting here is tricky. As I was waiting for the bus to get here (990) I found a taxi and got him to take me for $4,000 won. This saved me a lot of time. It might have been too much but it saved me time, since the bus comes by every 45 minutes or so. There are restaurants at the entrance, they over charge for water so make sure you are prepared if you like to drink water. Definitely an amazing experience and a must do in the area.

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.

There's a starting point and ending point, that shows this mysterious road's gravitational force. Many went with tour buses but it's best to experience this in your own rented car! Switch to neutral and let the mystery begin!

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The hot springs have a good reputation and are very popular amongst Koreans. There is a large indoor area, separated of course for male and female, and then an outdoor area with 4 small pools the size of a hot tub and one larger lap pool which has cold spring water. Out of the 4 smaller pools 3 have hot water, 1 has cold water.The overall condition of the outdoor pools is quite shocking actually and I was surprised. In Korea almost everything is well maintained and in good condition, at these hot springs the paint coating came off at the pools, the pool furniture was old and falling apart, just very surprised to see it in this poor condition. It was busy nevertheless. There is a mix of couples and families, kids running around, people talking loudly, so it is not really serene and peaceful as a hot spring should be. The bathing experience was good, very relaxing, no doubt, but the overall experience was mediocre.

The beach has beautiful, clear emerald waters (the pictures doesn?t do the place justice as its much better experienced in person), and a really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries. We got there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. Near the beach there are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice. Easy to hail a taxi there too for those who wants to travel to their next location  by cab. Parking lots available too for those who are driving.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

Really great to see and well maintained. Wonderful visit. Went on a rainy day and it was still a pleasant experience. The bus to the cave is very slow and infrequent so you either have to walk or take an expensive taxi which is inconvenient, but otherwise very good

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.

Parking was difficult to find in the area when we visited although the walk back to the markets was not too bad. The markets were busy with many local producers sold their wares. Tourist heaven for the local oranges, chocolates and teas with many eating places as well that served a wide range of foods from pork to sea foods, fruits, burgers, desserts, nuts and candy. Much to choose from! Smaller tourist items can also be found along with clothing of the island - not much for westerns sizes though. Fairly crowed, but an experience not to miss while on the island.

Our tour guide built up anticipation of this phenomenon hours before we arrived at the site, and by then, our entire bus load of tourists were completely curious as to what we would experience.It was all over in less than a minute, but still interesting to see how a natural illusion could occur if the conditions are right.It's not worth making the effort just to see this short stretch of road, but if you happen to be in the vicinity, by all means see if the illusion works on you!

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is a small building set in a tea farm. It's a well designed lovely space with a display area about the history of tea and an exhibit wall of teacups and pots a shop where you can try some tea (only one kind though) and a restaurant featuring green tea beverages and sweets. You can also walk around outside there is a garden area in and around the building and also small rows of tea bushes just outside. There's no admission fee and it's not so much of a museum as a commercial venue for selling O'Sulloc products although items can be pricey for the budget traveller. I visited O'Sulloc with a few other backpackers (5 foreigners 1 Korean) and we all had a terrible experience of their customer service. The staff were sour faced and gave us the impression that we were not welcomed glaring at us and tidying their display in a huff when we looked at the product samples (these are samples ok - they're meant to be touched and looked at!). The staff at the counter literally sneered in disdain at my Korean travel companion when he tried to make friendly small talk while we were purchasing our items. This was the worst experience I've had in my 3 weeks in Korea. All the other customer service staff I've encountered in Korea were either very polite and lovely or just neutral. I'm writing in formally to the management about this so hopefully by the time other TripAdvisor members visit they would have improved.In spite of that I did enjoy my visit (no point letting the staff spoil it) but I would recommend coming here only if you've done all your   must-do's   in Jeju or on a rainy day.

On a family trip, my fiance and I had one day to ourselves and we ended up here for a couple hours. We love being near water, so this was an easy choice for us. The natural pools were so clear and beautiful, even though it was November and cold we went into the water and enjoyed freezing our butts off from the water and wind. Still such a fun and unique experience we'll never forget. Because we came in November there were only a handful of people that came and went. We definitely recommend checking this place out for a hour or so. I imagine it can get pretty busy during the summer time but youd get to enjoy the water much more. Even in the cold weather it's worth just checking out if you're around the area.

Needs to be in a vehicle to enjoy this amazing experience, though we also pour water on the road to see how it flow   uphill  . Noticed local bus tour also pass through this attraction, but I'm not sure if they will allow the passengers to get off the bus and do the experiment.

My husband and I visited this park during our honeymoon and it was really beautiful. It consists of 8 botanical gardens which features different kinds of plants, a cave which you can walk through, and even an area with different kinds of birds that you can feed and interact with.We got there through the Yeha Bus Tour but you can also get there with a taxi.For those of you who are looking to experience some of the beauty of nature and interact with it, I recommend this place.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Love the walk. Advisable to use a pair of good shoes as the ground can be slippery. Very dark and cold. Difficult to reach by bus. Usually there will be taxis at the nearest bustop. Advisable to take taxi there from the nearest bustop. After the experience, do take some time to sit at the nearest cafe. Should try the Orange Freeze!

I've visited many caves but by far this is the first lava tube that I have experienced. It is interesting to know the science and geography behind this magnificent tube. However, only 1 km deep into the tube is open to tourists. You can take a public bus directly from the Jeju bus station if you opt to travel on a budget. The bus fare is less than KRW 2000 compared to very pricey tours with taxi. The bus ride is only slightly more than an hour away from Jeju City.

It was a really wonderful experience to cycle around the island, although a little tiring. You can rent a motorcycle or trike as well. It is really busy and sometimes a little crowded on the roads. There are many restaurants and a few beaches. Excellent food to be had

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It is quite windy here. Lots of people visiting this beach. The beach are covered by a beautiful black stones all the way. The most memorable experience i have here is to taste the grill squid! It was so fresh and nice until i almost left by the bus just because i want to buy the squid again..haha..if i ever come to Jeju again, i'll definitely come here and looks for this nice squid.

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the   jimjilbang   (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you   foreigners   out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.
If you're a free and easy traveller, I'll totally not recommend you to travel to see this mysterious road. If you're on a tour bus, this is an interesting experience.

If you want to enjoy around two hours walking without difficulties in the middle of an amazing and dense  forest I highly recommend you to visit Bijarim. Considering the time needed for these trees (nutmeg yew, family of the Taxus) to grow and the fact that normally you can only find it as bushes into other species's forest this place is a unique jewel with many of the trees aging more that 500 or indeed 800 years. Beautiful and relaxing experience that I will keep forever in my memories as a lover of trees that I am.

If you like nature then this will be a wonderful experience. It is a spectacular waterfall that connects with the ocean. It is quite busy, but the area is big enough as well. There are many steep steps to get down to the falls and back up again

I went with the Yeha Bus Tour so my experience may have been better than if I had simply driven there. I found the tour informative. It's not a reproduction it dates back over a hundred years, homes having passed down from generation to generation. A few have been kept original for tourist. Most of the homes continue to evolve and have electricity and modern comforts. People live there and largely ignore the tourist.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visit play kpop by taking bus 600 from sogwipo harbour. It was very exciting experience. Even though it is a hologram concert, it feels like a live concert and my wife won the card selection and my wife?s hologram was on stage and yonghwa singing for her. I never seen this technology and appearance anywhere else. Play kpop need to improve the 360 3d cinema because it makes visitor feel dizzy and to improve the sound system. Anything else is okay but need to pay every single shots with the celebrity. Overall i give 5 stars for the experience. Thanks Play Kpop!

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called   Orum   in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for   you silly tourist   sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. You can get here from Jeju bus terminal using the 701 bus (3,000 KRW). There is a stop for it about 40 mins in. It's near Manjangul cave (6,000 KRW taxi) so worth combining it with a trip with that.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I am not able to visit this park because of the bus. We went to the airport by bus in order to take the 131 bus for the park. To confirm this info from our hotel receptionist, we asked the airport tourist info counter. Correct, and we were directed to gate 1 and begun to wait for the bus. We missed the 1240 so we decided to wait for the 1340. The bus didn't come until 1400 and we went to double check with the info counter. Then we were told that 1340 is for the number 132, which is grouped together with 131. 132 doesn't head for Jeju stone park and we were told to wait for the 1530 bus. Isn't it amazing our bus waiting experience? I am sharing this as a gentle reminder for all. Plan your bus schedule properly especially for venues outside the city. Cheers

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Had a lot fun going through this maze. Don't use the map because it will spoil the experience. We kept on running into the other tourists that had the same look on their faces because we couldnt find the exit. But you could tell they were also having fun no translation needed. Took us about 45 minutes to finish the maze. Only problem was getting there. The nearest bus stop is a bit far and taxis are few and far in between.We took a cab going to the bus stop and planned on splitting the cab fare with other tourists. Turns out the driver wasnt using the meter and asked us to pay 2000 won each. We didn't argue too much with the driver because we were trying to catch the bus plus he didnt speak English. Just be careful because this might also happen to you. This was the only bad experience we had in Jeju (the cab ride, not the maze).

Good experience, but not so special as there are some other place in my home country that seems similar to it. We are on a group tour, upon reaching the road our driver stopped the engine, the bus continued running, the tourguide did some explanation, something about magnetic features of the area, if you will look around its just like an ordinary road.

For the ones who believe they are in good shape:Why struggle, why do it the hard way? because it is much more scenic and maybe only one tenth of climbers going that way. Taxi from town to starting point (approx 20 min) was 11.000 won on taximeter from my hotel in Nohyung-dong (near the int. airport) or take the bus but only on sat and sundays). Bus stop at Seongpanak when you come down from the mountain on the road. Check schedule and bus no. Taxi back 20.000 won (not on meter..)This is by far the most important place to look before you set out. THE WEATHER! http://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Hallasan/forecasts/1950 I wouldn't call my self an experienced climber but I did it in 3h10min up and 2h down. This is in a pace where I overtook and was not overtaken, and very short breaks, maybe only 2 min in total 5 times. The track is changes between rocks or stairs, I think it's well kept. Two toilet stations up and two down. None at the top. Bring 3-4L of liquids minimum, no passport nor entry is needed for the mountain (aug 2013). A windbreaker for the summit can be nice to have. The weather can change every minute so rain is likely. I did it in old worn-out runners. Bring food and nutrition - no shops. Good luck and enjoy

For the adventurous and those seeking a different experience. This place is located quite out of the way, however close enough to Halla arboretum as well. Quite challenging to find as Naver and googlemaps does not have this location up to date. If you are looking to find it, look for a bus that will take you to Halla arboretum stop and you could find it by following the street direction towards the arboretum. When you see a building with   playbox  , you've found it!There's an ice sculpture display area with an ice slide you can experience. Next level on is your VR experience that you could choose to experience (cost of entry varies depending on what experiences you would like to add on).As reference we chose the Basic A experience which provides us entry into the ice sculpture, Trick art area, 5D movie experience and 1 VR experience of our choice - cost 22000krw per person.You could spend at least an hour here and rest at the cafeteria before moving on.

First some people said it is   Mystic   supranatural thing but actually it's only a trick eyes illusions that twisted out logical thinking. The road looks like going uphill and makes the car or bus like climbing moving forward againts the gravity. When we saw from the end of the road, yes the road is going downhill not the opposite around. Well, still it's amazing thing to experience!

Even though this exhilarating experience lasted probably 10 minutes it was a moment to remember. I am happy we took the ride along mysterious road to experience this. The tour bus was switched off and the bus travelled on its own uphill. You wonder how it happened, it is puzzling.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.

review: Beautiful place to take a nice walk around the shore line. Can imagine it would get a bit busy in the summer, but it was empty when we visited as it was a snowy winter day which by all accounts added to the experience. Be careful though it can become a wee bit slippery when the rocks get wet.

As I rented a car to explore Jeju (highly recommended), we came here a couple of times to enjoy the experience putting the gear at N position and realizing how the car went up the hill.We also tried on the road with a can of beer that also was rolling hill up apparently. It is maybe an optical illusion but when you are there it looks clearly and without any doubt that cars and things go up the road. The kids were amazed and really enjoyed as we also did.Try to avoid the afternoons, as most of the guided tours are here at that time with many buses horning in hurry to repeat the experience several times and many pedestrians around. In the morning the day after it was almost empty !

As a part of our school's field trip program, we went to the one of the known attraction in Jeju-do which is the Jeju mysterious road. While inside of the bus, our tour guide asked the driver to turn the engine off. Our tour guide pointed out that even though the engine is turned off, the bus still continues to move   way up  . But in reality, our bus moved downwards. It was like an optical illusion. For me, this attraction is not that amazing, just a normal road. On a positive note, if you have a lot of time to spend in the island, give it a try and experience the illusion.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.
We stop here on the way to the airport. It's quiet interesting experience when the car moves. Can't help laughing inside the car as the power is off but it still moves.

We made a short stopover at the Mysterious Road on the way back from the south side of the island - just a quick 20 minute one would suffice. You can start the experience from either lane - there's a marker to demarcate where the Mysterious Road starts and stops.Basic Procedure: 1) Switch on your hazard lights; 2) Slowly come to a complete stop; 3) Prepare your video recording device; 4) Be mildly amused at how something like this can happen!You're done!

This is only a nice experience if it is not crowded. With us entered a family if four and they easily blocked 2-3 displays. The start of the tour is great. A lot of great photo opportunities. They gibe you examples and show how to pose. But suddenly this stops in the middle and you end up in a huge room with Aladdin Indiana Jones a volcano eruption? We had no clue what to do there.At the end there is a bug parking lot outside with even more displays. So if you are into instagram and pictures - this is yours. If not... well it is entertaining though. Unless there are tons of visitors.

The cause of forming a wonderful Island is a Volcano and hiking to the top of it is a wonderful experience. Roads up to the height of 1100 mtrs are made cautiously and traveler friendly for pleasure with least possibility of an accident. The hiking experience is also beyond the expression in words. I can only say that visiting JEJU and Hallim park are synonyms.

Our first time in Shinhwa World theme park visit in December 2017. One must come with the understanding that the theme park is not yet fully developed but it has some nice rides and you can spend a few hours there . My kids had a wonderful time . Since it is new  the park is not crowded. We had lunch at the food court and it was good Korean food . We were initially disappointed when the rides were suspended due to the snow. However the rides were resumed quickly after the snow stopped. We happened to have met the theme park Manager Mr Mason Kang when we ran into communication difficulty with one of the staff attending to the ride . He was very kind to explain to us that the rides would resume soon after they dry the area . His professionalism impressed us .  Our theme park experience was a great one . My kids tried the ice skating ring within the theme park compound . Everything is new and clean . We will come again ! They are going to have a Water theme park probably year after .

Our first stop in the Jeju trip was the Olloc Tea Museum.Here you can take a master class about how to make tea properly and try different kinds of teas.It was a very relaxing experience and the taste of the tea was very unique.If you like tea is definitely something you have to do if you travel to Jeju.Also you can visit the Innisfree shop right next to the museum and take beautiful pictures in the green tea fields around.
Nice experience. You will require to stop the car and change the gear to N and you will feel the car start moving slowly even though is sloop.

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

It was very far from what I expected and saw on photos they provided. I was outraged for what I got for $50. Frankly it ruined my experience in Jeju. 1. Everything (security instructions descriptions in the submarine) is in Korean/Chinese. Do not expect them to translate or be able to do so. 2. The submarine barely goes anywhere. It felt like we got into it moved 500m and stopped. 3. The place where we stopped was shallow and we couldn't see anything but rubbish and some algae. 4. What they do: they bring some fish (from container no natural fish there) to your window and take a photo of you with it (look point 5 about it). Do NOT expect to see real ocean WILD life. 5. SCAM: When you are boarding they will take a photo of you and say 'free photo included' but all photos except this one cost $5 each. We expected all photos to be free (they told us so) thus allowed them to take photo when they brought fish to our window and we did not take photo on our devices. Thus we had to buy photos.

I strolled into the stadium primarily for my interest in sports. Unfortunately  during my stay on Jeju Island there were no games scheduled. The stadium is rather impressive and I would love to attend a major soccer game here.For any sports fan  stop by the stadium at the very least (15 minutes is sufficient). If you can buy tickets to a game  even better. Watching any Korean sporting event is an experience.
Hiked to the very top and back for 12 crazy hours. Incredible experience!!

Hike this 19.2km return path *9.6km one way on a rainy and cloudy day is definitely an unforgettable experience. Rocky paths have turn into flowing streams. Took  9 hours non stop to reach the peak and return. Thick fog on the peak most of the time and only manage to get a glance at the lake. Great sense of achievement when reaching the top
We had a taxi tour and this just happened to be on the way to a museum. It was neat to experience and see, but I wouldn't stop by if it was out of the way.

We came just after the rain stopped. Love the layout of the whole place. Instantly brings you back to the past there are real people - Craftsmen Painter Potter man on the respective   villages   with living animals - chicken black pigs goats horses. It is a nice experience. There are old   games   for you to try on. Saw traditional drummers along the way. You can have greater understanding on how the past Koreans houses based on their occupations - fisherman farmer locksmith painter. There are school police station & court house too. Few of the famous Korean dramas been shot here namely Jewel In The Palace.  A worker told us if we came on a non rainy day there will be more activities. Entrance fee is on higher side - 8000 Won/ Person but it is worth a visit.

Visited in Oct, very windy and cooling. Walked up to the hill top in 10mins. Very good experience and the tracks and steps were very nicely constructed. But the place is extremely crowded so photo taking was difficult. Worth the visit and the climb.

Very interesting for the first time. The local guide told us they name this road as   monster road   cos locals belive there is a invisible monster playing with the cars that's why the car move forward when uphill even stop engine. Great experience

This tiny, delightful island feels miles away from anything familiar and mundane.  I highly recommend renting an electric scooter (for about 25 bucks for 2 hours) and driving around the entire island.  Driving around the island only takes about an hour, but give yourself extra time to stop for photo ops.  The place is dreamy and laid back - you can even spot the famous haenyeo (women divers) at work, and see their   dressing stations.    There is no   one particular amazing   thing to see on Udo, but rather it's about the whole experience of exploring this off-beat place and losing track of time.

This magnificent, iconic destination is well worth the struggle to the top. I'm seriously unfit and overweight but I took it slowly and made it. We saw deer grazing as we returned and it was a peaceful and serene experience

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

The queue was long starting from midnight. The tag was given starting 2:30am. The limit was for 1300 first come first served. The waiting was in 2 celcius temperature. The trek up started at 5:30am in an orderly manner in a hushed procession like atmosphere. At the top of the plateau there were decks facing the direction of the sunrise. All was ready for the first sunrise of 2020. Unfortunately it did not happen. The clouds was too thick and we headed back an hour after the sunrise time. Was I disappointed? Not really. The whole experience was exhilarating, the wait, the trek, the anticipation of the sunrise. It was a memorable experience which I hope to repeat one day.

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Several things that I didn't like about this place. First they completely do not respect nature, eg. There are a few chairs on top with Celine dion's titanic music playing! I guess Koreans think that makes the place more romantic but it completely ruins the experience for me. Then the crater itself is impressive but the entrance fee was 6000w per person which is a total rip off. If these two objections don't deter you from going then at least go early (we went at 8:30 on a Monday) and literally had the crater to ourselves for 15 minutes.

Nice looking beach and lovely water, but don?t recommend if you want to swim. Lifeguards are over authoritarian and you?re only allowed in a 10x10 square with many other people (who have inflatables)! We had a pretty bad experience here where the lifeguards seemed to be picking on us for no reason. Also not allowed to sit/walk on certain parts of the beach. Overall poor experience only saved but spotted an octopus!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

It was Autumn, when I visited this place. I enjoy playing indoor coz its very cold outside. Upon entrance, I enjoyed already the music that u will listen to from generation to generariion, it was fun to guess them until u reached the dance floor whic you can see yourself dancing in the platform also, after that u will experience also, to sing and play some music instrument.
