Beside that corner, u can also have a chance to hear top 100 music alonh the way, u can play and take photo with all ur favorite k-pop star on the stage! While enjoying inside, they will give u a call if their hologram concert starts, everybody will run to watch this. The best part is to shop items, with our favorite k-pop star logo/dasigns. See you there!

It was a good experience for me family with 2 children as they enjoyed ut the most. Weather as a bit chilly even during autumn, so bring extra layers with you so that you can get confortable. The train ride at the start of the trip really feels like the highlight of the trip, although you can board the train on and off later to get from one garden to another. There are 5 stops for you to stroll around, toilets, cafes and other facilities are available and very much well taken care off. We had a great time all in all. Highly recommended to friends and families.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

If you have no knowledge of the K-pop industry, this may not be the place for you. But, we love it. For the ticket price, things it offers is beyond our expectation. If you have a personal preference of 'which' pop star you wanna watch for the hologram show, you should check its schedule online. The ticket has a 3-hour validity (I think it's a bit short, if you really try all the stations/ experience) There are 3 levels where you could see lots of displays (music, costumes) and to try lots of fun interactive games with cutting edge technology. For instance, to dance with the stars, to shoot a picture with them, where you could actually scan your ticket and choose from the list, which star you want to pick. We stopped half way to watch the scheduled hologram show, which lasted for about 30 mins, and it was fabulous because that is the singer we really adore. After the show, we continued with our visit for a while. You can print whatever photos you snapped (if you like it) on the spot with a small fee. Likewise, you may download all the funny photos you have snapped from their website later that day. We enjoyed ourselves tremendously.

I went alone in this tour, and my driver was sooo nice! He helped me take pictures, gave me awesome tips and guidance about the places we went, and he even suggested some extra stops for me because I was new to Jeju~ It was so enjoyable, and my experience was excellent because my driver went the extra mile to make sure I was comfortable and well informed~

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

Here is the best was to try the experience of climbing up the hill Come from the loveland (from the north) and stop at what seems to the bottom of the hill (there will be a sign on the other sign of the road)Stop your car, go in neutral put you warning signals on.Make sure there is no pedestrian and car behind you and release the break The car will start climbing the hill in reverse mode It is a bit dangerous as there are lot of pedestrian and potential drivers that dont understand what you are doing but really the best way to experience the illusion

Great experience walking around and reading the story,  The owner had a lot of faith that he could change this area into something wonderful.  Glad we made the time to stop and check out the Bonsai's!

We went on a Sunday at about 10+AM and it was crowded. Transparent kayaks have to be reserved in advance so we opted for a floating water bike. When we bought our tickets we were told to come back at 12PM (the time was handwritten on the ticket). There are shade and chairs at the waiting area close to the rides where you get called out when your turn comes. Since we had more than an hour to spare we headed to Jeongbang Waterfalls (about 10 mins drive away) and made it back on time. The bike was easy to maneuver and unlike bicycles the handles do not steer. Overall an enjoyable 20 mins experience for 15000KRW.

We had an old Korean man who has lived there for all his life guiding us around his own house in English. He was very humorous and a very friendly guide. It was an interesting and refreshing experience of learning about the old village way of living in Jeju!

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.

To experience something different something unique not know how the car keeps going with the Engine turned off.  We did it on our way over and our way back to the hotel.  It was fun to see all the tourist on the roads waiting to see each car going without the start of the engine.

This place is considered clean for a local market. Mixture of raw fresh food and cooked food stores. We came here at around 10am and a number of cooked food stores are already open. Nice experience walking around and eating street food along the way. There are benches around for you to sit and have your food. Market closes at 8.30pm.
The only value here I think is let the kids make their own chocolates. It's a funny experience. Apart from that  the display is a joke. Anyway  the entrance fee is low and it doesn't matter much.

The lava tube was not claustrophobic at all. It was very comfortable and cool. The lighting is low but is still very visible and easy to navigate. Just did the first course but was glad we did! It was wet when we went and there was water dripping from the ceiling. It didn't bother me tho and didn't take away from the experience :)

The folk houses built well imitating earlier century jeju do livings. You can experience the way of living of older jeju do resident. Kinda way of knowing and understanding of Jeju resident. The living plant and animal were well maintain.

The car drives  up the road by itself! Great fun. ( visual effect)It only works one way. You need to drive in neutral towards the shops. If you arrived from Jejusi do a U turn after the shops to experience the effect. The effect is quite spectacular with a water bottle placed in the middle of the road. You will see clearly the bottle rolling up.

Tea Plantations are not my favourite places and this is not a museum as such. But the way the Koreans have done this makes it into a relaxing afternoon experience. The cherry blossoms just came out when we visited. There were scores of Korean students on a field trip but that's OK. It's spacious enough for everyone. A short display of tea cups from around the world lines the entrance of the building. Then it's tea shopping and testing. Try the buckwheat tea! Lots of chinese speaking staff (as with everywhere else in Seoul). Here I tasted the best green tea ice cream and cake. A walk in the surrounding garden and compound is nice. There is a glass building next to the main one by Korean brand Innisfree. In it there are soap making activities a cafe and skin care shopping.

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

Our taxi driver took us here after going to Horseland (by the way there are better horse places).  The driver switched the ignition off placed it in neutral and it rolled up hill rather than down.  A very odd experience.  If you are passing by it is definitely worth the experience.
No instructions. We went all the way and followed what everyone did... Tried twice but nothing happen and we had no mysterious experience....

My husband and I were visiting Jeju mid-August. A week before our trip I searched online for a dive experience and found Good Dive. My husband and I live in China and had no way of contacting the center by phone so good thing they had an email address on tripadvisor. I emailed…
It's a great experience and see the way. It's not really that difficult to walk inside and it's spacious.

If you want to experience the old way  of Korean life this is the place to go and visit. This is one of my favorite places. We took a taxi from Hyatt to here and it took us roughly 45 minutes. The cab driver was nice even though we were not able to communicate well since he was not well-versed in English.

If you want ride transparent kayak you have to do reservation. Sea and water is so clean transparent kayak is quite good experience. Water bicycles was good too but little bit harder to ride than kayak. Without reservation we can ride waterbycles. Anyway beautiful sightseeing and place.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

I went on a group tour around Korea last year and one of my highlights was seeing the lava tubes at Jeju. You might think a cave is just a dark place with little to no visual interest but this Unesco site is really cool because you're actually inside a tunnel formed by volcano pressure. There are lights that guide your way and handlebars so you don't slip. If you're into nature and on this island it's a must see because there are some extraordinary natural feats you observe and experience first hand as you explore these tunnels. It's very interactive.

I visited to Da vinci museum with my daughter last weekend.It was very interesting and educational place.There are many experience activities like making a paddle steamer  shooting water bomb  etc.My daughter made a paddle steamer  she really liked it. Anyway I was surprised that I can see the Da vinci's works in Korea not itary.

I have visited half a dozen Buddhist temples in Korea and so far this is my favorite! This temple is simply gorgeous. We arrived just as the monks started ring the outside bell. We were greeted with open arms and encouraged to come inside the main temple building and to go upstairs to see it all. I have always been hesitant to venture into the temples to take pictures because I do not want to offend anyone but we were invited in to explore it was fantastic. so ornate. The three gold Buddhist statues were very large and beautiful. The monks where in the middle of chanting it was a mesmerizing experience so peaceful and relaxing. The grounds of the temple were just as lovely.

I have seen many Korean Markets in the course of my 18 days in korea. To be honest  no market have truly captured my attention. You can go to any traditional market in any state of S.K and you wouldn't be missing out. My advice for any Korean Traditional Market in general:- Go to any market that is decently sized that is convenient to travel to from your accomodation. - Take note that they do not have rubbish bins there most of the time and you'd have to return your trash to the store which you have bought the food from. - Be very clear in the number of portions you order as I had a rather awful experience ordering one portion and receiving three person quantity since I had three people.- Go in the morning/day time since most markets will be closing shop by 6pm- The fishcake skewers and the broth are great to enjoy on a cold day. You grab a cup from the stall to get the broth and start eating the oden. Payment will come after you return the sticks to the owner.Lastly  enjoy yourselves in Korea. Learn some basic Korean before you come as you will definitely elevate your experience in Korea. Koreans will always treat you better if they see you making an effort to speak some Korean as all other countries.

Great place to experience how the early koreans lived. Learn more about their way of life by exploring the village. There are hands on experiences like grinding the corn playing traditional games pounding grains etc. There is also traditional folk dance performance daily. Really fun and interesting!
Good experience. Pull over your car once arrived in the road and enjoy the experience.  On your way to loveland you will pasd over the road.

Down steep stairs and into the lava tubes.You can go in a long way or a little way.I enjoyed this unusual experience.I did not like the fact that it was wet and surface uneven so difficult even with good walking shoes.
Didn't expect the lava cave to be that long. But it was an interesting experience. Wear waterproof non-slip shoes as the floor is always wet.

Cool experience. Not too hard to figure out the mystery but fun! We had a taxi hired and she drove us to the spot and turned off the engine and the car was rolling uphill! I loved it when she did it backwards. Pretty trippy. wouldn't go out of the way to see it but Loveland is literally right next to it so you might as well!

Yeah, this is a real village, whereby the Korean government had deemed it as a living historical site. The villagers are actually living there.You can get the Korean honey there for 40,000 won. A must get for you. Also if you had watched   Dae Jang Geum   drama, the daughter of the village head is one of the person giving the tour.And the way they greet tourist is unique. Experience it yourself. Not sure if there is any entrance fee as I was on a package tour and this was part of the itinerary.

While the hike was long it was definitely worth it. It wasn't too difficult, it was beautiful the whole way, and knowing I reached South Korea's highest peak felt like an achievement.It never felt too steep and even in the middle of summer the brutal heat didn't diminish the experience much. The only complaint I have is that parts of the path are covered with large, randomly distributed volcanic rocks that are a pain especially during the decent and my feat were pretty sore for quite a while afterwards.

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) ! After you flood yrselves silly with pics, you can try the maze. Its interesting walking in and out and along the way you can look out for cats that are just chillin by the greenery. Overall a good experience especially for families !

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

Went up and down seongpanak. Went with my parents who are in their early 50s. The way up gets a little tough after the 12:30 point. We started at 6:30 and got to that area by 11:00. On the way down gets very boring. Bring lots of water and wear shoes. You'll see old Korean people wearing stuff you'd wear to summit some crazy mountain but just good shoes with good grip (not converse) will be good for the hike. Of course hiking boots would help. Things to bring: hand sanitizer, water, sunscreen, gatorade/pocari sweat if it's very hot. Bring some food and bags for trash as you have to take it all with you. Overall probably 4/5 experience but nice to experience with family. Probably not good for young kids - people with health problems die each year per locals.

Went here with a tour package bought from Klook. Entering caves experience feels great however, for it requires like 30 minutes walk to the Lava Coloum and you have to walk back (there is no other way out) so you need to make sure to wear comfortable shoes because the floor is uneven.

We would have never imagined that you can make so much out of a teddy bear. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and I would suggest it for any bear lover but especially for families with young kids. As for the Alive Museum, I would strongly advice to go there either in the morning or early in the afternoon. We visited it in the morning and it was a bliss, but my guts' feeling tells me the crowds in the afternoon must be a little bit more stressful to deal with.PS: Don't forget the Elvis Presley Show. Yes, it is kind of tacky but really cute anyway!

We went with 3 children (aged 5,7 and 10) and two seniors, and they enjoyed the maze park. It was a smaller maze park compared to maze land, so it's not too difficult for kids. We spilt into two groups, one group managed to find out way out and rang the bell in 5 mins, while the other got lost in the maze and required rescue.  We spent about an hour or so, going through the maze thrice, and it was a fun experience.
We went here right as we landed, it was a fun way to get moving after sitting on the plane for a couple of hours.  Really enjoyed this cave experience.

We visited this place on a slightly gloomy day. This and the amazon green colours of the flora made it look like a mystic forest, something out of an animation. They say, walking among these nutmeg trees has healing properties, and eventhough I was sceptical at first, soon I could feel my nerves calming down. It felt like someone poured some sleeping powder on us. Oh and the smell! I've never felt such pungent yet clean fragrance in a forest before, it's truly unique. All those pretty colours and the distinctive smell of nutmeg and cinnamon trees makes this pathway a mesmerizing experience. The route takes at least 40 minutes-1 hour. There are some charming restaurants and coffee places before the entrance, and a huge parking lot. The whole are is beautiful.

We had no plans to see this, but on our way to the airport, we stumbled upon it. Put the car in neutral and slowly rolled   up hill  . We laughed for the 15 second experience and went on our way. Certainly not worth going out of the way to get there.

We had a guide to explain and tell us about the history of jeju and the way of life of the people that lived there. It is an eye opening experience, visit this place to have a better understanding of jeju island.
We got lost so we had to find our way, I did not expect it to be so funny))) we liked the experience. The weather was sunny, so the photos were great

We drove up to this attraction easily via an English GPS. No prams or strollers are allowed in there because it's mostly stairways and lots of rocks. You'll need to navigate across some amount of rocks to take a nice picture with the waterfall. There're a couple of old ladies selling seafood with a small fire burning nearby - we didnt buy anything coz they don't speak English. Not a huge waterfall, but the kids love it (not of the waterfall, but the rock walking experience) - if you're not careful, you can easily sprain an ankle or even break some bones.

We drove there and parking is free. The whole experience will take about less than 2hours? About 45mins to walk all the way inside to the end of the cave and another 45mins out. So remember to empty your bladder before entering. There is no loo inside the cave.The cave is cold. About 15 degree celcius? Luckily there is no wind. The ground is made up of rocky bits, and the place is constantly damped and slippery. So wear a light jacket and confortable shoes.Although there are lights in the cave, they are pretty dimmed. Not brightly lit. We used the torchlight function in our phones to further assist us to see the rocky ground. It is not unusual to carry a small portable torchlight if you want. Im not a person who likes cave, but well.. it is an experience i guess.

We discovered this market when we were wandering around after dinner. The tour guide did not tell us about it. It was an enjoyable experience. It was a clean, well organised wet market.I always like visiting markets whenever I travel. It gives an insight on how the locals live. It wasn't the mandarin season and what's available was expensive. But we bought lots of chocs & strawberries.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We caught the Nanta show in Jeju and it was such a fun night for the family. It is a combination of comedy, musical, martial art and drums. Though a Korean production with a Korean context but the storyline was kept simple and easy to understand. For a show that ran an hour and a half long, the performers were really awesome with great stamina! They kept their energy high up until the end, without missing a beat. Nanta is also known for its audience participation and without giving the plot away, this was done with a delightful, surprising twist. One that you should experience yourself if you ever get the chance to catch the show.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Walking the Dongmun Market is an experience that a visitor should not miss.  The local market has variety of daily food of the islanders.  Seeing the fresh fishes, seafoods, and other meats displayed in various forms for consumption was an eye opener.  We would love to buy and try some of the food if the merchant package them in ready-to-eat size.  On this entrepreneurs way, the Japanese market achieve high mark in its idea.  Visitors would love to try local food even to pay at a premium.

Three interconnected mazes come with a map to make sure you won't get lost, other sights nearby including a lovely and scenic walk under beautiful trees. On my way through one of the mazes the sprinklers above came on and then you're walking through mist. A very straightforward sight that is an interesting experience.

Though Udo is a small island, no matter you are renting bicycle/moto or even treking, its easy to get lost especially those tourists with limited Korean. So, just share my experience, make sure where you are onboard the island. There are 2 ports, please check the leaflet the ticket office pass to you. It helps to fix all troubles or uncertain durinf Udo trip.GPS is not quite user friendly there. When you clear the starting point, basically you can follow the simple map. Pls remind that you can use return ticket depart from either ports. Don't be panic. Check the leaflet again, don't throw it away! Enjoy, really a nice place and recommend to stay 1 night in the island too!

This was fun. it only took about an hour to go all the way through. there is a 2,000W charge. its chilly inside so if you bring the kids, pack their jackets. Its solid lava so it is not as colorful or full of stalagtytes as other natural caves but being in a lava tube is a unique experience and this one is really big. enjoy!

This underground shopping street is kinda cool. It has clothes, beauty products, a large number of children's stall, and no doubt impresses the many thousands of tourists that come through Jeju City every day. However, if you have ever been to Singapore, and experienced the underground warren of the connected malls on Orchard road, this will not in any way tantalize you. At best it will make you smile at the 1970's feel of it all ;-)

This place toally blew me away with the beautiful rock erosions.  I never expected that this would be the highlight of my trip to Jeju.  I could see the clarity of the blue green water up close.  Assured that the seawater was so clean without any fishy smell, we even ventured to sample the live seashells.  What an unforgettable experience we had, dining on the rocks with the gentle waves lapping in front of us.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This maze is fun and quite simple. And from what I've observed, it really tests a couple's relationship strength. ALong the way I see couples arguing on which way to go, I see couples helping each other out. It was a fun experience. Walk there from Manjanggul to get a 500won discount!

This is something different: a 2 km or so walk through an underground lava tube where molten lava has flowed several times over the centuries. A unique experience. Be prepared for a bit of a trek over uneven, rough ground, dodging puddles. It can be drippy and it's always cold so take a jacket. But it's good fun and just out of this world.

This is for the female Merchant who saved people in Jeju island 17,18 Century, Joseon dynasty. Very carefully and beautifully made. However, it is limited for 3rd floor. 2nd floor is for kids' experience museum. 1st floor is for some special exposition from time to time. It is FREE, worth to visit for an hour. It is located near by Jeju coastal international port and Dongmun traditional market. Actually from this market, exit/entrance #3, it is just 500 m away. In those times, people in Jeju island could not get out of the island, however, since she saved whole population in the island, The King Jungjo wanted to give a awards but she refused. Instead, she asked him she would love to visit the peninsular once, and wanted to travel in Diamond mountain(located in North Korea now). So she could get the chance to meet the King and travel inland. Under the Patriarchal system, it must be very hard for her to work as a merchant, but became the most rich person in Jeju, then when there was big famine, she released whole rice and food for free to Jeju people. Any way, it was great fun to enjoy each section from her birth to death. All explanation are in English and in Korean both.

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

There is a place for hand-made soap. If you buy a pack of raw material for making soap, you are able to sit down and design your own soap right away. The package is ~15,000 won which includes the material of making 3 pieces of soap and the final product wrapping stuff as well. It is a very good experience for ladies apart from shopping.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The three days of touring were really excellent. We saw so much, way more than we could have achieved if we just hired a car and drove ourselves. June was a very friendly and knowledgeable guide, and she continued to maintain a flexible approach throughout the tour, adjusting itineraries according to how we felt and how our kids were doing. She also chose some great lunch restaurants for us, based on our tastes, and we really enjoyed those lunch experiences in Korean restaurants with her.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The Cave was very different to other caves I have been to. It was like a Subway train tunnel. You can way approx 1 km of the reported 7km+ lava tube tunnel. Did have much of the usual Stalagmite and stalactite and crystal formations. The Lava tracks /grooves where interesting to me. But I was not a   Wow   experience.

The best way to experience nature and the beauty of Udo Island is not necessarily by being seperated by metal and a loud motor, but it sure is fun!  One of our best days while on vacation was riding the ferry to Udo and renting ATV's to tour around the island.

Taking a quick ferry ride will bring you to a breathtaking place called Udo Island. Rocky coasts, beautiful beaches, and crystal clear waters are what you will find on this little farming and fishing island. I decided to rent a bike on my trip and wander around the coastline. In my opinion, it was the best way to see the island. Amazing photo opportunities and tons of places to get some fresh seafood along the way. The clear and shallow water is great for children to play in. Tons of little tidal pools as well. Biking allowed you to be outside and experience the people and the culture of the island. It is probably not a place for people that do not enjoy the outdoors or those that are afraid of a little bit of exercise!

Such a beautiful place where I experienced peace of mind and heart. Reading how Bunjae and our lives are quite parallel really made me think twice about nature and how we should cherish it as if it was our own lives. The quote that I will keep with me forever is   Potted plants wither when their roots are not trimmed, and people age when they do not change their ways of thinking  . Thank you for providing a space for people to learn and reflect on life amongst nature. God bless.

Put your rented car on neutral going   uphill   and experience it. Mysterious probably because for most it?s a baffling experience having your car in neutral but going uphill, backwards or forward ? hands off the wheel and feet off that pedal. The place is on the way to Jusangjeolli by way of the Mount Halla route from Jeju town. 5-10 minutes (no crowd here) and you have covered one of the ?touristy? sites in Jeju. A woman attempted to see what would happen with a plastic water bottle placed on the road, nothing did.  Why would any vehicle with so much metals built into it got pulled but not a plastic bottle? Go figure. I have encountered a similar experience at a site in Saudi Arabia near Madinah which has a longer stretch for that ?mysterious? experience.

Our driver/tour guide took us here on the way back to the hotel. Actually, he said it was his first time there as well. My 17-year old son and I felt the uphill rolling and it was a weird feeling. Not sure why it was doing it, but we saw some tourists pouring water on the pavement and watching the water rolling uphill. Many years ago, I took my son to a similar   mystery road   in Manzanillo, Mexico. Back then, may be he was too young to feel it, or may be I was a terrible tour guide, but this time he finally got it. So, it was fun for us to take the quick detour and had some laughs.  Oh, and it was free and there are road signs tell you how to experience the   mystery  .

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

My own experience was during dark, and I loved it. There was a spotlight highlighting the rock. Relax listening to the waves coming from the sea to the shore. On the way here I recommend walking through Yongyeon bridge.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.

Located an easy walk from the Seogwipo Harbor, these waterfalls and surrounding area are quite pretty, and certainly worth the easy, pleasant walk to see them. It was only 2,000 won to enter the are, and about a 5 minute walk to the actural waterfall. As someone who loves swimming in natural water, I was a little disappointed, because you can't really swim here. It was quite crowded (when I went in early August), so all my photos are full of other people. It wasn't necessarily a beautiful nature experience, so in that way a bit underwhelming, but again, worth a look.

Just another market but in a different city. Similar in most ways.However, a distinct difference here is the huge amount of Jeju oranges (tangerines) on sale. Not just here but in other markets in Jeju too.Also it is common to see roadside trucks & makeshift stalls selling oranges - everywhere.Jeju is well known for its oranges , probably it's the season now. But they aren't exactly cheap despite the abundance of supply.We went to a nice Tangerine Orchard Farm right here in Jeju, where we paid 5,000?? admission fee per pax. And one can eat as much oranges as you want for unlimited time while at the Orchard.After which, every pax is entitled to pick/bring back 1kg free. Great experience & deal.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

June was a lovely guide - she speaks English very well, and is knowledgeable and patient. There was no problem adjusting the itinerary at short notice. Meals were varied and delicious, and catering for allergies was not a problem. She went out of her way to make sure we had a great experience, and we had great chats about kayaking and k-dramas. 감사 합니다 June 씨!

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

It's good place for experience the local community which they will arrange the local guide whom live tin the village to give you the informations and details about the village including the history and culture. There's the translator for the local people since they are hardly speak other language besides Korean. They will explain the way they hand the wooden stick at the gate. The meaning of the stone statue. They will have to room the tell us their history and story. They will have a village walk so everyone can see and experiences their village including photo shooting. They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. The Omecha is sticky so need to mix with water for drinking and contain a lot of vitamins. The local guide will try to up sales their local products after tour such as Omecha and horse bone. They make the bone into small pills and they said its good for those whom need calcium or need recovery from injury and also good for the growth of young kid. They also sell dried squids which already mix with sauce before dried it. It's a good experience as the village is very unique. The house is only one floor and low ceiling since Jeju is very windy. The wall also made with the lava stone from the hallasan mountain.Avoid to go during rainy day even they provide the umbrella during the walk but it's not convenience at all.

It's a new experience to us. It's great. Just walk inside the maze until you find the way. Maybe try and get help from your friends who have reached the tower. It's a great activity. Got some traditional games to play as well. There are lots of big fat cats at the ticketing counter. So cute, so fluffy.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.
Interesting place, walk in a lave tube & learn about formation along the way. it was very interesting experience. P/S Please wear shoe.

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

If you?re driving around Jeju Island, this place is a must. It took me a while to figure out what was the big deal (mysterious) about this road but after I figured out the way it was described to be, it was definitely cool and somewhat mysterious. So here it goes: you drive upto the starting point of mysterious road and put the car in neutral gear. The road certainly looks like and uphill, however the car drives forward until 100m to the end of the mysterious road. Anti-gravity huh? I?m not sure of the scientific explanation for this phenomenon, but I recommend you experience this if you?re driving around Jeju Island. Takes only 15 minutes and certainly worth the time and experience!

If you want to come here to buy Innisfree products, the offering are far lesser than what you can find in Myeongdong. The only attraction here is the soap making experience and a small piece of tea plantation. There are no location-only products sold here. Very limited merchanise on sale. The staffs are unfriendly and always pulling a long face. Not worth visiting.

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was here with my family. Thinking what is so mysterious about this road? Its just a road, with nature on the sides. It?s just another ?normal? road. Sigh, a total waste of time.Until I reach the place, I was blown away! Not because of the strong wind (I was there when it was raining heavily with strong winds), but the mysterious part of this road. I was told to stay in the car, to witness the mystery of this road. The engine got turned off, hand brake was let gone, brakes were let gone too, the car automatically went up the slope by itself!It is a new experience here for me in Jeju, a totally worth of time to visit!

I think this will be a fun experience for the family especially with small kids. I am not young anymore but it was rather interesting and fun for me as well. Not as easy as I thought and it took me 30mins to navigate through...for price of 3300won, it is a pretty economical way to spend a few light hearted hours after all the serious geographical sights in Jeju.

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I believe this place can be so much fun then how we experienced it. We were there quite late, hence the volunteers (as the tour guides) were in an extreme rush to go home. Totally understandable. However they were still nice enough to show us around. Interesting historical facts about the Koreans in Jeju-do and their houses. They promoted horse face cream towards the end of the tour. Apparently the appropriate time to visit this place is between 11 am - 1 pm or definitely way BEFORE 4.30 pm.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

For the last day of our Jejueco tour, the first attraction we visited in the morning was Jeongbang waterfall. Situated on a high cliff by the sea, Jeongbang waterfall is the only waterfall in Asia to fall into the sea. Admission fee is 2,000 won for individuals and 1,600 won per person if you are in a group of 10 or more.When we finally reached our destination, to actually get up-close to Jeongbang waterfall, we had to walk down some (more) steep steps and make our way over a field of rocks/boulders. It was a pretty slippery (and uneven) walk, so make sure you wear footwear with good grip. But the walk was worth it: the sight of the waterfall emptying itself right into the sea which makes it a pretty unique and amazing (since we don?t really have such waterfalls in Singapore).For more photos and our Jeongbang Waterfall experience, do check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jeongbang-waterfall.html :)

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

cool experience and worth to visit if you on the way to visit other attraction because its on the way to other place, But if you just come and just for  visit this mysterious way its not worth because its nothing to do there just an empty road.

Chose to visit this attraction because it is UNESCO world heritage site. I and my kids went into the cave, make our way to the lava column, took some photos, then u-turn to make our way out. Nothing to see unless you are a geological fan. It is OK, just another   for the experience   trip.

Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.? The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.? The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.? The calm music playing enhanced the experience.? The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.? Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

As the name implies, this is a street of restaurants offering black pork that is cooked in front of you. Basically, same offerings per restaurant with a lot of free side dishes (fish cake is a staple). Pork ranges fro thinly sliced to a little bit thicker. Flavorful, smoky but surprisingly, when you get out of the restaurant, the smell of cooking does not stick with you (unlike our experience back home). Way so much better than what we have in our home country as this is authenticity in the real sense of the word. We only tried 2 restaurants since we were only there for 2 nights, Dombedon and Donhyanggi. Both were ok. But I like Donhyanggi better.

Arrived around 4pm and bought 4 tickets...2,000?? for adults and 1,000?? for children. That's about $5-6 USD. It was 90 degrees outside but cool and refreshing inside. At the start it was 50F and got colder as we got deeper. If you get cold easily, you should bring a light jacket. I would wear shoes because it's a bit wet and rocky but I saw many people walk through with sandals and slippers. It's about a 25 minutes one way. It is pretty well lit for a  tunnel/cave. There's no climbing or steep terrain except for the way down but there are handrails. You will enjoy the experience. It's informative as well.

Was recommended by the people at my resort to visit this place. Reason being it is very clean. I did not do too many hikes in Jeju and this was just one of the few I did. It was a small forest garden owned by a family and now looked after by the 2nd generation daughter.She gave us a brief intro in English of the forest. One that actually does not have soil and one that offers a different season from what it actually should be.Unfortunately we did not experience this difference in season while in the forest. But we just enjoyed walking around this small forest garden admiring the trees that have sprout out.A good walk if the true forest hike may be too much to bear

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.

Was really excited when going up the crater as this place is one of the UNESCO heritage site. Upon reaching the entrance was a really beautiful place as it was well maintained. The hike is gradual, suitable for kids and elderly.However upon reaching the peak, it just looks like a patch of green field on the crater, nothing impressive at all. I guess it's just for the experience.

The hike was an easy one with stairs. Less than one hour slow pace hiking up. My brother brought his baby as well in baby carrier. There are a lot of souvenir shops nearby. In my experience, the souvenir sold there is much cheaper than the one in Jeju City.

Suggest to start early, before 7am. We started at 7am, and managed to reach the summit before 1pm, but had to descend before 1.30pm. Took a total of 10 hours, up and down. If I can do the hike, anybody else can too, for a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Remember to do proper warm-up before starting and bring along enough water to hydrate yourself. Proper hiking shoes are important and hiking sticks are definitely helpful.

Jeju is famous for hiking and its Olle walking routes, chosen to hike in Hallasan National Park as part of our itinerary. My first hiking experience in oversea and it is an unforgettable experience I ever had. Fantastic !

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.
For hikers this place was the good spot, but for some who doesn't like hiking you can still take pictures specially during winter and experience the snow.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.
We passed a couple of hours here enjoyably.? It's a museum-lite type of experience. Very close to a few cafes/convenience stores and other attractions in the area.

We came at night about 8pm after having dinner at a nearby noodles restaurant. And was the last to leave the museum. It takes about an hour plus to fully explore the huge facility. While it was really cool that we didn't have to worry about our silly poses and waiting in line (quiet at this time) we also realised that there was no one to help the both of us take couple shots for some poses. However we still enjoyed ourselves very much. Perhaps it'll be better to arrive 7pm for a better experience.

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

The park will appeal more for kids rather than adults. The train ride provides a nice experience and there are some attractions in the park that caters for children. The tour in the park took us about 3 hours to finish.

Out of our surprise no entrance fees needed when you visit Jeju Folk museum. There was a guide that told us about their culture and was a nice experience for us and even the kids. The village was small but a nice encounter. An hour is more than enough.
Never been to such museum before so it was a very fun experience. Spent about 2 hours here taking tonnes of pictures. Feel like i'm 15 yrs old again. A must visit for the young at heart!

It was unfortunate that the immersion tour group was delayed in setting out on a one hour journey to this natural heritage centre that we were not allowed to visit the 5 lava tubes. However the 4D film of a little boy 's adventure on this island more than made up for the disappointment of not visiting the lava tubes. It would have been a great trekking experience to the lava tubes from the museum exhibits & brochures ... perhaps it warrants another visit to this island?

In Jeju  we had the opportunity to visit the Jeju Art Museum & Glass Castle  which is a theme park featuring an exhibition hall  garden and models made entirely of glass. One must spent at least two hours or more to walk around the indoor and outdoor areas. Nearby the entrance  there is a display ?쏥lass Worldwide??and the countries that produced glass are mentioned here - China  Italy  Czech Republic  Arab and Japan. Once you step indoor  a large glass beanstalk from the fairytale ?쏪ack & the Beanstalk??will greet visitors.The world's largest all-glass labyrinth  glass ball  glass diamond  a glass stonewall  mirror lake and a glass bridge are found in the model parks here. In one part of the outdoor theme park are Cinderella's glass slippers and a glass carriage. One will be held in awe at the marvellous pieces of art  all made entirely out of glass! Truly an eye opening experience!

If you visit Jeju especially Seogwipo you don't want to miss to visit here. With entrance ticket KRW 9000 you can see and take photos of many art galleries in 3D. It's a fun experience. So many photos you could take in this big museum it's too bad that I only spent about 2 hours in here because I didn't have much time then. I suggest to visit this museum in the morning and prepare to spend 3-4 hours in here. I visited here at noon and it's a bit crowded with people.

I was alone but it was really great. The only negative thing that nobody took pictures of me. The place is huge so you better have 2-3 hours time if you want to visit every place. And the audio guide really helps and it costs only about $2. And we can experience a few things in there like wood crafting or wearing hanbok or playing traditional game. In weekdays the have train service which you can ride for free.

I have been to many traditional folk villages in Korea but this Jeju Folk Village is one of the most beautiful folk villages in Korea. If you are a fan of the Korean drama Dae Jang Geum also known as Jewel in the Palace you should visit this folk village as it is one of the filming locations of that Korean drama.Also I highly recommend renting a hanbok to take beautiful pictures by walking around the village. We had only 2 hours to explore but it wasn?셳 enough to cover the whole folk village. Here you can experience a unique activity ??to read comics and even play games on mini arcade machines in a traditional house.

Great for experiencing traditional Korean Culture. I recommend around 2~3 hours there. It's quite big and there's a lot to see and experience. We went there during the first weeks of October and it was very green and lush. I think in summer and spring it's gonna be even more pretty. Different types of Korean housing and different lifestyle (farmer student worker etc.) are portrayed very well and the tools they used are there to see. There is also a convenience store near the entrance which doesn't work with cash.

Great attraction to be included onto your Travelling plan. It provides insight to the natives lives in the early days and you can experience by checking some of the house yourself by going in and take a rest. Entry is 10000 won and tour takes about 2-3 hours if you check out all the places. Don't miss the donkey black pigs and cows.
Good experience and a cooling walk underground. I was expecting something more and was disappointed when reached the end. Took about an hour.
Estimate to spend 2 hours. wear good shoes and jacket. The cave is quite cold and wet. Uneven roads and required to walk on few staircase too. but overall experience is great.

Bored?  Run out of things to do for the evening?  this is good for about an hour's worth of entertainment.  Visit with low expectations and your experience will be improved.As others have stated the statues are redundant and some are just kind of creepy (fat lady in her panty with a skinny undersized man).  The high note are the dioramas depicting different sexual acts.Not only do they look accurate but they also look very cute.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .

When we have a summer vacation in Jeju, it was one of must see.  If you want to visit, visit when it is magic hour (golden hour). The sky makes perfect blue color. It was very good place especially for children. They had experience in making necklace with glass. The sculptures in the Glass Castle were beautiful.  Visit with children. It is good place for children.

We really enjoyed Udo. It's a small little island located about 30 minutes(ferry ride) off of Jeju. We got to the island with only about three hours before the last ferry was going to leave, so we wanted to pack in all that we could. First, we got some peanut ice cream. Then, we rented bicycles and tooled around the island's coast. It was beautiful and several times as I took in the sights, I kept thinking,   How cool is this? How many people I know will ever get to have this experience?   It was a neat feeling to be exploring a quaint and little-known spot in the world. We found a little beach and cooled off before heading back to the ferry.

We hired bicycles at a shop adjacent the pier and cycled around the whole island. Along country roods, there were many scenic spots, mostly adjacent to the sea,  where we could take pictures. Besides, there were many cafes and kiosks where we could dine and rest.  Cycling around the island in a relaxing pace took about 3 to 4 hours. It was a very good experience.

We arrived at 3:30 on Udo, and rented 2 electric scooters from a stand close to the dock. It was a bummer that i couldn't rent a real scooter (you need to bring your int. license btw). It was a lot slower, so it gave us more time to have a more relaxing ride. We visited 2 beaches, and both of them were very clear and very clean (Beware of silver fish though깎).
