Also, you wouldn't want to miss haha hoo because my friend told me they're incredibly popular. We got some peanut ice cream, and some tea with honey and the special jeju fruit that i can't name (which was absolutely incredible!!!) since everything else was sold out. I would have loved to spend more time there because we only got 3 hours on Udo. In all, it was an amazing and memorable experience.

Visited this place as part of a tour group, and spent slightly under an hour at this place There are a total of 3floors to explore, starting with a history tour to the current entertainment scene today. Several interactive booths and kiosks allow you to experience things such as singing, makeups and dancingAnd of course you can take photos of all these experiences

Visited at about 4pm, 2 hours before its closing time, however everything was still available. We tried out the DIY soap making and bath bomb making, which cost 15 000 won each. Do remember to bring along your passport, as you can get a tax refund too. The DIY sessions were very fun, and a great experience for children.The Innisfree House was although small, it is very well-maintained and therapeutic. It sells a range of Innisfree products, mostly for face and skin care. The cafe drinks and desserts were great as well, and definitely worth a shot if you?셱e there for tea break.

This is a nice place for sightseeing and exploring the Jeju waterfalls. There was a roughly 5-10 minutes walk before reaching the waterfall, which was fairly simple and pleasant too. The waterfall does not differ greatly from your other waterfalls, so if you?re looking for a unique and different sightseeing experience, I suggest giving this a miss. However, it was still quite magnificient and beautiful if you enjoy sightseeing and waterfalls. Overall, do spend about an hour here to leisurely stroll and sightsee this Jeju wonder.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

Seriously, just go UDO island to experience a different feel as the island is quite small. I managed to complete a circle with my rental vehicle within 1-2 hours. There's quite a lot of spots that you can get down and walk. (fuel will drain quite a lot as there's quite a number of up-slope)

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. Spend 3 hours there.Suggest to go for a toilet break before going thru the entrance.Bring baby carriers, cause the road is uneven. Have to be extra careful especially going with kids.There are 2 entrance. (follow the counter clock wise direction, where the entrance is situated behind the huge ship)Enjoy the scenery, watchout for the waves too.Their is a canola flower field where you can take some instagram photos too (need to pay to enter)

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.
If you wanna experience to swim in the ocean and in the volcanic water, this is the place. You hire the spot for couple of hours and until 6.

I think it was unfortunate that it rained the day we went. The grounds were muddy. The kids were having fun. The adults were grumpy. Thankfully, we were prepared with umbrellas and raincoats. Still, the kids' shoes got all muddy and we had other places to go to after this. So, not the most pleasant of experiences. But to be fair, the maze is challenging enough to provide good fun for about an hour or so.

I say this one should not be missed, just because there are not a lot of lava tubes that exist and are easily accessible! The whole journey from the mouth of the cave to the lava column, and back, can be done in an hour. Walking thru the varying sizes of the tube, some areas narrow and some really big with high ceilings, is a spectacular experience! The largest lava column in the world, towards the end of the permissible distance, is a little underwhelming. Still, overall a great visit. Highly recommended when in Jeju.

First time in a cave, so I really enjoyed the experience and learning about the history of the formation of the cave and Jeju island itself. Its a UNESCO site also, which gives the site a more special reason to visit. Be careful as the surface can be slippery, but in general the walk can take about over an hour.

Experiencing the Jeju Mysterious Road was cool for a few minutes. But that's about it.If you're gonna drive a few hours just to see it, I'd say just look for another attraction. But if it's just near you, go ahead and experience it.

Dongmun wet and dry market show lots of fish and seafood. One shop inside provides local korean food even Running man visited before. Jeji mandarin can be purchased by box. Small souvenirs are sold. If you want local experience, 2 to 3 hours walk can be arranged.

Definitely the most fun I have in the island. Not that I didn't have fun in other attractions however I just love how everything they got in this attraction is an interactive one. I have the chance to watch GD's hologram concert as well here, they have one hologram concert every one hour. It's fun! Oh, and if you're a VIP this place is a must visit. Their gift shop offers some selection of VIP merchandises, from Krunk, snapback hats and VIP's light stick.The entry ticket is 15.000 won if I'm not wrong, but it is definitely worth every bucks you spend. There's a dancing room, a 360 degree 3D experience, you can even take pictures with your favorite Kpoppers using their hologram tech.

Bought the tickets online to enjoy a discount. We arrived early to be amongst the first cars within the car park. Thus, we had a fuss free horse riding experience for the kids. The 50mins performance was also enjoyed by the kids. Unfortunately, the go karting wasn?t available due to rain a few hours before.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!
The place is well kept and there was a lovely souvenir shop on site. There is not much to see in this part of Jeju so climbing up this rock was definitely an uplifting experience.

I?ve visited many waterfalls during my travels but this one is unique as it is not located within a lagoon or by a river or along a forest but this is one that goes out to the ocean!! A unique experience for me :)Definitely no swimming here but you can actually walk up close to the foot of the waterfalls for pictures and such. Wear comfortable shoes as there is a significant amount of steps to climb up and down.

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

This is quite possibly the most beautiful spot on the island-- definitely worth the small entrance fee (I think it was about 7000 won for my family of 5). There are some fairly serious steps to get down the cliff, and then to actually get close to the falls, it's necessary to climb across a bunch of small/medium rocks. Most people will have no problems with either, but for someone with knee or foot problems it could be an issue.The only thing I didn't love was that it was SO crowded. It was impossible to get a decent photo without someone walking into the frame, and several times we were actually shoved off of rocks as more and more people tried to crowd in. It would be great if they would limit the amount of people allowed down at one time.Other than that-- a great experience that we definitely won't forget.

Our guide brought us here to see the 10-inch snow... we came from tropical climate you see...So there is no climbing for us, but the snow was fun for the kids as it was their first experience...they were so happy making snowballs and we took some really great pictures here.
just climbing up in darkness is an experience by itself. wear good shoes, warm clothes, water and some munchies. take your time coming down and enjoy the scenic beauty.

If you want to see sunrise, please go to Seongsan Ilchulbong: It's very beautiful place. You should wake up in the early morning. It'll take 20 mins to climb in the peak. And you can experience excellent atmosphere there. You can take lots of picture because of its beauty. Good luck to you, hope you can see sunrise in the Seongsan Ilchubong

I found this waterfall a better experience than Cheonjiyeon Falls as you can go very close to the waterfall. Be prepared to walk down a lot of stairs and then climb over rocks to get close to the falls, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Don't bother paying for the museum close to the gate, it's a waste of time but only 500 Won if you want to.

Well if an already successful huge company invest in something new it can't go too wrong. I expected this place to be more authentic but what we got was a commercialized sugar-coated tea plantation experience. Nonetheless the place is very professional of course the quality is great and both the tea and desserts are yummy. The surroundings are beautiful the air is fresh and the scent of the plantation is amazing. It's a safe choice if you prefer a guaranteed good time over something unexpected and little bit more unique. It's a sophisticated modern place that reminds me more of a spa than a tea house. Regardless you can buy good quality tea here and some other gifts that comes in beautiful packages. All in all we had a good time!

We went for the cake n ice-cream. We went there around 430pm the house close at 6pm. Be there early as by the time we queue and order the cake is sold out. Disappointed and in the end only had the ice-cream.Tried the box of 10 sachets instant green tea cafe latte it's very smooth and rich. Recommended. The green tea too. The aroma is totally different. Worth a visit for your tea experience. The ambiance is lovely too a lot of photo scene surrounding.
we hired taxi for a-day trip this is the last sightseeing in jeju.totally enjoy the fun experience and fill up the puzzle.must visit once in a life time.

We had an amazing time here at the spirited garden! There are so many beautiful trees to see and the people are lovely! It really felt like a spiritual experience. I felt so at peace while I was here. The citron tea was amazing and helped so much after I got a cold teaching my kids! Loved it and want to come back again!

We did only this folk village with my family and friends. This recreated the feeling of living a long time ago in korea it communicates well the differences of different backgrounds. We did not hire the audio guide and we had two korean speakers with us who were able to read everything. It was fabulous for my kids to see and touch most of the displays plenty to keep them occupied. We saw a dance and others getting photos taken in wedding costumes and a Korean Drama being filmed. Overall the experience was a good cultural morning out. We did not eat there as we were meeting friends for lunch but it looked very traditional
Very Nice place also very cold and we have a lot experience at this place..it is the 1st time i n my family go to the best place at jeju

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.

this is the place to go for food and shopping when at Seogwipo. The market is pretty huge to walk  see and experience the everyday routines of those worked there as well as the regular stream of tourists that makes the place crowded and noisy. if you stay around Seogwipo  chances is you will be there at least once or every evening for did or to pass time. take time to go around the entire interior with multiple lanes with as well as the outside shops. You might just find interesting things to see and get something you like.

This is first time we experienced a visit to a Green Tea plantation. Walking between the rows & rows of beautifully layed out fragrant tea leaves was just great.The cafe sells nice Green Tea ice creams & cakes plus tea leaves products obviously.An Innisfree shop sells the famous Korean cosmetics plus a small cafe included.Certainly this is an attraction that should not be missed when in Jeju.

The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.

So this was my fourth time visiting Jeju and so far this is the best experience i had. Mr. Kang was not only kind but also reliable. He took us to places we have planned and gave other ideas where we should go. My friends and I had a lot of fun during the trip. Both car and van were clean and comfortable; most importantly had wifi. Oh and he speaks English too. Definitely will contact him when I visit Jeju again :)

It was our first time riding a horse.Strict instructions were given not to make sudden noises when riding as the frightened horses will go crazy & will cause serious injury to riders.All handphones/sling bags are not allowed too.Each rider gets to choose a hat & were matched to horses according to height.The horses walked unguided on a short (about 5 mins) fenced circuit. About 100 metres near the finish point the horses suddenly start galloping slowly.It was not easy to balance oneself on a horse holding just 2 grips on the saddle while it was galloping. We were concerned for that moment if we will fall off & was also wondering what happened to the horse. This was probably the scary part of uncertainty.It was a good experience though it was a short ride. At least now we know how it was to ride a horse.

It was my first time walking through a lava cave which was an enjoyable experience. I appreciated the natural formation of the tubes and to think that lava once flowed through was exciting. Others might think it's just a cave and the first few meters is the same throughout which is fair enough but I loved it.
It is one of a few place with optical illusion on the slop of the road. First time seen this kind of scene.If anyone had any experience at other country. I guess it is just the same.

I visited Jeju Folk Village on my last day of my trio to Jeju. Jeju Folk Village is a place where the traditional culture of Jeju and the history of the Korean language since the 1890s the late Joseon Period Dinasty are well preserved in their original state. You can experience Folks Customs Life Folk games Crafts and Traditional Folk events. I recommend to visit if you have time. Last day of the trip can be perfect because you can relax and go back home with a good feeling.

I love exploring new places that require strength and Yongmeori Coast is absolutely that place! We got a chance to try seafood straight from the sea and it was pretty good for me since I'm not a big fan of raw seafood. We had a fantastic time there because we enjoyed the sea while eating seafood and had an experience that only Jeju can provide for us!

I found the second part of the drive more interesting and mysterious. The second part is having the car on neutral and it mysteriously reversing. You have to experience it for yourself! Doesn't take too much time of your day.

Had a great time and I?m not even a k pop fan. Lots of interactive things that kept it interesting and ended up buying a souvenir. You have to go to the holographic concert as it was a really rewarding experience. Wish I could have spent more time here.
Good experience for kids. Cute lloking models of famous landmarks. Not very big so should not take a lot of time.

First time visiting a lava cave. It was nice and enjoyable as a couple hiking in the cave. There isnt much and just an experience and a place to spend some time. Go only if you have extra time on your hands.

Experience狩狩狩狩狩Time worth狩狩狩狩狩Good for photos狩狩狩狩狩The Dragon Head rock was formed through volcanic activity and the surrounding beach is covered in a thick layer of volcanic ash and rock. The whole area is beautiful and great for taking photos though not worth visiting again as it's more of a love at first sight thing

being a glass museum  it really contains everything glass. i love the art pieces and how intricate the details are and all  but if youre short on time  this place is worth a skip unless youre REALLY into glass. i would recommend however  trying the glass making pendant pieces though. its worth the price and experience.

Whether you love nature or not, I strongly recommend visiting this cave. There is so much to learn on how the lava tube was formed and it provides you with a unique experience that is unforgettable. Do wear proper covered shoes as you will be walking on rocks almost the entire time and some parts might be slippery.

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

We were with a tour group so we did not see all the attractions, and our time was limited the ones we did experience were interesting, caves & botanical spirit gardens were worth the trip.  I really liked the stones - fascinating.
We went February 2015 during winter time, It freezed to death but well worth experience. Recommended and must place visit in Jeju

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.
we followed the instruction but did not experience the results like others. so i am not sure if the   mysterious road effect   is reproducible all the time

We enjoyed the experience of transversing the rocks to get to the falls. It can be a challenge though with young children. The feel of water vapour sweeping through your face and sitting close to the falls was great. I can't compare it with the other nearby falls as we didn't have time to visit those but we were satisfied with this fall. While heading out, there are a few hawkers selling stuff and bought boxes of Jeju chocolates and biscuits at really good price.

Visited this place as part of a tour package. Its horrible. Phototaking opportunities are limited. The guide there spent 10mins running through various aspects of the village and the other 30mins hard-selling their honey, horse oil and supplements. Horrible experience and an utter waste of time.

Though pork is my least preferred meat option, I decided to try due to its popularity. I first headed to the Dombedon restaurant, but was told the minimum order is for 2 person. Not willing to eat and pay for double portions, I chose the restaurant just across the street.I ordered a set pork belly for 18,000 won. The waiter, a Vietnamese student, spoke great English. He demonstrated to me how to use the leaf to wrap the side dishes together with the pork. My pleasant surprise was the free cold noodles in soup.  Overall, it was a great experience for first time dining. As for the black pork, I felt it was over hyped as it tasted no better than the typical roast pork in Asia. Once is enough for me.

This waterfall is easily accessible in south Jeju Island with spacious parking lot at entrance.  Entrance fee is 2000 won, reasonable and worth a visit.  We arrived around 4:50pm and was just in time to watch the sun set there.  If you want to get closer to the waterfall, be prepared to get a slightly wet but it?s a great experience.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!

There are a lot of shops and many things to buy, but they are repeated a lot of the time. There are a lot of fish and a lot of fruit. Then you also find some other goods as well. Very nice experience and one can buy a lot of souvenirs

The Mysterious road is really mysterious to me! As my friend and I booked a taxi for the day, we still had time on our hands before the day ends, so the taxi driver took us to this road and off his engine. Next thing we know, the car was moving on its on up the slope. Talk about creepy. Can't know what scientific explanation there could be behind this. If you are travelling by car and will pass by here, by all means, experience the wonder.

The experience is new and the music is nice. However, I go bored after some time because I am not a art person and do not quite grasp what the artists are trying to express. Driving through narrow road to get there.

The dragon head rock is in North part of Jeju, close to the airport. It is a rock that looks like a dragon head on the coast. The Seogwipo coast line like the Jusanjeolli Cliff or the Odelgae Rock are much more interesting than this. However, if you do not have time to visit the Jungmun/Seogwipo area, this is an alternative to see the rocky coastline. The sunset here is nice, but the place is packed with tourists fighting to get photos, so it's not all that romantic. I think a beach sunset at a more remote beach on the West side would be nicer and a calmer experience.
Superb place to go there. Check the cliff, if you have never experienced before. Spend time as much as you wish. Nice place to go.

So we are sat in the car, put on neutral mode and the car actually moved! This is a really cool experience and it only takes a minute to do- I have seen mysterious roads on the travel channel before but this was my first time doing it- if you find yourself on Jeju island check it out!

Service狩狩狩狩狩Experience狩狩狩狩狩Value for money狩狩狩狩狩Highly recommendedFolk village was great and authentic but the guide was probably the best attraction. Their honey is 100% natural and can cure a variety of ailments. Their umija tea is very sweet and bound to be a favourite for young kids. Highly recommended for tourists with kids.

Second time here with another friend. More time this round to walk leisurely.As said in the title, no wow, OMG thing inside you'll find unless probably you are an geologist, etc. The most memorable is probably the experience of walking on very uneven, ripply hardened lava ground spotted with many puddles in near total darkness through low and tall ceiling of an underground tunnel.

Real value for money being able to see he best of Jeju in the short time we had on the island. Our tour guide, Jin, was excellent and walked us through the itinerary adding in stories about the history of the island and his own experiences. Highly recommended.

Overall  the glass museum was a good experience. Everyone ranging from my 4 year old to my 70 mother found something to   ohhh   and   ahhhhh   about. My little one especially liked going through the   forest   with the glass mushrooms  butterflies  and lanterns. Our visit to Jeju Island for a wellness retreat was organized by Core Travels who did an amazing job. They were accommodating, flexible warm and kind and did their best ensure we had the best time possible. From the local food experience, the sightseeing and the transport it was all amazing.
On sunny day, beautiful rainbow and  really blue sea you can see. you need to walk down some steps, but it is valuable experience to take time and effort.you don't want to miss it ^^

Mr. Lee was an excellent tour guide! On time for both full day tours, patient and takes great pictures! As a solo traveler this was a wonderful experience in Jeju island mostly because of Mr. Lee. I did both East and West coast tours with him. Car is comfortable and very clean! He was very flexible with the itinerary and squeezed in his favorite waterfall in Jeju my last day! He was awesome and I highly recommend this tour to explore Jeju!

Mind your step! The cave is long, dark and slippery. This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience.The price is reasonable. A number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing.

Just like everyone already mentioned, the road is indeed mysterious as the car would really move uphill on its own. However, it is only a very short stretch of the road. But I would still recommend it if you are self-driving and it's your first time in Jeju. Definitely, something you have to experience.You can also head to the museums that is nearby too after going to this road.

I loved this place! My kids found the raw seafood smell a bit overbearing but they managed. I loved all the fresh seafood, vegetables & fruit along with all the kimchi & spices! This is a place to come to for locals & an experience for visitors. I wish our community had such a place as this. I would be shopping here all the time!

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Hamdeok is perhaps the most popular beach in Jeju but this was the first time I visited the island on summer during peak season. The beach is packed with families who took advantage of the low tide during the day (about ~30cm of water in a 50m stretch, at least on two weeks while was there) and let the kids in the water for a very enjoyable and risk-free time at the ocean.However I was surprised by the amount of   lifeguards   there. They will drag a security rope marking a no-swin zone after it starts getting   deep   (just after the water reaches your chest) which ok its a security measure specially with so many kids, but for adults who want to take a dip is horrible. They will start blowing their whistle and order you to go back even though half my body was above water.But the worst part is that they -- the lifeguards -- place beach umbrellas all across the beach and charge you ??20000 (~20USD) to open and use them! It's already very weird that the lifeguards are also operating a rental service at the beach, but thing is they will NOT allow you to sit anywhere near them without paying (even not using the damn umbrellas) unless you look foreigner (white) so they don't loose face. I don't so I got reprimended like if was a Korean and they wouldn't leave my side until I moved.Isn't the beach a public space? This didn't happen just once but every day during my time there, overall an awful experience due to these threatening and autoritharian lifeguards.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Getting close to the waterfalls looks easier than it seems. However, that adds to the thrill of getting nearer to mother nature. It is tricky manuvering around the wet, slippery & sometimes unstable rocks & boulders in cold weather. Many a times, you find yourself balancing precariously on the boulders or have your feet stuck between the rocks as you slip or slide from the smooth rocks. You will also find visitors around you lending you a hand to help you get back on your feet. Such spontaneous camaraderie !  For the young & agile, it is fun watching them jumping from rock to rock, like Tarzan in action.  It is a thrilling on the rocks experience not to be missed !  And you get rewarded by the beautiful sight & sound of a great waterfall!

For those visiting this cave expecting amazing cave formations you may be disappointed. On Jeju island all caves are more accurately defined as lava tubes. These vestiges from Jeju's volcanic origins are strange, dark, and geological wonders.Tips for visitors, expect Manjang Cave to be cold, dark, and rough surfaces to walk on. NO sandals or high heels! Hiking boots are a far better option. If you come into the lava tube expecting glittering cave formations you may not have a great time. However, if you want to explore a truly rare geological wonder, take this journey into the darkness to enjoy a unique experience.

Beautiful, peaceful, such an amazing experience. First time on jeju and it is def a place you must go and see. Mr. Sung is adorable and kind hearted

Absolutely beautiful place - a must-see-experience if you go to Jeju. Amazing what nature can create and then its just next to a mountain and a small temple with a giant gold-Buddha. Go see this asap! :)

The first impression and experience was good. After a while, everything else looked the same. The same sea, mountains and stones, albeit in a different formation. There are beach bikes for rent, which I think will be fun but we didn't enjoy that because we had hired a taxi for the Jeju trip.

A trip to Jeju's and S. Korea's highest mountain is a refreshing experience. It is still nice and cool in the morning up here but no snow in late May. Oh well, may plan a winter trip back here for a more thrilling and chilling experience!

Went there last week on my trip to Jeju. Its a local market where you can find shopkeepers selling almost everything. From souvenirs to sea food. And stuff is pretty cheap too. Visit once to experience the local flavour and to collect some stuff to take back
We rented a car in jeju and decided to experience the mysterious road. It was amazing how your car rolls backwards when it looks like an uphill road. A must visit place if you are in jeju.

Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. But dont be under the impression that it will be hot in there. It is very cold inside and be prepared with the winter clothing and a trekking shoes. It was a long walk and a nice experiences. Spectacular experience whereby you got to walk one kilometer in and walk back the same distance. It is the longest lava tube in the world. Very interesting experience.

My wife and I visited this road last year during our 4 days tour of Jeju. It was a good experience but once is enough. Jeju is a really wonderful island to visit and we will definitely come back in the future
Experience the car to move backward even though you are not reversing the car. My kids and I enjoyed the experience.Worth it.

All in a single location. We could go back and learn of the past.  There were even live animals in the pens e.g. black pigs cows etc. The village was also the location of various Korean dramas. Visitors could enter into the huts and experience how simple life was in the past.

Actually it is pretty cool to walk through a lave tube. It will take you back through history. The texture of the stone walls and the actual size of the cave is mind-boggling. If you come from an area that doesn't have volcanos it is a real educational experience.

We came down here because like anyone and everyone who visits Jeju, they're told to go try black pork at one of the restaurants at Black Pork street in Jeju City. So we were in town (stayed in Seogwipo) and decided to go.However me and my partner both thought that the food is over hyped and isn't as great as it's made out to be. I even go on to think that majority of the pork they serve is from regular pork... for anyone that thinks they'll be able to tell the difference is lying. Much prefer traditional Korean BBQ with beef cuts as I much prefer beef as the pork is quite fatty.Still visit for the experience but wouldn't go again if I was to go back to Jeju.

Walking 2km (to the end of the section open to the public, and back) in a lava tube is a cold, dark and wet affair, but it's a unique and educational experience. The floor is very uneven and there are many puddles to step around. There's not a whole lot to see, but every now and then, features of a lava tube are highlighted and explained. This is not for everyone but if you can appreciate that it's rare to get the chance to walk through a lava tube, go for it. Just be ready for the slightly challenging conditions

Visited Manjaggul Cave because it was a UNESCO Natural site, like Seongsan Ichulbong.  Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

Nothing fanciful but definately interesting.We were at night with minimal cars so our driver being a fun guy did it with the car facing front, then backwards.

This museum is intended for tourists who love to take photos. Most of the artworks housed in the museum are modified versions of original paintings so that you can integrate with the painting. Hence bringing a camera or a smartphone is a must! A companion is also a must since taking a   selfie   to achieve the desired effect might prove to be impossible.This is one of the two 3D interactive museums in Jeju Island. The other one Trick Art Museum is located farther in the eastern part of the island. We went to this place as it is nearer to the Jungmun Area where most hotels (Hyatt Regency Shilla Hotel Lotte Hotel etc.) are located.Aside from the in-house artworks there is also a park with sculptures and play sets that will be appreciated by kids. Tips: avoid flash photography to get the desired effect; bring a jacket w/ hoodie (can be used in some of the artworks); and black pants make people blend better with the background.Admission costs KRW 8000 per person. The entire area is air-conditioned and wifi access is offered for free. Other extras include lockers to deposit your bags as this may hamper your experience.This is a fun destination for couples families or small groups.

This is a massive lava tube that the public are allowed to visit and does give you a real sense of the magnitude of the volcanic activity that created this island. For that alone you should visit.It is a nice cool 1km walk to the end and then, of course, you have to come back.A good experience.

When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

For most tourist spots, warm and clear weather are the best, but I did visit the cliffs on a stormy day, and it might have been even better. The cliffs are nice, but what truly made this an amazing experience was the stormy weather. The sea was agitated and waves were breaking on the on the cliffs, making for a truly dynamic and wild sight. The only drawback is that the cliffs do not go on and on (only for a couple of hundred meters) and there are few good vantage points. So the scale is not overwhelming.

Everything rolls backwards on that 50m of road! We tried it with our car without its engine, and then with a bottle of water.. It works all the same! Takes about 10 mins to experience it.. Seeing is Believing!

DRAMA WORLD is consist of DRAMA STUDIO, TEDDY BEAR and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE. Drama studio is an indoor exhibition hall with a floor area of 5,000 square meters. Drama studio is actual TV drama studio and restored studio in KOREA, USA and EUROPE, in which the visitors can experience all costumes and accessories for free(except HANBOK, Wedding dress). Our exhibition is consist of town(street) studio and interior studio. Our exhibition is consist of Korean studio(K-DRAMA) and World studio(USA,EUROPE DRAMA). Visitors of all age groups can experience KOREA culture, Western(USA) culture and The Middle ages(EUROPE) culture through DRAMA STUDIO. We are the first experiment-type drama studio in Korea where the visitors wear the costumes and use the articles to be the main character in dramas. ※ Now, World Studio is consist of TEDDY BEAR EXHIBITION and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE with a background of Western and The Middle ages studio. Collaboration between DRAMA WORLD and TEDDY BEAR. TEDDY BEAR Exhibition Hall’s floor area is about 1,000 square meters. At DRAMA WORLD, visitors can see TEDDY BEAR, which produced scenes in drama of Korea, USA and Europe. Visitors can easily understand the scene of drama. Because the text(Chinese, English, Korean)is placed in each display of TEDDY BEAR. Visitors can take a picture with man-sized TEDDY BEAR using props and wearing costume for free. Visitors can learn about the Self-Wedding culture of Korea through the Wedding photo zone with a background of drama studio. Visitors can take a picture in wedding photo zone on studio of the Western Age in USA, the Middle Ages in Europe and Korea’s drama. In each Wedding photo zone, wedding accessories are placed. And they are available for free.

As we booked for a tour package in Jeju ofcourse Mt. Hallasan will be on the list. Experiences the thin layer of snow on the park which is perfect for strolling, walk a couple of meters and go back. And yeah visit the museum to see some photo gallery. Its worth to see.

We visited in the peak of winter so there was very heavy snow fall.We came quiet under prepared in terms of walking gear so the walk to the crater was pretty difficult. I wouldn't recommend for elderly or anyone with mobility issues but this is from my experience with snow so can't comment on the difficulty during other seasons.

We came here thinking it was the jeju folk village but it was not. A lady came to us. She cannot speak English, then  she  showed us very quickly around pointing this and that. Mr Kim is a very friendly and experience driver who can speak some english and some mandarin. He recommended a good foods to us and we enjoyed it a lot, also very helpful in finding answer for our questions. Good service and hope

I went to Udo with a group of friends. It was really nice, we went around the island with rented bicycles (10.000 KRW for the afternoon). We swam in an incredibly clear water.I recommend going to Sunrise peak afterwards, walking along the coast gets you there in 15 min and seeing the sunset was an amazing experience.

I was there to lead a Sacred Circle Dance event in memory of the 4-3 Massacre, which was the most touching and powerful experience of group dance and solidarity. Excellent experience. Good Diver was able to hook me up with an American speaking   buddy  . She was very helpful and even though it was 2 years since my certification she helped me thru the process and was very patient on my dives.

We just came from Seoul and went to a market very similar to this one. I actually liked this one better because it was less crowded and I s able to actually take it all in. Definitely an interesting experience.
Traditional wet market that selling fresh food. You can experience Korean market full of the culture atmosphere and great food.
This is not a very big market but there are lots of authentic Korean food here for you to choose. It?s a good place to experience the local fare.Recommended place to go if you are in Jeju.

This is like any other market in Korea. Cheap shopping for clothes  bags  food and souvenirs. If haven't visited one of these markets  then I would go just to have the experience. Otherwise not a must see.

Interesting place. Lots of Tangerine in boxes as gifts and many stalls sell snacks and souveniors.Is also a wet market where you see fresh produce. Not forgetting display of pig heads can be found in serveral stalls. Can visit for the experience.

In this market you can get to see and experience various things. I spent 2-3 hr and had dinner here. There is one segment selling seafood and preserved food. Another segment selling snacks and souvenirs. My dinner was at the row of street side hawker that only open from 6pm onwards. The food is delicious and well priced. But don?t expect clean and nice place to sit and have your food. This is no 5 star street hawker.
I experienced a nice and reasonable seafood meal at this Dongmun market.The stall owner is friendly.

At there if you looking for almost all kind of cloth and cosmetic there you will love it! Because some brand name is there and almost is a fashion cloths there! For cosmetic is so many brand there start from Korea product will go to almost every brand in the world  and the area is just next from dongmon market ...and don't forget you are shopping at underground shopping centre not in a big mall because I will experience some poor service...have a great shopping
Interesting experience to walk around the local market, we are there early, not many stalls open yet and some preparing to open...
the waterfall is not huge but we can walk close to it. we saw 2 women selling raw seafood nearby which is a nice experience to have the sashimi near the sea.

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

Manjanggul Cave was a thoroughly interesting experience. The structure itself is awe inspiring and feels like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Be prepared for water droplets plopping on your head! It was a bit chilly when we visited as well.

I've never experienced such a crowded beach with such a small swimming area. I couldn't even get into the water... the lifeguards designated such a small section for swimmers it was like being at the most crowded uncomfortable public pool. The tables and chairs were extremely close together I really hated it here. There was a ton of water space to surf however so if that's your thing I suppose this beach is for you! Nonetheless this was the least relaxing beach I have ever experienced
It sets you with AWE where you could see the waterfall meeting the sea.  You could experience the good ion in the air and listening to the music of the sea.
It is a wonderful sight to visit.  The only problem being smokers who don't adhere to the laws and smoke anywhere.  Other than that it was a wonderful experience and very easy walk to the waterfall

I took the PADI Open water diving course with Good Diver. I am contend with the service they provided and thinking of getting my Advanced Openwater diver license with Gooddiver next month. It was an amazing experience. I felt comfortable during the whole course and could enjoy my first diving experience 100%. All the instructors were so patient that they made sure I was fully ready to descend and start the journey. I am so looking forward to diving again!
I prefer this waterfall for strolling about. It was a pleasant experience. Do expect a crowd as it was easily accessible and near to the city.

Came with my 80-year old dad and we had a slow walk along the uneven ground. Would recommend wearing waterproof as water drips fr the ceiling. It's is also a little chilly inside the tube (abt 8 degrees C) The place is also dim so some agility is needed to prevent slipping but it is generally safe. Just walk slowly. Overall it's an enjoyable experience as we marveled at the forces of nature that made the tube possible.
Bring half full water bottle and try to experience the car is moving uphill without engine running! Don't forget to give hazard signal when you try this experiment ;)
A long walk although only 1km. Inside cave at low temperature and water keep dripping. Experience the nature of the lava cave formed since 20000-30000 years ago would be something not to miss.

You will have to try it youself to experience it! Tried it with a water bottle but it doesn't work. Tried it with a car and shifted to neutral, the car will ascend the inclining road. Quite interesting but will be bored after 5 minutes.

This was my 3rd waterfall visit in Jeju and my favourite, probably because the waterfall goes directly to the sea. Also, we saw some haenyeo (female divers) there and they were selling fresh sashmi seafood on the rocks next to the sea. It was definitely a very unique eating experience!

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

This fall flows right into the ocean. i liked this one better than the others in the city because you can get into the water at the base of the falls and get your feet wet. also there was a tent with some of the famous diving grannies selling raw seafoods. i highly recommend trying this as it was a truly unique experience. the raw plate cost 20,000w which was cheaper than most of the nearby restarunts.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. FYI: there aren't places there where you can refill your bottles with fresh water.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

Many tours include this spot for tourists.  I personally find it over-rated.  It is an illusionary experience where the environs surrounding the particular stretch of road gives one the impression that it is not what it is supposed to be.  Some guides would even spill water on the road to experiment.  Interesting - yes, but I would not include it as part of a tour itinerary.

It is a good experience to be there and see how mystery the road was. We were with our kind tour guide that gave us an experiment to test the road. Pour water and see where it flows, true enough it was a mystery (still need not to be solved).

I was excited to go see the Manjanggul caves, and had an image in my mind that unfortunately didn't fit what I saw. The whole experience is pretty cool, the floor is uneven, dodging water droplets becomes a game, the lava flow marks are beautiful, but lack of light, lack of stalactite formations, and a lot of areas that are fenced off let me down slightly. However, cheap entrance, and the atmosphere is actually quite lovely. If you get the chance to go, try and do it.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

We went down to the second pond in rain and the stairs is quite steep so u gotta be very careful with ur steps. Upon arrival there is a platform where u can take photo of the fall. For dipping experiences u can continue hiking to fall no 1. No 3 is the farthest. U can refer to the map.

We travelled on a rare rainy day in Jeju, but June, our tour guide, made our trip happy and smooth with her professional arrangement, detailed introduction of the scenic spots, fluent English, sharing on Korean culture and her personal experience on how she feels about Jeju. I am particularly impressed by the guided tour she gave us in the Manjanggul Lava Tube, her intriguing story of haenyeo and their livelihood and our hiking experience at Seongsanilchul Pong. In as short as a day we have seen most of what lies in the northern and eastern coasts of Jeju Island, felt for ourselves the beauty of the natural landscapes and understood how inhabitants of this island have lived since the last century. It was an amazing travel experience and we give credits to June for the nice private tour.

Wasn't planning to do any hiking, so just drove to Eorimok base station to experience the snow and took some photographs, as we came from a tropical country and never had any snow experience before. Turns out the drive up to the station is very beautiful with the snow covered trees along the road. The base station itself is also nice for a leisure walk especially for family with kids.

The footpaths were well-marked and easy to walk even for my 71-year-old mum. I enjoyed the walk and the fresh air. The only downside was there were a few noisy tourists around so it was not so calming an experience.

really didn't expect in such conservative country seeing this museum but making money is not easy so they made it . if u looking for fun experience and some kind of new pictures which probably can not share any where so go for it . when i visited place i met many old grand ma than young :D

Loved my visit here. It is one of the most relaxing islands that I've visited. Food's great and driving around the island is a pleasant experience. They have nice cafes and sceneries along the coastal road. getting around is easy with a car.

Walking through a lava tube is an incredible experience. You can see the flow of lava on the ground, the different historical depths of lava flow is visible on the wall due to the layers of layers, and other features such as the world?s largest lava column and lava rafts. Truly remarkable and easy to see why UNESCO regards this sight so highly.

This is one location where you do not have to worry about bad weather, actually I would recommend going here on a day with rain and wind since then you can actually experience the force of nature when the waves hit the cliffs.Easy access, parking (for a fee) and you can walk along the shore line on a board walk (sort of).

Not a bad experience. But they typically sell repetition food from one end to the other. The place is clean too. Had a dinner in one of the fish sashimi restaurant  enjoyed very fresh fish sashimi at a reasonable price.
my experience is this place is not a museum. it is more a green tea caf챕 where all the foods drinks and ice cream are based on green tea

I do not like they indirectly force a visitor to buy their entrance ticket to the souvenir shop though the entrance ticket after that can get discount when you purchase any chocolate. It is small  but can experience in making chocolate or macaron. Their sample chocolate got black chocolate and white chocolate mixed together but in fact the class provide one color of chocolate to each participant. Thus  we cannot mix the color together as we got one color only. Overall  is normal place without any surprise for us. But there is a nearby local restaurant selling local food (abalone bimbap and etc) providing baby chair which I truly appreciate it.

Good place to enjoy aquarium.  Sea animals.  My children enjoyed this place very much. It was perfect place for children for me and wife it was a little plain. But we sew the egg of shark and Hae Neoi (?대? woman diver to catch sea food) in a big aquarium it was amazing experience and that place was big and convenient.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: 깁?躍?? provides seafood for people to enjoy the delicious elements of the freshness and beautyness of it throughout eating. Although there are lots of different restaurants which provide good quality seafood, the service is not really good. As we arrived at around 5pm for afternoon tea, waiters aren't really willing to work and are quite lazy. After ordering our seafood, we finally found a better restaurant in tatami style. We also ordered a fresh fish which is nice and freshly made by local chefs in a reasonable price. Overall, it was a good afternoon tea experience.

With the help of Mr. Jang, our experience of Jeju local food has also been very exciting. Grilled Mackerel, Sundubu, Oysters soup rice, Samgyetang, black pork barbeque, abalone hot pot rice etc. We wish we could stay longer in Jeju.

We drove our car over to Udo Island via a ferry. It was a great experience. A tip for drivers to head for the parking at the jetty as you have to fill in a form with your particulars (car number, drivers details) to purchase a ticket at the tour office. It only takes 15 mins to cross the island and thereafter we drove around. There are no maps so we went one round. It was very crowded being a Saturday so try to go on weekdays. There are a lot of interesting cafes, 4 beautiful beaches, lighthouses, lots of lovely spots for sightseeing and great photos opp. You can also take a speedboat at the black beach or visit the caves. We took the seafood pot with instant noodles for lunch in a local small restaurant. The last ferry was at 6.00pm but maybe earlier on weekdays. Overall, it was a very interesting day trip and we enjoyed ourselves.

Tour guide was friendly, helpful, respected our privacy yet open to engage and hear our questions. Did not pressure us to finish sightseeing any site fast. Every area we went to was good, there were no places that we went to that tried to hard-sell us a service or product. Tour guide also brought us to really good food places, and even recommended us to other places for good food or for future exploration and sight-seeing. All in all a very enjoyable and pleasant experience! Definitely recommend this!

Located just a stone's throw from O'Sulloc Museum, this place is a must-visit! I strongly recommend making your own soap here - it is such a fun and unique experience! Do grab a bite to eat at the cafe as well as the food is not only healthy but delicious!

I called it 3 in 1 experience because we get to see tea plantation, showrooms for tea & Innisfree products and cafe at the same vicinity. It's a place with good product, food & service. It's a memorable experience for me and I enjoyed it very much!

Cute and fun place for little Sanrio fans. It's not that big and there's not much to see. Cafe is great - seats are fun and good cafe food. Have a little bit of everything - art work, history of Sanrio and Hello Kitty, bedroom stageroom, activities room - but it's not that big and not big on experience.

A quick 20 min ferry ride from Jeju.  We went there on a rainy day, however so did not get the whole experience of Udo.  It looked to be a beautiful and very serene island.  Seafood is good here.  Homemade peanut ice cream was also very good here.A great option for a day trip.

You can go underground and experience the cold temperatures close to 12 degrees.. its like walking through an igloo.. Cold air everywhere and some parts are wet due to the precipitation though the soil. Reminder to bring a jacket and good shoes as floor is slippery and area is dark! Very good experience!

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.
We loved walking throughout the cave and having the experience of walking on something that was once lava.  It is cheap and impressive.  Check out the worlds largest lava stack.

We learned a lots about how lava tube was formed and get to experience these natural phenomenon hands on. The kids thoroughly enjoyed the walk as well. Walking inside can be a bit tricky as it?s not flat and some part can be a wet and slippery. Overall a very educational trip for us.
Walking through the lava tubes is just an amazing experience.  It is surreal and beautiful to see what millennia of lava flow has created.  One of the best places to see on Jeju Island.

Traversing through Manjanggul was nothing like my other spelunking experiences! This was more civilized and organized :) Manjanggul's explorable/walkable area is only 1km but it's already enough for you to appreciate how Jeju's volcanic origins formed these natural wonders for us to see.
This was really excelent place and experience to walk in former lava tunnel. Just imagine thousands of years before here flew lava ...
This is a pretty fall wig a light walk.  The whole place is set up beautifully for a visit with a family. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience.
This is a nice tea farm where you can walk around a tea farm experience a tea ceremony buy tea and tea products a cafe as well as beauty products.

This is a must if you're on the island - a great experience to be in the middle of where lava has flown from years past.  Best to wear footwear that will handle uneven terrain.  Tempature is cooler but not uncomfortable with a jacket.  Really great visual xamples of how lava changes the landscape.  It's very dark but the lighting in place is enough to get you through and keeps the mystery / awe.  The walk to the end of the tunnel is about 1000 m (and worth it).
Make sure to wear good shoes.  Also wear rain gear to keep from getting wet.   Walk slow and you should be fine.   Great experience and would recommend to visit. !

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.

It was raining when we arrived and spent a fun afternoon at this museum posing with the different paintings photos and displays. Unfortunately the rain prevented us from taking photos with the various outdoor displays. Wheelchairs are available for loan and help make the experience more enjoyable for my mom who has difficulty walking. Entrance fee is KRW9000 per person. The Alive Museum covers a wider area and has more/different displays than the Trickeye Museum in Seoul.

It was an interesting experience walking through the immense cave network. It's mind-boggling that this is only a very small part of a much larger system formed through volcanic activity. Do go to the visitors center to find out more information before venturing in.

It was an amazing experience to visit this place. It's good that they only put on a few lights just so that we could really see how the various unique designs on the wall and the rocks look like. The tourist could somehow imagine walking through the lava tube in the dark. True nature artistry !

It only costs about $2 to visit (separate from transportation costs).  Very well maintained site but still a rough surface that requires suitable footwear and it can be wet and slippery in some spots; also quite cool.  This is a very impressive channel to walk through and imagine the lava flowing and leaving the characteristic marks and artifacts along it path.  Dim lighting gives a neat eerieness that somehow makes it even more exciting to explore.  Various well constructed boardwalks with built in floor lights improve access.  The entire tour is about 1 km in each direction.  Very interesting experience.
I went during the summer months so that it really helps that the manjang cave was really nice and cooling in there. Really nice experience to walk through the cave

i never been in a cave before. so its all new to me. it can get chilly inside when you go deeper. you need to walk about 1km in to the iconic lava thg. is a really good geographic experience on how such nature create wonders. have a good footwear cause it has uneven and wet surface.
Great to learn about local citrus history. Lots of space to walk around and enjoy. Tangerine plucking experience. Ask them how to choose sweet ones.
Experience one of the best sunrise at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Suggest to stay close by do that you can walk up the hill. Take about 20-30 minutes depending on your fitness level.
An eye opening experience to walk along a real lava flow cave! Bring along a small touch light; as well as a warm jacket as it can get a little chilly inside the cave.
An experience not to be missed. Walking for 1km underground through a subterranean tunnel created thousands of years ago by molten lava. Where else can you see such amazing lava tubes?
A little scary and very dark inside the cave and the ground is uneven making walking rather tiring and it was a long walk but overall a good experience for me.

Well worth the visit, especially if geology is your interest.Plenty of stairs in and out of the cave so not too advisable for elderly, or families with babies/ toddlers. (though i did bring both!) Being a lava tube, the flooring can be uneven and slippery within the cave so wear proper footwear.It will be cold and dimly lit down in the lava tube, so bring your sweaters if chill is a concern.The walk long to and fro the end, so be prepared.After the first half to the end, it can get boring for some especially the kids. That said it is still a unique experience for many.

We were at Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon before we went to Manjanggul. It was a god decision as it was a brief respite from the scorching sun.That aside, this place is itself a gem. Well maintained and interesting facts have their own boards for the visitors to read. Light jacket is highly recommended if you don't like cool places. Temperature is similar to if you blast your AC unit in your room. Very nice. Wear good shoes. Slippers and heels / platforms not recommended although we saw several girls wore them. You'll be walking on solidified lava. Hence, the walking surface is very unkind to ill-equipped feet. :).Overall, very good experience.

We went there by car that we brought from jeju. It's really beautiful nevertheless. 1 day is enough to tour all of it. If you want to try horseriding, there's some that offer price 5000 won per ride, while others 10k won. There's many place that offer horseriding, so if you want to save your budget without sacrifing the experience, walk some more to find cheaper ones.Try the Hallasan fried rice! It's really worth it!

We visited on a dull wet day but even then there was plenty of sparking glass to see.  Everything you can imagine made of glass.  I loved the mushrooms and pumpkins and some of the weirder sculptures.  On a sunny day it must be even better.  Great place to take kids and, except for woodland walk it is all accessible for people with walking problems.There are examples from different parts of the world and you can watch craftsmen making things - and even book an experience to try it yourself.

We brought our 3 young kids and two elderly mothers to the Manjanggul Cave in late Nov, and it was quite an experience descending into the dark and cold cavern.  It was lit sufficiently to walk, though some areas could be a little dark and wet.  The kids sure had fun, until it got a little boring for them after 500 metres. The entrance fee was reasonable, not expensive.

We agreed that visiting the Jeju Stone Park in the snow was one of the most enjoyable experiences we have had in Korea. The stones, sculptures, houses and other artefacts, as well as the lovely walks are beautiful in the snow. It also meant only a few people were visiting, so it was very peaceful and serene. The museum was excellent, very educational, and we really appreciated how the different lava types were displayed as sculptures. They are beautiful, nature?s art!
