beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.

Arriving parking lot around 4ish in the morning. It's dark but u can see other people going to same direction, just follow them. I guess we took around half an hour or less to reach the top. I didn't stop for a while because i'm so afraid I will miss the sunrise. Turns out some people arrived the top earlier than us! That day was a bit cloudy but still we can see the beautiful sunrise. It's really amazing experience! Besides I am quite impressive with their trail, well furnish with stones and woods. Quite interesting when u look down to the town, must go for Jeju trip.

Arrived at the Seongsan llchubong at about 615am, an hour before sunrise at 715am. The ticket counters were not opened (opens at 730am) but the trails were available. We hiked up the 1.5km or so trail up and it took us about 30mins with a couple of rest stops. Most of the trail were stairs, only the initial path was rocky. It?s rewarding and got to see the beautiful sunrise and Seongsan town/ port in the background.

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?
Amazing view in the autumn, especially u can see the peak at the end of Eorimok Trail and Yongsil Trail.

After reading the reviews i was a bit reluctant about visiting the park but i am glad i did. I only wish i had more time to see everything, like all the small trails leading to the folk villages at the far back. This is not just for people who are history buffs, this park can be enjoyed by anyone who appreciates nature and quiet, peaceful walks. It is a windy area so be prepared if visiting in cool seasons. For only ~$5 this is a nice park to spend a few hours if you want to slow it down and be in nature.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

A relatively easy hike going up Yeongsil trail (lots of climbing). Note that if you're taking the bus, you still need to do a pre-hike of 2.5km going up the mountain after you get off the bus stop. In my opinion, this was harder than the actual hike going up, but it was good preparation. There's also a cafe near the actual entrance. You can buy food here right before going up the trail.The cutoff time for Yeongsil trail is 2pm during the summer, but I would advise you to come early. The hike itself can be done in 1.5 hours, but with picture-taking, it can take as long as 3 hours (and the view at the top is gorgeous in many places!).Wear good hiking shoes. I've seen people wear regular sneakers (and even a guy with leather shoes -- what was he thinking?!), but I swear your feet will hurt if your shoe even manages to survive. Both Yeongsil and Eorimok trails have unpaved trails with unforgiving rocks. Hiking sticks would also help with the descent if you have weak knees.It's safe to hike solo (even for females) during popular days, so you're sure to hike with other people. It's also best to go down where most people are going if you started late (most people drive, so they go down the same trail they went up).In case of emergencies though, you can call their emergency number. (There's mobile coverage for most, if not all, of the trail). Take note of the location posts every few hundred meters. In case you get injured, there's this small train which can take you down, but you have to wait quite a while.

A must-see in Jeju island. During this time of the year, there are pink Azalea blossoms that decorate the mountains. Though the Eojimok trail is the most easiest one, it still took us more than 3 hours. The view along the Yeongsil Trail is particularly memorable. Hiking in Hallasan is a refreshing experience for travelers who would like to explore the essence of Jeju island.

A must see when on Jeju Island. The trail to the top is well maintained and well build. Gets a bit steep at some points. If you're going doing the summer, as i did brings som water. It gets very hot and humid.

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014.  Glass is a common item we use daily.  But there in the Glass castle, they have made beauty out of something ordinary to something beautiful, works of art actually.  However, many tourists were not aware that there is a trail going round the Castle where you can see more sculptures placed along the trail.  A prominent signpost placed at the entrance to the trail will be helpful.  i am glad my friends and I didn't miss this trail.  To make sure it is not slippery during rainny season, the managements have placed gunny sacks along the trail.  This helps greatly for many of us.So if you are in Jeju, don't miss Jejeu Glass Castle.

A great hike for people that like to spend the day hiking. I went during the week and it was not to busy but I was told weekends is very busy. I had trouble finding the bus up to Yeongsil trail head as no english on bus signs. Took a taxi which was 25,000 won but was able to take bus home from Eoimok trail head back to Seogwipo. But this hike had much scenery to offer, I was a little bummed that we were unable to hike up to lake in the crater. This would have made the experience fantastic. No waterfalls either as it seemed to be the dry season this time of year but still a great hike. A must if you are a hiker.

You want free entrance? Then go to this place and plunge into warm sea water in a cold weather.You will love the view and be amazed how the nature formed these rocks.The place is not so crowded by the time I visited this place.Going solo into this place. I met a kind Ajussi who lives in Jeju. He guided me to reach the top of the rock formation. He always come to this place to see dolphins and observe sunset.
you need to prepare extra energy to climb up the hill. Recommended to go there before dawn to see sunrise. Nice view form the top of the hill.

Would have been nice to visit for sunrise but we were reliant on public transport. Still glad we did it in the morning. Jeju is alot larger than we thought and it was more than an hour to get there on the bus from the bus station. It's less than 200m high but it felt like a struggle to get to the top! I think we took about half an hour for the climb. The pathways are very well laid out and it was very busy with visitors. Nice view while climbing. Right at the top it's more the crater you see so it was a sea of green when we were there. Defo worth a visit when in Jeju. From there we travelled to Seogwipo

Whether you are a tea fan or just want to see a nice view of the area this is a nice place to visit. The ?쐌useum??is quite small. The bigger draw is the store (with a sample) and tea/ice cream shop. It was very busy very touristy!

when we saw the peak we know that it can be death tiring for us because we not that fit and also we not love hiking but when see all the ajusshi and ajuhmma look very spirit to hike we being very competitive and take the challenge and it's not regretful decision because the views from top really amaze us and make us feeling refresh.

Went to visit this attraction even though I saw some negative reviews as I have planned some attractions based on region and this is some thing that I think the kids would love to visit.Entrance fee is pricey at $5k won as there is practicably nothing much to see and do inside. After buying the tickets  the staff would give the adults coffee and kids chocolates. The display were very old  like it has been there for 3 or 4 decades and we felt uneasy as it looks dirty. There is a kitchen whereby apprentice showcase their skils on chocolate making. Wanted to buy some chocolates since we are there. But they dont seemed to be interested as the minimum sale item cost about $39k for a box of chocolates. Not worth my moneh and thus left empty handed. Adults ans children were disappointed.

review: We were there in a bad timing when it was raining hard so we opted not to proceed for fear of slipping or whatnot but I have seen pretty good shots of the view from the peak. I heard the climb can be challenging too.

We went to hike here today and it was really fun. The air was clear and the view was beautiful. We didn't take the route to see the ponies  so our hike lasted about an hour. We walked around 5000 steps total. The stairs are well placed so it's easy to go up  and when we went there were only about ten-twenty people in total so it was quiet and lovely. Great place to hike before or after a nice meal to digest your food!
We went there to see the sunset and it was beautiful. We need to hike for 10-15 minutes to reach at the top and the view is worth for the effort.

We went there before the large crowd came. The place is relatively small and nothing much to see. You have got to use your imagination and eyesight to view the dragon head rock. Some people say it doesn't resemble dragon at all..hahaha

We went on an afternoon after our stroll around museums. It was nice view. It's free.  A lot of tourist though... Visitors will be able to view by walking stairs. It was windy and cold when we went. Dress appropriately. Nothing else to see but the cliff itself.

We wanted to catch the sunrise there but the sun was blocked by the clouds. It was a little disappointing as we climbed up when it was dark (cant see much scenery) and we had to descend without seeing the sunrise. It was nice to see the view from the top though!
We stumble upon this beach enroute to the caves. We didnt regret it a bit. The view is stunning and one of the most beautiful beach we have ever seen.

We just visited today. It is winter so maybe the beach looks better in summer time. The sand is covered with a cover and there is much washed up dirt / rubbish on the beach. The view on the city is not specially relaxing.Fun to see black sand but there are other parts of the island where black sand is combined with better views and clean.

We Enjoyed a leisure walk amidst the lovely silver grass swaying with the wind blowing :) reaching at the top ud be surprised to see swings  perched on top of the hill with piped in music. Love to just sit  there and enjoying the view and wind.the climb is not too hard as compared to other attractions.

We drove to check this Estuary out and we werent disappointed at all.Love the scenic view especially when the Estuary meets the Ocean half way....u have to see it for yourself... Good place to chill and there are cafes to while some time away too...

We come here for the lighthouse where Korean drama Iris was filmed. The view is exceptional and didn't disappointed. One unexpected experience is we got to see the women divers. They caught bunch of sea urchins and see their male partners cut it. I wish we could taste it but seeing it is good enough.

We came to this museum based on the previous reviews and came away extremely disappointed. The displays are very average and there's really not too much to see inside the display hall. The tunnel with the dioramas (which looked to be the most interesting one) was locked while we were there. There were no signs to indicate why it was closed or when it would re-open.The other tunnels were OK but once you've seen one tunnel you've seen them all - and the fairy lighting in the tunnels did seem a little out of place considering their history. There is a lot of painful history in this area but the museum fails to capture and relay it.It would have been better to see more of the human history alluded to in the video display in the other displays.Note that a lot of the pictures for this Trip Advisor listing may not actually be of this museum - we were quite confused trying to find it based on these pictures and they make it seem a lot grander than it really is.Overall wouldn't recommend and wouldn't go back.

We came to seogwipo to see the falls and have BBQ. The bridge was close to the parking lot for one of the falls and it is worth a stop to admire views although don't put your hopes up since it is just ok.

We came on a foggy and rainy day so we didn't had a great view like other did.  Nonetheless we enjoyed ourselves with the tea and cakes even though there isn't any WOW to those matcha cakes we ordered.  Beside the restaurant there isn't much to see inside other than tea tasting and tea goods.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.
We are pleased to provide you with the best experience at the garden. We appreciate your leaving amazing reviews. We are looking forward to seeing you next time.

Was there during winter  thus not much water can be seen under the bridge. Can see far away on the bridge  and the view was nice. Other than that  nothing much at the attraction. There was one fountain of various animals heads  and supposedly you are to face any one of them to throw in a coin and make a wish according to what you wanted.

Was curious about this rock formation as read the other trip advisor comment and was not disappointed at all. Its really a very interesting rock formation and its nice to just feast your eyes on this amazing view.Only 2000kW for entry fee but try to avoid peak times as I went on a Sunday the viewing bridge was packed with visitors doing their selfie shots so you are not able to see the view as clearly due to the crowds. Must visit when you Jeju island.

Walk to the top is quite easy with good views.Don't miss the signpost to the women divers near the bottom on the way down.  They do a few shows a day and you don't have to pay extra to see it.Lot's of parking and eateries in the area

This was one of our favourite places from the list of to do activities in Jeju. It was really exciting to see such wonders of nature . These rock formations are few million year old and have column like shape. View of the blue water from the board walk is breathtaking. A must visit spot when you are in Jeju.

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.
This tourist attraction has good view for photo. You can see the Jeju city landscape from here and the dragon head rock itself only the minor thing to see.

This stadium had an awesome design. I wouldn't travel far to see it but it was on the way so I popped it. I couldn't go inside so viewed from behind the gate. I can imagine watching a game their would be great
This small mountain has amazing view from the on top of mountain. When it is clear you can see the island of south in Korea.

This place was definitely not what I expected. Just quick overviews about tea history and its traditions. I would of liked to see more on the importance of tea culture. Some type of demonstration would be great too. It was just a rest stop with tea related snacks drinks and beauty products. If you enjoy that kind of stuff it?셲 a great place to visit. Only takes about 10-15 min to see everything but plan for 1-1.5 hours if you want snacks and a drink.

This place is really good. You can see the cliff right beside the sea and it?s really safe to walk at the walk area. The view is really nice but there are a lot of stairs. So it?s kinda hard for old people and for family who use baby strollers.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

This miniature park had all the famous attractions from around the world which was great for viewing  especially when we haven't had the chance to see the real thing. However  you could see the place was a bit old and definitely needed some maintenance. So this place is definitely not for the fussy  but still worth a visit if you had time.

This is one of the reason why I want to visit Jeju because I want to see this beautiful place and I was not disappointed though I was a bit breathless climbing the top but everything was worth the view is beautiful and I would definitely go back to this place and probably spend a day just enjoying this breathtaking place. My one regret is that I did not get to see the sunrise so hopefully next time if I came to Jeju I would try my best to see the sunrise here...

This is one of my wife's favourite walks. A lovely circular amble around the Songaksan peninsula mostly on boardwalks and steps. Lovely views of the unique geology of the cliffs. Can see pheasants cormorants peregrine falcons and occasionally dolphins if you're lucky. You can walk up to the summit which affords stunning views back to Sangbansan and Hallasan (clear day required). If you are that way inclined there's a Starbucks at the start/finish too.
This is just another bridge and I wouldn't drive especially to see it but if your visiting the nearby waterfall you should also check this out. It has a lovely view and looks great at night

this is a spot you must see if you go to Jeju in low season. Very few people. It is visited by families with kids that try to catch the crabs on the rocks. The black volcanic sand is nice especially if you are in the mood to look for the spots where the fountains emerges from the sea. Here sea water mixes with amazingly freezing river water that brings some white sand on the shore. The view of black sand mixing with the white sand allows you to take beautiful pictures. Romantic place
This is a must-see on Jeju Island.  A walk along a set of stairs (not strenuous) provides many varied views of this area.  Look for the hexagonal columns of lava.

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.

This is a beautiful destination. I would consider this a must do for all foreigners visiting Jeju Island. We did this stop as a part of our self drive 5 day holiday during the kids fall break. What I loved was the the design of the building and landscaping made the most of the site. It reminded me of visiting an upmarket winery. There is a fabulous view from the tower over the tea fields fabulous art displayed inside and precious tea cups to look at the amazing smell & sight of seeing tea roasting and demonstrations. The outside had sculptures. The kids loved airy ambiance of the cafe & wolfed down the Green Tea Swiss Roll. I loved my dacquoise! Plenty of parking bathroom facilities Well Done!

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There are places in Jeju that convince you that you made the right decision to go there -- they're just really beautiful. Oedolgae is one of those places. It's just a photo spot that will take about 15 minutes of your time. The rock formation is interesting and the place is just lovely in a natural way. I gave this a 4/5 because it's not difficult to get there from the entrance of the park -- no steep mountains and such to climb in order to see the view.There's not much to do here -- just check it out and move on.
The water fall easy to find from central seogwipo very beautiful view from entrance And easy going down to the sea to see the waterfallCan find some lady divers sell fresh seafood

The walk up the stairs is hard on knees but not specially challenging and can be done in 15-20mins. Make sure to be on top a bit before sunrise or otherwise gets quite packed with people and is hard to find a good spot to seat and see the sunrise. We got a somewhat cloudy morning so sunrise views were quite disappointing.
The view is not bad and you can see many small fishing boat parking there. But really not particularly impressive so I think it can be skipped if run out of time
The view is magnificent! The haenyu women were modeerately fun to watch. Parking is atrocious! The walk to see the sights is rather difficult.

The view is breathtaking. The location is near with soepjikoji (all in house) so remember to visit two of them.this one is the higlight of jeju attraction.After see around we lunch seafood around here. My taxi driver recommend this one.
The view from the bridge is really pretty but we wanted to see the fall and you could barely see it because it was so far away.
The view awesome ..we thought we can see flowers and all but what a pleasant surprise when we have snow view instead. Peaceful and scenary are so so beautiful
The scenery is amazing. Had never seen such nice view. Fantastic place for photography. So relaxing strolling with the green
The one place you have to see if you're in Jeju. No regrets going up in the midst of heavy rain. The caldera was still impressive. And the view from the top over the town is nice.

The number one attraction on Jeju and an impressive climb to the top. Lots of signs to explain the geological formations at key points en route. The attractions divides the ascenders from the descenders which helps with the climb. Wonderful view from the top. The attraction is beautifully looked after no litter and only about 짙1 to visit. If you are lucky you will also be able to see the women who dive for fish which has become infamous with the Jamie Olivier programme in the UK.Worth a visit.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.
The hike to Sunrise Peak is great with great view along the hike. You also get to see the performance by woman diver and enjoy the fresh seafood caught by the woman diver.

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.

The drive from jeju airport area to aqua planet is around 1 hour 10 minutes passing by many small towns. The entry tickets were quite costly and I used klook to get some discounts with the tickets. Upon parking the rented car outside the vicinity of aqua planet then picked up a number from the machine next to the ticket counter. Waited for the number and redeemed my wristbands without much hassle. Kids under 3 can enter for free.There are plenty to see and we were in time to watch fish feeding a seal and dolphin show. Outside the facilities has really good view and many people were taking photos.Food in the food court was not too bad and similar like incheon airport have to be ordered and paid at the cashier counter and picked up from the individual sections when the device buzzes.Overall experience was great and worth every cent spent.

review: The crater itself wasn't much to see but it was a pleasant little walk and there are very good views of Mt Halla - the best we had during our stay on Jeju.

The Bulsari Reace Pagoda is a dome-shaped Buddhist temple built in 1998. This structure symbolizes the national hope for the peaceful reunification between South and North Korea and it it just beautiful. There's really not much more to it than the structure itself but it's a lovely piece of architecture that is unlike any other in Korea that I've seen. And the view of the ocean from the pagoda is worth the trip too.

The beach's sand is actually volcanic sand/ash which is why it's black and on a good sunny day the view is marvelous. I'm not sure if it's a lucky occurrence but we spotted jumping fish a distance away from the shore line. I didn't have time to but you can rent transparent kayaks to explore the river which apparently has a whirlpool (not that dangerous according to my guide) at the head. The water is quite clear so you may actually be able to see fishes under the kayak. Otherwise enjoy the picturesque view of the estuary.

thank you so much for the visit and a good review. we always try to give our visitors good memories during the travel. we hope to see you again someday ^^
thank you so much for the lovely detailed review. we would reference your Cons advice and Be more attractive sightseeing place . thank you for coming and have a nice day ^^
thank you for the good review and your visit. Elvis show is one of  best attraction in our museum. we hope to see you again someday ^^
Special view on how the cliff formed in square and you will amaze with the nature beauty of this place as so far I didn?t see the same in countries I have visited.

South Korean is really great at preserving their historical stuff! One of many historical village. Love it. Beautiful experience and amazing views never seems to stop form fascination with their cultures. Oh this place once a shooting scene as well. Dae Jang Geum I supposed!~

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!
should walk to the peak to see the amazing view of jeju island. sunny day is the best day to go so you can get clearer view.
Scenic view by the sea and we can see lady divers on that day diving for their catch. We also tried fresh catches on the spot sold by Ahjumma and was a wonderful experience. A place not to be missed.

Really gorgeous view of the waterfall which flows right into the sea. A little bit challenging to go near it as you have to walk and hop on big rocks but you could still see it clearly just by standing near the stairs. Sat near to the waterfall and my shirt got slightly wet by the water splashes. Cold but refreshing. Do wear proper shoes if you intend to walk on the huge rocks to go near the waterfall.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

People say you should visit it as the sunrise. Too bad I was a bit late so I couldn't see the amazing view. But still even if you go later the view is amazing. If you go to the top of seongsan ilchilbong you could see the city by the sea. It's a bit tiring to go up coz there's so many stairs that you have to climb. But you get pay as you see the amazing view from the top

Our tour guide took us there and the road ahead seemed to be uphill when viewing from our tour bus. Our driver then put the bus in neutral gear and amazingly our bus moved slowly up (actually down) the road by itself.  An interesting optical illusion.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). The only down side is that the area as well as the park have limited street lights so you'll be needing a torchlight to walk either early in the morning or at night.
One of the must see attractions in Jeju Island. Lucky to visit during the non peak season. Nice views at the right time since we did not meet that many tourists.

One can go for a hike or just sit near the shore and enjoy the view. Along the coastline one can see a number of manmade caves which stands as a testimony to the importance of Jeju Island during WWII. These caves built by the Japanese troops served as a place for storing the weapons.Though called as a mountain it is more like a hill as it is not steep and one can enjoy the walk up the peak.
Nothing much view besides the crater. Seems not a good season to visit this place. We took just few photos and left in 30 minutes.

Not much to see or do except to take a few moments to take it the view and wind of Jeju. Many people (mostly Koreans) are seen walking along the beach picking shells or dipping their feet in the water. Not much sunbathers on this beach.
Not have to hike too much. Look peaceful but nothing much to see and the view is not too impressive. Can see autumn leaves far away. Can spend less than one hour here.

Normally as everyone is aware that the aquarium always be busy and crowd with people. Here also crowd but it's not too tight since the space is very big. Once we get into the aquarium you can buy the ticket at the lobby and the restroom is in the left. The lobby is very large so you won't get stuck with people.They will give the wristband tag and you get into aquarium on the right. You will experience sea animals like other aquarium separated into sections and time zone. The difference that I found its better is there have the seating at like the stadium in front of grand aquarium so we can sit and relax there.If you come at the right timeYou will see the special diving show by the local lady whom dive deep and find the seafood stuffs. So you will see the way of local people living as well.There's also the show available but the ticket would be different. At the end of tunnel you will see the souvenir shop which I think the items are not too expensive.I think it's better than other place I have been since some places you may see people more than sea animals.At the exit of aquarium you can see the nice scenic view of Hallasan Mountain

Nice little island to spend the day. If your a foreigner bring your passport with you to buy your ferry ticket.on the island itself you can walk around but by far the most popular way is to rent a bike. Pedal or electric powered that can seat 2 people.You will need a drivers license for the electric one though. Cute little beaches around and you can stop off and try some of the peanut ice cream which Udo is famous for. Also you can hike up to Udo lighthouse and get a good view from the top and see most of the island. A good way to spend a day

Nice hiking and walk for the great views. We managed to complete the hiking route round the mountain in about 2 hours.Also a good idea is to stop and walk slightly before the mountain as there are also nice scenery of the beach and sea.Beware that the buses out of the area are very irregular and it would be good to start the hike early in the morning and leave before noon as the buses seem to run more regularly early in the morning.We waited an hour for the bus out and gave up walking to the next town to get a cab.

Nanta Show was like a famous tourist attraction. I decided to see it while in Jeju since there was nothing much in Jeju anyway. The theatre wassmall but cosy. I seconded the previous review that 80-90% are all China tourists - They were noisy and some even tried to leave before the 90-min show ended. But we were here for the show so please yourself as the show was really entertaining.

My review is a little late but it's better late than never. We've visited this place when I was four months pregnant and I was able to hike up to the summit. This place is serene. It's breathtaking to see the wonderful view when you've reach the top. The kids love the lush greens at the hilly part of this place. It's very well-maintained. There are souvenir shops located at the entrance of the park.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!
Make sure you take time to see the mountain when you go to Jeju! You can't go wrong heading there to get great views of the Island.

Magnificent views even I only managed to climb half way. Here you can see people mountain people sea. Young and old. No wonder it's declared as another 7 Wonders of heritage of South Korea. A very worthy place to visit.
Love the view. It was spectacular! Went there during winter. Freezing cold but you could see the dragonhead! :D

Love the view here because of the lush greenery. You will also be able to see that there're people going some Kayaking. But it depends on the season as well. There's also cafes nearby and once you're done with the view you can also walk down along the coast towards the Yongdeum Rock (Rock that looks like a dragon). Definitely walkable distance With such lovely sea Breeze and beautiful greenery. Do make sure you wear a hat and sunglasses if you're going in summer though.

Location is really big finish the whole tour in around 2hrs time u can estimate how big is the location... great views around flowers ancient equipment of plowing fishing saw a cage of chickens ducks peacock saw ostrich rabbits/ hares deers and even horses. 1st time to see all the animals that near!!! ancient rooms that only seen in Korean dramas understanding the famous things that in Jeju Island 3 of many things
Jeju has many beautiful beaches and Jungmun is definitely one of them! Great place to see huge waves and surfers in action. You can go up to the cliff top for that aerial view of the beach.
I've seen many temples around Korea but this was one of my favorites! So spacious and with the best view. The colorful decorations were also so nice.

I've not been up a volcano before and the view is worth itIt's really not that high though if you get any exercise... Just 200m of climb... Remember you are climbing a volcano and not a building so it is a little strenuous !Shame you cannot walk around a little more At the top ... And I couldn't see Hallasan on this particular day..

Its three floors with aquariums but still not so big bu got pretty awesome one with big display where you can sit and enjoy the view. I also liked the show. They got 2 types of it one with humans and several with animals like dolphins and sea bear. Performance times are 11:10 13:00 15:00 and 17:00. There is also feeding times and female diver's diving. It opens from 10 to 19 so be sure you will see at least one of performance and have time to look around since performance lasts about 40-45 min each.

It?s a must hiking course in Jeju. You?ll be leading to the top by hundreds of well made stairs. All can be seen on the top. The place is very windy but it?ll dry your sweat and the great top view will make you take lots of pictures. Enjoy the view!

It was quite a strenuous climb up to the shrine in the cave at the top. Although it was a very hot afternoon. The views on the way up are beautiful and you can see for miles. Lots of great photos. Places to eat and souvenirs at the bottom near the car park.

It is my first time seeing a waterfall by the sea... The view was spectacular! Experience the breeze of the sea combined with the breeze from the waterfall. The majestic waterfall is already quite impressive itself...

It a pleasant place to visit: Lots of visitors n cars maybe was a weekendThe walk is not too difficult  you will enjoy if you take it slowly n see the view from different angle n height Need food shoes n the slope is pretty steep n may need to hold the rope/railing at certain height Feel good n nice when reach the top

In five visits to South Korea in four years I have not come across a museum palace or historical building I did not like.They are all well-maintained offer good information in Englishoften have multilingual guides and free tours and are free or cheap to get in.The Jeju National Museum is no exception. Our hotel was about 4km away and we walked to and from there seeing many interesting sights on the way and eating lot of local food.I am an unabashed fan of the curating skills of the Koreans; they do a very good job.Here they provided a great overview from prehistoric to modern times offering interesting exhibits and information.There was also a special exhibition on Canopus a star of great significance to the people who lived here.Entry is free. There are buses from the city and taxi fares are reasonable. We like eating so we need to walk.
Impressive and memorizing. Love the view. Can also have some fresh live seafood. Definitely worth going. One of the best waterfalls in Jeju. The rest are not really worth seeing.

If you`re a Zippo lover  this is a must visit spot. Museum locates in the ground floor of a modern seaside building with breathtaking pacific ocean view. There is 2 exhibition halls  one of those displays many special designed zippos in large size  and the other in fact is a zippo shop  you can see and buy different limited edition zippo there and many are designed by local designer.

I watched tv show a while ago about this place before we planned this trip.I really wanted to rent their see thru cayak to explore jeju's under water world.Unfortunately it was rainy windy and cold so there was no rental place opened.We enjoyed spectacular views but I was devestated..... please check weather reports before you come here if you want to rent any cayak or pedal boats.

I was on a group day tour so unfortunately didn't have as much time here. Walked through the museum very quickly ordered the ice cream and cake and quickly rushed to buy a few products at the shop. The view of the green tea fields provided a great photo op but was surprised to see 'beware of snake' signs walking through the garden fortunately didn't encounter any snakes though but they should take more precaution on this as I see a lot of small kids walking and running through the areas. There's an Innisfree house for buying the famous Korean brand cosmetic next door but quite frankly this was a bit disappointing for an Innisfree loyalist like me. The selections were limited compared to the shops in town all over Korea. One woman  in my tour group bought a bunch of products but was not offered any free samples which is common in other shops. I would suggest skipping this part and spend all the time in the O'Sulloc cafe and tea museum.

I was a little worried after reading some reviews but after going i am pleasantly surprised.  The entrance fee is a little high at 11000 won for an adult and if i had kids i might be worried they would get bored.  Seems perfect for couples and people who like taking pictures.  If you take your time and dont rush you can do the whole place in am hour.  Lots to look at.  Worth a stop.  Bonus...if your name is yoori you get free entrance and a free gift

I took my girlfriend here as she absolutely loves all things aquatic  especially shells  and she loves to go diving. A highlight of this museum is that the owner/operator collected all the exhibits herself  from oceans all around the world  and the museum represents literally a lifetime of work and passion for the sea.Taking that into consideration  if you love to dive  and love the sea  this place is simply amazing  my girlfriend was absolutely in awe  snapping picture after picture and commenting on the rarity and difficulty of finding she'll after shell in such amazing condition. The museum was an interesting oddity for myself  and I understand the reviews saying you could go through the whole thin g in 20-30 minutes  but for someone who is truly amazed by seashells  and the sea in general  you could easily spend more than an hour here (we were there somewhere around 2 hours) If you love seashells  an absolute must see  my girlfriend visibly lit up from the minute we walked in   all the way till we were back to our hotel in ?쒖＜??if you're not passionate about the shells  it's still worth a look at only 6$ (6 000?? per person. Some truly amazing art  especially if you consider it all came from the mind  hands  and worldwide dives of one very cool lady.

I felt like Jeju tried so hard to actually make sights out of nothing and this rock was a very good example of that... Along with Yongyeon pond this was one of the worst places I payed bus tickets for to see on Jeju. It's just a rock with a dirty water sea view and its in the middle of nowhere part of Jeju city where you can only go by taxi. Awful

I decided to visit this place after reading some good reviews and was not disappointed. The coastal view is breathtaking and breathing in the sea breeze was relaxing. Other than the church nothing much else to see  but you can take some nice pictures here. Seongsan Sunrise peak is nearby so don't miss that too. Tried the barbecued cuttlefish that they were selling there and it was fresh and delicious.
I came here without any plans. It was better than I expended. The warm house is beautiful and elegant. Must go up to the roof and you can see the astonishing view!!!

I am 6 years old and when I first got to sunrise peak it was really tall and big. I thought I couldn't climb it but I did. My mummy wanted to quit but I wouldn't let her. The best bit was we saw a shop that sold water and I bought juice. It was halfway up so mummy didn't need to carry water after all. I wish it wasn't such a cloudy day but the view was still cool. I saw a telescope to see everything. Me and my Brother had a fight over the telescope and mummy and daddy got mad. When we got to the top daddy said it was a crater but I did not see any lava so I think he was lying. The end. Finished.

I agree with the other reviewers in regards to the maintenance of the museum...but still fun to see all the models out in display. Theyre much largers than i had thought but some looked a little amateurish... great museum for pictures and history...

Hallasan the 2nd highest mountain in South Korea is a fantastic hiking place!! You can choose to hike from two different easy routes to enjoy different scenery. If this is your first hike after a long hiatus do be mindful that it's better to take the easy route. Cos at some points it's huge boulders that require some stamina to step up.Take the first bus from the bus interchange cos it's advisable for tourists to reach midpoint by noon so that you have adequate time to trek back and catch the last bus from the bus stop which is still 20 min from the start of trekking point. Alternatively there's taxi if you are a group or pair. There's only a hut at midpoint which sells cup noodles which is not cheap.  Thus advisable to bring along dry food and plenty of water for recovery. Along the way you would meet seasoned hikers and some are so friendly that they offer you a ginseng sweet if they see you resting.  There's a water point and the water taste so good! The viewing points offer such fantastic view and it's so breezy that we forgot ourselves!  Definitely a place to visit.

Gwangchigi Beach is a beach near Seongsan Ilchulbong.We park our rental car on the side road.There are a few cars & tourist bus park along the road.We can see beautiful view of Seongsan Ilchulbong from this beach. The beach is long and it has black sand.The beach is unique to it own because of the green stone/rock at the shore.It produce picturesque photo because the green stone contrast with the blue sea.This beach appears on drama Warm & Cozy starred by Kang Sora and Yoo Yeonseok.

Great  cosy  simple with a beautiful view  countryside atmosphere and the elegance of a modern coffee place. You can see how the plants grow and you can pet animals as well. A place to drink and eat something too.

Glad we went here. Quite busy on a Sunday but worth it. Great views of the formations and nice parks at either side to walk through or picnic in. Very reasonable admission and we took our dog in on a lead. Lots of stunning photographs to be taken. I would say it's a must see!
Free entry. Just a rock that doesn't seem to resemble a dragon as claimed. Nice view of the sea though. Not very worth to go out of the way to visit. Spent maybe 5 minutes there in total.

First my lower rating for this aquarium comes partly from expectations that were not met.  This aquarium used to have whale sharks but does NOT anymore.  They couldn't properly take care of them one died and they released the other back into the ocean.  Second this aquarium has been advertised as the largest in Asia which is not true.  It has the largest viewing window in East Asia.  Those misconceptions out of the way this is still a great aquarium.  Interesting sea life some of which I had never seen before.  Great displays and a show that is entertaining if you understand Korean at least somewhat.
