review: Every view from this observation point seems to be more dramatic and beautiful than the one before it.  You will enjoy learning the story behind these towering formations which have served as a backdrop to several Korean historical movies and dramas.

Considered one of the ten best view points of Jeju this attraction is not to be missed One can enjoy this visit if you like to soak yourself or would like to find yourself among the clouds. On a foggy day one can easily miss the existence of this mountain.If you are visiting during winter or rainy season better to plan the visit during afternoon as one can have a magnificent view from the top without much clouds around.This mountain believed to be formed by the volcanic lava houses the Sanbang-gulsa Temple and the Bomunsa Temple.It also has other attractions as Golden Bhuddha Tea Shops etc. Once on the top one can see the ridge called the Dragon Head where a memorial has been built for Hendrick Hamel the first westerner who was the first to introduce Korea to the western world after his ship got wrecked. This mountain is believed to be used as a watch tower and smoke used to be sent out during the day or fire was lit during the night if any urgent message was needed to be conveyed.Climbing the steps would be a little tough for those who are not regular walkers and for the old.

Breathtaking view of the surrounding landscape. A good way to discover by walking at leisure. There is so much to enjoy what the nature can offer right in front of you. The place is well kept and it deserve the UNESCO world heritage site. A must in your itinerary to Jeju. Only regret - could not climb as high to see the the peak of Halla due to time constraint.
Best place to sightseeing and the view is amazing.You will regret if coming to Jeju but not visit Seongsan Ilchubong
Beautiful!! Had to walk up to see the whole view..its breathingtaking !!For those who appreciate nature..shld come.

Beautiful landscape but failed to showcase the unique view in different season of Korea. There is nothing much to see in Mar as the spring has yet to set in thus what you can get is leaf-dropping trees and looking a little dry and crusty. I guess Japan has done a better job to ensure different plant is growing according to the season in their landscape which still make it look stunning during winter & autumn . But this place will definitely look beautiful when Spring set in.
Awesome view.Stones seems to be sculpted. Quite interesting. Wind is so strong so prepared for that.

At first glance this place looks like a fun place but quickly becomes a waste of time.  The outdoor garden is the only place that is fun.  They have fun statues and great photo opportunities but as soon as you walk inside you will quickly become disappointed.  With the coupon entrance is about $12 and is not at all worth it.  If you come from a culture where sex is a taboo then maybe you will enjoy this place but anyone from a western culture will find it boring.  90% of the signage is only korean and not much else to see or do inside.  If it's a rainy day and you have nothing to do then maybe this could be an option but even then I would say pick something else.  This museum has gone through some changes over the years and you will notice that the more recent reviews are pretty low where as the older reviews are better.  It used to be a much better place than it is now~~
as my view that was just a traditional temple. seem not too much local at here but part of trekking point on it. the cave Buddha also not special but ok to visit

Arriving at the location we were welcome with the view of tea garden and a large glass with Ossuloc writing. The tour guide help us to take a photo in the tea garden. Then we walk into the Ossuloc museum where we can see various collections of tea sets from various countries. Then try green tea ice cream and various cakes. Oh yes they are selling various tea.
Amazing views of volcanic activity. Jungmun-Daepo was one of our favorite places to see as a family.
A must-see but be prepared for a tough climb to the top. View is fantastic! Go early if you are driving to get a parking lot (free). Beautiful flowers.
A must go place as you can see how the lava formed meeting the sea. Be prepared for strong wind but spectacular view

A great place to start off is the Women Divers exhibition center to see the old photos and explanation from the staff on the history of Women Divers. Than a slow walk up the peak for a great view ....  the wind was hallowing when we climb up and the local told us its a normal day ...   plenty of great eateries just a short walk from the entrance after the climb . A MUST visit .

A great place to learn about history and culture of Jeju. Stone museum is a must-see for those who are interested in geology. Views of the Sky Pond reflecting nearby mountain are fascinating. There is a small traditional village. You can borrow an audio guide at the ticket office for free.

A good place. It is very near to jeju love land and it just looks like any other normal road but when you go there you will see the mystery of your car moving by itself without the external and engine force. Also there is a very scenic view around road. Had nice fun.

A good place especially for first-timers or those who are interested to see lava formations. Really gorgeous view when the sea hit those rocks. Nothing much to see so don't really have to spend much time here.
A definite must-see when in Jeju. The columnar formations were absolutely gorgeous. Unfortunately it was a little too crowded when we were there but the view was gorgeous with the crashing waves!!

?쁾 we came at the wrong time wrong season. Nothing much to see and do. So far only 1 beautiful view to see and for picture taking. Other than that all is pretty the same. Advise to visit during the right season. (Currently September) Ticket selling at KRW8000 per adult. And transportation hard to get by.

You'll have to go at the right time to get the best views of this place. During autumn, there'll be a short few weeks where the pampas flowers bloom all over the crater, making the views breathtaking and romantic! Go during sunset and you definately will not regret it. I went there on 2 Nov 2012, recommended by the owner of my guesthouse. By far my top favourite sight in Jeju-do. Do check with your guide or guesthouse owner if the pampas flowers are blooming when you're there in autumn cos if they are not, then this visit can be missed as there'll be nothing much to see.
You will have to walk a good while to get there. Worth the walk to see both falls. The bridge on our way was beautiful. Breathtaking view. We paid 2,500 won each. Which is under $5 for two people.

You can reach Ilchulbong by bus from the Intercity bus Terminal in Jeju-Si. It takes around 1h30 to reach it. You don't really care if it is an express or intercity bus you are taking, they more or less all go at the same speed... which is quite fast. You can't really miss the stop which is quite close to the crater. Dozens of buses parked in front of the mountain kind of spoil the nice atmosphere of the place but remember you are a tourist as well...  Left to the entrance, their is a nice small temple, worth the look. The climbing to the top is all made of wooden stairs and doesn't take too long (don't remember exactly, around 30 min). We did it with kids (youngest is 6) and she could do it easily. The view from the top is nice. It is a bit disappointing not to be allowed to walk around the crater. You can just see it from a platform. Before (or after) climbing, don't forget to take a look at the beach on the left of Ilchulbong specially between 13:00 and 15:00 when the old women divers are fishing.

Yeomiji, located in JoongMoon sightseeing complex, is one of the most impressive place in my memory. - Entrance ticket fee is under 10USD, which is quite reasonable. - Area is divided by its own theme like tropical, Japan, Korea ... - Why don't you order a cup of coffee(or ice cream) and take a rest at the center of greenhouse garden- Observatory has nice view. but it is easily get crowded.Tip: you'd better to go CheonJeYeon waterfall(천제연폭포) after here. that place also has beautiful natural scenery :)

Woke up early for this trip but only managed to reach there at 8am. Drove 1 hour plus from Seogwipo but it was worth it. The climb was torturous as the path was made of uneven rocks. There will be stairs further up the climb. it made me sweat even thou the temperature was below 10 deg. The view was amazing and when you reached the top, you forget all your problems and worries. You can see the whole outline of Jeju Island from here. Its a wonderful sight. A must go to place.

While it is not the only waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea as many think (I've seen them both in Indonesia and Philippines), it is definitely a cool waterfall to see and they are relatively rare. I would definitely recommend seeing this waterfall first if you're planning to check out all of the waterfalls on Jeju. It is very accessible and a great viewing experience.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

When you said about Jeju, this Ilchubung will appear in the advertisement and you will know that is Jeju. But for sure, you will not able to snap a photo like in the adver since that only can be done if you take a photo from the helicopter and etc.For family, it is a bit tough if you bring small kids below 10 yrs old since you need to walk to the peak via stair and for adults people also a tiring activity but worth it since you can see the good view of the city and sea around that area. For photography also it will a nice thing to have.They said, the best thing during sunrise to be at the peak, but we are not make it during the sunrise so could not provide any comments on that. Also there is free show of diverwoman at the beach area just that area, they showing the activity of catching octopus with diving and selling the octopus to the audience. Most of the korea people eat it raw with Korean Sauce, i'm yet try the tast.Souvenir shop also available at the entrance of the Ilchubung peak.Thank You.

When I went up in July 2014, it was cloudy and misty, so no views to be seen which was a pity a heck of a climb up, but even though knocking 66 years old I made it (my pulse settled down after less than 15 mins), so it wasn't that bad for the oldies, once again shame about the clouds/mist.Worth a visit, on a good day.I marked it down 'cause of the clouds.

When I first looked at the advertisement, I assumed that I could stand on some place where I can see the overview of the crater.But actually, standing on the edge of the crater, you cannot feel the overview.In addition, I was one of the first visitors coming on that day, so it was not crowded and I could feel the peace in the air.

What's there to see here? There's the rocks, the sea, and a few souvenir shops, but really, the place is, quite frankly, overrated. The rock doesn't even resemble a dragon's head!This may be one of my shortest reviews ever, but it's only because the place is not very interesting. Yes, there's a great sea view (the reason why I didn't give this attraction a   terrible   rating), but other than that, there's really no reason to visit this place.Only give this attraction a go if you really fancy posing with the rock, or if you really love the sea. My humble opinion is that Jeju definitely has more places worthy of your precious time.

What can be so great about a crater? First of all, it?s big. Understand that it?s 2 km circumference and 100m + deep. So it?s not just a crater, not just a park, it has its own eco system with its own unique flora and fauna. The crater itself is not accessible but they have built a park fronting it with high viewpoints overlooking the crater. The viewpoints also allow you to see the surrounding mountainous features such as the Hallasan in the distant. A well designed park which deserves a two hours of your time.

we've seen a few caves and this one is truly unique.  Its not loaded in formations such as stalagmites/stalagtites, but the lava shelves go on forever.  It literally takes over thirty minutes to walk from one end to the other at a decent clip.  Very humid inside, definately bring an umbrella or raincoat.  Also very chilly so if you are there in summer, the temperature change can be significant.  I brought a flashlight but you really don't need it as they do a great job in keeping you on the straight and narrow.  It really gives you a great understanding of what nature can do, well worth the detour to view

Went via a taxi tour in Early Feb 2014. Admission for each person: 2000 won.Hordes and hordes of tourists but you can still try to take some nice and pretty pictures while waiting for those tour groups passing by. Divers performance (if I am not wrong) is at 11am and 3pm. We did not went during that time so we did not manage to see it.Without going up to the peak, you can also see a nice view of the ocean and surroundings. There are also several souvenirs and food shops at the foot of the sunrise peak. It is a UNESCO site and it is a must to visit if you are in Jeju! Still awesome despite in winter.Don't forget that there are stairs and stairs up to the peak :P

Went there to catch sunrise, but was disappointed. Couldn't see the sun peek out over the horizon as it was cloudy.Went at about 5+ in the morning, it was freezing with the winds blowing. Its autumn. Be prepared to bring your thick windproof parkas and scarves. The walk up to the peak is about 30 minutes. For someone who doesn't exercise, I must say its quite a challenge going up. Take your time. Once up there, the view is gorgeous. Take lots of pictures.From Seogwipo-shi, we drove about 1 hour to get there. So do plan your time correctly to catch the sunrise.

Went there because I heard it's a good place for silver grass view, and I was welcomed with a full mountain of beautiful silver grass! Wear comfortable shoes as the oreum is quite steep. Below the oreum are some food trucks selling snacks, good enough to fill your tummy after the steep hike. It might not be easy to locate this place, as the phone numbers I key in the GPS failed to bring me to the correct place. Finally able to find this place by searching for   Everis Golf & Resort   phone number, and managed to see   Saebyeol Oreum   at the highway signboard. Try searching for Everis resort if you can't locate saebyeol oreum, as they are just next to each other.

Went there after having lunch nearby.View: spectacular view even before the climb. Nice view at the coast where the Seawomen show is held. Once you reached the summit, you can view the island & the sea but the sky was not clear when we visited.Seawomen Show: they sang a song before entering the sea. Not much to see them in action coz it's not the actual location where they will dive for abalones, octopus etc. We saw from afar there were Seawomen resting on the rocks nearby the Oedolgae rock.The climb: it's a pathway with steps so it's not hard to climb. Along the way there are many stops/benches for the elderly to rest. Just don't rush it if you bring your parents/grandparents along.

went there after breakfast and was a good time to start if you didn't care too much of sunrise view. Even though it was windy and chilly, got up to the top sweaty and hot. you see see pretty ckear view from the top; Udo island, the wind turbines in the east, Seopjikoji in the south.

Went during the winter season (end Dec), the cold isn't unbearable but the wind is! The climb may not be the easiest but it's doable. Plus you see many tourists and elderlies climbing it together with you, so it isn't that bad of a hike up. When you're up, the view is to shout for. Awesome view!

Well, it is a beach. With bus 101 roughly 15 minutes away from Jeju city.As far as I remember the beach feature something like a free gym and a few toilets.I did not see much of changing facilities, showers or lockers near the beach.In my view Hamdeok Beach is less good than the beaches in Busan.During my time in Hamdeok Beach I saw three surfers who practiced their skill.

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

We woke up at 3am for this and didn't regret it. It was really quite awesome. We drove in the wee hours of the morning for 1.5 hrs to get there, before hiking up for about 40mins to get to the viewing deck where there are seats to see the sunrise. To best enjoy this, be well prepared and equipped for the journey. We slept early at about 9pm the previous night because we knew we had to wake up at 3am. Prepare bread for breakfast on the road because you will need the energy for the hike. Wear proper walking shoes to make it easier to climb up. Remember to check the sunrise timing the night before, set your gps early and accurately if you are driving. If you need help with Korean gps or not sure if you got the right place, always ask your hotel or hostel host to help you set it right the night before. Charge and prep your cameras, go early to get a good spot, because you are going to get some really awesome sights of the sunrise at this spot. Definitely go for this if you are in Jeju. Not to be missed for the world!

We were there in mid-March, hoping to see the mossy beach of Gwangchigi. Sadly we were out of luck. It was high tide then. But still the sunrise view was breathtakingly beautiful. Would certainly come back again to see the moss. Anyone knows when is the best time please suggest. Thanks in advance!

We were there at around 10 am and there were already many tourists and tourist buses. At the entrance before we climbed to the peak, I found out why it was one of the most popular tourist spots in Jeju. The view was breathtaking. At some spots, we could see Udo. Despite the flocking of tourists (majority were foreigners including us) and the time of the day we reached there, the view was so stunning nevertheless. The flight of stairs was nothing compared to the view we witnessed.

We were lucky with the weather to visit the place, and it is important because during the rain it might not be so attractive.The nature is very beautiful, you will take good pictures for sure.We took a small electric car (for 2 people), but it was comparatively expensive for only 2,5 hours. It is possible to go around the island during that time but only without staying at all tourist points. Moreover, you cannot really enjoy the trip because of being in hurry.All Korean suggested to try peanut and mandarin ice-cream, that we did. Again the price was high, and mandarin one was so sweet that make us to put it in trash right away.People in the island are friendly, and even offer to pick us up to some places by car and shown the shortest way.Taking a boat to see caves was the best experience during the whole travel. For only 10 000 won you will have a lot of fun as the boat goes so fast, and definetly amazing view on the island.

We were lucky because when we went, there weren't a lot of tourist going up. Otherwise, it will be even more tiring as everyone will have to accommodate each other's pace. A lot of stairs to deal with but when you're at the top, it is worth the effort. We took about 20 mins (I think), stopping occasionally to take pictures of the scenic view down below. If you're tired, don't worry as there are enough benches on the way up to rest to regain your energy, if it comes to that. It is manageable overall.On our way down, we went to the black sand beach. Spent about 40 mins there, soaking in the view from another angle. If you want the full experience, you can take the boat out with the lady divers (Hanyeo) and see them in action. Alternatively, very fresh seafood is available for your palate should you want to try. From the sea, to the chopping board and straight to your plate (raw) and that's how they eat it. We didn't do that. Can't find the courage to do so. Lol. If the heat really got to you, after the climb down, go to one of the coffee places (Angel-in-us or Starbucks) to cool down before you go elsewhere. Be prepared to sweat buckets!!!

We were here in October, so we weren't swimming. We drove by here one day to check it out, a day or two after a typhoon hit, and the beach was trashed a bit (just from trees and debris and stuff), but people were cleaning it up and there were still lots of people enjoying the beach. It looks like a nice place to spend a day, and there seemed to be a bunch of restaurants and cafes dotting the beach as well. We stopped at one of the cafes for a coffee and to enjoy the view of the water for a bit.

We were cruising the Far East and stopped at Jeju. The cheapest excursion was $120 per person. $240 for the two of us. Instead we walked around Jeju a little then hailed a cab. He took us all over the island doing all the same things for $100. Personal service. Stayed. As long as we wanted. Left when we were ready. One of the many ways weve seen the world much cheaper than most. 73 countries and territories so far. The village is interesting. 100 huts. Some occupied. And a black pig. A guy will tell you about a tea they sell that if it tastes salty or sweet will diagnose your ailments. We passed. Not sure how many people read my reviews. If you hit ?helpful?,  I?ll get an email and they always encourage me to write more :)

We went up in 20 minutes and down in 15,  we are quite fit,  all age groups going up and even people in flip flops!) I would recommend you time your visit so that you get to see the women divers (13:30 and 15:00) either before or after your walk.  If I went there for just the walk I would have been disappointed,  the photos you see are of course ariel views and a walk up doesn't give you that view,  having said that the coastal views from above are nice.  It was raining when we went but it was still do-able.  We took bus 701 (runs every 20 mins 3300 wan per person each way) from seogwipo and back.  It stops at Seongsan-ri office,  ticket booth is a couple of minutes walk away.

we went up by erimok, was the slightly shorter course but scenery was still fantastic towards the top. took us 3.3hours to reach the 1700m resting point which sells korean cup noodles at only 1500+won (ard there). this is not the peak, if you like to challenge yourself further, will have to walk for another 3-4 hours to the peak. So if you really decide to go to the peak, then just use the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa course, its shorter.We were lucky to meet some locals who advise us to walk down by yeongsil. And apparently yeongsil has the most scenic view out of all the courses. Only thing is that its full of stairs... so dont advice ascending by yeongsil. We could see ppl giving up halfway on our way down yeongsil. One more problem abt yeongsil for those who dont drive is that the bus stops 2km away from the main entrance (20mins BRISK walk) and its quite steep on most parts. Or else you can actually catch a taxi from the bus stop, should be a 5mins journey.

We went to Yongduam Rock and the weather was nice, not too sunny but not too dark.On the side where we viewed the rock, you can't really appreciate the   dragon-form   of the rock. I suggest you go to the other side and see how it looks from there.The view was nice too. It was calming.

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)

we went to this place, but we didn't went up the park/hill/rock, as it will require lots of walking, which we didn't want to do :)you will still be able to have an impressive view at the entrance, and amazed by this natural creation. you can see the people walking up to the peak, enjoy the strong wind, as it is located by the sea, do a little shopping around the entrance area, or even find a nice cafe that is facing the spot to enjoy a hot coffee!

We went to see waterfall at 12PM, there were loads of people, nevertheless view was stunning, waterfall is huge. I'd say better go in day time as when sun is starting to set you'd get weird shadows on your pics and it just won't be the same. Bear in mind you'll have to walk on huge rocks so it's not very safe for toddlers and those carrying their babies, not suitable for those with walking difficulties. Better wear sports clothes which would cover legs in case you fall, to prevent scratches or whatever other injuries. It says no swimming but we took off our shoes and walked in shallow water. It was cold but fun. We also sat on rocks in close proximity to waterfall and splashes from it made us quite wet. But it was spectacular. Such a unique place! Tickets are 1,000 for 16-24 year olds, they require ID. For adults it's 2,000.

We went to Marado Island by taking a 1 h-long ferry from Jeju Island (Daejung-Eup, Hamo ri). The ferry was nice and the could stand in either deck to enjoy the scenic view of the ocean. When you approach the island you could see the beauty of volcanic layers that forms the island and the interface of volcanic rocks and ocean was amazing. Walking is the best way to enjoy the island and you may spend nearly 3 h in the island. There are a couple of restaurants, a beautiful buddha temple, a church etc. A nice half-day trip. Highly recommended.

We went there directly from the airport via bus (because it was too early for us to check in at our booked hotel).  At the place, the lockers were not available, unfortunately, and we cannot leave our bags somewhere. So we had to carry our things up to see the Seongsan Ilchulbong. We did not attempt to climb up to the peak due to our heavy bags. Instead, we opted to see the observatory at the side of the mountain (it was free... the side going to the peak has an entrance fee) and has a nice view of the sea and the mountain. Can even go down to the sea shore if you like (we didn't). The view from the observatory was breathtaking vast ocean, blue sky and cool green mountain. Will definitely go back someday to see the peak! Also, we tried the Hallabong softcone (ice cream) just near the entrance road to the place, and it was so delicious!!

We went just one hour and a half before closing time (7:30pm). At the counter, we were told that it took about 50-minutes for round trip until the top. It was huge and made my wife hesitated to climb it at first. But by seeing the surrounding scenery, and imagining on how awesome it will be from up there, we climbed the stairs about 40 minutes (also stopped for taking pictures since the scenery was too beautiful). We could see the night view when we reached the top. It was worth it :) the best scenery I have seen in Jeju.

We went at 10am and there was a huge crowd, all trying to climb up .  Took about 40 minutes climbing up, making many stops in between to enjoy the view below.   It was  too crowded at the top and there isnt really much to see, except for the view of course.   Most people climb up, take a quick photograph and quickly climb down.

We went around the island via a three- wheel vehicle we rented for two hours.  It was definitely a nice view going around, a lot of attractions to see, white beach with very deep blue water, lighthouse, mountains, cliff, and the island was almost in a very vibrant color of yellow due to the rapeseed flowers blooming that spring time. We also chanced upon old women divers, which were popular in the island. We had lunch and tried one of specialty in the restaurant which was sea urchin seaweed soup! It has a very nice flavor and very filling.  We also ate peanut ice cream!

We want to get sunset view thus we go up at 6PM after back from Udo Island. Be prepare to climb up stairs and I mean lots of it. Have few places to stop, rest and see the sun set down. The view from top is awesome. Do carry bottle of water up as there's only 1 stall selling water when you climb around 10 to 15min. Once you pass the water selling stall, the stair steps is getting harder to climb.

We visited Udo Island in October 2016 and took the hop on hop off bus and got off at the first stop to climb up to the peak where the lighthouse was.  The climb took about an hour and though there were steps and a well travelled path, it still required some physical effort. There were hardly any trees and you would be well advised to wear a hat and sun block. Wear comfortable walking/hiking shoes and bring plenty of drinking water.  We climbed to the peak on a hot sunny day and had to stop a few times before we reached the lighthouse. The view was worth our effort.  Then we climbed down to the surrounding park, which was basically grassland with minimal trees and hardly any shelter. There were lots of other tourists.  We saw some horses grazing here and could see across to the mainland and sunrise peak as well as parts of Udo below.  This is the most enjoyable part of UDO for us and highly recommended.

We visited this sunrise pick which is one of the Natural wondes of the world during first week of May. It is easy to climb, with lots of opportunities to take rest if you need. The views during climb are simply superb. While we were climbing we saw amazingly shaped cloud formations. After all the efforts of climbing, the views from the peak are beautiful. We could not see the sunrise, but I am sure it would be worth the early getting up.I will strongly recommend visit to this place.

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).
We viewed the falls from afar and the tide was out, so it wasn't so dramatic. We were glad we made the detour to see them anyway.

We took their local tour bus to go around, where it will go around the island for sightseeing. The first stop was near the udobong peak and great view of the sea. We had lunch and ice cream there (niceeeeee). We have spent too much time here and we decided to go back after 2-3 hours, and technically you will have to board the same number of bus to go back to the port. We met a kind bus driver that took us directly to the port.

We took the public bus from Seogwipo interchange bus terminal.  It took about 90 mins to get there. This place is a tourist hot favourite after being rated as one of new 7 wonders of the world. The climb up has some hundreds of well constructed stairs,  however sometimes it can be a bit crowded at the stairs with many paused to take pictures. Hill top has amazing views of it's surroundings and we saw the ferry crossing to other islands.  It has a tiered lookout platform big enough to house few hundreds of people.  From the platform,  it's quite visible that landmark was formed due to volcanic activity history. We were told this is best location to see sun rise although we have yet to try that. Tips,  going down the hill is different side to way up.  We found the views on way down has much better vintage points than way up.

We took bus 710 from intercity terminal, cost 3300won per way. A pretty long ride, about 1hr plus. Met two visitors, one from Singapore & another from Malaysia; very friendly and gave us lot of tips getting around. When we reached at noon, the place was packed with tour buses, people & soldiers (on sight-seeing). Not a difficult hike for reasonable fit person but certainly a challenge for older folk with the steep steps. Nice view but have seen better.

We took bus 701 from Jeju city... it only took 1hr 30mins when we were told it would take 2hrs which was a pleasant surprise. The walk up is (unsurprisingly) hard because of all the steep and often uneven steps. I would suggest going in the morning or late afternoon when it's not so hot because in the heat it was tough! People say it takes 20 mins which I would say is accurate but of course depends on your fitness levels. It was so worth it though, the views are incredible. They have an amphitheater like viewing platform I guess for those wanting to see sunset/sunrise. And you go down a different way so no clashing with people coming up. It can get quite busy though!

We took a walk along the Shores of the rock.. It sure beats jux standing at the top of the observertory and takin pictures! The views are once again spectacular, no complaints.. The walk was not terrible although but I'd warn you to be careful and pick proper shoes coz they can get slippery from the crashing waves! Along the walk you'll see ahjummas selling fresh seafood catches. Try it if you have time!

We stayed at Clouds Pool and Spa Hotel which is 1km away so we could reach there at 5am to do the climb. It is fairly an easy climb aided by a lot of stairs. We had breakfast at Paris Baguette which is opposite the mountain. They open at 5am. We had peaceful breakfast as we were the only couple there. The top of the peak offers beautiful panorama view of the green grass crater, sea view skyline and the other side is the Jeju city bird?s eye view.  Air is fresh and very windy on the peak (I thought I could fly away). There were only 3 persons on the peak when we arrived. We could stay there for about half an hour to enjoy the scenery and the peace. The female divers abalone catching activities happen at 1.30pm or 3.30pm below the mountain. It?s another steep way down from carpark infront of Seongsan Mountain. From my hotel room, I could see people walking up to the mountains all day and evening. It?s definitely a must visit when you come to Jeju!

We spent a nice & easy day on the island.  The island is small enough to complete within a day and yet big enough for you to do/see.  The ferry ride to the island was a short and easy one.  We didn't drive there which was good since we already pre-planned to ride around the island.  There were many rental shops to choose from.  There were many different types of vehicle you could choose from, e.g. manual bike, ebike, mini-car (not sure what you call them), etc. Do note that some will require international license.  We opted for the ebike which was in good use for the uphills. The route around the island was scenic and very instagrammable.  Many caf챕s to choose from. It is a good place to roam in your own pace and taking your own time to absorb the pretty views.Definitely a place worth going.

We really loved it here, we went there on winter time so sadly we couldn't see the sunrise. But we could see the beautiful view of the mountain with some covered by snow. So beautiful! Tip : Use good shoes that are not slippery especially on winter as there were much slippery frozen water.

We really enjoyed this hike with our family. It is steep, as the reviews noted, but it is very fast. Our five-year-old and seven-year-old had no problem doing it on their own. It has nice views, isn?t very difficult, and it?s right next to an interesting coffee shop (you can see it from the parking lot) that has been converted from an old horseback riding resort. The coffee shop also has a bakery with some delicious treats for after the hike.  Easy to find and plenty of parking.  Overall a great little outing.

We planned for a sunrise view at Ilchulbong Park, however, we couldn't manage to fight the sleep bug. We reached Ilchulbong Park around 9.30am. Stairs climbing is quite a difficult task for me as I do not exercise much. So, I do the climbing slowly, one step at a time and do not bother the people who surpassed me. We could enjoy different views of Jeju Island as we climbed. Me and my hubby were amazed by the view and scenery once we reached the top. All the sweats and pain were paid off when we see the amazing views of Jeju and Udo Island. We wished we were here for the sunrise.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

We made our climb to watch the sunrise early in the morning. Although the estimated time to reach the top is only ard 30mins, but I find the ascent to be challenging with the steep steps and we were rushing in hope to catch the sunrise.  The viewing area at the summit is quite small, luckily there were not a lot of people in the early morning. That morning's weather was very cloudy, and we were so lucky to see the clouds opening up a hole and the rising sun peeking out of it.The descent is via another route and it was more gentle and enjoyable, with views of surrounding places.

We intentionally left town on an alternate route so that we could see this road, and it was well worth the extra few minutes. Follow the directions and have fun! If you want to view the road correctly, then pull into the parking lot behind the pig monuments :-)

we hired a taxi driver for day-trip, it's just located nearby Eco Land Theme Park & Mini Land Theme Park.we visited on late april, so not much to see. not even green farmbut still a great view to have fun with it. good experience to have a nice walk.

We hiked up on a cloudy day. I really recommend choosing the day for hiking according to the weather forecast. The hike itself and the views and people on the path made it an unforgettable experience, but after like 2,5 hours of hiking on a really quick pace we made it to the top and couldn't see anything. The crater was filled with mist and it was so windy that staying up there would have been quite uncomfortable. It doesn't necessarily take 4,5hours to get up and 4,5 hours to get down, if you don't stop every two hundred meters. But make sure to get to the last milestone (the place to take a break and buy ramen) in time to be able to start the climb to the top.I can only imagine what the trip and the scenery would be like on a clear sunny day.

We hike around the crater on a very windy day and though the weather wasn't great, the views were beautiful. Hike down the side to see the historic women divers and their fresh catch then go up to the top to enjoy Jeju from above. It's not a serious hike and there are stairs with railings all the way up.

We heard and saw this on TV and view to visit when we get the chance so of course we had to see for ourselves. We had impression very crowded road but there were only a few cars. It was about 4pm. We were able to follow another car uphill turn around, follow to the start point.We put car on neutral then let it drive us. Very strange. It just move slow motion like haunted road feel.We stop by at a mart for coffee. There is a cafe too. A few people cos winter not nany tourists strangely, we saw a van and a bus doing same thing, just gliding down.It was just nice finally seeing and experiencing this in jeju.

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do). The Sangumburi entrance fee is expensive if not in season to see the wheat fields at their peak and the changing leaves of fall, I think it was 11,000won or $11. I recommend going to Chefline Park if you are seeing this April 2018. Entrance if free there and but no volcanic crater. We went here and there was construction going on and the wheat fields had been cut down. They should charge less when construction is going on and the field has been cut. The walk around the park only takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. There are some nice views and the crater is cool.

We had only a metre of visibility when we went, it was cold, rainy and foggy. My review probably doesn’t do it justice, we were just super unlucky that day. Don’t visit on a rainy day. There is however a restaurant with an exhibition on top and there is a restroom too. We didn’t even bother with the walk as it looked gloomy and we couldn’t see much.

We got there just before dawn and it was a 20-minute hike to the top.Once we got there, we were surprised to see that there were loads of other people there to enjoy the sunrise. There's nothing blocking your view as you see the sun rise in the horizon, as if behind the sea. Absolutely must-see if you're in Jeju!

We got here by public bus from the Manjanggul caves. It took about an hour as we had to transfer. Using the public transport is a bit of an adventure in itself. I think the bus routes have been updated lately so even some of the locals seem confused at times.We looked at the top of the peak and thought, 'no way, this looks like it'll take 2 hours to climb'. However after asking other tourists we were told it takes about 25 minutes. I was sceptical as I'm not the fastest at going up stairs.The entry fee was 2,000 krw and despite taking quite a lot of short breaks on the way up we reached the top in 20 minutes! The views were lovely.We ended up doing this around midday and it was HOT. I recommend coming here earlier or later in the day if you can when it is a bit cooler. It was rewarding to reach the top. They are selling some drinks in the way up but I recommend that you pack some water as well as a snack to eat when you enjoy the views at the top.

We entered this park with great expectations - the gardens themselves are great, the bonsai area stands out as superb, and the Lava Caves offer some welcome respite from the heat.Everything in the garden was destroyed by the horrific and unacceptable conditions of the birds and other animals.  There was a smallish section with parrots, a few other birds, a monkey in a tiny cage and a few other small furry creatures.  It was filthy, some of the animals had no water, the temperature must have been 35 degrees.  There was one small animal that was clearly suffering greatly (in one of the cages with no water). I emptied the contents of my water bottle into it's water bowl, and reported its condition to a member of staff - who did nothing.We went on to see peacocks and ostriches, yes in slightly larger enclosures, but with no shade, no vegetation, and 13 peacocks in a tiny cage.  The birds were in obvious distress with obsessive grooming and clear skin infections.I've travelled all over the world, and been to many places like this and never, from the poorest, to the richest countries, have I seen animals kept in these conditions. I rarely, if ever, write reviews, but I am so angry at the conditions here, that it's important to be aware.The gardens are immaculate, the conditions of the animals are disgraceful, and should be an embarresment to whoever runs this organisation.Do not visit!

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

We didn't take the 3-hour journey but rather followed our tour guide on shorter route (approx 45 mins one way) to the top of another similar peak. It was bright and sunny with cold breeze which made a perfect day for hiking and photo taking. It's mainly   country view   from the top where green fields and moutains cover majority of your sight. You can also see the beach and sea far away with planes taking off and landing at Jeju airport. Overall, it's a nice outdoor walk and a place to chill out after a hectic journey.

We did this hike by end of March 2014. The first part is indeed a kind of forest walk. Half way we were indeed surprised to see some snow on the hills and later on lots of snow on the path, Since we did not have those clampons it was pretty tough. At the 2nd shelter we did indeed buy those clampons whereafter the hike was more easy to do. The view from top was not that good due to the upcoming mist. We were amazed though to see so many RAVENS waiting for food.

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water. Most people were using walking poles as well, which became extremely frustrating as they tended to block the paths. The only people I saw fall were using these poles, they really are not required.It would be difficult to do this track in the rain, as it would get quite slippery in places. My advice would be to go early to avoid the majority of the crowds - the car park fills with tour buses by mid-morning. We started at 0700 and it was still relatively busy then. You need to be at the last rest station by 1230 to be able to continue to the summit and leave the summit by 1430.Overall - I wouldn't do it again, but if you had a free day on Jeju, it's a good way to burn off a few calories.

We chose the   short   hike up the mountain (volcano) and it was all up. We are Coloradoans and hike quite a bit and this one was a bit of a challenge. The first part was through an oak forest and it was hot and humid. We sweat like crazy and things got better once we got out of the oaks and into the pines. It took us 2+ hrs to get to the rest station and a bowl of noodles and a chocolate bar. The hike was amazing, though with strange vegetation and a miniature deer, the only wildlife we saw along with many butterflies. We did not go to the top since it was in the clouds and starting to rain, but the views of the ocean and Jeju-si were as advertised. This is a must see place and there is an easier hike than ours, but takes much longer we were told.
we came here during the end of autum, so the grass was all yellow and brown. there was not much to see.Not recommended when you come in March, coz the view is not very nice..but we still had fun

We arrived shortly before sunset and made our way up the mountain. It didn't take too long at all, and there are plenty of resting areas for those who get tired quicker, or want to take in the views. Once at the top we didn't have to fight for space and we watched the beautiful sky change colours over the quaint little town below. It was gorgeous. A must see if you can.

Waterfalls are very accessible in Jeju. Jeongbang is the most unique as we seldom see a waterfall that goes straight to the sea. Going by public bus is easy and the path towards the falls are already paved except for the rocky part near the falls itself. I suggest you take your time in sitting on one of the rocks and just enjoy the relaxing view. If you're patient, you can wait for 10-20 mins for tourists to leave and you can have the view all by yourself.  For photography enthusiasts, have a wide angle lens ready =D

Watching sunrise from the sea is amazing experience. You don't have to climb up too high, still can see the downtown below. And the way down is such a relax with beautiful view. Just 5 minutes walk from the bus stop and very near from Seopjikoji

Was wanting to catch sunset in Jeju, and it seems all will require some climbing. My family was tired, and hence chose this place instead.Not too bad for being lazy to climb. You will need to go to the far end near the hotel. The road alongside was quiet and very light traffic, so you can park there temporarily to view the sunset.

Was recommended to visit this crater by our driver cum guide. Initially we wasn't too keen from the view of main entrance but we were stunned by the beautiful silver grass surrounding after entering. Climbing slowly is possible thou pathway can be slight steep. My parent did it at their own pace and there was a little hut & mini playground at the top for a rest. Along the way up, silver grasses are fully bloom and it views are fascinating with mountains seen faraway (like a natural backdrop). It's a sight not to be missed and understood only occur during autumn into winter period!! Thanks to our taxi driver Mr Lee Hong Min for the great recommendations.

Was lucky to have been here as it was free for the entrance. Usually per entry would cost 2000 won but it was a holiday. The scenery and view is amazing up top. The view of the crater is nice but the view 180 degrees around is way better. You will see the town which you stopped at and the immense coastline around. Would highly recommend if you can catch the sunrise however it is quite a journey away from the Jeju city which means you have to time your travel right. Visiting during normal hours will still give you the breath taking view. Just a catch, you would have to hike. If you are fit enough, it should take you 15 to 20 mins up top. Can be pretty steep so take your time and rest along the way.
Was it worth the view? It was windy and a bit of a walk ...but was it worth the view? Nope! Our tour coach took us there. One has to use a lot of imagination to   see   a dragon's head!

Walking up the stairs is tiring but once at the top, you can see the craters which are filled with greenness of plants... View the surroundings from top is superb! Good for nature lovers yet those that do not want to hike the hill...At the seaside below the hill, you can enjoy seafood fresh fr the sea!

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html

Walked to the bridge as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel seogwipo). It's a nice bridge and you can walk across it to saeyong island, where you can have a short hike around the island. Nice views during the hike where you can see the ocean and three different islands. It's also near Cheonjiyeon waterfall.

Walked over from our hotel to the waterfalls and enjoyed the view.  Absolutely gorgeous. As a group, we enjoyed climbing up and down stones to get closer to the falls for pictures or over to see the fishermen (and women) slightly further away from the falls.
Walk up to the peak & you'll never regret...Healing by nature. Can see beautiful view of Jeju.Though a bit tiring to walk up to peak, you'll be amazingly surprised.Will come again soon!

Visited this museum with my kids.  There were hundreds of Teddy bears displayed over 3 floors. We saw Teddy bears in all sizes,  different era and occasions, celebrity characters dress up, themes etc.   Kids were excited to watch the free performance theatre with teddy bears dressed up as Elvis and his supporting singers singing. Every floor has different group of bears on display.   Entrance also allowed visitors to venture out to the back garden which boosted more Teddy bear statues.   Garden was well maintained and worth a visit.  Near the main entrance,  it also had a 2 storey high wooden Teddy bear which is a real attraction for the kids. The entry ticket is not cheap,  unless you are a real Teddy bear fan,  in my view,  it is not a must see destination.
Very peaceful and beautiful place. Loved walking around and seeing all the beautiful bonsais, scenic view, beautiful waterfall and fishes. Would definitely love to visit again <3

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.

Up & down of the mountain took us 9.5 hours including some short rest time during the hike. We started the hike around 9am (recommend to start early, we were late), and came down around 6:30pm. Our legs were like jelly legs after the hike, but is worth the hike. You can see nice view along the journey. Please do not forget to greet everyone you met with   anyeonghaseyo  , they are all very friendly people. Wear a pair of good hiking shoes, bring some snacks with you and also water. The stalls along the mountain are closed during our hike, luckily we have prepared enough snacks and water. The view at the peak is breathless. A lots of old korean aunties and uncles also managed to reach the peak, so I guess we all younger than them have no excuses of not fit to hike, right? haha...Wear sport attire, although some said it will be freezing cold at the peak (about 1950 meters height), but believe me, you wont feel cold as you have already all sweat during the hike. We spent about 30mins to 1 hour at the peak taking photos, resting and having our snacks before going down again. A pair of good hiking shoes is important so that you won't get blister on your feet. We will go back again in different season if we have the chance. We were travelling there in Oct 2018.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say   Udo  . The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the   old fashioned   bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Took bus 701 from Seogwipo (around 1hr20mins) to Seongsan IIchulbong entrance station. The bus doesn't exactly stop at the entrance, but you can see the crater from the station. Just walk towards it. A big innisfree building is where the entrance is. The wind was pretty strong on the day that I went, so it was a good thing I brought my windbreaker. I suppose on less windy days, it's not that cold as many were in shorts and t-shirt. ie, they weren't prepared for the wind and were shivering. To be honest, I wasn't quite sure what to expect before I saw this show. I knew generally it was about performers who drew and entertained the audience somehow on stage. BUT IT WAS AMAZING! We saw   Team Chaplin,   four   hunky   young men, all dressed in decidedly stylish paint-splattered black clothing, complete with Charlie Chaplin bowlers. It could best be described as a multi-media show in which the performers draw using charcoal, paint, LED touch screens (I think!) and other art mediums and techniques to create a wide variety of images from pop culture and the classics, most of it set to contemporary music. They dance plus do a little martial arts, mime and comedy, and they use audience participation very effectively. Among the images are Michael Jackson, the Little Mermaid, Bruce Lee, Beethoven and Jeju's own icon, Dolhareubang, or   Stone Grandfather.   Even after seeing the show, I am not sure how some of the effects were achieved. I'm not going to do any   spoilers   here of the action, because the element of surprise is important for this show. But trust me, you WILL be surprised. It has many entertaining moments. If you live in Jeju or plan to visit, you should make time for the show, which is performed on the campus of beautiful Cheju Halla College...you'll be treated there to one of the best views of Halla Mountain anywhere on the island...take your camera for that, and for the photo/autograph session at the end of the show.

To be honest, I didn't expect much at first, but when I started walking up the stairs, OMG! I was really awed by the clear blue sky, silver grasses, wind, everything! The view of the crater was just   so-so   to me but the view of the other side with the silver grasses was just way too amazing! I would say, it's not something that's so special that you must go to see no matter what but still, it's something that you won't be able to see everyday or everywhere. First of all, you must go at the correct timing. I went during mid-October, the view was magnificent! You can even see Hallasan from afar (check out my photo). Thereafter, you can walk through a small road where you literally being surrounded by silver grasses. That's a perfect place to take photos as well (photo attached).This can be a romantic place, or it can also be a peaceful place where you go to relax your mind and to see something different.

To be blunt, I couldn't see the dragon's head in the Dragon Head Rock, and I'm not alone. Apparently a portion of the formation fell off during a heavy storm long ago, so perhaps it was once more impressive. Currently, it has become iconic for a rather tired trend in Korean tourism. Pointing at the sky and finding clouds that look like other things is childlike. Officially naming rocks and then designating them as   important cultural artifacts   in order to manufacturer tourism is crass. In much the same way that the Korean government has become intimately involved in generating the so-called   Korean Wave   of K-pop and Korean television dramas, there is a constant rush to capitalize on landmarks, events, and experiences that will help distinguish Korea in general and Jeju specifically in the competitive marketplace of global cultural value. This push to invent cultural significance is monopolized by a predominately male class of older Korean bureaucrats who have capitalized on Confucian values in order to override younger, better ideas, fueling their own, often tedious marketing concepts despite the existence of far better and substantive materials from which to draw inspiration. Take for instance Jeju's rich history of folklore and deities. Sure, you can dawdle about with stories of a dragon stealing jade or herbs of immortality from Halla Mountain and being shot by a celestial arrow as punishment, turning it to stone; but the fact is there are literally hundreds of far better stories that have some basis in local lore rather than the distinctly artificial details surrounding the Dragon's Head Rock. If you're interested, look for books on the subject, some of which were written by expatriates in an attempt to save this rich heritage from being slowly whitewashed away by modern fabrications. A book called   Spirits: Jeju Island's Shamanic Shrines   by Joey Rositano comes immediately to mind. Or you can go to any number of local beaches and walk along paths where every 20 yards or so you can read a plaque that tells you what a large stone vaguely resembles if you squint hard and suspend your disbelief.    That said, there's nothing wrong with taking a nice stroll along the seaside in this part of town if you only have a short amount of time to spend and you need to get to the airport soon. There are some passable restaurants along the way, a couple of good caf챕s, and some great views of the ocean. However, make no mistake - this is an authorized conduit for tourists and as such you will be subject to a conveyor belt of people on the same walk, as well as an abundance of stores whose sole purpose is to extract money from you by selling tawdry bits of plastic.

This was the most fascinating and beautiful experience during my two week stay in South Korea. The long, winding path to get to the coastline to see the Women Divers Show is gorgeous from beginning to end. The mist hovering over the black volcanic sand was unlike anything I have ever seen. I never wanted to leave. The hike up to Sunrise Peak was sweaty but worth it. The long, windy path to get the the top of the peak is fairly easy to walk and offers many wonderful views along the way. The fog was too dense to see anything from the very top, but I'm still glad I did it. This was such an amazing part of my trip; one of my most fond travel memories ever.

This was rated as one of the top 3 to visit in Jeju so we actually stayed at the nearby Airstay Hamdeok Hotel.  It  was very nice.  The beach is clean and had pristine waters and black rocks.  The sand was fine and felt good to walk on with your bare feet.  There were some really nice picturesque views so we took a ton of photos. There was a connected path to a hill and it allowed for some decent small hikes.  We went in March so the flowers on the hill were blooming with yellow and purple colors.  There were also some white flower blossoms coming out from the trees. With the ocean or the city views in the background from the hill, it allowed for some very unique photos for your memories.
