After the little hike, we played around in the water on the beach and it was nice because it was low tide and you could hang out in one of the exposed sand bars. It was very pretty and relaxing. Definitely a must see if you're in Jeju!

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This was a great stop for us, and even the kids enjoyed it.  It was refreshing in the summer.  The walk was not bad at all, and the view was just beautiful.  It's nice to just pause and think about how those rocks were created.  There were a handful of people so it took some time to get a nice spot to take a photo without people in the background.  I can't imagine how much harder it is when the weather is better.  It's still a must-see when in Jeju.

This top site in Jeju island is also known as Seongsan Sunrise Peak or 掠길ε뷴낡 It earns its reputation as Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site, and once you reached the top, you will see why. Be warned, it is a reasonable difficult climb that will easily take 20min to hike up. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water during hot weather. The uphill stairway will take you to a majestic dormant crater that offers spectacular view of the sunrise, hence the name. Be prepared for massive crowd of tourists throughout your climb, and get your vantage point to capture some of the majestic scenery throughout your climb.On your way down after enjoying the panoramic view of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage surrounding, make sure you allow enough energy to take the downhill path on the left to explore the Haenyo women diver performance at certain times. We were there after 3pm, so missed out on them unfortunately.

This site consists of a large network of staircases that you climb to see a crater as well as a beach where the woman divers do a demonstration.The walk up the stairs is very long. It is not impossible and there are many places to take breaks without holding up the line. The spot is very busy so there will be an unbroken line of people going up and down. I would suggest taking water with you. The view from the top is quite nice. Allow 1 hour to do the climb at a leisurely pace.At the beach the woman divers do demonstrations on a set schedule. Check the times when you arrive. They will suit up for the dive, sing a song and then go into the water looking for seafood. When we were there a lady came back with an octopus. It does not take long for them to find something so it is worth it to wait to see the catch.There are bathrooms and snack shops there as well.

This review was told to me by my awesome afternoon English class student.  I love Korea; especially because I have great students.  It is very beautiful island. Next time I will go to U-do Island with Diisha.You should visit the ocean.  There are many nice beaches.  I didn't like the lighthouse because it was scary.  I liked the lunch. The noodles were delicious/very good. The smell was good. You can see everything in one day.  I was there for four hours.  (Monica/Sing hae).

This place was crazy crowded but it was a Sunday. Still, there was much to see. Unfortunately, the Haenyo weren't doing any demonstrations (I think the water was too rough or something). My wife and I hiked up to the 'peak' and got a nice view  both of Jeju, Udo, and also the crater. Pretty cool! The hike was a bit strenuous and it was a little warm that day, so make sure to pack enough water. There were quite a lot of people around too so mind the crowd. Either way, it's worth the visit but probably best to go mid-week if possible. There are numerous great views to appreciate both on the way up and the way down. The path down takes a slightly different route too, which is nice.

This place seems to be a lowkey secret place for the local. I went there early autumn so? maybe that's why it's so surreal and empty and looks like I had the whole   pools   for myself. Water's still not cold yet and don't forget to bring mask to see so many tiny fishes down under. Mother-nature created 3-4   pools   and amazingly, it happened to be different depth levels too so to make sure it safe, you can let your kids swim in the most shallow one, just be careful of the sharp rocks (hey it's all natural). Great view with the ocean and beautiful color on a sunny day!

This place is the signature sightseeing here. So every tourists would be here. It's crowd with people. There're many shops, kiosk, snack bar and food shops at the front of the sightseeing. So there are large space for parking. You need to buy ticket to get in there. Once you get ticket, you walk straight on the walk way till you see the junction. There's the highlight signage for photo shooting. And you need to choose either way to go. If you go to the right, you need to walk up to the hill and you will see the good view from there. The way to go up the mountain is fine, not too rough. But not recommend during rainy day.If you go to the left, you will see fisherman Village, sea sand sun and fresh seafood from local people. The highlight is the lady from the village dive deep into sea to get the seafood stuffs.

This place is new of 7 wonders by UNESCO. There are a lot of place for you to take a beautiful pictures with the view mountain, ocean and city. They call this place s sunrise peak, you can check the schedule of sunrise in the stones in the front gate. You can buy a ticket around KRW 2,000 to enter. Then you can climb the mountain with hundreds of stairs (I didn't count it). Prepare yourself before climbing, better take a bottle of water. There are a view rest area while you climb the stairs. At the top you can see the very beautiful landscape. It's worth dude!

This place is just to see the stone columns, not a must see place but worth a visit if you like the deep sea. Only 1 viewing scenic point. On good days you can see Mt Hallasan. Can take pictures there as your background.
This place is easily accessible. It offers a great view of the waterfall and it seems during the spring or summer season, you can even go into the waters for some refreshing moments.

This place is easily accessible by bus. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about more than an hour to get to Seongsan Ilchulbong. After you get off at Ilchulbong entrance station, walk right into the small alley and continue straight until the end to the Main Street, you will see sign leading to Ilchulbong. It was a nice hike but a lot of stairs. The view is beautiful up at the top. There are plenty rest stop along the way so no need to worry. When you come down, you can go to the beach where you?ll find the house of women divers. There are performances at certain time slot but since I visited in the winter, there was none. They also sell fresh seafood where you can have right at the restaurant. It was quite expensive but It?s fresh and also to support the women divers.

This place is caused by volcanic activity, specially beautiful on October full of Flame Grass. Entrance fee is quite expensive, but you can enjoy beautiful views ,can see volcanic cones in other place even Seongsan Ilchulbong when it's sunny.

This pedestrian bridge leads you to a small island where you can take a walk for around 30 minutes. There is not much to see on the island itself but I will say the view is quite nice. I visited around sunset time but it was a bit gloomy that day so we didn't get to see a nice sunset. There were many mosquitoes when we walked around so beware when you visit during Summer. Otherwise, this is a nice place to spend your time.

This park includes a variety of sights including two lava tubes, an aviary that includes a variety of peacocks, ostriches etc, a small traditional village, strange little rock people sculptures, and a very impressive botanical garden with outdoor sections around a pond and several green houses.   Some strange combinations in the outdoor section with large palms mixed up with various types of cacti and other random mixes of fabulous plant specimens from all over the world.  The greenhouse plants seem a bit more organized by regions or types (e.g., large cactus collection in one greenhouse; palms in another), with live animals interspersed between the plants (impressive boa and python collection, also some special turtles, and lizards such as nile monitors, iguanas, etc.).  In between plant viewing, I enjoyed a nice cool cactus juice relaxing in the herb bar.

This one is located near  Hyeopjae  Beach,  so you can see the Biyangdo island as well. i liked it. Its pretty spacious and got necessary facilities like combini nearby, toilet and place with free water. it also got nice view and some of typical jeju sculptures of  female divers and spirits that protect the Island. Sand is white and feels nice.

This island is like a mini-Jejudo. You can see entire Seongsan Ilchubon from this island. This place is more relaxing and peaceful than Jeju-do, a bit off-touritst path compared to other places. I like the view at Udobong at its atmosphere. Which I had more time, so I can bike around the island.

This is the highlight of our trip. For only KRW2,000, it's worth every won! A must visit. The hike to the top can be very tiring especially if you are not fit. That said, the air is fresh and invigorating, so take your time and pace yourself and you will reach there eventually. If ahjummas can make it up there, so can you! (what I was telling myself on my way up). When you finally reach the top, you get to see the crater, although I do prefer the view on the way up of the town and the surrounding areas. Even if you don't hike to the top, there is still much to see. If you take the scenic route, you can have a great view of the ocean and the cliffs. Great photo opportunities.

This is the climb for the unfit too. It is relatively easy compared to Hallasan or Elephant Mountain in Taipei (not even half as difficult) and the views all the way up and down is amazing. We did the sunrise climb as we stayed overnight at Illchubong Hotel. From the hotel, it is about 20mins walk to the base - we had a car. There are many public buses that come to this spot. If you have 4of you, you can cheaply get a taxi to the spot for the morning climb.At the top, we did not see the amazing postcard view (aerial view?). If you wanted to take the sunrise with the illchubong Seongsan, you actually do not have to climb up the mountain. There is a huge area to view it as you drive up the highway.There are public buses to the entrance/ base of the mountain. There are 2 women divers performance which we missed due to the timing. It's 11 and 1 or 3pm. You can probably go to Udo island and be back for the late performance.Highly recommended to visit.

This is the best waterfall I've seen among the famous ones in Jeju (Jeongbang, Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon). It also requires more physical effort since you have to climb and go down several stairs. There are also a number of viewing decks: for me, the one near the pavilion is the best (less people there too). Highly recommended unless you hate stairs. Best to bring shoes with good grip though since the stairs can be slippery when wet.

This is sunrise peak at Jeju island you should to add in your travel list. Before go to Seongsan pls check the sunrise time. You will see a very fantastic view point here. Anaway, pls prepare your cloths for strong windy and cold. Along the walking platform the view is beautiful also. Do not miss it.

This is such a great place!Even if you don't have enough time, you can see a lot.There are few stages and different   yards   to go to.Really peacefull place if you climb few stages up.After going up you can see beautiful view of the coast as well.And the helpful thing is that they have a small shop in front of the temple (downstairs) so after climbing all mountains and the temple place you can get nice drink or ice cream. Also, they have a car parking place.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is one of my favourite places to visit in Jeju. No matter which angle you are taking photos from, the views are gorgeous. You can hike up Seongsan as well, if you are up for it. Or you could go down nearer the shoreline to catch a glimpse of the women divers. Past that area, and you can make out Udo Island in the distance. It has gotten extremely crowded over the years though, with tons of tour groups making their way here. It still remains a must-see area in Jeju, in my opinion.

This is my second time here. On my first trip, we can't get close to the cliff because of strong waves. This time round, I finally get to see the unique rock formations that made this a unesco site. A few photo spots in this area. I think 30mins viewing time is enough.

This is my favourite one of the three waterfalls i visited in Jeju! (April 2018)This place consist of three level waterfalls. The first level you will only see the waterfall if it has rained enough and the waterlevel is high enough to create the waterfall. The second one is the biggest of the three levels. It can be seen from two places. First is by the staircase and upclose. The second one is going over the bridge and after that (stone) stairs up on your rightside after crossing over the bridge. You can get a great view for the 2nd waterfall!The third and last level is the furtherst and the smallest one of all. If you are not fit enough or you can't walk very well, I advise to skip this one as there are a lot of stairs to go down and up afterwards.The first 2 levels are good enough to get a great view out of the place.

This is like a must-see attraction according to the reviews and the crowds there.... so despite there is nothing much to see when you reach the summit.... just some balding green on a small concave patch of land  .. it is probably still worth the 20 odd minutes climb up , for health sake.. .   Some cardio exercise is always good after all the black pig meals ! If you arrive at the right time at the foot of the hill, you may be lucky to  catch some women divers performing there..

This is in my opinion the best waterfall in Seogwipo. I don't know if it's the biggest or the tallest, but it is truly unique, as water falls down into the ocean in the middle of a pebble beach. I visited it on a rainy and windy day, and because of it it might have left a stronger impression on me. I could really feel the forces of nature. Also, since the water falls onto the beach, you can take pictures really close to the waterfall. Overall, it is a must see waterfall if you come to Seogwipo, even though it doesn't get more than 20 minutes to get a nice view of the fall and its surroundings.

This is definitely a must do on Jeju Island.  Climb early in the morning to avoid the throngs of people.  If the pollution is low, you'll have a great view.  Beware, even if you climb early in the morning, it may not be peaceful.  There will be many selfie sticks! I was expecting lush green grass and canola flowers -- it became very apparent that the online images have been Photoshopped.  It is still well worth it to visit - just don't expect the view to be as stellar as what you see online.

This is by far the easiest rock formation to see on the island. It?s within a stroll from the carpark and very accessible, no Long trials or multiple flights of stairs to climb. Expect bus loads of tourist though. Good views of the coast from the viewing deck.

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

This is a real gem. You can enter for free and walk around, have a picnic and enjoy nature and the views. If you hike to the top of the hill you can see the whole city and the ocean and on the other side the mountain
This is a quick and easy tour- you are there to take just a quick look and pictures. Nothing much to do and see- great ocean view and rock formations but that's it, so 15 minutes will do

this is a must-see. A temple in the cave made by ancient volcano corruption. It is on the top on the hill. Great views on the sea, pieceful atmosphere. You can drink water from thespring, it is a water from the mountain and it is clean.

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This is a beautiful volcanic crater well worth visiting. It doesn?t take too long to reach the top from the entrance (despite the sometimes steep stairs). The views are magnificent as you ascend, from the summit, as well as when you descend. Plus there are various volcanic rock formations that you can appreciate along the way, both ascending and descending (the two paths are different). The crater is full of trees and grass of a very unique shade of green (I?ve seen this shade of green only in the vegetation of other extinct volcanic craters such as the ones in Tanzania). There are platforms to sit on at the summit from where you can appreciate the view. After descending, make sure to visit the cove where you can meet the Haenyeo or the traditional fisher women of Jejudo. The way to the cove is clearly marked with signboards and it?s only a couple of staircases down to the beach. The Haenyeo put up a performance twice a day, which is very touristy but interesting nevertheless. You can buy all kinds of fresh seafood from them and ask them to prepare it for you to eat at the restaurant. But it?s mostly eaten raw / semi-raw with various sauces and the typical side dishes. The sea weed is particularly good, which you get as a side dish. There is unfortunately no English menu. If you don?t want to eat raw seafood, after picking your seafood portion at the entrance, take it to the counter inside the restaurant and ask that it be stir-fried (?pokkum? in Korean). Beware that even when it?s stir-fried, it?ll still be more on the raw side than the fried side. The black sand beach in the cove is also a treat. If you look closely and attentively, you?ll find all sorts of marine life among the rocks, in the pools and on the sides of the mini cliffs facing the beach.

This cave is actually a volcanic Lava tube, not limestone cave. So don't expect to see amazing things like what you see in Guilin and Yunan.Same as reviewer ggkoh, I visited there after a day of persistent rain. The cave is wet, filled with small pool of water here and there. The floor bed is rocky and uneven. So be equipped with a jacket comes with hood (or raincoat) and a good pair of track shoes.

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don?t need to linger. It?s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...
There is no harm to walk and hike to see the view of coastline and ocean.? The temple is not grand or manificent.? It is hard to hike to the budda in the cave, but you can try.
There is a good view at 1100m streetway of hanla mountain.in Winter day, you can see the snowflowers at hereby

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

There are a few coastal scenary within this area and it's all within 10 to 20 mins drive. Even though it's not extending for miles and miles along the coast, most of the major viewpoints were wonderful. It's a must see if you are visiting Jeju island.

The Yeomiji Botanical Garden is easy to find and has parking places available. Entrance is not so pricy. The place is easier to enter with stroller or wheel chair. The glass house is quite big and divided into flower/aquatic/cactus/jungle and tropical fruits garden. The outdoor garden is also spacious but we did not go there. Not many people have visited the place. Consequently it was quiet and empty. The garden is very beautiful, interesting and green. It has also a lot of plants and trees but the wow effect is definitely missing.? On top of the glass house is also a view point with elevator connection. Finally I have seen much better botanical gardens.

The volcano is an impressive sight from the car-park. Get ready for the steps up 180 metres to the top. Be prepared to climb, climb, climb!As you ascend, the view is the best reward, and from the top you have a commanding panorama.Time it at sunrise or at sunset if you can - we went at sunset: it was remarkable and very moving to see the sun disappear behind the mountains.

The village has preservations from time past. It made for a pleasant morning walk through the village.It's used much for filming of historical period dramas. One gets to see, close up, relative size et al, a little of what life was like 100 years ago.I enjoyed the bright golden sunshine, flowering trees and the beautiful voice of our guide who sang 2 folk songs whilst using a wine jar as an instrument.We also viewed the daily life of the women divers . Amazing people who adapted so well to the harsh realities of their world.

The view was amazing even if you did not make it up to the top. From halfway point onwards, you could see the awesome seaview. We went in the afternoon so that we could catch the divers' performance at 3pm. What impressed me the most about the performance was that the Ajumma actually went into the cold waters in winter! For that, it was worth my time standing out in the cold to show them our support.
The view is nice. If you just want to see the view, half up just ok. If you want to see the crater then go up and see. Nice view
The view is breathtaking, a must see and must go location in my opinion. You will be amazed how lava can turn into such a beautiful scenary.

The temple complex is structurally interesting because it is spread out on the foot of the mountain. It's not actually very big and not of the structures are magnificient compared to other temples elsewhere, but very nice overall. But the view is really amazing. Look South and you'll see green slopes going down to the sea, look the other way and you'll see behind the temple rocky mountains that almost look like a cliff. This place captures perfectly the contrast between the sea and the mountain, and is very relaxing.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The stand-alone rock wasn't as impressive as say the Twelve Apostles in Melbourne, but it was nice to walk and take in the sights in the area.If you are a fan of Korean drama serial, Da Changjin (鸚㏝룝), you'll see that they filmed some scenes here (marked by some cut-out boards)On the way out, we saw a store selling black or red volcanic rocks (plus drinks and a really yummy grape ice bar). These rocks float cos of the air trapped in the holes. We bought some home as souvenirs to remember Jeju.I'll recommend taking a walk in the area. The views were great and it was most enjoyable.

The sorroundings are definitely better than the rock itself: nice little Korean hut, beautiful bridge. But the place is bigger than we thought and because of so many tourists and buses easy to find! To watch the waves and the ocean was also nice to see. Good to see if you are close by or want to walk around the coast! We walked there from the city centre, although it was raining, and enjoyed the view from the ocean!

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak has 2 main attractions. The first is obviously the climb to the peak itself. The second is the Woman Divers at the black sand beach at the bottom. We spent about 3 hours here and it was just barely enough. The climb is actually not that bad for the physically fit. The steps are steady and most are stone paved or have wooden stairs. There were quite a few elderly ladies/gents climbing too. Rest areas with benches are plentiful, so there really is no reason why you would not try for the top if you have the time. :-) Two thirds of the way up, you will see a big resting area with a marvelous view of the city below. Once you are up at the peak, you will also be able to see the city view AND into the crater. The climb back down is very safe with well made wooden staircases. Regarding the Woman Diver show at the bottom, I found the show to be a little underwhelming and a bit too touristy. However, it was still an interesting experience to see divers selling fresh seafood off the beach. If you have limited time, I would recommend that you focus on the hike/view, and just spend a couple of minutes to browse through the woman diver area. I think the Seongsan Iichulbong is a must-see in Jeju.

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The sea in Jeju Island was very clean and a good place to enjoy the natural scenery. There were many kinds of cafes and long coastal roads. Also, the cafes had unique personalities and were good places to take pictures and the taste of coffee was good. I went there for 2 nights and 3 days, and I could see the beautiful sea when the sun was bright, and there was a dark atmosphere of the sea when the weather was cloudy. However, unlike in the past, the whole atmosphere of the sea seemed to disappear as many buildings were built. There was a wish for a return to the old sea. Nevertheless, if I visited Jeju Island again, I wanted to go to Woljeongri Beach again. Viewers of this review also recommend going to Woljeongri beach where I went.
The rock with dragon head shape. Is a quite short time view and to feel the sea breeze. We took the staircase down to see the rock with dragon head shape. Other than that, nothing special here.

The previous review states that the climb was in 20 minutes but for a relatively unfit person like myself, it took me 30 to 40 minutes with numerous stops beginning from halfway till the top. Much to your agitation, we see older citizens and children alike happily and easily climbing the steps and overtook you to the top. Nevertheless, the view on the top was well worth the tough climb (according to my unfit status). Managed to take some photo shots of the surrounding and the crater itself. As it was just beginning spring, the crater floor was covered with brownish grass and vegetation, not the greenish color you would expect in summer. What I most remembered was the real cold buffeting wind of 2 Degrees Celsius blowing and you could really feel it even with winter jackets and caps worn while climbing the steps. But it was most memorable. Wife did not want to climb the steps but decided to go shopping for the famous Jeju orange chocolates in the shops at the foot of the park.

The place is super nice spot to chill with coffee/tea or snack while overlooking fields of green tea. Their food is ok but the presentation is super. We see many family's and couples came here to take pictures of the great green fields or kids would just run around enjoying themselves.The place is quite open so is not very noisy and everyone do still get some space to just relax.Also, if you look at the chair setting, you can tell that they purposely made it so you can enjoy the view while you are here!!

The period I went was very windy, the surrounding was very refreshing with patches of green. Very relaxing, peaceful  and is a good place for photography. A typical k-drama filming location for kfans to visit! Once you reach the highest point, you will see endless of   green    and can even spot mountains that is far away. You can actually relax and enjoy this view by sitting at this cute wooden swing. Very nice place which you probably won't want to miss it.However, to visit this place, you need an entrance fee of  6,000won, But if you booked a experience tour driver with your own group of friends, he can help you bargain it to a even cheaper price which is like 3,000won per person! So, afterall, it was pretty worth it for both the price and this exquisite experience! Recommended to rent a car there, inaccessible by public transport!

The park is divided to theme gardens from different areas (China, Japan, Italy, ...) Huge greenhouse has tropical fruit in glass domes so yo can learn how cocoa and bananas grow. There are also glass-fibre dinosaurs and crocodiles hiding in some of the more jungle-like parts. From the viewing platform you can see all the gardens and surroundings. Place was a must-do for schools trippers, who were plenty when I visited. A relaxing stroll in beautiful surrounding.

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.? There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).? In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.? If art is your thing, then definitely go.? Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.
The mountain isn't so high, but the view is wonderful. You can see the other peaks at the top of Halla, and it's astonishing. Definately the top thing to do when you're here.

The Moon Light Walking Tour at Jungmun Golf Club was pleasant and relaxing. The walking tour started and end at the same golf course with optimum safety rules for ongoing corona-19 spreading. The distance was shorter than expected, about 1.5 km which took only about 30 min. Walking was fun due to the group of new friends. During the walking, the sunset was very beautiful. Also, the scenery of the ocean view seen from the golf course was amazing. After walking for 30 minutes, we enjoyed an evening

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don?t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

The island was recommended by a friend, it’s fairly small with gorgeous ocean views. You can hire bikes to ride around the island, we chose not to and just took a slow stroll around stopping at one of the many pavilions facing out to sea for some lunch with a view. If you are a seafood lover you’ll be in heaven with several places to eat freshly prepared food however if you don’t eat seafood I’d recommend taking something with you (we had been warned). The green barley festival was on while we were there so lots of fields to see and take photos in. A perfect way to spend 3 hours in the sun (be warned there is no shady spots except for the pavilions so take a hat or buy one from the locals like I did)
The great place to hangout..i like the view.. have many shop,cafe to chill outAnd if you lucky you can see the women looking for a seafood , also can enjoy the fresh seafood

The ferry to Udo island is fairly close to the Seongsan Ilchulbong peak, close to a 15 mins walk. The ferry ride is 15 mins only, and you get to see some amazing views all through. In the island, there are many beautiful beaches and cafes. We rented bikes (do remember to ask them for a map if you do!), and rode all around the island. A complete round on the ocean road took like 3+ hours, but was loads of fun. Cos we could stop by at beaches to relax, or cafes for a quick bite or drink. We took lots of incredible pictures. A perfect day spent in gorgeous weather!

The experience was exactly like what I read from reviews and so I'll just focus on key things.-If for youngsters,  no issues.-For people not used to visiting caves-*wear shoes that don't slip*bring a torch if darkness is a concern *wear a light jacket- there are unexpected water drops, huge temperature difference with outside -Using mobile phones, not easy to take good photos. What you see is better than what is captured by phones. Online photos look so much better than what we saw.-Flowers outside the cave are lovely. Good photo taking spots.

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

The climb is not too bad with stairs going all the way up. The view from the top is amazing and definitely worth the climb.  Below there is also a show put on by the women free divers, as well as a short boat tour to see the other side.

The cliff was very beautiful and unique, and is definitely worth a visit if you?re looking for nice sightseeing views in Jeju. However, other than viewing the cliffs, there was nothing much to do, so spending an hour or less there would be sufficient. Do head down the viewing platform to the bottom of the cliffs, where you can get a magnificent view at sea level, with lesser tourists there. Overall, if you?re looking for a short sightseeing trip, these cliffs would be a good option to explore the wonders of Jeju.

The cherry blomsson at its carpark in April 18 was wonderful - one long row of beautiful sakura trees.Do not expect to see much inside (basically you walk 5 min into the park and you saw crater on your side. It will not look like crater, only valley). Rather it is the 360 degree view of the horizon that counts. The air is fresh and the mood will be lifted when you can see very far into the horizon dotted with mountains. It really look like you are in Europe or NZ. Go there for sunset as there will be no shelter from the sun above your head.

The best time to go is early in the morning, to see the sun rise. I had gone a little after the sunrise and many people were already on their way down. The views are spectacular and the way up is very safe, and good for all ages. This was probably the most memorable part of Jeju Island.

The beach has some of the finest sand I have ever seen, but beyond that it doesn?t attract me as it?s just an endless expense of sand. However we were told that this is a very famous beach especially for wedding photos. However what interest me are the cafes facing the beach. Most have decks open to the sky or constructed on the roof top, complete with deck chairs so one could order your favorite drink and enjoy the view at the same time. Interesting.

take about 15-30 minutes stairs-hike, depends on ur physical fitness. it's pretty easy hike.view from top was breathtaking, u can see udo island from top of this hill, sadly i missed a chance to see it on sunrise/sunset (a lot of people say this is the best place to see it)

Summary: You have to go here if you're on Jeju. But what can I add to the many reviews already here?The signs to the women's diving show are very clear. From the ticket office, just follow the signs down to the beach to the left of the peak. If the only way to make the show is to sacrifice something else on your itinerary, I wouldn't do it. But it was pretty cool if you happen to be there at the right time. You see the divers actually catch live octopus right in front of you.I recommend taking a snack up to the top and enjoying it there. There are plenty of places to sit down at the top and relax before you head back down. Also, definitely take at least one bottle of water if it's a hot day. You might even want two.If you plan to catch a taxi from this site to somewhere else, you'll have to walk just a little ways. We asked a taxi driver who was waiting on another family where we could get a taxi, and he told us where to walk. We had to wait about 10-15 minutes for one to show up that didn't already have people in it, but they always drive by eventually.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Spirited Garden is the #1 place to visit in Jeju in my opinion. I strongly recommend paying a visit.  the garden was actually bigger than I thought, and it took about an hour to see all the places. It definitely made me relaxed and laid back! Everything was well preserved and clean. There is also a cafe with a great view of the garden. You can buy different souvenirs related to Jeju and the garden on the floor below the cafe. Feeding the fish is 1000W and you can buy it freely (you just have to put the money in the box) and it's pretty amusing.

Special rock structure that looks like a dragon head and nice view. We also tried some fresh seafood that the local women sliced it in to pieces, serve with chilli and garlic. We haven't seen those seafood in Singapore! Very interesting!

Some of the reviews say it's a quick photo spot and that's all, but if you walk up the street just a little way, there's another path down where you can get some great pictures.  The main photo spot is kind of small and crowded, but this other area isn't, and you can still see the rock and more surrounding formations.I didn't really see the dragon, but it depends on your impression of what a dragon should look like.  This is definitely an Asian dragon, not a European one. :-)

Solo traveling in Jeju Island is not that scary:) Koreans living nearby this tourist spot can speak English. So I am not worried about it.It was raining that day when I reach the place. Nevertheless, still can see the view at the top.The wind blowing my hair together with the greenery grasses and leaves of trees surrounding the peak.The place is accessible by public buses so I don't have difficulty in reaching this site. Though you have to walk a few distance to reach the entrance gate.There are educational boards installed for all the tourists to read and understand the history of it.It's worth visiting this place. Entrance fee is also cheap:)I visited Unesco World Heritage!

So we saw great reviews and some great pictures online. Thought this was a must see place. To be fair, the island has some real potential to be fantastic, however it was a hot August day, it was getting very crowded.Highlights:- some really nice sights to take in and you can tour the whole island in about 4hrs (including stops along the way)- one let we went for a walk and ran into some people camping. Very pleasant and offered us coffee. We hadn?t encountered too many people willing to go out of their way, so was a nice touch. - took a high speed boat ride around the cliff that looks like the cow laying down (hence the name cow island). That was great and worth the 30k KRW for two adults.Low points:- way too much garbage around. Just about every beautiful sight is ruined by plastic bottles and litter. - a lot of areas were closed like it was low season (or maybe we were just early in the day)- lots people standing around endlessly. Got a little frustrating at times. Advice if you do go:- we took the bus. It was good, but we were on a bus schedule. If I did it again, I would have rented a small electric vehicle (which needs an international driving license to rent). Not sure if the cost, but they looked fun and you control your own timeline then.

Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. At first blush it may not seem too nice but Udo kind of grows on you. I'd recommend renting a moped or bicycle and bopping around the backroads; that would be the best way to see and enjoy Udo.

Skip this and head for Dodubong Peak, especially if you're on the Jeju Golden Bus day tour. This place is unremarkable and is honestly one of the dirtiest parts of the area; I attempted to have my photo taken and a rat scurried out from between the rocks. If you walk up the road (away from the site) about a half mile, maybe less, the photo ops are much nicer. The area near Dodubong Peak is also nicer and you can see great views of of Jeju from the summit.

Since there is not much to see in Jeju City, I liked this the most. The rock itself looks nice, so if you happen to be in Jeju City and have free time, it worth to check and enjoy the view on the rocky seaside. easy to get here from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal, just take local bus #17, and tell the driver   Yongduam   he will show the right bus stop. From there only 5 mins walk. It is just a rock, so don't expect much, but it's good trip for 20-30mins. Before going to the rock, you should definitely check the bus schedule back to the city center (bus timetable is displayed not on the bus stop, but on the shopwindow just nearby where no one would ever search), as there's 1-2 bus in every hour.

Since their official website is unclear about opening hours in June, I called the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline and was informed that the museum was indeed open late under summer hours. So after spending 45 minutes in and 30,000+ ?? on a taxi to visit the area with my girlfriend, who absolutely loves teddy bears, we arrived at 6:10pm. With doors still open and people still inside, we were told the museum closed at 6pm. After asking politely to let us enter the gallery and   No, no, no   being the only response, I asked the non-English speaking employee for management and soon they found someone who spoke English. I calmly explained the situation and again asked for an exception, that we were only here for a day, it would be doing us a great favor and that we would finish with the other guests and not prevent them from going home late. We were again met   No, no, no   To her credit, the English speaking manager(?) did include a   sorry   with her   no's   and did genuinely want to know how I received wrong information about their hours (and yes,if I can find a way to review the Korea Travel Hotline, they too will receive a poor rating). But ultimately, we were turned away. The only positive I could take from this experience is that, from what we could see from the lobby, the gallery looked small and over-rated. So I guess we saved ourselves the 20,000?? entrance fee.

Seongsan Sunrise Peak is one of the seven wonders of Nature, a Unesco Heritage sight not to missed while in Jeju. From the peak, you see the remains of an erupted volcano.From the entrance, you can see the green mountain  view. From one angle you can see rock of the mountain going all the way to the sea. All in all an awesome sight. All of these accompanied by strong wind from the sea that is a trademark of Jeju. The park has two main path, one that leads to the peak and another that leads to the sea. There is also a show featuring the diving women of Jeju. By the way, there is also a place where you can see Jeju Horses, smaller than usual horses.

Seongsan Ilchulbong or sunrise peak is one of the most visited spots in Jeju. We took a public bus here from port after visiting Udo Island. Lucky it is near the port as it was already late afternoon when we reached here.  The parking lot was crowded with tour coaches and and you could see the crowd climbing up and down the peak.  There was a well laid path which was fairly wide with steps leading up and separate steps leading down.  Certain parts had narrower steps and you have to slow down. Although the peak was not very high, you still need to stop now and then to catch your breath as the steps were quite steep. As usual, wear good walking shoes and stay hydrated. The views from the top were awesome and if you come before dawn, you can catch a beautiful sunrise here.  After climbing to the Udo lighthouse earlier, it was tiring to climb this peak as well but we managed.  There are platforms and steps to sit on at the top to rest and relax. By the time we got a public bus back to Jeju city, it was already getting dark.  You need to pay a small fee to climb up.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is very beautiful, but one thing our tour guide didn't mention was the difficulty of the walk up. You walk up a path and as the terrain gets steeper, the path turns into a bunch of stairs that you have to climb. If you are not physically able, this might be a difficult destination, but if you are able to reach the top the view is worth it.Here you can also see the haenyeos or Jeju women divers and learn a little bit about their history.For those of you who want to be one with nature and enjoy a good hike, I recommend this place.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the places to be visited in Jeju island, it has three kinds of beautiful views: the sea, the mountains and the meadow.No need to climb or hike the mountains to enjoy the view, just stay at the flat ground and see the surroundings and feel the wind ... it also a pleasant experience.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the best view I have ever seen in my entire life. The place is an epitome of beauty and calmness despite being flocked by tourists. It is very worthy of your time, effort and energy. Trek it to experience and see its beauty. There are plenty of activities being offered on site such as horse back riding, see a Jeju woman diver and even a tour around the area through boat. We were very interested with the boat ride unfortunately we did not have the luxury of time. if given the chance to go back to Jeju I will surely comeback here and try the boat ride as well as other activities offered. Moreover, the site has plenty of coffee shops and cafes around the area. There are also stalls selling Korean street food. It has huge parking area so get ready to walk from the parking area to the site. This site entails a lot of walking but because of its beauty and being windy you can never feel fatigue.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of Jejudo's famous icon.  I'm so glad i was able to climb this famous icon on one sunny mid day. When you reach this attraction, you will see so many shops for souvenirs and food just before the entrance and there is even a Starbucks nearby. Upon entering, you will see a ridge where you can go horseback riding or just do some leisurely walk.  The climb going up was quite a challenge for me but because of the magnificent and awesome views on the way up, i was able to make it to the top. At the middle part of the climb, there is a stall ( the only one there) selling some refreshments and souvenirs.  There is a resting area nearby to enjoy some refreshing drinks before you continue your climb.  Upon reaching the top, i enjoyed the cool breeze and the awesome view of the dried crater covered with grass.  Sharp  rocks around the crater makes it looks like a giant crown.  Coming down was a lot easier as there is a wooden stairs provided and the steps are even, not like the going up where the stone steps are uneven.  i would recommend this attraction to the physically fit only.  When you go down, you might be able to catch their scheduled show of divers and there are also boat rentals.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is certainly the top scenic spot in Jeju island. It?s basically a crater formed from volcanic eruptions, so it?s definitely has geological phenomena associated on top of being scenic. We drove from Jeju city to Seongsan for about an hour. There?s ample parking spots and entry fee is only 2000 KRW. Hiking involves climbing lot of stairs and takes about an hour to the top. We had a 2 year old with us and we could easily pick her and go to the top. I recommend carrying water and small snack items for energy. View from the top is very beautiful and obviously you see the crater when you reach the top. I think it?s top 3 spots to visit in Jeju Island and definitely a must if the weather is nice. Bonus if you during sunrise or sunset!! There are coffee shops (starbucks, McDonald, Paris Baguette etc.) and some local souvenir shop at the entrance. Enjoy

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seongsan Ilchulbong greets us in drizzled rain with fog everywhere making the place look mystic. However we put on raincoat and keep hiking. Halfway we stopped when all of us already looking dreadful.Since nobody want to keep climbing we make way to see the hanyeo. Eventho we didnt climb up to the peak, it was already so worth it. The view is something u cant get else where. Someday will come back to hike again!

Seongsan Ilchulbong - one of the main attraction in Jeju. Suitable for those who love sightseeing. Definitely worth a visit because of the view was extremely stunning. I went here in Feb, weekday..but surprisingly this place still packed with people, mostly local..but who cares..the more the merrier rite? :P

Sangumburi Crater is our 1st stop after we got a rental car.It's 40 mins drive from Jeju city.Entrance fee cost KRW6,000. There are several small souvenir & coffee shops.It quite unfortunate for us because that day is raining. We're freezing because of the cold weather.We didn't prepare any umbrella or raincoat. So from the parking to the entrance, we soak under the rain.Thankfully the souvenir shop inside sell raincoat with the cost of KRW4,000.From the entrance, you have to hike up to the crater.The path up to the crater was breathtakingly beautiful.What makes this place looks so gorgeous is because of the vast flame grass field along the way to the crater.Sadly, when we arrive at the top, we couldn't see the crater at all.It was cloudy all over.  However we still enjoy the view.The walk down is as beautiful as it was on the way up.

Sangumburi crater has a circum of over 2 km deserves its title of a Natural Monument. A must visit on Jeju island you can see the variety of plant-life in the crater. It was a great place to take pictures and has amazing views. It was really nice just to wander and admire the natural beauty of this place, a highlight of our Jeju island trip if you like nature.

Samchoon (Mr Kim Si-Nam), was our guide for a 2 day taxi tour in jeju! Samchoon was super friendly, considerate and warm hearted! Samchoon really felt more like family to us!Samchoon texted me 2 days before to confirm the time and location of pickup and asked about my itinerary and gave suggestions on the order of location we should visit first. Samchoon made sure we get the best experience we could have in jeju!Samchoon was very well prepared. In his taxi, he had prepared water, phone cable for charging, wet & dry tissues, umbrellas, raincoats and even torchlights for caves.First thing he told me was that we didn't have to worry about time and that we can take as much time at any location. He wouldn't rush or give us a time limit. So that we could enjoy every place to the fullest. Samchoon even said that he will not charge us extra even if we exceed 8 hours, he said that he would want us to enjoy and not feel rushed. Samchoo said he was a photographer in the past and actively helped to take beautiful pictures throughout the 2 day trip. He knew exactly where the spots to stand so that the pictures came out amazing!Samchoon was very accomdating to our changes in the itinerary he gave suggestions on alternatives. Samchoon knew that we like to take photos to so on the last day he brought us to see the sunset so that we could take nice pictures! True enough the sunset and view was breath taking! Samchoon is really familiar with all the places and routes and the rides between locations was really smooth and comfortable! Samchoon even has a 40 year accident free award!To Samchoon, A very big thank you for making our jeju trip so fun and enjoyable! Thanks for taking such good care of us! We will miss you and the beautiful Jeju island! Will definitely go back to look for him when in jeju!

Sabyeol Oreum definitely has lots to offer especially for tourists/foreigners. The stunning view from the top of the hill is obviously something worth to be explored, and the best part of it is that you don?t need to pay anything to experience such aesthetic view! It is a flexible place that offers different kind of experience depending on the seasons, and it does not take much of a hiker to climb it. Not only does it not take long to climb to the top, the paths are also significantly safe. Near the place, you can also see some horses without having to pay for it, and there are lots of places where you can take good pictures! If you are coming to Jeju, I believe it is a must visit place that you should consider in your itinerary!

Reminder: do check this place out , esp during sunning days. We got the chance to walk through the hiking track around it at 5PM and its just breath taking, later we found out it's the no.1 to do on jeju!You get a million dollar view of the ocean and the mountain and you probably have seen something like this in New Zealand or South africa but not in Asia. Very stunning !
Really love this place. You can see the diver performance. Amazing view from the top with fresh air, i would love to come back to this place again.

Reading some previous reviews for this place, I was rather puzzled how this place could be rated 3 or more stars by others. It has a number of different glass creations presented in a museum-like setting. Quite a few of these items were from Italy, Venetian glass. There are a lot nicer ones in Venice. Also, they have quite limited displays and very few look special to us. We managed to see all displays in about 20 minutes! Overall, we were completely underwhelmed by this place. If you are interested taking photos, there are opportunities for some nice photos. For others, there is nothing to learn and experience anything new here. There are other nicer museums or sights to see in Jeju, so this can be safely avoided.

positives: truly beautiful and amazing views of nature scenery and the waterfalls. also, one can take a leisurely stroll in the attached garden park. entry fee was only 2000 won.negatives: there was a bit of a crowd the day we visited, although it was still manageable. the entrance to the falls could be tricky to find if you planning to go there on foot from Seogipwo town. DO NOT follow google maps as it will only point you to the exact geographical location of the falls. You should walk down along taepyeong road until you see the bridge and the sea. cross the bridge and you will see a big carpark. the ticket office will be on the right side, near 7-11

Perhaps there was some misunderstanding on my part, but it seems that it is no longer possible to watch the sunrise from the peak, as the ticket office information says that it only opens at 7.30am (sunrise is around 7am in November). The views during a day climb is still good, though mostly of Seongsan.
