As compared to the views from the peak, I found the beach at the foot of the peak (along the downward route) more interesting, with the lava formations and rock pools. Try and catch the haenyeo (female divers) in action if you can!Also, try to visit either very early or very late in the day - the crowds in between are huge (from the top, I counted at least a dozen tour buses in the parking lot).

People who visiting Jeju island is to see its nature (except those to Casino), Hallasan is a must go to me.  Together with the family, we opted for the route of Yeongsil (shorter though not to the top and unable to see the crater), where we could easily accessed by self driving from Seogwipo city.  Along the hiking, we experienced the sub tropical environment in the bottom, then a much cooler environment after 1.5km of steep uphill.  The view is great though not fantastic, we spotted few wild deers having grass in the mountain.  The first 2-3 km was quite steep but mostly on boardwalk and constructed staircases, the last 1-2 km was rather flat.We ended in the point with toilet and food supply and then back down on the same route, due to the last section was closed.  An interesting hiking day to experience different climate, weather condition, meet locals, spot the wild animal, and do physical exercise.
People who are not used to climbing will have an extremely hard time in going up the mountaintop, but rest assured that the climb will be worth it.One of the best views I have seen.

Overlooking the cliff from the viewing platforms, the formation is indeed unique and a beauty. Walk along the surrounding path, we get to see the different angle of the cliff and the formation.However, you can omit the park. It is just an added attraction due to the price paid for the entrance.

Our initial plan is to visit museum then heading to the beach side to meet the divers to see how they work and that will bring us more understanding the history & culture behind. Unfortunately, we've no luck at all, we only manage to visit the museum.  Because the diver only work on some days which depend on the weather and sea condition. It is NOT every WEEKDAY! like most of the reviews in Tripadvisor and some other travel blogger who has been visited there before. I'm so so frustrated when I knew this from the locals. I don't understand why they put in their reviews or comment if they are unsure, its misleading and really let ppl down. So, if you plan to visit the divers, please check with the locals (people living nearby there or the restaurants nearby) on the first day you are in Jeju.

Other than Hallasan...the massive shield volcano that created Jeju Island and now sits at its center, Sunrise Peak is perhaps the greatest of the nearly 400 craters, cinder cones or shield volcanoes (  oreums   in Korean) found around the island.  It's a bit of a hike to get to the top, seemingly straight up at times.  But the incredible views from every angle will reward your diligence.  depending on the season, you can see fields of yellow canola (or   rape  ) flowers; also Udo (Cow Island to the east, Hallasan to the north/northwest and the incredible Pacific all around...vast and hypnotic on a clear day.  Nearby, you can check out the Aqua Planet Aquarium and the Women Divers Museum. Be sure to drive along the coast road and enjoy a coffee and dessert at one of the many unique cafes.  Although there are now several franchise coffeeshops near Sunrise Peak, the independents offer a more relaxing atmosphere.

Only discovered that we did not visit the indoor museum after seeing all other reviewers' photos.? We were only at the outdoor site and even with just those few cars, we enjoyed each one on display. Wish we had seen all the cars!
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: One of the top places to see in Jeju.  Great view of some craggy coastline.  The other reviews are pretty good and we experienced about the same - great place, but really crowded even though it was raining!  Again...people come in waves, just wait it out.  The wind was high and seas rough so it made pretty spectacular wave crashes.  On one side there was a consistent high wind and mist/spray coming at you, so watch your cameras!  There is a 1,000 W Parking fee on top of the 2,000 entrance fee.

One of the most visited Tourist attraction in Jeju, the Seongsan IIchulbong peak or the Sun rise peak was formed due to Volcanic eruption thousands of years ago. This peak has a huge cater in the middle surrounded by huge rocks making it look like a gigantic crown. In addition to this the other most sought-after attraction here is the old ladies diving deep into the water without oxygen masks to collect sea food. Twice a day a special show is conducted for the visitors.Though it was quite windy and cold when we visited, we were sweating a lot once on the top as we have to climb a lot of steps.Once on the top we were surrounded by the moving clouds, the experience which made us forget all the fatigue.We could not see the sunrise as it was quite cloudy when we visited, but as our guide informed, one can have a good view of the one during summer.At the base there are lot of eating joints which ensures everyone gets refreshed after a long trek.We thank our Jumbo taxi driver who shared the spare waterproof jerkins he had with him to wear when it started drizzling (Kin nam joon / +821046166650 / kimnj0424@naver.com)

One of the best stops we made in Jeju. This rock formation is pretty cool and the stop is more worth it since it's a good hour's worth of walking and snapping photos (as opposed to a number of the really touristy places where it's just one kodak moment).Check the tides. The rock formation that people walk on are really close to the water, so if the tides are high, it gets slippery. Actually, some parts are slippery as it is.You have two options: going counter-clockwise, which ends up being an upward movement OR going clockwise, a downward movement.  The views are nice-ish both ways (personally the counter-clockwise views were nicer). More than that though, going counter-clockwise is a lot easier as the steps are easier to deal with moving up. Many of the people coming down were cursing the steep rocks and were tired even before it began for them. Might not recommend this if walking is difficult for you as climbing and hoping around is a must. Little children were around and they seemed to be enjoying themselves, but none of them were younger than 3 years of age.No bathrooms once you enter the formations, but ladies will sell you food and drink (mostly alcohol) if you're interested in a seaside meal.

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area

Ok ok, to be honest...most of my rating is because of the seemingly endless cats that were here. I hadn't read any reviews of this place before going, I just thought it looked vaguely fun and was located right next yo Manjanggul Cave. Upon arriving, we noticed a couple of cats in the parking lot. I was so excited! When we got to the ticket booth, suddenly there were more cats! Directly beyond the booth is a small area with some handmade cat tower type things and some scratching posts. There were maybe around 15 cats in this area. I would estimate more than half of our time here was spent watching and petting the cats. The maze itself was fun. It was better if you ignored the map, I think. I think more people go here for kids, but if you're a cat lover, go!
Oedolgae was in fact quite ordinary.  The view was fine and there was not much to see.  Along the route down to the site, there were some stalls set up, which sold fruits, drinks  and local snacks.

Not just a temple, but amazing views of the coast and water. The temples are free to enter and offer an amazing experience. A must see if in this area. Plenty of drinks, food, views and restrooms. Only con is the steps are not very friendly. We have a 3, 7 and 8 year old. 3 year old needed carried.
Nice cliffs, but wouldn't go to this part of Jeju just to see this by itself. I'm not sure what the 2000won goes towards as there's only 1 crowded viewing platform.

My wife and I visited the sunrise mountain on our recent visit to Jeju Island.  Reviews had essentially undersold me on how strenuous the climb would be - it was a workout!  Took a proper 30 min of intense stair climbing to reach the top.  The views at the top were great, although the   crater   itself is just not that photogenic.  It's a big green area.  There's clearly a big appeal to seeing the sunrise but we didn't make that early morning trek.Don't miss the side paths toward the female cliff divers.  Offered some of the coolest views with the bay and the mountain.Overall, I thought it was really pretty and worth a visit but not necessarily mandatory if you're just in Jeju for relaxing.

My wife and I strolled around the market in  an early evening in mid-March 2017. The market was, as expected, already quite empty. However, the seafood stalls were still open and was quite a view. All sorts of fishes, clams, squids, octopuses and animals that I have never seen before were sold there.The whole market is huge, consisting of many sections selling various items, including fruits, vegetables, etc.Some street food stalls were still open too and we bought a cup of grilled octopus, sweet Korean pancakes and freshly-made orange juice. All were very nice.

My 'poetic' side has always loved gardens. Used to dream and draw secret gardens all the time. My heart and gut was somehow curious about this place, especially after reading reviews from travellers all over the world. Was made to understand that not many young people from our country like myself come to visit which intrigued the caretaker enough to see someone such as myself wandering around the garden and I was therefore approached with such warmth. Even had the pleasure of sipping tea and being in the company of the very welcoming founder owner himself Mr. Bum-Young Sung, who transformed, built and developed this garden over 40 years ago with his own bare hands when nobody but his wife believed that he could turn a wasteland into what is known and recognised now to be   The most beautiful garden in the world  . Like a poetic art carefully, passionately, calmly and beautifully crafted, Spirited Garden indeed does justice to its name. Even in winter where the trees and plants don't bloom as much, I could still feel the garden's spirit that it's almost like nature is speaking to you which gives you a sense of serenity. For a moment, Felt like I was in Edward Scissorhands's world ㅿ Learned so much about the bonsai tree, as well as the philosophical and wisdom in gardening. Thank you Spirited Garden for the beautiful inspiration.

My only concern with Hallim Park is the condition of some of the animals they have there. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. I don't want to give this an 'average' review because the caves are incredibly unique, the diverse array of trees and plants is also very special. But full disclosure, this place may not be for everyone.

My kids request for it & quite excited at 1st. The excitement last for the 1st train ride & once we got off the 1st station & need to walk nearly 1km the kids mood just went sour. Then it becomes a more sour when you need to wait for the next train & need to fight for a seat. They're several trains runs every 15-20m if i'm not mistaken. If you missed one you need to wait till the next train. There is no ticket system while waiting for the train & one must grab the seats. So for me with a 2 kids & a baby it was just very hard. Luckily we stayed at the far front of the track station. We managed to get the train & never get off till the end of the station. We went during end of spring. Nothing much to see. Some flowers & i think it will be a great view during summer. Pro's : A great way to relax while enjoying the ride. Con's : You need to walk a lot. The truth is the train tracks was just goes around the same land. 1st come 1st serve basic when taking on the trains. Not stroller friendly.  Tip's : If you have a tight schedule, just stay on the train. Don't go off.

My husband and I walked here from Jeju-si (not recommended, unless you just really like to walk) so it's not far from the big hotel district. It's free to get in, but is mostly just trees and bushes, the wildflower garden was completely bare, of course, we didn't really come at the right time for that anyway. Follow the signs for   Green Shower   and you'll go up a pretty steep climb (especially for us in our flip-flops) to a nice view of the city and the ocean beyond. There's a nice lily-pad pond and a nice green   lawn   for anyone wanting a place to sit in nature. Although, the entire island of Jeju is about nature, so this wasn't a must-see for us. Just behind the Arboretum (on the left as you drive out and behind a group of concrete apartment buildings) is the ＿?由쇱?? Buddhist Temple. It has a really gorgeous campus and nice view of the city and sea, as well. If you got to the Arboretum, take the time to visit the temple, too.

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My first time to Korea focusing on Jeju and Seoul. Generally I would think the overall experience to South Korea is kind of over rated. I expected more based on the comments from friends, reviews by travellers and most importantly seeing it in Korean Dramas.Udo island is an exception, it gave me the best experience in the entire 8-day trip, except the weather wasn't too good on my day trip to Udo. Rented a bike to travel almost the entire island which i think is the best mode to explore remote areas without using too much energy.  Hopping up and down to take photos by the beach, colorful cafes, yellow canola fields, uphill and downhill.Unforgettable squid volcano rice was one of its kind and one of the most satisfactory meal in the entire trip.

My first sightseeing spot upon arrival at Jeju-do. I was there last October, so the place was covered with pampas grass, with the cloud and sun giving the landscape different shades and colours, the view was simply wonderful.

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Marado island is small island but it has amazing view. You can see the wide field, blue sea,and Jeju-representing rocks.You can borrow a bike and look around the island riding a bike. And there is also a good restaurants. They use Jeju local specialities.

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.

Make sure to go when the day is clear, there are a lot of tourists during the peak times so keep that in mind as it could affect your views with all the group selfie stick shots. I highly suggest going off on the little paths around they all have views and are just lovely. If you bring a mini packed meal it's just spectacular for a picnic. It's very close to the falls and the botanical gardens and you can honestly walk (if you have good comfy shoes)This is a must see natural wonder!

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Located on the west side of Jeju, this gem has a very nice view, were you can see some mountains across the beach. We went there during late spring, the water was very nice while basking in the sun. There's not much people there, however when summer comes, most of them will swarm all over the place. It's better to go on spring, you can enjoy the view and just listening to the water splashing on the rocks. This is one of the best beaches in Korea.

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Like other traveller's review, this is not a place that worth the effort to purposely come by to visit. As it is really just a peace of rock that stood by the sea... It seems more attractive when the spot light is on at night.We dropby this place when we are on the way back to Yeha Guesthouse, surprisingly lots of tour buses stopping by! And you need to walk all the way down the staircase to have a better view of the rock, so old folks with knee problem would suggest to skip this sight seeing point.We couldn't identify which portion is the 'dragon head' until we over heard a tour guide's explanation to their guests @@

Lesser popular than others on Jeju like Ilchubong or Hallasan, but a pretty hike with a lovely view from the top. No sure what I expected for the silver grasses so was very impressed to see the effects of the sun on it as we took the short hike. I went late in the day so there were not as many people around which was nice. You pay a small fee to enter and the entire hike is relatively quite. The crater is nothing spectacular, however if you enjoy nature, the silver grasses are worth seeing.

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.

Just to pay 2000 won and tell yourself not to give up, you'll found it's definitely worth the climb up to the peak!  You'll never regret when you see the awesome view and the refreshing air! For sure I will come back again in the future to see the morning sunrise!

Jeju island is a really beautiful place and there is so many amazing sites but i was a bit underwhelmed by this view compared to others i saw. I'd say it was worth seeing if you are in the area but essentially its just a rock, and there are lots more, much prettier rocks, around the island!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

Its snowing when I visited this area. A short walk to the top will reveal a nice scenery covered with snow and a crater below. The nice view around actually overshadow the crater itself! Good place to play some snow throwing too. Its suitable for kids or even elderly as the climbing is very gradual, I would say its more like a nice walk. You will be able to see some tall grass on both side of the walk, which according to locals, was used as a roof cover. It is good to hold the weight of snow on some old buildings.

It's quite a walk going up this crater but there are 2 ways to get there. One is gradually, using concrete stairs or the otther one is by the plain path.Anyway, it's not that high and the view up there more than compensates the effort. Also, we get to see fields of Pampas grasses along thw way which is very beautiful
it's only an eye perspective view. when we see the car slowly run up while the machine off, the road actually go down. Nothing special

It's an easy climb to the top, and there are various stops for you to take pictures. The view was spectacular and you can see Jeju island stretching out below you. You can even spot the hazy outline of Mt Halla from there.

It's actually quite interesting as the road seems like an uphill slope but vehicles will move forward (slowly) without turning on their engine. It?s some sort of an optical illusion i suppose. But you can?t really see it from the side actually. It just.. seems like a normal road lolIf you are around the area, you can drop by to take a look.For full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/the-mysterious-road/

It's a really really nice place except for the diver women with the fishes and dead octopus, that's gross and I'm vegan. Anyway, you can pay for a quick boat trip to see the surroundings of this place like caves and also a rock full of birds (Think of Paracas, Peru, i think it's similar). The view at the top is AMAZING, like I said, you can see all Jeju? Seogwipo? I don't know but it's BEAUTIFUL. There are also many food spots and stores plus Starbucks and Dunkin Donuts.

It's a beautiful view, worth the climb even though we didn't manage to see sun rise due to the cloudy day but the view is pretty. Have to walk up and be there before 5.30am. Depending on your fitness level, it can take 20-40 mins to climb the peak.

It wouldn't usually be my first choice to visit on an island filled with so many views but it was a rainy day so it seemed reasonable. Wasn't disappointed. The indoor exhibition is well arranged and themed: there was jungle, desert, and other sections. You can climb to the last floor of the tower in the middle for a nice view of the area. Can't go wrong in any way if you stop by. Didn't see the outdoor gardens since it was pouring rain but wasnt disappointed even with the indoor one alone

It was raining with some strong winds when we got there. Nevertheless we decided to buy a poncho and went ahead with the climb which is a manageable 180 m.The climb up is relatively easy even for most elderlies as there are proper stairs along the way.Apart from the crater, you can see the surrounding areas and the sea from the top. The crater itself is covered by vegetation so you might want to tone down any expectation of a spectacular view. We spent about 15 min at the highest point and start our descend after that.Another attraction nearby is the female divers where they have scheduled performances every day if I remember correctly. We didn?t go for that due to the weather. But I?m sure it would be interesting.

It was raining when we went here. The steps were not at all slippery (they had rubber/metal bars at the end) Although it will be a long hard climb to the top of the mountain. If you started the climb up the mountain there is a different set of stairs going down. At the top of the mountain are set of seats, possibly a good view (it was raining) and a sign to commemorate your achievement. The place is also crowded with people. It is not suggestible for old people to go up the mountain but they could go through the sea. i would go back there again to see the wonderful view.

It was nice to visit Udo in the spring time. The rape flower fields were out of my imagination, and there was also a nice view on the Udo peak, where you can clearly see the Seongsan Sunrise peak on the other side of the sea.

It was kind of windy when I had my visit at Yeongmori cliff. At first, I thought it was another ordinary rock formation viewing after taking a few steps from the entrance...I was about to back out from the trek thinking I can see much of these in the Philippines, but as soon as my tour guide led me to the farther side of the cliff, I started to appreciate how unique the lava rock formation  was.  The best view to take a picture maybe is to include Mt, Sanbang in the back draft. You may also climb a few steps to the top or catch a good timing for huge strike of waves by the rocks.  Wear appropriate shoes as the pathways are always slippery and wet.

it was interesting to see these column-shape geological formations. The sea was calm when I visited so i did not get to see the waves getting on them. Nonetheless, the formations made really good photos.The sheer number of visitors on the small and narrow viewing platform could spoil your trip!
It was enjoyable to walk through this botanical garden,? but I have seen better. It was great fun to go up to the top of the tower for a 360 degree view of the area.

It was easy to tell the tourists from the locals - level of preparedness. Before I went on the hike, it amused me to see the locals fully dressed and equipped with hiking gear. As I understood it, the hike was child and elderly friendly, so I was not expecting much difficulty scaling this mountain. Halfway up, I was already regretting my choice of footwear. I had on a lightweight fleece jacket which helped to battle the cold winds at the top, so it did not feel too bad even though I was in shorts. In actual fact, it was not that difficult to climb (took me 4 hours to get to the summit) but the terrain was rough with rocks and stones making up most of the path. I guess it is my own fault that I have absolutely no instinct on where to put my foot next. Slipping often, I finally tore open my trainers on my way down after constantly stubbing my toes in the ground. My toes hurt so bad I had to stop several times (after peeling my socks off, I found two of my toes severely bruised and blackened) so the hike down took all of 4 hours. At the top, I regretted not having any headgear. The winds were so crazy it was close to impossible to take a photo without my hair whipping all over my face. Ah, even a bandana would have been enough. Overall, I would do it again, this time better equipped. Though the view was beautiful, what I remember best was climbers picnicking at the top, huddled together in groups in the bellowing winds, in their bright hiking outfits, just enjoying the time out. Next time, I will remember to bring kimbap and hot coffee!

It was at the end of Hamdeok beach. It is not too high and easy to walk. I loved the view from the hill and you can see hallasan from seoubong. If you are staying around Hamdeok beach, seoubong is a great place to see sunrise or sunset. I loved it!

It was amazing!This is the worth place to go. The entrance fee is very cheap just 2000 won and the transportation arround 3300 won.Then Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak will gives unique view that you will never see in another place. It is very easy to go here, just take a bus from Jeju intercity Terminal or Seogwipo Intercity terminal then stop on Seongsan Ilchulbong  Entrance, Just walk for 10 minute from the bus stop to the ticket booth.

It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. I didn't go up to the top but I did go up to the first viewing platform, which i think most people would be able to manage slowly, not matter your age. It is well paved, and the views are incredible. It was a very windy day too, so there was no show by the women divers, Haenyo, but you could see where they went out and to be honest the roughness of the seas showed how tough the women must have always been. There are a few shops near the bottom and one part way up, so you can purchase drinks and trinkets if you wish. There is a Starbucks and a Dunkin' Donuts and i think a McDonald's near the car park, as well as multiple Korean restaurants. Well worth a visit, even if you can't ascend to the peak.

It was a short walk from the entrance to get to the actual Jeongbang waterfall site, but was a grand sight to behold - you get to see the ocean from the waterfall! I also like that you could make your way closer to the waterfall by stepping on the big rocks around it.Between Jeongbang and Cheonjiyeon, my vote goes to the former. For the latter, the walk from the entrance was longer, the view was not as fantastic, and you can't get nearer to the waterfall even if you wanted to.

It was a rainy day when we went to this beach after visiting the Hallim park, end of october. It was however a very nice experience, the sand is white and contrast nicely with the black rocks that you can see at low tide. The view on the island makes the picture even nicer.

It was a nice view of ocean with rocks especially during sunset... It has safe path with stairs to go down and see better view of the dragin rock...  It has also a small markets there, where they sell tangerines which is a famous fruit there (felt regret that i didnt bought them)... Also there were also souvenir shops and seafood resto...

It was a cold, sunny, windy day, visiting this mountain. Make sure you wear enough layers!  Admission was 2,000won if you wanted to go all the way up to the crater, or free for just the lower level.  Be prepared to climb many steps to get to the top, and see crater.  On average, take 30-40 mins return to do this.  Otherwise, the view is nice from all levels...definitely worth checking!

It takes around 30-45 mins to climb up. But after this amount of time, it is worthy to climb because of the marvelous viewOne of the things I hate the most here is that there are so many Chinese. It seems to me that I was in China, not Korea.The toilet at the foot of the mountain was so smelly.You can ask for discounted price if you are below 24.

It takes 1.5 hours from Jeju Intercity bus station to Seongsan IIchulbong, by bus 701. After 30 mins drive, you can see the blue sky and green sea outside of the windows. The admin fee is 200 0 KR but the great view is worth of it. You can see large grass ground and hike to the top. If there is sunshine, no doubt you can have wonderful pictures and experience even with a phone camera.

It offers one of the best view in Jeju. It is free to go, no need to book, super easy to walk. I was lucky with weather this time and was able to see hallasan from here! I cannot describe how amazing it was.  It is breathtaking and good to visit anytime of days. Many people came for sunset and sunrise. It is definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju. Be prepare for strong wind and amazing view. Recommend going during fall

It is known as the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the ocean. The view is breathtaking, the most beautiful waterfall I have seen so far. Definitely worth the visit. The entrance ticket is 2,000 KRW, it is only 1,000 KRW for teenager.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.
It is a UNESCO world herritage, recommended to see if you go to Jeju. We need to hike around 30-45 minutes to the top to get the full view.

It is a truly magnificent sight to see this natural phenomenon of this Unesco Heritage Site. It's a short climb up with well maintained steps and the view from the peak is superb. We didn't make it for the sunrise as we stayed in Jeju City which is 1.5 hours away by local bus. However, the sunset is stunning. I went in December so the wind can be very chilly in the evening. Definitely worth the climb!

It is a nice walk up to the top, windy.From the top we do have a nice view, wide view with many hills. Nothing special about the plants or vegetation. The entrance fee of KRW6,000 is a bit high when this is all you see.

It is a good place to watch the whole seaside view and the horizon of the sea where the sky meets the sea. The view is breathtaking as you can see not only the sea view but the city view of Jeju island and the mountain in the background. However, one need to put in the effort and climb 45 minutes up to the mountain top in order to enjoy this view. And also hope for the best of luck that it is not a cloudy day.

Innisfree Jeju House can be got to by taking a bus to the O'Sulloc tea museum stop. The tea museum is a very short walk away from Innisfree Jeju House.The place is quiet and peaceful, save for the calming music they play and the chatter of tourists and other visitors, but that wasn't too bad when I was there. There's an area devoted to DIY lessons/sessions where one can try making their own soap. There's a few pretty exhibits where one can smell various scents or read a little about the Innisfree brand and its products. There's a store area, with a few products that are exclusive to Innisfree Jeju House. And there's a cafe with various light food, drink and dessert options.Outside, there are tables and benches that overlook a nice view of the tea plantation, which you can go and take pictures in. Rows upon rows of tea leaves and a few windmills. It's all very pretty and is probably the biggest selling point of the whole compound containing both Innisfree Jeju House and the nearby tea museum. It's really very pretty.I enjoyed my time there, but if Innisfree products are not for you, or if you're the thrill-seeking type, perhaps you should skip this place.

Initially, we were only planning on staying here for a few minutes to take some pictures because the reviews were so mediocre. We rented a car and drove to the entrance our GPS took us to (FYI if you rent a car and don't read Korean, make sure you get a GPS with it, Google maps/Apple maps/etc doesn't work in Korea, only Naver). I think it was some kind kind of back entrance, off the road, because no buses or anything were parked there. There wasn't even really a parking lot. When we walked through the village, to the other side, we saw the big parking lot and all the cheesy buildings and shops and stuff. But from the back side, it was just lots of nice little houses (some I think still had people living there) and pretty, walled-off yards. We were there in the morning and the are we were in had almost no one around, except for a few Chinese ladies who had decided to leave their tour and were having fun (we saw them rejoin with their tour later, so I didn't pull that out of thin air, lol). The main front entrance area is way more touristy and that's probably all people getting off the bus see, hence the bad reviews. If you keep walking through the whole town and take your time (if you can), it's actually pretty and peaceful. I think we spent a couple hours here.

Initially I wasn't sure if I would go to see this as I'd already gone to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak the day before, but it was definitely worth it! It was a cloudy June day which made the setting even more mysterious. Very simple but nicely kept grounds of rolling hills and volcanic rock walls. The crater itself was one of the more bizarre and intriguing natural landscapes I've seen. If you've seen the movie   The Mummy Returns,   it's like the end of that! The surrounding grounds are lovely and you have a great view of the mountains all around you. Would be a very romantic place as well, if you're with your partner. Great place for a picnic or just a long stroll! However, if you're looking for activities and souvenirs and snacks and other touristy things, you'll have to go elsewhere. Fortunately there is a bus stop right outside to go to Jeju City.

Information given in English about the legend of the rock.    You really have to use your imagination to see the woman.    While I didn?t think much of Oedolgae, there?s a lovely hike right along the coast, with pretty views.
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.

In my journey, I went to the Hallasan National Park at Jeju. Here is a good place to walk with family, since here has a wide stretch of land at the foot of hill, you can just walk around the hill. Children can play in a nature place with good air. All the building and transport are so far away, you must feel relax and do not want to leave.If you are younger and want to see more view, I really suggest that you must walk to the peak by stairs, but you must have enough energy, because it is really tired. Take water and some food are necessary. After that, you can see a good view at the peak, just like stand on the cloud.Finally, I suggest that you will climb at evening because of the sunset is very beautiful. Also the weather is better to climb the hill.

In my first visit there, it was very foggy and I couldn't see nothing; it was just an exercise (a not that hard one).But this time I was very lucky: it was a very fine day with little cloud and its view was fantastic. You should definitely climb it and see it for yourself, but check the local weather before and choose the day wisely.Climbing it wasn't that hard for my mother-in-law in her late 60s and my preteen daughter. But you should bring a bottle of drinking water or two with you as there's no stores that sell one near the peak (you can buy them at the CVS store in front of the gate).

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

I'm always fascinated with natural wonders so visiting this place amuses me. For a more meaningful experience, try climbing the peak (only takes less than an hour). The pathway is safe since there are stairs that you can climb to but it gets steeper as it nears the peak so make sure you wear comfortable shoes. Choose a clear day for the climb because when it is foggy (like mine), you can't see the crater once you reach the peak. It's quite windy here (since it's near the sea) so make sure your skin is covered to fight off the cold. Even if you don't attempt the peak, the view is still great and you can take a lot of beautiful photos here.Do not buy here, especially beauty products as they are more expensive. Buy in the downtown area for cheaper prices.

Ilchulbong is a huge rock/volcano/crater on the North East of Jeju Island. At first it seems a little daunting when you pull into the carpark as it looks really huge and steep. Yes, there are a lot of steps, but there are plenty of places to pause or sit for a rest and once you get to the top there's a great sitting/viewing platform. The views are really spectacular in all directions and you can see all over the mountain. It's really worth a visit if ou are going to Jeju.

If you've never seen hexagon rocks [I don't know what they're called], this is a pretty neat place to visit.  There are stairs and viewing platforms with smaller platforms you can stand on to get a better photo.  There's also a big park at the top where you can see the rocks from different angles and just enjoy the park.

If you're unfit like me, please be mentally and physically prepared before embarking on this   hike  , 4-5 hours upwards, another 4-5 hours downwards. The view at the top is great but that highly depends on the weather. Don't be surprised to see many elderly Koreans in their 50s or 60s even at the peak. And oh yes, please bring along good hiking shoes for this trip, it will definitely help you a lot.

If you're into nature, love moderate hiking and stairs climbing, love to see sea and city thru the bird eye view, taking plenty of photos of nature formations and also selfies (or wefies), then wjy don't you go to Seongsan Ilchubong, Jeju Island, South Korea. Designated as Unesco World Heritage site, this mountain is one the best place that you can hike and feels the wind blows your hair or maybe yourself too. The combination of flat lands and also the hike to the peak gives you an unforgetable memories. With each steps you take to climb to the peak, you will encounter several break spots or photo viewing for you to stops and take photos. Half way thru to the peak, you can see the entire city below you and starting to see the seas too. Hike to the peak, you can the see majestic view of the Seongsan Ilchubong itself. To your front is wide sea and the flat land (heard that it's actually a death volcano, correct me if i'm wrong) and to your behind is the view of the city and their surrounding. Don't forget to take photo at the peak's signboard. The formation of the clouds and the sun may give you the awe moments to you, especially when it reflects to the sea surfaces. When you go down from the peak, try to look at your right. You may see people going down to feels the sea water. Mind you, sometimes the wind blows a bit strong.  You need to pay for entrance and you don't like to hike to the peak, the ground is enough for you. Me and my friend, went there on Nov'15. Do try to enjoy nature at their best.

If you want to see a waterfall without the hassle of hiking a long way, go for this one. Just a little stairways descend from the entrance and voil - you'll be greeted by this pretty view of water flowing freely to the sea of Jeju.

if you want to go to his place, you must go on the morning to see the sunrise. Seongsan is quite far from Seogwipo, so after you explore Seogwipo city, you can go to the Seongsan for stay. And then you must wake up at 5 am, and go to seongsan ilchubong by taxi. it needs 5-10minutes. Better you ask to the hotel to call the taxi. You need 20-30minutes to go to the top. The view is amazing. Very recommended. For the hotel in this area i recommended jeju lux hotel. you can read my review also.

If you have a tight schedule and cannot afford a whole day climbing the Hallasan Mountain, or some of your group physically can't do Hallanshan, this is a good option, because it is closer to other sight seeing places so you don't need a whole day, also because it is a much easier climb compared to Hallasan.The day we visited this was not crowded at all because everybody went to Udo Island on the opposite, after a two day close of the ferry service due to weather. If there was a helicopter service i(not sure), it must be very spectacular from an aerial view.  From the ground level,  if you didn't see the photo from the Internet, nor post cards, you probably don't realize it is a flat volcanic crater.Anyway, it would be quite a nice walk close by other sightseeing places, but might look more impressive from opposite Udo, or from a plane or helicopter

If you go there just to see the Lonely Rock, you may feel somewhat underwhelmed. However, there is a nice walk along the coast. When I was there, it was sunny and breezy. I really enjoyed the walk, the beautiful coastal view, the clear water and the fresh air. I wasn't disappointed at all.
If you choose one fall out of 3 in this area, choose this one.  It has the best view, and no platform which really ruin any natural beauty.  This is one one the best waterfall I have seen.

If you are intending to go for the sunrise climb, please bring your own torchlight as lighting is minimal. About 2/3 of the climb comprise of a steep ascend. Not for the weak-hearted or those with circulation problems. It's physically challenging on the heart, not so much on the legs.Personally, a day climb (rather than a dawn climb) is better as you can see the view from the various heights. At the top, there are benches to sit and appreciate the view. Coming down was the easy bit as the stairs are well designed for the descend.

I went with my boyfriend and his dad. We had our cab driver take us there at 6am from our hostel. It took us about 12hrs round trip. I'm not a experienced hiker, so it took a loooonnnngggg time because of me. View is EXCELLENT from the peak. You can see the entire Jeju-do. Hallasan is a stony mountain, so if you can, bring a pair of hiking sticks to help you, and wear hiking shoes. The rocks are pointy, and not all of them are easy to step on.

I went to Seongsan Ilchulbong (SunRise Peak) during Mar this year 2015. The weather is cold but bearable around Jeju. However, to climb this mountain is not a great feat for my mum (age 65) but the chilling wind is the one we are defeated.We wanted to visit this peak for sunrise but somehow we are late and lost on our way there. We went to Jongbong Beach and along the coast line it is also very nice to see. We did not catch the sun rise as there are none (due to foggy weather). As we are ascending, the crowd was descending and show enthusiasm although they did not get any view of the sun rise. The climb was nice as there are even wooden/stone steps to the top. Once you reached the top, you will see the beautiful crater which happens million years ago. The view over the edge is equally stunning. Definitely a recommended place to visit when you are in Jeju-Si. The ticket cost 2000KRW each.When you descend, you may see the   Sea-Woman   whom they called Haenyeo will perform at 1.30PM and 3PM only. We did not wait for the show as there are many Sea-Woman around the whole Jeju Island.

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

I went there early morning on a sunny day - perfect for photo-taking. The wonderful view of the sea from the walk down was just a prelude to the beauty that was to come later. I was delighted to see that little rainbow at the bottom! If you're more gutsy (and have a good sense of balance), you can make your way nearer to the waterfall to feel the cool mist and enjoy the grandeur and the surrounding scenery. Not a sight to be missed!!

I was very excited to visit Jeju; and this probably one of the most accessible place by Bus. There's actually public transport to this place (Yongduam Rock) from my accommodation. However, when I reached this place , i was busy looking for this legendary dragon head rock. Much to my disappointment, the rock doesn't seem to look like dragon head, you must really view it from the other side with your imagination.However, in order to reach to the other side, you need to climb all the way down the stairs, Not recommended for elderly. And if you notice carefully, you will spot alot of cockroach crawling around the rock, that totally freak me out!! Very big turn off if you spot the cockroach.the period I went was very crowded, probably around 5-6pm, This timing was quite a good timing for me, as I manage to catch a sunset. The sunset there was relatively awesome with the endless view of sea. If you can walk all the way down to those seafood stores, whereby you can enjoy fresh seafood hot pot + splendid view of sunset & sea!

I was told the hike up will only take 30 minutes but when I looked at it I was convinced it would take longer. The hike up is quite steep, lots of stairs, however it really just took a bit more than 30 min, to my own surprise. The hike is not easy however, it requires some stamina, many people take a break or two on the way up. Definitely bring something to drink. Seongsan is quite crowded with tourists, so lots of people all over. The hike is worth it, amazing views from the top. And the hike down is much more enjoyable then the one up. At the foot of Seogsan is a large parking lot, easy to leave your rental there, plus again lots of cafes, restaurants etc. You have to pay a fee to enter.Overall worth seeing Seongsan!

I was in a rush so I briefly stoped by this fall to enjoy its amazing views.  It is simply amazing how it looks, I guess if you like nature, this would be one of the must see places.  I am a nature lover.  Take your time, and you can possibly have some of the fresh conch caught by the ladies by the bottom of the fall.

I walked 40 minutes from Jungan Rotary to this place. The ticket is 2000 won. When I was there, it was in the afternoon 4-5 PM, there were so many tourists. So it's difficult to get a good shot. I find there's nothing special about these waterfalls, back home I've seen bigger and higher than here. I visited this place because it was close to my guesthouse and I was also curious about it. I don't see people swimming on it. What I like about this is the view of the sea, I was sitting between those big rocks towards the sea and waiting for the sun to set. It was a good experience for enjoying the sunset with having a natural background sound from the waterfalls.
i think this place is over rated, other than the volcanic rocks formation, you can see planes landing to jeju airport. the view is nice though.

I think the word   museum   throws off this visit.  I expected to see many more interesting displays and films about tea but there is really just one room with some tea sets a few interesting facts and how Jeju tea is the best as the soil climate and underground water makes growing tea in Jeju at its optimal.  This so called museum is more of a flagship store where you can purchase tea and tea related items have a snack at the cafe/bakery that specializes in green tea ice cream and cake rolls and in a separate building building called   innis free   you can make natural soaps and enjoy Korean slushy ice in a cafe there as well and a store.  There are tea making classes but you must make a reservation to attend.  The grounds are nice and you can walk around the tea fields and go to the rooftop and get an amazing view of the surroundings.  The museum is free but for a true tea fanatic you may be disappointed as there are no samples or a big variety of tea products to choose from for purchase.

I think the best time to climb here is during Spring, went during Winter and couldn't see much except for nice view. It's quite high up, so make sure you're a bit fit to climb the stairs.I personally didn't go up to see the sunrise but I've heard it's an amazing experience. Do give it a shot but you did have to be there by 6am

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

I really enjoy my visit to this site at Jeju island... Recommended for those who loves to take a short hike and enjoy sunrise... The view of the city from the top of it is also beautiful... One side you can see the sea, other side enjoy the city view... On the afternoon in the right time, you can also met the woman divers who will dive to look for abalone and other sea animals... Love this place, hope can visit again someday... v(^_^)v

I must have chosen a very good day to visit Seongsan Ilchubong. When I arrived, there were practically a few dozens sightseeing buses there, tourists as well as students for school outing. The whole place, paths walking up the hill and down to the seashore, on the hill top, everywhere! was FULL of people walking, talking, taking pictures?§?o there as early as you can if you want to enjoy the view in a much relaxed way.

I might not have came at the right time to enjoy the view which was why I might not have enjoyed it that much? I arrived about 1 and the sun was so hot. Paid 5000 for entry ticket and climb to the TOP. The view was good but I felt not worth the sweat and effort haha. But upon making the way down, it is a must to go see the female divers who dive without any equipment to catch seafood like octopus. Their show time is at 3pm. Make sure to watch it.
I mean, its a decent bridge if you've got time to kill and want a good view, but I wouldn't go out of your way to see it.

I LOVE... this museum!!! I am a teddy bear fan so this museum feels like heaven to me aside from being a K-drama fan. Before visiting Jeju, I researched on the top sites recommended to be visited, i got fascinated with the reviews about Teddy Bear museum plus knowing that some of its Teddy Bears where featured in one my favorite Korean Drama of all time PRINCESS HOURS. The teddy bears are just so cute, you can see them perform different functions and dressed of different profession and famous personalities such as Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Madonna etc. Afetr visiting the exhibit halls, we then went to the lower ground floor area where tall Teddy Bears are on display alongside Teddy Bears items that are for sale.A must visit for Teddy Bear Lovers.

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I had requested Tripadvisor to add this as an attractive as it was along the Jeju City Tour bus route. We decided at the last minute to get off at 'Sarabong Peak' as we wanted to see the lighthouse. However, we had a 10 or 15 minute uphill walk to reach the lighthouse during a cold December day but the view more than made up for the inconvenience. We only stayed for half an hour as we wanted to catch the bus back to town as it was already getting dark.

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

I had no idea that there were going to be stiff hills/stairs to go top of the place. I was expecting kinda easy, but it was bit harder than I expected. Going to the top was a little tiring, but the view you get to see is magnificent. Make sure to have a bottle of water on the way! About 20-25 min of walking, and less than 20 to go back down. Would go again!

I had a lot of fun riding the carts but also enjoying the beauty of Jeju. It's situated in such a beautiful location where you can view the ocean and take Instagram photos! The interior of the building was also cool. It was futuristic and very clean. The staff were friendly and helpful! I didn't play indoor games but there were many indoor games as well, so it seems like a place that you can have fun in any season. I will definitely recommend this place for any ages!? I will go back in a heartbeat when I visit Jeju next time!!

I enjoyed this place even more than Jusangeolli, maybe because there were less people, or maybe because the view was just so serene.  It was a nice walk through some trees before getting to the viewing spot.  We went in the afternoon so the sun was just perfectly positioned.  I got some nice photos of this place, especially including the trees on top of the cliff to the right of the rock.  You can't miss seeing this place, even for just a few minutes.

I didn't get to see the sun rise there. We started the climb in the afternoon at about 2pm and it was pretty warm!To me, the highlight was taking in the views as we climbed up to the top to see the crater and back down. When we reached the top, it was quite an anti-climax actually. The crater looked like a huge green field. The climb was pretty easy for an unfit person like me. I saw a very pregnant lady successfully climbing to the top as well.Our tour guide took us to a beach area to take photos of Seongsan Ichulbong from a distance and that was really lovely as well.

I could see coming here to relax a little, the view of the crater was nice enough but not like it was a whoa moment attraction. I might go bak though, there were some lovely picturesque spots and the pampas grasses were quite nice. An easy walk up of, so good for those of you (like me) who aren't p for the massive hike up the other big crater by the women divers museum.

I climbed this with a friend and it took us about 4.5hrs in total. Easy hike but challenging enough to make it worthwhile. Lots of tourists climb this and they are mainly Korean; its a bus and popular hike. The views from the top are stunning, you can see the whole island almost, we went when the leaves were turning from summer to autumn, just gorgeous.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I am really unfit and the hike up to the peak is painful to me. But once i reached the top, all of my pain seem to go away. The view of the sunrise is so beautiful. I know i will take longer time to reach the top so i begin the hike up earlier. I started at 5.30 a.m and reach the top after excruciating 1 hour.

How often do you see hexagonal columns along the coastline? This is the place.We were there at about 6:30pm when they were almost closing. They close at 7pm. Although it was quite a rush, we managed to enjoy and soak in the scenery.The observation deck provides very good view of the columns. Be sure to read how the columns came about. It will make the views that much more interesting and meaningful.
