Hiking Mt. Halla was on my bucket list for a long time and finally i did it. There is a time restriction and you cannot enter the gate before 6:00 am during the winter time. You have to pass 'Jindalaebat Shelter' before 12:00 pm to continuously hike up to the summit. The park keeper will not let up pass the gate of Jindalaebat if you arrive after the noon. It took about 2 or 3 hours to get to Jindalaebat from Seongpanak gate, and another 2 or 3 hours to get to the summit. It took me 4 hours to get to the Baekrokdam, and took another 5 hours to get down to Gwaneumsa temple. I highly recommend to hike from Seongpanak because it is easier to walk and you are too tired to look around. Then, walk down to Gwaneumsa direction which has a really good view and nature. (Gwaneumsa route is shorter, but definitely harder...super stiff)You will see many people lining up to take a photo with a monument, and I didn't understand why people want to take a photo with just a rock. I learned that you will get a certification of Mt. Hallasan hiking if you show the picture with the monument. All you need to do is go to the ticket office, pay 1,000 KRW and show the picture. I've seen many people hiking with sneakers, but I recommend wearing hiking boots since you have to walk on rocks for 8~9 hours. I heard that you need to be luck to see the summit because Hallasan is always foggy and cloudy. I was lucky and weather was just amazing!! I also heard that it is slightly easier to hike when it snows. There are buses that you can use and I strongly recommend hiking Mt. Halla!!!!!!!

Hike to the peak for a wonderful view, Jeju island is blessed wit so many nature attraction & Seongsan IIchulbong is one of it, did not get to see the women divers performance as the wave was very strong during our visit but we manage to see live women divers at other place the next day. Walk around and enjoy the nature.

Hexagonal shaped rock formations jutting out of the ocean that reminds me of the kryptonite crystals I once saw in an early Superman movie. Unusual and definitely 1 of the places to see if you are in Jeju. Entrance is KRW2000, 50% off if you are below 24 ? foreign ID accepted. Unfortunately, since the best view is only through a series of stairs which ends at a platform, weekend crowds in bus loads can be a nuisance for that desired background photos effect or even a selfie. And I was continuously concern about the strength of the viewing platform to hold so many people at any one time. I got there in a rented car and discovered fields of canola flowers up front for good picture taking.

Here you can find a lot of beautiful flowers and tropical flora. It is very suitable for green lover. Besides, you can find some tropical fruits over here with some information. After visited four themed garden park at the ground floor, you may proceed to the top floor using the lift at the center. You can see the beautiful view at the top floor. Also, you can take a train tour outside the building. :)

Here at the Jungmun-Daepo Coast, you see the very unique and naturally beautiful Jusangjeolli!These are basically volcanic rocks that have been naturally formed by winds and waves into what seem like artisan-sculpted pillars!It was astounding and amazing to see how nature can create something that you could only imagine a person could do!Usually, there are a lot of people so you can't really stay long and soak on the view and the soothing Jeju breeze!But hey, it's worth the stop!

Hallim Park is a jack of all trades but a master of none. It is rather unusual to find a mini bird park, caves and gardens altogether in the same place (but not all of them were stunning). Some of the vegetation were not well maintained. That said, if you enjoy viewing cherry blossoms and tulips, this is your chance. When we went last week, the cherry blossoms and tulips were in full bloom and they were absolutely a wonderful sight. We were hoping to see cherry blossoms in Jeju and didn't know we will catch them right here at Hallim Park. You can miss everything else, but don't miss these seasonal flowers.

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.

Had a port of call in Jeju. The cruise offered a number of shore excursions. Instead, we took the free shuttle into town. It dropped us off right by the underground mall (half block past it)We walked around a bit then hailed a taxi. He agreed to a fixed price of $100 USD to take us to the folk village, then to sunset peak. (The cruise was $119 per person so we saved $138)We climbed to the top. It was strenuous but with frequent stops we made it. It?s like 59 stories. At the to you get a great view of the town and the sea. You also can look down into the volcano (and see a grassy crater)A million photos later we came down. We then went and saw the women diver demonstration. That was fun. They sang for a while then went fishing. While we were there, one of the ladies caught an octopus. I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)
great view of the waterfall and the sea, you can see the locals there selling crabs coconuts, oranges and other stuff like souvenirs

Great view of the rare animal cliff which is 20 meters height and surrounded by the beautiful islands. Hundreds of visitors went there to have a look of the amazing animal rock. The stone seemed independent and I like the fact that it is normal, nothing inorganic. The shape of Oedolgae formed by the daily erosion of wave and the weathering process. There is a small path in which it can walk along the edges of the island. In which I discovered that the venue was filmed by one of the most famous Korean drama - Dae Jang Geum. I was in love with the drama when I was young, I took tens of photos with the place that Jang Geum have been to.So, if you are I fan of Dae Jang Geum or you would like to see different shapes of stone, you are highly recommended to go there to have a look at the charming sea view.

Great place to explore, really. Worth a visit for sure.Before entering I would suggest though to visit the small museum, where some facts are explained before hand. We didn't see it before and then discovered a few facts after visiting the museum on our way out. Would have been better the opposite.I would also suggest to bring something warm and to wear snickers. As it is stated in almost all the previous review, it is quite humid and dump downstairs. No wheelchair access.
great experience, tiring when climbing up, but glad to see the sunrise and feeling the cool sea breeze. magnificent view, must visit

Gosh...this place is awesome... Its very well maintained and comfy for those people walking inside and enjoy the lava tube nature. Recommend to wear shoes or comfy sandal as it sometimes wet inside. Not just the view, but also there are boards for explaining the things we see inside. Love it!

Going to Seongsan Ilchulbong and climbing to the top to see the crater is on every  Jeju Island   To Do   list, but the best kept secret is down the mountain on the other side. In a gorgeous alcove, a handful of Jeju Haenyeo (women divers of Jeju) serves freshly caught mollusks in between diving and offering prayers of safety and a bountiful harvest. Some of these women are in their 80s and it is a very moving thing to experience. There are two shows daily 1:30 pm and 3:30 pm. It's free, although I suggest supporting these dynamic women by having some Makgeolli and a snack. The view is spectacular and so is the company.

God?s beauty with unique rock formations and the waves crashing. Short boardwalk to see the beauty. We bought a bag of oranges and explored a bit more on the side paths but it was so hot, we didn?t enjoy that part as much as cliff viewing.

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

First, we went to see the woman diver show. It appears to occur twice per day, at 1.30pm and 3pm if I remember correctly. They were singing, then entered into the water. I found their catch more interesting than their swimming. Afterwards, we climbed the   mountain   (small but cute is the motto). The view over the volcanic crater and the island is amazing, even despite the rainy weather that we experienced. The ascend is a bit physically challenging.

First stop for sight seeing in jeju and found the beach was crowded, specially family with children. Went straight to Delmondo cafe to have a better view and it was also pretty crowded at the deck with chairs facing the beach. Looked for facility to change and for shower as the water was tempting clear and the weather hot. Sadly, only found changing room but no shower facility.

First and foremost, you need to find a place to stay nearby the Sunrise peak as you need to wake up early to climb up in time to view the sunrise. It should take around 20-30 minutes to reach the top. It's quite cold and windy up there during autumn time so bring along a wind breaker. Once you are up there, just wait until you see the dark sky suddenly light up, then you will see the most marvelous sunrise you ever seen.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. One floor is for displaying teddies from different times, another one shows teddy related artworks and finally there's a floor where you find a souvenir shop and some cafes. In the outside park you can view Jungmun sea while seeing human-sized teddy sculptures. The whole surrounding area is beautiful. Ideal for friends, couples and families as well!

Easy boardwalk to see the attraction.  If you follow right, you will see the Oedolgae rock.  We happened to be there at sunset, and the view was magnificent & romantic!  You can also follow the boardwalk to the left for more view points.

Easily the most gentle slope you can find and is a great start in Jeju. Easy path with great views. Though touristy but still very manageable. Is 2000won per pax entry and only 1 waterfall to see, you can probably finish this in half hour but we stopped at the ladies selling conch and abalone for breakfast yummy and definitely a must try....still alive when we had it ?? and is 30000won for the plate.

During winter time, it is surely different experience when you hike up. The view is totally different from summer. Can see icy plant. So beautiful that we wont forget. It might take about 45min to hike up if you are in good shape during winter time as it is not easy to hike up because of cold air.

Do not miss the chance to climb up to the top (180m) to see the huge crater & Jeju view! it's definitely worth it ..the staircases might seems endless but it wasn't that high actually. it tooks us less than 30mins to reach the top and there are a few stops where you can catch a breath before continue to climb up again. Even my 4 years old nephew make it on top too. Going up and going down is 2 different route. Don't forget to get yourself mineral water at the convenient store before you climb up. you will need it.If you going over to the cliffs for the seaview, check out the Haenyeo performance. The performance hours are 1:30 p.m. and 3 p.m. twice a day during summer but we are out of luck we did not see any at the 3pm slot that day. Seongsan ilchulbong is sunrise peak - famous with sunrise from the cater! The gate is open 1 hour before sunrise for those who wish to watch sunrise from the top.

Disclaimer: this review is written by my better half since I?m obviously not part of the Hello Kitty! target audience.Omg! Everything is in pink! Look at the displays! They are sooooo cuteeeeee! I want to take photos with everything! I?m an adult in Kittyland! Omg, the cafe is so nice! I don?t wanna leaveeeeeeeeee......Back to the lesser half: if you are a guy, just pay the entrance fee and make the Girlfriend/Wife/kids happy. They will love you even more when you cough up for the overpriced merchandise. Seriously, I?ve never seen the Wife happier, not even on our wedding day.
Didn't expect to see such a good view there, the rock , island, and sea makes perfect scenario. Definitely a spot to visit if visiting Jeju!

Definitely worth the climb up to see the awesome view. I really liked that the route up and down were separate so you wouldnt have climbers coming on the opposite direction. We went in the afternoon after lunch which was rather hot, would definitely have preferred to go in the morning but our schedule didn't permit that. Still, definitely worth the climb.

convenient place for hiking and great view.. that i good place, street food nearby the parking place is nice... all snack nice yummy... and Seongsan will be good if see the sunset or sunrise, but while we arrive there to cloudy and windy.

Considering that the other craters type views Seongsan Ilchulbang (Sunrise Peak) and Hallasan are a ways up, and the seaside formations such as the Yongmeori Coast a slippery path of jumping about, the Sam-Gumburi Crater is nice and leisurely. The one place that seemed wheelchair friendly.It was also less crowded compared to the Seongsan Illchulbang so we really got to enjoy the nice leisurely walk up the small hill to see this crater. If you're a faster walker, you could probably do the whole thing in less than an hour (needless to say, we lazy walkers, took a little more than an hour). If you wanted to just roam about, you could spend a lot more time as well (there are different paths, one that's all stairs, one that is like a ramp, etc.). Anyways, this was probably the only geological tourist attraction that was wheelchair friendly and even seemed to have a few out in the front for rental. The ramp would be a bit steep but at least do-able. A lot of the other sites had either a lot of stairs/walking or way too many people for the elderly or others with bad knees to maneuver well.  Perhaps that's why we saw a number of couples with strollers.That said, this place had one of the most pricy admissions costs that we encountered. It is privately owned or something. So, instead of the usual 1,000-2,000KRW per person, we paid 6,000KRW per person. We were told that the place is nicer during the reed season, but we enjoyed the crater all the same. We'd recommended it to anyone looking to do a Jeju geotourist site without all the hard work.

Coming from a country where temples are famous for their stunning decoration I did not expect much from temples in East Asian countries. But Yakchunsa Temple was beyond my expectations. The temple is stunningly decorated. The Buddha statues are absolutely beautiful. I recommend you walk up to the second floor where you will see countless mini gold Buddha in different poses on the wall to your left and you can enjoy the view of the main hall and the main Buddha from high up. There is a small building to the left of the main hall with 500   heroes  . I think they are important monks or something. At least that's what it says in Chinese characters. All 500 of them have different facial expressions and poses. Some are very comical. Do take a quick look inside. And don't forget to drink the water from the water fountain before you leave the temple. The water there is refreshingly sweet.

Climbing up the iconic Seongsan Ilchulbong, by all means, is not an easy climbHowever, with the refreshing Jeju breeze, the beautiful landscape, and with a little thirst for excitement, it gets you going!The peak! though as you may predict how it would look like to be in the middle of the crater, the wind was so cool and refreshing and the view of Jeju, while going to the sides, makes the climb all worth it!Just too bad there wont be climbs at night to see glittering Jeju but seeing that it's no easy trek, I think it's understandableI am so thankful for the chance to see the sunrise and Jeju from the top!It was a breathtaking experience to see and not to mention, good exercise too!If you head over to Jeju, never miss this iconic place!To me, this is the overall representation of what Jeju has to offer!A promise of fun, beautiful and laidback adventure :)Another side of a Korean holiday experience

Climb was ok, first smooth hill roads, then mainly steps to the top. View wemhile climbing was nice. We did not manage to catch the sunrise due to cloudy skies. However, the view of jeju from pre dawn to dawn while climbing up was worth it. U literally see the city lights up before ur eyes.

By the time we reached Seongsan mountain, it's already 3.30 pm! On reaching there, and by the look at the mountain, it seems as if there's nothing to enjoy but after my daughter stated that it's world wide attraction, I reluctantly followed them up the 274 meter high mountain with unbelievable thought!But after going uphill, I have another thought!On looking down as I rested after some stairs, the beautiful scenery blaff me! Then as we climbed up stairs after stairs, we took lots of pictures. By the time we reached the top which is the most and satisfying view of sceneries surrounding all sides! I took only a few mountain top scenery because my camera's battery was flat! I sat on top of the mountain and look down at the serenity scene of parts of Jeju Island with the blending on sun setting! Just imagine the feel and satisfaction I gain and feel!But it's time to go down so as we're going down, we enjoyed ourselves by watching the sun going down slowly!

Bring along a lot of water before climbing. There is few cafe that open very early at the counter ticket area, for you to have anything if you feel hungry before climbing, but just for snacking. The entrance fee is 2k Won, if im not mistake. The view was great along the way from bottom to top. After half-way through, there is a checkpoint with nice scenery of the city and ocean during dawn, which is so beautiful. Better to take picture during that time of your climbing if you climb to see the sunrise, because when you get down, it is another daylight scenery. If you are not fit enough or dont have that much stamina, don't worry, it is still okay for you to climb, you just need a strong will to arrive at the peak and keep on going. As the view from top is worth the sweat!For you to see sunrise, its better for you to be down at the entrance as early as you can, during my time, I already there by 530am, the gate open at 6am as far as I can remember. If you climb slow and steady, it will take you about an hour to climb to the peak. Just keep in mind, if there is a lot of clouds, you might not be able to see the sunrise. So check your weather before you go.

Breathtaking view when you reached the peak. Time taken from entrance to the peak ~60mins. You can get a chance to see woman diver show but too bad we did not get a chance for it due to time constraint. Tips: please wear comfortable shoes for walking, the stairs can be steep, and eat some food before that for good stamina.

Breathtaking view of Jeju at the Peak of Seongsang iichulbong. Is cooling while walking up the Peak during winter. But no regret and is worth to go up the Peak and see the huge crater. Is not difficult to walk up, there is properly staircase and path. Young children and elderly also can walk up. There are CCTV at some of the pitstop.
best view to see sunrise but so crowed. if you want to take some photo without many pp around, you should come early then start to climb on. many nice small food talls and restaurant near by.

Been there during last autumn. This place is also known as Sunrise Peak. To reach the peak, you need to ascend 600 steps. The 1st 400 over steps seems easy but be more careful after that as the steps become steeper and more rugged. Also mind the autumn chilly strong wind which can blow your bags off (personal experience). Get there to the top for the panoramic view of the peak. Also, if you are in time, you can also watch the pearl diver women in action.

Beautiful scenery. Can be quite difficult for some people not used to climbing. Don't really need to go up to the top. Even from below, view is great. There's a women divers' performance several times a day. Great chance to see them up and close.

Beauitful! I came in early August when it was quite hot and humid. The climb up was a bit strenuous in that weather, but the cool air at the top was our reward. The view from the top is stunning and easily my favorite view from the trip. Too bad when we reached the top, the entire peak was engulfed by a huge cloud and we could not see into the crater. Still, worth the short hike.

Be prepared for stairs! There are 3 waterfalls to see. It can get crowded, so taking a nice picture may take a few minutes since people have to wait on each other to move. The area is full of trees, making the views all the more beautiful. Definitely worth the visit!

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed Jeju Olle Route 6 from Chilshimni Poetry Park (to see the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top) to Oedolgae and happened to see this Hwangwooji coast (probably part of olle route 6) which was my favourite spot of the day. You will walk along Namseong-ro road and passed by 외돌개나라 Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online). I love the place bcos it was like a private pool and it is free. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.? After-which we head to Oedolgae.You can walk there and you do not need a car. Probably a 15 minutes walk from the main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Poong Gyung Hotel or Park sunshine hotel jeju is) and walk in to Namseong-ro road where? 외돌개나라 Hostel is.

As reviewed here, the first 10-15 minutes guests are taken on a tour to the various stations to see how traditional living in korea were. However the sales pitch on honey and several other product seems to have nothing really to do with the traditional farm life (or not obvious)... Do note the sales is not compulsory, but often, guests are 'pressured' into buying something by other guests..

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.
Another in the city waterfall which means that if you are staying in Seogwipo, you must go to see this fall. Entrance is 2000 won which is justified. Beautiful views.
a-must-see place in jeju-do.easy hike, must try egg puff w/honey. yummy~great view on top of seongsan.

Although this place is called a sunrise peak, its even better in sunset! Managed to run up the hundreds of steps in about 30min to catch the sunset, but totally worth it as the views are amazing! Might need a bit of physical fitness but I have seen old ahjummas climb up as well, so just keep climbinh and do not give up.

Although there is not a lot to do here, it is a short walk from the parking to see this absolutely beautiful view!  If you take a few minutes to watch the water swirling around the cliffs it will mesmerize you, so pretty!
all of them are migled  to produce the best view and combiation. If you are at Sanbang temple, you can see the Dreagond head from the back side,

After some hiking (which was hard for me as I didn't really exercise), you can see a small museum on top to explain how light house works, interactive equipments for you to feel more relevant with the light house. You can have a bird eye view of Udo's scenary that will totally amazed you. It is less crowded hence you may enjoy chill and relax time on top.  It's a place worth visiting!

After seeing the waterfall, my family of four took a nice stroll down to the bridge.? The view in the evening is wonderful.? The bridge is also lit up nicely at night!? Of note, one can get tickets for the submarine or boat rides at this same location.

After my Manjanggul Cave   expedition   and since the park is just along the way back, I took the chance to see what's the place could offer. I paid KW 2800 for an entrance (I have read reviews that some paid more than the cost, maybe the cost vary by seasons, not really sure). The maze can be finished roughly 10-15 mins, yet completed the maze roughly 30 mins hahaha. I just enjoyed messing around. Didn't really paid attention to the map and it's goal to ring the bell. The maze is good for family to enjoy.

After climbing the stairs for the view of the lush, plant-filled centre of the crater, you should definitely walk along part of the black sand beach that arcs around to the ?glass house.? You?ll see some amazing views of Seongsan Ilchubon there, and your pictures won?t be filled with random tourists. There are also bits of sea glass scattered along the shore, shells, and if you walk down the beach far enough, a beautiful, large ledge of lava covered in green moss you can walk on and explore. It was really easy to get to the crater by bus from Jeju-si, and it only took about 75 minutes.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.

Admission fee for adult is 2000won. You will be able to enjoy walking up to the peak and see the entire sea/ Mountain View. It will be good to wear covered shoes or sport shoes so it?s easier to go up the steps. Not only that, there?s a 대? performance available but I missed the timing. But the 대? will be at their store selling fresh seafood. It?s a good place for solo travellers :)After exploring ilchulbong, head over to ㅼ“대?吏 for some abalone porridge :D

According to the tour guide, she told us it will take 25 mins to reach the top. But we took more than that.  Never mind just walk slowly and take short break in between. Feeling wonderful when reach the top. The sea view is perfect. Front side u can see the houses. I love the Back side view.
absolutely beautiful cliffs, great views of lava cliffs. a must see for anyone traveling to Jeju Island!only quirk is the small shops selling touristy things.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.

A very long and tiring climb if you are not used to climbing. There's lots of people both locals and tourists climbing along so you will definitely be motivated to continue climbing. Tip: bring sunglasses, pack light, grab a snack and bring a bottle of water, most importantly wear comfortable sports shoes. Just climb slowly and take a break along the way as you need so that you are not overly tired out. If you are thinking of combining this attraction with other nature sites that require ample walking or climbing, do take note that this attraction may already be rather tiring... the view and wind at the top is worth it, in my opinion. You do not see the bird's eye view you see online but nonetheless you see the vast greenery and top down view of the scenery below.

A truly beautiful part of the island - very touristy, but I can understand why.  Definitely worth the climb for the views.  We travelled there from Seogwipo by public bus (about one hour) and it was no problem.  Worthwhile to see!

A short 10 mins walk down down several flights of steps would lead u to the base of the fall. For the adventurous and nimble folks, you can navigate carefully across the rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. I was there on a crowded day and the task of leaping from rock to rock didn?t seem possible. It was still a nice view from the base. Do include this site in your itinerary. I think the volume of water was lesser since it was still winter when I visited.

A scenic spot to visit in Jeju. Recommended for travellers who like nature and sightseeing. However, It requires u to climb stairs in order to reach the peak. It might be tough for elderly. Scenery is definitely good with nice view and breezing air.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

A nice little hike up to the top. Not very long, Maybe 20 minutes but ALOT of stairs. Your legs will be feeling it. Good View at the top and its nice to see all the people taking 1 million selfies of themselves while at the top.

A must-see place when you visit Jeju. It may a bit tiring to climb until the top, but the view is breathtaking. The hiking track also made it easy to climb because they've built a stairs until the peak. Try to visit early in the morning, because around 9 am, the crowd starts to gather, so it may be a little difficult to take a picture without some people intrude in the background. In addition, if the weather forecast is great, try to see the sunrise from the peak. Too bad it's cloudy when we visited, so we didnt try to see the sunrise.

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.

A must do in Jeju. We hired a taxi driver to take us and it was 2000won a person to enter. We wanted to go for sunrise but there was an extra fee to hire them that early. (If you want to rent a car, make sure you have an international license - it's about 1.5hr from Jeju city) The hike really isn't too bad. It is an incline, and yes there are lots of stairs, but it is do-able. There were plenty of elderly hiking up and lots of places to stop. Beautiful view from up top. Entrance also allows you to go down to the beach and see the women divers and eat fresh catch.
A great view for sunset and at night, you can see the lights being light up at the Bridge with difference colors. Mainly place for you to take pic =)

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

20min climb up to peak, short time but take some energy to climb up, come down is easy. So get ready to take off your jacket even is cold day. But worthy, nice view. And can see haenyeo performance as well, but must check the time. One day 2 slot, afternoon is 3pm.

You need to see it once as an experience.There was not much to do except sit in the bus and watch the bus slowly moving upwards (looks like it). There is a stopover by the side of the road that sells food and snacks.

You can take bus 6000 from Seogwipo to this beach in the Jungmun tourist area. Feared that it would be overrun by tourists but that was not the case. The beach is big and very scenic. Be prepared that there are no umbrellas nor sun loungers and it is not possible to rent. This is THE surfing spot in Jeju and you will see a great number of surfers breaking the waves. Really cool.

While in Jeju - we booked the Yeha bus tour and this is one of the places included to visit.  We really enjoyed our time here and our guide did an excellent job of recommending how to see everything in the time we had allotted.

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy

We were quite frustrated when we arrived and see a crowd of people inside plus it is raining heavily on the day we arrived. Yet the tasty green tea crepe makes the whole trip worth it ! You can take bus 152 from new Jeju city.
We visited Oedolgae as part of our Yeha Bus tour - South Course and it is just another perfect spot to stop and see Jeju's beauty.

We visited and there were about 20 buses in the parking lot. The shop where you get the tea or ice cream was very full so we went out to the tea bushes and enjoyed our tea there. We did learn about how tea is made and seeing the actual plant was interesting to me. Wish it was less crowded.

We took city tour bus and stopped at this famous black pork street for dinner at the shop with long queue.   Minimum order is KWR 54000 for 600g pork for 2 pax ie roughly 300g per pax.  It seemed so meaty but the helper grilled the pork just nice and we finished all.

We got a local bus to this park. When we went there it was quite windy so take a sweater.The park is very large with lots of stones to see. There is no cafe so take water or food. It is really worth the visit.

We did this as part of the Yeha Bus Tour East Course tour and they had it timed perfectly for us to arrive and see the Women Diver Show and then after we had enough time to make the beautiful climb up Seongsan Ilchulbong.  We had beautiful weather in October - it was absolutely perfect!  I would definitely recommend tennis shoes and even if the weather seems chilly when you start out - wear a jacket that you can remove.  Lots of beautiful photo opportunities here!

Was there at about 10ish in the morning lots of (noisy) tourist and you can hardly find a decent seat in the cafe with unruly kids running around. Difficult to take photo at the photo spot cos some particular tourists pose like nobody business and after a long time posing change friend to pose again. I gave up and went outdoors where noise will not be contained and there is more fresh air.Sadly there isn't much nor exciting to see here - yet it is a spot you have read alot before coming. Suggest to just make a brief stop to have a look.I spent more time over at the Innisfree Jeju House instead which was surprisingly very peaceful.
Very small beach. Lots of families attending the beach as well. Pretty easy to get to by bus. Worth seeing.
Udo is small and very beautiful island. You can take the ferry from Seongsan for around 15mins. There are many buses on the island to take you for sightseeing.
Tourist flock in by the bus load to see cars (in neutral gear) roll mysteriously uphill

Took a Taxi to the waterfall from Cheonjiyeon Waterfall. Plan to get wet if you get close to the falls.Better get there before is closes. Admission of course. Lady at information desk was very helpful. We took the Airport Limo bus for 11000 won bus # 600 to the Cheoniyeon Waterfall. Since I wanted to see as much of the south end as I could before dark I am glad we got to see these areas. Go to KAL hotel and take the Limo Bus back to the Airport for 11000 Won.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This was our last station before we heading to airport to catch our flight to Busan. You will be able to see the rock that look like a dragon head. Overall this place what you see was the rock. It was near to the sea and lots of people too.

This was a tourist trap.No museum to me- just a bit of information about tea on the wall with a tea grousing machine- that?셲 it!Who calls this a museum?The rest of place was for cafe souvenir shop - some observatory deck where you could see the tea field.Honestly Amore Pacific did a great job to let people recognize that Jeju could produce tea that?셲 perfectly linked with their business. Very smart from business perspective- bravo in that sense.
This was a stop on our Yeha bus tour - East Course - we stopped for maybe 15 - 20 minutes and it was a beautiful spot to take some pictures and see Seongsan Ilchulpeak.

This was a stop of a bus tour through the weestern part of the Island. The so called tea Museum is a building where they sell  tea in all kinds of packaging such as bags and boxes. The word Museum is barely justified by the few pots and cups that are exhibited. You certainly should not come here from Europe because of the tea Museum. For those that never have seen the harvest of tea leaves is worth a stop.

This spot looks like it exists purely for the 15-20 tour buses that were there when we visited as its pretty much a rock with a different shape that you can see in the picture. Save your time and your parking fee and check out the world heritage listed rocks formations around the island otherwise you will need just 1 min here to take a photo and be off again

This small island is good for half or full day depends on what you going to do. The island provide with free shuttle bus but not sure it is summer period. Got two routes east and west. Check with driver before get into the bus. Light house stop and black sand see is a must.

This pavilion is something to visit when you get dropped off in town by the bus from the cruise ship.  It takes a few minutes to walk around and take a few pics but I certainly wouldn't consider it a must see destination to go to.
There was actually special rooms dedicated for tourists that sells Korean ginseng. Seems more like a touristy spot for bus loads of tourists. Not much to see.

The O쨈Sulloc Tea Museum and tea field is a treat!  It쨈s easy to get to by the airport bus we got to it by taking the Yeha West Tour.Be prepared for crowds in the cafe.  However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The cafe offers the most delicious green tea ice cream.  I쨈m dying to try the cakes but can쨈t get pass the ice cream.  There is also a brown roasted tea ice cream but I prefer the green tea one.  It isn쨈t sweet and has a distinctive green tea flavor left on your palate as you get ready for the next bite.Recommendation--I got the Cold Green Sticks which are perfect for a bottle of water.  The other teas you definitely need a strainer otherwise get the tea in teabags.Oh and O짢Sulloc has a cafe in the Nampo area in Busan if you need your green tea ice cream fix. Other cafes have green tea ice cream but OSulloc is yummy and my favorite.O쨈Sulloc seems to be branding itself as a high end tea so you just can쨈t purchase it in a grocery store nor do the hotels have it as complimentary tea a shame since it is a Korean brand. So stock up and enjoy.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

The last time I went to a similar place with during my childhood days. Visiting aqua planet in jeju again is a good experience. The whole place isn't all that big but there is plenty of sea marine life to see and a Enormous fish take. This place can give u a kind of relaxing atmosphere. At the end there is a performance where u can rest your weary legs. Good place to be If you have a busy trip before you came to jeju. A little break for a change. Overall I enjoy the trip here and will revisit again with my love ones if ever given the chance.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

the engine of the bus I am in was switch-off and yet it continue to move upwards.. only a stretch of about 250m of road.... a bottle of mineral water seems to roll upwards too...most puzzling was a bus moves up faster than a sedan car...simply strange...

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

strictly for those above 18.but beware that buses come here ends early.after 10pm i only see taxis and cars.Interesting stone sculptures of male and female organs.sex positions..a shop selling interesting condoms and penis keychains vibrators etc..super cold at night..open until midnight..there is a indoor museum and show clay figurines..

So you get to this place and will be faced with mountains of oranges  pork knuckles and fish. Bet its the place to be if your mission is to get groceries or some local snacks.But if you want to buy souvenior  this place isn't really ideal as most stuff 竊늨ranges you can't take overseas  fishe neither;packed snacks are like what you can see all over the island 竊뎤eems a bit mass produced.The interesting to observe is that most shops are ran by one solo lady  only. They took a lot of hardship to get the business running .

Small area but you can see clear waters around the rocks formed from the volcano. Do visit if you have time. I imagine it would be amazing to catch the sunset here but am unable to do so because of time constraints.Easily accessible by bus no. 462 from Jeju Bus Terminal.

Seriously the number of people that were there on a sunny afternoon stressed us out. It almost seemed like a one drop shop rather than a museum. There was very little to see in terms of the museum the shop and the cafe were f***ing noisy and busy we couldn't even walk through. We had set B which included a green tea roll cake a hallabong drink and a green tea ice cream. Very average. SKIP!

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.
quite far from what I've imaged. But the scene was worth to see. Except there was no bus stop around and very little sign to follow.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

Made plans to visit Jeju based on the availability of rentals at Olle. I am an AVID kayaker and this seemed like a good stop. Called 2 weeks in advance of my trip and confirmed that rentals would be available. 2 days before departure called again to confirm dates. Owner said rentals not available. When referencing the previous call the owner became hostile and extremely rude. He said we should take our business elsewhere. I will be and I suggest you do too.
Like - the experience and seeing a tour bus driver standing up and showing his passengers that he did not do anything will letting the bus roll uphill. Dislike - nothing.
Leave early as the final path to summit closes at 13 30 so I didn't see crater. Path is very clearly set out on wooden planks and steps. Very busy too.

Jeju World Cup Stadium is certainly worth stopping by if you are in the area. It looks superb from the outside and can be seen from a distance as you come down the hill from Seogwipo.Main entrance is open allowing you to walk in and spend some time in the stands for free. Tickets for Jeju United games are reasonably priced  and only attended up a small number of fans meaning they are up for grabs if you happen to time your visit in the K-League Classic season.Lots of busses pass by including the Airport Limo service (stop just in front) so pay a visit if you're a football fan or just want to see one of the 2002 World Cup's venues

It's quite far from main area and you need to change bus if you want to use public transport. We decided to go by taxi to save time. This place is quite big. Be prepared to walk and walk and walk. They have made huge statues of males and females in various positions. It's funny to see all this at a public place with so many people of different ages.
It's nice to see and easy to acces as it has an own bus stop.Something hapend there in a movie and therfore many people are there to see that place.

It isn't worth travelling all the way but if you are passing by it is an interesting stop. The optical illusion is really amazing. It looks like we are climbing uphill without any help. You can even try by placing a can or bottle or even water. Place is rather crowded though. Seem to be a common tourist stop for most with lots of buses.

It is fun to watch others here - a great people watching place.  To see masses of tourists walking backwards on what is really a busy road is great for fun and photos.  Sit outside at one of the lpocak food places - order some beers and snacks and enjoy the quirky road.  Good for an hour or so including lunch.

It is difficult to take the local bus to go to the Ferry station so we took a taxi from our hotel near the city centre. The ferry ride is short but the sea air is refreshing and it is kind of fun seeing excited kids feeding the seagulls. The scenery is beautiful on the island but the hop on and hop off bus service is pretty rough.I think they are overbooked and big groups also have special buses nobody else are allowed on. End up waiting a lot to get to the next site. Annoying..!
If you take the steps down to the rocks you will see some ladies peddling fresh sashimi seafood with soju. Location is very popular with tour buses so be prepared for crowds

I went to the Marine Park (Pacific Land) that proposes a show with dolphins  sea lions and monkeys. I went there with my friends  thinking it was an aquarium  and I do not recommend this place at all! What they're doing to this beautiful animals is pure cruelty. We can obviously see the intensive training  the abuse and the fear these poor animals (monkeys  dolphins) are going through. There was a baby dolphin completely lost and unable to do the show in this tiny tank  but they forced the adults to do the show again and again  until the baby succeeded it. The baby ended up banging his head on the wall.. It was just unbearable to watch. After that  no food in return for the others. The animals shouldn't be here  and treated like that. I visited this as part of an inclusive tour.  This is really interesting.  there is the story of tea and you can walk among the tea bushes.  This is the best Korea tea there is and of course you can buy their products and sample green tea foods in the cafe. Their sister beauty products company Innesfree also has a cafe and gift shop.  Again these products have a hig reputation in S. Korea.  I would have liked more time to spend here.  The main cafe was packed and I would have like to have had green tea and green tea cake or green tea ice cream but I wouldn't have been able to see anything else in the time we had.  A pleasant place to visit for a few hours.

I visited on a tour from Yeha Bus Tours. It was such an awesome experience that I would have never seen if it wasn't for being part of that tour. The buildings were really neat and the restaurant was delicious. I was there on a rainy day but it was still pleasant. The mist contributed to the mysterious and dreamy vibe that this place had. I recommend carrying a small umbrella. I needed it throughout my 2 week stay in South Korea.

I live just down the road from O'Sulloc and pass it on a nearly daily basis it's always busy always!.I have visited once get past standing next to a tea plant and a big tea pot and your pretty much done there is a collection of crockery and quite a nice cafe you need to like green tea though...It takes about half an hour to see and do everything.

I like Greek history. So when I heard about this place I decided to visit. My wife was not ready but I persuaded her. I like go to market to see what they have ! Fun place and you can try some food here and clean not bad to hangout for 2 or 3 hrs or so than from here you can take a bus go anywhere else you want to go !!

I found about this temple while looking for things to do around the waterfalls. great to walk the tunnels amazing to see some of the patterns on the walls its really cheap to enter easy to get to with a bus. dont bother paying a tour for it.

Great if u like tea quite a wide variety they sell and with a cafe that sells really good looking green tea chiffon cakes and tea snacks. Also have brunch items. There's also innisfree store there for u to make your own soaps that was quite popular with the kids and families. The museum itself has nothing much to offer I would say. But there are many many different green tea product. Shampoo shower bar tea bag latte tumbler make up item cleanser toothpaste mask green tea powder tea tea and some more tea... And the best is the restaurant! All the green tea ice cream drinks food! Everything has something to do with green tea! Make sure you try the green tea ice cream!

Easily accessible by public bus from airport! This garden is not so crowded & have nice decoration so can relax. Locals like to visit this place & not foreigners are seen during my visit there. Next to this garden have a waterwall so got another place to relax. Recommend to go teddy bear museum & kpop museum as very near to one another so this will spend one whole day.

Be careful what you do. Just kidding  fret not for breaking anything. The biggest chance of you breaking anything here would be in the souvenir shop. A beautiful museum to go to  to see everything created out of glass pieces. How a simple  yet breakable piece of glass can turn into an artpiece which seems as strong as the pillars of a temple.I like the glass tulips best  a great number of them around this museum. It really shows Korea being a Tulip country  as I get to see these lovely  brightly coloured flowers everywhere. There's a little cafe in there which I thought was a very beautiful cafe  made out of glass. The table you use  the chairs you sit are all made out of glass  added with colour.Surprisingly  the thing you should be checking out is the stand alone toilets  one for female  the other for male. Yes  it's made of glass and from the inside  you can actually see through to the outside! Don't worry  your privacy is intact while answering nature's call  because it's tainted black from the outside and people cannot actually see anything inside! So don't be surprised to see people taking a look at their reflections and doing funny poses while you are doing your business in the toilet. Have a good laugh instead!

As it was raining on the day we visited we could only have tea in the cave caf챕 and look at the souvenir shop.  Despite not being able to see more of the eco park - we heard there is a zip line over the tea bushes among other things we enjoyed ourselves at the tea caf챕 and the handmade jewellery selection.  The tea was of a good quality and the cake too.  Certainly they do not look as rich as the offerings at the O'Sulloc Tea Museum (which I did not taste).The jeweller efficiently modified the earring from hook style to a poke and push stud style for my sis. Actually I didn't know about this road until the Jeju Golden Bus City Tour ticket lady excitedly explained this strange phenomenon about the bus being able to move on its own while on neutral gear.So those on the Jeju Golden Bus Tour don't really have to go out of the way to see this mysterious road. It's just before the Jeju Museum of Art stop.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

You want to know about volcanoes? This is the place. The museum is interactive and informative. And not to mention it houses some of the most beautiful natural volcanic sculptures around. There are three courses to follow in order to see what the park has to offer - taking things at a leisurely pace, this can easily take 3 hours to complete. It is well worth it though - with the some of the paths in course two taking on an enchanted forest appeal. The entrance is 5000 won, and you can get to the park on the Jeju City Tour Bus. The stops are just outside the park. A good poncho will serve better during rainy weather than an umbrella here, as there are parts of the course with low lying foliage (and the wind can be a little ferocious at times too).

You need to take a ferry from the terminal near the sunrise peak and I had to queue for nearly 15 minutes to get the ferry tickets. Follow the direction sign to board the ferry. We waited at the wrong place but were fortunate to have a korean informed of the correct location. The ferry took 20 minutes to reach the islet.The islet was small but not small enough to travel on foot. There are several transport options to see go round the islet - shuttle bus, ATV, motorbikes or bicycles. We chose the shuttle bus. There are several locations which it brought us to. The driver would explain more about the attractions but in korean language. At each location, visitors can alight the bus and visit the attractions. Once you are done, you have to find the bus boarding point (strangely at some distance from the alighting point). The bus you board would be different from the one you alighted from.It was really crowded on Udo Islet. The attractions are just some natural geological formation, similar those on the Jeju island. They were scenic but got a little boring after some time.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

You can easily spend a half or full day sightseeing around the island. They have tour buses which will take you around to the major sights but I'd recommend renting a bike. There are heaps of places to rent bikes from after you get off the ferry. You'll need an international license to rent a scooter or ATV. But there are no serious hills in the island so (if you're there in fall/spring with fair weather) I'd really recommend a bicycle. It was so lovely cycling around the island and easily jumping on and off my bike to snap pictures.The bike rental was 4 hours for 10,000 won. They shop will give you a map of the island with tours and sightseeing locations on it. Although you don't really need it as you basically just cycle the seaside road. Don't forget your camera or to eat the famous peanut ice cream!

Yes, you can have chance to see the Korean old houses. However, there is nothing much for you to visit. No tourist information or any other services around. We take a long bus to reach there and go back in 10 minutes then.

With only one full day in Jeju and a list of places to visit, there was no way we can go see it all by ourselves in one day. So when we ran across this tour that included almost all of our must see places in Jeju we had to book it. Jin was our tour guide for the day and was very prompt with the pickup and was very knowledgeable of the sites that he took us to. Each stop of the tour was ??. And the option to go tangerine picking checked off one of activity that I wanted to do myself. The price for this tour is very reasonable considering that we didn’t have to figure out how to get place to place by bus or taxi. The cherry on top is the food and activity recommendations that Jin gave us as the tour ended so it felt like our tour continued on through the night even after the tour ended. Thanks Jin for the awesome tour!

What's interesting is that you really, actually get to see cars/buses with their engines obviously off, rolling up the slope. Expect to see a number of tour buses. Some tour guides will demonstrate the mysteriousness of the road even further by pouring water on the ground. The water will flow upwards. 10mins is enough time to spend here. Recommended to visit once for the experience.

What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

Well, if you like teddy bears, drop by this place to see their collection.  Honestly, I get more excited browsing teddy bears at a departmental store.  This place is probably losing its charm as it is mainly visited by tourists sent here by tour buses and very little koreans or free-n-easy tourists.

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We were dropped by the bus at the parking lot, and had to walked through a beautiful park where seashell statues and boats placed along the path. We have to queue for about 20-30 minutes before we could really see the amazing nature-sculptured cliff.It was very beautiful, especially at sunset.

We went there with a bus group, they organized a lot of activities and Mysterious road was one of these. We found out it's too crowded and there's nothing to see and to do, it's normal street, they said that the cars will move without a driver, but you can't see it or feel it, just the driver feels that. overall don't go there if specially for the street if it's on your way or you are with a group it's okay.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre.
