We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000\ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

We walked past Yongdu-am rock when we were trying to find the jimjilbang that we were staying at for the night. If we had made any effort to go and see it I would have been bummed but since it was in passing it was interesting in its own manner. I can understand how it looks like a dragon and you don't need TOO much of an imagination to be able to see it but unless your interested in folklore/'the dragon' means anything to you, you won't be overly excited/impressed.If it didn't have reams of tourists and tour buses or the tourist shops all around it Im not sure I would have even stopped to take a picture.(the ladies working in the tour information centre right outside of this area speak good english and are very kind and helpful if you need directions)

We visited as part of a group/tour and arrived late in the day (about 5pm). Huge carpark just outside.Not at all busy. Our guide walked us around the village and gave informative information (in English) about the history of the island and the life styles of the people that would have/do live here.The few residents that we saw didn?t want photos taken, I thought a little strange since they live in a ?theme park? and must see tourists every day of the year.We were allowed to poke our heads into specified rooms/houses.There was a shop for gifts etc and a WC block for the use of behind the guest villa at the backWe spent about 40 mins here

we tried to take bus and ferry ourselves to visit Udo. The weather on that day was very good, there were a lot of geographical scenes in Udo, beaches were beautiful, besides taking bus for seeing the whole island, take a walk along the seaside was also very good.  eating seafood in a famous restaurant, also tried the famous peanut ice cream of this island.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took ride on bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street to visit Teddy Bear Museum jeju which is nearby to Jungmun  tourist resort. Bus fare cost us only KRW 1150 per pax. The visit to Teddy bear museum was fantastic especially for my sister, teddy bear lover. It was amazing to see many collection of teddy bears from all over the world with different themes and events globally.  There were three sections of the teddy bear museum; starting from the history, artwork and forest of teddy bear. There was a garden outside of the museum with the construction of enormous teddy bear. We can get a glimpse of the LV and Swarvosky teddy bear. The most nostalgic teddy bear was the Princess Hour theme teddy bear. The most great thing to watch was the Elvis Presley show. However, the teddy bear sold there was expensive. It was worth to visit this place.

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We took a taxi to this road. The driver spoke limited English but it was sufficient for us to understand the explanation: when the vehicle gear is put to N on what seemed to be an up-slope, the vehicle rolls forward (it should have rowed backward instead)When we alighted the cab, we stood there longer to examine all the passing vehicles: mainly tour buses experimenting the same concept. You can hear their engines turned off and you will see the buses rolling   forward   on the up-slope. It was an intriguing experience but will be even better if you drive and experience it yourself. Other than the road itself, you may consider alighting and try out the two street food stores there.. or have a walk around the area, we saw herd of cattles grazing just beside the road too.

We took a taxi from our hotel in Jeju City, which took about an hour, to the Ferry Terminal. It was pretty easy to buy the ticket. Once we got to the island, it wasn't really clear what to do, so we followed everyone to a small building that was selling bus tour tickets. We didn't get the bus we wanted, though they both seem to just drive around the island and you can hop on and off. We found out later that we could have rented a little tricycle moped. We enjoyed ourselves. Worth the trip.

We took a cab from Ramada Plaza for 30,000 wan. It took about half an hour. The bus home 710 was great and took an hour. 3000 wan. The island was good fun. We cycled the island stopping along the way to see things. The elder diving women were really cool. Sad to see the garbage around from the sea :( Udo is in such a highly populated area of the world garbage is a big problem. It makes me want to really try to become green at home in Canada.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

We read how good the pork belly was and from what we read, recommendations were to go to  Hwaro Hyang instead of Dumbedon. We arrived, dropped our bags, took a taxi to get there to make sure we experience what everyone is raving about. Hwaro Hyang was not too crowded and we easily got a table. The server explained that we should get the set for a couple to be able to taste a good sample of the cuts and some abalone. That we did. We got the platter, he dropped it on the hot plate and that was the last time our server came to our table. We saw how he was going around to all the other tables, turning their food over, cutting it up. Finally, we saw this lady who was serving another table and we flagged her down to see who might help us. She had to yell and call/force a young person to help us. I?ll chalk it to a language barrier issue as they were busily chatting with the rest of the customers. Finally the boy cut up our food, and we had to help ourselves and towards the end, the lady came back to turn off our hot plate. The experience would have been enhanced if we had known how to pair the condiments. We didn?t want to offend anyone so we watched as they showed the other tables how to eat the food and just mimicked them. They even did the lettuce wraps for some tables to show them how the side dishes are rolled. So moral of the story, unless you?re local or can speak with them conversationally, prepare to be ignored and just watching to see how others do it.

We reached the ferry terminal at 11am and waited for a short while for the ferry. The ferry depart quite frequently so there is no worry for that. As mentioned by other people, you will need to bring your passport to purchase a ticket. If you intend to rent a motorised vehicle in Udo, you will need to bring along your international driving permit. We rented a covered motorised scooter for 3h at KRW40,000. The scooter has doors and can seat 2 people. It took us less than 2.5h to cover the whole island, we even took 45min lunch break in between. The entire island is around 17km, so if you intend to make stopovers for photo taking, renting for 2h will be good enough. Just follow the coastline and you won't get lost. I highly recommend travellers to opt for the motorised scooter for a relaxing trip around Udo island. It will take you just half day. There are not many cars on the road but there are many scooters and bicycles which share the same path. There are many tourists and they might not observe the driving rules very well, so do be careful when driving on the roads. However, if you intend to see some of the other sights on Udo, they are not accessible for these transportation as you will need to take a separate ferry to go there. There seems to be many people taking the shuttle bus in Udo, so I don't really recommend people to do so if you have an international driving permit.

We originally got the bus here to go to hallim park. we noticed this beautiful beach and decided to check it out. anyway we ended up staying here all day. Was so nice to be on such soft, yellow sand with clear waters. There was quite a few families with young children which was nice to see all the children playing. Unfortunately there was a digger truck digging the sand while we were there for a few hours and a man kept blowing his whistle at everyone walking near the truck. if it wasnt for this it would have been excellent. Theres shops and restaurants close by and toilet blocks that provide flowing water to wash off but this is cut off around 5 or 6 pm. Sunset here was amazing.

We made a quick little stop here on our way back to the airport. We came in the morning and it was fairly easy to get parking and not too busy for taking pictures. It's a nice spot if it's on your way somewhere, but it's not a super must-see attraction.

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We did this as part of Yeha bus tour - South Course - we were in the back of the bus, so it was really hard for us to see, but apparently, you put your vehicle in neutral and it rolls the opposite of what you would expect.  I'm sure the experience would be better in a car.

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

We could not come here to enjoy the famous sunrise, but we had the chance to see the sunset from the top. AMAZING! If you come with bus #701, you should get off at the bus stop called   Entrance to the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak  . from there, the entrance is only two blocks away. Climbing up to the top is takes around 20 mins. NOTE --> If you would not take your luggage or bag with you to the top, but leave the in the number coded lockers downstairs, don't forget to check the opening hours of the luggage store!!! When we were there it closed at 6 pm, we got there only 4 mins past 6, and despite the place was still open, the lockers could not be opened anymore even with the right codes after 6 pm. We had to call the emergency number shown on the locker side, to unlock it for us and retrieve our bags.

We caught the 7:30 am ferry from Seongshan Port to Udo.  The ferry left a bit early so we actually arrived at the island by 7:35.  The ferry ride should be about 15 minutes.  Cost was 17,000 kwr for 2 adults for round-trip tickets.  We struggled with whether we should have brought our car on board and immediately regretted not doing so once we landed.  Seems it is off season so not busy at all.  The first place we stopped at was the mango shop, where they also have a shop In the back for vehicle rentals.  Stopped there and tried to rent a mini-car/scooter but the staff said no rentals today because of the festival (seems it is the seashell festival).  Anyway, with no other option, we just took the hop-on and hop-off bus (5000 krw per person).  It?s about 21,000 krw round trip for a small car.  First stop was the lighthouse, got there at 7:45 and went back down to catch the next bus at 8:30.  The next stop after was the black sand beach.  Then to the other lighthouse on the northern tip of the island.  We concluded our trip at the stop after that which is the other ferry port.  We caught the 10 am ferry.  We skipped the white sand beach which is probably the most popular site as a lot of Korean dramas were shot there.  Some tips:- bring your car if you have one so you can visit the island on your own schedule - try the peanut ice cream at Jimmy?s Natural Ice Cream- most of the food places may be closed on a Sunday

We came on a hot August day by bus. It is about 2 hours from the Intercity Bus Terminal (701). There is much to see. You can climb the steep ridge to the top or go below and see some of the expert women divers. Bring a hat and a sturdy umbrella. This is a stunning natural landmark and one of the rather unspoiled places on Jeju Island, which is crawling with unnecessary development.

We arrived here by bus from our Jeju hotel on a Friday night.  It took approximately 35-40 minutes because of the traffic and the nondirect route our bus took.  The front of the market (across the street) has a small open square area where they would have live music for the night.  We also noticed a few drunks sitting around in the area, but they seemed harmless.The market itself is quite large.  The market seemed to specialize in selling tangerines.  There were stall after stall selling local tangerines.  There is a larger variety of items offered for sale as you walk into the market some more.  We tried some food that was being sold - in this case, some pork at around 9000 won.  There is also seafood and other vegetables and meats sold.  The market seemed to extend to other areas - it's quite close to the Black Pork Street, some other more upscale shops and restaurants.  It's definitely worth a 1-2 hour walk within the market to explore.

Visually, the road is seen to be an uphill road. But when the bus driver turned off the engine and release the brakes, it starts to move forward. Quite interesting. But don't purposely go there unless it's part of the journey. Not worth.

Visiting Manjanggul Cave is one of the main reason I visited Jeju. I and my family were not disappointed at all. We visited during late June 2015. The cave is a little bit cooler inside even in a hot summer day so remember to bring a jacket especially for kids. There was rain before our visit so the cave inside was a little bit wet but we could go inside and visit. There is a steep stair in the beginning of the tunnel/cave so one must walk very carefully. After entering the cave, there is no more stair and on flat level mainly.The whole cave is well lit so you should be able to see inside without bringing your own flashlight torches. (You can still bring it if you want to see everything in detail!)Only 1km of the cave is accessible by visitors. You go inside and walk to the end of the tunnel and then walk back the same way you go in. I suggest you riding a taxi to this place since public bus is not easily accessible to this tourist spot. There is a bathroom outside the cave only. So if you need to go to bathroom, you have to go before entering the cave.

Visiting Jeju ? Do it if you have at least4 days or more ! All the tourist attractions are in different corners of the island and they are far from each other .There are daily bus tours , running in one direction , starting at 9am coming back at 6 pm . Not every spot is so interesting , probably many of travellers have seen some similar somewhere else . The same is reg. this small beach . There are plenty of such beaches or even nicer around the world

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Visited here as part of my tour package. There is a ferry that can transport cars and people to the island. Upon reaching the island, we took a bus tour n brings us to a few locations. The most memorable one will be the hike up to the lighthouse. Tiring but fun and you can see the great ocean around. Took slightly more than a half day of tour in this island and it's fun :)

Visited DongMun on a Monday night after dinner at around 8pm and some seafood / fruit vendors are still open.  A small area adjacent to the market were doing bustling business selling street food / snack.  Having come from Seoul / Busan before JeJu,  DongMun market may be seemingly smaller but will still be a nice market to visit when in Jeju

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Udo was the best place in my jeju visit. although the weather was very hot, but its windy too. My hat even blow off by the wind. The sea and sand were just too beautiful. its really a relaxing place when seeing the green grasses dancing all over in front of you. Besides, the zha jiang mian was really tasted good. it costed 8000won. the peanut icecream was famous too, 3000won. We sent a whole morning there. In the island, we can take bus, rent bicycle or scooter.

Udo was easy to get to and a great place to camp with full amenities. There are 2 main beaches; one on the West side and one on the North East side. Both are beautiful but the one that has sand made of seashells (West Side) is a little hard on your bare feet  and it was much busier there. The other has soft fine sand that makes for a great camping spot. There are no taxis on the island. In hindsight, we would have taken the other ferry to the port that was a bit closer to Hagosudong Beach (the NE side), but there is this drop on and off Bus Tour System that costs 5000won/person. You can get on from the ferry, drop off and set up your camp at the beach, then hop back on. It runs frequently but only stops at 4 main sightseeing spots (beach 1, beach 2, caves and ___ ) . We were able to use the bus for the two days we were there for on the same fare, but there are times/stops that are crazy busy. We watched at least 6 packed buses go by before we decided to stay the night. Honorable food mention: Pirate Caf챕. Really interesting place and staff. Great BiBamBap and you get to sign a plaque and hang it from their wall when you?re done eating.Friendly people, campfire and camping friendly, personal beer cooler (at the convenience stores directly behind the beach), and lots of cats.

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

Travelled on September using the busdaytour. Its strange in this 100meter road, how it seemed to be going up, but yet though our bus' machine has been turned off, our bus seems to be going up, in about 5-10km/hour. Jeju people called this the ghost road, where they say that the ghosts are pushing us up.

Tour companies love this tourist trap because it add a good few lines to their tourist brochure while being totally costless for them and wasteful for us.If you can, ask your guide to just pass this, getting back to the hotel staring at your ceiling is better than this.My guide made it worse since he was totally excited of this place, yet when I get there, even before we stop, I look outside the bus to the row of trees and can see the reason behind   the mystery road   and I was   hmmm...lame, can we just move on  . But the guide insist that we spend our expensive time on this thing and my group members want to agree with him.And since I already see the row of tree and how the optic illusion would work, the optic illusion (which is weak) dissipates for me. Ask your guide to go somewhere else.

Took a bus from Seogwipo early morning and it takes around 1 hour 40 minutes to get there as the bus stops on all stops along the way. Once there, it is a short 10 to 15 min hike up to the top where you will be met with a green crater. Unless you have a drone, its not possible to capture the beauty of the place unfortunately. On the way down, we waited to see the women diving show, but it got cancelled which was a let down as we only got to know after the show was supposed to start.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This was a part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - and felt it was worth seeing.  It is a lava tunnel/cave, which makes it kind of unique.  Visitors are limited to how far you can explore, which is fine as you do need to watch carefully where you walk - it is a lava tube and the floor is very uneven.  It is known for   Stone Turtle   because it is shaped like Jeju island.  Be sure to have a light jacket.

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This roads' mysteriousness can only be seen by placing things that roll on the road because these things will roll the opposite direction it's supposed to!Bring a toy car and take a video, just look out for other free rolling things like cars and buses.

This place will be good for nature lovers and those who are in Jeju to relax and get away from busy city life. It only takes 1hour to cover the area at a slow pace. You may get a chance to see autumn foliage here from mid to late Nov as there are quite a number of maple trees in the forest. (Note: Autumn is mild in Jeju, while northern parts of Korea are having colourful autumn foliage, we hardly see any colourful trees in Jeju till we came to Bijarim forest)

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

This place is great, fresh seafood sold at the coast, seeing the sea ladies in action (we were lucky and saw her catching an octopus with a fork like stick) and beautiful scenery of the coast, sea and land. It's a short boat ride over from the main island, then one could choose to take their bus at a fee, which will stop by 4 or 5 stops near the beach, cliff, etc  then bring u back to the starting point. Alternatively, you could rent a motorbike or four wheel drive. For the latter, one needs an international driving licence. One thing that's everywhere is their peanut ice cream, basically soft serve with peanut powder. Also, there's grilled cuttlefish everywhere.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.

This is one of the most beautiful beaches in Jeju island. The sea was so amazing, water so clear and having light ocean blue color. from here you could see the Biyangdo island, very close. However, it was rather cold and windy for us, so we could not swim just wandering around. we spent around 2hrs here. we got here by intercity bus no. 702 (about 1 hr) from jeju bus terminal.
This is also a very nice site in Seogwipo, you can get there by bus, and then go down all the way to see the falls as close as you like, it is impressive.
This garden is really aesthetic and pretty!! I had been in Seoul for my stay in Korea so far and everyday is super busy, so it?s nice to relax and see this garden today! I would highly recommend!

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

There is a huge greenhouse with 7 separate areas of different plants including desert, aquatic, floral, jungle, and tropical fruit. ? The tropical fruit area had platters (examples)? of many different types of the fruit of the nearby trees. ? There are a couple small shops in the greenhouse selling different items as well as food and drink.? ? There is also an elevator going up to a 5th floor observatory. ? We went on a very rainy day.? ? Couldn’t see a thing. ? The greenhouse was extremely busy, I’m sure moreso due to the bad weather.? ? ? 10,000 won to enter.

There is a bus from Jeju bus terminal that takes 1hours and a half min and you have to take a Ferry that costs 5,500won.If you dont know how to plan one day travel I would like to recommend you to go Udo and  Seongsan Ilchulbong that is closer to each other If you start your day early you will probably have more time thoughTo see all island it takes 3~4hours by bus that there is Tour bus which costs 5,000wonHowever i would like to recommend you to ride a bike for some partIt is beautiful to ride around the sea and you can feel relaxed.There is 3 beaches that you can visit and those are all different atmosphereespecially there is Coral beach that are exists only 3palce on the world Please go towards the end where people are not crowdedYou will see more pretty coralUdo is famouse for peanut that if you like plz try only small amount since it is a bit expensiveI am not sure if there is famouse food for foreginer but street food is okay As my memory Udo is one of the best part in Jeju island I will recommend for my friends

The world's largest nutmeg forest can be found on Jeju Island, South Korea.  A beautiful, old growth forest with a gigantic nutmeg tree as the central attraction, this forest offers quiet beauty to stroll through in a relaxed and rejuvenating atmosphere. The smell of nutmeg is distinct immediately upon entering.  Parts of the forest have beautiful red crushed stone walking paths and other parts have very well maintained wooden pathways.  To do the whole forest takes about 60 minutes at a comfortable pace.  Picture opportunities abound, and you'll likely be able to see wedding couples posing for their formal pictures amidst the beauty of the forest surroundings.  A great break from the hustle-bustle of other attractions, this forest offers the opportunity to enjoy nature in a very unique way.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The waterfall is said to be the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the sea - although it seems to fall into a cove, not directly into the ocean.  The spot is very touristy and busy, but is a nice waterfall in itself.  You can paddle in the water to cool off and kids love playing on the rocks.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The products they sell are overpriced compared to the innisfree stores in Busan, Daegu and Seoul so don't bother buying from them. There really isn't much to see apart from the fact that it is rather close to the O?셲ulloc Tea Museum.TLDR: Not worth your time, Jeju is so beautiful go somewhere else!

The maze is closely located to Manjanggul cave.The entrance fee is KRW3,300. The entrance is fill of cute cats.The maze is constructed by high and neatly-trimmed bush walls.It is not too large.There is an observation decks/bridge. From here you can clearly see path.As we're running out of time, we use the map to solve the maze.It took us 8 min to ring the victory bell.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The island is beautiful, yet very cold especially in winter time. We aimed for halla rice and peanut ice cream. Just the shop near the port has peanut ice cream (not just putting nuts on that!). We used the sightseeing bus and by foot to travel around the island.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The hot springs have a good reputation and are very popular amongst Koreans. There is a large indoor area, separated of course for male and female, and then an outdoor area with 4 small pools the size of a hot tub and one larger lap pool which has cold spring water. Out of the 4 smaller pools 3 have hot water, 1 has cold water.The overall condition of the outdoor pools is quite shocking actually and I was surprised. In Korea almost everything is well maintained and in good condition, at these hot springs the paint coating came off at the pools, the pool furniture was old and falling apart, just very surprised to see it in this poor condition. It was busy nevertheless. There is a mix of couples and families, kids running around, people talking loudly, so it is not really serene and peaceful as a hot spring should be. The bathing experience was good, very relaxing, no doubt, but the overall experience was mediocre.

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Street markets are the same wherever you go, only the locality and design might change, so if you are looking for something unique this is not the place.I enjoy wandering through markets throughout the world, watching the locals go about their daily business and interact with each other. Also to see what the local delicacies are like.There are several entrances, with the street food stalls being close to entrances 1 and 2.

Stone park is a must see one. It has big outdoor. There are a lot of big stone shapes. This park is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park and Eco land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!

Sorry, guys if i am a bit skeptical for this kind of attraction.  For me, and perhaps for some others, it is just an optical illusion.  No surprise on that....lol.I watched closely the power lines running alongside the street and the top of the trees alignment you might be able to see that the street is actually going down and not up, giving an impression that the bottle is rolling upwards....  As the old saying states,   the law of gravity still applies everywhere on earth  .  It was quite crowded when i was there, and needed to be a bit careful when people were trying to walk backwards whilst buses and cars were trying to pass by on that narrow street.  There are few food stalls as well.

Since I am fan of Kitty White, I visited this place. Love the place so much, Kitty so cuteeee... But could be nicer if we can see the bathroom of Hello Kitty house (not only peek the picture from the door). Unfortunately the staffs not so helpful. There were only two staffs in entrance (one in ticket booth one who check the ticket). After I finished all, I went to front to ask what bus I should take to go back to Seogwipo. The one who were checking ticket asked me to ask the ticket booth girl, so I queued about 5 minutes. Then when I asked the ticket booth girl, she called the ticket checker girl to tell me the what bus should I take. All she said was   Go to across, bus number I don't know.   Hufffttttt!!!!

Really....it is just another rock with a legend.  It seems that everyone turns into rock while waiting for someone....story line is always the same.  If you are a big fan of Korean drama - Daejeonggeum, then this is the place for you.  A lot of tourist stops here....maybe becos it has no admissions fees.  Try and come early in the morning as the tour buses start coming in late morning.

Really great to see and well maintained. Wonderful visit. Went on a rainy day and it was still a pleasant experience. The bus to the cave is very slow and infrequent so you either have to walk or take an expensive taxi which is inconvenient, but otherwise very good

quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.

Pretty unique place, well worth to visit! Dress up well as it doesn't seem chilling down there at first, but if you walk until the very end, then back, it may take an hour. Also, getting there not that easy:take #701 from jeju city intercity bus termal to the bus stop named   Entrance to the Manjanggul Lava Tubes  . This is quite far from the entrace though, and the bus #990 supposed to go there is extremely rare, so not much chance except to take a taxi (it should not cost more than 3000 won/ride).

Pretty much everything in Jeju is available here. Within the city, easily accessible via car, taxi, bus. There's the traditional market, seafood market, fruits & veggies, night market (6pm onwards). However the zones seem kinda grey cos clothes shop can be next to fish shop, snack shop next to shoe shop, you get the picture. We bought some dried seafood, snacks, fruits. Then popped over to the underground mall. Good place for those wanting to shop and see everything in 1 spot.

Our tour guide built up anticipation of this phenomenon hours before we arrived at the site, and by then, our entire bus load of tourists were completely curious as to what we would experience.It was all over in less than a minute, but still interesting to see how a natural illusion could occur if the conditions are right.It's not worth making the effort just to see this short stretch of road, but if you happen to be in the vicinity, by all means see if the illusion works on you!

Our route would allow us to pass by the mysterious road. We stopped, and you can see the road is going uphill. Our bus driver turned off the engine, and slowly, the bus started moving by itself, as if being pulled by gravity.

Our plans to visit Hallasan were foiled by a typhoon the night before (we luckily still got to go, though), and we were all excited to do a nice hike. We came here probably 2 or 3 hours before the park closed (we did some other sightseeing instead of Hallasan, this happened to be close by), and the admission was free because the typhoon had caused some damage. Anyways, because of the typhoon and the time of day, the park wasn't very busy. It felt like we had the walking paths to ourselves most of the time (we chose one of the shorter routes because we didn't want to run out of time). It was a nice, easy, relaxing walk. It was also dead quiet except for the occasional group of ladies walking by with music playing on their phone's speaker. Oh and the crows going off every now and then, but that was kind of amusing since their call is funny to me (and different from North American crows). A good alternative if you can't go up some of the steeper stairs and stuff like in Hallasan. We got plenty of beautiful photos because the typhoon the night before gave all the woods a nice, moody atmosphere. If you like going for walks in the woods (even though these are all wooden paths), just being outdoors enjoying the fresh air, and you have enough time, this is worth a visit. If you are short on time and can only do one park or something, then make sure you try to at least go to Hallasan. I would definitely recommend this park over Hallasan though if you have any mobility issues, because the wooden paths are very easy to walk on and there doesn't seem to be a lot of uphill/stairs.

Our kids (7&10) enjoyed the rock climbing, surf and sand...not to mention the modestly price ferry ride.  We attempted to rent a motorized vehicle but there were no rentals for four people...maximum people limit per vehicle was two and one of us did not have a driver's license...so we took the modestly priced bus trip.  Note that a home-country drivers license will not work.  once we figured out the system (no English speakers found on the island of Jeju.), it worked to see most of the island.  The peanut ice cream was all variations of soft-serve...low quality ice cream.  There were enough snack shops for coffee or short orders.  Okay for a day trip.

on the way it seems that the road is upward - the bus moving on  on its own without the gas but upon reaching a certain point it did stop & looking back to where you've been, it seems that the road is leveled.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Of all the places we visited in Jeju via our taxi tour, this is what I would rank as #1 (see  http://www.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=1121529), with Sunrise Peak as #2.  This is a Buddhist temple set in a vast very pretty land.  Interesting Buddha statues ? very exotic particularly for those who have never been to a Buddhist temple.  Our taxi guide politely asked, I believe a caretaker, to see if we can actually go inside the temple.  We were allowed.  I?m not sure if it was early or this is not a traditional tourist place, since we only saw very few people (as compared to the other temple in Busan packed with too many people.)  Felt a little bit odd being a tourist spectator in a house of worship, but glad we did.  The landscaping and statutes in the area were very interesting.  So there's more to see other than the temple itself. I would recommend this place for sure.  Would go back again if have the chance.  Hopefully with less rain this time.  Free to visit.

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

Needs to be in a vehicle to enjoy this amazing experience, though we also pour water on the road to see how it flow   uphill  . Noticed local bus tour also pass through this attraction, but I'm not sure if they will allow the passengers to get off the bus and do the experiment.

Near the Osulloc Tea Museum, the Innisfree Jeju House has a cafe and a store. The selection isn't great, and they don't give you free samples, though you could score some Jeju only products. Admittedly, there weren't at lot of these products though. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store, so you can do it on your own), it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.I like Innisfree products, so I didn't stopping by, but if you're not into that or soap making, you may want to give it a miss.

Mysterious Road is amazing place where the buses, cars and event water are automatically running up the hill. I tried to take a wide round walk to study for the landscape, terrain to see if there is any eye cheating but I cound not find one. Anybody know the reason why?

mysterious and unique road!! even a bus can climb itself without start the engine! they have remark the start and end of the mysterious road. enjoy the experiance by stay in your can while your car climb the hill without its engine.. seeing, feel it to believe it by yourself!

My family was holiday in Jeju on 12 Dec 2011.  One of the tourists spots where we visited is the Mysterious road.  It really amazed us after we had seen in our own eyes and sitting in the car.  The driver took us to place near to our our hotel Ocean Suite Hotel.  He then switched off the engine of the car and of course, there is a spot where there is a sign show   start here  .  There it goes the moment he let off his brake, 5 of us including the driver were siting in the car and the car just move up the a slight steep slove (about 5 degrees) and the distance it travelled is about 50m.  After that he U turn and took us to the same spot where we can witnessed other cars, including buses and coaches also did the same thing.  What a wonderful and awesome sight I have seen.  So when you are in Jeju, please do not miss this.

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Markets have always been interesting to me. They show so much about how the locals eat, shop, trade and work. Dongmun Market is pretty laidback. The folks there are not pushy. It's hardly touristy but still attracts a fair number of tourists. You mainly get to see seafood, fruits and vegetables as you explore the many lanes at the market. Aside from the market itself, the businesses nearby are also colourful and pix-worthy.For me, the highlight of the visit is lunch at one of the several restaurants within a zone at the market. They specialise in seafood, of course, and offer sets (featuring sashimi, a grilled fish, fish stew and banchan) that are value for money.Also don't miss some snack stalls there. My favourite is operated by an old lady (probably in her 70s)  who makes hatteok, sort of a pancake filled with cinnamon sugar, on the spot. It's a sweet, hot treat.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.
Love this beach, we went in winter, wind very strong and cold, most of them hide inside the mini bus but few of us walk around, taking photos, see the raw seaweed near the stone

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)
It's very relaxing and convenient to take the shuttle bus to see various areas of the island. Tourists could hop on and hop off at each stops. Alternatively, there are bicycles available for renting.

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It?s a very big place.. there are a cave, garden, mang kind of birds, trees ans flowers.. i think it is a good place to visit in jeju.. you can see many things here.. but it is difficult to find a bus to here and the bus is not ontime..

It?s a beautiful waterfall, and rare since it seems to be the only one in Asia that falls directly into the ocean. It has easy access if you?re coming from Jeju-si. Just take the 780 bus to Dongman Rotary station, and you?ll see a brown sign pointing you in the right direction.  The bus was pretty fast as it only took about 75 minutes to get there.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.
