We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

We went here on our way to south jeju.It was a nice place where we can see the various art forms possible with glass.A sculpture of a horse made with glass was displayed, which was really looking cool...

We visited these as part of our guided tour and were impressed by the surrounding scenery and location. It's a wonderful way to see Jeju at its best, and the rocks are quite impressive. It doesn't take as long to see as you would think, but still worth an hour or so.

We visited the cave on the way back to Udo (very easy to do both of these in one day. Very interesting and well explained. It would probably be a good idea to bring a jacket because the temperature in the cave is significantly lower than on the outside. However, it's still really cool to see and think about the implications of the event that made the cave in the overall of Jeju. Very good for kids although it can be a bit slippery inside too.

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.

We rent a bicycle and just cycling along the sea coast. It's very windy and we even spotted the hanyeo picking up the seaweed! If you visit the island at the right timing. U can see lots of canola flower! We saw partial here and there still very pretty. If you are being lazy, you can just rent the ATV bike (which most of the people do so). If you plan to have lunch there. Give yourself 4-5 hours to explore this island (take photo, had an ice cream etc etc). Note: we didn't walk all the way up to light house as it is already mid noon and we can see something similar @ seopjikoji so we let go this one :)

We paid for the VIP seats, KW10,000 more than the standard seats. When we entered, noticed that VIP seats were in red right in the centre of stage, while standard seats were on both left n right sides of the VIP seats. Worth paying the extra to be at the centre. They also choose guest from the VIP seats for participation on the stage. Show was hilarious, enjoyed by both young and old. Even my 4 year old child was laughing all the way to the end. It lasted 100 mins, try to catch evening show instead of night show during winter a the hall would be freezing at night.If you have not seen this, include this show in either Jeju or Seoul.

We originally did not schedule this visit as we have already seen Mulu Caves in Sarawak-East Malaysia.  But our hotel (TGG) told us that this is a very different cave (lava tubes).   The cost is not high at KRW2,000 and if you are already going to Seongsan Ilchbong, might as well make a visit.  We did not regret the visit.  It is really interesting to see how the lava flowing from Mt. Halla makes its way underground and forming the cave.  It is huge so you can see the magnitude of the lava flow.  Be sure to wear sturdy shoes as the ground is rather rocky and wet and you will need to walk carefully so that you won't fall.  I am amazed on how some ladies worn high heels!  It is also dim and cool so you must bring a jacket with you.  It is also a UNESCO site so definitely worth visiting.

We heard about the dragon head rock and we were brought there by our tour guide. Our guide warned us to use   a lot of imagination   when we see the rock otherwise we will not be able to see the   dragon  . Well she was right about that. Lots of tour agencies bring their groups there to see the rock and there are lots of little restaurants all the way along the walkway to entice the tourists. After a short walk from the carpark, there is a steep staircase you have to walk down to, in order to get to the spot to see the dragon head from the side. Even so, you're pretty far from the dragon head rock. And to me, it's clearly just a natural process where the rock gets eroded into a certain shape and in this case it's going there for this one rock only... which I wouldn't have if I were on a free and easy route.

We have never seen or heard of anything like this before. Probably its the only one in the world. The 1km walk each way, was full of facts about lava formations.We had wonderful time, and just loved what we saw & learned.

We had no plans to see this, but on our way to the airport, we stumbled upon it. Put the car in neutral and slowly rolled   up hill  . We laughed for the 15 second experience and went on our way. Certainly not worth going out of the way to get there.

We drove there and parking is free. The whole experience will take about less than 2hours? About 45mins to walk all the way inside to the end of the cave and another 45mins out. So remember to empty your bladder before entering. There is no loo inside the cave.The cave is cold. About 15 degree celcius? Luckily there is no wind. The ground is made up of rocky bits, and the place is constantly damped and slippery. So wear a light jacket and confortable shoes.Although there are lights in the cave, they are pretty dimmed. Not brightly lit. We used the torchlight function in our phones to further assist us to see the rocky ground. It is not unusual to carry a small portable torchlight if you want. Im not a person who likes cave, but well.. it is an experience i guess.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We decided to include this in our tour after feeling a bit tired from all the hiking up mountains and paths. It's an easy couple of hours, especially if you have kids, whom seemed to be entertained with every variation of dressed up bear. There is also an extensive gift shop, with, you've guessed it, lots of bears and cuddlies. The prices aren't exactly cheap, but the quality seemed good. It's a good way to slow the pace down if you are in need of a rest.. Nice afternoon out.

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

We came to this village with our hired taxi driver. The driver had apparently informed the staff in this village in advance, because a Chinese-speaking woman came out to greet us just as we approached the village. The woman spent the next ten minutes bringing us to different places around the village and giving a brief introduction. We learnt a bit from her about their traditional way of living and even saw a live black pig in captivity. She then brought us to a room saying we could take a rest and had a sip of their tea since the weather was warm. For the next 20 minutes, she tried to persuade us to buy the pills which she claimed to be made from bones of Jeju horses and a bottle of tea, costing a total of 190,000 Korean won. When we said we weren't keen, she was flabbergasted and said everyone who came before us bought items from here. We still refused to buy and returned to our taxi. She followed us to our taxi and spoke in Korean to the taxi driver. Didn't know what she was saying but she might be complaining. She then asked us what could we have bought by not spending 190,000 Korean won here. I replied: a lot of things. We didn't like her tone and told the driver to drive off. It was a waste of our time coming here. We didn't have any time to wander around the village by ourselves and hence no photos. It seemed the main purpose was to sell those items to us.

We came here early in the morning (5:30am) and began the hike up. It seems to be free admission before sunrise. Unfortunately, we did not see the sun rising from the ocean perhaps it was because of the fog. The sky just became brighter and brighter. We just took some photos and descended. On the way down, the sun finally made its appearance. Beautiful! There is also a women divers place below close to the coast. Cafes like Paris Baguette, isaac toast and dunkin' donuts are just nearby the parking lot.
was there in March, temp in the cave is alot colder than outside. not much to see as the walkway is poorly light.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Walking the Dongmun Market is an experience that a visitor should not miss.  The local market has variety of daily food of the islanders.  Seeing the fresh fishes, seafoods, and other meats displayed in various forms for consumption was an eye opener.  We would love to buy and try some of the food if the merchant package them in ready-to-eat size.  On this entrepreneurs way, the Japanese market achieve high mark in its idea.  Visitors would love to try local food even to pay at a premium.

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

Today me and other guest are very lucky that the hostel owners very kind and friendly gave us a ride back to hostel, on the way back, he just de route to show us this place which near to love land, it's just a very short distance which the road seems like is going up slop, but, when the car put on free gear at the starting point, the car is actually keep moving on downhill. Visitors having fun by placing drinking water bottles on the road and let the bottle roll on its own. Personally, nothing very special, its just kind of illusions optic.

Tip: when you are on that road uphill, please put the car into NEUTRAL gear & switch OFF your engine. That's the only way to test. You will then see that the car is indeed going uphill when gravity tells you that you should be descending downhill on that slope.Having the engine on would offset the effect.Try it.

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This place toally blew me away with the beautiful rock erosions.  I never expected that this would be the highlight of my trip to Jeju.  I could see the clarity of the blue green water up close.  Assured that the seawater was so clean without any fishy smell, we even ventured to sample the live seashells.  What an unforgettable experience we had, dining on the rocks with the gentle waves lapping in front of us.

This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them.  The bears here are displayed as various characters and in a variety of situations.  They're cute and can be interesting, but if you're not really into this kind of thing then you'd be bored.  I'm sure children would enjoy it.  For myself, I enjoyed it but I've seen it once and wouldn't go back.

This place is a definite must see on my list. The market is huge and includes shops that sell about everything you can imagine (clothes, kitchen appliances, souvenirs, meat, fish, ice cream, pancakes, desserts, traditional street food, oranges, oranges and more oranges). The fruit is expensive, but that's normal for Korea. The street food is cheap and absolutely delicious. It is definitely a good way to kill a couple hours and try some of Jeju's famous treats.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This maze is fun and quite simple. And from what I've observed, it really tests a couple's relationship strength. ALong the way I see couples arguing on which way to go, I see couples helping each other out. It was a fun experience. Walk there from Manjanggul to get a 500won discount!

This market was near our hotel so we came by here a few times in the evenings (and a couple times in the day time). Mostly because we were trying to find this fried chicken restaurant that never seemed to be open and we kept going back to try to find it. Don't come here expecting a night market extravaganza like other parts of Asia. This is more strictly a   market   market, though there are lots of restaurants that have take-out. There are a few street food stalls, so you can get your fix in a couple spots. Definitely make sure you try the orange juice from one of the sellers here, Jeju has amazing oranges (and tangerines). There are some souvenir type places here, but nothing special. We bought some of the chocolates because they were dirt cheap and wanted to try them, but when we got home and ate them they were just waxy and artificial tatsing (you'll see which chocolates I mean when you get there. EVERY souvenir seller has them. Even in the airport). We bought some dried mandarins from the same vendor, and they were pretty good. We also bought a bunch of oranges to bring around with us as snacks while we were driving. If you've been to markets in Asia before, this will be nothing special. But if you're looking for something to do, it's probably worth visit - wouldn't go out of my way for it though.

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is an underground shopping center which is just around the corner of Orange Tree  Cafe & Hotel. This is just the normal shopping center which you would see in most of the subways thru out Seoul, however, the good thing about this underground shopping mall is that each of the exits leads to different streets which has more shops....eg. Uniqlo, ABC Mart, Daiso, and also various cafes.....and also to the Dongmun Market and also to the Black Pork Street.

This is an easy walk from the centre of Jeju city. It'a one of the main attractions along the seafront walkway which goes all the way from the port to the airport. You often see the famous Jeju ladies, dressed in their black wetsuits, diving for pearls without breathing equipment.

This is a weak but personal reason to visit this bridge, that is to say, it featured in the first Korean Drama series I ever watched. To put it in a nutshell, the guy followed the girl all the way to Jeju-do in order to convince her he was the one for her. The bridge scene featured just after they landed on the island, so it was just nice to see it in person as part of our stay here. There's not much more to say - I guess other people would have other reasons to visit. As a bonus we spotted women divers going out in their gear so that was some cultural aspect to the visit.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a neat little place to enjoy the ocean breeze and see a rocky area.You don't need much time here; about 15 minutes is adequate. Wear comfortable shoes as the surface is uneven. I'm sure you will enjoy he scenery here... You can combine it with a walk along the coast into town.  I stumbled across a nice bridge and gazebo area along the way, as I headed towards the downtown market.

This is a fun place to visit. I wouldnt get out of my way to see it, but if you are in Jungmun and have an hour, its a fun place to see. The part I liked best are the Teddy Bears in   historical situations  . Like the first moon landing,  the discovery of the Terracotta Army, the fall of the Wall in Berlin etc.

This folk village which has a collection of 600 years old thatched roof houses built using the volcanic basalt rocks and passed on from one generation to another, showcases the unique culture of Jeju Island. The stone statue of Harubang called the grandfather of Jeju and worshipped as the protector of this island can be seen in front of almost all the huts.This village is still inhabited by the locals and one can see them practicing their traditional rituals including rearing of the Black Pigs.By the way ,Jeju is famous for its Black Pork dishes.There are also sites for holding special rituals like praying God for good luck and health, place where breast feeding women pray for lack of milk etc.Our Guide cum Driver Mr Kim Nam Joon (+82-10-4616-6650) not only took us around the village but also ensured we had a good time.

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

This amazing landscape is a must place to go when you visit Jeju. You have to climb up to see the creater and do not worries, just prepare you leg for a stairs (a lot of stairs hahaha). You better wear a comfortable shoes. when i came was sunny, temperature around 18C but the wind was strong, it makes my hair messy & runny nose (prepare face masker will help). The scenery along the way was refreshing & amazing, you will not disapointed.
There is an hour long boat tour that shows you many of the sights, but was the best way to see these falls and get pictures for these Hallasan weary feet.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.

There are 3 levels for the visitors to try. The first one is the easiest before you are engaged in a more challenging maze. It is fun if you have 2 groups of children/ people visiting this place. Not only that they can help their group members to find their way, the competition between the 2 groups makes it more exciting. Finally, the 3rd maze is the most difficult but you will have no problem. There is a clue/ help (you will see, it is a secret here) when you really need it. I think, the children managed all 3 maze puzzles in 1 hour.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The temperature drops dramatically after you descend 15 stairs into the cave entrance.  There was a cloud that had formed at the entrance due to the humidity which was really cool to see.  Walked about a km to the end where there is a lava column - a frozen in time dripping of lava from above.  Fascinating walk, lots of people (some in heels which I wouldn't recommend).  Really beautiful way to spend an hour or so.  Especially when it is super hot and humid outdoors!

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The silvery field of   grass   or   weed   is amazing if you come at the right season. Definitely a great photo taking opportunity. You can also catch the Halla mountain in the backdrop. Romantic and almost magical if not for the crowd. The place is getting more popular as words spread.The crater itself is not much to see but could be interesting if the leaves turn red or yellow. Visited here while on the way to the Manjanggul Cave

The scenery at Sangumburi Crater is probably the most breathtaking I've ever seen. The path up to the crater was picturesquely beautiful. The eoksae (듭ⓒ, flamegrass) swaying in the breeze... The place is just like heaven.

The route of the tunnel is 1km one way, and then the same way back.  Its an interesting environment - dark and very cool.  Its quite interesting to see how the lava flow carved this tunnel and the size of it.  Its definitely something that is memorable and unusual.

The place is very organised with well created pathways to see the rock formations. However, the place is really quite crowded and it is hard to take photos because of the amount of crowd there. Everyone was just walking along the path and there isn't much space to move around. That being said, it is still quite worth it to pay it a visit.

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The Manjang Cave was one of the   must-dos   in my itinerary. I can only say it was somewhat a disappointment. It was not quite as spectacular as I have thought it would be. I was with my mum and dad both 60. My mum did not take the walk well and headed back halfway. My dad stayed behind to do some photo-taking, Here's the bottomline:- If you have never ever been in a lava cave before - go for it!- If you are traveling with young children / older folks / people with bad knees and weak ankles - give this a miss. The initial flight of stairs can be quite a walk. The floor of the cave can be wet and uneven- If you have been to lava caves before and if you do not have a mental benchmark - go for it if you have time- If you have seen the most wondrous lava caves and already formed expectations - skip it... more than likely this might underperform

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The Jeju Mysterious Road, also known as Dokkaebi Road, lies on a hill at the foot of a mountain, and connects two major highways on Jejudo Island. It has earned its name, as objects and liquid appear to roll and flow up the hill instead of down, when, in fact, such image of gravity defiance is an optical illusion rendered by the seemingly high surroundings.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The crater itself is nothing to crow about. As they say, see one see all. However the area around the crater is fantastic. A few nice pathways up to the crater sight. Not much colour although it is autumn but fresh air and the waving pampas grass made our day.

The building looks a bit old. There re space for parking. Inside the castle, there's hello kitty tree at the middle for photo shooting. When you walk inside, there're few theme of hello kitty for photo shooting and walk up the stair to the 2nd floor you will see a few rooms theme of hello kitty including the kitty cafe which sell drinks,Desserts and cakes. The restroom also there. The price is not high. The restaurant decorated in cute seating with hello kitty design. On the way back on ground floor you need to pass the souvenir shop. The price is not cheap for stuffs but if you are hello kitty fan it may worth.

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans

Taking a quick ferry ride will bring you to a breathtaking place called Udo Island. Rocky coasts, beautiful beaches, and crystal clear waters are what you will find on this little farming and fishing island. I decided to rent a bike on my trip and wander around the coastline. In my opinion, it was the best way to see the island. Amazing photo opportunities and tons of places to get some fresh seafood along the way. The clear and shallow water is great for children to play in. Tons of little tidal pools as well. Biking allowed you to be outside and experience the people and the culture of the island. It is probably not a place for people that do not enjoy the outdoors or those that are afraid of a little bit of exercise!
Take the afternoon and walk around this beautiful park and zoo. All different kind of plants, trees, flowers, and animals, this park is way better than it seems. Don't miss it!

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Spend a couple hours here walking through the village and seeing traditional Korean way of life.  There isn?t much interaction with anything outside of the performance they have, which is 2-3 times a day and with the vendors.  They do offer horse back riding here and you can also have photos taken in a hanbok.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.

Seongeup Folk Village of Jeju Island is the place that the past resident live in. The tour guide told us this place can keep well mostly because of the government. The government funds the residents to live here, let them to keep the old building and the culture well. When there have visitor like us, the resident will become a tour guide or shop assistant. It is a good way to spread the culture. Because the residents must know more about the culture than other tour guides. They will show the old tools and teach you how to use it, it is funny and you must be proud of their wisdom.If you like to watch the episode that comes from Korea. You must go here, because most of the building had appeared in the episode, such as ?Dae Janggeum?, if you are lucky, you will see the actor here.

Seems the name of the road has some psychological effect on the tourists. Is it mystery or reality? Hope anyone who is a land surveyor can throw some light on this with the appropriate surveying equipment or we need a long specially made spirit level to verify the inclination of the road. Without it, the so-called 'mysterious' is purely perception. By the way, there is a grave-yard nearby which adds to its spookiness.

Put your rented car on neutral going   uphill   and experience it. Mysterious probably because for most it?s a baffling experience having your car in neutral but going uphill, backwards or forward ? hands off the wheel and feet off that pedal. The place is on the way to Jusangjeolli by way of the Mount Halla route from Jeju town. 5-10 minutes (no crowd here) and you have covered one of the ?touristy? sites in Jeju. A woman attempted to see what would happen with a plastic water bottle placed on the road, nothing did.  Why would any vehicle with so much metals built into it got pulled but not a plastic bottle? Go figure. I have encountered a similar experience at a site in Saudi Arabia near Madinah which has a longer stretch for that ?mysterious? experience.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

overrated spot with overcrowded visitors and cars trying to test out the slope. but in fact it is just some form of landscape optical illusion. So unless you are popping by the sex museum too, there's no point going all the way to see this small stretch of road.

Our family really enjoyed this walk.? It was nice to see the lighthouse and islands around this area.? And when we were there, the brushes were full of beautiful spiders and webs.? Of course, they were far enough away to not bother you.? It was really cool to see.

Our children really wanted to spend time on the ocean. This was a great introduction to the power of the sea. Big waves. Rocky coast. Perfect for sea shell collecting, sand castle building, and glimpses of aquatic life. We managed to watch the Haenyo divers bobbing their way across Jungmun Beach and later walked the length of the beach to see their catch.
On the way to the mountain, you can see some horses, the kind that can only be raised in the mountain. There is some snow but not enough yet.

Not spectacular but unusual that it flows into the sea. You can walk across the rocks to get really close and many did for pictures. Be careful though. Some women selling freshly cut abalone, sea cucumber, snails - raw! Just 200m away from the base of the fall. Ticket is affordable at 2000 won even for foreigner which is the good part about most of the sights unlike some countries which cost double or more for foreigners.Don't see any restaurant so drive into the city seogwipo food street for plenty of choices.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.
Not much to see, looked a little bit worn out to me. Any way its nice if you have extra time on your hands
Not a must visit, though a spot of fun if you have 15 minutes free as your vehicle seemingly rolls its way 'up' a hill.

No point come to this fall, not even if you are nearby. Not worth your time. I walked all the way in just to find out that The waterfall is so small. I don?t see how they made an attraction out of this.

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.

My biggest regret, if there was one for Jeju, would be to miss this attraction. The crater may not seem much to some but this site was truly amazing. The natural occurrence was a sight to behold. It may be hard for some to imagine the significance of this crater but for me, I could relate to it and blessed to witness it. A not to be missed attraction albeit out of the way. The pampas grass fields were so scenic during fall that one just cannot miss this picture taking opportunity. The were so well grown here.
museum, full of teddy bears, so nice. we seem so much of different types of teddy bears with different way of presenting, cute way, rock way, lovely way and so and soooo...

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and it is a designated as a natural monument.Not an easy walk as lots of even walkway,  slippery and dark. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surrounding and was cooling as you walk. You will be able to see the trace of the lava that flow through the cave. I saw some who rush all their way in and out.With young children do note of their safety, for older people who having legs problem do not try. Partly, you need to walk down the stairs which is not easy and when you finished you need to walk up again.We really enjoyed the nature of this cave.
Lots of shops, but I wouldn't go out of your way to see this.  I just happened to be in the area.  Wouldn't be very nice shopping if it was crowded either.

Located an easy walk from the Seogwipo Harbor, these waterfalls and surrounding area are quite pretty, and certainly worth the easy, pleasant walk to see them. It was only 2,000 won to enter the are, and about a 5 minute walk to the actural waterfall. As someone who loves swimming in natural water, I was a little disappointed, because you can't really swim here. It was quite crowded (when I went in early August), so all my photos are full of other people. It wasn't necessarily a beautiful nature experience, so in that way a bit underwhelming, but again, worth a look.

Let's first get this out of the way: If you're not a teddy bear fan, if you're an over-serious person, or basically, if you had a fun-less childhood, don't bother visiting this place. Because then it would be pretty much a tourist ripoff kind of place, with nothing really worth seeing.But, if you do like bears, and regardless of how cheesy or a ripoff this place can be, you just want to have some fun, then by all means, check it out!Admittedly, I quite like teddy bears myself, and right from the moment I stepped in, I was constantly tickled by all the teddy bears modeled in the form of famous people, famous artworks, and even historical events. It can be sometimes strange to see the head of a bear in the place of what should've been a human one, but toss the strangeness aside and you'll realize there is so much to see and chuckle over. Having teddy bears in place of humans in the exhibits add a touch of innocent cuteness to everything.Do note that there's both an indoor and outdoor exhibit, so if you're on a schedule yet really want to see everything, make sure you plan your time well!

Just another market but in a different city. Similar in most ways.However, a distinct difference here is the huge amount of Jeju oranges (tangerines) on sale. Not just here but in other markets in Jeju too.Also it is common to see roadside trucks & makeshift stalls selling oranges - everywhere.Jeju is well known for its oranges , probably it's the season now. But they aren't exactly cheap despite the abundance of supply.We went to a nice Tangerine Orchard Farm right here in Jeju, where we paid 5,000?? admission fee per pax. And one can eat as much oranges as you want for unlimited time while at the Orchard.After which, every pax is entitled to pick/bring back 1kg free. Great experience & deal.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

Jungmun Daepo is the spot where the iconic columnar joint rock formations can be seen. There?s not much to do here, except take a few pictures from a distance, but it?s worth seeing if you?re in the area anyway. I can?t say much about it because there?s not much to say. except that you should allot about 15 minutes in total (including the time to get in an out).Further down the coast is Jungmun beach. I went here in March, so there wasn?t much to do when it?s 10 degrees Celsius. I imagine on a hot day it would be fun to swim here. The beach is pretty ? sand is slightly coarse but clean and lovely since it?s golden in color. The slope from the parking area/restaurants to the beach is pretty steep. I don?t know if it?s safe for people with mobility issues.One downer: I didn?t like the seafood restaurants playing loud, outdated music when we got there ? I think it would be a pain to eat here if you have to listen to that. Someone has to tell the tourism board about this.Where: Seogwipo west coast

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

It's not hot or cold and the water is warm. It's gorgeous, you can really go far in the water and it's not deep and you can see all the way to the bottom. I'm coming back tomorrow for another swim. Worth the visit!

It's good place for experience the local community which they will arrange the local guide whom live tin the village to give you the informations and details about the village including the history and culture. There's the translator for the local people since they are hardly speak other language besides Korean. They will explain the way they hand the wooden stick at the gate. The meaning of the stone statue. They will have to room the tell us their history and story. They will have a village walk so everyone can see and experiences their village including photo shooting. They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. The Omecha is sticky so need to mix with water for drinking and contain a lot of vitamins. The local guide will try to up sales their local products after tour such as Omecha and horse bone. They make the bone into small pills and they said its good for those whom need calcium or need recovery from injury and also good for the growth of young kid. They also sell dried squids which already mix with sauce before dried it. It's a good experience as the village is very unique. The house is only one floor and low ceiling since Jeju is very windy. The wall also made with the lava stone from the hallasan mountain.Avoid to go during rainy day even they provide the umbrella during the walk but it's not convenience at all.
It's an unusual formation, I'll give it that, but really I don't see why it's a tourist attraction. It's something I planned on missing, but stumbled upon anyway.

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. However, the grass/plant at the maze seem not well taken care as you can see a lot of holes along the plant fences of the maze.

It's a large building but light on exhibits, or maybe it just seems that way with so much open space. Several historical and current type aircraft, mostly military, and several interactive exhibits for kids. Nice digital movies and a flight simulator section for kids and adults!
It's a bit dark here and u hardly can see your way, so u need to be careful when u go inside. Every lava section is quite different that makes it quite special and memorable.

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

It worth a look just to see the beautiful coastline of the Island.Most of the rocks come in various heights and sizes shaped like hexagons and if you look at certain angles, they can take on various animals etc.The black lava colour offsets against the outstanding sea and coastline.These cliffs are very similar to the Giants Causeway in Ireland with a pancake rock system but on a much smaller scale.It was crowded the day were there and we assume it is the same most days in the summer months. So a lot of people were snaking along this narrow path around the cliffs and we needed to wait our turn to see over the barriers.There are a few stallholders near the carpark (fee charged) selling fruit, souvenirs and the local home made confectionary similar to nougat.On the way out you can go to a park with some gardens and perhaps a museum type building.The hours vary seasonally however it is the standard KRW 2,000 entry fee for most monuments around the Island.Place it on your ?must see? places to visit here just for the dramatic coastline and on a rough day you may get some blow hole situations with the force of the water.Enjoy your visit!

It was really hot when we arrived so we did not go up the summit but explored the surrounding. You could walk to the left where you will come to several flights of steps leading down to the beach where the haenyeo or women free divers will perform their skills. If you do not fancy walking all the way down, just continue left as you will come to a cliff overseeing the Udo island. Another go to place in jeju. Understand that this island is form from volcanic eruptions much like jeju is as well. There are also lots of photo opportunities at the foot of the 180m+ mountain(?). Of course the usual F&B outlets are here as well. We also see some signage for horse riding but did not explore.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was just amazing. Though the path way is well maintained but  it might be tough for some foreigners because of its slope but for Koreans it seems to be an easy task. But once you go uphill it looks so beautiful, not to be described in words rather to be felt by heart. As usual in Korea, I saw that every traveler keep the way neat and clean from waste food materials and carrying poly bags.

It was cool to see the lava patterns, but I don't think one needs to go beyond 70 meters.  It is dark and the ground is not level in the cave, so my caution to you is to watch your step.  A lady from my tour group had sprained her ankle while we were in there.  It is easy to just look up and sideways, but if you don't want your trip marred with pain and discomfort, watch your step.  It is very interesting, informative, and very cool to see how this little island was formed.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was a so-so attraction, mainly because it was merely to see the rock from afar. No interesting mythological background to it either besides knowing that it was formed by volcanic activity. Also the place has way too many people than it can handle.

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? It depends. If you're the kind of person who couldn't be bothered with science, optical illusions and whatnot, you'd be better off checking out the snack shops nearby, observing the other tourists and their interesting behavior, or skipping this place altogether.However, if you've always been interested in physics and seemingly unexplainable phenomenons which you know are actually explainable, give yourself an hour or more to thoroughly check this place out. Photography lovers may also deem this place worth their time.The bottom line? If you're heading to another tourist attraction (e.g. Hallasan) and it's on the way, and you have time to spare, feel free to check this place out. Otherwise, don't bother.

It is the year of the golden dragon.  So it was great excitement for us to be on our way to visit this dragon head rock, which the guide said could be discerned by going further down the vantage point.On arrival, we did just that, but we have to put our imagination to the test.  But then again who has seen a dragon before.  So we took pictures and we moved off in less than 15 minutes!Comparing pictures, I thought the dragon head looks better at night.

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.

Interesting rock formation open for imagination. Otherwise the area has not much other sights. There is no ticket required, so you can see the popularity is not great. Anyway, nice forested area is good for a quiet walk.

I'm not usually impressed by holes in the ground, but this lava tube was a blast.  It's always cold, damp and a enjoyably creepy no matter how sunny it is above ground, and you will love it!  Plenty of great rock formations to see and a sense of what goblins might call home, but the main attraction walking in this huge tunnel that once screamed with magma.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.

If you go in the summer, be sure to take some water with you.  It's a 10-15 minute walk to  the falls and there's not much shade on the return route or actually at the falls.  Everyone tries to get as close as they can, which is fine, but there are several places to take beautiful pictures up on the platform/courtyard in front of the falls.  There are also two smaller falls that you don't see much unless you cross the bridge about halfway between the falls and the parking lot.

If you find yourself in Jeju (May to June preferably) Halla is something that must be done. As the island is so small you can see the mountain no matter where you are. It sits there calling to you to climb it and you should. It is not one the most difficult climbs I have ever had, the end was a bit bad because there had be a storm that had damaged parts of the path. It is absolutely picturesque especially for the colour changes you see. I would suggest going up the easy path and going down the easy path for those who have trouble managing such large mountains, but no matter which you choose just go. The canteen at the halfway point was only serving instant noodles, so bring your own grub to be safe. Also have your pickup scheduled accordingly as transportation on the bottom parts of certain paths are almost non-existant.

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites, this is not a place. If there were, we probably missed them. It?s a dark underground cave and very interesting to see the lava flows. You can see imprints of such flows on the actual ground you?re walking on. It?s a bit nippy, so if you are prone to being cold, may want to take a light sweater. There is no bathroom in the tunnel (which my son figured out trying to get out halfway in the tunnel/cave. He had to run back the way we came to find one.) It?s interesting. I just wished that there were more lights in the tunnels so one can appreciate it more. Uneven ground due to the lava flows, as expected. 2000W/$1.75 to get in, half for kids.If you've never been into one of these types of caves, you should.  If you have, maybe worth skipping.

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)
I was there to see the sunset, which was really amazing. The entry was closed but we went to the volcano anyway. I recommend going there after Udo island.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was hoping to see how magnificient the lava is in one of the widest lava tube before going into the Manjang Cave. It is quite disappointing to realise that the cave is not entirely illuminated. The lighting is minimal in the cave which made walking and lava observation really difficult. I was going with my mum of around 60 years old, it is really difficult for her to see clearly in the tunnel. And the fact that you have to walk for  ~1 km into the tunnel and then the same way back is not entiring pleasing. When I was walking down the tunnel, I always thought   there will be better illumination/rocks in the next turn  . However, it was quite disappointing that this happens only at the end of the tunnel where you saw an illuminated lava pillar. I would recommend you to go to other caves if you want to see the lava clearly.

I think we paid KRW2,000 per adult for entry. Walked the lava tube where the temperature dropped by a few degrees. It was raining that day, so it was a good hideout from the downpour. The walk was rather long but many things to see along the way. Remember to wear good waking shoes tho! It can get slippery.
