I like to explore super markets in different cities and different countries. It's a good way to see what people are eating. Sometime when I have the courage, I will tried some of the local food. Dongmun Market is one of the popular traditional markets in Jeju. It is big, clean and colourful. They sell all kinds of stuff, like fruit, fresh or dry (some in gift boxes), vegetables, dry mushrooms, herbs, spices and fresh or dry sea food. There are some restaurants ready to serve you. They even sell clothing there. We walked around and took photos, but no one came to pressure us to buy stuff, I like that.Happy Travelling!

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I heard from the owner of our guesthouse that this place isn?t always open because of the tides and weather, so if you have the chance to go, take it. It?s an amazing rock formation, but unlike the ones that you can see at a distance, like Oedolgae and the Jungmun Daepo, you can actually walk on it. That rocks. It took us a while ? was it an hour? ? to walk along the perimeter of this massive rock. The terrain is not smooth ? think of desert sands except that the undulating surface is made of rock instead of sand, so wear study shoes that won?t split because of the damp. It looks like a movie set -- for an alien planet. Really, I didn?t know such a place existed on earth.If I were taking someone around Jeju, I?d recommend this place and I would definitely come back so we can exclaim together.Where: Seogwipo west coast

I have been here several times, I really do enjoy it.  It is just an easy and fun way to spend a day. Lots of photo opportunities.I see they occasionally offer glass blowing classes. I have never done this, but it is on my list of things to try!ProTip: There are 2 stores filled with glass items for sale.  Some tacky, but mostly rather reasonably priced gift ideas. Plus, lots of  cool looking jewelry.

I did not see the point of this activity, was just in the area and decided to go have a look, was rather disappointing. The south side offers way cooler things like the waterfalls and the hexagonal rock formations. Difficult to get a decent picture as you can not get too close either.

I did not find it interesting. Well if clouds could form human faces, then I guess rocks could form dragon head. Not that it is related.Anyway, I really could not see a dragon and while it does look like a head, well, it's just that. A head.The only thing I find interesting is the selling of sea-shell foods and being able to eat by the sea on the rocks.For me, if I were to miss this, I guess I won't be miss anything?!

I decided to see two waterfalls down south at Seogwipo! Jeongbang fall is one going into the sea.A bit rocky if you would like to have a photo been taken in front of it as close as possible. There are always many people down there, be careful of your steps when taking a nice photo!I like the fall as it?s open to the sea!

I checked out Samseonghyeol not even knowing what it was exactly but went anyway because it was close to my hotel and it was some sort of a cultural sight.  Upon entering I learned it was basically three unimpressive holes where three demi-gods supposedly emerged from.  While the main sight isn?t impressive, it was still a nice park to walk around in during spring with the cherry blossoms.  It?s definitely not a sight worth going out of your way to see unless you?re interested in Korean legends.

I can't recommend Mr Jang highly enough! He is a fabulous guide who is very generous with his time and will tailor the day to suit the customer completely. If you are short on time, then this is absolutely the way to see Jeju. Mr Jang is friendly and easy-going and giving. If you're going to book a trip to see Jeju then go with Mr Jang!

I am sorry to say it but it was a boring place to visit. It would be interesting if we didn't have internet to get to know the world. By the way, my 8 year-old son was scared on the second floor to see all the torture instruments.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

Here is much more the beauty of the man made. The Bonsai garden made in an Arboretum which otherwise would've been an entirely sandy/rocky area. A good place to stroll completely away from the coastline. But given that Jeju's primary attractions are natural, spend time here only after seeing the real natural stunners.

Having seen quite a few craters around the world I쨈m always in to see another one. After some cruisin쨈 through the middle of Jeju island, we arrived at the crater. To be honest it was pretty disappointing. Since the crater hasn쨈t been active for a 1000 years, the shape is still there, but beside that it쨈s just a green valley. Technically it쨈s a crater of course, but not very impressive. If you쨈ve never seen one before, have a look, otherwise skip it.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Half science, half art. A museum dedicated to the formation of the igneous rocks in the area, tectonic plate movements, volcanic eruptions, formation of lava tubes, and various methods of making craters. Extremely interesting!Then rock art. Lots of interesting rocks from around the island, arranged in a way that makes them just so fascinating.Budget a couple of hours here for a leisurely walk through these sections. Add a couple more hours to see the historical village section (which we didn?t go into as we had seen these elsewhere already).

Had a lovely half-day here. The island is small, but has beautiful beaches, and a tall hill. We rented a scooter and had a slow day driving around, seeing the sights and having our snacks.I'd say it's a fairly good place to take it easy and go at your own place to be close to nature, but not so close that a cafe by the sea isn't too far away.Visited in early November.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

Great place to see local food sold by local people. There is plenty of Jeju products to choose from, as well as some farmers clothes, souvenirs, packed local food and of course a lot of oranges. When you hungry just eat some yummy ttoekpokki or mandoo. Cheap and great. Wear full shoes as floor is always wet from fish tanks.

Forget what it's called because I can't see a dragon head even when I tried to go around the different angles of the rock formation. However, this is a cool place to visit, to have a stroll on a lazy day since it's near the airport side of jeju. Probably around 5000 won (4 USD) to take a cab from the airport. There are small food stalls nearby, and dunkin donut too for some coffee. There is a nearby tourist center where you can ask if they can call a cab for you on your way back to your hotel or anywhere. They don't have booking fee which is excellent.

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..

Could not expect that it is so huge, need a lot of time to visit all the places. So many different plants, birds, even caves. The whole way is well organized, u just need to follow arrows to see everything step by step.There are several cultures and climates that you can see in bigger size than just normal botanical garden. Jeju culture is represented there a lot as well, so will not regret about missing local features.

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

Chose to visit this attraction because it is UNESCO world heritage site. I and my kids went into the cave, make our way to the lava column, took some photos, then u-turn to make our way out. Nothing to see unless you are a geological fan. It is OK, just another   for the experience   trip.

Best way is to go to the starting point (where it's steepest and most deceptive).  Make sure that there's no car or people behind you, put car in N, then release your brake too, to see you and your car going backwards UP the hill.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

At eye level, the short stretch looked like an upward sloping road, but it was actually a 3 degrees downhill slant. A bit out of the way, would not recommend making a trip there unless you're from Jeju-si enroute to Hallasan National Park. Many of the 'mysterious bottle rolling uphill' videos have been posted on youtube in case you want to see the mystery! The real attraction here was the huge iconic black pig family statue. It was detailed and incredible. LOL

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini   jungle   that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.
As the only show in Jeju (while in Seoul have 3 theatre) so always full. Interesting, Fun & a Must see Show.

As it is UNESCO heritage site which I had planned to pay a visit. The temperature starts to drop slightly when you walk further in. There's low dim light installed along the walk however, the pathway full of small rocks, uneven ground and wet with little bit slippery. So might not be suitable for elderly or young kids. Wear comfortable shoes although i did see some ladies wear heels which i wondered how are they going to survive for the 2km walk. Worth visit if you are interested to know more on lava tube formation.

Another UNESCO site in Jeju, hence there are always a lot of people there. But the climb is actually not that difficult, as the way is nicely paved with stairs, and there are quite a few resting places along the way. Took us around 1 hour to climb up to the peak and down again, but other than climbing up to the peak you can also go down to the seaside to see the diver's performance! Unfortunately, when we were there the sea was rough, so there was no performance.

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.

Always you can see from Korean drama movies of their house. Now you can see from your eyes. How the house split in few session. Such as, toilet and bath area. Quite interesting. Do not miss it.. must go and visit.
Although the area seems small, but quite interesting. It took 30 minutes for us to find out the way out and we had great fun with lots of pictures. Well recommended for visiting.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

After being in the cave, this is a good way to warm your body under the sun (well, at least during this season).So, it took 10 minutes to work out the right direction with the map, then we tried without the map and again it was ten minutes, then we left our 5 years old daughter to find the way out...still 10 minutes.I cannot define it challenging but fun for sure and super-rewarding to see your kid beaming with light every time she play the bell!Definitely worth combining cave and maze!

After all the hype about Manjanggul Cave, our expectations were high but were disappointed. Nothing spectacular to see unless you are interested in the stones that you will walk on in the dim, damp cave. You will come out the same way you went in.

After a 1.5-hour drive in the wee hours of a beautiful night, we finally got to the ticket office at 5:50am.... we didn't expect to see this crowd (well, we thought we alone were the crazy ones).... we embarked on the trek saying... not bad!!! After 5 minutes, if was like... pooff!!!! After  another 10 minutes, we were exhausted.. after yet another 5 minutes, it was a killer.... anyways, we made it to the peak at 6:18am and imagine our shock... there was a sea of people up there all set with their cameras...At precisely 6:28, it was there... flaming orange and rising at a speed unmatched (in sunrise). Spectacular!!! Fabulous!!!! Breath-taking!!! Start of a new day... a new way... new hopes... everything positive. It was so worth that strenuous climb.. If you are in Jeju, you gotta do this! Yes, the steps are high and tough, but so doable. We saw some people in ballerina shoes, with their fancy skirts and stockings.. keep the dressing for the yatch tours.. for this one, be ready for a mini hike.

Actually originally didn't think to visit this place. But coincidence have the chance, me and my travel partners was shock to see with our own eyes for the water and bottle both run to the upfront road which its was suppose to be opposite way....Make youself drop by to see this amazing effect while you around in Jeju. This place is just very nearby the Sex Museum which we didn't go but passby~

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

50 minutes show. Is definitely worth for money as both my kids enjoyed it. There are Chinese subtitle shown on the side screen, thus I am able to understand. Perhaps we are the only foreigner there. I presumed they know we understand Chinese thus provided Chinese subtitle? I sat in the middle of the stage, in another way sometime this may not be the best place as some show like throwing basketball I can see the back of the elephant only. The ticket price is reasonable. Adult 15k, youth 12k and child 10k. There is elephant ride 18k per pax which I do not pay for it. After the show can take photo with the elephant. There are literally stairs everywhere in Korea, for everything you want to see.  The stairs down the the falls were well worth the hike down then up...

Sunrise Peak is the nickname - I was sadly not able to see the sunrise because the weather, but it was still a beautiful lookout. The hike isn't too bad - I did have to catch my breath a few times because some parts are steep, but it was worth it. The path is lit, so you don't need a flashlight. Interesting hike down a rare lava tube. Remember to bring a jacket, as it can get pretty cold down there. Not the most beautiful save out there, but definitely worth the visit to see the various lava formations. Do wear proper walking shoes as the walking surface can be quite undulating.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

Hallasan National Park is a fantastic place to explore. Firstly, the vegatation between Spring and Fall is beautiful. As you hike to higher elevations the landscape and plants slowly change. Numerous rare and even some endemic species are found here. Concerning wildlife, what visitors are most likely to see are the Roe Deer. These small deer are found throughout the park, and as I hiked quitely we came upon 5-10 throughout our 6 hour trek.In 2007 Hallasan became part of the Unesco World Heritage site calle   Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes  . This honor is only bestoyed on the most unique and important natural and cultural sites on Earth. Hallasan is a geolocial wonder, and is comparable to some of the most iconic national parks in the United States. The park probably deserves 2 days as visitors will want to hike to the crater lake on Hallasan peak, but the entirity of the park holds many exceptional sites. Many trips to Jeju island are scheduled around their trek at Hallasan. Make sure to bring plenty of water, and keep an eye on weather conditions. Hikers must start early if they want to hike to the peak, late arrivals will not be permitted to make the full trek as it takes anywhere from 6-10 hours depending on your pace.

Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.
It was a fun two hours in the museum especially for the children. They were excited seeing all the funny exhibits and posing for photos.

It is a short ferry ride from Jeju and an island worth visiting. It is a very small island so even just a few hours in Udo is enough to see all of its beauty. We rented a motorbike to get around the island. Make sure to remember to bring your camera~

Incredible work of art it was a great place to visit. The number of pictures were beyond my expectation; need more than 1 hour to see all exhibitions. Need a good camera for good quality. Sometimes need flash to get a brighter picture. ??0000 only.

So many photos you could take in this big museum it's too bad that I only spent about 2 hours in here because I didn't have much time then. I suggest to visit this museum in the morning and prepare to spend 3-4 hours in here. I visited here at noon and it's a bit crowded with people.

I was not impressed at all. Typical tourist trap to get you to spend some money. The driver just leaves you there for an hour and there isn't much to do or see here. I guess you can guy over priced tea if that is your thing

I had a lovely day at Hallim Park. There's a lot to see and do and I spent quite a few hours there. I would recommend this for couple/families/friends wanting a lovely day out in Jeju. It's also right next to the beach!!

Great for experiencing traditional Korean Culture. I recommend around 2~3 hours there. It's quite big and there's a lot to see and experience. We went there during the first weeks of October and it was very green and lush. I think in summer and spring it's gonna be even more pretty. Different types of Korean housing and different lifestyle (farmer student worker etc.) are portrayed very well and the tools they used are there to see. There is also a convenience store near the entrance which doesn't work with cash.
Got to see a lot of bears on displayed from day 1. Not a very big museum but can walk for around 1-2 hours. Got to buy a teddy bear there after the visit.

Good place to see all the monuments in one time.It takes around 1 hour and half to visit all the park and the price is 9 000Krw for one adult.Some monuments needs some refresh work but the others are in a good state.

can spend a couple of hours reading the many Greek myths and learn about the many names which you have heard of often. A very detailed museum and would probably take you about 2-3 hours to completely see everything. We enjoyed our time here despite the hot sun beating down on us. Many interesting sights including cows and real crops in the museum itself.

When we have a summer vacation in Jeju, it was one of must see.  If you want to visit, visit when it is magic hour (golden hour). The sky makes perfect blue color. It was very good place especially for children. They had experience in making necklace with glass. The sculptures in the Glass Castle were beautiful.  Visit with children. It is good place for children.

Went on a Friday afternoon at the suggestion of our hired taxi driver even though it was not in our planned itinerary as we happened to be in the area for lunch. There was no other visitor in there other then my friend and I. For 9000 won, there are many other attractions in Jeju to see. The place is small and just filled with colourful glass exhibits and decorations... we completed visiting in less than half an hour as it is a very small place.

Welcome to the Beautiful UDO, thats the word that will welcome all guest who will travel to this small island. I rent a bike for 10,000 Korean Won  (3 Hours) and I only used it for an Hour lol. There's a lot of thing to do andnsee in Udo and dont miss it. Ill be back soon.

We were there about an hour before closing so there weren't many people in the cave. It's pretty dark and wet in the cave. The floor is also uneven. But if you are into caves/rocks/Geography, I think you'd love it!

We went with friends to visit the museam and for all of us it was quite entertaining. Loved it.Finally, don't miss   Teddy Bear Elvis Music Show  .

We went there by ferry, it takes around 1 hour, small but really nice island, must visit if you are in Jeju, it is the southern area of south Korea, population is only 90 , no cars aloud on the island you can make the whole tour by foot in 1 hour and a lot of beautiful scenery to see so prepare camera

We went here mainly to see the cave network formed by Mt. Halla's eruption. It was really cool, literally. The temperature was about 17degrees so it was a nice rest from the 34 outside. There are about 3 sections to all the caves....It was very quiet when we went so not many people about which was nice, but it does get a bit hot walking around all the gardens as we went in the summer. We probably only stayed for an hour or two.

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We spent may be half an hour here and had a good time. The maze is very pretty and you don't see mazes made from trees in the US any more, so this was a treat. The mazes were not difficult, but can be confusing. The admission was quite reasonable, so I do recommend this place if your family is into mazes. Oh, there were a lot of cats roaming the ground and made good subjects for photos.

We arrived in late autumn nearing winter so there were not many flowers on display. We still managed to see chrysanthemum in various colours!! We also managed to spot the peacocks and ostriches. There's a small enclosure for kids (and adults) to see the various birds they have there. We also visited the 2 caves within Hallim Park. There's also a big bonsai area in the park.The park is huge, so allocate about 2 hours to visit everything!

This place is huge, with lots of plants, flowers, caves to see. Though it may not be extra especial since it felt so artificial, it is still a cool place to visit. Stroll and take lots of pictures with friends or family. Don't join the tour because they only allow 1-1.5 hours and you'll end up just walking and not really appreciating the things that you will see.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This is a relatively new Buddhist temple build in the 1990's.  Setting is wonderful in a set-back in an Oreum (a subsidiary volcano   mountain  ).  Gardens in front are very nice.  If you like to see Buddhist temples this is probably the biggest and nicest one on Jeju; I recommend visiting.  It's free just walk around.  Allow about 1 hour.

This is a really interesting place to visit. I have never seen any similar rock formations as the ones that can be seen here. If being in the area and for us who have an interest in nature and science, this is a must see place.It is very well organized with stair, walking paths and information signs.There is a small fee for entering and there are opening hours that must be considered.

This is a nice place for sightseeing and exploring the Jeju waterfalls. There was a roughly 5-10 minutes walk before reaching the waterfall, which was fairly simple and pleasant too. The waterfall does not differ greatly from your other waterfalls, so if you?re looking for a unique and different sightseeing experience, I suggest giving this a miss. However, it was still quite magnificient and beautiful if you enjoy sightseeing and waterfalls. Overall, do spend about an hour here to leisurely stroll and sightsee this Jeju wonder.

This is a great place for young children, with so many teddy bears to see and to play with. Even my husband and I were kept fully entertained. Inside you can see teddy bears in many different settings, all very cuddly and well presented. What I loved most is the outside area - I could spend hours just watching kids play, and it'll be great to have a picnic in the garden with all the nice surrounding, and with teddy bears of course.

This Hallim Park is a big area with the palm tree, tulips, cherry blossom, etc.  They also have some cave and near to the sea.  They have Historical Story since 1971 if you see the website.  We need to have 2-3 hours i think to go arround.  When i visit here last week, we still can see the tulips.

This crater is unlike the others seen on the island because it didn't form much of a surrounding cone due to its quick explosion without spewing much lava around. It is the only such kind of volcano seen in Korea.Apart from the special crater, there are miscanthus (the purple reed) and eulalia in different seasons. Very leisure walk around.We spent an hour inside, including a nap under the tree on a wooden swing.
There are lots of things to see here, we spend 2 hours here. Beautiful trees, caves, stones, small waterfall. It is all about nature and traditional korea living.
The park is quite big and there are many interesting stuff to see. There's a bonsai garden, a small hanok village, bird park etc. It's quite an interesting place where you can spend a good 2 hour.
The park has birds area , flowers area, caverns with lots of other attractions probably you need 4 hour to see it all.We like the caverns more than anything else

The lava tube was quite dark all around,.... Except some light they provided... You be Able to see the natural lava tube formation and some feature like lava shelf raft etc... The journey is around 1 hour round trip.Note that the dark surrounding coupled with uneven rock ground,make it extremely tiring for the ankle... Could easily twist an anke or knee here and there....

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The grounds are amazing and beautiful. Different times of year you can see beautiful blooms like azaleas, hydrangeas, bougainvillea, etc. It?s definitely worth some time to see the natural beauty of the flora. The animal enclosures are very disappointing, because as a true natural park, you would expect better conditions for the animals. The caves are a good break from the sun and heat. They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

The entry fee is abit on the high side, but if you love gardens, plants, nature, and especially flowers, it’s worth every penny. My absolute favourite place to visit in Jeju. I love flowers so we spent around 4 hours here. There’s a huge variety of flowers, and the gardens/areas are very well laid-out. Besides the greenhouse, there is also an area outside where all the different-themed gardens are (Korean, Japanese, French etc), there are about 12 gardens in total I think, and all of them are really beautiful. I think this attraction is still relatively new, as I could still see gardeners setting up the flower beds and so on. But this also means that it’s not crowded yet and there are relatively few tourists compared to the other attractions. Flower-lovers, this is a must-visit!

The cave takes about an hour, nice walk. Wear sensible shoes as the floor is not even and take a small jacket as it gets colder the further in you go. It was an interesting walk and we got to see bats at the end.

Spent approximately 5 hours walking in the park. The park is sub divided into different sectors with different themes. Didn?t go to all the different sectors because some didn?t appeal to us. What I found nice and interesting were;1. The Caves2. Cultural Village3. The Bonsai & Stone Garden4. Seasonal Section - Ume FlowersWhat I didn?t like;1. Birds and reptiles in captivity2. Wild Flowers Garden - area seems to be poorly maintained. I didn?t get to see anything except grass and weedsBe prepared to walk and walk so if walking is not your thing then u better reconsider. Limited restaurants on site, so it?s best if u bring your own food and drinks.

Spend an hour here to learn more about the background of the women divers. It gave me a new appreciation for the dedication of the women and I enjoyed seeing actual divers later, with a greater understanding of what they do and how they dive. I took a few moments to watch the video and then breezed through some of the other displays. Felt it was fairly priced for the value.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.

Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.

Our family has visited quite a few aquariums but this is the first one where we've seen some adorable otters. Adorable! Facility is beautiful clean airy-feeling.Tanks are well-kept it appears so my guess is that the sea creatures are   happier.   The aquarium is just the right size for anyone to finish in less than two hours.  What's also nice is that it's right next to the ocean.

입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Only 1km of the 7.5km lava tube is open to the public, but I highly recommend coming! Expect to spend about an hour admiring the beauty of this natural volcanic formation!While we were there, it had rained the night before and was still drizzling slightly, so the ground was damp. Good to wear proper shoes with good grip (we were thankful for our boots) as the ground is a rather uneven terrain and can be slippery when wet. It's also rather dimly lit, with some lighting inside to guide your path and highlight specific features found in the cave.Even though there is only one entry/ exit point, there is much to see (if you're into geology/ geography/ nature lover, otherwise it'll just look like the same dark cavernous backdrop) as you loop back to the exit point.

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Took about 10 minutes to walk down to the falls. Be sure to wear proper shoes as it's a rocky shore, all loose stones. Spent less than an hour at the place.
Not so good as all is make of glass. All in korean, nothing much to see. walk out of the castle within 1 hour. (quite a waste of money, dun go unless really got a lot of spare time)
Not much to do, but if you rent a vehicle, its certainly worth a couple of hours to see what it has to offer. Even if just to see how the locals live.
Not a big forest and you have to pay a small fee to enter, a quick hours stroll some pretty trees not much else to see though.

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

Kids were enjoying this, but for an adult, it's a waste of time. I was in and out in less than an hour, including the   Elvis show.   It is a bunch of teddy bears dressed up in famous scenes. There are some antique teddy bears on display, but everything is only in Korean. The Elvis show was a mechanical teddy bear in a jumpsuit that played Elvis music. It said things like,   Mahalo, I just love being here in Hawaii,   but no one else seemed to notice. Total. Tourist. Trap.

Jeju has some very interesting museums, they seem to have them about everything from electricity ,to tea to, to robots! Quite quirky here and you'll see Teddy bears dressed up as Michael Jordan to famous re-enactments of history. Spent about 2 hours here just because it seemed interesting and a lot of effort has been put into the place.

Jeju Glass Castle is a must see museum. It has outdoor which can be seen with in 2 hours & indoor as well. There are a lot of glass shapes. This museum is good for people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. The entrance ticket is little bit expensive.

It's an incredible lava cave! We spent half day in this sight seeing and my daughters loved! (2 teenagers) It's very difficult to do sight seeing in Jeju without a rental car! We took almost an hour to arrive there, and the same to come back!!
It will definitely not take you more than an hour to see everything it can offer. It only has a couple of waterfalls, a huge bridge and a lot of trees.
It is really amazing to see these formations.  Small fee to park and see the formations, but still super cheap, and well worth it.m you can see it all in a half hour.

It costs 10.000 won to enter and without kids you are going to be done within half an hour but you'll have a big smile on your face. Teddybear Ghandi, Bear Elvis and more. Very funny. With young kids a must see you would be a 'bad' parent if you deny them this. One of the better quircky museums in Jeju.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

I would recommend that you read the book ?The Island of Sea Women? by Lisa See before visiting the museum. I felt an emotional connection to the museum, the observatory and the grounds around the area, primarily because I had some background knowledge. The museum is well laid out and interesting. Do take the time to watch the video on the main floor before going through the exhibits. If you are there around 10:00 a.m. or 1:00 p.m. you may be able to see the women divers from the observatory on the 3rd floor.  Getting there: we were on a cruise ship and took a taxi from the ship terminal in Jeju City. It took about an hour and was a very scenic drive.  Our taxi driver gave us an hour to tour the museum and grounds and then dropped us off by the main market area in downtown Jeju City. It was under $100 for four people in a taxi.

I went to this museum just because a friend has suggested. Despite I am not a big fan of teddy bears this museum is really amazing! You will see the major events from the world history, famous singers and artists, as well as some scientists! I better don't tell everything not to ruin the surprise! There happens an Elvis Show at every hour or so. If you have time, definitely give it a go.

I wasn?t expecting much but the displays were certainly fun and interesting. Can see that?s lots of care have gone into it. Great for photographs with the missus and if u have kids, this is heaven for them. Around an hour to walk the whole museum.

I was staying in Booyoung hotel (next to the ICC - international Convention Center) and had a few hours to walk around. About 5-10 minutes walk from the hotel I entered this park where they made me pay a very modes fee to enter. Much to my delight I got to this fantastic rock (actually lava) formation, which was definitely worth seeing. If you are at an event in ICC do not miss the chance. While there, you may want to visit the Botanic Gardens and the Cheonjeyeon Falls, both within walking distance (about 30 minutes from Booyoung). For the Cliffs you may need only 15-20 minutes, plus the 5-10 minutes to walk there..

I was planning on going up gwaneumsa and coming down seongpanak but seongpanak is closed until 31st Jul, 18 so I came down the the same. It took me about 3.5 hr to climb up, and 3 hrs to come down. Together with my lunch breaks, I finished the entire round trip in a little over 7 hours. Unfortunately, it was  really misty when I was at the summit, so, i didn't get to see the crater lake. I highly recommend bringing a pair of trekking poles and good hiking shoes.
I visited this to see Goong Teddy Bears (Princess Hours), and i did not get disappointed. Everything here is cute, esp. the Elvis Presley show. They have a nice garden outside as well!

I visited in maze park last week with my family. The park is not big but you can enjoy the maze enough. It took about 1 hour to find exit for me but other people took 30~40 minutes. I recommend not to use map for more fun. You can also see the beautiful flowers and meet lots of cats. If you could find Dr. Dustin who made the park, ask him to take a picture together. He like that :).

I loved this seemingly unassuming place that I would have never really thought of visiting.  It was one of the most interesting and beautiful places I visited in Jejudo Island.  It is definitely a   must do  , as they say in Disney World!  We would have loved to spend more time there.  It's not just a park with a bunch of rocks so don't miss out!  It's like a natural museum/art gallery of indigenous Jejudo volcanic rocks with a splash of the island's history.  Highly recommended to spend a minimum of 3-4 hours here!!

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).

I am traveling with my 79 years old dad who has weak knees. When our driver brought us to yongmeori beach, we have no idea what we are in for. Because of my dad, we chose to enter the beach on the left entrance and exit by the right entrance which we heard is the opposite direction of what most people would do. From the entrance, we had to walk down a very steep stairs which led us directly onto the beach. Honestly, the walk down the stairs was a bit dangerous as there was no railing or any safety measures. Despite collecting entrance fee, there are no staff around if you need help. That said, the scenery was stunning. The natural formation of the rocks was beautiful and the water was clear. For a popular tourist destination, this is also one of the cleanest I have been. You don?t see any garbage around. I hope anyone who plans to visit, continue to keep this place clean. As we had to walk slowly, we completed one round of the beach in over an hour.

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.
Had a few hours before catching flight, chose this beach because of location, but turns out it was a good choice. the rocks, and clear water was something you do not see in the US

For 11000krw entry per person, we expected an eye opener and an attraction different than most. Upon entering, we can see from the number of glass exhibits on display that this place would've been a great place to visit for couples or families.Beautiful display with intricacies that you will need to understand to appreciate. The displays look quite challenging to maintain as there are so many glass objects that could be dulled due to weather conditions. Aside from that, we appreciated the effort it would've taken to create this glass wonderland and enjoyed it extremely. Even in the wintry snowy condition we were experiencing, although this is an outdoor exhibition, we enjoyed it!Would recommend 1-2 hours at a slow walk pace with many photo opportunities.

Experiencing the Jeju Mysterious Road was cool for a few minutes. But that's about it.If you're gonna drive a few hours just to see it, I'd say just look for another attraction. But if it's just near you, go ahead and experience it.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.
dont miss this, you can see how the underground magma made this amazing tunnel crafted by nature, really nice to visit. 1 hour tour (it took me to go to the end and back)

Do not plan your visit to the island if the weather is rainy. You will need your passport or driving license if you want to rent a bicycle, bike or any other vehicle. It will take you 3-4 hours to go around and see the island.

Dark cave, chilly, dripping water and uneven steps were all I felt for one hour journey in and u-turn out of the cave. Not much to see really unless you are acompanied by an expert or archelogist who can make rock and mud come alive and tell stories. I have been to few caves over the world and find this least interesting and dull.
Cave is big and long, take around 1 hour to come and back. Nothing much to see and it's dark so it's hard to take photo. Average compare to other caves
Came here with tour, cool installations to take a lot of photo. Will probably take about 1.5hours to slowly see all the teddy bears across 2 levels. Cool to see.

Bring your swimming gear along, it has a sea swimming pool during low tides, basically daytime. Seeing ppl drives and swimming. There is life-jacket rental available for snorkelling. No entrance ticket required. But the carpark attendance charged us W2K which seem only W1K per hour. No proper carpark control. See ppl park along road side.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said ?sure?.  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn?t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

At first, I did not see the point of going to a Teddy Bear Museum. I could not imaging myself checking all teddy bears dressed as popular celebrities and personalities. But I was suprised that I loved every minute of it and I was totally entertained. Me and my friend stayed in the museum for over an hour, longer than what we expected. Highly recommended.

All the museums were great in jeju island if you're in and out within a hour or so.? But i think i stayed in this automobile museum for at least 3 hours.? My hobby and passion is cars back home jn the States so for any car lover,? this is the place.? From the model T,? old school Bentley and rolls royce to The original 300sl class Mercedes,? you see it all.? A must for car lovers...
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
