review: Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. A place to go if you want to relax and have a nice walk or if you are really interested in history and stones..

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.

Went past the falls as we were looking for the tourist info office so decided to have a look. As it had been fairly dry the falls were not very spectacular and though it claims to be the only one in Asia that falls directly into the ocean I am pretty sure Duden falls in Turkey are in Asia and fall into the ocean. Some stairs take you down to the falls - they seem less lengthy when you are climbing back up which is a good thing and we rewarded ourselves with some ice cream!!

We didn't seek to visit Mt. Songak -- our driver just brought us there. Not knowing what to do and since he didn?셳 speak a word of English we just consulted a map near the entrance and decided that the only thing to do there really was walk up to the crater. It's a genuine natural wonder. I?셫 glad we went there because the place was just so beautiful it was worth the effort of climbing. And believe me there was some effort. Unlike other Jeju-do mountains there were rough parts in this mountain without steps or any pavement. Some bits were steep too. If you have mobility issues forget the crater; just walk around. One Korean grandpa lost his footing and scraped his hand on the rocks ??we felt bad for him.There were horses that you can ride briefly for a little bit of money. They were cute and surrounded by fields of flowers. It was like a dream to be there looking at the sky the sea the fields and the horses. Would come back if I have the chance.
This was one of our most favorite waterfalls in Korea. Amazing to see. Lots of steps down and up but worth the climb.
The place is well kept and there was a lovely souvenir shop on site. There is not much to see in this part of Jeju so climbing up this rock was definitely an uplifting experience.
One of the scenic places in Jeju. A must go even if you miss the sunset/sunrise. Didn't climb it but I went down to the the Hanyeo area. Tiring climb back up though. You can see Udo Island from here.
Mt. Songak is not high.  So climb can children with family. And has beautiful landscape. You can see the Mt.halla & Mt.Songak  seaside with clean weather.

How many places can you see that?  And be accessible.  It's very pretty I think maybe 20m tall.  There's plenty of stairs and rocks to climb but it's worth the extra effort. Our 10 yr old loved getting sprayed by the mist.  It's near the town and easy to get to worth the$4 admission.

When we reach this location, it was already 11am and from far, we can see hundreds of tourist climbing up hill. So we decide to just explore around the area with the mountain as background, you will be surprise on all the great locations around this place..

We were there on a clouded day, which was perfect since you don't want to climb those stairs in a heatwave. Not alot of visitors, so we made plenty of pictures without any bombers. Definitely a must-see if you are in Jeju.

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

This place was very beautiful.  In winter, you can see beautiful silver grass fields. It's a different charm than summer. If you visit Jeju Island, I recommend you to go here! You should wear sneakers when visit here. Because it's high that it's hard to climb up.

This Mysterious Road is nothing very special actually, but it can explain by the Physics explanation why we see downhill road but the car can climb up without engine on.. hehe.. so there nothing spooky here..

This happened to be our favorite place even though we got up early to see the sunrise but the clouds blocked the sun. It was still beautiful and the surrounding area is gorgeous. There are so many birds and flowers to see. Many photo ops. After climbing you might be tired, but when you descend make sure you go to where the little beach is. It's gorgeous there.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

The temple is at the foot of the Sambang mountain, where you have a choice to scale 400 steps to the mid point of the mountain to see another goddess statue there. A good 30 mins climb up and down at a casual pace with photo opportunities of the scenery.

The place is so great. The geopark is one of UNESCO heritage world. We must climb at about 500 stairs to reach the peak. In a good weather, you can go there early in the morning to see the sunrise. The combination of mountain and beach (with the black sand) is so beautiful. You can also see the performance of woman diver there and buy live seafood.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

Our guide brought us here to see the 10-inch snow... we came from tropical climate you see...So there is no climbing for us, but the snow was fun for the kids as it was their first experience...they were so happy making snowballs and we took some really great pictures here.

Made it a point to see the performance by the elderly female divers but was a little disappointed. Worth a watch if you can make it. One motto that we came up with was,   If you can climb Hallasan, you can do anything.  Surely enough, climbing llchulbong wasn't too difficult maybe 20-30 minutes climb?

I've never been able to go up so close to a waterfall that flows directly into the sea. You'll need to climb over rocks to go up near to the falls. I loved being so near the waterfall and the sea at the same time!If you only have time to see 1 waterfall on Jeju island, go to this one. Cheonjiyeon & Cheonjeyeon waterfalls were quite unimpressive in my opinion.

It's a nice place to take some nice photos with the teddies.  Lots of them there huge ones as well.  The most I've seen in one single location. Good effort. You can touch them,  hug them,  even climb over them.  Our children had a fun time.

If you want to see sunrise, please go to Seongsan Ilchulbong: It's very beautiful place. You should wake up in the early morning. It'll take 20 mins to climb in the peak. And you can experience excellent atmosphere there. You can take lots of picture because of its beauty. Good luck to you, hope you can see sunrise in the Seongsan Ilchubong

If you only see one waterfall in Jeju, I would see this one. It is beautiful how it goes into the see. We visited it during a taxi tour along with Cheonjiyeon Falls. They are very close to each other so there is no need to see just one but if you are short on time I would go to Jeongbang. For 2000 won each it is a bargin. Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet and can climb over rocks in, if you want to get close to the waterfall.

I went earlier to see the Cheonjiyeon waterfall and must say this is a better one because you can actually get to dip your toes into the water. I paid 2000 won for an adult. Basically there are steep steps you need to walk down and then in order to get nearer to the waterfall you need to climb over big rocks. If you are with little children or older folk you might have a hard time. With the waterfall, you can wade right up to it if you are brave enough the stand the cold.

I didn't know I was looking at this famous peak when we approached in a taxi (looking for a lunch spot that our kids would approve of). I was saying   Wow, look at that   as we drove towards it. Then our driver explained it was the famous peak. I can see why, even on a cloudy rainy day it was such a beautiful scene. We couldn't climb to the peak because it was closed to the public due to an impending typhoon. I was disappointed we couldnt climb but so glad that we got to see it, even from the base. Absolutely beautiful area. I want to come back to Jeju just to climb that peak and see the beauty from above.Incidentally there were plenty of restaurants and cafes and shops in the small town at the base. Even an American Embassy (i.e. Mcdonalds)

I could not recognise how horrible the place has become since my second visit in 2009.  Not only was it very crowded, I was sad to see lots of garbage on the rocky beach below.  It was also not possible to enjoy a nice walk by the cliffside for those of us not out to climb the mountain.  I left after no more than 15 minutes to the utter surprise of my cab driver.It was a beautiful and serene place and the authorities should take steps to limit the number of visitors and do more to clean up the garbage.

I choose to stay near to the peak so it only took us 5 mins to walk here. We didn't managed to see the sunrise as the weather was a great challenge. It was extremely windy and cold in the morning. Thus we came here at noon time. When we reach the foot of the peak, I could see that the whole peak was full of people climbing either up or coming down. The entrance fee is cheap, it cost only 2000won. The scenery was really beautiful, it worth coming here to take a look at the natural beauty.

Enjoyed this attraction a lot. There are bears everywhere and everywhere is a shooting spot. Most of the teddy bears are quite big in size thus everyone will have different pose to take pictures with them. They are all so adorable and even the smaller size teddy bears are very cute. Liked the giant teddy bear where have to climb up to sit on its back, I tried for at least 10 times and finally I am able to climb up, it was real fun. Also like to sit on the giant sofa in the teddy house surrounded by so many giant teddy bears. There are bears that feature Korean movie and pop stars but yet to see a Psy teddy bear
Easy climb down to see the waterfall. If you are adventurous, go navigate across the rocks for better photos angles and also for a challenge. A simple waterfall for photo ops and a light stroll.

Do not bother spending your time going here unless there is some specific item or shopping you need to do. Come on, you are on Jeju, a small slice of paradise on Earth, go see funny statues or climb a mountain.

At this place you need to walk, climb a little. Be very careful when climbing on and over rocks at the bottom of the fall to take pics. Some rocks are very slippery. You can see the water go straight into the ocean which is quite different to the other two waterfalls. It is a lovely sight!

Am glad able to get into the Peak just before its closing for ticket sales, you will regret not visiting it.  Though windy & cold during night time, it's worth for all the climbing to see the sunset? at least for me

When I was a kid I would see Ripley's Believe it or Not on TV.? This is a great collection of bizarre everything from Elvis's hair to antique torture tools.? Our family had a great time there.? Bonus that there is a Starbucks next door.

What is offered at the Glass Museum does not justify its 9 000 won entrance fee.There is a garden with glass flowers  glass birds  and other ornaments. The displays are dull and although they probably took a lot of time and effort to make  the whole place seems like something that would have been more interesting 15 years ago.
Went as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It really is like stepping back in time to see houses and the village preserved as it was before technology existed.
We went there and did see something but it?s probably a hit or miss place unless you have time.There?s a nice cafe with a huge garden there though.

We went here on a rainy day as we really wanted to see how the famous O'Sulloc tea was made. The museum is nothing more than a room (unfortunately not all texts are translated info english) and the majority of the space is taken up by the shop and the cafe which seems like the main focus of this location.Two things were nice getting a look of the tea plantations and having a quick tea tasting.I would recommend this only if you are a true O'Sulloc fan or if you have spare time not visiting all the other sights at Jeju island.

We regretted going to this place. The entrance fee is 5 000 won and they give you a 3 000 coupon to use when you buy their products. There is nothing to see except display of chocolates from different countries which is available at a supermarket. Really it is a waste of money and waste of time.

We only had a limited time in Jeju so we asked Jin to customize a tour for us to see the best of Jeju has to offer. Both Jin and June speak English fluently so it was not difficult to communicate. They are both flexible in terms of what we want to see. Excellent service!
we hired taxi for a-day trip this is the last sightseeing in jeju.totally enjoy the fun experience and fill up the puzzle.must visit once in a life time.
We had fun at this maze park! Seemed easy but not! My son and I had a good time trying to figure the maze out! Kids will definitely enjoy! Lovely place for good exercise too!

We had an amazing time here at the spirited garden! There are so many beautiful trees to see and the people are lovely! It really felt like a spiritual experience. I felt so at peace while I was here. The citron tea was amazing and helped so much after I got a cold teaching my kids! Loved it and want to come back again!

We did only this folk village with my family and friends. This recreated the feeling of living a long time ago in korea it communicates well the differences of different backgrounds. We did not hire the audio guide and we had two korean speakers with us who were able to read everything. It was fabulous for my kids to see and touch most of the displays plenty to keep them occupied. We saw a dance and others getting photos taken in wedding costumes and a Korean Drama being filmed. Overall the experience was a good cultural morning out. We did not eat there as we were meeting friends for lunch but it looked very traditional

Was expecting to see beautiful blossoms of camellia flowers but was disappointed as the blooms were over at that time. I believe if you come at the right time it will be awesome. The only blooming flowers that we saw were in the greenhouses. Park is not small so there's quite a bit of walking to visit the various parts of the park. Would recommend to check on the bloom timing before visiting the park.

Very interesting garden of native plants but you don't get much time to see before they herd you into a room to hard sell you into buying Ginseng. Their pitch is that they invented a new method to grow and harvest JeJu ginseng in the lab and is suppose to the best. Buy ginseng here is very expensive. I don't even think JeJu is know for ginseng.

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...
This waterfall is very tiny but really difficult to see the water itself because it dries up time to time. You must checkout the season before visiting this place.

This temple and the grounds are very well maintained. Take off your shoes before you enter the temple. More than a tourist attraction people still come to pray meditate and present offerings. Be respectful and use indoor voices or be silent.Give yourself enough time to explore the entire area. There are walking paths around the temple where you can see for yourself the perfect Feng Shui.

This rock formation was spotted on the eastern side of Jeju island. I was lucky enough to see this attraction having not spotted one a long time ago.The water present in these area is crystal clear where you can see different fishes swimming in the ocean breeze.
This just seemed like a mountain valley filled with trees that couldn't even be seen very well because of high brush and trees around the path. Not worth the time going there!

This is where physics takes over. Let the fun takes over. What you see don't really make sense until the guide explains it to you. All in natural surroundings and in good time. Don't forget to try out the street food there while you are at it. Made my day. Cheers again!

this is the place to go for food and shopping when at Seogwipo. The market is pretty huge to walk  see and experience the everyday routines of those worked there as well as the regular stream of tourists that makes the place crowded and noisy. if you stay around Seogwipo  chances is you will be there at least once or every evening for did or to pass time. take time to go around the entire interior with multiple lanes with as well as the outside shops. You might just find interesting things to see and get something you like.

This is such a beautiful place! Right next to the seaside the estuary is a great place to relax and take pictures. It?셲 very serene and great for visiting with family. It?셲 right next to a black sand beach where lots of people go to swim in the summertime. There is a cafe nearby called no. 183 that was very nice to relax after walking a bit. A must see when in jeju!

This is actually my second time here and this time without a guide as we go by car ourself. You need a guide to actually understand the history of these traditional houses. I went there around 3pm and the whole village seems like a ghost town. Very quiet. Only 2 families of tourist sighted. We took a nice walk around the village but our main reason for visiting is to eat the black pork meat cooked in spicy flavour. It was my best meal 11 years ago when I visited and best meal in Korea this time too.

This is a must see! An awesome show in Jeju that is very popular around the world. It has Korean culture involved which makes it even cooler. Hardly any talking but you can totally understand the story throughout the entire show! This show had my attention the entire time! Don't want to give to much info to ruin the surprise but I would definitely recommend this if you visit Jeju.

There are 3 terry bear museums in Jeju. The one which we visited is Terry bear and safari. The lower floor is the safari and upper floor is the bear. Think this also to attract the kids to visit the place thus the safari.Take your time to see and enjoy the many characters of the terry bear. One corner of displays is a very expensive due to diamond crown.
The water is very clean n clear.  Can see the fish clearly. Can drop by if have extra time. The entrance fee is 2000w for adult

The place is actually quite big but it seems to duplicate the little corners everywhere. It shows you the olden houses of the farmers (ranging from poor farmers to rich farmers and so on). Can give it a miss if there isn't ample time to cover everything!

The overall theme was a good one cause you get to see the various famous landmarks in a fraction of its size. We went on a day where there wasn't many people so thats a good thing cause we can take our time with the photographs. The entrance fee was the most expensive among all the entrance fee standing at 20000 won for 3 people (2 adult 1 student) but it was pretty fun despite the shabby appearances.

The overall theme was a good one  cause you get to see the various famous landmarks in a fraction of its size. We went on a day where there wasn't many people  so thats a good thing  cause we can take our time with the photographs. The entrance fee was the most expensive among all the entrance fee  standing at 20 000 won for 3 people (2 adult  1 student)  but it was pretty fun despite the shabby appearances.

The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.

The last time when i was visiting the glass museum was in the night time and this time round was in the day timeI have see the difference between the day and night and i personally like the night time as all the light are lighted up and it is so beautiful and romantic.

The cafe is pretty good with green tea drinks of all kind and dessert! We tried the green tea ice cream which was really good. However almost EVERYONE comes here so it will take some time to find a table. Be patient and enjoy the outdoor fields. I personally thought the outdoor fields had more to see than the so called museum. They also have a variety of green tea for you to buy as souvenirs too. Really easy to find with a huge free parking lot.

The aquarium is good and the penguins and sharks are worth watching. Huge collection of marine life you cant miss...The show seemed to be a bit dragging. Before the sealion and dolphin show there was a 'good pirate bad pirate ' show which for me was a bit boring. Dolphin show also wasted time showing videos. But towards last 5 mins it was good.

review: Tea plantation near the city center with a tea museum containing a few old tes pots (you will probably have wider assortment in a flea market). I will probably enjoy visiting an actual farm with fruit trees and greenhouses planted to vegetables than spending time at the tea plantation. There is no entrance fee but there is also no tour guide or someone or something to explain what there is to see.

Such a nice place.  I wish I was visiting Jeju island during the summer time to see all the different flower.  It was pretty in the fall so I can imagine how pretty it will be in the summer.  It's a must for Jeju.

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.

Nothing great about this place. read that it was a interesting little town but drove there and to see only replicas of the old houses. Lots of tourist were taking photos but that was about it. Visit if you have spare time
Not sure if there is a certain period of time to get this feel. Tried a few times but nothing seems to be as it mentioned.
Not so spectecular after you have seen all the beautiful scenery in Jeju. A quick visit is alright if you have the time. Just a rock formation.
Not a lot to see at this time. Probably a lot more activity during the summer season. Nice sandy beach.
Nice to see the different types of seashell. However if you are short of time  it is okay to miss the place...

My wife and I had a great time.  There was no sales trap that some people mention here (maybe because we weren't part of a tour group..)Highlights: Gorgeous flowers everywhere Female drummers performance Dressing up in traditional outfits seeing traditional houses.

My friends and I were so excited about Loveland before our visit. However we were quite disappointed afterward as the park was kind of old. We expect more to see after paying so much for admission but nothing else besides statues and some aged fountains. Only visit if you really have free time to kill.
My daughter enjoyed reading and seeing unusual and interesting facts. We had a good time at the museum.
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.
learn about the lives of the people in the olden days and get to see the traditional houses around the area. quite an interesting place to visit but not a place where i will go back for a 2nd time.

I've been to various Buddhist temples throughout South Korea and this by far has been the most breathtaking.  The monks were extremely welcoming and even pointed parts of the temple that I should go. The second floor of the main temple is best for pictures and found myself in that one spot for nearly 45 minutes.  Remember this is a holy place and be respectful especially for its monks who are so inviting.The best time to go is after 6:30 pm. The crowds are nearly gone and you'll be able to witness the ringing of the bells and 7 pm prayer by the monks.  The temple is lit and makes it more majestic than the day.Finally the giant golden Buddha statues were a sight to see. If you are in the Seogwipo area of Jeju- this is a must see!

It's wet and dark inside..we just walk and walk in dark sometimes we just talk about going back and not see what's in the end of the path. But somehow we reach the end..take a photo and then walk the same road to get out.
It's new and quite unique but not a must-see attraction. Recommended only to those who love teddy bears and have some extra time to spend.

It was nice to see how people live in thatched roof in time before however after a while you kind of see the same stuff.  For those who watched Korean movies  you will be able to identify a few sets there.  I wish they would have more entertainers maybe dressed up in period costumes  walking  around.  Managed to catch a short drum performance which was entertaining.  There is a small Korean eatery which serves nice bimbimbap.
It make us so excited! We love it and hope to see it next time! It is the most fantastic show I have ever seen!!!
It is one of a few place with optical illusion on the slop of the road. First time seen this kind of scene.If anyone had any experience at other country. I guess it is just the same.

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.
In here can see the traditional house structures of olden jeju people.And the living style of olden Time. The tour guides explain the customs of jeju people as well.

Imposing scenery! So many photo opportunities on this beautiful landscapeWent back twice cos I didn't realise the hanyeo diver women show is there..was searching around somewhere else.  Time your visit to see these amazing old ladies diving at 3pm.

If you have seen any miniature park before then this park will be boring for you. But if you have time remaining for the day then you can see this place. The entrance ticket is expensive if you are not a solo traveler.  Eco land Stone park and Sangumburi Crater are near this place.  I have been to a miniature park in Shenzhen city of China so this park was borning for me.

i went here in heavy rain. not much to see. but im having good time here with my friends. there are a lot of stones sculpture here. and also theres a museum regarding jeju.the museum tell us about types of stone. and the jeju itself formed by the volcanic activity happened before this.

I was so looking forward to visiting this museum to learn about the history of the island... after about 15 min tour and seeing only 2-3 homes (from outside) we were ushered into a mosquito infested shack for a 20 minute presentation of their icky old fermented tea that they were trying to sell as miracle supplement. It is very sad that they use these tactics to raise $$. I would've gladly donated money if they did not waste what little time I had in Jeju telling me about supplements I have no interest in.  This was second trap that day scheduled by the tour company (the first one was at some other 'museum' that was selling ginseng products that were outrageously expensive).  urgh!!!!

I visited Seongsan Illchulbong at 7:30. It was sunrise time and it was my first time to see sun rising from such a height. The effect of sun rays on the ocean made everything so beautiful. I can guarantee one thing that it is much beautiful if you see in person than seeing in pictures.

I thought I will see a museum but it was a cafe and a shop. I don't think it deserve the visit. If you have time and you love the green tea you might like it.Next to it Innisfree it is also a shop and a cafe and you can make your own soap there.

i think this is an over rated attraction.they say Jeju is becoming a growing honey moon attraction but I was very disappointed in my sight seeing in Jeju.Although folk village is rated high in the place I thought it was complete waste of time. No doubt the place itself is has beautiful scenery there are other places on my door step in Sydney which are more scenic.
I didn't see anything to great about this. Too me it was just a road which didn't really interest me. I wouldn't waste my time

Horse ridding for kids and teens not me!! Hahaha seen REAL horses in life that the adult one is almost as tall as me OMG can't imagine if it goes rampage that jumps up with the back legs how tall will it be and do feedings of the pony that the mouth open so bigPS - they do not have much food selling at this area but there is a small booth nearby the main entrance a convenience store near to the horse race trackBtw 1st time in life I seen real horse races can feel the wind and a the bet-ers  shouting their gambling numbers of the horse toooooo many people down there

Having a camera is a must for this museum. You can't see the illusions unless you take a photo. And there's a lot of people lining up to get photos so you do a bit of waiting around. I wouldn't go again unless I was maybe taking children and it was raining outside. It is located in a very good location though and easy to find. There were these outside sculptures which are a waste of time to look at
Had a great time here. Lots to see and do plus the ice cream and cake is awesome. Also learned a lot about tea! The scale of tea that is grown here is massive!

Going into the cave when it?s blazing hot outside is actually not a bad idea. It was 11degree inside the cave as you walked 1km to see the famous lava columns. Just need to be careful walking as the grounds are mostly uneven and sometimes can be slippery.

Don't waste your time or money here. It's a pure tourist trap and totally overrated for what it is. Long lines to buy silly overrated green tea lattes and soft serve ice cream that don't even taste that great. It's just a giant shop selling the same teas you can buy all over the city. The innisfree shop next door was even worst! Sorry but will not be recommending this place to anyone. That's why it's hard to believe what trip advisor says these days. Everyone seems so happy to come here but once you're here it's a big fat disappointment.
Definitely worth a visit to see nature's glory ! Incredible journey of ever changing nature with the passage of time.
Came here with my husband and we had a great time negotiating and bargaining for prices. I will say it's a bit overwhelming and I didn't see much variety for food but overall we had a good time.
Be prepared to spend a lot of time here. And be prepared to walk.  Much to see. Fantastic bonzais that are over 100 years + older

At the entrance of the plaza there is tourist information center where you can get any info related to the area. From this plaza there are occasional festival from time to time this time I just went to see sunset on the ocean. Above the big waves sunset was pretty. There is long sea-side walk which leads to Dragon head rock.

As the name implies we thought that this is the place where we can get to see and learn real Korean Culture and traditions but it turned out to be a disappointment.  The guide just gave a short description of the Jeju folks in the olden days.  Then we were ushered into a stuffy shack with no fans and windows all closed where the guide tried to introduce us to some kinds of health tonic honey and capsules made from horse's bone.  When none of us shown any interest to buy anything we were just left there in a lurch.  It was one of those compulsory shopping trap in a tour package.Not worth wasting  time there.  There are many better places to visit in Jeju island.

Aqua Planet was a last minute improvised of plans as the wind was exceptionally cold that day.However for the price we pay i am a tad disappointed. Yes the place is huge but the animals that were displayed weren't much. We've seen more and bigger arapaima sharks and stingray elsewhere.Theshow was half synchronized swimming and half animal show. The synchronized swimming wss just okay a bit too lengthy that it turned a little boring.Displays could have been more informative. It wasnt stated smaller shows like feeding times etc. We took our time wandering through the science part but overall there just isn't much.Not recommended.

review: An amusing theme park with plenty to see but not much to do (aside from take photos in compromising positions with statues). The museum does provide some interesting insight into sexuality in South Korea -- note that while full bodied male statues are plentiful the only time larger women feature is in sculptures where men are desperately trying to escape.

A very nice nature park with lots of flora and fauna. There is lots to see and do so do set aside more time to spend at this place. Do wear a pair of comfortable walking shoes and take lots of pictures!
A place to see all monuments and buildings around the world just in one place but should maintain some of our their miniature if they want to increase visitors. Great for the first-time visit
500 years okd village worth to see it. Do not miss oportunity to visit it. Next time I will come again.

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).
You can see there so well cared garden. There is also many different snakes, birds, turtles etc. The caves and botanic garden makes me happy too. Take time and relax. Eeva A

You can see teddy bears in a lot of human like professions and daily situations. They are really beautifully made.It's really attractive, so go for it when you have plenty of time.I was there in 2011.

When you see the symmetry of the cliff, you will be amazed.  The columns that have been created by Mother Nature are a sight to behold.  If you're looking for one of a kind sights, this is one of them.  There is an admission fee, but it's negligible.  From pictures I've seen when the surf is up, that might be a more awesome time to visit.

What a amazing waterfall. I heard that there are olny few waterfall forward the ocean in the world. I had seen several waterfall. If anyone ask me what waterfall is best in your life time, I will say Jeongbang is the best. It is not that big like Victoria or Niagara, but it make feel me cheer up.
Went to the cave, only walk for about 1-2 hrs as this is a short cave. see stone structure cause by volcano eruption. only go if you like nature. Can visit the maze park at the same time.

We were with a tour group so we did not see all the attractions, and our time was limited the ones we did experience were interesting, caves & botanical spirit gardens were worth the trip.  I really liked the stones - fascinating.

We went there with both of our children (at the time, 4 and 2 years old). There was plenty for them both to see and neither of them got bored. My 4 year old particularly liked the lava tubes and both my wife and I found them very interesting too!

We took the ferry to Udo Island. We went as walk ons with our tour guide. The ferry ride was short and easy. We were happy we had our guide with us because the weather was not very good that day and they were closing down the ferry service due to rough seas. We were glad she could translate this information for us.  We went over for a short visit and took the last ferry back to Jeju which was around noon. Because of the ferry schedule we did not have much time on Udo. We did go to 2 lookout spots. They were very pretty but the weather interfered. It would be a nice place on a sunny day, but there doesn't seem to be much to do on the island so plan on relaxing.

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We only brought to see the village with some traditional house and with old people there, with limited time here, cannot see all the village. But this place just symbol. We were offered with the some goods belings to this island Jeju. Like honey and horse backbone pills.

We love exploring caves, and we've been to quite a few worldwide. However, Manjanggul isn't really one of the best. The problem is, there isn't much special,. By the time you walk in half a kilometre, what you see becomes a little unchanging. Not bad for a short visit however. Tips: 1. It is a long walk and can be slippery. Wear comfortable shoes with grippy soles.2. A small torch may be useful

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

We have visited many caves in various countries. More or less they are quite similar. Dark, quiet, mysterious, cold, etc.As with every cave, it's not well litted & its quite dark in certain sections of the cave. Being a natural formation, the ground is usually uneven. Particularly for this cave , the unevenness is very bad. And rocky in certain parts. We spent the most of the time in the cave focussing on the rough/uneven ground rather than the place - in order not to slip or fall. One can easily slip or fall on the widespread/rocky uneveness here & darkness if you looked up rather than down ;& get sprained ankles or worse injuries if you fall.Do not recommend children, elderly or physically disadvantaged people to visit this cave or any caves.Frankly, we were not keen to see yet another cave but since it was part of our paid day tour, why waste it?

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.

We had a hard time locating the exact spot and drove around a few times. It was also a foggy day which made it worse. When we finally reached the sign that shows the start point, we tried to see if the car would defy gravity but it didn't. We tried twice. It was really a short stretch of road and we gave up. Sad. Perhaps we should go with a guide next time.

We had a fine time on Udo Island, where we rented one of the funny little electric cars and were able to see most of the island. It's better to arrive earlier in the day then we did, so you can spend time enjoying that Charming Island. Another highlight was feeding the seagulls with chips you can buy for $2 on the ferry.

We booked a 2 day private tour with Core Travel and it was awesome. It was highly flexible and we could customise it according to our preferences. The tour was done with a comfortable clean MPV and they were considerate to enquire if we needed a baby seat as we had a 10 month old baby with us. Our guide June was extremely polite and accommodating and very patient with us even though we were quite slow at times as we had older adults and a young baby in our small group. She was knowledgeable and explained all the geological processes that formed the various natural sites in Jeju that we visited. She went over the time of the tour and still assured us it was OK even though we felt bad that we couldn’t end the tour on time. She was kind and made suggestions that took into consideration our traveling requirements. One of the highlights was how she shared that she loved watching dolphins off one of the western coasts in Jeju and she drove us there when we expressed that we had not seen dolphins before. We were fortunate that we managed to catch a glimpse of dolphins jumping and playing in the sea before our eyes. If you are travelling to Jeju, it is highly recommended to book with Core Travel, especially more so if you have young kids or old folks as a private tour is so much relaxing and flexible. From booking to finish, the entire process with Core Travel was so efficient and easy. Ask for Guide June, she is the best!

Very interesting display of modern and old teddy bears. Take the time to see the Elvis Presley gig in the theatre! A bit pricey and as most museums on Jeju is quite small, but worth it on a rainy day.

Very commercialized tour spot in Jeju island. I visited this place a few days ago. I have been travel Jeju island tens of times but this is first time to visit this village and realized this place for selling someting to tourist. If you come to this village, just look around and don't enter the house. There are a lot of good spots you can see in Jeju island

Very beautiful place. Nice people, peaceful place. I want to come next time to visit it once more. We took photo with the founder of this garden. He is very nice person. In the garden you can see bansai trees and feed fishes, also there are some mini shops and cafe were you can drink coffee or the legendary rice wine.

Using Mr.Kang service for 2 days. He is very very nice and helpful. We gave our itinerary and he will drive for us. He is very nice and even gave us a bunch of orange.. my father love it very much. This is my first time in jeju. He even took good picture for my family too. He is very nice, i recomend you for using his service. Thank you Mr.Kang and see you again :)

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.
This was fun to check out. If you have time to pass, then I would recommend this place. Especially if you have kids, they'll love it here. Lots to read and lots to see.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!
This place was pretty kool, and it's great to take the kids there. I wouldn't say it would be a lost if you didn't have time to go here. Unless you really want to see teddy bears...

This place is truly one of a kind! The garden is immaculate and shows many years of hard work, patience and love.The story of the garden itself is worth the visit but the tranquility and peace this place brings is truly astonishingWe were also fortunate enough to spend some time with Director Sung, the creator of the garden. His passion and wisdom is beyond measure and this place is a must see for both locals and visitorsI cannot recommend this place enough and look forward to visiting again

this place is free and located nearby airport. it won't take too much time also, spend around 1hrs here.Sometimes u can see the airplanes landed as the background..kinda cool..the dragon-shaped rock is visible if u take picture with the right angle, otherwise it's just an ordinary rock.

This park has 9 different areas to visit, including a cave region, a bonsai section and a traditional Korean village.  This will take some time to see all of this, but is well worth the visit.  It is on the west side of the island, and near some nice beaches.

This market sells many products either fashionable clothes and branded cosmetics. There're many food shops available with reasonable place too. If you are seeking for sport shoes or toys.You can also find here. Some shops will give you the tax refund and some not.You need to check carefully. The famous cosmetic shops like ETUDE and skin food, some of famous items may not available. There're 11 gates which the even gate no. will locate on the right whereas the odd ones are on the left. It's not complicated and easy to walk. There's restroom available too.If you don't buy the well known brand, you will also find the local Korean cosmetic brand which is very cheap. I buy 12 hand creams with 10,000 won prize and can get the complimentary mask for 10 sheets. It's very good price. The souvenir shop also available here.I would also recommend to come as the choice of your shopping since it's not too crowded like duty free building and you don't need to buy a lot of same items in pack like duty free. As most of Korean cosmetics in duty free would be sold in pack of more than 2 pieces which sometimes you don't need that much.
This is the special place, have more glass decoration. But the decoration almost look old. if you have time you can go to see.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is one of the must see in Jeju. The most beautiful rocky beach in Jeju. Hamel ship (copy) is on beachside. You can check some pics on TripAdvisor. Spring season is high season.  Summer season is also high season, but check if typhoon is near. Check the typhoon, you cannot go close beach if there is typhoon. It is not normal beach, waves carved this beach for long time, hundreds of thousands of years.

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is not a cave, this is a lava tube so do not expect what you see in caves.  The tube is huge in size.  From the entrance you are able to walk 1km.  At the end you can see the remains of where lava had gone up and out of the tube.  It is not very impressive.  The tube itself is a large tunnel like structure.  There is not much to see and the lighting is a bit insipid.  The good thing is that the entrance fee is only like $2 so you don't need to worry about wasting money.  I am glad I visited but I would have been happy to have just walked down into the tube about 5 minutes, turned around and left.  Walking to the end of the open area is unnecessary and a bit of wasting time.  Spend about 10 minutes and its enough.

This is more of an   immersion   into what it was like to be in the earliest times of this culture. It is self guided and HUGE. You can literally wander through each hut and barn, use traditional tools, and play the children's games. You can make it take all day, or less... again a self-paced   see what you want   kind of place!

This is a must-see in Jeju city. It is a local market where they offer souvenirs, food, food, and more food. It is very different to anything I know from central Europe (not the market itself, but the offered food). Note: strong smell to spices and seafood. We bought a stone grandfather in one of the shops, which was offered for two to four (!!) times the price at touristic spots. Here, we found the cheapest price. No idea if tourists still pay a higher price, but we were fine with it (20000 KRW for a ~30cm stone grandfather).

This is a good location you should spend time to visit, nice and you can see some different kind of cave, some of the cave have spotlight follow so amazing. friendly reminder, please wear a shoes instead of slipper or sandals because the floor very wet.

This is a cute collection of teddybears and other stuffed animals in a variety of settings (a castle, a safari, etc.), but it's not what I was expecting with the name   Teseum   (teddy+museum).  There's a very small display of older teddybears (mostly photographs), but the main attraction is the displays you can see in the pictures.  There must be thousands here, ranging in size from one inch or shorter to probably eight feet tall. I imagine kids would be in hog heaven, but some of the older people in our tour group said it was a waste of time.  My favorites were the safari and the teddybear versions of old paintings.

This is a big park where you get to sample the attractions seen in Jeju . We enjoyed visiting the folk museum, flower and bonsai garden, Jeju stone park as well as the place where they have big palm trees. Our time was limited so we didn't really stay here for long.

this is  rare chance to walk down lava tubes and look at the odd shapes and formations caused by the molten rock. You can see different layers of lava that once flowed here and see how the laval squeezed through smaller passages.   Consider bringing an umbrella or a very light shell. It can be damp and sometimes water drips from the ceilings. Also, it's significantly cooler than outside.   All in all, a must.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

they charge admission now to see this seashore.  as if that's not bad enough, it was closed by the time we arrived at 5pm.  but what wasn't closed were the numerous vendor stands that seemingly sprung up to cash in on the tourists here.  the most interesting thing we noticed were various coconuts with small holes drilled in them with a straw sticking out.  this is supposed to be 'fresh' coconut water.  protip: there are no coconuts in korea.  superprotip: they re-use these containers without rinsing them out, over days/months/years, you get the idea.if you don't mind paying to see this 'natural wonder,' at least avoid the vendor stands like the plague, cause that's what you'll likely catch there.

They call this place because it looks like dragon's head. There is walking area around that stones so you can see that from the right beneath. But at that time of we are there, path is closed due to bad waves.

There was so much to see and do, and the actual burning of the hill is spectacular. I spent half a day there and hadn?t seen everything. The thing to be aware of is the time it can take to get out of the car park afterwards, but totally worth it !

There is nothing much to see except of the cave. But if you spend time to read and understand the formation of the cave. Its quite educational for me.You will be more enjoyed if you slows down your steps and admiring the unique walls in the cave. Instead just walk, walk and walk until the end and took picture of the end of the cave then went back.

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.
There are a number of waterfalls in Jeju, but only one deserves your time. It's amazing to see just how close the water flows directly to the sea.

The waterfall is not as impressive as it was advertised and there is an admission fee.Frankly, I don't think they should charge for admission as there is really nothing to do except to see the waterfall. If you have time to spare, visit other attractions.

The water here is gorgeous! For some reason, the sand was all covered up (strange) but we still had a nice time sightseeing. It was too cold for anything else! Lots of restaurants and places to stay. We stayed at the Beach Story Hotel, which was nice and cheap since no one was around!

The Spirited Garden is a great pastime to spend with friends, the garden is beautiful! There is so much plant life to see with a rich cultural and historical story behind each part of the garden! Plenty of great photo-ops here for your social media or if you are big fan of botany you will definitely enjoy it.

The professional photos are very well taken thus I was quite interested in this place before i go. But basically you will spend perhaps a good 20 to 25 mins walking from one end to another end seeing the same thing (unless you are very interested in rocks or stones) in very dark lighting.. and then another 20 to 25 mins back. I don't think its a bad place.. just not to my liking i guess. If you have time and a good camera and a tripod, you might take some very nice photos there lol

The place is good only for families with little children.Kids will be excited about the fact that a  car(or bottle) seems to go up on downhill. However, for adults? Not really...If u have plenty of time to spend on the road.

The park is big and have many to see, especially for people who don't know the culture of Jeju. It would be also good for family but since it requires lots of walks I wouldn't recommend elder people who can't walk for a long time. The weather of the day we went wasn't quite good, but the drizzle and fog made that place more mysterious which is quite special because we saw different type of scenery from those pictures you can find from the Internet.

The park is a it run down and not well maintained. Although the park is big, but there is nothing really big and great. There was a signboard (even on the brochure) stating there is white peacock but we see none. Flowers are dying (perhaps it's because of winter starting soon?) Feel a bit disappointed. I would advice you to plan this in your itinerary if you really have a lot of time as it take quite sometime to go to this park and entrance fees is not cheap.

The Mysterious Road is a little bit overrated I guess. Its just a road that has an optical illusion. You cannot really see the different it makes also. So, I would say it's just average place to visit here if you have extra time.

The grounds are HUGE! It felt like a nature forest walk, a geography and history field trip all rolled into one.I don't know if it's windy there all the time, but when we were there, it was freezing when the wind blew when we were in the shade.We had a tour guide who explained the various rock features and how/why people carved the stones for use in the past. But honestly, I was bored after awhile. This place had rocks/stones galore. Considering that there are so many other things to see/do in Jeju, I would give this place a miss.

The greenhouse structure and the design of the gardens were very nice.? However, it seemed that the staff was having trouble keeping up with it.? It may be just a bad time of year for them.? Still well worth the admission fee.

The dragon head rock is in North part of Jeju, close to the airport. It is a rock that looks like a dragon head on the coast. The Seogwipo coast line like the Jusanjeolli Cliff or the Odelgae Rock are much more interesting than this. However, if you do not have time to visit the Jungmun/Seogwipo area, this is an alternative to see the rocky coastline. The sunset here is nice, but the place is packed with tourists fighting to get photos, so it's not all that romantic. I think a beach sunset at a more remote beach on the West side would be nicer and a calmer experience.
the destination is built by legend about dragon who fall from the earth, as tourist object not much to see. it's nature rock, beach and on autum the weather is nice. no need much time

The cliffs are a real sight to visit. You can see the nice natural rock formations, and the beautiful blue sea in the background. A really beautiful and peaceful place which we were told transform itself during the different seasons. There is a 'resident' painter who is there the whole year round and he captures the beauty of the place in all seasons and during different times of the day.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

The bridge during night time was nice. I saw this on the plane from Seoul to Jeju. At first I came to see the sea next to it, but then I suddenly saw the bridge and thought it looked beautiful. It really brightens up the dark.

The best waterfall to visit! Don't waste time to other waterfall, this is the best one. I managed to see rainbow at the waterfall was simply amazing! Made the whole trip worthwhile! Just wear the right shoes there as there are some rocks to walk on before getting close to the waterfall

The best parts about this tour were the walk from the main road where you can admire the cherry blossom on both sides of the road and the newly opened Angel-In-Us coffee house. If not for the springtime cherry blossoms, there doesn't seem to be much else to see.
The admission to this waterfall for adults is 2000KW. It was very overcrowded, which caused the time to be rushed. Worth seeing, but come early in the morning to beat the crowds.

Tested on the car that we rented~N Gear and the car really move up slope~Tried it with water too, but did not see the effect~Not too sure if it cos the sky is dark~ Go at night if you rent a car~ Can reverse the car as many times as you want~

Stay in touch with nature and culture with this big park. Take time to appreciate the caves and read about the stories. I especially like the bonsai park. During spring, make sure to check out the rape seed canola flower beds and the cherry blossom trees on bloom.

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

So we are sat in the car, put on neutral mode and the car actually moved! This is a really cool experience and it only takes a minute to do- I have seen mysterious roads on the travel channel before but this was my first time doing it- if you find yourself on Jeju island check it out!

So much fun!  I've been twice and would like to go back very soon.  In the spring, tulips everywhere!  So many different things to do and see here.  I fed the birds this time around and what joy.Note that some animals were not in the best shape (summer heat maybe).

Second time visiting the maze. The kids loved the maze as did the adults. We broke up into single groups to try to time each other on who can get through the maze the fastest. this would only work on a non-crowded day! Ran through the maze a few times to beat each other's time and then broke into groups (kids vs adults) to see who could get through the fastest. Great time in the fall, as it is a reminder of the corn mazes in the states.

Really beautiful little island off another beautiful island.Great for a an afternoon or day visit and easy to travel. We went by ferry and got ourselves a scooter to travel around the island as we were short on time. Was really fun to use the scooter, probably the highlight of the island.But made us see the place quickly and so many places to eat! The people were really nice too and would visit again.

Real value for money being able to see he best of Jeju in the short time we had on the island. Our tour guide, Jin, was excellent and walked us through the itinerary adding in stories about the history of the island and his own experiences. Highly recommended.

quite near with my hotel but seem that was commercial food street with not so many food shop. we walk around 2-3times & try to select reasonable & maybe good service also tasty one. finally, we selected one of only Korean & English spoken restaurant. lucky that was ok.

Perhaps it was the time of day we were here. We got here really early around 8am to start our road trip down the east side of Jeju Island. So nothing was open yet. We saw the dragon rock and even walked down the side of the small cliff to see the rock from a different angle. It was raining quite a bit on the morning we visited so the walk down was a little slippery. It was interesting to see the dragon rock formation and read about it's significance in Korean folklore. We had a photo with the mermaid there too. Unfortunately due to the time of day we visited nothing else was open, but from what we could tell there were mainly souvenir, fruit and convenient stores and stalls. Worth a visit if you have time, but essentially a nice looking rock

Parking is free, next to Osulloc. The ajusshi will be there to direct you in the carpark. Lovely place. I love Innisfree products and im happy to be there. However, there are only skincare products, no makeup items. There is an area for soap-making but we didnt do it. During the time we visited, noone did it too, so i cant comment how interesting it is.There is also an area which you could do ink stamping on paper. If you like ink stamping, do remember to bring some paper along. Its free.The food is organic and took quite some time to prepare. So the best is to find a table first, order your food and then do your retail shopping. We ordered 4 drinks & 2 meals, it took about 20-30 mins to be done. Yes, its that long.There are also desserts and they are made beautifully. How i wish i still have the stomach space for them. I would just come back to have tea and dessert at the place. Dont forget to look at their   Jeju only   products. There is innisfree Hallabong jam and strawberry jam. Yup, jam for bread. So look closely at the retails. The price of the retail items are comparable to those in Seoul, so need not get them unless you desperately need it. Go for their   jeju only   items instead.There is a small tea planatation outside Innisfree, where most is seen taking OOTD. Toilets are behind Innisfree.

Our visit to Jeju Island for a wellness retreat was organized by Core Travels who did an amazing job. They were accommodating, flexible warm and kind and did their best ensure we had the best time possible. From the local food experience, the sightseeing and the transport it was all amazing.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands.On our free day we visited Dongmun Market which we thought was a better option than spending so much time in the shopping centers. Haenyeo literally means, 'Women of the Sea' and this museum pays tribute to the historical significance of this dying profession.  Solely carried on the backs of women on this island, these incredible ladies have carried their over 400 year old craft into the 21st century where instrumentally built the economic foundation for many of the Jeju natives.  Mothers who passed on their skills and knowledge of the sea to their daughters ensured that this lineage would endure the centuries of time.  However, as the world faces rapid changes and economies - the Haenyeo divers are slowly becoming a ghost of the past.  Recently recognized as an UNESCO intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016, tremendous efforts are in place to preserve this historical tradition.  A bonus of a visit to this museum is a trip to Sunrise Peak where there is a traditional Haenyeo performance.  (admission fee required)However - enroute to Sunrise Peak is the opportunity to meet a handful of Haenyeo divers!  What a thrill to visit with them in their modern 'bulteok' - warming huts.  Of all the sights of Jeju - this is perhaps the one that represents the very backbone of this amazing culture!This is definitely a 'must see'

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.
