A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A nice botanic garden with interesting elements. I particularly like the bonsai garden with lots of areas to sit and admire the specimens. Since we only had a very limited time, we were not able to see the other areas.

A fantastic show a must see in Jeju. Lots of laughs and you don't need to understand Korean. We brought our tickets at the show, which was full by the time of opening. They were very talneted actors. The show has been done in numerous countries around the world

Walk around the mountain and you can see different rock formations.  The water is very clear (look at the picture as if there is no water) that you can see sea urchins. I advise you wear rubber shoes to be more comfortable walking through sharp rock formations.

It was a beautiful mountain as tree leaves were changing colors.  And there was many many people who came to sightseeing from all over the country & some foreign countries. The weather was perfect as well.

Absolutely beautiful place - a must-see-experience if you go to Jeju. Amazing what nature can create and then its just next to a mountain and a small temple with a giant gold-Buddha. Go see this asap! :)

This place of interest is beside the beach and not far from the airport. It is a volcanic stone due to many years under the sun, water and wind which erode the stone and form this dragon head. It is also up to individuals to creatively imagine the head.There are also many tales about this dragon head - one about the Dragon king is sick and young son went up the high mountain to seek the eternal medicine for the father. After getting the medicine, he was discovered by the protection god who was angry of his act and use lighting to strike him resulting in this burnt head.

It is a volcanic rock formation in the form of a dragon?s head, created by strong winds and waves over thousands of years. However, legend has it that a dragon stealing precious jade from Mt. Halla was shot down by an arrow from the mountain deity. When he fell down on Yongduam, his body immediately sank into the ocean and his head rapidly froze looking at the sky. Another legend has it that a white horse dreamt of being a dragon and ascending to the sky. On his ascent, he was caught by a soldier and froze into the rock. While admiring the dragon?s head, one can see how the black rocks contrast with the emerald blue ocean.

If you love the sea, sand, mountain and great scenery, you will need to make a day trip to Udo!  You can take a ferry to Udo from Seongsan Harbour.  I highly recommend that you rent a car in Jeju and drive that over to Udo as there are so much to see and do in a single day.  You can drive your car up onto the ferry to Udo.

If you like tiking , I think you will like here! And you will see the layer of stone at the mountain. Don't forget to test very fresh seafood!! Eat like sasemi of Japanese food. And there has coffee shop as Starbuck , Dunkin donut too!

We got a very nice tour from a local resident who spoke fairly good English.  It was very interesting to see how the huts were designed and the durability of the thatch roofs.  There was a sales pitch to buy some locally made tea and other products (which were very expensive) but no one bought anything.  You would think that they would figure out international tourists wouldn't be buying any kind of drinks to bring back home.

Very Nice place to understand and enjoy Jeju in South Korea. There is old story that a women had been waited for her husband who was fisherman.  She became the rock statue(Oeidolgae) because her husband couldn't come back home while fishing sunk by windstorm.  Also another point of sightseeing is beautiful beach with rocks. There is beach of rocks in this region.   You may see pics in TripAdvisor.  Atlas Dream.

This little folk village was located right next to our hotel (Haevachi) so we figured we should check it out.  We were spoiled because we had just gone to the folk village and that is the bomb!It is only about $8 for admission and then we opted for the audio tours.  Most of the written signs are not in English so I'm glad we had the audio tours but they didn't work very well.  They are tripped by some sort of sensor when you go by but mine kept skipping back to the original message ugggg.It's a very large complex but somehow unauthentic feeling.  I thought the neatest part was the artisans that sell their crafts.  That was cool and they do have a nice gift shop.  It was very hot out so we went through fairly quickly.  If it hadn't been so hot we might have spent much longer just exploring.If this is your only opportunity to see such a thing then I would visit but if you have the chance to see the folk village in Seoul then I would wait for that one!
This beach is very beautiful.You can see red and orange color beach on evening.I want to comeback this beach.There are many pub and hostel and food-court.
There's really nothing much to see for a museum but the cafe is good for a tea break and the green tea plantation is a nice backdrop for photo taking if the weather is good

There is a big signage in Korean at the entrance next to the ticketing booth which we didn't apprehend  but the window of the ticketing booth was blocked with wood and when we moved to the back of the premises  we found back doors not closed and things which seemed to be exhibits were scattered on the backyard.

There are so much to see in this museum. The whole day is enough to spend here if you want to read and appreciate all the displays. Good collections. I learned a lot from this museum. I regret doing four museum tours in one day for we had to rush this one. I would love to go back here.

People generally come here for the green tea and buying tea products. It's the best green tea I've tasted in the whole of Korea. And triumphs Malaysia's also. Their cakes dessert are just so good and you have tons of tea products to choose fromThose who like to see tea plantation can also come here to take pictures otherwise just sit back relax and enjoy green tea

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Osulloc tea is known as one of the more famous and reliable brand in Jeju...most of the tea is expensive too. Thus it is not uncommon for travel agencies to include the Osulloc green tea museum into its itinerary. A walk around the museum shows you a little background of tea in particular. You can also be able to see tea cups from different countries on display. I tried the green tea ice cream and it was yummy. We were told that if we spend more than 30000 won we can get a tax refund at the airport. So we really spent more than 30000 won on tea :) I wandered alone out of the tea museum and saw Innisfree!!! They were conducting some soap making lesson when I walked in. The deco is very different from what I saw in the malls. And of course I ended up buying stuffs....some facial masks that I wasn't able to find in Singapore.

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

Just got back from Jeju and was talked into doing another submarine tour. I did one near the Ilchulbong Peak and wasn't keen on another one. But this tour was a bit longer and had more marine life. I recommend this tour and also in the same town you can go out in a boat for sightseeing or fishing cheaply.

Jeju National Museum is set almost in the middle of nowhere -- well it's beside an adult theme park but otherwise literally nowhere. Had a car so it wasn't tough to find but would be extremely tough using public transport.The museum and the garden that surrounds it is well sterile... for the lack of a better term. Beautiful but seems to lack any personality... it's quiet laid back and perfect for a long walk... but not much action.

It's supposed to be one of the seven winders of nature but not exactly my kind of travel destination. It's amazing for the sheer length of the cave (7km) although you are only allowed to go to the first km. We only managed to go 300 m since there wss not much to see except for molten rocks along the cave. There was not much to sustain interest in going further inside the cave so we decided to just go back. At least it was cool inside although the path was wet but nit muddy. Wear comfortable and non slippery shoes if you wish to see the cave.
It was amazing! One seemed to be on a uphill yet the car was moving backwards. And vice versa. Try using an empty water bottle (cylindrical in shape) to test it out as well.

There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.

If your a fan of everything green tea like my daughter is this is a great place to visit extensive gift shop and resteraunt selling everything you can imagine from the company great background n pics of the history of the place and outside see tea fields and sculptures.

During our visit to Jeju Island I fell in love with the Hareubang statues.  They are all over the Island a unique distinguishing statue you will see everywhere you look.  I had many pictures taken while standing next to one of these great statutes!  The Dolharbang Park was full of ancient statues many dating back to the 20th century.Dol means stone and Hareubang means grandfather So Dolharbang means stone grandfather.  In gift shops you can even buy small Hareubang statues keychains chocolates perfume bottles...to take home for a happy memory

a nice place to visit. walk around the green tea farm to see the green tea trees visit the gallery to understand the background and history of tea buy the tea products at the retail shop enjoy the tea at the cafeteria. there is an Innisfree Cafe next door also which is a must visit place to enjoy the soap making process and enjoy the food and drink where I had the best yam drink I had ever tasted!

We just stumbled across this attraction when visiting somewhere else. There was quite a few people there and people seemed to be very interested in the mysterious road. Our visit to this village was an amazing experience! We learned a lot about the history Jeju, specifically their culture and traditions. My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

DRAMA WORLD is consist of DRAMA STUDIO, TEDDY BEAR and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE. Drama studio is an indoor exhibition hall with a floor area of 5,000 square meters. Drama studio is actual TV drama studio and restored studio in KOREA, USA and EUROPE, in which the visitors can experience all costumes and accessories for free(except HANBOK, Wedding dress). Our exhibition is consist of town(street) studio and interior studio. Our exhibition is consist of Korean studio(K-DRAMA) and World studio(USA,EUROPE DRAMA). Visitors of all age groups can experience KOREA culture, Western(USA) culture and The Middle ages(EUROPE) culture through DRAMA STUDIO. We are the first experiment-type drama studio in Korea where the visitors wear the costumes and use the articles to be the main character in dramas. ※ Now, World Studio is consist of TEDDY BEAR EXHIBITION and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE with a background of Western and The Middle ages studio. Collaboration between DRAMA WORLD and TEDDY BEAR. TEDDY BEAR Exhibition Hall’s floor area is about 1,000 square meters. At DRAMA WORLD, visitors can see TEDDY BEAR, which produced scenes in drama of Korea, USA and Europe. Visitors can easily understand the scene of drama. Because the text(Chinese, English, Korean)is placed in each display of TEDDY BEAR. Visitors can take a picture with man-sized TEDDY BEAR using props and wearing costume for free. Visitors can learn about the Self-Wedding culture of Korea through the Wedding photo zone with a background of drama studio. Visitors can take a picture in wedding photo zone on studio of the Western Age in USA, the Middle Ages in Europe and Korea’s drama. In each Wedding photo zone, wedding accessories are placed. And they are available for free.

did not really go down to the beach as it was raining and need to pay to see the 'dragon head'. there's a small shipwreck museum which is good rainy day activity, nice for a free museum. like the yellow canola flower field at the parking area with sanbangsan at background. didn't went up sanbangsan due weather as well.

Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

review: Went to hyeopjae beach just to try swimming while i was in Jeju. Rented a car and drove there, thought that parking was gonna be a challenge but managed to get one in mere minutes. They guy attending to the rental didn't speak english, thank God for a local young chap who helped us translate.Loved the vibe of the beach, everyone there was enjoying the waves. We were very excited that our trip coincided with the market. This is my favorite place whenever I go to Jeju. You can walk up to the peak for forty minutes where you can see the East Sea of Jeju. From there, you can leave for Cow Islet on a cruise, another destination in Jeju. This place is famous for beautiful sunrises.

The cone-dome architecture is interesting, the roofs of different gardens within culminates to a peak into the center of the compound and u can take a lift up to catch a 360 panoramic glimpse of the surroundings (see pic). However, adult tix are at 9000krw per person which is not cheap for what u get within. The place has lots of potential but not that well-maintained as the place looks very weathered on the whole. There is a garden dedicated to tropical fruits but those are mostly common fruits for southeast Asians like us. There were only chrysanthemums at the entrance even though it's supposed to be in-season. Parking is easy though, and free, like most places of interests at Jeju. Overall, this place is more suitable for the elders and for people dropping by to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and Seonimgyo Bridge, which is just next door. Otherwise, my 2c worth - it'll be fine to spend your money elsewhere.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is the most eastern part of Jeju Island and has the same terrain as Punchball. When you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, you can see the beautiful sea and clear sky endlessly, and when you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with a cool breeze, you feel good. Also, there are many tourist attractions nearby, so it is convenient to move around. In addition, there are many restaurants that cook braised kingtail fish and roast caught in Jeju, and there are many unique and delicious restaurants around. I recommend that you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with your family at least once.

Not as touristy or crowded like Sunrise Peak. Walk to the crater was on the milder side, not too much steps.Leisurely romantic walk pass the fields of silver grass (graminee) which can only be seen late September to November. Some parts have swings for you to sit and enjoy the breeze. The crater was covered completely with vegetation and the nearby green hills was a picture of serenity and you feel removed from urban cityI wouldn't mind coming again. Near ticket area, there's a stall selling the sausage sticks that were flavorful and yummy.

My husband didn't want to go to this, but during the entire trip, the word 'mysterious' really peaked my curiosity so while he wasn't paying attention, I drove us to this 'mysterious road'. I didn't want to keep wondering after I left Jeju! I mean, It's got to be impressive if there are all these street signs, and they even have a food stand named after it right? Wrong!It was so anti-climatic, so short(1 minute?) and so stupid. Probably one of the dumbest attractions I have ever seen. Nothing mysterious or special about it. If you are disappointed, don't say I didn't warn ya.

Most people or tour guides will recommend you to go there for the seafood. However, the stall owners cannot speak other languages. The ones who do speak Chinese are too touristy. Those that sell abalone don't sell fish and vice versa. Better to go to a good restaurant for a taste of seafood stew. Fruits are ok. The good mandarin oranges are sold in boxes. I see locals buying boxes of oranges.

Knowns also as Sunrise Peak. We went there on afternoon as we did not know this place  can see beautiful sunrise. Must visit place when you in Jeju Island. Worthwhile hiking by stairs about 45 minutes. This wonderful craters formed from volcanic eruption l00,000 years ago. Entrance Ticket KRW2000. Twice a day can see women divers go to the sea and singing before catch their seafood such as abalone, sea urchin, etc. Overthere you can ride pony horses

I went to Udo with a group of friends. It was really nice, we went around the island with rented bicycles (10.000 KRW for the afternoon). We swam in an incredibly clear water.I recommend going to Sunrise peak afterwards, walking along the coast gets you there in 15 min and seeing the sunset was an amazing experience.

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.

Even in peak season Sehwa Beach didn?t have nearly as many visitors as some of the more popular northeast Jeju beaches mainly because most of it is covered in volcanic rocks.  We actually weren?t even sure it was a beach at first.  We did see a handful of people in the water who had sidestepped all the volcanic rocks but most seemed happy taking photos standing on the rocks.  Cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores line the beach and all were good spots to admire the nice scenery of the beach.  For actually going in the water, the other popular beaches are more popular for that reason.

A very small traditional village attraction with free guide who can speak Mandarin. Very limited traditional houses to look at. No big deal. The attraction is apparently made famous by a TV series that filmed there. Nothing much to see but the guide took great efforts in explaining about each mini-attraction in the village. We ended up in a hut being given explanations on the local products they were selling (e.g. local honeys, herbal health drinks, horse bone powder, horse creams). We were not forced to buy but given that the tour was free, we were obliged to buy stuff that we could easily find for lower prices as the markets, especially Dongmun Traditional Markets in Jeju City.

A tiring long walk but well-worth the workout as you get to soak in the beautiful green slops of the peak, and the ocean blue waters below. Lots of photo opportunities, and you also get to see the jet ski in the waters below.

A country is evaluated by its culture and only in a province of Jeju in South Korea that we visited many many museum. They are about arts, life and musics. This museum is to introduce the life of the divers in Haenyeo. Very interesting to see the divers reanimated in small scenes very real. The tour guide here could speak English, not very fluently but that?s the best English speaking tour guide in Jeju we?ve met.

Very disappointing. There were a few panels in the entrance hall that had information about chocolate and very poorly kept display boxes  but everything was only in Korean. Downstairs  you can see chocolate packages from different countries  but mostly ordinary products that can be bought in Korean supermarkets. No effort was given to make a proper display with special chocolates. Plus  some chocolates were mislabeled under the wrong countries. There was a station where chocolates in bags could be squeezed into molds. I was not able to participate because the staff panicked when they saw a non-Korean face  despite the fact that I spoke Korean to them. Do yourself a favor and go in the convenience store across the road - there is a better display of chocolate there.

This is like any other market in Korea. Cheap shopping for clothes  bags  food and souvenirs. If haven't visited one of these markets  then I would go just to have the experience. Otherwise not a must see.

The Stadium is closed almost all the week long except when a match is there  no visits are allowed inside  may be because that was in winter. The nice thing is that you can picture it from outside inside in  and a nearby small shops community & large e-Market place to shop & eat in their food-court. Nice play ground area around to check & may be to practice for free  you can see the local folks play around with some apparatuses  and machines to fit up

Located next to dongmun and jungang underground market so you can combine all three in one go. Not much to see and shop. You will probably eat in dongmun. We took dinner at the end of the street in a Japanese restaurant and was really good food. Jeju has a small population and do not really expect much shopping I could not find a memory card for my camera :-(
It's fun to walk around in the market and see all the different things.A lot of fish and other thinfs out of the sea are available alibe or dried.Great atmosphare in there!
It's a great place to visit and see what Local people eat here. The fishes are fresh and the place is clean. You can also buy Jeju souvenirs in this market.

Interesting place. Lots of Tangerine in boxes as gifts and many stalls sell snacks and souveniors.Is also a wet market where you see fresh produce. Not forgetting display of pig heads can be found in serveral stalls. Can visit for the experience.

In this market you can get to see and experience various things. I spent 2-3 hr and had dinner here. There is one segment selling seafood and preserved food. Another segment selling snacks and souvenirs. My dinner was at the row of street side hawker that only open from 6pm onwards. The food is delicious and well priced. But don?t expect clean and nice place to sit and have your food. This is no 5 star street hawker.
You can find everything and anything there, local fruits andveggies are excellent and cheap and you'll see an authentic Jeju market where Locals go to shop.

When we visited, oranges are everywhere! They did not seen to have varieties of fruits sold here. Everyone were selling the same type of fruiys and candies, which are pretty much boring! There were some food stalls and those selling fresh seafood and fish and meat too.Typical of a market. It is a big place though. We explore only two rows and detour.

We enjoyed walking through the colorful Dongmun Jeju market but the prices were very high, especially when they see Westerners, Chinese or Japanese. We later spoke to our hotel and they said the price is almost doubled for foreigners. We had a simple raw seafood dinner for four and it costs each person USD$44.00. We had no liquor (beer, wine, etc). So enjoy the colorful scenery but if you want to eat there be ready to pay a high price.

Very big market. Combination of a wet and dry market. Interesting cos they sell many live seafood, vegetables, fruits, sourvenir.The seafood seems expensive when i convert but it could be cos more for tourists. A fish can be $50. We enjoy eating the local food like cuttle fish, fish cake, fish ball, crab stick. About $4 to $7. Just immerse in local culture. The colouful array of oranges and by oroducts. 15 boxes orange chocolate for 10k won. Looks alot but one box only 8 pcs candies so bulky to carry.There is a store sells korean sourvenir like keychain, clipper, magnet, etc $3 to 5 a piece.Bought a sweatpants 5k won so less than $10.Did not dare buy hallabong oranges cos too heavy to carry home. More for local tourists.Overall we do enjoy this market. Near to the underground shopping and fashion street too.

Though Dongmun turns to commercial rather for local market, its interesting to see the rich supply of seafood in Jeju. If you know Mandarin, you can communicate with the food stall owners. Quite smelly and dirty, which is expected.

This is an awesome place to go with street sights and photography in mind, with all the locals and tourist here collectively, lots of items to see, and nearby jungang underground market. Visiting both, seems to be the smart thing to do. Interesting place but of course it is still a market.

There are lots of seafood you can choose from at this market. Also, we liked how there are tons of international flags hanging around. But most of all, you gonna see mandarins of all sorts and kinds, even mandarin chocolate and even cookies.

Our FIRST meal in JEJU and we were just spoilt for choices. This is traditional market and we had so much fun walking in the market.The large boxes of tangerines greets you at the entrance and as you explore further, you see endless rows of fresh seafood. We randomly selected some food and they tasted delicious!

Other than just a seafood market, there are lots of seafood restaurants serving very fresh seafood. Do check them out.Lots of shops selling their Jeju hallabong chocolates and we found them to be cheapest here.Very interesting market to see traders selling traditional Korean food and side dishes.
It is one of the good markets to see around. Very neatly maintained and you can find various types of seafood, pickles and fruits.

It is an ideal place to buy souveniors and see/taste the local food.  Rather clean even we went inside the fish and vegetable market.  Along we found few food stalls and restaurants to offer seafood, we were hesitated but decided to go for fish and cuttle fish sushimi in one with rather good environment, it's food and service were up to standard, price was not high compared to those in restaurant.  Interested to see local Kimchi, fish, fruits, herds, snacks from the stores
Is a nice market, a lot of things there. If so happen you can meet the day, then must go and see. clothes, vege, bird, fish, food, groceries bla bla bla.....

In this market you will see what Korean people eat usually in their daily lives. Oranges are everywhere and thry are pricy. They said the oranges are very nutritious and full of vitamins. The problem is we could not tell which stalls were genuine. At night, there were two rows of street food selling korean delicatessen. Check it out!

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

Every kind of locally caught fish and produce can be found in the Dongmun Market, as well as some imported items.  Don't miss out on getting a box of mandarins or Hallabong oranges.  Try the kiwifruit, too.  It's also a good place to sample Jeju's   street food   made by local vendors.  You can find all sorts of clothes and many household gadgets, accessories, rain shoes, Korean quilts, souvenirs...you name it, it's most likely in the market.  You can visit Dongmun during the day or at night.  Nearby, you can also see Sanjicheon Square, where local performers can also be found playing, singing or dancing for tips.  Some local seniors and maybe a few homeless persons frequent the area, adding to its   color.    The square is by a small tidal inlet, and features a quaint railing with traditional Korean characters on the railing.  Do check it out!

Came here in the evening to get dinner as well as to see what Dongmun Market was about.  With ample parking closed to the area, we entered via the night food market side.  The snacks sold here were very un-korean that largely appeals to the young family and the young.The market itself as expected were not all open, yet many stalls were. From Jeju Tangerines to chocolates and other local produce, it is still worth taking a look in the evening if u want to avoid the morning crowd.

Basically a market place that sells the usual basic seafood and fruits. Practically all the fruit stalls sell the same things; mango, Jeju mandarin orange, peaches, etc. Do try the peaches if they are in season. They are huge, soft and fragrant.A lot of stalls are selling the same Jeju chocolate, mandarin or Hallabong tea & jam, etc.There are several stores that sell street food like oden, teokbokki, sundae, etc. In fact there is one particular stall that seems to be very famous due to the Korean variety show 'Running Man'. There is a long queue by 5pm; with people waiting to get a table to try all their Korean snack food. The teokbokki, sundae and fried fritters are really good.Do try the Jeju orange ice cream on a stick if you come across them. They are really nice and fragrant; especially on a warm day.

As you are planning to visit jeju and there are not alot of activities there, i recommend you to visit this market. You will see lots of differnt and new things to see, also you can enjoy the food there, so dont miss it

actually we yet to go inside the museum but just walk around the street of LeeJoongSeop. not bad. however, seem that not too direct related to art but flea market or street market with some handmade stuff. if finish Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market, go here together if you like to buy something.btw, it has an old cinemas but seem already closed. we saw a band to do some rehearsal. one of artist maybe
You cannot see the water in the crater because its dry better to go there on Winter... But a must place to visit also when your in Jeju.

We drove past it on another parallel road and didnt realise how fun it was! So we made it a point to visit it and try it out before we returned the rental car. The speed went up to almost 20km/h! We didnt encounter any local motorists though there were some tourists placing water bottles to see them roll up the hill :)

Very popular tourist attraction (you know its popular when they have those cheesy fast speedboat tours on the water) but still worth the visit to see these unique shaped cliffs in the ocean if you are already in the area. Just a short simple walk along their boardwalk to see them so quite a short visit. Only 2000 Krw per adult to visit with kids under 4 free.
Very interseting to see our car moves uphill with the engine off. My tour guide explained the reason behind this but I still don't understand XD. Try to pour the water and the same thing happened.
Very atypical road. Strange to understand. Please take a bottle of water with you to see the mystery in action :) but do not spend more than 15 minutes here
U can Find all sports of planets there. Greenery every where. Can see Flowers from rachael seasons. The water gardens is beautiful. The bonsai trees are outstanding

Trip with friends to see underwater animals; sharks star fishes and other tortoise and outside aquarium full happiness with mini korean mart coffee and drinks and if you all like Korean food & beverages terrace

review: This waterfall truly was magnificent to see. I recommend going early in the morning (ticket office opens at 8:00 am). It was 8:30 am when I visited and there were a few people. At one point they all left and it was only me and the waterfall. Truly amazing. Definitely go before before all the tourists get there!!!

This waterfall is a poor second to the nearby Cheonjiyeon Falls. If you want to see everything Seogwipo has to offer then pay a visit but I much preferred the other falls for both the actual waterfall and the surrounding gardens that give you access to it.

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.

This is a three tiered waterfall. To see all three you must walk a lot of staircases. It is much smaller than what I thought but where it is quite beautiful. If in Jeju I recommend a visit(if you love the nature).

This is a large and well-kept temple by the water.There are 4 floors to visit and many murals and small statues to see. The large golden buddhas are impressive. You can take a mat and pray on the main floor or meditate in a second floor room.I spent a total of around 45 minutes at this site.

there's nothing much to do. just walk a bit and you see waterfall right down to the sea. they said this is the only one in Asia. i did spend few minutes here. people who love nature and photography will love it here.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The ocean waves against the beautiful volcanic rocks are just so amazing. The island is gorgeous and so much to see and do. We enjoyed going further down the beach to go into the water as well. The pineapple & tangerines are awesome.

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water
small & clean water but sand just so so. since cloudy so that the color not too significant but still well enough. one of jeju beach but i don't see quite much special on it.
Prepare umbrella or raincoat as water drips in the cave. It's amazing to see the rock formation and lava tubes. It's dark and the path is rocky and slippery so becareful.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.
Only waterfall in asia which falls in ocean.i was amazed.must must see.very high falling.entry fee 2000 won

My wife and I went to this place all of a sudden as We had no plan to cover this area. it is located in Jungmoon Resort area. the environment is like slience is spekaing everything. alongside the three water falls are awesome. Go and see.

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill
Just a road that seem to go against law of physics.Need a car to see how it roll uphill or maybe some water to see how the water flows.

Its winter now so there is no crowd at all except for the occassional photo maniacs. Beach and the clear blue water was out of this world but rubbish can be seen everywhere. My daughter went around picking up the rubbish cos it really did not do justice to the beauty.
It's so beautiful here and there are different type of boat for you to enjoy while seeing at the historical rocks clear water.

Its definitely one of the most impressive waterfall I have been to. Its only a 5 mins walk from the parking lot and you see this strong waterfall. The water was nicely cool. I wish I had my bathing suit with me.  Its a small area.. we only spent like 30 mins there.
It's beautiful but really cold. I dipped my foot in the water because I didnt see it ?? The water was so clear.. the sunset is soooo beautiful
Its a road with a convenience store beside it. Children would have fun to see how the water flows uphill but other then that not much else
It`s worth to see the waterfall going straight to the sea. Have good shoes - you'll need to walk on stones to get close to it.
It was huge and plenty to see. Especially if you have children. There are also different performances...like an aquarium showing women divers diving underwater.
