review: It was fun to see all cars and coaches slowed down completely with neutral gear to test the mysterious road. Some people did pour water onto the road and the effect was also very obvious.
It was a lucky day cause I could see the fall! A big one right after the rain. Normally there are no water falls but after heavy rain you can see this scenery!
It sets you with AWE where you could see the waterfall meeting the sea.  You could experience the good ion in the air and listening to the music of the sea.

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Make sure you carry rain coat or umbrella and have some warm clothese if you are not used to cold. The caves  has water dripping at place and its very cold even during the hot sun outside. We went there after noon and it was quite cold. Be careful while walking inside the cave and its slippery. Do read the story as you go through its. there is restaurant which server good korean food just outside the entrance which we felt was very good.
I seen waterfalls of over 70m so a 20m one is not so impressive but they did a really good job at making a nice park around it.
I don't like much the environment inside the cave. So much water dripped off and dark. Nothing much to see. I liked only the cooling temperature.
Good photo opportunity. Visit during high tide to see majestic falls flowing into the ocean.Visit during rainy season to see more water crashing down.

Amazing! Truly a sight to behold as the waters dash against the natural pillars. I am speechless to describe as I have never before seen this color of blue. A picture is worth more than a thousand words.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.
You can see wild grass and flower garden, caves, Jeju stones, folk village, bird garden, water garden and subtropical garden in the park.

Yes, you will able to see water bottle accend up the road without any force applied to it and when you switch off your car engine or shift to Neutral, your car still able to accend the inclining road. But after 10 minutes, you will be bored and it's only work a certain stretch of road only.
Worth seeing, and I liked that it was within walking distance of our hotel. The beach area was really pretty although it is not a place to go if you want a beach and not a waterfall.

When we arrived we were a little surprised at the ticket price to enter. There was quite a lot of steps to get down, as we walked down you can see the waterfall. when we got down to the rocks by the waterfall there was tons of people it was so crowded. but the waterfall was very beautiful and was very nice how it was all open without any barriers keeping you from the waterfall.

we visited this place with little or less expectation as many friends had said it too overrated but to our surprise is pretty awesome. Maybe because there was strong wind and rain the waves were very strong. The waves were hitting almost the observation point. We bought rain coat outside the cliff entrance for 2000wons (2$) and trust me its best decision we did. We were showered with water like anything as there was rain and wind. maybe in other season you dont need to worry aobut it. the phone number listed on site took to the parking lot the resort next to cliff, had to walk a bit to reach it but got to see the resort common area with some nice garden and statues!

We only managed to visit at night. The street food location is at gate 8. Some of the stalls have long long queue. The watermellon drink stall seems to be a hit... A bit pricey at KRW9000 for one watermellon drinks (2 cups equivalent).Other food is spaghetti, korean fried chicken etc. Grab the food you want and there are sitting area to eat.There are also few restaurants selling raw fish and sashimi at the same place

Visited this place which is really a lava tube rather than a cave.  It is about 1 kilometer from end-to-end.  Inside the tube you can see different rock formations created by the lava flow, among them the turtle-shaped rock at 600-meter mark.  It is cool inside the tube and water is dripping everywhere.  It is recommended that you wear appropriate footwear while taking this tour as it could really be slippery and some areas are not so well-lit.  Maybe this is intentional to give the place a more realistic feel.

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

Too fascinating when seeing all the traits of massive lava flow in the cave, which is actually part of the lava tube. Must bring along a powerful torch if you want to enjoy from the ceiling to the ground. Relying just on the phone torch or the lights inside will hinder your enjoyment and appreciation of this natural masterpiece as you will be only focusing on your steps. Do walk the entire 1 km so you can see the big massive lava lumps which stretches from the ground to the ceiling. Water drippings and water patches are common, wear a cap and windbreaker will help. In fact the temperature inside is a few degrees lower than the outside

To be honest, I didn't expect anything from this waterfall, but once we got there, it was pretty nice. It wasn't big like the one in U.S (Niagara fall), but this is only waterfall I know that flows right to the ocean! We paid about $2 to see the waterfall. We took some pictures and left there within 30 mins. Was this worth to see? It's a toss up but I'd say yes.

Though it just rain yesterday, but the waterfall seems to be so small and the water current also very little. Many says that it falls directly to the sea, but it is not true. it falls into a small pond where the water overflow(or may be connected under) into the sea. It is below my expectation.

This was the same village that Dae Jang Geum (鸚㏝룝) was filmed. It looked like a huge place in the show but in actual fact is that this place is really tiny! It should not take anyone more than 10 mins to complete. We were shown how water was collected from the rain by wrapping a rope on the tree that links into the water pots. The tourguide said that in those days, women in Jeju island work while the men stay at home. The lady touring us in the area carried the water trout to show us how Jeju women in the past used to carry water. There is one small house that according to the lady, is still inhabited. We were not allowed to enter but we can take pictures from outside the house. The house smells of the aroma of freshly cooked rice. We were told that someone is actually cooking. After touring the small compound comes the main part of the program - promoting honey. It seems like there are many version of how real honey should be. For this version, the honey doesn't melt in water. One can see the hives when it's placed in water and swirled around. We were given different honey to try: Pure honey, lingzhi and 5 flavors. For some reasons, they also sell handcream made of horse oil. It smells quite nice though. But I still have a whole box of lanolin cream at home so decided not to buy. They are not cheap either.

This place is really so pretty and peaceful! The assortment of various trees and flowers was so nice, especially in the fall as you could see all the different citrus fruits almost fully ripe. The waterfalls were so nice too and the big coi carps could be the sole reason for the visit!  A bit smaller than I expected but still worth it :)

This place is only about 8 km from Jeju downtown.  Worth a quick visit to see for yourself the   supposedly   optical illusion where things (water, cars, etc) seem to roll uphill, instead of downhill....

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.
This is to me the nicest waterfall in Jeju, having visited four in total as you can get close to it and see the waterfall right into the sea...Not grand but nice...

This is the only waterwall that flows directly into the sea. To give another better reason to see this waterfall, you'll catch a rainbow where the water is falling, but only in clear sky mornings. It's beautiful sight to behold so it's a must see!
this is the nice beach evervi seen, all water us so clean.beside have lots of resturant , hotel.. mini shop
This is the best waterfall to visit as it's rare to see a waterfall that goes straight into the sea. After seeing this waterfall, you won't want to look at the other 2.

This is my favorite as the waterfalls and the blue water coupled with mandarin ducks swimming and moving around, I really feel like I'm in a fantasy land or living in the fairy tales movie that we used to see.  Highly recommended for photography and relaxation!

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).
This is a fun place to visit, as apart from the waterfalls you can walk around the area and see many different attractions.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

This beach was ok. The sand felt nice and there were plenty of people around to make it feel like a happening spot, without being overcrowded. You can easily grab a bite to eat nearby. In my opinion, I would go here for a beach day if I really wanted a beach day, but I wouldn't plan to go there as a must- see beach.One thing I noticed about the beaches in Korea... The Koreans dress more modestly than at almost any other beach in the world ( including Dubai) ... Most seemed to be covered up with water - type shorts and shirts vs. the typical shirtless man and bikini clad women. It's something you should consider !

This beach is a great place for tourists! Upon arriving there are lots of vendors with delicious food and things you might need for the beach (towels, hats, beach mats, swim suits, booze, etc). The main beach is usually very crowded (understandably). I like to go to the beach to the right, it's just a 5 minute walk on the sidewalk, clearly visible with a clear understanding it's leading to another beach. This part of the beach seems to be less crowded with all of the same benefits! Great place to relax, enjoy the sun, and swim in the water!

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The wind blows hard in this area (as the wind turbines might hint at). But the water is beautiful, the sand is white and the rock formations around are really special. It gets crowded but not as crowded as some others on the island. I have seen better beaches for sure, but here in Jeju this one is probably as good as it gets.
The waterfall that falls direct to the sea. Although not as majestic as I thought. But you can see rainbow where the water is falling, in a clear day.

The waterfall is beautiful, it gave me the urge to jump in it under the hot sun. There is a entrance charge for that. For those who are from places like Malaysia, Philippines where surrounded with beautiful waterfalls, you might don't feel like spending money just to see this waterfall.

The water is amazing. There are 3 waterfall spots and a beautiful bridge to see at this attraction. Highly recommended although the walk can be a pain, especially the last waterfall.The bridge is also quite a sight to behold. This is probably the best waterfall in Jeju.

The walk to the waterfall was nice although it is kind of man made. The natural sights at the side was beautiful nonetheless.However, the waterfall itself was just ok. It didn't seem like that's the focal point of this attraction but it was good enough for a trip there.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000\ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

The best we have seen in Jeju.Though the water was a bit too cold for us to swim, it's great for wading during low tide.You can even rent clear bottom kayak to paddle around.There are lots of convenient stores, burger and coffee places and other local eateries around there.Definitely worth a visit.

Out of the 3, this is the most dangerous but also the most fascinating, mostly due to the old lady divers at the bottom selling freshly caught seafood. So fresh you can taste the salt. Waterfall is beautiful on it's own, the trek down is pretty steep but easy. Only concern is once you're nearby the waterfall you have to hop onto the rocks to get closer, which can be pretty dangerous for the elderly, kids or those who are not sure footed.A must see if you're into waterfalls.

Optical allusion or not, this is head scratching. I stood at bottom and then put car in neutral, it rolled uphill. Best yet, poured water on road and it too flowed up?close to airport and worth the few minutes drive to see.
One letter difference, but these are not the waterfalls you want to see. Better to go to the Cheonjiyeon falls which are 10 mins east. These ones are very average.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Oh gosh!  This is definitely one of the must-sees of Jeju Island!A short 15min (mostly flat) loop, and you will be rewarded with babbling brooks and crystal clear waters overlooked by towering cliffs.  Best of all, this is off the beaten path, and there were virtually no tourists around.  Oh...the tranquility.Some parts of the walk involve jumping from rock to rock in the streams.  Not a problem generally (my kids found it fun), but if you have mobility issues, you may want to bear this in mind.We would like to thank Victor of Jejueco Suites for helping us discover this hidden jem.

Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.
Not an impressive waterfall as many have described. If you have never see a waterfall, go for it. Otherwise just skip it.

many themes in the park such as tulip garden, Canola, rapeseed, cherry blossom, more than 100 years old bonsai, folk village with traditional restaurant 竊fresh grilled mackerel竊, well decorated water pond, peacock and bird park and many more. The folk village still maintain the culture of living that one should not miss. One need half a day in completing visiting the park.
Lucky to visit on sunny day, was slightly crowded but still managed to still the cliff. The volcanic structures were very interesting and you can see the clear blue water.

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Just one waterfall, not much of a sight to behold. However, it's the only touristy waterfall that doesn't have stairs, so if you have knee problems, this is waterfall to see. On the plus side, the souvenir store near the entrance has good merchandise at good prices. They had nice hats on sale when I was there.

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.

Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.
It's the only waterfall in Asia to fall directly to the ocean. But once you see the falls, that's it. Not much else to see.

It's a waterfall that goes directly to the see. Not many like that so you should visited it at least once. The road after the stairs was rocky, so you have to be careful. There's a woman diver, so there' s some people that ate her catch near the waterfall.

It is a good experience to be there and see how mystery the road was. We were with our kind tour guide that gave us an experiment to test the road. Pour water and see where it flows, true enough it was a mystery (still need not to be solved).
In case of typhoon, many tourism spot close in Jeju island, South Korea. In that case enjoy the beautiful scenery of waves and the 'breaks of water' See my picture too.

Ilchubong is an amazing place to see and one of my best expierences, but be sure to choose a cooler day to go there.Going up those stais would be nothing, if it wouldn't have been like +35 degrees that day..I sweated like a dog..But thankfully, they have some free water downstairs!
If you like to see waterfall falling into a sea, you cannot miss this waterfall. The place is rather crowded though... try going around the sunset because the scene is really beautiful.

If you are traveling to the south side of Jeju island, you must come see this cliff surrounded by emerald waters and roaring waves.Truly awesome. You will be even more surprised when you get home by the amazing photos you took. Don't focus on people shots, get the amazing rocks and waves instead! Don't worry about the apparent crowds around you, you will definitely be able to take some fantastic pictures without them.

I?ve never been this near to the base of a waterfall before.  No railings, just the raw power of a thunderous fall.  And a rainbow!  The kids loved jumping from rock to rock.  This may be a little precarious on a wet day, but we were lucky with the weather during our visit.You do get some splashes.  So if you have very expensive camera equipment, you may want to protect it?  The walk up was a little tiring, but not overly so.Absolutely love it.  A must see!
I went to Manjang Cave. It  was really good place to see. It was very cold when we got in side and we can see you cave of Volcano, while you are walking the water drop down and very lively..

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.
I was expecting a bigger waterfall but was disappointed with what I've seen.However, it's still a good place to visit to see nature in its own wonder.

I was excited to go see the Manjanggul caves, and had an image in my mind that unfortunately didn't fit what I saw. The whole experience is pretty cool, the floor is uneven, dodging water droplets becomes a game, the lava flow marks are beautiful, but lack of light, lack of stalactite formations, and a lot of areas that are fenced off let me down slightly. However, cheap entrance, and the atmosphere is actually quite lovely. If you get the chance to go, try and do it.

I think, this is really good waterfall. To see a water fall just beside of the sea is not usual... yes, very unusual. And it was good to see... A little bit high waterfall. 2,000 won for adult... If you enter it in another path, you don't need to pay. There is ticket checkpoint but the worker there didn't check.

I arrived to this temple because it was on my route between Seogwipo waterfalls. I was amazed. I thought I had seen enough temples, but this was something else. It is majestic with the palm trees and little ponds in front of it. This has been one of my favourite temples in South-Korea so far.

Have you ever seen a more mouthwatering set of pictures? ㄴ Today we are enjoying a famous traditional dish from Jeju Island, Black pork.  Thick cuts of juicy pork belly, cooked to a smokey crisp just how I love it. Alone the pork belly is enough to eat by itself and a side of rice. But we're not here to be basic, you either go big or go home, enjoy the side dishes that come with every meal.  For example bean sprouts, ssamjang is known as a Korean bbq dipping sauce. It was mildly spicy and salty flavor with nutty fragrant. And, most importantly it compliments well Korean pork belly bbq. Lastly the infamous cabbage Kimchi, enough of a kick but not too much where you cant taste the perfect blend of food. A perfect combination, Bon-Appetite!

First thing we've noticed is how civilized this beach is - loads of restaurants, shops , cafes nearby. We were lucky enough to visit it in September, when holiday season is over for majority of Korean guys - so, it was not that crowded. Water was very clean and the only downside, that it was already a little bit cold. If you walk few hundred meters in a right hand direction from the main beach (towards the hill), you would see a camping ground with even smaller strip of sand - and we were absolutely alone there.

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. A good thing we visited this Dragon Head Coast while doing the west coast route.The canola flowers site is a paid visitor spot (should be around KRW2K each adult). There is a Viking ride @ the base for the young ones to try. You can see many interesting lines and grains on the side of the rocks' walls. You get to see women divers selling fresh seafoods along the coast, youngest are already in their 50s and oldest are in their 70s (still diving)...they are simply amazing.

Come prepared and you'll love it, good walking boots and waterproof jacket. If you find it too cold or dump you can go in for a few metres, and go outside, but we kept going wanting to see what is at the end, and it was spectacular, with huge lava column in blue dim light.

Can't resist going there every night as it's near to my hostel. Kinda good place for dinner for solo traveller as most of the restaurant serving food for more than 2 persons. You can get local food, fusion, western, sashimi, fresh fish, pork knuckles, fresh fruits and vegetables. Price range around kw2000 to kw10,000 per dish. Now you can get hallabong orange everywhere. Sweet and seedless. Yummmm love it when it's cool. After dinner can catch the water show nearby at 8pm every night except Monday.

Bring your jackets, better to be water proof! Cave temperature is around 10 plus degree or lower. Also ground is uneven so wear good shoes and walk slowly. But overall fascinating to see how geography works

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.
Beautiful Waterfall. Because it was April there was no charge to see it, liked that part. It was sort of hot so it was refreshing to be  near the fall

Beautiful scene to be seen. Very natural. 20,000 stones of different verities. Natural as traditional village houses in India. Toilet facilities are everywhere. Very clean. Dogs and cats are not allowed.Water fountain is there. very good place for peace, health and meditation.Thanks.

Beautiful indoor gardens with several rooms leading off of main garden with specialized environments. The rooms leading from the main garden that I can recall right now are a tropical plant room with orchids, a fern room, water plant room with lilies and hyacinth, and even a cactus room. It is a large indoor garden with many colorful and unusual plants to see. It was raining the day we were there so we were happy that it was enclosed. There are beautiful Korean and Japanese style gardens, among other types of gardens too, outside. Jeju Island has many beautiful places to visit and this botanical garden was a great excursion for us.

Beautiful Falls. Also its rare to see falls directly in ocean apparently only one in Asia. It said that the dragon's spirit is contained in the water which can cure diseases and bring rain during drought. Easy to access. Make sue you wearing comfatable Shoes, it does get slippery. We had some lovely click out here, spl couple ;)
Beautiful clean beach!! one of the nicest I've seen, it was spring and a bit cold so not ideal for swimming but i guess in the summer it would be really nice to go a dip as the water is very clear.
Beautiful beach and surroundings!Very clean and vivid colours You can also try some water sports here, but seems like you had to stay around the renting area

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

Although the waterfall itself was very beautiful to see we only stayed for a few minutes if that there was a lot of people there taking pictures and sitting on the rocks once there, there wasn't much stuff to do. But on the bright side it was really nice to see.

After seeing Jeongbang waterfall, this Cheonjiyeon waterfall seemed average.  Admission was the same in both waterfalls, 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenagers (up to 24). To see this waterfall, you had to go thru the park, which had other monuments, trees, and flowers to admire...worth checking even in winter.

A must see when in jeju. Jeonbang Waterfall is the only waterfall that falls directly into the ocean. It?s a beautiful sight to see. However, if you are handicapped it is not accessible, as there are stairs. Make sure to wear gym/grip shoes as there are lots of rocks/ slopping hazard. There are also (henyo) female scuba divers that harvest abalone and various seafood that are available to eat nearby. Definitely check it out!

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It?s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn?t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.

We did the yeongsil walk and it was amazing. It was tough in parts of you are not used to hiking but walking all the kids and grandparents doing it lends you the stamina to keep going and gosh is it worth it. Some of the best scenery I have ever seen.

This is yet another bridge among the several others you will happen to see in Jejudo. It is not worth a special visit unless you go with the intention of hiking around the island that this bridge connects to the mainland. The Seogwipo Submarine tour starts from the dock located very close to this bridge. So you can easily explore this bridge and the surrounding area if you come for the submarine tour.

We travelled on a rare rainy day in Jeju, but June, our tour guide, made our trip happy and smooth with her professional arrangement, detailed introduction of the scenic spots, fluent English, sharing on Korean culture and her personal experience on how she feels about Jeju. I am particularly impressed by the guided tour she gave us in the Manjanggul Lava Tube, her intriguing story of haenyeo and their livelihood and our hiking experience at Seongsanilchul Pong. In as short as a day we have seen most of what lies in the northern and eastern coasts of Jeju Island, felt for ourselves the beauty of the natural landscapes and understood how inhabitants of this island have lived since the last century. It was an amazing travel experience and we give credits to June for the nice private tour.

This place is quite overrated when the cliffs aren't as majestic and huge as can be seen in pictures. These are lava columns that hardened upon meeting the sea and formed into pillar-like structures. Going into the platforms was easy, not too much hiking but after seeing it, there's not much to see or do. Beware of the shops nearby and try to haggle before buying.

The lava tube is different from other lime stone or erupted caves I seen before, this one is very big and the its formation and feature is fantastic.  Try to avoid the high crowd and prepare jacket, poncho and hiking shoes.  We took good camera and tripok to take picture.

I have never seen anything like it. The walk was unbelievable! A must see and do in Seogwipo. Great for travellers who love nature, hiking (must wear comfortable shoes) and photography. Highly recommended.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

We decided to pop over to the maze park as we were visiting mangajul lava tubes. We were greeted by a ten to fifteen cats basking in the shade. It seems like the owner loves cats. That was a great treat for my cat loving family. The maze itself was great fun and especially if you are in a group. Not very difficult but not as easy. We could easily go around with a stroller though there are a few steps. Has a small cafeteria for icecream and coffee. Overall great fun.

This is highlight of my Jeju West Coast Trip; it's beautiful scenic walk; however its not an easy walk. My mother has difficulty to walk on this path and return to the entrance after 10 minutes walk. There are some woman divers selling abalone near the entrance and its quite fascinating to see them.I highly recommend to visit this attraction while you are in Jeju and its very close to Mount Sanbang where usually people visit for trekking.
The park is a very big park to cover specially in a hot summer day .Has many different sections and it is easy to get lost without a map .It is a must see place
The museum has really cool exhibits and they were beautiful to see. It's easy to relax and forget about the outside world.
Spent 6 hr on the island with a car.Lots of things to see and do. Tasty fresh seafood everywhere.Easy drive on car ferry to island.
Really enjoyed exploring this cave. Easy and convenient car parking. Great facilities. A must-see on your trip to Jeju.

really didn't expect in such conservative country seeing this museum but making money is not easy so they made it . if u looking for fun experience and some kind of new pictures which probably can not share any where so go for it . when i visited place i met many old grand ma than young :D

nice place to visit to see how nature works!!!....u can see how jeju was made thousands years ago.....beautiful cave!!!...but you must be fit to walk about 2km and walking in a slippery floor is not really easy in the dark....beautiful!!!!

Jeju love land is one of those parks that is worth going to for simply being unique. If you have a sense of humour and love all things bizarre this is worth checking out. You can grab a penis shaped dessert ice cream or beverage and there are a number of quirky and interactive sculptures to gawk at. Getting around Jeju Island isn't that easy a taxi might be your best bet. Make sure you have the address up on google maps for your driver to see.

I heard about Udo Island from a few of the other ladies I was traveling with. They had seen pictures and couldn't wait to visit. I tagged a long for some good fashion outdoor fun. We rented bikes for the afternoon and took a ride around the island. The weather was perfect and we were able to see some great scenery. Great spot to visit!

Very easy to walk to. Eating places nearby. Very beautiful.  We had breakfast at Dunkin Doughnuts nearby. Cost is 2,000 won to see. Unique shopping near location.

Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Walking on the Olle is nice--a great pilgrimage for healing. If you really want to know about the unique history of Jeju and the Korean Peninsula however you must visit this museum. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The highlight of this museum is its peace garden. This huge garden made me pray for peace in the Korean peninsula.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.
This is a huge park and we go around by trains. Not much to see other than natural scenes, but good to walk around. Access is not convenient, you need cars.

This ancient historical & cultural village was meant to show its rich origin & history. Therefore, it was left intentionally in its original state ie old, rundown & unmodernised. Living in an ultra modern city, it was a very humbling experience for us to be able to witness what living conditions were like in those days.It is a very small village, so obviously there aren't much to see or photos to take. There were big portraits of the 2 lead casts of the famous Korean drama   A Jewel of the Palace,   filmed in 2003. This drama probably spark off the K-Wave phenomena worldwide. Maybe this was one of the filming sites.The resident guide gave us a walk & run up of the place. After which, we went to a small hut where she was explaining the honey & other products of this village.Sampling of honey was given. She did not hard sell nor push anyone to buy. It was the visitors' own free will if to buy.Many in our group (including us) bought the honey because they loved it & not because they were scammed or hard-sold.

The floor is uneven and the lighting is dim, not for those with walking issues. Nice place to see the strange wall formation due to lava. Only 1 km and mostly even.  The tourists can be a bit noisy, hope the bats in the other parts are not too disturbed

the cave is 1 km long you walk mostly in dark.not too.kuch to seeat the end there is a pillar but if you have been to.caves in the world before, it's not as fascinating as you see on the pictures not a real must

The cave has a number of formations throughout and there are information boards explaining what they re, and the English is good. The cave was a cool 13 degrees when I went down but outside was 34 so it was a welcome temperature.The steps down are a little deep so if you have vertigo or need help walking, it could be a little tough. It is wet under foot, I walked in flipflops and it was ok, but if you are a bit unsure of your footing, wear trainers. The cave is lit well  but some lights shine up into your eyes, which I found incredibly annoying, as it ruined my night vision. There are some areas with wooden bridges over the areas very difficult to walk on, so you aren't constantly in need of watching your footing.Worth a visit, as it it is not something you will see in many other places. I have been twice now, and it seems much more tourist friendly now.

The cave floor is uneven combined with inadequate lighting makes the winter walk very uncomfortable and after some distance, we gave up. Our youngsters were bored as the couldn't see the cave's beautiful features. Rather disappointed.

The beach itself could do with some TLC from the council.   There is a lot of debris which washes up daily onto the beach and along the coastal walk. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.

Seemed this is a set-up village with less than 5 residents. Walking around this village, I don't even find any children running around the village. Saw only one sample black pig in the sty. At the end of the walk around, we were escorted to a small hut to listen to the sales talk on their tea, wine, horse bone products. Can treat this place as a tourist trap or a toilet breaks.
Plenty to see here including traditional houses, a museum and plenty of... stones. Nothing special but a nice place to enjoy a walk.

Personally, this is my least favourite falls in Jeju.  Nothing special about it except that it is a fall that flows directly to the sea.  The walk down the steps to the falls are fine but I do not recommend walking on the rocks to be nearer to the rocks.  Kids and senior citizens should not attempt that is it is rather dangerous.  You can still see and take photo of the fall from a further distance.  Not worth injury during your holidays!

Perfect for couples to take a romantic walk through the woods. Be sure to take the shortcut if you just want to get to the end of it quickly and see the oldest tree around, or if you're a romantic be sure to take the long route and walk hand in hand with your beloved. Enjoyed the refreshing walk and highly recommended.

No ! Not again another Fall ! But this one worth the peaceful walk in a nice park and by a small river. If you pass by, go there. You have to see the harbour with small fishing boats. I liked this even better.
nicely labelled signs to explain the lava tubereally awesome to see the marks left by nature it's about a slow walk of about an hr, wear good shoes and a jacket as it gets cold
Nice walk around to see different carvings of stones which we took lots of picture with. Not spectacular, but nice to see. There is a small entrance fee.

Nice place to visit. U walk into the tunnel until its very derp end almost 1km in..... Then finally at the end of the tunnel u will get to see the light and the only stalagmite in the entire cave.... Lights in the caves are sufficient but not bright enough. The thing is, we thought the wet floors would be slippery but surprisingly thruout our entire walk into and out of the cave, there was absolutely no spot thatvwas slippery, thanks to the natural grooves on the ground which may have been created by the lava flow hundreds of years ago. Nice to explore, but obviously not for those who are claustrophobic.

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.

My family was recommended by our (Nam Yang Taxi) driver cum guide to this   must visit   place which was not in our initial planned itinerary. We are so glad to visit this captivating cliff by the beautiful blue sea!! It was a breezy cosy walk enjoying the marvelous scenery and shoreline natural volcanic black stone. It wasn't difficult for my parent (just walk at own comfort pace) especially for my dad whom was aided/help by our taxi driver/guide whenever required. This is our most loved sightseeing venue among others. Indeed a   must-see   attraction!!

Manjanggul Cave came to me as a surprise. To walk in a lava tube is an enchanting experience. There are steep stairs and long walk so be prepared. Don't bring heavy bags. Wear jacket because its cold inside the cave. Bring good camera. As you enter the cave, you will see the limestone that looks like lava flow (see picture attached). The path is dim that completes the enchanting atmosphere. By the end of the road, you can see the lava column.

Manjang cave in overall was really nice expierence, but we got a bit cold.When outside is more than 30 degrees, and you go downstairs, it's a bit...cool.And wet as well.But I won't whine about it, because the expierence you get there is more important!We were walking really slowly taking pictures of everything (if you don't have a good camera, pictures won't bet any good ://)They have diferent color lights and it makes cave more visitor-friendly.Only thing is that there is really crowded...Even though we went there on a weekday.So be prepared to see a lot of people there as well.

Love love love. Everything was beautiful. If you like just seeing different glass art works this is the place for you. It was between $11-12 for entry but of the   museums   in korea  this one is my favorite (lived in korea for 4 years). The jungle walk through that starts with some dinosaurs is kind of long but very gorgeous

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.

Jeju Glass Castle is the famous place at Jeju. When I first went inside, I just like walk in an unreal place. Since the entire thing is made by glass. You can see glass everywhere, such as the flowers, the trees and the artworks.One of the special things in this castle is an artwork that calls ?a moment of musical concert?, this artwork show that the moment of a band that is performing. The entire performers have different emotion and music instruments. It is very hard to do this, because each performer?s face is smaller than a coin.Here also have some funny place, such as Glass labyrinth and distorting mirror. Be careful, maybe you will lose in the labyrinth, or become a fat boy/girl in the distorting mirror.Finally, I suggest that you need to be very careful in this castle, if not you will break the glass.
It's where the locals go to shop. Fun walking around seeing what is being offered and mingling with the locals. I never realized there were so many varieties of the Korean classic, Kimchi.

Its definitely a worthwhile trip to make and just walking through the Lava Tube is quite an experience.  It is not everyday one has the opportunity to walk through and see the various formations, the caves formed, columns, the different textures formed, etc.One needs to be relatively fit to do the walk with comfortable shoes as the location tends to be wet. Elderly should have a walking stick which will help and carry a torchlight.  Its a few degrees lower underground.

It's a nice bridge, and takes you across to the little island on the other side. Not really a lot to see apart from passing through the quaint port and adjacent coastline. Would suit you if you just wanted to go out for a relaxing walk along a peaceful area.

It was raining when we reached the place. From the parking area, you will see this beautiful crater. As we are slowly walking up the slope, the wind was too strong for us to walk further up.Decided not to go up, but must had to take a few photographs of this beautiful place with the wind, rain and waves.On Normal day, there is also diving show by the famous Sea Women - Haenyeo. Mostly are 50 and above who dive for a living.Try to plan the visit during normal weather.

It was an interesting experience to walk through the 1km long tunnel if you enjoy understanding and seeing the various structures and rock formations formed from the lava flow. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!
It is just a long, dark, unending walk in a tunnel and nothing to see.Just a nice temperature inside. Don't bother and not suitable for older people...

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.
Intriguing to see teddy bear in different sizes, shapes and costumes! Enjoyed our walk in the garden as well!

If you love nature and have never seen any volcanic formation before, it would be worth the visit. Personally,  i enjoyed walking inside the cave and having a look at the volcanic formation.  It's like you can almost imagine how the lava flowed inside the tunnel a few thousand years ago :) i was in awe of how powerful mother nature can be. It was quite cold inside. Wear layers and proper shoes.  Can be quite slippery as well.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

I would highly recommend this place for an extremely hot or wet day.  Being covered and large enough, it was an enjoyable walk.  There was adequate lighting and enough fellow tourists not to make the cave walk too scary.  Despite the unevenness of the terrain - they are dried lava and so quite uneven, most people would be able to walk comfortably.It's certainly a nice change from limestone caves although some people may miss seeing amazing rock formations like the stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves.  In fact, I was not overly impressed with the gigantic lava mass on display at the end of the walk.  For me, the enjoyable walk was good enough.

I was staying at the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun and decided to go for an out door walk to enjoy the beautiful weather. I was walking along the coastline and it eventually lead me to this attraction. Although it is wonderful to see these unique rock formation, this attraction is rather small.

I was looking forward to seeing the traditional/indigenous village but after a quick walk around we were marched into a hut ...after a brief introduction about this ancient village,then the hard sell began. Impressive products made from horse bones & horse oil - with almost magical values! No, I didn't buy anything.This is not a living village. I could only sight tour operators.

I was excited to see the Manjanggul Lava Tubes up close and personal, but I was rather disappointed after my visit..The Caves were poorly lit and without using a flashlight, one can barely see the markings on the rocks. The ground is very uneven and understandably so. However, for older people, children and people prone to ankle injuries, the lighting does not allow one to see where one is walking and injury can can easily occur.

I think it really depends on what kind of traveler u are. Some people might find it boring, some people might find it cool. I love it. I've never been in a cave nor a lava tunnel so for me it was a new and exciting experience. The cave is huge, wet and super duper cold, colder than outside in fact and lit up enough to see where you're walking. It's nice to see and feel how hardened lava looks and feels like. Walking into Manjanggul's huge cave feels like a scene from Prometheus.. Awesome!

I saw one picture in instagram and decided to go Jeju olle train route 8. Actually, Route 8 is restricted, but you will see everyone just walk into. It is called 'Gaetkkak Columnar Jointing (媛二쇱?\由щ?)' It is better to wear comfortable shoes since you have to walk on rocks, but you better dress nice if you want to have a good picture. I saw many girls dressed up and walked on the rocks which looked extremely tiring but worth it. You might need to line up to take a photo, and I also waited to take a photo at specific spot. Now I have really cool pictures ;)
Great place to enjoy walking and see different species of plants, trees, we enjoy palms, something special, very quiet place

for me there is nothing special about this cave. the only thing we can do is just walking straight through the cave almost 1km (cmiww). and after we arrive to the end of the tunnel , we just see a small stage and some pic as i remembered. if you traveling with child , pls be carefull when you step the floor. because its really slipper..
Footbridge is of interesting architecture and good photo opp, walk across to the small island and trek around it (about 30 min) to see the sceneries around.

As there are not much railings inside the cave to guide the tourists while walking and steps are uneven, make sure to wear comfortable walking shoes. It is beautiful and a must visit when in Jeju. I joined a tour for this visit as it is quite far from where I stayed. Tourist spots in Jeju are not close to each other and I didnt quite see a lot of public transport the in the area.
About 40 min taxi from the airport. The cave is a must see if you visit Jeju. Walk inside the cave, beutiful lighting. Amazing.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.
A train ride that takes you from sight to sight, there is a gorgeous lake walk and a pretty garden, but sights are very simple and straightforward. Not a must-see.

A nice park where you can walk up easily to see the crater. The crater is long dried up with vegetation growing and on my visit, there was a excavation truck at the bottom working! Wonder how the truck and worker get down there.Recommend to all age group.

We rode most of the Olleh trail routes by bike and it was awesome.  We made a film about it (titled Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure) and met heaps of interesting people to interview.   I'd definitely recommend it as a not-to-miss part of visiting Jeju Island!   I'd like to walk some of the Olleh Trail routes next time to experience it differently and more slowly.

We hiked the mountain a bit late but still was very interesting. There are many trails to hike just make sure to be back to the bus station before 5:30. We missed throats bus and a Korean guy who works there showed his hospitality. He took me and 4 others to the next station and civilization ( 30 Klm away). Be light when hiking you will get some portable water and a shelter to get God about 3 Klm from the beginning. It was a very nice experience It an be very foggy

We didnt expect much from this park but was taken in by the amazing grand sight of the rock formations. There is also an interesting folk tale behind these formations. The scenery was beautiful and there was many small trails to explore within the park.

Sanbangsan Mountain is a wonderful bell-shaped huge body of lava situated nearby the ocean. At few places it stretches into the ocean where majestic rock structures can be seen. Almost vertical cliffs with columnar joints at this mountain are impressive. This mountain is visible from almost everywhere in the southwest plains of Jeju. Also the legend associated with this mountain is very interesting. According to the legend it was plucked out from the Hallasan Mountain peak by the angry Emperor when he got hit by a misfired arrow that was shot to white deer. Interestingly it is said that the circumferences of the Sanbangsan Mountain and the crater at Hallasan are of similar size. The Jeju Olle Trail Route 10 is connected to this mountain by stairs. A Buddha temple huge Buddha statue and the caves on this mountain are very beautiful.  This mountain along with nearby Yongmeori Coast are highly recommended especially to those who love coastal cliffs and interesting rock formations.

Place is good and interesting but an averagely.Nothing too special. I've been there at the end of season (September) - so trail was closed and not possible to rent a kayaks as well.Maybe in summertime it a bit more interesting but not sure :)

Jeju stone park was not part of the regular sightseeing itineraries and do we opted for a customized private tour to visit Jeju stone park. Requires atleast 3 to 4 hours if you want to walk along the trails to cover entire area. A visit inside the museum to understand the volcanic activities and formations will help in understanding the nature of the island better. Good to go with a local guide. Interesting statues and rock formations

It is accesible by public transport. There are near Seogwipo harbour.You can go from main road on foot like Olle trail-I forgot exact number-(there are blue and orange colors directions)-just follow one collor. Interesting bridge

It is a remote the only time we used a taxi instead of a bus in a week ay Jejudo. Glad we visited.  We were visiting the island to hike the Olle Trails and climb Mt Halla so this was a side trip.  We picked it because it seemed the most interesting attraction built for tourists and we agreed it was a good choice.
An excellent walking area with beautiful views and interesting seascapes.Trails were accessible and facilities were clean and pleasant.
a beautiful location for a good view and some interesting plantlife. also a trail where one can go hiking.

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

we were definitely not prepared for this - in terms of experience and equipment!started off at about 9am on the Eorimok route. the entrance was a 10 min walk from the bus stop. then, it was off on the hike!initially the trail was straightforward. then it gradually went into a steep ascent. the path was quite rocky and unstable. but there were sufficient rest stops along the way. also people going in the same and opposite direction to you so you will not be alone (unless you hike in the middle of the night)there were also multiple signboards along the route providing interesting facts about Hallasan and also maps showing your current location and remaining distances to go to the next point.there was almost a natural portable water point where you can refill your bottles. remember to stay hydrated throughout and take breaks when needed.needless to say, the views along the route were truly breathtaking but the higher elevation you reach, the colder it becomes. also, the winds were very strong!we reached the Witseoreum shelter at about 12pm and had lunch there. The locals actually brought hot water in their thermos flasks and had cup ramen there!after lunch, we started our descent on the Yeongsil trail and reached the entrance of Yeongsil at about 2pm and there was a 2km walk out of the entrance to the bus stop.by then our legs were aching and heavy, but we pushed on. overall the hike took about 5 hrs.in summary, we should have worn more proper hiking footwear, wear thicker clothing (as higher you go, the colder it gets) and more food and snacks!we decided we will come back to attempt the summit next time.

We went on the first Monday of the month, and the mountaineering trail was closed, so do take note when planning. However, the first portion of the trail was still available for free, which was still amazing and less of an exercise. The view from all spots were breathtaking, making this spot a must-see when you?re in Jeju.Do catch the woman?s diver show at 1.30pm and 3pm, located down the trail. It was an interesting experience to see the elderly women dive down to retrieve the seafood in the ocean, and you can buy and eat some of their fresh catches at the shop nearby.Highly recommend for a magnificent sightseeing experience in Jeju!

We visited this road on the way back to the airport (stayed on South side of the island).  I would recommend this attraction if you happened to be on road-1139 or in the vicinity (e.g., visiting Loveland, or hiking trails nearby.  There are plenty of nicer things to see and do on the island but it?s worth a look/see, if you?re in the ?neighborhood.?  My wife got a kick out of it, using the water bottle, as previously advised by another post.  I was less than thrilled and found the art along the road and cafes to be more interesting around the mid-way point of the attraction.

We visited Oedolgae with Jejueco Suite?s package tour.  Victor, our guide, told us an interesting story of a lady praying for her husband who is lost at sea.  As it was then near sunset (about 1 hour prior), the rocks were backlit and we could not take a photo of the ?praying lady and her fallen husband?. Victor told us to continue along the Jeju Olle Trail (marked by ribbons) for a seaside hike, and he will wait for us at the next carpark.  I forgot to ask him how long the walk is expected to be, so when I can?t see any carpark after 10-15min, I kept wondering if I had somehow taken a wrong path.  So for the benefit of Victor?s future guests, these are the approximate GPS coordinates:Oedolgae: 33.2390574,126.5446144Carpark: 33.2397470,126.5318070(You will pass by a cafe called 60 Beans)Along the path, there are other viewing platforms of Oedolgae Rock where it was not backlit by the sun.  However the angle was wrong, and from these other platforms, you can?t see the shape of the ?praying lady and her fallen husband?.

We like to hike.  Our idea of hiking is day trips and not super remote.  A 4-6 hour hike in a California Redwood state park is a good example.We took about 6 of the 20+ trails on the south and east coasts.  Every one was different and interesting in its own way.  We stayed in Jung-Mun on the south side.  Terrific little town with hole in wall places with tasty, healthy, cheap food and good bus transportation.These hikes were a little different from our standard in that they often took more than 6 hours. They also could dip in and out of populated areas. We liked that because we might trip across a restaurant run by old lady divers or an archery club doing target practice.  Most trails were not at all crowded. The worst was part of a trail where a Korean soap opera was filmed. It is hard to describe the Korean style of friendliness. They are very direct.  Example was a man at a bus stop who figured we were going to have difficulty getting to our destination. So he flagged a taxi, allegedly for himself, and invited us to hop on.  When we figured out what he was doing, we insisted on paying.  He refused. We got out, gave the driver money, he grabbed it and gave it back. We tossed the money into the window. He grabbed it again, tossed it back on the street and had the driver zip off.  There we were, picking up our money off the pavement. Anybody who has watched Koreans fight over who gets to pay the bill at a restaurant knows what I am saying. To Americans it looks like a hot argument when in fact it's best friends being best friends.  My advice is enjoy it but don't always loose the argument - sometimes you have to win and pay the bill.  This time we really tried but he was too clever for us;-)

We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area.
