The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Kids may enjoy posing with Cinderella's carriage & shoe collection and running around the grounds.  As I was not however, although a few glass sculptures were interesting, I did not think it was worth the time or effort (& of course the entrance fee) to go.  Agree with the comments of previous reviewers who rated   poor  .  The  fish lunch I had at the restaurant next door however, was enjoyable. On the plus side, the place is wheelchair accessible.

It's actually quite interesting as the road seems like an uphill slope but vehicles will move forward (slowly) without turning on their engine. It?s some sort of an optical illusion i suppose. But you can?t really see it from the side actually. It just.. seems like a normal road lolIf you are around the area, you can drop by to take a look.For full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/the-mysterious-road/

It was really pretty and there are horses which you can ride at the bottom. Climbing up includes of climbing up many flights of steep stairs which might be difficult for the elderly or the unfit(like me). It takes about 50 mins to go up and down. The view on top was nice but when i was there, there were some construction works on going and they chased us away if we were to stand at the peak to take pictures. Imagine climbing up all the way to the top just to get chased away. Not a gd feeling.At the bottom near to the sea, there is also the performance of the women divers at 1.30pm and 3.30pm. It was interesting to watch even though we were flooded by many china tourist. Be careful when walking on the rocks as it can be very slippery. There was also a small pile of shells that you can choose from and to bring home. You can also buy the seafood caught by the women divers and enjoy them at the cafe just beside.

It was raining with some strong winds when we got there. Nevertheless we decided to buy a poncho and went ahead with the climb which is a manageable 180 m.The climb up is relatively easy even for most elderlies as there are proper stairs along the way.Apart from the crater, you can see the surrounding areas and the sea from the top. The crater itself is covered by vegetation so you might want to tone down any expectation of a spectacular view. We spent about 15 min at the highest point and start our descend after that.Another attraction nearby is the female divers where they have scheduled performances every day if I remember correctly. We didn?t go for that due to the weather. But I?m sure it would be interesting.

It was nice experience when suddenly u find these kinds of roads... Some kind of mysterious nature behaviour that able to control your vehicles to suddenly runs on its own... Probably kind of magnetic field...Well, u can also enjoy a small view of grassfield and view restaurants around... I took a nice picture here with my travel friends, used a large stone (its carved with korean words) as background... Interesting experience... ;)

It was just an OK place to visit as it was part of our Tour Package. The old fashioned village homes were probably the only thing which was interesting to me. The lady who explained everything to us was very warm and friendly. Of course, at the end of the tour, you are brought to a 'special room' to view the products which they sell. I bought a bottle of Omija (Berry) Drink which was actually quite nice. I think I paid $50 (as expensive as it was, I just thought it would support their livelihood). She did not force us to buy the products but was very kind to let us try them all.

it was interesting to see these column-shape geological formations. The sea was calm when I visited so i did not get to see the waves getting on them. Nonetheless, the formations made really good photos.The sheer number of visitors on the small and narrow viewing platform could spoil your trip!

It is very interesting - the museum is right next to the house where he used to live. And there is a painting that paints the view from the museum looking down the port. it is called   The view of the port   I believe the city of Seogwipo has bought this painting a few years ago and placed it in this museum - this is my favorite. The painter is a genius and of course ahead of his own time. I am proud and also feel bad for his personal life, just like any other genius who had a not so happy personal life and was too far ahead of everyone else. Enjoy great paintings. I am glad the city of Seogwipo is making efforts to keep his painting in the meaningful spot, not random museums elsewhere in the world.

It is interesting and special when you view it, but it is actually like any rock formation, which can take many different form. If you are nearby, then go ahead, if not, don't have to drive there specially for it.

Interesting way they hide it from free view, but a  nice drop and fall into the ocean.  Careful clambering over the cobbles and boulders to get your shot.  Looks like local vendors selling raw oysters of sashimi down by the shore.  Other souvenir shops align the entrance and exit.

Interesting volcano hike up to the crater ledge. Good views out over the coastline, even tho we had a rainy, cloudy day so didn't get the best of it! Quite steep steps and climbing at times. Exposed to wind too. We saw some of the Jeju women divers from the top just about to launch themselves into the sea. I am told it's VERY busy on new year's day when everyone goes up to welcome in the dawn.

Interesting background as to how the peak was formed. The hike to the top gives a gorgeous view of Jeju Island, and if lucky the peak of Hallasan. Lots of visitors but the place is quite big enough not to make it crowded.
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.
If you're new to volcanic rock formations, this would be very interesting. It helps that the view of the sea water lapping against the rocks is beautiful too!

I would echo an earlier review that said that you should not bother with this if you have done any caving or similar - this is aimed at casual visitors not experts. It is a gentle wander in a cool cave that is appropriately lit, reasonably level and there is enough English signage to explain what you need to know. It is the fact that this was a lava tunnel that is not interesting and the signs do explain how the lava flowed, melted and cut down and through from other tunnels. 1) Wear sensible shoes.2) If it has been raining it can drip a lot inside though on our visit I did not think so.3) Some might feel it is cold - I did not

I think the word   museum   throws off this visit.  I expected to see many more interesting displays and films about tea but there is really just one room with some tea sets a few interesting facts and how Jeju tea is the best as the soil climate and underground water makes growing tea in Jeju at its optimal.  This so called museum is more of a flagship store where you can purchase tea and tea related items have a snack at the cafe/bakery that specializes in green tea ice cream and cake rolls and in a separate building building called   innis free   you can make natural soaps and enjoy Korean slushy ice in a cafe there as well and a store.  There are tea making classes but you must make a reservation to attend.  The grounds are nice and you can walk around the tea fields and go to the rooftop and get an amazing view of the surroundings.  The museum is free but for a true tea fanatic you may be disappointed as there are no samples or a big variety of tea products to choose from for purchase.

I really liked this part of the trip. We hiked up to the top, and I am a five month pregnant lady so you can do it too! The view of the city below is the most interesting view you are going to get from the top of the crater. The top of the crater itself isn't that spectacular. It was very pretty and fun! Also we happened to be there around the same time as the lady divers so we watched that and it was pretty interesting. When we were there in December they were doing shows around 1:30 and 3:30. You should definitely come here. There are also little restaurants and shops at the bottom if you are hungry!

I read many negative review about this place from other travellers but for me, it was quite an interesting place with strange phenomena going on. My taxi driver brought me here on the way to Seongsan and he show me what is so mysterious about this road and it was indeed very strange. He stop the car at one end of the road and the car will automatically move up towards the slope (even when the car engine is not on). It was just an experience and one will not spend more than 10 minutes here. A good short trip before going to other places.

I know little about So Korea, and had never heard of Jeju before my cruise ship docked there so I was VERY pleasantly surprised by this lovely park. I enjoyed hiking up the steep mountain and admiring the views. Although very popular, and fairly crowded, it was never unpleasantly so. The women divers in a little cove below were kind of interesting, but it was very crowded there.  And, because I spent some of my limited time there, I didn't have enough time to make it to the top of the crater and back before my tour bus left so was sorry I'd wasted some of my time there instead of making it all the way to the top.

How often do you see hexagonal columns along the coastline? This is the place.We were there at about 6:30pm when they were almost closing. They close at 7pm. Although it was quite a rush, we managed to enjoy and soak in the scenery.The observation deck provides very good view of the columns. Be sure to read how the columns came about. It will make the views that much more interesting and meaningful.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

First, we went to see the woman diver show. It appears to occur twice per day, at 1.30pm and 3pm if I remember correctly. They were singing, then entered into the water. I found their catch more interesting than their swimming. Afterwards, we climbed the   mountain   (small but cute is the motto). The view over the volcanic crater and the island is amazing, even despite the rainy weather that we experienced. The ascend is a bit physically challenging.

Excellent view and atmosphere! A long steep (with stairs) and challenging climb up the inactive volcanic island mountain that earns you good exercise and satisfaction! You can already enjoy the picturesque surroundings at the foot of the mountain with different views and you can buy some souvenir there and also enjoy a short horse ride (not free of course). If you are there on a sunny day, do buy some popsicle or ice-cream to go up.   There are entrance fees for the entrance as well. However, it is well worth it once you reached the top. It is fantastic to be on top looking down to the inactive volcano crater and enjoy the view of the sea that looks like touching the sky. You can literally feel like you are touching the sky too! The best time to go there will be during sunrise! Don't forget to take a selfie with the mountain height indicator board to boast your achievements! Oh, and just right before you reach the top, please take a look at the back downhill at the interesting look of the city below and take a selfie and also take some nice selfie around you.     On the way down, there is the fishing village where the you can enjoy the seafood while watching the women divers catch clamps and oyster. There are some fiexed timing but I have already forgotten the timing.    Seongsan Ilchulbong is indeed a must visit destination everytime you arrive in Jeju!

As per previous reviewers, we are greeted by a China lady who bring us around the village explaining the history of this village. I admit her stories and sayings are interesting and we learnt more about the old jeju village. After we say no to her products, she left us free to explore the small village. Not a place I will go back but i remembered the stories.

Although the weather was uncomfortably hot and humid, we decided to check out the Spirited Garden based on its raving reviews.  The garden is a pleasant peaceful spot to relax for about an hour.  Although it?s not as picturesque as some of the famous Japanese gardens, the bonsai tree collection is quite impressive.  The display on how to observe the trees was especially interesting.  Few demerits here for the excessive amounts of signs with visitor comments saying how great their visits were at this place.  The ?history hall? was just photos of famous visitors with quotes about how great the garden was.  One almost felt an obligation to enjoy the visit because these photos and comments were plastered all over the place.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy

We were taken to the folk village. We originally tried the Jeju Folk Village Museum but that was full of tourists. We were shown around several buildings that we were told were still lived in. Sorry but even primitive people had some form of furniture and cooking facilities. Yes some people may life on site and in other houses. But why show empty and it mean completely empty houses. Show us how you and your past folk lived. Some of the information was interesting until the sales pitch started. The selling of the honey and blackberry cordial which suppose to make you younger and fitter!!! I bought a ship load- not. They took us into a hut with chairs all in rows for a presentation on the value of the juice at $40 a litre bottle. Right next to the village are some restaurants which our guide wanted us to eat in at our expense!!! So I guess the real reason for coming here is their extra bit of money!!!!For most of us on our bus this stop was a complete waste of valuable time.

We visited and there were about 20 buses in the parking lot. The shop where you get the tea or ice cream was very full so we went out to the tea bushes and enjoyed our tea there. We did learn about how tea is made and seeing the actual plant was interesting to me. Wish it was less crowded.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

We got the bus to this amazing temple which we found quite easily.  It was one of the most beautiful temples we visited in Korea and one of the few which you are actually allowed to go inside free of charge. There are many parts to this temple which is comprised of several buildings all really interesting and it is set in pretty gardens.  Well worth a visit.

This is a great volcanic cave with very interesting information cards dotted around to teach the novice geologist more about how it was formed and the story of the cave. Its a bit out the way but you can get the 101 circle route to nearby then one of the 7xx buses up to it

However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

strictly for those above 18.but beware that buses come here ends early.after 10pm i only see taxis and cars.Interesting stone sculptures of male and female organs.sex positions..a shop selling interesting condoms and penis keychains vibrators etc..super cold at night..open until midnight..there is a indoor museum and show clay figurines..

So you get to this place and will be faced with mountains of oranges  pork knuckles and fish. Bet its the place to be if your mission is to get groceries or some local snacks.But if you want to buy souvenior  this place isn't really ideal as most stuff 竊늨ranges you can't take overseas  fishe neither;packed snacks are like what you can see all over the island 竊뎤eems a bit mass produced.The interesting to observe is that most shops are ran by one solo lady  only. They took a lot of hardship to get the business running .
Many tour buses with tourists the museum is nothing interesting at least to me. There is an innisfree outlet and an organic caf챕. The Green Tea Plantation is open to the public for photography.

It isn't worth travelling all the way but if you are passing by it is an interesting stop. The optical illusion is really amazing. It looks like we are climbing uphill without any help. You can even try by placing a can or bottle or even water. Place is rather crowded though. Seem to be a common tourist stop for most with lots of buses.

Interesting optical illusion. Most busses and car will stop at this stretch (near to 100m - 200m) to demonstrate this trick. However i felt it is quite unsafe as alot tourist are standing beside the road and some will try trick on their own like rolling bottle in the middle of road. Just around 5 mins walk to Loveland and around 20 mins taxi ride from jeju city.

I visited this as part of an inclusive tour.  This is really interesting.  there is the story of tea and you can walk among the tea bushes.  This is the best Korea tea there is and of course you can buy their products and sample green tea foods in the cafe. Their sister beauty products company Innesfree also has a cafe and gift shop.  Again these products have a hig reputation in S. Korea.  I would have liked more time to spend here.  The main cafe was packed and I would have like to have had green tea and green tea cake or green tea ice cream but I wouldn't have been able to see anything else in the time we had.  A pleasant place to visit for a few hours.

I enjoyed the scenic beaches with aquamarine waters.. u can rent a escooter or take the shuttle bus (loop) to explore the island..there are many interesting cafes on the island..the specialty shld be their peanut ice cream..

I ate here on two of my four nights in Jeju. Excellent food stalls at night and it was busy but to me a buzz. It is always interesting to wander round and see what is available before choosing. I know little Korean but the signs are self explanatory and most of the stall holders help

An interesting place to visit though there is nothing much except for the short stretch of road.. It's amazing to see that the bus really glide uphill.. Some cars are not able to do a good job and the driver ended up starting their engine and start driving

Although the museum's location is in the middle of nowhere and from Jeju city I had to switch the buses it was definately worth visiting. If you are interested in history and you would like to know what was happening in the island during the war you will find the answers there. It was very interesting and heartbreaking I am glad I found all this information in English and that I had a chance to have a glimpse into Jeju's past.

After getting bad instructions on the bus route we arrived late to the tea museum and walked through the museum quickly.  I missed my chance of purchasing the green tea ice cream and did not know it was near closing time.  By the time we walked back to the cafe the doors were locked and told they were closed!  We took pictures of the tea fields and of the giant cup with their sign. I didn't think the museum was very interesting as I wanted to taste the tea itself.

What's interesting is that you really, actually get to see cars/buses with their engines obviously off, rolling up the slope. Expect to see a number of tour buses. Some tour guides will demonstrate the mysteriousness of the road even further by pouring water on the ground. The water will flow upwards. 10mins is enough time to spend here. Recommended to visit once for the experience.

What is so mysterious about this road is that vehicles can still move upslope with the engine switched off. We had the engine of the bus switched off and experienced it first hand what it felt like. The bus was first moving at a very slow speed but it started to gear up towards the end of the road. We then got off the bus to watch other vehicle move on the road. It was quite an interesting sight. Somewhere nearby, I even saw a stand giving out free Christian literature. Lots of snacks available. My first time trying the milk. At first, I thought it was some yoghurt drink or a big bottle of Yakult. Tried the one with black cap and realised that it's banana milk. I never like flavoured milk but this taste nice.More pictures available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html

We were staying in the Seogwipo area (near the International Convention Center), so it took us about an hour by bus to get to the Stone Park. It was interesting, with some unususal lava formations, but the drizzling rain didn't help in enjoying the scenery. The   museum   is OK, but nothing spectacular. When you (if) select a sunny day!

We went to the cave by a convenient bus frm Jeju city. There is a 2km-wlak form bus station to the cave (I would not recommend to take the taxis that are waiting for you as a total tourist). After the 20mn-minute walk, the cave is very interesting and informations about it are quite depth.

We walked past Yongdu-am rock when we were trying to find the jimjilbang that we were staying at for the night. If we had made any effort to go and see it I would have been bummed but since it was in passing it was interesting in its own manner. I can understand how it looks like a dragon and you don't need TOO much of an imagination to be able to see it but unless your interested in folklore/'the dragon' means anything to you, you won't be overly excited/impressed.If it didn't have reams of tourists and tour buses or the tourist shops all around it Im not sure I would have even stopped to take a picture.(the ladies working in the tour information centre right outside of this area speak good english and are very kind and helpful if you need directions)

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We must have been very lucky, because there was almost no one else around the day we went and we were there in the middle of the afternoon. We were there in October, so maybe it's less busy (but we were there during Chinese Golden Week, so I dunno?). It's definitely worth checking out if you enjoy unique and interesting rock formations.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We didn't have great weather when we were on the island so couldn't climb the mountain. This was an alternative activity and glad we did it as it was really interesting. Make sure you go all the way to the end as you don't want to miss the lava flow. The ground is slippy in places and not suitable for small children, strollers or wheelchairs. If you're using public transport get the bus 900. Not the 701 as we did! The 701 has a stop called 'Manjamggul Cave entrance' but it's 2km walk away from the entrance!!

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

Visually, the road is seen to be an uphill road. But when the bus driver turned off the engine and release the brakes, it starts to move forward. Quite interesting. But don't purposely go there unless it's part of the journey. Not worth.

Visiting Jeju ? Do it if you have at least4 days or more ! All the tourist attractions are in different corners of the island and they are far from each other .There are daily bus tours , running in one direction , starting at 9am coming back at 6 pm . Not every spot is so interesting , probably many of travellers have seen some similar somewhere else . The same is reg. this small beach . There are plenty of such beaches or even nicer around the world
Very interesting road that the car or bus or water bottle can walk by themself without anything, very weird

Udo was easy to get to and a great place to camp with full amenities. There are 2 main beaches; one on the West side and one on the North East side. Both are beautiful but the one that has sand made of seashells (West Side) is a little hard on your bare feet  and it was much busier there. The other has soft fine sand that makes for a great camping spot. There are no taxis on the island. In hindsight, we would have taken the other ferry to the port that was a bit closer to Hagosudong Beach (the NE side), but there is this drop on and off Bus Tour System that costs 5000won/person. You can get on from the ferry, drop off and set up your camp at the beach, then hop back on. It runs frequently but only stops at 4 main sightseeing spots (beach 1, beach 2, caves and ___ ) . We were able to use the bus for the two days we were there for on the same fare, but there are times/stops that are crazy busy. We watched at least 6 packed buses go by before we decided to stay the night. Honorable food mention: Pirate Caf챕. Really interesting place and staff. Great BiBamBap and you get to sign a plaque and hang it from their wall when you?re done eating.Friendly people, campfire and camping friendly, personal beer cooler (at the convenience stores directly behind the beach), and lots of cats.

This was an interesting experience. I am usually ok in small spaces and felt this would be a great thing to do. But once I was in the middle of the first maze I felt a little uneasy. They provide a map and the maze itself is pretty easy to do. You also hear people walking around, but just something about the possibility of making a wrong turn made me not want to do the second and third maze. But there are really cool towers and a museum where you can take amazing pictures. the museum is free, they have trick art and a puzzle art. Getting here was a little bit difficult. Ask around your previous destination at the bus stop perhaps some people are willing to share taxi with you. Since the bus that goes around this area takes almost 45 minutes. And once you get to your destination you sometimes still have to walk a while to get to where you want to.

This was a very interesting Lava Tube cave.  There were signs in English as well as various other languages describing what you were looking at.  The signs were informative.  The cave is cool, so I recommend a zippered sweatshirt or windbreaker.  Also, the floor of the cave is uneven, so you definitely want to have good walking shoes.  I was just fine wearing old jogging shoes.  We went as part of a guided tour - I would have liked to spend just a little more time there, but that's how it goes on bus tours...  There may be more beautiful caves, but overall, it was the nicest cave I've been in - very nice Lava Tube - you will enjoy it.

This village was very interesting. A lot of people still live in this village and they make a living off of the products that they sell. The village is free to go to, so we made sure to purchase some things in the village. We encountered a couple English speakers that guided us and explained some things to us. They were so sweet, they held onto some of our belongings at their home while we walked through the village. When we were done they offered to call us a taxi. When we told them we planned on taking the bus they insisted on driving my entire family to our next destination. They were so sweet, it was very heartwarming!

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This road is interesting! When we are about to reach the site, the driver turned off the engine, and yet the bus is moving upwards!! Amazing!We even went down the bus to try running backward on the road, and one can feel like you are being pulled from the back. Also, we try by pouring water onto the road itself, which is a good test.And yes, the food stall along the road is more interesting.

This is a really interesting place to visit, although, be warned, if you're taking the city bus, the actual caves are about a 20 minute walk from the stop. Be prepared to pay for a taxi (who will hassle you to hire him for a full day tour) or walk.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

the pinky building and all kitty stuffs! Very interesting and nice place for pictures. they have cafe & shop for kitty stuffs, Kitty fans this is the place do not be missed. things slightly expensive because of   Sanrio   brand. but not so tourist friendly cos its not a walking distance from town, either by bus or taxi. We took bus to Kitty island (but missed one station cos we dont understand Korean language, we only stop the bus driver when we passed kitty island), for return in convenient we pick taxi (black color), cost us 60USD back to town (like 10mins distance only)

The Mysterious Road is an interesting to visit while in Jeju and don't need to pay. The Bus Driver show that even with the engine stopped, the bus still able to move forward. The visit won't take too much of the time, just interestingly an eye illumination.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The exhibits were pretty interesting actually but as mentioned in the title, it's a mainly outdoor venue! The glass sculptures look better in the day time or at night when the lights are on.. SO..! If the weather is not helpful, save it for another day! It's pretty far out, so if u are gonna go, do the O'sulluc tea museum and this together... Don't leave too late coz it's terribly difficult to get a cab, unless you have a pre-arranged driver. That said, the staff there really are very, very nice.. We were actually the last few patrons out and we were stranded without a cab, in the bloody freezing rain.. We had 3 ahjussis trying to help us call cabs and eventually one of em offered to drive us to the nearest bus stop instead coz no one was responding, and FYI the nearest bus stop is abt 10mins out too..

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.
Small museum, but provides nice insight into Haenyeo business. You can miss it, though - the exhibition was not that interesting

Seriously, this rock simply had a good marketing team that created a story and a good image of this rock.. Bus visually you can find so much more interesting rocks in any other place of the Jeju island

Read the introductions and you will find the visit to this cave that much more interesting. It is not that dark so you don?t really need a torchlight. Take bus 201 from Jeju city bus terminal. It is worth making that 1hour trip. If you don?t wish to walk 25min or so from the bus stop, change to another bus that will bring you to the doorstep

quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.

Our tour guide built up anticipation of this phenomenon hours before we arrived at the site, and by then, our entire bus load of tourists were completely curious as to what we would experience.It was all over in less than a minute, but still interesting to see how a natural illusion could occur if the conditions are right.It's not worth making the effort just to see this short stretch of road, but if you happen to be in the vicinity, by all means see if the illusion works on you!

One of the many very interesting sites in Jeju Island.  These women would dive for 2 minutes at a time to harvest food from the ocean bottom, using no tanks or other equipment.  They were the only known groups of women who resisted during the Japanese occupation.  Also good access by bus.  Easy to get there by bike, depending on where you are staying on the Island. NIce bike paths, though often are covered with the drying sea weed that the old women still harvest from the rocks. There is also a very small Buddhist temple with a Quan Yin statue in front, about a half mile to the west along the coast.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Of all the places we visited in Jeju via our taxi tour, this is what I would rank as #1 (see  http://www.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=1121529), with Sunrise Peak as #2.  This is a Buddhist temple set in a vast very pretty land.  Interesting Buddha statues ? very exotic particularly for those who have never been to a Buddhist temple.  Our taxi guide politely asked, I believe a caretaker, to see if we can actually go inside the temple.  We were allowed.  I?m not sure if it was early or this is not a traditional tourist place, since we only saw very few people (as compared to the other temple in Busan packed with too many people.)  Felt a little bit odd being a tourist spectator in a house of worship, but glad we did.  The landscaping and statutes in the area were very interesting.  So there's more to see other than the temple itself. I would recommend this place for sure.  Would go back again if have the chance.  Hopefully with less rain this time.  Free to visit.

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Markets have always been interesting to me. They show so much about how the locals eat, shop, trade and work. Dongmun Market is pretty laidback. The folks there are not pushy. It's hardly touristy but still attracts a fair number of tourists. You mainly get to see seafood, fruits and vegetables as you explore the many lanes at the market. Aside from the market itself, the businesses nearby are also colourful and pix-worthy.For me, the highlight of the visit is lunch at one of the several restaurants within a zone at the market. They specialise in seafood, of course, and offer sets (featuring sashimi, a grilled fish, fish stew and banchan) that are value for money.Also don't miss some snack stalls there. My favourite is operated by an old lady (probably in her 70s)  who makes hatteok, sort of a pancake filled with cinnamon sugar, on the spot. It's a sweet, hot treat.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.

I've visited many caves but by far this is the first lava tube that I have experienced. It is interesting to know the science and geography behind this magnificent tube. However, only 1 km deep into the tube is open to tourists. You can take a public bus directly from the Jeju bus station if you opt to travel on a budget. The bus fare is less than KRW 2000 compared to very pricey tours with taxi. The bus ride is only slightly more than an hour away from Jeju City.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It took about 10 minutes to travel on a ferry to visit Udo (thanks to G map)!I decided to walked around the coastline after lunch on arrival.An interesting island with some public arts and you wouldn?t stop taking photos!It worth spending some time walking around! (A number of transportation options are available, such as bike, e-bike and bus)!

Interesting road... My bus was shifted to neutral gear and went up th hill by itself....Had saw this before in Taiwan and china... It was actually an optical illusion .. Nonetheless quite amaze by it. Other than this generally speaking the attraction has no depth... Can go if visiting some other attraction in the area, but not worth it if travelling long distance for it .
If you're a free and easy traveller, I'll totally not recommend you to travel to see this mysterious road. If you're on a tour bus, this is an interesting experience.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

As with everything on Jeju, this is built for tourists. The cave itself is interesting but understand there is nothing but this one section of one cave that you can access. This is not in the least bit adventurous - the cave is lit well all along its length. It's the kindergarten of caves but if you haven't been in a lava tube before then it may be for you. Beware that if you take the bus to the caves, you still have 2.5 km on foot to the cave entrance, though you can flag a cab down if one happens past.  Overall ok, but don't expect to be blown away.

Apart from walking 2.5km in the extreme summer heat from the bus stop outside (pls find alternative routes), the cave was unique and pretty interesting to see. Love the temperature inside to cool us down and be away from the heat too.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.
A small market by Seoul's standards. But still interesting to see, quite touristy and there is a main street that sells seafood, another that sells fried snacks. A bustling place even at night

A seemingly slightly uphill slope that can move a stationary vehicle. Many vehicles such as buses and taxis stopped there, presumably with tourists, and were moving without engine revving; an interesting sight to behold. Puzzling, but loses charm after a while, unless you are physicists who needs to get to the bottom of it

A place to walk, relax, and connect with nature! The Spirited Garden is regarded as one of the world's most beautiful gardens. The entire garden was designed by one man, Mr. Sung, which is quite interesting. The Spirited Garden includes 7 smaller gardens. The Secret Garden, one of the seven small gardens, is a world-class location for business meetings and diverse performance. It has received several awards, including Korea Unique Venue, Green MICE Venue, Jeju Unique Venue, etc. This garden is an unmissable place for those who love nature!
We stop here on the way to the airport. It's quiet interesting experience when the car moves. Can't help laughing inside the car as the power is off but it still moves.
Waterfalls have always been interesting to me and this one certainly was among the top 10 I have visited.

this park is right next to Jeongbang Waterfalls  and only costs 500 SKW. We spent an hour there reading up the interesting story of how Xu Fu  the elixir who was said to have stopped here while his envoy with 500 (3000) boys and girls set sail in search for immortal medicine for the Qin Emperor in 219BC. He was said to have left inscriptions on the cliff next to the waterfall marking his presence there.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내

review: The interior was beautiful and the cafe served interesting food and drinks. Had the Tangerine tea which was flavoursome and beautifully set. They even had a Mount Hallasan cake which was made of Green Tea cake with white chocolate frost topping

The cliff is formed from lava flow. Hexagonal basalt columns like those in Ireland. It is interesting if you have not seen this kind of formation. It will be interesting if you could visit during high tide and high waves as the crashing waves may reach all the way to the top.
It's shorter distance in real than I thought. But definately an interesting place to stop by! I both walked and drived along the road!
It's an illusion so you have to see it to understand. Quite interesting and also funny to see all cars stopping their engine to slide down the slope.
It used to have some light water activity around but it has been stopped for some environmental conservation purposes. But it is still interesting to see where the streams meet the tide.
Interesting on a rainy day and only if you have visited all of the important sights on Jeju. Worth a stop if you are on your way to Sanbangsan but not worth a special trip just to visit.

Given the trials and tribulations faced by the Dutch crew all those centuries ago  I did find it irritating that the top deck of the boat was closed because the wind had risen to a slight breeze. I am unsure what sort of risk or danger the owners were trying to mitigate against  as I am sure the bridge would have been perfectly sate and noone was going to be blown overboard by a tiny puff of air. The display inside the boat tells an interesting story. The Covid temperature readers at the entrance were causing the staff member a bit of trouble (and they are inaccurate) and we almost got the impression that it was our fault for being foreign humans unable to work broken temperature readers. Hamel would have given up trying.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안

review: An interesting museum with various glass sculptures including a large pyramid that you can walk through. Staff were kind enough to let us try glass blowing and have a few activities available - we made candles. Worth stopping for if you're in the area  but probably not worth a detour.

Went to the 1100m point where the wetland reserve is. Didn?t occur to me that wetland exists on mountain top. A round trip takes about 20mins and was quite scenic. It was foggy when we were there, which adds to the ambience. Our guide pointed out some of the edible leaves and tree sap. Very interesting stopover on the way to the south.

We were attracted by the promise from the literature that this was the only waterfall in Asia with 'debouches' into the ocean. Hmmm, you almost get the impression from above that some channel engineering has helped this along. Anyway, Wikipedia tells me that this claim is not quite correct. Anyway, we arrived as then had to purchase entry tickets. The stressed out man next to the ticket gate then seemed to think that we have not purchased the correct amount of tickets. We had. It was all the more puzzling because he was only 2 feet from where we bought the tickets. Maybe he was so bored he was asleep at the wheel. Or maybe it was because we were foreigners. Anyway, once that nonsense was resolved we headed down the steps, only to be stopped half-way down at yer another ticket check! Ridiculous, three check for a 1000-or-so won entry ticket. We thought we must be in for something very special. Alas not. Said waterfall falls a few score metres, generates a modest amount of spray and attracts thousands of people taking selfies of themselves and said insipid attraction. There are some older folk selling ghastly looking octopus slices by the rocks - poor animals (the octopus that is). We were not stopped for more ticket checks on the way out, thankfully. I suggest you just look at the photo on the web and go and do something more interesting instead.

We went to the market wanted to try some fresh octopus. We bought an octopus from a stall and the nice lady told us in broken English that we can have it prepared at the nearby restaurant. So we went into that restaurant just opposite the seafood stall. None of them can't speak English, even a little bit. So went back to the seafood stall and asked the nice lady to help us. So we seated in the restaurant waiting just for our octopus to be prepared. Then they bring out the cutlery.. we were quite puzzled... why does one octopus need so many cutlery.. then they took out the big steamboat with all the seafood in it! We keep using sign language to say show we don't want the steamboat and just want our octopus prepare... after a while we gave in. and our octopus came out serve in a plate, fully chopped into tiny bits like being blended in a food processor :(we have had enough seafood steamboat over the past few days in Jeju and this is not the time we want to eat the steamboat again. oh well, all because of language barrier and luckily we still have enough cash to pay for the meal as they don't accept credit card.Besides the story, local products sell in this market are quite interesting.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

We stopped here without planning, and the road looks like it?s inclined hill, but when you put ur transmission in neutral, the car still goes forward for like few yards. But that?s it. Nothing more interesting tho. It was pretty quick tour spot

We stopped by the mysterious road on the way back to the hotel, Our guide did the customary demonstrations- car in neutral brakes, water bottle and measuring tape. Interesting to see if you happen to be in the vicinity but don't go out of your way.

Very interesting for the first time. The local guide told us they name this road as   monster road   cos locals belive there is a invisible monster playing with the cars that's why the car move forward when uphill even stop engine. Great experience
Underwhelming. We needed a stop and there were some interesting shops nearby (persimmons and mushrooms, I think) so it wasn't a total loss, but not worth the detour.

This was the last stop of our tour so the sun was setting by the time we got there. I recommend coming in the morning for good pictures. It was quite solemn, cold, and eerie because it was just the tour guide of the village, our tour guide, and the rest of our group in the area. The assigned tour guide had very interesting insights on the place and the rest of Jeju culture. She also sold us some products that the folks of the village made. The berry honey is definitely worth buying.

This was our first stop during our weekend trip to Jeju. I had heard about these women before but didn't know much. First, they showed us a video (in English) all about the history. I was immediately hooked! The rest of the museum is so interesting. The pictures and artifacts tell a great story. I just wish I could have met the Haenyeo personally! Also, the women working at the museum were nice and helpful as we tried to get to our next stop.

This was one of our stops in our taxi tour for that day.This is a small place showing the traditional homes of that area a long time ago.  It?s free. An English speaking guide will tour you around.  Some interesting facts, like two separate doors (one bigger for the male I think.) They will offer you a drink made of honey and some fermentation of some berries.  It?s like juice but with some tart aftertaste.  Taste good though that we spent I think $40.00 for a bottle.  In hindsight, maybe a bit too much considering it?s not an alcoholic drink (tongue in cheek).  But while drinking that juice at home, it sure brings in mind our visit to Jeju.  While there we saw a black pig with a small companion rat.  Well seems the rat was hovering near the pig pen.  Interesting place and the guide did tell some interesting stories and tidbits! (Can be done in half an hour).

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This is just another roadside attraction that many people visiting Jeju stop by to see only because it is in the city proper. It is just a rock that could appear to look like any number of different animals.If your tour guide takes you out of your way to see this then you need a new tour guide because this rock is typical of any of the millions of rocks you run into along the seashore in Jeju.There are a lot of interesting things to see and fun places to go in Jeju but, this isn't one of them.

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

The title Theme Park may confuse some people. This is not an amusement park, just some natural park with lots of greenery, ponds, windmill, etc. You get on a train that takes you around the park, stopping at several stops where you can get off and later get on the train to move on to the next stop. Honestly, the park is just okay. Not much to see or do here.  I recommend you save your time and find other, more interesting attraction in Jeju

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The musueum is dedicated to the Haenyeo - female divers who traditionally fish for molluscs and octopuses etc. without using oxygen masks.  UNESCO has declared the Haenyeo part of humankind's intangible cultural heritage.  We visited the museum shortly after having seen a group of Haenyeo sing their traditional song before heading out into the sea to fish.  Having just witnessed the women fist hand added an extra element of interest.  The museum is well set out, informative and interesting.  Its models, life stories of individuals and displays of clothes and tools  really bring home how tough the life of the Haenyeo was in the past (and it's not easy today).  There is also a short movie explaining the history and traditions of the Haenyeo.  Well worth a visit!

The lava tubes are very interesting and quite large - especially compared to those in other parts of the world. The only word of caution is to bring a raincoat and sneakers if it has been raining, as the water will trickle down through the rock and will drip considerably as you walk through. Definitely worth a stop.

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The dragon head rock makes for an interesting photo souvenir. It is a nice place to visit, but probably would not count as one of the must-see places in Korea. Shops selling grilled octopus and other snacks line the route to the attraction, but the food is nothing spectacular as well. Allocate 30 minutes for the place.

Nice place to stop by, especially if travelling with kids but an interesting attraction all the same for adults. Teddy bears in various displays from famous movie, artworks and different eras. Lots of photo opportunities!

Must walk..hike to the top.  Worth to go..because the nice scenery. Not suitable for old people & wheelchair. Really a huge place. Actually is a die volcano. But really beautiful.. when you on top the hill. Definate you wont regret . But must have a good stamina. Certain hour, there is a woman diver show. Quite interesting.

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool...
