I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Along the Mysterious Road, have a few food stall, try out the grilled black pork sausage and many delicious food. For those driving, key in the number 7126988 (yup.. heading to Loveland, you will reach Mysterious Road first), most people stop by here on the way to airport.

It rained almost nonstop on our trip to Jeju so we visited a lot of museums we probably would normally have not. The hologram concert is the major attraction in Play Kpop and it was good fun. The rest? Meh. The entry ticket is 15 000 won which is rather expensive since most museums on the island just cost a few thousand won. On top of that, a lot of the other attractions (like photo booths) cost extra. Kpop history was interesting enough, but most of the other stuff was quite boring.
it looks just like any other waterfall. this place can be skipped if you have other interesting places to go, or you can just stop over for a short while.
It is very interesting place, amazing. However if you wanna reach the top, you will have to put effort to go there.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is interesting because people actually live there in the old style.  The physical village wasn't much different from other villages you can stop at.  Even though some other places were created for tourist, at least the villagers acted happy and were willing to share some information.
Interesting to learn about the wood positioning at gate, durable rooftop, ceramic tanks in kitchen, building of crib, above ground toilet and shade.Delighted to pass by a winery social area.

In my opinion the best way to go around the island is a bicycle. About 16km. Took us 4h to make it, with stop in every single possible place, including a lunch brake, rest on a beach, etc. Most interesting for us were diving women, we had a chance to see at work in few places. Probably the island is crowded in a season. In May we had good time and enjoy the trip very much.

I'm coming from a developing country and would expect more from the markets in developed country such as South Korea. The market is as dirty as my country's wet markets. Generally the country is not tourist friend enough. A lot of interesting consumable   seafood   types in the market that I haven't seen in my country and wished to try. However, I couldn't find any label of the seafood stated in English or han zi (chinese character). The shop owners too couldn't communicate in any languages that I know. A lot of times my desire to try was stopped upon not knowing the best way to eat, eating raw? Deep fried or stir fried is better?Frankly, I would expect the overall standard close to the markets in Japan or other western countries.
If you are around it will be interesting to see. There are also candies, fruit & vegetables. Saw an octopus trying to scape and remember Finding Dory. ;)

I was really impressed by this museum, designed by the famous Japanese architet Tadao Ando. The architecture of the building and the beautiful garden make this place worth a visit, but the collection is also really interesting. I really loved the collection artefacts from the late Joseon period an the special exhibition 'Carriage to Heaven' that shows sangyeo (traditional funeral bier) and kkokdu (small statues used as decoration for the sangjyeo). The joyous artwork of Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama were a nice extra on top of all that.Not to be missed when visiting Jeju.

I think it was more academic then entertaining. Despite cutting edge technology based attraction, this place has enough mixture of both interesting facts and entertainment. Restaurant was lots of fun as well. And I think it means a lot to see the corporate name. People all know   Nintendo   but not many knows a top Korean game corporate. I think it is nice.

I really did enjoy working my way through this maze. The entire area is beautifully put together and is the kind of place you just want to spend time in and enjoy. Unfortunately, uniqueness comes with a price. I thought nearly $5 per person was a little steep but it isn't every day you get to walk through a hedge maze. The maze itself is a lot of fun and is large enough to actually be a bit of a challenge. We met the owner and he is very friendly and interesting to talk to. I am glad we stopped here but, because of the price, I don't think I would do it again.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

For us - it was a last 'must see' on Jeju Island.  Our tour books featured it as a top site, so we went.  We didn't have much time, and it worked (since it's near the airport) for a quick stop off.  I didn't hate it - it was crowded though.  Lots of tour groups, teens, etc.  There were several shops nearby that were handy for our last bit of shopping.  You don't need to spend a lot of time here, but the rock formation is neat and the myth behind it is interesting.
For me it's not a very special sight, though it's adventurous and interesting to walk down the stairs to the coast and see the   diving women   serving octopus, shells and abalone on the rock
Enjoyed wandering through flowers, and bonsai trees. Interesting look at the folk village and some gorgeous peacocks. Takes a couple hours tops but a nice place to visit

As with many cars that went there, my taxi stopped, turned off the engine, switched to Neutral gear and yes, the car started rolling uphill......But interestingly, the road is also called the demon road there. Look around the place, and you will see some cute little   devils   around the place.Nothing much there else, expect that you need to be there and say you done that.

We went to the memorial hall to see the exhibition on Kim Manduk after we visited a recreation of her travellers' in that is about 150m away.I have always admired Korea's efforts to recreate buildings and scenes fron the past that are both infirmative and interesting.The exhibit at the hall added to what we had learnt at the inn.What comes across from the information cards and exhibits was a woman dedicated to the service of others.Profit was never her main motive. Nor self-aggrandizement.We need more people like her today.

We visited here as part of a ships tour. The 8 minute film was very interesting. There are three exhibit halls. The first two were the best. You can see the whole thing in less than an hour. I wouldn?t go out of my way to come here

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We had an old Korean man who has lived there for all his life guiding us around his own house in English. He was very humorous and a very friendly guide. It was an interesting and refreshing experience of learning about the old village way of living in Jeju!

We drove around Jeju and decided to give this thing a go cos we didn't believe it would be possible. So we reached the road and there were signs that told you that its the starting. So all you have to do is to put your car in neutral gear and release the accelerator at the starting point and watch your friend's jaw drop. Recommended to visit together with Jeju Loveland as its just 3 minutes driave away. Admission at 8000 won per pax. pricey but its a pretty interesting visit XD
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

Very interesting maze. First 2 are fairly easy but the 3rd one gets a little tricky. Water mist kept getting in the way as you try to navigate so it gets a little more complicated. The kids and adults had a fun time. Should do it without the maps given so you just have to rely on sense of direction.
very cool. a cave that was chilling yet interesting always cool to have a look into the past as it is.

this place offers audio guided tour which we loaned kind of gotten lost along the way and didnt really follow the sequence. there are many interesting places to see but more of less are quite similar with regard to the houses and all the area is big and spaced out. it will be great if there are a little more resting areas/bench along the road for visitors to rest along the way. better wayfinding would be good as well.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.
The Manjanggul Cave was a nice outing for my family and I. Very dark and wet and long but was interesting to read the facts along the way. Would definitely visit again.

The butterfly museum is interesting showcasing many species of insects but the information are all in Korean. Walk out of the building there is an outdoor park with a maze. The mirror maze is not to be missed the kids had so much fun finding their way out!

Spent a few hours at the museum along with many many others! Small building with some good information but crowds crammed the shop which leads into the cafe. This caused overcrowding and did not make for the most enjoyable afternoon. Outdoors area is worth wandering through and the gardens and fields are worth looking at. The Innisfree Jeju House across the way is probably more interesting.

Quite interesting maze. It took us a bit more time than expected to find the way out and it was funny. If you plan to take a brake in this area I would certainly recommend spend about hour to play in the maze.

Plenty of interesting glass installations in the park and museum. Really worth to see. Very nice and friendly owner. Many beautiful things and funny toys in the shop. The best way to get there is by taxi  it's about $15 from Seogwipo city center.

Our hotel room overlooks this sea. Don't think there is a way to get down but the waterfront makes for a nice breezy walk. I suppose the reason for the decoration on the barrier is to make the walk interesting and photo worthy.

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.

Must visit if you are traveling with kids. It's in the southern part of Jeju. Site is interesting and educational. Taxi fare from main city is around 35KRW one way. There also other interesting sites around the place.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.

It?셲 not much of a museum really but more like a short glorification and summary of the history of O?셲ulloc. I would?셶e actually been interested in finding out more about how tea is grown tea types production etc. the tea fields surrounding the actual museum are more interesting. Following the (very small) museum (which is also free of entry to be fair) one is led to the tea shop/ cafe in what I can only describe as a controlled stampede! I didn?셳 find any way to actually sample some tea or at least smell it before buying; I kinda wanted to get a better idea of a bag of tea that costs up to 100$ before buying it. At Twinings in London they understand that and offer free samples. In other places you can at least smell the tea. At O?셲ulloc you get what you see on the shelf (if you can reach it that is). The most interesting part a traditional sampling is exclusive to Koreans only. Yes foreigners (even those speaking Korean) are not welcome in those (if they didn?셳 change their policy on that at least; I didn?셳 try booking one admittedly). So all that is left really is a big commercial party without any sense of tea culture or educative elements at all. Quite disappointing!

It was very fun with all the interesting paintings to take photos with. Initially there wasn't much crowd. Halfway through suddenly there was an influx of Korean students and it was very difficult to take photos with each and every painting. It was better near the evening when the students left. Conclusion: worth going!

It was a 2km walk (1km each way) and it is not easy to walk in low light and on uneven ground. Suggest to make bring your own led light especially if with old folks. It was interesting to see how this cave was formed by lava.
It is interesting of the maze and provide bonding time with family when try to explore our way out of the maze.

It is hard to say anything good about this place. Basically  it is a small chocolate gift shop that charges $3 a person to enter. You receive a coupon good for $3 back on any purchase. I suppose it is their way to ensure that you buy something.The only interesting thing was that they had these cookie balls that you smashed with a hammer to eat.

Interesting to see the way the old buildings were built nut was a tad boring. I thought we'd see people making things in the old methods but most of the buildings were empty. Not what we thought we'd see. With the lack of time we had a Jeju I would have preferred to see something else.
Interesting but not a must. The village tries to explore the way of life in the past. Not to impressive.

I would not go out of my way to try to swim here. But it is pretty and interesting next to the cliff.  Water bathrooms and other services not available when we were there but it was off season so maybe there's something there during the summer. The stairs up the cliff will kick your butt.

I visited to Da vinci museum with my daughter last weekend.It was very interesting and educational place.There are many experience activities like making a paddle steamer  shooting water bomb  etc.My daughter made a paddle steamer  she really liked it. Anyway I was surprised that I can see the Da vinci's works in Korea not itary.

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.
History behind very interestingGood to see onceShort visitWay of making the visit more attractive

Has serene garden  $3 entrance fee. They preserved the deceased artists study which was interesting. The photos had a rare spiritual feel to them. Out of the way  took almost an hour to get there from our hotel in seoguipo  be careful not to speed above posted speed limit - there were about 20 traffic cameras along the way and even saw two impromptu mobile speed camera setups.

Great place to experience how the early koreans lived. Learn more about their way of life by exploring the village. There are hands on experiences like grinding the corn playing traditional games pounding grains etc. There is also traditional folk dance performance daily. Really fun and interesting!

Generally a fun and interesting exhibition due to the interactivity of the exhibits/3D photos. However if you are expecting a large variety of interaction you will be slightly disappointed. About halfway through the museum most exhibits start to feel similar. More enjoyable for teenagers-like crowds. Recommend about 1-1.5 hours for the whole museum.

Fun...but not ONE that you would go all out to do it. Some of us manage to complete and ring the bell in 30mins other do got lost if not good at reading maps. The maze is lacking in maintenance. The checkpoints do not correspond with the maps and the chops has no inks disappointing the children. If you are a cat lover it is a interesting place. We visit the maze on the way to Manjanggul Lava Tube.

Didn't have much time so decided to watch the woman diver show first at the shores of seongsan ilchulbong (otherwise known as Sunrise peak). Shows are 130pm and 3pm. Quite interesting but they didn't seem to collect many sea creatures during the show. So the diving is mainly drive for tourists' sake. Can also buy fresh sea food from the women divers and get the restaurant right there to cook it. Walked up half way after that to grab some photo shots.
Didn't expect the lava cave to be that long. But it was an interesting experience. Wear waterproof non-slip shoes as the floor is always wet.

Could have spent half a day here. Gardens were beautiful. The lava caves were nice to walk through to break up the heat! Interesting animals throughout.  Ran out of time and missed seeing the water gardens.  Great way to spend a day outside. Especially enjoyed the bonsai garden.

As a resident of Jeju  I enjoy walking through this park every week. It is a great and safe place to take kids or walk dogs. There are two parts to the park: north of the road and south of the road. In the southern part  there are interesting ponds and pathways.I would not recommend this place to tourists only because there is so much else to see in Jeju Island that is far more impressive than this park. However  it is only a five minute walk from the city Center (Jungang Rotary) to the northern part so it is not far at all.

Across the street from the museum is a green tea patch where people can take touristy pictures and just walk around. The day I was there it was way too hot to even attempt to take photos. Inside the building isn't really a museum but a tea shop that has a lot of variations of teas. There's also a little cafe that serves hot and cold tea drinks along with simple snacks to have with you tea. Out back there is a walkway for people so that they can see the open landscape. There is also a Innisfree Jeju Island shop that has make-up and it was interesting to see some of the main ingredients in their skincare line out on display. The Innisfree shop also had it's own separate cafe with beverages and food.

You may find it interesting if you are interested in a legend, folk tale or something like that. The story goes like this, there were three gods who came to Jeju and lived peacefully... And one day.... But it's usually in Korean. Especially the movie was dubbed in Korean. It should have English version. But I am not sure there is. The movie is good way you come to know the story.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) ! After you flood yrselves silly with pics, you can try the maze. Its interesting walking in and out and along the way you can look out for cats that are just chillin by the greenery. Overall a good experience especially for families !

what made this place interesting besides the dragon head was the locals selling their wares.  We also bought our first hallabong here.  I can tell you prices are pretty much the same all over for those hallabongs.  If you walk down there are a lot of ajjumas selling I think sea food, I did not walk all the way down since I did not have the right foot wear but it seemed like fresh sea food.It is a very touristy place, we just took a look few pictures and left.  Its one of those places we dont have to go see again once you seen it thats good enough.  But were are glad we did see it.  Again I would have walked down to the ocean side but opted not to might have been interesting, so make sure you have the right footwear, it is rocky and maybe a little wet.

We were there with a tour group and this itinary was compulsory.  Interesting to understand the history and a better understanding of the culture.  The guide of the village was obviously a Chinese but they spin it to say she is Korean (didn't see any)!  Sold products after the talk and items were not cheap.  360,000 Won for the Horse Bone Powder.  50,000 Won for the Horse Oil.  Saw at other shops away from the village, selling at 30,000 Won for the Horse oil.  Bought the Horse Bone powder and realized everything was in Korean!  If this is a State product and only sold in the village, pamplets of it should be in multi - languages as it is targeted at tourists.

We went to this cave as friends want to visit even it was not on my bucket list. It was impressive to see volcanic layers and massive path inside. We walked down all way to the end i.e. 1 km away and walk back again. Personally, I don't find it interesting.

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We visited the cave on the way back to Udo (very easy to do both of these in one day. Very interesting and well explained. It would probably be a good idea to bring a jacket because the temperature in the cave is significantly lower than on the outside. However, it's still really cool to see and think about the implications of the event that made the cave in the overall of Jeju. Very good for kids although it can be a bit slippery inside too.

We visited on a very wet day so it was good to be inside even if the inside was the lava cave.  The lighting is very low in the cave and the floor, made by lava flow is very uneven so close attention needs to be made to where you are going. Its one kilometre each way to the end of the public bit and you miss quite a bit watching where the feet go so not to fall over.mAn interesting place to visit but take a torch!

We originally did not schedule this visit as we have already seen Mulu Caves in Sarawak-East Malaysia.  But our hotel (TGG) told us that this is a very different cave (lava tubes).   The cost is not high at KRW2,000 and if you are already going to Seongsan Ilchbong, might as well make a visit.  We did not regret the visit.  It is really interesting to see how the lava flowing from Mt. Halla makes its way underground and forming the cave.  It is huge so you can see the magnitude of the lava flow.  Be sure to wear sturdy shoes as the ground is rather rocky and wet and you will need to walk carefully so that you won't fall.  I am amazed on how some ladies worn high heels!  It is also dim and cool so you must bring a jacket with you.  It is also a UNESCO site so definitely worth visiting.

We had a short very informative visit at this village as part of a day tour. There are many old-style buildings. Very interesting. A very friendly local man explained us the houses, the surroundings and the past way of living there. We tasted some fermented tea. It was very nice. They sell the tea at 40000 KRW. We would have bought a smaller quantity for maybe 10000 if offered, but they had only the large units at 40000.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

Very interesting road on the way from Jeju City to Hallasan. Haven?t quite figure out why at a certain stretch the car actually rolls upwards on a neutral gear and without brakes. Probably an optical illusion but I didn?t stay to figure out - better just take it as a mysterious road, it?s more interesting. There?s some statues of pigs nearby, symbolizing prosperity and many children. Take a picture, touch the pig?s head.

Three interconnected mazes come with a map to make sure you won't get lost, other sights nearby including a lovely and scenic walk under beautiful trees. On my way through one of the mazes the sprinklers above came on and then you're walking through mist. A very straightforward sight that is an interesting experience.

This place is interesting only in concept - because it's one of the longest lava tunnels in the world.  But in reality, you climb down a hole and then walk for about a kilometer in what looks like a dirt tunnel made for a subway train with virtually northing to look at.  Then you arrive at a lava column which is far from impressive.  There are numerous amazing caves in the world such as the ones in Ha Long bay.  We are very unimpressed.

This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them.  The bears here are displayed as various characters and in a variety of situations.  They're cute and can be interesting, but if you're not really into this kind of thing then you'd be bored.  I'm sure children would enjoy it.  For myself, I enjoyed it but I've seen it once and wouldn't go back.

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This Hallasan Fried Rice is a must have, must Go, must try, if you are in Udo Island. It is available at the 'Pungwon' restaurant. It is about 20mins walking from the harbour. If you are driving, key in the Tel no. 7841894 in your GPS device.First you will have to order either Black pork or cuttlefish according to your preference. There is a minimum number of portions to order based on the number of pax. There were 4 of us and we order 2 Pork and 1 Cuttlefish. We will begin by BBQ the meat. Until we are about halfway through, you can order the rice from the staff. The staff will put aside some meat and start by cooking the rice. The whole idea of Hallasan Fried Rice is that the staff will tell you the story about Mount Hallasan and the islands nearby; all these while making the rice into the shape of a mountain. He will then pour in the egg mixture and meat and cheese... and after numerous of flipping the rice, it's done. Fret not if you don't understand Korean, they have Chinese staff who can do the story telling in Mandarin. The process of hearing about the story is very interesting coupled with the visual of the staff cooking the rice. Not to mention, it tastes damn good too!

The visit to the lava tube is interesting, but the way leading there is not good, and might definitely be dangerous under certain weather circunstances. Lightning is precarious and there are only few explanatory boards. definitely not adequate for people with walking restrictions of any kind

The silvery field of   grass   or   weed   is amazing if you come at the right season. Definitely a great photo taking opportunity. You can also catch the Halla mountain in the backdrop. Romantic and almost magical if not for the crowd. The place is getting more popular as words spread.The crater itself is not much to see but could be interesting if the leaves turn red or yellow. Visited here while on the way to the Manjanggul Cave

The route of the tunnel is 1km one way, and then the same way back.  Its an interesting environment - dark and very cool.  Its quite interesting to see how the lava flow carved this tunnel and the size of it.  Its definitely something that is memorable and unusual.

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.

The maze park is suitable for photo-shoots, the beautiful alley filled with green-leaves and also stone-walls. There are 3 maze available in this place. The first one is the easiest one, round shaped, and we can have a shortcut just by going to the side way. The side way also makes us easier to travel through the second maze. The third maze is the hardest, where it doesn't have a shortcut, and we have to go through the map by ourselves. Interesting if we are travelling with our little ones. On my last trip here at the end of September 2015, it was raining so bad, the wind was also very strong. So avoid to come here when the weather forecast predicts the weather to be raining.

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The concept of the Innisfree Jeju House is nice. Good brand extension. However, don't expect great bargains on cosmetics. As a matter of fact, the range is limited. Best to buy from Seoul or other major cities. The cafe is a nice place to rest with some interesting food choices. However, it's always crowded and thus the ambience is not too conducive for a nice tea session. Overall, it's a nice short introduction to the use of tea in Innisfree product range.

The Cave was very different to other caves I have been to. It was like a Subway train tunnel. You can way approx 1 km of the reported 7km+ lava tube tunnel. Did have much of the usual Stalagmite and stalactite and crystal formations. The Lava tracks /grooves where interesting to me. But I was not a   Wow   experience.
Special geographical zone & it is interesting to visit.  But, if you have been to other bigger lava column sites such as The Giant Causeway, you may skip this one.

Rather interesting show about the life of Genghis Khan. But a lot of dialogs on Korean, so it is better to speak Korean or know history a bit. Anyway, there was beautiful and spectacular stunts on horseback. We were glad we visited this show.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

Our guide brought us here to understand the striking cultural lifestyle of the local folks of Jeju.  The unique and exquisite architectural design of the `primitive'' huts and cottages of the natives was impressive. The pair of well carved and exotic Jeju deities statues that were made from volcanic lava stood spiritually on guard at the entrance. The sculptures matched harmoniously with the decorative Kimchi clay vases left unattended in the manicured lush green lawn compound displaying a special cultural taste that reminded me of the unique Hindu traditions on the island of Bali. I always think that it is the vibrancy and dynamism of the native folk culture that made certain attractions so special. The unique Alisan native lifestyle in Taiwan is just remarkably outstanding and different from that of the Maori in New Zealand and again, distinctively unique from the Dayaks longhouse traditions. It is thus a pleasure and a must thing to do to visit a folk village in Jeju to look at how the culture of the natives and how it is being preserved here.  We were introduced to a guide speaker who showed us the many agricultural tools used by the local natives but the real commercialized promotion began when we were `lured' into a room with seats and the speaker started marketing a type of drinks made from `Wuweiji' traditional herb that grew in abundance in Jeju and is believed to strengthen and invigorates the mind and body. It looks like another `tourist trap' and on the pretext of going to the toilet, I escaped the aggressiveness of the marketing talk. I wandered around the cottage compound admiring the foliage and the surrounding native architectural designs until my group of friends came out from the promotion. One of my group members was anxious to purchase the `elixir' drinks to enhance her youthfulness and she shared the drinks with the rest in the group.   I came out from the cottage and saw there were many similar cottages around the village and there were many sales talk going on in the other cottages. The admission to this folk village was free but I am not sure if my guide earned any commission from the purchase of the herbal bottled drinks by my friend.Except for the commercialized promotion, it is interesting to visit a folk village in Jeju.
Our cab driver brought us there on the way to loveland! Quite an interesting sight, no fees required! Do drop by if you're in the area :)

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Mount Halasan is located in the southern most tip of the Korean Peninsula. The height is 1950 m, a young volcanic mountain. The scenery is lovely and unique. The climbing route is interesting and versatile. Stones, rocks, wooden planks, concrete and steps is what makes the path up to the peak Baengnokdam. It takes 4 hours one way to reach the peak and about the same time for descent. Only one canteen is available where we can get coffee, chocopie and noodle boxes. The vivid autumn colors brought joy to the heart. Thoroughly enjoyed climbing this mountain
More for kids, quite interesting in the way they exhibited the history of teddy bears. The outdoor display is also fun for the kids. Not high on priority list but still worth a visit.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was interesting but not too mysterious.  It's just a trick of the eye because of the surroundings.  Anyway, it was a fun little detour and makes for good videos/pictures to show my students back in the States.
It was freezing in the tube! There were puddles of water everywhere so be careful when walking. The stones were interesting and do walk all the way in. You've already paid,so why not?

It was cool to see the lava patterns, but I don't think one needs to go beyond 70 meters.  It is dark and the ground is not level in the cave, so my caution to you is to watch your step.  A lady from my tour group had sprained her ankle while we were in there.  It is easy to just look up and sideways, but if you don't want your trip marred with pain and discomfort, watch your step.  It is very interesting, informative, and very cool to see how this little island was formed.

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was a so-so attraction, mainly because it was merely to see the rock from afar. No interesting mythological background to it either besides knowing that it was formed by volcanic activity. Also the place has way too many people than it can handle.

It was a hot day so felt great to get away from the  heat and descend into the cave. It felt about 10 degrees colder so be prepared with a light jacket. As with all caves, this has rocky wet floors that are very treacherous for those without proper track shoes. Very interesting signboards with geographical  information about the formation of lava caves too.

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? It depends. If you're the kind of person who couldn't be bothered with science, optical illusions and whatnot, you'd be better off checking out the snack shops nearby, observing the other tourists and their interesting behavior, or skipping this place altogether.However, if you've always been interested in physics and seemingly unexplainable phenomenons which you know are actually explainable, give yourself an hour or more to thoroughly check this place out. Photography lovers may also deem this place worth their time.The bottom line? If you're heading to another tourist attraction (e.g. Hallasan) and it's on the way, and you have time to spare, feel free to check this place out. Otherwise, don't bother.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

Interesting sight, w lots of tourists. Only 2000 won per adult, not expensive.There is another waterfall 40 mins away but other than that not much in that area. So plan well before making a trip there esp if you are going to use public transportation.

Interesting rock formation open for imagination. Otherwise the area has not much other sights. There is no ticket required, so you can see the popularity is not great. Anyway, nice forested area is good for a quiet walk.
Interesting place, walk in a lave tube & learn about formation along the way. it was very interesting experience. P/S Please wear shoe.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you book a car to travel around, probably you can consider to drive pass this mysterious road which took less than 20min when you're on the way to other attraction. This mysterious road is quite interesting, it is about rolling up this   Down slope  .  You can try it, just by asking the driver to off the engine of your car, and let it roll freely. I also tested it out with my water bottle, it was quite funny, the bottle actually roll up. At first, i thought this was due to law of gravity, but i realize is just optical illusion caused by the surrounding that cause this illusion of   down looking slope  . Fun place with interesting facts.

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites, this is not a place. If there were, we probably missed them. It?s a dark underground cave and very interesting to see the lava flows. You can see imprints of such flows on the actual ground you?re walking on. It?s a bit nippy, so if you are prone to being cold, may want to take a light sweater. There is no bathroom in the tunnel (which my son figured out trying to get out halfway in the tunnel/cave. He had to run back the way we came to find one.) It?s interesting. I just wished that there were more lights in the tunnels so one can appreciate it more. Uneven ground due to the lava flows, as expected. 2000W/$1.75 to get in, half for kids.If you've never been into one of these types of caves, you should.  If you have, maybe worth skipping.

I think this will be a fun experience for the family especially with small kids. I am not young anymore but it was rather interesting and fun for me as well. Not as easy as I thought and it took me 30mins to navigate through...for price of 3300won, it is a pretty economical way to spend a few light hearted hours after all the serious geographical sights in Jeju.

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I did not find it interesting. Well if clouds could form human faces, then I guess rocks could form dragon head. Not that it is related.Anyway, I really could not see a dragon and while it does look like a head, well, it's just that. A head.The only thing I find interesting is the selling of sea-shell foods and being able to eat by the sea on the rocks.For me, if I were to miss this, I guess I won't be miss anything?!

I believe this place can be so much fun then how we experienced it. We were there quite late, hence the volunteers (as the tour guides) were in an extreme rush to go home. Totally understandable. However they were still nice enough to show us around. Interesting historical facts about the Koreans in Jeju-do and their houses. They promoted horse face cream towards the end of the tour. Apparently the appropriate time to visit this place is between 11 am - 1 pm or definitely way BEFORE 4.30 pm.

I am sorry to say it but it was a boring place to visit. It would be interesting if we didn't have internet to get to know the world. By the way, my 8 year-old son was scared on the second floor to see all the torture instruments.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

Heard there are several entrance, but only one is open to public. The cave has been fitted with a pathway that takes away the hard work of walking on rocky surface for you. It is still quite deep though and will be challenging for anyone with lower fitness level. The tube is lit along the way and it is quite cold. If you've visited a natural cave before, this cave might be less interesting.

Half science, half art. A museum dedicated to the formation of the igneous rocks in the area, tectonic plate movements, volcanic eruptions, formation of lava tubes, and various methods of making craters. Extremely interesting!Then rock art. Lots of interesting rocks from around the island, arranged in a way that makes them just so fascinating.Budget a couple of hours here for a leisurely walk through these sections. Add a couple more hours to see the historical village section (which we didn?t go into as we had seen these elsewhere already).

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.
As the only show in Jeju (while in Seoul have 3 theatre) so always full. Interesting, Fun & a Must see Show.

An interesting melding of pop dance and painting with 4 eccentric young painters creating unique pieces. that is when they are not vamping, dancing or goofing their way on the stage. I think a worthwhile show for kids to give them some appreciation for painting and for adults who have just had a sochu laden dinner.It's entertaining enough, but seriously, a bit weird.

Always you can see from Korean drama movies of their house. Now you can see from your eyes. How the house split in few session. Such as, toilet and bath area. Quite interesting. Do not miss it.. must go and visit.
Although the area seems small, but quite interesting. It took 30 minutes for us to find out the way out and we had great fun with lots of pictures. Well recommended for visiting.

A long lava tube with about 1km opened to public.  Very easy to walk as perfectly level all the way apart from the initial steps, and wide and spacious (up to 23m high and 18m wide). Lots of interesting volcanic geology, features, etc. Well worth visiting.

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.

Interesting hike down a rare lava tube. Remember to bring a jacket, as it can get pretty cold down there. Not the most beautiful save out there, but definitely worth the visit to see the various lava formations. Do wear proper walking shoes as the walking surface can be quite undulating.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

While I'm getting more and more tired of museums this was a huge surprise for me. It costs 9 dollars and it's in the middle of nowhere in the island like everything. But it is so funny I spent almost 2 hours there and it was totally worthy. The illusions they create are so real and so interesting.

What I know Jeju not just have outside tour but Alive museum is really an interesting place worthy to go. My hubby and I took many funny photos with vivid pictures. They look like the real and we posted to our blog and got many friends liking! We spent almost two hours there!

We were recommended Alive Museum by our guide who wasn't so sure what it was all about. The facade is not like any other museums we had visited in South Korea..more like an American building. It actually reminded me of the movie 'Night at the museum'! When we entered we realized that it was all about 'trick art'. We ended up marveling at and trying out almost all the paintings. My whole family really enjoyed the exhibits. The museum is quite big and divided into several sections. There is also a nice spacius cafe there which has fresh delicious egg tarts among other ood and drinks sold. Just outside the cafe is a garden with many interesting sculptures which await you to join in. The museum which I thought would be boring actually gave my family a couple of fun and exhilarating hours!

We visited this museum as women diver is an unique culture in Jeju. The museum is very informative and trying to education people about the history and current stage of women diver and their significant contribution to the economy. It was an interesting place to spent an hour and we left with a whole new found respect for these brave women.

We arrived at 10am and the place was delightfully empty. The downside was that there was no glassblowing display. However  the walks  the gardens and the exhibits are all interesting and enjoyable. Families of all ages can spend a good hour here.

Walking through this outdoor museum was fabulous.  There many interesting things to see and learn about the Korean history.The visit itself took about an hour and some of the things to purchase was quite interesting.  It was interesting to find out how the privilege and not so privilege lived.

Very nice small museum. Not as boring as much of them. I found it interesting. I hate wandering for 8 hours in a museum with tons to read. That one is fesable in a normal amount of time. There was also a little show they did with movable boats showing how they worked in the days. Girls doing it were laughing the whole time as it was hilarious. My bf got picked to go help as cast along with others working the nets. I loved the whole scene with the chants. There are old boats outside you can go in and visit. Small souvenir shop with not much. Very helpful employees who offered to keep our luggages behind the counter as they did not fit in the lockers.

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It?s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

This place of interest has a very large estate in which you can almost spend close to an hour walking all of it.  It was interesting to see how glass can be made to be all kind of artifacts.  The place is located in a area where other place of interest are closely located too so add this to one of your visit if you can.

This area is a traditional village area with loads of space displays and things to see and do. A huge cultural complex created to show case all the various aspects of life in a Korean village. Working displays and demonstrations make the wandering around even more interesting as do the small shops that are spread throughout the complex. A really great couple of hours.

The aquarium is spacious.  You can see a lot of sea animals no matter how hot cold or rainy the outdoor is.  Taking a leaflet at the entrance is a must because the show time is up-dated.  It is so funny to see the penguins line up to eat food and jump up the stairs.  The otters are also interesting when you see them playing through the tunnels and on the swinging bed.  The 'stars' of the aquarium can be seen at the theatre which is attractive and interesting. My family stayed there for more than three hours.  The soft toys sold there are in good quality and my daughter bought a penguin as a souvenir.  There are food shops for people to enjoy but we didn't try any.
