review: Our guide added this on to our tour as we had a bit of time free and it proved to be very interesting and informative. You wouldn't need a lot of time to visit so maybe an hour or 90 mins would do but proved to be a lovely insight into Korean life. We particularly liked the story behind the number of wooden logs the put across their front gates whe the villagers go out ask your guide!

One of the highlights of my visit in Jeju - there's about a 1km walk in the cave which allows you to explore the after effects of lava tubes at your own pace; very interesting and spectacular. Would advise to bring additional clothing and comfortable covered shoes as the temperature is quite cooling with moist grounds. We used flashlights from our iPhones at a few points where it gets very dark; this helps us to better see the route ahead or for looking at details of the lava tubes.  Spent about an hour at this location. A must in your itinerary!
It's an interesting village to visit as it's quite different to the ones on the mainland. Highly recommend visiting this village. You need at least 3 hours in this village to explore.

It was my first time ever to any of the ALIVE series and honestly it wasn't fantastic but I could be bias cause I hate crowded attractions and people hog and does not wait for their turn. My recommendation is to go during off peak season with at least a group of 3 as some of the displays can fit in a couple. I guess it will be more fun as well. Condition of displays are pretty good and one could easily spend at least 1.5 hours in there. There is also an outdoor park which features more abstract art which is pretty interesting. Overall worth the money? I'll say it's alright but it will be a place that I'll visit once.

is a place where you will spend at least 3hours there. you must get prepare SD card with memory space & extra battery for your camera. you must catch the right angle if order to get the interesting result from the photo. stand at the photo point to take photo to catch the right angle.

Interesting site to learnt about the earlier settlements of Jeju island.  Be prepare to walk for an hour or more in the large estate and bring lotsa of water.  They preserve the huts pretty well.  There are mannequins but with REAL LIVESTOCKS.

I think the museum is open until 11 pm so this could be one of the things to do on a slow evening if you are near Seogwipo. Lot of interesting 3d art sorta stuff and if you are in a group or with kids and are into taking pictures it's worth it. Prices are ok and you can spend a good 2 hours in the museum. Overall though I would say it's nothing THAT great so better manage your expectations.

A very detailed museum and would probably take you about 2-3 hours to completely see everything. We enjoyed our time here despite the hot sun beating down on us. Many interesting sights including cows and real crops in the museum itself.
A casual walk to various areas (with different themes) within the park was very relaxing. The park was well maintained and landscaped.  It deserved spending a few hours visiting interesting areas.
Worth it, Super good! Done in about an hour and with young children. Eye opening and interesting geography lesson. UNESCO 3 Star site.
Working hours from 8AM (or 9?) till 5PM.Spend 2-3-4 hours there, many flowers (in season), animals, folk village inside, two interesting caves. Just nice! :)

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We spent around 2-3 hours in Hallim Park, and didn't regret it. The flowers and the botanical garden were beautiful, the cave and the water area were also very interesting. Very good opportunities to take photos. As we went in April, we got to enjoy the countless cherry blossoms! My personal highlight was the 300-year old bonsai in the bonsai area. If you're in the area, this is definitely worth a visit. There are several restrooms inside the park, as well as spots where you can buy food at a reasonable price.

Very underwhelmed. Arrived by ship & took free port shuttle into Jeju-si (capital) & dropped by the Jungang underground shopping street & Guandeokjeong. Walked past Yongyeon Bridge & past park to Dongduam rock. Pleasant walk. Then back to find Black Pork St, but didn't try it as we had heard it was nothing special. Enough to fill in a day (about 6 hours ashore.) Friends who went on a trip round the island said it wasn't terribly interesting & worth the cost. Do pick up a map from the tourist info kiosk, not far from where you arrive, then you can walk round sights described

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is a very nice park with some diverse points of interest. The lava tubes were interesting. Especially stunning is the walk through many, some quite old, bonsai. What was an aside visit for us became one of the highlights of our trip. I?d suggest two hours at least.

this is a very interesting park, they have at least 3 sections; a museum, 2 parks and smaller exhibits. If you like stones and interested in how they are formed and how they look like and appreciate by the people of the past and present, do visit. some stones have interesting tales like: Goddess and her 500 Sons. The whole park is pretty big, it can take up to more than 3 hours if you go through all the writings and descriptions. do go after a meal.

This is a really interesting place to visit. I have never seen any similar rock formations as the ones that can be seen here. If being in the area and for us who have an interest in nature and science, this is a must see place.It is very well organized with stair, walking paths and information signs.There is a small fee for entering and there are opening hours that must be considered.

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

The theme is good and it is very funny and interesting. Although we arrived the entrance at 18:00, we were able to complete the adventure within half an hour. Highly recommend for you especially with kids.

The soap making workshop is fun and interesting for kids and couples. Innisfree Jeju House is next to the famous O'Sulloc Green tea, you can spend at least 2 to 3 hours in these two placesfor soap making workshop, tea break and photograhping in the tea plantation.
The park is quite big and there are many interesting stuff to see. There's a bonsai garden, a small hanok village, bird park etc. It's quite an interesting place where you can spend a good 2 hour.

The cave takes about an hour, nice walk. Wear sensible shoes as the floor is not even and take a small jacket as it gets colder the further in you go. It was an interesting walk and we got to see bats at the end.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

Spent approximately 5 hours walking in the park. The park is sub divided into different sectors with different themes. Didn?t go to all the different sectors because some didn?t appeal to us. What I found nice and interesting were;1. The Caves2. Cultural Village3. The Bonsai & Stone Garden4. Seasonal Section - Ume FlowersWhat I didn?t like;1. Birds and reptiles in captivity2. Wild Flowers Garden - area seems to be poorly maintained. I didn?t get to see anything except grass and weedsBe prepared to walk and walk so if walking is not your thing then u better reconsider. Limited restaurants on site, so it?s best if u bring your own food and drinks.

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

Our stay in Jeju coincide with the operational day of one of the biggest and oldest traditional market in Jeju - Grandma Market which runs on days that end with 7th of the calendar month. There are lots of other smaller scale traditional markets which are opened on different days (e.g days ending on 5th, 2nd, etc...) thru out the island but we were told that this is the biggest.There is also an area which are designated for elderly ladies aged 65 and above whereby they are not charged any fees for selling there, hence, the name of Grandma Market.Lots of things can be found in the market, from plants, to snacks to clothings to housewares. We bought some fresh ginseng, chilly flakes and also fresh gingko from the market (after tasting some that were steamed and sold as snacks), The gingko there is different from those that we get in MY (most imported from China). Their is more creamy in texture and rounded as compared to ours.Overall, quite an interesting walk for an hour or two if you're looking to buy some of foodstuff.

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Took about 10 minutes to walk down to the falls. Be sure to wear proper shoes as it's a rocky shore, all loose stones. Spent less than an hour at the place.
Not bad, interesting, but didn't really stayed for longer than necessary. It took us around and hour or less, I think.

Nice park, relaxing. The Lava Tubes within the park were nice and cool. Try to go on a cool day. The grounds are nicely kept. The ostriches were not taken care of very well. The rest of the birds were ok. Bonsai garden was interesting. Only the hydrangeas were in season, so no flowers. Only spent a couple of hours there, then headed to the beach across the street.

Jeju has some very interesting museums, they seem to have them about everything from electricity ,to tea to, to robots! Quite quirky here and you'll see Teddy bears dressed up as Michael Jordan to famous re-enactments of history. Spent about 2 hours here just because it seemed interesting and a lot of effort has been put into the place.

I would recommend that you read the book ?The Island of Sea Women? by Lisa See before visiting the museum. I felt an emotional connection to the museum, the observatory and the grounds around the area, primarily because I had some background knowledge. The museum is well laid out and interesting. Do take the time to watch the video on the main floor before going through the exhibits. If you are there around 10:00 a.m. or 1:00 p.m. you may be able to see the women divers from the observatory on the 3rd floor.  Getting there: we were on a cruise ship and took a taxi from the ship terminal in Jeju City. It took about an hour and was a very scenic drive.  Our taxi driver gave us an hour to tour the museum and grounds and then dropped us off by the main market area in downtown Jeju City. It was under $100 for four people in a taxi.

I wasn?t expecting much but the displays were certainly fun and interesting. Can see that?s lots of care have gone into it. Great for photographs with the missus and if u have kids, this is heaven for them. Around an hour to walk the whole museum.

I loved this seemingly unassuming place that I would have never really thought of visiting.  It was one of the most interesting and beautiful places I visited in Jejudo Island.  It is definitely a   must do  , as they say in Disney World!  We would have loved to spend more time there.  It's not just a park with a bunch of rocks so don't miss out!  It's like a natural museum/art gallery of indigenous Jejudo volcanic rocks with a splash of the island's history.  Highly recommended to spend a minimum of 3-4 hours here!!

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I found this museum really interesting. I knew a little about Hanyeo beforehand but this gave me a much more detailed understanding. The exhibits (consisting of genuine Haenyeo clothing, tools and equipment alongside dioramas, videos and various documents) are well laid out and the accompanying explanations and labels almost all have high-quality English translations. I read every word and it took me a little under 2 hours to complete my visit, which considering the entrance fee is only 1100 won is excellent value for money. Recommended, especially if you are already on the east side of the island.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).
Fascinating village,  lovely homes, very interesting place. Enjoyed our visit visit.  Allow about half hour

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

Dark cave, chilly, dripping water and uneven steps were all I felt for one hour journey in and u-turn out of the cave. Not much to see really unless you are acompanied by an expert or archelogist who can make rock and mud come alive and tell stories. I have been to few caves over the world and find this least interesting and dull.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Although we know how the illusion works, it is still crazy to watch how the bottles or cars go up hill instead of going back. You don't need much time over there though. One mysterious road (according to our touri map there are two) is located right next to the Jeju Lovepark which is interesting and funny. You can go there for 9000 Won, spend about an hour watching love sculptures. :-)

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

I lived on Jeju and took school groups 3 times and every visitor I had to learn about  the history of the island. There is a video (not recommended for children due to disturbing images and video) at the start which is in several different languages. Then the display hall (formerly a dusty collection of artifacts but now a shiny new display hall) then there is a trip through the oreum. Free guided tour too. Very interesting. Also for kids there is a tank to play in in the grounds (there used to be a plane I don't know where that's gone) and the oreum itself is well worth a climb. Great museum which is still developing. Well worth it.

Really enjoyed watching how the water flowed into the sea. Interesting. Pretty much that's all you can do with a Waterfall. Beware though, the steps to climb back up from the Waterfall are quite steep, so if you're traveling with elders and kids, be prepared to walk up.

Interesting if short visit. Not too well signposted, but once found, plenty of parking and a short climb downn to the beach. Depending on the season entry if 2,000 Won or free. Demonstrates well the islands volcanic cliffs.
You don't have to spend a lot of time here but the displays are well done and interesting.  There is a small shop at the end from which you can purchase a bear

What is offered at the Glass Museum does not justify its 9 000 won entrance fee.There is a garden with glass flowers  glass birds  and other ornaments. The displays are dull and although they probably took a lot of time and effort to make  the whole place seems like something that would have been more interesting 15 years ago.

Went during the summer and its still pretty cold down there. Its a good rainy day itinerary as its entirely underground. Be warned that it can get really cold when  its raining though. Advised to wear good shoes are you wont be walking on flat ground and its quite wet and slippery. Its pretty interesting to learn  of the formation of the lava tube and a must go if its your first time in Jeju.

Very interesting garden of native plants but you don't get much time to see before they herd you into a room to hard sell you into buying Ginseng. Their pitch is that they invented a new method to grow and harvest JeJu ginseng in the lab and is suppose to the best. Buy ginseng here is very expensive. I don't even think JeJu is know for ginseng.
Underground shops over around 2 blocks. Nothing really interesting. You can skip it if you run out of time. Some clothing shops. Better save your money and time for Seoul.

Total waste of money (6000 for adults). Tragically outdated  tacky  uninteresting. Not much focus on actual chocolate - we were expecting samples  exciting cafe  lots of choice to buy from. There is none of this. Shop super overpriced. Don't waste your time.

review: This place is cool - we visited at night (possibly the best time to visit due to the lighting). Every corner had something interesting and creative.

this is the place to go for food and shopping when at Seogwipo. The market is pretty huge to walk  see and experience the everyday routines of those worked there as well as the regular stream of tourists that makes the place crowded and noisy. if you stay around Seogwipo  chances is you will be there at least once or every evening for did or to pass time. take time to go around the entire interior with multiple lanes with as well as the outside shops. You might just find interesting things to see and get something you like.

This has to be the best museum on Jeju. I have lived here for over 5 years and I have been there at least 3 or 4 times. The exhibits are interesting and there is even a couple of places where you can play old video games for free. If you enjoy computers or video games at all this the place for you.
The sculptures are interesting but Im not sure its worth my time visiting it. Can give it a miss if you are short of time.

The musical performance was actually really entertaining but you will have to pay extra so please take note. The price for Aqua Planet is actually quite high (similar to SG). Another interesting thing is that outside of the Aquarium you can get some really sick shots near the sea if you are more courageous. The shark hype-man from the musical really stuck with me throughout the 18 days of Korea so Aquaplanet is a fine attraction to visit if you have to fill time.
