review: The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.

The land is big with many miniatures but I get tired of the figures real quickly. However there are some interesting photo worthy displays. Go if you have time to spare or if you are going with kids. Entrance fee is 8000won.

The erotic and exotic art sculptures are interesting and daring but a bit dated.I think the museum has already operated since 20 over years ago based on our driver's comments. It sure is time to undergo an overhaul to spice up the place with digital technology 3D virtual arts and robots.

So many choices of tea particularly green tea. Bought different variety of green tea concoction in time for Christmas. I thought the tea capsules which you put in a sports bottle and shake is interesting and convenient.  I shall test it on my next biking exercise.

Nothing great about this place. read that it was a interesting little town but drove there and to see only replicas of the old houses. Lots of tourist were taking photos but that was about it. Visit if you have spare time
My daughter enjoyed reading and seeing unusual and interesting facts. We had a good time at the museum.

Many of the interactive segments were closed but it was still interesting. A beautiful sunny day allowed us time to stroll and take in the grounds. Lucky to come across an artist who worked wonders with wood.
learn about the lives of the people in the olden days and get to see the traditional houses around the area. quite an interesting place to visit but not a place where i will go back for a 2nd time.
It was not interesting at all! Go if you have so much time and you do not have any other place to go!

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

Interesting to learn about the history of citrus  including the local history of the mandarin organges  but you won't need to spend a lot of time here. Museum includes green houses with citrus trees from all over the world.
Interesting museum with lots of teddy bears. Amusing time for adults and kids alike.  Lots of photo opportunities and there's an Elvis concert as well as shop/cafe for further amusement!
Interesting museum i will recommend it to visit for adult and for kids it's great spend the time we enjoy that day

I was so immature at this museum! But I have to admit it was very educational and interesting. You will learn quite a bit about sexual liberation and such. I guess you can bring your kids here if you so choose as a parent. Lol but mostly it's a great place to go with your significant other. I enjoyed my time there.

I visited in the past many caves but this is the first time for a lava cave. It is not so beautiful and interesting as a natural cave but it is something new for me. Three stars only because it is not the best place I ever visited but it is interesting.The entrance is really cheap and the cave is long 1 Km so the visit is really fast.

I found the second part of the drive more interesting and mysterious. The second part is having the car on neutral and it mysteriously reversing. You have to experience it for yourself! Doesn't take too much time of your day.

Halla Mountain is the tallest mountain in South Korea and dominates Jeju Island.  It is an old shield volcano and is snow capped.  The part of the national park that we went walking in was swathed in fog the day that we were there.  The fog gave the national park an eerie ethereal feel as you never knew what interesting things would come up ahead.  Had a great time.

Had a great time and I?m not even a k pop fan. Lots of interactive things that kept it interesting and ended up buying a souvenir. You have to go to the holographic concert as it was a really rewarding experience. Wish I could have spent more time here.

Except if you're a soccer or stadium fanatic  I wouldn't make a huge detour to go there  but if you have some time and are in the vicinity  it can be interesting. The stadium itself isn't all that huge (35 000 seats)  but it's fairly modern and has a truly beautiful roof that looks like a canopy. There are things to do in the structure of the building (cinema  restaurants)  but make sure to actually get Inside the stadium  which you can do freely and was a pleasant surprise for me. I guess it would be nice to go there on a match day but I didn't have this opportunity.

An amusing theme park with plenty to see but not much to do (aside from take photos in compromising positions with statues). The museum does provide some interesting insight into sexuality in South Korea -- note that while full bodied male statues are plentiful the only time larger women feature is in sculptures where men are desperately trying to escape.
A large variety of tea and tea sets. Nice litle store where they sell the tea's and set together. Too many groups and very crowded but interesting enough to spend a short time inside the tea museum.
+18 enjoy your time there Interesting sculptures of male and female organs sex positions all over the place and a shop

We were with a tour group so we did not see all the attractions, and our time was limited the ones we did experience were interesting, caves & botanical spirit gardens were worth the trip.  I really liked the stones - fascinating.

We went there with both of our children (at the time, 4 and 2 years old). There was plenty for them both to see and neither of them got bored. My 4 year old particularly liked the lava tubes and both my wife and I found them very interesting too!
We went here as a detour and sure it is a tiny bit interesting... but would not recomend any detour here, many fabolous places on the island to spend time on instead.

We visited this just because it was rainy, and realized that it would be great to visit otherwise.  It was interesting because of the theme-based teddy bears in thousands, spread across 3 floors.  Loved the Gandhi bear, Times square scene, Mother teresa bears, Charlie Chaplin bears, most expensive teddy bears (Louis Vuitton) and so on.Do visit if you can fit it in your schedule!

we took some interesting shots. cool place to spend some time outdoors, it's not too big and easy to walk around. definitely worth going there!! in fact, we thought this was pretty much the most interesting thing in Jeju

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.

Very interesting display of modern and old teddy bears. Take the time to see the Elvis Presley gig in the theatre! A bit pricey and as most museums on Jeju is quite small, but worth it on a rainy day.

Took quite some time to find the road. I was there few years ago and I find it very interesting, but this week when I bring my family there, I was very disappointed. We drive pass a few small stalls and want to try on the road and the nearby stall owner was very rude and tell us not to park in front of him. Thus we drive up and down slowly and try on the gravity without having the hand break on. It's a 5 minute thing, will not go again.

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

they charge admission now to see this seashore.  as if that's not bad enough, it was closed by the time we arrived at 5pm.  but what wasn't closed were the numerous vendor stands that seemingly sprung up to cash in on the tourists here.  the most interesting thing we noticed were various coconuts with small holes drilled in them with a straw sticking out.  this is supposed to be 'fresh' coconut water.  protip: there are no coconuts in korea.  superprotip: they re-use these containers without rinsing them out, over days/months/years, you get the idea.if you don't mind paying to see this 'natural wonder,' at least avoid the vendor stands like the plague, cause that's what you'll likely catch there.

The museum is interesting and probably really fun with children. It is a little strange as there are bears dressed up as princesses, maybe even British royalty and whole safaris. It was interesting to say the least, but I would rather spend my time outside.

The dragon head rock is in North part of Jeju, close to the airport. It is a rock that looks like a dragon head on the coast. The Seogwipo coast line like the Jusanjeolli Cliff or the Odelgae Rock are much more interesting than this. However, if you do not have time to visit the Jungmun/Seogwipo area, this is an alternative to see the rocky coastline. The sunset here is nice, but the place is packed with tourists fighting to get photos, so it's not all that romantic. I think a beach sunset at a more remote beach on the West side would be nicer and a calmer experience.

The attraction is not so exciting but still worth a visit if it is your first time in Jeju. This attraction is also pretty near Jeju's Loveland, an interesting and popular attraction that is not mentioned in TripAdvisor.

Perhaps it was the time of day we were here. We got here really early around 8am to start our road trip down the east side of Jeju Island. So nothing was open yet. We saw the dragon rock and even walked down the side of the small cliff to see the rock from a different angle. It was raining quite a bit on the morning we visited so the walk down was a little slippery. It was interesting to see the dragon rock formation and read about it's significance in Korean folklore. We had a photo with the mermaid there too. Unfortunately due to the time of day we visited nothing else was open, but from what we could tell there were mainly souvenir, fruit and convenient stores and stalls. Worth a visit if you have time, but essentially a nice looking rock

Parking is free, next to Osulloc. The ajusshi will be there to direct you in the carpark. Lovely place. I love Innisfree products and im happy to be there. However, there are only skincare products, no makeup items. There is an area for soap-making but we didnt do it. During the time we visited, noone did it too, so i cant comment how interesting it is.There is also an area which you could do ink stamping on paper. If you like ink stamping, do remember to bring some paper along. Its free.The food is organic and took quite some time to prepare. So the best is to find a table first, order your food and then do your retail shopping. We ordered 4 drinks & 2 meals, it took about 20-30 mins to be done. Yes, its that long.There are also desserts and they are made beautifully. How i wish i still have the stomach space for them. I would just come back to have tea and dessert at the place. Dont forget to look at their   Jeju only   products. There is innisfree Hallabong jam and strawberry jam. Yup, jam for bread. So look closely at the retails. The price of the retail items are comparable to those in Seoul, so need not get them unless you desperately need it. Go for their   jeju only   items instead.There is a small tea planatation outside Innisfree, where most is seen taking OOTD. Toilets are behind Innisfree.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands.On our free day we visited Dongmun Market which we thought was a better option than spending so much time in the shopping centers. There are several lanes organized according to the wet market section, fruits and vegetables, packaged goodies to take home, food stalls and dry goods such as clothes. The clothes are of Korean origin of good quality and reasonable price, i.e. a dress for 12,000 kw. In a small stall we tried the Korean fried chicken with hot sweet sour glazing and it was very delicious. The fruit section was a good photo spot with its stalls abound with tangerines. Overall one can see how the vendors, locals and non-locals interact to reflect one aspect of Jeju life.  Very interesting, indeed!

Not a must-visit but it's good place to explore for first-timers. The stretch of road looks like it's uphill but rolling a water bottle will make it roll uphill instead of downhill. It's interesting to watch. Since I self-drive, there is no exact gps phone number for this but you can key in Loveland and you will see signboard to mysterious road. Parking here is free and there's a nearby convenience store and one can chill at caffe bene afterwards.

My frd and i been looking forward to visit the teddy bear museum cos we heard tat it hv a outdoor areas displaying e bears but reslise it is jus a small area which u can finish within 15mins.The 2 storey museum seem smaller than e 1 at seoul tower.Overall,is still worth to visit if u hv e extra time cos u will find e bears cute and hv a interesting background for each display.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

I've never think that bonsai garden could be such interesting.Very energy place with good vibes. Don't be in hurry, spend enough time (1-2hrs minimum) for visit that unusual place and you'll feel current moment, your mind will become peaceful and calm. If you are lucky enough - you'll meet the owner and creator of the garden, very special person, who is living directly in heart of his creature.Absolutely recommended as a trip into your inner shiny space! :)

It's my second visit to Jeju and since I am staying in Jungmun area, we decided to visit this nearby attraction. I can't remember the name of the teddy bear museum of my previous trip but it's definitely bigger than this. You will find this attraction amazing if you are visiting a teddy bear museum for the first time, but being my second visit to such attraction, I don't find anything particularly interesting.

It's more of a shopping place. The green tea ice-cream is quite blandand there's not much green tea taste.But the   saving grace   is the tea plantation . There are giant cupslots of flowers and is overall a photo taking place. We did not have enough time and did not visit the museum . There are interesting sample tea blands that you can smell with names like   Moon Walk   and   Jeju Green Tea  . Overall could be better. Might come again.
It's interesting to see and   be there   but not something you would kick yourself if you don't have the time to go.

It's a nice place and interesting concept but some of the attractions seem run down and nothing much to see.. It's good to go with kids to explore the fresh air or play area , got spare time or if u on tour good to pay a visit . If not there are many other places in Jeju with nice scenery to visit ..

It is one of the few villages that still exist on Jeju with complete retention of the traditional houses. The villagers still live in these houses but with modernized technology. They no longer uses the open air toilets, rearing black pigs and using electricity for lights, television and wifi. This is also the village that Dae Chang Guem were filmed in the early 2000s. Interesting to walk in the village as if we have travelled the time back in the past.

It is an interesting showcase of lifesize and all sizes of teddy bears being used to personify famous art pieces, fables, fairy tales and etc.  There are many interesting photo opportunities.  The Koreans are very creative in coming up with such a museum dedicated to teddy bear lovers, but I would not return a second time.
It is an interesting road and we had a car so we can do it a few times. I would say that if you are not going in that direction, there is no need to drive there specially for it.

Interesting guided tour of a traditional Jeju village, showing how people in Jeju used to live. Tour was conducted in mandarin, as we were a group from Singapore. Interesting highlights include the different meanings of the poles (at the front door), the outhouse (with a pig in it) and their honeyed drink (with some kind of berry in it).  They did bring us into a small room and introduced their products for sale - products include honey, the special honeyed drink as well as horse bone powder. Could have done without the sales pitch, and have had more time with the history and culture.

Interesting facts about the formation of the lava tube. Malaysia has no such thing so i was definitely eager to learn more and to experience it. Walking into the lava tube really exciting as i step on to the solid harden lava ...beautiful formation of harden lava, adores the lava pattern ... careful stepping onto the path as it is uneven and can be challenging to some ... just take your time walking in. As i adores nature, i really enjoy exploring the lava tube...as you go deeper into the tube it gets warmer than the windy cool air outside of the tube. Enjoy it, a must.

in front of mt sanbangsan, this is a nice place to visit to see the great scenery and cliffs where you can take a walk along the coast around the cliffs with the interesting formations. When we were there, there is a sign that states the opening time (for entry to the coast) is from 3pm when the tide is low.

I wouldn't say this is a must visit attraction. Our driver took some time to show us this place since we were passing thru. The kids found it somewhat interesting, we spent about 10 mins trying out the optical illusion in the car.

I went their with my wife. I didn't find the place as interesting and exciting as other people claimed. My recommendation, unless you are a geologist this place has nothing substantial to offer. Take a warm cloth and comfortable shoes when you visit this place. The temperature in the cave is low(you feel cool even in summer) and the floor is wet and a little bit slippery.A person can have knowledge about lava tubes but personally I felt unsatisfied. The cave is very dark for anyone to figure out things inside. Information boards inside give information about the site. If a visitor has enough time to visit, you can drop by this place. But, if your schedule is tight you can skip this place.

I still enjoyed checking out the bear museum but I must say that the entrance fee is too much and unreasonable considering the bear museum is not that big.You can visit this place in less than 30 minutes because nothing much to see, they have small collection.This is just across the road from Ripleys Believe it or Not Museum. You better skip bear museum and just spend more time in Ripleys as it is more collection of interesting items and reasonable entrance price.

I must say I am not a doll lover, nor a child, so maybe my opinion is a little bit biased. It was a disappointing visit as it took up my time and I was not enjoying myself in the museum. It was very childish and not that visit-worthy. The settings of each place were not well thought as immersions between themes are poorly structured. I believe there is not enough interesting effects to keep all audience entertained.

I learnt a lot about the brave women divers of Jeju by visiting this museum. I had hired a driver/tour guide for sightseeing in Jeju Island and got to visit some of my ?must see? attractions that were not close to my hotel. My tour guide was good so I had a great time. We visited this museum as part of our itinerary for the day, and I was glad we did. The museum charges a small entrance fee. I got to see a very interesting video about the history and lives of the women divers. There also a lot of painting, sculptures that is centered on the lives of these brave women. The museum is small but I liked it a lot. I came out more knowledgeable about the women and Jeju Island as a whole.

I heard about this folk village 'cause it is very popular for filming location of some Korean Dramas such as De Jang Keum, Juno, Merchant Kim Man Doek...This is an interesting place to see the daily life of locals in old times. We visited the village one day after storm so there were fewer tourists, quieter and no sales presentation, so maybe lucky us.

I have to say it was nothing special for me. The good news is that the museum is located in the jungmun complex, where other interesting attractions available, like trickart museum, jusangjeoli cliff, pacific land, etc. So if you have time, why not visit it as the entrance fee is not that expensive. But it's not a must visit attraction in my opinion

I found the volcanic caves here interesting but apart from that it was just another botanic garden. We went when the rapeseed and cherry blossoms were in bloom which was very pretty and a good photo opportunity. However, the same flowers are everywhere in Jeju at that time of year and don't cost anything to take a photo.

I came here by chartered taxi, I got rate 130k KRW for 8 hrs use. Not sure how to come here with public transport though. For a first timer underground trip like me, it's quite interesting. The track is not very long, not suggested for Claustrophobic person (like my friend) as it's dark,wet and getting smaller inside. Suggested to bring a raincoat with you, if you forgot don't worry you can buy on convenience store in there.

I brought my 13 year old daughter to Play Kpop in Jungmun without much expectation. We both are not huge fans of K Pop, expecially YG entertainers like Big Bang. So we didn't have much expectation. We just needed a place to spend some time in the hot summer days. Actually, We really had fun there. I strongly recommend that you should attend the hologram concert. We watched G dragon and Psy, and it was really amazing. It felt like you were in real concert. There are many interesting place you can take picture and game. There are a few VR games, and we enjoyed it a lot.

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.

Had read and heard about Ripley's Believe it or not before but this was our first time visiting.There were a lot of interesting and somewhat interactive exihbits on display. I didn't think these were the real thing though, but rather they were replicas. You could learn a lot of new facts here. One can tell that Mr Ripley really had a talent and knack for discovering and collecting quirky stuff.One thing to note is that some of the exibhits involved morbid subjects such as cannibalism, death and torture, etc. So might not be too suitable for little children.

Go with an unknowing mind.You can easily find the explanation for this phenomenom but don't! I didn't, so when my car rolled up slope in neutral, I was thrilled! But it lasted at most 5 minutes so not for people with an already packed schedule. An interesting side trip for those who have time though.

First time to see a lava tube. It was not the most impressive thing to see but it was such an eye opener for me! Learned a lot about this amazing geological formation. Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! Bring a layer!

First  there is nothing worth seeing in this place. The exhibits were not even interesting-think chocolates shaped after teddy bears and placed in display cabinets. Their ultimate objective is to lure you to their shop which sells chocolate that....can be bought all over Jeju island. They don't even make their own chocolate.Second  they are liars. The saleswoman introduced the jeju orange chocolates to me  gave me a sample to try and recommended the   best   tasting brand. I tried it and i did like it. She recommended getting the set of 5 small boxes (each box containing 8 pieces of chocolates) because it was more worth it than the bigger box which was going for the same price but had 2 pieces less. I bought the set of 5 small boxes. When I got back  i tried the chocolates. Guess what? They tasted like cheap imitation chocolates. Nothing like the sample she gave me. Worse  each box only had a MAXIMUM<- note  of 6 pieces of chocolates. In addition  the saleswoman had such a bad attitude after I said i would only get one set of 5 small boxes. This place is totally not worth the trip. You can get better chocolates even at the airport  at a cheaper price. Don't waste your time and money.?룷?렆

Expected the place to be bigger. Only reason we went here was to kill some time before heading to the airport. Could have gone to the Ripley's museum instead which was just across the road. As expected, lots of teddy bears in the museum. Only interesting part was the history section. They had teddy bears from as old as 1905 on display. The bears were still kept in good condition.

Did it once with the SO, and then a second time as a race against each other. I saw a group of guys doing the maze with money on the line, if you want to make it more interesting.Also, there are loads of cats near the ticket office, if you're into that.

At start, the guide will demonstrate their traditions and culture which is quite interesting. At the end, they will try to sell you their premium honey. 50% of the time wasted listening to their premium honey introduction.

As its name, here is an idea to visit for Teddy Bear lovers and who interested in. Many zone that's quite interesting such as the first Winnie the Pooh, world's all time classic paintings x Teddy Bear, characters bear like Michael Jackson or Audrey Hepburn from Breakfast at Tiffany, and Steve Jobs. Entrance fees isn't cheap but still OK. For the exhibition of Bear dolls is good but for the shop, just soso nothing attractive.Parking available. Good for friends and family.

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the   mini car   or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A nice botanic garden with interesting elements. I particularly like the bonsai garden with lots of areas to sit and admire the specimens. Since we only had a very limited time, we were not able to see the other areas.

We got a very nice tour from a local resident who spoke fairly good English.  It was very interesting to see how the huts were designed and the durability of the thatch roofs.  There was a sales pitch to buy some locally made tea and other products (which were very expensive) but no one bought anything.  You would think that they would figure out international tourists wouldn't be buying any kind of drinks to bring back home.

This Teddy bear Museum is interesting however I would not recommend if there is no kids traveling with you.Giant Teddy in the back yard was fun to watch.Dolls in the store are little pricey.Kids perspective: 5/5Adults perspective: 3/5
Spectacular experience whereby you got to walk one kilometer in and walk back the same distance. It is the longest lava tube in the world. Very interesting experience.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.
Car is going backward at down slope road. Mysterious! Interesting. Can incorporate into your itinerary. The place is not very big. Nothing much other than the road.

As far as I know there are two bear museums on Jeju Island. One is the Teddy Bear Museum while the other is the Joanne Bear Museum. My aunt decided to go to the Joanne Bear Museum due to her friends' recommendations. It was the best decision she has made for that Korea trip. I wasn't a fan of teddy bears but I was surprised and overwhelmed by all bears  coming in different colours and sizes. It's even more special because every bear in the Joanne Bear Museum is handmade.Furthermore  the decorations in the Joanne Bear Museum are very interesting too. I have never seen such decorations  using bears to enhance the decorations. I will definitely come back for a second trip!
Aqua planet was big and many interesting fishes & performance ...nice food serve at the canteen only set back was that there was no more whale shark
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Turn off the car engine, release the brakes and the car moves by itself. Up the tiny slope. It is something very unique which you do not normally experience. Nothing fanciful but definately interesting.We were at night with minimal cars so our driver being a fun guy did it with the car facing front, then backwards.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

It's actually just one short stretch of the road but interesting. The road gives you an impression that its going up hill instead it's actually going down the hill. The surrounding including the plants, trees, field and fencing are giving you that up hill impression. So when you switch off the vehicle engine that you are in, the vehicle will continue to move forward. Same goes to the test where they will show you by rolling a water bottle. Try walking backward and you can feel it. You might feel a bit disappointed as there is nothing else over there

It's a great and interesting place! When else can you just go through a   natural tunnel   made by lava? The whole place is very well maintained and clean. Price is inexpensive and there is also a small restaurant and shop. You may think of bringing a second shirt because inside the lava tube is it cold (12째C/54째F). Fun fact, there is no exit at the end of the tube, you have to go all the 1 km back again ;)

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.

It is interesting to see this authentic folk village that is the only one that still exist in Korea with people living there. Our Chinese guide allocated to us was good and she explained everything to us on their culture and how this village is sustaining. There wasn't so much of pressure that she pushes us to buy the products as she explains that she is just doing her job to explain but if we decide not to buy, that's totally fine too. We tried the products and we like it and bought some. It maybe a little pricey but she mentioned that the proceeds go back to these villagers too. It was a happy sale to me. No pressure.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

Interesting place... Love to see how they really appreciate haenyeos, as one of their mother culture... A unique and honourable profession for jeju women in the old days and even now... How women are very appreciated since born and high hopes for doing the profession as backbone of the jeju families..The museum really tells a lot about how the haenyeos lives and even their struggle in the war era... For those who loves visiting museums, its really recommended!

Interesting experience  as we we pull to neutral gear, release the accerator, the car just go forward, upwards. The mysterious road is short, we made a few rounds. There is a car park where you turn in to go a few rounds if you wanted to. We tried the  same stretch to road after the end point. The car just go backward on the upward facing slope.

Interesting cave, for someone who has stayed in a city for the whole of her life. We went in winter and what is interesting is that the cave is considered warm for winter. Be prepared for the long walk to and back and the path would be too rocky for strollers or wheelchairs

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

A veey dark and long walk with informative description on different formation of rocks created after cooling of the lava. Interesting and educational, no exit @ the end of the walk so would have to take the same route back.

We had a guide who could speak Chinese bring us around and introduce bits of the places and provide explanations on the history and culture. I found the information pretty interesting and I quite enjoyed it though it was a short visit.
An interesting museum that was extremely well catered for English speaking tourists. A part of history that we knew nothing about and was moving to hear it from the perspective of the people of Jeju.

The cone-dome architecture is interesting, the roofs of different gardens within culminates to a peak into the center of the compound and u can take a lift up to catch a 360 panoramic glimpse of the surroundings (see pic). However, adult tix are at 9000krw per person which is not cheap for what u get within. The place has lots of potential but not that well-maintained as the place looks very weathered on the whole. There is a garden dedicated to tropical fruits but those are mostly common fruits for southeast Asians like us. There were only chrysanthemums at the entrance even though it's supposed to be in-season. Parking is easy though, and free, like most places of interests at Jeju. Overall, this place is more suitable for the elders and for people dropping by to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and Seonimgyo Bridge, which is just next door. Otherwise, my 2c worth - it'll be fine to spend your money elsewhere.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.

A country is evaluated by its culture and only in a province of Jeju in South Korea that we visited many many museum. They are about arts, life and musics. This museum is to introduce the life of the divers in Haenyeo. Very interesting to see the divers reanimated in small scenes very real. The tour guide here could speak English, not very fluently but that?s the best English speaking tour guide in Jeju we?ve met.

We just came from Seoul and went to a market very similar to this one. I actually liked this one better because it was less crowded and I s able to actually take it all in. Definitely an interesting experience.

Not as big as the 5 day market but still provides an interesting insight into the daily food norms of the locals. It's sheltered so rainy days is not an issue though parking may be. There are a few local eateries inside but the one we went in insists we order one portion (they are big) per person. Rather than having to waste food we walked out.

It's very much a market for locals but interesting to walk around. There are lots of colourful displays of fruit and vegetables. Dried fish stalls are also common  as are live shellfish and fish tanks where you can choose your purchase. It's a bit smelly in parts  particularly around the meat stalls.

It's a nice shopping street that is about 5 min walk from Dongmun Market and beside Jungang underground shopping place that is closed till August 2016. There is Tommy Hilfiger interesting souvenir store The Islander local designer and mid-range fashion shops shoes and stationery stores and cafes as well. Nearby at one end is the attraction Gwandeokjeong Pavilion. At the other end of the street there is also a black pork street.

Interesting place. Lots of Tangerine in boxes as gifts and many stalls sell snacks and souveniors.Is also a wet market where you see fresh produce. Not forgetting display of pig heads can be found in serveral stalls. Can visit for the experience.
Interesting Folk Village with all traditional life in the past. but at the end the guide will try to sell the product which price more expensive than city / market (maybe cause its tourist object ?)
Great to know some of the interesting facts about the village but It was more about product marketing than introducing how they managed daily life in the past

Very big market. Combination of a wet and dry market. Interesting cos they sell many live seafood, vegetables, fruits, sourvenir.The seafood seems expensive when i convert but it could be cos more for tourists. A fish can be $50. We enjoy eating the local food like cuttle fish, fish cake, fish ball, crab stick. About $4 to $7. Just immerse in local culture. The colouful array of oranges and by oroducts. 15 boxes orange chocolate for 10k won. Looks alot but one box only 8 pcs candies so bulky to carry.There is a store sells korean sourvenir like keychain, clipper, magnet, etc $3 to 5 a piece.Bought a sweatpants 5k won so less than $10.Did not dare buy hallabong oranges cos too heavy to carry home. More for local tourists.Overall we do enjoy this market. Near to the underground shopping and fashion street too.

Though Dongmun turns to commercial rather for local market, its interesting to see the rich supply of seafood in Jeju. If you know Mandarin, you can communicate with the food stall owners. Quite smelly and dirty, which is expected.

This is an awesome place to go with street sights and photography in mind, with all the locals and tourist here collectively, lots of items to see, and nearby jungang underground market. Visiting both, seems to be the smart thing to do. Interesting place but of course it is still a market.

Other than just a seafood market, there are lots of seafood restaurants serving very fresh seafood. Do check them out.Lots of shops selling their Jeju hallabong chocolates and we found them to be cheapest here.Very interesting market to see traders selling traditional Korean food and side dishes.
Interesting experience to walk around the local market, we are there early, not many stalls open yet and some preparing to open...

For those that love fish, this market is a place to visit. Very interesting but not for me. You can also shop for shoes, clothes, chocolate, souvenirs and fruit. I found it a little on the dirty side but it might be because I don't care for fish much.

Crowded with a good mix of locals and tourists; jostling along for something.But the items on offer are common, with lots of seasonal clothing on display. Snacks are plentiful, so you have lots of choice. It's an interesting market, with old hands working at street food corners.
Able to find lots of local produce in this market. Fruits especially orange varieties, black pork knuckles, kimchi of various kind. An interesting market to visit. Recommended.
Using bare eyes to look at the roads it appears to go up while actually its going downhill. If you put a water bottle on the road it will slide down. Interesting.

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.
The stretch of road looks like it's uphill but rolling a water bottle will make it roll uphill instead of downhill. It's interesting to explore.

The 1k walk is really interesting and had good info in english. It's much cooler as soon as you walk down the steps and raincoats are useful as there are water drops and wear comfortable shoes for the rocky and wet floor. Most of it is quite dark but you can still get good photos. Definitely worth the visit

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

Nice park surrounding this unique canyon.  3 sets of waterfalls.  An interesting bridge that goes over the canyon and a path that takes you through the woods.  Takes a bit of effort but it's worth doing if you're in the area.  The falls are not that impressive but the formations and the foliage is nice.

Manjanggul Cave was a thoroughly interesting experience. The structure itself is awe inspiring and feels like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Be prepared for water droplets plopping on your head! It was a bit chilly when we visited as well.
Lovely waterfall that fall directly into the sea. Very interesting and fun! Highly recommended. Great to bring children too!
Long lava tube and if you are into stones and caves you will find it interesting. Inside was cold and some water drops coming from ceiling. Once you reach the end that it just take a picture then go.

Car move uphill automatically when in neutral gear. Water don't flow down but up. Pretty interesting when you are in a car experiencing so. Suggest to come here if you are going to Love Land else skip it. Suggest to spend maximum 15mins here.

An aquarium with the typical fishes both salt and fresh water. What was interesting was the display of many species of frogs from the marshes. Also very very expensive tickets for a rather small exhibition. Would probably be more worth while if going with children as  there is an experiential exhibition which is kids-friendly.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: You will have to try it youself to experience it! Tried it with a water bottle but it doesn't work. Tried it with a car and shifted to neutral, the car will ascend the inclining road. Quite interesting but will be bored after 5 minutes.

We went with my 63 year old mom, husband, and 15 and 6 year olds. It was great! It's waaaay longer, wider, taller and more interesting of a lava tube than at Volcanos national park in Hawaii! The largest accessible in the world. Bring a waterproof camera, hiking shoes or at least tennis goes, a raincoat or jacket. Won't wear white. I still can't get the ash stain out of my sons sleeve after he fell in a puddle. It's only a few dollars to get in. Do the quick museum first, if you want to know more about it. Cold, wet, dark, tired but Loved it!

We visited Mysterious Road on our return journey from Hallasan. We tried rolling water bottles, but failed lol. Eventually we did the touristy thing of shutting the car engine and letting the car   roll up the slope  . Interesting.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

This place is known for its so called gravity. A lot of tourists will visit this place when they are at Korea. My tour guide demo to us by putting a water bottle down the slope, instead of going down, it goes the opposite direction . Very interesting.

This is quite an interesting place to visit. Do remember it's a long lava tube cave.Take note:1) Stairs to the cave can be steep.2) The floor of the cave is in its natural form. It's wet, slippery, jagged and uneven. There are large puddles everywhere so watch where you step.3) When we went, there isn't really any special colorful lighting in it. It was quite dim. We used our cellphone as our flashlight in some of the darker and very uneven floor areas.4) It's cold so wear some warm clothing. There may be water dripping from the ceiling as well. Overall we enjoyed the lava cave.

This is a very interesting place to visit. Our driver put his car in neutral gear, turned off the engine and put his keys on the dashboard, and the car rolled uphill! We got off and watched other people put bottles of water on the road and they rolled uphill as well! It is actually an optical illusion, but still a strange sight to behold. You don't have to stay here for long - maybe 30 minutes will do.

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

There was a tour group with a guide when we visited. We saw his demonstration of water flowing upstream and a water bottle that roll upstream too. very interesting, when you switch off the car engine and witness the car rolling upwards.
the waterfall wasn't really interesting but the 2000 years old Chinese signature and the diving women who serve seafood that only a minute ago was alive, were very interesting.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. FYI: there aren't places there where you can refill your bottles with fresh water.

Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.

Many tours include this spot for tourists.  I personally find it over-rated.  It is an illusionary experience where the environs surrounding the particular stretch of road gives one the impression that it is not what it is supposed to be.  Some guides would even spill water on the road to experiment.  Interesting - yes, but I would not include it as part of a tour itinerary.
Lucky to visit on sunny day, was slightly crowded but still managed to still the cliff. The volcanic structures were very interesting and you can see the clear blue water.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

It's just a road, but if you want to make it interesting, do some experiment on it. Get out of your vehicle, and try walking down/up the road. Or test the road by pouring water/ walk inversely. We enjoyed it!
it is Only waterfall in Asia falls directly to the ocean. Not that interesting, easy to walk down, a lot of kids and old people can visit.
Interesting! There are quite a few things to visit like Botanic Garden, Bonsai Garden, Folk Village, Lava Cave, Bird Garden, Water Garden etc. Recommended!

Interesting waterfalls with a park. Lighted up at night. We came by at 8pm.  The clear and deep water of Cheonjiyeon Falls is designated as Natural Monument No. 27 and is renowned as a habitat for Mutae eels. Take a walk around the beautiful park. You can also take photos with the props such as 'Summer', hearts etc.

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. A good thing we visited this Dragon Head Coast while doing the west coast route.The canola flowers site is a paid visitor spot (should be around KRW2K each adult). There is a Viking ride @ the base for the young ones to try. You can see many interesting lines and grains on the side of the rocks' walls. You get to see women divers selling fresh seafoods along the coast, youngest are already in their 50s and oldest are in their 70s (still diving)...they are simply amazing.

As a scuba diver I was very eager to go to this museum and get to know more about the   Jeju Mermaids  . The museums has lots of interesting information about how they live, the risks of their profession, the   team system   they use (I loved this part). If you like the underwater world, I highly recommend a visit to this neat museum.

An interesting showcase into the folk customs of people who place men on pedestals and where women does most of the chores, while being trained to dive deep into the surrounding waters to harvest seafood for a living.
Went here with our two sons (8M and 4Y) and it was very interesting and a bit cold.Cheap entrance fee being in Jeju.Easy to park and restaurant in front was OK.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

Many interesting paintings for great picture moments. Really fun taking funny photos and you will be surprised with the amount of creativity to put these pictures together. Pretty easy to locate if you drive and use a GPS. It is near Jungman beach so if you planning to head to the beach you can drop by.

Easy access using public transportation and I remind you to bring a good camera and prepare yourself with extraordinary pose and don't be shy to act silly even lots of people will watching you. But don't worry they will do the same. Alive museum in Jeju is waaaaay bigger than in Seoul and the paintings are more interesting.

this is the largert lava tube in the world (well, that we have found) and it's fascinating.  Really huge tube, interesting rock formations all through.  The walk is quite easy (a little uneven and damp, headlight recommended) and the informative signs are useful.  Not that expensive and well worth the trip.

I read a lot about this rock before I saw it, and I tried hard to see the dragon-like figure. To be honest, it wasn't easy, but it is an interesting rock on a little piece of beach that I was happy to visit. That said, in order not to be disappointed, remember, it's just a funny shaped rock.

From Jeju city it?s quite easy to reach by car. I had rented a car so no problems with public transportation or finding cabs.Going to the caves with a cab won?t be the problem. Unless you have instructed your driver to stay, you will get a problem to find a taxi.The cave can be a bit wet and slippery, so don?t go there thinking you are going to the beach. Dress accordingly is the advice.I found it quite interesting and definitely a must see when you are staying in Jeju.
Awesome,unique place and interesting cultural history, fresh and green,easy to find and will cone again
You can find almost everything here from fresh seafood to local eateries to clothing stalls. Things may not be real cheap here but it's interesting to walk around.

To get the most from this attraction it would really help if you like green tea! Everything is based on it including the food and treats. I had the (very expensive) ice cream and it really wasn?셳 to my taste. The museum on tea equipment was very interesting. Don?셳 make this your day?셲 primary focus but if you are passing it?셲 worth popping in.
The museum part was interesting a bit crowded at the food area but the queue was fast and quite a lot of tables. Purchase 30000won to get tax refund. Lots of tea selection.

The folk village was quite large with some interesting buildings but everything looked samey after a while. I was hoping to see a variety of performances on the stage but it was only a few songs sung by a group of women - charming enough but not what we were expecting. The foodie street also didn't have alot of stalls open though we did buy some cactus taffy which tasted like treacle and raisins and lasted us most of our trip in SK. One good thing was the interactive bits such as the old games children used to play. Having been in folk villages in other countries where there were people in traditional costumes showcasing different crafts and activity the Jeju one was a little disappointing.
Lots of interesting stuff to see. Variety of Korean food and all sorts of seafood and local specialties.Won't be disappointed.
It is interesting to walk around the shops and see the food and souvenirs they sell.The vendors are very friendly!

It is a hilly place with rows of eateries and shops. There are interesting street performances that are usually held in the evening. Look out for the shops where the local visit as they offer authentic Korean food. Do visit Gambit Gallery an unassuming shop that stocks hand-dyed clothes.

We drove our car over to Udo Island via a ferry. It was a great experience. A tip for drivers to head for the parking at the jetty as you have to fill in a form with your particulars (car number, drivers details) to purchase a ticket at the tour office. It only takes 15 mins to cross the island and thereafter we drove around. There are no maps so we went one round. It was very crowded being a Saturday so try to go on weekdays. There are a lot of interesting cafes, 4 beautiful beaches, lighthouses, lots of lovely spots for sightseeing and great photos opp. You can also take a speedboat at the black beach or visit the caves. We took the seafood pot with instant noodles for lunch in a local small restaurant. The last ferry was at 6.00pm but maybe earlier on weekdays. Overall, it was a very interesting day trip and we enjoyed ourselves.
It is wonderful and interesting with rectangular stones and beautiful landscapes. Interestingly, you may find woman divers nearby and you may like to each fresh raw seafood there.

Interesting, many different types of local food and daily items.  We had fresh seafood hotpot at one of the local eatery stalls.  30,000 wons, enough for three people.  The fresh fish slices are, in particular, very delicious.

Innisfree is a well-known brand with numerous outlets throughout Korea and Asia. As it originated from Jeju, this is their main outlet in Korea. It was much smaller than expected, with only a single long building housing both the shop and cafe.The shop stocked quiet a good range of their toiletries and cosmetics, with an natural soap-making activity available. You can purchase a pack from the counter, choose the scent of soap you want, and there are stations with a screen to guide you through the soap-making process step-by-step. Shop staff are on hand for assistance as well. At the end of it, you can pack the soap into an eco-bag as a gift.The organic green cafe had ample seating and a good range of food, compared to the adjacent O Sulloc tea museum. Their drinks are served in funky bottles with interesting tastes, and make a pretty picture.If in the area, the soap-making is interesting and wouldn't take too long.

If you like Hello Kitty, this is an interesting place to go. a 2 storey building converted into wholesomeness of Kitty everywhere. The cafe is nice too - but you need to pay for entrance fee to the museum in order to get into it. The food is average, but presentation is what people are paying for. Definitely a nice place for tonnes of photo taking. It's suitable for any weather. I went when it was snowing outside - so it's nice and warm inside.

When we were there they were having a special limited showing of the ancient art of making furniture jewelry boxes etc using shells.  The displays were beautiful and it was interesting to learn how involved the process is.  The museum was nice we went on a rainy day when we needed indoor activities.  The museum is laid out so you walk through different period of history.
Well maintained. It is basically a km long walk into a cave (which is created by lava). Some structures inside from the lava. But otherwise nothing interesting. It is cold in there so be prepared.

We had heard about the tea plantation first on the television show Kimchi Chronicles on PBS (http://www.kimchichronicles.tv/). As an avid tea drinker I could hardly pass up the chance to check it out in person and it is amazing. We drank tea walked in the tea fields checked out the tea museum watched the roasting of tea bought tea tea soap tea lotion and tea ice cream. The museum and center are quite stunning and the drive out there interesting on some very well maintained roads. Don't miss this one if you are on Jeju Island.
Visited the park when it was raining. Still very enjoyable and there is some sort a mini bird park in there. Very interesting and relaxing walk through the park.

Unfortunately  I cannot say that this place is worth visiting. The surrounding area and sites (Sanbangsan and the temple  Yongmeori Coast) are worth the visit though  and I speculate that this is the only reason the museum has survived.The ship museum itself provides information about the Dutch sailor who landed on Jeju and was held captive and against his will for several years by Koreans (not sure why this is a source of pride as it seems to be made out). The story itself could be quite interesting  but to be honest  I would rather read about it in a well-written book than in a tacky and very cheesy museum using broken English. Children might enjoy walking through the ship replica so I suppose it could be worth visiting if you also visited the other nearby sites.I personally would never recommend this place to anyone.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안
