review: There are many interesting places to visit in jeju. Limited range of products. Disappointing. That is why I am giving it low rating. Soap making? All stations are full.. You don?셳 see products flying off the shelves. And neither do you see people walking out of store with lots of shopping. Telling signs! Go next door. Osulloc Tea Museum. Eat and spend there...
The lava tube is very interesting to walk around. It can get pretty chilly underground so prepare accordingly.

The building itself is pretty cool  when we were there the tall grass was in in its full glory and towered over either side of the path into the building. We were given discounted admission because one of the exhibits inside was temporarily closed. It's interesting to walk around inside a bit (there are some nice clean bathrooms in there too) and see the several art exhibits inside. It's very peaceful and relaxing inside the building.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.

Quite a big museum and there are many fun and interesting spots to take photos. Entrance fee is around 9000 krw per person but you can spend a good 40mins to 1hr in the museum walking around and taking photos. Very good place to visit. Not too sure how accessible it is by public transport as I booked a driver for the day.

Nothing really special. 1000 (for youth) and 2000 (adult) admission fee. I wouldn't go there if it wouldn't be close to my guesthouse.Maybe it would be interesting for families with small children. But for a walk i would rather prefer going to the beach.
Lovely walk among the rows of tea. Very good concept to put Innisfree shop there. Interesting activities there like soap making. Attractive display

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.

It was pretty interesting that place is so unusual in Korea me and my friends were walking around discovering more and more statues and figures around. I think that place is unique and it?셲 very clean tickets are not expensive at all so if you have a chance - go there there aren?셳 many things to see on Jeju island.
It was an interesting visit but make sure you are able to walk two kilometers in dim lighting and on uneven flooring which can be wet and slippery. Wear comfortable shoes.

It was an interesting experience walking through the immense cave network. It's mind-boggling that this is only a very small part of a much larger system formed through volcanic activity. Do go to the visitors center to find out more information before venturing in.

it was a hot summer day when our tour guide took us to this park. It has a very large variety of plants and bonsai. Some of the bonsai plants are more than 100 years old!! The most interesting bit in my opinion was going into the lava tubes which are like under ground caves with unusual rock formations. Wear comfortable shoes. Its not strenuous but best to be comfortable when walking.

It only costs about $2 to visit (separate from transportation costs).  Very well maintained site but still a rough surface that requires suitable footwear and it can be wet and slippery in some spots; also quite cool.  This is a very impressive channel to walk through and imagine the lava flowing and leaving the characteristic marks and artifacts along it path.  Dim lighting gives a neat eerieness that somehow makes it even more exciting to explore.  Various well constructed boardwalks with built in floor lights improve access.  The entire tour is about 1 km in each direction.  Very interesting experience.

It is worth a visit when you are in Jeju Island.We enjoy the two kilometres walking vv. please make sure that you have a comfortable shoes no  as the surface is really from the lava. This cave is one of three unesco heritage sites in Jeju Island.Nice and cool inside the cave and interesting marks of lava. We enjoyed it very much.

It is interesting to see and then read how did these lava columns came to formation. It?s worth a quick walkaround. Place is not big so it gets pretty crowded but people are understanding to disperse so that you can have a chance to take some pictures too.
Interesting walk but didn't appreciate it much - this is probably a lot more interesting for a geography buff.
Good walk around the park and the cliffs were quite spectacular! Very interesting rocok formations that were built by lava flows.
Black Pork Street - Interesting an unique place to visit in the town of Jeju. Nice walk with friends.

An interesting outing to learn about volcanic activity and how the lava tube was formed. Not suitable for elderly visitors with the dim and uneven terrain. Many information board to explain unusual structures. Educational. Some wooden boardwalk in certain areas. The stairs at the entrance leading into the tube can be steep and slippery.

An interesting 2km round-trip walk through the Manjanggul lava cave in cool conditions. Was told by our guide that the temperature stays like this all year round. Really intriguing to see the various histotical lava formations and literally walk through a part of Jeju's history.

An absolute must-see on a visit to Jeju. Walk a kilometre in an underground tunnel formed by lava flow. The display boards explain what you're seeing so the rocks are interesting even if you have no previous knowledge of geology. Included in most tours of the West side of the island.
A fun and interesting maze to walk through. The map is a definitely must have or it will be challenging.

2000 won fee and well wooden path for tourist. Wind can be very strong since at the open sea and you can imagine the conditions in bad weather. If you like geography this is very interesting. Otherwise still a good place for some photo and walk in the south of the island.
You can enjoy a cool breeze and a walk around the yongduam area. The dragon head is not that interesting but since it's free admission, why not? We spent about 20 minutes walking around the area.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. Although the path throught the three sections of the cave are shorter, you can see much more. Go to Halim Park and skip Manjang Cave.

While the Crater is interesting and as is usual presented well, by Korean standards the prices are excessive.There are many more things to see on Jeju for free (or a minimal charge) that I can't understand why this was so expensive.The grounds are attractive and the path well made.However it was not possible to get really close to the crater and I would have liked to walk the rim.I wouldn't bother including it on your itinerary, unless you are a fan of the drama that is shot there.

We were at Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon before we went to Manjanggul. It was a god decision as it was a brief respite from the scorching sun.That aside, this place is itself a gem. Well maintained and interesting facts have their own boards for the visitors to read. Light jacket is highly recommended if you don't like cool places. Temperature is similar to if you blast your AC unit in your room. Very nice. Wear good shoes. Slippers and heels / platforms not recommended although we saw several girls wore them. You'll be walking on solidified lava. Hence, the walking surface is very unkind to ill-equipped feet. :).Overall, very good experience.

We walked the slippery, uneven and poorly lit path 1.5 km to the 7 meter column. It was again good to do some walking and the cave was interesting but how the cave was made was still a mystery after reading all of the panels (Wikipedia said lava flows of differing temperatures).

We did not had a chance to really walk around the village due to the on-going construction. Only manage to explore the front part of the village. There are students who volunteer themselves to walk you through the history of the village. Quite an interesting one. At the end of the sharing, they also do some selling.

Very interesting cave, which has been created by the vulcano. 1km long tunnel available for tourists inside of old not active  vulcano. Not difficult to reach and walk. Little dark, but lamps inside are giving sufficient light. Very good level of safety. Info how long to walk, communication system with support team,  stairs, bridges, walking paths. Information boards describing what you can see in cave. Even young children like 3-6y can easily enjoy this trip.
This was worth the entry fee. There is a nice walking tour of the   museum  . It was interesting to see all the glass displays in the forest. We really enjoyed the walk through the exhibits

This was an interesting place that was well preserved. Wear a good pair of walking shoes as the place is quite dark with very uneven floors so watch your step. The air in the cave is kept at a constant temperature of about 19-20 degrees all year round, not a problem as we went in winter. Very good if you have not seen anything similar to this before.

This lava cave is interesting if you are into nature and ok to walk in the dark on uneven rocks for 2km. I like the experience but my elderly parents didn't really appreciate the dark long walk, especially with the steep stairs. So unless your elderly members are physically fit, it will be much better if they skipped this.
The texture of the cave and the formation were very interesting and unique. The walk into the cave was a bit tedious due to the uneven ground. Otherwise, had a great outing.

The rocks surrounded by the island have different size and have eroded for years. But the most interesting thing is that rocks are eroded into different levels of cylinders, so it is worth to spend a couple of minutes there taking photos and have a look. Moreover, there are paths for visitors to walk around the edges of the island to have different look of the rocks. It is the margin of Jeju, so when the wave flaps the cliffs, it creates a huge noise. At first, I thought it was something like weapons exposed, my heart pumped faster than normal. After I recognize it is only the wave hits the cliffs, I can clearly experience that how the level of power that the nature can be. It was an unforgettable experience.So, if you have an iPhone which contains the program of Live Photo, try to open it before you take photos. It is because you can record the energetic movement of wave in your photo.

Place for everyone who like caves, volcanos or geology. The cave is long, but the one kilometre available for tourists is enough. There are many interesting lava formations, described in English. Beside that the cave is just beautiful. The temperature inside is around 10째C, humidity close to 100%. If you are not very fond of caves, stones or walking, probably you should skip it. :-)

Not many such places are open to public visit, so I will say this is something interesting to explore if you visit Jeju. Temperature is lower than outside, so do bring a jacket or wear long sleeves if you are scare of cold. Physical mobility is required as there are steep steps to walk down to the entrance and paths are uneven.There is a restaurant and convenient store on site. We had lunch at the restaurant after the visit. Pretty decent Korean meals. Have translation app ready if you do not read Korean as menu is in Korean .

Nice place to go for a walk through the fields. The   museum   itself is not much and very little in English. The tea shop is OK with great but expensive green tea ice cream.The best bit is the other   Innisfree   shop and coffee shop in the grounds. Nice range of teas and coffees and interesting snacks. Inside and outside seating available. There are also stations in the shop to shape and   flavour   soap - if you buy the $15 kit that is. instructions on the supplied Ipad in several different languages.

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.

I've never been in a lava tube before, but it was a lot like a cave. The formations inside are pretty interesting and the park does a good job lighting them colorfully. It was a nice walk. However, it is very touristy and if you've been to bigger caves in other parts of the world it's just cool, not extremely impressive.

It was an interesting experience to walk through the 1km long tunnel if you enjoy understanding and seeing the various structures and rock formations formed from the lava flow. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

I find walking in this lava cave is interesting as it is so cool inside and surprisingly there is no bad smell as it is rather wet. The cave produces it's on air conditioning as the temperature inside is around 15-17 Celsius. Some areas are well lighted and some are not, proper walking shoes are needed as there are many uneven areas along the path provided. Good experience for the ones who loves outdoor!

I am interested in world heritage and Manjang Cave is included in sites of Jeju's world heritage so I went there. I had never walked inside a cave before, so it was an interesting experience. And I appreciate the carving in the walls and the shapes of rocks that were formed by volcanic activities.The temperature inside the cave is colder than the temperature outside, so it's better to bring a jacket.
Footbridge is of interesting architecture and good photo opp, walk across to the small island and trek around it (about 30 min) to see the sceneries around.
An interesting walk underground in a 1 km long cave. Some people would find fascinating, others might get abit claustrophobic.Very cheap, about 90 pence per person. Beautiful grounds on the outside.

Amazing cave carved by molten lava moving underground with many interesting features, however, you need to be prepaired for dim lighting, uneven floor with many tripping hazards as well as uneven steps/stairs.  Not suitable for young children or older folks who have trouble with sight or walking.
A nice evening walk at sunset.There were many locals lying down on the benches, playing loud music.? Although it lacked tranquility, we found it interesting to observe local customs.

We finally got a good clear day.Yesterday at Sunrise Mountain we had been in the clouds.  Some nice views down the coast. Not a terrible tough or long hike to get to the end of the trail with a small temple cave. Number of mostly coffee shops at the bottom and bathroom facilities.

We didn't get to spend as much time on Udo as we would have liked. I would have liked to so the Olle Trail but there wasn't enough time.  We had walked up a steep hill thinking we could get to the lighthouse but you go at it from the other side.  If you don't want to walk rent a motorcycle.  Don't forget your driver's license.  I hear the lighthouse is wonderful and we will go back.  Lots of cute little places to eat or have coffee and there's a nice beach. There's not really a fee to get on the island but you have to take a ferry and there's a fee for that.

We climbed to the top of Mt.  Hallasan via the seongpanak trail. We are in just above average shape and we had no issues getting to the top with not stops in 2hrs 40 mins. There are three rest areas along the way that you can stop at if you need a good break. The last 1.5k to the top is the real shocker. We did not do our homework and went up real early on the morning and it was so windy and cold we did not stay long at the top. It was cloudy at the top anyway so we were not able to see 20 feet off the mountain so we headed back down. There is little to no people climbing the mountain at 6am but I'm out way down there was more people ascending to the top. Overall it was a good trip but I recommend bringing a windbreaker and not starting until around 7 on a clear day.

We actually stayed at a hotel right on this beach.  The water is beautiful but there are signs saying no to swimming in some parts of it.  There is a cafe bene right next to it so you can grab a cup of coffee and go sit on the beach.  The only problem is that it is pretty far from anything else like all the museums and nature trails of jeju and it is kind of small which makes me think that in the summer it can get really crowded.

This is a well maintained natural forest. You can walk here after visiting the Roe Deer Observation Centre or take the Jeju City bus.  There are many trails and a fair amount of visitors. Entrance fee is payable and a car park is available at the entrance.

There are 7 trails that you can climbs the mountainBut there are 2trails  only to reach to the top.Since i took 4courses i will explain where i visited that is also most people goTo SummitTrails : If you want to go to the top there are 2trails Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa  trail. Normally people go up by Seongpanak and go down by Gwaneumsa since Gwaneumsa is more difficult to go upTaking time : round trip takes 9 to 10hours so you better start your day early otherwise they will stop you to go up in some area Especially Jindalrea shelter will close at 1230pm or 1pm which can be vary depends on seasonAlso on your way to Jindalrea shelter there is another short trail Sara oreum which is really beautiful and takes only 40min. so it is YOU MUST VISIT place unless you are not hurry by time.How to get to : from Jeju bus terminal there is a bus that ofpen goes every 15min and takes 30min For beautiful viewTrail : Yeonsil trail and Eorimok Trail People normally go up by Eorimok and go down by Yeongsil but for me the opposit is betterTaking time : round trip takes 5hours and easy to walk if you like climbingHow to get to : there is only one time every hour so you better check in the termimalEorimok takes 35min from terminal and Yeonsil is 2stops more from EorimokPersonally i prefer Eorimok and Yeongsil trails.Also i highly recommend you to have climbing shoes otherwise your feet will be beaton up by rocks and enough waterall trail has shelters that sell food and drink but you better bring your own water Even it rains it is another feeling climbing mountain very attractive to go with lots of fogI never thought it is good to climbs when raining but i liked it a lotHowever prepare a nylon raincoat  from jeju bus terminal since it is very windy Poly raincoat would be ripped It is double price from the entranceThis is the best montain among i have visited in Korea

Seriously stunning display of flowers at Camellia Hill; the biggest arboretum in Asia famous for its forest path and beautiful gardens of camellias. The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!

It's one of the stops between Seogwipo and Jungmun on the Airport Limousine route (bus no. 600). Or if you are on the Jeju Olle Trail no.8 you would pass by this temple. They don't charge entrance fee and it is less crowded compared to other tourist sites in Jeju. Take a stroll around the temple and take your time to soak in the serenity. If you are up for a temple stay program they do provide such service.

It takes 45-60 minutes to hike around the whole trail. The trail is diverse in the scenes that it presents along different coastal views. Brace yourself for high wind speeds during the colder months. There are a lot of inclines/declines on the trail so be wary of that on the way. There are a couple of restaurants/eateries spotted along mid-trail but I have no comment on those establishments. Before the trail officially begins there is a little rest-stop with coffee shops convenience stores and restrooms so I would recommend using the facilities before you embark on your hike.

I just love the view in Jeju that I could see a mountain stand next to the sea. Songak-san is really green you could feel refreshed while hiking to the top of it. The hiking trail was covered so that you wouldn't slip. The hike won't take that long about half an hour to the top and then you could enjoy the view above like the island which was the very southern part of South Korea.

I go here every day to walk up the steep hill to the right of the beach for exercise.  It's the start of the No. 19 Olle Trail.  I usually always see bride and grooms having their photos taken on the beach and in the fields of rapeseed.  Views from the top of the hill are amazing.  Sometimes if there are horses around I'll pick grass and feed them in exchange for a little pat and nuzzle from them.  If you look carefully there are quite a few different flowers around.  If you pick a green rapeseed that hasn't yet flowered and peel the stalk you can eat the stalk.  It tastes like sweet brocalli.  The cherry blossoms are lovely there too if you happen to be there in early April.  The water is clear.  I like to feed and water some of the stray dogs.  It kills me that I can't give them a home.  They appreciate a bit of a cuddle too but you can see their priority is getting food.  There are some very good restaurants in Hamdeok as well.  Ive put a pic of one of the ones on the main street of Hamdeok. .its a local one that serves a set menu at lunch time and its very good.  The sunsets are spectacular.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.
You can feel the coastal and the sea breeze along this trail.You can visit nearby Cheonjiyeon waterfall, or Saeseom (Saeyeongyo Bridge).

Wow! I'm glad I saw this before leaving! Jeju is full of surprises and this is one of them. We were extremely lucky this was a foggy day because seeing this place in fog was really special.  The amazing display of wood carvings etc at the wood exhibition place was amazing as we're all the large insects carved out of cedar wood. It's a 20 min drive from Jeju City. Apparently in summer you have to protect your lunch from the crows! A nice easy walk and an oreum (hill) trail if you want something a bit harder. There are lots of carved statues all along the way and one of those stone paths which you can walk on with your shoes off.  I manage about 2 feet, too hard for me! Haha!

Will never forget our longest hike in our entire life! Our earlier plan was just to enjoy the view of fall foliage during the autumn and it happened that Mount Halla was the only place... Did our homework earlier before our trip there so that we can get a perfect picture of the foliage in Hallasan. Ended up, we only managed to see a lot of deciduous trees, perhaps, due to the heavy rain and wind the night before our trip. Wrong timing... There were some trees along the Yeongsil trail (the route we used) but the leaves had turned brown, not the orangey red... My husband and I couldn't feel our legs after the hike and I lost my cap due to the very strong wind! Anyhow, the view was spectacular as Hallasan is the highest mountain in Jeju!

Went on a day hike up and down the Seongpanak trail! It was a gorgeous day, about 18C and I couldn't have asked for better weather. It took about 10 hours round trip. Started around 8:30am and made it down by 6:30pm. Luckily the sun didn't go down until 7:15ish so I had plenty of light to guide me.Now, I am not a hiker by any means and this was one of the toughest hikes I've been on. To be honest, it wasn't because the trails were all that difficult - it was actually quite pleasant through the woods and there were 2 rest stops along the way. The first stop is basically a bathroom break and the 2nd had some food available before heading up the last (somewhat steeper) trail to the lake up top. Oh, by   food   I mean some cup ramen and snacks. They also sold water and sports drinks. It would be helpful for you to bring food of your own. They also have no garbage cans so you need to carry and dispose of your own trash once you get back down.The reason why this trail was difficult for me was because I simply wasn't ready for a 20km hike! By the last 5km of the descent, I felt my feet and legs were going to fall off or give in to becoming jelly due to all the stairs and rocks. Make sure you have proper shoes! All in all, I'm glad I did this hike - it was worth it when I got to the top and was able to experience amazing views and clean air. And the flowers!! It was simply beautiful. Just expect to have sore calves for a few days following :)

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!
