review: The beach area as well as the water are looking clean. The sand is white. We did not go in since it was late October. The view is nice and the neighbourhood has shops and restaurants available. There is a coffee shop directly at the beach where you can rest if you find a place to rest. Usually the shop is quite crowded. At night time some fireworks ongoing. We had the Golden Tulip hotel and we were enjoying the view to the beach every morning.

Sunrise Peak. Sunset PeakWe travelled as part of a tour and on arriving were given the usual coach departure time. 1hour in this instance! Not sure of the entrance fee as it was included in our tourNot hanging around we set off immediately for the top with several good rests in between. The pathway is steep in places but in good order with plenty of resting/passing places. Separate paths up and down. Quite a climb but well worth it. Half way up is a little stall/shop for soft drinks and snacks (they have to manhandle everything up!)Once at the top there are plenty of viewing spots. Really worth the climb. We witnessed a superb sunset over the island and took some wonderful photosOn the path down there is a WC.We made the round journey just about in time with 15mins at the peak and a wander around the cliff edge on the way downFrom what I?ve heard the sunset is equally as breathtaking as the sunrise but not as crowded. Sunset was at approx 7.30 and on the way down the path is fairly well lit

Songaksan was one of the places that had actually a very small crowd of tourists so it make the hike a bit more enjoyable. At the foot of the mountain is a large parking lot with some coffee shops and restaurants from there it is a light hike up the mountain. Lots of greenery and nice views along the way. The center which I believe is a crate is closed right now I think for recovery from too many tourists. it is still a good destination to visit the hike is easy and relaxing peaceful and enjoyable.

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!

Really nice view coz the waterfall is right next to the open sea. I could feel the splash on my face when I approached its bottom.Tips: be ready to climb the stairs after viewing the waterfall. It's not too long but you may get tired after a long day of touring in Jeju.Be careful if you want to go near the waterfall coz it's all big rocks at the bottom.

read reviews on this place and thought should visit and ee all the hype. To start of with there is an entrance fee of 12000 KW its not worth it for the exhibits and it was all in Korean so really didn't get it at all. Anyways since I was already there just make the most of it. nothing so special so you can give this a miss if you have spare time enjoy the beach view is much better than wasting time here.
Pretty excercise to get up to hill ... 500 steps you can feel in legs but final view worth it. Do not miss this place!

Our driver drove us to the rest stop and from there we hiked about 30 minutes to the top. It had just rained so don't try it without solid walking shoes as it's easy to get a nasty fall. It was cloudy so we couldn't get a view of Jeju city but the feeling of being on top of the world was worth it!

Nothing much to do over there. You will only walk walk walk to look at the view. With the cooling wind and nice view. I made me feel very relax and the walk is enjoyable. I think it is a must visit place if you have not been here before.
not too bad to climb up as it looks. definately top 5 things to do in Jeju.I go there everytime I go to Jeju island.Always nice view and great feeling on the top.

Not much to see or do except to take a few moments to take it the view and wind of Jeju. Many people (mostly Koreans) are seen walking along the beach picking shells or dipping their feet in the water. Not much sunbathers on this beach.
Not bad for visiting the entrance ticket fees is 12000won per person . Inside have a lot of things to view for sex and health...

nice view everywhere. took the ferry and saw people feeding the birds. took the bus tour but seems more fun taking the ATV which many young people are taking. we took the speed boat at udo peak area and was quite fun & exciting. can spend at least half a day in udo.

Nice quiet temple compound with a sea view. Place is rather big and is nice for a walk. One tends to feel peaceful there.We went there around late afternoon. Perhaps that?셲 the reason why there are not much people around. Just nice for us to explore the temple and do some photo taking.Worth a visit.
Nice place to view all sorts of native Camellia. Entrance fee is cheap around 5000-6000krw.It's a good place for couples basking in the sun and enjoying the flowers at the same time.

My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our time at these gardens. The effort that has gone into creating different exhibits both indoor and outdoors in extraordinary. It has an extremely relaxing feel and a great view of the volcanic mountain.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Moonlight is a great walking activity to do with your friends or family. It's pretty easy and the view is awesome. We walked on a golf felid for about 30min until arriving at a cliff with a great ocean view. Walking barefoot on the grass felt fresh and was pretty fun! After watching the sunset we head to watch a mini-concert just for us! this was the perfect getaway to feel relaxed again!
Might not be worth the $2 entry fee. If you walk behind the first ticket counter you get one of the best views of the falls. There's another ticket booth that they punch your ticket at.
Love the view at the top and the peacefulness feel before the tourist buses arrived.Hate that it gets filled with noisy tourist after mid-morning.

Its three floors with aquariums but still not so big bu got pretty awesome one with big display where you can sit and enjoy the view. I also liked the show. They got 2 types of it one with humans and several with animals like dolphins and sea bear. Performance times are 11:10 13:00 15:00 and 17:00. There is also feeding times and female diver's diving. It opens from 10 to 19 so be sure you will see at least one of performance and have time to look around since performance lasts about 40-45 min each.

review: It was a bit difficult to find but totally worth the drive. It is so peaceful and pretty that its hard to believe it is a fully functioning church. There is also a cafe across the church building that has good coffee and good views.
It only take a 1 hour to 1 1/2 hour to top of the Mt. but view is awesome. They close aroud 6:00 pm. entrance fee is 2000 won per person.

It is listed as a Unesco World Heritage and definetly a place to stop. Highway 1132 will bring you there and you cannot miss it. Be prepared that parking might not be easy and you may have to spend some time. The place is quite busy and many tourist buses are coming too. We had a cloudy day and it was very windy. Entrance fee is 2000 adult and 1000 child. Couple of shops at the entrance where you can buy each and everything. Please keep in mind that waste management is terrible as everywhere in Korea. If you buy something keep in mind that no any trash beans are available. The way up and down is quite crowded and loud. Obviously many tourists are rushing on top to get the selfies done to rush down again. The walk is definetly nothing for stroller or wheel chair. We went up slowly enjoying the view and getting some pictures. On top it is quite nice to look into the volvano and rest. Sure some pictures not to forget. But again very busy place and loud. Again our day was cloudy and windy but as long as it is not raining worth to visit the peak. So conclusion would be to visit the place very early.

It a pleasant place to visit: Lots of visitors n cars maybe was a weekendThe walk is not too difficult  you will enjoy if you take it slowly n see the view from different angle n height Need food shoes n the slope is pretty steep n may need to hold the rope/railing at certain height Feel good n nice when reach the top

I was here last week with my wife and we enjoyed the walk around this part of the coast. On a light drizzly morning the walk took on a determined bent but we were certainly not alone. There were loads of people when we were there. The backdrop is fairly dramatic looking and there is a small entrance fee. The view from the top at the carpark is quite beautiful too.

I was a little worried after reading some reviews but after going i am pleasantly surprised.  The entrance fee is a little high at 11000 won for an adult and if i had kids i might be worried they would get bored.  Seems perfect for couples and people who like taking pictures.  If you take your time and dont rush you can do the whole place in am hour.  Lots to look at.  Worth a stop.  Bonus...if your name is yoori you get free entrance and a free gift

I don't understand when I saw that people gave poor reviews for this place. Camellia Hill for me was nothing short of magic. Even in autumn when it wasn't supposed to be the peak season it was beautiful. You can take slow walks and just enjoy the relaxed feeling. It's made to be beautiful for every season and you can't deny it. I can imagine myself just being there reading a book or just sipping warm tea at the cafe. It's definitely well thought of.

Herb hill located a bit far from town and we having bit hard time searching for the right place. If happen to drive there by urself just key in Herb Dongsan navigation will lead the way. The journey from Seogwipo to this place it's approximately 40mins. There's two different entrance fees charges which is day entry or night entry the charges is 3k differences. Day entry - 9am - 530pm (9000won per person) Night entry - 530pm onwards (12000won per person) Before you get into this lovely place  they you hand you a map of this place which stated 15 Mark points. The park is really good for photography  remember to get ur tripod with you if you travel alone or just couple. =) come in at day time go back at night time so you have two different view of pic. We arrive at 3pm but we told the lady that we wish to stay until 8pm. and they need us to paid 12000 per person. But I personally think that you can pay the day entry price and stay till late night becos no one is checking the ticket when going out from the park. (At least no one check mine ticket although I paid 12000  so your own risk ya. Just a small tips)
Great beach Great viewsAnd amazing picture spotsI recommend having a coffee at a cafe dolmondo ..  there which is right over the beach Beautiful scenery

Great  cosy  simple with a beautiful view  countryside atmosphere and the elegance of a modern coffee place. You can see how the plants grow and you can pet animals as well. A place to drink and eat something too.
Good view if you go on the day they don't have a heavy fog like me 555Please look for the weather forecast before you go.You have to pay 2000 KRW for a parking fee
Everyone should try reaching the peak with your loved ones. The summit view is amazing and you would feel a sense of achievement once you reached the top. Beginners can do this within 40mins!
Cheap entry fee ( 2.000 won) since it's managed by government. It took around 1-2 hours here. Check the wheather before go. Beautiful view.

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.

Calling this place a museum is absolute fraud. The entrance fee is 3000 won which is returned to you in the form of a coupon for the cafe or gift shop - both of which are insanely overpriced. The 'displays' are ridiculous - chocolate gold coins  chocolate Easter eggs  Guylian seashell-shaped chocolates  posters of the film 'Chocolat ' a statue of Willy Wonka. It's almost as if the museum is teasing the West for its chocolate traditions - if it can even be called that. There is really nothing of interest in this museum. There is  however  a pretty nice view of the ocean to the rear of the museum.

C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) This temple was not famous in Jeju area but there was very good temple and had good seaview. There was not traditional temple shape and magnificent. Becasue there was not many people it was good to me with quietness and enjoying reserve. Recommenable place I think. No entrance fee.
Breathtaking! Enjoyed the walk and picturesque view. Really enjoyed the view. Entrance fee about 2000 won for adult and 1000 for kids
Be sure to witness the sunrise view. Its worth the climb to the top.entrance fee is 2000won. Wear comfortable shoes preferably sneakers

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

Amazing views all the way up and at the top. If visiting in summer - better to visit in evening or early morning.  We climbed up twice - once at 5pm and then at 5.30 the next morning.  Both were excellent - with different sun position giving different light and shadows.  Both worth it.  Fee is 5000 won per person ( half price if child or youth under 24).  If you go before 7 in the morning - there is no charge.  When you come down make sure that you take the path around to the right - good views down to the small beach and also on the main peak
A must visit when you come to Jeju. Great ocean views. Its quite a drive from the city around 2 hours but its worth the experience and super views . Entrance fee : 2000 KW

A good place with nice view of the bridge and open sea. No entrance fees is required and is accessible via public transport and some walking is needed. Restaurants are available within the bridge area and other attractions such as submarine is located just right before the entrance into Saeyeongyo Bridge.

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.? Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!? It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

Yes, the walk is steep and if you go for sunrise, you will be starting off in the dark, but it doesn't take long to reach the top (16-30 minutes for reasonably fit people). The most important thing is to watch the forecast beforehand to ensure a lovely sunrise. The views are outstanding. It can get quite crowded at the viewing   steps   at the top, so get there early to stake out your perfect viewing spot. The walk down will obviously be in much lighter conditions, affording some incredible views of the coastline and the little town of Seongsan. Early morning or during the day, any time would be a fantastic time take this short - but oh so worth it - hike. There is plenty of accommodation for all budgets in Seongsan at the foot of the mountain and bus 701 or 710 can take you directly there from Jeju City Bus Terminal. In April, 2016, the entrance fee cost 2000 Won for adults.

Yeomiji, located in JoongMoon sightseeing complex, is one of the most impressive place in my memory. - Entrance ticket fee is under 10USD, which is quite reasonable. - Area is divided by its own theme like tropical, Japan, Korea ... - Why don't you order a cup of coffee(or ice cream) and take a rest at the center of greenhouse garden- Observatory has nice view. but it is easily get crowded.Tip: you'd better to go CheonJeYeon waterfall(천제연폭포) after here. that place also has beautiful natural scenery :)

Worth a visit to capture the incredible sunrise and sunset views. Take a walk up and around the peak, listen to the waves crashing and feel the mighty wind sweeping.We were during winter. We were glad to be wearing enough to bear the chilly wind beating at us.

When you visit Jungmun Resort, don't forget to visit Jungmun-Daepo Coast (Jusangjeolli Cliff). The location is near the ICC and the Seaes Hotel & Resort. For KRW 2000 entrance fee, you get great view and it is perfect location for taking photos! It is said that the best time to visit here is during sunset.

When I first looked at the advertisement, I assumed that I could stand on some place where I can see the overview of the crater.But actually, standing on the edge of the crater, you cannot feel the overview.In addition, I was one of the first visitors coming on that day, so it was not crowded and I could feel the peace in the air.

Went in the morning. The view is breathtaking. Must visit. Korean artists love this place for a good reason. Featured in some korean shows as well. It's very pretty. Packed some sandwiches, lay a mat, have a breakfast and feel the breeze.

We were lucky because when we went, there weren't a lot of tourist going up. Otherwise, it will be even more tiring as everyone will have to accommodate each other's pace. A lot of stairs to deal with but when you're at the top, it is worth the effort. We took about 20 mins (I think), stopping occasionally to take pictures of the scenic view down below. If you're tired, don't worry as there are enough benches on the way up to rest to regain your energy, if it comes to that. It is manageable overall.On our way down, we went to the black sand beach. Spent about 40 mins there, soaking in the view from another angle. If you want the full experience, you can take the boat out with the lady divers (Hanyeo) and see them in action. Alternatively, very fresh seafood is available for your palate should you want to try. From the sea, to the chopping board and straight to your plate (raw) and that's how they eat it. We didn't do that. Can't find the courage to do so. Lol. If the heat really got to you, after the climb down, go to one of the coffee places (Angel-in-us or Starbucks) to cool down before you go elsewhere. Be prepared to sweat buckets!!!

We were here in October, so we weren't swimming. We drove by here one day to check it out, a day or two after a typhoon hit, and the beach was trashed a bit (just from trees and debris and stuff), but people were cleaning it up and there were still lots of people enjoying the beach. It looks like a nice place to spend a day, and there seemed to be a bunch of restaurants and cafes dotting the beach as well. We stopped at one of the cafes for a coffee and to enjoy the view of the water for a bit.

We went to three or four different beaches on the island and this one hands down is the best. We didn't swim as it was in September already but spent a couple of hours strolling on the boardwalk. There are plenty of eateries across the street from the beach and some were on the beach side as well. The view was fantastic and definitely worth a visit. Also, parking was quite easy as well. We stopped for coffee (of course) and sweets at the nice coffee shop right on the beach before leaving and sitting there drinking coffee and watching sunset was a real treat.

we went to this place, but we didn't went up the park/hill/rock, as it will require lots of walking, which we didn't want to do :)you will still be able to have an impressive view at the entrance, and amazed by this natural creation. you can see the people walking up to the peak, enjoy the strong wind, as it is located by the sea, do a little shopping around the entrance area, or even find a nice cafe that is facing the spot to enjoy a hot coffee!

We went there directly from the airport via bus (because it was too early for us to check in at our booked hotel).  At the place, the lockers were not available, unfortunately, and we cannot leave our bags somewhere. So we had to carry our things up to see the Seongsan Ilchulbong. We did not attempt to climb up to the peak due to our heavy bags. Instead, we opted to see the observatory at the side of the mountain (it was free... the side going to the peak has an entrance fee) and has a nice view of the sea and the mountain. Can even go down to the sea shore if you like (we didn't). The view from the observatory was breathtaking vast ocean, blue sky and cool green mountain. Will definitely go back someday to see the peak! Also, we tried the Hallabong softcone (ice cream) just near the entrance road to the place, and it was so delicious!!

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited on a sunny day, a nice change from the rain from the day before.At the entrance, you have the choice to walk around the short & free pathway by the sea or you could pay an entrance fee to hike up to the top of Seongsan for a birds eye view. We opted for the hike up.I wasn't very fit so it took me a couple of stops before I got up eventually..but the view was worth it. If you go earlier, you could catch the performance by the Haenyeo down by the shore at the bottom of Seongsan. Sadly, we did not manage to catch the performance.

We visited Jongbang waterfall (諛⑺) during our stay in Seogwipo. It's very conveniently located and easy to find. Entry fee is just 2000. There's very short hike (~130 steps) to get to the waterfall. It's a small-ish waterfall and don't expect it to be Niagara Falls kind of but the view is nice. Once you get down the stairs there are rocks that you can walk over to get to the bottom of the Falls, take some nice pictures and feel the water droplets. I wouldn't say it's THE things to do in Jeju island but if you happen to be staying in Seogwipo or driving by, it's worth a visit. It takes less than an hour and can be visited with kids...and if you happen to go here try some orange juice or chocolates!!

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance (I have attached the photo) and you can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We alighted and headed to the dark brown beach along Seongsan. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore where to can pick clams and walkway with dry cuttlefish along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum as we reached Jongdal Elementary school at 5.30 pm. Noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market to Jongdal Elementary school (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier. We decide to go back as it was late by bus 701 back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal from Jongdal Elementary school  as we noted that the bus will take about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.

We really enjoyed this hike with our family. It is steep, as the reviews noted, but it is very fast. Our five-year-old and seven-year-old had no problem doing it on their own. It has nice views, isn?t very difficult, and it?s right next to an interesting coffee shop (you can see it from the parking lot) that has been converted from an old horseback riding resort. The coffee shop also has a bakery with some delicious treats for after the hike.  Easy to find and plenty of parking.  Overall a great little outing.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

We heard and saw this on TV and view to visit when we get the chance so of course we had to see for ourselves. We had impression very crowded road but there were only a few cars. It was about 4pm. We were able to follow another car uphill turn around, follow to the start point.We put car on neutral then let it drive us. Very strange. It just move slow motion like haunted road feel.We stop by at a mart for coffee. There is a cafe too. A few people cos winter not nany tourists strangely, we saw a van and a bus doing same thing, just gliding down.It was just nice finally seeing and experiencing this in jeju.

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do). The Sangumburi entrance fee is expensive if not in season to see the wheat fields at their peak and the changing leaves of fall, I think it was 11,000won or $11. I recommend going to Chefline Park if you are seeing this April 2018. Entrance if free there and but no volcanic crater. We went here and there was construction going on and the wheat fields had been cut down. They should charge less when construction is going on and the field has been cut. The walk around the park only takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. There are some nice views and the crater is cool.

We got here by public bus from the Manjanggul caves. It took about an hour as we had to transfer. Using the public transport is a bit of an adventure in itself. I think the bus routes have been updated lately so even some of the locals seem confused at times.We looked at the top of the peak and thought, 'no way, this looks like it'll take 2 hours to climb'. However after asking other tourists we were told it takes about 25 minutes. I was sceptical as I'm not the fastest at going up stairs.The entry fee was 2,000 krw and despite taking quite a lot of short breaks on the way up we reached the top in 20 minutes! The views were lovely.We ended up doing this around midday and it was HOT. I recommend coming here earlier or later in the day if you can when it is a bit cooler. It was rewarding to reach the top. They are selling some drinks in the way up but I recommend that you pack some water as well as a snack to eat when you enjoy the views at the top.

We enjoyed our time in Innisfree Jeju House very much and will definitely return if we ever visit Jeju Island again! It links to Osulloc Tea Museum. Just a few steps away and you will arrive at Innisfree Jeju House. The retail area was crowded. While ladies shop for their skincare, we had some really unique desserts, coffee and tea in the cafe. You can also purchase the hand soap making kit and make your own soap there. Not to forget to enjoy the tea field view before you leave the place!

We decided to go to Audi because of the 3 different beaches the were there (and for Haha Hoho Burgers). Getting there was more difficult than expected. We had a rental car which was nice to be able to retreat back to air conditioning. But the line for the ferry was so long that it took about 2 hours to get on the ferry. Once on the island our first stop was for lunch at Haha Hoho. We were lucky in that they didn't sell out of burgers by the time we got there at 1:50. Buy by the time our burgers were ready 2:40 they were sold out and not taking any more orders. So get there early for lunch. The drive around the island was nice  and picturesque. The first beach we stopped at was a disappointment. The water was green with algae and smelled. There was also quite a bit of trash. With the number of people there I would expect more maintenance. We stayed only briefly hoping for better beaches down the road. The next stop was a black sand beach nestled in a cool looking cove. But again there was trash everywhere. We didn't stay long. The first two beaches were a   bust.    The third was the   coral beach.   It was clean but the water still green with algae and seaweed. The beach was rough under our feet but the kids had fun. It was pretty crowded and the water became deep quickly so not much space to play for new swimmers. The views from the island were great, especially at sunset. Overall we were underwhelmed and felt we probably should have stayed on Jeju and just visited the northern beaches.

Visited May 2016, season of summer but the day we visited it was a bit of rainy thus our tour guide told us to explore it before the rain totally pours as the place will be foggy means the view will be blocked. The view is nice, I traveled with my pregnant wife so we didn't went to the top as I assume you need to take that hundred or more steps to reach the top. Also, for the reason of not giving a perfect rating, the place is very crowded, though there is an entrance fee but no control of the number of tourist going inside. Its too many that we didn't enjoy much thinking that we visit it in off season, rainy weather, and even just wandering on the lower ground still crowded (refer to my picture that I took just in the entrance part only).
Very unique waterfall by the sea. walk up close and feel the water spray across your face, while the sea waves lap your feet below. great view and refreshing experience.

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.

Up & down of the mountain took us 9.5 hours including some short rest time during the hike. We started the hike around 9am (recommend to start early, we were late), and came down around 6:30pm. Our legs were like jelly legs after the hike, but is worth the hike. You can see nice view along the journey. Please do not forget to greet everyone you met with   anyeonghaseyo  , they are all very friendly people. Wear a pair of good hiking shoes, bring some snacks with you and also water. The stalls along the mountain are closed during our hike, luckily we have prepared enough snacks and water. The view at the peak is breathless. A lots of old korean aunties and uncles also managed to reach the peak, so I guess we all younger than them have no excuses of not fit to hike, right? haha...Wear sport attire, although some said it will be freezing cold at the peak (about 1950 meters height), but believe me, you wont feel cold as you have already all sweat during the hike. We spent about 30mins to 1 hour at the peak taking photos, resting and having our snacks before going down again. A pair of good hiking shoes is important so that you won't get blister on your feet. We will go back again in different season if we have the chance. We were travelling there in Oct 2018.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unless one is interested in its history or legend about how the 3 holes came about, there is nothing much to explore. The compound is rather small and quiet, just a handful of visitors. In one pavilion is a 3D multimedia presentation, lasting 14 mins, which explains the legend behind these 3 holes. Unfortunately, visitors cannot get close to these holes, hence have to view from afar. 30 minutes is sufficient to cover this place, admission fees 2,500 won.Recommend to drop by only you have spare time to kill or already nearby. Else can skip this place.

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say   Udo  . The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the   old fashioned   bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.
