took our family of 3 about 11hrs round trip. it can be done in 9 if you ha e the right gear and move fast. its gradual grade, so its not strenuous but the terrian is terrible. it is 85percent big rocky jagged lava chunks. if you are prone to ankle injury, this hike is not for u. you have to watch your feetthe whole time  which is fine since there is no view until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. so all in all i do not really recommend this hike unless you have lots of time in Jeju and you really wanna say you climbed Koreas highest peak.

Took bus 781 from City Hall in Jeju City about 30-40min bus ride for 1300KRW. Had some breakfast at the Seongpanak bus station (base camp), got a bottle of water and a snickers then started the hike. Read that it would take 8-9 hours roundtrip, got to the top in less than 3, a very slow and steady rising hike firstly through the forest and later up the mountain. Stunning views from about 1800m and up, saw some water also in the crater, quite crowded at the summit. Ate my chocolate bar, took a selfie and started walking down. Total time return trip to the bus station was 6 hours. Best tip is to not pause at the middle camp which you must reach before 12:00 if you want to get to the peak, but instead just walk on to the top and have some lunch or break up there, you will then skip most of the crowd, try to head back down before 13:00, as you need to leave the peak before 13:30 it does get crowded on the descent and will just increase your time spent by waiting for slow groups.The views are spectacular, do recommend, no fees.

Took around 6 hours up and 4-5hours down the volcano. Really pretty with all the snow around, but on the way down snow started to melt and the ground is slightly muddy. traveled there in the winter period from December to January. You should go and reserve an entire day for this winter hike!If you choose not to climb to the peak, at around half way mark there is a crater which is around 3 hours up and another 3 hours down. The crater is filled with water but is frozen in winter. But i would recommend heading to the peak for the best views! There is a rest station at 2/3 hours mark with toliets and 2nd rest station at the 4/5hours mark near to summit. The 2nd rest station has a small shop that sells coffee, instant noodles, gloves, small tidbits. But best if you bring along some gimbap along to fill your stomach.

This waterfall is not very big as compare to other but the view is breath-taking as the water falls into the edge of the cliff at the sea front. One can feel the mist of the water fall spraying onto the face as one walk closer to the cliff of the water fall. However, be very careful while walking on the rock towards the waterfall as the rock gets more slippery as one get nearer to the waterfall. But it is definitely worth the risk and the slow walk as the pictures that comes out from the shot is gorgeous!

This waterfall is beautiful and worth visiting. The only drawback is the slightly treacherous rocks to get to the water, but our boys thought it was a real adventure. A very reasonable fee of 2,000 Won which clearly helps maintain the area, which had nice toilets. Very clean. I wish I could have enjoyed the fresh sashimi from the free divers, but the boys got restless! Worth a visit for some gorgeous views and photo opportunities!

This was rated as one of the top 3 to visit in Jeju so we actually stayed at the nearby Airstay Hamdeok Hotel.  It  was very nice.  The beach is clean and had pristine waters and black rocks.  The sand was fine and felt good to walk on with your bare feet.  There were some really nice picturesque views so we took a ton of photos. There was a connected path to a hill and it allowed for some decent small hikes.  We went in March so the flowers on the hill were blooming with yellow and purple colors.  There were also some white flower blossoms coming out from the trees. With the ocean or the city views in the background from the hill, it allowed for some very unique photos for your memories.  After the little hike, we played around in the water on the beach and it was nice because it was low tide and you could hang out in one of the exposed sand bars. It was very pretty and relaxing. Definitely a must see if you're in Jeju!

This was our second trip to Udo.   We were riding around Jeju Island by bicycle so decided to explore the island on foot.   The weather was very hot and exposed (Summer), so you really need a big hat.    The island is quite unique, we walked up through the middle of the island and enjoyed the barren landscape.   We came across a Buddhist temple and met the lone monk there who chatted and gave us cups of coffee and tea.  He also introduced us to his friends - a haenyeo and visiting Butoh dancer who we interviewed for our website.   We briefly visited the beaches which were nice but crowded.  The unique landscape and interesting people was the best thing about Udo.

This was one tiring experience, since it was freezing cold back in December.I am not sure if hiking in boots is a good idea, but hey who said that you can't hike in slippery boots? This was honestly worth a thousand words.Watching the sun set into the the buildings was such a beautiful experience. When i stood right on top with the cold breeze slapping my face, admiring the view and the nature, i felt like time has stopped and that feeling was quite amazing. That feeling was everything. I fell in love with that place.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This place is caused by volcanic activity, specially beautiful on October full of Flame Grass. Entrance fee is quite expensive, but you can enjoy beautiful views ,can see volcanic cones in other place even Seongsan Ilchulbong when it's sunny.

This one is located near  Hyeopjae  Beach,  so you can see the Biyangdo island as well. i liked it. Its pretty spacious and got necessary facilities like combini nearby, toilet and place with free water. it also got nice view and some of typical jeju sculptures of  female divers and spirits that protect the Island. Sand is white and feels nice.

This is the largest waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea, and one of the only ones that is not fenced up at the bottom. Usually, when you visit waterfalls, it's always staring at it from a distance, where a viewing platform has been built. This is different, you get to walk ALL THE WAY to below that waterfall, and if you are open to wading through knee deep water, go touch that waterfall.The spray of water is refreshing, and the scenery rocks. You'll feel one with nature.

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

This is in my opinion the best waterfall in Seogwipo. I don't know if it's the biggest or the tallest, but it is truly unique, as water falls down into the ocean in the middle of a pebble beach. I visited it on a rainy and windy day, and because of it it might have left a stronger impression on me. I could really feel the forces of nature. Also, since the water falls onto the beach, you can take pictures really close to the waterfall. Overall, it is a must see waterfall if you come to Seogwipo, even though it doesn't get more than 20 minutes to get a nice view of the fall and its surroundings.

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This crater was a 40 mins drive from our hotel, its absolutely worth the trip. It offer one of the best view among the rest of the jeju major attraction.The climb up to the crater was relatively easy and relaxing which was suitable for all ages, entrance fees to the crater was 9000 won which was reasonable for the stunning view which the crater offered.

This beach is amazing. It is by far one of my favorites on Jeju. As soon as you arrive there is just a great atmosphere and a great vibe! The view is amazing. There are rocks to take pictures on, chairs set up for the perfect beach picture. The white sand and the blue sea water are beautiful. The water is clear and inviting! It also has great places to eat, a burger place, a taco place, and many cafes where you can get coffee, teas, ice creams, etc. It can get crowded, but should be expected for any beach in Jeju during beach season.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

There's parking place but there's a fee to pay around 2000 won for my rented Kia Sportage   , Entrance fee was 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for youth . We walked around the park nearby the stairs leading to view the cliff from here .

There were sooo many people  and the view was also not that great. I couldn't even take a proper picture. First i wasn't even sure if this is the right place, because it didn't look like the pictures i saw online.Go there if you want to have a walk at the cost (2000 won admission fee) and en passant you can look at the cliffs.Going there by bus is not really convenient. The bus station is a bit far and the bus comes about every hour (timetable not reliable).By the way this kind of view you can also have at the Phoenix island (near ilchulbong).

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

There are no words to describe the beauty of this beach. OMG a little piece of heaven. The water, the sand, the view was soooo beautiful and peaceful. Loved it!!!!I'm a girl who grow up  on a beautiful Mediterranean island and Hamdeok beach made me feel like home!!! Please take me back there!!!

There are a lot of negative reviews basically saying this waterfall is just average. It may not have that 'wow' factor but one should not visit if they are expecting the niagra falls. The one valid complaint are the stairs, slightly steep, and the rocks that need to be traversed to get closer to the falls. One has to be careful when hopping and stepping from rock to rock. Also, it can be a bit crowded with picture taking tourists.I found Jeongbang to be a modest waterfall, but nonetheless very charming. Great pictures can be taken on approach and up close, right next to the pool where you can feel the freshwater spray. Turn your back to the waterfall and a nice ocean view greets you, with two small mountain isles off in the distance. For the more adventurous, there are rocks of all sorts to be found closer to the sea. Most visitors snap a few pics and leave, but hanging out by the sea for a spell was also quite enjoyable.  While the rocks won't be confused with the rainbow, it was fun to pick out unique looking rocks from the saltwater, but watch out for the waves!

There are 3 memorial towers, one of Kim Man Duk, civil uprising volunteers, and one of patriot at the end of Joseon dynasty. There is Kim Man Duk's grave stone, original one which moved here because of road construction in its original place. This is located in Sara-bong(hill) park. It is very low hi,, but you can enjoy beautiful sunrise on the top of hill. Even day time, I could enjoy nice view toward Jeju international port. I recommend walk around the hill first then visit Mochungsa afterwards, The Sarabong walk path is part of Olle #18. There are many locals who work out here. You can feel like a local!

The waterfall is in walking distance from the center of Seogwipo, even if there are a fee steps to get to the waterfall it's worth the visit!The view is fantastic, and the vapour coming from the waterfall is refreshing (especially in summer).Beware just of the last few meters because are on rocks, and sometimes slippery.

The walk up sunrise mountain was  windy and relatively easy. Steps all the way up with many spots for you to rest and take in the beautiful view. Don't miss out on this mountain if you are going to Jeju. Entrance fee is 2000W. They charge for everything here, waterfalls and parks all have an entrance fee.

The sea in Jeju Island was very clean and a good place to enjoy the natural scenery. There were many kinds of cafes and long coastal roads. Also, the cafes had unique personalities and were good places to take pictures and the taste of coffee was good. I went there for 2 nights and 3 days, and I could see the beautiful sea when the sun was bright, and there was a dark atmosphere of the sea when the weather was cloudy. However, unlike in the past, the whole atmosphere of the sea seemed to disappear as many buildings were built. There was a wish for a return to the old sea. Nevertheless, if I visited Jeju Island again, I wanted to go to Woljeongri Beach again. Viewers of this review also recommend going to Woljeongri beach where I went.

The route to go down to the beach is very challenging! If you bringing kids, extra cautious is a MUST! Quite dangerous as the routes is very steep, but once you arrived the view is AMAZING! For a few seconds, there is NO WORD can describe the feeling! I can't believe I go down that steep routes! A place to heal & purify your mind as well SOUL! They charge you with a very small amount of 2000 won for adult, 1500 won for kids and FREE for senior.
The rock with dragon head shape. Is a quite short time view and to feel the sea breeze. We took the staircase down to see the rock with dragon head shape. Other than that, nothing special here.

The previous review states that the climb was in 20 minutes but for a relatively unfit person like myself, it took me 30 to 40 minutes with numerous stops beginning from halfway till the top. Much to your agitation, we see older citizens and children alike happily and easily climbing the steps and overtook you to the top. Nevertheless, the view on the top was well worth the tough climb (according to my unfit status). Managed to take some photo shots of the surrounding and the crater itself. As it was just beginning spring, the crater floor was covered with brownish grass and vegetation, not the greenish color you would expect in summer. What I most remembered was the real cold buffeting wind of 2 Degrees Celsius blowing and you could really feel it even with winter jackets and caps worn while climbing the steps. But it was most memorable. Wife did not want to climb the steps but decided to go shopping for the famous Jeju orange chocolates in the shops at the foot of the park.

The place is super nice spot to chill with coffee/tea or snack while overlooking fields of green tea. Their food is ok but the presentation is super. We see many family's and couples came here to take pictures of the great green fields or kids would just run around enjoying themselves.The place is quite open so is not very noisy and everyone do still get some space to just relax.Also, if you look at the chair setting, you can tell that they purposely made it so you can enjoy the view while you are here!!

The period I went was very windy, the surrounding was very refreshing with patches of green. Very relaxing, peaceful  and is a good place for photography. A typical k-drama filming location for kfans to visit! Once you reach the highest point, you will see endless of   green    and can even spot mountains that is far away. You can actually relax and enjoy this view by sitting at this cute wooden swing. Very nice place which you probably won't want to miss it.However, to visit this place, you need an entrance fee of  6,000won, But if you booked a experience tour driver with your own group of friends, he can help you bargain it to a even cheaper price which is like 3,000won per person! So, afterall, it was pretty worth it for both the price and this exquisite experience! Recommended to rent a car there, inaccessible by public transport!

The park covers a vast area. One has to decide how far you wish to explore and watch your time. A map is given at the ticket counter and we did not expect it to be so big. We went according to the numbered stops. The view was spectacular for some parts of the park that we spent so much time on taking pictures. We tried to move quicker however, in the end, we did not even complete Course 1 (there are 3 different routes). It was enjoyable for some walk & laughter. There are scripts on stones to tell you about the legendary story of this stone park. You may decide, whether you want to keep walking and cover the whole park (I am not sure whether this is even possible in a day) or would you just want to have a feel of this peaceful and beautiful park.

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.? There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).? In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.? If art is your thing, then definitely go.? Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

The cliff is located on the southern side of Jeju Island in the township of Seogwipo. A well-laid stair-way/boardwalk has been constructed for visitors to view and appreciate the natural rock formations of hexagonal lave tubes. These make great photo shots when framed with overhanging pine trees, crashing waves, clear blue skies and setting sun. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry and hordes of tourists, especially students on excursion. What an incredible place to spend an hour or two!
The beach itself is quite small, however, viewing it from the windows of one coffee shops along the beach is a very nice feeling
The attraction is not very large. There is a charge of 2000 won per person, which I feel is expensive as compared to other natural wonders in Jeju. Still the views are nice and unique.

Sunrise is at 615 am . The entrance fee is free if you arrive before 7 am . Free Car park to the viewing points a short  8-10 minutes walk away , very doable and you get one of the most memorable sunrise sights . A most do except the getting there so early in the morning is hard .

Spirited Garden is the #1 place to visit in Jeju in my opinion. I strongly recommend paying a visit.  the garden was actually bigger than I thought, and it took about an hour to see all the places. It definitely made me relaxed and laid back! Everything was well preserved and clean. There is also a cafe with a great view of the garden. You can buy different souvenirs related to Jeju and the garden on the floor below the cafe. Feeding the fish is 1000W and you can buy it freely (you just have to put the money in the box) and it's pretty amusing.

Spectacular views from the bottom, the side, the peak and everywhere else. I couldn't put down my camera. After two rainy, cloudy days at Jeju, the morning of our visit to Sunrise Peak we were blessed with blue skies.The ticket booth (2000 won for adults, 1000 for youth) listed the roundtrip time as 50 minutes, but we spent 2+ hours climbing and descending the tuff cone, followed by checking out the 1:30 p.m. Haenyo woman diver performance. (There is a second performance at 3:00 p.m.)The tuff cone at the peak is something else, and the climb itself is not that bad, especially if you take it slow. The descent is arguably just as good, with cooling breezes and more picture opportunities. One Con: It can get fairly crowded. Dozens of tour buses are parked at the base, carrying mainly Chinese tourists. It get can a bit competitive at times waiting out the best picture spots, but luckily they like taking pictures by signs. Overall it's not that bad, though it was funny watching the korean couples' responses to the crowds, with the girl posing for the picture and giving the side eye while the guy patiently crouched several feet away.But hey, it's a UNESCO heritage site and definitely worth a trip!

Solo traveling in Jeju Island is not that scary:) Koreans living nearby this tourist spot can speak English. So I am not worried about it.It was raining that day when I reach the place. Nevertheless, still can see the view at the top.The wind blowing my hair together with the greenery grasses and leaves of trees surrounding the peak.The place is accessible by public buses so I don't have difficulty in reaching this site. Though you have to walk a few distance to reach the entrance gate.There are educational boards installed for all the tourists to read and understand the history of it.It's worth visiting this place. Entrance fee is also cheap:)I visited Unesco World Heritage!

So we saw great reviews and some great pictures online. Thought this was a must see place. To be fair, the island has some real potential to be fantastic, however it was a hot August day, it was getting very crowded.Highlights:- some really nice sights to take in and you can tour the whole island in about 4hrs (including stops along the way)- one let we went for a walk and ran into some people camping. Very pleasant and offered us coffee. We hadn?t encountered too many people willing to go out of their way, so was a nice touch. - took a high speed boat ride around the cliff that looks like the cow laying down (hence the name cow island). That was great and worth the 30k KRW for two adults.Low points:- way too much garbage around. Just about every beautiful sight is ruined by plastic bottles and litter. - a lot of areas were closed like it was low season (or maybe we were just early in the day)- lots people standing around endlessly. Got a little frustrating at times. Advice if you do go:- we took the bus. It was good, but we were on a bus schedule. If I did it again, I would have rented a small electric vehicle (which needs an international driving license to rent). Not sure if the cost, but they looked fun and you control your own timeline then.

Since their official website is unclear about opening hours in June, I called the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline and was informed that the museum was indeed open late under summer hours. But ultimately, we were turned away. The only positive I could take from this experience is that, from what we could see from the lobby, the gallery looked small and over-rated. Seongsan Ilchulbong or sunrise peak is one of the most visited spots in Jeju. We took a public bus here from port after visiting Udo Island. Lucky it is near the port as it was already late afternoon when we reached here.  The parking lot was crowded with tour coaches and and you could see the crowd climbing up and down the peak.  There was a well laid path which was fairly wide with steps leading up and separate steps leading down.  Certain parts had narrower steps and you have to slow down. Although the peak was not very high, you still need to stop now and then to catch your breath as the steps were quite steep. As usual, wear good walking shoes and stay hydrated. The views from the top were awesome and if you come before dawn, you can catch a beautiful sunrise here.  After climbing to the Udo lighthouse earlier, it was tiring to climb this peak as well but we managed.  There are platforms and steps to sit on at the top to rest and relax. By the time we got a public bus back to Jeju city, it was already getting dark.  You need to pay a small fee to climb up.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the places to be visited in Jeju island, it has three kinds of beautiful views: the sea, the mountains and the meadow.No need to climb or hike the mountains to enjoy the view, just stay at the flat ground and see the surroundings and feel the wind ... it also a pleasant experience.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of the best view I have ever seen in my entire life. The place is an epitome of beauty and calmness despite being flocked by tourists. It is very worthy of your time, effort and energy. Trek it to experience and see its beauty. There are plenty of activities being offered on site such as horse back riding, see a Jeju woman diver and even a tour around the area through boat. We were very interested with the boat ride unfortunately we did not have the luxury of time. if given the chance to go back to Jeju I will surely comeback here and try the boat ride as well as other activities offered. Moreover, the site has plenty of coffee shops and cafes around the area. There are also stalls selling Korean street food. It has huge parking area so get ready to walk from the parking area to the site. This site entails a lot of walking but because of its beauty and being windy you can never feel fatigue.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is certainly the top scenic spot in Jeju island. It?s basically a crater formed from volcanic eruptions, so it?s definitely has geological phenomena associated on top of being scenic. We drove from Jeju city to Seongsan for about an hour. There?s ample parking spots and entry fee is only 2000 KRW. Hiking involves climbing lot of stairs and takes about an hour to the top. We had a 2 year old with us and we could easily pick her and go to the top. I recommend carrying water and small snack items for energy. View from the top is very beautiful and obviously you see the crater when you reach the top. I think it?s top 3 spots to visit in Jeju Island and definitely a must if the weather is nice. Bonus if you during sunrise or sunset!! There are coffee shops (starbucks, McDonald, Paris Baguette etc.) and some local souvenir shop at the entrance. Enjoy

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seongsan Ilchulbing / Sunrise Peak ε뷴낡 , is a wonderful place for sunrise & sunset !? Yes it is. But I came here during 3pm ~ manage to walk up to the peak within 40mins ~ Although I do not have time to stay until sunset but I feel satisfy with the view of Jeju ; cooling weather and beauty of Spring.

Sangumburi Crater is our 1st stop after we got a rental car.It's 40 mins drive from Jeju city.Entrance fee cost KRW6,000. There are several small souvenir & coffee shops.It quite unfortunate for us because that day is raining. We're freezing because of the cold weather.We didn't prepare any umbrella or raincoat. So from the parking to the entrance, we soak under the rain.Thankfully the souvenir shop inside sell raincoat with the cost of KRW4,000.From the entrance, you have to hike up to the crater.The path up to the crater was breathtakingly beautiful.What makes this place looks so gorgeous is because of the vast flame grass field along the way to the crater.Sadly, when we arrive at the top, we couldn't see the crater at all.It was cloudy all over.  However we still enjoy the view.The walk down is as beautiful as it was on the way up.

Sagumburi Crater was one of the highlights of my trip in Jeju Island. The view and scenery was breathtaking. The hike to the top was easy and you get to take pictures along the way. It is really relaxing when you get to the top, you get to feel the wind and appreciate nature.

Quite long caves, but we do enjoy walking through it until the end of the caves. It was cold inside, feels like we are walking inside a room with air-conditioner. Lols. My friend do enjoy reading all those facts and information on the formations, and I find it quites helpful for those who are interested in geology thing. Maybe.It is quite large caves too. For those who are on tight budgets like us, you can take a bus and walk 2km to the caves. Not tiring at all as the view is very nice.

Probably even better at sunrise, but we have been there about 11AM.Great view from the top. Center of the voulcano is nothig special at the time.Take a hat or umbrella and other protection from sun, even at not too sunny day.* Operating Hours:April-October 07:00-20:00November-March 07:30-19:00* Fees for foreigners: Adults 5,000 won / Teenagers & Children 2,500 won

positives: truly beautiful and amazing views of nature scenery and the waterfalls. also, one can take a leisurely stroll in the attached garden park. entry fee was only 2000 won.negatives: there was a bit of a crowd the day we visited, although it was still manageable. the entrance to the falls could be tricky to find if you planning to go there on foot from Seogipwo town. DO NOT follow google maps as it will only point you to the exact geographical location of the falls. You should walk down along taepyeong road until you see the bridge and the sea. cross the bridge and you will see a big carpark. the ticket office will be on the right side, near 7-11

Plenty of visitors,an extinct volcanic crater on the eastern tip of Jeju about 182 feet splendid view from the peak,on the lower part is the famous sea woman house present oldest sea woman at the age of 90 plus year old and younger sea woman at the age of 50 years old continue to dive in the sea for living. The House of sea woman sell fresh oysters and abalones.

Other than Hallasan...the massive shield volcano that created Jeju Island and now sits at its center, Sunrise Peak is perhaps the greatest of the nearly 400 craters, cinder cones or shield volcanoes (  oreums   in Korean) found around the island.  It's a bit of a hike to get to the top, seemingly straight up at times.  But the incredible views from every angle will reward your diligence.  depending on the season, you can see fields of yellow canola (or   rape  ) flowers; also Udo (Cow Island to the east, Hallasan to the north/northwest and the incredible Pacific all around...vast and hypnotic on a clear day.  Nearby, you can check out the Aqua Planet Aquarium and the Women Divers Museum. Be sure to drive along the coast road and enjoy a coffee and dessert at one of the many unique cafes.  Although there are now several franchise coffeeshops near Sunrise Peak, the independents offer a more relaxing atmosphere.

One of the top places to see in Jeju.  Great view of some craggy coastline.  The other reviews are pretty good and we experienced about the same - great place, but really crowded even though it was raining!  Again...people come in waves, just wait it out. There is a 1,000 W Parking fee on top of the 2,000 entrance fee.

Okay so we went to the address given by Tripadvisor, and to our astonishment it was just a small garden behind a hotel. The only reason I can think why it was set to that address - is perhaps there's free parking? Dont give up if you're there! Because the actual site is only about 800m further down. The actual cliff site is open to public and free for viewing..Path is quite family-friendly.

Not a difficult climb, but if you haven't worked out in awhile, your legs will definitely feel like jelly on the way down. It took about 20 minutes to hike up the stairs to the top and another 20 minutes to get down. The volcanic cone and the view are totally worth visiting the top for.
Nice View and good for health,Guys try going this place and you will feel the Fresh of Air at top of mountain.

My view is totally different from the rest of reviews on trip advisor.I actually wonder if I had went to the right place. I was expecting a entrance fee, but we were free to walk around the hotel gardens for 10-15mins till we reach the edge where u get a clear view of the coastal line and jungmum cliffs are.This jungmum cliff is supposingly behind a hotel garden, so if ur GPS brings u to an hotel like my 2 GPS (provided by car rental company), apple map and google map did then I got the right place.I saw some cliffs, strong sea waves smashing against it....... This is it????? .Was quite a waste of time especially after I drove round and round for almost 2 hrs looking for it, didn't knew it was behind a hotel garden.

My 'poetic' side has always loved gardens. Used to dream and draw secret gardens all the time. My heart and gut was somehow curious about this place, especially after reading reviews from travellers all over the world. Was made to understand that not many young people from our country like myself come to visit which intrigued the caretaker enough to see someone such as myself wandering around the garden and I was therefore approached with such warmth.
