Like a poetic art carefully, passionately, calmly and beautifully crafted, Spirited Garden indeed does justice to its name. Even in winter where the trees and plants don't bloom as much, I could still feel the garden's spirit that it's almost like nature is speaking to you which gives you a sense of serenity. For a moment, Felt like I was in Edward Scissorhands's world ㅿ Learned so much about the bonsai tree, as well as the philosophical and wisdom in gardening. Thank you Spirited Garden for the beautiful inspiration.

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My husband and I had an absolutely fabulous day pheasant hunting at the Daeyoo Hunting Preserve on Jeju Island in South Korea and then an excellent meal of (our) pheasant sashimi roast pheasant etc. washed down with wine at their excellent pheasant restaurant! Daeyooland also has lovely gardens a charming helpful staff and great coffee!We hunted with a guide and his trusty dog walking for miles thru the beautiful countryside... and my husband did get us a pheasant! We also got to shoot skeet (and they have ATVing as well). My husband had hunted on Jeju many years ago when he was in the US Army and stationed in Korea and I wanted to take him   home   and go hunting with him- and tourists can hunt at Daeyooland! As their website is only in Korean our concierge at the JW Marriott in Seoul (an EXCELLENT hotel which I've also reviewed) was kind enough to help make the arrangements for us. We flew to Jeju Island for the day went hunting and then walked around downtown Jeju going to museums and some of the historic markets (there are 22!) buying and eating those famous Jeju oranges! Then we flew back to Seoul in the evening having had  a GREAT day!

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My family walked from our hotel to the top of Ilchulbong and down. From the entrance, the mountain(?) looked formidable and it looked to be a painful hike, but it turned out to be rather a short hike. I wish I had taken more time on the way up and enjoyed the views more. On the way down, we saw a restaurant by the rocky shore.  I believe this is where mermaids do their demonstrations and sell raw oyster dishes.  I wanted to go down but my 10 & 12 yr olds won't have it.  So I missed out.         The guy who took the tickets at the entrance surprising had a good nack for taking pictures.  If he is not too busy, ask him to take your group photo.         After the hike, we went to a bakery just by the entrance.  From the second floor, we had a nice view of the Ilchulbong and enjoyed cup of coffee with various breads.  The owner was very kind and let us wait out the rain in the store.

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Might not be very tall at 1950m but it's no walk in the park. The best part though is that the path is clear and generally easy to walk especially when there are planks. Otherwise walking on volcanic rock and boulders are not so comfortable for the feet. Great views at the top and as we went in spring, flowers are in bloom.
Loved this island, I recommend exploring it by foot.  We interviews the monk the temple for our film   Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure   and he was super kind and served us coffee and drink.

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Located next to   Loveland   this museum is small modern place with beautiful outdoor features such as a reflecting pool sculptures and a small surrounding forest. There was a little bit of everything from an exhibit about a famous national artist who lived for decades on Jeju to an interesting video and poetry collaboration of Korean rappers talking about social issues. The upstairs is currently showcasing drawings and sculptures made by Korean schoolchildren in a surprisingly cheeky cheerful exhibit. Much of the museum was in English but others were only in Korean. The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Lesser popular than others on Jeju like Ilchubong or Hallasan, but a pretty hike with a lovely view from the top. No sure what I expected for the silver grasses so was very impressed to see the effects of the sun on it as we took the short hike. I went late in the day so there were not as many people around which was nice. You pay a small fee to enter and the entire hike is relatively quite. The crater is nothing spectacular, however if you enjoy nature, the silver grasses are worth seeing.

Less than 15 min walking, the waterfall was beautiful, and there?s food photo spot where everyone line up when u get to the waterfall. In my opinion, the admission fee was little too much for the quick walk and waterfall view. But good to visit once!

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Kids may enjoy posing with Cinderella's carriage & shoe collection and running around the grounds.  As I was not however, although a few glass sculptures were interesting, I did not think it was worth the time or effort (& of course the entrance fee) to go.  Agree with the comments of previous reviewers who rated   poor  .  The  fish lunch I had at the restaurant next door however, was enjoyable. On the plus side, the place is wheelchair accessible.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).
Just a normal bridge like many others,it's kind of relaxing with a seaview..as it has no entrance fee, it's no harm to come to this place since it is near to where I was staying.

Jeju island is a really beautiful place and there is so many amazing sites but i was a bit underwhelmed by this view compared to others i saw. I'd say it was worth seeing if you are in the area but essentially its just a rock, and there are lots more, much prettier rocks, around the island!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

I've visited Seongsan Ilchulbong 11 years ago and this is my 2nd visit. Why? Because this place is so beautiful. The climb is really worth it. I took about 30 minutes to reach the peak. View of the peak and below are lovely. As the path to the peak involve stairs, be careful as it can get pushy (there are just so many tourist there). Entrance fee is 2,000 won per adult. Parking area is large but you will find yourself searching for an empty lot if you come late.

Its worth it to climb up there. such a beautiful and breath taking view from the top. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. entrance fee is just 2000krw per person. we actually drove there from our pension. many parking space. other than climbing the peak, you can also catch a Haenyo Diver Women performance at the bottom of mountain right beside it. its amazing to watch those elderly women  holding their breath for several minutes without any oxygen mask! overall its awesome! for those muslims, there's fast food restaurant Lotteria for you to grab your lunch or dinner since they have shrimp burger available. its located on your left when exit the car park area.

Its really easy to reach this attraction. Parking is free however you are required to pay a minimal fee in order to view this waterfall. Walking on the stairs is easy but if you do wish to get close to the waterfall , a good pair of shoes with good grip is required as you have to walk on the slippery stone/rock. There are some women selling fresh seafood by the waterfall.

It will take about 30 to 40 minutes to hike up the mountain which involves lots of stairs. View is superb, especially during sunrise because you will be facing east. There are quite a number of shops and restaurants down there, perfect for breakfast after morning hike. Spacious carparks. p/s: I read somewhere that there will be entrance fees (KRW2000-3000). However when we went there, the ticket booth was closed, perhaps because we went there at dawn.

It was really pretty and there are horses which you can ride at the bottom. Climbing up includes of climbing up many flights of steep stairs which might be difficult for the elderly or the unfit(like me). It takes about 50 mins to go up and down. The view on top was nice but when i was there, there were some construction works on going and they chased us away if we were to stand at the peak to take pictures. Imagine climbing up all the way to the top just to get chased away. Not a gd feeling.At the bottom near to the sea, there is also the performance of the women divers at 1.30pm and 3.30pm. It was interesting to watch even though we were flooded by many china tourist. Be careful when walking on the rocks as it can be very slippery. There was also a small pile of shells that you can choose from and to bring home. You can also buy the seafood caught by the women divers and enjoy them at the cafe just beside.

It was nice to enjoy 15-20 minutes here. Expect to compete for photo taking opportunities. 2000 won/ticket, walk down a few flights of wooden stairs, and climb over some big slippery rocks to get the best vantage point for viewing. Can feel the spray from across the pool. Accessible by bus 281 from Jeju city.

It was easy to tell the tourists from the locals - level of preparedness. Before I went on the hike, it amused me to see the locals fully dressed and equipped with hiking gear. As I understood it, the hike was child and elderly friendly, so I was not expecting much difficulty scaling this mountain. Halfway up, I was already regretting my choice of footwear. I had on a lightweight fleece jacket which helped to battle the cold winds at the top, so it did not feel too bad even though I was in shorts. In actual fact, it was not that difficult to climb (took me 4 hours to get to the summit) but the terrain was rough with rocks and stones making up most of the path. I guess it is my own fault that I have absolutely no instinct on where to put my foot next. Slipping often, I finally tore open my trainers on my way down after constantly stubbing my toes in the ground. My toes hurt so bad I had to stop several times (after peeling my socks off, I found two of my toes severely bruised and blackened) so the hike down took all of 4 hours. At the top, I regretted not having any headgear. The winds were so crazy it was close to impossible to take a photo without my hair whipping all over my face. Ah, even a bandana would have been enough. Overall, I would do it again, this time better equipped. Though the view was beautiful, what I remember best was climbers picnicking at the top, huddled together in groups in the bellowing winds, in their bright hiking outfits, just enjoying the time out. Next time, I will remember to bring kimbap and hot coffee!

It was amazing!This is the worth place to go. The entrance fee is very cheap just 2000 won and the transportation arround 3300 won.Then Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak will gives unique view that you will never see in another place. It is very easy to go here, just take a bus from Jeju intercity Terminal or Seogwipo Intercity terminal then stop on Seongsan Ilchulbong  Entrance, Just walk for 10 minute from the bus stop to the ticket booth.

It was a very windy and rainy day... we could not climb to the summit but the experience was trilling! Recommended for trekking amateurs and pros! There are many coffee shops around the routes but bring your own food, comfortable clothing and decent equipment. It's totally equipped with stairs and view points but safety is always first!

It takes quite awhile trekking down the stairs to catch the view of the waterfall which flows to the ocean. There are some   halmoni   selling fresh raw abalones, sea cucumbers, sea potatoes and blanched octopus at the side of the waterfall. It's a great experience to enjoy the seafood with a bottle of soju while enjoying the view of the waterfall and ocean while feeling the sea breeze dancing around your face^^~

It takes 1.5 hours from Jeju Intercity bus station to Seongsan IIchulbong, by bus 701. After 30 mins drive, you can see the blue sky and green sea outside of the windows. The admin fee is 200 0 KR but the great view is worth of it. You can see large grass ground and hike to the top. If there is sunshine, no doubt you can have wonderful pictures and experience even with a phone camera.

It is very interesting - the museum is right next to the house where he used to live. And there is a painting that paints the view from the museum looking down the port. it is called   The view of the port   I believe the city of Seogwipo has bought this painting a few years ago and placed it in this museum - this is my favorite. The painter is a genius and of course ahead of his own time. I am proud and also feel bad for his personal life, just like any other genius who had a not so happy personal life and was too far ahead of everyone else. Enjoy great paintings. I am glad the city of Seogwipo is making efforts to keep his painting in the meaningful spot, not random museums elsewhere in the world.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is most satisfactory to complete our climb to the top to experience the cold air, sea breeze and overlooking at the mountains and sea below you.  The feeling is so good and the view is just simply awesome!  It's a great place not to be missed!

It is an attraction for people to take photos of the special ?Dragon? like stone with the endless sea. That stone is 100% organic and experience years of erosions to form today?s ?Dragon? appearance. You can spend a couple of minutes with that ?Dragon? and spend another few minutes buying and enjoying the traditional outdoor cuisines. If you are interested in buying souvenirs like key chains or the ?Dragon? like badges, there is a shop for you to go shopping. Even though the viewpoint just for people to take a photo, there would always be many tourists standing in front of the best position for taking photos, so if there are many tour groups at the moment, you really have to spend time on waiting for just a photo. So, if you don?t mind the feel of crowded or if you get plenty of time, you are recommended as it is a special attraction in Jeju. It is nearby the international airport of Jeju so you can go there at the time you arrived or before you leave Jeju.

It is a nice walk up to the top, windy.From the top we do have a nice view, wide view with many hills. Nothing special about the plants or vegetation. The entrance fee of KRW6,000 is a bit high when this is all you see.
Is a relaxation place. We visited in early Feb, still it cover with snow. Beautiful snow view. Take a some relaxing slow walk to enjoy the cooling feel of the nature.

In my journey, I went to the Hallasan National Park at Jeju. Here is a good place to walk with family, since here has a wide stretch of land at the foot of hill, you can just walk around the hill. Children can play in a nature place with good air. All the building and transport are so far away, you must feel relax and do not want to leave.If you are younger and want to see more view, I really suggest that you must walk to the peak by stairs, but you must have enough energy, because it is really tired. Take water and some food are necessary. After that, you can see a good view at the peak, just like stand on the cloud.Finally, I suggest that you will climb at evening because of the sunset is very beautiful. Also the weather is better to climb the hill.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

If you're into nature, love moderate hiking and stairs climbing, love to see sea and city thru the bird eye view, taking plenty of photos of nature formations and also selfies (or wefies), then wjy don't you go to Seongsan Ilchubong, Jeju Island, South Korea. Designated as Unesco World Heritage site, this mountain is one the best place that you can hike and feels the wind blows your hair or maybe yourself too. The combination of flat lands and also the hike to the peak gives you an unforgetable memories. With each steps you take to climb to the peak, you will encounter several break spots or photo viewing for you to stops and take photos. Half way thru to the peak, you can see the entire city below you and starting to see the seas too. Hike to the peak, you can the see majestic view of the Seongsan Ilchubong itself. To your front is wide sea and the flat land (heard that it's actually a death volcano, correct me if i'm wrong) and to your behind is the view of the city and their surrounding. Don't forget to take photo at the peak's signboard. The formation of the clouds and the sun may give you the awe moments to you, especially when it reflects to the sea surfaces. When you go down from the peak, try to look at your right. You may see people going down to feels the sea water. Mind you, sometimes the wind blows a bit strong.  You need to pay for entrance and you don't like to hike to the peak, the ground is enough for you. Me and my friend, went there on Nov'15. Do try to enjoy nature at their best.

If you go there just to see the Lonely Rock, you may feel somewhat underwhelmed. However, there is a nice walk along the coast. When I was there, it was sunny and breezy. I really enjoyed the walk, the beautiful coastal view, the clear water and the fresh air. I wasn't disappointed at all.

I would say that this waterfall is higher and have better view than cheonjaeyeon waterfall althought cheonjaeyeon waterfall is close by from teddy bear museum, we take taxi in the afternoon from teddy bear museum to jeongbang waterfall and it cost around 25-30 usd, and the street is almost empty. The road down to the waterfall is much nearer and easier than cheonjaeyeon waterfall. When you take pictures, off course you would like to get closer to the waterfall, but be carefull of the rocks, they were quite slippery, we spend an hour to take pictures and sitting in the rock. The admission fee on nov 2014 is still 2,000 won per adult about $2. On winter it opens from 08.00 to 18.00

I would echo an earlier review that said that you should not bother with this if you have done any caving or similar - this is aimed at casual visitors not experts. It is a gentle wander in a cool cave that is appropriately lit, reasonably level and there is enough English signage to explain what you need to know. It is the fact that this was a lava tunnel that is not interesting and the signs do explain how the lava flowed, melted and cut down and through from other tunnels. 1) Wear sensible shoes.2) If it has been raining it can drip a lot inside though on our visit I did not think so.3) Some might feel it is cold - I did not

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

I went there early morning on a sunny day - perfect for photo-taking. The wonderful view of the sea from the walk down was just a prelude to the beauty that was to come later. I was delighted to see that little rainbow at the bottom! If you're more gutsy (and have a good sense of balance), you can make your way nearer to the waterfall to feel the cool mist and enjoy the grandeur and the surrounding scenery. Not a sight to be missed!!

I was told the hike up will only take 30 minutes but when I looked at it I was convinced it would take longer. The hike up is quite steep, lots of stairs, however it really just took a bit more than 30 min, to my own surprise. The hike is not easy however, it requires some stamina, many people take a break or two on the way up. Definitely bring something to drink. Seongsan is quite crowded with tourists, so lots of people all over. The hike is worth it, amazing views from the top. And the hike down is much more enjoyable then the one up. At the foot of Seogsan is a large parking lot, easy to leave your rental there, plus again lots of cafes, restaurants etc. You have to pay a fee to enter.Overall worth seeing Seongsan!

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I think I was deceived by the   Museum   term. If you expect an actual museum you'll be disappointed as the museum itself is really just one room. So I did feel like it was a bit of a scam... It's more of a premium flagship O'Sulloc store which sells tons of tea products and memorabilia. If you're into buying you'll have a good time but don't go there if you want to learn about tea or the history of tea. One redeeming quality of the place is that the building is nice and it has good views from the top.

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I LOVE... this museum!!! I am a teddy bear fan so this museum feels like heaven to me aside from being a K-drama fan. Before visiting Jeju, I researched on the top sites recommended to be visited, i got fascinated with the reviews about Teddy Bear museum plus knowing that some of its Teddy Bears where featured in one my favorite Korean Drama of all time PRINCESS HOURS. The teddy bears are just so cute, you can see them perform different functions and dressed of different profession and famous personalities such as Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Madonna etc. Afetr visiting the exhibit halls, we then went to the lower ground floor area where tall Teddy Bears are on display alongside Teddy Bears items that are for sale.A must visit for Teddy Bear Lovers.

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I cannot remember the number of steps(some steep and chip steps) I climb up to the top. Very tiring climb  and almost give up along the way. Among the climb, there are pretty views and I feel satisfied reaching the top.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.
great experience, tiring when climbing up, but glad to see the sunrise and feeling the cool sea breeze. magnificent view, must visit

From the bottom Seongsan Ilchulbong looks daunting, but once you get walking its relatively easy, with many well placed rest spots along the way. The views at each spot are pretty great - you can really appreciate the black sand beaches from there. Take some water with you!The top of the volcano is amazing - covered in a sea of green grass, it looks like it could easily be a set in a Jurassic Park movie. There is something so primal about the feeling up there. And despite the many other hikers you will find up there, its pretty easy to find a spot to sit and appreciate it for a bit!The entrance is 2000 won. Take some water, a camera and some coins for the scopes. Also, it gets really, really gusty up at the top and along the walkway to Ilchulbong beach, so try and avoid any flyway items of clothing.

Formed from the eruption of a hydrovolcano, this is the most popular sight on the east coast of Jeju. Ample parking space, a reasonable admission fee and a spectacular view from the top. If you plan on going early for the sunrise, I would advise catching it from a beach just south of the outcrop rather than from the crater itself.

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

Excellent view especially at sunrise. Hiking was good for a beginner level. Many places to stop and take a rest if needed. If not an experienced hiker, it takes maybe 40 minutes to get up to the top. No entrance fee if you go super early. Lots of lovely places around to grab coffee or some food after you hike down as well. I would do this again in a heartbeat!

Excellent view and atmosphere! A long steep (with stairs) and challenging climb up the inactive volcanic island mountain that earns you good exercise and satisfaction! You can already enjoy the picturesque surroundings at the foot of the mountain with different views and you can buy some souvenir there and also enjoy a short horse ride (not free of course). If you are there on a sunny day, do buy some popsicle or ice-cream to go up.   There are entrance fees for the entrance as well. However, it is well worth it once you reached the top. It is fantastic to be on top looking down to the inactive volcano crater and enjoy the view of the sea that looks like touching the sky. You can literally feel like you are touching the sky too! The best time to go there will be during sunrise! Don't forget to take a selfie with the mountain height indicator board to boast your achievements! Oh, and just right before you reach the top, please take a look at the back downhill at the interesting look of the city below and take a selfie and also take some nice selfie around you.     On the way down, there is the fishing village where the you can enjoy the seafood while watching the women divers catch clamps and oyster. There are some fiexed timing but I have already forgotten the timing.    Seongsan Ilchulbong is indeed a must visit destination everytime you arrive in Jeju!
Entrance fee costed me 4 000 krw. Reachable by bus. The view inside of the cave is very intriguing and fascinating. For me, it is worth it to visit.

Easy to travel to from either bus terminal (Jeju or Seogwipo). The hike is not daunting at all as it is primarily a flight of stairs and some inclined stones at the beginning. Entry fee is $2. No food is allowed inside so forget about having picnics. Provides a great view and the tuft is something special and best viewed in person , so do the short hike. Gets rather crowded but there are a number of places to eat at. I enjoyed it!

Do it with your partner, not with your mates, not with your friends and not with a group. This is a tiny island and the ideal thing to do is to rent a bicycle and just glide around the island for a few hours. It is mostly just farms and a couple nice views, but it does make you feel like that scene in wedding crashers if you do it right. Half day is all you need, the ferries are fairly punctual but check to make sure as you would not want to get stranded. Not the number 2 thing to do in Jeju by any means, but it is pleasant.

Disclaimer: this review is written by my better half since I?m obviously not part of the Hello Kitty! target audience.Omg! Everything is in pink! Look at the displays! They are sooooo cuteeeeee! I want to take photos with everything! I?m an adult in Kittyland! Omg, the cafe is so nice! I don?t wanna leaveeeeeeeeee......Back to the lesser half: if you are a guy, just pay the entrance fee and make the Girlfriend/Wife/kids happy. They will love you even more when you cough up for the overpriced merchandise. Seriously, I?ve never seen the Wife happier, not even on our wedding day.

Definitely worth visiting. Although with 50 mins of climb, you will feel all well worth it after reach the peak. The view was just simply amazing. The best spot for photo taking beautiful natural, landscape and with friends. When I was there, was so crowed with people. This place is so popular. A must go. UNESCO sight.

Came early at 5.15 am. Reached the peak at about 5.35 am but there was no sunrise. Maybe because it was a bit cloudy due to the rain? The view however was still spectacular. I am a solo traveller and was worried about being the only person there early in the morning but nope, a lot of people including locals were there. The path was not too dark and it was a fair hike up. A few areas to stop by if you ever needed some rest. If you come in the morning for the hike, you do not have to pay any entrance fees which is actually necessary during the day (2000W).Oh the woman divers show. It was really a ?show? and then, they were off to the sea. I didn?t wait until they were back though. You need to pay the general entrance fee to Seongsan Ilchulbong of 2000W to gain access to the area of the woman diver.So basically I came here twice - once for the morning hike and the other one for the woman?s diver show.

By the time we reached Seongsan mountain, it's already 3.30 pm! On reaching there, and by the look at the mountain, it seems as if there's nothing to enjoy but after my daughter stated that it's world wide attraction, I reluctantly followed them up the 274 meter high mountain with unbelievable thought!But after going uphill, I have another thought!On looking down as I rested after some stairs, the beautiful scenery blaff me! Then as we climbed up stairs after stairs, we took lots of pictures. By the time we reached the top which is the most and satisfying view of sceneries surrounding all sides! I took only a few mountain top scenery because my camera's battery was flat! I sat on top of the mountain and look down at the serenity scene of parts of Jeju Island with the blending on sun setting! Just imagine the feel and satisfaction I gain and feel!But it's time to go down so as we're going down, we enjoyed ourselves by watching the sun going down slowly!

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Bring along a lot of water before climbing. There is few cafe that open very early at the counter ticket area, for you to have anything if you feel hungry before climbing, but just for snacking. The entrance fee is 2k Won, if im not mistake. The view was great along the way from bottom to top. After half-way through, there is a checkpoint with nice scenery of the city and ocean during dawn, which is so beautiful. Better to take picture during that time of your climbing if you climb to see the sunrise, because when you get down, it is another daylight scenery. If you are not fit enough or dont have that much stamina, don't worry, it is still okay for you to climb, you just need a strong will to arrive at the peak and keep on going. As the view from top is worth the sweat!For you to see sunrise, its better for you to be down at the entrance as early as you can, during my time, I already there by 530am, the gate open at 6am as far as I can remember. If you climb slow and steady, it will take you about an hour to climb to the peak. Just keep in mind, if there is a lot of clouds, you might not be able to see the sunrise. So check your weather before you go.

Beautiful view from the cliff and surprising rock formations. Went on a rainy morning so we took our time and walked around a lot too. Snacks from the vendors near the front gate were tasty. The entry fee and parking was 8,000 KRW for a family of 5.
Beautiful place with an amazing view...managed to get here just before the sun goes down, lucky me..really enjoyed the moment(priceless!!)Entrance fee = freeParking fee = 1000 won
beautiful beach, clear waters witha great view. a cafe is nearby where you can sit by the beachside and enjoy a hot cup of coffee with some nice pastries
Beautiful beach if only few tourist there. Clear water, decent sand. Can visit with Hallim Park. There is a G25 which can provide basic food and snacks.  Nice view from Coffee Bene.

As my country does have lotsa waterfall, this short walk for the scene just a ok to us.  Well, the difference is since we are tourist, so we visited the place. You can skip to pay the entrance fee if you are not keen on waterfall as it can be viewed and spotted before climb down for a nearer view of it.

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.

After some hiking (which was hard for me as I didn't really exercise), you can see a small museum on top to explain how light house works, interactive equipments for you to feel more relevant with the light house. You can have a bird eye view of Udo's scenary that will totally amazed you. It is less crowded hence you may enjoy chill and relax time on top.  It's a place worth visiting!

Admission fee for adult is 2000won. You will be able to enjoy walking up to the peak and see the entire sea/ Mountain View. It will be good to wear covered shoes or sport shoes so it?s easier to go up the steps. Not only that, there?s a 대? performance available but I missed the timing. But the 대? will be at their store selling fresh seafood. It?s a good place for solo travellers :)After exploring ilchulbong, head over to ㅼ“대?吏 for some abalone porridge :D

According to the tour guide, she told us it will take 25 mins to reach the top. But we took more than that.  Never mind just walk slowly and take short break in between. Feeling wonderful when reach the top. The sea view is perfect. Front side u can see the houses. I love the Back side view.

About 35 - 1hr hike to reach up the hill. The view at the top is amazing, it's worth to hike. Halfway through the hike there will be 1 pit stop if you would like to purchase any drink and some resting point. There are 2 points where you can U-turn if you feel that you are unable to complete the hike. Once you miss the last turn, you have to complete it hike as it's one way direction.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A stunning architecture, indeed a church. Public access available except for church service hours. beaturiful view of the island from the location too.  There is a coffee house by the parking lot with pretty good coffee too.

A nice little hike up to the top. Not very long, Maybe 20 minutes but ALOT of stairs. Your legs will be feeling it. Good View at the top and its nice to see all the people taking 1 million selfies of themselves while at the top.

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.

A must do in Jeju. We hired a taxi driver to take us and it was 2000won a person to enter. We wanted to go for sunrise but there was an extra fee to hire them that early. (If you want to rent a car, make sure you have an international license - it's about 1.5hr from Jeju city) The hike really isn't too bad. It is an incline, and yes there are lots of stairs, but it is do-able. There were plenty of elderly hiking up and lots of places to stop. Beautiful view from up top. Entrance also allows you to go down to the beach and see the women divers and eat fresh catch.

A hike to the top is quite challenging especially for the elderly and family with young children as there are heaps of steps. Make sure to bring something to hydrate you as there were no drinking fountains available on your way to the top. Enjoy the views of the sea and cityscape once you're at the top. Also, there are a number of restaurants, coffee shops and food stalls at the bottom of the peak.

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.

A fantastic view of jeju and sea.... it takes about 40 to 45mins to climb up slowly... remember wear a pair of comfortable shoes to climb all the stairssss   and bring a bottle of water as you can have rest a point to view some scenary and rest your feet and thirst  before continue to climb to the top . You can get a very nice view at the top of the peak.. it quite cold windy as we went in October early morning around 7am seoul time, so do bring a jacket /wind breaker as well.
2000 won entrance fees for adults, but really gorgeous waterfall, nice views. Worth a visit, much more so than Cheonjiyeon Falls :)

When you go to a country you haven?t been before its nice to find out what it used to be like especially if it?s changed. This is the perfect place to go and look how it was. It?s busy but large so you don?t feel the many people.

Went there in May 2015 by jeju golden city bus tour (which sucked!) and totally enjoyed our 1 hour visit! The exhibitions were amazing and the atmosphere itself is beautiful there! Adm fee is good: just 1000 won as much as I remember. Though the prices at a coffee shop were pretty expensive.

We went on a rainy day and feared it would be too busy to enjoy but it was ok (the first section was the busiest but the crowds thin out the further you get in).  A lot of fun for kids and adults alike.  It took us longer than we thought to get through you could spend hours so would suggest bringing some snacks if you are travelling with kids like we did. There is a coffee shop on site but it only had sweets and ice cream.A fun outing if you've never been to a trick museum before.  Don't forget your camera!!!

We went here today for first time and love it?s it?s so beautiful and fun to walk around have good restaurants and coffee shop and good shop to buy thing make from jeju !! You can take bus or taxi too

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

Was feeling really amazing when passing through this road.   The tour bus was moving even though the driver has turned of the machine. Recommended anyone coming to Jeju to try this herself/himself.* TK

Transportation- You can take bus 755 to the museum takes half an hour from jeju downtown. Food- nothing nearby but you can get pretty decent coffee and jeju-special tea/drinks at the 'innisfree organic green cafe' at the same compound. The museum itself is not that exciting took us 15 mins finishing off everything including the teatree garden. The innisfree cafe/store nearby is so much more fun especially for the female fellow travellers.;)

This was part of our Yeha Bus Tour and I am really glad it was one of our stops as one of our daughters is a tea lover.  She got some lava cake and a coffee and it was enjoyable just watching her.  It was very busy and we did have to be patient for a table so just keep that in mind.

This spot looks like it exists purely for the 15-20 tour buses that were there when we visited as its pretty much a rock with a different shape that you can see in the picture. Save your time and your parking fee and check out the world heritage listed rocks formations around the island otherwise you will need just 1 min here to take a photo and be off again

This small island with a unique history and is classified as a national recreation area.  It  is accessbile by a low cost ferry from  Seongsan which includes the entrance fee to the area.  Bus tours and ATV rentals are available.  The island has many small farms and peanuts are a major crop.

This is so amazing beach to walking around and relax even 11 pm we still walk and feel so peaceful and good food and good clean bar I always stay here when ever come to jeju and you can take the bus anywhere you want to go around jeju it?s beautiful island and I am from Hawaii tham you know what I mean alright

There are several museum of sex & health in Jeju islands.  Jeju Loveland is one of them located a short drive from Jeju Town or Jeju Airport.  It is also a stop of Jeju Golden Bus City Tour.  There are hundreds of sexy and comic sculptures which are placed outside in a well maintained park.  There is also a soft core art galleries and adult toy stores where things are quite expensive. The entry fee: Won 12000 Timing: 0900 to 2300 hrs. Entry allowed for adults above 20 years of age.  It is something different.

The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. The entrance fees is 2000 won and there are 3 levels of teddy bears exhibition and the ground floor is where all sorts of teddy bears are being sold. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

The admission fee for trickeye museum in Jeju is cheaper than other branch in Hongdae and Busan. I dont know if there's different inside the museum of every branch or not but the Jeju branch is relatively small. But its not too crowded so you can take the picture freely without long queue with other visitors.

Strictly for adults this open air museum has many stone sculptures of male and female in various positions. There is also an indoor museum with miniature clay figurines a souvenir shop and a food stall within the compound. Admission fee 12.000 won. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Nexon Computer Museum.Transport tip: From the airport take bus 331 332 465 466 at airport bus stand 6 between gates 4 & 5. Alight at Jeju Museum of Art walk 400m. Bus fare is 1150 won journey about 30 mins.

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!

Soesokkak is a great place to visit if you are in Jeju-do. From Seogwipo area take bus 110 and get off at Hyodon Middle School. It takes another 20 minutes of walking passing by orange farms. No entrance fees is required but if you want to try the transparent kayak or the traditional hand-pulled raft you will need to buy tickets at the counter situated on your right side before you reach the estuary. The clear green blue water is mesmerizing and definitely a great place to visit. Stop-by for a bottle of fresh orange juice to quench your thirst or a cone of ice-cream to complete the trip.

Small but great little beach.  We didn't get much time here as we were on a tight schedule for our business trip but we had enough time for a half hour swim.  There were many surfers and the water was perfect.  There were many people at the beach but it was not crowded.  The beach slopes very gently into the ocean so even 20 30 feet out you're barely to your shoulders.  Nice low waves so a great place to just chill and have a leisurely swim.  There was a changing/showering place conveniently just beside the beach so that made it easy to change and be ready to go again.  Lovely little spot.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.
It was quite a cool experience to feel the bus that we were in moving up the hill with the engine off.

It is difficult to take the local bus to go to the Ferry station so we took a taxi from our hotel near the city centre. The ferry ride is short but the sea air is refreshing and it is kind of fun seeing excited kids feeding the seagulls. The scenery is beautiful on the island but the hop on and hop off bus service is pretty rough.I think they are overbooked and big groups also have special buses nobody else are allowed on. End up waiting a lot to get to the next site. Annoying..!

In the front there is a bus stop. Along the road to the temple is full of orange tree. Big temple with beautiful decoration. Just feel silent and peaceful here. You can just go inside free of charge. I think this is the best temple in Jeju!

I visited this place in January 2018. I traveled alone so I decided not to get into the theme park. I just take pictures in front of the entrance but I feel that this theme park is very exciting. I'd love to play when I come again in the future. Access to this place is accessible by bus/taxi. This place is still not crowded by tourists probably because this place has just opened and many tourists don't really know the whereabouts of this place.

I recently visited this beach with a group of friends and it was definitely worth it.  We were staying in Jeju City so it was about an hour bus ride to get to the beach.
