There isn't any space to lay down a blanket so you have to rent an umbrella.  The water is crystal is clear and the tide is very low.  I had to walk about 300 meter in order to get water that was waist high. There are all kinds of coffee shops and restaurants located along the strip of the beach so you can eat and hang for  as long as you like.  The water is beautiful and makes it worth it.

Hello went there on a family trip with our small kids on children's day. Overall ok not so crowed as expected nice park and arrangement. However here some points which should be improved:1. Ticket price is 39.000 KRW for adult and 29.000 KRW which is too high for what is offered (still construction ongoing). Price should be reduced during construction time to attract more tourist. There should be family tickets with reduced price. 2. Bump Tube Car in New Oscar World. Its not mentioned on the map/guide and even worst its not free! You have to pay extra 5.000 KRW for adult (any maybe even more for kids) but nobody explained to you nothing was mentioned on a board. When you think you can take the tube car the staff ask for your ticket. So you wait 15 min then have to buy a ticket and line up again. Poor communication and every parents were very angry but had to pay because their child already lined up and wanted to take trip tube car. Very clever from the management. Why there is a need to pay for this attraction it should be included in entrance fee as this is already very high.  3. Helium balloon price is 13.000 KRW which is already 1/3 of entrance fee which is too expensive for a simply balloon. Should be less than 9.000 KRW at least. 4. The worst all the food where sold out in Food Court. Can happen but all food? We asked to call the other cafeteria and ask what kind of food they still have. They still had one food where we had to run to get it. We also asked what will happen if there is no food but the staff could not answer. Later we had to eat at the snack corner where as along cue and you had ti wait 20 min to get something. 5. Shuttle bus frequency to parking lot F shall be at least doubled currently one but and you have to wait again in the cue for 15 min. 6. Before you decide to go there with your kids you should check witch attractions your child can take. There are some restrictions on children's height (good due for safety reasons). Sorry the park might be nice.

Been here since in tour itinerary and feel amused! Our big bus with 30people in it still able to run when the driver put the engine in off position! And it's quite fast as well maybe 20-30km/hr When we off from our bus and try to pour a water they go to the side or even go up instead of flow down. Recommended tourist spot to visit and try by yourself!
A must. Breath taking and unique. Wear the right shoes.  Take bus 201 from bus terminal and alight at the cave bus stop. Walk for 2km and you will reach the cave.  Entrance fee is won2000

A must stop during our busy vacation here in Jeju! They have free parasols that we used during the sunny day and it made the garden a lot nicer to enjoy. We bumped into the Director that created the garden and he was very kind. I highly recommend buying his book from the store and he even gave us an autographed copy:)) You can tell that each bonsai tree in the garden has a lot of love invested. There are koi fish in the water flowing through the garden and they are well fed and taken care of. There is also a cafe in the garden that has fancy drip coffee. We went in early October and the weather was perfect.

A grand n majestic temple. Upon entering the temple vicinity you can feel truly blessed n at ease.Even though the history of the temple aint long the architecture of the temple n beautiful landscaping are truly marvellousThe airport limousine bus from airport/ jeju city stops in front of the temple on the way to Seogwipo.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

What a waste of money! Very disappointing especially given the very high entrance fee (6K). The crater is just a hole in the ground covered with trees and a 1.2 km walk is a loop around grass patch and small forest on one side (next to a busy road, so you can hear the traffic). If you have never left a city before you might like it (like, you get to walk on a grass for a moment, not on a concrete sidewalk, UNBELIEVABLE NATURE EXPERIENCE, right?). Just save your money, for 6K you can have a nice lunch, not 30 minutes grass walk.

We went there with a bus group, they organized a lot of activities and Mysterious road was one of these. We found out it's too crowded and there's nothing to see and to do, it's normal street, they said that the cars will move without a driver, but you can't see it or feel it, just the driver feels that. overall don't go there if specially for the street if it's on your way or you are with a group it's okay.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre. We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000\ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

We planned this for the kids but the adults had fun too. When we arrived, we bought the tickets while the kids were busy with the numerous cats around the area. It turns out that this is also a place for cat lovers, this place is a mini cat world too. You can get cat food from the ticket counter to feed the cats.In the maze, the kids formed a team and raced with us, the parents. Each team had to find the stamps hidden around the maze and stamp on the paper given. First team to collect all 6 stamps and ring the bell to exit the maze wins.Upon exiting the maze, as we passed thru the ticket counter again, the lady manning the counter asked us to visit the gift shop to claim a free postcard.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We felt peacefulness in this place even if it is next to a main road. The entry fee is only 1000 won and clean facilities.From Seogwipo bus station take bus 700 for 1500 won each way.The building in the Korean style are well maintain and the climb all the way to the grotto is a good exercise. The golden Buddha sit up there under the dripping mountain. People collect the water for? believe of power, may be like Christian for Easter water..Well! Each are different, Friday for the Jews, Saturday the Muslim, Sunday the Christians, everyday for Buddhas...

We didn't spent much time here as we are rushing. Overall is a nice place to visit. You can rent a bike or motor cars to go around the island or take the bus tour. At first we planned to drive car inside the island. However, due to many vehicles in the island and to avoid traffic jam, they have set the rules that only local island cars can drive into Udo island. I forgot the timeline but it took around one year period. For those who plan to drive car enter the island you may need to further check on it. When purchased the ferry ticket, you are required to fill in the two forms. Please bring along your passport as well. The counter personnel not many can speak English where we feel a bit challenge. Overall, is a nice place to visit. And if possible do spare around one day to enjoy the environment here.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Very well maintained and beautifully laid out area around the falls. Only costs a couple of AUD to go in and wander round the tree lined river. Plenty of lucky charms around for your wishes too. Very popular with tourists, I expect it can get very busy. Recommend the Angel caf챕 near entrance coffee ok and great free wifi. Also take a walk past the fishing boats with there large glass squid lights and over the nearby bridge on to the island.

Very lovely island. But travelling is an issue if you do not have international license to rent the atv. The roads were pretty narrow hence, a little scary to ride bicycle around. Hence the best would be by feeder bus.The seafood noodle, peanut makgeolli and peanut yogurt were fantastic and must try!

Udo, is a small island located on the east side of Jeju Island. You can get there by taking a boat (around 20min) on the east side of Jeju. you can also bring your vehicle onto the boat and bring it to Udo.The island is quite big that you cannot walk around the island by feet. If you are not bringing your own vehicle, you can rent a ride near to the harbor BUT you need to have a driver's license. So prepare an international driver's license maybe (I am not sure if they accept international license though:( )There is also a bus that goes around the island and once you buy a ticket near the harbor, you can get off from the bus and get back into any bus without any extra charge.The sight around the island is beautiful. You can stop your vehicle at any time and enjoy and take photos.

Udo was easy to get to and a great place to camp with full amenities. There are 2 main beaches; one on the West side and one on the North East side. Both are beautiful but the one that has sand made of seashells (West Side) is a little hard on your bare feet  and it was much busier there. The other has soft fine sand that makes for a great camping spot. There are no taxis on the island. In hindsight, we would have taken the other ferry to the port that was a bit closer to Hagosudong Beach (the NE side), but there is this drop on and off Bus Tour System that costs 5000won/person. You can get on from the ferry, drop off and set up your camp at the beach, then hop back on. It runs frequently but only stops at 4 main sightseeing spots (beach 1, beach 2, caves and ___ ) . We were able to use the bus for the two days we were there for on the same fare, but there are times/stops that are crazy busy. We watched at least 6 packed buses go by before we decided to stay the night. Honorable food mention: Pirate Caf챕. Really interesting place and staff. Great BiBamBap and you get to sign a plaque and hang it from their wall when you?re done eating.Friendly people, campfire and camping friendly, personal beer cooler (at the convenience stores directly behind the beach), and lots of cats.

Udo or ?Cow Island? lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing ??5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It?s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

Transportation: There are several buses that make stops at this destination, but just like everything in Jeju, rental car is the recommended mode of travel. Food: the lava tubes does have a restaurant colocated but I did not eat. There are also some snacks you can purchase here but you are not allowed to bring them down into the lava tubes. Attraction: The scale of the lava tube really surprised me. We descended roughly 30 feet into the lava tube after we purchased our tickets ($4 pp). The stairs were slippery, so be cautious when descending. Don?t worry if you have claustrophobia, The tube is about 25ft across and 20 feet high! There are no tour guides, so you won?t have anybody explaining the history or the geology of the tubes, but there are educational signs posted about every 100 feet. There was also a great museum on sit I recommend visiting prior to going into the lava tubes. Great place to visit, and it took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

To get to this island, one has to fill in a form and pay for the fees. All is convenient and easy peasy. Then, the ferry ride is quick. We opted for a bus tour. The tour was in Korean and we couldn't understand a thing but considering it is one of the easiest method to get around the island,we just go along with it. We would like to ride one of those adorable scooters but we don't own an international license. Overall a good experience.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This was a big disappointment. We'd read that it was a real functioning village, but it was mostly deserted, the houses falling down and no sign of any residents. The buildings are picturesque enough but overall it had a rather sad, melancholy feel. We only spent half an hour there and regretted the long bus journeys entailed.

This road is interesting! When we are about to reach the site, the driver turned off the engine, and yet the bus is moving upwards!! Amazing!We even went down the bus to try running backward on the road, and one can feel like you are being pulled from the back. Also, we try by pouring water onto the road itself, which is a good test.And yes, the food stall along the road is more interesting.

This place is great, fresh seafood sold at the coast, seeing the sea ladies in action (we were lucky and saw her catching an octopus with a fork like stick) and beautiful scenery of the coast, sea and land. It's a short boat ride over from the main island, then one could choose to take their bus at a fee, which will stop by 4 or 5 stops near the beach, cliff, etc  then bring u back to the starting point. Alternatively, you could rent a motorbike or four wheel drive. For the latter, one needs an international driving licence. One thing that's everywhere is their peanut ice cream, basically soft serve with peanut powder. Also, there's grilled cuttlefish everywhere.

This place is easily accessible by bus, next to O'Sulloc tea museum. Makes me feel very cosy the moment I stepped in. It's a cafe as well as a place for soap making workshop. It also sells own products (limited).I love the healthy breakfast which is organic and surprisingly very tasty. However, it is on the pricey side.

This place exceeded my expectations, it is definitely a highlight of Jeju, it is perfectly organized to be a journey itself. We spent around 3 hours walking around ( it has 3 different routes well explained in the map) and simply feeling the nature was already healing. The entrance is 6.000 Korean won per person. They have drinking fountains and toilets inside. You can reach it by bus!

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.

This is probably one of my favourite beaches of all time. Do not be put up by busy pictures... The water is shallow, for about 200m or more out to sea so the area for children to play and people to swim or snorkel is huge. We set up towels on the short and put up our own umbrellas and it really didn't feel crowded at all. There are loads of shops and restaurants around, as well as loads of places to rent rubber rings etc. I also saw lots of water sports happening outside of the safe swim zone. Truly a great day or so out!! And sunset is beautiful too.

This is one road which really left my puzzled. The bus driver did turn off his enjoy but the bus still managed to roll on, to my eyes, the path was an up-sloping one. So how did the bus manage to move on its own? Does it mean the path is actually downwards sloping?This is just any other road along Jeju Island which after completion, people found out about this weird phenomenon. Well, the locals will explain to you the whole reason to this phenomenon. Don't worry, expect a crowd there with tour buses pulling over, but don't expect a fee to be paid unless you patronize the little snack shops there.

There is a bus from Jeju bus terminal that takes 1hours and a half min and you have to take a Ferry that costs 5,500won.If you dont know how to plan one day travel I would like to recommend you to go Udo and  Seongsan Ilchulbong that is closer to each other If you start your day early you will probably have more time thoughTo see all island it takes 3~4hours by bus that there is Tour bus which costs 5,000wonHowever i would like to recommend you to ride a bike for some partIt is beautiful to ride around the sea and you can feel relaxed.There is 3 beaches that you can visit and those are all different atmosphereespecially there is Coral beach that are exists only 3palce on the world Please go towards the end where people are not crowdedYou will see more pretty coralUdo is famouse for peanut that if you like plz try only small amount since it is a bit expensiveI am not sure if there is famouse food for foreginer but street food is okay As my memory Udo is one of the best part in Jeju island I will recommend for my friends

There are 3 waterfalls near my guesthouse and I chose to visit Jeongbang Waterfall first; no special reason as I have a direct bus to there. Admission fee for adult is 2000 won, and youth will be 1000 won (the ticket ahjumma will ask for your birth year). So you will have to walk down a few stairs and cross over stones to reach the waterfall. It was cooling to just sit down here and enjoy the waterfall. But please remember to wear cover shoes in order to prevent falling. Not only you can take photos with the waterfall, there?s a connecting sea right beside and you can take beautiful picture. Solo travellers please remember to bring a selfie stick :)

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

The maze is closely located to Manjanggul cave.The entrance fee is KRW3,300. The entrance is fill of cute cats.The maze is constructed by high and neatly-trimmed bush walls.It is not too large.There is an observation decks/bridge. From here you can clearly see path.As we're running out of time, we use the map to solve the maze.It took us 8 min to ring the victory bell.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The beach was almost empty when we went there. It was sunny, quiet and very nice. The beach is very shallow, so it requires like a hundred meters of walking to reach a place where a grown up guy's feet don't touch the sand anymore. It was the perfect beach for just walking around in the shallow water. I would absolutely go there again. We took a bus from Seogwipo (＿?洹?ъ), which took quite a while but they're not expensive. And the drivers are crazy so be prepared for a thrill ride!

The beach is beautiful on a sunny day - calm, clean, safe and relaxing. Suitable for couples or family with seniors/kids. We got there by bus no. 10 from the city. Very convenient with good facilities. You pay a small fee to shower otherwise the usual toilets are available if you just want to have a change of clothes. If it rains there are plenty of cafes to take shelter at.We spent a few hours at the beach in the afternoon and had a seafood banquet for dinner at one of the many restaurants close by during sunset.

The beach has beautiful, clear emerald waters (the pictures doesn?t do the place justice as its much better experienced in person), and a really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries. We got there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. Near the beach there are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice. Easy to hail a taxi there too for those who wants to travel to their next location  by cab. Parking lots available too for those who are driving.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

The beach has beautiful, clear  waters, and really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries and tea.We went there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. There are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice near the beach . Easy to get a taxi there too. Parking lots are available too.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

Strolling numbers of beaches in Udo or climb the peak of Udobong. Simply taste the peanut ice cream and hallabong ice cream from the various stall along the coastal lines. The local turban shell is a must try in Udo. Getting around is easy either by shuttle bus, ATV, bike ride or just a pair of feet is all you need.

Seongsan Ilchulbong, also known as ?Sunrise Peak?, is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The peak is 182 metres (600 ft) above sea level. It is around 30 - 40 minutes walk/hike to reach the top. Make sure you are fit enough because the weather is cold and windy in the morning. I've been there in early March recently and it was 4째c. To reach this place, you may drive by rent a car or take a bus from Seogwipo or Jeju City. The journey takes approximately an hour and half. Starbucks is just nearby the carpark to enjoy a cup of coffee.

Really....it is just another rock with a legend.  It seems that everyone turns into rock while waiting for someone....story line is always the same.  If you are a big fan of Korean drama - Daejeonggeum, then this is the place for you.  A lot of tourist stops here....maybe becos it has no admissions fees.  Try and come early in the morning as the tour buses start coming in late morning.

Our kids (7&10) enjoyed the rock climbing, surf and sand...not to mention the modestly price ferry ride.  We attempted to rent a motorized vehicle but there were no rentals for four people...maximum people limit per vehicle was two and one of us did not have a driver's license...so we took the modestly priced bus trip.  Note that a home-country drivers license will not work.  once we figured out the system (no English speakers found on the island of Jeju.), it worked to see most of the island.  The peanut ice cream was all variations of soft-serve...low quality ice cream.  There were enough snack shops for coffee or short orders.  Okay for a day trip.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is a small building set in a tea farm. It's a well designed lovely space with a display area about the history of tea and an exhibit wall of teacups and pots a shop where you can try some tea (only one kind though) and a restaurant featuring green tea beverages and sweets. You can also walk around outside there is a garden area in and around the building and also small rows of tea bushes just outside. There's no admission fee and it's not so much of a museum as a commercial venue for selling O'Sulloc products although items can be pricey for the budget traveller. I visited O'Sulloc with a few other backpackers (5 foreigners 1 Korean) and we all had a terrible experience of their customer service. The staff were sour faced and gave us the impression that we were not welcomed glaring at us and tidying their display in a huff when we looked at the product samples (these are samples ok - they're meant to be touched and looked at!). The staff at the counter literally sneered in disdain at my Korean travel companion when he tried to make friendly small talk while we were purchasing our items. This was the worst experience I've had in my 3 weeks in Korea. All the other customer service staff I've encountered in Korea were either very polite and lovely or just neutral. I'm writing in formally to the management about this so hopefully by the time other TripAdvisor members visit they would have improved.In spite of that I did enjoy my visit (no point letting the staff spoil it) but I would recommend coming here only if you've done all your   must-do's   in Jeju or on a rainy day.

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

review: Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Hair and beauty treatment was the first thingwe went for. it was just awesome,. they made us feel us like superstars. One my friend spent all her time in the casino. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

It took a little over 2 hours by bus to get here. I feel conflicted with it, as a part of me liked the place but another part of me thought there was (yet again!) nothing special here. Plus the journey to get there was already exhausting so probably my feet were already asleep halfway into my walk.So only go if you can rent a car, it will take much less time to get here. All in all a relaxing place to take a stroll or read in.

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town

If you have seen any of the large dramatic water falls around the world then you will be disappointed by this tiny cascade. Barely 60/70 ft tall and about 20/25 ft wide. A small stream tumbles directly into the ocean. The tourist brochures make this more dramatic than what it actually is. Have uploaded pictures of the falls from the top (from the platform adjacent to the ticketing office and entry barriers) and from the bridge over the stream just before it tumbles down. Would give you some idea of the size.But having said all of that, this a pleasant enough area. Pay Won 2000 for entry (entry hours 8am - 6pm/7pm, depending on summer/winter) and leisurely climb down about 60 odd feet i.e. equivalent of climbing down about 6 stories. You will arrive at a rocky area. Clambering over about 1/5th mile (300 odd mts) of large rocks to where the water falls, isn't for the aged like me! But it would be nice to get to the water's edge if you can.Not a bad idea to carry sandwiches and beer and sit on the rocks, moments of peace and quiet, isolated from bustling Segwipo all around.You wouldn't miss anything if you haven't been here. But it would be a shame to miss it if you are on Jeju.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. There's also an outdoor gardens with bear exhibits, fountain and lake and a blooming grapefruit tree. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. Get your tickets cheaper via taobao, the China online shopping site. They have almost 50% discount for foreigners, which we tapped on. Just need to print our confirmation and entry was a breeze. Also, this place is accessible via a bus from Jeju intercity bus terminal. Stop at jungmun resort. Nearby are alive musuem, yeomiji botanical gardens and cheonjiyeon waterfalls, good for a self planned one day trip.

I visit play kpop by taking bus 600 from sogwipo harbour. It was very exciting experience. Even though it is a hologram concert, it feels like a live concert and my wife won the card selection and my wife?s hologram was on stage and yonghwa singing for her. I never seen this technology and appearance anywhere else. Play kpop need to improve the 360 3d cinema because it makes visitor feel dizzy and to improve the sound system. Anything else is okay but need to pay every single shots with the celebrity. Overall i give 5 stars for the experience. Thanks Play Kpop!

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I never been to such places before so i have no reference to compare it to. I think it was worth the entrance fee, a bit hard to get there with the buses. You pay the fee for inside baths that are separated by male and females, where most of the people are naked. You pick a small locker room for your shoes and with the same key you can open a bigger locker for the fest of your belongings. You should shower before getting in the tubs and must pay to use the outdoor tubs, where both man and women can use(not naked). Try to follow the instructions in english of how to use the baths, for how long and in what order and it will be worth it. They also have massages, sleeping rooms, lounges, vibrating chairs, small restaurant ...

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I happened to notice a separate entrance desk that had pictures of SCUBA divers on it. I asked an attendant nearby in simple English sentences if they had any SCUBA diving and how much was it? It was only 119000 KWon and they happened to have availability right away! I've dove in other aquariums but this was the cheapest and didn't even require a reservation on a busy day! Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids. They loved it!I still had to pay the separate entrance fee for the aquarium (about $40 but I received a 20% off coupon at the airport) but it was worth it. The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Would definitely go back.Note: A lot of the aquarium features the image of a whale shark. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.

review: I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I got to visit this museum as part of an inclusive tour so I can't comment on the value of the entrance fee, but I loved this museum.  I haven't laughed so much in ages.  I am not sure if it is meant to be so delightfully funny!  It is famous in S Korea for a TV series   about a Princess that was filmed there.What you get is several galleries of teddy bears dressed up as historical figures, famous art works, and scenes from history or of S Korean culture.  There are several large bears around the place suitable for having your photo with eg Charlie Chaplin, Michael Jackson.  Outside there are several bears enjoying the gardens again suitable for being photographed with.  There is a cafe and a gift shop.  The cafe was closed when we visited late afternoon. There is a short running show of an automaton Elvis-Bear again hilarious!  I would definitely go back.  This museum is located in the Jungmun resort area on the Bus Route 600.  Get off at PlayKpop stop - its just next door.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

Fairly small place for a hefty KRW10,000 entrance fee; the most expensive Jeju attraction. Features 2 galleries of teddy bears from various countries and themes and a teddy souvenir shop.  Will appeal to ladies, children and couples keen on photo snaps with huggable teddies, especially the human-sized ones at the corner of each floor and in the gift shop. Be prepared to jostle with crowds on a busy day.  There is a 5 minute T-Elvis performance held at every 15 minute interval in the Elvis Presley theatre.  Can skip if you're not a teddy lover or been here before as exhibits hardly change.

Eco land has big landscape. Inside there are 4 trains station. A small train that drops people in all station, after reaching a station, people can look around and get into next train. One part is good for children, since there are kids house, kids coffee shop(miniature), fire station (miniature), bank(miniature), movie theatre(miniature) . This whole place is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park, Sangumburi Crater  and stone land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places. Usually if you taxi for using between 9 AM to 5 PM, you will have to pay 120,000 KRW.

Easy to get to, a small entry fee, then a short walk down, out and around a spectacular and unique geological area that is set on the edge of the island. Very picturesque and a great spot for photos, but it can get very busy depending on the time of the day. Worth a visit and a wander - places for picnics - however if the day is wet, an hour or two will be enough time.

Cars and buses usually demonstrate this seemingly mysterious trick. They have their engines turned off at the beginning of the road stretch (there's an indicated sign). And while the engines are off, it seemingly feels and looks like there's this   mysterious force   pulling the vehicles towards the end of the road. Civilians also use a water bottle and place it on the road surface. Mimicking the vehicles, it too would roll towards the end of the road. Just like the saying goes, looks can be deceiving. Optical illusion is what it is.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Tour guides poured water and empty round mineral water bottles but it did not seem to give any credence to the anomaly. However I did see one car roll backwards (uphill) rather fast but couldn't tell if it was already in-gear, nevertheless the reverse lights weren't illuminated so I guess it wasn't rolling on it's own steam.

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. There is a long steep path in order to reach the lighthouse on top. But that shouldn't be a problem as the scenery along the road is empowering your feet to work. In the middle of the path  there is a candy house like building. But unfortunately  it was reconstructing at that moment. So  I bought a chocolate ice cream beside the reconstruction to settle my unhappiness. The ice cream tastes unexpectedly good  it is rich in chocolate and smooth when I put it into my mouth. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the lighthouse  we took several pictures there  but no one is perfectly taken because of strong wind  our hair flowing like crazy  so we didn't spend much time on the lighthouse.We took about 30 minutes there and didn't have a chance to visit the building at that time  so I strongly recommend you to go there at autumn or spring and plan more than half an hour if you are deciding to visit there.
The only waterfall in Jeju that e water flows into the ocean. U can go very close to it & feel e cool Breeze. Was so amazed to c rainbow too! Worth stopping by.

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

It is easy to find and has a few parking places. No entrance fee. Restroom availabe at the parking lot. You walk alonxg the coast line and dont forget your camera.
