It is a must see place for a tourist to visit the area near to the convention center especially place near to the beach at the back side of convention center. You can also sea them during feeding time.There is also a big aquarium with fishes sharps and stingrays. What I liked most were the small aquariums with exotic fish variety. Turn out we reached there too early. The sunrise only happened past 630am. The sun added magical colours to the coast. Splashing waves at the coast created rainbow, many photo opportunity. Can see Edo Island. Came back again during sunset. Love the colourful sky. Had abalone porridge and seafood pot at a nearby restaurant, so yummy. Nice finishing touch to the day.

We were attracted by the promise from the literature that this was the only waterfall in Asia with 'debouches' into the ocean. Hmmm, you almost get the impression from above that some channel engineering has helped this along. Anyway, Wikipedia tells me that this claim is not quite correct. Anyway, we arrived as then had to purchase entry tickets. The stressed out man next to the ticket gate then seemed to think that we have not purchased the correct amount of tickets. We had. It was all the more puzzling because he was only 2 feet from where we bought the tickets. Maybe he was so bored he was asleep at the wheel. Or maybe it was because we were foreigners. Anyway, once that nonsense was resolved we headed down the steps, only to be stopped half-way down at yer another ticket check! Ridiculous, three check for a 1000-or-so won entry ticket. We thought we must be in for something very special. Alas not. Said waterfall falls a few score metres, generates a modest amount of spray and attracts thousands of people taking selfies of themselves and said insipid attraction. There are some older folk selling ghastly looking octopus slices by the rocks - poor animals (the octopus that is). We were not stopped for more ticket checks on the way out, thankfully. I suggest you just look at the photo on the web and go and do something more interesting instead.

We walked to the peak of Hallan Mountain from Seongpanak. We used around 5hours to walk from a height of around 800m to 1950m. The top of Hallan Mountain is a small pond - Bakrokdam. After returning to Seongpanak, you can get the certificate to show that you have arrived to the peak of Hallan Mountain (fee: 1000won)

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

We hiked up Hallasan the first weekend in March 2012.  We brought coats, hats, gloves and scarfs, however we were not prepared for the amount of snow on the mountain.  Check the conditions ahead of time and be sure to bring walking sticks and spikes for your boots.  My family hiked for awhile but stopped about 1km from the top after we were in more than two feet of snow and freezing.

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

We drove our rented car onto the ferry which took us to Udo in 15 minutes. If the weather hadnt been so cold, we would have tried the fun looking electric scooters. We stumbled into a seafood restaurant to the left of the ferry terminal and enjoyed a sumptuous seafood kimchi hotpot. Ordering was not a problem as the service staff spoke mandarin. The place was an obvious favourite with locals. We spent 4 hours exploring various sites and even got lost. A friendly local policeman kindly pointed us the right way. We stopped by quaint coffeeshops and hugged their cute puppies. We were reluctant to leave this idyllic tiny island.

We did a back to back sunset/sunrise hike. Sunset was great because it wasn't hot and it was really nice and breezy up there after 20 minutes of stomping up stairs. You get to see the sunset on one side of the peak while you see the moon rise over the crater at the top. Pretty awesome. There is a water/coffee stand about halfway up in case you forget water, but the it wasn't open when we hiked it in the morning (big fail). We camped on the beach nearby, not the greatest...Garbage EVERYWHERE! Not just your typical beach garbage (cups, bags, broken plastic boxes) but long fluorescent light bulbs, peices of boats, clothing... The water had lots of debris in it and despite the sweltering heat, we just couldn't get ourselves to wade past the trash into the deeper areas so we left for Udo Island instead. It was also pretty tricky finding a good spot to post our tent. The tide comes up REALLY high there and the garbageless, flat tide-safe spots are pretty much non existant. Pretty uncomfortable night/morning, but at least we didn't have to get up until 5am to hike the peak. There are washrooms in the village which is about 10 min from the beach, but bring a flashnight cause the lights and water turns off at night.

We came just after the rain stopped. Love the layout of the whole place. Instantly brings you back to the past there are real people - Craftsmen Painter Potter man on the respective   villages   with living animals - chicken black pigs goats horses. It is a nice experience. There are old   games   for you to try on. Saw traditional drummers along the way. You can have greater understanding on how the past Koreans houses based on their occupations - fisherman farmer locksmith painter. There are school police station & court house too. Few of the famous Korean dramas been shot here namely Jewel In The Palace.  A worker told us if we came on a non rainy day there will be more activities. Entrance fee is on higher side - 8000 Won/ Person but it is worth a visit.

Was there last Friday morning before back to Seoul! The wind was so strong and I love the cold freeze! The wave and sound makes you feel relax and you can visit diver women sheltering under the small wooden house and they are selling the live seafood that caught from the sea such as abalone, sea cucumber, oyster etc. You can also see non stop airplane landing towards Gimpo airport.

Udo island offers push bike and motorised bike hire for a small fee at both of the docking locations. You can also drive your car onto the ferry and just drive. I used the push bike so I could enjoy the feel of the coast roads without rushing past but you'll still see everything (without the muscle pain) with the other options. There are several little eatery places scattered along the road that offer very fresh and yummy food. I spent about 3-4 hours riding around the coastal road stopping for freshly squeezed juice, lunch, the local peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine. If your looking for adventure this isn't for you but if a quiet relaxing back to nature is what your looking for be sure to stop by.

This tiny, delightful island feels miles away from anything familiar and mundane.  I highly recommend renting an electric scooter (for about 25 bucks for 2 hours) and driving around the entire island.  Driving around the island only takes about an hour, but give yourself extra time to stop for photo ops.  The place is dreamy and laid back - you can even spot the famous haenyeo (women divers) at work, and see their   dressing stations.    There is no   one particular amazing   thing to see on Udo, but rather it's about the whole experience of exploring this off-beat place and losing track of time.

This show is Amazing...I don't feel bored or sleepy on the entire show. Enjoy every minute of it and can't stop laughing by their performance. The characters are funny without talking and the story is simple yet truly entertaining. They are interactive and skillful. This show is highly recommended when you go to Korea! But, don't use the toilet it was horrible when I visited this place.

This place was the first on my list of place-to-go in Jeju. We were quite rushing as we don't want to miss the Haenyeo show (I totally adore them since years ago while watching documentary!). We would love to go for hiking to the peak, but we are pretty much time-constrained. Make sure to wear comfy shoes as there are lots of stairs. Go downstairs (it's really tiring to go upstairs later) to the Haenyeo house for the show and be there early as those ahjumma (auntie) in diver suit will perform their Haenyeo song and dance before going to the sea (this is so much fun!). There is boat service provided if you'd like a tour. You may enjoy fresh raw seafood (abalones, octopus etc.) from their catch, approx. from KRW10000 for a plate. If you love horse-riding, give it a try!The area is surrounded with souvenir shops. Try Hallabong (citrus fruit), one of Jeju specialities! The sight is way too gorgeous to be missed. MUST-GO-PLACE!Haenyeo (women diver) show: 1.30 pm & 3.00 pmAdmission fee for adult: KRW2000Boat ride: KRW10000Horse-riding: approx. KRW5000++Hallabong: KRW2000 each

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

This beach was a short stopover point for us. We were on the way to another place.It was mid afternoon & the sun was very very hot, probably that's why there were so few people then. My guess is that those who are here came for the same reasonThe roaring sounds of the waves & the deep blue sea always gives one a nice relaxed feeling. In countries like Korea, there are lots of similar beaches & seas. So although it is nice, there is no need to make a special trip unless you are on the way to another place & passes through here for a short stop. Or for toilet breaks.

There is a small fee to enter the area, I think around 2-3000W. Once you are inside the park, you can hang out on the paths, admiring the rolling green fields, or head up some few hundred stairs to the top of the little mountain and look at the crater. The little mountain was formed by a volcanic eruption a long time ago and around the rim of the crater there are 99 'peaks' which they call the crown. That's cool. I think that's cool.After you have taken an inappropriate amount of selfies you can head back down to a small beach area and watch traditional women divers...diving. There is also a small black stoned beach by the women divers which you can walk along and admire the beautiful black stone of the small mountain, which is Seongsan Ilchulbong.We travelled there by public transport and it wasn't difficult at all.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

The park is well manicured and you can take great pictures of scenery with fences. There are swings near the top where you can enjoy the breeze while taking in the scenery of the surrounding lands and mountains.  You can also see the bottom of the   green crater   from the top.This is one of the more expensive natural attractions in Jeju (KRW6,000) but I feel it's a good place to relax and worth a visit.

The Botanical gardens is set up in to different gardens and a large doom/ indoor area set up into zones. The plants on show were very nice but I have seen a lot better. This could be because of the South Korea climate. Look at the surface and it's well kept then you notice dirty water in the ponds. What I did enjoy was watching some of the workers weed some of the areas they are so methodical. As we were part of a day tour this was just one of our many stops and our time was limited. Perhaps I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have such a tight schedule. I would rate this attraction as Good but there isn't a good rating and average would do it a disjustice. I thought the entrance fee to be very high considering the country it's in. You don't pay much more to go in Kew Gardens, London's Botanical garden that can actually take you days to get round.

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

spent a long day in Udo - so idyllic and relaxing.  There are endless seaside beaches, cliffs, cafes, ...  Just drive your own car there (via car ferry - costed us 32k Won) for a small car and 2 pax, or rent one of the bikes, motor tricycles (very cute), and just drive and stop anywhere (almost) you like and take photos, drink coffee, or just doing nothing and daydreaming. Excellent scenery, food- freshest seafood, burgers, ..... How nice to spend a day.

Several things that I didn't like about this place. First they completely do not respect nature, eg. There are a few chairs on top with Celine dion's titanic music playing! I guess Koreans think that makes the place more romantic but it completely ruins the experience for me. Then the crater itself is impressive but the entrance fee was 6000w per person which is a total rip off. If these two objections don't deter you from going then at least go early (we went at 8:30 on a Monday) and literally had the crater to ourselves for 15 minutes.

Rent bikes and escape the tour groups, and you can stop where you like. We found Udo was quieter than the rest of Jeju Island. There are plenty of coffee shops, small eateries and ice cream places. Things to see include lighthouses and beaches - but there is a huge amount of litter around the rocks and headlands.  Peanuts are grown on the island and there was a peanut festival at the ferry terminal when we visited.

quick, easy, enjoyable.  our kids enjoyed the challenge (age 7 & 10).  we attended early in the day and missed the numerous school groups.  a small event with a modest fee....a very nice stop before we headed to the lava tubes.

Pretty much boring, probably one will only get really excited if the person is a hardcore teddy bear fan .. Else it's really just a   oh ya I've been there.. Full stop    kinda trip.. Was lucky I went during the children days weekend so quite a good no of attractions were free.. Else I will probably feel $ wasted on this

People still live here!     There was no admission fee.   We drove right in and walked around.     Obviously, the biggest thing is the roofs which are replaced every year.     You still have the stone walls and the entry gate.     We saw several people who still live here but didn?t interact with any of them.    The village was a convenient stop on our way back from the eastern side of the island.     I wouldn?t make a special trip to see it but it?s certainly worth 20-30 minutes if it?s on your way.

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

It's just a 1km tunnel walk, feeling the chill a little.  Kind of dim, ground is uneven, therefore watching our steps took most of our focus, stopping occasionally for pictures taking. Nothing exceptionally awesome.

It's a dramatic coastline, just like blocks of puzzles stacking on top of each other. It's a unique sight. The entrance fee is KRW2,000 and the overall walk is easy, takes maximum 15-20 mins including photography. The sea water is clear and you can actually see the formation from below.

It's a bit of a climb to get to the top, which is mostly stairs. Once the stairs start they don't stop until the top. By this I mean there are no real breathers in between the flights of stairs and when you're on a schedule - getting to the top before sunrise, the climb can take a bit out of you. Plan for about 30 minutes or less for the healthy folk and 40 minutes or more for those of us who aren't from the parking lot.Also didn't pay entrance fees as there's no one there at sunrise.

it was a very cold windy day we visited this place. climbed for about 30 mins to reach to the top to enjoy the scenery which is worth the climb. There are many people there but don't feel crowded at all. When you are in Jeju, make sure you visit this place, really beautiful

It was a good experience for me family with 2 children as they enjoyed ut the most. Weather as a bit chilly even during autumn, so bring extra layers with you so that you can get confortable. The train ride at the start of the trip really feels like the highlight of the trip, although you can board the train on and off later to get from one garden to another. There are 5 stops for you to stroll around, toilets, cafes and other facilities are available and very much well taken care off. We had a great time all in all. Highly recommended to friends and families.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

I'm not a big fan of Hello Kitty (my friend does), but it was fun to stroll around the place. It was filled with Hello Kitty goodness in pink and such a nice place to take pictures. There are so many rooms to be visited, and they even have a rooftop garden! Some of item showcased are very interactive and enjoyable. I believe it's worth the visit as every adult has their own inner-child side. Unravel your younger side out, and you'll enjoy the place lot more than you think. Recommended for families. Make sure to visit their cafe that serves nice choco drink (approx. KRW4000) & the gift shop!Admission fee for adult: approx. KRW10800++

If you have no knowledge of the K-pop industry, this may not be the place for you. But, we love it. For the ticket price, things it offers is beyond our expectation. If you have a personal preference of 'which' pop star you wanna watch for the hologram show, you should check its schedule online. The ticket has a 3-hour validity (I think it's a bit short, if you really try all the stations/ experience) There are 3 levels where you could see lots of displays (music, costumes) and to try lots of fun interactive games with cutting edge technology. For instance, to dance with the stars, to shoot a picture with them, where you could actually scan your ticket and choose from the list, which star you want to pick. We stopped half way to watch the scheduled hologram show, which lasted for about 30 mins, and it was fabulous because that is the singer we really adore. After the show, we continued with our visit for a while. You can print whatever photos you snapped (if you like it) on the spot with a small fee. Likewise, you may download all the funny photos you have snapped from their website later that day. We enjoyed ourselves tremendously.
I wondering how their built the road and the environment to make it so mysterious! The taxi driver stopped the engine for us to feel the different, it was amazing!

I really feel sorry for those went earlier this year and totally missed the beauty of the silvery purple grass we have not seen elsewhere. It is such an easy walk so even you push baby strollers, or having a baby buggy, it shouldn't be too difficult. Anyway, you probably stop Sao many times on the way to take photos so it is not a tiring climb.There's only one small snack place at the bottom but a few nice wooden picnic booth for people to rest.  We saw some Korean families enjoying their homemade kimba at the top enjoying the scenery. I think it's a great family trip for about one to two hours depending on the age difference in your group.Selfie stick is quite useful here if you want to post in from too the unique grass.  Obviously don't dress in silver (autumn time).After this we went on another 20~30 min to the world's biggest nutmeg forest which is on the way to the east coast (5 Day Market and Haenyeo Women Diver Museum) to,follow in the afternoon.

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I have heard people said the sunrise from the crater is magnificent. But, I have visited Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon and it was just awesome! Thanks to the wide green field surrounded by the dark blue sea and cover with the bright blue sky! It was so relaxing there hearing the wave sound and feel the wind blowing pass through me. Hiking to the top of the crater would be good too, but you may need at least 2 hours to walk around the area.

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

Great place to gawk at all the live seafood that Jeju has to offer. All manner of sea creatures, alive and dead, to be savoured & haggled over if you so wish to partake of feasting on them. Besides seafood, there are also veggies, Jeju souvenirs (mainly foodstuffs), a couple of seafood restaurants (which charged seating fees per person so we skipped going in) and some cooked food stalls. Great to stop by to check out the local market scene.

Great location with beautiful sightseeing...Jeju Island, also known as the   Island of the Gods,   is a popular vacation spot for Koreans and foreigners. It remains the top honeymoon destination for Korean newlyweds, and is also regarded as one of the top honeymoon destinations in the world. Despite attempts to market the island as   the Hawaii of Korea,   climatologically and geographically it bears little in similarity to the Hawaiian Islands in the U.S. The island offers visitors a wide range of activities: hiking on Halla-san (South Korea's highest peak) or Olle-gil(routes), catching sunrises and sunsets over the ocean, riding horses, touring all the locales from a favorite television K-drama, or just lying around on the sandy beaches. Although tourism is one of the main industries on the island, many of the hotels and other tourist areas are run by mainland companies, so much of the income never gets put back into the local economy. Also, since the attractions are geared towards tourists, many of the entrance fees can be hefty (although the locally owned and operated ones tend to be cheaper). Similar to Gyeongju and some other areas, local residents can enter most places for free or for a steeply discounted price.

Great day out doors. Many options of travel within the island (drive from mainland, rent bicycles, various motorized vehicles) making it really easy.Roads are narrow so personally would avoid driving. Further the ferries can only hold that many cars which means expect long wait times during peak periods.Many nice small eateries for coffee or ice cream along the way. Beaches are really pretty too and water clear though I didn't see anyone swimming in dec (winter).Only thing that I didn't quite like was the rentals were pricey at 70000 won for 3 hrs (two motorized bicycles and one two seater). And that was after some bargaining . The guy mentioned that it takes 45 min to go around the island without stops

Few hundred feet of road that makes you feel like your rolling uphill with the car in neutral.  Best is to begin at the start point from a full stop place the car in neutral and release the brake, the car will begin to roll very slowly and it appears that you are going up a slight incline.   I would not go out of my way for this... although I did.  If you have plenty of time or nothing to do because of rain then why not.

Even though my family and I stayed in Breeze Bay Hotel which is within 3 minutes? drive to the Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak) car park, we couldn?t wake up so early to hike up to the summit to catch the sunrise. Eventually, we were at the base of the Seongsan Ilchulbong at 10am, together with hordes of tourists and locals?nd the sunny weather.Getting there and fees: GPS coordinate/code for this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument site/attraction located in the east Jeju is 7830959. As the parking lots are limited, I suggest you drive (arrive) there early (before 9am). Parking is free.  The entrance fees are 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.The attraction: A non-stop no-rest ascent for a fit person takes about 30 minutes, but with my young children and with stairs-climbing not part of our daily routine, we took about 1 hour to make complete the 182 metres climb to the summit. There are several pointers that you may want to take note:(1)
address: If you can, go on a weekday. We were there on a Wednesday mid-morning and already it was quite crowded, so I cannot imagine what the weekend would bring(2)
입력주소: Wear a pair of good-sole and comfortable walking shoes and bring enough water to hydrate yourself (you could still buy water at only one place during the ascent)(3)
X: On a sunny day, you could bring an umbrella or wear sunglasses or a cap and preferably put on sunscreen lotion(4)
Y: Take note that the ascending trail or route is different from the descending trail or route, so do take lots of photos and selfies along the way. (5)
CLSS: Hike at your comfortable pace (although I understand that may not be possible when the tour guide requires you to be back at the bus within a certain timing) and do rest at the benches and the viewpoints or points of interest (e.g. huge rocks) whenever you are out of breath (give you an excuse to take photos and selfies)(6)
PNU: There is no need to bring a jacket or sweater unless the weather becomes chilly or windy or cold (e.g. winter) or you are hiking in the wee hours of the morning to catch the sunrise. In fact, it was scorching hot when we reached the crater summit at around 11am(7)
주소구분: When you reach the summit, remember to pose with the signage says ‘Top of Seongsan Ilchulbong 180m’We started the climb after the 4 bronze round inscriptions (one of them is ‘New 7 Wonders of Nature’) on the uneven rocky or bumpy uphill sloped path. After a certain distance, this sloped ascending path became one that comprises of proper (stairway) steps. Look for the signage “Ascending Trail” and continue your ascent. Somehow the last stretch is a steep climb on continuous stairway steps and with so many people behind you, you simply cannot stop to rest. But once you reach the top, before you have time to catch your breath, your breath will be immediately taken away by the breath-taking panoramic views! You could see the flora-covered 600-meters diameter crater with 99 jagged rocky spires that resemble a crown, in addition to the Seongsan town (village), Seongsanpo-hang harbour, Cheju Haehyop (Cheju Strait), Mount Hallasan and others. It amazed me when I considered the almost symmetrical tuff cone crater was created by the explosion of an underwater volcano thousands of years ago. Due to the barriers, all visitors cannot walk into the tuff cone crater.Of course, the descent was relatively easier along wider wooden stairways with railings. When near the bottom, there are two directions to take. Going to the left, you could ride a Jeju pony (Jorangmal), which we didn’t go. Going to the right (signage “Women Diver Performance”), you would come to a black basalt rock cliff and also to a place to see the famous female divers (Haenyeo). To the right too, you would come to a lookout point for Udo Island (South Korea’s second largest island)Comparing with the only other tuff cone crater that I have climbed ? Diamond Head in Honolulu ? I find the Seongsan Ilchulbong more challenging to climb but it offers more breath-taking scenery.  So don’t miss Seongsan Ilchulbong on your Jeju itinerary! Start the ascent early to avoid the crowd.
표준구주소: If you can, go on a weekday. We were there on a Wednesday mid-morning and already it was quite crowded, so I cannot imagine what the weekend would bring(2)

review: Entrance Fee is 8,000KRW but our driver manage to get some discount for us.The idea is creative and brilliant. Everything is made of glass and its really beautiful. You can't stop but keep taking photos in every part of the place.

Entrance fee is 10,000KRW.I visited during Spring and the place is so beautiful with flowers all around! Daisy, roses, lavender are everywhere. It's so breathtaking!The place is divided into 3 parts, and they take you to these places via train. The train will stopped at each stop and you can get down to visit and explore the places and get on to the next trip of train to get to next destination.Their ice cream is good too! Tasty and fresh! Worth trying.Good place to enjoy beautiful scenery. The air is so fresh and you could really enjoy your time here.We visited this place for like 2 hours.

Don't talk, just feel yourself on the walk way to clim to the top. Open your eyes and record the scene to your soul. It will treat your mind, very well. Don't forget your water bottle. Be careful when taking your selfie.

don't forget to be early for this and as this is privately owned attraction, the entrance fees is KRW6000 instead of the government owned ones at KRW2000. Wear comfortable walking or hiking shoes as it is a bit of walking towards the crater. Good place for photographs at the top and be   lost   around the pampas green field for dramatic photographs.
Cold, damp, slippery and uneven ground, but I loved it! Made many stops to look up and feel the side as well!

Circumnavigated this little island on a bike in an afternoon, and it was a lovely excursion. The older culture is still somewhat alive (weeding through the tourist stops), but even the bitsy coffee shops are endearing. Bicycle is the way to see this place, for sure!

A little bit hard and tired for people who don't exercise so much to climb up this height but worth it. Trust me, you can see almost of the island from the top of the mountain, feel the sea breeze and hear the wave sound. If you don't familiar with climbing mountain just try to go with the way down. There will be stair so you can walk easily. This way should be fit for handicap and elderly people too.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.

6 hours to reach the peak, but it was worth it! Start your trip early as you need to be at the entry point by 12PM in order to make it to the top as everyone needs to start heading down at 2PM (depends on seasonality)...Certain parts of the hike is tough, but the feeling at the top of the mountain looking over the lake, is speechless!

With a minimal fee of KRW10k one gets to kayak along the stream for 20 mins. The water is clear and deep. Each wooden kayak can only take 2 passenger with only one person rowing. The catch is the ticket counter is a distance away from the port. And the best time to go is on a weekdays. Weekends are usually crowded.

We went up at 6am in the morning to see the sunrise. With cold rainy weather the event was less romantic than expected but well worth and good fun for us. We went up with our 3yr old boy. The way up is very well prepared and suitable for children who like walking/climbing a bit. We carried out son partly and party he walked. Well Organised tourist attraction.Entrance fee is only W2000.Have fun!

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

Udo island is perfect for short day trip where you can enjoy the peaceful ambiance of the ocean while aboard a ferry.It may seem so plain and simple but for me it is perfect for a qucik romantic get away with a breeze of fresh air..It feels like the ocean is all yours...

This was really a nice long walk. Will advise to wear good walking shoe. The route was easy to walk just that when the wind come you can feel the wind blowing at you. You have to walk all the way up and you will be able to see the nice surrounding. It was really nice and we really enjoyed it.

This museum is located a short distance from the city center. However a taxi ride from our centrally located hotel only cost about 6000 Korean won. On the day that we went to the museum we were able to get free admittance because they had some special promotion though I think that the admission fee is very inexpensive anyway. We enjoyed the museum very much especially the special exhibit entitled ?쏞hoe Bu`s Diary: An Unexpected Encounter with China.??This exhibition will run from July 21 to October 4 2015. There is also a fascinating diorama of a Jeju village.If you like history and historical artifacts you will enjoy this museum. It?셲 well worth a visit.

The water park is ok. It would have been way better if you didn't have to pay extra for swim vests and extra for sun beds. So practically paying entrance fee doesn't mean you go and have fun. You are forced to spend good amount of money to have a good time.

The outlook has been dressed up and over designed. It looks like a candy house rather than a church. It is quite disappointed especially when you have been walking from a long way out there in order to move closer to it but it does not give you any romantic feeling at all.
The only value here I think is let the kids make their own chocolates. It's a funny experience. Apart from that  the display is a joke. Anyway  the entrance fee is low and it doesn't matter much.

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

Shinhwa Theme Park is unique in many ways.  First it tries to make its own characters seems as popular as Mickey Mouse and Spider Man - it doesn’t work but it’s great fun just trying to figure out who is who.  Second everything seems brand new - so it’s spotless and at the same standards as a Disneyland or Universal Studios.  Third - the rides are small but oh so knock out fun.  And there is rarely anyone there.  I don’t know if they sell a fast pass but there is no need for one because i don’t ever imagine it getting that crowded.  The food was quite delicious too - great offerings at multiple locations.  You can easily do this park in a half day and not feel like your exhausted or missing anything.  Like everything in Jeju I think they think they are expanding but who knows..  and as i remember the entry price is super affordable.  So this is really a great time for anyone with kids or who enjoys theme parks.  Don’t go in thinking it’s Disneyland though and get picky - just enjoy it for what it is...a bold effort to start something special and first class and doing very well right from the start.  It was a great day for me and my daughter and her two cousins.  Enjoy!
Romantic place to strolling with beautiful grass/weed around along the way to the crater. Took lots of nice foto :) Heard every season the grass have different colours. Entrance Fee : KRW2000
Perfect place for renting a bike and it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to paddle around the island. Coffee shops and attranctions along the way.
Paid a 1000 (or 2000?) won entrance fee and my breath was taken away by the beautiful sight! There was even a rainbow at the end of the waterfall... simply beautiful :)

Okay if visitor is kind of tea lover. Like being here for shopping which is not that extraordinary or the must spot. Just okay for the museum zone and cafe easy and relaxing tea field or area to walk but not that wow anyway. For food and drinks good but for cake and desserts I personally feel soso. For the shop and products' variety are good. Free parking on site.

Nice way to enjoy the history of korean lifestyle in the past and at the same time walk through some of the shooting locations of the popular K-dramas...great use of the massive landspace and attractive to both young and old...my little gal enjoyed feeding the goats and other lil animals in the village...
Located in the southern part of Jeju Island. It holds a lot of stuffed teddy bear displays. Entrance fee is cheap. Taxi fare from main city is around 30KRW one way.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.
