review: I've visited the original Da Vinci Museum in Florence in the middle of my school field trip many years ago. Since I visited fancy museums in that trip like the Louvre or Orsay  I never expected the Da Vinci Museum to be as good as those. However  it was one of the best places I've visited in the trip. Other museums only let people to look at the exhibits but those in Da Vinci was to be operated. I think touching was stronger feeling that looking. The memory is still clear.With the good memory from Florence  I also visited the one in Jeju and it was also great. I went there with my girlfriend and worried if she doesn't like it since it seems a bit for students and children. Anyway  turned out she liked its clean and pleasant facility. I think I like the one in Jeju little more since it is not in the middle of crowded city. Maybe because the one with me matters.
It's a Lava cave about 1 km. The walkway was very hard to walk because it's a lava rock. And it's wet because of the rain. It's OK. I didn't feel woww. If you have a free time you can go there.

It's 3000 Won to enter and it is mostly just a chocolate shop. They do chocolate making classes  if you are interested  but that costs an additional 10 000 - 12 000 won (sorry  I am not sure about the exact price. We asked  but I don't remember). You can use your entrance fee to purchase chocolate  but way not just buy chocolate somewhere else?

It was heavily foggy with strong wind when I went there. It rained too. We bought a raincoat for krw 2000. Entrance fee about krw 2000 as well. A lot of fog we could not see the caldera but we hiked all the way

It was a butterfly and insects theme park. Entry fee 9500 won. It doesn't display real butterflies and insects I think. There were just fake but they really did a great job by setting up for the exhibition. I really adored their creativeness to potray various human activities and historic scene by using insects and butterflies. The miniature were really nice. If you are expecting to see some real butterflies flying around you wouldn't see one :(We also went to mirror maze. This was superrr awesome! The maze was small but it really did made us feel excited to find our way out. Beware not to bump to those mirrors hehe.

It is located near seogwipo (southern region in jeju island). I stayed in value hotel seogwipo hence decided to pay a visit in the morning before my afternoon flight back. Just 10mins away from the hotel. No parking or entrance fee needed. U just need to trek 250m to come to the best photo spot. Overall worth paying a visit if you staying in seogwipo area.

If you want to see a bunch of boxes of chocolate from all over the world  this is the place for you. The 3000 won you pay to enter gives you a discount to what you can buy there so if you want to buy chocolate you won't feel ripped off  but you can buy the same chocolate in any gift shop for the same price. There are a lot of great places on Jeju. I wouldn't go out of your way to visit here.

I wouldn't go out of my way to see it but it is fun walking through the place. There are still some shops and a small waterpark/spa that only opens fully in the summer. Very quiet almost ghost town type of feel. Go karts are near by to if your into that

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

I totally missed the sunrise at this point despite setting the alarm at 4am. But the trip to the peak in the afternoon was refreshing enough. I feel that it has heighten my spirit to cope with what I always wonder. Hiking up the mountains has been what I love most. But seeing the end is really rewarding. I believe that the sunrise marks it all.

I know it is soon tiring waking up at least an hour before the sun is even up and then be driven all the way there. It could take an hour for some as it did for me but MAAAN WAS IT WORTH IT! Loved it even though I had climed the Mt Hallasan yesterday and my legs and feet were killing me I was so happy to see the sun rising from this beautiful location.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

Has serene garden  $3 entrance fee. They preserved the deceased artists study which was interesting. The photos had a rare spiritual feel to them. Out of the way  took almost an hour to get there from our hotel in seoguipo  be careful not to speed above posted speed limit - there were about 20 traffic cameras along the way and even saw two impromptu mobile speed camera setups.

Generally a fun and interesting exhibition due to the interactivity of the exhibits/3D photos. However if you are expecting a large variety of interaction you will be slightly disappointed. About halfway through the museum most exhibits start to feel similar. More enjoyable for teenagers-like crowds. Recommend about 1-1.5 hours for the whole museum.

Beautiful scenery! Take a relaxing stroll on the black sand beach. There is a hidden gem of a cafe called Terarosa and it is an awesome place to have a good coffee and just chillax away. The tiramisu is great too.

Admission fee 12.000won per Person. Free parking. Coffee and souvenir shop inside.I would give 4 points but this museum has no information in english at all. Although they advertise the museum with ?쐀iggest sex museum in the world?? so in my opinion the translation of information in english is a must. The admission fee is way too overpriced for not understandig everything. They do translate in chinese.By the way the museum is more funny instead of ?쐓exy?? Would just go here with friends not with a date because some statues/pics etc kill every possible erotic moment. XD

A group of us were actually trying to get to another location but stumbled upon this beauty by mistake. It is quite large and may consume 1-2 hours depending on how extensively you want to trek this. Good way to get out of the city without going too far or hiking an oreum. Had a really nice calming feel. Would recommend it :)

Yeah, this is a real village, whereby the Korean government had deemed it as a living historical site. The villagers are actually living there.You can get the Korean honey there for 40,000 won. A must get for you. Also if you had watched   Dae Jang Geum   drama, the daughter of the village head is one of the person giving the tour.And the way they greet tourist is unique. Experience it yourself. Not sure if there is any entrance fee as I was on a package tour and this was part of the itinerary.

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

What WERE they thinking of! The   museum   is a few glass cases with examples of bars/boxes of chocolates. The   factory   is a table where you can buy cooking chocolate and make your own. The only good news is that your (HUGE) entrance fee is refunded in the way of a coupon to use at the (VERY OVERPRICED) chocolate shop. There is NOTHING here. It's AWFUL.Buy your choccies in the supermarket and give this place a wide berth.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

Went here with a tour package bought from Klook. Entering caves experience feels great however, for it requires like 30 minutes walk to the Lava Coloum and you have to walk back (there is no other way out) so you need to make sure to wear comfortable shoes because the floor is uneven.

We would have never imagined that you can make so much out of a teddy bear. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and I would suggest it for any bear lover but especially for families with young kids. As for the Alive Museum, I would strongly advice to go there either in the morning or early in the afternoon. We visited it in the morning and it was a bliss, but my guts' feeling tells me the crowds in the afternoon must be a little bit more stressful to deal with.PS: Don't forget the Elvis Presley Show. Yes, it is kind of tacky but really cute anyway!

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We went in summer, so the waterfall was less impressive (due to less rainfall in summer months) especially the 1st waterfall... the water was beautifully clear... be aware the the are plenty of steps up and down... my mum gave up after the first waterfall... the second waterfall is really pretty but there is no way to get access to the water below (unlike the 1st) as the observation platform was rise high from the river below... everyone including the fit and young gave up on the third fall due to the tough & long steps and punishing summer heat... its definitely worth going if you are in the area... fees for admission

We walked over the bridge, it was very windy and we could feel the bridge moving a little which was quite scary but was really nice to get some air. The island was really peaceful and was a lovely walk around. Unfortunatly there was two children with their dad shouting all the way round, we could hear them from the other side of the island so we sat on a bench for a while to wait for them to leave. We went before sunset and saw the sun set, just be careful of mosquitoes at this time as we got bit loads while on the island.

We visited this place on a slightly gloomy day. This and the amazon green colours of the flora made it look like a mystic forest, something out of an animation. They say, walking among these nutmeg trees has healing properties, and eventhough I was sceptical at first, soon I could feel my nerves calming down. It felt like someone poured some sleeping powder on us. Oh and the smell! I've never felt such pungent yet clean fragrance in a forest before, it's truly unique. All those pretty colours and the distinctive smell of nutmeg and cinnamon trees makes this pathway a mesmerizing experience. The route takes at least 40 minutes-1 hour. There are some charming restaurants and coffee places before the entrance, and a huge parking lot. The whole are is beautiful.

We visited this area with kids ages 3-11. Easy paved walk through a beautiful scenic shaded walkway. The falls were breathtaking. We took our shoes off and soaked our feet at the end of stairs leading into the water. Ate an easy convenience store lunch when we returned to the parking lot before heading to our next destination of the day. 1,000won for kids, 2,000won for adults. Can?t beat the price.

We visited on a very wet day so it was good to be inside even if the inside was the lava cave.  The lighting is very low in the cave and the floor, made by lava flow is very uneven so close attention needs to be made to where you are going. Its one kilometre each way to the end of the public bit and you miss quite a bit watching where the feet go so not to fall over.mAn interesting place to visit but take a torch!

We decided to include this in our tour after feeling a bit tired from all the hiking up mountains and paths. It's an easy couple of hours, especially if you have kids, whom seemed to be entertained with every variation of dressed up bear. There is also an extensive gift shop, with, you've guessed it, lots of bears and cuddlies. The prices aren't exactly cheap, but the quality seemed good. It's a good way to slow the pace down if you are in need of a rest.. Nice afternoon out.

We book a tour on line from the cruise ship before we arrived at the port. The tour included a visit to Seongeup Folk Village.  There was an admission fee to the village.  There are several walkways around the village. The walkways are well maintained and there are no steps to climb.  There are exhibits our old building, farming and animals.  There are clean restrooms along the walkways.

Very pretty beach on a sunny day. The colour of the water is so beautiful. Nicely prep walkway all along the whole beach area. Lots of places for coffee and a quick lunch. We had dinner at a local eatery, the owner was nice and friendly.  He helped BBQ our black skin pork belly for us. So yummy with water Kimchi and beer.

This was a nice little excursion from the main island. Gotta take a ferry which means you need to head over to Udo early and be prepared to come back in the early evening as the ferry schedule will dictate your movement. There used to be a nice coffee shop halfway up at the base of the stairs to the lighthouse exhibits (October 2013). They had the cutest dog too but they were closed when we went back in December 2013. We took our car on the ferry. But you can also walk onto the ferry and then rent mopeds or four wheelers once you get to Udo so you can get around. I was thankful for the GPS in the car though because the roads are very winding, narrow, confusing, and I don't think are marked with names.

This underground shopping street is kinda cool. It has clothes, beauty products, a large number of children's stall, and no doubt impresses the many thousands of tourists that come through Jeju City every day. However, if you have ever been to Singapore, and experienced the underground warren of the connected malls on Orchard road, this will not in any way tantalize you. At best it will make you smile at the 1970's feel of it all ;-)

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

this is one of those strange Jeju adventures that's worth a quick check.  yes, just like they describe, it's a road which, when you walk down it, it feels like you're going up - and vice versus.  be careful, so you don't get hit by a car - but on your way to something else to do in Jeju, give it a go.  BTW, I  m sure kids won't get it - this is an adult thing, and I don't think I'd want my toddler walking down an active road.

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.
This is a cool waterfall. With 35 degree heat the splashing from the powerful waterfall was a nice way to cool down. Of the many waterfalls in Jeju, I feel that this is the best one.

This folk village which has a collection of 600 years old thatched roof houses built using the volcanic basalt rocks and passed on from one generation to another, showcases the unique culture of Jeju Island. The stone statue of Harubang called the grandfather of Jeju and worshipped as the protector of this island can be seen in front of almost all the huts.This village is still inhabited by the locals and one can see them practicing their traditional rituals including rearing of the Black Pigs.By the way ,Jeju is famous for its Black Pork dishes.There are also sites for holding special rituals like praying God for good luck and health, place where breast feeding women pray for lack of milk etc.Our Guide cum Driver Mr Kim Nam Joon (+82-10-4616-6650) not only took us around the village but also ensured we had a good time.

There is walk along the  nice promenade to get to this rock. It is hard to make out the dragon in the rock but Asians love strangely shaped rocks. In my opinion it was not so spectacular but the walk along the promenade is very nice, over nice bridge and coffee shops along the way.
There is an hour long boat tour that shows you many of the sights, but was the best way to see these falls and get pictures for these Hallasan weary feet.

The place is small. According to the guide (a man who lives there), that is his house passed down to him by his ancestors. He speaks English and some of our Malay language (impressive). It was very compact with the history of the island, culture, food, the roles of men/ women in Jeju, architecture, etc. He was a fun man with a lively way of presenting the information. I think it was excellent. Listening to him is like reading a small introductory chapter about Jeju. There was no fee collected, I appreciate that. However, at the end of the visit, he showed us some local products which we happily bought (the tea) because the children like it.
The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of   impressive historical sites   compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The day was dark, cloudy, windy with heavy drizzle. It gave a rustic feel to the little fishing village by the beach. There were two families there and a couple who were taking pre-wedding photos. If the above was a normal situation, then it would be a perfect gateway for writers and people who want to get away from the rat race.

The bridge is beautiful to look at, and provides a nice walk to an island that provides more opportunity to stroll near the water.? Big tourist attraction, and if you prefer staying away from the crowds, you may not enjoy this.? Great picture taking venue, and it doesn't cost anything, except a little workout for your feet and legs.
Since when did it became samsung ? The place spelling is wrong.! Anyway.. Nice to visit, entrance fee for adults 2500krw only and nearby is the folklore and natural history museum.

Sangumburi crater is a designated Natural Monument touted as the world's only flatland crater. The car park entrance showcases several large rocks from the crater such as the volcanic bomb and lava tree mold. During the eruption, molten rock flew from the volcano into the air and cooled into many exotic shapes. The area near the crater also contain several traditional Jeju graves - wide, trapezoidal stone walls surrounding the burial mounds. Visitors can walk around the extinct volcano crater rim, peer into it but cannot venture inside the crater pit covered with lush vegetation. The hills and Hallasan surrounding the crater is a picture of serenity and rustic greenery. Sangumburi is especially popular in autumn when the slopes are covered in Jeju?s famous Eulalia. Crowds and couples will be lining up for photos among the tall plume-like, silver grass swaying in the breeze. At a quiet spot, listen to the whispers of the eulalia dancing against the blue sky to add a pensive mood to the autumn romance.  Note: KRW6000 entry fee is quite expensive. Closes at 6 pm, except Nov-Feb closing at 5 pm.

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

Put your rented car on neutral going   uphill   and experience it. Mysterious probably because for most it?s a baffling experience having your car in neutral but going uphill, backwards or forward ? hands off the wheel and feet off that pedal. The place is on the way to Jusangjeolli by way of the Mount Halla route from Jeju town. 5-10 minutes (no crowd here) and you have covered one of the ?touristy? sites in Jeju. A woman attempted to see what would happen with a plastic water bottle placed on the road, nothing did.  Why would any vehicle with so much metals built into it got pulled but not a plastic bottle? Go figure. I have encountered a similar experience at a site in Saudi Arabia near Madinah which has a longer stretch for that ?mysterious? experience.

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Perhaps I've been in Asia too long, but I feel like a lot of these markets start to look, feel and smell the same. It was fun to walk through but I didn't feel like it had a whole lot to offer that felt special. If you're new to Asia, certainly worth a walk though I wouldn't go out of my way to come here.

Our driver/tour guide took us here on the way back to the hotel. Actually, he said it was his first time there as well. My 17-year old son and I felt the uphill rolling and it was a weird feeling. Not sure why it was doing it, but we saw some tourists pouring water on the pavement and watching the water rolling uphill. Many years ago, I took my son to a similar   mystery road   in Manzanillo, Mexico. Back then, may be he was too young to feel it, or may be I was a terrible tour guide, but this time he finally got it. So, it was fun for us to take the quick detour and had some laughs.  Oh, and it was free and there are road signs tell you how to experience the   mystery  .
Our cab driver brought us there on the way to loveland! Quite an interesting sight, no fees required! Do drop by if you're in the area :)
On the second day when i gave her my feedback about how she always silence and not really guiding throughout the tour, she snapped and her answer is “ this is my style “.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

Mr Kim, also affectionately known to us as Samchoon was introduced to us by a friend. Even before we arrived in Jeju, he was so ever helpful whenever I had questions about planning the day. He would offer the best ideas and try to accommodate to your requests as much as possible so that your day would be a breeze and convenient. He didn?셳 mind that we stayed almost an hour away from Jeju city and arrives early at our hotel to make sure our day starts off well. He actually does research and make calls for you and made sure that attractions and restaurants are open when you get there. He really goes to the extra mile to put a smile on your face! Mount Halasan is located in the southern most tip of the Korean Peninsula. The height is 1950 m, a young volcanic mountain. The scenery is lovely and unique. The climbing route is interesting and versatile. Stones, rocks, wooden planks, concrete and steps is what makes the path up to the peak Baengnokdam. It takes 4 hours one way to reach the peak and about the same time for descent. Only one canteen is available where we can get coffee, chocopie and noodle boxes. The vivid autumn colors brought joy to the heart. Thoroughly enjoyed climbing this mountain

Massive ground. A full walk about will take 2hrs easily. Even though all the stones look similar after an hr, it's a very effective way to understand the folklores of Jeju. Cheap entrance fee of only 2K won.Some places near the museum are still under renovation when we were there.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Lots of fun! Dozens of tame affectionate kitties greet you at the entrance. Cute kittens too! There is a toddler playground with toddler-sized shops play kitchens, jungle gym, rope course, teeter totter? al kid sized. Plenty of great spots for selfies of all kinds. The maze is very tall and take a good 15 minutes at full sprint to wind through and capture stamps on the way to ringing the bell. If you are feeling silly or have small a children with you, this is the spot!

Just another market but in a different city. Similar in most ways.However, a distinct difference here is the huge amount of Jeju oranges (tangerines) on sale. Not just here but in other markets in Jeju too.Also it is common to see roadside trucks & makeshift stalls selling oranges - everywhere.Jeju is well known for its oranges , probably it's the season now. But they aren't exactly cheap despite the abundance of supply.We went to a nice Tangerine Orchard Farm right here in Jeju, where we paid 5,000?? admission fee per pax. And one can eat as much oranges as you want for unlimited time while at the Orchard.After which, every pax is entitled to pick/bring back 1kg free. Great experience & deal.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It worth a look just to see the beautiful coastline of the Island.Most of the rocks come in various heights and sizes shaped like hexagons and if you look at certain angles, they can take on various animals etc.The black lava colour offsets against the outstanding sea and coastline.These cliffs are very similar to the Giants Causeway in Ireland with a pancake rock system but on a much smaller scale.It was crowded the day were there and we assume it is the same most days in the summer months. So a lot of people were snaking along this narrow path around the cliffs and we needed to wait our turn to see over the barriers.There are a few stallholders near the carpark (fee charged) selling fruit, souvenirs and the local home made confectionary similar to nougat.On the way out you can go to a park with some gardens and perhaps a museum type building.The hours vary seasonally however it is the standard KRW 2,000 entry fee for most monuments around the Island.Place it on your ?must see? places to visit here just for the dramatic coastline and on a rough day you may get some blow hole situations with the force of the water.Enjoy your visit!

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? It depends. If you're the kind of person who couldn't be bothered with science, optical illusions and whatnot, you'd be better off checking out the snack shops nearby, observing the other tourists and their interesting behavior, or skipping this place altogether.However, if you've always been interested in physics and seemingly unexplainable phenomenons which you know are actually explainable, give yourself an hour or more to thoroughly check this place out. Photography lovers may also deem this place worth their time.The bottom line? If you're heading to another tourist attraction (e.g. Hallasan) and it's on the way, and you have time to spare, feel free to check this place out. Otherwise, don't bother.

It falls into the sea,  very unusual. Wear walking shoes if you're going there as there are uneven rocks leading to the fall. Saw several kids slipped & fell down. Painful indeed.  After purchasing the entrance ticket,  there's a walkway that leads you to the fall.  But the last 100m or so is uneven rocks surface.  It's nice to walk nearer to the fall so you can feel the mist.  Refreshing.

In general, Jeongbang Falls is a nice looking waterfall that plunges into the blue ocean. Entry fee is low too at 2000 krw. However, this place is way, way too crowded with tourists. Chances of you getting 'photo bombed' is 100%, unless you risk your safety by walking over the rocks to the point near the waterfall like most tourists did. Hence, it is not recommended for travellers with walking difficulties.

If you love Alice in Wonderland you will love Maze Land.  The mazes are fun to explore and make you feel like a kid again. Also, the statue garden and rose garden are worth a look.  A really fun, unique way to spend a day on Jeju.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

I walked Routes 6 and 7 on 23rd-24th Oct 2017. The distance was 15km and 18km respectively.The weather was perfect - sunshine and cool breezes. These 2 routes are reputed to be the more beautiful ones. There are a couple of picture-perfect waterfalls and breath-taking shorelines along the way. 2,000Won per entry is charged for the waterfall. Along the way are small fishing ports where one can get to taste local seafood. There are small cafe along the way too, where one can sit, relax and taking in the beautiful scenery. Coffee is +/-4,000won. As I was staying at the starting point, from the finishing point I took taxi back It costs about 8kWon. Oh yes, there are clean restrooms every 5km or so. Just a little minus point, the blue & red ribbon is not easy to be found in urban area. So try looking for the blue line on the tar road.

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I hadn't heard all that much about this beach and I was really pleasantly surprised, in a big way. The beach itself is fairly wide, and the sand is great. Moreover, the water is crystal clear, and the water is warm, so if you actually want to go swimming, it's a great spot (unfortunately I didn't have enough time). But this place is more than just a beach. Right behind the beach is a nice little town so it is lively and you have shops and dining options there. On the beach you have a nice fancy  coffeeshop that is perfectly located, directly overlooking the sea. Add to that the rocks on each side of the beaches, as well as the small mountain to the East, so this place is not only perfect for relaxing, but also for taking pictures.

I had always wanted to go to a maze park, and finally I did in jeju :) it was a small maze but enough to make us excited to find our way out. The entrance fee is 33,000 won for adult. In front of the entrance, there were lots of cats and quite tame too.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

Forget what it's called because I can't see a dragon head even when I tried to go around the different angles of the rock formation. However, this is a cool place to visit, to have a stroll on a lazy day since it's near the airport side of jeju. Probably around 5000 won (4 USD) to take a cab from the airport. There are small food stalls nearby, and dunkin donut too for some coffee. There is a nearby tourist center where you can ask if they can call a cab for you on your way back to your hotel or anywhere. They don't have booking fee which is excellent.

For the last day of our Jejueco tour, the first attraction we visited in the morning was Jeongbang waterfall. Situated on a high cliff by the sea, Jeongbang waterfall is the only waterfall in Asia to fall into the sea. Admission fee is 2,000 won for individuals and 1,600 won per person if you are in a group of 10 or more.When we finally reached our destination, to actually get up-close to Jeongbang waterfall, we had to walk down some (more) steep steps and make our way over a field of rocks/boulders. It was a pretty slippery (and uneven) walk, so make sure you wear footwear with good grip. But the walk was worth it: the sight of the waterfall emptying itself right into the sea which makes it a pretty unique and amazing (since we don?t really have such waterfalls in Singapore).For more photos and our Jeongbang Waterfall experience, do check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jeongbang-waterfall.html :)

Finally we met a Filipino tourist guide here in Seongeup Village. She can speak english very well but of course we used our native tounge/language so she was able to explain to us very well the history of the village and Jeju as well. It's only from her where we learned that the famous Jeju Black Pig used to eat human poop/dung (but that was circa 1940's or earlier).  We also learned from Grace (name of the Filipino guide there) that Korean women, during the early years, were the one who work for the family while the husbands only stay at home. Sad to hear that. =/ We also learned about the history of Stone Grandfather Harabong as well as the various symbolisms used in Jeju.When in Seongeup, make sure to try their Omija, an herbal drink made out of fermented berries. It can help cure acne, headache, kidney problems and good for diabetics. Kinda pricey but worth a shot. They also have other herbal medicines which you can try. As we all know, Koreans, especially their ancestors, are used to taking medicinal plants so I guess they are really credible enough when they say that this or that plant is effective for healing ailments. Google the benefits of OMIJA.By the way, this is also the place where the famous Koreanovela Dae Jangeum (Jewel in the Palace) was filmed.If you happen to visit Seongeup Village, ask for Grace as a guide. You will definitely learn a lot. And oh, we get to check out old korean houses as well. ^_^NOTE: I think there are many communities within Seongeup village but ask your guide to specifically drop you off at the community where Grace is. No entrance fee as well.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..

Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.? The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.? The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.? The calm music playing enhanced the experience.? The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.? Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.
Although the weather wasn't perfect for a visit this afternoon, however, it hasn't spoiled a positive impression. Lots of tourists anyways, and it leaves a good feeling of connectedness with nature.

A bit out of the way so had to take a taxi. The bar gives you your taxi fee x2 in free drinks which is great. We arrived early so wasn?셳 many people but didn?셳 matter as were so many bar games to play for free.Filled up later on and ended up being packed. Lots of entertainment and games with prizes. Jump rope, dance competitions etc

Pyoseon Beach might not be the most picturesque beach in Jeju but it's vast and didn't feel that crowded even in the middle of the high season. Because of the large sand area exposed during low tides  it can be quite the hike to the water then. But the low depth of the water and the large sand area makes it a good beach for children. As with most other popular Jeju beaches  there is a good selection of restaurants nearby.

On Happy New Years Day, We(my family including me) have hiked Mt Halla. we expect cold weather and much snow but weather was quite similar to spring so small amount of snow there. at first frustration but as close to destination I feel happy about small snow and weak wind. If Mt halla was normal, I couldn't bear that situation. I usually hate cold weather. I post some pictures. plz enjoy these.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

I thought we were the minority few that would brace the darkness and hike up. Boy, I was wrong. When we reached the Sunrise Platform, some 100-200 people were there with us.And when the golden egg yolk broke the horizon, there was a chorus of 'ooooooh' as people gasped in awesome wonder. It only took 2 minutes or so for the sun to fully risen from the horizon.If the ticket counter is not open for sunrise hikers, please do not wait. Get in and begin the hike. Bring a flask of hot coffee and enjoy. Sorry, no food allowed in the park.
We liked the place and very well keptWe spent a good three hours here and had snacks coffee and icecream (twice...) All good. easy to park too

We got an ATV (40000KRW for 2 hours) and rode around the island. It was really fun and you get to explore the whole island. There are small little cafes where you can just park your ATV and pop in for a coffee and a cake. The water is amazingly clear and blue.

We first went to this museum 7 years ago and wanted to visit this place again hoping there is some new attraction.  Sadly nothing has changed and lesser crowd.  Entrance fee is not cheap and I don't think its really worth to go unless you love teddy bear. We are out by 1 hour and kids wasn't very excited with the same display.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.

This is a very lovely maze park with a beautiful garden! We absolutely enjoyed the hour we spent here. The garden is well kept and we were given little bags of cat food to feed the 40 cats scattered throughout the garden.

This is a pretty big park that has a little bit of everything from history folklore and stones.  I had to convince my friends to check it out and only won when i told them it was like 15 minutes from where we were staying.  However they both were quiet happy with the decision since it was empty and just a lovely walk through nature with some great smells.  Even the trash cans are made out od stone pits.  I thought we would only go for like 30 minutes but ended up being there for an hour and a half.  Other bonus is that for the month of may there is no entrance fee!

The village is huge explaining about the cultures of jeju folks. Plenty of photo shooting corners beautiful flowers farm.There is also a shop renting korean traditional clothes (hanbok renting) where you can wear the clothes and walk around the village for photo shooting. the price is reasonable (comparable to those hanbok renting shop in jeju city)estimate to spend 3 hours there.youth and kids got discount for the entrance fee (do bring passport along)is a must visit spot if you come to jeju.

The parking is free . Entrance fee was 2000W per Pax. You first descend about 5 minutes to a blue pond with the first waterfall . Beautiful and stunning . Then you proceed to the second waterfall about 10 walk . There was a third waterfall but it was about 40 minutes walk so we decided not to do that one . A five minute walk brought us to a bridge  which would bring you to another route . Overall expect to spend between 1-2 hours here .

The aquarium is good and English-friendly (so you know what you're looking at). The show at the end is aimed at kids and solely in Korean but as it's mostly visual that's not a problem. Families can definitely spend a fun few hours here. However the admission fee is excessive (40900 won for adults at time of writing) especially when most of the other main attractions in Jeju are either free entry or priced around 2000 won. I think this one ticket cost me more than all other entrance fees during my 5 day visit to the island combined. If you aren't visiting with children I suggest giving it a miss.
