review: Personally I find this place to be one of the most undervalued sights in Jeju. Mokwana represents the historic administrative center in the oldest part of Jeju City. The place is not large yet has a lot to show with stories at every corner. It takes only about half an hour from the airport and it took us about an hour to get around once inside. They have nominal admission fee (~ 1.4USD) and it was worth. The only complaint is that some of the labels for exhibits were provided only in Korean.

Out of our surprise no entrance fees needed when you visit Jeju Folk museum. There was a guide that told us about their culture and was a nice experience for us and even the kids. The village was small but a nice encounter. An hour is more than enough.

one of my destinations in Jeju recommended for green tea lovers. Green tea ice-cream is excellent can spend 3 hours there to deeply understand the cultivation processing and taste of green tea.  More you can find Innisfree house in the Museum.  Feel relax feel the nature there~~
Nice place but not really impressed with it. Pretty small place and take less than one hour to complete my visit.  Once is enough. There is entry fee to the park
Never been to such museum before so it was a very fun experience. Spent about 2 hours here taking tonnes of pictures. Feel like i'm 15 yrs old again. A must visit for the young at heart!
Nature lovers find this place a most relaxing n peaceful place. You can spend number of hours without anyone. Go n feel the nature. Best place!

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

Love Land is the place i visit and having so much fun in jeju! entrance fee w9000 per person but seriously worth it cos place is huge with indoor and outdoor. outdoor with all the sex pose statues very embarrassing while walking around the park. but i really do enjoy! its cute and some sexual knowledge >///< visit during January spend about 2 hours plus in the park. i believe can be more but due to weather is super cold we couldn't stand the windy cold we left right after round the whole park. basically is 80% outdoor and 10% indoor + 10% indoor souvenir shop.

Jusangjeolli are stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju Island. Jusangjeolli Cliff was formed when the lava from Hallasan Mountain erupted into the sea of Jungmun. There is a admission fee and parking fee to enter this place. We reached there by car the other day and it was an hour journey from Seogwipo city.

It's fun about this place. Entrance fees 12 000 won per person. There's is a show every hour about 15mins each show. But one thing need to highlight is  the explanation are all in Korean words. So for foreigner like us may have difficulties on understand the instructions on the activities. But so far I very enjoy. Is good for indoor visit especially during raining day.

If you just wan to spend for few hours while waiting for your flight. Here the good place. Entrance 8000KRW.  A small area block up for your big luggage you will have locker for your shoe. Once you enter inside you will find a long locker to store your belonging. It can fit in a small backpack.  Take a spa relax and rejuvenate before go for rest room. There are a lot ppl go there for overnight stay even it is weekday perhaps just their culture. The living hall area and sleep place rather to say it's hot I will say is steaming. If you kind of person can't stay for hot this might not be a good place to sleep for you unless you are very tired. You can take blanket from the counter you pay for your entrance fee. Where the pillow just look it from any empty room

I visited this place since my hotel is directly opposite it and I had an hour to spare before my flight home. This is the former central government office from 1392 to 1910. The compound consists of 7 buildings with signages in English. It was quiet and peaceful there as I met less than 10 visitors during my visit. Entrance fee is 1500 won. Toilet facilities available.Tip:  One can wear the traditional costume and take photos with 2 figurines for free. It is unmanned just help yourself. It is located at the left corner of the entrance building.

Great place for nature lovers to soak in multi themes and explore the Hyeopjae & Ssangyong caves in one location for admission price of KRW10000. Park is wheelchair friendly and is a great place for friends and family to spend a few hours together. The park does not feel overly crowded as it is spread over 80 acres. Visitors still enjoy tranquil surroundings even though the park is crowded.

Admission fee: 9k each person. Went about noon time. It is located near Believe it or Not museum and teddy bear museum. We spent about 3 hours in this musueum as we took really a lot of pictures here...but at the end you will be so tired with all the postures of taking the pictures! We gave up taking some pictures near the end :PAt the start there aren't many people but more people start coming when it gets later. Go early if possible. Else it will be difficult for you to take pictures and you have to waste time waiting.

A wonderful hour of Korean/Mongolian drama with beautiful horses and very talented Mongolian riders.Had a chance to pet and feed the horses before the show.Great acrobatics.Would be good for all ages.

We really enjoyed Udo. It's a small little island located about 30 minutes(ferry ride) off of Jeju. We got to the island with only about three hours before the last ferry was going to leave, so we wanted to pack in all that we could. First, we got some peanut ice cream. Then, we rented bicycles and tooled around the island's coast. It was beautiful and several times as I took in the sights, I kept thinking,   How cool is this? How many people I know will ever get to have this experience?   It was a neat feeling to be exploring a quaint and little-known spot in the world. We found a little beach and cooled off before heading back to the ferry.
To do after Hallasan hiking. Very good place to feel relax and quiet for one hour! In case you feel hungry, go to the hotel next to it they have a grocery!

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This is a really interesting place to visit. I have never seen any similar rock formations as the ones that can be seen here. If being in the area and for us who have an interest in nature and science, this is a must see place.It is very well organized with stair, walking paths and information signs.There is a small fee for entering and there are opening hours that must be considered.

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!

The road brings you to an altitude of 1100 m close to e Mt. Hallasan which with 1900 m is the highest mountain in South Korea. They have built a walk with wooden planks that brings you to nice trees without getting wet feet. The walk takes about one hour when taking Pictures, if you rush it is only 20 minutes.

The museum has a lot of teddy bears (e.g.   Goong   or   Princess hours   teddy bears, etc) well protected in a glass boxes. A total of 3 levels in the building, displaying different kind of teddys and you can buy some souvenirs from the ground level. At the grond level, there are also teddys which you can take picture with (e.g. Steve Jobs, Psy, etc).Outside the building, there are some other teddys which you can also take pictures with. It would be fun if you love teddys but if you are not, it would be quite boring. Nothing much you can do, other than taking pictures and buying souvenirs. However, it still worth a go if you are curious about the variety of teddy bears being displayed inside. The admission fee is around 8,000 won (if i didn't remember wrongly).

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The entry fee is abit on the high side, but if you love gardens, plants, nature, and especially flowers, it’s worth every penny. My absolute favourite place to visit in Jeju. I love flowers so we spent around 4 hours here. There’s a huge variety of flowers, and the gardens/areas are very well laid-out. Besides the greenhouse, there is also an area outside where all the different-themed gardens are (Korean, Japanese, French etc), there are about 12 gardens in total I think, and all of them are really beautiful. I think this attraction is still relatively new, as I could still see gardeners setting up the flower beds and so on. But this also means that it’s not crowded yet and there are relatively few tourists compared to the other attractions. Flower-lovers, this is a must-visit!

Taxi took us here as part of a few hours tour.  It's a pretty waterfall, but I thought Cheonjiyeon Falls was more impressive with 3 layers so if you are nearby, it's worth going, however, if you only have time to go to one, I'd choose the latter :).  Both have small entrance fees per person.

Seriously, just go UDO island to experience a different feel as the island is quite small. I managed to complete a circle with my rental vehicle within 1-2 hours. There's quite a lot of spots that you can get down and walk. (fuel will drain quite a lot as there's quite a number of up-slope)

Rent a bike (costs about 10,000 KRW / 10 USD for 3 hours) to go around the island. It took me only 2.5 hours to go around with quick rest at one of the coffee shops (about 20 minutes). Take your time and enjoy your ride on Udo!

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

Our stay in Jeju coincide with the operational day of one of the biggest and oldest traditional market in Jeju - Grandma Market which runs on days that end with 7th of the calendar month. There are lots of other smaller scale traditional markets which are opened on different days (e.g days ending on 5th, 2nd, etc...) thru out the island but we were told that this is the biggest.There is also an area which are designated for elderly ladies aged 65 and above whereby they are not charged any fees for selling there, hence, the name of Grandma Market.Lots of things can be found in the market, from plants, to snacks to clothings to housewares. We bought some fresh ginseng, chilly flakes and also fresh gingko from the market (after tasting some that were steamed and sold as snacks), The gingko there is different from those that we get in MY (most imported from China). Their is more creamy in texture and rounded as compared to ours.Overall, quite an interesting walk for an hour or two if you're looking to buy some of foodstuff.

Our family has visited quite a few aquariums but this is the first one where we've seen some adorable otters. Adorable! Facility is beautiful clean airy-feeling.Tanks are well-kept it appears so my guess is that the sea creatures are   happier.   The aquarium is just the right size for anyone to finish in less than two hours.  What's also nice is that it's right next to the ocean.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Not a big forest and you have to pay a small fee to enter, a quick hours stroll some pretty trees not much else to see though.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Loved it. Great cycling route. 16km can be done in less than an hour. But take a break to enjoy a coffee or some delicious food and just enjoy the food. If you want to test out future tourism, take one of the available electronic scooters.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.

It took us more than an hour to get there. The wind was so chilly that you could feel your fingers freezing up when you take your gloves off to take photo.  But it is absolutely worth it !  The rock formation,formed layer by layer from lava erupted long long ago is so mystic & original. It's like touching rocks that are a million years ago.  Come dressed warmly in comfortable shoes  if you plan to walk along the coast as it is very very cold, wet & slippery. Nevertheless, not to be missed if you are travelling to Jeju!
It is really amazing to see these formations.  Small fee to park and see the formations, but still super cheap, and well worth it.m you can see it all in a half hour.

It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot.  It is about 40-45 minutes drive either from Jeju Airport or Seogwipo area.  You need 1-2 hours to go around the complex and the museum.  Opening hours: 0900-1800 hrs.  Closed on first Monday of the month unless it is a holiday.  Entry fee: KRW 5,000.  It should be a MUST in your itinerary of Jeju Island.

If you're a fan of teddy bears, then you should visit this place. You can probably complete this in 1 - 2 hours time. There's a outdoor park with more pictures to capture. Didn't really change much as compared to the first visit few years ago.. You have to pay an admission fee to enter, which i can't really remember but it's not expensive.

I was staying in Booyoung hotel (next to the ICC - international Convention Center) and had a few hours to walk around. About 5-10 minutes walk from the hotel I entered this park where they made me pay a very modes fee to enter. Much to my delight I got to this fantastic rock (actually lava) formation, which was definitely worth seeing. If you are at an event in ICC do not miss the chance. While there, you may want to visit the Botanic Gardens and the Cheonjeyeon Falls, both within walking distance (about 30 minutes from Booyoung). For the Cliffs you may need only 15-20 minutes, plus the 5-10 minutes to walk there..

I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.

I saw all 3 waterfalls near Seogwipo and I liked this one most. It is an only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean (sea). It is really big and it gets pretty crowded, so if you want to enjoy it without a lot of people taking photos go in the morning. There are opening hours and small entrance fee, so check it before going. Really nice  and big waterfall worth visiting.

I found this museum really interesting. I knew a little about Hanyeo beforehand but this gave me a much more detailed understanding. The exhibits (consisting of genuine Haenyeo clothing, tools and equipment alongside dioramas, videos and various documents) are well laid out and the accompanying explanations and labels almost all have high-quality English translations. I read every word and it took me a little under 2 hours to complete my visit, which considering the entrance fee is only 1100 won is excellent value for money. Recommended, especially if you are already on the east side of the island.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).

I am traveling with my 79 years old dad who has weak knees. When our driver brought us to yongmeori beach, we have no idea what we are in for. Because of my dad, we chose to enter the beach on the left entrance and exit by the right entrance which we heard is the opposite direction of what most people would do. From the entrance, we had to walk down a very steep stairs which led us directly onto the beach. Honestly, the walk down the stairs was a bit dangerous as there was no railing or any safety measures. Despite collecting entrance fee, there are no staff around if you need help. That said, the scenery was stunning. The natural formation of the rocks was beautiful and the water was clear. For a popular tourist destination, this is also one of the cleanest I have been. You don?t see any garbage around. I hope anyone who plans to visit, continue to keep this place clean. As we had to walk slowly, we completed one round of the beach in over an hour.

Highly recommend visiting Dongmun market! The market has plentiful, and affordable fresh meat, seafood, as well as Jeju-only snacks, beverages, restaurants and dried food. For a small fee (depending on the store, around $5 for 9 Kg), food including fresh meat and seafood can be shipped from Jeju to mainland Korea. Shipment takes about a full day. I have tried this option for fresh pork belly and abalone and both arrived the next day fresh and ready for consumption.Parking around the area is a bit difficult and waiting for an available spot does get frustrating. Parking garage fees around less than $3 for a few hours.

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.

Entertaining Mongolian horse show. We caught a taxi here as it's not easy to get to by other public transport. Impressive expert performance by the young horse riders who did some amazing acrobatics on horses. The Park's website is in Korean and the show was all in Korean but we managed to follow what was going on!  The horse show is on 3 times a day. After the show, kids can have fun riding a horse or driving a swing car (7 minute ride) or go kart (not sure of the minimum age for that).  Need to pay additional fees for each activity.  Worth spending a couple of hours or half a day here.

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said ?sure?.  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn?t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. A place to go if you want to relax and have a nice walk or if you are really interested in history and stones..

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!

It is easy to access the fall for those who dislike climbing steps.  It was only a short distance from the entrance via some steps.  Nice feeling to get up close and personal to the fall however just gotta beware of wet ones which at times can be slippery.  Smaller rocks tend to move when you are stepping on them so be careful.

i have visited the Seongsan in Udo. I think Seongsan is a must go place because it has average difficultiy to climb up (108m). It's named as one of the new 7 wonder natural places. reasonable entrance fee applied.

We saw many people taking photos around the waterfall. It's not the tallest nor grandest waterfall so I'm not sure what's the fuss about.Entrance fee is only 2K/pax. It's a short climb back up from the waterfall, ie very suitable for family and elderly.The rocks around the waterfall are rather pointed so please watch out while taking your selfies.

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.

This is quite possibly the most beautiful spot on the island-- definitely worth the small entrance fee (I think it was about 7000 won for my family of 5). There are some fairly serious steps to get down the cliff, and then to actually get close to the falls, it's necessary to climb across a bunch of small/medium rocks. Most people will have no problems with either, but for someone with knee or foot problems it could be an issue.The only thing I didn't love was that it was SO crowded. It was impossible to get a decent photo without someone walking into the frame, and several times we were actually shoved off of rocks as more and more people tried to crowd in. It would be great if they would limit the amount of people allowed down at one time.Other than that-- a great experience that we definitely won't forget.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

Our 70 year old tour guide could climb these rocks to get here. The Grand Canyon of Jeju. Whilst it was breathtaking, I couldn?t help but constantly call out to the kids to be careful of the slippery rocks. There are life rings hanging on the cliffs but let?s be realistic. With currents that strong, if you fell into the water, the current would crash you straight into the rocks. We went early morning when the tide was out but could feel the tide level rising. Our guide wanted to go further as he said it was more spectacular.Make sure you go with good gripped sneakers and a jacket. You are on the edge of the ocean after all.

Loads of people/tourists! But still is a site not to be missed. Need to climb up steep and narrow stairs towards the peak. For people who are afraid of heights, do note that you might feel extremely insecure as the surrounding though spacious might looks exposed.

Is worth going if u have young kids and a husband/wife who enjoyed looking at vintage cars instead of young woman (:p). My kids enjoyed driving the cars and they were issued a license with photo after the 10mins ride. Although they say no phototaking but trust me, phototaking opportunity are plenty once u r out of their sight. Read that there's an outdoor area where we can feed the deer. Unfortunately it was raining shortly after we were there. Hence didn't manage to do there. This place is very near to the ossulloc green tea museum. Easy to swing over after the visit to ossulloc. But beware to check weather. There's a unsheltered slope uphill from the entrance area (remb to bring enough umbrella for whole family in case it rains). My hubby only brought 1 from the car hence he needs to go bk to the car and climb uphill again just to pass us the ponchos and umbrellas). :P
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

I choose to stay near to the peak so it only took us 5 mins to walk here. We didn't managed to see the sunrise as the weather was a great challenge. It was extremely windy and cold in the morning. Thus we came here at noon time. When we reach the foot of the peak, I could see that the whole peak was full of people climbing either up or coming down. The entrance fee is cheap, it cost only 2000won. The scenery was really beautiful, it worth coming here to take a look at the natural beauty.

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls consists of 3 waterfalls. Such a nice turquoise water. There is an entrance fee to enter this place. Make sure you have some energy because you need to climb stairs to reach each point. There is a bridge called 'Seonimgyo Bridge', meaning 7 nymphs as there has an arch carved on the side. This place open from 8am to 6pm. We came here late in the evening in a rainy day but the admin staff were so nice to allowed us to enter but with time restrictions.

As we couldn't enjoy so much autumn scenery in Seoul, Mt Hallasan in Jeju is the best spot to get revenge..haha..it is due to most of leaves are already changed their colour compared to in Seoul. The parking fee is KRW 1000 and we just enjoy the beautiful scenery from the start point of jungle trekking area as we are tired enough to climb the mountain :PThere is free wifi available and some restaurant in case that you need to fill your empty tummy.. :)

When we came around this time there were abundant hydrangeas and a few other types of flowers. Unfortunately it can be very crowded especially where the lanes are small and everyone is fighting to take a picture there.The entrance fee is quite expensive too which os 8000??for an adult. All in all only go there if you enjoy looking at flowers.

What is offered at the Glass Museum does not justify its 9 000 won entrance fee.There is a garden with glass flowers  glass birds  and other ornaments. The displays are dull and although they probably took a lot of time and effort to make  the whole place seems like something that would have been more interesting 15 years ago.

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !

We went as we read many positive feed-backs from families and we were not disappointed. All our family enjoyed it to the last minute including also the garden outside and the cafeteria.My only strong suggestion would be to do it either in the morning or early afternoon (enter before 2.00pm) as when we were leaving (5pm) the crowd was definitely bigger than when we got in. We walked back to the main entrance to still have a look and by that time it would have been almost impossible to take a pic without being interrupted many times by 'passer-by'.

We regretted going to this place. The entrance fee is 5 000 won and they give you a 3 000 coupon to use when you buy their products. There is nothing to see except display of chocolates from different countries which is available at a supermarket. Really it is a waste of money and waste of time.

Haenyeo literally means, 'Women of the Sea' and this museum pays tribute to the historical significance of this dying profession.  Solely carried on the backs of women on this island, these incredible ladies have carried their over 400 year old craft into the 21st century where instrumentally built the economic foundation for many of the Jeju natives.  Mothers who passed on their skills and knowledge of the sea to their daughters ensured that this lineage would endure the centuries of time.  However, as the world faces rapid changes and economies - the Haenyeo divers are slowly becoming a ghost of the past.  Recently recognized as an UNESCO intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016, tremendous efforts are in place to preserve this historical tradition.  A bonus of a visit to this museum is a trip to Sunrise Peak where there is a traditional Haenyeo performance.  (admission fee required)However - enroute to Sunrise Peak is the opportunity to meet a handful of Haenyeo divers!  What a thrill to visit with them in their modern 'bulteok' - warming huts.  Of all the sights of Jeju - this is perhaps the one that represents the very backbone of this amazing culture!This is definitely a 'must see'

Going to the Jeju Folk Village is like taking a trip back in time.  I can only imagine how hardy the people of Jeju were in order to survive.  You can see replicas of ancient houses, learn about the different social classes...even play dress up....my mom dressed up as a queen of the Joseon Dynasty and I dressed up as a kisaeng (not fun with my big feet) and we got our pictures taken and had a good laugh.  For those of you who have watched Dae Jang Geum, the folk village is not to be missed.
Glass everywhere, but nothing special. Only to pay it a visit if you have extra time. The admission fees around 9,000 Won (~USD8)

Getting close to the waterfalls looks easier than it seems. However, that adds to the thrill of getting nearer to mother nature. It is tricky manuvering around the wet, slippery & sometimes unstable rocks & boulders in cold weather. Many a times, you find yourself balancing precariously on the boulders or have your feet stuck between the rocks as you slip or slide from the smooth rocks. You will also find visitors around you lending you a hand to help you get back on your feet. Such spontaneous camaraderie !  For the young & agile, it is fun watching them jumping from rock to rock, like Tarzan in action.  It is a thrilling on the rocks experience not to be missed !  And you get rewarded by the beautiful sight & sound of a great waterfall!

Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! We gave a 4 stars owing to its mysterious element.The 100m stretch of road appears to be uphill but it is actually and in fact downhill. This can be done by several experiments. E.g. pour water on the road, put a bottle of water and it will roll towards the   uphill  , walk or run backward along this road; you will feel the difference whether it's uphill or downhill.There are a few stalls selling food so you can eat and think how this is possible.

All the waterfalls were spell binding, gushing with water even in summer (April) However, 2 are fenced for safety reasons and the third one has a board warning you against swimming. You can, although, dip your feet in the cold water at the unfenced one. At the first one, you can make a wish and throw a coin into the shallow end of the fall. And if your schedule isn't packed, it's a great place to sit back and read a book.

It is one of many museums in Jeju, and it's dedicated to Teddy bears. It is full of its history with all the teddy bears from all over the world. All of the ancient teddy bears is well preserved but with relatively minimal background story. Some of the information are written only in Korean, so there isn't many interactive attraction here. There is also an open garden with a few sculptures on it, a Lotteria restaurant and of course the store. The merchandise there is quite expensive and we didn't buy anything. The entrance fee when we came there is 8000 won, a little bit expensive, but quite worth it.

I came here after visiting the nearby Jeju Loveland. This museum has 4 floors. First floor is the Welcome Stage, which traces the history of computers and hardwares. Second floor is Open Stage, which depicts the history and development of computer games. Third floor is Hidden Stage, which showcases how computers changed and expanded our everyday life. The Basement 1 is Special Stage, which is used for special exhibitions.Second and third floors allow visitors to play old computer and arcade games such as Space Invaders, Galaxy etc. Playing these games bring back fond memories of my younger days. Before leaving, I headed to the cafe at B1 and ordered the keyboard waffle for its novelty, not cheap at 12,000 won.Admission fees 8,000 won. Note it is closed on Monday. Worth a visit if you have half a day to spare. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Jeju Loveland.

Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

Udo feels like more of an island than Jeju itself, because it is much smaller and rural. You can hire a car, golf buggy, cycle or simply walk around this scenic little island. Very short and cheap ferry ride from Seongsan, so add this into your trip to Sunrise Peak.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is the most eastern part of Jeju Island and has the same terrain as Punchball. When you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, you can see the beautiful sea and clear sky endlessly, and when you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with a cool breeze, you feel good. Also, there are many tourist attractions nearby, so it is convenient to move around. In addition, there are many restaurants that cook braised kingtail fish and roast caught in Jeju, and there are many unique and delicious restaurants around. I recommend that you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with your family at least once.

Not as touristy or crowded like Sunrise Peak. Walk to the crater was on the milder side, not too much steps.Leisurely romantic walk pass the fields of silver grass (graminee) which can only be seen late September to November. Some parts have swings for you to sit and enjoy the breeze. The crater was covered completely with vegetation and the nearby green hills was a picture of serenity and you feel removed from urban cityI wouldn't mind coming again. Near ticket area, there's a stall selling the sausage sticks that were flavorful and yummy.

In April, the waters are not warm yet, so sitting here is quite beautiful and not crowded. A sense of both oceanic drive close by at the coastal road, a coffee deck behind and an almost cove like open white sand isolation which will probably disappear in peak summer

As we didn't manage to watch the Haenyeo performance at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak - we decided to visit the museum instead. The museum is quiet, probably because it's quite off the center.Fee: 1100 won per personStart with a short film on the history of haenyeo, the museum has 2 floors. Display of Haenyeo's life, their tools and equipment and other deep sea fishing and farming information.A particular section caught my attention - a digital map showing where the Haenyeo went to make a living, leaving behind their home town, to make more money like Hokkaido, Russia...There is also a section featuring the Haenyeo anti-Japanese campaign, which is very much inspiring.

It's one of the biggest traditional markets and has many shops so you can buy almost anything you need.I usually go for seafood and vegetables which are fresh and low cost.  I particularly like raw fish (Sashimi) which can be purchased by fish (shop will catch a live one and cut sashimi while you watch) or pre-packaged (around $10 ~ 20)The market also has many street food, like spicy rice cake and pancake like dessert.It's not as clean/convenient as a shopping mall but has a lower price and more cultural feeling.

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

A traditional market which sells a lot of Jeju Oranges, jeju chocolates, seafoods (e.g. Fish, abalone, etc), pork, orange juices and many more.. the price of the chocolates is the same as any other stores outside. The price of the other products are also reasonable.You can visit this market and have a feel of their largest traditional market in Jeju. I went there with my friend before 8pm but some of the stores had started cleaning and preparing to close the shop. The market is open till 9pm (if I am not wrong).
You have to go down to get the waterfall. Entrance fee is 3k won. Crowded with people. The waterfall is quite beautifull as it

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.

Was expecting more. I think once you are in Jeju you just feel like everywhere will be magical but when you reach places that give off mediocre vibes you tend to get disappointed. So don't come here with high expectations.This place is too touristy and honestly I'd rather kayak in Bali (actually water rafting there is awesome) or in Laos. Or even in Kota Kinabalu or Thailand.

Visited this place in Feb19 and was quite appalled by the treatment of the animals. The rabbits were allowed to roam within an enclosed area accessible to visitors. However there is no one monitoring that the rabbits are treated properly. The living conditions of the animals are filthy. The absolute horror was the black pig show. What's so entertaining about forcing terrified black pigs down a water slide?? Tasteless entertainment with no educational value. Paying the entrance fee of 13000won per person  I would expect some of it to be channeled to upkeep the living conditions of the animals. The blooms in the park were alright with spots for Instagram pictures but nothing spectacular.

The rocks were quite slippery and could be dangerous for young kids and elderly.  Overall a nice place to visit even if you only have 30mins to spare.  The entrance fee was cheap.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

Take the step down the cliff and you will find yourself a unique waterfall that is near a sea. Usually you will find waterfall upstream of a river not close to sea. The force of the water is quite huge so you can feel the breeze when you nearer to the waterfall. There are other cultural stuff nearby the waterfall as well.

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill

Manjanggul Cave was a thoroughly interesting experience. The structure itself is awe inspiring and feels like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Be prepared for water droplets plopping on your head! It was a bit chilly when we visited as well.

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.
Just beautiful and breath taking. The waterfalls give you such peace of mind and clarity. You can feel the beauty all around you. Just enjoy the sites and the sounds.

Jungmun is a sand beach and it is perfect to visit. The water is so warm and there are waves which are fun to swim in. A minus for the changing rooms where they charge a fee for what? It's not a fresh area to change in I would rather change on the beach or the bathrooms. The bathrooms were also not so fresh. If they could improve these things it could be better for everyone.

There are houses of all kind of people like craftsmen usual habitants prisoners and etc. Also some photos of women divers from Jeju. Its probably better to use a guide since all information is in Korean and  there are several traditional korean games on the ground that need to be explained. There are several shops inside: some craftsmen shops like wooden crafts and caligraphy and also souvenirs and some local candy. We enjoyed our walk here. Its nice park that also got some ponds and small waterfalls. Its quite big one also. fee amount is 10000 krw per person.
Even on a cloudy rainy day it is still beautiful.  The waters were clean. There are restaurants and cafes lining the beach.  Free fountain to clean feet.

Beautiful waterfall near the ocean. The water is icy cold. You can't swim in all the waterfall in jeju. Too bad as the weather very hot and I really wish can dip inside here to cool down my body. Entrance fee of 2000won.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

You need to purchase a ticket at 2000won each and then take 130 steps down a flight of stairs to get to the waterfall. Comfortable shoes are recommended if you want to get closer to the waterfall. It is advisable to use your feet to check for the stability of the rocks before stepping on them as there were some loose and moving ones amongst the pile of rocks. The rocks nearer to the waterfall are wet so be careful if you want to get even closer to the fall. The waves crashing on the shore are also rather strong, so be more cautious if you?re moving nearer towards the shore.

With a 2,000?? fee, this waterfall is well worth a visit! It's a short walk down from the parking lot - not hard to get to at all. You should, however, wear comfortable and supportive shoes because you need to balance on rocks in order to get close to the falls.
Well, another water fall, again! haha, its nice, give it a try if never bit there. Photo look nicer tho, actual scene you might feel that the waterfall is not as big as you imagine.

Visited this place which is really a lava tube rather than a cave.  It is about 1 kilometer from end-to-end.  Inside the tube you can see different rock formations created by the lava flow, among them the turtle-shaped rock at 600-meter mark.  It is cool inside the tube and water is dripping everywhere.  It is recommended that you wear appropriate footwear while taking this tour as it could really be slippery and some areas are not so well-lit.  Maybe this is intentional to give the place a more realistic feel.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

This places is one of the a must place to visit in jeju. i think its getting more popular after 1bak2il had recording here, so many tourist and their fans come here to visit. Admission 2000won, you also can try raw seafood while watching the waterfall. and you can feel the cold water sprinkle on your face.

This is unlike most Korean beaches because most Koreans go to the beach right up the road. Lots of space to play and relax in the sand and in the water. Beautiful sunset. Emerald water. And white sand. Shallow water is great for kids. No parasols (umbrellas), and no commercial building stores  - nice! Doesn't feel like a Korea beach at all. Tip: Park on the right near the camping area. That's where you will find a nice quiet sandy spot next to natural sand dunes. Wow!

This is my favorite as the waterfalls and the blue water coupled with mandarin ducks swimming and moving around, I really feel like I'm in a fantasy land or living in the fairy tales movie that we used to see.  Highly recommended for photography and relaxation!

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This fall flows right into the ocean. i liked this one better than the others in the city because you can get into the water at the base of the falls and get your feet wet. also there was a tent with some of the famous diving grannies selling raw seafoods. i highly recommend trying this as it was a truly unique experience. the raw plate cost 20,000w which was cheaper than most of the nearby restarunts.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

This beach was ok. The sand felt nice and there were plenty of people around to make it feel like a happening spot, without being overcrowded. You can easily grab a bite to eat nearby. In my opinion, I would go here for a beach day if I really wanted a beach day, but I wouldn't plan to go there as a must- see beach.One thing I noticed about the beaches in Korea... The Koreans dress more modestly than at almost any other beach in the world ( including Dubai) ... Most seemed to be covered up with water - type shorts and shirts vs. the typical shirtless man and bikini clad women. It's something you should consider !

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The waterfall is beautiful, it gave me the urge to jump in it under the hot sun. There is a entrance charge for that. For those who are from places like Malaysia, Philippines where surrounded with beautiful waterfalls, you might don't feel like spending money just to see this waterfall.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000\ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.

The place was hot and mosquito infested honestly due to the Aug weather. However if you have enough repellent with you, this is a good place to walk over, sit on the rocks, chill by the waterfall, feel the cold clear air and pose till you are tired.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

The best we have seen in Jeju.Though the water was a bit too cold for us to swim, it's great for wading during low tide.You can even rent clear bottom kayak to paddle around.There are lots of convenient stores, burger and coffee places and other local eateries around there.Definitely worth a visit.

Ofcourse is a nice waterfal but i think it was a little overrated. Like everyplace att Jeju you have to pay a small entrance fee (2000 won) and then its just what it is, a waterfall. For sure you can take some nice pictures but thats it.

Nice wiev, cold water. Not that big but worth going in hot summer days. Easy to reach, wide car parking. Entrance fee than stairs to reach sea level. Fun for kids, if you dare:...... get into the water!!!

My friend took me here because he said it was beautiful. Indeed, a waterfall next to the ocean is as picturesque as it gets. We took some dope pictures and dip our feet into the cool and refreshing water when I saw my FIRST EVER DOUBLE RAINBOW. Life is good haha

Located in Seogwipo, it is the only waterfall in Asia that falls straight to the sea. You may cool your feet in cold river water (or even the whole body if you brave enough). There are 3 women divers who offer to try raw seafood for 20 000 won.
It's not an easy feat, walk about 2 km round trip filled with stairs. There is a 2500 Won enterance fee. 3 waterfalls and a huge bridge

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

i like this waterfall that connect to the beach but i dont understand why they have to take entry fee for that because its really close to car park.other than that, all good. beautiful and huge waterfall cool you down.

Entrance fee is 2000 won which is not that bad but again, the waterfalls are not that big. There are other falls on Jeju with greater magnitude you should consider instead unless you stay in Seogwipo as this is literally just on the outskirts of the city.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .
Beautiful beach with crystal clear water, white and smooth beach sand that you may ever feel from the others beaches.

A really beautiful sight to behold! Its a short but steep walk down to the waterfall, with an entrance fee of 2000 won. You wont be able to get too up close and personal though - the waterfall   guards   get a little touchy if you get too close to the rocks that are wet.
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.

We travelled on a rare rainy day in Jeju, but June, our tour guide, made our trip happy and smooth with her professional arrangement, detailed introduction of the scenic spots, fluent English, sharing on Korean culture and her personal experience on how she feels about Jeju. I am particularly impressed by the guided tour she gave us in the Manjanggul Lava Tube, her intriguing story of haenyeo and their livelihood and our hiking experience at Seongsanilchul Pong. In as short as a day we have seen most of what lies in the northern and eastern coasts of Jeju Island, felt for ourselves the beauty of the natural landscapes and understood how inhabitants of this island have lived since the last century. It was an amazing travel experience and we give credits to June for the nice private tour.
Went here with our two sons (8M and 4Y) and it was very interesting and a bit cold.Cheap entrance fee being in Jeju.Easy to park and restaurant in front was OK.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

We decided to pop over to the maze park as we were visiting mangajul lava tubes. We were greeted by a ten to fifteen cats basking in the shade. It seems like the owner loves cats. That was a great treat for my cat loving family. The maze itself was great fun and especially if you are in a group. Not very difficult but not as easy. We could easily go around with a stroller though there are a few steps. Has a small cafeteria for icecream and coffee. Overall great fun.

Larger than anticipated with lots of interactive displays.  Bring a camera and be willing to be funny in a crowded space.  The indoor attractions were bettrr than the outdoor ones.  There is a coffee and snack bar with a lounge in the middle that made a very nice break point.  Easy to get to and staff was nice and helpful.  Staff spoke pretty good english and even called a cab for us.
It was easy for me to relate and discover the true beauty of Jeju. The natural hills and nature was this late photographer's muse. It opened my eyes to actually feel Jeju.

Car parking near the beach is a nightmare... too many cars... cars parked improperly...  but at least it was free.I really like this beach as it was very clean... although there were a lot of people the beach can easy absorb them due to its size... lots of cafe and coffee shop nearby I arrived at low tide and it wasn?t suitable for swimmers as the deepest point (next to shark nets) was only up to my thighs. So I was disappointed by that.. maybe it?s a lot better during high tide....Another negative is you have to pay to use the SHOWERS.. 3000w for adult and 2000w child.... shower gel and shampoo is available... for a price
A must visit to this attraction . Entrance fee is 2000W . Short and easy walk to the cliffs . Expect to spend around 30-60minutes here if you want to take photos .

We rented bikes, very old bikes... and toured the island.  It is easy to do so and there is lots to see.  We arrived at 11am and saw the Udo women divers out collecting seaweed and shellfish.  By afternoon they had seaweed drying all over the island.  There were lots of picnic spots, coffe shops, and other forms of getting around.  This is a great day trip from Jeju or you can stay on island.Not alot of English spoken but did run into a couple of people in coffee shops that spoke English.  We didn't mind.  All signage is in English so it is still easy to get around.

This is one location where you do not have to worry about bad weather, actually I would recommend going here on a day with rain and wind since then you can actually experience the force of nature when the waves hit the cliffs.Easy access, parking (for a fee) and you can walk along the shore line on a board walk (sort of).

This forest has a nutmeg tree that is over 826 years old.  We enjoyed walking on the paths that weave through the forest.  Beautiful trees, flowers and lovely singing birds.  We saw a snake and loved the fresh smelling air.  There is a small store selling drinks and snacks and a small coffee shop.  No gift shop.  The paths are well maintained and very easy to walk on.

The museum has many airplanes on display and also an outdoor area where you can walk into the planes. ? Very well done, lots of information and displays. ? Hands on activities instructions are only in Korean, but easy to figure out. ? A steal for the 10,000 WON entrance fee.

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.
Quite pretty and relatively easy to get to. Granted you have to go down some steps to get to the falls. Entrance fees are KRW2,000 per person.
Part of Hallim Park. Your entrance fee to the park grants access to this site. Nothing special, but already included, so check it out. Easy to go thru, even for the older less mobile people.
It's very scenic and a good location for photography, it's near to town and easy to reach. The entrance fees is affordable

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.

Good sight seeing place and jungle trekking. Wear sport shoes for easy walking if you plan to walk   round the sea  . Weather was just nice for walking in April. Crossing the bridge and standing there watching the big sea was feeling awesome.

Drove to Udo island on a self-drive trip and took ferry from Seongsan pier in the morning. It was easy driving in Udo island - it was a tiny island and there weren't many tourists around. While strolling up Udo-bong, saw a group of physically challenged students brought to Udo-bong by their teachers. A very heart warming sight. There isn't anything much to do yet if you are interested in exploring the nature (like I do), it is a good place to spend a morning just feeling the nature.

A pretty long walk over some decent grounds and some stairs to get through the entire cave. Its a little chilly down there so bring some easy to shed clothing. Really a vast and large cave, not something you get to see very often elsewhere and for the small entry fee... you cant beat it.

We visit the tea farm on our trip at Juju island. We were impressed with how green tea become a nice farm only to grow tea but a nice place for coffee and food. We tried and love the green tea Icream. Will return with our daughter :)

Our guide bought us here as my young daughter is with us and out guide thought this is something that would delight her and he was not wrong. We spent about ten minutes feeding the deer and went off. Didn’t really explore the place as we were rushing the complete the days itinerary. Didn’t really learn much here except that we are suppose to release the food once the deer bites it or the staff will get very worried.

No fee to enter but honestly not a museum! Just a place to eat green tea ice cream and other yummy green tea products. Plus buying Tea. There is a tea farm behind it which is pretty cool to see. I went when it was raining so beware the slippery. Innisfree next door has better food and drinks in my opinion.

Went there to see how the locals interact, to feel and absorb the local vibes. Nice to see how the locals live and behave. Pleasant to stroll through the stalls. Went there in the morning and saw many fresh local produce like seafood, meats, fruits, vegetables, household items, clothes, bags, shoes .......just about everything. We also saw many stalls selling street food - bungeoppang ( fish shaped bun-filled with sweet red beans) , eomuk ( fish cake ), hoppang ( steamed buns) , tteokbokki. ( stir fried rice cake) , gyeranppang ( egg bread ), dak-kkochi (korean chicken skewers ). Had a great breakfast on these streetfoods. We also saw lots and lots of hallabong too. Very juicy and sweet these Jeju?s iconic mandarin oranges. Not to be missed one must try the hallabong fruit juice and hallabong icecream. We also bought some local korean snacks , kimchi and souvenirs to bring home.

Very friendly and helpful to all of us, he is also very kind in recommending us the must-go attractions and even getting us discounted entrance fee around Jeju. He even brought us to the delicious restaurants, introduce us to all the different food around Jeju, gifted us some rice cakes. Would gladly recommend to my friends or anyone going to Jeju ?몟?뤍狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘

This place is great for enjoying a sunset with coffee, so relaxing. The place around 700 m from the Ramada plaza, make its perfect place to release your stress after meeting and enjoy the beautiful panorama. Its also many seafood restaurants there. Just perfect!!!

The stacked cliffs of Yongmeori are beautiful! This was one of my favorite sites in Jeju. It's a very windy walk but in the summer, this provided respite from the humid heat. The rocks are uneven and bumpy, so it is a good idea to wear sturdy shoes.You have to pay a small fee but it's very much worth it. Along the walk, there are women selling raw seafood meals for 10,000 a pop. It's a very simple set-up: plastic stools and chairs, some garlic, gochujang, and soju if you wish.

It's for kids.  Good to take pictures at a distance, but when watching closely, I got the feeling that things are not that clean and new.  The cafe is particularly messy with no one clearing up the food leftover or liquid on the floor, table sticky.

If you like Hello Kitty, this is an interesting place to go. a 2 storey building converted into wholesomeness of Kitty everywhere. The cafe is nice too - but you need to pay for entrance fee to the museum in order to get into it. The food is average, but presentation is what people are paying for. Definitely a nice place for tonnes of photo taking. It's suitable for any weather. I went when it was snowing outside - so it's nice and warm inside.

As coaching parking and no admission fee needed.You could plan to visit within 30 minutes.  Don't try the seafood stall down there as not worth to do so.  Indeed, there is not much to see except popular place for group tourists guide.

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.

We were mesmerized with the glass art. Such detailed work! The route made it easier to walk and enjoy all the glass art. Admission fee is 11 000 won. There were also one part of the park that showed glass palace  but we end up walking about 10minutes and no castle was in our sight  quite disappointed. P/S: you can find cute fridge magnet of jeju at the end of the souvenir shop. There were only 1 000 won for one. Very cheap for a fridge magnet I think.

We discovered Jeju Mokgwan (the Governors historical admin center) when we drove past it then walked to it from our hotel. Of all the places we visited in Jeju City it was our favorite. Most of the signage included English translations of how Jeju-do was run in the past. The buildings are well restored pieces of art. Very relaxing.  There were also ancient games for children. The venue seemed to be set up mostly for locals for who this venue is free. Foreigners enter for a nominal fee.If you found this rating beneficial please click the helpful button.
The walk from the harbour to the falls is pleasant and flat if a bit crowded on some days.  Well worth the entry fee though.

Quite a big museum and there are many fun and interesting spots to take photos. Entrance fee is around 9000 krw per person but you can spend a good 40mins to 1hr in the museum walking around and taking photos. Very good place to visit. Not too sure how accessible it is by public transport as I booked a driver for the day.

People say if you want to know about the place you must understand the culture. So this place are all about it. They show the history of their lives the culture the utilities the household etc. A large place to walk to reach at each point but worth the knowledge. You have to pay the entrance fee just before entrance gate and they will provide you with the map/pamphlet according to your language.

Nothing really special. 1000 (for youth) and 2000 (adult) admission fee. I wouldn't go there if it wouldn't be close to my guesthouse.Maybe it would be interesting for families with small children. But for a walk i would rather prefer going to the beach.

Nice path all with light for evening walk all around the small island with places to sit here and there. An expensive suspended bridge with wood floor goes across  may be a lot for a 30 minutes walk.There is no fee to cross but next to the entry you can buy a trip in submarine. Well! Just nice walk when you stay close by.

Nice feeling as you walk around the quaint little village which are still lived in by residents.  There was a free tour given and tour guide spoke English. Ended tour with a little presentation of the products sold by the village.  Good for a 1/2 day adventure.
Luckily no need to pay for entrance fee. Go only if you like tea. Can take a nice walk outdoor other than that nothing much.

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable.
