The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.
it's a long walk through the end..but it feels great when you are actually walking in where the lava used to pass.the fee is not expensive and this is a place not to miss when you are in jeju
It?s a lovely place. Calm and peaceful feeling. Walked around and enjoyed the serenity of the place.

It was raining when we arrived and spent a fun afternoon at this museum posing with the different paintings photos and displays. Unfortunately the rain prevented us from taking photos with the various outdoor displays. Wheelchairs are available for loan and help make the experience more enjoyable for my mom who has difficulty walking. Entrance fee is KRW9000 per person. The Alive Museum covers a wider area and has more/different displays than the Trickeye Museum in Seoul.
If you got 45 mins to spare and like some shade and a beautiful walk then this is for you. Annoying Usd 2 fee but thats life.

I fee bad giving it 2 stars but few places like this in Asia explain things clearly enough to us Americans. It feels kinda new in places hard to understand and it would have been better to demonstrate or offer a live walk through visit explaining how and what and why you do things at each stage.
Good to walk around and enjoy a nice meal or have a cup of coffee! Only 5min from the airport by car.
Bring your jacket: is super cold as walking into cave. Entrance fee is KRW 2000. Wear sport shoes: cave floor is slippy.
Beautiful but packed with tourists. Lots of walking but definitely worth it. Probably the most crowded place in Jeju but you won?t feel claustrophobic here.
apparently this is starting point of one of 'olle' walking course.we only walked little but if you feel like serious walking Oedolgae seems very nice point to start. very beautiful costal line here.

A short walk from the parking lot to the falls. Walk a little further onto the rocks to get even closer and feel the cool spray from the falls and nice breeze. Relax and watch the waves break on the rocks. Beautiful! Not to be missed!
A nice n serene place to stroll n relax. It took about 30minutes to walk around the reserve. Definitely worth the KRW2000 entry fee.

2000 won fee and well wooden path for tourist. Wind can be very strong since at the open sea and you can imagine the conditions in bad weather. If you like geography this is very interesting. Otherwise still a good place for some photo and walk in the south of the island.

We were at Seongsan Ilchulbong in the afternoon before we went to Manjanggul. It was a god decision as it was a brief respite from the scorching sun.That aside, this place is itself a gem. Well maintained and interesting facts have their own boards for the visitors to read. Light jacket is highly recommended if you don't like cool places. Temperature is similar to if you blast your AC unit in your room. Very nice. Wear good shoes. Slippers and heels / platforms not recommended although we saw several girls wore them. You'll be walking on solidified lava. Hence, the walking surface is very unkind to ill-equipped feet. :).Overall, very good experience.

We brought our 3 young kids and two elderly mothers to the Manjanggul Cave in late Nov, and it was quite an experience descending into the dark and cold cavern.  It was lit sufficiently to walk, though some areas could be a little dark and wet.  The kids sure had fun, until it got a little boring for them after 500 metres. The entrance fee was reasonable, not expensive.
Walk into a 3 storeys building. Gift shop, 3D theater, Hello Kitty Cafe and all sorts of Hello Kitty. Good fun place to explore, feeling happy and young again.

Visited with wife, it was not in our schedule. Didnt want to head for west without any of memory in northern place. The place seems to be just a town park not more than that precisely so they dont ask for parking fee or any tolls. Not worth to visit if you expect more than just place for walk
This was worth the entry fee. There is a nice walking tour of the   museum  . It was interesting to see all the glass displays in the forest. We really enjoyed the walk through the exhibits

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn?t find some key sights.

This is a real village with households living inside, opposite from folk villages built in museums. In fact, the people live there are mainly the haenyeo (women divers) - there is a museum for them in the east coast of Jeju. There is no entrance fee, so the village depends on the sale of souvenirs, basically the blueberries fermented drink and the organic skin creams. A volunteer will assist you to walk around the town, which is very helpful. A site note is that it is often used as a movie set, for example for the movie entitled Dae Jang Gum.

The visit to Bijarim Forest is a relaxing visit with a closer touch to the nature, feeling calm and peace. The trees looks aged and birds chirping, soft wind blowing. There are many locals walking or jogging in the forest during my visit. I would love to revisit it again if I visit Jeju again.

The beach itself could do with some TLC from the council.   There is a lot of debris which washes up daily onto the beach and along the coastal walk. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.

Stayed by Hyeopjae beach two nights, wish we stayed longer.Lovely place with a real local feeling, many caf챕s and restaurants around.Large and free car park.Don?t miss the beer battered chicken with beer by the walk down to the beach, opposite to the foot cleaning bath

One of the best UNESCO place. Worth it to come here and visit this place. We spent approximately 50minutes here included walking and taking photos. The addmission fees is ??2,000 per person still affordable for me and the rate still the same as we went here last year. The parking space were spacious with numerous parking units available for visitors. Gentle reminder, please be cautious on your steps as some of the areas are quite dark and jacket is a must to wear to enter this lava tube place.
Nice walk around to see different carvings of stones which we took lots of picture with. Not spectacular, but nice to see. There is a small entrance fee.

Nice place to go for a walk through the fields. The   museum   itself is not much and very little in English. The tea shop is OK with great but expensive green tea ice cream.The best bit is the other   Innisfree   shop and coffee shop in the grounds. Nice range of teas and coffees and interesting snacks. Inside and outside seating available. There are also stations in the shop to shape and   flavour   soap - if you buy the $15 kit that is. instructions on the supplied Ipad in several different languages.

Korea can feel very touristy and materialistic. Udo is the antidote to this. A beautiful, small island... with stone fences and perfectly kept fields of rye. Cute cafes and stone beaches. You can walk all over or cycle or drive your own rickshaw. Picturesque and less changed by tourism. I wished I had spend 2-3 days here instead of Jeju.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.
its better to discover the place in summer, but enjoyed the cold and excitement, walking around feels better

In my opinion, there are two world heritage sites that visitors to Jeju must visit. One is Manjanggul Cave and the other one is Seongsan Illchubong. Manjanggul Cave is unique as it was formed by lava movement thousands of years ago. It provides an insight into Jeju's geographical structure. The temperature in the cave could be chilly, so bring a jacket along. Visitors to the cave usually walked for about 2 km to reach the end, where photos with a large stalactite pillar could be taken. Other features in the cave include lava formations that look like elephant feet, turtles and book shelves.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you are interested in caves at all, this one is unique.  Easily accessible, this horizontal lava tube demonstrates the vocanic processes happening over 100,000 years ago.  Cool, wet and accessible with helpful descriptions in multiple languages and little anthropromorphizing of geological shapes.  A quick visit taught us a lot....and our 7 and 10 year old kids enjoyed the walk.  Modest fee.

if you are a nature lover like me, you should not miss this while you are in Jeju. Be ready to walk for 1 km and get prepared to experience some cold with dark which gives you an awesome feeling to enjoy the cave more.

I visited this place on October 23 2020 on my trip to Jeju Island. It was marbelous! So beautiful everywhere! Spirited Garden in Jeju is a beautiful place to relax, walk through and contemplate. It also has a healing buffet with healthy, tasty and pleasant meals for visitors. Contemplating the garden, I got inspiration and relax feeling. In the papers they say that the Spirited Garden is a symbol of Korean spirit: pioneer spirit and progressiveness, perseverance, and ceaseless endeavor.
I tried walking and rolling in car to feel the effects of such claims... no luck, felt cheated... at least the kids had fun.

I think it really depends on what kind of traveler u are. Some people might find it boring, some people might find it cool. I love it. I've never been in a cave nor a lava tunnel so for me it was a new and exciting experience. The cave is huge, wet and super duper cold, colder than outside in fact and lit up enough to see where you're walking. It's nice to see and feel how hardened lava looks and feels like. Walking into Manjanggul's huge cave feels like a scene from Prometheus.. Awesome!

I have a deep love and appreciation for the artist Lee Jung Seob. The museum itself? and the neighboring art-walk is a great tribute to the artist, but the exhibition itself does not do the artist that much justice. They have a great selection of his smaller works from the earlier periods but they do not house his bigger, dynamic paintings that he is known for. This visit would be a great place to take the family as the entrance fee is very manageable. The museum offers a closer look at the artists' context and life story rather than a display of his most prominent works. In short, a brilliant artist but not the best exhibition space/display method.

I bought a ticket which included access to all 3 museum buildings for 16 000 won. The museums are within walking distance of one another. A map as well as an audio guide is available. The   abandoned   buildings gave it an eerie feel that I thoroughly enjoyed. I was surprised around every corner and turn - the whole experience felt very dreamlike. I loved it.

I am really amazed and really love walking inside the forest you will feel delighted very clean and green trees, smells good and you can relax and breath well. Bijarim Forest-Is a group of about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old. They are 7-14m in height and 50-110cm in diameter. This is the largest nutmeg tree forest in the world. In the middle of the forest is an 800-year-old tree, called ?Ancestor tree of the Bija trees.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

For those who are interested in geology as my family is, this is a fascinating, and not too difficult, walk through a lava tube created by the molten lava. Worth a visit and the entrance fee is extremely cheap. UNESCO heritage.

Entrance fee 5,000 won and free for senior and disable as this place is not wheelchair friendly. Thank God my aunt could walk a little so those part that cannot be pushed on wheels.... she had to walk slowly..

A short walk to these falls - low ticket price at the entrance and then about 100 steps down to the base of the falls - quite rocky and need to watch the step - fortunately we went on a day without many tourists. Could feel the refreshing cool spray, nice when in the sunshineI love the fact there?s no littering here - helps maintain the natural state

You definitely need more than 5-6hrs to explore this beautiful island. Last ferry which leaves back from Udo is 6pm so kindly plan your day accordingly. We were there only for 2 hrs so took a bicycle to explore this little paradise.  Views and trails on this island are amazing with a lot of food options available. My recommendation is to rent the little car to drive around if you are short on time and its easier to go up the slopes in the car . The ferry ride is also not very expensive up and down from Udo.
What a beauty! Cant stop taking pictures while doing Olle trail. Took about 6hrs. Please do not forget the sunblock if you come in the summer. Locals are friendly.

Went in the autumn and was absolutely worth it. I took Gwaneumsa trail up (a bit boring) and Seongpanak trail down (spectacular). Leave early - I went at 6am as summit closes around 11 - 12 depending on the season.
Well maintained boardwalk along the coastline. Small stalls selling misc items. Not too crowded and there's even a small swimming hole on the east end of the trail
We went this trail up and can recommend it surely for everyone who is in doubt of their stamina. It was a steady elevation with nice stops on the way

We went here as per the recommendation on Tripadvisor. We wanted to go to Udo island and then come to see the sunset on this peak.since the ferry to Udo was cancelled due to rough sea and strong winds we had to change our plan and come to peak right in the afternoon.Since it was overcast and cloudy weather we could hike easily to the top. the 360 view from top is breathtaking.hiking trails is good. You can see the black sand beach and also see the jeju fishing lady show.

We visited Yakcheonsa Temple on our Jeju Olle Trail Route 8. This temple looks delightful because of its architecture and beautiful surrounding scenery. The views from the second floor were amazing! We even had a chance to ring the bell and make wishes here! A recommended place for photographers to get vivid pictures. You can also experience a temple stay activity in this Buddhist temple.
We took the easiest hike trail and climbed up about 1.3km.It was tiring but worth the climb because of the splendid views from the top!! You can see the city and the Halla mountain.

We rode most of the Olleh trail routes by bike and it was awesome.  We made a film about it (titled Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure) and met heaps of interesting people to interview.   I'd definitely recommend it as a not-to-miss part of visiting Jeju Island!   I'd like to walk some of the Olleh Trail routes next time to experience it differently and more slowly.

We hiked down to Jungmun Beach from the Lotto Resort and had a  great time.  The schlep was a little strenuous for a 70 year old especially on the way up.  We went pretty early in the morning on a grey and rainy day at the end of June.  There we no crowds but the water was rough and dangerous for swimming.  This made the whole scene romantic and enjoyable.  The trip was worth the effort but how worth it for you will depend on the weather and the crowds. We walked the beach as part of Olle Trail #8.  We got lost a couple of times.

We have 4 kids (youngest is 6) so we did Yeongsil trail.  It took us about 2 hours up and 1 hour down.  My Fitbit said it was the equivalent of about 175 flights of stairs up. It was tiring but had gorgeous scenery.  Our kids were tired but we're all enthusiastic about the hike and said they loved it.  I thought it would be a bit easier based on some of the reviews.  Highly recommended.

We finally got a good clear day.Yesterday at Sunrise Mountain we had been in the clouds.  Some nice views down the coast. Not a terrible tough or long hike to get to the end of the trail with a small temple cave. Number of mostly coffee shops at the bottom and bathroom facilities.

We end up at the wrong trail and did not have the time to complete it. Choose the right trail for your budgeted time. Weather is pleasant enough in late Sep but the trail requires proper hiking shoes if you don't want to hurt your knees and avoid sprain.

We drove from seogwipo which took around 1H drive from 4am because the sunrise at 5.40am. It took us roughly 20-30mins uphill trail to reach the peak (sunrise view point). Worth spending a morning for this beautiful sunrise view.

We didn't get to spend as much time on Udo as we would have liked. I would have liked to so the Olle Trail but there wasn't enough time.  We had walked up a steep hill thinking we could get to the lighthouse but you go at it from the other side.  If you don't want to walk rent a motorcycle.  Don't forget your driver's license.  I hear the lighthouse is wonderful and we will go back.  Lots of cute little places to eat or have coffee and there's a nice beach. There's not really a fee to get on the island but you have to take a ferry and there's a fee for that.

We climbed to the top of Mt.  Hallasan via the seongpanak trail. We are in just above average shape and we had no issues getting to the top with not stops in 2hrs 40 mins. There are three rest areas along the way that you can stop at if you need a good break. The last 1.5k to the top is the real shocker. We did not do our homework and went up real early on the morning and it was so windy and cold we did not stay long at the top. It was cloudy at the top anyway so we were not able to see 20 feet off the mountain so we headed back down. There is little to no people climbing the mountain at 6am but I'm out way down there was more people ascending to the top. Overall it was a good trip but I recommend bringing a windbreaker and not starting until around 7 on a clear day.

Visited Hallasan during Autumn season and the weather was chilly. Best to bring an extra layer of clothing to wear esp when you?re at the top. Did the climb at 9ish in the morning and managed to reach the shelter before the cutoff time at 1230pm (if my memory didn?t fail me). Took about another 2 hours or so before we reached the peak. The trail we took was pretty gentle in the beginning but it was filled with loads of steps at the end. We were rewarded with a great view at the top so the pain of going up & down was definitely worth it. Gotta do it at least once when you?re in Jeju!

Visited at mid-day in August.  It was very hot but beautiful.  had a picnic near the carpark and took a stroll along the trail on the east end of the beach. There is a small freshwater spring on the beach at the start of the trail
Very close to the Ocean palace hotel. Easy walking trail. Worth a visit for people of all ages! Recommend to arrive early before the tour busses arrive.
Took me and my friend 6.5 hours up yongsil trail and down by erimok trail. Scenery was a killer. Love it so much! Will visit again!

Today I hired a car and drove to Hallasan National Park. Only 1000 won to enter and park.Plenty of clean toilets. An excellent Visitor center who gave me an informative map. I did not have time to do Eorimok Trail today but will do tomorrow.I climbed the Eoseungsaengak Trail which is only 1.3km and has wooden steps all the way up so no problem with any fitness level.30 minutes up to the top. Great 360 deg.view of the surrounding mountains and a small Japanese bunker to see too. Friendly Jackdoor birds wanting a scrap of food..
This place has several themed hiking trails. You can choose one of them according to your allotted time. You can walk comfortably under the shady trees. I recommend this place is a must-see in Jeju.

This is the first thing you should do if you visit Jeju. The tallest mountain in South Korea and you shouldn't miss it. Climb to the top if you can for awesome views of Jeju and its surrounding oreums. Locals recommend winter and spring but autumn is beautiful too especially along the Gwaneumsa trail.
This is a great place for to hike especially if you have been binge eating in Jeju. You can burn some fats and take pretty photos at the peak. Recommend you take the 1 hour trail for amateurs.

There are 7 trails that you can climbs the mountainBut there are 2trails  only to reach to the top.Since i took 4courses i will explain where i visited that is also most people goTo SummitTrails : If you want to go to the top there are 2trails Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa  trail. Normally people go up by Seongpanak and go down by Gwaneumsa since Gwaneumsa is more difficult to go upTaking time : round trip takes 9 to 10hours so you better start your day early otherwise they will stop you to go up in some area Especially Jindalrea shelter will close at 1230pm or 1pm which can be vary depends on seasonAlso on your way to Jindalrea shelter there is another short trail Sara oreum which is really beautiful and takes only 40min. so it is YOU MUST VISIT place unless you are not hurry by time.How to get to : from Jeju bus terminal there is a bus that ofpen goes every 15min and takes 30min For beautiful viewTrail : Yeonsil trail and Eorimok Trail People normally go up by Eorimok and go down by Yeongsil but for me the opposit is betterTaking time : round trip takes 5hours and easy to walk if you like climbingHow to get to : there is only one time every hour so you better check in the termimalEorimok takes 35min from terminal and Yeonsil is 2stops more from EorimokPersonally i prefer Eorimok and Yeongsil trails.Also i highly recommend you to have climbing shoes otherwise your feet will be beaton up by rocks and enough waterall trail has shelters that sell food and drink but you better bring your own water Even it rains it is another feeling climbing mountain very attractive to go with lots of fogI never thought it is good to climbs when raining but i liked it a lotHowever prepare a nylon raincoat  from jeju bus terminal since it is very windy Poly raincoat would be ripped It is double price from the entranceThis is the best montain among i have visited in Korea

The parking is 1000w. Don?t stop right after the entrance keep driving or you?ll end up walking very far. The trail is well marked no chance of getting lost. I got there about 0900 and it wasn?t busy. When I was heading back to the entrance at 1200 it was getting very crowded. The ?peak? wasn?t much of a peak. It was a flat staging area with the rock slab marking the elevation. There is a trail that leads off left of the seating area and one behind the rock slab. I followed it about 1 hour before I decided to turn back. I wasn?t sure where the path led and my car was at one end. Beautiful but easy hike. Little to no shade to wear sunscreen or hats.

Soooo pretty! Absolutely stunning glass sculptures and the trail through the forest was an absolute highlight of my stay in Jeju. The glass tangelo trees must have taken FOREVER to complete and they were so well done. Loved the little farmhouse in the forest and the huge glass spider webs. So peaceful looking out at all the colours across the lake. Definitely recommend this place for something a little bit different.

Seriously stunning display of flowers at Camellia Hill; the biggest arboretum in Asia famous for its forest path and beautiful gardens of camellias. The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!

Sanbangsan Mountain is a wonderful bell-shaped huge body of lava situated nearby the ocean. At few places it stretches into the ocean where majestic rock structures can be seen. Almost vertical cliffs with columnar joints at this mountain are impressive. This mountain is visible from almost everywhere in the southwest plains of Jeju. Also the legend associated with this mountain is very interesting. According to the legend it was plucked out from the Hallasan Mountain peak by the angry Emperor when he got hit by a misfired arrow that was shot to white deer. Interestingly it is said that the circumferences of the Sanbangsan Mountain and the crater at Hallasan are of similar size. The Jeju Olle Trail Route 10 is connected to this mountain by stairs. A Buddha temple huge Buddha statue and the caves on this mountain are very beautiful.  This mountain along with nearby Yongmeori Coast are highly recommended especially to those who love coastal cliffs and interesting rock formations.
place is quite hugecan spend an entire afternoon there. they even have a mini theme park with a pirate ship. you may hike up the trail or visit the temples as well.

Place is good and interesting but an averagely.Nothing too special. I've been there at the end of season (September) - so trail was closed and not possible to rent a kayaks as well.Maybe in summertime it a bit more interesting but not sure :)

My family took the Eorimok Trail and the path is well maintained.  Remember to bring food and water along.  Recommend to start early morning as it gets hot at noon and early afternoon. It is worth the effort and a must see if you go to Jeju.

Make sure you go early enough.  Koreans are extremely cautious and the trials close far earlier than necessary so we did not make it to the summit.  It is quite a nice trail and I highly recommend it.

Lovely views from every corner. We were lucky that weather cooperated that day. Make sure that you take your time walking the several trails.  Some of them have a few steep steps but not impossible unless you have issues with your legs or balance.Great spot for picture talking. Highly recommended.

Long trail relatively easy.. specially the first 4 KM .. are flat basically The rest is a hit steepThey will give u a certificate if u take a picture up for 1000 wanBring ur own food.  And water.. In the winter wear ur gears as its super sleepery dont go with out gears i went in april. . And in the last 1/3 of the road i slipped and injured myself many times.. Fantastic hike.. Definitely recommend it
Located along Olle 7 (I believe) Oedolgae is a gorgeous coastline and certainly worth a visit! Spend the day walking the Olle trail and stopping for drinks and snacks along the way. Recommended!

It's very crowded on the weekend as usual. I was on my olle trail #1 trekking and passed by this almost at the end point of the trail. The view is so much better from afar than close up. Try walk to the beach side and I can guarantee you the beauty of seongsan is right in front of your lenses. And stairs hiking is awaiting for you there. Be ready for that :)

It takes 45-60 minutes to hike around the whole trail. The trail is diverse in the scenes that it presents along different coastal views. Brace yourself for high wind speeds during the colder months. There are a lot of inclines/declines on the trail so be wary of that on the way. There are a couple of restaurants/eateries spotted along mid-trail but I have no comment on those establishments. Before the trail officially begins there is a little rest-stop with coffee shops convenience stores and restrooms so I would recommend using the facilities before you embark on your hike.

If you like to visit beautiful scenery this should definitely be one of the places you go in Jeju. If you start near the beach it'll only take you a few minutes to see the best parts. If you're like me and you enjoy seeing a bit more you can walk for about 10-15 minutes along a boardwalk trail up the estuary. The trail (and river) are next to the road the whole time so it's a very easy walk. I'd probably recommend starting up the river a bit and walking to the beach that way the scenery gets nicer and nicer as you go.As for the kayaks I had no expectation of being able to go on one since the reviews all suggest you have to come early and wait for a long time. It was a pleasant surprise then that the kayaks were not operating. There were none to be seen anywhere. This was great because it meant there weren't too many people and the river looked serene with no one paddling around in it.If you're keen on doing the kayaks people have told me that they're stopped for good  and other people have told me that they're just stopped temporarily. I would recommend calling a tourist office or tour agency to find out the latest news.

i love hiking and outdoor activities although my seminal not s perfect compare to my friends. Great is option trail for your to choose for the length of visit. this is make me can enjoy the trail to the Peak.Sure will challenge Halla again.

Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

Good place to visit for experiencing the lava tube. But.... Pease please please prepare a good walking shoes if you were to visit this place. You'll need to walk on rough and uneven surface and the trail is pretty long. Not recommend to bring kids and elderly to visit this attraction.

First obtain the Olle walking trails book from tourist information counter near the central bus station. From there you can ask for recommendations. I chose the scenic routes and it required walking up slopes which allowed paranomic view of scenery and also along the coastal area which was slippery due to rain. Some routes bring you directly to the beach whereby you can enjoy Jeju famous mandarin oranges and buy souvenirs such as their honeyed tea and famous chocolates! Do ask for discount like for all tourist attractions and at times the lady boss will throw in more pieces of the chocolate.You can also take partial route but check for the correct bus and you need to check which stop to alight. Unfortunately despite being a popular tourism attraction bus drivers can't communicate in English. Good luck if you encounter locals who can speak English.

Enter the national park through the Eorimok trail and get down through the yeongsil trail. There are different scenary when you arrive at each check point. Can't describe more by words. Experience it yourself and you will know that those endless staircase that you climbed up is just so much worth for the view up there!
came here through booking a tour with driver Mr Ann. highly recommend him and this place. This place is highly scenic and great if you do not have time to complete long trails in mount hallasan.
A great place to go hiking. A range of trails to choose from and follow for beginners and advanced hikers. Spend one or two hours or the whole day - best to go in the fall or spring.

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.
Worth a visit either for sunrise or sunset. Went there for sunset and it was amazing. Hike isn't very tough as there's proper stairs, railings and trails for ascending and descending.

With a few different trails to choose from, climbing Hallasan is an experience I'd recommend to anyone visiting Jeju and wanting a close experience with its nature. Careful preparation of equipment is still necessary, as the easy trail was quite slippery even while wearing winter shoes. The change in scenery when ascending the mountain was magnificent, even though the snowstorm at the top prevented us from seeing the scenery at apparently one of the best sightseeing spots in all of Jeju.

Will never forget our longest hike in our entire life! Our earlier plan was just to enjoy the view of fall foliage during the autumn and it happened that Mount Halla was the only place... Did our homework earlier before our trip there so that we can get a perfect picture of the foliage in Hallasan. Ended up, we only managed to see a lot of deciduous trees, perhaps, due to the heavy rain and wind the night before our trip. Wrong timing... There were some trees along the Yeongsil trail (the route we used) but the leaves had turned brown, not the orangey red... My husband and I couldn't feel our legs after the hike and I lost my cap due to the very strong wind! Anyhow, the view was spectacular as Hallasan is the highest mountain in Jeju!

Went today - very clear day. Reminded me of Falcor from the Never Ending Story. Hahahha!  We took the southern trail to the lookout. Was a great place to stop and see the local female divers gather fresh mussels, clams, abalone, squid and sea cucumbers. They quickly set up shop with a few kids stools and rock formations (ready made table top). They brought out a few bottles of soju (I think they hid it in the ocean to keep it cool. Luv the grapefruit flava) and they were ready for customers.  Freshest seafood I've ever tasted- Anthony Bordain would've been proud.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. The Gwamneumba trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre.. And not to mention the fattest and most active flies inside and outside the cubicle..We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa. Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved. Yes it is a mountain, and I hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan which did not put me through the physical pain without much reward that hallasan did. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope!Enjoy!

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long? It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

We went to Seongsan IIchubong after our lunch.  We bought our admission ticket ??5,000 per person.  When we enter the park, we saw that the climb can be quite steep and decided to take the left trail which has very nice scenery of the cliff and sea.  If you do not intend to climb up the Peak, just take the left trail which has gentle slopes and its free admission.  You can also watch the Haonyeo performances around 3 pm from the left trail.

We went on the shortest trail as it was really hot when we traveled here. But the scenery is beautiful. The trail was not difficult and all the people we passed were very friendly! Would definitely recommend checking it out, but just be careful of the heat.

We went on the first Monday of the month, and the mountaineering trail was closed, so do take note when planning. However, the first portion of the trail was still available for free, which was still amazing and less of an exercise. The view from all spots were breathtaking, making this spot a must-see when you?re in Jeju.Do catch the woman?s diver show at 1.30pm and 3pm, located down the trail. It was an interesting experience to see the elderly women dive down to retrieve the seafood in the ocean, and you can buy and eat some of their fresh catches at the shop nearby.Highly recommend for a magnificent sightseeing experience in Jeju!

We went on a very rainy day so there weren?t many people.     The white seafoam crashing against the rock was amazing.     The formations were breathtaking.     Information given in English about how they were formed.      It doesn?t take very long to walk the trail, no more than 30 minutes.     There are toilet facilities and a couple shops with limited food and other items for purchase.   On a nicer day, there would probably be a lot more vendors.

We went for Oedalgae and ended up taking an unplanned walk along Olle trail #7.It was drizzling when we arrived, we took some photos of the rock and explored the area. Further into the park, we followed the trail which hugged the coastline. Beautiful views all the way... We went past a cafe at some point, it would be a nice place to relax but we were short of time. We ended our hike near Storyville as the pathway was blocked by fallen trees/branches due to the recent typhoon.

We wanted to hike to the summit of the Hallasan mountain, and decided to use the Seongpanak trail.It's roughly 9 kms from the parking lot to the summit, and it took us around 2h50m at a constant pace with few stops. This is a very scenic hike starting in the middle of the forest, and close to the top through prairies. The hike is properly maintained with stairs and paths, but some parts have many rocks, and thus proper hiking shoes are highly recommended.The views from the summit are spectacular!

We walked up Yeongsil and down Eriomok. Would definitely recommend getting a taxi right up to the start of the trail if you want to start walking straight away. As other mentioned, it is a long, winding up hill 2.5 km walk from the bus stop. It cost us 30,000 won in a taxi from the other side of Seogwipo. The walk up was beautiful and the rest area with bathrooms at the top was  a surprise. We brought all our own food and drinks and didn?t see anywhere selling, which we enjoyed at the top. The walk down was equally lovely although the hard bit lasted longer so we were glad we did it on the way down. A short 10 minute walk from the base of Erimok are the bus stop going to Jeju City or Seogwipo. All in all it was a lovely hike and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Took us about 6 hours including numerous stops here and there and a 30 minute lunch break.

We visited this road on the way back to the airport (stayed on South side of the island).  I would recommend this attraction if you happened to be on road-1139 or in the vicinity (e.g., visiting Loveland, or hiking trails nearby.  There are plenty of nicer things to see and do on the island but it?s worth a look/see, if you?re in the ?neighborhood.?  My wife got a kick out of it, using the water bottle, as previously advised by another post.  I was less than thrilled and found the art along the road and cafes to be more interesting around the mid-way point of the attraction.

We visited this place while walking the Olle trail route 10 and its great view and fresh seafood were very pleasing and I strongly recommend it. Definitely great to snap some fantastic photos while enjoying the rocky beach. The whole place was very clean and I just really enjoyed my time there chilling and staring at the ocean and volcanic cliffs. It took about 30min to walk the whole path but if you want to take everything in, chill and take some pictures 1 hour and more would be perfect.

We visited this place out of curiosity and was quite surprised how peaceful it was. It was a weekday when we were there but it might get a lot more crowded on weekends.Give this place a chance if you would like to experience a walk, albeit on man made trails, in the forest as it was quiet, peaceful and there are many great photo ops.

We visited Mount Halla National Park yesterday, Aug 25th, and it was an excellent experience and great views!It is very easy to get there by the 740 bus from Jeju Bus terminal, now here is the tricky part.. there are several entrances and trails. All of them are intense hiking. Use comfortable shoes, take lots of water and snacks.. there is nothing to buy up until the very top, which is noodle soup, water and chocolates......We took the Eorimok trail to go up to Witsae Shelter and took the Yeongsil trail to return down and my recommendation is:Take Yeongsil train, the view is by far much better than the one from Eorimok trail.In order to get there:Take 740 bus and get down on Yeongsil ticket office (@45m) and from there take a taxi to the main entrance (there is a taxi that goes up and down all the time and charges 5000). Please take the taxi, otherwise you will end up walking uphill for @2km. Once at the entrance... just follow the signs to Witse Shelter. Take lots of pictures along the way!Again ... it is uphill .. from @900m to @1750m, with lots of stairs and rock trails on both trails. Up and down in @5 hours is an ok time.Enjoy !!

We visited Hallasan National Park in mid-November. We did the Gwanwum-sa trail up to Hallasan peak and went down the Seongpanak trail. Although Gwaneum-sa is more challenging on the way up, we totally recommend this route as Seongpanak is way more transited. The trees' autumn colours were beautiful and although at the top it was below 0 degress and misty (making it hard to see the volcano cone and lake), it was an amazing experience. Would definetely repeat!

We visited Hallasan National Park in mid December. We ascended via Gwaneumsa trail (8.7km) up to the peak and descended via the Seongpanak trail (9.6km). Gwaneumsa is shorter but more challenging on the way up, it is easier on the knees. We started at 07:30hr, which is the sunrise time. The initial hike was relatively flat, walking on uneven big rocks. There were signs throughout the trail, indicating where you are, distance and estimated time to the peak. Snow started to appear midway and we had to put on crampons on our boots. We took about 3 hours to reach the shelter and another 1 hour 45 minutes to reach the peak. Unfortunately, the weather was cloudy at the peak with low visibility. It was very windy and cold. We joined the queue to have photos taken at the iconic landmark.We started our descent at 12:45hr, arrived at the shelter at 15:15hr, had a short break before descending the remaining 4.1km. We took about 4 hours for the entire descent, exhausted by then.This is the first time my friend and I hiked in snow during winter. We took longer than expected as we were extra careful and also took many photos. Overall, it was a great first time experience hiking on snow.Tips for winter hiking:1. Start as early as possible so that you are not pressured to reach the shelter before 1200hr.2. Wear comfortable shoes, preferably water resistant or waterproof.3. Be extra careful when stepping on the big rocks during the initial trail. They are uneven and may twist your ankles. 4. Crampons are necessary, while trekking poles are optional.5. Wear layers of clothing so that you can add/remove when necessary.6. Wear beanie hat and neck covering to protect your ears/neck from the cold, especially at the peak.7. Bring your own food, snacks and water/energy drink. There are no food stalls nor toilet at the peak.8.Toilet facilities are only available at the shelters, hence relief yourself before proceeding.Hope you enjoyed the hike.

We travelled from Seogwipo by bus to Jungmun Elementary school.  Thereafter, we were supposed to hop on another bus to the stop nearest to the entrance of Yeongsil Trail.  However, we did not read the bus schedule careful enough to notice the change in the schedule during winter.  The bus starts later and ends earlier during winter.  We ended sharing a cab with the other 2 tourists who happened to be there earlier than us and were heading to the same destination.  The guy who mended the convenient store near the bus stop was so nice that he helped us to call the taxi.   It was a blessing in disguise since the taxi actually sent us right to the door step of the Yeongsil Trail entrance in which otherwise, we would have to walk up for about 2 km to the starting point of the trail.  Should you travel with baggage, the park office (which I guess so) can keep them for you.  I?m not sure of the storage capacity or if lockers are available, or this is just an additional service provided for those who happen to travel there with their baggage.It took us slightly more than 3 hours to hike up to Witsoreum Shelter since we?re quite slow and took plenty of photos.  The Koreans took 2 hours only.  The wind was very strong, so do take care of your scarf or anything which is light.  Witsoreum Shelter is where you can opt to go back down with the same trail or by another trail, Eurimok Trail.  However, the other trail was closed on that day.There?s a canteen and restrooms at Witsoreum Shelter.  The canteen sells instant noodle and simple snacks.  After eating and disposing the residue of the noodle, you have to bring the trash back for disposal.  Plastic bag for keeping your trash is provided but I find it rather thin.  However, we brought some plastic bag along with us for this purpose as well since we had some snacks while hiking up.The fog was building up when we left at about 1:10 am.  It took us about an hour and 40 minutes to descend.  Overall, this was a good experience.  We were just on time to catch the last bus back to Jungmun Elementrary school (if I recall this destination correctly).

We took up this challenge in early April, just stepping into Spring. We took the bus from Jeju Express Bus Terminal, took about 40 minutes to reach the Eorimok bus stop. Before taking the bus though, we highly recommend to check with the Tourist Information Center just outside the bus terminal on the last returning bus. Thankfully we checked, the last bus in March period was 4.55pm at Eorimok. Summer periods probably have a later last bus back. This bus serves the Yeongsil trail entrance as well.There is still a ~20 mins walk along the road before reaching the entrance to the Eorimok trail. Impressive mountain views once you reach the park entrance.The Eorimok trail starts off deceptively tame for about 500m. Once you get the past the wooden bridge, the tough hike starts. For the next 2km, we experienced the toughest climb of the entire trail. Steep and large steps at times, with large, uneven rocks littering the way up. The view is mostly green at this point.Near the end of the first 2km, we started to see melting ice along the trail. Certain parts were still iced up; we had to climb on top of the ice to traverse. Due to the melt, it was quite slippery. A hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended, though we had not brought any for our trip.After 2km, the trail leveled off into a plateau, a welcome rest after a seemingly endless slog. Strong winds and rain pummeled us that day, but all the more made the challenging climb more exciting and enjoyable. The rest of the way to the Witse Oreum was of average difficulty, and the landscape was foggy and snowy/icy. We encountered many instances that we had to walk on the ice so be sure to be equipped with good shoes to reduce the chance of slipping on the ice.We finally reached the Witse Oreum after about 3 hours, and bought and slurped down the ramen and its soup, as well as a chocolate energy bar. They also carried stuff like crampons and plastic sheet raincoat (we bought it for the heat trapping characteristic rather than for shielding against rain, we foolishly did not expect snow and ice in April tbh :P).We originally wanted to go down via the Yeongsil trail which meets the Eorimok trail at the Witse Oreum, but a pair of local, seasoned hikers who turned back for Eorimok warned us that the Yeongsil trail is still mostly frozen over and is very difficult to traverse at this time. Due to the lack of proper equipment, we heeded their advice and went back down Eorimok instead.The trip down was much faster, but hurt our knees more due to the impact. Tread with care as the uneven terrain may cause slip and falls.The journey down took approximately an 1.5 hours.Overall it was really challenging but fun.Things to note:1. Take note of the last bus timing or you may have to hitch a ride back to town.2. And of course, cater buffer time to reach the bus stop, there is still a 20 min walk to it.3. Hiking gear, especially proper shoes and a hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended.4. Early April features unmelted snow in the terrain, wear proper clothing.5. The same bus goes to the Yeongsil trail, may want to try hiking that as well (on different days of course)6. The Eorimok is pretty challenging for a novice like myself, heard from locals that the Seongpanak trail on the Eastern side is more relaxing but longer.7. The Eorimok trail does not reach the summit, if you want to reach the summit, try the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa trails instead.

We took the steeper but shorter gwanumsa trail up to the summit from where we got brilliant views of the crater lake, and the gentler but longer seongpanak trail down-I think this was a good choice because both my friend and I find going downhill more difficult than up. We took a taxi to the gwanumsa starting point. We comfortably reached the summit by 1 pm and ate our lunch of kimbap(bought from a store near our hostel,  there's no kimbap sold at the gwanumsa trailhead, so make sure you buy beforehand). Although the trail is relatively easy, there are only a few points where fresh water is available,  so bring enough drinking water.  If you want to climb to the summit, there's also a fixed time by which you have to reach a checkpoint,  which is closed after that time. I really liked the varying landscape and vegetation. The only bad part was the washrooms - extremely dirty.

We took the Seongpanak trail up to the summit, and Gwanuemsa to descend. We agree with other reviewers that this is a better arrangement (gradual ascent, and beautiful descend - going up by Gwanuemsa could be a little too steep). It is a great idea to trek with a hiking pole - it is especially useful for the descending trek.Hallasan was a colourful parade of trekkers on October days - trekkers need to even queue up to take photo with the summit rock (with writing of Hallasan on it!) Less people descended through Gwanuemsa. It was a long, long way but there was no regret - this trail offered picturesque scenery. We even crossed two bridges.It is however, better to get the telephone number of the cab company on a weekday as it was not easy to secure a cab from the end point of Gwanuemsa (buses only ply the road during weekends). We were lucky to be able to carpool with 2 locals who were also heading back to Cityhall area, and they managed to call a cab only after they obtained the contact from another call taxi.

We took the Seongpanak trail for both ascend and descend, took us a whooping 9 hours! Please wear a good pair of shoes as the trail is rocky, that explains why we couldn't run up and down afraid of slipping and fall. Parking is very limited there, we reached at 8am and parked at the roadside because there weren't any parking left inside. Beware of the time as you would need to reach the last rest house at 12.30PM in order to continue your hike to the summit. Great view at the summit but it was very crowded. Overall, it wasn't a very difficult climb but it'll take you a whole day.

We took the Gwaneumsa trail up to the peak. There is a checkpoint halfway, after 2-2,5 hrs. of hike. The trail gets harder after the checkpoint, but it's also nicer with bridges and very steep stairs. If it's possible, go after rain, because then you can see a small pond in the crater of the volcano. I would recommend to take the Gwaenumsa trail up, because it offers a nice view. To get down, we took Seongpanak trail. The whole tour took us around 8 hours, with a lot of rests and photo-time. :)

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal as we knew that we needed to take an early bus to Hallasan. We noted that we needed to reach a certain point on Hallasan by 12.30pm as they would not allow people to continue to hike up after 12.30pm due to foreseen danger. We took bus 782 at 6.00am sharp from seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and alight at Seongpanak bus stop to start our hike at Hallasan. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The ride took about 30 minutes. The cost of the ride was less than 2000won and the bus driver could provide change if needed. We alighted at Seongpanak bus stop on the side with a hiking track. That track was not the track up to Hallasan. We needed to cross to the opposite side and pass the souvenir and rest stop place to the correct Hallasan track (free entrance). In the beginning the track was gentle and doable. We managed to spot birds and deer grazing around. However, the rest of the track up was pretty boring as there was nothing much to see. After 1-2km, the hike started to be more steep (as in more elevated with steps) as there were many rocky steps to hike up. There were two rest stops before the summit that provided fairly clean and well-maintained toilet with toilet paper. However, there would not be any tap to wash hands. Therefore, remember to buy wet wipes to clean your hands. At the second rest stop, raman, drinks and crampons were sold. Get all the supplies you need before hiking up as there is no shops at the summit. It will be good to bring tomatoes or fruit for the hike as those provide fluid as well as sugar (instead of salty food item with msg ? this will make you feel sick). Anyway, you are not suppose to cook at the summit. Remember to bring trash bag to clear your trash too. From the second rest stop onwards, the steep rocky steps continued with harsher windy condition as you progress to the top. Therefore, remember to bring windbreaker and windproof pants as the wind was rather strong 1 to 2km before reaching the summit. We hike on 24 April with a summit temperature of 6 to 12 degree Celsius. We were blessed as there were no rain snow during the hike. The 1 to 2km up the summit consist of wooden steps that I found difficulty tracking up due to the wind and my lack of motivation (as I kept on looking at the summit and felt that it was so far away). Therefore, it would be better to just look at the steps in front of you and conquer those instead. When we finally reach the summit, we had a view of Baengnokdam crater and the surroundings. I was feeling nausea partly due to the fatigue as I did not exercise for 2 month prior to this hike. However, we managed to hike up to the summit in 3.5 hours. The wind continued to be harsh on us. Therefore we stayed for 15 minutes and decide to just hike down. Take pics even if you feel unwell. You will feel better as you ascend down. We hike down from the other hard track, the Gwaneumsa Trail although I was super tired. I did not regret that choice as it was much more scenic in comparison with the Seongpanak track. I thought that descending would not be a toll on me but I was wrong. As the track consist of many rocky steps, it was hard on my knees and I had to work on my balance too. The ajumma (they were over 50 years old) were able to hike way faster than me (in my early thirties). There was one rest stop only and we stop for the toilet. It was again clean with toilet paper provided. Generally, it was a descending hike with minimal ascending (with only a few flights of stairs up). We took 4.30 hours to hike down and I was totally shacked. The rest area at the bottom was also much more beautiful as compared to the Seongpanak rest stop. We wanted to take a bus back but we were told that there were no buses on Monday. There were buses back to Jeju city on other day from Gwaneumsa. (we noted that one of the bus come around 4pm towards Jeju city). We took a cab back to Jeju Dongmun Traditional Market for 20, 000 won. From the traditional market, we took a taxi for 3200 won to the bus terminal (bought bus ticket from the counter) to take bus 781 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (the journey was more than 1.5 hours).Personally, I find the hike difficult and I would suggest some stamina training to enjoy the hike better. I would suggest to hike when there is good weather as I find the hike difficult even in good weather (due to the rocky steps). Having said these, I would still recommend the hike as I love the challenge.

We started with Yongsil Hiking trail passing through: Byeongpung Rock, Witse Oreum till the South Wall Folk and then to go down we followed the Donnaeko Hiking Trail. The way up is ok, the way down is quite difficult, ai recommend proper shoes.

We selected yeongsil trail since we rarely hike in own country and it is recommended for beginner. We started our hike at 9:30am and it took us 3 hours to reach the shelter while 2 hours to come down. We used back same route to come down since we drove there. The cup noodle shop was closed when we reached the shelter, grateful we brought some biscuit and roti else we will starving after long hike hours. We didn?t expect still having ice on mountain since it is turning spring. This get bit challenging especially to me as my shoes a bit tough to walk on the ice. But luckily a korean lady offered her stick to me and hold my hand to cross the ice path. It really make a different with the stick support. It is really recommended to get prepare self well with good hiking shoes, enough water and food.

We rented an ATV at the ferry drop off, (an international driving permit is necessary), the clockwise drive around the coast was easy and dotted with many eateries and cafes. Stopped at mulko's house for some excellent seafood lunch, then picked up peanut ice cream near the bottom of the udobong trail. There's peanut rice wine and peanut bread available as well. Took 11am ferry over and 2pm ferry back. Highly recommended

We rented a car to drive around as the attractions are scattered around the island. We ascended through Eorimok trail and went down on the Yeongsil trail. Both trail were really beautiful and serene in autumn. Yeongsil trail was a lot shorter than Eorimok however prepare to climb steep steps if you're going up Yeongsil. Both trails will lead you to the Witae Oreum Shelter. It is extremely windy up there so it'll be wise to dress warm. Jacket with a hood would be good. There is toilet (only one you'll find throughout the hike), resting area and a cafe selling instant noodles at the shelter. It is rather strange that the toilets do not have basins to wash hands so bring along wet wipes and hand sanitiser. We fueled up at the sheltered resting area. We took 4 hours to finish the hike including rest time at the top. The walk down was breathtaking. The trees were changing colours and you could see a shades of red and green in the landscape. It's handy to have some tissues in hand to clean your running nose. Taxi back to the Eorimok parking was a rip off at 20,000 won. I think the drivers knew we were too tired to walk back so they took advantage of that.

We really enjoyed our hike up Hallasan.  From the tropical, palm-tree lined streets at the bottom to the barren, snow coated, rocky pathways at the top - at times it felt like we had wandered into Narnia.  After reading some of the previous reviews on this website and following a stern warning from the concierge at the Lotte Hotel, we almost opted out of our plan to take the more challenging Seongpanak trail to the peak and Gwaneumsa path back down.  In the end we decided to give it a go and turn around if it became too challenging.  For people who have hiked up mountains previously, the difficulty is actually fairly reasonable (mostly steps and handrails etc).  We did not have crampons, walking sticks or colourful walking gear like our Korean accomplices, yet somehow we made it to the top and back anyway.  It took us 3 hours up and 3 hours down (starting at 8am).  I suspect the time of year largely will determine the difficulty so check the weather on the mountain carefully before you go.  And avoid the toilets.  Trust me.

We made the round trip from Jeju to the north entrance to the Park by taxi, then climbed tto the summit from there, descending on the trail on the east side. The tracks are really well looked after, great scenery. Took us about 7.5 hours in total. We caught the bus back to Jeju which was very easy to find.

We like to hike.  Our idea of hiking is day trips and not super remote.  A 4-6 hour hike in a California Redwood state park is a good example.We took about 6 of the 20+ trails on the south and east coasts.  Every one was different and interesting in its own way.  We stayed in Jung-Mun on the south side.  Terrific little town with hole in wall places with tasty, healthy, cheap food and good bus transportation.These hikes were a little different from our standard in that they often took more than 6 hours. They also could dip in and out of populated areas. We liked that because we might trip across a restaurant run by old lady divers or an archery club doing target practice.  Most trails were not at all crowded. The worst was part of a trail where a Korean soap opera was filmed. It is hard to describe the Korean style of friendliness. They are very direct.  Example was a man at a bus stop who figured we were going to have difficulty getting to our destination. So he flagged a taxi, allegedly for himself, and invited us to hop on.  When we figured out what he was doing, we insisted on paying.  He refused. We got out, gave the driver money, he grabbed it and gave it back. We tossed the money into the window. He grabbed it again, tossed it back on the street and had the driver zip off.  There we were, picking up our money off the pavement. Anybody who has watched Koreans fight over who gets to pay the bill at a restaurant knows what I am saying. To Americans it looks like a hot argument when in fact it's best friends being best friends.  My advice is enjoy it but don't always loose the argument - sometimes you have to win and pay the bill.  This time we really tried but he was too clever for us;-)

We hiked up the Seongpanak Trail and hiked down Gwaneumsa Trail.  These are the only 2 trails to the summit and hence it is the best option to get the best of both trails.Iit was a huge satisfying feeling to reach the top and then to descend safely.  It was not difficult if we were more prepared.  Here are some pointers to note:(1) We went in Spring and therefore we were not expecting any snow.  However, probably due to a snow storm 1 or 2 weeks ago, some areas were still covered in snow.  As we didn't bring any hiking sticks nor cramptons, the descend was difficult and dangerous.  I slipped many times.  There was even one path which was totally covered with snow and we had to detour to the side which was hard given the little space and all the snow.  As we descended via Gwaneumsa Trail, it was more steep and therefore the snow made it such a challenging task to hike down.(2) There are no water point.  We thought we could get some water from toilets but there are no taps in toilets too.  We ran out of water towards the end.(3) No food.  Do bring your own food as you would not be able to buy any on the way up and down.  We  brought our own snacks.  Also be prepared to bring your own rubbish down the mountain.  There are no rubbish bins for you to discard your rubbish.(4) Do allocate more time for the hike.  We thought we could do it within half a day but we spent much longer time.  By the time we reached the bottom, it was already 4 - 5 plus.  Even though we were relatively fast and hardly stopped, we still require that much time which probably was also due to the snowed paths (lots of snow).It was a unforgetable experience and we were so happy we did it!  Will we do it again?  Definitely!

We hiked up the gwaneumsa trail (shorter, steeper but more scenic route). Really glad we chose this route as there was far less people and the views were spectacular.We arrived to the trail head at 7am and paid the 1800 krw fee for parking. The trail head is clearly marked and there's a nice washroom that you can use before beginning the trek. The trail is well marked (there's no way you can get lost) and also well maintained.You reach the first rest stop around 3km into the hike. There's a very smelly washroom there (there's a better one at the next rest stop). You must reach the last rest stop by a certain time or else you won't be able to proceed. The time posted today was 1300 although it looked like the only barrier was a small chain that you could walk around so I'm not sure how enforced that rule actually is. After the final rest stop the trail goes downhill a bit then the steepest climb begins. The stairs don't seem to end for the last 2.7km!! The views are spectacular though. Once we reached the top there was so many people! Where did they all come from? The seonpanak trail.
