I was very wrong. It doens't look hard but the trail is cut straight up, (no switch backs). After reaching the top you know that you climbed a mountain and it feels good. You look back wondering how many steps you climbed.If you're going bring plenty of water and start early. Now I've been up about 5 times and I feel like I don't need to go again.There are tails to the top from almost any direction.It's worth doing at least once.

If you want a good workout, take this adventure on. I'm in average shape and it took me just around two and 1/2 hours to climb the Seongpanak Trail (9.6KM) going non-stop. The trail is definitely steep in sections and please use caution on the way down. I learned the hard way that tired legs don't descend as well as normal legs and took a pretty good fall.  Fortunately I was able to careen into the bushes on the side of the trail much to the suprise of all the hikers around me. There are stairs...lots and lots of stairs. There is an trolley car too hidden off to the side that they use to resupply the shops at the two shelters and maybe for medical evacuation if needed.

If you plan to go to Udo, spend at least a day here. Enjoy every part of Udo : Udo Olle Trail, Udo lighthouse, Beach. Trying the popular Halasan Fried Rice and peanut ice cream, so yummy. Really enjoy my time in Udo, fresh air, clear blue water, white sand, warm local people, beautiful scenery. This is what I picture Jeju in my mind. Everything in Udo are beautiful for me. I will regret if I didn't come here, this is my favourite part in Jeju.

If you like trails and hikes, this is it. Do it korean style and eat ramen at the top and even cucumber (take them along with you and even other snacks cause you'll get hungry). Plus, go in the morning, I want at 12:00 and thank goodness made friends in the way to get me back to my hostel. Around 17:00 there are no more buses and I would have been stuck there if it weren't for my new friends!

If you are there and have no place to visit, perhaps you may want to waste and hour or 2 to walk into the cave. There is no special attraction inside the cave that will give you a WOW factor. By end of the trail, you would just like saying...err...thats it? Its cold in winter and the floor are wet with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Its dark too.

If you are fanatic about nature then you would probably really like this park. However if you enjoy nature but are more swept away by breath-taking scenery then in my opinion you will be really disappointed. We did the Seogwipo trail and for the effort involved the reward was just not enough. The trail took around two hours each way, and part of that was over some extremely difficult terrain. It's not that step, but walking over really large stones and boulders for over an hour can get really tiring, especially when there is no view to distract you, you are just surrounded by trees, There is nothing to see at all for the most part! At the end of the trail, the mountain lake and view of the valley is nice, but nothing that special or amazing. We were there in low season and even then it was extremely crowded, so you never have the feeling that you are really hiking a mountain. I wouldn't do it again.

I would die to visit Udo again, it's a tiny island and can be covered in one day with a scooter which can be rented once you're off the ferry but I'd love to stay a few day next time so I can really enjoy the island.  Everything here is like straight out of a book, the beaches, the hiking trails, the lighthouses, the food, OMG the food.  Anyone visiting this island, I recommend starting early morning and renting a bicycle, a scooter if you're good with directions or pay for a bus ticket that with have drop off locations as well as pick up so you can explore at leisure and when you're ready to go to your next location, just stop by one of their pick up locations and you're ready to go.

I woke up really early to get ready for this hike. I took the first bus 281 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo leaving at 6am. We arrived at Seongpanak trail entrance about half an hour later. I did this trail mid January and you need crampon for this. Personally, I don?t like slippery surface so crampons really give me the confidence. But I saw people on the hike didn?t have crampons. Some other people hiked in their running shoes. Snow was thick but you basically walked on top so I guess You don?t necessarily need hiking boots. Unless you go off trail, the snow will be knee deep. It was such a nice feeling to see everybody get up and early to start the hike when it?s still dark out. The hike up was not very challenging and it took me about 4.5 hours. I?m an extremely slow walker. Keep in mind that there is cut off time. If you start too late and couldn?t get up to the last shelter on Seongpanak trail before 12pm, you are not allowed to go to the summit. The view at the top was so beautiful. It was very windy though. I took Gwaneumsa trail down since I wanted to change views. That was challenging. My knees hurt so bad even though I already wore knee braces. It?s shorter than Seongpanak trail but it took me almost the same amount of time. There was one part quite steep and I didn?t notice the rope which you can hold on to, I slid down and broke my trekking pole. Apart from being slippery, the trail is quite rocky and by the end of the day, after a beautiful sunny day, the snow started melting and made the trail very slushy. There was time I almost gave up, my whole body hurt and I started to get blister on my toes. When I got to the entrance of the trail, I took bus 475 for 10 mins to a university entrance station then changed to bus 281 to go back to Seogwipo. I guess you can take 281 directly from Gwaneumsa to Seogwipo but I didn?t know where it was so I followed the crowd. I totally recommend this hike.

I was told by the reception assistant at the guesthouse that the trails to hike Mt Hallasan were closed when that day it was snowing heavily.When the weather got better, I made a mistake when we reached the office ticket too late to hike.  No one is allowed after 1200 noon, winter time.Also, I made a mistake of not being alert to the weather forecast.  Due to the rain and ill equipped, I decided against hiking.  Thus, I ended up at the nearby rest area and visited the wetland instead.  It was beautiful

I visited Hallasan in early March, some parts of the trail were still covered in snow. At the lower area I had some difficulties because of the melting snow. It's doable without crampons or walking sticks, but be careful. Past Witseoreum shelter, it's recommended to have walking gear. I have an average condition and I did the Yeongsil trail up in 2h15 and the Eorimok trail down in less then 2h. I think it's better to do the opposite. Yes, Yeongsil trail is longer, but easier. The Eorimok trail is covered with rocks, and if you don't watch out, it is easy to twist your ankle when coming down.

I took the eorimok trail which took about 2.5 hours to get to the top with the rest rooms, the first part of the trek is hard work and quite strenuous. After reaching the top I took the yeongsil trail back down which had some of the most stunning views along the way. As I came by bus the walk down from the yeongsil trail to the yeongsil ticket office where the bus stop is located takes another 40minuts or so depending on the pace. I Would highly recommend visiting this area and trying the trails.

I started from Eorimok Trail and came down by Yeongsil Trail. Eorimok trail starts off with steps then followed by wooden walk way before you reach Witseoreum Shelter. Shelter is a basic one with just toilets and resting rooms. We took around 2hrs to reach the shelter. Yeongsil trails starts off (from shelter) with wooden walk way then followed by countless stairs. You are like literally hiking on the edge of the mountain up/down. We took 1.5hrs to descend.Definitely recommend going down by Yeongsil trail rather than heading up due to the countless number of stairs. Both trails offer truly beautiful scenery and great for photos. I cant forget the view which the horizon mixed with the sea level that you can differentiate. Stunning!Advice:Bring food like energy bar, fruits etcBring water enough to reach water points. There are a couple of water points for you to refill along Eorimok trail. Else 1.5 litres for 2 pax is enough.Bring jacket and wear hiking shoes. Sports shoe is possible like what most korean did but be v careful as you will be walking on uneven rocks at times. Probably suggest ankle guard to go with sports shoe.For those who want to scale the mountain but doesn't wish to try the 9-10hrs climb to summit, i would really recommend this 2 trails.

I really enjoyed wandering through Hallasan National Park. I spent 4 days here, and was quietly impressed. At times there were way too many hikers, as they often come by the bus load, but mostly you were alone with your thoughts and the environment. The trails were well marked out, and easy to follow (even for people who don't read Korean). There was plentiful assistance if you get lost, but you felt like you were alone. The other tourists were polite, interested and friendly, definietly great for conversation. Jeju would have to be one of the highlights of this particular trip to South Korea. Would definietly makee the trip again.

I made the climb on 22.11.2013 but few days before my climb, I have been keeping my eye on the weather on the mountain. The first snowstorm hit the mountain top a few days earlier and I know that my hike will be much difficult with the snow along the path to the top of the mountain. I chose to ascend from Gwanuemsa trail and descend from Seogpanak trail and I know that I have made the right choice. Starting from Gwanuemsa trail was much tougher, with the rocky pathways in the beginning to the steep climb in the middle of the trail and snowy trail all the way up to the mountain top. Along the way, there is no food on sale but there is a shelter for people to fill up their water, at the Samgakbong Shelter. The total length of Gwanuemsa Trail is about 8.7km and Samgakbong shelter is about 6km from the starting point. To make it here will take about 2 hrs of normal walk. There is also a toilet available here but the you wouldn't want to spend more time at this toilet. The trail after Samgaokbong SHetlter has obviously been much tougher, with a lot of steep steps, or even no steps at all (all covered by thick snow) and at some point, the is a need to pull the rope along the trail to move upwards. The efforts are all worthwhile upon reaching the top of the mountain. It is good to come on a clear day because the view along Gwanuemsa trail especially upon approcahing the mountain top is spectacular.At the top of the mountain, the wind can be really strong. Be prepared with the chill and wear enough layer to prevent from getting cold. As mentioned, I descend from Seogpanak trail and this is somehow a boring trail. The total length is about 9.5km but all I can see is trees along the way. There is nothing much to see but it was quite a flat trail that make it the choice among many hikers. There are food on sale at the Samgakbong Shelter, and also a big toilet there. A good stop for hikers to build up their energy before continuing their hike. Crampon also on sale for 5000 won. Overall, it was a fresh and good place for first time traveller. If there is a chance to come back to Hallasan, I will sure try the other 2 trails on the western side of the mountain.

I loved my hike in Hallasan. We were a couple and we decided to take the 'most challenging trial' - Gwaneumsatrail (8.7 km).  There are four Hallasan trails on and around the mountain, but only two of these trails will take you all the way up to the volcano?s crater lip ? theGwaneneumsa trail is one of these, theSeongpanaktrail is the other one. It is important that you check beforehand which trial is open, because it depends on the weather forecast. In my case all the 4 trials were partially open which meant that the crater lip was not accessible unfortunately. There is a website you  check (in Korean) or you can simply do what I did and ask the staff at the reception of the hotel. Each trials is easily accessible by bus, however the buses are not that frequent - for example 1 every hour for the Gwaneneumsa train, so you might need a bit of planning. Our trail was accesible for 6 out of the 8.7 km and took us to the first shelter (1500m elevation) the hike took us.6 hours back/forth including a quick lunch break; the pace wasn't that high but we weren't that slow either. If you want to access the crater lip, one think that you need to bear in mind is that you need to make it to the first shelter by 12-13 depending on the season (November was 12.00pm).Another thing to remember is that there is no convenience store or food vendor available during the hike, so you want to pack some food (kimbap is a good option) and water. As the hike itself, I really enjoyed it, you will feel immerse in the nature and you will enjoy a nice variety of vegetation depending on the altitude.

I hiked up the Seongpanak trail, which was easily accessible from Jeju-si. It took only ~45 minutes to get to Seongpanak station on the 780 bus. It was crowded, but it was still a very nice hike (and luckily the weather was pretty good!). You have to reach the Jindallaebat Station by 1 pm in order to be allowed to climb to the summit. Then, you have to start your descent by 2:30 pm. Please note, the time may change depending on the season, but I?m not sure (I climbed late April). It?s a big hike, and I definitely recommend wearing good hiking boots and wearing a proper backpack. Bring lots of water. If you forget to pack food, there is some available at the Jindallaebat Station. The summit is breathtaking! I hiked back down the Seongpanak trail since the bus to get back to Jeju-si seemed more frequent than the other one. During the descent, I took a side-trip to the Sara Oreum and scenic view. It was just a good 30 minute detour, and well worth it! Once at the bottom, it was easy to catch the 780 bus back to Jeju-si.

I hiked up Mt. Halla in the winter of 2007. It was my first hike up a mountain and relatively easy getting up to the first summit as a beginner. Unfortunately, I dont remember exactly what trail and how many hours it took but it was a day trip (up and returning down). The only downside with visiting during winter was that the snow and ice made it a bit challenging in some parts, since I didnt have proper footwear. My body ached a bit the next day, but spending the day at the spa made it all worth it!

I hiked to the top today.  I had decided not to do this but at breakfast this morning a gal from Korea highly suggested I go, so I did. I took the Seongpanak trail up and back. I got there a little after 10 and was told that it was a bit late to make it to the top so I went out very quickly so I would make it to the Check station by 1 PM. If you get there after that time they won?t let you up to the top. I made it and got to the top. At 2:30 they make everyone come down. I came down slowly and at the end I was all by myself walking those trails as it got darker. I didn?t get down until about 7 PM. Because I was in such a hurry to get up it took me much more time to come down than it did to go up. As I was walking down a deer jumped right in front of me And then jumped away. I brought two bottles of water and lunch. That was perfect for me. There are restrooms on the way up but not at the top. They are outhouses. I do not have hiking shoes with me, just my slip on sketchers, so my feet are still sore from walking on those lava rocks with these shoes. This is also the reason it took me so long to get down, my feet were really sore At that point and I had to rest them during the descent. There is a Monorail track next to the trail. Today I saw them taking down some people who couldn?t make it down on that.

I have read a lot of reviews about Hallasan Mountain and before going there, you have to know that this is not easy to climb. Going to the top of the mountain is really hard and you should get some really good shoes, especially because at the end, it really hurts the ankles. I took the Seongpanak trail and it is 19.2 km in total, the view is not spectacular when you climb, it is beautiful when you are on top of the mountain but the problem is that it is so exhausting that I really could not enjoy the view as I could have if I was full of energy. I was lucky and so a deer in its natural environment. It is difficult but after doing this, you feel really happy. There is only a thing really annoying ; toilets are really really dirty with no toilet papers so take tissues with you (and a big bottle of water, two are too heavy for the back).

I hadn?t hiked in years, but thought I?d give it a try at a friend?s suggestion. I dressed in layers as the weather was still cold, but knew I?d get warm on the climb up. I didn?t use crampons and there was only a small amount of ice in some places, it was easy to avoid. I did use poles, which I?ve never used before, but was thankful to have them, especially on the way down. The terrain was rocky, but there are lots of stairs and ropes as you reach the summit. It was much colder at the summit and the view was clearer than I expected. The crater is impressive. I did see a deer and a couple red squirrels. The hike down was much more difficult. My legs were in so much pain by the end of the day. Bring lots of food and water. Many people have picnics at the summit. I arrived to the trailhead by taxi and found a taxi at the trailhead when finished. I had to wait around a bit for a taxi to show up.

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. There is a small entrance fee.  The first half mile is along a wide crushed rock road. It is lined with young   nutmeg   trees. The trees are in the yew family. They are Torreya nucifera and are native to Japan. I  visited in October when the small edible nuts ripen. The nuts are encased in a thin husk that has a wonderful aroma. You will see people collecting them under the large trees.  Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet.  The crowds end at the beginning of the narrow trail so you can walk through this section in peace and really marvel at the enchanting colors and smells of the forest and hear the songs of the many birds.  There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Also many of the other plants have English name labels which is nice. The trail is flat and should take a leisurely couple of hours or less if you rush.  I noticed a lot of people sitting on benches in the first section enjoying picnic lunches.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I enjoyed the hike although it was very steep. They now have an ascending and descending trail to help avoid getting overcrowding trail, which can happen with the common bus loads of Chinese tour groups or student groups. The hillside is beautiful and the trail has amazing views. When you get to the top, it seems a little underwhelming but the hike itself gets 5 stars even in April when a lot of vegetation is dry. The hike takes about 30 minutes to get to the top. It cost 2,000 won a person to enter. I also saw that you could ride horses at the base of the mountain.

I did the hike just 2 days back from the Seongpanak trail and I was really glad for the   gator   spikes that I rented from the guesthouse that I stayed at...the snow was thick such that you hardly see any steps at all. At the early part of the hike, the snow is hard and easier for grip but as you go higher, the snow gets soft and with every step, you will slide a little down. The last part was the hardest being very steep but with the summit in sight, I don't anyone is going to give up at that point. Going down proved even more tougher as the tendency to lose your footing and slide down is very real. Hiking stick is necessary. For a city person like me without much exercise and preparation, I took 4hrs to reach Jindallaebat shelter and 1.5hrs to reach summit and 3.5hrs to come down. The view is gorgeous and worth the hike but do not underestimate the difficulty especially in winter.

I decided to hike the Yeongsil trail to Mount Hallasan, since it was the shortest of all the trails. It was estimated to take roughly 2 hours and that it did. I gotta say this hike is one of the more vigorous hikes I have done and requires a very good pair of hiking shoes! The views as you ascend only get better and put you in awe. Once you reach the top there is a rest area with toilets and an area to rest. I suggest for those that plan to do this bring a snack and drink so you can enjoy the views once you get to the top.

I decided to go with Seongnapak trail, and was planning to go up to the summit!Rocky and stony path made me really exhausted, I managed my breath okay and left the last 1.5km as my keens!You will be accompanied by many people along the trail! It?s highly recommended to start early, I arrived by 8am, reached the shelter around 11:00am!Weather was mild as you?ll be covered by trees most of the time!

I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

I choose the most difficult route (Gwaneumsa Trail) as the website said it offers the best view of the mountain and I stupidly assumed their difficult is not too difficult if compared to Malaysia's route (because Malaysia's one is not a proper/well maintain path).And so I was wrong :p It is all the way up up up and up, stone path (which I hate most) and wooden staircase (so descending is definitely more blessing but very challenging to your knee). I hike @ 26 April, didn't get to see much fantastic scenery as I guess I'm not at the right season as I saw some other people's review they saw great scenery. So this was more like a physical training to myself. To train the mind especially. But, the sound of the wind is like ocean waves, this was indeed very beautiful, I even record it down during descending. It took me 4hrs 10mins to reach the top, in between there are... 2 toilets I think, and if you manage to reach samgakbong shelter (1500m) not later than 12.30pm (spring/fall) you are allow to continue to hike to the top, else you'll need to return. Cross this check point there is a spring water ahead before the bridge for you to refill your water! Then what's lying ahead is the super strong wind and the sturdy steep stone/wooden staircase path ==|Long story short:1) Hike at the right season I'm sure you can see more than what I see2) choose the trail wisely. I would say as long as you have a strong will, even you are not very fit also you can do this trail, just start little bit earlier than others to give yourself more time (say 5hrs to the top). 3) Make sure you are well equip to keep yourself warm. Windbreaker and glove is a must. I had 4 layers (t shirt, thermal, windbreaker & sweater & I was still shivering at top, the wind is just too strong that we couldn't even stand still) 4) Bring water, food, chocolate and candies! 5) Good shoes is a must for less struggling during descending & less stress to your knee. Personally I don't use hiking stick so suit yourself for this. 6) count the time and familiar with your own pace if you want to reach the top. Just make sure you reach the check point then you can take your own sweet time to get to the top.Last but not least, just don't under estimate this well develop stone & wooden staircase path. Although it's only 8.7km, 1950m height, it took me 4hrs plus up and 3hrs 15mins down (with very little time rest at top coz its just too cold!)Good luck!

I and my boyfriend traveled here by public bus. We visited the place at the end of October not really December but I did a very late review. It was very easy to get to the place by public buses. The bus stop right in front of the entrance and crossing the street the take the return bus. I researched the bus number, it was wrong. So I asked the bus ticket woman for help and she was really helpful.It was a very challenging hike. Be prepared with a lot of water bottles with you and really exercises before the hike. The trail we took was Seongpanak trail, which is the easiest one. It was early of the fall season. Leaves started turning into different colors, chilling, not so cold, sunny and very enjoyable.We just finished 1500m of height and ate a noodle in a shelter. Then, we turned back (blaming non-stop walking in the previous days :D) and took a quick turn in a shortstop in Saraoseum (beautiful lake, nice view of the mountain).Overall, really enjoy it! Will try it again one day.P/S: it is a natural place so not clean bathroom. A very natural way of toiletry but I really don't like it but can't blame!!

I am a complete beginner to mountain climbing but was there thankfully with an experienced climber. We took a taxi from jeju city to Seongpanak visitor centre and the journey costs around 20,000 krw and approx 40 min. I was there on 7 December after a snowy night, and the trails were covered in snow. Poles, proper hiking shoes and crampons are absolute necessity as the snowy paths were hard to walk.  Gwaneumsa, the popular trail for descent after reaching the crater summit, was closed that day as the snowy trail was too dangerous, so it was pretty rough to get up while people are trying to get down. Especially since the trail was already made quite narrow by the snow. However, the view is great and it's like a winter wonderland all the way up. The last stretch to the crater summit was hard for a complete beginner like me. It was however considered easy for seasoned hiker like my friend. On the whole a great experience and certainly worth the trouble for the views but would recommend complete beginners like me to do some training before getting up. The rest stops are well stocked and constant announcements were made (in Korean only) to keep the hikers moving up before the gate closes at 12 pm and down before it's gets dark. Note: we were staying in Jeju city before the climb and the weather was grim with lots of rain. The weather on Hallasan was however completely different. Sunny and pleasant for climbing.  Be sure to check the weather forecast on Hallasan and not Jeju!

I absolutely recommend you to take a day trip and hike up Hallasan if you are in Jeju. Even though if it takes the whole day, since it is about 20km walking, it is worth it. If you are in okay shape I'd recommend you to go up on the Seongpanak trail. It is longer but easier than Gwaneumsa trail. The hike has a lot of stairs, so don't expect climbing. Once getting up, the most thing that shocked us what the loads and loads of bugs, since we never heard about that. They don't bite but they do get on you which is annoying. That said, the view is beautiful, to the island but also to the crater. Going down I'd recommend Gwaneumsa trail since it is a lot more beautiful and more to see. It is only the first third part that is the hardest, after that it gets okay. Remember to start climbing early since you have to reach the checkpoint before a certain time depending on the year. It takes about 3 hours to get to the checkpoint so try to check what time you have to be there before. The time is there because it takes a longer time to get down than you expect. Also bring water with you. There is only one point where you can buy going up, and only one point where you can fill your water bottle on both trails!

Hyeopjae is a beautiful beach with everything you would want in a beach it's very long with thick soft sand. But, the best thing about Hyeopjae beach is the Ollhe trail that starts at the Northeast end of the beach and goes for ever. The trail runs along the shore so close to the sea that at high tide on a windy day it becomes inpassable because of the waves submerging the trail in some places. The volcanic rock along the trail forms different things. If you look at the rock closely you might see a dragon or a horse or maybe a bird. If you stay on the trail long enough you walk by G-Dragon's cafe. If you go even further you will come across a Smoke Tower that is hundreds of years old used to send a signal of a enemies ship approaching.So, while Hyeopjae Beach is 1st rate when you are done swimming take a walk through history down the Olleh trail.I'm an American that has been living in Jeju for the last 12 years and I walk this trail 3 to 4 times a week and it never gets old.

Hiking Hallasan is the number one experience to do on Jeju. You have to be reasonably fit but it's fairly easy to complete as a day hike and no guides are needed. The trails are well maintained and easy to follow and there are great views. If you climb in winter, it's well worth getting small instep crampons for about 10 dollars from the shop at the bottom of either the Seongpanak or Gwameumsa trails. I recommend walking up the steeper Gwaneumsa trail, and down the Seongpanak trail. I've been up four times now, different routes, and this is definitely my preferred approach. The views are much better and Seongpanak is much easier on the knees coming down.

Hiked up to the summit via the Seongpanak trail. A 35 minute ride on the 5.16 bus from the Jeju main bus terminal drops you off right at the entrance to the trail. Great hike up. Took me a little under 4 hours including a 30 minute detour which breaks off from the trail to go see the Saraureom. This trail is mostly wooden steps. Both the Saraoreum and summit crater lake were dry, but still beautiful. I do not recommend relying on the   store   at the Jinderaebal shelter. They do have hot water if you want to bring your own instant noodle mix. Bring your own food and be prepared to bag your garbage and carry it. walked down via the Gwaneumsa trail which is a bit shorter. I defenitely recommend this since the trail also has a different type of scenery, including a beautiful bridge crossing. Not sure if there is a bus back to the city from the bottom of the Gwaneumsa trail, but by the time I made it down (3 hours) I was ready to take a taxi, one of many which are available which cost me 15,000 Won (about $ 15) back to the city. Certainly worth it. Overall, a beautiful and amazing experience.One last recommendation would be NOT to attempt this hike with less than proper hiking shoes.

Highly recommend everyone to do at least one of the Jeju Olle trail routes. We chose route 6 as it?s being classified as the easiest route. The route is filled with beautiful sceneries. Some part of the route takes you onto the roads, into the bush, along the coastal and up some hilly roads. We meet a lot of locals along all way and they are helpful & friendly. Lot of cafes for one to take a rest too.

Highest mountain in Jeju Island with a lot of hiking trails. We pass by the place as there was not enough time to do any hiking as some of the trails takes quite a no. of hours. It is one of Korea's and the world's natural heritage. Instead we hiked up to Sunrise Peak, another attraction which is not so high but has really impressive and great views from the top of the peak. Would recommendas it only takes about an hour from summit to peak.

Hallasan was a good challenging climb, with the hike splits into 3 parts. The first 2 hour or so, we were hiking through mostly level ground, some rocks and little steps. As we reach the middle ground, the trail gets steeper, more rocky and almost half are made up of steps, mostly made of rocks. Using a hiking stick at this time really helps in making the climb easier. When it rains, which happened the entire day when we went, the ground gets covered with puddles and pools of water, so it was extra effort trying to choose the rocks to step on to avoid getting our feet wet. Towards the top, there are flights and flights of steps, followed by a trail made of rocks where u have to use a rope to climb up the steep rocky surface. It was challenging but overall, felt good.As it was raining, we didn't manage to get any view of the crater or lake at the summit. But the sense of accomplishment making it up was great!The way down was more challenging as after a day of rain, the trail became wetter and what used to be steps, some were submerged in water. Hence, even with a good waterproof shoes, ur feet could still get wet. Also, note that the sky turns dark at around 5pm in winter and there's no lighting in the reserve. Hence, make sure u buffer enough time to reach the foot of the mountain before that time. Otherwise, u would be hiking in the dark. Nevertheless, there would be a ranger moving down the rail lines in a cabin moving on a rail line, looking for stranded hikers. So no need to panic. However, I would still recommend planning well, checking the weather and choosing a clear day to climb. Start early so as to buffer enough time to reach the 3rd rest station by 12pm, as anytime after that, they do not allow hikers to go up to the top. Think it is for safety reason to buffer enough time for the ascend and descend. Also, to wear waterproof shoes and if available, bring a hiking stick along. Do standby a raincoat in case of light drizzle. Also bring some food along. Though they sell instant ramen and some bento at the resting stations, it closes by 2pm or so and you don't want to end up hungry.  Lastly, enjoy the climb!

Halla mountain can be hiked in 3-5 hours easily. I have hiked the Seongpanak Trail (on the east side)  and the Gwaneumsa Trail (on the north side). These are the two trails that go all the way up to the summit. If you are fit, these runnable, but Geaneumsa trail especially gets very steep at the end. Get to your trail of choice early to miss the crowds, and also note that the half way points of each trail close around 12 (depending on the time of year it is sometimes 12:30). Een when it is foggy it is beautiful, but, of course, it is best when you can see clearly down to the crater lake and across off of Jeju to the ocean. Pack a lunch and enjoy it on top of the mountain! (Or instant ramen is the traditional food to pack).My favorite time to go is in winter when the top of the mountain is covered in a few feet of snow! Make sure to bring crampons for your shoes (simple ones are OK, you aren't hiking K2!)

Good driving views.  You will be blown away. Should visit this place in the morning before 9am to avoid the crowd especially during weekend. There are so many trails.  Please ensure you know which trail you are taking as the mountain is so huge.  Must wear proper trekking clothes and shoes. If you are driving, please ensure you go down the same way as you climb up or else, you need to get a cab to bring you back to your car. Bring water, snacks and plastic bag to throw your rubbish. You must bring down your rubbish with you.

Going to Hallasan by bus #701 from our hotel in Hamdeok area, through Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal, change to bus #740 departing every 1 hour.  Stop at Eurimok Trail point. Walking from bus stop to the gate for about 5 minutes. There was a nice facilities at the gate: clean toilet, small convenient store with drinks vending machines, and police station too.Please be aware that   sleepers   are not allowed to be use for trekking due to heavy terrain. Including our son's crocs shoes. Unfortunately, the shop run out shoes stock so He can't join us.Eurimok trail quite heavy for untrained persons, we just only reached 1.300 meters before deciding to turn back to base.The bus #740 was picking us up at 15:35 back to Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal.

From the Jejusi bus terminal we took bus 201 to Udo. It took about 1 1/2 hours. Definitely download the app Naver to navigate your way around the island, as Google Maps does not have any results for public transportation. We spent 4 hours on the island. Ferry ride from the port is only about 15 minutes each way. Buying a ticket can be a little chaotic as there are no signs in English but we just held up 2 fingers for two passengers and were given 2 round-trip tickets. Upon arrival in Udo expect to be bombarded with shop owners yelling at you to rent bicycles, ebikes, motorcycles, or 3-wheeled cars (for 2 people). 2 people renting 2 ebikes for 4 hours cost us 40,000 won. Need int?l drivers license for the latter 2. I definitely recommend the ebike over the bicycle unless you really want to get strenuous exercise. Lots of hills and 11.4 km of trail to follow. Lots of little mini-towns where you can buy food, have coffee or peanut ice cream (recommend). Tons of photo opps so take your time. We finished in 3 hours, 40 mins (and my hubby wanted to stop A. LOT. Last ferry back to Jeju is at at 5 pm this time of year. Plan accordingly.

Free admission to coastal path overlooking Saeseom Island Saeyeongyo Bridge Walk at the other end of Oedolgae Rock. Real hidden gem, much quieter than the main Oedolgae.? A flight of steep stairs leads down to the emerald green rock pools. Saw a haenyo diving for ocean catch in the open sea. Be warned of swimming at your own peril at? the rock pools as lifeguards are not on duty.? The boardwalk trail leads to more breathtaking scenery of the vast ocean and rocks, lined by pine trees. Look for the plaque honouring the valour of Seogwipo Police and South Korean military who valiantly battled against a North Korean incursion in 1968. Makes a wonderful picnic spot, so do pack your basket of food. Note: Korean GPS 7328027

For someone with bad stamina like me, it would take about 2.5 hours to reach the end of the trail.The tip is, to go there early in the morning, then you can take some leisure time to rest from time to time. When we're going down to trail at about 10p.m., there are lots of people coming up the trail and it is quite packed with people.For person with knees or legs or ankle problems, must be really careful as I fell down several times due to rocky trails at certain places. However, the view along the trail were awesome and it feels really worth it! The warm ramyeon at the shelter was the climax!I went in April 2016. The wind is super strong on top. So make sure you're ready for that. Hotpack, jackets, windbreaker or whichever deems to keep you warm. You may not need them in the beginning of the trail but you might need it in the end of the trail.

For people who love nature and the great outdoors especially hiking, this day trip up the highest mountain in South Korea is not to be missed if you are in Jeju. It took us 10 hours  ( 5 hrs up, 1 hr at summit and 4 hrs down ). Trails and directions are very clearly marked. Best tip I can give is to go up via Gwaneumsa and back down via Seongpanak. But dress in layers. When we were up there end March, it was a beautiful spring day ( temp about 15C ) but 2 days later, it was about 8C and very windy in the city ( so you can imagine the conditions at the summit if we had climbed later ). A tiring day but no regrets whatsoever.

For hiking enthusiasts, this is a must do!  The Seongpanak (9.6km) trail has an average hiking time of 4.5 hours and Guaneumsa (8.7km) trail has an average hiking time of 5 hours.  One must reach the Jindallaebat Shelter by 1pm to be permitted an attempt at the Baekrokdam summit.  My husband and I completed the hike in 7hrs 35mins but were perplexed to understand how it took us 5 minutes longer to descend, given that we did not take breaks while descending. Guaneumsa has the reputation of being the roughest trail on the crater, but does live up to its reputation for breathtaking views.  - There was one potable water area on each trail where nature provided delicious water refills.  - Emergency posts appear through the trails, each with its own number, so keep track of the number in case you need assistance, rescue workers can narrow down your location.  - There are incredibly handy signs along the way to pinpoint your progress and identify the level of difficulty along the trail.  Paths are well maintained and varied; wooden, rocky, skree, etc. - If you take the bus to there is no fee for hiking.- Although we did not have cell phones with us, many folks seemed to be talking an walking throughout the trails.- We chose to end at the Guaneumsa trail head because it was the closest in proximity to our hotel.  Cabs are available at the trailhead.

For a beginner hiker like me, this trail is acceptable, mostly stairs without much of stone paths. The view of the mountain is captivating. Hiking sticks would provide some help during the hike. I try to hike down through Donnaeko trail, it has more stone path comparing Yeongsil trail. In the end I turn back to Yeongsil trail.

For 1st time hikers climbing Mount Hallasan, take note of the different hike trails AND the closing time for each trail. This is especially if you drove on your own and parked at 1 of the 5 (one of the locals told me there are 5 different car parks at different foot of the mountain)If you are climbing Mt Hallasan to reach Baengnokdam (the crater top), do not take the Eorimok trail as it does not lead there. I made the 1st mistake taking this trail and the trail ended 3 quarters way up the mountain and you only get to see the side of the mountain top. I made the 2nd mistake not watching my time and could not descend Hallasan from the trail (Eorimok) where I came as apparently it closes at 2pm, and there was a park warden stopping me from taking the trail back and kept ushering me to take the other way (towards Donnaeko trail) to descend. The descend took 4 hours and the trail was treacherously full of rocks. You could tell that it was a trail less taken as there were over-grown bushes covering parts of the trail. Your only guidance of where to go was a      thin cord string tied from tree to tree and red strips of cloth tied on the string. If you weren't too careful and lost sight of the guiding string, you may actually go off tangent of the trail. There are no lights, very few signage and are all in Korean, so if you are like me with no understanding of Korean, good luck. And that wasn't the end. Donnaeko trail actually ends up at Donnaeko cemetery. So when I got to the foot of Hallasan, it was pitch dark (6pm+ and no street lamps), by myself, and I had to walk for 1 hour through the cemetery to get to Donnaeko car park (which was 30 mins driving distance away from Eorimok car park where my car was T-T).

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Eorimok trail ends at Witse Oreum, at about 1700m up Hallasan. From carpark to the hut and back, including half an hour for noodles at the top is close to 4.5 hours. This includes photo times. Like everything on Jeju, this is a tourist walk, for pretty much anyone who can put one foot in front of the other up a very well marked or board-walked track. That notwithstanding, the walk is pleasant and the area itself is nice. In early Feb you will still likely have snow (we had snow from carpark to hut) and will require some small walking crampons to ensure grip. These are 5000W from the small shop at the carpark, beside the toilets and are pretty good actually. If you have some full mountaineering fangs it would almost be worth taking them for a laugh. We were the only westerners on the trail from perhaps 3-400 people and it would have only added to everyone's curiosity. Taxi from Jeju city will set you back about 20 000W and you can easily get a cab from the carpark taxi stand for your return trip. Hallasan is definitely the best, and some would say only real, attraction on Jeju and if you have half a day, then this is the track for you.

Disclaimer: Not a seasoned/experienced hiker. Was done on a cloudy day with a scattered drizzles.I had high expectations for the highest point in South Korea and a highly rated tourist attraction on TripAdvisor but was greatly disappointed by the experience.The reason I am giving a score of 1/5 is because there is a long hike (approximately 3-4 hours one way) with very little to see along the way, with ultimately what I would consider an   okay   view of a   crater lake   up the top. In addition, whilst walking the unpaved bits of the trail (rocks, which account for about half of the trails we walked) you will need to focus hard on walking to ensure you don't slip as it can be quite slippery. This means you don't have the luxury of looking around at the scenery/surroundings while doing the hike.It is not that the view up the top is objectively poor. It is actually decent. it is simply that the effort (3-4 hours one way) to reward (the view up top) ratio is terrible.The group of us hiked up the East trail (Seongpanak) and went down the North trail (Gwaneumsa). The hike down along the North trail provided a handful of views that were decent - better than the East trail.My experience at Mount Hallasan was preceded by Seongsan Ilchulbong the day before which to me provided a much much better experience. The hike was a lot easier and the view was much superior, offering a beautiful view of the Jeju City skyline. I personally would highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong over Mt Hallasan and would recommend against doing Mt Hallasan, unless you are someone that personally loves hiking as an activity anyway.Summary: Long 3-4 hour one-way hike (7-8 hours return) to the summit rewarded with a decent view, with a lot unpaved trail which can be slippery. Not good for people with bad knees, those expecting plenty of beautiful views, and those wanting to enjoy scenery while hiking.

Climbing Mt. Halla was a highlight of our trip to South Korea! We climbed up the Eorimok trail and then down the Yeongsil trail. I would recommend going this way because Yeongsil was a lot of stairs - I'd rather do that on the way down than up. Going up probably took us a little over two hours and wasn't too strenuous (though we are in good shape). The trails are very well kept and there are signs all along (in English) showing how far you've gone and how far you have left, and how easy/difficult the next stretch is. The view from the top (even though it wasn't even the top) was unbelievably beautiful! To get there, we hailed a cab from Jeju city. We just told him we wanted to start at Eorimok trail. I would recommend a cab because if you take the bus, you have a pretty large hill to walk up before you even get to the mountain because of where it drops you off. I think the cab cost about 15,000 won. The way home, we were waiting for a bus and then saw a cab so we hailed him. This guy charged us 30,000 won, I think because Jeju city was out of his way. Make sure to bring plenty of water - at least two bottles per person - and snacks.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As unexperienced hikers, we did the 9,6 km Seongpanak trail and it took us around 9 hours to finish the trail back and forth (breaks included). The view at the top of the mountain is stunning and very rewarding. The hike itself is not very scenic as you walk in a forest for almost 90% of the time (which is beautiful and relaxing though). We were quite exhausted at the end of the day, but it was all well worth it. To memorize this day, we decided to buy a certificate (which can be bought for 1000 won at the Seongpanak trail entrance).

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.

An amazing scenic spot with stunning view. Try to hike along the trail for panoramic view of jeju island and the ocean. If you have limited time, it is not necessary to hike up the peak since the best scenery is blocked by the fences. The descending path has much better scenery that the ascending one! p.s. Try out the hanrabong ice-cream! One of the best way to recharge after hiking
Amazing view in the autumn, especially u can see the peak at the end of Eorimok Trail and Yongsil Trail.

After reading the reviews i was a bit reluctant about visiting the park but i am glad i did. I only wish i had more time to see everything, like all the small trails leading to the folk villages at the far back. This is not just for people who are history buffs, this park can be enjoyed by anyone who appreciates nature and quiet, peaceful walks. It is a windy area so be prepared if visiting in cool seasons. For only ~$5 this is a nice park to spend a few hours if you want to slow it down and be in nature.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014.  Glass is a common item we use daily.  But there in the Glass castle, they have made beauty out of something ordinary to something beautiful, works of art actually.  However, many tourists were not aware that there is a trail going round the Castle where you can see more sculptures placed along the trail.  A prominent signpost placed at the entrance to the trail will be helpful.  i am glad my friends and I didn't miss this trail.  To make sure it is not slippery during rainny season, the managements have placed gunny sacks along the trail.  This helps greatly for many of us.So if you are in Jeju, don't miss Jejeu Glass Castle.

A great hike for people that like to spend the day hiking. I went during the week and it was not to busy but I was told weekends is very busy. I had trouble finding the bus up to Yeongsil trail head as no english on bus signs. Took a taxi which was 25,000 won but was able to take bus home from Eoimok trail head back to Seogwipo. But this hike had much scenery to offer, I was a little bummed that we were unable to hike up to lake in the crater. This would have made the experience fantastic. No waterfalls either as it seemed to be the dry season this time of year but still a great hike. A must if you are a hiker.
you need to prepare extra energy to climb up the hill. Recommended to go there before dawn to see sunrise. Nice view form the top of the hill.
You can access it by ferry. Rent a scooter at the Island. With little kids I would recommend to take the car with on the ferry. Nice sights and views!
Wonderful place to visit. Not too far from Jeju Airport.You can visit with family and friends in day time.Seaview from the top is just spactaclur.

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

When it is raining this is one of the place you should come you can just relax and have  some tea besides they sell variety of Tea which is very nice and good. They have a tester too where you can taste certain tea. There is a cafe too but mind you it's a long queing so I just skip it maybe because it is raining time so everyone go there. My favorite is the pack O'sullac Milk Tea it is so very nice. I should buy more of it. Next time will surely buy a lot of it.Besides the tea thing there is innisfree house beside it. you can make your own soap the organic cafe at the innisfree house is also nice too.So I recommmend you to come here whenever it is raining for indoor activity. even if it is not raining it is good for relaxing and enjoy the view of the tea trees.

What a GREAT place to spend the day. Entry was $5 and I did not expect much. We intended to spend 30 minutes here but ended up spending most of the day. Take a picnic and bottle of wine and enjoy the serenity of the park. For a full video review of this place check out my YouTube clip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LlgzW0VCQHw

Went there a few days after Xmas and the weather was cold and hence made the climb easier. If we had came during summer I would never have wanted to make the climb. As it is with the cold weather and strong winds we made the climb with 2 or 3 stops in between to catch breath and take photos of the magnificent views. If you have kids or old folks to take care I wouldn't recommend the climb.
We were wondering near our hotel and found the falls it was a great way to spend afternoon.  Lots of stairs so wear good shoes...but every step is rewarded with a beautiful view ?
we went to this lovely park with our children and we ride the horses for a 15 minutes enjoying the spectacular views. I recommend it for a visit.

We wanted to catch the sunrise there but the sun was blocked by the clouds. It was a little disappointing as we climbed up when it was dark (cant see much scenery) and we had to descend without seeing the sunrise. It was nice to see the view from the top though!

We visited on 23rd October. A misfortune happened at about 5.15pm when we were about to leave  our rented car could not start due to no battery. Our baby was temporarily locked in the car so a helpful bystander helped us to opened the door using manual lock and called the car rental company. After a long wait we gotten the staffs at the park to help.the 'gatekeepers' were friendly enough to let us stayed there while awaiting help to arrive. A thin tall lady staff without spectacles came to our help and called the car rental company as we could not understand the options given in Korean. She explained to us and reassured us in English fluently. She also took extra care to follow up and waited til a tow car to help to jump start the rented car. I think by that time her shift is over as few staffs waiting for her too. We are indeed thankful for her and the staffs on that day. Cocomong Ecopark does have a good commendable staff. thank you.Park wise games and design are well thought and worth the entry ticket. The slide down on tire is fun though it looked a bit scary but it is safe. Cafe has got a nice sea view.

We visited at the beginning of May and it was cold. It also rained when we were on the beach. So could not enjoy the water.However beach is very nice and clean. We had coffee in the coffee shop on beach which gives you nice view of the beach.Its just opposite Hallim park so can be combined.Would nice to spend a warm and sunny day on this beach.

We started at 9am before the busloads Of tourist started arriving. It was a tough hike because the flights of stairs were literally endless. There were many resting areas along the way and I was not shy about just sitting on the stone benches to catch my breathe. Many reviewers shared that they took between 20 to 40 mins to reach the summit. I took 1 full hour. The stairs and tracks were well maintained and most stretches had handrails. The views at mid point and the summit were superb and makes this hike so rewarding! Don?t miss visiting this UNESCO world heritage site!

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

We made a stop there for lunch as recommended by our B&B owner. There are now 2 coffee shops. We had lunch in the new one. The steamed bun with sausage was nice. The brunch set menu was a bit bland. The best thing in the brunch set is the homemade yoghurt with marmalade. We enjoyed the view while having lunch. Quite relaxing. More Korean day-trippers and foreigners. We had green tea ice cream from the old coffee shop afterwards. Really good green tea ice cream. Better than some that we had in Japan. If you want a quick lunch and want something non-local this is the place to go.

We finished the route #10 (17.5KM) in about 5 hours (we walked pretty slowly and took a lot of pictures). The whole experience was unforgettable. The magnificent view of the ocean on the left and mountain on the right was amazing.
