I thought it would be hard since I'm not that much used to walking for long hours but it didn't feel exhausting at all. Every sight was so gorgeous that I just didn't want to leave. I felt very fresh and relaxed after the walk. Even the tiredness after it was finished was worth all of those pretty shots I took and the healing. STRONGLY RECOMMEND!

We didn't bother with the museum itself. Not my thing.But the Sunday Brunch at the cafe is legendary.Smoothies come in cute glass jars with thick straws and are so full of chunks of fruit that you almost have to chew them as you drink.The brunch itself is a mix of odd elements that I wouldn't normally put together - but they work..... creamy butternut squash soup scrambled eggs mustard coated potato wedges plus a ham/cheese/vegetable panini with salad leaves and balsamic vinegar on the side. Really good food.We sat outside the weather was lovely. Great view of the tea field (part of the museum) and the road. If I come back to Jeju on a trip sometime I'll definitely return for Sunday brunch!

We didn?셳 spend much time here which was a pity but in any case there were too many tourists. Would be a better experience when less crowded. The buildings are stylish and there is a nice view of the tea gardens. You can try the tea and they explain the tea making process. The cafe looked good with desserts like green tea cake and ice cream but we didn?셳 try as the queue was too long. Nearby was the Innisfree building where many people were making handmade soap. There was also a cafe and exhibits of the different distilled essences of flowers and plants in Jeju.

We decided to take the ferry to Udo at the last minute. We could have taken the rented car but decided not to. That was a right decision in my view. We took the hop on hop off bus and visited most of the tourist attraction. Be mindful of the bus schedule. Most people don't understand or speak English so one has to be patient. The scenery was lovely and the island unadulterated. I recommend to spend half a day here - just relax. The island is well known for peanuts which I find quite expensive. We had seafood ramen and abalone porridge. Yummy!

We came to this museum based on the previous reviews and came away extremely disappointed. The displays are very average and there's really not too much to see inside the display hall. The tunnel with the dioramas (which looked to be the most interesting one) was locked while we were there. There were no signs to indicate why it was closed or when it would re-open.The other tunnels were OK but once you've seen one tunnel you've seen them all - and the fairy lighting in the tunnels did seem a little out of place considering their history. There is a lot of painful history in this area but the museum fails to capture and relay it.It would have been better to see more of the human history alluded to in the video display in the other displays.Note that a lot of the pictures for this Trip Advisor listing may not actually be of this museum - we were quite confused trying to find it based on these pictures and they make it seem a lot grander than it really is.Overall wouldn't recommend and wouldn't go back.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

Viewpoint on the western end of Jeju Island.  Great place for sunset observation.  High on a cliff with good views all around.  There is a weather station here.Was here on a windy day - with field of swirling grass. To the north of the hill is a tail along the shore where it is possible to rent electric scooters.  There is also a small museum on the prehistoric settlement found in the area.
Very nice view and relaxing environment for families. I recommend this site for families with small and youth kids. Dunkin Donuts is great.
Very cold and windy too crowded and packed by tourist however the view of the dragon head rock is splendid.

Tourists are not allowed to descend to the beach for a close up of the rock. So we only took photos from the top of the platform. Would be a nice place to view the sunset but we arrived right after and therefore missed the window opportunity to do so.

To reach the place  need to walk along not properly paved route with long bushes  initially thought the guide had taken us to wrong place. Quiet place with nice coastal view. Unfortunately  we didn't manage to go to the church as there's sudden downpour  left us no choice but to end the visit. I saw horse carriage and shuttle bus service that can bring you around.

This would be my favourite place in Jeju. Evey single view is so beautiful. Too bad we went with a tour and did not have much time to explore around. We did climb up to the top though. We can easily spend half a day there. Suggest to give much time and go on your own instead of tour so you will have more time to enjoy it's nature

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.

This site explains everything one needs to know about the island's historical past.  It has a long walkway leading one through outdoor exhibit areas each section with attendants who can give information.  There also was a traditional musical performance available to view.  It was chilly when we were there so we left earlier than desired but if we had known there was a cafe in which to warm up and perhaps have lunch we could have made a day of it.  One perk of going in February was that the crowds were very very small here and at other locations.

This sight is at the extreme south east of Jeju. There are many great views and cafes within this area. This is a short hike up a beautiful hill and after the hike there is a haenyo performance where old ladies dive without oxygen tanks to collect abalones. I regretted not spending a full day in this area to chill.

This place is worth visiting given it's nice environment and a lots of things to do. Food:  I highly recommend the green tea icecream and cake at the O'Sulloc tea museum which appears to be the focus of most visitors.  But I also want to take some time to remind you that there's another little gem inside the organic cafe of Innisfree that's also within the complex--DON'T MISS OUT THE TANGERINE SHAVED ICE! It comes in a big original size that can be sufficiently shared among 3 persons or there's a mini version if you only want a taste of it.  It's not cheap but worth trying because they use Jeju Tangerine which tasted somewhat more intense and flavourful.  Drinks:  They have free tea-demo which you can try their teas.  They also sell a selection of other drinks like tea latte.  Most of them tasted and smelled spectacular.  The teabags are also wrapped individually so they make good souvenirs as well. Soap making:  If you go early do try making your own soap at the Innisfree house it's a fun experience and make good souvenirs.View and/or pictures:  The environment around and within the museum is a great place for pictures with the open tea-farm and the delicate glass buildings or the colourful interior of the Innisfree house.  There's also a viewing deck in the O'sulloc Tea Museum which you can access by taking a lift.  The view up there is pretty amazing.  Tip:  1. Go on a sunny day if you want to take great pictures in the tea-farm2. Go early if you are worried that they sell out the cakes.  The tangerine shaved ice wasn't available after 5.30pm so we went to visit again on the next day.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: This place is not wheelchair/pram accessible. The climb is relatively easy but steep. Lots of warning about flooding when heavy rain. The pond and falls are simply beautiful. The bridge has a splendid view. It's really worth visiting!

This park is relatively new and a haven for kids. Within the park there are play areas for toddlers and young kids. There is a sandpit  a tube slide  an outdoor playground  swings  car and train rides  flying fox  indoor playground etc. The train and car rides are available at extra charges.There is a baby changing room  makes it convenient for parents with babies. Flying fox is for kids above 100cm but they have the mini version for kids below that height. Indoor playground is a rather big area which is toddler friendly. There are seats for parents to wait while the kids play their fill in the indoor playground. There is also a restaurant within the park with amazing sea views. My daughter had an amazing time as the park was not crowded when we visited. Overall its a nice park to visit if u have kids below age of 7.

This musuem provides quite an extensive overview of Jeju's history in relation to the 4.3 incident that occured after WWII. Gives you a lot of emotion and there is also a great outside area commeorating the ones that have been lost. Recommended to go and visit this place if you are interested in culture and history!

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

This mountain is definitely worth a visit. I recommend a nice espresso and carrot juice at the bottom at Lazy Place Cafe - cool place with great views. It takes a little effort to get up to the cave with the water falling from the ceiling but well worth it especially if you?셱e a spiritual person. The other temples are serene. It is an UNESCO site of outstanding natural beauty with an historical layer at the coast below. A Dutchman was shipwrecked here in the C17th and wrote the first description of the Kingdom of Korea published in the West. I had a wonderful time with my girlfriend. Close place to stay is Mirabil.

This is THE place if you crave green tea desserts!! Tried both the green tea soft ice cream and green tea roll cake with cream cheese...absolutely delightful! Small museum with history of tea culture lots of tea types for purchase...even green tea based chocolates and jam! The rooftop offers a good view of the surrounding areas! Place can be packed with visitors so ensure sufficient time to spend!
This is really amazing. I loved the view. The place is well taken care of. The walk is of moderate intensity. We had wonderful weather. Recommend this place

This is one of the reason why I want to visit Jeju because I want to see this beautiful place and I was not disappointed though I was a bit breathless climbing the top but everything was worth the view is beautiful and I would definitely go back to this place and probably spend a day just enjoying this breathtaking place. My one regret is that I did not get to see the sunrise so hopefully next time if I came to Jeju I would try my best to see the sunrise here...

This could be a quick stop or you could spend time enjoying the view.  There weren't too many people when we were there but of course it could be busy.  The falls are unique in that the fresh water falls directly into the sea below.  You have to take stairs to get down to the sea level.  You can't get right up to the falls but you can get close enough to feel the spray and hear the roar of the water.
they tell us very interesting stories about this dragon head rock. all the legend and believes from the local people is nice to hear. also the view from the sea is awesome

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!
The whole area is astoundingly beautiful and clean with spectacular views all around. Recommended to all as long as you don't mind a whole day's hiking. Spectacular.
The view of the green tea field is really wonderful. And there are good things to give your parents and friends as gifts.

The view is breathtaking. The location is near with soepjikoji (all in house) so remember to visit two of them.this one is the higlight of jeju attraction.After see around we lunch seafood around here. My taxi driver recommend this one.
The view is breathtaking. I wish we could spend more time there but it gets dark so you might want to head down before the sunset.

The temple itself is breathtaking. It is one of the largest temple I had visited. The architecture and scuplture of the temple is unique and beautiful. Climbed up to the third floor the view from the window toward the sea is just magnificant. Spend some time to admire the marvelous architecture especially during the evening.

The tea caf챕 and museum were extremely crowded so we headed for the Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a delightful oasis of calm comprising an organic food caf챕 a large space for making your own soap and a smallish retail space dedicated to bath and arotherapy products as well as a small selection of exclusive souvenirs.  We had the house special bingsoo (the Korean ice kachang) and it was so refreshing.  Not only was the shaven ice powdery soft the red beans were tasty the selection of healthy nuts crunchy and various Korean rice cakes both soft and crispy were delicious - all in a great dessert.  Being starved of clean fresh air for a while during the haze season back in Singapore it was very refreshing to sit outside enjoying the cool clean air and view the miles of tea bushes.We were so entranced by the place that we returned for lunch the next day.  I had the rice balls with soba & oden soup while my sis had a mini hot dog with the same soup.  We then proceeded to relax with a cup of coffee.  What utter bliss!Besides enjoying the F&B we picked up body scrub facial wash and some soft drinking bottles.  The staff was friendly and fluent enough in English which made our buying experience very smooth indeed.  We will definitely return when we are next in Jeju.

The Sanbanggulsa Temple is located SSW of Mt. Hallasan directly at the coast. It is a very unique and colourful temple which reminds us more on the temple in Taiwan as in Korea mainland. The temple is located just below Mt. Sanbang. We had our junior with us but with older kids it is probably a nice tour on top including the temple. The view from the temple is very nice and gorgeous. Probably from top of Mt. Sanbang even better. The area is quiet and peaceful.? Except the opposite place where noisy? Korean caterwaul being played at a swing boat. The place is not reachable for stroller and wheel chair. Parking place available. Entrance fee is negligible for parking and temple access. It is definitely worth to stop and to spend some time. Religious people are probably also allowed to pray i guess. Doors are open.
The ocean view is splendid but the rock doesnt live up to its name possibly due to erosion just like the 12 apostles in the Great Ocean road.  And its very crowded ...

The number one attraction on Jeju and an impressive climb to the top. Lots of signs to explain the geological formations at key points en route. The attractions divides the ascenders from the descenders which helps with the climb. Wonderful view from the top. The attraction is beautifully looked after no litter and only about 짙1 to visit. The name of this mountain means that there is a room in the mountain. The mountain room has a mysterious statue of Buddha and a view of the sea from the room. You do not need much time to explore this mountain. I recommend that you take a short tour in Mt. Sanbang and spend more time at nearby Songak Mountain.

The museum is limited in size but the fantastic shop and cafe make up for that. The history is interesting but the ability to smell and taste teas is awesome!  Highly recommend the Hallabong Fredo!  The green tea was great too. Pretty views of the landscape.

the indoor as 5 themes each of them very tidy and pretty. the exterior has different zones and a large lawn. i went there thinking just another botanical garden but i was well impressed i recommend.from here you can have a nice view from the entire red bridge and from the top of the indoors garden you can have a 360' view from entire city and surrounds on a clear dayreally worth to visit
The hike up will take around 20-30 mins depending on your speed. It's pretty steep stairs going up but you can take your own sweet time to enjoy the breathtaking view while hiking.

Seongsan Ilchulbong also called as Sunrise Peak! It's located on the Eastern end of Jeju do Island. There is a huge crater at the top of the peak! Really gorgeous view of the waterfall which flows right into the sea. Sat near to the waterfall and my shirt got slightly wet by the water splashes. Cold but refreshing. Do wear proper shoes if you intend to walk on the huge rocks to go near the waterfall.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.
Quite an eyeopening day with many great art installations to explore and view. Would not recommend this for prudish people! Most of the art is outside remember to pack a jacket/umbrella.

Place where you can consider one of the exercise from steps and all the way to the end to view the nature of Lava.You can learn about the Manjanggul Cave as there's information along the way. Cool weather as we went during the winter. Not sure if you go during any other season.Must come as you might not get it from your own country.
One of the UNESCO World Heritage site. Highly recommended to view its natural beauty.  The path is not easy to walk but it's worth the effort. Cold and wet!

One of the most memorable places during my visit to Jeju is Songaksan. Only a slight hike up and you'll get the best coastal view. The hike is so gradual that everybody can do it. One of my best spot in Jeju. We went in July end and the climate was very very hot. We were sweating like anything and in the mid way my wife said lets go back but i was like we have to go. The view is so astonishing and it definitely looks like a world heritage.Tip: Do keep lot of water if visiting in summer.This peak has lot of stairs (not advisable old person or for heart patient).

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.
Not have to hike too much. Look peaceful but nothing much to see and the view is not too impressive. Can see autumn leaves far away. Can spend less than one hour here.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Nice views out to the green tea fields.  Very pleasant.
