I came to jeju with my friends and the first place we visited is Iho tewoo beach! Ocean view is amazing and the tidal waves are amazing.We had really good moment as a group there despite the fact the weather was cold. Iho tewoo beach is a must go place if u're traveling alone or with your family.
I came here without any plans. It was better than I expended. The warm house is beautiful and elegant. Must go up to the roof and you can see the astonishing view!!!

I am 6 years old and when I first got to sunrise peak it was really tall and big. I thought I couldn't climb it but I did. My mummy wanted to quit but I wouldn't let her. The best bit was we saw a shop that sold water and I bought juice. It was halfway up so mummy didn't need to carry water after all. I wish it wasn't such a cloudy day but the view was still cool. I saw a telescope to see everything. Me and my Brother had a fight over the telescope and mummy and daddy got mad. When we got to the top daddy said it was a crater but I did not see any lava so I think he was lying. The end. Finished.
Hundreds of steps going up. Well organized with a few view point stops. On the top we found volunteer guides that  was friendly and informative.The view from the top is impressive

Have never fired a live round before so this was pretty exhilarating for me. There are about 7-8 pistols and revolvers to choose from and i settled with a Beretta. There are computer screens that can help you to view where your last shot was. And at the end you can keep your target paper. We ate at the buffet downstairs on the 3rd floor before coming up as there is a 35% discount on the shooting range price after. The original price for 12 rounds is 35k won. The staff are not able to speak english at all which was quite a bummer as they will usually guide you and teach you how to shoot the target properly.

Hallasan the 2nd highest mountain in South Korea is a fantastic hiking place!! You can choose to hike from two different easy routes to enjoy different scenery. If this is your first hike after a long hiatus do be mindful that it's better to take the easy route. Cos at some points it's huge boulders that require some stamina to step up.Take the first bus from the bus interchange cos it's advisable for tourists to reach midpoint by noon so that you have adequate time to trek back and catch the last bus from the bus stop which is still 20 min from the start of trekking point. Alternatively there's taxi if you are a group or pair. There's only a hut at midpoint which sells cup noodles which is not cheap.  Thus advisable to bring along dry food and plenty of water for recovery. Along the way you would meet seasoned hikers and some are so friendly that they offer you a ginseng sweet if they see you resting.  There's a water point and the water taste so good! The viewing points offer such fantastic view and it's so breezy that we forgot ourselves!  Definitely a place to visit.

Green tea Roll & ice cream with a nice view maybe thats a fit words for this place. The tea fields covers a large area green and fresh air. Cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/ cakes and ice cream to visitors. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream. I?셫 Highly recommended this place for green tea lover.
Great view with sunset and mythical legend. Definitely a must visit for all. Plenty of restaurant nearby as well! Live the ocean view and rock is just cherry on to of icing. Highly recommend!!
Great beach Great viewsAnd amazing picture spotsI recommend having a coffee at a cafe dolmondo ..  there which is right over the beach Beautiful scenery
Good view. Very amazing tea recommended for people who love to drink tea. Have Great cafe to chill and relax. Varieties of place have museum cafe and tea plantation

Good place to visit. We joined YEHA's East Course tour and this is one of the stops. A 20-25 mins walk up the slope to the tip of the peak. Nice to do this at end Nov where weather is cool. You can get a good view when you reach the top. You can visit Woman Drivers taking their dip at the base. There are many shops at the base where all buses and cars park.

Friend and I visited this museum on our first trip to Korea (while on the island of Jeju) and was pleasantly surprised by a great live performance of traditional African dances and drum beats/riddim. The artifacts are also very interesting and place was so big (3 floors) that we didn't have time to view everything.

Fantastic place with lots and lots of teddy bear. Didn't know that teddy bear is named after America President. Worth spending a few hours looking at museum. Its even more better view outside at the garden.
Family fun...there were views in every direction & everyone was friendly...a family allowed our daughter to walk their dog. The beautiful yellow flowers were everywhere. It was a nice little hike.

Experience狩狩狩狩狩Highlly recommendedWonderful for taking pictures and lovely views. Highly recommended for couples on honeymoons and hikers wanting a picturesque view while hiking and climbing all the way up

Enjoy the breathtaking views of the ocean and impressive rock formation while walking along the coast. Very beautiful and unique scenery that is really beyond description. The beauty of nature is really awesome. One has to be there to experience it! Thanks to our guesthouse owner for recommending this place!

Do try to catch the sunrise. The view is awesome and the tour groups will start coming in around 9am onwards. Please check with your hotel staff the night before for sunrise timing. Do try to reach there at least 45mins before it rise. My friend and i overslept and had to literally run up in order not to miss the sunrise.

Cute little beach. Hamdeoks a nice area to chill out with a lot of cafes by the beach and you can eat with a view of the ocean. Koreans are not very big on swimming but you can jump in and go for a quick dip yourself. Only down side is sometimes there can be a bit of rubbish around. But recommended for a day trip

Considered one of the ten best view points of Jeju this attraction is not to be missed One can enjoy this visit if you like to soak yourself or would like to find yourself among the clouds. On a foggy day one can easily miss the existence of this mountain.If you are visiting during winter or rainy season better to plan the visit during afternoon as one can have a magnificent view from the top without much clouds around.This mountain believed to be formed by the volcanic lava houses the Sanbang-gulsa Temple and the Bomunsa Temple.It also has other attractions as Golden Bhuddha Tea Shops etc. Once on the top one can see the ridge called the Dragon Head where a memorial has been built for Hendrick Hamel the first westerner who was the first to introduce Korea to the western world after his ship got wrecked. This mountain is believed to be used as a watch tower and smoke used to be sent out during the day or fire was lit during the night if any urgent message was needed to be conveyed.Climbing the steps would be a little tough for those who are not regular walkers and for the old.

Climbed it on a windy afternoon. Will take you around 20-30mins if you are reasonably fit. Spectacular views all around even before you reach the peak. Very worth the exercise. Its a 200m climb and steep at some sections. Wear comfortable shoes and clothing. Will recommend climbing early to catch the sunrise at the summit.

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.

Came to this temple as we only wanted a view of Mt Hallasan. But we kinda ended up with a pleasant surprise. Temple grounds are huge and it's peaceful to be away from the hustle and bustle of the city for a while.

Before flying to Jeju-do (island) many of my friends suggested me to do a one day jeju tour that completes the island in one day. But I'm the type of person to enjoy my vacation slowly. Although the island is not that big I wanted to enjoy every bit and detail of the island. I choose to focus on one area at a time. Three months before my trip I researched top 5 beaches in Jeju. After researching I decided my hotel and location place where to spend my vacation. I choose Seogwipo end of Jeju.  The hotel I stayed in was Grand Mer Hotel. I stayed 3 nights there it was a new hotel and the best part was it was across the ocean. You can wake up to the view of the Jungmun beach. Which was listed top beach in Jeju. It's a little far out so you'll need to rent a car. Shopping and museums and hiking was 10 mins drive away. But the view was spectacular and my morning walk was so refreshing. If your ever in Seogwipo you have to try Hawaiian Shrimp restaurant which was 15 mins away from my hotel
Been here during last autumn (Nov 2016). I was mesmerized by the view because that time the sun was setting as well. Recommended for nature lover.
Beautiful waterfall with an amazing view - can recommend buying a drink or an icecream before going the stairs down and then chilling on the big stones

Beautiful small beach with lots of resteraunt and cafes around. Each cafe is so beautifully decorated with some having their own outdoor area for you to chill and enjoy the view. There are multiple area with allocated photo opportunities for those who likes to take pictures. Definitely a place to recommend coming in Jeju Island.
Beautiful cave with lava rock sides. Hard to take beautiful pictures but amazing views. Specially the end of the 1km hike inside the lava tube.

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

As someone said earlier this one is really more of a store for green tea rather than a museum although certainly there are display cases of tea ware to make the museum claim credible. What it is without a doubt is a gorgeous tea store. Aesthetics-wise -- it's so excellently designed it can easily inspire anyone to spend about a hundred U.S. dollars or so just on green tea stuff.The tea you can buy even in Seoul so if you don't want to lug them you can buy O'Sulloc stuff in Seoul. But I don't think you can easily find a place elsewhere that serves the O'Sulloc food they were serving here. I tried the green tea cappuccino the green tea cake green tea cookies and green tea soft serve. They were reasonably yummy although nothing to rave about. It's really the novelty of it that makes the food purchase worth it. Great view of the tea fields from the rooftop.I recommend it to all green tea loving people.

As noted by other reviewers there are indeed large crowds to beat on a weekend visit but the tea museum is definitely worth a visit. Good to note that here is English subtitling on most of the signs in the small museum. The biggest draw for me was the beautiful architecture of the building. Local volcanic stone is used in combination with brick glass and steel. The result is beautiful and the building has featured in quite a few design magazines for good reason.

All the reviews I read of Udo made it sound so beautiful and quaint but I found in reality it was actually rather anti-climactic. The sights don?t begin to compare to those on Jeju and while the island is quaint I didn?t find it endearing enough to justify the trip over. The peanut ice cream is worth trying though!

A short climb to the top of the top of the hills for the crater view. Be sure to wear comfortable shoe and small bottles of water as it involve steep stairs. Recommended to go in the morning to avoid tourist congestion and ugly scene (Chinese tourist spitting around like nobody business)

A good place especially for first-timers or those who are interested to see lava formations. Really gorgeous view when the sea hit those rocks. Nothing much to see so don't really have to spend much time here.

A compact park around a crater. Walk to the top and down the slope to various parts that can offer some quiet relaxation. The view is peaceful rather than spectacular but worth spending a couple of quiet hours.

You'll have to go at the right time to get the best views of this place. During autumn, there'll be a short few weeks where the pampas flowers bloom all over the crater, making the views breathtaking and romantic! Go during sunset and you definately will not regret it. I went there on 2 Nov 2012, recommended by the owner of my guesthouse. By far my top favourite sight in Jeju-do. Do check with your guide or guesthouse owner if the pampas flowers are blooming when you're there in autumn cos if they are not, then this visit can be missed as there'll be nothing much to see.

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.? Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!? It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

You can climb up to the peak, you can climb down to the beach, or just walk around in between, & still have beautiful views. You could spend most of the day here. The women divers were not diving the day we were there.

Wouldn't really recommend this place as i don't find it very interesting. Think it's a very good idea (since Korean Dramas are so popular) but very bad execution. If you have the spare time, don't mind spending the money, you are nearby and you loveeeeee korean drama, maybe you can consider coming.. else, don't waste your time here.Full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/drama-world/

While we are attended an business meeting, after finishing all we went to visit some places. This place is very natural, but you need to walk a little bit to reach until the fountain.Keep some time for this place to explore and perhaps enjoy. Taking photos also can be very beautiful as it offers stunning views.

While it is not the only waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea as many think (I've seen them both in Indonesia and Philippines), it is definitely a cool waterfall to see and they are relatively rare. I would definitely recommend seeing this waterfall first if you're planning to check out all of the waterfalls on Jeju. It is very accessible and a great viewing experience.

When we arrived, we were welcomed by beautiful views of the meadows and fences. The view from the top is also very nice.Not recommended for parents and young children, because the trip to the peak is around 20-30 minutes depending on each person's stamina.Overall the view of the is very beautiful.There was also a female diver show catching fish without modern equipment around 11 or 12 o'clock (forget the exact time), mostly of the female divers are aged. The catch is sold quite expensive.

we've seen a few caves and this one is truly unique.  Its not loaded in formations such as stalagmites/stalagtites, but the lava shelves go on forever.  It literally takes over thirty minutes to walk from one end to the other at a decent clip.  Very humid inside, definately bring an umbrella or raincoat.  Also very chilly so if you are there in summer, the temperature change can be significant.  I brought a flashlight but you really don't need it as they do a great job in keeping you on the straight and narrow.  It really gives you a great understanding of what nature can do, well worth the detour to view

Went there without much training as I envisage that winter time is more pleasant to climb. We reached the base around 7.30am as we try to take the first bus. As we envisage there are snow, I have a pair of crampons bought before arriving in Jeju. Fortunately I did as the crampon sold at the shop is rather expensive. Then it was a relax 2 hours climb, I did not want to rush, but took time to appreciate the environments and snow. The crampons came in useful as you climb further up, it gets slippery. Good to have walking sticks too. At about the 1000+ meter stop, there is shop where you could buys hot noodles and drinks. I bought another set of crampons there as it is reasonable compared to the shop at the base of the mountain.After a short rest, the final climb to the top. Here there is a series of steps and staircase that leads to the top. At some point it was rather steep so have to climb up slowly, catching my breaths as the higher altitude and cold tends to slow you down. There is a timing to get down from the mountain per regulations, hence the need to get to the top early to enjoy the view and triumph. Finally reaching the top, was rewarded with a gorgeous scenery. It was kind of crowded and there was a queue of climbers taking turns to take picture with the summit monument.  After taking lots of pictures, hiking down was relatively easily, reaching the base in half the time. Took the bus back to town to enjoy a beer and fried chickens. A trip not to be missed.

Went there by bus using the 201 bus line, it will stop you to the 'entrance' (basically the highway) which is a long far walk into the actual entrance. There's a small bus stop where you can take another bus in (slow) but taxis will frequent the highway entrance looking for customers. The cave itself its a magnificent sight to behold..it's huge! Not sure about all the negative reviews about it poorly lit and all, because the place is actually adequately lit (to fit the ambiance of a cave, no artificial colored disco lights) and concrete steps are placed everywhere in the tunnel to prevent accidental missteps. The ground is naturally uneven, you can't expect marbled tiles here. It can get quite cold and wet at 10-13deg, so bring a light jacket and proper walking shoes. Overall it's quite an experience, you can tell your friends that you've been in the underbelly of a volcano!

Went there and hike up the hill for less than 20 minutes. Not suitable for elderly people to hike up the hill. Toilets at the hillside currently under construction. So there is no toilet at the peak. View was spectacular at the peak. Upon leaving, purchase a huge long foot sausage nearby GS shop. The pair of old couple was indeed very friendly ><

Went during the winter season (end Dec), the cold isn't unbearable but the wind is! The climb may not be the easiest but it's doable. Plus you see many tourists and elderlies climbing it together with you, so it isn't that bad of a hike up. When you're up, the view is to shout for. Awesome view!

Well-known by Korean tourists to Jeju as a filming location for the very popular drama   Daejangguem  , Oedolgae is perhaps the most scenic volcanic rock formation on the island. The area is more of a viewpoint attraction, you walk the beautiful coastline only so far. Most visitors spend 30-60 minutes visiting the site, cameras are usually busy. If you're visiting Jeju during the summer, it is probably best to visit Oedolgae in the morning before it gets too busy. Jeju is full of dramatic coastline, this is one of the most picturesque locations.

Well maintained, easy hike up and down with the peak. Designated route for upwards hike and descending, so do not go against the flow. Very rewarding view at the peak. Take note of the women driver performance, twice a day. We missed it as we read online that it was 3.30pm, but it was actually 3pm.

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

We were on a tour bus when we passed by the road. There were quite a lot of people so we couldn't really go down and take pictures. It was literally a 5 minute driveby. Luckily, I was near the front so I had a view of the road and it's optical illusions. I recommend coming with a rented car or taxi, not with a big group. Then you get to really appreciate why it's called the Mysterious Road. I heard from our tour guide that some golf ranges in the area have the same effect to. Golfers should ask around so you can play there.

We were lucky with the weather to visit the place, and it is important because during the rain it might not be so attractive.The nature is very beautiful, you will take good pictures for sure.We took a small electric car (for 2 people), but it was comparatively expensive for only 2,5 hours. It is possible to go around the island during that time but only without staying at all tourist points. Moreover, you cannot really enjoy the trip because of being in hurry.All Korean suggested to try peanut and mandarin ice-cream, that we did. Again the price was high, and mandarin one was so sweet that make us to put it in trash right away.People in the island are friendly, and even offer to pick us up to some places by car and shown the shortest way.Taking a boat to see caves was the best experience during the whole travel. For only 10 000 won you will have a lot of fun as the boat goes so fast, and definetly amazing view on the island.

We were here in October, so we weren't swimming. We drove by here one day to check it out, a day or two after a typhoon hit, and the beach was trashed a bit (just from trees and debris and stuff), but people were cleaning it up and there were still lots of people enjoying the beach. It looks like a nice place to spend a day, and there seemed to be a bunch of restaurants and cafes dotting the beach as well. We stopped at one of the cafes for a coffee and to enjoy the view of the water for a bit.

We went up in 20 minutes and down in 15,  we are quite fit,  all age groups going up and even people in flip flops!) I would recommend you time your visit so that you get to see the women divers (13:30 and 15:00) either before or after your walk.  If I went there for just the walk I would have been disappointed,  the photos you see are of course ariel views and a walk up doesn't give you that view,  having said that the coastal views from above are nice.  It was raining when we went but it was still do-able.  We took bus 701 (runs every 20 mins 3300 wan per person each way) from seogwipo and back.  It stops at Seongsan-ri office,  ticket booth is a couple of minutes walk away.

we went up by erimok, was the slightly shorter course but scenery was still fantastic towards the top. took us 3.3hours to reach the 1700m resting point which sells korean cup noodles at only 1500+won (ard there). this is not the peak, if you like to challenge yourself further, will have to walk for another 3-4 hours to the peak. So if you really decide to go to the peak, then just use the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa course, its shorter.We were lucky to meet some locals who advise us to walk down by yeongsil. And apparently yeongsil has the most scenic view out of all the courses. Only thing is that its full of stairs... so dont advice ascending by yeongsil. We could see ppl giving up halfway on our way down yeongsil. One more problem abt yeongsil for those who dont drive is that the bus stops 2km away from the main entrance (20mins BRISK walk) and its quite steep on most parts. Or else you can actually catch a taxi from the bus stop, should be a 5mins journey.

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)

We went to Marado Island by taking a 1 h-long ferry from Jeju Island (Daejung-Eup, Hamo ri). The ferry was nice and the could stand in either deck to enjoy the scenic view of the ocean. When you approach the island you could see the beauty of volcanic layers that forms the island and the interface of volcanic rocks and ocean was amazing. Walking is the best way to enjoy the island and you may spend nearly 3 h in the island. There are a couple of restaurants, a beautiful buddha temple, a church etc. A nice half-day trip. Highly recommended.
We went there. picture perfect view, quiet and serene. We had a chance of  spending time there on 1 July, 2017. perhaps one of the best beach in Jeju. Please go. you will enjoy.

We went there right after rain, which is a recommended time to visit since there are more fresh air pumping out from all those trees. The view reminded me of Totoro, the mysterious forest atmosphere!! I would definately visit again.

We went Seongsan Ilchulbong in the evening, even though it's known as the Sunrise Peak. The hike up was a little tiring for us as we had previously scaled up a few other peaks the same day. There are quite a few resting spots around, so rest assured you can always catch a breather before ascending the next flight of steps.Bring enough water with you as drinks sold along the way can be quite expensive!The view at the peak is surreal. The sun sets rather slowly in Jeju, so you'll have ample time to scale up and take multiple shots of the place.I will definitely visit the peak again. This time, I'll go for the sunrise. :)

We went in fall and took the Youngsil pathway. There are about 4-5 different ways to hike up. I thought ours was supposed to be an easier one, but Id say it is like walking up the stairs endlessly. Once you get high up enough, you have a fantanstic view, and in fall, it is all red and yellow leaved. It's absolutely gorgeous and worth the hike. The way up and down is also very much enjoyable. But there is quite a bit of people, so if you are slow, make space for others coming behind you.

We went as group of 25 people (friends) but it only took us 10 mins for photo taking and we left.Overall, the view was nice but i would say, worth viewing once only since it is not far away from the airport.

We visited Udo Island in October 2016 and took the hop on hop off bus and got off at the first stop to climb up to the peak where the lighthouse was.  The climb took about an hour and though there were steps and a well travelled path, it still required some physical effort. There were hardly any trees and you would be well advised to wear a hat and sun block. Wear comfortable walking/hiking shoes and bring plenty of drinking water.  We climbed to the peak on a hot sunny day and had to stop a few times before we reached the lighthouse. The view was worth our effort.  Then we climbed down to the surrounding park, which was basically grassland with minimal trees and hardly any shelter. There were lots of other tourists.  We saw some horses grazing here and could see across to the mainland and sunrise peak as well as parts of Udo below.  This is the most enjoyable part of UDO for us and highly recommended.

We visited this sunrise pick which is one of the Natural wondes of the world during first week of May. It is easy to climb, with lots of opportunities to take rest if you need. The views during climb are simply superb. While we were climbing we saw amazingly shaped cloud formations. After all the efforts of climbing, the views from the peak are beautiful. We could not see the sunrise, but I am sure it would be worth the early getting up.I will strongly recommend visit to this place.

We visited the Jungmun Golf Club for doing the Moon Light Walking Tour. We went there to warm up for the Jeju Olle Walking Festival. The view was awesome and it was a nice experience to walk there during sunset. At the end, they prepare a concert for all the participants there.

we took tour to east of Jeju fm our guesthouse, Yeha. We intended to go to Seongsan Ilchulbong that why we were excited to know our time was perfect with Yeha tour. No idea that Seongsan Ilchulbong had sooo many stairs, we took a lot of stops before top. While we took rest, we turned back and saw beautiful view down the hill. Once we got on top, the view was so nice as well. It was worth it every single stair by looking the view from the top.We enjoyed our time to go down, windy and cold. We also enjoyed performance woman diver and saw directly what they collected fresh from the sea.

We took bus no 100 from seogwipo city to the last bus stop. Walk up the road to the next bus stop and got on the intercity bus no 701. Got off at the beach overlooking seongsan illchubong. Plenty of spots for great pics here. Walked all the way to the entrance and up. Manageable. Highly recommend wearing good comfortable shoes. The climb up was not as bad as I thought it would be. The view from the bottom was quite intimidating at first  though. Many restaurants with reasonable prices to stop for lunch after the climb. Overall, good place to visit.

We took bus 710 from intercity terminal, cost 3300won per way. A pretty long ride, about 1hr plus. Met two visitors, one from Singapore & another from Malaysia; very friendly and gave us lot of tips getting around. When we reached at noon, the place was packed with tour buses, people & soldiers (on sight-seeing). Not a difficult hike for reasonable fit person but certainly a challenge for older folk with the steep steps. Nice view but have seen better.

We took bus 701 from Jeju city... it only took 1hr 30mins when we were told it would take 2hrs which was a pleasant surprise. The walk up is (unsurprisingly) hard because of all the steep and often uneven steps. I would suggest going in the morning or late afternoon when it's not so hot because in the heat it was tough! People say it takes 20 mins which I would say is accurate but of course depends on your fitness levels. It was so worth it though, the views are incredible. They have an amphitheater like viewing platform I guess for those wanting to see sunset/sunrise. And you go down a different way so no clashing with people coming up. It can get quite busy though!

We took bus 182 early morning reached there around 7.30am and started to hike about 8am. It's good to bring hiking stick as there are lots of steps up, with a hiking stick it's easier to move up the rocky paths. It was very cold at the mountain so it's good to wear in layers and can remove the jackets if it gets too warm during the hike. We managed to reach Saraoreum shelter before 12pm where we ate and took a break before moving on to the summit. After 12pm no one is allowed to move on up to the summit from the shelter as it gets dark very early during winter time. We reached the summit just before 1.30pm. The ranger already chasing people to get down. It was very cold and windy at the top and it started to drizzle. So it's important to bring a raincoat too. I could'nt get a good view as it was very foggy and windy. We did'nt get some rest and started to descend. It took a long while to descend too as the path is very rocky and slippery. Lucky i have my hiking stick with me. Half way down it started to get dark we needed to use our handphones as touch light to guide us down the path. Very happy we are all able to reach the summit. It's a nice experience.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

We love the story around the Innisfree Jeju House. It's organic and farm to table supply chain and mission is admirable. We had the the diver's special bento and it was delicious. My wife had the blue colored tea ade and I had fresh carrot juice and all of it was great. The have beautiful cakes in the shape of Halla mountain and tiramisu with delicate flower designs. The prices are in the higher end but well worth the refined quality and experience for those who like this sort of thing. My wife loved the purity of the food and calm views of the tea plantation.They also have products for sale as well as a tea extract exhibit. They have fun hands on tea soap making as well you can purchase and do there. Or they have other ones you can purchase and take home to do. Great place to calm down, re-energize, and enjoy.

We hiked up on a cloudy day. I really recommend choosing the day for hiking according to the weather forecast. The hike itself and the views and people on the path made it an unforgettable experience, but after like 2,5 hours of hiking on a really quick pace we made it to the top and couldn't see anything. The crater was filled with mist and it was so windy that staying up there would have been quite uncomfortable. It doesn't necessarily take 4,5hours to get up and 4,5 hours to get down, if you don't stop every two hundred meters. But make sure to get to the last milestone (the place to take a break and buy ramen) in time to be able to start the climb to the top.I can only imagine what the trip and the scenery would be like on a clear sunny day.

We hiked this in December in the snow.  We started from the Yeongsil entrance, and just went up to the Shelter as we started pretty late.  The hike is tough for those who are out of shape but perfectly doable for regular hikers.  It took us about 2 hours up and about 1.5 hours down - the snow making it much slower than we would normally take (and more scenic, but very slippery in places).I would recommend good hiking shoes as the rocks are tough and slippery in places - I saw some people wearing what I would consider to be bedroom slippers and they were really struggling!  Those mini-crampons were also a godsend in the snow (the shop at the bottom sells them).Great views on the way up and from the top.  As we had a car, we had to go back the way we came but next time we will come when the plants are green and do a loop hike.  Can't wait.

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do). The Sangumburi entrance fee is expensive if not in season to see the wheat fields at their peak and the changing leaves of fall, I think it was 11,000won or $11. I recommend going to Chefline Park if you are seeing this April 2018. Entrance if free there and but no volcanic crater. We went here and there was construction going on and the wheat fields had been cut down. They should charge less when construction is going on and the field has been cut. The walk around the park only takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. There are some nice views and the crater is cool.

We had a tour inside a golf club and since it's a huge land, it actually takes time to go back and forth. So I recommend it for people who enjoy walking especially in such a beautiful place. At the end of the tour, we had a mini-concert organized by them and they were signing us a live song which made me goosebumps because it was like in a movie where you enjoy the ocean view, nature, and good music with the best company.

We got here by public bus from the Manjanggul caves. It took about an hour as we had to transfer. Using the public transport is a bit of an adventure in itself. I think the bus routes have been updated lately so even some of the locals seem confused at times.We looked at the top of the peak and thought, 'no way, this looks like it'll take 2 hours to climb'. However after asking other tourists we were told it takes about 25 minutes. I was sceptical as I'm not the fastest at going up stairs.The entry fee was 2,000 krw and despite taking quite a lot of short breaks on the way up we reached the top in 20 minutes! The views were lovely.We ended up doing this around midday and it was HOT. I recommend coming here earlier or later in the day if you can when it is a bit cooler. It was rewarding to reach the top. They are selling some drinks in the way up but I recommend that you pack some water as well as a snack to eat when you enjoy the views at the top.

We found the reviews here very useful for preparing ourselves for the ascent so I'm contributing my own, hoping that others will find it equally helpful!   I'd say that it's a simple ascent for those already used to hill walks and there's no way one can lose the path, as it's between ropes or handrails all the way.  The path surface is mainly made of railway sleeper type large wooden beams and rocks which provide good terrain when dry.  However, for our descent it was raining and slippery and we were constantly bracing ourselves for a slip caused by the crowds - beware those with spikey walking poles! - descending more quickly than we were!  Our ascent to the peak took a leisurely 3 1/4 hours so we were delighted, although we weren't rewarded with any views but the sense of achievement and relief was great!  Our descent took 3 3/4 hours and sometimes my pace felt a little faster than comfortable, as had to concentrate so hard on each footstep placing. It looked as if some sections of the path near the summit have been replaced fairly recently, as we found it to be in good condition and not like the experience of other reviewers - and that was a relief!  I'm very glad that I wore my walking boots to protect my ankles, as the rocks are uneven and a few are slightly unstable.  So, short, if you're fit and used to hill-walking, you have nothing to fear but if you're not usually very active, then give yourself a plan B e.g. opting for the side-path to Sara Oreum if you realise, by the junction with the path off to that (round trip 40mins) that you're struggling.  That would mean that you'd still have the great satisfaction of a spectacular view from Korea's highest mountain but without the stress of having had to climb - and descend! - the 1200 metres from the bus stop to the peak!  Make sure you have enough layers of clothes and a good hat and gloves for the summit and descent, as, at this time of year, you'll definitely need them.  Oh, and if you're looking at the frequent posts with figures on alongside the path and which start with a '1' at the bottom which then progress to '2' etc, the peak is '36'.  Hoping you find this as helpful as we found other reviews!

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

We did this hike by end of March 2014. The first part is indeed a kind of forest walk. Half way we were indeed surprised to see some snow on the hills and later on lots of snow on the path, Since we did not have those clampons it was pretty tough. At the 2nd shelter we did indeed buy those clampons whereafter the hike was more easy to do. The view from top was not that good due to the upcoming mist. We were amazed though to see so many RAVENS waiting for food.

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water. Most people were using walking poles as well, which became extremely frustrating as they tended to block the paths. The only people I saw fall were using these poles, they really are not required.It would be difficult to do this track in the rain, as it would get quite slippery in places. My advice would be to go early to avoid the majority of the crowds - the car park fills with tour buses by mid-morning. We started at 0700 and it was still relatively busy then. You need to be at the last rest station by 1230 to be able to continue to the summit and leave the summit by 1430.Overall - I wouldn't do it again, but if you had a free day on Jeju, it's a good way to burn off a few calories.

We can to Jeju island for a couple of days just for this park! You have different paths to get up to the top! We decided to take the easier one to get up and than the harder one to come back! (In the end it was a good decisions) the nature is incredible and is very peaceful! On top, if you are lucky and have clear wether, the view is outstanding! If you want to do the hard way, is important to have good shoes as you walk over rocks and stones!

We came to visit in the late afternoon, it was lovely and quiet, with a lot of plants to enjoy and two fish ponds. Very nice afternoon stroll, and a welcome escape from the city hustle and bustle. The staff were all very friendly and eager to teach us how to best view and appreciate the plants and gardens. Overall a lovely place to visit in the afternoon

We came here for the sunset view, because that was the recommendation for this place. But we were disappointed.We reached Jeju via plane around 1pm and went to Hallim park (5min walk to Hyeopjae beach) after check in. After a walk around Hallim park we walk to Hyeopjae Beach for sunset watching. The weather is just nice, no rain, not too hot. The sand beach was covered with plastic material (?), I guess so tourist can walk on it. There was few garbage lying around the beach and it was a bit crowded with people, both local and tourists. The sunset view is not that nice.Again, to be fair, we come from the tropic. The Bornean sunset is probably the best sunset. So for people from the tropics, you can skip this place if you want to. But if you have nothing to do in Jeju, I guess you can come here to relax, after a walk at Hallim Park.To go here: Take bus #710 bound for Hyeopjae beach (or Hallim Park if you want to go there first. It's just 5min walk to Hyeopjae beach).
we came here during the end of autum, so the grass was all yellow and brown. there was not much to see.Not recommended when you come in March, coz the view is not very nice..but we still had fun

We came here as part of a tour from Hong Kong and no one else went to climb up to the top, but me and my boyfriend did. It's about a 30 minute walk - you can take it slowly and take photos along the way, but it can be a bit steep. However, the views are great (on a clear day) and you get a good workout (after sitting on a bus for so long). The ascent/descent paths are clearly marked and separated, so it's quite well organised and the path/fence is very well maintained. At the top, you can overlook the big crater, which is now overgrown with lots of lush grass and trees - quite beautiful. You can also overlook the water and the town below etc. The way down has lots of stairs, so watch out if you have bad knees.

We booked Mr Ko for 4 days.Though we prepared our itinerary but we end up leaving the schedule to him as he will change based on the weather condition.Looking through the photos he took for us, it?셲 all fun memories! We never had so many group photos taken as if we had a personal photographer with us.He does impromptu stops for us to take sceneries like sunset, cherry blossom view and gave us tips how we can capture those moments.He brought us to local restaurants with good value.He patiently waited for us as we time to enjoy the scenery, ended up he has to take v late lunch....He has made our jeju trip fun and memorable. We recommend his service though he speaks very little English. He provides WiFi in the jumbo taxi so we can do google translate when we had problem communicating.Thanks again Mr Ko!

Was wanting to catch sunset in Jeju, and it seems all will require some climbing. My family was tired, and hence chose this place instead.Not too bad for being lazy to climb. You will need to go to the far end near the hotel. The road alongside was quiet and very light traffic, so you can park there temporarily to view the sunset.

Was recommended to visit this crater by our driver cum guide. Initially we wasn't too keen from the view of main entrance but we were stunned by the beautiful silver grass surrounding after entering. Climbing slowly is possible thou pathway can be slight steep. My parent did it at their own pace and there was a little hut & mini playground at the top for a rest. Along the way up, silver grasses are fully bloom and it views are fascinating with mountains seen faraway (like a natural backdrop). It's a sight not to be missed and understood only occur during autumn into winter period!! Thanks to our taxi driver Mr Lee Hong Min for the great recommendations.

Was lucky to have been here as it was free for the entrance. Usually per entry would cost 2000 won but it was a holiday. The scenery and view is amazing up top. The view of the crater is nice but the view 180 degrees around is way better. You will see the town which you stopped at and the immense coastline around. Would highly recommend if you can catch the sunrise however it is quite a journey away from the Jeju city which means you have to time your travel right. Visiting during normal hours will still give you the breath taking view. Just a catch, you would have to hike. If you are fit enough, it should take you 15 to 20 mins up top. Can be pretty steep so take your time and rest along the way.

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html

Visited on my self drive with my 60+ old parents, wife and 2 & 4 yo kids. Easy to find on GPS,  plenty of parking. Those who don't fancy the hike up can choose to take a scenic path that's still pretty good (wheelchair accessible). We did the suicidal and hiked up baby carrying our kids. Wife and mum thighs are still aching after 3 days lol. It's quite a hike up multiple flight of stairs to get to the top but boy it was worth it! Great views of the crater and the city around, with a nice viewing area to park our tired bums. Mum almost gave up halfway though. Recommended for relatively fit people, think hard if you have old or young in your group.

Very nice, for some reason some people gas different view. This is volcanic cave, cave size is very big, you don't neet to bend. Just enjoy. A little dark. In my opinion, if you mix this cave with other tousist spot it is really good place.

Very interesting inside and out. The first floor is mostly modern about sexual preference health and rights but it is 95% in Korean. I would recommend to bring a Korean friend who doesn't mind translating if you are interested in that part. There was also a big wall of history at the very front which was all in Korean that would be worth translating. It wasn't very busy and some of the   hands on   things that would show examples were broken so I started with a mediocre impression. The bigger and more impressive part though is the number of historic sexual things they have on the second and third floor. Lots of artifacts about sex in Eastern cultures with some in Western cultures but a lot of things have their English translation. This part is much more impressive and interesting to look at. A lot of phallic objects and   traditional   pieces but it's historic and that is how people viewed sex in history. The more modern section is more modernly-styled and was a bit confusing (a lot of sex dolls...? kind of weird) and included more fetish stuff than I expected. Not much on queer and non-hetero there was a small section (in Korean) on the ground floor and then one very gray area display on the top floor but not a whole lot can be expected of Korea (where homosexuality is still viewed very negatively). Overall it was worth the price and was pretty interesting to look at. Having a translator or understanding Korean would make it more memorable.

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.

Up & down of the mountain took us 9.5 hours including some short rest time during the hike. We started the hike around 9am (recommend to start early, we were late), and came down around 6:30pm. Our legs were like jelly legs after the hike, but is worth the hike. You can see nice view along the journey. Please do not forget to greet everyone you met with   anyeonghaseyo  , they are all very friendly people. Wear a pair of good hiking shoes, bring some snacks with you and also water. The stalls along the mountain are closed during our hike, luckily we have prepared enough snacks and water. The view at the peak is breathless. A lots of old korean aunties and uncles also managed to reach the peak, so I guess we all younger than them have no excuses of not fit to hike, right? haha...Wear sport attire, although some said it will be freezing cold at the peak (about 1950 meters height), but believe me, you wont feel cold as you have already all sweat during the hike. We spent about 30mins to 1 hour at the peak taking photos, resting and having our snacks before going down again. A pair of good hiking shoes is important so that you won't get blister on your feet. We will go back again in different season if we have the chance. We were travelling there in Oct 2018.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unless one is interested in its history or legend about how the 3 holes came about, there is nothing much to explore. The compound is rather small and quiet, just a handful of visitors. In one pavilion is a 3D multimedia presentation, lasting 14 mins, which explains the legend behind these 3 holes. Unfortunately, visitors cannot get close to these holes, hence have to view from afar. 30 minutes is sufficient to cover this place, admission fees 2,500 won.Recommend to drop by only you have spare time to kill or already nearby. Else can skip this place.

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say   Udo  . The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the   old fashioned   bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo Island is a small island located in the east side of Jeju. We visited there due the great reviews given below in TripAdvisor. It cost about 5,500 won for the ferry ride to and fro. My friend and I wanted to ride the ATV while we were there however the rental shops were strict on the rental without international driving license so in the end we took a tour bus that stops at 4 different locations and cost 5,000won per person. The bus comes at an interval of 30 minutes so once you get down in one location, you can stay at the location for 30 minutes before moving on to another place. As we went there in Spring, the canola flowers are blooming beautifully. We also went to the Black Sand Beach and also the Hyopje Beach. Quite a good worth of money if you are looking at short tours around the island.

Udo is just picture perfect. We spent a few hours driving around this beautiful small island in early October. It only takes a few minutes on the ferry to go to Udo. You can hire scooters on the island but we actually brought over the scooters that we had hired in Jeju. It was approx 8000 (i think) to bring the scooter over and back. It was extremely busy when I was there but I did travel during Chuseok so I am not sure how busy it would be outside of holidays.I would definitely recommend a trip here as there are some fantastic and beautiful views. Just hire a scooter and drive around. As i mentioned earlier, if you are planning to hire a scooter on Jeju itself then do so and bring it over and it will be cheaper than renting one in Udo.

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Udo is a beautiful island by itself but due to the time constrain we had, we didn't had time to digest the beaches and scenic views. We had always wanted to rent an ATV there and even applied for international driving license as advised by many reviewers, however, we were greatly disappointed as the rental places only rent ATV to holders of Korean driving license. IDL are not accepted so don't waste money to apply for one. We rented electric bike in the end but had a dispute with the rental store nearest to the udo habour. One of our electric bike tyre went burst as the tyres were already old and the store owner wanted us to pay. We had an disagreement as the tyres when rented to us were already worn out. I must attribute to miscommunication as the people at udo are not conversant in English nor mandarin. We beared half the cost only after calling udo police to mediate the situation. But not much help from the police who told us to   go home  . Quite a memorable experience for us though.
