Okay so we went to the address given by Tripadvisor, and to our astonishment it was just a small garden behind a hotel. The only reason I can think why it was set to that address - is perhaps there's free parking? Dont give up if you're there! Because the actual site is only about 800m further down. There's a walking path (goes uphill from the hotel garden) along the coast, so simply walk along that and forgo the stone garden (needs an entry fee). The actual cliff site is open to public and free for viewing..Path is quite family-friendly.

Ok ok, to be honest...most of my rating is because of the seemingly endless cats that were here. I hadn't read any reviews of this place before going, I just thought it looked vaguely fun and was located right next yo Manjanggul Cave. Upon arriving, we noticed a couple of cats in the parking lot. I was so excited! When we got to the ticket booth, suddenly there were more cats! Directly beyond the booth is a small area with some handmade cat tower type things and some scratching posts. There were maybe around 15 cats in this area. I would estimate more than half of our time here was spent watching and petting the cats. The maze itself was fun. It was better if you ignored the map, I think. I think more people go here for kids, but if you're a cat lover, go!

Not just a temple, but amazing views of the coast and water. The temples are free to enter and offer an amazing experience. A must see if in this area. Plenty of drinks, food, views and restrooms. Only con is the steps are not very friendly. We have a 3, 7 and 8 year old. 3 year old needed carried.

Nice getaway island. We drove to the passenger terminal, park our car and take the ferry. The ferry ride there was fantastic. We fed the seagulls flying around the boat. it was a spectacular view!To travel within the island, take a bus or pay for a bike..it is a covered bike really cute. Or you can ride a bicycle.We took the bus, need to pay 6k won. There is a ticket office for shuttle bus. Buses numbered k1,k2,k3,rtc..there were 4 stops.the first stop has many actuvities, cafes, restaurants.You can spend an hour or more here. Second stop is lighthouse so we stop too.   The 3rd and 4th stops are the beaches. We did  not get off the  bus  l

My wife and I visited Ilchulbong at 5 pm, and unfortunately, couldn't catch the women divers in action. We made it to the top and it was quite a steep climb. We were completely winded by the time we reached the peak which has a beautiful viewing deck. The moon was up on one side while the sun was setting on the other side. It was our last day in Jeju and Korea and the beautiful sunset against the skyline of Jeju was the perfect ending we could have  asked for.

My number 2 favourite place in Jeju after Oedolgae. The rock formation of the cliff on this volcanic island is really fascinating! Before going, do make sure it's low tide time because it will be closed during high tide as it will be too dangerous. We also saw some women (should be women sea divers) who were selling fresh sea produce to those who want to eat them fresh and raw there. From there too, we could get a clear view of Sanbang Mountain which is just nearby. There's also a ship there and you can read about the history of how the ship ended up there. Be careful as you walk along the coast as sometimes you might be shocked by the sudden strong waves that come hitting towards the coast. I saw someone who was so shocked that she nearly dropped her mobile phone into the sea. Overall, it's one of the must go places in Jeju.

My mum who's 69 hiked up with difficulty, not because of the height, but more of the heat. Don't recommend hiking up during summer, the sun hits direct to you as you hike and dismount. But despite this, the view was amazing.

My kids request for it & quite excited at 1st. The excitement last for the 1st train ride & once we got off the 1st station & need to walk nearly 1km the kids mood just went sour. Then it becomes a more sour when you need to wait for the next train & need to fight for a seat. They're several trains runs every 15-20m if i'm not mistaken. If you missed one you need to wait till the next train. There is no ticket system while waiting for the train & one must grab the seats. So for me with a 2 kids & a baby it was just very hard. Luckily we stayed at the far front of the track station. We managed to get the train & never get off till the end of the station. We went during end of spring. Nothing much to see. Some flowers & i think it will be a great view during summer. Pro's : A great way to relax while enjoying the ride. Con's : You need to walk a lot. The truth is the train tracks was just goes around the same land. 1st come 1st serve basic when taking on the trains. Not stroller friendly.  Tip's : If you have a tight schedule, just stay on the train. Don't go off.

My husband and I walked here from Jeju-si (not recommended, unless you just really like to walk) so it's not far from the big hotel district. It's free to get in, but is mostly just trees and bushes, the wildflower garden was completely bare, of course, we didn't really come at the right time for that anyway. Follow the signs for   Green Shower   and you'll go up a pretty steep climb (especially for us in our flip-flops) to a nice view of the city and the ocean beyond. There's a nice lily-pad pond and a nice green   lawn   for anyone wanting a place to sit in nature. Although, the entire island of Jeju is about nature, so this wasn't a must-see for us. Just behind the Arboretum (on the left as you drive out and behind a group of concrete apartment buildings) is the ＿?由쇱?? Buddhist Temple. It has a really gorgeous campus and nice view of the city and sea, as well. If you got to the Arboretum, take the time to visit the temple, too.

my group of friends and I was bad luck when we visit this place, due to that day was a rainy day. Hence, when we reached the Samgumburi Crater, the weather was a rainy and windy day. When we reach the peak of mountain, the surroundings was full of mists and very windy. However, the view was great filled with green grass and trees.Hope I will come back one more time with the nice weather, I believe it will appear to be more awesome and nice than the view that I saw during rainy day.

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My friends and I didn't expect much when we headed out here. We thought it would be a short hike but we were in for a surprise. From the moment we got out of our car, the view of the ilchulbong was breathtaking. After a short 10-20? minute hike, we took a pause at the peak to take in the grand view in front of us. I believe this is the #1 attraction of Jeju island.

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My friend and I joined the East Coast one day tour - it’s meant to be a small group tour but only my friend and I joined today’s tour, so it was a private tour! Weather wasn’t nice today - it rained all day and was windy, but it was still a good trip after all. Beautiful scenery from the summit of the Seongsan Sunrise Peak - where you can have a view from above of the shore of the island. Our tour guide was June - a hiking expert with excellent knowledge of Korean culture and history. A memorable experience after all!

My first time to Korea focusing on Jeju and Seoul. Generally I would think the overall experience to South Korea is kind of over rated. I expected more based on the comments from friends, reviews by travellers and most importantly seeing it in Korean Dramas.Udo island is an exception, it gave me the best experience in the entire 8-day trip, except the weather wasn't too good on my day trip to Udo. Rented a bike to travel almost the entire island which i think is the best mode to explore remote areas without using too much energy.  Hopping up and down to take photos by the beach, colorful cafes, yellow canola fields, uphill and downhill.Unforgettable squid volcano rice was one of its kind and one of the most satisfactory meal in the entire trip.

My favourite one in Seogwipo, it may be not as large as Kpop Live in Seoul  but its still good one. With fifteen-thousand-won ticket you could experience the 4D media concert of Big Bang, GD, PSY...Remember to choose the showtime for concert because your ticket is available for max. 3 hours. Besides that you could experience over 31 attractions including be the star, meet the star, recording with star, make up and dancing with star. Its cool one when you could take pictures or singing with TOP, GD or PSY. There is also a section for Korean music history that you could help you have an overview of Korean music industry. Play Kpop will catch some of your moments and then you could download your photos and videos you take there by filling the ID ticket. Worth your money & well recommended!

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My 4 year old found the road very fascinating and he kept mentioning mysterious road throughout the day. It was probably just an average experience for adults but if you are travelling with the little ones, it may be worthwhile to spend some time to bring your kids to view this road.

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.
Lovely view.  However u need to clinb endless stairs, which was horrible for me as I was using a babycarrier.  Nonetheless, everyone should visit, lovely views.
Lovely view even at sunset with manageable climb up. Down hill steps are new, even and better. Wished uphill can also be nicely renovated. Recommend a visit
Lovely beach for an evening visit. Clean, picturesque view with nice cafes around . Would recommend a visit
Loved this island, I recommend exploring it by foot.  We interviews the monk the temple for our film   Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure   and he was super kind and served us coffee and drink.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Long long route indeed ! Best is to go via one route and come down via another. Scenery could be a bit monotonous but at the end being surrounded by nature is always more rewarding. Ensure to be on the checkpoint by 1pm else one can be very close yet so far to the summit - since you won't be allowed to climb up the remaining 2.5 kms of stretch. If its a brighter day, view is what makes the climb worthwhile.. if its not, aaah bummer, bummer... !

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Living in a country where there is no chance the snow will fall, we are so excited to experience snow even though by that time it is nearly end of March. The view is amazing, though I cannot go for the hike as I went there with my mom. Will definitely go again and bring my hiking partner next time.

Liked: The view, the walk.Disliked: Many tour buses spend time here which means the place was full of (literally) thousands of Chinese tourists. It was really hard to relax and enjoy the tranquility when you are in a constant scrum with many loud tourists yelling at each other in tonal dialects.

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

Jusangjeolli Cliff, designated as a natural monument of Jeju Island, is the largest columnar-jointed lava in South Korea. It was formed due to the sudden cooling of lava from the Hallasan Mountain, which erupted into the sea of Jungmun, thousands of years ago. Witnessed a picturesque view of the sea and the cliff. I recommend not wearing any hat or cap when you visit Jusangjeolli Cliff as the wind is strong there.

Jeju Island in Korea is a exceedingly wonderful place to have vacation for family and also a  place to have honey moon for lovers. After doing some traveling plans, I went to Korea with friends in April this year. It?s really a nice time to meet Jeju Island in spring, the weather is comfortable, and the flowers were growing beautifully at that time. A vast , blue as well as clear sea came into my horizon, relaxing my body and purifying my mind dramatically. Not annoyance and trouble anymore, but freedom and joy there. The blue sea does calm me down. Additionally, because of its great geographical location, we are able to taste some delicious local food, such as fresh octopus, deep-sea fish, oysters, and also famous Jeju orange chocolate.In a word, Jeju is worth going, especially for whom are fond of view of sea.

Jeju Island depend 75% on tourist business nothing much in Jeju Island except for scenery viewing. A ladies brief and conducted a short tour in Folk Village.This place is very small less than 20 min you can cover the whole area. And trying to sell us very expensive Raw Honey and Omicha Health Cordial 1000gm at 40000 won each which claimed using the raw,fine,fresh,ingredient to process it.While other pharmacy and e-mart sell only approximately at 20000 won

I've visited this place many times and every time I love it. So pretty, the best view and a really nice garden as well. The only downside is the strong wind so I don't recommend any hats and warm clothes!
It's crowded but the view is amazing. If you're a first timer, I personally will recommend this than the other waterfalls in Jeju.

Its a very do-able climb up although at the first look it might look daunting. Even grannies reached the top! Once you slowly work your way up with plenty of pause in between, the reward at the end is amazing. Breathtaking views of the ocean and the crater.I'll do it again next time I go there!

Its a really short strip of street where most BBQ restaurant are located. Most of them serve black pork . As mentioned in most reviews , the price is on the steeper side. If you like some BBQ black pork then this is the place to go. Its a tourist friendly place after all.

It's a lot of stairs and little walking to get to the top, but it's worth it with great views and a wonderful sea breeze. On one side you have views of the crater, on the other of Jeju island. There are lots of other tourists (mostly local) going up and down so be prepared for some level of crowds. There was abundant parking when we visited. There are also plenty of food stalls at the bottom along with bathrooms. On the way up, there are lots of benches, rest areas, and viewing platforms. We saw people of all ages - really old to really young doing the climb. If you're in town and you have a couple hours to spare, we'd recommend it!

It's a beautiful waterfall. As described by another reviewer, there is a flight of stairs you have to descend to reach the waterfall. At the bottom of the stairs, you will have to carefully traverse across rocks if you want to get nearer to the waterfall to take a good photo with it in the background. Be sure to get good shoes to avoid injury as the rocks can be slippery. Not recommended for pregnant ladies or old folks, especially so when the rocks are wet from rain.

It's a beautiful view, worth the climb even though we didn't manage to see sun rise due to the cloudy day but the view is pretty. Have to walk up and be there before 5.30am. Depending on your fitness level, it can take 20-40 mins to climb the peak.

It was very meaningful to spend 3 days to join the Jeju Olle walking festival in November, 2018. One route per day not only an physical exercise and challenge to myself but also a good opportunity to meet friends or make new friends there. No one push you to walk faster but we could take pictures, enjoyed nice views and landscapes on each route. Local food for lunchs were delicious. What a beautiful island, good for gathering and good for vacation. I love Jeju. It was my third time participating Jeju Olle Festival. Different experience every time.

It was raining with some strong winds when we got there. Nevertheless we decided to buy a poncho and went ahead with the climb which is a manageable 180 m.The climb up is relatively easy even for most elderlies as there are proper stairs along the way.Apart from the crater, you can see the surrounding areas and the sea from the top. The crater itself is covered by vegetation so you might want to tone down any expectation of a spectacular view. We spent about 15 min at the highest point and start our descend after that.Another attraction nearby is the female divers where they have scheduled performances every day if I remember correctly. We didn?t go for that due to the weather. But I?m sure it would be interesting.

It was raining when we went here. The steps were not at all slippery (they had rubber/metal bars at the end) Although it will be a long hard climb to the top of the mountain. If you started the climb up the mountain there is a different set of stairs going down. At the top of the mountain are set of seats, possibly a good view (it was raining) and a sign to commemorate your achievement. The place is also crowded with people. It is not suggestible for old people to go up the mountain but they could go through the sea. i would go back there again to see the wonderful view.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

It was nice experience when suddenly u find these kinds of roads... Some kind of mysterious nature behaviour that able to control your vehicles to suddenly runs on its own... Probably kind of magnetic field...Well, u can also enjoy a small view of grassfield and view restaurants around... I took a nice picture here with my travel friends, used a large stone (its carved with korean words) as background... Interesting experience... ;)

it was my second time visiting there.The stairs are very steep and narrow, so I don't recommend wearing any shoes that's slippery. Do bring a camera!! the view is amazing just everywhere!and it's a bit windy once you reach the top

It was my first time climbing. Being the unfit person I was, I was panting a little when we crossed the halfway mark. It was cold and windy in March, so I was all wrapped up, but with every break I took, I was busy taking my layers off! It's not that hard to climb up, just that I was not prepared for it. It's important to stay hydrated. It's worth the effort - the view is really stunning, even through the ascend. Enjoy!

It was just an OK place to visit as it was part of our Tour Package. The old fashioned village homes were probably the only thing which was interesting to me. The lady who explained everything to us was very warm and friendly. Of course, at the end of the tour, you are brought to a 'special room' to view the products which they sell. I bought a bottle of Omija (Berry) Drink which was actually quite nice. I think I paid $50 (as expensive as it was, I just thought it would support their livelihood). She did not force us to buy the products but was very kind to let us try them all.

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.

It was easy to tell the tourists from the locals - level of preparedness. Before I went on the hike, it amused me to see the locals fully dressed and equipped with hiking gear. As I understood it, the hike was child and elderly friendly, so I was not expecting much difficulty scaling this mountain. Halfway up, I was already regretting my choice of footwear. I had on a lightweight fleece jacket which helped to battle the cold winds at the top, so it did not feel too bad even though I was in shorts. In actual fact, it was not that difficult to climb (took me 4 hours to get to the summit) but the terrain was rough with rocks and stones making up most of the path. I guess it is my own fault that I have absolutely no instinct on where to put my foot next. Slipping often, I finally tore open my trainers on my way down after constantly stubbing my toes in the ground. My toes hurt so bad I had to stop several times (after peeling my socks off, I found two of my toes severely bruised and blackened) so the hike down took all of 4 hours. At the top, I regretted not having any headgear. The winds were so crazy it was close to impossible to take a photo without my hair whipping all over my face. Ah, even a bandana would have been enough. Overall, I would do it again, this time better equipped. Though the view was beautiful, what I remember best was climbers picnicking at the top, huddled together in groups in the bellowing winds, in their bright hiking outfits, just enjoying the time out. Next time, I will remember to bring kimbap and hot coffee!

It was at the end of Hamdeok beach. It is not too high and easy to walk. I loved the view from the hill and you can see hallasan from seoubong. If you are staying around Hamdeok beach, seoubong is a great place to see sunrise or sunset. I loved it!

It was a very windy and rainy day... we could not climb to the summit but the experience was trilling! Recommended for trekking amateurs and pros! There are many coffee shops around the routes but bring your own food, comfortable clothing and decent equipment. It's totally equipped with stairs and view points but safety is always first!

It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. I didn't go up to the top but I did go up to the first viewing platform, which i think most people would be able to manage slowly, not matter your age. It is well paved, and the views are incredible. It was a very windy day too, so there was no show by the women divers, Haenyo, but you could see where they went out and to be honest the roughness of the seas showed how tough the women must have always been. There are a few shops near the bottom and one part way up, so you can purchase drinks and trinkets if you wish. There is a Starbucks and a Dunkin' Donuts and i think a McDonald's near the car park, as well as multiple Korean restaurants. Well worth a visit, even if you can't ascend to the peak.

It was a rainy day when we went to this beach after visiting the Hallim park, end of october. It was however a very nice experience, the sand is white and contrast nicely with the black rocks that you can see at low tide. The view on the island makes the picture even nicer.
It was a cold, sunny day, but the landscape in this area was just awesome!  There is a boardwalk lookout point where different landscapes could be viewed on each end.  Definitely worth checking out!

It was a bit cold to swim during our Sept visit but found beautiful turquoise water, beautiful breeze and lively neighbourhood with pretty cafes around. Our tour/driver highly recommended us to visit Woljeongri beach instead of other beaches and glad that we did. We found cafe on the right corner of lane on 1/F was with great view.

It took convos with my friends who are from Korea to find out about this (I am from New York), but man was it worth it!  On a clear day this is up there with one of the prettiest sites and generally awesome vibes of anywhere I've been.  You get an incredible view, a nice short   hike   (up the stairs), AMAZING food all around, etc.  Definitely try the raw seafood caught by the diving ladies!  Explore the area.  I took a bus from Jeju City

It offers one of the best view in Jeju. It is free to go, no need to book, super easy to walk. I was lucky with weather this time and was able to see hallasan from here! I cannot describe how amazing it was.  It is breathtaking and good to visit anytime of days. Many people came for sunset and sunrise. It is definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju. Be prepare for strong wind and amazing view. Recommend going during fall

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.

It is an attraction for people to take photos of the special ?Dragon? like stone with the endless sea. That stone is 100% organic and experience years of erosions to form today?s ?Dragon? appearance. You can spend a couple of minutes with that ?Dragon? and spend another few minutes buying and enjoying the traditional outdoor cuisines. If you are interested in buying souvenirs like key chains or the ?Dragon? like badges, there is a shop for you to go shopping. Even though the viewpoint just for people to take a photo, there would always be many tourists standing in front of the best position for taking photos, so if there are many tour groups at the moment, you really have to spend time on waiting for just a photo. So, if you don?t mind the feel of crowded or if you get plenty of time, you are recommended as it is a special attraction in Jeju. It is nearby the international airport of Jeju so you can go there at the time you arrived or before you leave Jeju.
It is a UNESCO world herritage, recommended to see if you go to Jeju. We need to hike around 30-45 minutes to the top to get the full view.

Interesting way they hide it from free view, but a  nice drop and fall into the ocean.  Careful clambering over the cobbles and boulders to get your shot.  Looks like local vendors selling raw oysters of sashimi down by the shore.  Other souvenir shops align the entrance and exit.

Initially I wasn't sure if I would go to see this as I'd already gone to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak the day before, but it was definitely worth it! It was a cloudy June day which made the setting even more mysterious. Very simple but nicely kept grounds of rolling hills and volcanic rock walls. The crater itself was one of the more bizarre and intriguing natural landscapes I've seen. If you've seen the movie   The Mummy Returns,   it's like the end of that! The surrounding grounds are lovely and you have a great view of the mountains all around you. Would be a very romantic place as well, if you're with your partner. Great place for a picnic or just a long stroll! However, if you're looking for activities and souvenirs and snacks and other touristy things, you'll have to go elsewhere. Fortunately there is a bus stop right outside to go to Jeju City.

Information given in English about the legend of the rock.    You really have to use your imagination to see the woman.    While I didn?t think much of Oedolgae, there?s a lovely hike right along the coast, with pretty views.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

If you're unfit like me, please be mentally and physically prepared before embarking on this   hike  , 4-5 hours upwards, another 4-5 hours downwards. The view at the top is great but that highly depends on the weather. Don't be surprised to see many elderly Koreans in their 50s or 60s even at the peak. And oh yes, please bring along good hiking shoes for this trip, it will definitely help you a lot.

If you're into nature, love moderate hiking and stairs climbing, love to see sea and city thru the bird eye view, taking plenty of photos of nature formations and also selfies (or wefies), then wjy don't you go to Seongsan Ilchubong, Jeju Island, South Korea. Designated as Unesco World Heritage site, this mountain is one the best place that you can hike and feels the wind blows your hair or maybe yourself too. The combination of flat lands and also the hike to the peak gives you an unforgetable memories. With each steps you take to climb to the peak, you will encounter several break spots or photo viewing for you to stops and take photos. Half way thru to the peak, you can see the entire city below you and starting to see the seas too. Hike to the peak, you can the see majestic view of the Seongsan Ilchubong itself. To your front is wide sea and the flat land (heard that it's actually a death volcano, correct me if i'm wrong) and to your behind is the view of the city and their surrounding. Don't forget to take photo at the peak's signboard. The formation of the clouds and the sun may give you the awe moments to you, especially when it reflects to the sea surfaces. When you go down from the peak, try to look at your right. You may see people going down to feels the sea water. Mind you, sometimes the wind blows a bit strong.  You need to pay for entrance and you don't like to hike to the peak, the ground is enough for you. Me and my friend, went there on Nov'15. Do try to enjoy nature at their best.

If you want to see a waterfall without the hassle of hiking a long way, go for this one. Just a little stairways descend from the entrance and voil - you'll be greeted by this pretty view of water flowing freely to the sea of Jeju.

if you want to go to his place, you must go on the morning to see the sunrise. Seongsan is quite far from Seogwipo, so after you explore Seogwipo city, you can go to the Seongsan for stay. And then you must wake up at 5 am, and go to seongsan ilchubong by taxi. it needs 5-10minutes. Better you ask to the hotel to call the taxi. You need 20-30minutes to go to the top. The view is amazing. Very recommended. For the hotel in this area i recommended jeju lux hotel. you can read my review also.

If you one got time for 1 of the 3 waterfall in Seogwipo, you should choose this waterfall. View is spectacular, need to walk down the stairs to view the waterfall. and some actually walk very close to the waterfall by walk on the big rocks to get some nice photo. Plenty of parking space available, youth below 25 years get some discount for the entrance ticket (do bring along your passport). suggest to spend 1 hour there.
If you enjoy walk , is fine. Good view, so natural . Specially the air & wind. Fresh and clean. Family and friends can snap a good photo for remember.

If you are planning to visit the Hello Kitty Island, beware: there is a specific audience that his place caters to; it is not recommended for everyone. Our tour group went here in lieu of the Trick Eye Museum.Little girls and Hello Kitty fans would love this place. Hello Kitty merchandise are displayed everywhere. There is also a room that narrates the history of how Sanrio characters came about.  There is a Hello Kitty Caf챕 at the 2nd floor. On the 3rd floor, there is an auditorium that plays a Hello Kitty-themed show. Outside is an open-air Hello Kitty-themed miniature garden maze. The view of the landscape from here is wonderful. For me, it was meh. I am not among those that this place was built for.On the plus side, there a postcards available at the souvenir shop, which you pass through as you exit the building. I also liked the stamping stations spread around the place, which are reminiscent of postmarks.

If you are interested in the history and culture of Jeju island, and of Korea, then I would recommend spending an hour or two at this park. If you aren't, or are expecting something more exciting, skip it. For me, who lives in Korea and is already familiar with much of Korean history, I wish I had gone elsewhere. True to previous reviews, it was beautiful, but so is most of Jeju, and there are many other places more beautiful than the park itself. Overall: if you don't care about the history behind the park, it's 2 hours of looking at rocks.

If you are intending to go for the sunrise climb, please bring your own torchlight as lighting is minimal. About 2/3 of the climb comprise of a steep ascend. Not for the weak-hearted or those with circulation problems. It's physically challenging on the heart, not so much on the legs.Personally, a day climb (rather than a dawn climb) is better as you can see the view from the various heights. At the top, there are benches to sit and appreciate the view. Coming down was the easy bit as the stairs are well designed for the descend.

I'd highly recommend visiting 9.81 Park on your next trip to Jeju. This place is a lot of fun. The karts are in excellent condition, the course offers some amazing sea views and the staff are very professional and helpful. Definitely worth a visit.

i wouldnt have rate poor until i went to   Teseum  . things in teddy bear museum all mini sizes in a box well protected. they have 3 floors, and only the ground floor have some bears for picture. For me kind of bored compare to Teseum, Teseum you can touch and picture closely with those teddys. Jeju has 2 or 3 teddy bear museum, i been to 2 one is teddy bear museum & another is Tesuem. more recommended to Teseum instead of this.   links: http://english.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=701764http://www.tripadvisor.com.my/Attraction_Review-g297885-d3805571-Reviews-Teseum_Jeju-Jeju_Jeju_do.html

I would say that this waterfall is higher and have better view than cheonjaeyeon waterfall althought cheonjaeyeon waterfall is close by from teddy bear museum, we take taxi in the afternoon from teddy bear museum to jeongbang waterfall and it cost around 25-30 usd, and the street is almost empty. The road down to the waterfall is much nearer and easier than cheonjaeyeon waterfall. When you take pictures, off course you would like to get closer to the waterfall, but be carefull of the rocks, they were quite slippery, we spend an hour to take pictures and sitting in the rock. The admission fee on nov 2014 is still 2,000 won per adult about $2. On winter it opens from 08.00 to 18.00

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

I went with my boyfriend and his dad. We had our cab driver take us there at 6am from our hostel. It took us about 12hrs round trip. I'm not a experienced hiker, so it took a loooonnnngggg time because of me. View is EXCELLENT from the peak. You can see the entire Jeju-do. Hallasan is a stony mountain, so if you can, bring a pair of hiking sticks to help you, and wear hiking shoes. The rocks are pointy, and not all of them are easy to step on.

I went to this peak three times during my stay for a year on Jeju island! First time was in August when it was sweltering hot, so I never climbed it just took pictures from the bottom. The second time I went was in September when it was cooler and I climbed it and it only took the recommended time of 30 minutes. Such a beautiful view and the sign saying you reached the top is very nice. My last time climbing it was in December for the sunrise and my mom and I made it to the top just before sunrise but it was an overcast day so we only saw a tiny bit of pink under the clouds but still it was a nice view of Jeju from that height! Definitely recommend doing this while you are in Jeju :)

I went to Seongsan Ilchulbong (SunRise Peak) during Mar this year 2015. The weather is cold but bearable around Jeju. However, to climb this mountain is not a great feat for my mum (age 65) but the chilling wind is the one we are defeated.We wanted to visit this peak for sunrise but somehow we are late and lost on our way there. We went to Jongbong Beach and along the coast line it is also very nice to see. We did not catch the sun rise as there are none (due to foggy weather). As we are ascending, the crowd was descending and show enthusiasm although they did not get any view of the sun rise. The climb was nice as there are even wooden/stone steps to the top. Once you reached the top, you will see the beautiful crater which happens million years ago. The view over the edge is equally stunning. Definitely a recommended place to visit when you are in Jeju-Si. The ticket cost 2000KRW each.When you descend, you may see the   Sea-Woman   whom they called Haenyeo will perform at 1.30PM and 3PM only. We did not wait for the show as there are many Sea-Woman around the whole Jeju Island.

I went Thursday morning with my girlfriend and it was quiet enough. Nice walk, but be prepared for stairs and bring water! The bridge you can cross is exquisite and crazily steep (so be careful in the winter). The views are outstanding on a clear day.I really enjoyed this site; the wooden walkways, the history behind the irrigation channels and of course the waterfalls really kept my interest.Would recommend!Shane & Jill

I was very excited to visit Jeju; and this probably one of the most accessible place by Bus. There's actually public transport to this place (Yongduam Rock) from my accommodation. However, when I reached this place , i was busy looking for this legendary dragon head rock. Much to my disappointment, the rock doesn't seem to look like dragon head, you must really view it from the other side with your imagination.However, in order to reach to the other side, you need to climb all the way down the stairs, Not recommended for elderly. And if you notice carefully, you will spot alot of cockroach crawling around the rock, that totally freak me out!! Very big turn off if you spot the cockroach.the period I went was very crowded, probably around 5-6pm, This timing was quite a good timing for me, as I manage to catch a sunset. The sunset there was relatively awesome with the endless view of sea. If you can walk all the way down to those seafood stores, whereby you can enjoy fresh seafood hot pot + splendid view of sunset & sea!

I was very excited to visit after reading the reviews; while it was very nice, I left slightly dissapointed. Maybe we visited at the wrong time of year, but almost nothing was blooming outside. The different outdoor gardens were pretty, but I was expecting a lot more colorful displays.Inside was a bit more of what I expected (although again, not as many flowers as I thought there would be). The main area is air-conditioned, which is a HUGE relief from the heat outside (and some of the display rooms are pretty toasty, as well).? We were lucky to get a clear day, so the view from the top of the glass dome was fantastic.The garden is in a great location, with plenty of restaurants and other attractions nearby, and just a short drive from Pacificland and the beach. As a stand-alone, the garden may have been a bit of a let-down, but since we were able to spend a couple of hours here, get some lunch, and then head down to the beach for some waves, it ended up being a fun family day.

I was on my way to another destination when I saw this place. I caught the 700 bus that runs around the outside of Jeju island for a cost of around $2, and wondered why so many people were getting on and off at this stop, so on my way back I got off. It ended up being my highlight of the day.It was a lovely sunny day with a few hundred people climbing up, and with ramps and steps all the way it was easy. I got to the top in about half an hour if not less. The views from the top were probably the best I experienced for my whole trip in Jeju, and that includes the view I saw from top of Mt Hallasan.At only 2000 won entry, it's a must-do when visitng Jeju, and there's lots of restaurants at the bottom.

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I visited this place with my family, my parents are seniors. Costs 2,000 won per person. The stairs were ok for me to climb, but will be more challenging for seniors. It?s approximately 40++ floor climb (based on my watch tracking) and takes around 20++ minutes of brisk climbing to reach the top. The uneven stone flooring in certain areas can be a little tricky to climb. The views were more beautiful halfway, rather than the top. Different paths for ascending and descending so the foot traffic is smooth. The view from the peak was slightly obscured by rocks and the fence, but there?s binoculars available for use for 500 won. We visited this location close to sunset, but the view was amazing nevertheless. Surrounding the area is a lot of eateries, and there?s washroom etc nearby (important in winter :) ). Ample FOC parking spots available.

I think the word   museum   throws off this visit.  I expected to see many more interesting displays and films about tea but there is really just one room with some tea sets a few interesting facts and how Jeju tea is the best as the soil climate and underground water makes growing tea in Jeju at its optimal.  This so called museum is more of a flagship store where you can purchase tea and tea related items have a snack at the cafe/bakery that specializes in green tea ice cream and cake rolls and in a separate building building called   innis free   you can make natural soaps and enjoy Korean slushy ice in a cafe there as well and a store.  There are tea making classes but you must make a reservation to attend.  The grounds are nice and you can walk around the tea fields and go to the rooftop and get an amazing view of the surroundings.  The museum is free but for a true tea fanatic you may be disappointed as there are no samples or a big variety of tea products to choose from for purchase.

I spent few hours at the museum, I had jet lag  because of 6 hours difference in my biological hour, & it is near Hana Hotel where I stayed. It is a nice walk to the museum. I thought it is a happy place, because most of the visitors were happy especially those with children. I took my time looking at the museum & the shop. I enjoyed my time. The museum have stairs & elevator. I took lunch at the resturant , it is fast food, with reasonable price.Bathrooms at each level & they are clean. The view from outside the resturant is nice & relaxing, & the outside garden is beautiful.I watched the Elvis show,it is nice & professional work. I think to enjoy & appreciate the museum you have to spend few hours, not a quick visit.I thought it is a delightful happy place.

I specifically spend half a day here during my trip at Jeju and has no regret. We rented a electric scooter with KRW30k for 2 hrs, do note that you need International Driving License to rent it. We had burger at HahaHoho cafe and the Pork burger is delicious. The landscape and view is so pretty. The road is narrow so I don't recommend you to drive rented car there. Udo island trip is definitely one of the highlight of our trip to Jeju!

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I really enjoy my visit to this site at Jeju island... Recommended for those who loves to take a short hike and enjoy sunrise... The view of the city from the top of it is also beautiful... One side you can see the sea, other side enjoy the city view... On the afternoon in the right time, you can also met the woman divers who will dive to look for abalone and other sea animals... Love this place, hope can visit again someday... v(^_^)v

I read many negative review about this place from other travellers but for me, it was quite an interesting place with strange phenomena going on. My taxi driver brought me here on the way to Seongsan and he show me what is so mysterious about this road and it was indeed very strange. He stop the car at one end of the road and the car will automatically move up towards the slope (even when the car engine is not on). It was just an experience and one will not spend more than 10 minutes here. A good short trip before going to other places.

I reached out to Mr. Kang due to all the amazing reviews here and I'm glad I did! We had booked him for a single day since we unfortunately didn't have too much time at Jeju. He is super friendly and knowledgeable about the island. You could tell he really loves Jeju by his passion when talking to us even with his limited English. Although his English is limited, we never had trouble with communication. He helped with pictures and took us to an amazing lunch spot when we asked for recommendations! He took us to a seafood hotpot/stew spot and it was by the far the best I've ever had. Throughout our day, if there was a place that had a local discount he would let us know and offer to get it for us if we wanted as well. But the greatest show of service from Mr. Kang was that we had a spot that wasn't originally on our itinerary that he also didn't know about. Mr. Kang went above and beyond trying to figure it out and fit it into our day. I would HIGHLY recommend Mr. Kang to anyone and will definitely be reaching out to him whenever I visit Jeju again!

I LOVE... this museum!!! I am a teddy bear fan so this museum feels like heaven to me aside from being a K-drama fan. Before visiting Jeju, I researched on the top sites recommended to be visited, i got fascinated with the reviews about Teddy Bear museum plus knowing that some of its Teddy Bears where featured in one my favorite Korean Drama of all time PRINCESS HOURS. The teddy bears are just so cute, you can see them perform different functions and dressed of different profession and famous personalities such as Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Madonna etc. Afetr visiting the exhibit halls, we then went to the lower ground floor area where tall Teddy Bears are on display alongside Teddy Bears items that are for sale.A must visit for Teddy Bear Lovers.

I love nature and if you do too this is a must visit if you are in jeju. A Unesco site and a new seven wonder, the view from the top is worth the climb. Depending on individual it can take up to 30 minutes to climb but take your time and enjoy the crisp air and the beautiful view of jeju. Also walk to the sea to buy life seafood caught by the locals

I hiked up Hallasan during Spring March 2013. It was my first time scaling such mountains and i found it relatively tough. (20yo M) I would say its a very satisfying hike, as its really mind over body for my case. The mountain is roughly 1960m, and I started with the Seongpanak course at 700+m. It took roughly 4 hours to get up and slightly more to get down. Descend is more generally difficult as you have to take note of the ice and snow which gets very dangerous even with proper hiking equipment.Just some points to take note of.Hiking during Winter would provide very nice views but very dangerous.Remember to be well preparedIt takes around 10 hours round trip for a first time beginner

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.

I have read many Super review of Mr Kang being a good driver. I decided to use his service. Diana and 2 others took a 2 day taxi tour with Mr Kang on 14-15 Jan 2020. Mr Kang, though English is limited, we did not have any difficulty in our conversation. He arrived at our place on time. He was very friendly and a careful driver. He was very flexible as we changed our itinerary last minutes. He also suggested some nice places to visit, and good and cheap resturant to eat. The food was sumptuous. He took photos for us every places we visited and they were so well taken. He also helped us to carry our luggages up to our new location, 3-storey, without lift. He had done beyond his duties. We were much appreciated for his great help and service.We enjoyed our 2 day tour with Mr Kang. Will highly recommend him to my friends.Thanks Mr Kang, who made our journey so comfortable and pleasant.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I had a lot of fun riding the carts but also enjoying the beauty of Jeju. It's situated in such a beautiful location where you can view the ocean and take Instagram photos! The interior of the building was also cool. It was futuristic and very clean. The staff were friendly and helpful! I didn't play indoor games but there were many indoor games as well, so it seems like a place that you can have fun in any season. I will definitely recommend this place for any ages!? I will go back in a heartbeat when I visit Jeju next time!!

I had a great afternoon there. Loved the hike up. However, I must say that I enjoyed the hike more than the view. The view was nice, but the peak looks more impressive from the photos taken from afar. I recommend it if you love nature and hiking.

I got 28 hour spare time before my flight to Dhaka in my last visit to Korea. When I got this break at the very last moment, I searched Jeju air ticket and hotel booking online without any delay. As I purchased it at the last moment, I had to spend USD 125 more for air ticket and hotel booking. Jeju is a rush destination in summer. It's is a fairly large island to cover within 24 hours. Thanks to TripAdvisor and reviewers for helping me to select Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hamdaeok beach from many other attractions.Tourists have time, usually visit Seongsan Ilchulbong before dawn to observe Sunrise. That why it is also known as Sunrise peak. As I did?t had that option in hand, I climbed it at afternoon. I took a taxi from my hotel at Hamdaeok beach and it costs around USD 28. Bus is always cheaper but I had only 20 hours left in my hand to catch my return flight. Sunrise peak entry ticket costs USD 2 for adults and USD1 for child. Most of the review I read earlier suggests it takes 20 minutes to climb on the peak but as an amateur I took roughly 40 to 45 minutes to climb. There are two wide and convenient stairway to climb on the peak. I selected the left side stairway and eventually it was a right decision. Because there is a small grocery in the midway selling soft drinks and water for those who didn't buy it from the base. As usual they charge double for each drinks but it was a life saver for me. When I came down from the other way I didn't find any shop like this. There are also a  midway station if you are tired want get refreshed for a while. When I reached on the peak I was almost exhausted. The view is literally breathtaking. I was sitting there more than one hour and a half as it is so charming that made for  forget everything else of life. I came down from the other stair way. The surrounding is so calm and comfortable that I stayed their until it?s dark. Tips: Try to book air ticket and hotel upfront to save cost. Rely more in internet than locals advise because there is a high chance of misleading information due to language barrier. I lost twice in the island for relying on them and lost around 3 hours of my precious time. There are halal restaurant ( Bagdad and Rajmahal) in Jeju island. 4 days are fairly enough to cover most of the attraction of Jeju. It costs total USD 400 all inclusive  for me for a quick tour , however if you are two them many cost will be shared within you. If I could catch the early morning flight from Gimpo airport at 7:30 am and save three more hours to arrive Jeju island then I could go to Udo island as well. I couldn't do that because I had to come from Suwon city. So if you stay at Seoul, you can catch 7:30 morning flight comfortably.

I first heard of Saebyeol Oreum when watching Hyori's Bed & Breakfast, and I really wanted to visit this famous oreum. The hike was insanely steep, and we huffed and puffed to get to the summit (520m above sea level). The view from the top was breathtaking, and the eoksae (flamegrass) covering the entire oreum was absolutely gorgeous. We were lucky to catch the magnificent sunset, and it was a great end to our Jeju trip. Highly recommended!

I did this attraction around 3pm. Not only was the sun hitting me directly the whole time, but there was way too many people to do it in the suggested time. The suggested time is of about 50 minutes. It took me twice as much (sometimes I would stop to rest but mainly too many people to move any faster). I recommend doing this in the AM when the sun is hitting the other side of the stairs. Also I heard, from people in my hostal, if you do this in the morning you beat the crowd and you can have better pictures. I definitely think its something to do in the area. The views going up and once at the top are breath taking.

I did the hike in January, and it was amazing.  Parts were pretty difficult so you may need trekking poles or crampons.  The views from the top are stunning, but be sure to leave really early (before sunrise) as you'll be sharing the views with hundreds of your closest friends if you don't.

I definitely recommend this place altough it's popular among tourists. Anyway, the view on the top is absolutely amazing and for me walking on the top wasn't too hard. It was very windy but sunny day (and I burned my nose) so I recommend to remember the sun lotion! Or if it's cold and windy to wear warm clothes. On the top there were many places to sit and take a brake. The journey down was also lovely because of amazing views. Before you start to walk to up remember to go to toilet and eat something (there are toilets and food in the same area). If you haven't used to walk lot of stairs it can be quite challenge but it is definitely worth of it.

I climbed this with a friend and it took us about 4.5hrs in total. Easy hike but challenging enough to make it worthwhile. Lots of tourists climb this and they are mainly Korean; its a bus and popular hike. The views from the top are stunning, you can see the whole island almost, we went when the leaves were turning from summer to autumn, just gorgeous.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I am used of the garden by the bay in Singapore which is great, so I went there just to depend some time and expecting something just .. so so.I was actually wrong. The garden is nice, outside as inside. The round shape with all kid of plants, the elevator to go on the top and enjoy a great view, the type of gardens outside (japanese, coreen, italien, french...).Sometimes a lack of maintenance but.. definetely a nice place. Entrance is about 7usd for adults. A little train can bring you around but I didnt use it and.. not sure it is free.

I am not an early morning riser. However, since this place is one of the most recommended place to visit in Jeju, my friends and I decided to wake up super early to watch the sunrise. The stairs to get to the peak were steep, I had to stop to catch my breath a few times before reaching the peak. It was worth it though, the sunrise view was so pretty, and actually one of my best experiences in Jeju.

I am in the middle of living in Jeju for a year and visited the Haenyeo Museum with three friends a couple of months ago.
