It was a really great visit and showed really well the changes in Haenyeo lifestyle as time has gone on. The top floor has a beautiful picture gallery with gorgeous views. Highly recommend. I think you need about an hour - an hour and a half here.Also the gift shop is great for cute Jeju-y things. I put some   Jeju stockings   together for my cousin's kids for Christmas all with keyrings/books/purses/other stuff bought here.

I am a huge fan of Udo.  I have been numerous times and I never get tired of exploring a new road or a new cafe.At times it is soooo overrun by tourists that it can be a little overwhelming, but if you are smart and plan your trip during quiet times of the year, it is really rewarding.  The roads are quieter, the stores less busy.  There are numerous ways you can tour the island:I usually take my car.  I have heard that NO rental cars are allowed on Udo anymore.  so be aware of that.But once off the ferry there are so many scooter and electric bike shops* around.  *Foriegners be aware that you do need a license to rent these!ProTip:  I absolutely recommend you get off the beaten path and go explore the inner part of the island. So many cute cafes and splendid views!

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Hiking Mt. Halla was on my bucket list for a long time and finally i did it. There is a time restriction and you cannot enter the gate before 6:00 am during the winter time. You have to pass 'Jindalaebat Shelter' before 12:00 pm to continuously hike up to the summit. The park keeper will not let up pass the gate of Jindalaebat if you arrive after the noon. It took about 2 or 3 hours to get to Jindalaebat from Seongpanak gate, and another 2 or 3 hours to get to the summit. It took me 4 hours to get to the Baekrokdam, and took another 5 hours to get down to Gwaneumsa temple. I highly recommend to hike from Seongpanak because it is easier to walk and you are too tired to look around. Then, walk down to Gwaneumsa direction which has a really good view and nature. (Gwaneumsa route is shorter, but definitely harder...super stiff)You will see many people lining up to take a photo with a monument, and I didn't understand why people want to take a photo with just a rock. I learned that you will get a certification of Mt. Hallasan hiking if you show the picture with the monument. All you need to do is go to the ticket office, pay 1,000 KRW and show the picture. I've seen many people hiking with sneakers, but I recommend wearing hiking boots since you have to walk on rocks for 8~9 hours. I heard that you need to be luck to see the summit because Hallasan is always foggy and cloudy. I was lucky and weather was just amazing!! I also heard that it is slightly easier to hike when it snows. There are buses that you can use and I strongly recommend hiking Mt. Halla!!!!!!!

Hiked up this mountain with a friend. Quite an easy hike and the views of the surrounding area are pretty nice. Crowds of tour groups around this site and bad quality food  stalls at the base make this an unpleasant place to hang around. Get in, get up the top and get out.
Highly recomended going around sunset. Way up probably takes 40 minutes, if not too rushing. It is very beautiful view from top, and nice photos) Watching sunset from top was extra bonus )

Hexagonal shaped rock formations jutting out of the ocean that reminds me of the kryptonite crystals I once saw in an early Superman movie. Unusual and definitely 1 of the places to see if you are in Jeju. Entrance is KRW2000, 50% off if you are below 24 ? foreign ID accepted. Unfortunately, since the best view is only through a series of stairs which ends at a platform, weekend crowds in bus loads can be a nuisance for that desired background photos effect or even a selfie. And I was continuously concern about the strength of the viewing platform to hold so many people at any one time. I got there in a rented car and discovered fields of canola flowers up front for good picture taking.

Hamdeok Beach is really splendid! Clear aquamarine water, super fine sand, mountain in the  background.... the view is to die for! You will find beautiful volcanic rocks all around the area. There's a bridge that stretches out into the sea that gives you an even more fantastic view. A must visit if you are in Jeju!

Hamdeok beach is just so beautiful. It offers you black rocks, white sand, and breathtaking views. It was our first destination for the day after we landed in Jeju. I found the beach quite peaceful and calm. It is very near to Hallim park. Just took us about 2 mins to reach the park by a car. I wish we could spend some more time at the beach but we had to rush to our next destination. Good place to stop by and click some nice pics. Good luck!!! :)

Hallsan is the highest mountain in Korea. You will have to hike up 1200m.  It is tiresome but it is not very tough, you can take your time. The time estimations indicated in the panels along the way are overestimated (specially if you have some hiking experience).Hiking up this mountain is like being on a highway with a lot of very noisy companions. It is packed, you will most likely be queuing up the mountain if you go in summer.If you are looking for a communion with nature, this is not the place. The hike up is almost entirely man-made, you will be walking up on wooden stairs and on wooden paths. Once you reach the top, it is so packed that you can barely enjoy. Views are excellent though.As you go up, there is a small path to the left to go to another lake. I will recommend this on your way down. Much much quieter as most tourists just want to go to the top.

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.

Had a port of call in Jeju. The cruise offered a number of shore excursions. Instead, we took the free shuttle into town. It dropped us off right by the underground mall (half block past it)We walked around a bit then hailed a taxi. He agreed to a fixed price of $100 USD to take us to the folk village, then to sunset peak. (The cruise was $119 per person so we saved $138)We climbed to the top. It was strenuous but with frequent stops we made it. It?s like 59 stories. At the to you get a great view of the town and the sea. You also can look down into the volcano (and see a grassy crater)A million photos later we came down. We then went and saw the women diver demonstration. That was fun. They sang for a while then went fishing. While we were there, one of the ladies caught an octopus. I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Great Views, Must Go, Wear to walking shoes, Not Baby friendly for Strollers as you will have to climb a lots of stairs. If you have child?s on stroller make sure you carry Baby Pouches/Bags for carrying the baby. Drink the Tap Water - Very Springy & Natural.

Great view of the rare animal cliff which is 20 meters height and surrounded by the beautiful islands. Hundreds of visitors went there to have a look of the amazing animal rock. The stone seemed independent and I like the fact that it is normal, nothing inorganic. The shape of Oedolgae formed by the daily erosion of wave and the weathering process. There is a small path in which it can walk along the edges of the island. In which I discovered that the venue was filmed by one of the most famous Korean drama - Dae Jang Geum. I was in love with the drama when I was young, I took tens of photos with the place that Jang Geum have been to.So, if you are I fan of Dae Jang Geum or you would like to see different shapes of stone, you are highly recommended to go there to have a look at the charming sea view.

Great view and friendly people! A wonderful place to relax from the stressful working environment and find peace. It's very very very windy in May, do remember to bring along a hat or sth else to make sure your hair won't fly all around like mad~~~Very friendly people who are also patient despite language barrier.
Great place! A must visit if you?re in Jeju. Do give it a climb if you have the endurance. Awesome view and lots of picturesque scenery. If you are in luck, may even catch the sea ladies diving.

Gosh...this place is awesome... Its very well maintained and comfy for those people walking inside and enjoy the lava tube nature. Recommend to wear shoes or comfy sandal as it sometimes wet inside. Not just the view, but also there are boards for explaining the things we see inside. Love it!
Gorgeous view, didnt have to climb to the top! Try to catch the woman divers show at 130pm..some women divers are friendly too!

Friends, my husband and I rented ATV's, Scooters and a Golf Cart to check out this island. It was so much fun touring around and stopping at the beaches and different view points. We even saw the diving ladies who dive by only holding their breath! This wasn't the most spectacular views of Jeju we saw but the adventure was a lot of fun!

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

First, we went to see the woman diver show. It appears to occur twice per day, at 1.30pm and 3pm if I remember correctly. They were singing, then entered into the water. I found their catch more interesting than their swimming. Afterwards, we climbed the   mountain   (small but cute is the motto). The view over the volcanic crater and the island is amazing, even despite the rainy weather that we experienced. The ascend is a bit physically challenging.

First and foremost, bring good walking shoes. You will need to hike up the hill to have a good view. There are many stalls at the base of the hill, before you pay to go into the entrance. As this location is near the sea, it is rather windy. A windbreaker may be required depending the time of the year you are travelling.Lots of toilets around, so there's no worry about needing it.There are many tourists as well as locals visit this scenic spot. Bring you camera as well. Note: This location is open depending on weather.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. One floor is for displaying teddies from different times, another one shows teddy related artworks and finally there's a floor where you find a souvenir shop and some cafes. In the outside park you can view Jungmun sea while seeing human-sized teddy sculptures. The whole surrounding area is beautiful. Ideal for friends, couples and families as well!

Do not miss the chance to climb up to the top (180m) to see the huge crater & Jeju view! it's definitely worth it ..the staircases might seems endless but it wasn't that high actually. it tooks us less than 30mins to reach the top and there are a few stops where you can catch a breath before continue to climb up again. Even my 4 years old nephew make it on top too. Going up and going down is 2 different route. Don't forget to get yourself mineral water at the convenient store before you climb up. you will need it.If you going over to the cliffs for the seaview, check out the Haenyeo performance. The performance hours are 1:30 p.m. and 3 p.m. twice a day during summer but we are out of luck we did not see any at the 3pm slot that day. Seongsan ilchulbong is sunrise peak - famous with sunrise from the cater! The gate is open 1 hour before sunrise for those who wish to watch sunrise from the top.

Do it with your partner, not with your mates, not with your friends and not with a group. This is a tiny island and the ideal thing to do is to rent a bicycle and just glide around the island for a few hours. It is mostly just farms and a couple nice views, but it does make you feel like that scene in wedding crashers if you do it right. Half day is all you need, the ferries are fairly punctual but check to make sure as you would not want to get stranded. Not the number 2 thing to do in Jeju by any means, but it is pleasant.

Do check the sunrise forecast and depending on fitness level, allow 20 minutes to an hour to reach the peak. Very doable hike even for non-fitness enthusiasts. The stunning views along the way and at the peak will be worth every effort! On the way up, there will be a few points where you can sit and take a breather. Great activity to start off the day!

Disclaimer: this review is written by my better half since I?m obviously not part of the Hello Kitty! target audience.Omg! Everything is in pink! Look at the displays! They are sooooo cuteeeeee! I want to take photos with everything! I?m an adult in Kittyland! Omg, the cafe is so nice! I don?t wanna leaveeeeeeeeee......Back to the lesser half: if you are a guy, just pay the entrance fee and make the Girlfriend/Wife/kids happy. They will love you even more when you cough up for the overpriced merchandise. Seriously, I?ve never seen the Wife happier, not even on our wedding day.

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.

Despite the reviews saying that they could solve it quickly, I failed 3 times ut I had fun taking in the nature and smelling the sweet pine trees. There are many cats hanging around the place too. They are really fat, friendly, lazed around for a pat or a cuddle. A relaxing place for fun with the young at heart and children.

Despite missing the sunrise on a gloomy drizzling day, we enjoyed our time at this attraction. In order to get some amazing view, one have to climb up the steps which isn't too steep. The view going up and going down from the other side is totally different. Highly recommend this place for nature lovers.

Depending on your fitness level, conquering the mountain will take you anywhere between 20 to 50 minutes, the latter with room for many rest breaks. The climb is shorter than you think, however, and very very soon after the second pavilion you reach you will find yourself at the top and before a gorgeous volcanic crater. The views are 360 degrees spectacular and the mountain is a must visit if you come to Jeju, even if you're not there for sunrise or sundown.

Depending on the weather, it was scorching for me, this is an easy hike for all ages. It takes no longer than an hour to get to the top and back. The views of the crater and surrounding landscape is beautiful. A nice view of U-do island off the coast as well. Well worth a morning hike followed by a boat across to U-do island, where boats go very regularly.

Definitely worth visiting. Although with 50 mins of climb, you will feel all well worth it after reach the peak. The view was just simply amazing. The best spot for photo taking beautiful natural, landscape and with friends. When I was there, was so crowed with people. This place is so popular. A must go. UNESCO sight.
Definitely go there if you've got a car. We went there when it was snowing and sleeting, still a perfect view. Wish I could spend more time there - definitely go on a good day!

Considering that the other craters type views Seongsan Ilchulbang (Sunrise Peak) and Hallasan are a ways up, and the seaside formations such as the Yongmeori Coast a slippery path of jumping about, the Sam-Gumburi Crater is nice and leisurely. The one place that seemed wheelchair friendly.It was also less crowded compared to the Seongsan Illchulbang so we really got to enjoy the nice leisurely walk up the small hill to see this crater. If you're a faster walker, you could probably do the whole thing in less than an hour (needless to say, we lazy walkers, took a little more than an hour). If you wanted to just roam about, you could spend a lot more time as well (there are different paths, one that's all stairs, one that is like a ramp, etc.). Anyways, this was probably the only geological tourist attraction that was wheelchair friendly and even seemed to have a few out in the front for rental. The ramp would be a bit steep but at least do-able. A lot of the other sites had either a lot of stairs/walking or way too many people for the elderly or others with bad knees to maneuver well.  Perhaps that's why we saw a number of couples with strollers.That said, this place had one of the most pricy admissions costs that we encountered. It is privately owned or something. So, instead of the usual 1,000-2,000KRW per person, we paid 6,000KRW per person. We were told that the place is nicer during the reed season, but we enjoyed the crater all the same. We'd recommended it to anyone looking to do a Jeju geotourist site without all the hard work.

Coming from a country where temples are famous for their stunning decoration I did not expect much from temples in East Asian countries. But Yakchunsa Temple was beyond my expectations. The temple is stunningly decorated. The Buddha statues are absolutely beautiful. I recommend you walk up to the second floor where you will see countless mini gold Buddha in different poses on the wall to your left and you can enjoy the view of the main hall and the main Buddha from high up. There is a small building to the left of the main hall with 500   heroes  . I think they are important monks or something. At least that's what it says in Chinese characters. All 500 of them have different facial expressions and poses. Some are very comical. Do take a quick look inside. And don't forget to drink the water from the water fountain before you leave the temple. The water there is refreshingly sweet.

Climbed the mountain with my wife 5 year old daughter and some friends. Not a strenuous climb, but a long one. 9 hours all tolled for the return journey. Very busy on the mountain (even more so at weekends and holidays) but really worth the effort. You do not need to be too fit (I really wasn't when I did it) as long a you take your time. Take plenty of snacks and water - although there is a snack bar 2/3 of the way to the top. Glorious views on a cloudless day, and a real sense of achievement having scaled the tallest peak in Korea.

Came here during sunset time. The view is very beautiful and natural. Many tourist took photo over here. During your walking distance to Yongduam Rock, don?t buy any fruit from the first stores! Very rude and not friendly. Make sure those of you beware of them.

By the time we reached Seongsan mountain, it's already 3.30 pm! On reaching there, and by the look at the mountain, it seems as if there's nothing to enjoy but after my daughter stated that it's world wide attraction, I reluctantly followed them up the 274 meter high mountain with unbelievable thought!But after going uphill, I have another thought!On looking down as I rested after some stairs, the beautiful scenery blaff me! Then as we climbed up stairs after stairs, we took lots of pictures. By the time we reached the top which is the most and satisfying view of sceneries surrounding all sides! I took only a few mountain top scenery because my camera's battery was flat! I sat on top of the mountain and look down at the serenity scene of parts of Jeju Island with the blending on sun setting! Just imagine the feel and satisfaction I gain and feel!But it's time to go down so as we're going down, we enjoyed ourselves by watching the sun going down slowly!

Breathtaking views, beautiful weather, awesome photo-ops, cool ferry ride! Make sure to take the bus tour($5pp). I found it was more convenient to hop on and off as you please instead of riding a bike or scooter, and you just use your tickets to hop on another bus. They don't speak English, so go with a friend if you can. Out taxi driver was nice enough to help us get our ferry tickets and suggested we take the bus tour.

Borrowing the words from our innkeeper,   don't give up   until you have reached the peak. The 180m high volcano gives a full panoramic view of the sea and the eastern coastline. Stairs are available all the way, but gets narrower as it approaches the peak. At intervals, there are magnificent viewpoints for postcard-worthy shots, even with a phone camera (which I have uploaded). Not to worry if you aren't that physically fit, you can always take a timeout at these points and take in the scenery. Highly recommended to go during pre-winter when the air is cooler for a comfortable trek. For those who are less fond of the cold, recommend to bring a light jacket/coat as the wind can be pretty chilly during this time.

Book the jeju tour under Rakso travel from the Phillipines. Visited mt halla on dec.31,2015. We were lucky as snow during the week was scant but during our visit, snow is falling and everything transformed to a magical sight.This is the first time my children saw snow falling. However, i noticed that the falling snow are not flakes but more like 'dippin dots' unlike the one i experienced in switzerland.Nevertheless, the moment and the view were enchanting!. Highly recommended!!.

Been there during last autumn. This place is also known as Sunrise Peak. To reach the peak, you need to ascend 600 steps. The 1st 400 over steps seems easy but be more careful after that as the steps become steeper and more rugged. Also mind the autumn chilly strong wind which can blow your bags off (personal experience). Get there to the top for the panoramic view of the peak. Also, if you are in time, you can also watch the pearl diver women in action.

Beautiful view from the cliff and surprising rock formations. Went on a rainy morning so we took our time and walked around a lot too. Snacks from the vendors near the front gate were tasty. The entry fee and parking was 8,000 KRW for a family of 5.

Awesome view.I went to hike from Eorimok.i went there by taxi because the bus from Jeju city to Eorimok only operate on weekend Saturday and Sunday.Due to the winter season and I do not wear specific hiking gear, i only hike halfway.Want to hike Hallasan again next time.

Attended the 1st day of the 2014 Jeju Olle Walking Festival, infectious mood with music and performances at various parts of the scenic seaside trek during the full day walk. We climbed up the Dodu-bong, a short hill with a panaromic view of the route, planes taking off from the airport runway and the sea. While it was quite sunny, late afternoon the sea breezes can get quite chilly. However at the end of the trek there were performances and hot local food, so overall it was a satisfying Day 1 of the trek.

At east spot of Jeju. Takes about 1.5 hour bus ride from the intercity bus terminal. Free entrance. Although the peak is only 180 metres, it's still challenging to climb because of the steepness. Very beautiful view along the way. The ocean and the mountain are all visible. Highly recommend.

As mentioned in the title, out of the few waterfalls that Jeju have, i think Jeongbang waterfalls is the best one. It?s just a short descent and you can go close to the waterfalls depending how brave you are. You get a good view of the sea as well.
Amazing view, one of the nicest place & must visit attraction to discover beauty of jeju.Highly recommended.
Amazing view , the unique of natural for the cliff rock. Must not miss during visited Jeju island. Highly recommended visited during sunny day.

Although this mountain is nice from afar, I will still recommend to take the ~ 30-40 mins hike up. It?s a bit tiring but they have many rest stops if needed. Fantastic views from the top to make the trekking worthwhile.
Although it's raining and foggy day, the view is wonderful.  The sea women show is funny. Highly recommend.

Although a very steep hike, this long flight of stairs does include many view points and amazing views at the summit. It was a little cloudy the day we climbed the summit and so did take away from the view a little but nevertheless was still great. I did the climb around  March but it was still very windy, make sure if you go during this time you take something to cover you face/ears if possible as the strong winds make your face go numb with the cold. Would highly recommend to anyone who visits Jeju Island.

Also known as Sunrise Peak, this crater formation can be ascended and descended in about 50 minutes total. Path is uneven and includes lots of stairs, some steep. The viewing platform up top is all stairs, but many places to rest. Very windy. Accessible by bus 201 from the downtown Jeju/Jeju-si bus terminal.

According to the locals, it is mostly cloudy during winter and there's no point going there for sunrise view. However we did paid a visit. As the sunrise time predicted to be at 743, we started ascending the hill at 645am. Reached the peak at 7am and there were a lot visitors waiting. However, as advised, it was very cloudy and everyone was totally disappointed . The eateries around the area closed early by 830pm, left a few local expensive local hot pot and BBQ restaurants..

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A visit to Sanbanggulsa Temple was part of one of my favourite day trips in Jeju. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo-si by bus and across the street (albeit a bit of a hike) from Yongmeori Coast which I very highly recommend. Getting to the temple requires a short and easy climb up some stairs where there is a huge golden Buddha, an army of miniature mint-green budhhas, and a gorgeous panoramic view of the ocean and village below. A little further up is another fascinating statue of Buddha in a cave. Overall, this is a nice place to visit and a great opportunity for photography.

A total of 19.7 KM hikeThe walk in early spring will be having snow so be prepared.. Buy the show snow covers Crampons its a must , its a must , its a must , i went without and sliped dozens of times  and injured myself once.. its snowy on the last third.. I hiked manytimes before in different parts of the world i go with sports shoe.. this one deserves crampons.. and maybe walking sticks as well.. Its long and tiresome. . But fun.. the view is great from up .. but make sure its not foggyat the end if u show them a picture taken at the top they will give u a certificate for 1000 won.. its a certificate of achievement really after a long hike. . Its 4 hours up and 4 hours down..

A scenic spot to visit in Jeju. Recommended for travellers who like nature and sightseeing. However, It requires u to climb stairs in order to reach the peak. It might be tough for elderly. Scenery is definitely good with nice view and breezing air.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

A great way to enjoy the view and burn off a few calories at the same time. It's a lovely coastline with a spectacular panorama of the area, definitely a nice little hike. You can easily spend a couple of hours here. Very enjoyable.

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.

A good place to start your visit to Jeju, the place is very accessible to people of all ages.  There is a decent spot for photo taking though there is also a stairway down to the beach to marvel at the eroded stones as well as a view of the   Dragon Head   from the other side.  Stairs to the beach not recommended for young kids and elderly with movement issues.  There are cafes nearby like Dunkin Donuts and some hot local titbits.

a coastine with beautiful cliff and rock - the line and layer of the rock are ideal for photography or selfie.  Not difficult to walk but cautious for the waves, also there is open view over the outlying islands. I recommend people go to the end of the path which has a exeptional setup by the nature.

A climb with lots of stairs and lots of tourists. The place is crowded and with little shade. I recommend to come for either the sunset or if you are like me and cannot wake up in time, do this walk in the evening time, so it's not too sunny. The view is very nice and offer a wide vista of the greenery. After the walk, you can enjoy exploring the adjacent black sand beach.

A cheap half-day activity. Udo Island was the perfect little get-away. We took a nice little ferry ride over to the island and rented peddle bikes to ride around. (You must have an international driver's license, however they took just our American driver's license.. depends on who you talk to) Took us about 3 hours to loop the whole thing (with stopping for icecream, a snack, a drink, etc) Beautiful views around very corner. Make sure to stop and get a burger at HAHA HOHO (located on the left around the bend from ferry drop off) it was definitely an Udo highlight as well as their local icecream. Pack some snacks and have a picnic, great spots to stop and enjoy! Friendly NOTE: Bring sunscreen! The sun is brutal!

20km return, 8 to 10 hours hiking (be there really early in the morning - around 7-8am), some steep parts, beautiful views and pics, bring water and food (they sell only water and noodles up there) highly recommended for hike lovers. Best thing to do in Jeju!

While in Jeju - we booked the Yeha bus tour and this is one of the places included to visit.  We really enjoyed our time here and our guide did an excellent job of recommending how to see everything in the time we had allotted.

We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)

Went to this welcome center for some advice and guidance for what to do during my short stay here in Jeju and the staff there was very friendly knowledgeable and were able to give me very useful suggestions. Any specific question I asked such as what bus to take or would I be interested in going a place they were able to give me insightful answers. If you don't know what to do and your hotel is close by it should definitely be worth a visit for you.

Went to the tea museum. The place was busy with loads of tourists. The area was very well maintained with a lot of Instagram potential shots. The Innisfree flagship store is just next to the museum. Ended up going to the innisfree store to look for potential buys. This shop has some products which are exclusive only to it. It also had diy packs where one can make bath bombs (shaped like leaf or horse) or regular soaps. Once bought you can either spend some time nsking it on site (needs any half hour) or you could take home to make it. There's also a lovely cafe attached to this shop.Had a lovely time here.?몟

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

We were staying in Seogwipo and had an extra day with nothing to do. So decided to book tickets from Klook on the day of visit. From Days Hotel in Seogwipo we would have to take two buses 201 and then 295?. The first bus is 1 hr 10-15 mins and much more frequent than the second bus which is a 5 mins ride or a 25 mins 2 km walk. Taxis are cheap starting fare of 2800 krw will get you to Aqua Planet from the 201 bus stop but they are a needle in a sack - hard to come by! Other countries??hard to reach facility ir tourist site may provide some form of free shuttle/transport but not here. Once you enter the main facility it would take you a long time to find the toilets - certainly not tourist friendly. Live shows are also all in Korean  albeit with English & Chinese subtitles. The size of this Aquarium is about one third or one quarter of the Okinawa one so we were seriously disappointed with its size and varieties of fishes available. Visit if you have a car or join a local tour or book a taxi. If using public transport like us think twice about going as its 3-4 hrs to and fro Seogwipo.

review: We went on a rainy day and feared it would be too busy to enjoy but it was ok (the first section was the busiest but the crowds thin out the further you get in).  A lot of fun for kids and adults alike.  It took us longer than we thought to get through you could spend hours so would suggest bringing some snacks if you are travelling with kids like we did. There is a coffee shop on site but it only had sweets and ice cream.A fun outing if you've never been to a trick museum before.  Don't forget your camera!!!

We travelled here by bus and got completely soaking wet walking the 20 minutes from the main road to the cave. Unfortunately it wasn't worth the soaking! It was pretty boring and after 30 minutes walk up and down we were out in the ran again.I would only recommended visiting if you have a thing for geology or if you have a car and happen to be passing by.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.
We had a great time. Beautiful sites and refreshing experiences. Highly recommend this tour instead of a large bus tour. More time for interaction and conversation. Thanks Jin!

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

We did this as part of the Yeha Bus Tour East Course tour and they had it timed perfectly for us to arrive and see the Women Diver Show and then after we had enough time to make the beautiful climb up Seongsan Ilchulbong.  We had beautiful weather in October - it was absolutely perfect!  I would definitely recommend tennis shoes and even if the weather seems chilly when you start out - wear a jacket that you can remove.  Lots of beautiful photo opportunities here!

We caught the ferry over to the island (remember your passport or other form of photo ID) and hired a two person battery operated bike which was great fun.   Hired for 2 hours which was ok but if you want to spend longer at each stop then I would recommend at least 3 hours.   We went all around the island.  We stopped the longest at a small village where you can go down some steps to the beach and go and investigate a large cave.   There was an outdoor cafe on the beach serving fish -  very busy.  Can't remember the name of the village but it was towards the end of our circuit.  Definately a good weather day activity.

Was there at about 10ish in the morning lots of (noisy) tourist and you can hardly find a decent seat in the cafe with unruly kids running around. Difficult to take photo at the photo spot cos some particular tourists pose like nobody business and after a long time posing change friend to pose again. I gave up and went outdoors where noise will not be contained and there is more fresh air.Sadly there isn't much nor exciting to see here - yet it is a spot you have read alot before coming. Suggest to just make a brief stop to have a look.I spent more time over at the Innisfree Jeju House instead which was surprisingly very peaceful.

Was feeling really amazing when passing through this road.   The tour bus was moving even though the driver has turned of the machine. Recommended anyone coming to Jeju to try this herself/himself.* TK
Very small beach. Lots of families attending the beach as well. Pretty easy to get to by bus. Worth seeing.

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.

Took a Taxi to the waterfall from Cheonjiyeon Waterfall. Plan to get wet if you get close to the falls.Better get there before is closes. Admission of course. Lady at information desk was very helpful. We took the Airport Limo bus for 11000 won bus # 600 to the Cheoniyeon Waterfall. Since I wanted to see as much of the south end as I could before dark I am glad we got to see these areas. Go to KAL hotel and take the Limo Bus back to the Airport for 11000 Won.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This small island is good for half or full day depends on what you going to do. The island provide with free shuttle bus but not sure it is summer period. Got two routes east and west. Check with driver before get into the bus. Light house stop and black sand see is a must.

This place was crowded when we arrived and had to wait a while before we could get seats in the cafe. The museum part was small and did not provide much information. The tea plantations are also open to visitors but the grounds were muddy due to the rain hence we didn't enter them. The variety and price of products are similar to those in their seoul busan branches hence I wouldn't recommend a special visit to this place if you have been to them before.

This is a very popular tourist destination there are a wide variety of teas for purchase and well as a little cafe to stop and chat over the famous green tea ice cream. Innesfree has a little shop in location where you can make your own soap. The only problem is to wash your hands afterwards you need to go to the bathrooms (outside) so I?셝 recommend taking some hand wipes unless you want soap everywhere. The property has a perfect spot to take photos with the tea plants and take a small stroll. This place can get very busy do either early morning or a little later in the afternoon are better times

This beach was very beautiful and relatively clean. Water was clear and not too cold fot September. Altough it was posted reccommend  not to swim bc season ended in august the water and weather was great. Bathrooms were close by (though toilet paper was out at the one on the beach). The water was easy to swim in with children as it was very shallow and not rough. Got busier toward aftwrnoon with tourist buses and crowds though. Nice also as there were restraunts and snacks within walking distance as well as showers. 2000 won for parking but was worth it.

the ticket price is cheap but place a bit far away from city..sculptures are not well kept so looked run down.but there are many beautiful world buildings which make good photo spots.i am very disappointed there is not even a small cafe for us to take a snack.there is a drink vending machine though..i checked the surrounding for staff.think less than 6staff..this can be a very good attraction place if jeju govt can pump in some money to repaint the buildings open a cafe and make the bus stop nearer so we do not have to walk so long.

The place is relatively small and when I was there there where a lot of people. The beach is with black sand nice. I had a very nice Mandarin Orange icecream and that was worthwhile. From there I walked along the beach maybe 5 kilometers until I came to a little fishing port. From there a very nice person took me along in the car... there was a bus stop but the busses only come at a long interval...it would have been possible to wark until Seogwipo but that would have been another 3 or so kilometers. A long but really beautiful walk...the stones are all vulcanic and black. If you have the time and inclination I recommend

The O쨈Sulloc Tea Museum and tea field is a treat!  It쨈s easy to get to by the airport bus we got to it by taking the Yeha West Tour.Be prepared for crowds in the cafe.  However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The cafe offers the most delicious green tea ice cream.  I쨈m dying to try the cakes but can쨈t get pass the ice cream.  There is also a brown roasted tea ice cream but I prefer the green tea one.  It isn쨈t sweet and has a distinctive green tea flavor left on your palate as you get ready for the next bite.Recommendation--I got the Cold Green Sticks which are perfect for a bottle of water.  The other teas you definitely need a strainer otherwise get the tea in teabags.Oh and O짢Sulloc has a cafe in the Nampo area in Busan if you need your green tea ice cream fix. Other cafes have green tea ice cream but OSulloc is yummy and my favorite.O쨈Sulloc seems to be branding itself as a high end tea so you just can쨈t purchase it in a grocery store nor do the hotels have it as complimentary tea a shame since it is a Korean brand. So stock up and enjoy.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.

The last time I went to a similar place with during my childhood days. Visiting aqua planet in jeju again is a good experience. The whole place isn't all that big but there is plenty of sea marine life to see and a Enormous fish take. This place can give u a kind of relaxing atmosphere. At the end there is a performance where u can rest your weary legs. Good place to be If you have a busy trip before you came to jeju. A little break for a change. Overall I enjoy the trip here and will revisit again with my love ones if ever given the chance.

review: The falls are really beautiful but extremely crowded. I would recommend taking the first bus you can to the area to be there as soon as it opens if you want to try to get decent pictures without hundreds of people in your photo.  We arrived around 11am and the sheer numbers of people detracted from the beauty of the falls.

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

strictly for those above 18.but beware that buses come here ends early.after 10pm i only see taxis and cars.Interesting stone sculptures of male and female organs.sex positions..a shop selling interesting condoms and penis keychains vibrators etc..super cold at night..open until midnight..there is a indoor museum and show clay figurines..

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!

So dont get this place confused with maze land.  This one is near the lava cave.  Here it has one maze only.  It would have been fun and peaceful but then 3 buses of middle school children arrived and all hell broke out.  Very hars to walk around it when a bunch of kids are running past you.  But the maze owners also have a bunch of cats that were super friendly.
Recommend ~3 hrs. It was a relaxing hike up the stairs. Very easily accessible via public bus. Beautiful environment for nature lovers. Recommend to come here after udo island trip.
One of the larger temples we visited in Jeju. Beautiful well tended grounds and architecture. There is a bus stop right outside the temple which is handy!

On a 3 day trip to jeju we needed more indoor activities due to the daily snowy conditions and found Jeju National Museum. With low expectations and dampened spirits as we were expecting to visit more outdoor activities we were pleasantly happy with our choice.This museum was easily accessible from our hotel as it was only a 28 minutes bus ride (costs us 1150krw). The bus stop just outside the museum.The museum itself is quite out of the way from the city centre but so was all the other places we wanted to visit and therefore was not an issue for us.Highly recommend you taking your time to read and inspect each exhibit. It is quite amazing how history laid out the changes made due to advancement through discovery. Although for a quick browser it may only take you half an hour (it took us more than 1 hour).Entry was free and I'm not sure if this is the norm but surely worth a visit even if just as a time filler.
My friend told me to make sure I visit Udo island before leaving. We truly enjoyed the ferry ride and riding around the island on a bus.

Location is bit difficult if you get there by Bus I'd recommend taxi or rent a car.Tea Museum however it's more like mini shopping place where they sell green tea stuffs and cosmetic stuffs as well.Also their restaurants is quite nice and tasteful.Must visit there when the weather is good since it is very nice to take picture outside.

Jeju World Cup Stadium is certainly worth stopping by if you are in the area. It looks superb from the outside and can be seen from a distance as you come down the hill from Seogwipo.Main entrance is open allowing you to walk in and spend some time in the stands for free. Tickets for Jeju United games are reasonably priced  and only attended up a small number of fans meaning they are up for grabs if you happen to time your visit in the K-League Classic season.Lots of busses pass by including the Airport Limo service (stop just in front) so pay a visit if you're a football fan or just want to see one of the 2002 World Cup's venues

Jeju has tonnes of 'museums' to draw in cash from tourists. Most of these are silly  man-made museums having no connection whatsoever to Jeju or even Korea. It is almost a sin to spend time in these museums while in Jeju  instead of enjoying the scenery outdoors.However I would reallly recommend a stop at the seashell museum if you have an hour to spare in the Seogwipo area. The labor of love of 1 woman  this place houses a staggering collection of shells from all over the world  crafted into stunning displays. Seashells so pretty  its hard to believe they are real..but they are.There's also a small shop to purchase souvenirs if you'd like but they don't pressure you. Also attached is a cafe.Close by to a bus stop.
It's nice to see and easy to acces as it has an own bus stop.Something hapend there in a movie and therfore many people are there to see that place.
It?s a small island but very popular! Very easy to get on the bus to go around the island! Very windy there! Recommend black beach and Cow?s head peak!

It is difficult to take the local bus to go to the Ferry station so we took a taxi from our hotel near the city centre. The ferry ride is short but the sea air is refreshing and it is kind of fun seeing excited kids feeding the seagulls. The scenery is beautiful on the island but the hop on and hop off bus service is pretty rough.I think they are overbooked and big groups also have special buses nobody else are allowed on. End up waiting a lot to get to the next site. Annoying..!

It is a very nice tea museum about 40 minutes from Jeju airport. It was fields and fields if green tea bushes. The museum itself is tiny and overpriced but if you're in the area the bushes are gorgeous and very picturesque. I would recommend.

I went to the Marine Park (Pacific Land) that proposes a show with dolphins  sea lions and monkeys. I went there with my friends  thinking it was an aquarium  and I do not recommend this place at all! What they're doing to this beautiful animals is pure cruelty. We can obviously see the intensive training  the abuse and the fear these poor animals (monkeys  dolphins) are going through. There was a baby dolphin completely lost and unable to do the show in this tiny tank  but they forced the adults to do the show again and again  until the baby succeeded it. The baby ended up banging his head on the wall.. It was just unbearable to watch. After that  no food in return for the others. The animals shouldn't be here  and treated like that. I'm surprised no one launched a petition against this facility yet. Its just pure sadness  cruelty. It's not something children should see... I do not recommend it.

I went to Jeju after spending 6 days in Seoul. After Namdaemun  Myeondong  Hongdae and many undergeound shopping malls naturally Maeil Oleh Oleh did not excite me. Mainly targeting tourist business and restaurants amd stuff is not cheap there.

I visited this as part of an inclusive tour.  This is really interesting.  there is the story of tea and you can walk among the tea bushes.  This is the best Korea tea there is and of course you can buy their products and sample green tea foods in the cafe. Their sister beauty products company Innesfree also has a cafe and gift shop.  Again these products have a hig reputation in S. Korea.  I would have liked more time to spend here.  The main cafe was packed and I would have like to have had green tea and green tea cake or green tea ice cream but I wouldn't have been able to see anything else in the time we had.  A pleasant place to visit for a few hours.

I visited on a tour from Yeha Bus Tours. It was such an awesome experience that I would have never seen if it wasn't for being part of that tour. The buildings were really neat and the restaurant was delicious. I was there on a rainy day but it was still pleasant. The mist contributed to the mysterious and dreamy vibe that this place had. I recommend carrying a small umbrella. I needed it throughout my 2 week stay in South Korea.

I took my parents in law to Korea and visited Jeju to show unique Korean folk village and the culture. The village was just full of tricky business people selling products. I would not recommend this place to anyone!

I took buses from central of jeju to this area for fishing trip it takes about 1 hours with 2 buses wait time for buses quite long ~30m. Bus driver and local residents are friendly dry squid is delicious and cheap. 4k - 6k won per squid (depend upon the size) you can ask them to grill and enjoy. I love this quite place and people

I recently visited this beach with a group of friends and it was definitely worth it.  We were staying in Jeju City so it was about an hour bus ride to get to the beach.  There isn't any space to lay down a blanket so you have to rent an umbrella.  The water is crystal is clear and the tide is very low.  I had to walk about 300 meter in order to get water that was waist high. There are all kinds of coffee shops and restaurants located along the strip of the beach so you can eat and hang for  as long as you like.  The water is beautiful and makes it worth it.
I loved the vistas here for photos and the large open spaces. Vendors sell local fruit. You can take the number 8 bus from downtown for 900 won or a taxi for about 2500 won.
I love their tea but I rarely come to the cafe because it's always so uncomfortably busy.  I would recommend visiting though especially to purchase things from their shop.

I like Greek history. So when I heard about this place I decided to visit. My wife was not ready but I persuaded her. Although this place is bit off way bus service is limited so I booked a taxi for to-fro. When we reached there it was foggy weather so could not see much from outside.I come to know that it is combo Greek+Trick eye museum.When we enter Greek Museum I was surprised on white environment cleaniness....really a good place. We end up taking lots of pics.Wouls recommend to go there.

I have some work lead a group tour to Jeju. My bos choose this company. Thanks for guide us while we doing Jeju tour with a bus. Really recomended cheap price. And Mr John really help me to handle tour. See you again Mr John. You are nice best guide Jeju ever.

I found about this temple while looking for things to do around the waterfalls. It's quite a drive from them and I'm not pretty sure if by bus it's possible to get there but since it was my first temple we drove there anyway. It's a nice big temple though some of its decorations seem to be amateur. Nevertheless it was a nice experience. It's not very crowded so that's also a bonus. I don't recommend this temple for people who are disabled or have a hard time walking since there's a fare amount of stairs till you get to the temple.

Easily accessible by public bus from airport! This garden is not so crowded & have nice decoration so can relax. Locals like to visit this place & not foreigners are seen during my visit there. Next to this garden have a waterwall so got another place to relax. Recommend to go teddy bear museum & kpop museum as very near to one another so this will spend one whole day.

Cheonjeyeon waterfall is located at the southern tip of Jeju island near Seogwipo-do. It is about 1.5 hours bus ride from the airport. It is called the 3-tier waterfall as it falls over 3 cliffs before ultimately ending up in the ocean. The legend has it that there are 7 nymphs who visit at night to bathe in the ponds. You will also find the Seonimgyo Bridge on your walk to the waterfall which is adorned by the 7 nymphs  beautifully done in metal.A definite must-do while visiting Jeju-do.

Came here just to try the tea but not visit the museum. The cafe offers a good variety of nice tea. I enjoy the cakes and ice cream too. There are gifts that you can buy for friends here. Things such as green tea chocolate biscuits and facial products. It?셲 quite a walk from the carpark for my tourist bus to the museum itself.

Been here since in tour itinerary and feel amused! Our big bus with 30people in it still able to run when the driver put the engine in off position! And it's quite fast as well maybe 20-30km/hr When we off from our bus and try to pour a water they go to the side or even go up instead of flow down. Recommended tourist spot to visit and try by yourself!

Aqua Planet is a very nice place to visit especially with a toddler. Many things to see dont miss the seal and dolphin show its very well worth it. It tends to get pretty busy and crowded. Purchase your tickets online if you can you can get discount.

review: An interesting place to visit though there is nothing much except for the short stretch of road.. It's amazing to see that the bus really glide uphill.. Some cars are not able to do a good job and the driver ended up starting their engine and start driving

All the promotions are for Koreans only even though I showed them my membership abroad. Really not enthusiastic to do business with tourists. Why do I have to spend my money here? Let?셲 be honest I didn?셳 have to buy this brand compared to all others available. The tea museum next door is also just a one room exhibition and place for shopping.

A must stop during our busy vacation here in Jeju! They have free parasols that we used during the sunny day and it made the garden a lot nicer to enjoy. We bumped into the Director that created the garden and he was very kind. I highly recommend buying his book from the store and he even gave us an autographed copy:)) You can tell that each bonsai tree in the garden has a lot of love invested. There are koi fish in the water flowing through the garden and they are well fed and taken care of. There is also a cafe in the garden that has fancy drip coffee. We went in early October and the weather was perfect.

A beautiful park there so many local tourist using this park for photo spot. The ticket price - Quite expensive. So many photo spot! Hard to find restaurant or eating place here. If you are using bus please double check the bus time. I recommend to use taxi.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

You can easily spend a half or full day sightseeing around the island. They have tour buses which will take you around to the major sights but I'd recommend renting a bike. There are heaps of places to rent bikes from after you get off the ferry. You'll need an international license to rent a scooter or ATV. But there are no serious hills in the island so (if you're there in fall/spring with fair weather) I'd really recommend a bicycle. It was so lovely cycling around the island and easily jumping on and off my bike to snap pictures.The bike rental was 4 hours for 10,000 won. They shop will give you a map of the island with tours and sightseeing locations on it. Although you don't really need it as you basically just cycle the seaside road. Don't forget your camera or to eat the famous peanut ice cream!
Yeha bus tour with Joy as guide. brilliant, concise, excellent knowledge and good language communications. Recommend very highly

With only one full day in Jeju and a list of places to visit, there was no way we can go see it all by ourselves in one day. So when we ran across this tour that included almost all of our must see places in Jeju we had to book it. Jin was our tour guide for the day and was very prompt with the pickup and was very knowledgeable of the sites that he took us to. Each stop of the tour was ??. And the option to go tangerine picking checked off one of activity that I wanted to do myself. The price for this tour is very reasonable considering that we didn’t have to figure out how to get place to place by bus or taxi. The cherry on top is the food and activity recommendations that Jin gave us as the tour ended so it felt like our tour continued on through the night even after the tour ended. Thanks Jin for the awesome tour!

When I went for the first time, my friend and I were late so we were rejected so please come earlier than 5.30 pm.We managed to find time to come again on another day and Cheonjeyeon Falls was a nice place to spend a couple hours here.Take note that there are stairs so it can be a little tiring to some. We had just came back from a day of Hallasan hiking so our legs were busted.

What's interesting is that you really, actually get to see cars/buses with their engines obviously off, rolling up the slope. Expect to see a number of tour buses. Some tour guides will demonstrate the mysteriousness of the road even further by pouring water on the ground. The water will flow upwards. 10mins is enough time to spend here. Recommended to visit once for the experience.

What is so mysterious about this road is that vehicles can still move upslope with the engine switched off. We had the engine of the bus switched off and experienced it first hand what it felt like. The bus was first moving at a very slow speed but it started to gear up towards the end of the road. We then got off the bus to watch other vehicle move on the road. It was quite an interesting sight. Somewhere nearby, I even saw a stand giving out free Christian literature. Lots of snacks available. My first time trying the milk. At first, I thought it was some yoghurt drink or a big bottle of Yakult. Tried the one with black cap and realised that it's banana milk. I never like flavoured milk but this taste nice.More pictures available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html

we've been Udo island on the day 2 at Jeju Island after hiking to Sunrise Peak Seongsan Illchulbong. we going to the port by walking about 15 minutes from Illchulbong, and takes ferry only for 11.000W returns. the ferry takes 15 minutes to island and schedule every 10 minutes. We have only for 3 hours at the island before going back, so we chose to hiking Udo peak. takes 40 minutes - 1 hours to reach the peak, just follow the path. really recommend to going Udo island, very beautiful scenery of Seongsan Illchulbong and the cave.You also can rent a bike for around the island or motorbike if you have international license. Or shuttle bus.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

Went there twice. Once on a rainy day and on a sunny day. Do not go on rainy days! We went on the bus tour which told us that English tour will be provided but the guide spoke korean throughout instead. Bus tour took us to a few attractions which were pretty scenic and impressive. However, the wind was too strong and it was freaking cold. Always have a poncho/raincoat prepared in case of rain! Went on a sunny day the next day and rented the ATV for 15,000 won for an hour. Managed to explore and rode the ATV round half of the island. Fantastic experience, would definitely recommend it and do it again! Also, try the peanut ice cream!

We were staying near Seogwipo and took the two hour bus trip to the cave.  We enjoyed the cave but it wasn't worth a four hour round trip bus trip.
