Would recommend if you are staying on that side of the island.  At the bus terminal in Seogwipo, most people spoke no English but the lady at the information desk did and was very helpful.

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We went to the cave by a convenient bus frm Jeju city. There is a 2km-wlak form bus station to the cave (I would not recommend to take the taxis that are waiting for you as a total tourist). After the 20mn-minute walk, the cave is very interesting and informations about it are quite depth.

We went there on July 17, 2016. We asked the hotel front desk how to get there by public bus, 2 bus numbers to take to the destination. There are plenty of bus for the first leg, but the 2nd bus no. 990 there are only 2 or 3 available in a day and the next one for us like 2 hours away, so the few people/tourists that was there with us decided to walk to the destination for about 3 kilometers. When we got there sweaty and tired we pay the cheap fare of KW2,000 (mind you cheap attraction). The good thing is the cool breeze inside the cave, mind your steps because its wet and some puddle of waters in there. Many people in there, mostly Korean tourists. The few inside the dimly lighted cave is not impressive neither beautiful as I thought. When we got out at about 4:30 pm. we happened to catch the bus no. 990, to our surprise the bus driver told us to get out of the bus while he let the Korean passengers in. We asked why and he keep telling us taxi..taxi..taxi.. So apparently, he does not take foreigners to go to the next bus stop and forced us to take taxi, sure enough, a taxi driver in the area approached us. I felt so discriminated by the bus driver, we didn't even want to negotiate with the taxi driver (because, I believe they do this on purpose). We decided to walk back 3 km. to the next bus stop. It was a waste of almost a day of our time, definitely not recommended to visit this place, NOW I KNOW WHY IT'S CHEAP!

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We went on a cloudy day and the driver drove us all the way to the entrance at Yeongsil.  Having a hot afternoon the day before, we thought it would be warmer thN the day before as we Han to walk uphill. The driver saw us in our thin layer, offered me a rain and wind breaker and a pair of gloves. I reluctantly accepted them out of courtesy but later genuinely thanked him after four hours.On a windy and cloudy October morning, the temperature actually dropped as we ascended. Two hours later it got even much colder with strong gusts, as we approached near to split of the main road to either continue uphil to the top, or to go downhill to the other parking lot. I had to use my gloves and another layer there. My husband regretted not bring his hat on a cloudy day to protect his cold ears (anyway later I found his nose sunburnt even on a cloudy day)We used our walking sticks and wore our hiking shoes, which I found very helpful. We saw some people who really had difficulty completing the loop.  I suggest tourists first decide whether you physically can complete the four hour trip (adults) to the other parking lot. If not, better discuss with your driver (if using one) to meet in the starting point, or decide where to park your car, if not taking the bus.Pack your bag reasonably and don't take any unnecessary items. Some snacks are helpful though as there are no snack bar at all. I suggest also try to bring your garbage downhill as I don't think there will be regular cleaner everyday up/downhill for hours'hike.

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre. We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000\ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We traveled here by public transport. The bus stop turned out to be quite a bit away from the cave itself, but we were lucky enough to get a lift from a friendly lady. The cave itself is nice, with lights everywhere. It's not a long walk through, nor is it a difficult one. I would recommend wearing shoes, rather than sandals or flipflops, as the rocky surface isn't easy in the low light. Also recommend a jacket/vest because it gets cold and drops fall from the ceiling.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We read how good the pork belly was and from what we read, recommendations were to go to  Hwaro Hyang instead of Dumbedon. We arrived, dropped our bags, took a taxi to get there to make sure we experience what everyone is raving about. Hwaro Hyang was not too crowded and we easily got a table. The server explained that we should get the set for a couple to be able to taste a good sample of the cuts and some abalone. That we did. We got the platter, he dropped it on the hot plate and that was the last time our server came to our table. We saw how he was going around to all the other tables, turning their food over, cutting it up. Finally, we saw this lady who was serving another table and we flagged her down to see who might help us. She had to yell and call/force a young person to help us. I?ll chalk it to a language barrier issue as they were busily chatting with the rest of the customers. Finally the boy cut up our food, and we had to help ourselves and towards the end, the lady came back to turn off our hot plate. The experience would have been enhanced if we had known how to pair the condiments. We didn?t want to offend anyone so we watched as they showed the other tables how to eat the food and just mimicked them. They even did the lettuce wraps for some tables to show them how the side dishes are rolled. So moral of the story, unless you?re local or can speak with them conversationally, prepare to be ignored and just watching to see how others do it.

We reached the ferry terminal at 11am and waited for a short while for the ferry. The ferry depart quite frequently so there is no worry for that. As mentioned by other people, you will need to bring your passport to purchase a ticket. If you intend to rent a motorised vehicle in Udo, you will need to bring along your international driving permit. We rented a covered motorised scooter for 3h at KRW40,000. The scooter has doors and can seat 2 people. It took us less than 2.5h to cover the whole island, we even took 45min lunch break in between. The entire island is around 17km, so if you intend to make stopovers for photo taking, renting for 2h will be good enough. Just follow the coastline and you won't get lost. I highly recommend travellers to opt for the motorised scooter for a relaxing trip around Udo island. It will take you just half day. There are not many cars on the road but there are many scooters and bicycles which share the same path. There are many tourists and they might not observe the driving rules very well, so do be careful when driving on the roads. However, if you intend to see some of the other sights on Udo, they are not accessible for these transportation as you will need to take a separate ferry to go there. There seems to be many people taking the shuttle bus in Udo, so I don't really recommend people to do so if you have an international driving permit.

We originally got the bus here to go to hallim park. we noticed this beautiful beach and decided to check it out. anyway we ended up staying here all day. Was so nice to be on such soft, yellow sand with clear waters. There was quite a few families with young children which was nice to see all the children playing. Unfortunately there was a digger truck digging the sand while we were there for a few hours and a man kept blowing his whistle at everyone walking near the truck. if it wasnt for this it would have been excellent. Theres shops and restaurants close by and toilet blocks that provide flowing water to wash off but this is cut off around 5 or 6 pm. Sunset here was amazing.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We didn't have great weather when we were on the island so couldn't climb the mountain. This was an alternative activity and glad we did it as it was really interesting. Make sure you go all the way to the end as you don't want to miss the lava flow. The ground is slippy in places and not suitable for small children, strollers or wheelchairs. If you're using public transport get the bus 900. Not the 701 as we did! The 701 has a stop called 'Manjamggul Cave entrance' but it's 2km walk away from the entrance!!

We did not rent a car and took the metro bus and got dropped off at the entrance.  We saw a sign for a bus pickup and waited thinking a shuttle would come.  No shuttle so we walked approx 1.5 miles to get to the lava tube.  We were told there is no shuttle.  The lava tube is an awesome site to see and think about but it's surely not for everyone especially those who can not walk on uneven surfaces.  There are puddles everywhere and some places dripped more than others.  There are adequate signs with information about the area.  The end of the tube is interesting but if you've been in caves, there is not much variety and it is mostly dark colored lava to look at.  I've been in caves where the rock turns a different color and shape.  There were no taxis to take us back to the bus stop so we kindly asked a Korean couple who understood our English for a ride.  What we can say are the Korean people are so kind!

We decided to visit this   Green tea Museum   because it was a rainy day but could not find much of a direction - there was a mention of the tea stone experience but no further information.  We ended up going to the busy restaurant through a small 'museum' and ended up 'enjoying the $9 green tea'.  On the fields across from the museum there are kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures for photo opportunities.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

We arrived here by bus from our Jeju hotel on a Friday night.  It took approximately 35-40 minutes because of the traffic and the nondirect route our bus took.  The front of the market (across the street) has a small open square area where they would have live music for the night.  We also noticed a few drunks sitting around in the area, but they seemed harmless.The market itself is quite large.  The market seemed to specialize in selling tangerines.  There were stall after stall selling local tangerines.  There is a larger variety of items offered for sale as you walk into the market some more.  We tried some food that was being sold - in this case, some pork at around 9000 won.  There is also seafood and other vegetables and meats sold.  The market seemed to extend to other areas - it's quite close to the Black Pork Street, some other more upscale shops and restaurants.  It's definitely worth a 1-2 hour walk within the market to explore.

Was on YEHA bus tour (which is really great), but this particular place is not that special. Do not spend any time going here unless it is included in some tour package. Basically a road where stuff kind-a sort-a roll upwards but not really.I was more interested of the over-priced street food and the pig statues down the road.

Visiting Manjanggul Cave is one of the main reason I visited Jeju. I and my family were not disappointed at all. We visited during late June 2015. The cave is a little bit cooler inside even in a hot summer day so remember to bring a jacket especially for kids. There was rain before our visit so the cave inside was a little bit wet but we could go inside and visit. There is a steep stair in the beginning of the tunnel/cave so one must walk very carefully. After entering the cave, there is no more stair and on flat level mainly.The whole cave is well lit so you should be able to see inside without bringing your own flashlight torches. (You can still bring it if you want to see everything in detail!)Only 1km of the cave is accessible by visitors. You go inside and walk to the end of the tunnel and then walk back the same way you go in. I suggest you riding a taxi to this place since public bus is not easily accessible to this tourist spot. There is a bathroom outside the cave only. So if you need to go to bathroom, you have to go before entering the cave.

Visited the cave as a part of a bus tour. We entered through the 2nd section and were given 40 mins to walk to end of the cave and back. Grounds are uneven and slippery due to water dripping from the ceiling, hence proper shoes are necessary. The lighting was quite dim and there were only a couple of descriptions along the way. I didn't come out with a full appreciation of the lava cave. The cave wasn't very spectacular but it's worth a visit if you are in the area.

Visited DongMun on a Monday night after dinner at around 8pm and some seafood / fruit vendors are still open.  A small area adjacent to the market were doing bustling business selling street food / snack.  Having come from Seoul / Busan before JeJu,  DongMun market may be seemingly smaller but will still be a nice market to visit when in Jeju

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Very well maintained and beautifully laid out area around the falls. Only costs a couple of AUD to go in and wander round the tree lined river. Plenty of lucky charms around for your wishes too. Very popular with tourists, I expect it can get very busy. Recommend the Angel caf챕 near entrance coffee ok and great free wifi. Also take a walk past the fishing boats with there large glass squid lights and over the nearby bridge on to the island.

Unless you are seriously prepared for an all out ascent, do not go on this trip.  It is beautiful, and we by no means tried it all, but our ascent from Seongpanak station was insane!  The paths are uneven, unsteady and unmaintained.  Handrails where they are most needed are not present, those that are present are in a terrible state of affairs.  To top it all off, the staff was 50%-50%...  some were excellent while others were downright rude and obnoxious...  and to end it all, I didn't like the looks of two of the taxi drivers who were ready to get into a knock-down, drag out fight with me when I selected a third taxi...  all I can say...  BRING IT!!!  I personally hope this attraction winds up out of business or under new management....   Was the low point of our trip to Jeju!!!

Udo was easy to get to and a great place to camp with full amenities. There are 2 main beaches; one on the West side and one on the North East side. Both are beautiful but the one that has sand made of seashells (West Side) is a little hard on your bare feet  and it was much busier there. The other has soft fine sand that makes for a great camping spot. There are no taxis on the island. In hindsight, we would have taken the other ferry to the port that was a bit closer to Hagosudong Beach (the NE side), but there is this drop on and off Bus Tour System that costs 5000won/person. You can get on from the ferry, drop off and set up your camp at the beach, then hop back on. It runs frequently but only stops at 4 main sightseeing spots (beach 1, beach 2, caves and ___ ) . We were able to use the bus for the two days we were there for on the same fare, but there are times/stops that are crazy busy. We watched at least 6 packed buses go by before we decided to stay the night. Honorable food mention: Pirate Caf챕. Really interesting place and staff. Great BiBamBap and you get to sign a plaque and hang it from their wall when you?re done eating.Friendly people, campfire and camping friendly, personal beer cooler (at the convenience stores directly behind the beach), and lots of cats.

U-do is more of a small village, the citizens are so down to earth and friendly! Lots of fresh seafood be sure to try them out! Hop on a tour bus, driver will intro the island to you!Great for family vacations or exploring the island with friends and taking lots of amazing photos

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

Transportation: There are several buses that make stops at this destination, but just like everything in Jeju, rental car is the recommended mode of travel. Food: the lava tubes does have a restaurant colocated but I did not eat. There are also some snacks you can purchase here but you are not allowed to bring them down into the lava tubes. Attraction: The scale of the lava tube really surprised me. We descended roughly 30 feet into the lava tube after we purchased our tickets ($4 pp). The stairs were slippery, so be cautious when descending. Don?t worry if you have claustrophobia, The tube is about 25ft across and 20 feet high! There are no tour guides, so you won?t have anybody explaining the history or the geology of the tubes, but there are educational signs posted about every 100 feet. There was also a great museum on sit I recommend visiting prior to going into the lava tubes. Great place to visit, and it took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.

Tour companies love this tourist trap because it add a good few lines to their tourist brochure while being totally costless for them and wasteful for us.If you can, ask your guide to just pass this, getting back to the hotel staring at your ceiling is better than this.My guide made it worse since he was totally excited of this place, yet when I get there, even before we stop, I look outside the bus to the row of trees and can see the reason behind   the mystery road   and I was   hmmm...lame, can we just move on  . But the guide insist that we spend our expensive time on this thing and my group members want to agree with him.And since I already see the row of tree and how the optic illusion would work, the optic illusion (which is weak) dissipates for me. Ask your guide to go somewhere else.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

This was an exciting attraction. It takes about 1 hour to get to the end of the tube and back. The closer you get to the end the colder it gets. Also pe prepared to get a little wet, as there are drops of water falling from the top. You wont need an umbrella or anything like that. Getting here is tricky. As I was waiting for the bus to get here (990) I found a taxi and got him to take me for $4,000 won. This saved me a lot of time. It might have been too much but it saved me time, since the bus comes by every 45 minutes or so. There are restaurants at the entrance, they over charge for water so make sure you are prepared if you like to drink water. Definitely an amazing experience and a must do in the area.

This was a very interesting Lava Tube cave.  There were signs in English as well as various other languages describing what you were looking at.  The signs were informative.  The cave is cool, so I recommend a zippered sweatshirt or windbreaker.  Also, the floor of the cave is uneven, so you definitely want to have good walking shoes.  I was just fine wearing old jogging shoes.  We went as part of a guided tour - I would have liked to spend just a little more time there, but that's how it goes on bus tours...  There may be more beautiful caves, but overall, it was the nicest cave I've been in - very nice Lava Tube - you will enjoy it.

This was a great beach and was easy to get to with a bus station right on the corner. Entrance was lined with a variety of vendors and there was a supermarket, well stocked in case you forgot something. There were many stores and restaurants nearby to quench your post-swim hunger. The beach was quite nice, water felt great and overall was pretty clean. The shower/bathroom area wasn't that good, but we didn't expect it to be.

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This place was really unexpected. Through the Yeha Bus tour this was one of the stops and I am glad we visited this place. A lot of mini exhibits with bears dressed up according to the theme and the gift shop is great as well. For teddy bear lovers and lovers of all things cute, we recommend this place.

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.

This is arguably the longest running South Korean LIVE show ever!  Now, it is branching out to other popular tourist destinations such as Jeju Island.  You needn't understand Korean language to appreciate the show, which is leaning more towards physical action and slapstick comedy based on timing.  It revolves around cooking.  Nanta show is leaning heavily towards satisfying tour groups and the day I was there, two thirds of the theatre was filled up by tourists that came in bus loads.  Nanta is interactive too, with occasional involvement with the audience.  Children thoroughly enjoyed the show.  It was pure 90 minutes of unadulterated fun and enjoyment.  In terms of price, you can get cheaper price booked through YEHA website.  Commendable fun:)
This garden is really aesthetic and pretty!! I had been in Seoul for my stay in Korea so far and everyday is super busy, so it?s nice to relax and see this garden today! I would highly recommend!

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

There's a starting point and ending point, that shows this mysterious road's gravitational force. Many went with tour buses but it's best to experience this in your own rented car! Switch to neutral and let the mystery begin!

There is a bus from Jeju bus terminal that takes 1hours and a half min and you have to take a Ferry that costs 5,500won.If you dont know how to plan one day travel I would like to recommend you to go Udo and  Seongsan Ilchulbong that is closer to each other If you start your day early you will probably have more time thoughTo see all island it takes 3~4hours by bus that there is Tour bus which costs 5,000wonHowever i would like to recommend you to ride a bike for some partIt is beautiful to ride around the sea and you can feel relaxed.There is 3 beaches that you can visit and those are all different atmosphereespecially there is Coral beach that are exists only 3palce on the world Please go towards the end where people are not crowdedYou will see more pretty coralUdo is famouse for peanut that if you like plz try only small amount since it is a bit expensiveI am not sure if there is famouse food for foreginer but street food is okay As my memory Udo is one of the best part in Jeju island I will recommend for my friends

There are 3 mazes in this park which you are encouraged to try all of them. There were buses of students visiting the maze land when we were there. the kids were good in the mazes and we simply followed them to get out of the mazes. There are also a 'tower' where the teachers made sure the kids don't get into accidents while playing in the mazes. Pretty amazing and fun to spend some time there. But will not return again as we have completed all 3 mazes. Unless, they expand and created a few more, then will consider visiting again the next time I go Jeju.

The trip ti Mt Halla is great and do not miss it. Youu really should start early, and it takes a little less than recommended times, about one hour less if you walk clow but continuously.We walked three 15, 30 and 55, two males - my son and me and one female accompanied us.We traveled by bus from Seogwipo, busses go every 15-30 minutes since early morning to Seongpanak - busstop.Back we walked to Gwaneumsa and there is no direct bus connection, but take a taxi (for 5 thous WON) or walk about 5 km. We finaly shared taxi with very kind Korean directly to Seogwipo, thank again to the kind man. It was good and exhausting and we slept nicely after all. The next day we were ready to walk again. Unfortunatelly was very cloudy and walked upon clouds finally, however it was June, it was not too hot. There are two springs along the way - one up and nexd on the way down. Recommended to every who travels with teenagers:) Normal hiking shoes like trainers were OK, dont worry.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

the pinky building and all kitty stuffs! Very interesting and nice place for pictures. they have cafe & shop for kitty stuffs, Kitty fans this is the place do not be missed. things slightly expensive because of   Sanrio   brand. but not so tourist friendly cos its not a walking distance from town, either by bus or taxi. We took bus to Kitty island (but missed one station cos we dont understand Korean language, we only stop the bus driver when we passed kitty island), for return in convenient we pick taxi (black color), cost us 60USD back to town (like 10mins distance only)

The park is the mystical legend of how three gods arrived in Jeju-do and started to develop the island. The place is a great escape from the busy city of Jeju, surrounded with trees and pavilion of traditional Korean architecture. You can also sit in for a 15 minutes long animation, available both in English and Korean  describing the origins of Jeju.

The mountain is extremely busy with tons of people and older koreans are not always very friendly toward foreigners, but the rude people are exceptions. In general the hike is wonderful, just very long. There is beautiful scenery and forests to enjoy. Take a jacket for the top as its cold and start early.

The market is 60% local 40% tailored to tourist, hence depending on what you are after you can choose the part that suits your expectation.It is the local fresh meat , fish and vegetable market--fresh goodies are sold at a very reasonable price and exceptional quality. The touristic part is nice also-- lot of old aunties promoting the snacks, personally i dont think that's the most authentic souvenir so we decided to go to the pottery shop and ending up buying soup copper pot and stone pot back (though it's heavy) as it did remind us a lot more about the trip.The fresh snack stands are very busy and people are elbow to elbows. Food was yum but probably you don't wonna spend more than 2 hours there. Btw, there is a night food market outside after 5 pm and it's worth grabbing a snack or two.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The cave is nice if you are natural lovers, weather becomes cold inside the cave around 13 degree celcius. It should takes around 1 or 2 hours to explore the cave. For people travelling by bus, i recommends to use kaokao map and naver at the same time to find bus route and english name of bus station to get off

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The beach has beautiful, clear emerald waters (the pictures doesn?t do the place justice as its much better experienced in person), and a really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries. We got there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. Near the beach there are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice. Easy to hail a taxi there too for those who wants to travel to their next location  by cab. Parking lots available too for those who are driving.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

The beach has beautiful, clear  waters, and really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries and tea.We went there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. There are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice near the beach . Easy to get a taxi there too. Parking lots are available too.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

Such a beautiful small island. You can reach Udo island by ferry then there are buses available in the island to move you around. Try their peanut and orange ice cream. Personally, I like thier peanut ice cream very much. Highly recommended.

Spent the day here after going to to the Tuff Cone. I like how they have a lot of business by the beach and how the main beach is enclosed like a cove.  You have either the option to pay to sit under an umbrella, I believe it was 20,000 KRW for all day or you can just go find a shaded area to sit by the rocks.  We chose to latter as you wouldn?t be in the sun and didn?t have to spend the 20,000 KRW.  The water is beautiful and clear, there are plenty of lifeguards at the beach, and it?s a family oriented beach.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

So we went to Hallasan but didn't have much time, so we've decided to do the yeongsil train until the shelter and then go back the other way (eorekon? Haha). It was about 2hours each ways so 4 hours total. The mountain is free but to get there it's either a bus from Jeju city hall or a taxi (about 27.000 won - 25???). You have to be there before 12:00 pm otherwise it's closed. Really good activity, winter time so there was snow, pretty cool!!But wear good shoes and some coat because it's super windy there !I recommend it 100 times.

Really....it is just another rock with a legend.  It seems that everyone turns into rock while waiting for someone....story line is always the same.  If you are a big fan of Korean drama - Daejeonggeum, then this is the place for you.  A lot of tourist stops here....maybe becos it has no admissions fees.  Try and come early in the morning as the tour buses start coming in late morning.

Really enjoyable walk through the dark and luminous cave created by the eruption of Halla. It will take a decent time and is right next to a maze filled with cats!Unfortunately there isn't convenient bus transport as you have to walk about 30 minutes from the bus stop but if you're relatively fit, it will be no problem (aside from your friends nagging you how long till you get there).

Pretty unique place, well worth to visit! Dress up well as it doesn't seem chilling down there at first, but if you walk until the very end, then back, it may take an hour. Also, getting there not that easy:take #701 from jeju city intercity bus termal to the bus stop named   Entrance to the Manjanggul Lava Tubes  . This is quite far from the entrace though, and the bus #990 supposed to go there is extremely rare, so not much chance except to take a taxi (it should not cost more than 3000 won/ride).

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.

Our plans to visit Hallasan were foiled by a typhoon the night before (we luckily still got to go, though), and we were all excited to do a nice hike. We came here probably 2 or 3 hours before the park closed (we did some other sightseeing instead of Hallasan, this happened to be close by), and the admission was free because the typhoon had caused some damage. Anyways, because of the typhoon and the time of day, the park wasn't very busy. It felt like we had the walking paths to ourselves most of the time (we chose one of the shorter routes because we didn't want to run out of time). It was a nice, easy, relaxing walk. It was also dead quiet except for the occasional group of ladies walking by with music playing on their phone's speaker. Oh and the crows going off every now and then, but that was kind of amusing since their call is funny to me (and different from North American crows). A good alternative if you can't go up some of the steeper stairs and stuff like in Hallasan. We got plenty of beautiful photos because the typhoon the night before gave all the woods a nice, moody atmosphere. If you like going for walks in the woods (even though these are all wooden paths), just being outdoors enjoying the fresh air, and you have enough time, this is worth a visit. If you are short on time and can only do one park or something, then make sure you try to at least go to Hallasan. I would definitely recommend this park over Hallasan though if you have any mobility issues, because the wooden paths are very easy to walk on and there doesn't seem to be a lot of uphill/stairs.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is a small building set in a tea farm. It's a well designed lovely space with a display area about the history of tea and an exhibit wall of teacups and pots a shop where you can try some tea (only one kind though) and a restaurant featuring green tea beverages and sweets. You can also walk around outside there is a garden area in and around the building and also small rows of tea bushes just outside. There's no admission fee and it's not so much of a museum as a commercial venue for selling O'Sulloc products although items can be pricey for the budget traveller. I visited O'Sulloc with a few other backpackers (5 foreigners 1 Korean) and we all had a terrible experience of their customer service. The staff were sour faced and gave us the impression that we were not welcomed glaring at us and tidying their display in a huff when we looked at the product samples (these are samples ok - they're meant to be touched and looked at!). The staff at the counter literally sneered in disdain at my Korean travel companion when he tried to make friendly small talk while we were purchasing our items. This was the worst experience I've had in my 3 weeks in Korea. All the other customer service staff I've encountered in Korea were either very polite and lovely or just neutral. I'm writing in formally to the management about this so hopefully by the time other TripAdvisor members visit they would have improved.In spite of that I did enjoy my visit (no point letting the staff spoil it) but I would recommend coming here only if you've done all your   must-do's   in Jeju or on a rainy day.

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

One of the many very interesting sites in Jeju Island.  These women would dive for 2 minutes at a time to harvest food from the ocean bottom, using no tanks or other equipment.  They were the only known groups of women who resisted during the Japanese occupation.  Also good access by bus.  Easy to get there by bike, depending on where you are staying on the Island. NIce bike paths, though often are covered with the drying sea weed that the old women still harvest from the rocks. There is also a very small Buddhist temple with a Quan Yin statue in front, about a half mile to the west along the coast.

On a family trip, my fiance and I had one day to ourselves and we ended up here for a couple hours. We love being near water, so this was an easy choice for us. The natural pools were so clear and beautiful, even though it was November and cold we went into the water and enjoyed freezing our butts off from the water and wind. Still such a fun and unique experience we'll never forget. Because we came in November there were only a handful of people that came and went. We definitely recommend checking this place out for a hour or so. I imagine it can get pretty busy during the summer time but youd get to enjoy the water much more. Even in the cold weather it's worth just checking out if you're around the area.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Of all the waterfalls we visited, which included all the major ones, this waterfall takes the cake. How to get there:It is easy to reach, a quick walk from anywhere in Seogwipo to the shore. Taxi's help.Once you get there you pay entrance and climb down the steps to the beach.What we liked:Waterfall falling into the sea.Nice way to cool down in the summer heat (water spraying everywhere, cold sea water).Busy, but not too busy.There are much appreciated ice creams and cold drinks at the top of the stairs.What we didn't like:The idea that we looked as silly as everyone else with our selfie stick. Would we recommend others to go?Yes

Of all the places we visited in Jeju via our taxi tour, this is what I would rank as #1 (see  http://www.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=1121529), with Sunrise Peak as #2.  This is a Buddhist temple set in a vast very pretty land.  Interesting Buddha statues ? very exotic particularly for those who have never been to a Buddhist temple.  Our taxi guide politely asked, I believe a caretaker, to see if we can actually go inside the temple.  We were allowed.  I?m not sure if it was early or this is not a traditional tourist place, since we only saw very few people (as compared to the other temple in Busan packed with too many people.)  Felt a little bit odd being a tourist spectator in a house of worship, but glad we did.  The landscaping and statutes in the area were very interesting.  So there's more to see other than the temple itself. I would recommend this place for sure.  Would go back again if have the chance.  Hopefully with less rain this time.  Free to visit.

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

mysterious and unique road!! even a bus can climb itself without start the engine! they have remark the start and end of the mysterious road. enjoy the experiance by stay in your can while your car climb the hill without its engine.. seeing, feel it to believe it by yourself!

My sister and I went to Udo on a ferry ride after spending a couple of hours at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Because we did not want to go back at dawn, we limited our time to be on the island for about 2-3 hours.It is actually best recommended to spend half a day touring the island either on bus or motorbike. Since we did not have much time, we only walked to the nearby beach which was pretty deserted and that was the best part. Most of the tourist places in Jeju was crowded, but not Udo at the time we were there. The beach was beautiful with small stones and black rocks layering the sand. It was beautiful.There were plenty of cafes within walking distance but we chosed a bench facing the sea in front of a GS25 mart.I love the serenity the island offered. I just wish we had more time to go around the island.

My husband and I visited this park during our honeymoon and it was really beautiful. It consists of 8 botanical gardens which features different kinds of plants, a cave which you can walk through, and even an area with different kinds of birds that you can feed and interact with.We got there through the Yeha Bus Tour but you can also get there with a taxi.For those of you who are looking to experience some of the beauty of nature and interact with it, I recommend this place.
