review: My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Just a rock formation that looks more like a bunny than a dragon.  Nothing much.  FOC entry but if you're driving, parking is paid when you exit the carpark.  Payment is to an attendant.  Highly touristy area and can be quite packed when the tour buses arrive.  This attraction is open 24hrs.

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Hair and beauty treatment was the first thingwe went for. it was just awesome,. they made us feel us like superstars. One my friend spent all her time in the casino. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

It took about 10 minutes to travel on a ferry to visit Udo (thanks to G map)!I decided to walked around the coastline after lunch on arrival.An interesting island with some public arts and you wouldn?t stop taking photos!It worth spending some time walking around! (A number of transportation options are available, such as bike, e-bike and bus)!

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

I'm not a Hello Kitty fan so I'm not really all that head over heels in love with the place but it is not boring as well. For those who likes Hello Kitty and its pink stuffs, you'll definitely like it here (especially little girls). There are definitely a lot of HK stuff you can find here and rooms to play with. For adults - you can stay at the HK cafe and enjoy their yogurt, read the HK history or go to the souvenir shop while your kids or friends are busy roaming around the place.

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the   jimjilbang   (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you   foreigners   out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.
If you're a free and easy traveller, I'll totally not recommend you to travel to see this mysterious road. If you're on a tour bus, this is an interesting experience.

If you were to Seongsan Ilchulbong and to Manjang cave next, you can grab the taxi if there is no bus.. The fare is quite reasonable.Wouldnt expect that the cave would be that cold but it is as cold as Seoul during Spring time.. The lighting is very good. Though it is  a long walk to the end, it id worth it.. The deeper, the colder it is..

If you want to enjoy around two hours walking without difficulties in the middle of an amazing and dense  forest I highly recommend you to visit Bijarim. Considering the time needed for these trees (nutmeg yew, family of the Taxus) to grow and the fact that normally you can only find it as bushes into other species's forest this place is a unique jewel with many of the trees aging more that 500 or indeed 800 years. Beautiful and relaxing experience that I will keep forever in my memories as a lover of trees that I am.

If you have seen any of the large dramatic water falls around the world then you will be disappointed by this tiny cascade. Barely 60/70 ft tall and about 20/25 ft wide. A small stream tumbles directly into the ocean. The tourist brochures make this more dramatic than what it actually is. Have uploaded pictures of the falls from the top (from the platform adjacent to the ticketing office and entry barriers) and from the bridge over the stream just before it tumbles down. Would give you some idea of the size.But having said all of that, this a pleasant enough area. Pay Won 2000 for entry (entry hours 8am - 6pm/7pm, depending on summer/winter) and leisurely climb down about 60 odd feet i.e. equivalent of climbing down about 6 stories. You will arrive at a rocky area. Clambering over about 1/5th mile (300 odd mts) of large rocks to where the water falls, isn't for the aged like me! But it would be nice to get to the water's edge if you can.Not a bad idea to carry sandwiches and beer and sit on the rocks, moments of peace and quiet, isolated from bustling Segwipo all around.You wouldn't miss anything if you haven't been here. But it would be a shame to miss it if you are on Jeju.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. There's also an outdoor gardens with bear exhibits, fountain and lake and a blooming grapefruit tree. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. Get your tickets cheaper via taobao, the China online shopping site. They have almost 50% discount for foreigners, which we tapped on. Just need to print our confirmation and entry was a breeze. Also, this place is accessible via a bus from Jeju intercity bus terminal. Stop at jungmun resort. Nearby are alive musuem, yeomiji botanical gardens and cheonjiyeon waterfalls, good for a self planned one day trip.

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I went here on Friday 31.05.2019. The front desk staff were very helpful, the museum is really easy as there's arrows on the floor directing you where to go. There is loads of information in English, it's easy to follow and very informative. The island has some really sad history, for anyone interested in history, and the impact of splitting Korea, this is a must do. The information does not make easy reading, but you will never forget this story, and it's an important one to remember. The gardens have lots of memorials, and outside is a nice space.It's not a pop in memorial/museum, it's bigger than expected. I'd recommend 2.5 hours to do the museum and outside. Unfortunately I had to rush as I got there late in the day and wish I'd had more time, but I'm pleased I went, and got most stuff done. It's accessible by bus. The museum closes at 6, last entry 5, but I'd suggest you get there no later than 3.30pm to do it properly.For clarity, this is the 4.3 peace park on the east side of the island, as there is one on the west side with a similar name, I've no idea what that one is like.

I was thinking about Seongsan Ilchulbong, dreaming about it, visualizing  the moments & details of  the day, and just rushed to the legendary place sponteneously. Moved from Jeju Bus Terminal totally on my own. An hour & a half  and you are there! Enjoy:-)

I was on exchange with a couple of friends in Busan, Korea. We decided to head to Jeju for some exploration trip. The teddy bear museum is an awesome place to visit if you are a teddy bear fan! They have different themes of teddy bear at different areas! :)

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I stayed 4 night in Hamdeok Beach. If you are visiting Jeju for the very first time, you might want to move around because Jeju is quite big. Hamdeok is a great location to start your trip. It takes 20 mins by car, 30~40 mins by bus from Jeju International airport. It has many bus lines which offers you easy access to Airprot, Mountain Halla, Jeju city centre and even Seogwipo. I love the beach itself, but also there are lots of place to eat and chill. If you like to camp, there is a camping & caravan park at the end of beach. I loved it !!

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for   you silly tourist   sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. You can get here from Jeju bus terminal using the 701 bus (3,000 KRW). There is a stop for it about 40 mins in. It's near Manjangul cave (6,000 KRW taxi) so worth combining it with a trip with that.

I have spend a week on Jeju Island in September, and of my Highlights was Udo. I had time only for a day trip, and if I ever make it back to Jeju, my priority will be to spend at least one night there. Its such a lovely, small and relaxed place. From Seongsan its only 15 minutes to Udo by Ferry. There, you can take the local bus that runs along the island, you can rent small tuk-tuks / quad bikes / scooters or bicycles, you can join a tour (I think only in Korean) or you can walk (like I did, but then of course you dont get to cover the whole island).

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I happened to notice a separate entrance desk that had pictures of SCUBA divers on it. I asked an attendant nearby in simple English sentences if they had any SCUBA diving and how much was it? It was only 119000 KWon and they happened to have availability right away! I've dove in other aquariums but this was the cheapest and didn't even require a reservation on a busy day! Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids. They loved it!I still had to pay the separate entrance fee for the aquarium (about $40 but I received a 20% off coupon at the airport) but it was worth it. The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Would definitely go back.Note: A lot of the aquarium features the image of a whale shark. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: I got the bus here from Jungmun - a couple of hours in total but it was worth it. Really good value, lots to look at, peaceful place to walk around, beautifully done and looked after. There weren't many other people there so it felt as if I had the place to myself. I had lunch in the restaurant and that was also good. Make sure you take your camera. Hugely recommended.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

How silly is a museum of stuffed bears, if you don쨈t have kids or never had a Teddy bear?  We opted to forgo this museum for the Cheonjeyeon Falls which are amazing but when we got back on the tour bus, every person uniformly said they liked the Museum.So we went back another day and were mesmerized by the display of teddy bears dating from the 30쨈s and the overall cleverness and charm of the bears.  It finally got to me at the end when I could appreciate the bears in famous paintings like Laguna Beach쨈s Pageant of the Masters event with bears!A unique concept for a museum.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

From Jeju City Local Bus Terminal, take bus #701, stop at Seongsan Port. It takes 90mins, 3300won.Fill up the boarding form for the ferry, before you proceed to buy the ferry ticket at the counter. Round trip charges 5500won, which takes 10mins per trip. Expect a lot of visitors during weekends or public holidays.At Udo, there are shops offer rental of bicycles, ATV, automatic scooter, etc. which can accommodate every one either youths, elders or children.You could enjoy cycling around the island the best during a windy chilling day.When I think of Udo, I will remember the kindness of restaurant owner of щ 대Ъ珥. When I was eating, I accidentally hit my dental braces with the spoon, and I was rubbing to ensure it was alright. The ajumma approached me and asked me what happened, I showed her my braces, and she was quick-witted to get scissor to cut banchan into smaller pieces, while cutting, she repeatedly saying   ottoke ottoke  .. I was really grateful to her, and I enjoyed the lunch well.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

For the adventurous and those seeking a different experience. This place is located quite out of the way, however close enough to Halla arboretum as well. Quite challenging to find as Naver and googlemaps does not have this location up to date. If you are looking to find it, look for a bus that will take you to Halla arboretum stop and you could find it by following the street direction towards the arboretum. When you see a building with   playbox  , you've found it!There's an ice sculpture display area with an ice slide you can experience. Next level on is your VR experience that you could choose to experience (cost of entry varies depending on what experiences you would like to add on).As reference we chose the Basic A experience which provides us entry into the ice sculpture, Trick art area, 5D movie experience and 1 VR experience of our choice - cost 22000krw per person.You could spend at least an hour here and rest at the cafeteria before moving on.

First some people said it is   Mystic   supranatural thing but actually it's only a trick eyes illusions that twisted out logical thinking. The road looks like going uphill and makes the car or bus like climbing moving forward againts the gravity. When we saw from the end of the road, yes the road is going downhill not the opposite around. Well, still it's amazing thing to experience!

Easy to get to, a small entry fee, then a short walk down, out and around a spectacular and unique geological area that is set on the edge of the island. Very picturesque and a great spot for photos, but it can get very busy depending on the time of the day. Worth a visit and a wander - places for picnics - however if the day is wet, an hour or two will be enough time.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.

review: Disclaimer: Everyone has their own tastes, and just because I may not like something, it doesn't mean you won't like it. And even though I might be dismissive and even sarcastic about this attraction, I am not attempting to insult anyone who thought that Jeju's   Mysterious Road   was fun. The fact is, this road would be amazing IF it wasn't swarming with tourists and IF you just happened to find it one day when you were driving around on the stunning back roads of Jeju. Jeju has Korea's best scenic driving, hands down. But this...Here's the deal. Yes, your brain will lie to you about the incline of this road and it will appear as if you are not rolling downhill, which you are. And that's a fun fact about human neurology and perception. My brain also tried to lie to me in order to convince me that the illusion was worth the large, obnoxious crowds of people that clogged the road, the busloads of hyperactive tourists on a conveyor belt from the airport, and the shops set up on either side of the road in order to overcharge them for very average products. Basically, it's a tourist trap. Sure, it has its appeal, but of all the things you could do on Jeju, why would you spend your time doing this?

Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

Cars and buses usually demonstrate this seemingly mysterious trick. They have their engines turned off at the beginning of the road stretch (there's an indicated sign). And while the engines are off, it seemingly feels and looks like there's this   mysterious force   pulling the vehicles towards the end of the road. Civilians also use a water bottle and place it on the road surface. Mimicking the vehicles, it too would roll towards the end of the road. Just like the saying goes, looks can be deceiving. Optical illusion is what it is.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Beautiful location. Relatively easy to get to (just one change from Jeju City Bus Terminal). The park is beautiful and I'd really recommend taking your time and enjoying the scenery as much as possible. The park contains different areas (bonsai, water gardens, caves, animals, cactus) and it's so hard to believe that it's man-made. Loved the diversity here.

Basically nothing much here. The road seemed to be uphill and when the engine of the vehicle is switched off, it will   roll uphill  . However, it is a natural optical illusion, and the road is actually downhill. Spend not more than 15mins here if you drive as the road is just about 50 metres. Also, the   rolling down   phenomenon only works on large vehicles like buses or truck. Small saloon cars will not encounter the   rolling uphill   effect.

As I rented a car to explore Jeju (highly recommended), we came here a couple of times to enjoy the experience putting the gear at N position and realizing how the car went up the hill.We also tried on the road with a can of beer that also was rolling hill up apparently. It is maybe an optical illusion but when you are there it looks clearly and without any doubt that cars and things go up the road. The kids were amazed and really enjoyed as we also did.Try to avoid the afternoons, as most of the guided tours are here at that time with many buses horning in hurry to repeat the experience several times and many pedestrians around. In the morning the day after it was almost empty !

As a part of our school's field trip program, we went to the one of the known attraction in Jeju-do which is the Jeju mysterious road. While inside of the bus, our tour guide asked the driver to turn the engine off. Our tour guide pointed out that even though the engine is turned off, the bus still continues to move   way up  . But in reality, our bus moved downwards. It was like an optical illusion. For me, this attraction is not that amazing, just a normal road. On a positive note, if you have a lot of time to spend in the island, give it a try and experience the illusion.

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Although it takes about an hour by bus from Seogwipo hiking up this volcanic peak was one of the highlights of our trip to Jeju.  The hike only takes about an hour round trip, if you go at 1pm or 3 pm they have a women diver's show.  Cost about 2,000 won each and there's many food vendors at the entrance of the park.

Against the warnings we ended up in this village after visiting the Kim Younggap Gallery (highly recommended) and getting bored of waiting for the right bus. This   village   is not much more than some normal village with a few thatched roofs, interiors setup purely for presenting products. We sneaked in and out after a few snaps (luckily it was only 2 of us) only to have a woman literally running after us with a small 25000 krw box of blueberry pills. Avoid it, especially with a group or day trip!

After visiting the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, we proceeded to head to the ferry terminal for Udo Island. We were surprised we couldn?t get a cab during winter. Hence, we ended up walking to the ferry terminal instead.Note you need to show your passport and fill up a boarding form in order to take the ferry, at 30 mins interval. We took the 1400hr ferry. A 2-way ferry ticket costs 8,500 won. Upon arriving the island, one has the option of renting an electric scooter, manual bicycle or take the bus. For us, we took the round island bus. Bus fare is 5,00 won, which you can hop in and out at any attraction stops.  We headed to Udo-bond Peak stop and hiked up. Unfortunately, it was drizzling the whole day. We spent about an hour before returning to the ferry terminal.I suggest you allocate an entire day for Udo island. If the weather is fine, it is worthwhile to stop by all the attractions, enjoy the beach and food there.

A nice stop on the yeha bus tour, a lot of tourists so it easily gets overcrowded as the observation platform is small. Nice walk nearby with a small park next to the ocean. Pentagonal and heptagonal rock formations from lava cooling down. Enjoyed it and do recommend if in the area!

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

We stopped by this place mainly to try tea but ended up buying so many gifts for our friends and families. Tea cosmetics and other souvenirs are pretty good here. Don't forget to check out the tea farm on the opposite site.

We stopped by this museum at the end of a long day because my daughter  who loves science  was begging us to go. We were all pleasantly surprised. There were quite a few hands on displays like static balls  using bikes to light up a display  a few trick eye displays  plasma globes  and of course Tesla coils. The staff were incredibly friendly and although they didn't speak much English they went out of their way to show us around. The Tesla coil music show was quite cool - the coils were used to create different pitches and played both classical and modern music. It took about an hour to go through everything and cost ??0000 for 2 adults and 2 kids. My kids loved it! Great hands on science.

We paid our entrance fees and simply stayed on the top to get some good pictures. There were hordes of people down below so I don't recommend taking a long walk down and then back up just to get some pictures of other tourists.

We drove along mountainous route 1139 from SEOQWIPO to this place before heading to the airport.  We drove very slowly from the start to finish point and didn't feel the illusion effect.  Some said to see the effect one needs to roll a bottle on the road. I dunno.. i just drove on without stopping. I would however recommend those who drive to drive along route 1139 skirting the mountain and reaching the 1000m height.

We are glad that we have our wonderful tour guide was with us thus we were able to gain better understanding n knowledge about the green tea n it's plantation.The museum itself actually showcase the different type of green tea products (including facial products) so it's a shopping paradise for some.  There are free sampling of the green tea however we like the cafe most. Though a little pricey but the green tea yogurt ice cream n also the green tea milk ice cream is yummy (it has strong green tea taste).As it was crowded when we were there the cafe seemed to be under stocked for the crowd.  A friend managed to get herself green tea macaron n said it taste superb.A good stop over for some retail therapy n tea break n photo taking.
This place is very popular in Jeju for climbing mountain and see natural beauty from the top. Highly recommended.

This large market is located on the East side of the island. You'll find a variety of places to eats  souvenirs  fresh produces  meats  seafood and variety of other things. It's where the locals to their shopping  as the super markets are small  so it's one stop shopping. After taking a tour on that side of the island  its worth a visit to grab some fresh items if you're tired of eating out all the times  just make sure to bargain with the stall vendors.

This is our last stop for the day trip so we can't spend too much time at there. There are totally 3 mazes and we went through 2 big mazes and last one without knowing it. Is fun if go with a group of friends. Abit boring for the elderly people.

This is only a nice experience if it is not crowded. With us entered a family if four and they easily blocked 2-3 displays. The start of the tour is great. A lot of great photo opportunities. They gibe you examples and show how to pose. But suddenly this stops in the middle and you end up in a huge room with Aladdin Indiana Jones a volcano eruption? We had no clue what to do there.At the end there is a bug parking lot outside with even more displays. So if you are into instagram and pictures - this is yours. If not... well it is entertaining though. Unless there are tons of visitors.

This is an unusual three story Buddhist temple which is quite beautiful. It is a bit of a drive from Jeju City so we hired a private taxi tour and this was one of five stops in our day. It definitely is recommended.

There is a long steep path in order to reach the lighthouse on top. But that shouldn't be a problem as the scenery along the road is empowering your feet to work. In the middle of the path  there is a candy house like building. But unfortunately  it was reconstructing at that moment. So  I bought a chocolate ice cream beside the reconstruction to settle my unhappiness. The ice cream tastes unexpectedly good  it is rich in chocolate and smooth when I put it into my mouth. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the lighthouse  we took several pictures there  but no one is perfectly taken because of strong wind  our hair flowing like crazy  so we didn't spend much time on the lighthouse.We took about 30 minutes there and didn't have a chance to visit the building at that time  so I strongly recommend you to go there at autumn or spring and plan more than half an hour if you are deciding to visit there.

There are lockers for you to keep your bags in. You have to change and shower in the gender-designated shower areas before you put your spa outfits (shorts and a shirt) on and head to the sauna area (where both men and women are). Try the steam and sauna rooms for a good sweat (you can bring your phones in if you want to listen to music). Be prepared for crowds of tourist though as this seems to be a popular stop for large tour groups.

The temple is very impressive and is worth stopping at for an hour if you're passing the general area - that said I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to visit.No charge for entrance but a donation box on entry/exit.

The scenery is absolutely stunning at the top. We brought our 4-years old kid along and we were initially worried if the hike is too tiring for him. We were so wrong! He loves the hike and has lots of fun along the way. Just make sure that you have sufficient time to finish the hike before it closes. Would strongly recommend this place for families even with young children!

The Museum caffe offers very delicious tea and I recommend the very fragrance green tea latte and creamy Osulloc milk tea. There are other types of tea offer too such as red papaya milk tea. The tea must go with the green tea cake roll and green tea ice cream or green tea O fredo. The cake roll is soft and like the green tea ice cream it's just melt in your mouth with great green tea taste and scents . All the food is not too sweet. On top of this the free wet tissues that offer in the cafe provides extra cooling effect probably it has added some green tea extract just the company cosmetic brand  Innisfree green tea mask.

The green tea plantation of O'sulloc was my last stop prior to my flight for Seoul. My recommendation is to try the O'Sulloc green tea ice cream. There were also other green tea based products displayed like soap and beauty products. As for me I enjoyed my green tea ice cream under the flowering Cherry Blossom tree.

The cause of forming a wonderful Island is a Volcano and hiking to the top of it is a wonderful experience. Roads up to the height of 1100 mtrs are made cautiously and traveler friendly for pleasure with least possibility of an accident. The hiking experience is also beyond the expression in words. I can only say that visiting JEJU and Hallim park are synonyms.

Stop by Alive museum on the way to visit other places spend an hour inside the optical illusion museum and play kart outside.  Karing part is fun with the two seater. (Kids can sit next to parent) and it is 4 times faster than the ones in Disney.

So we did minimum research on this thinking that the trip up would be somewhat difficult but we were way off that. We made it to the top but we had to push through it. Highly recommend bringing lots of water and snacks.

Our first time in Shinhwa World theme park visit in December 2017. One must come with the understanding that the theme park is not yet fully developed but it has some nice rides and you can spend a few hours there . My kids had a wonderful time . Since it is new  the park is not crowded. We had lunch at the food court and it was good Korean food . We were initially disappointed when the rides were suspended due to the snow. However the rides were resumed quickly after the snow stopped. We happened to have met the theme park Manager Mr Mason Kang when we ran into communication difficulty with one of the staff attending to the ride . He was very kind to explain to us that the rides would resume soon after they dry the area . His professionalism impressed us .  Our theme park experience was a great one . My kids tried the ice skating ring within the theme park compound . Everything is new and clean . We will come again ! They are going to have a Water theme park probably year after .

Osulloc is famous for their teas. They have a green tea field right outside the museum/cafe. Recommended things to try are their green tea ice cream green tea cake and green tea latte! Great location for picture taking in the green tea field; Bring a wide angle lens! right next door is the innisfree jeju house. Estimated time spent at osculloc is 30-45 minutes tops.

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.

Nothing really fancy here unless you?셱e really passionate about tea. Great stop for some photos and perhaps buy some tea souvenirs for your family and friends. Souvenirs can be pretty pricey; approximately $10 for a bottle of spread.

lots of little homes and friendly villagers. They are very traditional. It is probably one of the quietest tourist attractions i've ever been to. I don't really think it's a necessary place to visit but if you are in the area it might be nice to stop by quickly.

It was winter when we came so most of the trees at the entrance were naked. But people were doing their warm ups for the climb to the crater with the lake. It's the highest peak in Korea so it takes about 4 hours to get to the top. It was advised to bring a packed lunch. I recommend climbing during the spring though. More trees and flowers to look at during the climb. The park is a UNESCO heritage site so it is definitely well maintained. They also have a building that shows the different eco systems that can be found in the park. Not only is it for the physically inclined people but the smart minds as well.

It was so close to being excellent reason I did not rate it as excellent is because the 3D movie was closed due to covid so obviously could not comment on that. Only other thing to add was the animal enclosure at the top of the park was rather smelly and did need a good clean out however the parrot/parakeet aviary section was amazing and very clean. The park is excellent value and you could spend the whole day here with the kids providing that you bring a packed lunch.

It was fun to walk thru but for the food products  much of the time I had no idea what anything was. I especially liked the fresh fish vendors with the live fish  octopi  and shellfish in the tanks. Quite a lot of fresh produce and clothing for sale as well. If you haven't been to a Korean market  it's fun to spend maybe 1/2 hour going thru.

It was at the end of a residential alley and its huge!. When i saw it i never thought how big it was until we parked and look at it from the front. The temple is huge! Since they were preparing for the spring festival there were colorful paper lanterns all over. The golden buddas were amazing too! I really recomend stoping by at this temple. It is worth it.

It very beauty place in the jejudo. If you go up the top of mountain where you can see all of the jeju do and can see the sunrise. But if you have many times the best recomended for you should go out and biking or trecking around the beach streets. It so better than by car...

It takes entrance fee to enter the museum  but that's okay as there are three venues in total. With lots of different appearances bears  such as dressing up like students and wedding. The most memorial teddy bear is the president Obama  it is similar to the real Obama but in bear form. The top floor of the second venue is about wedding and relationships between lovers  so it is a great place for lovers to take pictures and have memories with the teddy bear couples. Although I am not a teddy bear fan  I took lots of photos in that first two venues. And in the third venue  bears are for sell  so please remember not to photo bears in the third venue as it is subjected to copy right. Finally  my father bought me a bear which I think is the cutest as a present of graduation. It takes about 40k-80k unequally per bear  but I think it is valuable as all bears are made in Jeju.So  if you think you don't have any way to spend your money  you can go to this teddy bear museum and buy your favorite bear as an emblem of stepping on Jeju.
It is a park like Topu in Japan and world park in China. But comparing to others the models of world famous buildings statues are very small. The park is small too. Not so much recommend this place.

Innisfree is a Korean cosmetics brand known for its natural ingredients sourced directly from Jeju in Korea...think of it as a Korean Body Shop. The Innisfree House in Jeju is a combined shop and cafe located inside the Osulloc Green Tea Museum complex. You can buy products and make your own soaps as well as sit and chill with some Korean and Western fusion drinks and cafe style food. Good stop for lunch or afternoon tea and to pick up souvenirs. Recommend spending only 1 hour (combined with the green tea plantation photo op)

If you've never been to one of these grab a camera and have a good time.  We had a couple of hours to spend so we thought we'd stop by not knowing what it was.  We were surprised at the good time we had. We took lots of great corny pictures and were entertained. These will make for some fun memories.  Definitely worth the stop.

If you like green tea I strongly recommend stopping by here... Their tea is really good... BEWARE... they are really expensive. Also for sampling one scoop of green tea ice cream - approx $8; one slice of green tea pastry - approx $9... one small bag of lower grade green tea - approx $25.
I was convinced by my friend to climb and see the unesco world heritage. I was disappointed to see nothing on top. it was so tiring a climb only to see a bare area. Really nothing on top.

I strolled into the stadium primarily for my interest in sports. Unfortunately  during my stay on Jeju Island there were no games scheduled. The stadium is rather impressive and I would love to attend a major soccer game here.For any sports fan  stop by the stadium at the very least (15 minutes is sufficient). I rented a car near from the airport so this is the best way to get the chills up your back in this place. Dive up here. Leave your gear in NWhen you were clearly moving forward in a downhill.... Your car just slows... Stops then moves backwards!!!! What the hill????? LolI did it like 5 time still fled funny in a very great way. I recommend visiting this place just for the heck of it!

I recommend riding the bicycle if the weather permits to enjoy the island fully! It took me about  about 3-4 hours (with picture stops) to complete the whole island and it was a very enjoyable and easy ride.

I have seen all the a lot of Aquariums in Asia and America. Comparatively this is not big as that with big shows but it makes use of its space and is a natural stop over from Seongsan sunrise peak. 10 minutes away. There are amphibians like exotic frogs iguana and Lizzard from all over the world Penguins and Pelikans Walrus seals and sealion. You can also sea them during feeding time.There is also a big aquarium with fishes sharps and stingrays. What I liked most were the small aquariums with exotic fish variety. It did not have whale shark which require big space and are usually in the wild. This I have seen in the open sea while swimming near it. Overall the place is cool although smaller by comparison but spacious inside. It is recommended because it is part of the it is on the way to or from Seongsan and educational especially for children.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: I and my wife went to this beach as this beach was the first pitstop for west package in Yeha Tour. The place was very cold since we visited during winter season. But the scenery was very beautiful and lovely. Seriously recommended for the honeymoon lovers.

Here was held the biggest event of the 2002 Korean and Japan Football World cup. The stadium blends in well with its surroundings  reminiscent of a small volcano in shape. The 6 pillars inside the ground represent the 6 continents.In rooms around the stadium  you can see memorabilia from the 2002 World Cup.Certainly worth a stop even if you're not a football fan.

Having arrived in Jeju eager to see as much as possible in a short time frame - the art work was top on my hit list. I stumbled across the website for the Museum of Contemporary Art and was very excited to go (as there are so many museums to choose from!)I would recommend a whole morning to visit Jeoji as there is more than just this Museum there. The first Gallery I went to showed a lovely exhibiton on the Sound of Nature this gallery was on the left hand side of the road and was a free two floor exhibition. I then walked along the road to the Museum of Contemporary Art on the right. The Museum had 4 big rooms of Art - all of which had a meaningful message behind the artist's work in both Korean and English! The receptionists were very helpful when directing me as to where to go and I finished my self-guided tour with a visit to the Art shop which was outside in the sculpture garden. A lovely morning well spent taking in the delights of Korean art.
Had so much fun biking around Jeju and stopping by this lovely beach. I highly recommend going there for half a day.
Great service from Mr Kang. He even has help us take photo at every stop. Will definitely recommend him to friends
Great fish and oranges.... on weekends there is a lively food court . Clean and . We like markets so we think it?s a good stop in Jeju colorful

Another UNESCO World Heritage you should visit!This place is a peak form from previous volcanic eruption!I was allocated about 1 hour by the driver to went up all the way to the top hill and come down. Feel little bit rush. This place definitely should spend about 2-3 hours to enjoy the natural scenery in this place!

A mountain with beautiful scenery. I did not manage to climb all the way up to the top as I was having knee problem but my friend did. It was really beautiful even when I was only half way up the mountain. I also enjoyed the nice cooling breeze that made me want to stay longer if possible. Worth the visit. Probably will visit this mountain and climb up again next time.

A good short stop to see a waterfall. There is a few steep steps so not recommended if u are bring a baby or toddler. The waterfall is not extremely fanciful though.  There are some old ladies trying to sell the usual seafood.

Yep, there are a lot of stairs here. It honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting it to be, seeing as how stairs are my natural enemy. You will probably be tired when you get to the top, but little kids and elderly people are doing it, so it's not crazy. It's over a lot faster than it feels like it's going to be as you're ascending. We were there in the late afternoon, and it was a little crowded, but not too much trouble. Most people move along at a pretty good pace and don't stand in the way too much when taking pictures. It's a bit more difficult to get good pictures at the top though, because everyone stops up there to rest and take tons of photos. It's worth the climb and you'll get some good pictures out of it if the weather permits. Even if you think you are unable to go up to the top, it's worth coming out here just for the landscape.

Went to Hallim Park on the end of September 2015, its a good thing we came at Autumn because the weather was not hot and not too cold either. The leaves were turning orange - just like in the movies. There are several flower parks in the Hallim park, such as flowers park; cactus park; bonsai park; stone cave; bird park; and folk village - where we can stop by for lunch. This place is suitable for families travelling with old ones, since the scenery is beautiful for photo-shoots.

Went there just because our driver recommended us to make a stop there (at first we only wanted to go to Hyeopjae Beach) but now we thought Sehwa Beach was a lot nicer and less crowded than the Hyeopjae Beach. The calm sea, the soft sands all to yourself! They also have one and two spot set up, specially to take picture, and it IS a very instagrammable spot indeed haha

Went in August, so it was really hot outside. Was so pleased to be welcomed by the cool temperature of the cave. It will take you about 2 hours to go in and back out with some stops to take pictures. Recommend everyone to wear proper shoes as the cave surface is really uneven since it used to be flowing lava coupled with low visibility of the cave. The floor is also wet, so advice to wear something non slippery. I wore normal slippers and i got my feet wet and dirty, no worries though, there's a place near the toilet specifically to clean you feet outside the cave.I saw some locals even wearing heels inside, not recommended, but i guess it's possible to come out unharmed.

We, a group of friends had visited this place last week. It was awesome! The journey to get there, parking and the walk up and back were all good. There is ample parking space and plenty of eateries that offers various types of snacks and cold drinks.The area is impeccably clean and the walking path was clear and safe. The steps may seem a little steep at certain points, but you will be well rewarded once you reach the top. The crater is a beautiful sight! Not surprising that it's the iconic image of Jeju which appears on Google. You need about an hour or so for the entire visit.

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

We went to the market wanted to try some fresh octopus. We bought an octopus from a stall and the nice lady told us in broken English that we can have it prepared at the nearby restaurant. So we went into that restaurant just opposite the seafood stall. None of them can't speak English, even a little bit. So went back to the seafood stall and asked the nice lady to help us. So we seated in the restaurant waiting just for our octopus to be prepared. Then they bring out the cutlery.. we were quite puzzled... why does one octopus need so many cutlery.. then they took out the big steamboat with all the seafood in it! We keep using sign language to say show we don't want the steamboat and just want our octopus prepare... after a while we gave in. and our octopus came out serve in a plate, fully chopped into tiny bits like being blended in a food processor :(we have had enough seafood steamboat over the past few days in Jeju and this is not the time we want to eat the steamboat again. oh well, all because of language barrier and luckily we still have enough cash to pay for the meal as they don't accept credit card.Besides the story, local products sell in this market are quite interesting.

We visited this site with a group of friends.Everybody had their own take on the mysterious road and all had their theories. A quick visit to the internet would provide the answer. However, this all detracts from the pure fun of the site itself. However, part of the fun is discussing the   mystery   of the road.The site is a simple narrow two-lane road. It is not huge. There is plenty of parking for visitors to stop and examine the surroundings.  There are snack stalls along the road where refreshments and some simple snacks can be bought. I noticed some posts on TA that say this is a   tourist trap  . I do not see how this would be the case as nobody is forced to buy or pay for anything.  Anything we bought was food, which, to me, does not seem to be predatory on tourists. In fact, I was hungry and thirsty and was happy to purchase some cooked local yams and cool refreshment. There are tourist traps on the island, but this is not one of them.Having said the above, the attraction is not a major development and is not meant to be a huge event to take up one's itinerary. It is a fun and simple site to visit which can be added to the list of places to visit when in Jeju.

We visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on two separate days - the first was in the afternoon to see the women free-divers' performance (1pm/3pm) and the second was in the wee hours of the morning (5+am) to see the sunrise. The free-divers were all middle-aged women who looked old enough to be our mothers. Despite their age, it was amazing how they managed to hold their breath so long underwater to harvest the seafood which you could buy from them and eat on the spot (they'll prepare/cook it in whichever way you want). The way they sang prior to the dive and the way they chatted and swam out to sea together reminded us of the friendly grannies in our neighborhood enjoying a nice chit-chat over tea. To see the sunrise at the peak, we started our climb at 4+am (it helps to stay in a hotel within walking distance to Ilchulbong). It was pitch-dark and torchlight was a must. The climb was shorter than expected and we reached the top before 5am. Thankfully the sky was clear that morning and we managed to catch a beautiful sunrise (around 5:30am) that was nothing short of amazing.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We took the ferry at around 9:30am. 15 min rides and we are there.
