Since we did not have our international driving license, we can only rent the electric tandem bicycle which was great for the kids.Cycling around the island is around 12km. Just go with the flow and stop at leisure for peanut ice cream.Must stop plave for lunch is ha ha Ho Ho Cafe famed for the burger. The best burger we ever had.We ended our bicycle trip at around 2pm and managed to catch the 2:30pm ferry back.

We thoroughly enjoyed our day on Udo. We hired manual bikes and stopped at the little beached and cafes along the way. It was cold and really windy so I think it was quite quiet in terms of people compared to a normal day which is why I think we enjoyed it so much. The bigger beaches (especially the black sand beach at the end) are a terrible example of sympathetic tourism and are blights against the beautiful natural landscape. Blaring music, ugly buildings and structures detract from the stunning island itself. We chose to eat at a cute little cafe which had character and that was away from the others.

We stopped off here after lunch and easily spent 3 hours walking the grounds.  And that was at a fairly quick pace.  The garden has 8 separate sections that provide a contrast.  The garden is very well kept.  So if you are into shrubbery, its not a bad place to spend a few hours

We love this place!!! It is so so so so so so so beautiful! Travelled with my hubby and 2 kids and took the earliest ferry to Udo. The ferry we took is those that doesnt come with seats and we have to sit on the floor like the Koreans do. Rented 2 scooters and rode the around the entire island for 2 hours with our kids sitting behind us. It is really safe to ride but you need to make sure you have your international driver license with you before you can rent a scooter. My hubby doesnt know how to ride a scooter, but no worries, simple instructions and quick lessons were given and within 10 mins we were off to our adventure. Though it was winter when we visited, the wind did not stop us from visiting every checkpoint to take photo and of coz, eating the famous peanut icecream. I really felt like I had jumped into a K-drama, especially when I have my Oppa with me, haahaa! It was quite cold so we din manage to get into the water. But already we had spent like 4 hours just wondering around the island. The fun part was to get lost into some residents farms and got directed to get onto the right path. The sceneries are breathtaking! I cant describe better. Really beautiful. Definitely highly recommended, even for people with young kids!

We just stop in here taking picture. No many people visited there when i was going there maybe because it was raining.I went there by taxi,we rent taxi for two days and the taxi driver recommend us to visit this beach when i said i wanted to go to the beach

We hiked up Hallasan the first weekend in March 2012.  We brought coats, hats, gloves and scarfs, however we were not prepared for the amount of snow on the mountain.  Check the conditions ahead of time and be sure to bring walking sticks and spikes for your boots.  My family hiked for awhile but stopped about 1km from the top after we were in more than two feet of snow and freezing.

We had lunch at this restaurant as it came highly recommended and we had heard that it was on the Michelin list of restaurants of 2011. We got there just as it opened which was a good thing as it filled out quite quickly. We later found out that reservations are highly recommended if you plan to go there for dinner. We got the mixed set for 2 and it was a lot of food for the price. The pork was very good, obviously very fresh. The side dishes were also top-notch. Service was quick and efficient and very friendly. It was a little hard to find as a number of streets around the area were being repaired when we were there but it was totally worth it.

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

We drove to Udo Island by taking the ferry from Seongsanpo Port.  We had to pay ferry charges for the car and the number of persons going to the island. We spent about  6 to 7 hours on the island. While we drove around the island, my daughter & friend rented each a bike when we reached Udo.  Scenery and the beaches in Udo Island are not as nice as in Jeju itself.  The fun parts were riding the e-scooter or bike around the small island, stopping by for the famous peanut ice cream and hiking the udobong peak.

We drove our rented car onto the ferry which took us to Udo in 15 minutes. If the weather hadnt been so cold, we would have tried the fun looking electric scooters. We stumbled into a seafood restaurant to the left of the ferry terminal and enjoyed a sumptuous seafood kimchi hotpot. Ordering was not a problem as the service staff spoke mandarin. The place was an obvious favourite with locals. We spent 4 hours exploring various sites and even got lost. A friendly local policeman kindly pointed us the right way. We stopped by quaint coffeeshops and hugged their cute puppies. We were reluctant to leave this idyllic tiny island.

Visited 4 times during my one year assignment in Jeju. Udo Island is very beautiful and peaceful. Rent a bike to tour around the island will definitely bring you fresh air and excitement. Stopped by at any cafe to try their peanut ice cream from udo! Really nice! I give average for their hallasan fried rice, it?s good to try but the taste is just normal. Udo has a very nice beaches around and good for photo:) recommend to go when you visit jeju.

Udo was the best part of my Jeju visit. My sister and I rented scooters for two hours to get around the island, stopping wherever we wanted to take pictures or rehydrate (it was blazingly hot). We stopped at one of the beaches for a couple of hours, but it was just too hot to sit still on the sand. Rented scooters for the rest of the day and just zoomed around the island. True, there isn't too much to do on the island besides going to the beach or riding around the island. And the scooters/ATVs available for rent are a bit expensive (15,000won for 2 hours). But if you're looking for a relaxing day with beautiful sights, I highly recommend a visit.

Udo is gorgeous and so relaxing. You can just rent a bike, they also have electric bikes and they are so easy and comfortable to ride. And on your own pace, go around the whole island in 2 to 3 hours, taking pictures, stopping by to enjoy beautoful scenary. I loved spending half a day, where you can enjoy natural beauty and simple life without big buildings, traffic or noise. Just a short ferry ride from the port in east jeju.

Udo is an amazing place We took our car in the ferry ... Costs only 22000 KRW for return trip plus 6000 KRW for each person. We stopped at so many places and took pictures every where. You could also rent a scooter or electric car, but it you have a car, I would recommend taking your own car esp if you are a group unless you like to enjoy on bike. But be ready to face high wind.Though people recommend a few hours only, this place is worth full day spend.

Though am not craving for Teddy Bear, still find it ok to stop by if you have time.  You may know the history of teddy bear via this museum.  Only too bad, we can't find Mr. Bean best friend, Teddy in it.  However, you will find Elvis Presley, The Beatles & many others.

This would just take you 5 minutes of your time. Get out of the taxi and snap some pictures. No, it did not look like a dragon's head to me no matter how I pictured it. But oh well, I have been told I could do with more imagination. One of those things that you do to strike off another   to-go   in your itinerary. If you are keen, walk down the stairs - you will see vendors selling fresh octopus sashimi - worth a try!

This was the last stop on our vacation. Unfortunately it was also the only grey/cloudy/cold day. The island was still a must see for us. The ferry ticketing area can be very confusing, so be prepared if you don't know any Korean. We figured it out after about 5 minutes of standing around, staring in confusion. Once we reached the island, we rented an electric car (from Gulliver's Travels) with side-by-side seating for 占35,000 for 2.5 hours and cruised around the island following the path. The beaches were incredible. White sand, crystal clear water at the shore, turning into turquoise water a little farther out. Even with the grey sky, it still looked amazing. We didn't climb out to the lighthouse (if you climb to the top of Hallasan on your visit, you'll understand why. Ow.) but we got some great photos of it. Peanut ice cream is way overrated in my opinion, but it was still a must since we were on Udo! My husband got the hallabong ice cream. We liked that one more, but the stuff they put on it tastes like mashed up hallabong peel, so it was bitter and we just scraped it off. There is a restaurant that serves (I forget the name, I am guessing) Hallasan fried rice. They make it look like a volcano! We really wanted to go, but needed to catch the ferry back. Overall, if it had been warmer and the we could actually see the sun, it would have been much more enjoyable. We talk about going back and spending a night on the island so we have the time to walk around it, instead of having to drive/rent a bike.

This was the last stop of our tour so the sun was setting by the time we got there. I recommend coming in the morning for good pictures. It was quite solemn, cold, and eerie because it was just the tour guide of the village, our tour guide, and the rest of our group in the area. The assigned tour guide had very interesting insights on the place and the rest of Jeju culture. She also sold us some products that the folks of the village made. The berry honey is definitely worth buying.

This was recommended by a friend and it ended up being the highlight of our trip in Jeju! We rented an ATV and just drove around the island taking in the sights. Udo Island is also where the famous women divers go to catch abalone, octopi and other seafood and it was cool just to watch them work. The shore caves were definitely a must-see for us and they did not disappoint. I would definitely go back to Udo if I'm ever in Jeju again.

This was our first stop during our weekend trip to Jeju. I had heard about these women before but didn't know much. First, they showed us a video (in English) all about the history. I was immediately hooked! The rest of the museum is so interesting. The pictures and artifacts tell a great story. I just wish I could have met the Haenyeo personally! Also, the women working at the museum were nice and helpful as we tried to get to our next stop.

This was a nice place in Jeju to take the kids, preferably in cooler weather because we went in July, and we were dying.  Besides the weather, everything else was nice.  There's a train that will take you to different stations.  We only stopped at stations 2 and 3 because we brought our boys ages 5 and 7, and those stations had more stuff for them to enjoy.  We probably could have stopped at all stations, but it really was just so hot!  There were lots of places for photo ops, whether all cute or nature-like.  The restaurant at the main building was very limited in the food that they sell.  We ended up eating light food at station 2's cafe and also got drinks at station 3.  All the staff there were very friendly and seemed to enjoy their work.  Overall, nice place to visit.  Oh one warning though, our rental car's GPS brought us to different places even though we entered the correct phone number and even when we asked someone for help and they entered it in Korean.  Just make sure you research how to get there because it was very frustrating for us.

This tiny, delightful island feels miles away from anything familiar and mundane.  I highly recommend renting an electric scooter (for about 25 bucks for 2 hours) and driving around the entire island.  Driving around the island only takes about an hour, but give yourself extra time to stop for photo ops.  The place is dreamy and laid back - you can even spot the famous haenyeo (women divers) at work, and see their   dressing stations.    There is no   one particular amazing   thing to see on Udo, but rather it's about the whole experience of exploring this off-beat place and losing track of time.

This show is Amazing...I don't feel bored or sleepy on the entire show. Enjoy every minute of it and can't stop laughing by their performance. The characters are funny without talking and the story is simple yet truly entertaining. They are interactive and skillful. This show is highly recommended when you go to Korea! But, don't use the toilet it was horrible when I visited this place.

This place was breathtaking! After getting a yummy octopus pancake we walked around the cliffs admiring the beauty and the ocean. We started on the west and ended on the east it was a beautiful, windy, gorgeous day! Great place to get fresh seafood from the lady fishermen too.

This place is name the world 7 wonder of nature, and defintely live it up to the name. I love the Jeju woman's diver perfomance, they are so lively and bubbly... Climbing up the stairs is totally panting (however nearing to the top, the stairs are very steep so be more cautious) but wait till u reach the peak of it, you will find it totally worth it. You can see the blue sea from this side and the other part of Jeju on the other side. The curve in volcano is amazing too.Totally recommended but please dun go there during noon when the sun is hot...

This is worth a trip to Jeju all by itself!  Going up to the peak looks intimidating, but it was pretty easy and we saw a woman in her 70s at the top.  It's hundreds of stairs and took about 35 minutes, but they have benches and a lot of shade on the way up.  There's a path designated for ascending and another for descending, and I recommend following them as intended.  We saw some people trying to beat the crowd by going up the 'down' path, but there aren't benches to rest on and not much shade on that path; also, the ascending path is a LOT steeper and the stairs are kind of narrow (like a typical home staircase), so if you go down the 'up' path, you'll be going down very steep stairs and shuffling around people, while the designated 'descending' path is a very gradual slope and much wider.  We went on a hot & humid day, but I unquestionably would do it again.

This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. When i visit Jeju, i stayed in a hotel nearby, so i can see the sunrise from the top of seonsan Ilchulbong. To see the beautiful sunrise, i walk from my hotel at 4.30 am. You need to buy an entrance ticket to this place.You need to walk the stair path, uphill, and soon you arrive on top, you'll find so many people already setting up the camera to capture the sunrise. after enjoying the beautiful scene from top, on our way down, my eyes can't stop admiring the beauty scene of Jeju City. Everything is taking your breath away in this place.You also can ride a horse or watch the mermaid show (lady divers). If you want to buy some goods for your family from Jeju (orange, souvenirs, cake, snacks), you have to buy it in Jeju, because you can't find any of these goods in Seoul. If you want to give a second thought on it, your last chance to shop is in the Jeju International airport (price is the same everywhere in Jeju).This is a very highly recommended place to visit in Jeju Island!

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is just another roadside attraction where you stop your car on a road and if you're lucky and the wind is blowing your car will seem to roll up hill. You might think that the world is about to end or that little green men have finally arrived but, it is just an optical illusion. The lay of the land and the slope of the road is all it is. If you're driving past it wouldn't hurt to stop and check it out. Just a few minutes is all you need. If you stop by keep an open mind and don't expect too much. It might help if you have a few drinks before you go, (but no drinking and driving).What is a mystery to me is who discovered it and how and why?

This is a very long beach along the south Jeju coast near the south-western end.  You can bike (there's trial, do segway, or a long walk) or drive and stop along places to take beautiful photos. At the end of the beach is Songacsan where you can hike for an hour or so - very easy.

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

This could be an amazing place to visit provided you have good weather and great friends. Scootering around the tiny island can be fun if you stop off at the beaches, swim along the way and explore the caves and tunnels by the black sand beach. Definitely keep an eye out for the giant burger restaurant and the peanut Makgeolli stand (留嫄몃━, it's alcoholic rice wine!), both are delicious! Don't over-hype it or expect too much, just go to have fun and you'll be happy you went.

There is a stair to reach to top to this extinct volcano. It seems easy at first but you will need to be prepared to reach its top. They put places to sit through the course.Since I was there during summer time, I sweated a lot. But reaching the top pay all physical efforts!Then you can walked down in order to see (and get enjoyed by) the friendly ladies who dive! It was nice to see that they also served the seafood they've just captured! You need to see them because they are now just a few and how knows if there will be more of them in the future.Remember 1: the presentations of this ladies happen in specific times (I got their 13:30pm presentation, so I had to walk fast up and down the volcano in order to see them)Remember 2: you should pay a ticket to get inside the park.I truly recommend you to reach both the top of the volcano and see the women divers presentation.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are sign posts to mark the start and end of the 100 metres stretch of the Mysterious Road.  Pretty fun to play   magic   with family and friends. Put your car to neutral gear, release your foot off the accelerator and notice the car moving   uphill   on the road.  Recreate the same effect with a bottle or ball rolling uphill.  The Mysterious Road is actually a gravity hill i.e. a place where a slight downhill slope appears to be an uphill slope due to higher surroundings, creating the natural illusion that water flows uphill or that a car left out of gear rolls uphill.  Worth a fun stop if you self-drive!

There are 3 different mazes you'll get to go through. It's tricky and fun at the same time. Once you've solved the last one, take time to go to the top of the main building and see the vista from there! At the end of the maze, you might need refreshment so there are drinks and ice cream available! Definitely a fun place to go to!

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The waterfall is rather small, but it is almost in the middle of a city. When you arrive you will be on top of the cliff in which Jeongbang flows off of. Located near Seogwipo city, Jeongbang Waterfall is 23 meters high and is very close to the sea. This is why people tell that the water falls directly into the ocean. A legend says that servant of Emperor Jin of China, called as Seo Bul, sent to the area in order to search the magical herb of eternal youth in Mount Halla. People interested in seafood can taste fresh abalone sashimi with garlic slices & hot pepper paste as dipping. It is offered by ajummas, who collect them directly at this spot. Don쨈t forget to wear good shoes to avoid becoming a casualty.

The title Theme Park may confuse some people. This is not an amusement park, just some natural park with lots of greenery, ponds, windmill, etc. You get on a train that takes you around the park, stopping at several stops where you can get off and later get on the train to move on to the next stop. Honestly, the park is just okay. Not much to see or do here.  I recommend you save your time and find other, more interesting attraction in Jeju

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The hike to the end of the cave was not short, so be prepared to walk a few kms if you plan to visit this place. The cave itself was wet and cool, which is good if outside was hot. You get to see different formations and immerse yourself deep underground at the same time. So, the time was well spent here. Afterward, you can stop by the restaurant near the entrance and have some cheap Korean food.  The admission to the cave was very reasonable as it is a government owned attraction.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time??? The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

spent a long day in Udo - so idyllic and relaxing.  There are endless seaside beaches, cliffs, cafes, ...  Just drive your own car there (via car ferry - costed us 32k Won) for a small car and 2 pax, or rent one of the bikes, motor tricycles (very cute), and just drive and stop anywhere (almost) you like and take photos, drink coffee, or just doing nothing and daydreaming. Excellent scenery, food- freshest seafood, burgers, ..... How nice to spend a day.

So, one might think that this is a great place to see artifacts or historic pieces, but as far as we saw, everything was a replica. To include the replica lava tube entrances. Sigh. They couldn't even be bothered to completely thatch a straw hut- they had concrete roofs with thatch done at the top and edges. They do have quite the array of carefully placed rocks and replica stone statues, but seeing as how none of it was real (the whole thing was built on the site of a landfill) there are more real things to go do on Jeju. The price is cheap. Spend it looking at the columnar basalt on the beach. At least that is real.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. Toilets are unfortunately not clean, so you may want to bring some disinfectant lotion and/or toilet paper.The first part of the hike is easily accessible, the latter part less so. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!

quick, easy, enjoyable.  our kids enjoyed the challenge (age 7 & 10).  we attended early in the day and missed the numerous school groups.  a small event with a modest fee....a very nice stop before we headed to the lava tubes.

Pretty much boring, probably one will only get really excited if the person is a hardcore teddy bear fan .. Else it's really just a   oh ya I've been there.. Full stop    kinda trip.. Was lucky I went during the children days weekend so quite a good no of attractions were free.. Else I will probably feel $ wasted on this

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.

One of Jeju Island attraction, the rock formations that looks more like a horse head to me. Well, legendary it was a head of a dragon. We stop by for a photo stop on our way to airport.A good nice photographing platform for visitor to take picture. There is a stairway leading down to the rocky beach, down there you can see many locals selling fresh seafood.  It is not a wheelchair friendly place. Be there before sunset otherwise you will not able to take a clear photo.

No regrets coming here.   The climb up via slopes and steps is quite manageable with some stops in between.   Tho for inactive person like me, legs became a little wobbly as I came down 븝 Windy & cold at times, so better have jackets ready.     We took about 40 mins to ascend, stayed around for 30 mins.    Descend was slightly faster

Nice looking beach and lovely water, but don?t recommend if you want to swim. Lifeguards are over authoritarian and you?re only allowed in a 10x10 square with many other people (who have inflatables)! We had a pretty bad experience here where the lifeguards seemed to be picking on us for no reason. Also not allowed to sit/walk on certain parts of the beach. Overall poor experience only saved but spotted an octopus!

My partner & I chose park our car at seongsan harbour so we could take the ATV. To our dismay, their ATV can only carry 1 driver. Therefore we rented the sheltered scooter that can sit 2. The rental of that scooter is charged at an exorbitant 15,000krw/hr. We exceed the return time by a mere 20 minutes and had to top up 10,000krw T.T Advise to all: Just drive up your car to the ferry. It's much cheaper than spending so much on a cramp scooter, especially during winter.Aside from the transport misfortune, our day afternoon in udo was well spent, but could be better. We took the 12 noon ferry and reached udo at 12:30pm. Last ferry back to seongsan was 4:30pm. We did not have time to hike up, nor enter the cave. Spent too much time cam whoring to take in every bend of the scenery. The Seobin-baeksa beach is beautiful, surrounded by crystal clear waters.Advise to all: Go in earlier, so cater time for hiking, cam whoring, and chilling by the beach. Must have lunch too, the seafood noodles has the freshest abalone and soup ever.

My mother-in-law bought my husband and I entry to this   museum   and I went in expecting ultra-hokey and a waste of time. I was really pleasantly surprised!There are a few   galleries  . The highlights for me were the Teddy Bear History gallery - where they use teddy bears to display historical dioramas including a Teddy Moon Landing, teddy bears knocking down the Berlin Wall, Teddy Disney World and more. These are pretty creative and well made. Some even include music.There's also an   art   gallery, with some famous paintings or sculptures reenacted with teddy bears. This gallery extends into more dioramas such as the   runway   and a Korean wedding scene. Not always logical in where they put things, but fun anyway. There are a few honestly significant teddies in the museum - a Louis Voittan teddy that cost millions at auction, and a small side gallery of Teddies combined with historical memorabilia from Teddy Roosevelt, with some brief English descriptions of where the teddy bear came from.It's not a top attraction if you're here for a short visit, but if you're around a while and want something cute and fun, it's worth an hour or two!

Must visit place if u come to Jeju Island. I rent a bicycle, cycling & round the island. It will takes around 2-3 hours. It will getting easier to stop everywhere and snap the picture. I visited Udo Island end of March and it full with the Canola Flowers!!! Don't forget to try the nut ice cream too. There have a lots of stall and restaurant selling it!!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Last weekend, I climbed up to the top of Hallsan Mountain and saw the crater on the top called Baerokdam. Hallasan is the highest mountain in Korea, 1,950m above sea level. It took 5 hours to go up to the to top, which means it took another 5 hours to climb down. Climbing was kind of fight with myself and I won! I'm really proud of it and the most unforgettable thing is Baerokdam itself. I can't express with a word. As it snowed for the first time this year, it was more beautiful.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is just beside the Manjang Cave, so I recommended a short 1hr stopover if you are heading to the cave.  Avoid the maze park on rainy days as the ground gets really muddy when it rains.

It's a 100m road whereby majority of the tourists are fascinated by this mysterious road. All the drivers will put it on neutral gear on the   starting point   and you find the car moving up but the road looks like incline. A short stop is given and you can have a good photo shoot over there. Most of the tour guide will tell you the truth behind this mysterious road and you will realise that    Things really cannot be judge by it's appearance.   Beside the Mysterious Road, there are a few stall selling some snacks. You must go to the first stall which is near to the ending point of the mysterious road, and try their strawberries. It's the most fresh strawberry i have ever seen and eat! It's a must to try.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It was the best decision to travel around the beautiful island of Jeju with Jeju Taxi Tour Samchoon Kim! He brought us to all the places in our itinerary that we intended to visit and he even checked the weather prior to that so that we would not be caught in the rain. The whole trip was very comfortable and it was not in a rush. We took our time to see and soaked in all the goodness of Jeju! Samchoon Kim is also very kind and polite, I remembered one of the day he stopped by a morning market and ran down coming back with 6 freshly made Bungeo ppang (a Korean dessert) for us. That act really warm our hearts =) Not to forget, he also always offered to snap pictures for us so we do not need a selfie stick! Thank you for being a great tour guide and driver!

It was our 2nd time visit Udo,absolutely loved it.Few tips for anyone who plan to visit Jeju:* Bring your ID with you! We went to Udo in July and we were asked to present ID at ticket office, Seongsanri Port. Saw lots tourists queuing at ticket office and pretty much everyone was holding passport!! We didn't have passport with us, but luck enough I had my driving licence in my purse. My boyfriend didn't have any ID with him, and we bought 2 ferry tickets with showing 1 ID only.  * it's an absolutely beautiful place. Tried peanut ice cream which was very refreshing. * scooter or bike? My opinion is get bike!! It costs 10000 won to get 1 bike and you can ride as long as you want, no time limit what so ever, it costs 25000 won to get a scooter, and you need to be back within 2 hours. It was kinda electric bike, so presuming the power only lasts 2 hours. If you plan spend move than 4 hours on this lovely island, bike is the option, not hard to ride around and you can stop at any cafe for a ice cream or drink and chill out at the beach for 1 hour. That's what we did :) rather than just sitting on the scooter and kept checking time consistently to make sure to get back  within 2 hours.

It was my second visit, it's as windy here in winter as in autumn. Spend at least 2 hours here. Take the stairs down to the coast, there's a small house/shop there that sells fresh seafood like small octopuses and abalones.

It was a good experience for me family with 2 children as they enjoyed ut the most. Weather as a bit chilly even during autumn, so bring extra layers with you so that you can get confortable. The train ride at the start of the trip really feels like the highlight of the trip, although you can board the train on and off later to get from one garden to another. There are 5 stops for you to stroll around, toilets, cafes and other facilities are available and very much well taken care off. We had a great time all in all. Highly recommended to friends and families.

It took everything in me to make this climb.  But at the end of the day, my legs wobbling, I could say,   I hiked Korea's tallest mountain  Make sure to bring your food as the only thing available for sail will be ramen noodle, a favorite among Koreans.One tip, push through till you get to the area set up for sitting and eating.  Doing this instead of many stops along the way will definitely save you some time.

it is very easy and friendly track to reach the peak, but for me the beautiful things about Seongsan Illchulbong are scenery from everywhere. so, I made a little tour by walking by from beaches till Saepjikoji and to Udo island. Never get missed from sunrise to sunset, everything is beautiful. is not wrong to choose stay near the Hills, Goseong-ri is perfect village to stay.But, if you just a few time to visit is good to stopping by. My wife loves here in spring time, lots of canola and pretty flower in the green green grass.You will found starbucks, convenience market, and lots of food.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

I'm not a big fan of Hello Kitty (my friend does), but it was fun to stroll around the place. It was filled with Hello Kitty goodness in pink and such a nice place to take pictures. There are so many rooms to be visited, and they even have a rooftop garden! Some of item showcased are very interactive and enjoyable. I believe it's worth the visit as every adult has their own inner-child side. Unravel your younger side out, and you'll enjoy the place lot more than you think. Recommended for families. Make sure to visit their cafe that serves nice choco drink (approx. KRW4000) & the gift shop!Admission fee for adult: approx. KRW10800++

I'm coming from a developing country and would expect more from the markets in developed country such as South Korea. The market is as dirty as my country's wet markets. Generally the country is not tourist friend enough. A lot of interesting consumable   seafood   types in the market that I haven't seen in my country and wished to try. However, I couldn't find any label of the seafood stated in English or han zi (chinese character). The shop owners too couldn't communicate in any languages that I know. A lot of times my desire to try was stopped upon not knowing the best way to eat, eating raw? Deep fried or stir fried is better?Frankly, I would expect the overall standard close to the markets in Japan or other western countries.

If you have no knowledge of the K-pop industry, this may not be the place for you. But, we love it. For the ticket price, things it offers is beyond our expectation. If you have a personal preference of 'which' pop star you wanna watch for the hologram show, you should check its schedule online. The ticket has a 3-hour validity (I think it's a bit short, if you really try all the stations/ experience) There are 3 levels where you could see lots of displays (music, costumes) and to try lots of fun interactive games with cutting edge technology. For instance, to dance with the stars, to shoot a picture with them, where you could actually scan your ticket and choose from the list, which star you want to pick. We stopped half way to watch the scheduled hologram show, which lasted for about 30 mins, and it was fabulous because that is the singer we really adore. After the show, we continued with our visit for a while. You can print whatever photos you snapped (if you like it) on the spot with a small fee. Likewise, you may download all the funny photos you have snapped from their website later that day. We enjoyed ourselves tremendously.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.

If there is nothing else you do go see this temple. It is a sprawling complex that goes all up to the base of the mountain. Along the way if you do hike all the way up to the top, there are signs to explain the legends behind the names of the places you walk and why there is a temple there. But even if you don't it is still an sight to see

I went there with my family members in a cloudy day. This place is composed with several parts of themes. Lake, play ground, short hiking with spa, and snack bars.My kids(9, 5yrs) really enjoyed the place with running, taking pictures, and eating.Even I visited in Jeju more than 10 times, this place is the most memorable place to visit. Because kids didn?t have any bother others.Additionally, there were packed with people and very noise when I waited for tour train. Then please be sure to keep you eyes on your kids. I visited there at the last of tour then I couldn't have enough time to hiking.However, I recommend you to take a walk at the picnic garden station (2nd stop).There are kids town and eco-land at Picnic garden station

I think it was more academic then entertaining. Despite cutting edge technology based attraction, this place has enough mixture of both interesting facts and entertainment. Restaurant was lots of fun as well. And I think it means a lot to see the corporate name. People all know   Nintendo   but not many knows a top Korean game corporate. I think it is nice.

I started off by lowering my expectations for this tourist stop.  The building is a little outdated from the outside and I wasn't sure how good it could be.  The whole family was pleasantly surprised.  We learned about the fun character and her family and friends.  Everything was well done and there was more to the museum than expected.  My daughter and son both had smiles from ear to ear, making for a great day.

I really feel sorry for those went earlier this year and totally missed the beauty of the silvery purple grass we have not seen elsewhere. It is such an easy walk so even you push baby strollers, or having a baby buggy, it shouldn't be too difficult. Anyway, you probably stop Sao many times on the way to take photos so it is not a tiring climb.There's only one small snack place at the bottom but a few nice wooden picnic booth for people to rest.  We saw some Korean families enjoying their homemade kimba at the top enjoying the scenery. I think it's a great family trip for about one to two hours depending on the age difference in your group.Selfie stick is quite useful here if you want to post in from too the unique grass.  Obviously don't dress in silver (autumn time).After this we went on another 20~30 min to the world's biggest nutmeg forest which is on the way to the east coast (5 Day Market and Haenyeo Women Diver Museum) to,follow in the afternoon.

I really did enjoy working my way through this maze. The entire area is beautifully put together and is the kind of place you just want to spend time in and enjoy. Unfortunately, uniqueness comes with a price. I thought nearly $5 per person was a little steep but it isn't every day you get to walk through a hedge maze. The maze itself is a lot of fun and is large enough to actually be a bit of a challenge. We met the owner and he is very friendly and interesting to talk to. I am glad we stopped here but, because of the price, I don't think I would do it again.

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Great location with beautiful sightseeing...Jeju Island, also known as the   Island of the Gods,   is a popular vacation spot for Koreans and foreigners. It remains the top honeymoon destination for Korean newlyweds, and is also regarded as one of the top honeymoon destinations in the world. Despite attempts to market the island as   the Hawaii of Korea,   climatologically and geographically it bears little in similarity to the Hawaiian Islands in the U.S. The island offers visitors a wide range of activities: hiking on Halla-san (South Korea's highest peak) or Olle-gil(routes), catching sunrises and sunsets over the ocean, riding horses, touring all the locales from a favorite television K-drama, or just lying around on the sandy beaches. Although tourism is one of the main industries on the island, many of the hotels and other tourist areas are run by mainland companies, so much of the income never gets put back into the local economy. Also, since the attractions are geared towards tourists, many of the entrance fees can be hefty (although the locally owned and operated ones tend to be cheaper). Similar to Gyeongju and some other areas, local residents can enter most places for free or for a steeply discounted price.

For us - it was a last 'must see' on Jeju Island.  Our tour books featured it as a top site, so we went.  We didn't have much time, and it worked (since it's near the airport) for a quick stop off.  I didn't hate it - it was crowded though.  Lots of tour groups, teens, etc.  There were several shops nearby that were handy for our last bit of shopping.  You don't need to spend a lot of time here, but the rock formation is neat and the myth behind it is interesting.

Entrance fee is 10,000KRW.I visited during Spring and the place is so beautiful with flowers all around! Daisy, roses, lavender are everywhere. It's so breathtaking!The place is divided into 3 parts, and they take you to these places via train. The train will stopped at each stop and you can get down to visit and explore the places and get on to the next trip of train to get to next destination.Their ice cream is good too! Tasty and fresh! Worth trying.Good place to enjoy beautiful scenery. The air is so fresh and you could really enjoy your time here.We visited this place for like 2 hours.

Engaged a taxi driver to get here.  When you arrive, you need to buy tickets to enter the park.  Although the sun was out, it was also raining, so we didn't enjoy the Park as much as we could have done.  The train was a hop on/hop off style and had it not been raining, we probably would have explored more at each stop. As it was, we needed to stay under cover of the train!  Would only recommend going to this place on a rainless day!

Dived back to those nostalgic childhood moments when teddy bears once played as friends in your life. This Teddy Bear Museum has a wide array of collection of teddy bears, dressed beautifully in different costumes. The most popular bear will probably be the one dressed in Louis Vuitton clothes.What particularly caught my attention was the exhibition which actually used famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa, and the Teddy Bear was dressed to depict her. A creative way to carry out this exhibition. However, those expect to see a wide range of   depiction  .Overall, I felt that this was only an average stop-over, but will be good for families traveling with their young children. There's a souvenir shop on site too, where I'll be expecting young children to be bugging their parents to get them a teddy bear each!

Did a solo hike in the hot summer of July, and wasn't disappointed.It was a long, easy hike up with some steep steps near the end of the hike. 10KM up and down, in total 20KMThere are some stops along the way, especially the 'base camp' where you can purchase ramen to eat.There are no railings or ropes to hold on to a few metres close to the peak, so this would be harder to do on a winter's day.Was kinda sad that the peak was shrouded by a large cloud, but nonetheless satisfied with the easy hike.Public transport starts as early as 6AM, so if you drive and want to end early, it would be better.
Depends on your agenda, there are stalls selling nice snacks like bbq octopus, fish cakes, etc. Many raw seafoods, oranges, chocolates and snacks for gifts.

Cruise stop. Jeju tour. On the way back we walked through both this and the underground mall. A million oranges and fish stores. Neat to be among the Jeju people going about their day. Try some of the food! But watch out for the guys DRIVING up and down the aisles on mopeds!I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Couldn't believe that a car museum of such excellence would be found on Jeju Island in South Korea.the large number of cars covered all makes, types and brands and we just loved all the old advertising posters around the museum.The displays outside were also a delight and the museum was not hard to get to by public transport.? We stopped off to watch some of the races on the way back and that is also worth a visit.? They use descendants of the Mongolian ponies, and with their colourful jockeys they made a wonderful display.? The extensive grounds have lots to entertain children as well as a mini golf course in the centre of the race track.? Would definately recommend both destinations.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: Circumnavigated this little island on a bike in an afternoon, and it was a lovely excursion. The older culture is still somewhat alive (weeding through the tourist stops), but even the bitsy coffee shops are endearing. Bicycle is the way to see this place, for sure!

By the time we visit Ecoland, it's already 4pm so  time limited as it closes at 5 pm!We took a long train that stop at every 4 places of visiting.In the first stop, we went through attraction on beautiful scenery and artistic work and went to another second stops to wait for the train. Then the train took us to third stops and another attraction artwork of beautiful small houses and Christmas artwork and many others.  Then we went to last stop that is garden which grows lavender,green tea and many types of flowers. It's a beautiful garden on the whole. On whole, I'll come to again another time again on next visit!
big enough & diff topic in park. you could see the flower, bird, cave etc,,,,not too crowded when i visited, good place for spending time

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.

A visit to the ice museum would be recommended. Do try the ice slide (or slope), where you have to drag your own donut tube up the stairs to the top of the slide. Its great fun and the kids loved it. The rest of the ice sculptures and the big igloo is nicely done as well. We skipped the 5D and VR attractions as we spent too much time on the ice thingy.

A road seems to be uphill, but it is in fact a downhill. The driver shut off the engine at the 'downhill' but the car moves itself towards the 'uphill' without the help of anyone. Fun fact by tour guide: This mysterious incident was discovered by a taxi driver when he intend to take a leak at the roadside and found out the car moves itself towards the uphill after he stopped the car.

6 hours to reach the peak, but it was worth it! Start your trip early as you need to be at the entry point by 12PM in order to make it to the top as everyone needs to start heading down at 2PM (depends on seasonality)...Certain parts of the hike is tough, but the feeling at the top of the mountain looking over the lake, is speechless!

180m to the top but more then worth it in the end. Taking the hike up the steps was quite a workout, so I highly suggest, prepare to break a sweat. My favorite part was taking pictures on the way down, there are many great picture opportunities. One thing I recommend is to take the extra steps down to the ocean, take your shoes off and enjoy the cool refreshing water. It is well worth it after after walking down.

With a minimal fee of KRW10k one gets to kayak along the stream for 20 mins. The water is clear and deep. Each wooden kayak can only take 2 passenger with only one person rowing. The catch is the ticket counter is a distance away from the port. And the best time to go is on a weekdays. Weekends are usually crowded.

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)

We wwnt here because it was on the way to the airport.  It isnt really special but a good place to pick up some last minute souvenirs like chocolates and jeju oranges.  We looked around for 15 minutes then headed off because most of the venders were all selling the same items

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.

We went there on our way back after a day of sightseeing. It is good to just drive pass that stretch. But not worth if it is not on the way. You could just spend a brief less than 5mins there while staying in the car.

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We visited this last for the day at Jungmun Resort since this opened till rather late (~8+pm). Last entry should be around 7pm since it would take you around 1 1/2 - 2 hours if you're gonna snap alot of the photos inside. If you are already inside Jungmun Resort and are travelling in groups you can take a cab to this place since it would not cost much and you can save the hassle of walking. The paintings inside are really cool and we had a fun time snapping photos away. Effects came out rather cool on the photos. There are several sections in the museum and each sections has its own theme. Definitely worth a visit and we really didn't regret it. Initially we intended to spend only 1 hour in the museum since we really rushing off to other places in the night. We ended up spending 2 hours there. So do equip yourself with a camera and of course have someone with you to take photos for you.

We took VIP tickets from Jungmun Tourist centre  at 50 percent off. The show is very entertaining and involves lots of interaction with the crowd. The place is a bit far away and close to Jeju university. If you are going for 8:00pm show booking a taxi is recommended. The show is value for money for the deal we got from the tourist office. Apparently there is a rush pass which is available for discounts on shows for the same day.

We stumbled upon this market while walking around Jeju. It was very vibrant inside with many vendors selling their products. The vendors were very friendly and tried to speak English to us. Some even gave us samples of their products. We bought some local chocolates. It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend some time.

We spent the night at a Pension at the base so it was easy to get to to catch the sunrise. From the base we could already see people making their way up. We were prepared to spend at least 40 mins to climb the stairs but surprisingly we got there within 20 mins. I would not say it was a breeze as we (and most people there) were panting and had a good sweat. Regardless of your fitness level just go at your pace with comfortable shoes and attire - the beautiful sunrise against the ocean is definitely worth it (unless it's bad weather)
We really enjoyed visiting this place! I recommend you to bring your car with you. but any way you will enjoy there
We loved the Alive museum. It was so much fun!!!So many funny poses you could make and was a lovely way to spend the day out.

We had an old Korean man who has lived there for all his life guiding us around his own house in English. He was very humorous and a very friendly guide. It was an interesting and refreshing experience of learning about the old village way of living in Jeju!

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.

We drove around Jeju and decided to give this thing a go cos we didn't believe it would be possible. So we reached the road and there were signs that told you that its the starting. So all you have to do is to put your car in neutral gear and release the accelerator at the starting point and watch your friend's jaw drop. Recommended to visit together with Jeju Loveland as its just 3 minutes driave away. Admission at 8000 won per pax. pricey but its a pretty interesting visit XD
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

Was very crowded the day/time we were there.  There's a tiny museum which leads to shop and cafe.At the cafe we had the trio of  green tea cake/roll smoothie and ice cream which were very good.Then we headed next door to the Innisfree Jeju house.A nice way to spend a couple of hours.  There's a couple of very uncrowded O'sulloc cafes in Seoul too.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Use your 3D imagination and spend a couple of fun hours. Where you can become part of each scenario from hungry dinosaurs to a VanGong painting from an explosive mine to be on a boat in Venice. Great museum best recommendation don't go alone to enjoy it more. Although other tourists are always kind to take some pic for you.

Understand that the day we went weather was harsh as there?셲 typhoon warning ; the parking escort/attendant wasn?셳 helpful at all is was raining and very windy we were traveling with a 2yr old baby  ask him nicely to let us ?쁃rop off??only but he insisted that we go to the other carpark to park our cars (the carpark has open lots and a few cars are coming out) ; I don?셳 know his against foreign or what but after we parked our car Far far away carrying the baby  pram  umbrella diaper bag we saw he letting the locals go in and park .
