We were so piss ; and it ruin our trip in jeju as my toddler felt sick after. His now down with flu thanks to them and I still got 12 more days in Korea . Very disappointed  will not recommend any of my friends and family period

This was just like Legoland in California just on a much smaller scale (no pun intended). It looks like it was once a better place and has gone to the wayside. My first visit was around December then again in June. December was really rundown then June the grass and greenery covered up the poor parts from the winter. Kids will enjoy it you will be wondering why you gave KRW to see it!

This was a great way to spend an hour!  It would have been more fun had I been able to navigate alone.  My friend was not interested in using the map and just wanted to finish for the photo op as quickly as possible.  We did go back into the maze to each of the six stations and stamped our cards.

This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

This natural attraction isn't that remarkable (rock that looks like a dragon) but it would have been nice except it is PACKED with tourists. It is way too crowded for my liking and most photos taken will include a bunch of other random tourists in it as well. My boyfriend and I were far more interested in the little food stalls set up around this tourist attraction - as you can try some local snacks. We came here as a part of a tour from Hong Kong.

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.

This island is only about 10 mins away by ferry from Jeju Island. The environment is very clean and very beautiful. You can either take your own car or hire a scooter to go around the island. It only takes less than 2hrs to complete a full circle. I seriously recommend you to spend a least a day or two.

This is an excellent play place for teenagers. If you are a child 120 cm and under you must go with an adult. I recommend that if you’re really tall or big you might not want to go because this place has narrow tunnels. I almost got stuck in one of the hammock tunnels... haha.We saw this place on a pamphlet we got from the airport and really wanted to go right away and it was totally worth going.Remember to wear something comfortable because you’ll be moving around a lot so clothing with shenanigans hanging off from it probably won’t be a good idea. Or excessive jewelry. The price was 12000 per person for the Maze ep.3 and the Level 2 (harder level with timer) was around 5000?? But as a package it was 16000 per person. We had so much fun here!

This is a farm for Green Tea. First and foremost it is near the Glass park 5 mins drive away. So if you are planning to visit this place and have no budget constraints and have lots of time you can consider to spend 30mins at the glass park as well.The Tea farm sells tea (of course) and remember to try the green tea ice cream in the building. You can walk around the farm but be careful of the snakes. We seen one there.Nice place to visit whether alone in a group or with your family and kids.

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.
There are three connected mazes.  You can go through one or all.  A great way to spend a few hours.  There is also a museum/exhibit maze in the building.

The water park is ok. It would have been way better if you didn't have to pay extra for swim vests and extra for sun beds. So practically paying entrance fee doesn't mean you go and have fun. You are forced to spend good amount of money to have a good time.

The five-day markets in Jeju Island are fascinating places where locals converge for their everyday needs. Everything from hundreds of different Kimchi to farm tools to live rabbits - a visitor will find anything you need. These markets are located in various places around the island with the largest one located in Jeju city! Mostly under cover - it was a wonderful way to explore despite a rainstorm!What struck us the most was the incredible friendliness of the Korean merchants - knowing that we were not Korean - they were patient and was very open for us to try some of their foods! One vendor offered me some Kimchi and when she saw my reaction to the spicy-ness - she handed me a piece of pickled lotus root to help cool my mouth followed by a big smile!

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

Teddy bear museum was such a curious place ever. Many kinds of teddy bear are displayed on there and also great to take photos. Think takes 1~2 hours to look around here. I really liked it and also teddy bear souvenirs are pretty good to prepare as gifts but a little expensive to buy a lot. Anyway i would like to recommend to visit here. This museum is worth a visit:)

Small museum which showcases lots of green tea cups from around the world. As it was raining at the time of visit I spent more time indoors and at the cafe. As this is a tourist hotspot the cafe is always full and finding a table is quite a challenge (I was lucky though). I recommend ordering the green tea ice cream and the cold drip tea which is only sold at the Jeju outlet.Will probably visit again next time to see the green tea plantations which I missed out on.This museum is a stone's throw away from Innisfree Jeju House - barely 90 seconds walk which is worth a visit as well.

Recommended place to visit for family with young children and teddy bear lovers as this museum holds a large collection of teddy bears with themes all over the world. Downside is that souvenirs are way too expensive.

Recommended by our guide. We spent around 1hr here in a Spring afternoon. Big crater with many green trees growing in it. Also able to see farms far away. Many spots to take nice photos. I would say good to visit but ok to skip it.

Quite interesting maze. It took us a bit more time than expected to find the way out and it was funny. If you plan to take a brake in this area I would certainly recommend spend about hour to play in the maze.

Plenty of interesting glass installations in the park and museum. Really worth to see. Very nice and friendly owner. Many beautiful things and funny toys in the shop. The best way to get there is by taxi  it's about $15 from Seogwipo city center.
Past by Wolijeongri beach on my way to other attractions. The beach is very beautiful. Good to spend 15 mins of your time there to take some nice shots.
Paid a 1000 (or 2000?) won entrance fee and my breath was taken away by the beautiful sight! There was even a rainbow at the end of the waterfall... simply beautiful :)
Our guide June gave us a detailed explanation of all the places we went to. She was also helpful in many ways and answered our queries. She even recommended a good dinner place for us!

O'Sulloc Tea Museum  is actually a shopping paradise for those who fancy for tea. O'Sulloc itself is famous for its Tea product. In front there's a collection of used cups that they arranged in such a way so it's picturesque.Since It's a green tea field expect for green tea product for sale including all side products (Cake Drinks etc). We also have a little chat with the tea-picker ajumma. If you go to the upper floor you will be able to take picture of overall green tea field but don't expect too much.I recommend time of visit when the sun not in its brightest Enjoy!

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.
one of Main tourist object. You must use your image to get the head. A lot shop on the way which attract tourist to spend more time than the main object.
Not a must see if you are press for time. It was dark most of the way and you don?t get to see much. The star attraction is towards end of the 1km walk.

Magpie Brewery is a great place to have some decent western food and high quality craft beer. Their Baltic Porter is particularly good as is their Kolsch. You probably need a  car to get to the place or a taxi which will cost you \10000 to \15000 each way depending which part of Jeju City you are in.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

Lava tunnels stem from liquid hot Lava that makes its way under the ground and leaves empty tunnels when the Lava stream comes to an end. This tunnel is very long but is lacking something of a mysterious atmosphere which we had seen before at other Lava tunnels.
Lava tube isn't something extraordinary. Exploiring just halfway (of the recommended in brochures) is enough

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

review: I've visited the original Da Vinci Museum in Florence in the middle of my school field trip many years ago. Since I visited fancy museums in that trip like the Louvre or Orsay  I never expected the Da Vinci Museum to be as good as those. However  it was one of the best places I've visited in the trip. Other museums only let people to look at the exhibits but those in Da Vinci was to be operated. I think touching was stronger feeling that looking. The memory is still clear.With the good memory from Florence  I also visited the one in Jeju and it was also great. I went there with my girlfriend and worried if she doesn't like it since it seems a bit for students and children. Anyway  turned out she liked its clean and pleasant facility. I think I like the one in Jeju little more since it is not in the middle of crowded city. Maybe because the one with me matters.
It is worth seeing these homes and way of life.  Of course they want to see  you something at the end but the short tour was worth it.

If you go for brands (local and international) this short street is probably the place to go to on this part of the island. The street is closed to traffic so you could spend a while walking in comfort. The street is on the way to dongmun market and the underground shopping centre. Along the way it also branches off into some kind of roofed shopping arcade which we did not visit.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

I went here in the afternoon with friends. The place is a little bit dark with a minimum lightning. Please mind your steps especially during rainy days. Prepare sports or appropriate shoes to visit this place because the way is so uneven.
I was with a local Korean friend that didn't understand himslef what the fuss was all about... Unless it's on your way you can skip it!

I visited to Da vinci museum with my daughter last weekend.It was very interesting and educational place.There are many experience activities like making a paddle steamer  shooting water bomb  etc.My daughter made a paddle steamer  she really liked it. Anyway I was surprised that I can see the Da vinci's works in Korea not itary.

I totally missed the sunrise at this point despite setting the alarm at 4am. But the trip to the peak in the afternoon was refreshing enough. I feel that it has heighten my spirit to cope with what I always wonder. Hiking up the mountains has been what I love most. But seeing the end is really rewarding. I believe that the sunrise marks it all.

I loved this cave! 2 km in and out. It was a very educational trip as you'll get explanations about what you see along the way. It's dark and wet and there's water dripping from the ceiling so bring a cap and good boots to avoid slipping. Don't wear a long skirt as it will get wet. A bit hard to take pictures though because of the lighting :/ But the ending and the way it was presented with the lighted walkway at the end was great!

I have visited half a dozen Buddhist temples in Korea and so far this is my favorite! This temple is simply gorgeous. We arrived just as the monks started ring the outside bell. We were greeted with open arms and encouraged to come inside the main temple building and to go upstairs to see it all. I have always been hesitant to venture into the temples to take pictures because I do not want to offend anyone but we were invited in to explore it was fantastic. so ornate. The three gold Buddhist statues were very large and beautiful. The monks where in the middle of chanting it was a mesmerizing experience so peaceful and relaxing. The grounds of the temple were just as lovely.

I have always wanted to visit a maze.  This one was lots of fun.  Just when we thought we found our way out  we were at a dead end.  The Korean people who were actually at the end were up on the platform laughing at us and cheered when we arrived. No translation was needed.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

Hydrangea season so that friends chose this rainy season reach jeju. that was not good travel season as too hot & rainy always. but Camellia hill getting quite many flowers & not too crowded as jeju has many place to have this flower show. the garden big enough & well organize. good for taking picture & walk around if you love flowers

Great place if you are into culture and history as you will enter the medieval village and learnt about how ancient Jeju people lived and some continued to live in straw roof houses and lived the traditional way of life. Recommend to go and follow a local guide to go unless you speak Korean.

Could have spent half a day here. Gardens were beautiful. The lava caves were nice to walk through to break up the heat! Interesting animals throughout.  Ran out of time and missed seeing the water gardens.  Great way to spend a day outside. Especially enjoyed the bonsai garden.

Came here looking for lunch. If u r not a fan of sashimi  stay away then. The market primarily sold fresh seafood for the purpose of making sashimi. Easy walking with lots of vendors selling a variety of food - primarily seafood. There was one stall that sold braised pork trotters and very popular. Do watch out for the myriad of vehicles though. The walking paths and the roads does seem too integrated  sometimes forgetting that u were walking on the road already.

Black Pork Street was recommended to us by our Hotel when I asked about where is the best place to eat the famous Black Pork on the Island. We were quite disappointed as we walked down the street there were hustlers from each of the restaurants approaching you trying to sell you on their restaurant which we found odd. Almost every restaurant required you to buy two orders of Black Pork and my Wife had her heart set on kimchee stew. 3/4 of the way down the street we found a restaurant that didnt require two servings so we ate there. I excitedly took pictures of the pork to find out later that it it wasnt black pork. My advice is find a local and ask where they take their family to have Black Pork and you will truely be able to enjoy their Island delicacy.

As a resident of Jeju  I enjoy walking through this park every week. It is a great and safe place to take kids or walk dogs. There are two parts to the park: north of the road and south of the road. In the southern part  there are interesting ponds and pathways.I would not recommend this place to tourists only because there is so much else to see in Jeju Island that is far more impressive than this park. However  it is only a five minute walk from the city Center (Jungang Rotary) to the northern part so it is not far at all.

After visiting the lava tubes we got to try out the maze park.  A fun way to spend a half hour and the site of many k-dramas and korean commercials.  Romantic for a date and fun if you have kids.  We even got to ring the bell at the end!A fun excursion if you're walking to the lava tubes it's on the same road.

You may find it interesting if you are interested in a legend, folk tale or something like that. The story goes like this, there were three gods who came to Jeju and lived peacefully... With total of 2km walk in the tunnel (2 ways), you will be able to see different types of volcanic stones with good explanation notes in multiple languages. Not suitable for old people as it is dark and the walkpath is not even (all natural). Spend 1 hour.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

While this is  just of the roadway, it?s fairly free of visitors.   The path goes alongside running water (or not - depending on rainfall).    There was about a 30m section where the path ended and we had to walk from rock to rock before the path restarted.    On the other side was a cave - Rock Shade Residence - which olden people used as shelter.   Entire area is a beautiful evergreen valley, well worth a visit.

While it is not spectacular like other caves around the world that are open to tourists, they are worth visiting due to their geographical nature.They are easy for families to visit, no bending over or crawling necessary.The temperature inside stays around 16-18c all year round. It is always damp, and most areas are dimly lit.

What a great place to visit especially on a rainy dayIt traces the history of computing from the 50s to the present day in a very informative wayHowever of somewhat more interest to particularly children is the very interactive history of computer gaming. This includes the ability to play the old games like tv tennis and space invaders to more modern gamesA great way to spend a couple of hours , it certainly kept me and the grandchildren entertained

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

went there with my sister joining a local tour and met some new friends. strongly suggest NOT doing it alone... would be soooooooooo boring, but with someone else you can fight on which way to go.Learn more about your sense of direction,bring pen for easy remembering which way did you go.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

Went there in the morning via taxi. Not many people. Admission: 2000 won each.There are flights of stairs to climb down when you first reach, so imagine the climb back up once you are done. To get nearer to the waterfall, you have walk over many many many rocks. Not recommended to go after rain as it will be super slippery. However, I love this waterfall more than Cheongjiyeon waterfall. It is nicer actually and you can get closer to the waterfall (of coz getting passed the obstacles of rocks).Love it actually but no way near magnificent.

Went there after visiting the Manjanggul caves, fairly close by. Not necessarily a tourist attraction, but if you're looking to spend an hour or two in a nice forest away from all the coach visitors, this is a great spot. All we saw were Koreans out for a Sunday walk. There is a circuit path through the forest, all level, well maintained, took us maybe an hour to complete. Totally relaxing and peaceful.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We were a little disappointed after walking all the way down the hill at Sunrise Peak to see the women divers, only to find out that because of the holiday, they wouldn't be diving today.So as a consolation, our tour guide took us to the Haenyeo Museum.  This museum was dedicated to the Haenyeo women divers of Jeju and Japan.  It's a very nice museum with excellent displays, and you will learn a lot about the divers.I recommend seeing the video show before you start wandering around.

We went to this cave as friends want to visit even it was not on my bucket list. It was impressive to see volcanic layers and massive path inside. We walked down all way to the end i.e. 1 km away and walk back again. Personally, I don't find it interesting.

We went to the one at T 724-0228, mainly after the ferry landed and we were hungry, 'tween lunch and dinner parking wS available out front.  Staff were a little underworked so we go the full service treatment, good thing not tips expected (?);  we had the less fatty pork neck.  Served with a nice crab soup and nangymun noodles as a dessert.  Can't seem to get away from grilled fatty pork in Korea, have they heard of lean tenderloin here? Marinated  Pork skin was also served,

We went as a couple  not expecting much  but this place was really fun! Lots of little experiments to do with electricity  plasma  light. The   tesla coil music orchestra   was impressive... or did I just got high on the ozone? Even the arcade games upstairs were great.We ended up staying for more than 2 hours and left only because they were closing down.I only wish they put more effort into the English information/displays. There are little English summaries  but the Korean version always looked way more exhaustive.There also an   organic salad bar   and a black pork restaurant at the facility  but we didn't have time to visit.

We visited this area with kids ages 3-11. Easy paved walk through a beautiful scenic shaded walkway. The falls were breathtaking. We took our shoes off and soaked our feet at the end of stairs leading into the water. Ate an easy convenience store lunch when we returned to the parking lot before heading to our next destination of the day. 1,000won for kids, 2,000won for adults. Can?t beat the price.

We visited this area on our volcanic forces lava tour through Expedia in November 2016.  It was a cool, windy day so we didn't spend even an hour here.  Maybe 45 minutes.  You have to take stairways down to the cliff area.  Then we were freezing even with our layers and coats due to the wind blowing right through us.  It reminded us of the lava cliffs along the coast of Volcanoes National Park on the Hilo-side of the Big Island.  There are even palm trees in the garden area before you start descending towards the Oceanside cliffs.

We visited Seongeup Folk Villagein end Jan 2018, it?s snowing during our visit. There is a lady tour guide that speak English assign to us. She did it well and we enjoy the visit. The building in village are unique. We were there on the good timing where snows make the area really beautiful. You also can buy some of the products they sell over there, anyway is optional.

We visited on a very wet day so it was good to be inside even if the inside was the lava cave.  The lighting is very low in the cave and the floor, made by lava flow is very uneven so close attention needs to be made to where you are going. Its one kilometre each way to the end of the public bit and you miss quite a bit watching where the feet go so not to fall over.mAn interesting place to visit but take a torch!

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.

We paid for the VIP seats, KW10,000 more than the standard seats. When we entered, noticed that VIP seats were in red right in the centre of stage, while standard seats were on both left n right sides of the VIP seats. Worth paying the extra to be at the centre. They also choose guest from the VIP seats for participation on the stage. Show was hilarious, enjoyed by both young and old. Even my 4 year old child was laughing all the way to the end. It lasted 100 mins, try to catch evening show instead of night show during winter a the hall would be freezing at night.If you have not seen this, include this show in either Jeju or Seoul.

We happened to be staying near the Hyeopjae Beach so we went there a couple of times, but I wouldn't recommend going out of your way for it. The water is clear and beautiful, but a bit cold for our tastes. I'm sure it warms up in July and August though. - Kanannie

We had the best time at the 3D Alive Museum.  As you walk through there are pictures on the walls and floors that you pose in certain ways to make it appear the picture is   alive  .  You can be sky diving riding on a magic carpet in King Kongs grip etc.  We edited our pictures once home and they are wonderful!  Highly recommend this museum!!

We had a wonderful time with our taxi tour guide, Mr Ko竊?遙섉닇?? I highly recommend to travel around Jeju island together with Mr Ko. He was very willing to fit in all the attractions that we wanted to go, and gave his recommendations to great locals attractions as well. He was always on time and gave accurate time estimates for traveling distances.Many times he became our photographer and helped to create wonderful memories of our trip. His rates are very affordable and he knows the history of Jeju-do like the palm of his hand.Being able to speak Mandarin fluently, it was definitely a plus point for our family in terms of communication. Also, he drives a jumbo taxi, which allows us to fit our luggage comfortably as a family of four.If you are ever in Jeju island, do ring him up at the following:Phone: +82-10-3698-2854Email: jejeksj@naver.comWechat: jejeksj2854

We had a short very informative visit at this village as part of a day tour. There are many old-style buildings. Very interesting. A very friendly local man explained us the houses, the surroundings and the past way of living there. We tasted some fermented tea. It was very nice. They sell the tea at 40000 KRW. We would have bought a smaller quantity for maybe 10000 if offered, but they had only the large units at 40000.

We drove there and parking is free. The whole experience will take about less than 2hours? About 45mins to walk all the way inside to the end of the cave and another 45mins out. So remember to empty your bladder before entering. There is no loo inside the cave.The cave is cold. About 15 degree celcius? Luckily there is no wind. The ground is made up of rocky bits, and the place is constantly damped and slippery. So wear a light jacket and confortable shoes.Although there are lights in the cave, they are pretty dimmed. Not brightly lit. We used the torchlight function in our phones to further assist us to see the rocky ground. It is not unusual to carry a small portable torchlight if you want. Im not a person who likes cave, but well.. it is an experience i guess.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

We caught the Nanta show in Jeju and it was such a fun night for the family. It is a combination of comedy, musical, martial art and drums. Though a Korean production with a Korean context but the storyline was kept simple and easy to understand. For a show that ran an hour and a half long, the performers were really awesome with great stamina! They kept their energy high up until the end, without missing a beat. Nanta is also known for its audience participation and without giving the plot away, this was done with a delightful, surprising twist. One that you should experience yourself if you ever get the chance to catch the show.

We came to this village with our hired taxi driver. The driver had apparently informed the staff in this village in advance, because a Chinese-speaking woman came out to greet us just as we approached the village. The woman spent the next ten minutes bringing us to different places around the village and giving a brief introduction. We learnt a bit from her about their traditional way of living and even saw a live black pig in captivity. She then brought us to a room saying we could take a rest and had a sip of their tea since the weather was warm. For the next 20 minutes, she tried to persuade us to buy the pills which she claimed to be made from bones of Jeju horses and a bottle of tea, costing a total of 190,000 Korean won. When we said we weren't keen, she was flabbergasted and said everyone who came before us bought items from here. We still refused to buy and returned to our taxi. She followed us to our taxi and spoke in Korean to the taxi driver. Didn't know what she was saying but she might be complaining. She then asked us what could we have bought by not spending 190,000 Korean won here. I replied: a lot of things. We didn't like her tone and told the driver to drive off. It was a waste of our time coming here. We didn't have any time to wander around the village by ourselves and hence no photos. It seemed the main purpose was to sell those items to us.

We came here early in the morning (5:30am) and began the hike up. It seems to be free admission before sunrise. Unfortunately, we did not see the sun rising from the ocean perhaps it was because of the fog. The sky just became brighter and brighter. We just took some photos and descended. On the way down, the sun finally made its appearance. Beautiful! There is also a women divers place below close to the coast. Cafes like Paris Baguette, isaac toast and dunkin' donuts are just nearby the parking lot.

Wasn't aware that some of the restaurants don't serve individual. Wanted to try Dombedon as it was highly recommended by friends and online raves, but was turned away in the face as they not only refuse to serve one-person (what if I can eat 2 pax portion?), they did not bother to offer other food options at all.Disappointed yet no choice, so I tried my luck at other restaurants - the one beside it was alright to serve even for one pax. Order their grilled black pork belly and it was tasteful. The side dishes were plentiful! However it was not especially fantastic with wow factor (considering it is the famous Black Pork Street area). So I guess it really depends on individual visitors. Do visit later in the day, as not all restaurants are open early.
Was on the list of coach tour, so no choice. Great if you like that sort of thing. Boring, if not! You can always purchase your usual holiday tack at the end.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Very pretty beach on a sunny day. The colour of the water is so beautiful. Nicely prep walkway all along the whole beach area. Lots of places for coffee and a quick lunch. We had dinner at a local eatery, the owner was nice and friendly.  He helped BBQ our black skin pork belly for us. So yummy with water Kimchi and beer.

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

Today me and other guest are very lucky that the hostel owners very kind and friendly gave us a ride back to hostel, on the way back, he just de route to show us this place which near to love land, it's just a very short distance which the road seems like is going up slop, but, when the car put on free gear at the starting point, the car is actually keep moving on downhill. Visitors having fun by placing drinking water bottles on the road and let the bottle roll on its own. Personally, nothing very special, its just kind of illusions optic.

Tip: when you are on that road uphill, please put the car into NEUTRAL gear & switch OFF your engine. That's the only way to test. You will then see that the car is indeed going uphill when gravity tells you that you should be descending downhill on that slope.Having the engine on would offset the effect.Try it.

Though Udo is a small island, no matter you are renting bicycle/moto or even treking, its easy to get lost especially those tourists with limited Korean. So, just share my experience, make sure where you are onboard the island. There are 2 ports, please check the leaflet the ticket office pass to you. It helps to fix all troubles or uncertain durinf Udo trip.GPS is not quite user friendly there. When you clear the starting point, basically you can follow the simple map. Pls remind that you can use return ticket depart from either ports. Don't be panic. Check the leaflet again, don't throw it away! Enjoy, really a nice place and recommend to stay 1 night in the island too!

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This place is such a gem ? literally ?? awe found it by accident and were blown away. Seriously one of the best parts of the trip! Highly suggest as a couple or with friends. (Solo is fine too, honestly)

This place is AMAZING. I can't describe with words how incredible it was so I will upload pictures too. I visited this place during the Jeju Olle Walking Festival and it was my favorite place. I highly recommend to visit this place. If you can, do Route 10 of the Jeju Olle Walking and you would come across this place. Also, in that place you can found ladies who are fishing and preparing dishes right away. You can try raw fish from Jeju right there. We tried and it was delicious!

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This park provides a pleasant, albeit uninspiring, afternoon. It's across from a pretty beach, has some nice landscaping, a sampling of lava tubes, and a some nice gardens. I wouldn't recommend driving all the way to the west side of the island just to visit Hallim, but if you're in the area, it's worth a few hours.

This museum, which focuses on the women divers of Jeju, is well designed and well laid out. It offers a fascinating look into the lives (past and present) of these divers, who spend up to 2 minutes underwater at a time without any breathing apparatus to catch abalone and other sea life. Our guide told us that the divers' current age range is 55 to 85. Younger women have no interest incontinuing this cultural tradition, which is an incredibly difficult way to earn a living and to help support a family.Nicely curated, the museum offers an excellent film about the divers and shows various aspects of their lives, including past and current swim wear. the tools that have been used, models of fishing villages and the Jeju traditional fishing boat. I thoroughly enjoyed this close look at a rare way of life that likely won't be around much longer.

This market was near our hotel so we came by here a few times in the evenings (and a couple times in the day time). Mostly because we were trying to find this fried chicken restaurant that never seemed to be open and we kept going back to try to find it. Don't come here expecting a night market extravaganza like other parts of Asia. This is more strictly a   market   market, though there are lots of restaurants that have take-out. There are a few street food stalls, so you can get your fix in a couple spots. Definitely make sure you try the orange juice from one of the sellers here, Jeju has amazing oranges (and tangerines). There are some souvenir type places here, but nothing special. We bought some of the chocolates because they were dirt cheap and wanted to try them, but when we got home and ate them they were just waxy and artificial tatsing (you'll see which chocolates I mean when you get there. EVERY souvenir seller has them. Even in the airport). We bought some dried mandarins from the same vendor, and they were pretty good. We also bought a bunch of oranges to bring around with us as snacks while we were driving. If you've been to markets in Asia before, this will be nothing special. But if you're looking for something to do, it's probably worth visit - wouldn't go out of my way for it though.

This is similar to Dongdaemun market concept in Seoul though this time around so many oranges, Jeju oranges. They are all of the same price, you got your numbers, there is no need to go further. The famous Jeju oranges looked fresher here though I think more expensive than those sold at the Dragon cliff site ? another friend had bought hers there. I am assuming that all other things go the same way here at Dongmun market, so we didn?t venture further in. Parking is a hassle if you are driving a rented car, I saw yellow lines everywhere and cars parked almost everywhere.

This is not really part of our tour in Jeju but since I researched on how to enjoy the tour with 30+ friends, I chanced upon this garden maze near Manjanggul lava tubes site (as in 500m away only).I really recommend this to friends and families who'd like to solve a mystery together and have fun doing it. The price in finishing the maze is a banner and the right to be the first to ring the bell.Please try the ice cream at the exit. You'll enjoy it after an exhilirating yet fun game (30 minutes estimated)

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a great show reenacting the life of Genghis Khan. The horsemanship and acrobatics are amazing and the riders, I believe, are all horsemen/women from Mongolia. There is also horse riding, but the guide maintains control of the reins.  The show is narrated in Korean and some Mandarin, but the action speaks for itself. It is a little out of the way, but if you rent a car or have some form of transportation I highly recommend it!

This is a facility that houses multiple attractions  and they are all basically geared toward separating the tourist from his or her money. Notwithstanding this  our family had a great time spending a couple of hours here. The main attraction appears to be the indoor cart racing track. It's not cheap  around KRW 40 000 for a package that includes 10 minutes on the track and a ticket to the   unique objects   museum. We actually found the items in the museum quite entertaining - objects that trick your eye  weird inventions. The go cart driving was a bit disconcerting (no helmets  no apparent real concern for safety) but in the end it was fun. I was glad I was on the track with just another father-son pair. On the way out  my kid bought carrots for horses that were in a corral  and the guy there was nice enough to take my kid around a lap on the horse (again  no safety gear). My kid was fine but I was glad when both the go cart ride and the horseride finished without any problems.If you are desperate to kill a couple of ours and the weather is bad  this may be a good place to go with tweens or teens. They also offered a   Survival Game   attraction which looked like it was done with laser-tag type guns (not paintball).

This is a beautiful waterfall that empties directly into the sea. Once at the bottom the mist was very refreshing on a hot day. There are places where kids can wade but I'd recommend water shoes. I saw an adult sandal get swept into the sea. I brought my two kids (age 8 and 4). At the bottom of the stairs there were some very big rocks that were difficult for my 4 year old to navigate, had to carry him part of the way. My 8 year old did just fine. We didn't have water shoes and even though they had fun, they would have been a lot more comfortable with better foot protection. Good site, family friendly with some caution due to big rocks/slippery, not good for toddlers or smaller.

This huge place has many shops and stalls selling household items, fish and seafood.   And there is also the food street selling all kinds of local food.   Just be careful and remember which gate/entrance you enter or else you may find yourself lost and spend time trying to find your way out.

This high peak volcano is worth going for climbing... We went with my friend early march, the path was still snowyall the way!  Better to bring some equipement although it is possible to rent shoes at the convenient store down there.We were in march in a very low touristic season so it was quite nice to hike under the frozen pine trees with a beautiful blue sky. I think in high season on weekend, it could be crowdy! As it is a volcano, the walk is really sportive, meaning 6-10% continously during 2h. Get the first plane area, bring some candy bar or fruit, water of course, you will be enjoy this break on the roof of south Korea :=)

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The three days of touring were really excellent. We saw so much, way more than we could have achieved if we just hired a car and drove ourselves. June was a very friendly and knowledgeable guide, and she continued to maintain a flexible approach throughout the tour, adjusting itineraries according to how we felt and how our kids were doing. She also chose some great lunch restaurants for us, based on our tastes, and we really enjoyed those lunch experiences in Korean restaurants with her.

The temperature drops dramatically after you descend 15 stairs into the cave entrance.  There was a cloud that had formed at the entrance due to the humidity which was really cool to see.  Walked about a km to the end where there is a lava column - a frozen in time dripping of lava from above.  Fascinating walk, lots of people (some in heels which I wouldn't recommend).  Really beautiful way to spend an hour or so.  Especially when it is super hot and humid outdoors!

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The place is small. According to the guide (a man who lives there), that is his house passed down to him by his ancestors. He speaks English and some of our Malay language (impressive). It was very compact with the history of the island, culture, food, the roles of men/ women in Jeju, architecture, etc. He was a fun man with a lively way of presenting the information. I think it was excellent. Listening to him is like reading a small introductory chapter about Jeju. There was no fee collected, I appreciate that. However, at the end of the visit, he showed us some local products which we happily bought (the tea) because the children like it.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.
The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

The park is a great snapshot of what the island has to offer.  The gardens highlight a number of different plant species as well as shelter the lava tube which is both breathtaking and refreshing is the weather outside is toasty hot.  There are bonsai exhibits, traditional korean village exhibitions and even an aviary.  Very neat and pleasant way to spend an afternoon.

The maze park is suitable for photo-shoots, the beautiful alley filled with green-leaves and also stone-walls. There are 3 maze available in this place. The first one is the easiest one, round shaped, and we can have a shortcut just by going to the side way. The side way also makes us easier to travel through the second maze. The third maze is the hardest, where it doesn't have a shortcut, and we have to go through the map by ourselves. Interesting if we are travelling with our little ones. On my last trip here at the end of September 2015, it was raining so bad, the wind was also very strong. So avoid to come here when the weather forecast predicts the weather to be raining.

The market is full of local appeal with fresh fruits, vegetables, and local snacks to seafood and various sundries. A great way to spend a few hours walking around, doing some souvenir shopping, and eating local treats. The market is full of warm and friendly people who are interested and appreciative of the tourist that venture to visit the attraction. I would recommend to any one who appreciates the local things about traveling.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).
