The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The Jeju Mysterious Road, also known as Dokkaebi Road, lies on a hill at the foot of a mountain, and connects two major highways on Jejudo Island. It has earned its name, as objects and liquid appear to roll and flow up the hill instead of down, when, in fact, such image of gravity defiance is an optical illusion rendered by the seemingly high surroundings.

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of   impressive historical sites   compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.
The black pork was really good. I love BBQ pork belly, but the black pork was a tad different -in a good way. It had more flavor and was more tender. I would go here again to eat!

the best thing to do in jeju, it wasnt that attractive for me while i search udo online, my friend made me go with her, when i got there, im so glad i did it, it was so laid back, so nice, the circle island bike was awesome, the sunset, nice people. we enjoyed it a lot and forgot the boat time. we were late for the boat back to jeju, so we have to paid for personal boat, was way so expensive.

Such an awesome excursion. Doesn?t take too long and there are cool explanation signs along the way. Highly recommend and is super fun. Gets chilly so make sure you bring a sweater, it?s a nice escape from the hot humid jeju weather. Easy to park and easy to find.

Spend a couple hours here walking through the village and seeing traditional Korean way of life.  There isn?t much interaction with anything outside of the performance they have, which is 2-3 times a day and with the vendors.  They do offer horse back riding here and you can also have photos taken in a hanbok.

Saw the show with a group of friends, one of whom was selected for the audience participation segment.  This increased the enjoyment for us, but the show was entertaining anyway even for non-Korean speaking people.

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street ? you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

Our guide was very knowledgeable about the history and culture of Jeju, and he recommended some wonderful food and activity options that we hadn't thought of, despite doing some research. Highly recommend this way of experiencing this place!

Our guide brought us here to understand the striking cultural lifestyle of the local folks of Jeju.  The unique and exquisite architectural design of the `primitive'' huts and cottages of the natives was impressive. The pair of well carved and exotic Jeju deities statues that were made from volcanic lava stood spiritually on guard at the entrance. The sculptures matched harmoniously with the decorative Kimchi clay vases left unattended in the manicured lush green lawn compound displaying a special cultural taste that reminded me of the unique Hindu traditions on the island of Bali. I always think that it is the vibrancy and dynamism of the native folk culture that made certain attractions so special. The unique Alisan native lifestyle in Taiwan is just remarkably outstanding and different from that of the Maori in New Zealand and again, distinctively unique from the Dayaks longhouse traditions. It is thus a pleasure and a must thing to do to visit a folk village in Jeju to look at how the culture of the natives and how it is being preserved here.  We were introduced to a guide speaker who showed us the many agricultural tools used by the local natives but the real commercialized promotion began when we were `lured' into a room with seats and the speaker started marketing a type of drinks made from `Wuweiji' traditional herb that grew in abundance in Jeju and is believed to strengthen and invigorates the mind and body. It looks like another `tourist trap' and on the pretext of going to the toilet, I escaped the aggressiveness of the marketing talk. I wandered around the cottage compound admiring the foliage and the surrounding native architectural designs until my group of friends came out from the promotion. One of my group members was anxious to purchase the `elixir' drinks to enhance her youthfulness and she shared the drinks with the rest in the group.   I came out from the cottage and saw there were many similar cottages around the village and there were many sales talk going on in the other cottages. The admission to this folk village was free but I am not sure if my guide earned any commission from the purchase of the herbal bottled drinks by my friend.Except for the commercialized promotion, it is interesting to visit a folk village in Jeju.

Our family visited   Cheonjiyeon Falls   on June 8th, 2019. To get to the waterfall, you have to walk a lot. There were a lot of small markets that sold simple snacks, which was sweet, but the way to the waterfall was not worth it. Although the way to the waterfall was harsh, still the waterfall was beautiful. I recommend this waterfall to whom that likes walking. If your stamina is poor, you will be tired . I don't think the waterfall was worth walking a lot.

Our children really wanted to spend time on the ocean. This was a great introduction to the power of the sea. Big waves. Rocky coast. Perfect for sea shell collecting, sand castle building, and glimpses of aquatic life. We managed to watch the Haenyo divers bobbing their way across Jungmun Beach and later walked the length of the beach to see their catch.

one of the many trick art museums in Korea. The first bit has the usual pose-with-renaissance-paintings stuff but if you don't have that much time skip that stuff and make your way through to the end where there's a pretty cool arabian nights themed room where you pretend to run from giants climb into the sky or escape over burning bridges. the station where you pretend to skydive while strapped to a backpack on the floor is quite special. warning : wear pants when visiting this museum if you wish to avoid inadvertently flashing other tourists. the sculpture garden is nothing fantastic and   little provence   is a bunch of stuffed dogs dressed in french peasant outfits in a lackluster room.

one of a kind museum... and it was weirdly funny in it's own way.. thankfully my son was asleep all the time... Sells kinky and   bachelor party   stuff... it was quite funny when you are with your friends!!

on reaching the car park ., Go and grab a J - Shape ice cream before you buy the entrance ticket to this Unesco Sights . To those who is not so fit you will be able to rest on the way uphills with the friendly stools provided at different stage of the climb upwards . Wonderful Sight await you on reaching the peak and you will want to catch up on your breadth as you soak in the sights . Never to be missed !!

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Nothing spectacular, but I would recommend watching the sunset from the bridge if you just so happen to be in the area. It is also a short bike ride away from Cheonjiyeon Falls which is a nice site to visit during the evening.

Not suitable for old folks, because is full with rocks.. Better prepare a torch light or you handphone torch light. Inside very dark. The lights not that bright enough. Prevent any injury. Walking distance to the end about 1km, one way. Winter season, very fresh air inside the cave.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.

Nevertheless, people always recommend us to visit this cave when we're in Jeju. what we found is around 2km long cave with cold temperature all the way. if you quite a fan for geology and similar, this cave is exactly for you.the 'main' attraction is located at the very end of the cave. nothing more , nothing less...come if you have free time.. but not suitable for older people due to steep stair and slippery.

My own experience was during dark, and I loved it. There was a spotlight highlighting the rock. Relax listening to the waves coming from the sea to the shore. On the way here I recommend walking through Yongyeon bridge.

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.

Mr Kim, also affectionately known to us as Samchoon was introduced to us by a friend. Even before we arrived in Jeju, he was so ever helpful whenever I had questions about planning the day. He would offer the best ideas and try to accommodate to your requests as much as possible so that your day would be a breeze and convenient. He didn?셳 mind that we stayed almost an hour away from Jeju city and arrives early at our hotel to make sure our day starts off well. He actually does research and make calls for you and made sure that attractions and restaurants are open when you get there. He really goes to the extra mile to put a smile on your face! Not to mention showering our family with little treats and souvenirs. He also made sure my mum who wasn?셳 feeling well is okay and offered to get us some medicine. That really warmed our hearts. He?셲 very familiar with the places and routes in Jeju and knows the best restaurants for quality and value. He drives safely and makes the ride really comfortable. I have to say, most drivers would just drive and drop you at places but he went with us and explain how do we enjoy the best out of the attraction. As a bonus, he?셲 always ready to take the best photos for you without you asking! At the end of the trip, Mr Kim really felt like a family friend to us.You won?셳 regret hiring his taxi tour service when you?셱e in Jeju :??

Maybe we expected too much of the beach but it we didn't enjoyed this beach too well. We hoped for a large beach where you can swim and relax and maybe some small shops/cafe쨈s around to buy some drinks/food. We spent 25 hours and it was enough since it didn't reach our expectations. We stayed at Seogwipo and took the taxi to Jungmun for around 13000 won one-way. The beach is nice/OK but its crowded (July 2018) and the beach is too small. You can't swim because of the waves and only a small area where you can stay. The rest of the beach is for surfing. You can rent two sun beds and one parasol for 40000 Won (only cash) and other services on the beach (that we did not use). The good thing that it is a GS25-store (or 7/11 store don't quite remember) so you can buy drinks and small food. Near the beach there is a small   restaurant   but we didn't it looks so nice to eat there. There's also a restroom available and a parking lot. If you want to relax on the beach I would not recommend this beach. You might skip this beach and try to find another one. If you are in this area/Jungmun maybe its more preferable to stay at a resort.For families with kids; I think this beach would suit very well.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Just makes you wonder nature creativity. Need to have camera able to take photo in low light.Note: Long walk, water dripping, uneven and dark pathway. However don't loose hope, beautiful @ end of tunnel. Worth the efforts.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

I've never done something like this before so it was a first time for me. We tried it in one direction but it didn't work, but when we tried it in the opposite direction (heading away from Loveland), it works and the car accelerated to 13 km/hr whilst on neutral. I would recommend a visit here if you haven't done something like it before.

It's a new experience to us. It's great. Just walk inside the maze until you find the way. Maybe try and get help from your friends who have reached the tower. It's a great activity. Got some traditional games to play as well. There are lots of big fat cats at the ticketing counter. So cute, so fluffy.

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

Its a beautiful and quiet park to visit. Enjoyed the bonsai area and birds area alot with my 5 year old daughter. There are bonsais as old as 300 yrs old! Signages are clear to indicate the different areas in the park.There is a restaurant within the park itself at the folk village, serves korean food and also small food outlets selling convenient food, ice cream, drinks and beer. There is also a herb cafe in the park, selling herbal teas.A place that is away from crowds to spend an afternoon leisurely with your kids.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was a rainy morning that my friend and I visited this cave. We were greeted with a flight of stairs entering the cave. The temperature in the cave was so much lower, approximately 10 degrees celsius. It was dark and slippery too. The further we walked in, the colder it gets. The pathways are actual lava that hardened over the years therefore, it was not a smooth walk. A lot of locals enjoyed their walk, some strolling while youngsters brisk walk, talking and laughing along the way, making the whole cave not too scary. It was a nice morning walk looking through the structure left behind by the once active volcano forming rocks, mini wells naturally. The work of nature. Beautiful!

It was a hot day so felt great to get away from the  heat and descend into the cave. It felt about 10 degrees colder so be prepared with a light jacket. As with all caves, this has rocky wet floors that are very treacherous for those without proper track shoes. Very interesting signboards with geographical  information about the formation of lava caves too.

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? It depends. If you're the kind of person who couldn't be bothered with science, optical illusions and whatnot, you'd be better off checking out the snack shops nearby, observing the other tourists and their interesting behavior, or skipping this place altogether.However, if you've always been interested in physics and seemingly unexplainable phenomenons which you know are actually explainable, give yourself an hour or more to thoroughly check this place out. Photography lovers may also deem this place worth their time.The bottom line? If you're heading to another tourist attraction (e.g. Hallasan) and it's on the way, and you have time to spare, feel free to check this place out. Otherwise, don't bother.

It is surely a must-go attraction in Jeju. With only KWN2000 (adults) to this nice park, it is reallt worth it. Too many steps in descending and ascending way, not a wheelchair or elderly friendly place

It is an old village that show us the homes for the people of Jeju in the past few hundred years. We have been guided through the village by a lady, who speaks very good Chinese's Mandarin. After the tour, they try to sell their products. Some of those are quite expensive. The thing that made us a little unhappy is   I think they have been trying too hard to make us buy something   so we end-up to select the cheapest product but then it became worst when the price was 10X different from what was being offered. It was already nicely packed and we did not want to make her unhappy so we just swipe the card.Anyway, it could be a communication error but both of us are Chinese and heard the same thing. It is a nice place but just be a little careful when you purchase those items.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

In this cave, you're allowed to walk about one kilometer in the lava tube where you'll find a lot of variation in the formation and environment. It's a lot of space in one of the tubes (the other one was closed off during our visit). In the tube, there has been several different lava levels and different factors, creating unique patterns on the walls, floor and ceiling. It's recommended to bring something warm down the cave, since it's a bit chilly.Along the way, there is several signs about detail information (both in Korean and English) about the different shapes and things in the cave.

In general, Jeongbang Falls is a nice looking waterfall that plunges into the blue ocean. Entry fee is low too at 2000 krw. However, this place is way, way too crowded with tourists. Chances of you getting 'photo bombed' is 100%, unless you risk your safety by walking over the rocks to the point near the waterfall like most tourists did. Hence, it is not recommended for travellers with walking difficulties.

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

If you?re driving around Jeju Island, this place is a must. It took me a while to figure out what was the big deal (mysterious) about this road but after I figured out the way it was described to be, it was definitely cool and somewhat mysterious. So here it goes: you drive upto the starting point of mysterious road and put the car in neutral gear. The road certainly looks like and uphill, however the car drives forward until 100m to the end of the mysterious road. Anti-gravity huh? I?m not sure of the scientific explanation for this phenomenon, but I recommend you experience this if you?re driving around Jeju Island. Takes only 15 minutes and certainly worth the time and experience!

If you want to come here to buy Innisfree products, the offering are far lesser than what you can find in Myeongdong. The only attraction here is the soap making experience and a small piece of tea plantation. There are no location-only products sold here. Very limited merchanise on sale. The staffs are unfriendly and always pulling a long face. Not worth visiting.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you love Alice in Wonderland you will love Maze Land.  The mazes are fun to explore and make you feel like a kid again. Also, the statue garden and rose garden are worth a look.  A really fun, unique way to spend a day on Jeju.

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.

If you have some time to spare, it is recommended to check out this place. However if you are in a really short trip, IMO i dont think its worth to drive here as its just a road, unless you are on your way to love land.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.

If you find yourself in Jeju (May to June preferably) Halla is something that must be done. As the island is so small you can see the mountain no matter where you are. It sits there calling to you to climb it and you should. It is not one the most difficult climbs I have ever had, the end was a bit bad because there had be a storm that had damaged parts of the path. It is absolutely picturesque especially for the colour changes you see. I would suggest going up the easy path and going down the easy path for those who have trouble managing such large mountains, but no matter which you choose just go. The canteen at the halfway point was only serving instant noodles, so bring your own grub to be safe. Also have your pickup scheduled accordingly as transportation on the bottom parts of certain paths are almost non-existant.

If you are looking for a remote island off the coast of Jeju then this might not be for you. However, if you are after an island that is a short ferry ride away and has many activities to offer then this is it! Udo is beautiful, and attracts many tourists especially in the summer time. You can rent a bicycle for the day at about 10,000-12,000W, or rent an electronic bike/scooter thing (with an international drivers license). Caves, mountains, as well as many beaches to explore. Stay the weekend on Udo or ride the ferry back to Seongsan, you'll have a great time :).

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

If we had known that the rock formation was disappointing, we wouldn't have taken the effort to get lost on our way there! We went there at night, and all we saw were a few spotlights shining upon a small piece of rock jutting out of the land mass - there are other wayyyy better ways to spend your limited time in Jeju. Seriously! Don't bother please.
I was there to see the sunset, which was really amazing. The entry was closed but we went to the volcano anyway. I recommend going there after Udo island.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was not sure what to expect when we went to Hallim Park, but we really enjoyed it. It's a really nice walk, with flowers, statues waterfalls, caves and animals. It's nice to get away from the city noises if you have been on the mainland for a while. It's not a place you can spend an entire day, and for us was a bit of a trek to get there so make sure you plan your day to only be there a couple of hours.

I was hoping to see how magnificient the lava is in one of the widest lava tube before going into the Manjang Cave. It is quite disappointing to realise that the cave is not entirely illuminated. The lighting is minimal in the cave which made walking and lava observation really difficult. I was going with my mum of around 60 years old, it is really difficult for her to see clearly in the tunnel. And the fact that you have to walk for  ~1 km into the tunnel and then the same way back is not entiring pleasing. When I was walking down the tunnel, I always thought   there will be better illumination/rocks in the next turn  . However, it was quite disappointing that this happens only at the end of the tunnel where you saw an illuminated lava pillar. I would recommend you to go to other caves if you want to see the lava clearly.

I visited this place because of friends' recommendation. In the end, I was glad that I made it. It took me 3.5 hours for the whole trip. During this trip, I met a few friendly Korean people, which gave me a great company. there are lots of birds and greens along the away.In the summer, pls put sunscreen on your skin before/during the trip. Otherwise, you will get sunburn easily.

I think this will be a fun experience for the family especially with small kids. I am not young anymore but it was rather interesting and fun for me as well. Not as easy as I thought and it took me 30mins to navigate through...for price of 3300won, it is a pretty economical way to spend a few light hearted hours after all the serious geographical sights in Jeju.

I really liked this cave, or lava tube as it's also called. I was hoping for more stalagmites and such but the lack thereof doesn't bring down the points due to it's massive size and length. There are also signs along the way with information about the   tube   in different languages. I really recommend giing to this place when you go to Jeju!!

I moved to the U.S. (from Korea) 26 years ago when I was 15. I have been coming back to visit almost every year in the past 15 years or so and visited Jeju five times thus far. I don't get to take long weeks off from work, so I always try to pack as many activities into any given trip, so I squeezed this one in on my way back from a day trip to Udo (which is my favorite place in Korea). I wanted to pay this place a visit because I came to learn of what 4.3 incident last year, and I didn't want to pass up the opportunity to learn more about it.The memorial hall was very well organized with plenty of pictures, exhibits, and videos to see. The history before and after the incident was explained thoroughly, and even the resistance movements in other parts of the world are also included in the exhibit hall. My 16-year-old kid, who almost never bothers to read through anything at museums, was taking photos and reading through the exhibits, which I found impressive.My appreciation for the island (and its residents) grew tenfold after the visit to this memorial hall. I highly recommend this place to anyone who likes history/Jeju.\臾몄쇰＊? ＿?깊 理50 댁ⓒ\ 由щ럭??댁⑹＿? 湲곗쇨 ???＿? 湲?濡  以＿?  \. ??ъ 愿?ъ 遺＿?ㅼ대?? 二쇰＿? 泥대 醫＿? 遺＿?ㅼ? ＿?援щ 瑗 諛⑸Ц 蹂쇰□? 듯 μ쇨 ⓒ媛\ ⑸.

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I heard from the owner of our guesthouse that this place isn?t always open because of the tides and weather, so if you have the chance to go, take it. It?s an amazing rock formation, but unlike the ones that you can see at a distance, like Oedolgae and the Jungmun Daepo, you can actually walk on it. That rocks. It took us a while ? was it an hour? ? to walk along the perimeter of this massive rock. The terrain is not smooth ? think of desert sands except that the undulating surface is made of rock instead of sand, so wear study shoes that won?t split because of the damp. It looks like a movie set -- for an alien planet. Really, I didn?t know such a place existed on earth.If I were taking someone around Jeju, I?d recommend this place and I would definitely come back so we can exclaim together.Where: Seogwipo west coast

I have been here several times, I really do enjoy it.  It is just an easy and fun way to spend a day. Lots of photo opportunities.I see they occasionally offer glass blowing classes. I have never done this, but it is on my list of things to try!ProTip: There are 2 stores filled with glass items for sale.  Some tacky, but mostly rather reasonably priced gift ideas. Plus, lots of  cool looking jewelry.

I checked out Samseonghyeol not even knowing what it was exactly but went anyway because it was close to my hotel and it was some sort of a cultural sight.  Upon entering I learned it was basically three unimpressive holes where three demi-gods supposedly emerged from.  While the main sight isn?t impressive, it was still a nice park to walk around in during spring with the cherry blossoms.  It?s definitely not a sight worth going out of your way to see unless you?re interested in Korean legends.

I can't recommend Mr Jang highly enough! He is a fabulous guide who is very generous with his time and will tailor the day to suit the customer completely. If you are short on time, then this is absolutely the way to see Jeju. Mr Jang is friendly and easy-going and giving. If you're going to book a trip to see Jeju then go with Mr Jang!

I believe this place can be so much fun then how we experienced it. We were there quite late, hence the volunteers (as the tour guides) were in an extreme rush to go home. Totally understandable. However they were still nice enough to show us around. Interesting historical facts about the Koreans in Jeju-do and their houses. They promoted horse face cream towards the end of the tour. Apparently the appropriate time to visit this place is between 11 am - 1 pm or definitely way BEFORE 4.30 pm.

I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

I  don't like Teddy bears because I am a adult. But my friend is big fan of teddy bears. I don't get it.There are tons of teddy bears and the bears cute and lovely.In my eyes, big bears are much better than othersAnyway we spent few hours in the Museum and enjoyed the museum even me.

Here is much more the beauty of the man made. The Bonsai garden made in an Arboretum which otherwise would've been an entirely sandy/rocky area. A good place to stroll completely away from the coastline. But given that Jeju's primary attractions are natural, spend time here only after seeing the real natural stunners.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.
Had a great time to find my way out of the maze!!! The owner of this place, has cats family! They are friendly cats of black and white fur with spots!

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

Expensive pork which is only found in jeju?Cant make out the difference between normal pork except for the price.Anyway should try once since is so famous.My family dined at Dombedon during the 1st day, compare to the another black pork restaurant in jeju (Donsadon), all of us voted for donsadon. (better taste)Anyway, the owner of Dombedon is very friendly and serve us well.both the black pork restaurant have chinese speaking staff

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

Before we arrive, the tour guide told us the story of the dragon and how the mark of the dragon landed create all the cracks on ground. At night with spot lights, it added some mysteries of the legend and when we climb all the way down hill at the dragon head,. it complete the story itself. A good trip full of imagination

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

At eye level, the short stretch looked like an upward sloping road, but it was actually a 3 degrees downhill slant. A bit out of the way, would not recommend making a trip there unless you're from Jeju-si enroute to Hallasan National Park. Many of the 'mysterious bottle rolling uphill' videos have been posted on youtube in case you want to see the mystery! The real attraction here was the huge iconic black pig family statue. It was detailed and incredible. LOL

As a bear lover, I enjoy this museum & appreciate all the hard work put into each & individual presentation & its theme. Be warn that its really for the young & young at heart. My only regret is that I missed the outdoor cafe. Didnt realised after I exited & look down thru the windows. Must have missed the signages? Overall , a good way to spend 1-2 hours

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

Numerous rare and even some endemic species are found here. Concerning wildlife, what visitors are most likely to see are the Roe Deer. These small deer are found throughout the park, and as I hiked quitely we came upon 5-10 throughout our 6 hour trek.In 2007 Hallasan became part of the Unesco World Heritage site calle   Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes  . This honor is only bestoyed on the most unique and important natural and cultural sites on Earth. Hallasan is a geolocial wonder, and is comparable to some of the most iconic national parks in the United States. The park probably deserves 2 days as visitors will want to hike to the crater lake on Hallasan peak, but the entirity of the park holds many exceptional sites. Many trips to Jeju island are scheduled around their trek at Hallasan. Make sure to bring plenty of water, and keep an eye on weather conditions. Hikers must start early if they want to hike to the peak, late arrivals will not be permitted to make the full trek as it takes anywhere from 6-10 hours depending on your pace.

We went there during the first weeks of October and it was very green and lush. I think in summer and spring it's gonna be even more pretty. Different types of Korean housing and different lifestyle (farmer student worker etc.) are portrayed very well and the tools they used are there to see. There is also a convenience store near the entrance which doesn't work with cash.
Good experience and a cooling walk underground. I was expecting something more and was disappointed when reached the end. Took about an hour.

Go there to buy the various teas and even chocolates! Didn't have much time to spend to go through the museum. In fact we had our drinks at innisfree instead because the place was super packed! It felt like a starbucks during rush hour. And this place was huge so that's saying something. The outdoors so pretty for pictures. Take advantage of it.

For those going to Seoul Lotte world after visiting Jeju please note that there are some pictures available in Seoul Lotte world too. Having said that i still highly recommend you to visit this place. The photo is funny and your kids will surely love it. We spend around 2 hours inside taking all kinds of photo. The air-conditional place makes the stay more comfortable. There is an out-door venue but as it is still hot (9 sept) outside we have given it a miss.

Except a receptionist  very good place.I strongly recommend this place.Museum  Korean mandarin cookies making  foot bath  a large botanical garden  picking Korean mandarins.You can stay just a hour  but You'd better use more time.It's not free  but absolutely not expensive.
Estimate to spend 2 hours. wear good shoes and jacket. The cave is quite cold and wet. Uneven roads and required to walk on few staircase too. but overall experience is great.
Enjoyed the displays and live shows there. Ticket prices are quite steep but worth it if you have about 2 hours to spend there.
