review: Crowded with tourists during lunch hours. We had a green tea cakes amd icecream. They are wonderful. Service staff speaks good command of English. Highly recommended.

can spend a couple of hours reading the many Greek myths and learn about the many names which you have heard of often.  Do the 3 quizes at the end to see if you have missed anything (or you already knew about it much).  The Trckeye Museum is at the same place and there is also a mini- maze to keep the family and children occupied.
Built within a mall like building the Alive museum is a fun place to spend 2 hours in and capturing memories for your trip.
Beautiful place with huge plots of green tea plantation. Lots of tourist. Popped by innisfree next door. Beautiful cafe space. Crowded with tourists. Spend an hour there. Nothing much really.

Awesome Museum! Has everything for singles and couples who want to visit! It was only 20 minutes from the hotel and the taxi service was great! Spend about 2 hours with the gift shops mini museums inside and looking at the statues. It was raining however the staff was prepared for the rain and had rain coats available for 2000 won! I would definitely recommend!

Amazing rock formations. We spent about 45 mins at the park. Its a very well-pathed park with some stairs; suitable for most people. We went in July and it was super hot. I'd recommend going either early morning or an hour or so before sunset.  The adult tickets are krw 2000 each. I think it's a fair price.

Admission fee: 9k each person. Went about noon time. It is located near Believe it or Not museum and teddy bear museum. We spent about 3 hours in this musueum as we took really a lot of pictures here...but at the end you will be so tired with all the postures of taking the pictures! We gave up taking some pictures near the end :PAt the start there aren't many people but more people start coming when it gets later. Go early if possible. Else it will be difficult for you to take pictures and you have to waste time waiting.

A very fun place. My 1.5 to and 5yo enjoyed it very much. Reasonable priced (27000won for whole family play for 2 hours). Baby is free. A-must do thing for Tayo fans! Though not very English friendly. There's a cafeteria where you can eat and drink (you can ask for English menu). Staff are friendly. There are different colouring sheets of Tayo and friends that you can take for kids to colou

A quaint but charming little place with lots of teddy bears! Highlight was the Greek Gods teddy bears and the teddy bear art gallery. Fun photo opportunities and a teddy bear safari to boot. It is an imitation attraction but not a bad place to spend an hour.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .
A good place to spend 1-2 hours. The green tea plantation area was well-maintained. Great green tea latte. I thought they should offer sampling of various merchandise.
A casual walk to various areas (with different themes) within the park was very relaxing. The park was well maintained and landscaped.  It deserved spending a few hours visiting interesting areas.

You should visit the Folk Village if you : Want to see how they lived back in those days, you love to watch Korean drama's, you have time to kill or you want to keep the kids occupied.Overall not a bad place to spend a few hours

You can easily spend 2 or 3 hours walking around the stones and getting to know the  past lifestyle of the island population as well as the geological history of Jeju. Volcanic rocks are exposed as real art pieces in a museum, allowing you to have a different look at them and admire the work of nature.

Yongmeori Beach is a great place to visit, the erosions along the coast is just amazing. The place is just located along the coast, there are no fences or anything to keep you off. The place may not be open to public every day because if the winds are too strong they do not allow entry, so you may want to check before you come. It gets quite windy and there is not much shelter so remember to wear a jacket and bring a hat. I recommend spending around 1.5 to 2 hours here, it will make a great walk.

Wow-this place is huge, gorgeous and meticulously maintained. Spent 3 hours there wandering aimlessly, just loved it and the calming vibe. Just wish the shops and vendors stayed until 7 pm close as I missed the chance to try cactus ice cream. Don't drive past this place if u have an hour or a few to spend.
Working hours from 8AM (or 9?) till 5PM.Spend 2-3-4 hours there, many flowers (in season), animals, folk village inside, two interesting caves. Just nice! :)

What a breathtaking, incredible walk through a well-manicured garden with hundreds of bunjae (bonsai) trees lining the path. Everything is so green and there are so many excellent places for photos. Great to spend at least an hour enjoying the nature.

Went on a Friday afternoon at the suggestion of our hired taxi driver even though it was not in our planned itinerary as we happened to be in the area for lunch. There was no other visitor in there other then my friend and I. For 9000 won, there are many other attractions in Jeju to see. The place is small and just filled with colourful glass exhibits and decorations... we completed visiting in less than half an hour as it is a very small place.

We went with friends to visit the museam and for all of us it was quite entertaining. Really nice recreation of historial moments and famous personalities   Teddy Bear Style  .Since I am a big fan of k drama Goong / Princess Hours, for me it was a must to visit the Museum and I was not dissapointed at all. There is an specific exhibition of this drama and it is amazing, showing the most memorable scenes as seen on TV and also there is a music video. Loved it.Finally, don't miss   Teddy Bear Elvis Music Show  .

We went there for the DIY soap workshop. Fun and easy, just follow the steps in the video showed at the computer in front of you. You can then make a unique soap of your own. There is also a cafe for light lunch. And many Innisfree product to buy ad well ! A nice place to spend an hour or so during the raining day.

We spent may be half an hour here and had a good time. The maze is very pretty and you don't see mazes made from trees in the US any more, so this was a treat. The mazes were not difficult, but can be confusing. The admission was quite reasonable, so I do recommend this place if your family is into mazes. Oh, there were a lot of cats roaming the ground and made good subjects for photos.

We didn't know what we could do with that one hour before sunset, so we decided to relive our childhood by going to this maze park. We completed the maze in slightly less than an hour. But boyfriend wanted to have some more fun by collecting all the ink stamps at various points in the maze, so he attempted the maze again and he got himself lost in the park while I waited for him at the elevated finishing point. It was fun. For children, if they managed to collect all the stamps, they will give a small gift from the park. We got a KimYoung Maze Park pen although we are not children :x The lady was nice. haha :)
We could spend hours in this market. There are alots of yummy foods, fresh seafoods, sashimi that can make you droll. Fresh fruit and the jeju orange so tasty and fresh.

We arrived at 3:30 on Udo, and rented 2 electric scooters from a stand close to the dock. It was a bummer that i couldn't rent a real scooter (you need to bring your int. license btw). It was a lot slower, so it gave us more time to have a more relaxing ride. We visited 2 beaches, and both of them were very clear and very clean (Beware of silver fish though깎). Also, you wouldn't want to miss haha hoo because my friend told me they're incredibly popular. We got some peanut ice cream, and some tea with honey and the special jeju fruit that i can't name (which was absolutely incredible!!!) since everything else was sold out. I would have loved to spend more time there because we only got 3 hours on Udo. In all, it was an amazing and memorable experience.

Very underwhelmed. Arrived by ship & took free port shuttle into Jeju-si (capital) & dropped by the Jungang underground shopping street & Guandeokjeong. Walked past Yongyeon Bridge & past park to Dongduam rock. Pleasant walk. Then back to find Black Pork St, but didn't try it as we had heard it was nothing special. Enough to fill in a day (about 6 hours ashore.) Friends who went on a trip round the island said it wasn't terribly interesting & worth the cost. Do pick up a map from the tourist info kiosk, not far from where you arrive, then you can walk round sights described
Unless you are a geologist, you probably only need to spend an hour or 2 max here.  Yes scenery is unique and be sure takes lots of pictures.  But depending on the day it can get really crowded.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

This place is huge, with lots of plants, flowers, caves to see. Though it may not be extra especial since it felt so artificial, it is still a cool place to visit. Stroll and take lots of pictures with friends or family. Don't join the tour because they only allow 1-1.5 hours and you'll end up just walking and not really appreciating the things that you will see.

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.

This market sells many goods. I would recommend it for buying souvenirs from Jeju, like chocolate crunch and chocolate. There were also shoes and clothes for sale but not so fashionable. There are many shops selling dry and wet goods, mandarin oranges and other Jeju products. It is really large and you can spend quite a few hours there. Good for wet weather as it is covered.

This is a relatively new Buddhist temple build in the 1990's.  Setting is wonderful in a set-back in an Oreum (a subsidiary volcano   mountain  ).  Gardens in front are very nice.  If you like to see Buddhist temples this is probably the biggest and nicest one on Jeju; I recommend visiting.  It's free just walk around.  Allow about 1 hour.

This is a nice place for sightseeing and exploring the Jeju waterfalls. There was a roughly 5-10 minutes walk before reaching the waterfall, which was fairly simple and pleasant too. The waterfall does not differ greatly from your other waterfalls, so if you?re looking for a unique and different sightseeing experience, I suggest giving this a miss. However, it was still quite magnificient and beautiful if you enjoy sightseeing and waterfalls. Overall, do spend about an hour here to leisurely stroll and sightsee this Jeju wonder.
This is a must if you have an hour to spend.  The crater is so beautiful, and the sunrise was stunning.  Steps are steep, but worth the 25 minute walk up.

This is a great place for young children, with so many teddy bears to see and to play with. Even my husband and I were kept fully entertained. Inside you can see teddy bears in many different settings, all very cuddly and well presented. What I loved most is the outside area - I could spend hours just watching kids play, and it'll be great to have a picnic in the garden with all the nice surrounding, and with teddy bears of course.

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

They are selling variety of products ranging from skin care, hair care, body care and even food and beverage. Their skin care products are popular in Korea and well known. Besides, if you have times try to buy a hand made soap pack and try to make the soap yourself. It might take time around 1 to 2 hours as there are 3 pieces of soap inside the pack. I would strongly recommend you to try this as this is only available in Jeju island not at other's innisfree branch.

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)
There are lots of things to see here, we spend 2 hours here. Beautiful trees, caves, stones, small waterfall. It is all about nature and traditional korea living.

There are 4 main attractions and you easily spend 1.5- 2 hours there, we only go to 2 waterfalls as we afraid there won?t be enough time to go to other places.4 main attractions :Seoningmo bridgeCheonjiyeon Waterfall2nd Waterfall3rd WaterfallSome stairs here and there, don't miss it if you are in Jeju,

The title summed it all up. I love stuffed toys, but even I found the place overpriced and boring. The ones that held my interest were those actual historical bears. But that's the end it. The elvis show was terrible too. We left the place within the hour.  Take your money and time else where. Jeju has more to offer than this!

The theme is good and it is very funny and interesting. Although we arrived the entrance at 18:00, we were able to complete the adventure within half an hour. Highly recommend for you especially with kids.

The spirited garden has a unique and impressive collection of beautiful bonsai trees, stone artwork, and tranquil ponds. Its a great place to spend a couple of hours while visiting Jeju and offers some great photo opportunities. The staff were very kind and helpful.

The soap making workshop is fun and interesting for kids and couples. Innisfree Jeju House is next to the famous O'Sulloc Green tea, you can spend at least 2 to 3 hours in these two placesfor soap making workshop, tea break and photograhping in the tea plantation.
The park is quite big and there are many interesting stuff to see. There's a bonsai garden, a small hanok village, bird park etc. It's quite an interesting place where you can spend a good 2 hour.

The natural beauty of the lava tubes entertained my mother, husband, and myself for nearly two hours of appreciating God's creation. For only 2,000 kw per person, I recommend this highly as one of Jeju's most impressive tourist spots!

The grounds are amazing and beautiful. Different times of year you can see beautiful blooms like azaleas, hydrangeas, bougainvillea, etc. It?s definitely worth some time to see the natural beauty of the flora. The animal enclosures are very disappointing, because as a true natural park, you would expect better conditions for the animals. The caves are a good break from the sun and heat. They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

The cruise ship docked in Jeju South Koren for a few hours. We didn?t plan anything, just walked around downtown.  We saw a flight of stairs, looks like it leads to some metro station, so we went down to take a look. It is a huge underground shopping center. They sell clothing, accessories, shoes and cosmetics. This is a shopper?s haven. They also have free Wi-Fi that you can connect with family and friends. Although we don?t know their language, but the people are very friendly and helpful. I don?t mind to visit Jeju again.Happy Travelling!

The cave takes about an hour, nice walk. Wear sensible shoes as the floor is not even and take a small jacket as it gets colder the further in you go. It was an interesting walk and we got to see bats at the end.
The beach is family friendly with shallow, calm and beautiful color of turquoise water.  White soft sand.  My kids had so much fun snorkeling and chasing small fish for hours.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

Taking ferry to the island with a car is a little bit pricy, so it's better to get and ATV and go around the island. One hour or two chill hours are enough to go around the whole island.Hey!If you are searching for something cheap but decent, then I would recommend hostel called Galaxy in Seogwipo. I was planning to stay there for one night, as I thought it's yet just another cheap hostel, but ended up staying there for 2 nights. There are some beautiful beaches and food places, so you might want to take it easy..If you want some more information on what you can find on the island, you can check out this video: http://youtu.be/X2RwSnOMgYk?list=UUYEqXBrHobdnJF591_o-vcg
Spend at least 2 hours here. Worth the climb. Beautiful scenery. If you bring kids or older adults, it?s worth the walk at the ground level and also to the sea.

Spend an hour here to learn more about the background of the women divers. It gave me a new appreciation for the dedication of the women and I enjoyed seeing actual divers later, with a greater understanding of what they do and how they dive. I took a few moments to watch the video and then breezed through some of the other displays. Felt it was fairly priced for the value.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.

Our stay in Jeju coincide with the operational day of one of the biggest and oldest traditional market in Jeju - Grandma Market which runs on days that end with 7th of the calendar month. There are lots of other smaller scale traditional markets which are opened on different days (e.g days ending on 5th, 2nd, etc...) thru out the island but we were told that this is the biggest.There is also an area which are designated for elderly ladies aged 65 and above whereby they are not charged any fees for selling there, hence, the name of Grandma Market.Lots of things can be found in the market, from plants, to snacks to clothings to housewares. We bought some fresh ginseng, chilly flakes and also fresh gingko from the market (after tasting some that were steamed and sold as snacks), The gingko there is different from those that we get in MY (most imported from China). Their is more creamy in texture and rounded as compared to ours.Overall, quite an interesting walk for an hour or two if you're looking to buy some of foodstuff.

Only 1km of the 7.5km lava tube is open to the public, but I highly recommend coming! Expect to spend about an hour admiring the beauty of this natural volcanic formation!While we were there, it had rained the night before and was still drizzling slightly, so the ground was damp. Good to wear proper shoes with good grip (we were thankful for our boots) as the ground is a rather uneven terrain and can be slippery when wet. It's also rather dimly lit, with some lighting inside to guide your path and highlight specific features found in the cave.Even though there is only one entry/ exit point, there is much to see (if you're into geology/ geography/ nature lover, otherwise it'll just look like the same dark cavernous backdrop) as you loop back to the exit point.

Nothing much else to describe but it's a musuem full of teddy bears. Only a place for teddy bears or soft toy loversThey had displays of teddy bears enacting scenes from human history. Also teddy bears depicting famous people like Albert Eindtein, Michael Jackson and Elvis Pressley.There is also an outdoor area with a couple more exibhits. I think about 1 to 1.5 hours would be enough to spend here.

My Korean friend brought me to this place when I visited Jeju. It was a hidden jem. I spent a couple of hours to take holographic pictures and watched the Kpop videos at the 3D theater. It was close to many tourist spots in Seogwipo city (Teddy bear museum, lotte hotel, and etc.). If you are a kpop lover, you will have unforgettable memories. It was so much fun!!!

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. Spend 3 hours there.Suggest to go for a toilet break before going thru the entrance.Bring baby carriers, cause the road is uneven. Have to be extra careful especially going with kids.There are 2 entrance. (follow the counter clock wise direction, where the entrance is situated behind the huge ship)Enjoy the scenery, watchout for the waves too.Their is a canola flower field where you can take some instagram photos too (need to pay to enter)

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Manjanggul cave is world historic place of volcanic lava formation! The cave path is very unsmooth with bumpy small rock patches and wet so we had to walk steps by steps very slowly to the end! All along to the main attraction, there are small lamps and lamppost to guide us along.Took us one and a half hours to reach the main attraction of lava formation.We spent a few minutes taking some picture there and proceeded back out of the cave.I think I won't be going there again because I'm not interested in geography.

Main target is the teddy bear in Goong drama  but just one section there..a lot of cute, handsome, pretty teddy bears are gathered in this farm..you should spend hours here as the farm is huge! easy to park your car and enjoy your fairytales day there!!

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.

Jeju Stone Park is a vast area with everything stone related.  With Jeju being a volcanic island, the lava stones are everywhere from the Harubang statues to the walls surrounding houses.  The park is divided into three courses which would take about an hour each at a leisurely pace.  The first course has mostly rock statues (including the Harubang statues) that most likely had some religious significance.  The second course shows how the rocks were used for more practical purposes (tombstones, tools, housing, etc) through the different eras of Korean history.  The third course specifically shows the different Jeju style housing made with mostly the volcanic rock walls.  It?s probably not the best place to be in the middle of heat in the summer but when the weather is nice, it?s a fantastic spot to spend a few hours.

It's a tiny island which will only take about 1 and a half hour to explore around with an auto-bike (renting required) or spend about 2-3 hours cycling around the island. This place is surrounded with mountains, sea, greens, flowers and lovely people. Lots of tiny restaurants and decent cafes can be found in the island. Would recommend everyone to try their peanut/hallabong ice-cream! It's something very different and worth to try.
It was a good place to bring the girlfriend and rent a scooter for a 2 hour, romantic, oceanside drive.
If you watched Korean Drama   Dae Jang Geum   some scenes were taken here.  It speak volume of this museum.  The whole walk may take 2 hours or so if you read the description. Well recommended.

If you come to Jeju island, Hala mountain tracking is No. 1 recommendation for you if you are health and have strong two legs. My recomendation is Yong-Sil course and it will take about 5 hours round tracking. It is totally different scene when you up to the mountain and never forget this memory.

I would recommend that you read the book ?The Island of Sea Women? by Lisa See before visiting the museum. I felt an emotional connection to the museum, the observatory and the grounds around the area, primarily because I had some background knowledge. The museum is well laid out and interesting. Do take the time to watch the video on the main floor before going through the exhibits. If you are there around 10:00 a.m. or 1:00 p.m. you may be able to see the women divers from the observatory on the 3rd floor.  Getting there: we were on a cruise ship and took a taxi from the ship terminal in Jeju City. It took about an hour and was a very scenic drive.  Our taxi driver gave us an hour to tour the museum and grounds and then dropped us off by the main market area in downtown Jeju City. It was under $100 for four people in a taxi.
I would recommend others to spend an hour or so in this site. Spend good time with wife strolling the path and of course, took some beautiful pictures.

I went to this museum just because a friend has suggested. Despite I am not a big fan of teddy bears this museum is really amazing! You will see the major events from the world history, famous singers and artists, as well as some scientists! I better don't tell everything not to ruin the surprise! There happens an Elvis Show at every hour or so. If you have time, definitely give it a go.

I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.

I was planning on going up gwaneumsa and coming down seongpanak but seongpanak is closed until 31st Jul, 18 so I came down the the same. It took me about 3.5 hr to climb up, and 3 hrs to come down. Together with my lunch breaks, I finished the entire round trip in a little over 7 hours. Unfortunately, it was  really misty when I was at the summit, so, i didn't get to see the crater lake. I highly recommend bringing a pair of trekking poles and good hiking shoes.

I visited in maze park last week with my family. The park is not big but you can enjoy the maze enough. It took about 1 hour to find exit for me but other people took 30~40 minutes. I recommend not to use map for more fun. You can also see the beautiful flowers and meet lots of cats. If you could find Dr. Dustin who made the park, ask him to take a picture together. He like that :).

I say this one should not be missed, just because there are not a lot of lava tubes that exist and are easily accessible! The whole journey from the mouth of the cave to the lava column, and back, can be done in an hour. Walking thru the varying sizes of the tube, some areas narrow and some really big with high ceilings, is a spectacular experience! The largest lava column in the world, towards the end of the permissible distance, is a little underwhelming. Still, overall a great visit. Highly recommended when in Jeju.

I loved this seemingly unassuming place that I would have never really thought of visiting.  It was one of the most interesting and beautiful places I visited in Jejudo Island.  It is definitely a   must do  , as they say in Disney World!  We would have loved to spend more time there.  It's not just a park with a bunch of rocks so don't miss out!  It's like a natural museum/art gallery of indigenous Jejudo volcanic rocks with a splash of the island's history.  Highly recommended to spend a minimum of 3-4 hours here!!

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I found this museum really interesting. I knew a little about Hanyeo beforehand but this gave me a much more detailed understanding. The exhibits (consisting of genuine Haenyeo clothing, tools and equipment alongside dioramas, videos and various documents) are well laid out and the accompanying explanations and labels almost all have high-quality English translations. I read every word and it took me a little under 2 hours to complete my visit, which considering the entrance fee is only 1100 won is excellent value for money. Recommended, especially if you are already on the east side of the island.

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).

I crossed the Believe it or not museum many times, in New york, in Baltimore.. but never stepped in.Finally I tried the one in Jeju island and I really liked it. It is certainly similar to the others, but if you never visited one... who cares?I imagined it small but it took me 2 hours to do everything. I mean... read all, not just give a look and say : oh.. ok!It costs 10usd per person. Expensive or not depends of you.If you are curious and love to travel and discover... it is nice place.

I came to Udo on my 4th day in Jeju and it was the spotlight of my trip. I love the island itself and everything about it. You can rent a bicycle or a motorbike to go around the island. I didnt bring my licence so you didnt let me rent the motorbike even I told them that I am Vietnamese, I really can drive ( in Korean ) =)) It was a funny conversation, but I end up with riding the bicycle for 4 hours .. quite tired but amazing place and worth to visit.I went to Korea alone, and my days in Jeju was quite boring but Udo made my trip more memorable ^^

Highly recommend visiting Dongmun market! The market has plentiful, and affordable fresh meat, seafood, as well as Jeju-only snacks, beverages, restaurants and dried food. For a small fee (depending on the store, around $5 for 9 Kg), food including fresh meat and seafood can be shipped from Jeju to mainland Korea. Shipment takes about a full day. I have tried this option for fresh pork belly and abalone and both arrived the next day fresh and ready for consumption.Parking around the area is a bit difficult and waiting for an available spot does get frustrating. Parking garage fees around less than $3 for a few hours.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place
Had a lot of fun here with my friends. I think there were 3 total mazes? Probably could spend like 3 hours here, but we just ran the mazes real quick before heading to the airport.

Geumneung Beach and Hyeopjae Beach are the two beaches of Hallim located about a kilometer apart from one another.  While swimming is not allowed for some stretches, both areas are absolutely stunning during sunset.  The stretches of the camping area looked like a great place to spend the daylight hours and at low tide, there was plenty of space for kids to run around and play.

For 11000krw entry per person, we expected an eye opener and an attraction different than most. Upon entering, we can see from the number of glass exhibits on display that this place would've been a great place to visit for couples or families.Beautiful display with intricacies that you will need to understand to appreciate. The displays look quite challenging to maintain as there are so many glass objects that could be dulled due to weather conditions. Aside from that, we appreciated the effort it would've taken to create this glass wonderland and enjoyed it extremely. Even in the wintry snowy condition we were experiencing, although this is an outdoor exhibition, we enjoyed it!Would recommend 1-2 hours at a slow walk pace with many photo opportunities.

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

First, do not get lost, second prepare to spend at least 3 hours here. If you don't like nature, this is not a place for u. It's like all nature in one. There's cave inside which is to be the only cave that has limestone and lava.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

Entertaining Mongolian horse show. We caught a taxi here as it's not easy to get to by other public transport. Impressive expert performance by the young horse riders who did some amazing acrobatics on horses. The Park's website is in Korean and the show was all in Korean but we managed to follow what was going on!  The horse show is on 3 times a day. After the show, kids can have fun riding a horse or driving a swing car (7 minute ride) or go kart (not sure of the minimum age for that).  Need to pay additional fees for each activity.  Worth spending a couple of hours or half a day here.
Drove to this national park as planned, the park are well organised with the different type of flowers and cactus, caves tunnels, animals and birds. My family spend almost 3 hours in this huge park.
dont miss this, you can see how the underground magma made this amazing tunnel crafted by nature, really nice to visit. 1 hour tour (it took me to go to the end and back)

Don't miss this show if u are in Jeju. Only available & performing until October 2020....awesome immersive show.? @ 빛의 벙커 Bunker de Lumieres. The floors and walls become the canvas of this highly immersive digital art that come to life, as Van Gogh's art work are displayed all over and synchronised with beautiful clasical music. Definitely worth the more than an hour show.We enjoyed it tremendously!

Definitely the most fun I have in the island. Not that I didn't have fun in other attractions however I just love how everything they got in this attraction is an interactive one. I have the chance to watch GD's hologram concert as well here, they have one hologram concert every one hour. It's fun! Oh, and if you're a VIP this place is a must visit. Their gift shop offers some selection of VIP merchandises, from Krunk, snapback hats and VIP's light stick.The entry ticket is 15.000 won if I'm not wrong, but it is definitely worth every bucks you spend. There's a dancing room, a 360 degree 3D experience, you can even take pictures with your favorite Kpoppers using their hologram tech.
Clear skies, great sun, not overly hot. Only bad thing is the parking but other then that spend about 2-3 hours here sipping jeju famous harubong tea is definately a luxury!

Bring your swimming gear along, it has a sea swimming pool during low tides, basically daytime. Seeing ppl drives and swimming. There is life-jacket rental available for snorkelling. No entrance ticket required. But the carpark attendance charged us W2K which seem only W1K per hour. No proper carpark control. See ppl park along road side.

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said ?sure?.  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn?t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

At first, I did not see the point of going to a Teddy Bear Museum. I could not imaging myself checking all teddy bears dressed as popular celebrities and personalities. But I was suprised that I loved every minute of it and I was totally entertained. Me and my friend stayed in the museum for over an hour, longer than what we expected. Highly recommended.
An decent park to spend 2-3hrs.Nothing great just decent.Lots of tourist thought, so don't expect a peaceful walk unless you go at odd hours.The park close at 6pm.

Although we know how the illusion works, it is still crazy to watch how the bottles or cars go up hill instead of going back. You don't need much time over there though. One mysterious road (according to our touri map there are two) is located right next to the Jeju Lovepark which is interesting and funny. You can go there for 9000 Won, spend about an hour watching love sculptures. :-)

After paying for the tickets (2000 won per adult and 1000 won per child/youth), we walked about 5-10min to the waterfall. It was a therapeutic walk through the park to reach the waterfall. Recommend to stay about an hour here to take photos with the waterfall as the backdrop.

Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. A place to go if you want to relax and have a nice walk or if you are really interested in history and stones..

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.
A novel idea to showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. Very camera-friendly but it's not a big place. We had a leisure walk in here and comb the area in about an hour.

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.

A good place to go if you love Teddy Bear. For us, I had a good time having some history lessons with my 8 year old daughter. There's a display of historical events using Teddy Bears as characters, eg, opening of disney land, WW2, man landing on moon, return of Hong Kong to China in 1997 etc. the place isn't very big. spending 1 hour here would be sufficient. make sure you take photos with PSY as Teddy Bear, or Steve Jobs as Teddy Bear! There are 12 characters in total.

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.
Short visit but the scene is beautiful. Steep climb is not recommended for old folks though. Really like the waterfall that goes into the ocean!

It is easy to access the fall for those who dislike climbing steps.  It was only a short distance from the entrance via some steps.  Nice feeling to get up close and personal to the fall however just gotta beware of wet ones which at times can be slippery.  Smaller rocks tend to move when you are stepping on them so be careful.

I lived on Jeju and took school groups 3 times and every visitor I had to learn about  the history of the island. There is a video (not recommended for children due to disturbing images and video) at the start which is in several different languages. Then the display hall (formerly a dusty collection of artifacts but now a shiny new display hall) then there is a trip through the oreum. Free guided tour too. Very interesting. Also for kids there is a tank to play in in the grounds (there used to be a plane I don't know where that's gone) and the oreum itself is well worth a climb. Great museum which is still developing. Well worth it.

A lovely puppy greets you at the start of the walk! You walk past a lovely stone house on the left and the dry riverbed on the right. They have well built stairs to the falls. At this time of year there are no falls - due to lack of rain  however there is a lovely pond at the bottom and the ability to climb down the rock's and close to the water. A lovely place to sit and contemplate! Don't recommend kissing the kissing cave...a blarney stone it's not haha!

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

This place was very beautiful.  In winter, you can see beautiful silver grass fields. It's a different charm than summer. If you visit Jeju Island, I recommend you to go here! You should wear sneakers when visit here. Because it's high that it's hard to climb up.

This is a UNESCO site and I find it quite awesome, how Mother Nature made these underground caves. Do note that you'll have to climb steep stairs up and down to the caves, so I wouldn't recommend the elderly folks to go in. Do bring along a jacket as it can get chilly down in the caves. Also bring along a torch and have good anti-slip walking shoes as it can be a little wet and slippery.

This happened to be our favorite place even though we got up early to see the sunrise but the clouds blocked the sun. It was still beautiful and the surrounding area is gorgeous. There are so many birds and flowers to see. Many photo ops. After climbing you might be tired, but when you descend make sure you go to where the little beach is. It's gorgeous there.

The weather was extremely good and the scene was nice.Only have 2 hrs to walk this time, will definitely climb up if i have a chance to go again.Recommended to go in the morning, less tourist and more fresh air.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .
Sunrise peak another UNESCO,drizzling while we climb the peak. Crowded even the weather wasn't good. Descending is nice.

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

It costs a few thousand won to get into this attraction. BUT, I highly recommend that when you get to the area right before the ticket office, walk left instead of right. You'll be at a free beach with some very cool lava formations. My friend and I were able to climb the lava formations without a soul around. All of the tourists were at the paid location, so there was literally no one on the other beach (and it was a 1 minute walk from the main area. Why was noone there??)

Interesting if short visit. Not too well signposted, but once found, plenty of parking and a short climb downn to the beach. Depending on the season entry if 2,000 Won or free. Demonstrates well the islands volcanic cliffs.

I didn't know I was looking at this famous peak when we approached in a taxi (looking for a lunch spot that our kids would approve of). I was saying   Wow, look at that   as we drove towards it. Then our driver explained it was the famous peak. I can see why, even on a cloudy rainy day it was such a beautiful scene. We couldn't climb to the peak because it was closed to the public due to an impending typhoon. I was disappointed we couldnt climb but so glad that we got to see it, even from the base. Absolutely beautiful area. I want to come back to Jeju just to climb that peak and see the beauty from above.Incidentally there were plenty of restaurants and cafes and shops in the small town at the base. Even an American Embassy (i.e. Mcdonalds)

Do not bother spending your time going here unless there is some specific item or shopping you need to do. Come on, you are on Jeju, a small slice of paradise on Earth, go see funny statues or climb a mountain.

Climb down stairs to reach this waterfall but the place is hard to reach cause no ground at all, have to walk on different shapes and size of stone to reach the waterfall. Only need to spend about 15 minutes here will do. Natural scene than Cheonjiyeon Falls that with man made paths.

amazing landscape. A nice spot to take beautiful pictures of tranquil waters with pitch black rocks and white sand. Walk right from the main entrance till the end, you will fine some nice restaurants and cheaper places to stay. From there you can climb the hill and get the whole picture of Hamdeok area.

You will enjoy this place depends on how u spend your time :1. Take photo in the tea garden & entrance2. Order you green tea/ green tea ice cream or drinks and bring it outside the cafe (depend on weather) 3.Walk around4. visit the innisfree museum & shop for some innisfree product.
You don't have to spend a lot of time here but the displays are well done and interesting.  There is a small shop at the end from which you can purchase a bear

Worth spending the money and time to have a good laugh. Even the kids were laughing loudly. Not much talking but many actions. They speak good English so not a problem to understand.I was even being selected to go on the stage to perform with them!! Unforgettable!

While learning about the life of Jeju folk village we enjoyed the gardens farms and orchards. They are beautiful and being taken care well. It was our first time that we saw cabbage with flowers.During our visit it was almost toward the end of closing time and probably that's the reason there're not many visitors.
We went to Hallim Park and decided to spend a little time on the beach as it's right next door. Nice place for some fresh air and a quiet walk

We went here on a rainy day as we really wanted to see how the famous O'Sulloc tea was made. The museum is nothing more than a room (unfortunately not all texts are translated info english) and the majority of the space is taken up by the shop and the cafe which seems like the main focus of this location.Two things were nice getting a look of the tea plantations and having a quick tea tasting.I would recommend this only if you are a true O'Sulloc fan or if you have spare time not visiting all the other sights at Jeju island.

We went for the cake n ice-cream. We went there around 430pm the house close at 6pm. Be there early as by the time we queue and order the cake is sold out. Disappointed and in the end only had the ice-cream.Tried the box of 10 sachets instant green tea cafe latte it's very smooth and rich. Recommended. The green tea too. The aroma is totally different. Worth a visit for your tea experience. The ambiance is lovely too a lot of photo scene surrounding.

We like this maze a lot as it's not that easy as you can think of. Several times we went to an dead end and travel around similar corners!! Some kids running around to be the first ringing the bell at the finish point. It's a place full of laughter and we enjoyed it very much!!

We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!
We got here just before closing time and so it was very quiet.  It had a peaceful calm atmosphere despite being a large temple.  Just the place to wonder around the gardens at the end of the day.

We did only this folk village with my family and friends. This recreated the feeling of living a long time ago in korea it communicates well the differences of different backgrounds. We did not hire the audio guide and we had two korean speakers with us who were able to read everything. It was fabulous for my kids to see and touch most of the displays plenty to keep them occupied. We saw a dance and others getting photos taken in wedding costumes and a Korean Drama being filmed. Overall the experience was a good cultural morning out. We did not eat there as we were meeting friends for lunch but it looked very traditional

We did not spend much time at the tea plantation as it was very sunny. We were spending time in the cafe and ordered green tea ice-cream and green tea swiss roll cake. Both are delicious especially the ice-cream! Rich in flavor and not bitter at all. Swiss roll cake is fluffy enough and not overly sweet. Must try!

We decided to do this spontaneously and it was actually much funnier then I expected. The teddy bear through time stuff was really well done and the museum didn't feel like a drag despite its very limited options of showing teddy bears. Would recommend for pretty much all ages if you've got a day in Seogwipo.

Was expecting to see beautiful blossoms of camellia flowers but was disappointed as the blooms were over at that time. I believe if you come at the right time it will be awesome. The only blooming flowers that we saw were in the greenhouses. Park is not small so there's quite a bit of walking to visit the various parts of the park. Would recommend to check on the bloom timing before visiting the park.

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

Visited the tea museum as heard so much about it but there is nothing that special just some tea history and at the end of it  they sell the tea to visitors at touristy pricing. There is a caf챕 that serves green tea and ice cream too and that is ok to try out. There is an Innis free shop next door to tea factory but it was closed the day we visited. I would say its ok for a visit if you have spare time in your hands otherwise nothing really to shout about.

Very well managed green tea museum. They have a small museum to show the process of tea and how it has evolved over the years. Upon finishing the museum you can buy different green tea products from the shop. And there is also a cafe within the museum that sell excellent green tea ice cream and also green tea Swiss roll. If you have time you can walk further into the next building which is the innisfree shop within this building you will be able to make your own green tea soap under the supervision of the Innisfree staff. There is also a cafe that sell jam and cake in this building. Perfect to spend your afternoon in this place.
Unexpected place. Really huge. Good for family visit. Fun time with the kids. You may need to spend the whole day in the area.

To be clear - perfectly managed.  Gorgeous property.  Nice atmosphere.  Not sure I could be there more than 10 minutes.  Sure my wife could spend copious time and money on all things green tea.  If you like tea and tea things - a five!

This waterfall is much smaller than Jeongbang Falls  and is worth spending the time walking to it if you're in the area. Beautiful clear blue water beneath  it would make a good swimming spot in hot weather!

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.
This relaxing adventure is full of all kinds of beautiful flowers. I have been here 3 times. I recommend going in the spring when many flowers are in bloom.

This place shows miniature buildings which are famous from all over the world. However they are poorly kept some have wrong information and are definitely not for young active children. I do not recommend coming here as this may be a waste of time.

This museum is EXTREMELY well put together.  It is not often in Korea where you will find proper English translations.  This place does not disappoint. There is a wealth of knowledge to be found here for those interested in the sad history Jeju people have had to endure.  ProTip:  Make sure you take time to explore the outside part (the lands and the memorial wall). ProTip:  You do not want to rush thru this.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to really walk around and read about the history.  The museum covers almost 6 years worth of events and details!

This is the place where Running Man shooting happened previously. Nice place to spend some time but it will be time consuming.Didn't manage to play the maze. But I'm like facade of the design of this park. And it is chilling too!

This is really nice place!Also I would reccomend to go there in the evening when it's dark outside.Even though working monks told us that we are here at bad time (it was getting dark) I think completely otherwise.Because when it gets dark they have really beautiful lights on so temple looks magical!

This is not only a museum but a cafe.  There is a main cafe in the first building where you can also purchase many tea products.  There is also another quieter cafe in the building up the hill where are can also take time to make soap.  The second cafe is not visited by most travelers and I would highly recommend it.

This is not a bias assessment. I would be glad if the establishment owner would take in advise from visitor feedback. This is my first time to rate an establishment with such a low rating. It is a total rip-off as entrance fee is collected before cafe and store. There nothing impressive with the collection and exhibit area is extremely small. There is another fees impose for DIY chocolate making session. No educational value  no entertainment value. I would not recommend it to anyone.

This is no Caribbean beach so don't expect warm turquoise waters and endless stretches of fine white sand. Considering the area however it is a decent beach and worth checking out if you are in the area. It is located within the Jungmun Resort complex in Seogwipo but there is no charge so anyone can visit.Here's what to expect: yellow/orange rough sand with lots of bits of shell; water that gets deep quite quickly; STRONG undertow on stormy days. The resort restricts people from swimming during certain months (wintertime I think) because of the risk of undertow.  I mention the last point because the beach is actually quite beautiful to watch on a windy day as the waves crash into the volcanic rock.Quite often on weekends foreigners gather to play rounds of volleyball.There are spots to get food near the beach and in the resort but be ready for sky-high prices.

This is a must see! An awesome show in Jeju that is very popular around the world. It has Korean culture involved which makes it even cooler. Hardly any talking but you can totally understand the story throughout the entire show! This show had my attention the entire time! Don't want to give to much info to ruin the surprise but I would definitely recommend this if you visit Jeju.
This is a good place to spend some time. I really love the Obama bear. It looks so cute! and also the ones with Korean traditional clothes. Joanna is really obsessed wtih teddy bears!!

This garden is a deeply beautiful example of how nature is made art. My only regret is not coming during a time of the year when it is all in bloom. My wife and I will certainly be returning before the end of the year.

These caves are quite common all around the island  and this one is a well maintained and easily accessible example. Be aware though that if its been raining the day before you are likely to be dripped upon  but it's tolerable. Also  depending on the time of year  you will probably want to wrap up warm as it can be quite fesh inside.

There wasn't much to look and read (all in Korean) but caring and friendly staff made our day.For one of the most visited city or area for foreign tourists  it's hard to believe that the most of the places do not have English speaking staff.We were having hard time finding good place to go and dine  recommendations by the staff at the Chocolate Land were very very helpful. Also  the chocolates we purchased with his help turned out very good.If you are in Jung Moon tour sector  need a little break for a free coffee (it's free with a coupon you get when you pay an admission) and some help from an English and Chinese speaking staffs.

There is a night market which originally operate for few months but now extended till unknown time. Visited this place after raining thus a lot of stalls not opening. But I am able to try the fried porky which is delicious and I will be back for this! There is table and chairs for you to eat in but please be aware of mosquito.

There are many glass exhibits in this park with indoor and outdoor sections. There is a myriad of colours once you step inside and it is sure to lift your mood. It is recommended for families and couples as there are many chances for memorable photos. You can try out glass blowing if you have the time and willing to pay.

The temperature in the cave is at least 5 to 10C lower so please bring a jacket and wear proper shoes when going in. The entrance fee is cheap at 2K each for an adult.There are many locals visiting during the weekends so it's recommended you visit during weekdays if possible.The cave is dark and wet so we spent more time watching the floor as opposed to the cave.
The rock formations near the water are absolutely remarkable. I recommend taking the time to visit if you are on Jeju Island.

The museum is really made for kids.  The museum is filled with endless pieces of slightly altered art that enhances optical illusions.  Kids would probably love the museum and the endless optical illusions.  If you are adult you will be amused by the paintings for approximately two minutes and then you'll be quite bored after a while.The middle of the museum also contains some sort of self playing organ or set of instruments which was not very impressive.There is also a karting facility on-site but I did not try it.  The karts did look a bit slow though and it didn't look too fun.If you do decide to spend the 10000 won per person then keep your expectations low and don't try to over-analyze the paintings.  Just don't think too much and you'll enjoy your time there then...

The ?Dragon Hair? rock location is near Jeju airport and a good recommendation if you are trying to burn some time prior to departing Jeju. The location has spacious parking and allows visitors easy access to the actual rock.

That was amazing. I used to be student in SKorea. And it was my best memorable trip in that time. Its a little expensive specially for students. We were around 30 persons and our hotels was really good smin services and the price. I really recommend u to travel Jeju once go to SK.

Tea plantation near the city center with a tea museum containing a few old tes pots (you will probably have wider assortment in a flea market). I will probably enjoy visiting an actual farm with fruit trees and greenhouses planted to vegetables than spending time at the tea plantation. There is no entrance fee but there is also no tour guide or someone or something to explain what there is to see.

So this was my fourth time visiting Jeju and so far this is the best experience i had. Mr. Kang was not only kind but also reliable. He took us to places we have planned and gave other ideas where we should go. My friends and I had a lot of fun during the trip. Both car and van were clean and comfortable; most importantly had wifi. Oh and he speaks English too. Definitely will contact him when I visit Jeju again :)

So this is more a shop than a museum to me. But the cafe there is highly recommended!! You need to try the green tea cakes and the cookies as well! Wish i could've tried the ice cream but i was afraid i get sick. It's literally the best roll cake. The garden was nice and you can make your own shop at innisfree didnt have enough time though.. Remember to take pictures at the cup made of plants across the street..

Second time at O Sulloc and the grounds are beautiful and offers nice picture opportunities and a relaxing vibe. Spent a good amount of time at Innisfree House where you can buy packages of soap and customise them for friends. Good activity to engage the kids and also make gifts for friends :) Green tea ice cream was good and the tea leaves smelled really good as well.

Reminds me of kenyas hells gate. The place is a sight to behold. Be carefull to put on comfy shoes that have great treads and grips so that you dont slip on the sometimes slippery rocks. Also find out about tides. If its high tides then definately you will be soaked by action of water on your feet. Good place though. I recommend finnishing it with a horse ride by the ajoshi at the exit for man won and a cold jeju tangerine juice.

Pyoseon Beach is just the opposite of Jeju Folk Village.So after visited the Village  we came here.The beach is pretty large with wide white sands.It is the perfect place for families to spend some time relaxing  particularly at low tide with its lake-like pools.It has abundant parking space  public toilet (with shower) and cam-ground around the square.Near the beach  there is white lighthouse near the shore.This lighthouse is where the last scene in Kdrama Iris (2009) was film.
Place to buy famous jeju orange and the stuffs related.. Fresh seafood and vegetables are all around. A must visit place when one spend the time in Jeju

Personally I love this place very much.It's a good place to relaxing your mind.The place is huge yet I do find peace at every corner and section inside.You should come by yourself or with your family.I've been to couple of aqua place in several country and I think its worth it to spend time here.However don't waste your time with a cheesy diving show.I recommend you to go to nearby White House (actually Light House) rather than waiting for the diving show time. So I'll definitely come again!
