review: Our driver Kang Dae-Hyun was super friendly and we saw a lot of things :) we could take many pictures and he showed us the best spots in Jeju :) next time we would take the tour again with him! Thank you very much!

Open air museum that hosts a plethora of weird statues that are lewd and sometimes bizarre. It is really more of a photo-taking venue than one that is educational. Even so I felt embarrassed posting any of the photos I took here on Facebook as some of the sculptures were just too sexually explicit. Great if you are going with a group of good friends for a good laugh. Don't go if you are easily offended by sexual content.

Only one of the passengers is allowed to row. No explanation of what is going on. My gf was upset she didn?셳 get to row. The staffs were very rushing. Did not give enough time for you to think. Everything from finding entrance to the activities and safety was very poorly organised. Plus unbelievably rude staffs made me speechless. I would never recommend to go here for a kayaking. I do think the staffs need to be educated better.

One of my all time favourite brand of tea! Great to finally step foot into the museum. There are specialty teas that is only available at the museum eg the freshly roasted green tea and the herbal tea lines coupled with a few award winning teas!There are set options at the cafe and the weather was beautiful so we took our order outside and it was great sitting amongst the trees and enjoying a fine cup of tea and dessert! Highly recommend the green tea roll and green tea cheesecake! Do bring your passport along so that you can do the tax rebate once you spend 30000 won and above! Right across the street you can also take photos amongst the rows of luscious greens!
Not a bad place to spend your time at Jeju. Although there are 3 theatres  in whole Korea. Therefore if u didn't manage to went to another 2 theatres. This is a must.

My friends and I were so excited about Loveland before our visit. However we were quite disappointed afterward as the park was kind of old. We expect more to see after paying so much for admission but nothing else besides statues and some aged fountains. Only visit if you really have free time to kill.

My friend had completed the maze shorter time by instinct and not following the map.  Me and my partner collected all the marking stamp but takes a longer time to end.  But it was a great fun. Worth visit!

Me and my friends really enjoyed our time around the Sanbanggulsa temple and really enjoyed the serenity and tranquillity it provided. The location within the mountain itself is breath taking and it really does give this temple a unique look compared to other temples. The stream that runs down into the cave is incredible and this place allows you to connect with your spiritual side.
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.

Lots of fun to tour around with friends or family and a camera. Can be crowded though. Nice restaurant with pizza and gelato just before you head into the big sculpture garden. My 5 year old daughter had a blast of a time there!
I've been here 3 times already.  my latest visit is last Oct 2017 to accompany my friends.  I love the scenery.

It's wet and dark inside..we just walk and walk in dark sometimes we just talk about going back and not see what's in the end of the path. But somehow we reach the end..take a photo and then walk the same road to get out.
It's new and quite unique but not a must-see attraction. Recommended only to those who love teddy bears and have some extra time to spend.
Its indeed mysterious rd!! A kind that cannot be found anywhere else.. Very unique n puzzled s we did experimented few times from the start to the end...

It's a tourist packed beach in the summer time. It's quite expansive so you can go to your own spot thats semi private. Recommend you to travel outside the vacation period unless you love swarms of families with children.
It was great!! Allot of pictures n exciting things to do.  The 3D pictures were so funny n they had some scary pics to take part in. Friends had a great time acting scared or being eating.

It looks like it has been abandoned for years  it has very nice artwork but it is also very dirty. The bathroom was disgusting. The gift shop smelled like cigarettes and had puddles of water every where. And the staff looked extremely bored and uninterested. I came at night so maybe the daytime is better. How ever I don't recommend it  definitely not worth the $8 per person day or night. (Got some nice pictures though)
It is just a rock that looks like a dragon's head but only if you are looking at it from up close. I wouldn't recommend spending lots of time here.
It has a great green tea maze we spend a lovely time reaching the end of the maze and the smell of the green tea its all over the place

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

Interesting to learn about the history of citrus  including the local history of the mandarin organges  but you won't need to spend a lot of time here. Museum includes green houses with citrus trees from all over the world.
Interesting museum i will recommend it to visit for adult and for kids it's great spend the time we enjoy that day

I wish I had more time to spend here when I visited. It was such a great place and was very interactive. It was great to have the English audio tour available too as we learned so much more. So well laid out and I would highly recommend it to others.

i went here in heavy rain. not much to see. but im having good time here with my friends. there are a lot of stones sculpture here. and also theres a museum regarding jeju.the museum tell us about types of stone. and the jeju itself formed by the volcanic activity happened before this.

I went here a couple of times during my stay on Jeju Island. I loved the Innisfree shop where you could buy packs of soap that you then made with either green tea tangerine or volcanic rock ash. It was so cool and they made lovely souvenirs for when I came home. Also the green tea roll cake there is delicious! And the gardens are great for taking photos. 10/10 would recommend.
I was slightly surprised by the number of exhibits that the museum had.  It kept my tweens very entertained and they enjoyed their time here very much.  Recommended

I walked along the garden path together with my best  friends during our trip to korea.each plant has their own story and some piece of advice regarding life that we can learnt from tree.The garden well kept and all the staff very friendly and can speak englishWe had a great time hereWe even get free tea.KamsahammidaⅠ

I visited Soesokkak Estuary during October after reading about it online.I went there sometime in the afternoon approximately around 2pm or so after lunch. There was a huge crowd (mostly locals) and lines were formed to book the activities.I had wanted to try out the transparent canoe but to my dismay it was sold out fully till late evening. Instead I tried out the aqua bicycle (I suppose that's what it's called?) where you get to paddle with a partner around the river. It requires quite a level of coordination with your partner in order to steer it in the right direction. I can't remember the exact prices but it wasn't too expensive.Bring along an extra set of apparel in case you get wet in the water and do go early if you interested in the transparent canoe!In conclusion great place to visit for enjoyable bonding time for family and friends!

I visited Jeju Folk Village on my last day of my trio to Jeju. Jeju Folk Village is a place where the traditional culture of Jeju and the history of the Korean language since the 1890s the late Joseon Period Dinasty are well preserved in their original state. You can experience Folks Customs Life Folk games Crafts and Traditional Folk events. I recommend to visit if you have time. Last day of the trip can be perfect because you can relax and go back home with a good feeling.
I used to go here as a child all the time and it left me with so many good memories. I recommend checking it out if you have young children with you!

I initially wasn't too keen on visiting this attraction as it was a hot day and inside the village it looked even hotter but via peer pressure I went in.I ended up really enjoying myself and although all the houses look the same it was still a very nice walk and large enough that it keeps you occupied for sometime.If you're into Korean Drama's you would most likely really like this place along with killing some time.

Huge place with lesser crowd as compared to Singapore's. More photo points and less people makes the visit more enjoyable. There's even an outdoor park towards the end. Go in the daytime to capture clearer shots outdoor.Ticket cost 9000krw for each adult. Should be cheaper if you get it online via the official website.

how lucky we are can reach this place at perfect time  a good weather and sunset. Enjoy every single of the land  peaceful. If I have more times I will stay here for couples day.The park was pretty enough  for couple or family  kids will fun here. they can ride horse or just running around the garden. very recommended to visit.

Had a great time and I?m not even a k pop fan. Lots of interactive things that kept it interesting and ended up buying a souvenir. You have to go to the holographic concert as it was a really rewarding experience. Wish I could have spent more time here.

Great day tour at small price with small group We did the east course tour. There were eight passengers plus one driver in a car for nine persons (i.e. very small). The driver was very friendly. He gave us some basic explanations but apart from that we were on our own (as advertised I have to say). We were sometimes in a rush but overall we saw a lot and appreciated it. There is lunch included. We liked the tour.

First time visiting a lava cave. It was nice and enjoyable as a couple hiking in the cave. There isnt much and just an experience and a place to spend some time. Go only if you have extra time on your hands.

Don't waste your time or money here. It's a pure tourist trap and totally overrated for what it is. Long lines to buy silly overrated green tea lattes and soft serve ice cream that don't even taste that great. It's just a giant shop selling the same teas you can buy all over the city. The innisfree shop next door was even worst! Sorry but will not be recommending this place to anyone. That's why it's hard to believe what trip advisor says these days. Everyone seems so happy to come here but once you're here it's a big fat disappointment.

Dec 2019 My husband and I (in our 40s) went on a free & easy to Jeju Island in Dec 2019 and engaged Mr Kim Choong Kun for 4 days from 14th to 17th. We touch base with him via what's app and listed the activities & food we wished to try and places of interest we wished to visit prior to our travelling. He could text in English converse in Mandarin & English. He planned our itinerary in an organised manner which ensured travelling time efficiency. He did such a good job in planning our itinerary that we could visit so many places of interest plus completing all our intended activities such as horse riding shooting Go karting and catching a NANTA show. Mr Kim not only drives us to destinations he was knowledgable and could enlighten us with historic information to the various places of interest. This was a big bonus to us as he served as a good tour guide and doubled up in helping us take photographs. He brought us to places for meals which are patronised by locals (not touristy places) for instance we had a yummy authentic ginseng chicken soup pork knuckles sashimi and other Korean local dishes. If you are willing he is able to join in for meals and personally we liked the arrangement as he was able to communicate on our behalf when placing ordersand even suggested to us which food goes well with which sauces. His sensitivity and personality made dining together very comfortable. He is patient and accommodating to our preferences and needs. He is friendly and we enjoyed conversations with him along our rides. He is also sensitive hence for travellers who are introverts I am sure he is able to gauge his involvement in conversations accordingly. He definitely made our stay in Jeju enjoyable and memorable. These are his info/ contact: Mr Kim Choong Kun Taxi licence plate: 2984 +82-10-63425688 Highly recommended. Good Value.

Caves are pretty common but first time walking through a lava tube. It is quite a walk (close to 2kms) to the end where the lava poured in (column like structure) but worth the walk. The cave is rather chilly & wet with uneven surfaces. Do come prepared. Decent lighting throughout however can get rather dark. Maybe a small torchlight or glow stick so you can enjoy it more.

being a glass museum  it really contains everything glass. i love the art pieces and how intricate the details are and all  but if youre short on time  this place is worth a skip unless youre REALLY into glass. i would recommend however  trying the glass making pendant pieces though. its worth the price and experience.

Before you leave Jeju enjoy the last minutes. It is nearby Jeju airport. You can maximize your time utilization. You can enjoy fishing on a breakwaters. Good or bad is depends on you : how to utilize it. That is the question.  In my opinion.
Be prepared to spend a lot of time here. And be prepared to walk.  Much to see. Fantastic bonzais that are over 100 years + older

At least Pyeoson Folk Village had more flowers and more greenery and smaller than this one sk you don't have to spend so much time walking around looking at basically the same hut in different locations.Not worth the exhorbitant entrance fee. I'd rather buy food with that money.

At 12usd per pax and with the first floor being all in korean we think it's a rip off... It's the first time we've been to such a museum and we were quite disappointed to not be able to read a word of what they're saying. The second floor has english though so it was slightly better... But 12usd... we wouldn't recommend people who do not understand korean to go...

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

Aqua Planet was a last minute improvised of plans as the wind was exceptionally cold that day.However for the price we pay i am a tad disappointed. Yes the place is huge but the animals that were displayed weren't much. We've seen more and bigger arapaima sharks and stingray elsewhere.Theshow was half synchronized swimming and half animal show. The synchronized swimming wss just okay a bit too lengthy that it turned a little boring.Displays could have been more informative. It wasnt stated smaller shows like feeding times etc. We took our time wandering through the science part but overall there just isn't much.Not recommended.

review: All figures of teddy bear. Worth the moment here. I'd like to visit it again next time with my friends. Hopefully you would enjoy it.

A very nice nature park with lots of flora and fauna. There is lots to see and do so do set aside more time to spend at this place. Do wear a pair of comfortable walking shoes and take lots of pictures!

A place where you could learn a lot about Korean's traditional live and their culture. The guide giving us the tour was hilarious and we had a lot fun in the village. It is a place worth spending time to visit.
A large variety of tea and tea sets. Nice litle store where they sell the tea's and set together. Too many groups and very crowded but interesting enough to spend a short time inside the tea museum.

Whether you love nature or not, I strongly recommend visiting this cave. There is so much to learn on how the lava tube was formed and it provides you with a unique experience that is unforgettable. Do wear proper covered shoes as you will be walking on rocks almost the entire time and some parts might be slippery.

When we arrived in jeju it was raining so we needed to do something that was more indoor.  We drove out to the cave.  The entrance fee is cheap at 2000 won per person.  Then you walk down some steps and enter the lava tube.  It is really dark down there and the floor can be slippery.  I think we spent most of our time looking down at where to walk rather than looking around.  You walk 1km to the end and there is a rock formation.  Nothing too special.  Then you turn around and walk back.  Overall it is a nice cool 2km walk, perfect to escape the heat of jeju.  Just watch where you walk

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html
Went there. Nothing about this road is mysterious or mystical. It is simply based on illution. Well, for anyone who curious about it can try to pass on that road. No need to spend so much time there.

Went there twiceFirst time we went there was already late, around 10pmOur hotel concierge recommended one particularly bbq restaurantBut, the restaurant that we want to eat was already closedSo we ate restaurant next to itIt was good and cost us around 30.000 won for 2 personThe next day,We ate the restaurant that we wantIt was amazingBetter than beforeI definetely come here again

We were here last week so Camellias weren't blooming - it was the time for full blooming hydrangeas. If you're a fan of hydrangeas you must come here in June! Otherwise the rest of the garden felt too   planned   and too Instagram friendly they've marked the places with cheesy signs like   Love is here   or whatever crap like that. The huge cafe was lovely though. We were just overwhelmed by the number of people there but this can't really be avoided or planned.
We went here as a detour and sure it is a tiny bit interesting... but would not recomend any detour here, many fabolous places on the island to spend time on instead.
We went February 2015 during winter time, It freezed to death but well worth experience. Recommended and must place visit in Jeju

We visited Udo with my brother as part of our trip on Jeju. It is easily accessible via ferry (don't forget to bring your passport to buy a ticket!). We did the recommended tour (4h, with lunch time) and it was beautiful: campaign, port, cliffs, lighthouse... We definitely recommend it. We rate it 4 stars and not 5 because of the garbages on the island, it wastes the beautiful landscapes!

we took some interesting shots. cool place to spend some time outdoors, it's not too big and easy to walk around. definitely worth going there!! in fact, we thought this was pretty much the most interesting thing in Jeju

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

We have visited many caves in various countries. More or less they are quite similar. Dark, quiet, mysterious, cold, etc.As with every cave, it's not well litted & its quite dark in certain sections of the cave. Being a natural formation, the ground is usually uneven. Particularly for this cave , the unevenness is very bad. And rocky in certain parts. We spent the most of the time in the cave focussing on the rough/uneven ground rather than the place - in order not to slip or fall. One can easily slip or fall on the widespread/rocky uneveness here & darkness if you looked up rather than down ;& get sprained ankles or worse injuries if you fall.Do not recommend children, elderly or physically disadvantaged people to visit this cave or any caves.Frankly, we were not keen to see yet another cave but since it was part of our paid day tour, why waste it?

We have been to many waterfalls & certainly this one is at the lower end of the range.Nothing spectacular, rather small & very normal. Skip this place if you have limited time - there are better places to go.

We had a much better time here than at Hamdeok Beach. The water was much more shallow, more friendly for swimmers, less seaweed at low tide areas too. The water was clean and the cafes nearby were cute too.

We had a great time walking thru the lava tubes, talking about how they were formed and all the science behind this ecosystem.  Our friends ask if we recommend it and we do, but you need you to understand its a cave/lava tube and NOT a theme park style attraction.

We had a fine time on Udo Island, where we rented one of the funny little electric cars and were able to see most of the island. It's better to arrive earlier in the day then we did, so you can spend time enjoying that Charming Island. Another highlight was feeding the seagulls with chips you can buy for $2 on the ferry.

We enjoy shopping underground. We were able walk from one end to another. Just remember where you enter. There is a number so you will not get lost.There were beauty products, children clothing, adult clothing, bags, shoes, restaurants, etc. They are not your designer stuff but cheap items. Since winter, they sell winter wear. We bought some face masks, cleanser for less than $10. We also bought bags for $15. The lady said made in korea so we think ok. The backpack is great cos very spacous. Good for traveling. Quality is just ok. Then at one exit near to the wet market, we found a shop called bang bang. It belongs to a friend of the korean actor who starred in the famous korean drama   my love from the star   we were able to buy simple T shirts, socks. They are less than $10. Socks about $3. We actually shop here 2 times when we were staying in ocean suites hotel. It was just 10 to 15 minutes walk to this underground shopping area.There are restaurants here too. We found a good korean restaurant here. It was good food and affordable.

We booked one day tour, but had the best time with Andy so we decided to book one more day. We really think Andy is the best tour guide available in Jeju. Not only professional but he is very caring and very kind.He recommended the best destinations and kindly tried his best to find restaurants for us (we are vegans so it’s quite hard). It was our first time to Jeju and we felt safe traveling with him. You really want him to guide you for your Jeju trip!

We booked a 2 day private tour with Core Travel and it was awesome. It was highly flexible and we could customise it according to our preferences. The tour was done with a comfortable clean MPV and they were considerate to enquire if we needed a baby seat as we had a 10 month old baby with us. Our guide June was extremely polite and accommodating and very patient with us even though we were quite slow at times as we had older adults and a young baby in our small group. She was knowledgeable and explained all the geological processes that formed the various natural sites in Jeju that we visited. She went over the time of the tour and still assured us it was OK even though we felt bad that we couldn’t end the tour on time. She was kind and made suggestions that took into consideration our traveling requirements. One of the highlights was how she shared that she loved watching dolphins off one of the western coasts in Jeju and she drove us there when we expressed that we had not seen dolphins before. We were fortunate that we managed to catch a glimpse of dolphins jumping and playing in the sea before our eyes. If you are travelling to Jeju, it is highly recommended to book with Core Travel, especially more so if you have young kids or old folks as a private tour is so much relaxing and flexible. From booking to finish, the entire process with Core Travel was so efficient and easy. Ask for Guide June, she is the best!

Was here during the winter, winter clothes sold at value. You can get a whole set here, from undies to mittens at a discount price.  Place is well maintained, underground so you're warm.  Not too many restaurants but the space is sprawling and windy, you can get lost. Thankfully there are maps, just remember your entry point to keep your bearings.  Toilets all around, with no bidet.  Things sold were all more or less the same as you spend a bit of time browsing.
Very good for relax and some swimming (water in September was not too hot). If you had a time - visit a nice small island ahead, very recommended! :)

Very beautiful place. Nice people, peaceful place. I want to come next time to visit it once more. We took photo with the founder of this garden. He is very nice person. In the garden you can see bansai trees and feed fishes, also there are some mini shops and cafe were you can drink coffee or the legendary rice wine.
Very beautiful beach for a short visit. Spend some time at the cafe , drink coffee and have some amazing bread

Using Mr.Kang service for 2 days. He is very very nice and helpful. We gave our itinerary and he will drive for us. He is very nice and even gave us a bunch of orange.. my father love it very much. This is my first time in jeju. He even took good picture for my family too. He is very nice, i recomend you for using his service. Thank you Mr.Kang and see you again :)

Understand there are three courses here - 30 mins, 60 and 90. Basically it?s a very light forest with pine and a few other trees that I am not familiar with. You choose the course and just take your time to walk - the air is fresh, nobody speaks loudly. The path will meander through trees, laughing statues, water fountain, and more trees. Would definitely recommend coming this place for those who want to calm their nerves and leave the city behind. We took the 30 mins course and came out refreshed.
Udo is a must visit place in Jeju island! go there as early as you can, so that you can spend a day trip there! Half day trip not enough time to look around.

Total rip off!  The place is very small and totally not worth the ticket price.  We tour the area as best as we could but certainly won't recommend this place to anyone.  Go ONLY if your kids are huge hello kitty fan and you have plenty of time to spare.  Otherwise, save your time and money.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.
This was fun to check out. If you have time to pass, then I would recommend this place. Especially if you have kids, they'll love it here. Lots to read and lots to see.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!

This small rock which located next to beach is famous maybe because of many chines visitors , Highly recommended to not waste your precious time to going there , if u want to eat local food nearby there maybe is not bad idea to visit here otherwise don't .

This place is truly one of a kind! The garden is immaculate and shows many years of hard work, patience and love.The story of the garden itself is worth the visit but the tranquility and peace this place brings is truly astonishingWe were also fortunate enough to spend some time with Director Sung, the creator of the garden. His passion and wisdom is beyond measure and this place is a must see for both locals and visitorsI cannot recommend this place enough and look forward to visiting again

This place is small but surprisingly occupied us half a day. Largely it?s because of the photo moment and also the activities it has to occupy the kids. These activities are drawing, taking self portrait, kids playground, and watching cartoon etc. There is a small cafe to rest your feet while your kids spend sometime at the indoor playground.

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This place is going to be boring if obviously you do not have an interest to look at teddy bears because this is what the place is all about, various themes of teddy bears on display. It also depends on some children, they may or may not like this place. My family love this place (including my parents) so it's not only for children if one have the interest. I even bought a teddy bear wearing a hanbok as a souvenir for myself. There was also a free Elvis teddy bear mini performance which is so cute. Only consider adding this location to your itinerary if you do have the interest, don't waste your time if you don't.

this place is free and located nearby airport. it won't take too much time also, spend around 1hrs here.Sometimes u can see the airplanes landed as the background..kinda cool..the dragon-shaped rock is visible if u take picture with the right angle, otherwise it's just an ordinary rock.

This place is big and we didn?t go through each inch of this place as both of us felt tired when came to this place. If you have time and the leg can support the walk, a good place to spend time with.

This market sells many products either fashionable clothes and branded cosmetics. There're many food shops available with reasonable place too. If you are seeking for sport shoes or toys.You can also find here. Some shops will give you the tax refund and some not.You need to check carefully. The famous cosmetic shops like ETUDE and skin food, some of famous items may not available. There're 11 gates which the even gate no. will locate on the right whereas the odd ones are on the left. It's not complicated and easy to walk. There's restroom available too.If you don't buy the well known brand, you will also find the local Korean cosmetic brand which is very cheap. I buy 12 hand creams with 10,000 won prize and can get the complimentary mask for 10 sheets. It's very good price. The souvenir shop also available here.I would also recommend to come as the choice of your shopping since it's not too crowded like duty free building and you don't need to buy a lot of same items in pack like duty free. As most of Korean cosmetics in duty free would be sold in pack of more than 2 pieces which sometimes you don't need that much.

This market is a great embodiment of a traditional market. There are vegetables, fruits, fish, clothes, shoes, Korean food joints..etc. I recommend visiting it in the morning as it become more crowded after that time. Food smell might be disturbing but you may be able to overcome it. If you are a fan of traditional markets then visiting this market is considered a MUST.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won
This is something for children or adults who have not grown up! Spend your time as you wish, we just walked on...

This is NOT something to do on your own. Going with a small group is best because you will need someone to take photos of you/your friends interacting with all of the   art  . It's a silly good time with lots of themed rooms each one with loads of photos or interactive displays. Watch the floor for markers of where to stand to get the best angle for the optical illusions!

This is not a cave, this is a lava tube so do not expect what you see in caves.  The tube is huge in size.  From the entrance you are able to walk 1km.  At the end you can see the remains of where lava had gone up and out of the tube.  It is not very impressive.  The tube itself is a large tunnel like structure.  There is not much to see and the lighting is a bit insipid.  The good thing is that the entrance fee is only like $2 so you don't need to worry about wasting money.  I am glad I visited but I would have been happy to have just walked down into the tube about 5 minutes, turned around and left.  Walking to the end of the open area is unnecessary and a bit of wasting time.  Spend about 10 minutes and its enough.

This is a good location you should spend time to visit, nice and you can see some different kind of cave, some of the cave have spotlight follow so amazing. friendly reminder, please wear a shoes instead of slipper or sandals because the floor very wet.

This Eco Land is nice and Comfortable for doing Recreation.  Relaxing and Quiet Place to visit.  They also provide Train Inside the Park.   The Train come every 5-10 minutes Here we can decide which area we want to go.  There are area with Park, Lake, Holland Decoration.  There also a place that we can do Recreation with Family Complete with the children playgrond area.  They also have Garden with some Flowers, such as Lavender, Tulips, etc.  They also have Place to have some snack like coffee, churros, ice cream.  Enjoyable place to relax and need some time to enjoy all the area.  Good to Visit.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

They told us the story of korean village and people from last time that how they live and how they do. Actually, I love to know about history of korean. However, all the story that they said it's about the product they gonna sell at the end of the tour. They sell honey, horse bone powder to make you strong, vinegar drink which is more expensive than you buy from supermarket. Horse cream and etc.

they charge admission now to see this seashore.  as if that's not bad enough, it was closed by the time we arrived at 5pm.  but what wasn't closed were the numerous vendor stands that seemingly sprung up to cash in on the tourists here.  the most interesting thing we noticed were various coconuts with small holes drilled in them with a straw sticking out.  this is supposed to be 'fresh' coconut water.  protip: there are no coconuts in korea.  superprotip: they re-use these containers without rinsing them out, over days/months/years, you get the idea.if you don't mind paying to see this 'natural wonder,' at least avoid the vendor stands like the plague, cause that's what you'll likely catch there.

There is nothing much to see except of the cave. But if you spend time to read and understand the formation of the cave. Its quite educational for me.You will be more enjoyed if you slows down your steps and admiring the unique walls in the cave. Instead just walk, walk and walk until the end and took picture of the end of the cave then went back.

The Spirited Garden is a great pastime to spend with friends, the garden is beautiful! There is so much plant life to see with a rich cultural and historical story behind each part of the garden! Plenty of great photo-ops here for your social media or if you are big fan of botany you will definitely enjoy it.

The professional photos are very well taken thus I was quite interested in this place before i go. But basically you will spend perhaps a good 20 to 25 mins walking from one end to another end seeing the same thing (unless you are very interested in rocks or stones) in very dark lighting.. and then another 20 to 25 mins back. I don't think its a bad place.. just not to my liking i guess. If you have time and a good camera and a tripod, you might take some very nice photos there lol

The place itself is huge. We went before lunch and it was a good time because the sun was up. Being a glass museum, most of the art are made of glass and having the sun at its brightest made the art look even more amazing. It's nice to look at the reflections made. There are different signs in Korean, Japanese, and English. They also have shop where they sell little glass artwork. You can bargain with the sellers too. They're nice and friendly.

The place is good only for families with little children.Kids will be excited about the fact that a  car(or bottle) seems to go up on downhill. However, for adults? Not really...If u have plenty of time to spend on the road.

The people here still preserve the living style from ancient time. When we mention to our driver that we wanted to visit a folk village, he asked us if we wanted to visit the   fake   or   authentic  , and here we are, chosen the original folk village.We were greeted by one of the villager there 竊sorry for not remembering his name). He brought us around for a 15 mins tour, introduction to jeju, an island with no gate, no thief and no beggar. And the introduction to jeju's   gate  , haruebang, etc.Towards the end of the trip, he was trying to sell the cactus honey and horse bones medication to us. There's no hard sell though, he just let us go after we said no.

The park is big and have many to see, especially for people who don't know the culture of Jeju. It would be also good for family but since it requires lots of walks I wouldn't recommend elder people who can't walk for a long time. The weather of the day we went wasn't quite good, but the drizzle and fog made that place more mysterious which is quite special because we saw different type of scenery from those pictures you can find from the Internet.

The park has a beautiful array of flowers and other well kept vegetation. The animal displays are somewhat of an after thought, but are ok. This is a good place to spend time outdoors with friends, family, or in a tour group.

The Mysterious road is really mysterious to me! As my friend and I booked a taxi for the day, we still had time on our hands before the day ends, so the taxi driver took us to this road and off his engine. Next thing we know, the car was moving on its on up the slope. Talk about creepy. Can't know what scientific explanation there could be behind this. If you are travelling by car and will pass by here, by all means, experience the wonder.

The museum was very very hard to find. The employees were rude and unpleasant. The glass   art   is just a pile of glorified junk. I regeret wasting my time there with my boyfriend. The entrance fee is a joke  please Do NOT go there

The museum is interesting and probably really fun with children. It is a little strange as there are bears dressed up as princesses, maybe even British royalty and whole safaris. It was interesting to say the least, but I would rather spend my time outside.

The market mainly consists of two parts: a fruit market (mostly for visitors) and a fish market (mostly for local, as visitors basically can?t do anything with the raw fishes). In night time, there is also food stalls near Gate 8 but the number is limited (I think there?s about 20) so the queue is often long - mostly Korean youngsters. My Korean friend told me that Jeju is unique with its rice cake (similar to Japanese mochi) and orange that even Koreans ?have to? purchase as gifts when visiting Jeju thus their prices are not cheap.
the destination is built by legend about dragon who fall from the earth, as tourist object not much to see. it's nature rock, beach and on autum the weather is nice. no need much time

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket
Superb place to go there. Check the cliff, if you have never experienced before. Spend time as much as you wish. Nice place to go.

Service狩狩狩狩狩Experience狩狩狩狩狩Value for money狩狩狩狩狩Highly recommendedFolk village was great and authentic but the guide was probably the best attraction. Second time here with another friend. More time this round to walk leisurely.As said in the title, no wow, OMG thing inside you'll find unless probably you are an geologist, etc. The most memorable is probably the experience of walking on very uneven, ripply hardened lava ground spotted with many puddles in near total darkness through low and tall ceiling of an underground tunnel.

Real value for money being able to see he best of Jeju in the short time we had on the island. Our tour guide, Jin, was excellent and walked us through the itinerary adding in stories about the history of the island and his own experiences. Highly recommended.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands.On our free day we visited Dongmun Market which we thought was a better option than spending so much time in the shopping centers. There are several lanes organized according to the wet market section, fruits and vegetables, packaged goodies to take home, food stalls and dry goods such as clothes. The clothes are of Korean origin of good quality and reasonable price, i.e. a dress for 12,000 kw. In a small stall we tried the Korean fried chicken with hot sweet sour glazing and it was very delicious. The fruit section was a good photo spot with its stalls abound with tangerines. Overall one can see how the vendors, locals and non-locals interact to reflect one aspect of Jeju life.  Very interesting, indeed!

One of the nicest beaches I ever been too and I been to Aruba. The sand is white and clean, waters were shallow for great part of it. I wish I had more time to spend there. I just went but it was warm enough that if I wished I could have swam. I could see it being really crowded in summer. Loved it! Must visit in Jejudo.

On a recent vacation in Jeju, I decided to check out the Ramada Plaza Jeju Casino. My visit was in the mid-afternoon, and there were only a handful of casino patrons inside this small casino.When you enter the casino, they ask for your ID, and then they make a photocopy of it. I do not believe that there is a legal requirement for them to photocopy your passport (or in my case, Korean residency card) for their permanent records. Frankly speaking, I was offended by this requirement. To check a visitor’s identification, yes; permanent photocopied record, no.I had the intention of playing some blackjack, but as soon as I saw that they use continuous shuffling machines, I walked out. It is impossible for a blackjack player to gain the tiniest of advantages when such machines are used. My recommendation to blackjack players: don’t waste your time going to this casino.

review: Named as Eco-park but really artificial at all... Nothing special with ordinary decorations and plants. Fairly speaking, young children will enjoy the train ride but for adults/teenagers not worth spending time here...

My hotel was almost next to exit 1 of this mall so spent quite a bit of time here shopping for Korean cosmetics but otherwise it's just a regular shopping center, nothing special. Didn't try any of the restaurants down there, as I'd prefer to spend more time in the open air. But this mall serves as a great connection point to many other areas of interest within the city including the Mok provincial government historical site and Dongmun traditional market, with clearly marked signs at each exit.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

Mr. Lee was an excellent tour guide! On time for both full day tours, patient and takes great pictures! As a solo traveler this was a wonderful experience in Jeju island mostly because of Mr. Lee. I did both East and West coast tours with him. Car is comfortable and very clean! He was very flexible with the itinerary and squeezed in his favorite waterfall in Jeju my last day! He was awesome and I highly recommend this tour to explore Jeju!

Mazeland was both beautiful AND fun!  We got there close to closing so we didn't get to stay long, but the time we were there was awesome.  I got some awesome photos, and it was really fun to walk around in.  *HIghly recommended.

Lovely autumn morning, clear blue skies, coolest breeze and morning sun, what else do you need for a perfect morning over hot coffee and some oven-fresh pastries?Absolutely nothing else but time to stand still. Plan a late lunch of grilled abalone after this for a prefect ending to a great day.

Just like everyone already mentioned, the road is indeed mysterious as the car would really move uphill on its own. However, it is only a very short stretch of the road. But I would still recommend it if you are self-driving and it's your first time in Jeju. Definitely, something you have to experience.You can also head to the museums that is nearby too after going to this road.
just go and have a look, snap some photo and leave. Dont need to spend too much time on this.  If your schedule are tight, just forget about it

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

I've never think that bonsai garden could be such interesting.Very energy place with good vibes. Don't be in hurry, spend enough time (1-2hrs minimum) for visit that unusual place and you'll feel current moment, your mind will become peaceful and calm. If you are lucky enough - you'll meet the owner and creator of the garden, very special person, who is living directly in heart of his creature.Absolutely recommended as a trip into your inner shiny space! :)

I've never imagine that I could spend 3 hrs for a botanical garden and that will be not enough :)The garden is very well and smart planned! Some small shops with hand made decorations and one or two coffee shop are inside of main building.Possible to   rent   a small funny train for to travel around of territory - but in this case just not possible to see and feel every perfect corner of the external garden as the train is going by schedule and route.

Haenyeo literally means, 'Women of the Sea' and this museum pays tribute to the historical significance of this dying profession.  Solely carried on the backs of women on this island, these incredible ladies have carried their over 400 year old craft into the 21st century where instrumentally built the economic foundation for many of the Jeju natives.  Mothers who passed on their skills and knowledge of the sea to their daughters ensured that this lineage would endure the centuries of time.  However, as the world faces rapid changes and economies - the Haenyeo divers are slowly becoming a ghost of the past.  Recently recognized as an UNESCO intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016, tremendous efforts are in place to preserve this historical tradition.  A bonus of a visit to this museum is a trip to Sunrise Peak where there is a traditional Haenyeo performance.  (admission fee required)However - enroute to Sunrise Peak is the opportunity to meet a handful of Haenyeo divers!  What a thrill to visit with them in their modern 'bulteok' - warming huts.  Of all the sights of Jeju - this is perhaps the one that represents the very backbone of this amazing culture!This is definitely a 'must see'

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

Just got back from Jeju and was talked into doing another submarine tour. I did one near the Ilchulbong Peak and wasn't keen on another one. But this tour was a bit longer and had more marine life. I recommend this tour and also in the same town you can go out in a boat for sightseeing or fishing cheaply.
Definitely recommend the green tea ice cream and tangerine tea.  Brought it back to the States and such a huge hit!
buy the products back unless you intend to go japan. the green tea is one of the best tea ive tasted and im a tea lover so you wont be disappointed.

As far as I know there are two bear museums on Jeju Island. One is the Teddy Bear Museum while the other is the Joanne Bear Museum. My aunt decided to go to the Joanne Bear Museum due to her friends' recommendations. It was the best decision she has made for that Korea trip. I wasn't a fan of teddy bears but I was surprised and overwhelmed by all bears  coming in different colours and sizes. It's even more special because every bear in the Joanne Bear Museum is handmade.Furthermore  the decorations in the Joanne Bear Museum are very interesting too. I have never seen such decorations  using bears to enhance the decorations. I will definitely come back for a second trip!
A family friendly place that you should visit in jeju. Tell in details different type of layout of houses back then.

We went to this beach during the day and kayaked and swam. It was a lot of fun! Then we went at night and it had a wonderful nightlife with restaurants and lights!  *I really recommend this beach!  It wasn't too crowded like the others, and there weren't too many black rocks, and no seaweed.  It was great to walk in the water at night too.  We're going back to this beach again this year!

We just stumbled across this attraction when visiting somewhere else. There was quite a few people there and people seemed to be very interested in the mysterious road. We didn't try driving on it, we just stood and watched the cars.Basically it's a road with a slope, but the cars roll backwards up the slope with the engine turned off. It was quite intriguing to witness and I would definitely recommend seeing it if you are in the area. I wouldn't travel ages to see it though. Right next to the Mysterious Road is street food and drinks if hungry!

We enjoyed this cave.  It's about 1 km to the end where the largest lava  pillar is located and then another 1 km back,  although the walk was relatively flat (no inclines) it was very uneven and slippery in places.  Wear shoes with good traction.  The cave is in a beautiful setting with many public toilets around.

We can't quite remember the order but my wife and I saw 3 waterfalls when we went looking for one. All the waterfalls were spell binding, gushing with water even in summer (April) However, 2 are fenced for safety reasons and the third one has a board warning you against swimming. You can, although, dip your feet in the cold water at the unfenced one. At the first one, you can make a wish and throw a coin into the shallow end of the fall. And if your schedule isn't packed, it's a great place to sit back and read a book.

Was with my photographer here for my prewedding photoshoot. The forest was amazing for a background photoshoot as the trees were tall and very densed. Lighting from the sunlight was just nice, and well covered by the tall trees. There were also a few spots that has wooden chairs built for resting. Recommended for prewed photoshoots!

Walking 2km (to the end of the section open to the public, and back) in a lava tube is a cold, dark and wet affair, but it's a unique and educational experience. The floor is very uneven and there are many puddles to step around. There's not a whole lot to see, but every now and then, features of a lava tube are highlighted and explained. This is not for everyone but if you can appreciate that it's rare to get the chance to walk through a lava tube, go for it. Just be ready for the slightly challenging conditions

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

Very educational walk through the lava tubes.  Be sure to bring a sweater and wear proper footgear (uneven ground).  If you are wearing any light coloured pants or shoes, be prepared to get them soiled alittle.  Basically its a   walk-to-the-end   and back type of attraction.  After the walk, you'll learn more about lava tubes and volcanic eruptions.

This museum is intended for tourists who love to take photos. Most of the artworks housed in the museum are modified versions of original paintings so that you can integrate with the painting. Hence bringing a camera or a smartphone is a must! A companion is also a must since taking a   selfie   to achieve the desired effect might prove to be impossible.This is one of the two 3D interactive museums in Jeju Island. The other one Trick Art Museum is located farther in the eastern part of the island. We went to this place as it is nearer to the Jungmun Area where most hotels (Hyatt Regency Shilla Hotel Lotte Hotel etc.) are located.Aside from the in-house artworks there is also a park with sculptures and play sets that will be appreciated by kids. Tips: avoid flash photography to get the desired effect; bring a jacket w/ hoodie (can be used in some of the artworks); and black pants make people blend better with the background.Admission costs KRW 8000 per person. The entire area is air-conditioned and wifi access is offered for free. Other extras include lockers to deposit your bags as this may hamper your experience.This is a fun destination for couples families or small groups.

This is an amazing market which sells almost everything you can think of. We went with the objective to enjoy some local snacks, get some hallabong tangerine and some jeju chocolate for our friends back home. Although the season for tangerine is over, there are still many available in the market. Prices for the tangerine are quite consistent so we just bought from the first few stalls we saw. There is not many brands for the jeju chocolate so we just picked one and we were told to compare prices with different stalls. For the same brand and quantity, I was quoted 7k, 8k and 10k korean won by 3 different stalls. We ended up buying from one of the biggest stalls in a corner. That said, I do encourage you to buy from the market. I found the same chocolate at the airport and it was selling at 15k korean won. We were too tired to get any local snack in the end but if I ever go back, I will try the seafood restaurant in the market. Was told they serve the cheapest and freshest sashimi in Jeju.

This is a massive lava tube that the public are allowed to visit and does give you a real sense of the magnitude of the volcanic activity that created this island. For that alone you should visit.It is a nice cool 1km walk to the end and then, of course, you have to come back.A good experience.

Really cool volcanic flowlines and terrain.  Bring a rain jacket with a hood or umbrella and decent shoes.  Although I saw a woman in heels, but wouldn't suggest it. ouch.Take flash off your camera and use tripod for good pics.Does not take long at all to get at end and back.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands. One of these was the Chilseongro Shopping Street. Fortunately, I had bookmarked Dongmun Market on Kakao map and it was a short walk from there. I had no plans to buy branded clothes (nor any clothes for that matter) so I ditched Chilseongro and headed to Dongmun.The Dongmun Market is a wet market, a traditional market. Pretty much everything in Jeju is available here?clothes, tangerines, chocolates, seafood, household items, food. The prices here were a lot lower than the chocolate stores and souvenir centers that our tour group operator brought us to.At Dongmun, you can haggle, especially if you buy plenty. I decided to buy chocolates to bring back home to our office staff. Since there were plenty of stalls selling chocolates, I compared prices first. I ended up buying from an elderly lady who offered the lowest price. I got more than 60 boxes and she gave me lots of freebies. There are stalls that had different types of food. Some even had live seafood available and they will cook it for you. I was too full to try out the local food, but I did miss having photos taken.There were a handful of stalls that sold kitsch souvenir items like keychains and magnets. There were two large stalls that had numerous items on display; their prices were high though. I ended up buying from the other stalls whose main items being sold were something else and just happened to have magnets and keychains on the side. Nevertheless, the prices at the souvenir shops in Seongsan IIchubong were lower; I wished I had bought there instead.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

It's a great and interesting place! When else can you just go through a   natural tunnel   made by lava? The whole place is very well maintained and clean. Price is inexpensive and there is also a small restaurant and shop. You may think of bringing a second shirt because inside the lava tube is it cold (12째C/54째F). Fun fact, there is no exit at the end of the tube, you have to go all the 1 km back again ;)

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

Interesting place... Love to see how they really appreciate haenyeos, as one of their mother culture... A unique and honourable profession for jeju women in the old days and even now... How women are very appreciated since born and high hopes for doing the profession as backbone of the jeju families..The museum really tells a lot about how the haenyeos lives and even their struggle in the war era... For those who loves visiting museums, its really recommended!

Interesting experience  as we we pull to neutral gear, release the accerator, the car just go forward, upwards. The mysterious road is short, we made a few rounds. There is a car park where you turn in to go a few rounds if you wanted to. We tried the  same stretch to road after the end point. The car just go backward on the upward facing slope.

If the header caught your attention then do not miss the show and watch acrobatic dolphins seals etc jump fly and talk... no I'm kidding! LOL! But it's really a neat place to bring the kids to spend the day. Daddies and mummies it'll be educational back to   school   and it's not just aquatic. Expect to spend at least a gd half day. Enjoy!!!

review: I’ve visited Jeju in mid-April with my friend and we’ve gotten John to bring us around in Jeju. It was a great experience, John was punctual and well-articulated(telling us fun facts/history) along the tour. Also, he took initiatives to show us more spots throughout the tour for “instagram worthy” photos! We will definitely get John as our tour guide if we come back to Jeju again!

I have 2 little boys. One thing for sure, this not a place for them. Probably the girls might like it. I don't recommend this place to those who do not fancy Teddy Bears. But if you wish to buy teddy bear souvenirs this might be the right place. In fact we bought several souvenirs for the little girls back home. My advise is SKIP this place if you're not Teddy Bear lovers.

I guessed many have mentioned that this was a typical market and I do not think they were wrong. However, it really depends the reason for your visit. If you are here to try cheap and good raw and fresh seafood (eg: raw fish slices for 10000won only), OR to try a variety of local food (eg: Sundae aka blood sausage, traditional fishcake stick, Kimbap, fresh Jeju orange juices, different types of kimchi, korean rice cakes, croquette, Tteokbokki, hotba, Modeumjeon - where they eat during new year and jeons, OR to purchase souvenirs and snacks for your family and friends then you are at the right place! It was also cheaper to purchase dried goods like ikan bilis and kelp in the market than supermarkets.We were at Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market before coming to this market and we found that stalls that sell Jeju's souvenirs and local snacks such as Jeju crunch chocolate were cheaper in this market. The shop owners also gave us a handful of other snacks to try after our purchase in hope that we would be back for more. In Summary, this was a good place to try many local food at a smaller amount and a place to purchase affordable snacks for gift at a cheaper price.

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

A veey dark and long walk with informative description on different formation of rocks created after cooling of the lava. Interesting and educational, no exit @ the end of the walk so would have to take the same route back.

We visited in the peak of winter so there was very heavy snow fall.We came quiet under prepared in terms of walking gear so the walk to the crater was pretty difficult. I wouldn't recommend for elderly or anyone with mobility issues but this is from my experience with snow so can't comment on the difficulty during other seasons.

I got my discount ticket online via KLOOK. If visit on the day without buy online cost 39800won per person.

review: Some sports brand but nothing exciting. We came twice but still we did not find any shops we like. Compared to shops in Seoul this is pale. Most shops selling winter coats. At end of this street turn left and just outside the wet market we find a shop bang bang. They have 2 floors lower for women and second for men. Managed to get some simple t shirts. Design was just very simple. Other than these nothing exciting here. The wet market is more exciting with tourists the korean snacks there were great! Here in this shopping street you get cafe. Very quiet cos winter. There is a shop selling desugner embroudery hackets and jeans gor guys but very expensive. The staff was speaking cantonese to the chinese customers so we assume Hong Kong shop. Nicer Jackets were $500 onwards.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is a UNESCO World Heritage site. I love it going there. Very peaceful and very greenish place at the bank of the see. I will strongly recommend you to go there. Really an awesome place to visit. Do NOT miss it.

Not that easy to find foods for muslim  but if you are not strict the muslim-friendly will do for you if you ask around what theyre put inside.. i looked around the musling speaking person to guide me on this. This one kind Korean salesgirl helped me on this. ^^ so please dont be shy to ask around yaa..^^

My girlfriend and I went for fun. It literally is like a museum. They have a bunch of statues outside and inside there is a lot of information to explain themes relating to sex. There is two floors. The first floor is about different positions amongst a lot of other stuff. The whole first floor is almost exclusively written in Korean. Unless you can read Korean I would skip it. The second floor does have English. I would only go if both floors have English. It is not for non-Korean speakers.
Just a quiet place with so much greenery ... :) fantastic green tea ice cream :D The staff is very friendly despite not being able to speak English .
