What was originally a cultural and historical tour ended with a sales talk of the local health products. They were peddling hard, so be strong with your will power if that's not what you want. The whole village is van be finished in 20 minutes and it felt more like China than Korea with the many fluent Chinese speaking guides who I think are actually Chinese

Went to hyeopjae beach just to try swimming while i was in Jeju. Rented a car and drove there, thought that parking was gonna be a challenge but managed to get one in mere minutes. Mum didnt swim, so we rented an umbrella + mat for her to wait at. Cost us 15K won. Not sure if it was cheap or expensive. They guy attending to the rental didn't speak english, thank God for a local young chap who helped us translate.Loved the vibe of the beach, everyone there was enjoying the waves. Where I'm from, our sea is not as rough. so it was really different to see everyone in their floaties waiting for waves to hit them.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We visited May 2016, rainy weather but still open. The staff or local tour guide are very helpful that they provide umbrella that we can use around the folk village. Take note, the staff tour guide we met don't speak much of English, good thing we have our own private tour guide that help on translation. Appreciate the staff for her patience because even though all of her explanations need to be translated, I felt like she didn't skip any detail that we need to know. My favorite part when she showed us those black pig that is famous for their BBQ. Also, the drink that they offer is good that we end up buying one.

we saw a signage stating 'can speak mandarin' with some car parking space outside so we went down, apparently is a very small 'display village' which the 'guide' explained some of the history & activities. didn't manage to see live black pigs. the 'guide' saw we cannot enter the actual village as was occupied with people (which I am not sure how true it is). and they started selling us product in the end... however we manage to see folk village which we think should be the 'real / correct' one when we left and go straight down the road and see walls surrounding with flag & a big map (which too bad we can't understand)

Very nice island. You take a ferry from Jeju Island to Udo in 5-10 minutes you get there. I rented a quadricycle and it was fun to discover the island by this transportation mode. The ocean is clean and warm; pretty nice to bathe!The shops however don't speak English normally. If in Jeju, I totally recommend Udo as a spot to visit.

The tour was neat until we were all trapped in a little room for a sales pitch at the end.  It felt a bit awkward for a while as the little Jeju lady gave us a bit of a stare down to purchase some tea and horse oil skin moisturizer.  If you don't speak any Korean, you do not want to go here.  You wouldn't know what is so intersting about this place other than the old, traditional looking homes with thatch roofs.

The cone-dome architecture is interesting, the roofs of different gardens within culminates to a peak into the center of the compound and u can take a lift up to catch a 360 panoramic glimpse of the surroundings (see pic). However, adult tix are at 9000krw per person which is not cheap for what u get within. The place has lots of potential but not that well-maintained as the place looks very weathered on the whole. There is a garden dedicated to tropical fruits but those are mostly common fruits for southeast Asians like us. There were only chrysanthemums at the entrance even though it's supposed to be in-season. Parking is easy though, and free, like most places of interests at Jeju. Overall, this place is more suitable for the elders and for people dropping by to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and Seonimgyo Bridge, which is just next door. Otherwise, my 2c worth - it'll be fine to spend your money elsewhere.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is the most eastern part of Jeju Island and has the same terrain as Punchball. When you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, you can see the beautiful sea and clear sky endlessly, and when you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with a cool breeze, you feel good. Also, there are many tourist attractions nearby, so it is convenient to move around. In addition, there are many restaurants that cook braised kingtail fish and roast caught in Jeju, and there are many unique and delicious restaurants around. I recommend that you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with your family at least once.

Mr Kim is a very friendly and experience driver who can speak some english and some mandarin. He recommended a good foods to us and we enjoyed it a lot, also very helpful in finding answer for our questions. Good service and hope

Most people or tour guides will recommend you to go there for the seafood. However, the stall owners cannot speak other languages. The ones who do speak Chinese are too touristy. Those that sell abalone don't sell fish and vice versa. Better to go to a good restaurant for a taste of seafood stew. Fruits are ok. The good mandarin oranges are sold in boxes. I see locals buying boxes of oranges.

If you need a good work out, this forest in Jeju is worth paying a visit. The autumn 10C air is perfect, although the leaves were only starting to blend with the sun, you can imagine the shades of red, orange and yellow if it's at its peak!  The old nutmeg trees provided good photo opportunities for those with a passion for nature.

I went to Udo with a group of friends. It was really nice, we went around the island with rented bicycles (10.000 KRW for the afternoon). We swam in an incredibly clear water.I recommend going to Sunrise peak afterwards, walking along the coast gets you there in 15 min and seeing the sunset was an amazing experience.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.

A very small traditional village attraction with free guide who can speak Mandarin. Very limited traditional houses to look at. No big deal. The attraction is apparently made famous by a TV series that filmed there. Nothing much to see but the guide took great efforts in explaining about each mini-attraction in the village. We ended up in a hut being given explanations on the local products they were selling (e.g. local honeys, herbal health drinks, horse bone powder, horse creams). We were not forced to buy but given that the tour was free, we were obliged to buy stuff that we could easily find for lower prices as the markets, especially Dongmun Traditional Markets in Jeju City.
Went there to browse around local market and foods. Ended up eating lots of local food fare and buying goodies at good bargain. Would recommend a visit there

We visited for the night market. Nearby there is a multi storey public parking. The first stall butter fried rice with spicy pork is truly delicious and their orange juice (hallabong) freshly made is very nice though it is slightly expensive than the other stores. But it is freshly blend thus I love it and it taste good. Others stall look okay for me.
Visited during a weekend and it is full of life. A lively market that sells local produce with a handful of restaurants within the market. Worth a short visit if you are around the area.
This is not a very big market but there are lots of authentic Korean food here for you to choose. It?s a good place to experience the local fare.Recommended place to go if you are in Jeju.

The street food stalls at night were awesome in the market. However all the good one has long lines and slow moving as most of them are cooking in front of you. Not knowing which one is the best  we choose to join the crowd and stand in line with others and skipped the other with short lines. Parking is terrible even Google Maps shows many nearby parking lots. We tried two separate lots and both were full. Instead of waiting someone to pull out  I ended up parking on the side of nearby street and walked to the market.
The market sells mainly Jeju produce such as the famous Jeju oranges. Colourful market. Come during weekends where there is a small section selling inexpensive local food.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

Perhaps it was too early in the morning (0900) and the food stalls are just starting. Didn't end up eating any snacks which I originally was planning for breakfast.Nice authentic place for local marketing.

Market place selling mainly seafood and fruits. We reached there around 12pm was hoping to have lunch. However most of d restaurant looks closed. How can one place be closed on a Saturday?? We end up drinking hot chocolate in one of the cafe.

Located next to dongmun and jungang underground market so you can combine all three in one go. Not much to see and shop. You will probably eat in dongmun. We took dinner at the end of the street in a Japanese restaurant and was really good food. Jeju has a small population and do not really expect much shopping I could not find a memory card for my camera :-(

It's a pretty big local market but after awhile u realised it's repeating. Be adventurous I say and try the different local food and snacks despite the language barrier. The stall ajuma are really friendly.Parking is a bit challenging and don't forget to check out the Black Pork street nearby (10-15mins walk) for some nice BBQ.

It's a nice shopping street that is about 5 min walk from Dongmun Market and beside Jungang underground shopping place that is closed till August 2016. There is Tommy Hilfiger interesting souvenir store The Islander local designer and mid-range fashion shops shoes and stationery stores and cafes as well. Nearby at one end is the attraction Gwandeokjeong Pavilion. At the other end of the street there is also a black pork street.

It is a big market selling vegetables and local products. However plenty of plastic tent restaurants at the end of the market and prices are much lower than in town. You can get all the cooked korean food here and delicious too.Also a place to buy all the korean street food and snacks.No problem with taxis as there is a proper taxi stand. Market is clean and well arranged.
Interesting Folk Village with all traditional life in the past. but at the end the guide will try to sell the product which price more expensive than city / market (maybe cause its tourist object ?)

If you are looking for variety of street food for consumption  don't go too early for breakfast. Strangely  I thought markets opens early  especially on weekends but I guess I was wrong. Otherwise  I returned in the evening to try out the street food and check out the varieties of fresh food.
I like Dongmun market most. You could get gifts for your family and friends. They sell nice and big orange. There's a lot to sell and a lot to eat.
I experienced a nice and reasonable seafood meal at this Dongmun market.The stall owner is friendly.

Chilsungro Shopping Street consists of 2 sections. One section is the covered arcade with shops selling international and boutique stuff. This stretch is much quieter. Perpendicular to it is the open space section much more human traffic with shops in the lower to mid tier ranges such as New Balance ABC Mart etc.Suggest to visit this section in the evenings. The shops lightings plus the music add to the shopping ambience in Jeju. You can also visit the nearby Dongmun market Jungang underground shopping centre and the black pork street.
... With more unfriendly than friendly people.You should try the food prepared by lovely people at the side entrance to the market.

You might go in the market which is partially underground and think you?re in this. You?re not. This is about 100 little shops with similar wares. About 3 places to eat including don burger. One neat thing about this is that they say it is the largest in the world. It?s one block but in the middle flares out to several aisles. I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)
we had so much fun in the market.   ajumas' were very friendly. we already ate alot in the market without spending lot of money. i really liked having korean rice sake

We had dinner at a resto in Blackpork street in Jejusi which locates opposite Dongmun market. The price was 14.000w/200gr (normal pork) and 18.000w/200gr (black pork). Our meal was so delicious, it costed nearly 40.000w for two of us. You are highly recommended to have a try with this once you visit Jeju, as black pork bbq is one of the island?s specialties. Near the Blackpork street is the shopping street and underground shopping area where you could have a walk after a heavy meal.
This market sell a lot of Jeju specialities, eg, Hallabong, seafoods etc. Nothing really very special unless you intended to get some souvenirs from Jeju Island or you wanna to get some local food.

This market is popular amongst the locals and tourists, hence expect this place to be crowded. Majority of shops are selling oranges and fresh seafood. Besides these, there are other sections selling meat, vegetables, spices, snacks etc. I bought 1 stick of crab and seafood balls for 4,000 won. Recommend to try their famous peanut ice cream for 1,500 won. Yummy.

This is an authentic market which embodies local life on the island. It has so much to offer... There is an entire section devoted to the economy of the elderly, selling their goods and calling sweet encouragements to passerbys. There are regional fruits and veggies, artisan crafters, cloth and clothing sellers, seafood and fresh meats, animals, and a multitude of food trucks/stalls.This is the ideal market for immersing yourself in Jeju and Korean culture. It's open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27thPictured: a pressure cooker used for puffing rice and corn, cooking beans, etc...

This is a very big market with lots of local foods you can try while walking around. Prices are very reasonable too, and the people friendly and helpful, no pressure sales at all. Best market we've been to whilst travelling!

Our FIRST meal in JEJU and we were just spoilt for choices. This is traditional market and we had so much fun walking in the market.The large boxes of tangerines greets you at the entrance and as you explore further, you see endless rows of fresh seafood. We randomly selected some food and they tasted delicious!

On our second day in Jeju, my parents and I went on a market blast in Jeju. We went to the following (1) Seogwipo Olle Market (2) Seogwipo 5-Day Market and (3) Dongmun Market.I highly recommend both Dongmun Market and Seogwipo Market. If you are living in Jeju City, visiting Dongmun would suffice. Fresh and relatively reasonable prices. Go to those stalls that display price tag to avoid paying a   premium  .

My wife and I live in China and have been to our share of markets all around Asia.  That said, this is one of our favorites!  Great street food, friendly vendors, plenty of selection, and without the terrible smell that is typical for Asian markets like this!

Its fish market but have a lot of store sale a souvenir and gift item like small soju and jeju orange, jeju cohocolate and sama candies and friend...and at the end of dongmun market they have delicious street food....and yummy

Its a short street UG mall sells things you will find in normal shops in Jeju.  The catch here is that this place is not just underground BUT its air conditioned.  Its maintained very well with clean toilets.  We spent about 40 mins leisurely but didn't buy anything in the end.  I won't say its a must-go place but if you happened to be at Dongmun market, its a short walk to this place.

I live quite close to this beach and really love it. On days ending on 1 and 6, there is a traditional market which is nice. Many restaurants to choose from, as well as an Olive Young, Spanish restaurant, Starbucks, etc however I prefer buying CU drinks and sitting in the sand. Sunset is AMAZING here.

Every kind of locally caught fish and produce can be found in the Dongmun Market, as well as some imported items.  Don't miss out on getting a box of mandarins or Hallabong oranges.  Try the kiwifruit, too.  It's also a good place to sample Jeju's   street food   made by local vendors.  You can find all sorts of clothes and many household gadgets, accessories, rain shoes, Korean quilts, souvenirs...you name it, it's most likely in the market.  You can visit Dongmun during the day or at night.  Nearby, you can also see Sanjicheon Square, where local performers can also be found playing, singing or dancing for tips.  Some local seniors and maybe a few homeless persons frequent the area, adding to its   color.    The square is by a small tidal inlet, and features a quaint railing with traditional Korean characters on the railing.  Do check it out!

Dongmun Market is filled with every possible product that you can make out of tangerines.They grow tangerines on the island. There is tangerine chocolate, tangerine juice, tangerine cakes etc. There is also fish and food stalls. If you want to get your friends gifts or souvenirs from Jeju, you can buy them from here.

As you are planning to visit jeju and there are not alot of activities there, i recommend you to visit this market. You will see lots of differnt and new things to see, also you can enjoy the food there, so dont miss it

Although there are many small vendors and shops during the day, the best part is at night when the food stalls appear. There are many (mostly Korean) options. From burgers, to tempura and ice cream burritos, you will not go hungry! On average, the food costs around 7,000 krw per meal. Smaller items like gimbap and individual tempura is cheaper. I would not recommend this market for any type of clothing shopping. The interior is mainly dried fish, nuts, juices, souvenirs, some bbq, and a couple sit down restaurants.
Able to find lots of local produce in this market. Fruits especially orange varieties, black pork knuckles, kimchi of various kind. An interesting market to visit. Recommended.

A traditional market which sells a lot of Jeju Oranges, jeju chocolates, seafoods (e.g. Fish, abalone, etc), pork, orange juices and many more.. the price of the chocolates is the same as any other stores outside. The price of the other products are also reasonable.You can visit this market and have a feel of their largest traditional market in Jeju. I went there with my friend before 8pm but some of the stores had started cleaning and preparing to close the shop. The market is open till 9pm (if I am not wrong).

*Firstly, don't go here. Instead, go to the 5 Day Market (誘쇱ㅼ쇱 Minsok O-il Jang) in Jeju-si. It is open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27th.*As for Dongmun, the best part is the 몃 (Hoddeok). Along one of the side alleys are these beautiful grandmas (癒몃 Halmeoni) who sell fried rice pastries filled with cinnamon, brown sugar, and nuts (Hoddeok). This is some of the best I've had in Korea. SO delicious. There are three of these stalls in this alley. The best, and oldest one, is furthest inside the market.The bad: vendors are rude and over priced. Their goods are not the highest quality and they know that the tourists don't know how to find better quality.

Wonderful beach in Jeju island. Very clear water. Amazing colors and good vibes all around. You can spend here one day to have relax and chill out. And If you want you can walk around. There are close to the beach a lot of restaurants and caf챕s

While its really small against Western style theme parks we enjoyed an afternoon on the rides.  Also if you arw a US military service member or have a military ID (they don't know the difference between a dependent or soldier) you can get an amazing deal.  It was 9k won for 2 day combo pass for the theme park and the water park!!! Which is usually 39k won.  There is also a discount if ypu are staying at one of the resort hotels.  The park was clearly designed by someone who has visited and studied the Disney parks specifically Tokyo Disney Sea.  Which isnt a bad thing just needed to be mentioned.  This was our 2nd visit and have never had to wait in a line for the rides.  Also the rides are enjoyable the staff is friendly & helpful and the park is very well maintained.

Was expecting more. I think once you are in Jeju you just feel like everywhere will be magical but when you reach places that give off mediocre vibes you tend to get disappointed. So don't come here with high expectations.This place is too touristy and honestly I'd rather kayak in Bali (actually water rafting there is awesome) or in Laos. Or even in Kota Kinabalu or Thailand.
Very beautiful series of waterfall with each ranging 100 to 200 meters apart from other (3 stages waterfall). Recommended for nature lover and those who love to know the history.

Very beautiful beach although one has to pay a large amount for a spot with an umbrella on the main beach. You can however walk just a bit further and find another beach. Beautiful beach with clear water. It can become crowded in summer over the weekends
Very atypical road. Strange to understand. Please take a bottle of water with you to see the mystery in action :) but do not spend more than 15 minutes here

Trip with friends to see underwater animals; sharks star fishes and other tortoise and outside aquarium full happiness with mini korean mart coffee and drinks and if you all like Korean food & beverages terrace

review: This waterfall truly was magnificent to see. I recommend going early in the morning (ticket office opens at 8:00 am). It was 8:30 am when I visited and there were a few people. At one point they all left and it was only me and the waterfall. Truly amazing. Definitely go before before all the tourists get there!!!
This was so beautiful! I went during April and there was a lot of water going down the falls. Such a picture perfect spot! I highly recommend it to all visitors.

This is a three tiered waterfall. To see all three you must walk a lot of staircases. It is much smaller than what I thought but where it is quite beautiful. If in Jeju I recommend a visit(if you love the nature).

there's nothing much to do. just walk a bit and you see waterfall right down to the sea. they said this is the only one in Asia. i did spend few minutes here. people who love nature and photography will love it here.

The temple is super huge and well decorated. There are three layers the first layer is for the believers to worship the Buddha. Second floor is a place where you can talk to the Buddhist monks about your difficulties you faced in your life and have their spiritual purification. Of course some ?쁤oodwill??you have to forgive to this temple I saw one of the believer distribute a considerable fortune to that temple that believer must treats Buddha sincerely. In the entrance of the temple there was rice selling which is the accumulation of capital for the construction use. My mum bought one small pack of rice which costs 10K to support the running of the temple. There is also a water well besides the temple which brings lucky to the people who drink you shouldn?셳 miss that opportunity.Even though you are not a Buddha believer like me you are strongly recommended to go to that temple to have a look of the huge architecture and take pictures with the nice atmosphere.

The cave is cold and wet. It's not easy to walk on undulating floor filled with watery potholes. Certain section you have to bend your body as the ceiling is too low. The cave looks the same from the opening to the end.

Staying in Seogwipo we were lucky enough to be able to walk to these amazing waterfalls which fall into the sea.  We descended  down some wooden steps to the beach and clambered over rocks to get close to the falls.  There was a great atmosphere there with many tourists all happy to help take photos of each other with the falls behind.  Well worth a visit.
Spent several afternoons here. When you have nice sunny weather for the day the beach is a good place for young kids - the water is calm and clear. Highly recommended.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill
Lovely waterfall that fall directly into the sea. Very interesting and fun! Highly recommended. Great to bring children too!
Long lava tube and if you are into stones and caves you will find it interesting. Inside was cold and some water drops coming from ceiling. Once you reach the end that it just take a picture then go.

Less crowded than many other attractions somehow. A beautiful temple and big! Small cave behind temple worth checking out. Don't forget to drink of the water legend has it you will live a longer life!

It?s does appears that the law of gravity is defied! Haha. Big ample car park available at site if u drive. Nice lady at the stalls along the road facilitated my science experiment by lending me a water bottle to roll on the road. And yes! It does appears that the water bottle was rolling uphill against the law of physics. Its worth a visit if u are in town!

I took the PADI Open water diving course with Good Diver. I am contend with the service they provided and thinking of getting my Advanced Openwater diver license with Gooddiver next month. It was an amazing experience. I felt comfortable during the whole course and could enjoy my first diving experience 100%. All the instructors were so patient that they made sure I was fully ready to descend and start the journey. I am so looking forward to diving again!

I am 6 years old. And I like to swim. It was very cold and cool. The water was kind of yucky. Plastic and rubbish. It looked like it was good for sand castles but daddy forgot to bring the bucket and spade for sand castles. Some waves were big and at first I was scared but then I learned to jump the waves. The surfers were clumsy because whenever there's big waves the surfers fall off. There were a lot of surfers. Mummy's Favourite bit was eating the shells on the rocks with the old aunties. The shells looked like snails and they moved and I thought they are disgusting! My Brother and me really really like Swimming. The end. That's all.

Had a long bikecycle trip from Jeju-do city to which I ended at this beach.It's like a small bay with white sand beach. was pretty crowded although it wasn't the season. water sport wasn't operational

Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.It was really nice  I recommend it.It's not a waterfall all year around  some people say they didn't find a waterfall  I did though.Visited in Summer of 2015

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction. We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water. Walking through the cave was thrilling and filled with excitement. Round trip to and fro the cave took us about 1hr30mins. Would highly recomend to anyone visiting Jeju Island. Proper shoes are also recommended as it can be very slippery and slip and fall may happen. Kids and Older people may find this attraction tough and difficult to walk through.

Cool and refreshing. The rocks just at the foot of the waterfall are difficult to walk down. Not recommended for old people.I could not find the inscription which this waterfall is famous (go check out the history/story behind this)!

Car move uphill automatically when in neutral gear. Water don't flow down but up. Pretty interesting when you are in a car experiencing so. Suggest to come here if you are going to Love Land else skip it. Suggest to spend maximum 15mins here.

Came with my 80-year old dad and we had a slow walk along the uneven ground. Would recommend wearing waterproof as water drips fr the ceiling. It's is also a little chilly inside the tube (abt 8 degrees C) The place is also dim so some agility is needed to prevent slipping but it is generally safe. Just walk slowly. Overall it's an enjoyable experience as we marveled at the forces of nature that made the tube possible.

And a nice one too :) You can watch seals penguins otters being fed. The main tank (5000 t of water) is full of stings sharks and smaller fish. Very calming. They also have the outside arena with dolphins and sea lions. Reccomended :)

review: a cliff beside the sea fell with fresh water. Thre is a historical legend about a staff of the 1st great empire of China that he wants to be immortal. The story is also about the name of this city. sea woman inside the park.

You will have to try it youself to experience it! Tried it with a water bottle but it doesn't work. Tried it with a car and shifted to neutral, the car will ascend the inclining road. Quite interesting but will be bored after 5 minutes.

You need to purchase a ticket at 2000won each and then take 130 steps down a flight of stairs to get to the waterfall. Comfortable shoes are recommended if you want to get closer to the waterfall. It is advisable to use your feet to check for the stability of the rocks before stepping on them as there were some loose and moving ones amongst the pile of rocks. The rocks nearer to the waterfall are wet so be careful if you want to get even closer to the fall. The waves crashing on the shore are also rather strong, so be more cautious if you?re moving nearer towards the shore.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.

review: Yes, you will able to see water bottle accend up the road without any force applied to it and when you switch off your car engine or shift to Neutral, your car still able to accend the inclining road. But after 10 minutes, you will be bored and it's only work a certain stretch of road only.

yes we took that long but it was definitely a highlight of our trip...start early, 630 to 7am would be good... as it was nov, we ended trekking the last part in the dark... a torchlight would be a good idea...there's a shelter 3/4 up that sells water and instant noodles...still some snacks as you trek might be a good idea
Would recommend to all visitors of Jeju. Nice atmosphere, clean beach, blue water, and great scenery. A little rocky in the water but overall it was peaceful!

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

We went on a very rainy day, so not many people.    Neither of us had any trouble with footing.   It was not slippery at all!     Huge level of water flow.    I can?t believe they found it necessary to have a no swimming sign as if anyone would even attempt it.   Maybe when the water flow was greatly reduced.    We only went to the 1st and 2nd falls.     Enjoyed them.   Entire walk for the 2 doesn?t take more than 30 minutes.   I imagine on a nice day there were be a large number of vendors at the end  but this day, there was no one out.
We went in July end and found this waterfall good.It was loud,nice place to get some snaps. scenic beauty is good.Recommended for family.

we visited this place with little or less expectation as many friends had said it too overrated but to our surprise is pretty awesome. Maybe because there was strong wind and rain the waves were very strong. The waves were hitting almost the observation point. We bought rain coat outside the cliff entrance for 2000wons (2$) and trust me its best decision we did. We were showered with water like anything as there was rain and wind. maybe in other season you dont need to worry aobut it. the phone number listed on site took to the parking lot the resort next to cliff, had to walk a bit to reach it but got to see the resort common area with some nice garden and statues!

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

we can enjoy this place with family and toddler or young kids,  not recommend for gentlemen. but very educative for children. located inside the Jungmun Tourist Complex, you can get anythink you need in this tourist complex like various restaurant, hotels , 3D art museum, Belive it or not. Kpop Museum , Conventionl Centre , Waterfall Etc

We came here after the Manjungal caves. The maze is challenging enough and took us about 35min to solve, but it was fun and worth the entrance price. It was a hot day so take a bottle of water with you to stay hydrated. Also, whilst in the maze we noticed some pretty large spider webs with some fairly big spiders, so careful of those. All in all, its a great family activity. There's also some lovely cats in the park that are friendly and you can pet them.

Visited this place which is really a lava tube rather than a cave.  It is about 1 kilometer from end-to-end.  Inside the tube you can see different rock formations created by the lava flow, among them the turtle-shaped rock at 600-meter mark.  It is cool inside the tube and water is dripping everywhere.  It is recommended that you wear appropriate footwear while taking this tour as it could really be slippery and some areas are not so well-lit.  Maybe this is intentional to give the place a more realistic feel.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

This waterfall falls into the ocean so it?s higher than the Cheon ji Yeong falls. The steps are steep, easy going down, harder to get up. Not recommended for people with limited mobility. No wheelchair or stroller friendly.
This landmark is very well maintained with beautiful structures. Very instagram friendly. Location is also pretty near many places like teddy bear museum, several waterfalls and casino resorts.

This is, so far, the best waterfall I have ever been. You need to go down from a lot of big rocks to go near the falls. That is what makes it exciting. Wear comfortable shoes and I recommend to wear pants.

This is my favorite as the waterfalls and the blue water coupled with mandarin ducks swimming and moving around, I really feel like I'm in a fantasy land or living in the fairy tales movie that we used to see.  Highly recommended for photography and relaxation!

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

This fall flows right into the ocean. i liked this one better than the others in the city because you can get into the water at the base of the falls and get your feet wet. also there was a tent with some of the famous diving grannies selling raw seafoods. i highly recommend trying this as it was a truly unique experience. the raw plate cost 20,000w which was cheaper than most of the nearby restarunts.

This beach is surrounded by cafes, seafood, and one amazing restaurant in particular -   Arepa Grill!   At the end of the main strip facing the water, this place offers the most amazing Venezuelan food and ice cold beer They have a delicious vegetarian arepa that they can make vegan upon request. It's a nice change from the cafes that are all quite similar. I did, however, enjoy the bean bags at   Woodstock.

This beach is a great place for tourists! Upon arriving there are lots of vendors with delicious food and things you might need for the beach (towels, hats, beach mats, swim suits, booze, etc). The main beach is usually very crowded (understandably). I like to go to the beach to the right, it's just a 5 minute walk on the sidewalk, clearly visible with a clear understanding it's leading to another beach. This part of the beach seems to be less crowded with all of the same benefits! Great place to relax, enjoy the sun, and swim in the water!
There are many caf챕s, restaurants and convenience stores. Not my favourite beach but in general very nice and clean water. I recommend it if you come with children.

The waterfall is beautiful, it gave me the urge to jump in it under the hot sun. There is a entrance charge for that. For those who are from places like Malaysia, Philippines where surrounded with beautiful waterfalls, you might don't feel like spending money just to see this waterfall.

The water is amazing. There are 3 waterfall spots and a beautiful bridge to see at this attraction. Highly recommended although the walk can be a pain, especially the last waterfall.The bridge is also quite a sight to behold. This is probably the best waterfall in Jeju.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000\ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.

The cave is very nice, different from all other sights in Jeju. It?s a short walk but the ground is wet inside and can be slippery, also a bit dark in certain places. Wear a hoodie as water drops from the cave roof. Not recommended for people with mobility issues.Once inside, the sight is beautiful, it?s an amazing work of nature.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. One of the most beautiful waterfalls in Jeju! I didn't ecpect it to be so nice! Definitely worth spending 45 minutes there. Good spot for photoes, too.

nice beach with many caf챕s and restaurants. The water is clean and i can only recommend going there. But there are quite a lot people, so if you look for a lonely beach this is not appropriate for you.

My friends and I spent an afternoon at the beach. It was really not crowded, but probably because of the weather. It was windy which was nice to sleep on the beach but not to go in the water.Lots of foreigners and families, the atmosphere is really relaxing !

My friend took me here because he said it was beautiful. Indeed, a waterfall next to the ocean is as picturesque as it gets. We took some dope pictures and dip our feet into the cool and refreshing water when I saw my FIRST EVER DOUBLE RAINBOW. Life is good haha

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Last summer, our school went to Hamdeok Beach as a field trip. The place was conserved very neat and clean. All of my friends were excited to play around. The beach was enormous and the water was green and blue, looking amazing. However, the weather made us suffer very much. The temperature on that day went up to 29 degree, and all of us were almost burned. I highly recommend that you guys go to Hamdeok Beach when the weather gets cooler.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.
It was an easy walk, lots of street vendors, waterfall was beautiful. Perfect weather in October! We spent 2 days in jeju and just about did it all.
Interesting! There are quite a few things to visit like Botanic Garden, Bonsai Garden, Folk Village, Lava Cave, Bird Garden, Water Garden etc. Recommended!

Impressive sight withthewaterfall ending directly into the sea, walking down to the foot of the waterfall can be challenging with the rocks formation and without proper path, so don't wear heels!!!If you want to get near to the waterfall, be prepare for a shower of blessings

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.
I loved all the waterfalls in Jeju, did not meet one I didn't like.  Highly recommend this one as well as each one is a bit different.

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Have you ever seen a more mouthwatering set of pictures? ㄴ Today we are enjoying a famous traditional dish from Jeju Island, Black pork.  Thick cuts of juicy pork belly, cooked to a smokey crisp just how I love it. Alone the pork belly is enough to eat by itself and a side of rice. But we're not here to be basic, you either go big or go home, enjoy the side dishes that come with every meal.  For example bean sprouts, ssamjang is known as a Korean bbq dipping sauce. It was mildly spicy and salty flavor with nutty fragrant. And, most importantly it compliments well Korean pork belly bbq. Lastly the infamous cabbage Kimchi, enough of a kick but not too much where you cant taste the perfect blend of food. A perfect combination, Bon-Appetite!

Great waterfall, not very high but impressive nonetheless.  Spend a while looking about and then try some of the seafood brought up by the   haenyeo   [ladies who free-dive for shellfish].  Fresh as can be, washed down with a glass or two of soju.

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

Come with my little girl, stayed at the hotel besides the beach.It is very hot in jeju in july, 35 degree in the afternoon.  We went to the beach at noon, water is clear and cool and the sand is smooth.Rental of umbrella and shelter at 25000w and 100000w respectively.  It is recommended to bring your own shelter.

Come prepared and you'll love it, good walking boots and waterproof jacket. If you find it too cold or dump you can go in for a few metres, and go outside, but we kept going wanting to see what is at the end, and it was spectacular, with huge lava column in blue dim light.
beautiful moutain~not so high but highgreen,clean water,sound,windeverything is perfectrecommend

As a scuba diver I was very eager to go to this museum and get to know more about the   Jeju Mermaids  . The museums has lots of interesting information about how they live, the risks of their profession, the   team system   they use (I loved this part). If you like the underwater world, I highly recommend a visit to this neat museum.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.
A natural spot form by the volcano. It is very cold inside, recommended to bring raincoat as there as water dripping from above.
A crowded place to visit during the summer but a lovely waterfall with clean amenities for visitors. Very family friendly, reasonable prices on tourist goods.

1st falls was kinda disappointing cos there was no water coming down. Perhaps dry season? On the + side, the still water surface made excellent photo opp. After more staircases, we had the option to descend a long staircase to 2nd falls. Which we skipped and proceeded on. We crossed the bridge of the 7 nymphs - indeed an odd architecture with such a curved surface to near centre of bridge. Easiest is to walk in reverse to give the hamstrings some relief. Later on, there was a lookout point for 2nd falls. Yay. All done, we rewarded ourselves with icecream :)

We did the yeongsil walk and it was amazing. It was tough in parts of you are not used to hiking but walking all the kids and grandparents doing it lends you the stamina to keep going and gosh is it worth it. Some of the best scenery I have ever seen.
Visited on 17th October 2019.If you going with friend it would be great.A relax mini hiking walk along the breezy turquoise sea.It's a must go. Nice place to take photo too.

I have never seen anything like it. The walk was unbelievable! A must see and do in Seogwipo. Great for travellers who love nature, hiking (must wear comfortable shoes) and photography. Highly recommended.

Definitely a special cave. As it is a lava tube, the floor is also made of solid lava, aka uneven flooring. Bring good hiking boots as it takes at least 40 minutes to reach the end. Advice to use a tripod for good photos.

This is highlight of my Jeju West Coast Trip; it's beautiful scenic walk; however its not an easy walk. My mother has difficulty to walk on this path and return to the entrance after 10 minutes walk. There are some woman divers selling abalone near the entrance and its quite fascinating to see them.I highly recommend to visit this attraction while you are in Jeju and its very close to Mount Sanbang where usually people visit for trekking.

The Manjanggul Cave is splendid and provides an excellent Geology lessons on how the caves are formed over thousands of years. A must for cave lovers and nature lovers. The walk is relatively easy for elderly and young kids as well.

I didn't really know what to expect when friends said we were going to a maze. I thought it might be small and easy to navigate but I was surprised by how challenging the maze really was. We teamed up boys against girls and the most fun was getting up on the bridges over the maze to see where the other group was!
A must visit to this attraction . Entrance fee is 2000W . Short and easy walk to the cliffs . Expect to spend around 30-60minutes here if you want to take photos .

When me and my friend tried to look for a car rent with a driver who can guide us, we chose Hi Jeju Taxi Tour, at first because the term of payment is really easy (We can pay cash directly to the driver), and we can customize the places we love to visit.

this is the largert lava tube in the world (well, that we have found) and it's fascinating.  Really huge tube, interesting rock formations all through.  The walk is quite easy (a little uneven and damp, headlight recommended) and the informative signs are useful.  Not that expensive and well worth the trip.

This is one location where you do not have to worry about bad weather, actually I would recommend going here on a day with rain and wind since then you can actually experience the force of nature when the waves hit the cliffs.Easy access, parking (for a fee) and you can walk along the shore line on a board walk (sort of).

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.
Our guide June is very informative on Jeju, and we had a wonderful trip to the southern part of Jeju. She is friendly and easy-going , and took good care of us and the kid.

Mr. Kang was super nice to my friends and I from the day one. We had to change our schedule a lot and did not get to stick with our itinerary because of the rain. He would advise us some travel hot spots we could go to instead. Also, he was very flexible and patient. Thanks to his great service, my three days travel went smoothly. I would advise anyone who is looking for an easy transportation on a Jeju trip to book Mr. Kang’s taxi service.

Easy to find, definitely worth visiting :) Teddy Bears are fantastic: some are very old, some - very expensive, all of them showing great sense of humor and healthy distance to the world. Recommended not only for children!

Drove to Udo island on a self-drive trip and took ferry from Seongsan pier in the morning. It was easy driving in Udo island - it was a tiny island and there weren't many tourists around. While strolling up Udo-bong, saw a group of physically challenged students brought to Udo-bong by their teachers. A very heart warming sight. There isn't anything much to do yet if you are interested in exploring the nature (like I do), it is a good place to spend a morning just feeling the nature.
Cool scenic cliffs at the ocean, easy path to get to them, not a very long walk, highly recommend it.

Attractive to me and my son as it was a volcano. it has amazing size! I was told that it?s a popular place to film movies. The park is not very big, so you can take it easy. I would recommend you visit this place in autumn for more colors.

Went around with a friend and the place is huge. I think we managed to walk from gate 8 to gate 4 before we realized we cane there looking to eat and ended up just window shopping because there?s lots to feast your eyes on. There?s mostly food and fresh produce and seafood and food products made from Jeju oranges.

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe. For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!

Very nice place for a day trip. Rented a quad bike for half a day at 30000 Won. Beautiful scenery and enjoyed the slow pace at the islands. Tasted their seafood ramyeon in one of the local restaurant. Would recommend to try if you happened to pass by.

This place offers specialty items/ food of jeju. Vendors are cash only and they offer samples. There are snack stalls and a couple of restaurants inside. One restaurant even have an English translation on it.

the facilities are excellent  very spacious  and comfortable. staff great. out on it own with little to attract you and but great facility. not sure who supplied the food first night plenty to eat second night they ran out. end of our evenings there was no where to book/order a cab so thank goodness the BooYung hotel assisted.
Small light garden 50% tar road 50% rocky road. Definitely will not recommend to visit. Limited choice of food.

Not a bad experience. But they typically sell repetition food from one end to the other. The place is clean too. Had a dinner in one of the fish sashimi restaurant  enjoyed very fresh fish sashimi at a reasonable price.
Large tea plantations and tea Museum cave Cafe and tea-themed food.In particular unlike other tourist establishments and also with great food and friendly staff are the best.

Highly recommended to come during sunrise and/or sunset - absolutely gorgeous scenery and wonderful air. Also has a lot of good food and convenience stores in the area. Only downside is that it can get quite crowded.

Hallam Park is one of the best botanical gardens we?ve visited. The paths are clearly posted and friendly to foreign visitors that don?t read Korean. We loved it. The restaurant at the entrance is only a good choice if you like Korean food. The barbecue spot inside might be a better choice for western visitors.

Dragon shape rock. The rock will bring you good fortune. It is also famous for fishing site. The lighted rock is also beautiful at night. Make a wish and the rock help you. Regardless of the legend you can enjoy the beautiful scenery.  Omegi ddeok (cake) is also good food to try.
Actually pretty fun to race your friends and see who locates the end (bell) first. Cute cats with free cat food too. Just request it at the gate.

Windy Island15 minute taking ship from Sungsan dock to Woo-do, it?s really convenience to visit there.The road were well maintained and there were variety of vehicles could I used.Before I got there, I heard that the peanut jam is famous and ice-cream made by peanut is good. Some people also strongly said to me ?you should have Spicy seafood noodle soup(Jjamppong)?. Well, I actually tasted it..so..so..nothing special.Many people recommend me to visit the island woodo, there are not a special place at all.You can take almost everything in Jeju what Woodo can do..

Well worth the trip! The museum is very well presented and organized. So cute! So pink! Lots of kids and laughter about. You can opt to pay for extras, like buttons, passport stamp collecting and heart shaped tag to write on and lock onto the balcony. Some furniture is a bit run down but overall it is really well cared for. The staff is very friendly and helpful. You can also get small food and drink from the cafe and there is a jungle gym are for children to play. They have a short movie and photo station on the roof at the end. The gift shop had lots to choose from and prices were pretty good compared to official merchandise sold elsewhere online. Spent almost the whole day there and I loved every second of it. The museum is incredibly interactive, it would be hard not to have fun. Brought my boyfriend and even he couldn't believe how fun it was :)

We were looking for Dombaedon Restaurant in the black pork street.  We couldn't find it.  We went into a nearby shop to ask for info and were told that the restaurant at the corner - Dombedon Restaurant was good.The Dombedon Restaurant is a michelin starred restaurant.  It was quite crowded, we waited 30 minutes for our table.There were four of us, thought of ordering 3 portions to share (do not want to waste food).  We were told to order at least 4 portions.  So instead of ordering 4 portions of the black pork meat set, we ordered 2 portions of black pork set and 2 black pork bulgogi instead.The black pork bbq set came with steamed egg custard and kimchi stew.  The black pork was tender but a little fat though.  The meat was tasty and good to wrap and eat with perilla leaf.The black pork bulgogi was well marinated and juicy.  The black pork set 450g was KRW43,000 for two persons.  The bulgogi 180g was KRW18,000 for one person.  Though the price of this restaurant is higher compared to the other nearby restaurants, it's worth every cent of it.

We stayed nearby and went in to find dinner. There's gate no 8 which is full of people selling food and those with long queue usually means It's nice. We tried some of it but it will be quite pricy as in the end, both of us not full.

Very friendly and helpful to all of us, he is also very kind in recommending us the must-go attractions and even getting us discounted entrance fee around Jeju. Tour guide was friendly, helpful, respected our privacy yet open to engage and hear our questions. Did not pressure us to finish sightseeing any site fast. Every area we went to was good, there were no places that we went to that tried to hard-sell us a service or product. Tour guide also brought us to really good food places, and even recommended us to other places for good food or for future exploration and sight-seeing. Since my hotel is located at one end of this shopping centre, I visited this place every day during my stay in Jeju. Being underground, it was great to shield the winter cold especially in the evenings.The shops essentially sell similar products - clothings, cosmetics, shoes, accessories, bags, hats, etc. There are few eateries and fast food chains too. This shopping street tends to be crowded in the evenings. There are free toilet facilities at one end, i.e. exit 1.

Located just a stone's throw from O'Sulloc Museum, this place is a must-visit! I strongly recommend making your own soap here - it is such a fun and unique experience! Do grab a bite to eat at the cafe as well as the food is not only healthy but delicious!

Innisfree is a well-known brand with numerous outlets throughout Korea and Asia. As it originated from Jeju, this is their main outlet in Korea. It was much smaller than expected, with only a single long building housing both the shop and cafe.The shop stocked quiet a good range of their toiletries and cosmetics, with an natural soap-making activity available. You can purchase a pack from the counter, choose the scent of soap you want, and there are stations with a screen to guide you through the soap-making process step-by-step. Shop staff are on hand for assistance as well. At the end of it, you can pack the soap into an eco-bag as a gift.The organic green cafe had ample seating and a good range of food, compared to the adjacent O Sulloc tea museum. Their drinks are served in funky bottles with interesting tastes, and make a pretty picture.If in the area, the soap-making is interesting and wouldn't take too long.

If you are on the west end of the island you should definitely see this wonderful place.  And, if you are lucky enough to see a few 'women divers' selling their fresh seafood (and you have a stomach for unusual and raw seafood) you should try this unusual treat.  They will also sell you a shot of Suju if you need it!

i won't repeat what others have mentioned.personally i love this place.i went during spring in april 2017,weather was perfect.food was presented beautifully,the latte i had was delicious.the garnishing is really insta-worthy!my friends and i had breakfast at the outdoor area,overlooking the tea plantation.some of the skincare product sold was exclusive to this outlet,glad i bought a few.would surely return if i happen to visit jeju again.

I had high hopes for this spot, but it is hard to recommend it.  What was once a pretty island is now circled by identical seafood restaurants, cafes, burger joints and other tourist shops.   Biking a loop around the island is nice enough, but the road is jammed with little electric   rickshaw   things and noisy scooters.  Honestly, this place would be a perfect case study of bad development for a tourism management class.

Great food and local gifts such as sashimi, steamed pork, fresh fruit, and gifts.If you want to buy for yourself and friends, family, visit here to buy the things.You will love to visit for delicious local food.
A trip made more memorable by great food, great scenery, and a great guide. Highly recommended to anyone who wishes to visit Jeju!??
A super crowded place. I do not recommend it unless you like crowded beaches to show off or meet :)The infrastructure are fine (drinks, food, etc)

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.

We were mesmerized with the glass art. Such detailed work! The route made it easier to walk and enjoy all the glass art. Admission fee is 11 000 won. There were also one part of the park that showed glass palace  but we end up walking about 10minutes and no castle was in our sight  quite disappointed. P/S: you can find cute fridge magnet of jeju at the end of the souvenir shop. There were only 1 000 won for one. Very cheap for a fridge magnet I think.

We walked in at 5:30pm. The place was lit and was surprised by the size of the garden. Wouldn’t recommend it any earlier since you will not be able to enjoy all the lights...Must visit inside studio where a lot of sets are set up with the lights for DIY semi-professional photo shoot.The staff were very nice and offered to take photos for you.
We really enjoyed this part of the weekend. I would even like to return. Superior glass art and plenty of outdoor walking through the facilities. Highly recommend this be on your short list.
We enjoyed walking until the end point.It is recommended during summer since inside the cave is cool ..

We came with high hopes of being awed by beautiful camellia Flowers but left disappointed. There was really nothing much except the blooming flowers in the greenhouses. Maybe it was the timing of our visit but we felt cheated. Be prepared to walk a bit to visit the various parts of the park. I will not recommend this park.

Unfortunately  I cannot say that this place is worth visiting. The temple is extremely new as it was built only in 1990s. The outlook was grand and the temple architectural style was reminiscent of the early Korean Joseon Dynasty.  Buddhism in Jeju is unique with its own characteristics and distinctive feature. Unlike the main stream counterpart in mainland Korea Jeju's Buddhism accepts combines and adapt to the local characteristics to form an integrated form of its own. The native folks were staunch followers of Shamanistic beliefs pray to stone deities and attend to superstitious rituals but Buddhism in Jeju embodied the local belief in her Buddhist temples. Behind the Shamanistic gods idols stood the compassionate and tolerant statue of Buddha. Jeju is famous for her natural environment and Jeju's Buddhism takes a natural path towards enlightenment. In fact the repressive Joeson Dynasty suppressed Buddhism but this Buddhist temple incorporated the beauty of the Joseon temple architectural style with Buddhism worship. The compassionate hands of the Buddha practiced acceptance and non-hatred non violence in pursuit of the emancipation of the human soul. I observed that the Buddha statues in the prayer hall were magnificently golden and the grand prayer hall with a height of 28 m was reputed to be the largest in Asia. The ambience here was tranquil and serene. It was a place most suitable for meditation and prayer. I walked around the temple and felt the calmness and peacefulness in the air. From a distance I could hear the dim chanting of the Buddhist prayer. Historically this lovely island of Jeju had suffered tremendously under the repressive hands of the Mongol Empire and also during the Japanese tyrannical rule. But the island survived with the most scenic and gorgeous natural wonders of the world and may this temple bring continual peace to this natural place!.

Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.
