First of all ensure you hike on a non rain day.  We were worried all week because it was raining.  We got a non rain day but cloudy. When got pass 1 km up it was beautiful sunny weather.Know there are 6 trails and they start in different places and not all go to the top. We took the Eorimok Trail (Northwest). It was one of the shortest. We didn't do good research and started too late to do a longer trail.I'm moderately fit. The trail was steep! I was definitely challenged for the first 2km. It was balance of even and uneven ground. Anyone can make it up but it might take you a bit longer if you were unfit. There isn't a drone restrictions and was able to take some great video. Bring water and food.  There are places near the top to grab instant noodles and water. There is no washroom on the way up.  Bring some tissue and wet wipes just in case.Although we didnt get to go to the summit, it is a must do while visiting. Jeju.

fascinating  view from bottom until top. but we went on saturday, pack with local hikers. the path is quite easy. about 18km back and forth using seongpanak trail. on the way back we tag along with the person incharge/worker of mt. hallasan, and being offered to use the little train to the way down. best of all, there is no entrence fee charge to hike the  national park.

Even though it was rainy weather during the days spent in Jeju, hamdeok beach compensated for the bad weather with with pretty coastline, wide range of eateries, cafes and also an olle-gil trail to explore the area. Drive along the coastline for a scenic view too. We stayed in co'op City hotel for a night, comfortable hotel where offers guest free beer in the evening. Beach area is less than 30mins drive to Jeju airport.

Driving from the city to the Seongpanak trail is the most convenient way to do it, it's only 20 minutes away from the busy area of Jeju.I hiked the mountain at early morning January 01 and when i reached the Seongpanak trail the parking was crazy long that it goes as far as 1km from the side of the road. If you want to save time in walking you should be at the trail around 3am at Jan01. Anyway, the trail was relatively easy on the first 7km, it was cold around -1 to 5C that time, still manageable but the trail was slippery due to ice forming on rocks and the trail was covered with snow. So, to prevent accidents wear a mini crampons or a Yaktrak coil underneath your shoes.Don't worry hiking alone, you can do this without a guide, you probably are blind if you get lost out there. Also, the trail was properly maintained that hiking at the peak was a breeze except the last 2km of the hike. When you reached the final kilometers it starts to get steep, so take your time and avoid slippery rocks and you should be fine. Finally, the peak was amazing, you would be able to see sea of clouds if the weather permits. Overall not bad for a hike.

Disclaimer: Not a seasoned/experienced hiker. Was done on a cloudy day with a scattered drizzles.I had high expectations for the highest point in South Korea and a highly rated tourist attraction on TripAdvisor but was greatly disappointed by the experience.The reason I am giving a score of 1/5 is because there is a long hike (approximately 3-4 hours one way) with very little to see along the way, with ultimately what I would consider an   okay   view of a   crater lake   up the top. In addition, whilst walking the unpaved bits of the trail (rocks, which account for about half of the trails we walked) you will need to focus hard on walking to ensure you don't slip as it can be quite slippery. This means you don't have the luxury of looking around at the scenery/surroundings while doing the hike.It is not that the view up the top is objectively poor. It is actually decent. it is simply that the effort (3-4 hours one way) to reward (the view up top) ratio is terrible.The group of us hiked up the East trail (Seongpanak) and went down the North trail (Gwaneumsa). The hike down along the North trail provided a handful of views that were decent - better than the East trail.My experience at Mount Hallasan was preceded by Seongsan Ilchulbong the day before which to me provided a much much better experience. The hike was a lot easier and the view was much superior, offering a beautiful view of the Jeju City skyline. I personally would highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong over Mt Hallasan and would recommend against doing Mt Hallasan, unless you are someone that personally loves hiking as an activity anyway.Summary: Long 3-4 hour one-way hike (7-8 hours return) to the summit rewarded with a decent view, with a lot unpaved trail which can be slippery. Not good for people with bad knees, those expecting plenty of beautiful views, and those wanting to enjoy scenery while hiking.

Climbing Mt. Halla was a highlight of our trip to South Korea! We climbed up the Eorimok trail and then down the Yeongsil trail. I would recommend going this way because Yeongsil was a lot of stairs - I'd rather do that on the way down than up. Going up probably took us a little over two hours and wasn't too strenuous (though we are in good shape). The trails are very well kept and there are signs all along (in English) showing how far you've gone and how far you have left, and how easy/difficult the next stretch is. The view from the top (even though it wasn't even the top) was unbelievably beautiful! To get there, we hailed a cab from Jeju city. We just told him we wanted to start at Eorimok trail. I would recommend a cab because if you take the bus, you have a pretty large hill to walk up before you even get to the mountain because of where it drops you off. I think the cab cost about 15,000 won. The way home, we were waiting for a bus and then saw a cab so we hailed him. This guy charged us 30,000 won, I think because Jeju city was out of his way. Make sure to bring plenty of water - at least two bottles per person - and snacks.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

Climbing Hallasan Mt. Is one of my bucket list and It's in jeju island thats why i love jeju. The climb is so worth it and really something you can achieve even choosing the most difficult trail. You get close to the nature as you walk through the vast rich forest with different species of trees, Hear the birds singing harmonizing with the crickets chirping, Colorful flowers & sighted a roe deer along the way. The sweats you get from those steep rocky path is nothing when you reach the summit, it was so awesome! witnessing the wonders of nature & learnt some historical events happened many years ago. It is well preserved and well managed. Definitely will come back again to try another trail to see more what hallasan Has to offer. RockNroll!P.S. Going there must wear proper hiking attire that suits the weather condition.You can still try to hike even though you're not that hiking type of person as the trail has pretty nice part. Just be pro and you're good to reach the summit! Have fun!

Climbed the Seongpanak trail (9.7 km) going up, which took us 4 hours and 47 minutes \ including rest and photobreak... This trail is longer than Gwaneumsa trail.. Started with a kinda   walk-in-the-park   trail in the forest for few kilometers.. We saw wild deer and crows.. Then, the trail became challenging and more difficult towards the peak.. Unfortunately when we reached the peak, it had very low visibility and was very windy... We were not able to see the crater  because it was covered with thick fog/cloud...

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Beautiful waterfall. I went to all 3 waterfalls in Jeju, and this is the most amazing and my favourite. It's also along the Jeju Olle Trail 6. A short walk from the waterfall, there is a mini waterfall called Sojeonbang waterfall, which also falls into the ocean.

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

As per suggestion of our taxi driver, we decided to climb up along the Eorimok trail as according to him, it was the easier of the two. The first 2km was upwards slope of big rocks stairs so it was a little tiring but after that, the course was breezy. Took us about 2h to the top. The day we went was super windy so it was really really cold and everyone took cover in the shelter at the top, but if the weather permits, you can sit outside and enjoy the view. The climb down by Yongsil trail was really beautiful and it's a very different kind of view than Eorimok. We understood why the driver said Eorimok was easier to climb up as Yongsil had more rocks that would have been a little difficult. I'm not an avid climber but both trails were doable and the views were worth it.

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

An amazing scenic spot with stunning view. Try to hike along the trail for panoramic view of jeju island and the ocean. If you have limited time, it is not necessary to hike up the peak since the best scenery is blocked by the fences. The descending path has much better scenery that the ascending one! p.s. Try out the hanrabong ice-cream! One of the best way to recharge after hiking

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

Absolutely hike Oedolgae, it's a beautiful coastal walk that is part of an Olle trail. You wind all around a part of the southern coast of Jeju, and can walk as long as you please. Lots of shops and restaurants along the way. The Jeju trails are my favorite attraction on Jeju, definitely walk one! And they're free!

A short but steep walk is rewarded with a spectacular view of the crater, ocean and the surrounding parts of the island. Very special to have the opportunity to visit such a special geological site. Informative signs along the trail help to educate visitors about the formation of the volcano.

A relaxing trail with picturesque scenery. I went during autumn and the climate was just right. The leaves turning brown was a breathtaking sight and if you're lucky, you will be able to catch a glimpse of deers along the trails.Do be careful along the steep slopes during certain parts of the trail as a missed step could result in some pain. There are water points on the trail though located a substantial distance from each other. Do bring your own food or you can buy it from a store near the summit. Bear in mind that you will have to bring along your trash and don't leave it on the mountain! (Bring along extra trash bags!)

A relatively easy hike going up Yeongsil trail (lots of climbing). Note that if you're taking the bus, you still need to do a pre-hike of 2.5km going up the mountain after you get off the bus stop. In my opinion, this was harder than the actual hike going up, but it was good preparation. There's also a cafe near the actual entrance. You can buy food here right before going up the trail.The cutoff time for Yeongsil trail is 2pm during the summer, but I would advise you to come early. The hike itself can be done in 1.5 hours, but with picture-taking, it can take as long as 3 hours (and the view at the top is gorgeous in many places!).Wear good hiking shoes. I've seen people wear regular sneakers (and even a guy with leather shoes -- what was he thinking?!), but I swear your feet will hurt if your shoe even manages to survive. Both Yeongsil and Eorimok trails have unpaved trails with unforgiving rocks. Hiking sticks would also help with the descent if you have weak knees.It's safe to hike solo (even for females) during popular days, so you're sure to hike with other people. It's also best to go down where most people are going if you started late (most people drive, so they go down the same trail they went up).In case of emergencies though, you can call their emergency number. (There's mobile coverage for most, if not all, of the trail). Take note of the location posts every few hundred meters. In case you get injured, there's this small train which can take you down, but you have to wait quite a while.

A must-see in Jeju island. During this time of the year, there are pink Azalea blossoms that decorate the mountains. Though the Eojimok trail is the most easiest one, it still took us more than 3 hours. The view along the Yeongsil Trail is particularly memorable. Hiking in Hallasan is a refreshing experience for travelers who would like to explore the essence of Jeju island.

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014.  Glass is a common item we use daily.  But there in the Glass castle, they have made beauty out of something ordinary to something beautiful, works of art actually.  However, many tourists were not aware that there is a trail going round the Castle where you can see more sculptures placed along the trail.  A prominent signpost placed at the entrance to the trail will be helpful.  i am glad my friends and I didn't miss this trail.  To make sure it is not slippery during rainny season, the managements have placed gunny sacks along the trail.  This helps greatly for many of us.So if you are in Jeju, don't miss Jejeu Glass Castle.

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.
A counterpart of Giant?s Causeway. It?s part or along the Olle trail of Jeju. The viewing place is not that big, but if you are visiting Jeju, it is worth visiting.

You should go there. Lovely view. Great for riding a bike around the island. It takes only 1-2h only but the view is so stunning. You should not eat at restaurants at the dock. There is a lot of places to eat along the way. Food is a bit more expensive but acceptable.

You need a certain level of fitness to be able to climb the many steps to the top. Great views along the way but the view from the top is spectacular. Very popular destination so prepare for the crowds.
Wished they opened more of the cave for public viewing though! It was very well preserved and maintained. A really long walk to and fro. My favourite attraction in jeju by a mile.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

When it is raining this is one of the place you should come you can just relax and have  some tea besides they sell variety of Tea which is very nice and good. They have a tester too where you can taste certain tea. There is a cafe too but mind you it's a long queing so I just skip it maybe because it is raining time so everyone go there. My favorite is the pack O'sullac Milk Tea it is so very nice. I should buy more of it. Next time will surely buy a lot of it.Besides the tea thing there is innisfree house beside it. you can make your own soap the organic cafe at the innisfree house is also nice too.So I recommmend you to come here whenever it is raining for indoor activity. even if it is not raining it is good for relaxing and enjoy the view of the tea trees.

Went there as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It is a great walk and views. Avoid if raining or cloudy. The walk to the top of what is known in English as Sunrise Peak is quite strenuous and involves a lot of stairs. There are rest stops along the way. There are no lifts. It can get quite windy so jackets are required. There is a town centre area at the base with restaurants and shops.

We went to the beach after hallim park. It was a nice place for my little one to run around as the sand is very soft. Must be a lovely place to relax in summer. The view was beautiful. Lovely cafes along the way and we had nice pizza.

We visited on 23rd October. A misfortune happened at about 5.15pm when we were about to leave  our rented car could not start due to no battery. Our baby was temporarily locked in the car so a helpful bystander helped us to opened the door using manual lock and called the car rental company. After a long wait we gotten the staffs at the park to help.the 'gatekeepers' were friendly enough to let us stayed there while awaiting help to arrive. A thin tall lady staff without spectacles came to our help and called the car rental company as we could not understand the options given in Korean. She explained to us and reassured us in English fluently. She also took extra care to follow up and waited til a tow car to help to jump start the rented car. I think by that time her shift is over as few staffs waiting for her too. We are indeed thankful for her and the staffs on that day. Cocomong Ecopark does have a good commendable staff. thank you.Park wise games and design are well thought and worth the entry ticket. The slide down on tire is fun though it looked a bit scary but it is safe. Cafe has got a nice sea view.

We stopped by Wolijeongri Beach for about 30 min. on the way to UDO; the water was very clear.  There were kids playing sand on the beach. The view was peaceful. We enjoyed our short walk along the beach. You can get some snacks and a good coffee from a caf챕 or a convenient store nearby. There is a restroom facility too.

We started at 9am before the busloads Of tourist started arriving. It was a tough hike because the flights of stairs were literally endless. There were many resting areas along the way and I was not shy about just sitting on the stone benches to catch my breathe. Many reviewers shared that they took between 20 to 40 mins to reach the summit. I took 1 full hour. The stairs and tracks were well maintained and most stretches had handrails. The views at mid point and the summit were superb and makes this hike so rewarding! Don?t miss visiting this UNESCO world heritage site!

We finished the route #10 (17.5KM) in about 5 hours (we walked pretty slowly and took a lot of pictures). The whole experience was unforgettable. The magnificent view of the ocean on the left and mountain on the right was amazing. I thought it would be hard since I'm not that much used to walking for long hours but it didn't feel exhausting at all. Every sight was so gorgeous that I just didn't want to leave. I felt very fresh and relaxed after the walk. Even the tiredness after it was finished was worth all of those pretty shots I took and the healing. STRONGLY RECOMMEND!

We didn?셳 spend much time here which was a pity but in any case there were too many tourists. Would be a better experience when less crowded. The buildings are stylish and there is a nice view of the tea gardens. You can try the tea and they explain the tea making process. The cafe looked good with desserts like green tea cake and ice cream but we didn?셳 try as the queue was too long. Nearby was the Innisfree building where many people were making handmade soap. There was also a cafe and exhibits of the different distilled essences of flowers and plants in Jeju.

Walking along the sides of the mountain next to the open sea was quite thrilling for us seniors to say the least.  We had to be careful of our steps in the uneven stone/rocks which were wet.  But it all paved for a good adventure with lovely views photo opportunity and a chance to take some great photos standing up on the rocks.  We enjoyed the visit.

Visited Sangumburi Crater as our first stop from Jeju city centre. It was in the morning and was rather cooling and relaxing. Not much visitors at the time. Sangumburi Crater was one of my favorite attractions of Jeju (the other being Udo-bong). It was a short stroll along the way and viewing of the greenery and flowers.

Viewpoint on the western end of Jeju Island.  Great place for sunset observation.  High on a cliff with good views all around.  There is a weather station here.Was here on a windy day - with field of swirling grass. To the north of the hill is a tail along the shore where it is possible to rent electric scooters.  There is also a small museum on the prehistoric settlement found in the area.

View is beautiful but too crowded It pretty amazing that such nature formation is almost perfect for taking beautiful shots which make the place looks so big in actual it is quite small Perhaps should have more viewing point or benches along the way  so can just seat n enjoy the serene  view
Turkoise waters and great views of the beaches from multiple restaurants and coffee places all along the shoreline.May be a bit difficult to find parking though.

To reach the place  need to walk along not properly paved route with long bushes  initially thought the guide had taken us to wrong place. Quiet place with nice coastal view. Unfortunately  we didn't manage to go to the church as there's sudden downpour  left us no choice but to end the visit. I saw horse carriage and shuttle bus service that can bring you around.

This site explains everything one needs to know about the island's historical past.  It has a long walkway leading one through outdoor exhibit areas each section with attendants who can give information.  There also was a traditional musical performance available to view.  It was chilly when we were there so we left earlier than desired but if we had known there was a cafe in which to warm up and perhaps have lunch we could have made a day of it.  One perk of going in February was that the crowds were very very small here and at other locations.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: This place is one of the place that I wanted to visit in Jeju. I am glad that i did. I love the walk alongside  the field of tall flamegrass which bloom from Sep-Oct. The walk to the crater was nice and it was quite romantic. Though on the day of our visit it was raining  but nevertheless we enjoy and appreciate the beauty of this place. You can view the crater below and also the surrounding mountains. Will visit again when I come to Jeju next time.
This place gives you great views of the ocean as well as the famous rock formation-Oedolgae. It doesn't take long to get to it.

This is a world heritage site where a pathway leads to the peak of a long dead volcano. There are great views along the way. On the path leading downstairs to the ocean beach- they have the women divers show-at 1:30 and 3 pm as well as a seafood restaurant.
This is a must-see on Jeju Island.  A walk along a set of stairs (not strenuous) provides many varied views of this area.  Look for the hexagonal columns of lava.

This is a must-do! You get to the peak using staircases which allows any age group to do this activity also. There are also toilets along the way. The view of the peak as well as Jeju Island is amazing.There are shops where you can buy souvenirs. You should try the tangerine ice cream 'cuz it's yummy!
This is a must visit here in jeju island. The climb is much easier than it looks.Take some beautiful pictures along the way and more at the summit.Enjoy the view and breeze at the top.

This is a beautiful place to learn about the gardens and native korean plants.? There are many different types of gardens here and they are all well maintained and interesting.? You could stay here for a long time just learning or you could breeze through casually enjoying the scenery.? There is a tower you can go to the top of for lovely views of the area.? Bring a water bottle.

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There isn't much there but it is a beautiful view and a nice walk along the coast.  Some of the fancier hotels with casinos are nearby.  It wasn't very busy when we went but I think during the summer peak season it would be a bit crowded.

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!
The whole area is astoundingly beautiful and clean with spectacular views all around. Recommended to all as long as you don't mind a whole day's hiking. Spectacular.
The view is amazing and lovely! Enjoy your long drive with scenic view and take as many as you can picturesque memorable photo!

The scenery is definitely beautiful and you feel achievement and reward once you make it to the top but the journey up is steep. If you are not in shape like me it can take a while but stopping along the way to look down and enjoy the view is nice.

The scenery here is very beautiful and picturesque. However the sole propose of coming to this location was because the reviews stated that you could kayak here. However when we arrive we were disappointed to learn that the kayaks and other water sports were gone. In addition all the signs for the water sports were still up advertising and pointing you to their location. None of the locals could explain to us why the company no longer was in business.

The museum can be improved with more English explanation. Go to the open air top for the best 360 view of the area and plantation. There are signs at the plantation warning of snakes but none spotted during our visit. There is a crowd at the cafe and shop but the turnover is quick as most of them followed a group tour and hence can't linger that long. You can get a seat if you are not in a rush. The stuff are expensive but it won't deter a green tea fan. Do be extra careful when crossing the roads to the opposite car parks. The cars and trucks are speed demons.

The mountain's peak itself was covered with fog signaled rain will soon came pouring. I did not hike the mountain as the weather is somewhat not on my side. Just walk along the canola field in front of the mountain and snap some photos. There are paid field if you want to take photo with better view costs around KRW1000. I walked down heading to Yongmeori Coast but ended up in a small snack shop called Mongma Reukabuden. The shop owner is very nice person. While I had my Cheese Octopus Bread with Hallabong Juice the rain started to pour down. It was just drizzling at first as I finish my last bite of the octopus bread the drizzles turned to somewhat heavy downpour. The shop owner's wife generously gave me a new raincoat that never been used. Though they were speaking in local Korean and all I could understood bits and pieces of what she tried to convey in her effort to tell me to have this raincoat with no charge. I was solo traveling and generous shown by strangers really moved me ?졼뀪 For that piece of raincoat I humbly thanks them!

The hike up to the crater is quite easy with elevation gain of less than 100m and even my elderly mother can do it. There are several routes to choose from and we took the easy route that winds through fields of thatch grass. The view along the way was just beautiful. At the top you can look down into the huge crater which has a circumference of 2km.
The hike to Sunrise Peak is great with great view along the hike. You also get to see the performance by woman diver and enjoy the fresh seafood caught by the woman diver.

Temple is nice design and along our walk we found many tangerines tree which I believe during the spring season the temple view will be good. Since It's FOC do drop by if you have time. It's along the way to Teddy Bear Museum and Cheonjeyon Fall Yeomiji Botanical Garden

Songaksan was one of the places that had actually a very small crowd of tourists so it make the hike a bit more enjoyable. At the foot of the mountain is a large parking lot with some coffee shops and restaurants from there it is a light hike up the mountain. Lots of greenery and nice views along the way. The center which I believe is a crate is closed right now I think for recovery from too many tourists. it is still a good destination to visit the hike is easy and relaxing peaceful and enjoyable.

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!

Songaksan area in Daejeong-eup can be easily missed when driving through the southwest corner.  It?셲 a small volcano about 2 km in diameter which can be circled in about an hour on foot and was not demanding at all.  Even though the crater was off limits the perimeter was a pleasant hike that offered some spectacular views of the volcano itself along with some nearby islands like Gapado and Marado.

Really nice view coz the waterfall is right next to the open sea. I could feel the splash on my face when I approached its bottom.Tips: be ready to climb the stairs after viewing the waterfall. It's not too long but you may get tired after a long day of touring in Jeju.Be careful if you want to go near the waterfall coz it's all big rocks at the bottom.

Place where you can consider one of the exercise from steps and all the way to the end to view the nature of Lava.You can learn about the Manjanggul Cave as there's information along the way. Cool weather as we went during the winter. Not sure if you go during any other season.Must come as you might not get it from your own country.
One of the pit stop along the way to Yongmeori Coast via halim park route. Offer a great view. Ample prking space is available.

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. The sudden contraction of molten lava due to the cooling effect of water has resulted in these rocks splitting into polygonal columns and forming a coast of almost 2 km long.This attraction is worth the visit and can be reached directly by trekking from Cheonjeyeon falls or taking a bus and pass thru the garden (Jusangjeollidae Promenade) and then reach the cliff at the end.Walking around the garden would be relaxing and one should not miss it. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.

One can go for a hike or just sit near the shore and enjoy the view. Along the coastline one can see a number of manmade caves which stands as a testimony to the importance of Jeju Island during WWII. These caves built by the Japanese troops served as a place for storing the weapons.Though called as a mountain it is more like a hill as it is not steep and one can enjoy the walk up the peak.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).

Nothing spectacular in terms of size other than the water is running into the ocean. It was a nice walk to get there and the view is nice from the rocks along the sea.  Ladies selling fresh seafood on the rocks.

Nothing much to say but great view!You shoud wear lightweight hiking shoes and bring water; umbrella along.Food are not allowed.You should try boating also. (10000- 20000 won per person)It is really great!

Not much to see or do except to take a few moments to take it the view and wind of Jeju. Many people (mostly Koreans) are seen walking along the beach picking shells or dipping their feet in the water. Not much sunbathers on this beach.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!
MUST go!!! Must climb!!! The view is nice.  Nice view for photo taking. Do stay up there longer to enjoy the nice view.

Mostly domestic tourists here. This hour-long hike offers both idyllic and dramatic views of the Songaksan volcanic craters and the open ocean. Walk on right till the end to make a complete loop journey so that you won't miss the breathtaking almost vertical volcanic crater wall rising up over the sea.

Love the view here because of the lush greenery. You will also be able to see that there're people going some Kayaking. But it depends on the season as well. There's also cafes nearby and once you're done with the view you can also walk down along the coast towards the Yongdeum Rock (Rock that looks like a dragon). Definitely walkable distance With such lovely sea Breeze and beautiful greenery. Do make sure you wear a hat and sunglasses if you're going in summer though.
Long line of majestic windmills along the coast powering the future.  Spectacular  views in a storm with waves crashing around.
It's just some rocks along the beach. Luckily i saw the nice view during sunset time. Please go for something else in Jeju.

It?s a must visit place in Jeju. The time I went there was in Winter but surprisingly all trees along with the side walk bloomed so much. The walk in the forest and a big fall blew my stress away. Enjoy the view!

It takes a little effort climbing  up the peak but the fascinating view to Jeju from the top worth the climb. Do enjoy the view along the way & suggest to make an early morning trip to enjoy the stunning sunrise view from the top . There is haenyeo show beside the walking path which worth to explore how this great diving skill passing down the generation to women only divers can dive into the sea to pick up abalone & others sea produce without an oxygen tank

It is listed as a Unesco World Heritage and definetly a place to stop. Highway 1132 will bring you there and you cannot miss it. Be prepared that parking might not be easy and you may have to spend some time. The place is quite busy and many tourist buses are coming too. We had a cloudy day and it was very windy. Entrance fee is 2000 adult and 1000 child. Couple of shops at the entrance where you can buy each and everything. Please keep in mind that waste management is terrible as everywhere in Korea. If you buy something keep in mind that no any trash beans are available. The way up and down is quite crowded and loud. Obviously many tourists are rushing on top to get the selfies done to rush down again. The walk is definetly nothing for stroller or wheel chair. We went up slowly enjoying the view and getting some pictures. On top it is quite nice to look into the volvano and rest. Sure some pictures not to forget. But again very busy place and loud. Again our day was cloudy and windy but as long as it is not raining worth to visit the peak. So conclusion would be to visit the place very early.

If you are near by or driving around the island this is definitely one of the places to check. It's not the place to stay longer than 2 hours since the place is small. I would recommend to get off the car and take a walk around the water enjoying the scenic view for about 1/2~an hour. My family were there in May when it was not too busy. There were only a few locals jogging and walking so we enjoyed the quiet peaceful and almost mystic moment there. The kayaks are no longer operating for the sake of environmental conservation. It definitely would have been amazing to have that clear water beneath when you paddle but I am glad that they've prohibited them. The place is amazing as it is. I would come back next time.

I visited Sanbangsan Mountain after walking along the coast at Yongmeori Beach. It's a walk which takes around 30 minutes to get to the top which is where you are allowed to reach. There is a really tall cave hole located on the top with a Buddha where people will do some offerings. The view is quite nice. You can certainly come here for a walk. Overall I will say it's an average spot.

I felt like Jeju tried so hard to actually make sights out of nothing and this rock was a very good example of that... Along with Yongyeon pond this was one of the worst places I payed bus tickets for to see on Jeju. It's just a rock with a dirty water sea view and its in the middle of nowhere part of Jeju city where you can only go by taxi. Awful
i didn't go into the house but only walked along the path outside. the sea view is beautiful and you can plan to go with some other attractions nearby

Hallasan the 2nd highest mountain in South Korea is a fantastic hiking place!! You can choose to hike from two different easy routes to enjoy different scenery. If this is your first hike after a long hiatus do be mindful that it's better to take the easy route. Cos at some points it's huge boulders that require some stamina to step up.Take the first bus from the bus interchange cos it's advisable for tourists to reach midpoint by noon so that you have adequate time to trek back and catch the last bus from the bus stop which is still 20 min from the start of trekking point. Alternatively there's taxi if you are a group or pair. There's only a hut at midpoint which sells cup noodles which is not cheap.  Thus advisable to bring along dry food and plenty of water for recovery. Along the way you would meet seasoned hikers and some are so friendly that they offer you a ginseng sweet if they see you resting.  There's a water point and the water taste so good! The viewing points offer such fantastic view and it's so breezy that we forgot ourselves!  Definitely a place to visit.

Gwangchigi Beach is a beach near Seongsan Ilchulbong.We park our rental car on the side road.There are a few cars & tourist bus park along the road.We can see beautiful view of Seongsan Ilchulbong from this beach. The beach is long and it has black sand.The beach is unique to it own because of the green stone/rock at the shore.It produce picturesque photo because the green stone contrast with the blue sea.This beach appears on drama Warm & Cozy starred by Kang Sora and Yoo Yeonseok.

Green tea Roll & ice cream with a nice view maybe thats a fit words for this place. The tea fields covers a large area green and fresh air. Cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/ cakes and ice cream to visitors. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream. I?셫 Highly recommended this place for green tea lover.

Good place to visit. We have visited the place in he beginning of July on rainy season. In spite of that we really enjoyed the view. There's a track with the same name follow it. On the top of mountain there are some public trainers you may use any time and kind of garden houses to rest.  You can meet local salesmen selling local products and have a seat on the benches along the track to enjoy the view.

Enjoy the breathtaking views of the ocean and impressive rock formation while walking along the coast. Very beautiful and unique scenery that is really beyond description. The beauty of nature is really awesome. One has to be there to experience it! Thanks to our guesthouse owner for recommending this place!
Climb up to the peak of the hill and you?ll get a fantastic view from the peak. Make sure you bring along a jacket with you as the wind is quite strong (the wind js strong during my visit).

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls are a must visit spot for Jeju visitors. These falls are surrounded by greenery and bewildering rock formations ideal for snapping photos. We took a nice stroll along the falls area and also on the scenic bridges for better views.

Young kids will struggle up the 1,000 steps but the 5 year old with us made it! A lot of people/tour busses but the crowds diminish somewhat as you climb. Many places to rest along the way up. Great view at the top.

You can reach Ilchulbong by bus from the Intercity bus Terminal in Jeju-Si. It takes around 1h30 to reach it. You don't really care if it is an express or intercity bus you are taking, they more or less all go at the same speed... which is quite fast. You can't really miss the stop which is quite close to the crater. Dozens of buses parked in front of the mountain kind of spoil the nice atmosphere of the place but remember you are a tourist as well...  Left to the entrance, their is a nice small temple, worth the look. The climbing to the top is all made of wooden stairs and doesn't take too long (don't remember exactly, around 30 min). We did it with kids (youngest is 6) and she could do it easily. The view from the top is nice. It is a bit disappointing not to be allowed to walk around the crater. You can just see it from a platform. Before (or after) climbing, don't forget to take a look at the beach on the left of Ilchulbong specially between 13:00 and 15:00 when the old women divers are fishing.

Yes, the walk is steep and if you go for sunrise, you will be starting off in the dark, but it doesn't take long to reach the top (16-30 minutes for reasonably fit people). The most important thing is to watch the forecast beforehand to ensure a lovely sunrise. The views are outstanding. It can get quite crowded at the viewing   steps   at the top, so get there early to stake out your perfect viewing spot. The walk down will obviously be in much lighter conditions, affording some incredible views of the coastline and the little town of Seongsan. Early morning or during the day, any time would be a fantastic time take this short - but oh so worth it - hike. There is plenty of accommodation for all budgets in Seongsan at the foot of the mountain and bus 701 or 710 can take you directly there from Jeju City Bus Terminal. In April, 2016, the entrance fee cost 2000 Won for adults.

Yes it is worth to go here, you need only 50 mins to complete this park. The scenes are very stunning along the coast, the cliff, the fields and the volcano landscape. The ladders to the crater is well constructed but don't expect too much about the view up there! trust me.
White sand, clear water. View of several islands. Family beach. Easy to get to, great to walk along the water's edge.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

Went up on a cloudy day before the typhoon hit so the view was not too clear, but it was a quick climb up a ton of staircases. Took us 16 minutes to reach the top and we stopped a few times for photos. It was a pretty tiring hike up so young children or elderly people may find it difficult. The view was nice along the way and they have stairs so the path is very well maintained. It was crowded with a lot of tourists.

Went there by bus using the 201 bus line, it will stop you to the 'entrance' (basically the highway) which is a long far walk into the actual entrance. There's a small bus stop where you can take another bus in (slow) but taxis will frequent the highway entrance looking for customers. The cave itself its a magnificent sight to behold..it's huge! Not sure about all the negative reviews about it poorly lit and all, because the place is actually adequately lit (to fit the ambiance of a cave, no artificial colored disco lights) and concrete steps are placed everywhere in the tunnel to prevent accidental missteps. The ground is naturally uneven, you can't expect marbled tiles here. It can get quite cold and wet at 10-13deg, so bring a light jacket and proper walking shoes. Overall it's quite an experience, you can tell your friends that you've been in the underbelly of a volcano!

Went there and hike up the hill for less than 20 minutes. Not suitable for elderly people to hike up the hill. Toilets at the hillside currently under construction. So there is no toilet at the peak. View was spectacular at the peak. Upon leaving, purchase a huge long foot sausage nearby GS shop. The pair of old couple was indeed very friendly ><

Went there after having lunch nearby.View: spectacular view even before the climb. Nice view at the coast where the Seawomen show is held. Once you reached the summit, you can view the island & the sea but the sky was not clear when we visited.Seawomen Show: they sang a song before entering the sea. Not much to see them in action coz it's not the actual location where they will dive for abalones, octopus etc. We saw from afar there were Seawomen resting on the rocks nearby the Oedolgae rock.The climb: it's a pathway with steps so it's not hard to climb. Along the way there are many stops/benches for the elderly to rest. Just don't rush it if you bring your parents/grandparents along.

We were cruising the Far East and stopped at Jeju. The cheapest excursion was $120 per person. $240 for the two of us. Instead we walked around Jeju a little then hailed a cab. He took us all over the island doing all the same things for $100. Personal service. Stayed. As long as we wanted. Left when we were ready. One of the many ways weve seen the world much cheaper than most. 73 countries and territories so far. The village is interesting. 100 huts. Some occupied. And a black pig. A guy will tell you about a tea they sell that if it tastes salty or sweet will diagnose your ailments. We passed. Not sure how many people read my reviews. If you hit ?helpful?,  I?ll get an email and they always encourage me to write more :)

We went to the island based on the reviews we read.Overall we were disappointed with the island,, it looks very nice but unfortunately the entire beach area around the island is strewn with garbage, and is very apparent against the black rocks. We hired bicycles and cycled around the island and could not find a spot not spoilt by the garbage sight.Also remember to bring your id along as is needed when you purchase your ferry ticket to the island.

We went to Marado Island by taking a 1 h-long ferry from Jeju Island (Daejung-Eup, Hamo ri). The ferry was nice and the could stand in either deck to enjoy the scenic view of the ocean. When you approach the island you could see the beauty of volcanic layers that forms the island and the interface of volcanic rocks and ocean was amazing. Walking is the best way to enjoy the island and you may spend nearly 3 h in the island. There are a couple of restaurants, a beautiful buddha temple, a church etc. A nice half-day trip. Highly recommended.

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

We went Seongsan Ilchulbong in the evening, even though it's known as the Sunrise Peak. The hike up was a little tiring for us as we had previously scaled up a few other peaks the same day. There are quite a few resting spots around, so rest assured you can always catch a breather before ascending the next flight of steps.Bring enough water with you as drinks sold along the way can be quite expensive!The view at the peak is surreal. The sun sets rather slowly in Jeju, so you'll have ample time to scale up and take multiple shots of the place.I will definitely visit the peak again. This time, I'll go for the sunrise. :)

We visited here as part of of our cruise ship day tour of the island. This is a very pretty place with amazing photo opportunities throughout. We purchased one of our favorite souvenirs from a kiosk selling genuine Jeju produced hats. We enjoyed the gardens and the walk over the bridge with the amazing views of the gorge and waterfalls. Be aware that the VERY long walk down to the   close-up   of the waterfalls is rather taxing and may not be worth the effort. Overall, a great experience!

We took bus 710 from intercity terminal, cost 3300won per way. A pretty long ride, about 1hr plus. Met two visitors, one from Singapore & another from Malaysia; very friendly and gave us lot of tips getting around. When we reached at noon, the place was packed with tour buses, people & soldiers (on sight-seeing). Not a difficult hike for reasonable fit person but certainly a challenge for older folk with the steep steps. Nice view but have seen better.

We took bus 182 early morning reached there around 7.30am and started to hike about 8am. It's good to bring hiking stick as there are lots of steps up, with a hiking stick it's easier to move up the rocky paths. It was very cold at the mountain so it's good to wear in layers and can remove the jackets if it gets too warm during the hike. We managed to reach Saraoreum shelter before 12pm where we ate and took a break before moving on to the summit. After 12pm no one is allowed to move on up to the summit from the shelter as it gets dark very early during winter time. We reached the summit just before 1.30pm. The ranger already chasing people to get down. It was very cold and windy at the top and it started to drizzle. So it's important to bring a raincoat too. I could'nt get a good view as it was very foggy and windy. We did'nt get some rest and started to descend. It took a long while to descend too as the path is very rocky and slippery. Lucky i have my hiking stick with me. Half way down it started to get dark we needed to use our handphones as touch light to guide us down the path. Very happy we are all able to reach the summit. It's a nice experience.

We took a walk along the Shores of the rock.. It sure beats jux standing at the top of the observertory and takin pictures! The views are once again spectacular, no complaints.. The walk was not terrible although but I'd warn you to be careful and pick proper shoes coz they can get slippery from the crashing waves! Along the walk you'll see ahjummas selling fresh seafood catches. Try it if you have time!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance (I have attached the photo) and you can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We alighted and headed to the dark brown beach along Seongsan. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore where to can pick clams and walkway with dry cuttlefish along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum as we reached Jongdal Elementary school at 5.30 pm. Noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market to Jongdal Elementary school (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier. We decide to go back as it was late by bus 701 back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal from Jongdal Elementary school  as we noted that the bus will take about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.

We started our climb at 9am by which time the tour buses had arrived. Eventhough it was crowded it was a safe climbing environment because the paths were well paved with grab railings. The elderly and young could stop at rest points along the way. The view of the crater at the summit, the scenic coastline up and down the paths is worth the climb. Give yourself at least an hour to enjoy this amazing Unesco site.

We hiked to the top of the volcano. The walk was pretty easy but long. Lots of information signs make it really easy to manage. The first part is in the wood, which means no view but shadows.
