The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Me and my bf did ＿?깊肄 (Sungpanak Course) which is the longer but relatively easier course than the other one that goes to the top. Not counting the time we rested, we hiked 8.5 hrs in total round trip. It was VERY tiresome, but the view at the top was definately WORTH it!!!

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.
Long trip and not easy, so we took a taxi. Many Asians taking selfies and ruining the view which is beautiful if only not all those mobiles around!

Long long route indeed ! Best is to go via one route and come down via another. Scenery could be a bit monotonous but at the end being surrounded by nature is always more rewarding. Ensure to be on the checkpoint by 1pm else one can be very close yet so far to the summit - since you won't be allowed to climb up the remaining 2.5 kms of stretch. If its a brighter day, view is what makes the climb worthwhile.. if its not, aaah bummer, bummer... !

Located on the far western shore of Jeju Island, Hyeopjae receives a fraction of the visitors compared to other well-known Korean beaches. My wife and I enjoyed a spectacular sunset here after a fun half-day spent swimming and exploring the volcanic tide pools. The beach is superb for three reasons. 1) Great location (not a city-beach), scenic view of islands and volcanic rocks strung along northern portion of the beach.2) Relatively few visitors compared to other Korean beaches3) Water and beach are clean, shallow water makes the beach great for families

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

It's quite a walk going up this crater but there are 2 ways to get there. One is gradually, using concrete stairs or the otther one is by the plain path.Anyway, it's not that high and the view up there more than compensates the effort. Also, we get to see fields of Pampas grasses along thw way which is very beautiful

Its big, full of trees, nice view for taking pictures. Dont go there during holidays, lots of people, long queue for the service train that will bring you around. We didnt enjoyed the place coz its raining during our visit. The windmill area is beautiful, not so much flowers around coz its start of autumn. I think its better to visit during spring season.

It's a lot of stairs and little walking to get to the top, but it's worth it with great views and a wonderful sea breeze. On one side you have views of the crater, on the other of Jeju island. There are lots of other tourists (mostly local) going up and down so be prepared for some level of crowds. There was abundant parking when we visited. There are also plenty of food stalls at the bottom along with bathrooms. On the way up, there are lots of benches, rest areas, and viewing platforms. We saw people of all ages - really old to really young doing the climb. If you're in town and you have a couple hours to spare, we'd recommend it!

It was raining with some strong winds when we got there. Nevertheless we decided to buy a poncho and went ahead with the climb which is a manageable 180 m.The climb up is relatively easy even for most elderlies as there are proper stairs along the way.Apart from the crater, you can see the surrounding areas and the sea from the top. The crater itself is covered by vegetation so you might want to tone down any expectation of a spectacular view. We spent about 15 min at the highest point and start our descend after that.Another attraction nearby is the female divers where they have scheduled performances every day if I remember correctly. We didn?t go for that due to the weather. But I?m sure it would be interesting.

It was raining when we went here. The steps were not at all slippery (they had rubber/metal bars at the end) Although it will be a long hard climb to the top of the mountain. If you started the climb up the mountain there is a different set of stairs going down. At the top of the mountain are set of seats, possibly a good view (it was raining) and a sign to commemorate your achievement. The place is also crowded with people. It is not suggestible for old people to go up the mountain but they could go through the sea. i would go back there again to see the wonderful view.

It was a short walk from the entrance to get to the actual Jeongbang waterfall site, but was a grand sight to behold - you get to see the ocean from the waterfall! I also like that you could make your way closer to the waterfall by stepping on the big rocks around it.Between Jeongbang and Cheonjiyeon, my vote goes to the former. For the latter, the walk from the entrance was longer, the view was not as fantastic, and you can't get nearer to the waterfall even if you wanted to.

It was a short range climb, about 20mins (if you walk fast), about 40mins (if you take frequent rest along the way).. It is quite steep and tiring.The view from the top is really superb! The sea is really wonderful.

It was a nice, warm yet windy weather when I was there. The climb was easy and safe, really a good exercise. Along the way up, there're small gazebos with benches for people to rest and catch their breath. Whoever climbs up are always drenched with sweat but when reached to the peak, the view was really breathtaking. It was worth the climb.
It is worth the climb up. Although tiring, it is all worth it. I'm on top of the crater! Along the way, there are nice view.

It is such a beautiful place to go! The scenery inside the cave is breathtaking and it is unbelievable for such a view. It is a bit cold and dark tho, but it has light installed along the pathway. A very nice place!

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.
it is a long walk up to the top of this peak, but the views are remarkable.  Bring water and be prepared to make the long climb.  Parking is difficult so go early or take a tour bus.

Initially I wasn't sure if I would go to see this as I'd already gone to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak the day before, but it was definitely worth it! It was a cloudy June day which made the setting even more mysterious. Very simple but nicely kept grounds of rolling hills and volcanic rock walls. The crater itself was one of the more bizarre and intriguing natural landscapes I've seen. If you've seen the movie   The Mummy Returns,   it's like the end of that! The surrounding grounds are lovely and you have a great view of the mountains all around you. Would be a very romantic place as well, if you're with your partner. Great place for a picnic or just a long stroll! However, if you're looking for activities and souvenirs and snacks and other touristy things, you'll have to go elsewhere. Fortunately there is a bus stop right outside to go to Jeju City.

Information given in English about the legend of the rock.    You really have to use your imagination to see the woman.    While I didn?t think much of Oedolgae, there?s a lovely hike right along the coast, with pretty views.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

If you're unfit like me, please be mentally and physically prepared before embarking on this   hike  , 4-5 hours upwards, another 4-5 hours downwards. The view at the top is great but that highly depends on the weather. Don't be surprised to see many elderly Koreans in their 50s or 60s even at the peak. And oh yes, please bring along good hiking shoes for this trip, it will definitely help you a lot.

If you want to see a waterfall without the hassle of hiking a long way, go for this one. Just a little stairways descend from the entrance and voil - you'll be greeted by this pretty view of water flowing freely to the sea of Jeju.

If you one got time for 1 of the 3 waterfall in Seogwipo, you should choose this waterfall. View is spectacular, need to walk down the stairs to view the waterfall. and some actually walk very close to the waterfall by walk on the big rocks to get some nice photo. Plenty of parking space available, youth below 25 years get some discount for the entrance ticket (do bring along your passport). suggest to spend 1 hour there.

If you go there just to see the Lonely Rock, you may feel somewhat underwhelmed. However, there is a nice walk along the coast. When I was there, it was sunny and breezy. I really enjoyed the walk, the beautiful coastal view, the clear water and the fresh air. I wasn't disappointed at all.

If staying in or visitng Seogwipo, this is a must. It's no Niagra Falls, but the quality-to-price ratio of this georgeous waterfall is difficult to overstate, as it costs only 2000 won (less than 2USD). A short walk down several staircases, passing shops along the way, will lead you to a stoney beach and the nearby waterfall. You're free to get as close as you wish, but, as many other reviewers have pointed out, the myst created by the falls makes the rocks slippery. So, wear shoes with decent treading and proceed with caution!

If I would have been staying in the area, I would have given this five stars.  However, I had to travel more than 90 minutes to get here, so it wasn't absolutely worth it to me.  But, I really enjoyed the view.  It's also nice that it doesn't take very long to climb to the top.

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

I went to Seongsan Ilchulbong (SunRise Peak) during Mar this year 2015. The weather is cold but bearable around Jeju. However, to climb this mountain is not a great feat for my mum (age 65) but the chilling wind is the one we are defeated.We wanted to visit this peak for sunrise but somehow we are late and lost on our way there. We went to Jongbong Beach and along the coast line it is also very nice to see. We did not catch the sun rise as there are none (due to foggy weather). As we are ascending, the crowd was descending and show enthusiasm although they did not get any view of the sun rise. The climb was nice as there are even wooden/stone steps to the top. Once you reached the top, you will see the beautiful crater which happens million years ago. The view over the edge is equally stunning. Definitely a recommended place to visit when you are in Jeju-Si. The ticket cost 2000KRW each.When you descend, you may see the   Sea-Woman   whom they called Haenyeo will perform at 1.30PM and 3PM only. We did not wait for the show as there are many Sea-Woman around the whole Jeju Island.

I wasn't expecting to have to walk up this thing, but I guess that should have been obvious to me. It was a hot and panting walk, but it was not that long. It was a sunny day, which made for great views, but not for a cool walk. I had JUST MISSED the show with the women divers, I guess it is at 1:30 and 3:00 daily. Nice panorama at the top, the view is certainly impressive.One other thing I liked a lot about this is that it is a fairly touristy area, which meant that most restaurants I passed had pictures and/or English on the menu outside and inside the restaurant, making it easier to order food,

I was told the hike up will only take 30 minutes but when I looked at it I was convinced it would take longer. The hike up is quite steep, lots of stairs, however it really just took a bit more than 30 min, to my own surprise. The hike is not easy however, it requires some stamina, many people take a break or two on the way up. Definitely bring something to drink. Seongsan is quite crowded with tourists, so lots of people all over. The hike is worth it, amazing views from the top. And the hike down is much more enjoyable then the one up. At the foot of Seogsan is a large parking lot, easy to leave your rental there, plus again lots of cafes, restaurants etc. You have to pay a fee to enter.Overall worth seeing Seongsan!

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I ran along the coast line and the park a couple of times, and thoroughly enjoy the view and surroundings. Had a hard time finding the   dragon   rock. Finally found it only when I saw some people taking photos. You have to stretch your imagination quite a bit to visualize the   dragon   leaping into the sky.

I LOVE... this museum!!! I am a teddy bear fan so this museum feels like heaven to me aside from being a K-drama fan. Before visiting Jeju, I researched on the top sites recommended to be visited, i got fascinated with the reviews about Teddy Bear museum plus knowing that some of its Teddy Bears where featured in one my favorite Korean Drama of all time PRINCESS HOURS. The teddy bears are just so cute, you can see them perform different functions and dressed of different profession and famous personalities such as Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Madonna etc. Afetr visiting the exhibit halls, we then went to the lower ground floor area where tall Teddy Bears are on display alongside Teddy Bears items that are for sale.A must visit for Teddy Bear Lovers.

I had requested Tripadvisor to add this as an attractive as it was along the Jeju City Tour bus route. We decided at the last minute to get off at 'Sarabong Peak' as we wanted to see the lighthouse. However, we had a 10 or 15 minute uphill walk to reach the lighthouse during a cold December day but the view more than made up for the inconvenience. We only stayed for half an hour as we wanted to catch the bus back to town as it was already getting dark.

I found this to be the best attraction in Jeju. It really is a lot of stairs, so if you are not good in health condition, this might be very tiresome. But there are rest points a long the way, so you can take your time. There are little shops and restaurants around after you finish your hike. Beautiful views to take pictures both going up and down.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I cannot remember the number of steps(some steep and chip steps) I climb up to the top. Very tiring climb  and almost give up along the way. Among the climb, there are pretty views and I feel satisfied reaching the top.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

I am really unfit and the hike up to the peak is painful to me. But once i reached the top, all of my pain seem to go away. The view of the sunrise is so beautiful. I know i will take longer time to reach the top so i begin the hike up earlier. I started at 5.30 a.m and reach the top after excruciating 1 hour.

How often do you see hexagonal columns along the coastline? This is the place.We were there at about 6:30pm when they were almost closing. They close at 7pm. Although it was quite a rush, we managed to enjoy and soak in the scenery.The observation deck provides very good view of the columns. Be sure to read how the columns came about. It will make the views that much more interesting and meaningful.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Hiking Mt. Halla was on my bucket list for a long time and finally i did it. There is a time restriction and you cannot enter the gate before 6:00 am during the winter time. You have to pass 'Jindalaebat Shelter' before 12:00 pm to continuously hike up to the summit. The park keeper will not let up pass the gate of Jindalaebat if you arrive after the noon. It took about 2 or 3 hours to get to Jindalaebat from Seongpanak gate, and another 2 or 3 hours to get to the summit. It took me 4 hours to get to the Baekrokdam, and took another 5 hours to get down to Gwaneumsa temple. I highly recommend to hike from Seongpanak because it is easier to walk and you are too tired to look around. Then, walk down to Gwaneumsa direction which has a really good view and nature. (Gwaneumsa route is shorter, but definitely harder...super stiff)You will see many people lining up to take a photo with a monument, and I didn't understand why people want to take a photo with just a rock. I learned that you will get a certification of Mt. Hallasan hiking if you show the picture with the monument. All you need to do is go to the ticket office, pay 1,000 KRW and show the picture. I've seen many people hiking with sneakers, but I recommend wearing hiking boots since you have to walk on rocks for 8~9 hours. I heard that you need to be luck to see the summit because Hallasan is always foggy and cloudy. I was lucky and weather was just amazing!! I also heard that it is slightly easier to hike when it snows. There are buses that you can use and I strongly recommend hiking Mt. Halla!!!!!!!

Here at the Jungmun-Daepo Coast, you see the very unique and naturally beautiful Jusangjeolli!These are basically volcanic rocks that have been naturally formed by winds and waves into what seem like artisan-sculpted pillars!It was astounding and amazing to see how nature can create something that you could only imagine a person could do!Usually, there are a lot of people so you can't really stay long and soak on the view and the soothing Jeju breeze!But hey, it's worth the stop!

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hallsan is the highest mountain in Korea. You will have to hike up 1200m.  It is tiresome but it is not very tough, you can take your time. The time estimations indicated in the panels along the way are overestimated (specially if you have some hiking experience).Hiking up this mountain is like being on a highway with a lot of very noisy companions. It is packed, you will most likely be queuing up the mountain if you go in summer.If you are looking for a communion with nature, this is not the place. The hike up is almost entirely man-made, you will be walking up on wooden stairs and on wooden paths. Once you reach the top, it is so packed that you can barely enjoy. Views are excellent though.As you go up, there is a small path to the left to go to another lake. I will recommend this on your way down. Much much quieter as most tourists just want to go to the top.

Great view of the rare animal cliff which is 20 meters height and surrounded by the beautiful islands. Hundreds of visitors went there to have a look of the amazing animal rock. The stone seemed independent and I like the fact that it is normal, nothing inorganic. The shape of Oedolgae formed by the daily erosion of wave and the weathering process. There is a small path in which it can walk along the edges of the island. In which I discovered that the venue was filmed by one of the most famous Korean drama - Dae Jang Geum. I was in love with the drama when I was young, I took tens of photos with the place that Jang Geum have been to.So, if you are I fan of Dae Jang Geum or you would like to see different shapes of stone, you are highly recommended to go there to have a look at the charming sea view.

Great view and friendly people! A wonderful place to relax from the stressful working environment and find peace. It's very very very windy in May, do remember to bring along a hat or sth else to make sure your hair won't fly all around like mad~~~Very friendly people who are also patient despite language barrier.

Gorgeous view of the ocean and surrounds, but extremely crowded in summer. You should be moderately fit to make it up the steep stairway here. Tip: walk on along the main coastal road to the east of to get an alternative view of this World Heritage site.

Gorgeous view of Jeju when you reach the peak and a satisfying climb to the top. For someone who is not fit, it took me almost 45mins to hike to the peak as it was drizzling when I went there. People usually come here to catch the sunrise or sunset but it was a long drive from my guesthouse area. I also planned my timing here so that I could catch the Haenyo performance at around 1.30pm on the way down the peak. Do wear suitable shoes if you are hiking to the top as the steps get very steep as you go further up and if it rains, it's going to be very slippery. Also, do check out the weather forecast before visiting because there wouldn't be a nice view if there's fog.

From the bottom Seongsan Ilchulbong looks daunting, but once you get walking its relatively easy, with many well placed rest spots along the way. The views at each spot are pretty great - you can really appreciate the black sand beaches from there. Take some water with you!The top of the volcano is amazing - covered in a sea of green grass, it looks like it could easily be a set in a Jurassic Park movie. There is something so primal about the feeling up there. And despite the many other hikers you will find up there, its pretty easy to find a spot to sit and appreciate it for a bit!The entrance is 2000 won. Take some water, a camera and some coins for the scopes. Also, it gets really, really gusty up at the top and along the walkway to Ilchulbong beach, so try and avoid any flyway items of clothing.
Fresh air and beautiful scene of the sky, sea & rocks all together. Walk along the coastal path to take in the views from different angles. It is supposedly also the filming location of 鸚㏝룝.

For those who are not really into long hikes and yet still want a good panaromic view of Jeju?s surroundings, this is the place. There are also live performances apparently involving the female divers but we missed the timing.

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

For family with kids, this will be a nice to visit as there's a nice steam train ride which brings you around to many scenic areas within Eco Land. A nice break from all the nature views and long trekking walks.

First and foremost, you need to find a place to stay nearby the Sunrise peak as you need to wake up early to climb up in time to view the sunrise. It should take around 20-30 minutes to reach the top. It's quite cold and windy up there during autumn time so bring along a wind breaker. Once you are up there, just wait until you see the dark sky suddenly light up, then you will see the most marvelous sunrise you ever seen.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Excellent view and atmosphere! A long steep (with stairs) and challenging climb up the inactive volcanic island mountain that earns you good exercise and satisfaction! You can already enjoy the picturesque surroundings at the foot of the mountain with different views and you can buy some souvenir there and also enjoy a short horse ride (not free of course). If you are there on a sunny day, do buy some popsicle or ice-cream to go up.   There are entrance fees for the entrance as well. However, it is well worth it once you reached the top. It is fantastic to be on top looking down to the inactive volcano crater and enjoy the view of the sea that looks like touching the sky. You can literally feel like you are touching the sky too! The best time to go there will be during sunrise! Don't forget to take a selfie with the mountain height indicator board to boast your achievements! Oh, and just right before you reach the top, please take a look at the back downhill at the interesting look of the city below and take a selfie and also take some nice selfie around you.     On the way down, there is the fishing village where the you can enjoy the seafood while watching the women divers catch clamps and oyster. There are some fiexed timing but I have already forgotten the timing.    Seongsan Ilchulbong is indeed a must visit destination everytime you arrive in Jeju!

Even though it was autumn when i visited, the sun was glaring. It was quite tiring to climb the stairs all the way up to the top but totally worth it! The view along the way up and the view of the town and island from the top is magnificent even though the top was just kind like a crater. Very important to be in good comfortable shoes.Will gladly climb again, hopefully this time i get there in time for sunrise or sunset.

Do check the sunrise forecast and depending on fitness level, allow 20 minutes to an hour to reach the peak. Very doable hike even for non-fitness enthusiasts. The stunning views along the way and at the peak will be worth every effort! On the way up, there will be a few points where you can sit and take a breather. Great activity to start off the day!

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.

Depending on the weather, it was scorching for me, this is an easy hike for all ages. It takes no longer than an hour to get to the top and back. The views of the crater and surrounding landscape is beautiful. A nice view of U-do island off the coast as well. Well worth a morning hike followed by a boat across to U-do island, where boats go very regularly.

Climbed the mountain with my wife 5 year old daughter and some friends. Not a strenuous climb, but a long one. 9 hours all tolled for the return journey. Very busy on the mountain (even more so at weekends and holidays) but really worth the effort. You do not need to be too fit (I really wasn't when I did it) as long a you take your time. Take plenty of snacks and water - although there is a snack bar 2/3 of the way to the top. Glorious views on a cloudless day, and a real sense of achievement having scaled the tallest peak in Korea.

Climbed Mount Halla as part of a group tour. It was definitely a challenging climb as I would not call myself fit. I did get to the top though and that was after 3 and a half hours of climbing. It's easier at the bottom and tougher towards the top because of the various flights of stairs. Also something to note is that it's very cold on top and requires layers, as well as proper hiking shoes. The view for me wasn't the best but having been able to push my body that far was a reward in itself. People brought food and had picnics at the summit. It was more difficult coming back down as your're moving on uneven ground for long periods of time. Overall glad I did it
Clear waters, soft sand beach and you can find many people taking strolls and chilling by the beach. You can also visit the cafes along the beach which provides a nice view

Chilshimni Poetry Park is part of Jeju Olle Route 6 that was easy to located as it was along the main road, Namseongjung-ro road where Park sunshine hotel or Poong Gyung Hotel were. It was a free general park with playground where the locals hang out and it can be finish in 30 minutes for less. However, the highlight of the park was the ability to have a clear view Cheonjiyeon waterfalls from a height for free! We spent some time chilling at the table and benches to appreciate the falls. There was also a stairway down to Saeyeongyo bridge. As the park was part of Jeju Olle Route 6, we went out to the main road, Namseongjung-ro road, and followed the orange/blue ribbons to Oedolgae. I have rated this park a 4 stars for the beautiful view of the Cheonjiyeon waterfalls.

Came here to checkout the views and totally loved it. A nice small town to chill at with lots of parking if you're driving. Many restaurants, cafes and food trucks along the beach. Beautiful white sand and blue waters. Not crowded. Definitely coming back here! Didn't get enough of it.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!
Brought my baby (14 months old) along , climbed the stairs together,  nice view, very good experience, awesome !

Bring along a lot of water before climbing. There is few cafe that open very early at the counter ticket area, for you to have anything if you feel hungry before climbing, but just for snacking. The entrance fee is 2k Won, if im not mistake. The view was great along the way from bottom to top. After half-way through, there is a checkpoint with nice scenery of the city and ocean during dawn, which is so beautiful. Better to take picture during that time of your climbing if you climb to see the sunrise, because when you get down, it is another daylight scenery. If you are not fit enough or dont have that much stamina, don't worry, it is still okay for you to climb, you just need a strong will to arrive at the peak and keep on going. As the view from top is worth the sweat!For you to see sunrise, its better for you to be down at the entrance as early as you can, during my time, I already there by 530am, the gate open at 6am as far as I can remember. If you climb slow and steady, it will take you about an hour to climb to the peak. Just keep in mind, if there is a lot of clouds, you might not be able to see the sunrise. So check your weather before you go.

Beautiful little hike, worth all the stairs (130 stairs). Shady little spots along the path to pause and sit, and there?s different platforms to get different angles of the view as you approach. But it?s worth going down to the bottom. $2 per person to get in. The women at the juice stalls were also super sweet!

Be prepared to climb a long flight of steps to reach the top. Once you are at the top, the view is breathtaking. I love the view and the climbing is worth all the effort. There are a lot of restaurants and shops below and you can catch live performance of women divers are the bottom at certain time.

At east spot of Jeju. Takes about 1.5 hour bus ride from the intercity bus terminal. Free entrance. Although the peak is only 180 metres, it's still challenging to climb because of the steepness. Very beautiful view along the way. The ocean and the mountain are all visible. Highly recommend.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed Jeju Olle Route 6 from Chilshimni Poetry Park (to see the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top) to Oedolgae and happened to see this Hwangwooji coast (probably part of olle route 6) which was my favourite spot of the day. You will walk along Namseong-ro road and passed by 외돌개나라 Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online). I love the place bcos it was like a private pool and it is free. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.? After-which we head to Oedolgae.You can walk there and you do not need a car. Probably a 15 minutes walk from the main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Poong Gyung Hotel or Park sunshine hotel jeju is) and walk in to Namseong-ro road where? 외돌개나라 Hostel is.

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.

Although a very steep hike, this long flight of stairs does include many view points and amazing views at the summit. It was a little cloudy the day we climbed the summit and so did take away from the view a little but nevertheless was still great. I did the climb around  March but it was still very windy, make sure if you go during this time you take something to cover you face/ears if possible as the strong winds make your face go numb with the cold. Would highly recommend to anyone who visits Jeju Island.

Along with Go Carts and a hot air balloon ride, the Maze Park has enough to keep everyone busy and happy! The Maze is fun to watch people navigate from the hot air balloon. A great view of World Cup Stadium too!! This was a fun day!
Along the way have very beautiful view especially during autumn . With Nice weather ,enjoy beautiful tree color during autumn.

After my Manjanggul Cave   expedition   and since the park is just along the way back, I took the chance to see what's the place could offer. I paid KW 2800 for an entrance (I have read reviews that some paid more than the cost, maybe the cost vary by seasons, not really sure). The maze can be finished roughly 10-15 mins, yet completed the maze roughly 30 mins hahaha. I just enjoyed messing around. Didn't really paid attention to the map and it's goal to ring the bell. The maze is good for family to enjoy.

After climbing the stairs for the view of the lush, plant-filled centre of the crater, you should definitely walk along part of the black sand beach that arcs around to the ?glass house.? You?ll see some amazing views of Seongsan Ilchubon there, and your pictures won?t be filled with random tourists. There are also bits of sea glass scattered along the shore, shells, and if you walk down the beach far enough, a beautiful, large ledge of lava covered in green moss you can walk on and explore. It was really easy to get to the crater by bus from Jeju-si, and it only took about 75 minutes.
After a long way climbing up to the death volcanic, you can enjoyed the paranomic view at the peak of the seongsan. It's worth .

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A very long and tiring climb if you are not used to climbing. There's lots of people both locals and tourists climbing along so you will definitely be motivated to continue climbing. Tip: bring sunglasses, pack light, grab a snack and bring a bottle of water, most importantly wear comfortable sports shoes. Just climb slowly and take a break along the way as you need so that you are not overly tired out. If you are thinking of combining this attraction with other nature sites that require ample walking or climbing, do take note that this attraction may already be rather tiring... the view and wind at the top is worth it, in my opinion. You do not see the bird's eye view you see online but nonetheless you see the vast greenery and top down view of the scenery below.

A total of 19.7 KM hikeThe walk in early spring will be having snow so be prepared.. Buy the show snow covers Crampons its a must , its a must , its a must , i went without and sliped dozens of times  and injured myself once.. its snowy on the last third.. I hiked manytimes before in different parts of the world i go with sports shoe.. this one deserves crampons.. and maybe walking sticks as well.. Its long and tiresome. . But fun.. the view is great from up .. but make sure its not foggyat the end if u show them a picture taken at the top they will give u a certificate for 1000 won.. its a certificate of achievement really after a long hike. . Its 4 hours up and 4 hours down..

A nice little hike up to the top. Not very long, Maybe 20 minutes but ALOT of stairs. Your legs will be feeling it. Good View at the top and its nice to see all the people taking 1 million selfies of themselves while at the top.

A must for visitors tot he island. An area of beauty, amazing geographical formations, haenyeo (diving women), shops and foods. A very steep climb to the top but the steps are well developed and there are small seats along the climb to take a break. Great views fro the top, but if the day is windy be prepared for some discomfort. Take a water bottle, camera and coat! Worth every step!

Went with two boys that dislike shopping. Good thing they hv soap or bubble bath craft to keep both busy while I shop. Surprisingly it took them longer to finish their craft then my shopping! A win-win place for me!

Went here expecting a museum but this is simply a store and caf챕. One room with a few tea sets on display; that's pretty much it. The surroundings are pleasant enough with fields with tea bushes and the garden and buildings are above average museum standard. Not worth a trip or detour. But if you're nearby checking out the tea ice cream might be ok; long lines to get that.

We were staying in Seogwipo and had an extra day with nothing to do. So decided to book tickets from Klook on the day of visit. From Days Hotel in Seogwipo we would have to take two buses 201 and then 295?. The first bus is 1 hr 10-15 mins and much more frequent than the second bus which is a 5 mins ride or a 25 mins 2 km walk. Taxis are cheap starting fare of 2800 krw will get you to Aqua Planet from the 201 bus stop but they are a needle in a sack - hard to come by! Other countries??hard to reach facility ir tourist site may provide some form of free shuttle/transport but not here. Once you enter the main facility it would take you a long time to find the toilets - certainly not tourist friendly. Live shows are also all in Korean  albeit with English & Chinese subtitles. The size of this Aquarium is about one third or one quarter of the Okinawa one so we were seriously disappointed with its size and varieties of fishes available. Visit if you have a car or join a local tour or book a taxi. If using public transport like us think twice about going as its 3-4 hrs to and fro Seogwipo.

review: We went on a rainy day and feared it would be too busy to enjoy but it was ok (the first section was the busiest but the crowds thin out the further you get in).  A lot of fun for kids and adults alike.  It took us longer than we thought to get through you could spend hours so would suggest bringing some snacks if you are travelling with kids like we did. There is a coffee shop on site but it only had sweets and ice cream.A fun outing if you've never been to a trick museum before.  Don't forget your camera!!!

We took city tour bus and stopped at this famous black pork street for dinner at the shop with long queue.   Minimum order is KWR 54000 for 600g pork for 2 pax ie roughly 300g per pax.  It seemed so meaty but the helper grilled the pork just nice and we finished all.

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

We caught the ferry over to the island (remember your passport or other form of photo ID) and hired a two person battery operated bike which was great fun.   Hired for 2 hours which was ok but if you want to spend longer at each stop then I would recommend at least 3 hours.   We went all around the island.  We stopped the longest at a small village where you can go down some steps to the beach and go and investigate a large cave.   There was an outdoor cafe on the beach serving fish -  very busy.  Can't remember the name of the village but it was towards the end of our circuit.  Definately a good weather day activity.

Was there at about 10ish in the morning lots of (noisy) tourist and you can hardly find a decent seat in the cafe with unruly kids running around. Difficult to take photo at the photo spot cos some particular tourists pose like nobody business and after a long time posing change friend to pose again. I gave up and went outdoors where noise will not be contained and there is more fresh air.Sadly there isn't much nor exciting to see here - yet it is a spot you have read alot before coming. Suggest to just make a brief stop to have a look.I spent more time over at the Innisfree Jeju House instead which was surprisingly very peaceful.

Very beautiful and serene temple. there is also an option for temple stay here. it's tucked away from the hustle and bustle of city life so it will be a good retreat. There were prayers ongoing when we were there which was very relaxing to listen to. you can enter the temple through the side doors (not through the centre) make offerings of rice (you can get this at the counter inside) or donations. it may be a little difficult to get there by public transport. we hired a driver Mr Yang (+82 10-3639-7469) to help us get around - he was most helpful quite humorous and very easy to get along with even taking photos for us and giving short descriptions of the sights at the attractions.

This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.

the ticket price is cheap but place a bit far away from city..sculptures are not well kept so looked run down.but there are many beautiful world buildings which make good photo spots.i am very disappointed there is not even a small cafe for us to take a snack.there is a drink vending machine though..i checked the surrounding for staff.think less than 6staff..this can be a very good attraction place if jeju govt can pump in some money to repaint the buildings open a cafe and make the bus stop nearer so we do not have to walk so long.

The place is relatively small and when I was there there where a lot of people. The beach is with black sand nice. I had a very nice Mandarin Orange icecream and that was worthwhile. From there I walked along the beach maybe 5 kilometers until I came to a little fishing port. From there a very nice person took me along in the car... there was a bus stop but the busses only come at a long interval...it would have been possible to wark until Seogwipo but that would have been another 3 or so kilometers. A long but really beautiful walk...the stones are all vulcanic and black. If you have the time and inclination I recommend

In the front there is a bus stop. Along the road to the temple is full of orange tree. Big temple with beautiful decoration. Just feel silent and peaceful here. You can just go inside free of charge. I think this is the best temple in Jeju!

I took buses from central of jeju to this area for fishing trip it takes about 1 hours with 2 buses wait time for buses quite long ~30m. Bus driver and local residents are friendly dry squid is delicious and cheap. 4k - 6k won per squid (depend upon the size) you can ask them to grill and enjoy. I love this quite place and people

There isn't any space to lay down a blanket so you have to rent an umbrella.  The water is crystal is clear and the tide is very low.  I had to walk about 300 meter in order to get water that was waist high. There are all kinds of coffee shops and restaurants located along the strip of the beach so you can eat and hang for  as long as you like.  The water is beautiful and makes it worth it.

First of all the cave is not accessible by public transportation. We got dropped off the main road by public bus but it is still a long way in by foot.  My expectation was we will be dropped very close to it but it wasn't. The cave was ok.  Nothing special.
