A grand n majestic temple. Upon entering the temple vicinity you can feel truly blessed n at ease.Even though the history of the temple aint long the architecture of the temple n beautiful landscaping are truly marvellousThe airport limousine bus from airport/ jeju city stops in front of the temple on the way to Seogwipo.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Yes, you can have chance to see the Korean old houses. However, there is nothing much for you to visit. No tourist information or any other services around. We take a long bus to reach there and go back in 10 minutes then.

Well, it is and arboretum, but it being a garden with quite the hustle around it we did expect a lot more. We walked through 3/4 of the garden in about 20-30min and then left. They had two greenhouses, but they were closed (under construction). A waste of time, there are many more botanical gardens in which you can have a better time without the long travel (it is quite a bus ride out of the city). It was free though...

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We were dropped by the bus at the parking lot, and had to walked through a beautiful park where seashell statues and boats placed along the path. We have to queue for about 20-30 minutes before we could really see the amazing nature-sculptured cliff.It was very beautiful, especially at sunset.

We went with high expectation, thinking that we could go into the larva tube. To our utmost disappointment, besides a 4-D movie, It was just a museum with some picture exhibits, and glassed up exhibits of a very small part of the larva tube. Admission was W3,000. It took us a long time to get there, as the bus was a 50 minute wait and it was extremely cold that day.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

we tried to take bus and ferry ourselves to visit Udo. The weather on that day was very good, there were a lot of geographical scenes in Udo, beaches were beautiful, besides taking bus for seeing the whole island, take a walk along the seaside was also very good.  eating seafood in a famous restaurant, also tried the famous peanut ice cream of this island.

We traveled here by public transport. The bus stop turned out to be quite a bit away from the cave itself, but we were lucky enough to get a lift from a friendly lady. The cave itself is nice, with lights everywhere. It's not a long walk through, nor is it a difficult one. I would recommend wearing shoes, rather than sandals or flipflops, as the rocky surface isn't easy in the low light. Also recommend a jacket/vest because it gets cold and drops fall from the ceiling.

We took bus 701 to the foot of the hill. We thought we had got off at the wrong stop as it was very quiet at the bus stop. We walked a little uphill and saw that we were on the right track. Admission was W2,000. The stairs made it a very easy climb.  One direction up and one direction down.  Very scenic along the way and at the peak. Very windy though.

We took a taxi to this road. The driver spoke limited English but it was sufficient for us to understand the explanation: when the vehicle gear is put to N on what seemed to be an up-slope, the vehicle rolls forward (it should have rowed backward instead)When we alighted the cab, we stood there longer to examine all the passing vehicles: mainly tour buses experimenting the same concept. You can hear their engines turned off and you will see the buses rolling   forward   on the up-slope. It was an intriguing experience but will be even better if you drive and experience it yourself. Other than the road itself, you may consider alighting and try out the two street food stores there.. or have a walk around the area, we saw herd of cattles grazing just beside the road too.

We took a relaxing stroll through a beautiful forest Bijraim Nutmeg Forest. The shade of the forest is perfect for a hot summer day. It's a beautiful small forest, but getting there was a bit time-consuming, involving a bus ride from Jeju City and some brief hitch-hiking. (We were to take a second bus, but we waited so long that decided to hitch a ride instead.) However, from Bijraim, there is a bus that takes you directly to the popular Manjanggul, so it's a good idea to visit both in the same day.

We took a cab from Ramada Plaza for 30,000 wan. It took about half an hour. The bus home 710 was great and took an hour. 3000 wan. The island was good fun. We cycled the island stopping along the way to see things. The elder diving women were really cool. Sad to see the garbage around from the sea :( Udo is in such a highly populated area of the world garbage is a big problem. It makes me want to really try to become green at home in Canada.

We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

We reached the ferry terminal at 11am and waited for a short while for the ferry. The ferry depart quite frequently so there is no worry for that. As mentioned by other people, you will need to bring your passport to purchase a ticket. If you intend to rent a motorised vehicle in Udo, you will need to bring along your international driving permit. We rented a covered motorised scooter for 3h at KRW40,000. The scooter has doors and can seat 2 people. It took us less than 2.5h to cover the whole island, we even took 45min lunch break in between. The entire island is around 17km, so if you intend to make stopovers for photo taking, renting for 2h will be good enough. Just follow the coastline and you won't get lost. I highly recommend travellers to opt for the motorised scooter for a relaxing trip around Udo island. It will take you just half day. There are not many cars on the road but there are many scooters and bicycles which share the same path. There are many tourists and they might not observe the driving rules very well, so do be careful when driving on the roads. However, if you intend to see some of the other sights on Udo, they are not accessible for these transportation as you will need to take a separate ferry to go there. There seems to be many people taking the shuttle bus in Udo, so I don't really recommend people to do so if you have an international driving permit.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We didn't spent much time here as we are rushing. Overall is a nice place to visit. You can rent a bike or motor cars to go around the island or take the bus tour. At first we planned to drive car inside the island. However, due to many vehicles in the island and to avoid traffic jam, they have set the rules that only local island cars can drive into Udo island. I forgot the timeline but it took around one year period. For those who plan to drive car enter the island you may need to further check on it. When purchased the ferry ticket, you are required to fill in the two forms. Please bring along your passport as well. The counter personnel not many can speak English where we feel a bit challenge. Overall, is a nice place to visit. And if possible do spare around one day to enjoy the environment here.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

We could not have gotten to so many attractions on our own in one day, so great time taking the bus tour from Yeha.  Wish we had booked more days in Jeju to explore other parts of the island such as Seowipo.  The cave is 1km long and a nice attraction to check out, especially for families.  Cold inside!  Bring an extra layer...

Visited the cave as a part of a bus tour. We entered through the 2nd section and were given 40 mins to walk to end of the cave and back. Grounds are uneven and slippery due to water dripping from the ceiling, hence proper shoes are necessary. The lighting was quite dim and there were only a couple of descriptions along the way. I didn't come out with a full appreciation of the lava cave. The cave wasn't very spectacular but it's worth a visit if you are in the area.

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Udo or ?Cow Island? lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing ??5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It?s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

Took a bus from Seogwipo early morning and it takes around 1 hour 40 minutes to get there as the bus stops on all stops along the way. Once there, it is a short 10 to 15 min hike up to the top where you will be met with a green crater. Unless you have a drone, its not possible to capture the beauty of the place unfortunately. On the way down, we waited to see the women diving show, but it got cancelled which was a let down as we only got to know after the show was supposed to start.

To get to this island, one has to fill in a form and pay for the fees. All is convenient and easy peasy. Then, the ferry ride is quick. We opted for a bus tour. The tour was in Korean and we couldn't understand a thing but considering it is one of the easiest method to get around the island,we just go along with it. We would like to ride one of those adorable scooters but we don't own an international license. Overall a good experience.

This was a big disappointment. We'd read that it was a real functioning village, but it was mostly deserted, the houses falling down and no sign of any residents. The buildings are picturesque enough but overall it had a rather sad, melancholy feel. We only spent half an hour there and regretted the long bus journeys entailed.

This village was very interesting. A lot of people still live in this village and they make a living off of the products that they sell. The village is free to go to, so we made sure to purchase some things in the village. We encountered a couple English speakers that guided us and explained some things to us. They were so sweet, they held onto some of our belongings at their home while we walked through the village. When we were done they offered to call us a taxi. When we told them we planned on taking the bus they insisted on driving my entire family to our next destination. They were so sweet, it was very heartwarming!

This road is interesting! When we are about to reach the site, the driver turned off the engine, and yet the bus is moving upwards!! Amazing!We even went down the bus to try running backward on the road, and one can feel like you are being pulled from the back. Also, we try by pouring water onto the road itself, which is a good test.And yes, the food stall along the road is more interesting.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

This is one road which really left my puzzled. The bus driver did turn off his enjoy but the bus still managed to roll on, to my eyes, the path was an up-sloping one. So how did the bus manage to move on its own? Does it mean the path is actually downwards sloping?This is just any other road along Jeju Island which after completion, people found out about this weird phenomenon. Well, the locals will explain to you the whole reason to this phenomenon. Don't worry, expect a crowd there with tour buses pulling over, but don't expect a fee to be paid unless you patronize the little snack shops there.

This is arguably the longest running South Korean LIVE show ever!  Now, it is branching out to other popular tourist destinations such as Jeju Island.  You needn't understand Korean language to appreciate the show, which is leaning more towards physical action and slapstick comedy based on timing.  It revolves around cooking.  Nanta show is leaning heavily towards satisfying tour groups and the day I was there, two thirds of the theatre was filled up by tourists that came in bus loads.  Nanta is interactive too, with occasional involvement with the audience.  Children thoroughly enjoyed the show.  It was pure 90 minutes of unadulterated fun and enjoyment.  In terms of price, you can get cheaper price booked through YEHA website.  Commendable fun:)

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

The trip ti Mt Halla is great and do not miss it. Youu really should start early, and it takes a little less than recommended times, about one hour less if you walk clow but continuously.We walked three 15, 30 and 55, two males - my son and me and one female accompanied us.We traveled by bus from Seogwipo, busses go every 15-30 minutes since early morning to Seongpanak - busstop.Back we walked to Gwaneumsa and there is no direct bus connection, but take a taxi (for 5 thous WON) or walk about 5 km. We finaly shared taxi with very kind Korean directly to Seogwipo, thank again to the kind man. It was good and exhausting and we slept nicely after all. The next day we were ready to walk again. Unfortunatelly was very cloudy and walked upon clouds finally, however it was June, it was not too hot. There are two springs along the way - one up and nexd on the way down. Recommended to every who travels with teenagers:) Normal hiking shoes like trainers were OK, dont worry.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The park is the mystical legend of how three gods arrived in Jeju-do and started to develop the island. The place is a great escape from the busy city of Jeju, surrounded with trees and pavilion of traditional Korean architecture. You can also sit in for a 15 minutes long animation, available both in English and Korean  describing the origins of Jeju.

The mountain is extremely busy with tons of people and older koreans are not always very friendly toward foreigners, but the rude people are exceptions. In general the hike is wonderful, just very long. There is beautiful scenery and forests to enjoy. Take a jacket for the top as its cold and start early.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The island is windy. Quite convenient to go around as there's shuttle bus with blue and red route that bring you around the island. The bus driver will narrate in Korean to explain the places, although we don't understand but is a fun trip to go along with mostly korean. The field grows full of canola flowers (yellow), very beautiful. Also, with nice cliff with plunging waves, good place to take pictures. The water is clear blue at the beach. Unfortunately, we only planned for half day trip so we can only complete the blue route. So, best to plan for a day as it probably takes you full day to admire the scenery.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Strolling numbers of beaches in Udo or climb the peak of Udobong. Simply taste the peanut ice cream and hallabong ice cream from the various stall along the coastal lines. The local turban shell is a must try in Udo. Getting around is easy either by shuttle bus, ATV, bike ride or just a pair of feet is all you need.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!

Sorry, guys if i am a bit skeptical for this kind of attraction.  For me, and perhaps for some others, it is just an optical illusion.  No surprise on that....lol.I watched closely the power lines running alongside the street and the top of the trees alignment you might be able to see that the street is actually going down and not up, giving an impression that the bottle is rolling upwards....  As the old saying states,   the law of gravity still applies everywhere on earth  .  It was quite crowded when i was there, and needed to be a bit careful when people were trying to walk backwards whilst buses and cars were trying to pass by on that narrow street.  There are few food stalls as well.

Really enjoyable walk through the dark and luminous cave created by the eruption of Halla. It will take a decent time and is right next to a maze filled with cats!Unfortunately there isn't convenient bus transport as you have to walk about 30 minutes from the bus stop but if you're relatively fit, it will be no problem (aside from your friends nagging you how long till you get there).

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.

Parking was difficult to find in the area when we visited although the walk back to the markets was not too bad. The markets were busy with many local producers sold their wares. Tourist heaven for the local oranges, chocolates and teas with many eating places as well that served a wide range of foods from pork to sea foods, fruits, burgers, desserts, nuts and candy. Much to choose from! Smaller tourist items can also be found along with clothing of the island - not much for westerns sizes though. Fairly crowed, but an experience not to miss while on the island.

Our tour bus driver parked the bus along the road,and stopped the engines. In a little while, the bus started moving forward. As pointed out by our tour guide, we have to take note of the inclination of the trees lining the road, which gives the impression that the road is uphill. So,that's it!As in any tour, one has to keep an open mind, curious to learn about the lives and culture of the place being visited, as well as the different places of interest.

One should definitely visit this market to get the local flavour of Jeju. Usually crowded and has a lot of hustle bustle all day long. One can buy souvenirs , spices , fruits , fish and other wholesale items. Do checkout timings before visiting as it opens very early in the morning and closes early as well.

One of the many very interesting sites in Jeju Island.  These women would dive for 2 minutes at a time to harvest food from the ocean bottom, using no tanks or other equipment.  They were the only known groups of women who resisted during the Japanese occupation.  Also good access by bus.  Easy to get there by bike, depending on where you are staying on the Island. NIce bike paths, though often are covered with the drying sea weed that the old women still harvest from the rocks. There is also a very small Buddhist temple with a Quan Yin statue in front, about a half mile to the west along the coast.

review: Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was along the way to Manjanggul Cave. As we had missed the bus 990 which could take us to the Cave, we had to walk the 2.5km way. About 1.4km's walk, we came to the Gimnyeong Maze Park. It was a fun place even for adults. We did not follow the map so that it would be exciting. Indeed it was, and the more lost we were, the more exciting it got.

It took me a long time to get there. All those folks with cars would have no problems. But I am on a budget, and I am bussing it all the way. I came here from the Seongsan Ilchulbong crater thing, and I took the 701 bus to the stop that said it was for the cave. Then I walked 2.5km to the cave. The cave was gloriously cold inside, as I was a hot sweaty mess by then (Korean people staring at the fat, sweaty American haah!). I took my time through the cave, it was nice and worth the trip for me, even though it took me almost 2 hours to get back after I was finished. I think you could take a cab for a reasonable price... but I am cheap.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

Interesting road... My bus was shifted to neutral gear and went up th hill by itself....Had saw this before in Taiwan and china... It was actually an optical illusion .. Nonetheless quite amaze by it. Other than this generally speaking the attraction has no depth... Can go if visiting some other attraction in the area, but not worth it if travelling long distance for it .

Iho Taewoo Beach 댄명고대? is the closest beach to Jeju-si (city) and is closed to airport too, one can look down from the plane of the two very special red and white horse-shaped lighthouses when it almost reach Jeju Airport. Beach are sandy white and swallow water that are safe to swim. It is open for public and no admission charges except if is Jeju Iho Taewoo Festival.Visitors are welcomed to camp at the camping site. Facilities like charging room and shower room with locker are available too, is chargeable.There is two entrance to Iho Taewoo Beach, one is closer to the sandy beach and camping site located in the pine forest but less parking space. The other one is close to the horse-shaped lighthouses with huge free parking space and food trucks selling food and beverage. Here you can cycling and photographing. The two white and red horse-shaped lighthouse is famous for sunset photographing, it is best to be there around 5-6pm for the best sunset moment. Iho Taewoo Festival is around Jul-Aug every year. Local and tourist will be coming to witness the happening festival and event like boat ricing, fishing competition and many more fun activities. It will be a long day event.If you are driving, key in 728-3393.If you are taking public transport, take green bus 7,17 or 60 or blue bus 36

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the   jimjilbang   (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you   foreigners   out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.

If you were to Seongsan Ilchulbong and to Manjang cave next, you can grab the taxi if there is no bus.. The fare is quite reasonable.Wouldnt expect that the cave would be that cold but it is as cold as Seoul during Spring time.. The lighting is very good. Though it is  a long walk to the end, it id worth it.. The deeper, the colder it is..

I went to see the crater in middle day. Was a long bus ride to get there for a 10 min visit in all. Not what I expected. It is a very rare formed crater in the world and the explanations are on a board but kind of deceiving to look at for me. All full of lush green trees and very wide, it does not give great pics and you don't see it that well either. Not as impressive as I expected. Would tell you to prioritize other stuff if you have a tight schedule. Souvenir shop has not much to buy and there is a small restaurant for snacks or ice cream.

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I thought it was a long winding road but the distance is short an it gave optical illusion of our bus going uphill. Well when you got down the bus to see yourself, it makes no differences. Just a road filled with curious people.

I never been to such places before so i have no reference to compare it to. I think it was worth the entrance fee, a bit hard to get there with the buses. You pay the fee for inside baths that are separated by male and females, where most of the people are naked. You pick a small locker room for your shoes and with the same key you can open a bigger locker for the fest of your belongings. You should shower before getting in the tubs and must pay to use the outdoor tubs, where both man and women can use(not naked). Try to follow the instructions in english of how to use the baths, for how long and in what order and it will be worth it. They also have massages, sleeping rooms, lounges, vibrating chairs, small restaurant ...

I love this cave as it was calmy, a little bit wet but make you comfortable after a long walk from the bus stop. I had to walk 3km or more (I think) coz my legs felt so sore, but I love the walk inside the cave. If you take a public bus, don't finish up too late as you might miss the last bus.

I have spend a week on Jeju Island in September, and of my Highlights was Udo. I had time only for a day trip, and if I ever make it back to Jeju, my priority will be to spend at least one night there. Its such a lovely, small and relaxed place. From Seongsan its only 15 minutes to Udo by Ferry. There, you can take the local bus that runs along the island, you can rent small tuk-tuks / quad bikes / scooters or bicycles, you can join a tour (I think only in Korean) or you can walk (like I did, but then of course you dont get to cover the whole island).

I have been wanting to visit the Teddy Bear Museum for the longest time but did not get to visit the one in Seoul 2 years ago. So, when we decided to plan a 2D1N trip to Jeju, this attraction is in my itinerary list. It is not located conveniently near the city centre and about an hour's bus ride to go to the attraction. I was so excited when I saw the museum when the bus passed by and alighted with much excitement. We were greeted with a huge bear at the entrance and it was like entering a wonderland. We walked around admiring the displays, the history of teddy bears etc. We also visited the outdoor park right behind the museum which are meant for visitors only. It was a fruitful visit and did not fail my expectation though. Love all the bears on sale at the gift shop but couldn't bring them all back so only got to admire them when I was there. If you are visiting Jeju, do drop by this museum to bring back childhood memories.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I happened to notice a separate entrance desk that had pictures of SCUBA divers on it. I asked an attendant nearby in simple English sentences if they had any SCUBA diving and how much was it? It was only 119000 KWon and they happened to have availability right away! I've dove in other aquariums but this was the cheapest and didn't even require a reservation on a busy day! Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids. They loved it!I still had to pay the separate entrance fee for the aquarium (about $40 but I received a 20% off coupon at the airport) but it was worth it. The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Would definitely go back.Note: A lot of the aquarium features the image of a whale shark. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.

review: I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Great photo spot, many people use this beach for camping. Hard to find eating place or restaurant. The public transport also quite hard here! We wait so long for bus and finally we use taxi for way back hotel

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

Even though this exhilarating experience lasted probably 10 minutes it was a moment to remember. I am happy we took the ride along mysterious road to experience this. The tour bus was switched off and the bus travelled on its own uphill. You wonder how it happened, it is puzzling.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.
