review: Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Bangju Church is a picturesque little church that?s unmissable on the way to Bonte Museum.  It?s the unique ark-shaped exterior along with the surrounding water that makes it photogenic and there isn?t much inside (which is off limits most of the time anyway).  Despite being a short stop, there were always a half dozen cars in the parking lot with people busy taking photos around the church.

As with everything on Jeju, this is built for tourists. The cave itself is interesting but understand there is nothing but this one section of one cave that you can access. This is not in the least bit adventurous - the cave is lit well all along its length. It's the kindergarten of caves but if you haven't been in a lava tube before then it may be for you. Beware that if you take the bus to the caves, you still have 2.5 km on foot to the cave entrance, though you can flag a cab down if one happens past.  Overall ok, but don't expect to be blown away.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

Am not much of an active person who trek but managed to finish the hike.  Pretty easy to find alternative transport instead of cab.   I took a cab to Jeju bus terminal and ask for the bus to seongpanak hallasan.  There are announcements and signboard to alert one for each stop and hence I manage to align at the seongpanak stop with no difficulty.  The trek was okay for the first leg (pre-rest stop) and got more challenging at the final leg.  Not knowing much, realised that most of the hikers have their hiking stick while I was on my own - then again I survive the hike abit limping for the long long hike :). In all, I enjoy the hike with not regrets

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.

Although we went in the evening when some stalls are closed the place is quite vibrant nonetheless. If you hire a taxi for the day ask the driver to drop you off here. We kind of regretted we didn't as the taxi we hired went overtime and we were a bit tired. We took a bus at 1200 won from Jeju City (500) and it was a long and crowded trip as it had to pass through the airport first. Definitely worth a visit. Nothing much to buy other then tangerines (sold in bags of about 12 to 13) and jeju orange chocolates which you can find in Seoul. You can see the live seafood such as abalone, octopus, fishes etc. Also enjoy food such as gimbap, oden, tteoboki, fried stuff, blood sausages etc. There is also a stall selling orange jam filled cookie in the shape of the stone grandfather. Tastes good when eaten warm.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Actually like the other ones, I felt quite surprise at the my first visits since last year 2011. The guide showed me that I were in the bottom of the slope, she pointed to the tree lines along  the side of the road and truly, it has made me believe what she said. A few seconds later, the driver shut the engine and release the bus's brakes, the 45 seated bus was beginning move slowly then faster and faster.  Could you believe ? The huge bus was moving up to the top of the slope without working engine! A man of my group - an 50 ages supposed there were the natural magnetic power that dragged up the 2,5 tons iron bus to about 5-8 meter height during approximately 80 metes !!!It was happened about 10 mins then all of our group's participant disembarked the bus, they were starting to talk about what they saw during the past 10 minutes. Some one said it caused by a natural magnetic power (as above), other one assumed by the trick of the sun's lighting a man nearly lying face down to the road parallel to look forward to the starting point... others wisely poured the water to see the flows .... Of course, our guide has explained the cause but I really do not want to tell you, let's explore by yourself.Definitely, this places is quite appropriated for your family with kids. Aside the road, there are the Korean traditional food shops who sells fried fish ball, rice cake... but they are almost fried into the oil ...This places are really attracted a lot of people from Asia like Chinese, Vietnamese, Indian... I think you might found the similar road like the Jeju Mysterious Road of your own country but the Korean was wise to promote it via the drama film series currently expanding over the Asia.Totally, Jeju is an beautiful island and you should visit one time. With me, I could said   you could make the money by the very simple things

A nice beach with fine sand and lots of facilities such as parasols for hire, cocktails and food stalls. There are showers and toilets close by too. On the downside, it's incredibly busy and parking is a nightmare. Once all the parasols and tables are out there's very little sand left! The amount of space available for swimming is small. We preferred to go to the less popular beach along the road. It's more spacious and more relaxed.

A great place to enjoy beautiful scenery, fresh air, the sun and the beaches. The island tour bus service is very convenient (only need to pay once) and runs on round trips whole day long, bringing you to 4 different scenic spots if you do not want to rent the bicycles, ATV or scooters. There is also a nice restaurant named Rodem Garden which offers spicy squids on hot plate and can add on with hallabong fried rice after you almost finish the squids.

You're given a map at the beginning but it's much more fun to try and find your way without it! We got there pretty early so it wasn't very crowded. It didn't take us very long to walk through it but it was definitely worth the stop.

We stopped by this museum at the end of a long day because my daughter  who loves science  was begging us to go. We were all pleasantly surprised. There were quite a few hands on displays like static balls  using bikes to light up a display  a few trick eye displays  plasma globes  and of course Tesla coils. The staff were incredibly friendly and although they didn't speak much English they went out of their way to show us around. The Tesla coil music show was quite cool - the coils were used to create different pitches and played both classical and modern music. It took about an hour to go through everything and cost ??0000 for 2 adults and 2 kids. My kids loved it! Great hands on science.

We paid our entrance fees and simply stayed on the top to get some good pictures. There were hordes of people down below so I don't recommend taking a long walk down and then back up just to get some pictures of other tourists.

We had no intention of going to the top as it is a long day long activity . However how could we have missed seeing the HallaSan from up close. So we asked our driver to take us as far as he could . There is a driving spot till 1.1km where the driver took us . But it was nothing much than a regular hilly drive .So my personal reco if not going up there you can also avoid going to the 1100m point . See the Hallasan from far away. It's beautiful .

We drove along mountainous route 1139 from SEOQWIPO to this place before heading to the airport.  We drove very slowly from the start to finish point and didn't feel the illusion effect.  Some said to see the effect one needs to roll a bottle on the road. I dunno.. i just drove on without stopping. I would however recommend those who drive to drive along route 1139 skirting the mountain and reaching the 1000m height.

We decide to go up the mountain on foot. It was a long way but worth it. The scene from the this mountain top is unforgetable and undeniably great. We could have stayed here all day seeing the nature changed if the weather weren?t cold. Walking the way up was exhausting but the fresh air and the sights we saw at different heights really cooled us down.

This place is quite far from the main city so we hired a driver to take us there because you need to start early to be able to make it in time for sunrise.  When we got there it was still really dark since it was barely 5.  We started hiking up and there were few people along the way but once you got up to the top there's already a bunch of people sitting around waiting for the sunrise.

This market is a must visit if u are in Jeju. It sells almost everything u nerd to eat along with some souvenirs and cheap clothes. We went in December and it was coincidentally the island's very famous tangerine season where we bought a big box of Jeju's Hallabong tangerines as well Jeju's chocolate / tangerine / strawberry / cactus coated rice snacks. Definetly an important pit stop in your Jeju itinerary.

this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

There is a long steep path in order to reach the lighthouse on top. But that shouldn't be a problem as the scenery along the road is empowering your feet to work. In the middle of the path  there is a candy house like building. But unfortunately  it was reconstructing at that moment. So  I bought a chocolate ice cream beside the reconstruction to settle my unhappiness. The ice cream tastes unexpectedly good  it is rich in chocolate and smooth when I put it into my mouth. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the lighthouse  we took several pictures there  but no one is perfectly taken because of strong wind  our hair flowing like crazy  so we didn't spend much time on the lighthouse.We took about 30 minutes there and didn't have a chance to visit the building at that time  so I strongly recommend you to go there at autumn or spring and plan more than half an hour if you are deciding to visit there.

The top of Sunrise Mountain was obscured by clouds when we were there.      We climbed up.    It?s somewhat steep but there are benches for stopping along the way along with one restroom area about 1/3 of the way up.    Signage also in English.   It was extremely windy up at the top and we were in the clouds.   We had some visibility downward but very little outward.

The scenery is absolutely stunning at the top. We brought our 4-years old kid along and we were initially worried if the hike is too tiring for him. We were so wrong! He loves the hike and has lots of fun along the way. Just make sure that you have sufficient time to finish the hike before it closes. Would strongly recommend this place for families even with young children!

The aqua show was really the only thing we really enjoyed but it was too long and very crowd. This place is definitely on top list but very overpriced when it comes to entrance fee. Our family two adults paid entrance so if you have several children over the age of 3 it will cost lots of money and honestly not worth it. It was at the time we visited very crowded and long queues. We had for example wait 30 min in line to order food. It was raining heavily that day so maybe that caused it but to sum up nice visit but not worth it

review: Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.
Nothing spectacular but wouldn't mind a stop by as its along the way to nearby restaurants. Should try the hot rice cake and fish cake though.
Nice to stop over for lunch and have a walk along the river and at the beach but not suggest going there on purpose unless you want a ride on the raft

Love this natural rock formations along the coastal beach walk ... definitely not your usual sandy beach ... lots of opportunities for great photosThere are ladies selling fresh seafood catches along the way ... we didn't have time to stop for that though ...

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html
It's shorter distance in real than I thought. But definately an interesting place to stop by! I both walked and drived along the road!

It was low tide so the rocks were dry and there were lots of little pools.  It was fun to see little kids playing in the pool water for hours.  We were just there for a little time. Our teenagers had fun walking on top of the lava rocks along the beach.  Careful not to step on crabs. Beautiful serene beach.

In my opinion I?셶e been to probably a dozen saunas/jimjilbangs in Korea so I think I have a decent base to compare this place up against. It doesn?셳 deserve to be a special tourist destination. Having arrived in Jeju eager to see as much as possible in a short time frame - the art work was top on my hit list. I stumbled across the website for the Museum of Contemporary Art and was very excited to go (as there are so many museums to choose from!)I would recommend a whole morning to visit Jeoji as there is more than just this Museum there. The first Gallery I went to showed a lovely exhibiton on the Sound of Nature this gallery was on the left hand side of the road and was a free two floor exhibition. I then walked along the road to the Museum of Contemporary Art on the right. The Museum had 4 big rooms of Art - all of which had a meaningful message behind the artist's work in both Korean and English! The receptionists were very helpful when directing me as to where to go and I finished my self-guided tour with a visit to the Art shop which was outside in the sculpture garden. A lovely morning well spent taking in the delights of Korean art.
dont be afraid of the distance to the top. just go ahead. it doesnt take too long. i think it was around half hour for people to
A stretch of public road that gives you an illusion of travelling against gravity. You may stop along the road as many others would.
A nice venue to visit along your way - didn't see the divers but a pleasant stop off along the way as part of an overall tour.
A must do when visiting Jeju Island!  After the long trek to the top the scenery was worth every step it took to get there.

A mountain with beautiful scenery. I did not manage to climb all the way up to the top as I was having knee problem but my friend did. It was really beautiful even when I was only half way up the mountain. I also enjoyed the nice cooling breeze that made me want to stay longer if possible. Worth the visit. Probably will visit this mountain and climb up again next time.

A great place for new travellers who want to explore or have an interest in Korea's traditional culture. This place is huge and there are many things for you to explore. It was raining heavily when I was there but it did not stop other people there to explore this place. There are some rest stops along the way to take shelter in case it rains. Ticket price for adult is 10000won.

A beautiful beach with turquoise water on the north east coast of Jeju island.  Lots of cafes overlooking the beach.  popular in summer.  The coastal road along this northwest portion of jeju is spectacular with many beautiful coves and places to stop.  there are also a lot of windmills along the coast as well as the Korean Energy Research Institute

Yep, there are a lot of stairs here. It honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting it to be, seeing as how stairs are my natural enemy. You will probably be tired when you get to the top, but little kids and elderly people are doing it, so it's not crazy. It's over a lot faster than it feels like it's going to be as you're ascending. We were there in the late afternoon, and it was a little crowded, but not too much trouble. Most people move along at a pretty good pace and don't stand in the way too much when taking pictures. It's a bit more difficult to get good pictures at the top though, because everyone stops up there to rest and take tons of photos. It's worth the climb and you'll get some good pictures out of it if the weather permits. Even if you think you are unable to go up to the top, it's worth coming out here just for the landscape.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

We were attracted by the promise from the literature that this was the only waterfall in Asia with 'debouches' into the ocean. Hmmm, you almost get the impression from above that some channel engineering has helped this along. Anyway, Wikipedia tells me that this claim is not quite correct. Anyway, we arrived as then had to purchase entry tickets. The stressed out man next to the ticket gate then seemed to think that we have not purchased the correct amount of tickets. We had. It was all the more puzzling because he was only 2 feet from where we bought the tickets. Maybe he was so bored he was asleep at the wheel. Or maybe it was because we were foreigners. Anyway, once that nonsense was resolved we headed down the steps, only to be stopped half-way down at yer another ticket check! Ridiculous, three check for a 1000-or-so won entry ticket. We thought we must be in for something very special. Alas not. Said waterfall falls a few score metres, generates a modest amount of spray and attracts thousands of people taking selfies of themselves and said insipid attraction. There are some older folk selling ghastly looking octopus slices by the rocks - poor animals (the octopus that is). We were not stopped for more ticket checks on the way out, thankfully. I suggest you just look at the photo on the web and go and do something more interesting instead.

We visited this site with a group of friends.Everybody had their own take on the mysterious road and all had their theories. A quick visit to the internet would provide the answer. However, this all detracts from the pure fun of the site itself. However, part of the fun is discussing the   mystery   of the road.The site is a simple narrow two-lane road. It is not huge. There is plenty of parking for visitors to stop and examine the surroundings.  There are snack stalls along the road where refreshments and some simple snacks can be bought. I noticed some posts on TA that say this is a   tourist trap  . I do not see how this would be the case as nobody is forced to buy or pay for anything.  Anything we bought was food, which, to me, does not seem to be predatory on tourists. In fact, I was hungry and thirsty and was happy to purchase some cooked local yams and cool refreshment. There are tourist traps on the island, but this is not one of them.Having said the above, the attraction is not a major development and is not meant to be a huge event to take up one's itinerary. It is a fun and simple site to visit which can be added to the list of places to visit when in Jeju.

We visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on two separate days - the first was in the afternoon to see the women free-divers' performance (1pm/3pm) and the second was in the wee hours of the morning (5+am) to see the sunrise. The free-divers were all middle-aged women who looked old enough to be our mothers. Despite their age, it was amazing how they managed to hold their breath so long underwater to harvest the seafood which you could buy from them and eat on the spot (they'll prepare/cook it in whichever way you want). The way they sang prior to the dive and the way they chatted and swam out to sea together reminded us of the friendly grannies in our neighborhood enjoying a nice chit-chat over tea. To see the sunrise at the peak, we started our climb at 4+am (it helps to stay in a hotel within walking distance to Ilchulbong). It was pitch-dark and torchlight was a must. The climb was shorter than expected and we reached the top before 5am. Thankfully the sky was clear that morning and we managed to catch a beautiful sunrise (around 5:30am) that was nothing short of amazing.

We thoroughly enjoyed our day on Udo. We hired manual bikes and stopped at the little beached and cafes along the way. It was cold and really windy so I think it was quite quiet in terms of people compared to a normal day which is why I think we enjoyed it so much. The bigger beaches (especially the black sand beach at the end) are a terrible example of sympathetic tourism and are blights against the beautiful natural landscape. Blaring music, ugly buildings and structures detract from the stunning island itself. We chose to eat at a cute little cafe which had character and that was away from the others.

We have no idea that such place exist until we drove along the Hallasan range from North to the southern part of the island. Spotted the beauty along the road, we saw a parking space opposite the 1100 Altitude Wetland, decided to stop and take a look. There is a 1-km boardwalk which we stroll along the peaceful woods and admire the trees, stones, frozen stream, mountain range. As it is winter, we could not spot any birds, or wildlife.However, we are pleased with a little surprise that we have added a new destination of the day to our itinerary.

We did a back to back sunset/sunrise hike. Sunset was great because it wasn't hot and it was really nice and breezy up there after 20 minutes of stomping up stairs. You get to see the sunset on one side of the peak while you see the moon rise over the crater at the top. Pretty awesome. There is a water/coffee stand about halfway up in case you forget water, but the it wasn't open when we hiked it in the morning (big fail). We camped on the beach nearby, not the greatest...Garbage EVERYWHERE! Not just your typical beach garbage (cups, bags, broken plastic boxes) but long fluorescent light bulbs, peices of boats, clothing... The water had lots of debris in it and despite the sweltering heat, we just couldn't get ourselves to wade past the trash into the deeper areas so we left for Udo Island instead. It was also pretty tricky finding a good spot to post our tent. The tide comes up REALLY high there and the garbageless, flat tide-safe spots are pretty much non existant. Pretty uncomfortable night/morning, but at least we didn't have to get up until 5am to hike the peak. There are washrooms in the village which is about 10 min from the beach, but bring a flashnight cause the lights and water turns off at night.
We climbed a lot of slopes and steps to reach the top and we found nothing as the volcano is dead since long time it does not deserve the money ,effort nor the money

We came just after the rain stopped. Love the layout of the whole place. Instantly brings you back to the past there are real people - Craftsmen Painter Potter man on the respective   villages   with living animals - chicken black pigs goats horses. It is a nice experience. There are old   games   for you to try on. Saw traditional drummers along the way. You can have greater understanding on how the past Koreans houses based on their occupations - fisherman farmer locksmith painter. There are school police station & court house too. Few of the famous Korean dramas been shot here namely Jewel In The Palace.  A worker told us if we came on a non rainy day there will be more activities. Entrance fee is on higher side - 8000 Won/ Person but it is worth a visit.

Udo island offers push bike and motorised bike hire for a small fee at both of the docking locations. You can also drive your car onto the ferry and just drive. I used the push bike so I could enjoy the feel of the coast roads without rushing past but you'll still see everything (without the muscle pain) with the other options. There are several little eatery places scattered along the road that offer very fresh and yummy food. I spent about 3-4 hours riding around the coastal road stopping for freshly squeezed juice, lunch, the local peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine. If your looking for adventure this isn't for you but if a quiet relaxing back to nature is what your looking for be sure to stop by.

This was one of our stops in our taxi tour for that day.This is a small place showing the traditional homes of that area a long time ago.  It?s free. An English speaking guide will tour you around.  Some interesting facts, like two separate doors (one bigger for the male I think.) They will offer you a drink made of honey and some fermentation of some berries.  It?s like juice but with some tart aftertaste.  Taste good though that we spent I think $40.00 for a bottle.  In hindsight, maybe a bit too much considering it?s not an alcoholic drink (tongue in cheek).  But while drinking that juice at home, it sure brings in mind our visit to Jeju.  While there we saw a black pig with a small companion rat.  Well seems the rat was hovering near the pig pen.  Interesting place and the guide did tell some interesting stories and tidbits! (Can be done in half an hour).

This mistery road is about half kilometer long. Stop you?re vehicle at the start of this road, put the gear in neutral, and turn off the engine. Your car slowly climbs up a pretty steep slope. At least what it looks like upward slope. It is really hard to believe that the upward slope is an optical illusion and it in reality slopes down. I have seen magnetic hill in Moncton, Canada and they have a road like this. But there is just below a mountain slope and the optical illusion is very understandable there but here there is no such thing, just a plain stretch of road. I really could not figure out how your eyes are deceiving your brain. Not a big deal,but worth experiencing it if you are in Jeju.

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This is just another roadside attraction that many people visiting Jeju stop by to see only because it is in the city proper. It is just a rock that could appear to look like any number of different animals.If your tour guide takes you out of your way to see this then you need a new tour guide because this rock is typical of any of the millions of rocks you run into along the seashore in Jeju.There are a lot of interesting things to see and fun places to go in Jeju but, this isn't one of them.

This is a very long beach along the south Jeju coast near the south-western end.  You can bike (there's trial, do segway, or a long walk) or drive and stop along places to take beautiful photos. At the end of the beach is Songacsan where you can hike for an hour or so - very easy.

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

This could be an amazing place to visit provided you have good weather and great friends. Scootering around the tiny island can be fun if you stop off at the beaches, swim along the way and explore the caves and tunnels by the black sand beach. Definitely keep an eye out for the giant burger restaurant and the peanut Makgeolli stand (留嫄몃━, it's alcoholic rice wine!), both are delicious! Don't over-hype it or expect too much, just go to have fun and you'll be happy you went.

There is a small fee to enter the area, I think around 2-3000W. Once you are inside the park, you can hang out on the paths, admiring the rolling green fields, or head up some few hundred stairs to the top of the little mountain and look at the crater. The little mountain was formed by a volcanic eruption a long time ago and around the rim of the crater there are 99 'peaks' which they call the crown. That's cool. I think that's cool.After you have taken an inappropriate amount of selfies you can head back down to a small beach area and watch traditional women divers...diving. There is also a small black stoned beach by the women divers which you can walk along and admire the beautiful black stone of the small mountain, which is Seongsan Ilchulbong.We travelled there by public transport and it wasn't difficult at all.

There are many waterfalls in Jeju, we decided to have a look at Cheonjiyeon. There is a large parking lot, eateries and a couple of souvenir shops, 7eleven etc when you arrive. To walk to the waterfall is about 10-15 min along a small tree lined river. Many tourists and tourists groups are visiting the waterfall so it will be quite crowded. The waterfall as such is nice, but not too tall or spectacular. everybody takes a few selfies and then heads back to the parking lot pretty much. If nearby it makes to stop by and visit but it is not worth a long journey just to see this waterfall.

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.

The queue was long starting from midnight. The tag was given starting 2:30am. The limit was for 1300 first come first served. The waiting was in 2 celcius temperature. The trek up started at 5:30am in an orderly manner in a hushed procession like atmosphere. At the top of the plateau there were decks facing the direction of the sunrise. All was ready for the first sunrise of 2020. Unfortunately it did not happen. The clouds was too thick and we headed back an hour after the sunrise time. Was I disappointed? Not really. The whole experience was exhilarating, the wait, the trek, the anticipation of the sunrise. It was a memorable experience which I hope to repeat one day.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time??? The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

spent a long day in Udo - so idyllic and relaxing.  There are endless seaside beaches, cliffs, cafes, ...  Just drive your own car there (via car ferry - costed us 32k Won) for a small car and 2 pax, or rent one of the bikes, motor tricycles (very cute), and just drive and stop anywhere (almost) you like and take photos, drink coffee, or just doing nothing and daydreaming. Excellent scenery, food- freshest seafood, burgers, ..... How nice to spend a day.

So happy we took the time to make the climb.  It's a lot of stairs to the top, so I would suggest you take along some water, and possibly some snacks, so you can take a rest part way up.There is one way up, and another down, which keeps things moving quickly.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. Toilets are unfortunately not clean, so you may want to bring some disinfectant lotion and/or toilet paper.The first part of the hike is easily accessible, the latter part less so. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Along the Mysterious Road, have a few food stall, try out the grilled black pork sausage and many delicious food. For those driving, key in the number 7126988 (yup.. heading to Loveland, you will reach Mysterious Road first), most people stop by here on the way to airport.
It's about 1.3km from the bottom to the top. Along the way to the top, u can really enjoy the fresh air and the woods. From the top, u can see hills and jeju town.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It was our 2nd time visit Udo,absolutely loved it.Few tips for anyone who plan to visit Jeju:* Bring your ID with you! We went to Udo in July and we were asked to present ID at ticket office, Seongsanri Port. Saw lots tourists queuing at ticket office and pretty much everyone was holding passport!! We didn't have passport with us, but luck enough I had my driving licence in my purse. My boyfriend didn't have any ID with him, and we bought 2 ferry tickets with showing 1 ID only.  * it's an absolutely beautiful place. Tried peanut ice cream which was very refreshing. * scooter or bike? My opinion is get bike!! It costs 10000 won to get 1 bike and you can ride as long as you want, no time limit what so ever, it costs 25000 won to get a scooter, and you need to be back within 2 hours. It was kinda electric bike, so presuming the power only lasts 2 hours. If you plan spend move than 4 hours on this lovely island, bike is the option, not hard to ride around and you can stop at any cafe for a ice cream or drink and chill out at the beach for 1 hour. That's what we did :) rather than just sitting on the scooter and kept checking time consistently to make sure to get back  within 2 hours.

It took everything in me to make this climb.  But at the end of the day, my legs wobbling, I could say,   I hiked Korea's tallest mountain  Make sure to bring your food as the only thing available for sail will be ramen noodle, a favorite among Koreans.One tip, push through till you get to the area set up for sitting and eating.  Doing this instead of many stops along the way will definitely save you some time.

It takes 10 min tops to actually enjoy the rock.  Its unique and pretty but that's all folks!  You have to pay for parking (500 won every 30 min) and believe me, it doesn't even take that long to see all there is to see.  We had extra time before rental car needed to be returned so we stopped.  But I wouldn't have otherwise gone out of my way to see this rock formation.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

If you have time along the way and want to stop for some black fur pig, you can learn about the history about the pigs from this village. It was great to learn and appreciate the culture first before we ate at a local black fur pork place nearby. Plus you get to taste some tasty tea where you can apparently taste all 5 different flavors, and horse placenta which makes a funny story to tell that it tastes like almonds.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If there is nothing else you do go see this temple. It is a sprawling complex that goes all up to the base of the mountain. Along the way if you do hike all the way up to the top, there are signs to explain the legends behind the names of the places you walk and why there is a temple there. But even if you don't it is still an sight to see

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

Hotel was right across this market so I stopped here on my first night for dinner. I was amazed by the selection of street food stalls, fresh produce and desserts. Most of the signs were in Korean but just follow the crowd and where there's a long line you'll never go wrong! I got a taste of the rice with fried black pork plus some fried octopus in batter, which were both great. Bought some boxes of cheap chocolate as well. Areas of the market selling fresh fish and vegetables are wet though so beware when walking through.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Great day out doors. Many options of travel within the island (drive from mainland, rent bicycles, various motorized vehicles) making it really easy.Roads are narrow so personally would avoid driving. Further the ferries can only hold that many cars which means expect long wait times during peak periods.Many nice small eateries for coffee or ice cream along the way. Beaches are really pretty too and water clear though I didn't see anyone swimming in dec (winter).Only thing that I didn't quite like was the rentals were pricey at 70000 won for 3 hrs (two motorized bicycles and one two seater). And that was after some bargaining . The guy mentioned that it takes 45 min to go around the island without stops

Form by lava stalagmites and a long lava tube tunnels. It was cooling inside the tunnel . Stone pillars and stalactites are widely spread and the tunnels shows off the cave?s topographical features.   Stone Turtle   is especially eye-catching.

Did a solo hike in the hot summer of July, and wasn't disappointed.It was a long, easy hike up with some steep steps near the end of the hike. 10KM up and down, in total 20KMThere are some stops along the way, especially the 'base camp' where you can purchase ramen to eat.There are no railings or ropes to hold on to a few metres close to the peak, so this would be harder to do on a winter's day.Was kinda sad that the peak was shrouded by a large cloud, but nonetheless satisfied with the easy hike.Public transport starts as early as 6AM, so if you drive and want to end early, it would be better.

Completely worth the early morning waking up to see the sunrise. It looks completely difference bathed in the early morning light than after the sun has arisen, so check when the sun rises and wake up early!Is it easy to climb up? My wife doesn't work out, and we took about 40 minutes to walk up the stairs, with occasional stops along the way. I do work out, and even I had to pause a little here and there - bring some water, you'll be glad you did. Otherwise, it's not really difficult, just takes a bit of stamina.

By the time we visit Ecoland, it's already 4pm so  time limited as it closes at 5 pm!We took a long train that stop at every 4 places of visiting.In the first stop, we went through attraction on beautiful scenery and artistic work and went to another second stops to wait for the train. Then the train took us to third stops and another attraction artwork of beautiful small houses and Christmas artwork and many others.  Then we went to last stop that is garden which grows lavender,green tea and many types of flowers. It's a beautiful garden on the whole. On whole, I'll come to again another time again on next visit!

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.
all the ways up the top is basically stairs ,the design has quite a lot of resting places along the way ,if you are fast,half an hr can reach the top

2 days in Jeju, this was probably the highlight of our trip. We didn't for the sunrise/sunset, but came in the middle of the day.  The place was packed with tourist, but it didn't take away from the beauty of the place.  The is a fairly long climb of a series of stairs to get to the top.  But totally worth it.  On our way down, we were able to catch the women divers head out, which was a nice treat.

With a minimal fee of KRW10k one gets to kayak along the stream for 20 mins. The water is clear and deep. Each wooden kayak can only take 2 passenger with only one person rowing. The catch is the ticket counter is a distance away from the port. And the best time to go is on a weekdays. Weekends are usually crowded.

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)
Well made wooden stairs lead you all the way along with the cliff line. Octagon shaped stones are amazing over the clean blue ocean. You?ll be taking tens of pictures over there!!

We manage to visit this Mysterious Road while on our way going to Hallasan but we are unable to try the road on our own. The road is really mysterious but the length of the road is not that long. We just try the road by using a mineral bootleg water and it is really awesome. You can try Visit it if you are curious about the road.

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.

Visited on a rainy day.  Limited parking - so had to park along the road and take a muddy path through the team garden.  Tea shop was very crowded to went to the Innisfree jeju House about 60 m away - great food and can make your own soap.

Today is the last day in Jeju but since the plane is evening time so we went to Jeju folk village museum.It's worth visiting there! Every one of us really enjoyed ourselves going to learn their traditional style and ways of living! Furthermore the place is very beautifully designedmaking us just want to know what that's waiting ahead of us as we go along!I'll visit this place again if ever to go to Jeju again!

This was seriously one of the coolest things I've ever seen. The waves crashing against the rocks was incredible. I went on a rainy day and that didn't take away from how amazing it was. Since it was rainy it wasn't that crowded. I stayed longer than many people though. I just couldn't believe it. Stay longer if you want. Definitely try to see this in Jeju.

This was really a nice long walk. Will advise to wear good walking shoe. The route was easy to walk just that when the wind come you can feel the wind blowing at you. You have to walk all the way up and you will be able to see the nice surrounding. It was really nice and we really enjoyed it.

this place offers audio guided tour which we loaned kind of gotten lost along the way and didnt really follow the sequence. there are many interesting places to see but more of less are quite similar with regard to the houses and all the area is big and spaced out. it will be great if there are a little more resting areas/bench along the road for visitors to rest along the way. better wayfinding would be good as well.

This place is ok if you have some spare time and want a peaceful walk.As long as you don't meet any tours because they can me noisy.Its nothing special just trees and very little else.Not worth it if you have to come out of your way.

This place is considered clean for a local market. Mixture of raw fresh food and cooked food stores. We came here at around 10am and a number of cooked food stores are already open. Nice experience walking around and eating street food along the way. There are benches around for you to sit and have your food. Market closes at 8.30pm.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!

The performance itself is worth the price of admission. Make sure you arrive before one of the three showtimes during the day. They provide drums and you can jam along with the performers. I find this satisfying when you have so many museums in area feigning novelty. So again  If you can get your toddlers away from the stuffed animals  then there is a rewarding human element waiting on the bottom floor.

The outlook has been dressed up and over designed. It looks like a candy house rather than a church. It is quite disappointed especially when you have been walking from a long way out there in order to move closer to it but it does not give you any romantic feeling at all.
The Manjanggul Cave was a nice outing for my family and I. Very dark and wet and long but was interesting to read the facts along the way. Would definitely visit again.
The cave is very cool and seems to go on forever.  There are informative photos with descriptions along the way so you know what it is you are looking at.
Take your time to read the information plaques along the way to fully appreciate the geological aspects of this unique place.

Superb scenery especially on the way up the peak.Great place to take photos of the island.The climb up is no kidding for older people as steps are very narrow and steep. Luckily there are places for you to rest along the way up.

Spent a few hours at the museum along with many many others! Small building with some good information but crowds crammed the shop which leads into the cafe. This caused overcrowding and did not make for the most enjoyable afternoon. Outdoors area is worth wandering through and the gardens and fields are worth looking at. The Innisfree Jeju House across the way is probably more interesting.
Romantic place to strolling with beautiful grass/weed around along the way to the crater. Took lots of nice foto :) Heard every season the grass have different colours. Entrance Fee : KRW2000
rock formation. nothing particularly special about it. visit if along the way or have time to do so.
Really nice calming atmosphere and was not crowded with too many tourists. Beautiful estuary connecting to the ocean. Nice walkway with not too many steps running alongside the estuary.

Put your vehicle on neutral and it will seemingly be rolling uphill. Very intriguing.Unable to figure out how it happened but definitely have something to do with the way the trees were planted along the road.

Pro: nice place as you will get free explanation of jeju. We were able to get first hand information about the traits of jeju woman and good history background of jeju.Cons: you will be exposed to v. long sales talk of made in jeju products. quite expensive and I was sitting through the talk half way i decided to leave.
Perfect place for renting a bike and it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to paddle around the island. Coffee shops and attranctions along the way.
one of the smaller waterfalls of he two but very well kept. shades of water can be seen along with a wishing well and a few picture spots on the bridge and walk way

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)

My 10 yo daughter and I have really enjoyed seeing the waterfall. It was a quick 20 minute walk up a scenic paved path with some other small falls. It was definitely worth a visit. Cost couple won to get in. There are several shops right outside and along the way to buy souvenirs and snacks.

Many Korean villages are reproduced so as you walk you glimpse at the way of life from long ago.  Korean dramas are filmed here and we were able to watch filming.  You can try your hand at games arts and crafts as you wander through the various areas and there  is a free train for those who prefer to ride. The blooming flowers and trees made for beautiful pictures.  This was one of our favorite places we visited while in JeJu it should be on your list of places to go!

Manjang Cave is made of lava formation or lava tube as it is called. We walked about 1-2 km stretch of it only as not the whole tube was opened for tourist visitation.It is cold and dark. it is one of the longest lava tube in the world but it just is not my cup of tea. No  remorse on going into it but just was not awe blown away with it either. Go if you are a nature lover. skip if you are looking for awesome scenery to capture picture moments

Magpie Brewery is one of the handful of craft breweries in Jeju with a great selection of seasonal and year round selections.  The pina colada ale was a tasty seasonal brew along with their classic kolsch beer.  The brewery is a bit out of the way but the outdoor picnic benches are a great spot to chill when the weather is nice.  Tours are also offered at 20000 won.

Little walk down pathway along the cliff on the seaside.Something to see while in the area.May be difficult for elderly or those with weak walking abilities as walk to the waterfall from parking lot consist of lots of stairs and wet floors.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

Lava tunnels stem from liquid hot Lava that makes its way under the ground and leaves empty tunnels when the Lava stream comes to an end. This tunnel is very long but is lacking something of a mysterious atmosphere which we had seen before at other Lava tunnels.

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

review: It was very crowded at O'Sulloc and a tad chaotic. As there were no seats and the queue for their desserts was very long we went to Innisfree which was a 2-minute walk away. It's a beautiful place. Parking was easy. If the main parking area is full there is a big open space across the road to park at. There were persons helping to redirect cars so it was not stressful at all.

Irion (magma) carved the small valley. This is the place where the magma carved the valley long long ago. The small valley meet the sea here. You can enjoy transparent canoe and see under water(not always).  Scenery is exotic.  It is also good for you to walk along here.

If you go for brands (local and international) this short street is probably the place to go to on this part of the island. The street is closed to traffic so you could spend a while walking in comfort. The street is on the way to dongmun market and the underground shopping centre. Along the way it also branches off into some kind of roofed shopping arcade which we did not visit.

If you go for brands (international or local) this short street is probably the place to visit on this side of the island. It leads to the dongmun market and the underground shopping centre. Along the way this branches off into a covered shopping arcade which we did not visit.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

I was told this lava tube is about 9 km long but only 1 km is accessible right now. It's really huge but kinda dark so you can't really appreciate the tube except in some parts where a spotlight is placed - I guess that's where the authenticity lies. Anyways wear comfortable shoes and be careful since it gets wet and slippery.
