I thought I would see and actual museum. But instead just a hallway with international data on tea leading to their restaurant. Where the line was way too long to try their green tea delicacies. By the time it was my turn around 4 pm they were sold out of a lot of things. I also purchased some tea. Some people where very helpful if they couldn't help they would find someone who spoke English to help. Others would rather deal with the foot traffic that they would give up and ignore me. There are green tea samples if you get to the people passing them out in time. People are always huddled there waiting for the samples I couldn't get any.

I loved this cave! 2 km in and out. It was a very educational trip as you'll get explanations about what you see along the way. It's dark and wet and there's water dripping from the ceiling so bring a cap and good boots to avoid slipping. Don't wear a long skirt as it will get wet. A bit hard to take pictures though because of the lighting :/ But the ending and the way it was presented with the lighted walkway at the end was great!

I love this place and how I wish that there were a film shooting there....poor me?. It was a long way to go there but as always it was worth it. If you like Korean Historical Drama Films that this place is must to visit.

I love open-water swimming and just plain jumping off rocks. This spot is ideal for both and is also a good way of interacting with locals. you don't even need to speak Korean to get along with folks here!

I had never seen dried lava before (other than when hiking hallasan which was only the day before) so I thought this was super cool. There are tons of informative signs along the way too. Oh and it's cool inside--not humid!

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

Has serene garden  $3 entrance fee. They preserved the deceased artists study which was interesting. The photos had a rare spiritual feel to them. Out of the way  took almost an hour to get there from our hotel in seoguipo  be careful not to speed above posted speed limit - there were about 20 traffic cameras along the way and even saw two impromptu mobile speed camera setups.

Good chance to explore natureof lava tube..I shall recommend for walk alley to be build along the way inside the tube..its to hard to walk on the slippery rocks.Hence to put more highlight inside the tube..its too dark inside

Down steep stairs and into the lava tubes.You can go in a long way or a little way.I enjoyed this unusual experience.I did not like the fact that it was wet and surface uneven so difficult even with good walking shoes.

Do visit this place along your way to or after manjanggul. Great fun for family. We managed to reah the bell in  <30mins. Also great for cat lovers cos there are really many of them here n soooo adorable n friendly. 1km frm manjanggul stn
Didn't expect the lava cave to be that long. But it was an interesting experience. Wear waterproof non-slip shoes as the floor is always wet.

Across the street from the museum is a green tea patch where people can take touristy pictures and just walk around. The day I was there it was way too hot to even attempt to take photos. Inside the building isn't really a museum but a tea shop that has a lot of variations of teas. There's also a little cafe that serves hot and cold tea drinks along with simple snacks to have with you tea. Out back there is a walkway for people so that they can see the open landscape. There is also a Innisfree Jeju Island shop that has make-up and it was interesting to see some of the main ingredients in their skincare line out on display. The Innisfree shop also had it's own separate cafe with beverages and food.

A nice tea museum good to learn some history about tea plantation on Jeju. But the tea sold there and the food serve is slightly over priced. The tea plantation however is nothing spectacular it?셲 only unique during spring and summer is where you get to see wild flowers blooming along the the way.

A long way to reach the other end. The road was slippery and uneven. The place was dark and the only light source was tiny statues with lamps along the cave. The temperature inside was 11-18째C and well maintained throughout the year. If you are interested in geology you should probably check in here but it was quite mesmerizing for non geologist as well

A good long hike up but really worth it. The vista is stunning.We had bought 6 very nice Hillabong oranges just next to the restroom in a little shed (really worth it) and found out that we needed to leave the rest of them and all our other food at the counter where they check the tickets. What we didn't know is that the counter closes at exactly 6pm. When we heard the announcement we were only half way down... one person in our group decided to run the rest of the way and then managed to negotiate (in Korean) with the guardian to get the oranges and food back...

A beautiful scenic walk along the coast and the path was well taken care of. We walked to the right first and walked most of the path up until it started to inclined towards the end and then turned around and walked down the left path all the way to the parking lot. Definitely recommend walking both paths since you see different rock formations and the walk is not too difficult or long.

A  unique cave with 70 cm lava stalagmites and lava tube tunnel . Lighted with dim lights. Floor rocky and slippery but manageable  with comfortable shoes . A kilometer long but takes about 20-25 minutes one way . The Lava  formed at the end is a beautiful one worth seeing.

While this is  just of the roadway, it?s fairly free of visitors.   The path goes alongside running water (or not - depending on rainfall).    There was about a 30m section where the path ended and we had to walk from rock to rock before the path restarted.    On the other side was a cave - Rock Shade Residence - which olden people used as shelter.   Entire area is a beautiful evergreen valley, well worth a visit.

While the hike was long it was definitely worth it. It wasn't too difficult, it was beautiful the whole way, and knowing I reached South Korea's highest peak felt like an achievement.It never felt too steep and even in the middle of summer the brutal heat didn't diminish the experience much. The only complaint I have is that parts of the path are covered with large, randomly distributed volcanic rocks that are a pain especially during the decent and my feat were pretty sore for quite a while afterwards.

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) ! After you flood yrselves silly with pics, you can try the maze. Its interesting walking in and out and along the way you can look out for cats that are just chillin by the greenery. Overall a good experience especially for families !

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

We were staying in Jungmun so it was a long drive to the peak. It was a rainy day so the steps were slippery. I made it up half way but turned back when the rain came. It was not a very difficult climb as there are steps and signs to guide you. I saw the older local people climbing up with no problem. There are many foreign and local tour groups there. On the left at the base of the mountain, you could see the female divers diving at specific time. There are many restaurants at the base for you to reward yourself after the climb.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went in summer, so the waterfall was less impressive (due to less rainfall in summer months) especially the 1st waterfall... the water was beautifully clear... be aware the the are plenty of steps up and down... my mum gave up after the first waterfall... the second waterfall is really pretty but there is no way to get access to the water below (unlike the 1st) as the observation platform was rise high from the river below... everyone including the fit and young gave up on the third fall due to the tough & long steps and punishing summer heat... its definitely worth going if you are in the area... fees for admission

We visited this area on our volcanic forces lava tour through Expedia in November 2016.  It was a cool, windy day so we didn't spend even an hour here.  Maybe 45 minutes.  You have to take stairways down to the cliff area.  Then we were freezing even with our layers and coats due to the wind blowing right through us.  It reminded us of the lava cliffs along the coast of Volcanoes National Park on the Hilo-side of the Big Island.  There are even palm trees in the garden area before you start descending towards the Oceanside cliffs.

We visited these as part of our guided tour and were impressed by the surrounding scenery and location. It's a wonderful way to see Jeju at its best, and the rocks are quite impressive. It doesn't take as long to see as you would think, but still worth an hour or so.

We travelled long way only to be told a short story on how the village people survive previously before we were presented their expensive products. The guide told us the quality is good but we were not told elsewhere the price of the products are 50% cheaper. They said their horse oil treat allergies. I bought, used but it didn't get any way better.

We spent a day on Udo island and enjoyed the bicycle ride along the coastal road here. However, because we were based in Seogwipo city, the journey to the ferry itself was 1.5 hour per way - so I would suggest you visit Udo if you are based in Jeju city or somewhere around this port. Or else, you may not seize the best out of the trip.There were not many food options near the ferry port on Udo island, so you can have lunch on Jejudo first, or head to some gathering places near the White Sand beach or the Cliff area where there would be much more eateries.Pricing for bikes here was quite standard so you may not have to bargain - but make sure you pick ones that work :) Check their brakes and bells as you will need them for sure.

We rent a bicycle and just cycling along the sea coast. It's very windy and we even spotted the hanyeo picking up the seaweed! If you visit the island at the right timing. U can see lots of canola flower! We saw partial here and there still very pretty. If you are being lazy, you can just rent the ATV bike (which most of the people do so). If you plan to have lunch there. Give yourself 4-5 hours to explore this island (take photo, had an ice cream etc etc). Note: we didn't walk all the way up to light house as it is already mid noon and we can see something similar @ seopjikoji so we let go this one :)

We heard about the dragon head rock and we were brought there by our tour guide. Our guide warned us to use   a lot of imagination   when we see the rock otherwise we will not be able to see the   dragon  . Well she was right about that. Lots of tour agencies bring their groups there to see the rock and there are lots of little restaurants all the way along the walkway to entice the tourists. After a short walk from the carpark, there is a steep staircase you have to walk down to, in order to get to the spot to see the dragon head from the side. Even so, you're pretty far from the dragon head rock. And to me, it's clearly just a natural process where the rock gets eroded into a certain shape and in this case it's going there for this one rock only... which I wouldn't have if I were on a free and easy route.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

We caught the Nanta show in Jeju and it was such a fun night for the family. It is a combination of comedy, musical, martial art and drums. Though a Korean production with a Korean context but the storyline was kept simple and easy to understand. For a show that ran an hour and a half long, the performers were really awesome with great stamina! They kept their energy high up until the end, without missing a beat. Nanta is also known for its audience participation and without giving the plot away, this was done with a delightful, surprising twist. One that you should experience yourself if you ever get the chance to catch the show.

We book a tour on line from the cruise ship before we arrived at the port. The tour included a visit to Seongeup Folk Village.  There was an admission fee to the village.  There are several walkways around the village. The walkways are well maintained and there are no steps to climb.  There are exhibits our old building, farming and animals.  There are clean restrooms along the walkways.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

Very pretty beach on a sunny day. The colour of the water is so beautiful. Nicely prep walkway all along the whole beach area. Lots of places for coffee and a quick lunch. We had dinner at a local eatery, the owner was nice and friendly.  He helped BBQ our black skin pork belly for us. So yummy with water Kimchi and beer.

This place is interesting only in concept - because it's one of the longest lava tunnels in the world.  But in reality, you climb down a hole and then walk for about a kilometer in what looks like a dirt tunnel made for a subway train with virtually northing to look at.  Then you arrive at a lava column which is far from impressive.  There are numerous amazing caves in the world such as the ones in Ha Long bay.  We are very unimpressed.

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This museum, which focuses on the women divers of Jeju, is well designed and well laid out. It offers a fascinating look into the lives (past and present) of these divers, who spend up to 2 minutes underwater at a time without any breathing apparatus to catch abalone and other sea life. Our guide told us that the divers' current age range is 55 to 85. Younger women have no interest incontinuing this cultural tradition, which is an incredibly difficult way to earn a living and to help support a family.Nicely curated, the museum offers an excellent film about the divers and shows various aspects of their lives, including past and current swim wear. the tools that have been used, models of fishing villages and the Jeju traditional fishing boat. I thoroughly enjoyed this close look at a rare way of life that likely won't be around much longer.

This maze is fun and quite simple. And from what I've observed, it really tests a couple's relationship strength. ALong the way I see couples arguing on which way to go, I see couples helping each other out. It was a fun experience. Walk there from Manjanggul to get a 500won discount!

This is one of the attraction in Jeju that nice to visit! The cave made by volcano lava. When we went there it's rain, so along the way inside the cave wet and dirty! Inside the cave quite slippery and dark. Overall I like this place! We manage to go to the deepest point and come out within 1.30 hr.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is an easy walk from the centre of Jeju city. It'a one of the main attractions along the seafront walkway which goes all the way from the port to the airport. You often see the famous Jeju ladies, dressed in their black wetsuits, diving for pearls without breathing equipment.

This is a neat little place to enjoy the ocean breeze and see a rocky area.You don't need much time here; about 15 minutes is adequate. Wear comfortable shoes as the surface is uneven. I'm sure you will enjoy he scenery here... You can combine it with a walk along the coast into town.  I stumbled across a nice bridge and gazebo area along the way, as I headed towards the downtown market.

this is a local market where you can get snacks and cooked food take away or have a dining too. explore and discover the many food and fruits stall. Look out for stall with long queue, there are a few local favourites. there is also a segment for fresh seafood, shasimi, competitive ladies fighting to offer you their menu!

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

This amazing landscape is a must place to go when you visit Jeju. You have to climb up to see the creater and do not worries, just prepare you leg for a stairs (a lot of stairs hahaha). You better wear a comfortable shoes. when i came was sunny, temperature around 18C but the wind was strong, it makes my hair messy & runny nose (prepare face masker will help). The scenery along the way was refreshing & amazing, you will not disapointed.

There is walk along the  nice promenade to get to this rock. It is hard to make out the dragon in the rock but Asians love strangely shaped rocks. In my opinion it was not so spectacular but the walk along the promenade is very nice, over nice bridge and coffee shops along the way.
There is an hour long boat tour that shows you many of the sights, but was the best way to see these falls and get pictures for these Hallasan weary feet.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don?t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.

The place is very organised with well created pathways to see the rock formations. However, the place is really quite crowded and it is hard to take photos because of the amount of crowd there. Everyone was just walking along the path and there isn't much space to move around. That being said, it is still quite worth it to pay it a visit.

The place is usually crowded.  Make sure to wear good walking shoes to walk and climb, some drinking water to quench thirst along the way. Not suitable for elderly and people who are not keen in climbing. Otherwise, is worth to visit - it is a Unesco World Heritage site after all.  If you are not there to catch sunrise, any season is fine.

The Peace park serves both as a memorial to the victims of the April 3 uprising as well as the long period of persecution of islanders that followed. The museum shows the background of the conflict, connected to the division of Korea, in great detail. It could benefit from more signs in other languages. But it does give a detailed and balanced look at the period and also mentions reconciliation in the future, in contrast to many other memorials in Korea, which only look at the suffering in the past. Well worth to get to the out-of-the-way Peace Park.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

Taking a quick ferry ride will bring you to a breathtaking place called Udo Island. Rocky coasts, beautiful beaches, and crystal clear waters are what you will find on this little farming and fishing island. I decided to rent a bike on my trip and wander around the coastline. In my opinion, it was the best way to see the island. Amazing photo opportunities and tons of places to get some fresh seafood along the way. The clear and shallow water is great for children to play in. Tons of little tidal pools as well. Biking allowed you to be outside and experience the people and the culture of the island. It is probably not a place for people that do not enjoy the outdoors or those that are afraid of a little bit of exercise!

Such an awesome excursion. Doesn?t take too long and there are cool explanation signs along the way. Highly recommend and is super fun. Gets chilly so make sure you bring a sweater, it?s a nice escape from the hot humid jeju weather. Easy to park and easy to find.

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Seems the name of the road has some psychological effect on the tourists. Is it mystery or reality? Hope anyone who is a land surveyor can throw some light on this with the appropriate surveying equipment or we need a long specially made spirit level to verify the inclination of the road. Without it, the so-called 'mysterious' is purely perception. By the way, there is a grave-yard nearby which adds to its spookiness.

Put your rented car on neutral going   uphill   and experience it. Mysterious probably because for most it?s a baffling experience having your car in neutral but going uphill, backwards or forward ? hands off the wheel and feet off that pedal. The place is on the way to Jusangjeolli by way of the Mount Halla route from Jeju town. 5-10 minutes (no crowd here) and you have covered one of the ?touristy? sites in Jeju. A woman attempted to see what would happen with a plastic water bottle placed on the road, nothing did.  Why would any vehicle with so much metals built into it got pulled but not a plastic bottle? Go figure. I have encountered a similar experience at a site in Saudi Arabia near Madinah which has a longer stretch for that ?mysterious? experience.

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street ? you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

Perhaps I've been in Asia too long, but I feel like a lot of these markets start to look, feel and smell the same. It was fun to walk through but I didn't feel like it had a whole lot to offer that felt special. If you're new to Asia, certainly worth a walk though I wouldn't go out of my way to come here.

Our guide brought us here to understand the striking cultural lifestyle of the local folks of Jeju.  The unique and exquisite architectural design of the `primitive'' huts and cottages of the natives was impressive. The pair of well carved and exotic Jeju deities statues that were made from volcanic lava stood spiritually on guard at the entrance. The sculptures matched harmoniously with the decorative Kimchi clay vases left unattended in the manicured lush green lawn compound displaying a special cultural taste that reminded me of the unique Hindu traditions on the island of Bali. I always think that it is the vibrancy and dynamism of the native folk culture that made certain attractions so special. The unique Alisan native lifestyle in Taiwan is just remarkably outstanding and different from that of the Maori in New Zealand and again, distinctively unique from the Dayaks longhouse traditions. It is thus a pleasure and a must thing to do to visit a folk village in Jeju to look at how the culture of the natives and how it is being preserved here.  We were introduced to a guide speaker who showed us the many agricultural tools used by the local natives but the real commercialized promotion began when we were `lured' into a room with seats and the speaker started marketing a type of drinks made from `Wuweiji' traditional herb that grew in abundance in Jeju and is believed to strengthen and invigorates the mind and body. It looks like another `tourist trap' and on the pretext of going to the toilet, I escaped the aggressiveness of the marketing talk. I wandered around the cottage compound admiring the foliage and the surrounding native architectural designs until my group of friends came out from the promotion. One of my group members was anxious to purchase the `elixir' drinks to enhance her youthfulness and she shared the drinks with the rest in the group.   I came out from the cottage and saw there were many similar cottages around the village and there were many sales talk going on in the other cottages. The admission to this folk village was free but I am not sure if my guide earned any commission from the purchase of the herbal bottled drinks by my friend.Except for the commercialized promotion, it is interesting to visit a folk village in Jeju.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.

Nevertheless, people always recommend us to visit this cave when we're in Jeju. what we found is around 2km long cave with cold temperature all the way. if you quite a fan for geology and similar, this cave is exactly for you.the 'main' attraction is located at the very end of the cave. nothing more , nothing less...come if you have free time.. but not suitable for older people due to steep stair and slippery.

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.

Lots of steps but there are plenty of places to rest along the way. Probably prettier to visit in Spring or Fall. It was a cold, gray and windy day, though the sun did come thru a little.  The Haenyeo, lady divers performance at 13:30 and 15:00 is very good and we enjoyed eating some of their very fresh catch! Easy to get to by public transportation but takes a long time. Easier if you have a car.

Just makes you wonder nature creativity. Need to have camera able to take photo in low light.Note: Long walk, water dripping, uneven and dark pathway. However don't loose hope, beautiful @ end of tunnel. Worth the efforts.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

It's very near to Jeju city, within walking distance. It's nice walk strolling along the seaside to dragon head rock and even walk further from there. However this place is always full of tourist, and not easy to get a good picture of this attraction. Nevertheless the environment and surrounding is beautiful and relaxing and I was here during sunset and foggy evening, absolutely beautiful.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

It's deep and long and wet and cold but pretty amazing.  It's lit with pathways and only 1 way in and out.  It's about 1km long and you double back the same way you came.  It's pretty easy to access, saw a lot of seniors and children, there's about 20-40 stairs I guess to get you down. Not too many opportunities where you can walk actual lava tube.  Give it about 1 hour to do.

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. However, the grass/plant at the maze seem not well taken care as you can see a lot of holes along the plant fences of the maze.
It's a lava cave, national herritage. Nothing special in there, it was dark and only rocks along the way. You need to be careful because the floor was wet and slippery.

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

It?s very cheap to get in- 2000 W per adult.Once going down the steps, it?s cooler and wet. Make sure to wear comfortable shoes. No flip flops or heels. Ideal for rain boots as lots of water patches along the way.Relatively dark inside. Some random lights but not perfect. Before looking around lava floating lines or some interesting shape of rocks foamed by lava, you really should pay attention to your feet - so many paddles and slippery, muddy areas.The walk was quite long. Once you hit the dead end, you could take a picture of statue like rock then return to the same entrance that would be over a kilo one way.Kids around elementary schooler and up could handle but definitely toddlers and younger were not suggested.

It worth a look just to see the beautiful coastline of the Island.Most of the rocks come in various heights and sizes shaped like hexagons and if you look at certain angles, they can take on various animals etc.The black lava colour offsets against the outstanding sea and coastline.These cliffs are very similar to the Giants Causeway in Ireland with a pancake rock system but on a much smaller scale.It was crowded the day were there and we assume it is the same most days in the summer months. So a lot of people were snaking along this narrow path around the cliffs and we needed to wait our turn to see over the barriers.There are a few stallholders near the carpark (fee charged) selling fruit, souvenirs and the local home made confectionary similar to nougat.On the way out you can go to a park with some gardens and perhaps a museum type building.The hours vary seasonally however it is the standard KRW 2,000 entry fee for most monuments around the Island.Place it on your ?must see? places to visit here just for the dramatic coastline and on a rough day you may get some blow hole situations with the force of the water.Enjoy your visit!

It was very nice taking a walk along the beach of Udo, the sea is clean but unable to swim because of sharp rocks. We are happy that they keep this place just the same as it is, not making it into a tourism spot. And once again,  most of them cannot speak English, we couldn?t say any word to the locals and the tour guide was helpful all the way through.

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

It was early afternoon & very sunny, & super hot during our visit. Coupled with the long walk & return climb up from the bottom, it was terrible in the heat.Perhaps if we had come in early morning or in spring climate, would probably have enjoyed it better.The Jeju Women Divers Performance was a disappointment. With due respect to this fantastic women, the show was too commercialised.Have read much about these tenacious women & was looking forward to something better than this.However, our guide arranged for us earlier to meet up with these women not far away in another area.Most are in their 70s & had been doing this job almost their whole lives. They are so fit even at this age.Certainly respect them.There are paid boat rides as well round the area & horse riding too.

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was a rainy morning that my friend and I visited this cave. We were greeted with a flight of stairs entering the cave. The temperature in the cave was so much lower, approximately 10 degrees celsius. It was dark and slippery too. The further we walked in, the colder it gets. The pathways are actual lava that hardened over the years therefore, it was not a smooth walk. A lot of locals enjoyed their walk, some strolling while youngsters brisk walk, talking and laughing along the way, making the whole cave not too scary. It was a nice morning walk looking through the structure left behind by the once active volcano forming rocks, mini wells naturally. The work of nature. Beautiful!

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? It depends. If you're the kind of person who couldn't be bothered with science, optical illusions and whatnot, you'd be better off checking out the snack shops nearby, observing the other tourists and their interesting behavior, or skipping this place altogether.However, if you've always been interested in physics and seemingly unexplainable phenomenons which you know are actually explainable, give yourself an hour or more to thoroughly check this place out. Photography lovers may also deem this place worth their time.The bottom line? If you're heading to another tourist attraction (e.g. Hallasan) and it's on the way, and you have time to spare, feel free to check this place out. Otherwise, don't bother.
Interesting place, walk in a lave tube & learn about formation along the way. it was very interesting experience. P/S Please wear shoe.

In this cave, you're allowed to walk about one kilometer in the lava tube where you'll find a lot of variation in the formation and environment. It's a lot of space in one of the tubes (the other one was closed off during our visit). In the tube, there has been several different lava levels and different factors, creating unique patterns on the walls, floor and ceiling. It's recommended to bring something warm down the cave, since it's a bit chilly.Along the way, there is several signs about detail information (both in Korean and English) about the different shapes and things in the cave.

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

If you want to come here to buy Innisfree products, the offering are far lesser than what you can find in Myeongdong. The only attraction here is the soap making experience and a small piece of tea plantation. There are no location-only products sold here. Very limited merchanise on sale. The staffs are unfriendly and always pulling a long face. Not worth visiting.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I walked Routes 6 and 7 on 23rd-24th Oct 2017. The distance was 15km and 18km respectively.The weather was perfect - sunshine and cool breezes. These 2 routes are reputed to be the more beautiful ones. There are a couple of picture-perfect waterfalls and breath-taking shorelines along the way. 2,000Won per entry is charged for the waterfall. Along the way are small fishing ports where one can get to taste local seafood. There are small cafe along the way too, where one can sit, relax and taking in the beautiful scenery. Coffee is +/-4,000won. As I was staying at the starting point, from the finishing point I took taxi back It costs about 8kWon. Oh yes, there are clean restrooms every 5km or so. Just a little minus point, the blue & red ribbon is not easy to be found in urban area. So try looking for the blue line on the tar road.

I visited this place because of friends' recommendation. In the end, I was glad that I made it. It took me 3.5 hours for the whole trip. During this trip, I met a few friendly Korean people, which gave me a great company. there are lots of birds and greens along the away.In the summer, pls put sunscreen on your skin before/during the trip. Otherwise, you will get sunburn easily.

I think we paid KRW2,000 per adult for entry. Walked the lava tube where the temperature dropped by a few degrees. It was raining that day, so it was a good hideout from the downpour. The walk was rather long but many things to see along the way. Remember to wear good waking shoes tho! It can get slippery.

I really liked this cave, or lava tube as it's also called. I was hoping for more stalagmites and such but the lack thereof doesn't bring down the points due to it's massive size and length. There are also signs along the way with information about the   tube   in different languages. I really recommend giing to this place when you go to Jeju!!

I moved to the U.S. (from Korea) 26 years ago when I was 15. I have been coming back to visit almost every year in the past 15 years or so and visited Jeju five times thus far. I don't get to take long weeks off from work, so I always try to pack as many activities into any given trip, so I squeezed this one in on my way back from a day trip to Udo (which is my favorite place in Korea). I wanted to pay this place a visit because I came to learn of what 4.3 incident last year, and I didn't want to pass up the opportunity to learn more about it.The memorial hall was very well organized with plenty of pictures, exhibits, and videos to see. The history before and after the incident was explained thoroughly, and even the resistance movements in other parts of the world are also included in the exhibit hall. My 16-year-old kid, who almost never bothers to read through anything at museums, was taking photos and reading through the exhibits, which I found impressive.My appreciation for the island (and its residents) grew tenfold after the visit to this memorial hall. I highly recommend this place to anyone who likes history/Jeju.\臾몄쇰＊? ＿?깊 理50 댁ⓒ\ 由щ럭??댁⑹＿? 湲곗쇨 ???＿? 湲?濡  以＿?  \. ??ъ 愿?ъ 遺＿?ㅼ대?? 二쇰＿? 泥대 醫＿? 遺＿?ㅼ? ＿?援щ 瑗 諛⑸Ц 蹂쇰□? 듯 μ쇨 ⓒ媛\ ⑸.

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I heard from the owner of our guesthouse that this place isn?t always open because of the tides and weather, so if you have the chance to go, take it. It?s an amazing rock formation, but unlike the ones that you can see at a distance, like Oedolgae and the Jungmun Daepo, you can actually walk on it. That rocks. It took us a while ? was it an hour? ? to walk along the perimeter of this massive rock. The terrain is not smooth ? think of desert sands except that the undulating surface is made of rock instead of sand, so wear study shoes that won?t split because of the damp. It looks like a movie set -- for an alien planet. Really, I didn?t know such a place existed on earth.If I were taking someone around Jeju, I?d recommend this place and I would definitely come back so we can exclaim together.Where: Seogwipo west coast

I always wanted to visit the Devils Postpile National Monument in California. It is a surprise to find Columnar basalt on the seashore of Jeju-do, South Korea. One can walk behind the Sailboat ladders to take a closer look at the Columnar basalt. If you have time, you can stroll along the park to enjoy the beautiful seashore.

Heard there are several entrance, but only one is open to public. The cave has been fitted with a pathway that takes away the hard work of walking on rocky surface for you. It is still quite deep though and will be challenging for anyone with lower fitness level. The tube is lit along the way and it is quite cold. If you've visited a natural cave before, this cave might be less interesting.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Hallim Park, located western 33km away from Jeju City and west of Mt. Hallasan along the beach in Hallimeup, is one of the most popular tourist spots on Jeju Island. It faces the pleasant scenery of Biyangdo Island, Hyeopjae Beach and Geumneung Beach. The park was established on barren land in Hyeopjaeri, Hallimeup, and covered with tons of earth and began planting assorted subtropical plants in early 1971.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

Get lost in the mazes and have fun exploring your way out. Great for everyone. This is the maze park featured by the Running Man. There are 3 mazes in this park, two with grassy walls which is for beginner and intermediate maze solver. The longest stone maze measures about 5.3km in length and it is for the advance players. If you get lost, you can get stuck there for more than an hour.
Enjoyed the cool air, the lovely outdoor smell of nature and that it was not at all a long walk through the forest. Well tethered and constructed pathways.

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

Cheonjeyeon Falls are very near to the Booyoung hotel and the ICC (International Convention Center), an easy 5 minutes walk takes you to the bottom of a very steep flight of wooden steps. If you chance to go up there (no English signs, and as far as I could judge, they do not mention the fall even in Korean) you will find the falls, only to climb down - and then up again.
