I found it very exhaustive. The falls had very little water, so were somewhat disappointing. Apparently there is an easier, but somewhat longer, way to get there from Booyoung, going to the Botanic Gardens along the main road.

Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.? The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.? The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.? The calm music playing enhanced the experience.? The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.? Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

Be sure to wear good shoes for the somewhat uneven - but not particularly slippery - walk and a raincoat for the dripping water.    There is only 1km of the lava tube which is open to tourists, so the entire walk is 2km roundtrip.   There are a number of informational plaques along the way as well as before you even enter.    There are restrooms and a restaurant by the parking lot.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

As someone who loves walking on rocky surfaces (yes it does sound weird when I type it like that), I really enjoyed walking down to the base of the waterfall. You don't have to walk the rocky part to get you to the waterfall though - the steps from the carpark down to the base will take you close enough. Someone the rocks are slippery so be careful. Along the way I think there were haenyeon with their very freshly caught seafood. Loved this place; would come back in a heartbeat.

As it is UNESCO heritage site which I had planned to pay a visit. The temperature starts to drop slightly when you walk further in. There's low dim light installed along the walk however, the pathway full of small rocks, uneven ground and wet with little bit slippery. So might not be suitable for elderly or young kids. Wear comfortable shoes although i did see some ladies wear heels which i wondered how are they going to survive for the 2km walk. Worth visit if you are interested to know more on lava tube formation.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Another UNESCO site in Jeju, hence there are always a lot of people there. But the climb is actually not that difficult, as the way is nicely paved with stairs, and there are quite a few resting places along the way. Took us around 1 hour to climb up to the peak and down again, but other than climbing up to the peak you can also go down to the seaside to see the diver's performance! Unfortunately, when we were there the sea was rough, so there was no performance.

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

A quiet valley in an evergreen forest, the place is almost free of foreign tourists and allows one to capture the most tranquil moments of nature. Where cliffs and reflective pools of crystal clear water meet, lined by stones, guarded by trees and filled with crisp air. The sunlight peeking through the trees permeates a serene and mesmerising ambience in the valley. Look out for the stone wells and Rock Shade Residence along the way. The Rock Shade Residence formed from volcanic lava were used by ancient inhabitants of Jeju Island as shelter. It is said that Andeok Valley has water flowing all seasons long.  With such charming beauty, its no wonder Chusa Kim Jeong-hee, a renowned Joseon-era scholar, used to visit here for contemplation and perhaps, inspiration. Spring and fall would be great for light trekking while the cool forest provides the ultimate summer shade. Nearby attractions: O'Sulloc Tea Museum, Camellia Hill and Jungmun Resorts.Trivia: Andeok Valley was also the filming location of historical K-drama   Slave Hunter   (Chuno in Korean)

A long lava tube with about 1km opened to public.  Very easy to walk as perfectly level all the way apart from the initial steps, and wide and spacious (up to 23m high and 18m wide). Lots of interesting volcanic geology, features, etc. Well worth visiting.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

This is just like a paradise on earth! Super beautiful and totally worth visiting! Wear comfortable shoes and some cute clothes for the most beautiful pictures! The walk is around an hour long so prepare for a bit of a hike! The price is super cheap in comparison to what you get
It's a long hike but for me it's worth it. Its has different nature scenery from my country. Make it to the peak.

Hello everyone! This is a must do if you are on Jeju Island. It is a TON of walking and I will not ever recommend doing it on a hot day in the middle of the day because there is very little shade. It is a hard walk up a lot of steps but some very beautiful scenery. If you do hike it bring water and some fuel bars. It won't take you very long unless you are out of shape but even then it is worth every pain to get there. Truly breathtaking.

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.
Wonderful hikes, but even the easiest ones can be long with some steeper sections. Bring lots of water. The hikes are popular and can be crowded, even in the off-season.

To see the sunrise, one has to wake up early and hike along the stairs and some stone steps and must remember to bring along a torchlight or use our smartphone's torchlight as it can be still very dark during the hike. My husband & I took 30 min to reach the peak, while waiting for the sun to rise there were many people waiting and getting ready their cameras. At the crack of dawn, one will see the sun starts to peak out and see the first rays of the sun grace the Earth. During that moment, everyone started exclaiming with delight as I believe it is not easy for some of us who do not have strong stamina when comes to hiking but it was worth seeing such glorious sight. If I have the chance to visit Jeju, I would want to visit this place again.

Suggest to start early, before 7am. We started at 7am, and managed to reach the summit before 1pm, but had to descend before 1.30pm. Took a total of 10 hours, up and down. If I can do the hike, anybody else can too, for a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Remember to do proper warm-up before starting and bring along enough water to hydrate yourself. Proper hiking shoes are important and hiking sticks are definitely helpful.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

Very nice small museum. Not as boring as much of them. I found it interesting. I hate wandering for 8 hours in a museum with tons to read. That one is fesable in a normal amount of time. There was also a little show they did with movable boats showing how they worked in the days. Girls doing it were laughing the whole time as it was hilarious. My bf got picked to go help as cast along with others working the nets. I loved the whole scene with the chants. There are old boats outside you can go in and visit. Small souvenir shop with not much. Very helpful employees who offered to keep our luggages behind the counter as they did not fit in the lockers.
There are some forests that are a bit more special on the island in my opinion. But this was a lovely hourlong walk that was easy and perfect for my five year old.

The village is huge explaining about the cultures of jeju folks. Plenty of photo shooting corners beautiful flowers farm.There is also a shop renting korean traditional clothes (hanbok renting) where you can wear the clothes and walk around the village for photo shooting. the price is reasonable (comparable to those hanbok renting shop in jeju city)estimate to spend 3 hours there.youth and kids got discount for the entrance fee (do bring passport along)is a must visit spot if you come to jeju.
Long dark cooling walk. Only a small section of the cave was opened. Amazing sight. The entire walk will take more than 1 hour

Long cave path that has been carved out by lava flows.  Its just basically a walk thru the cave and back.  Paths are not paved and can be treacherous at times.  Wear good walking shoes.  Bring a tripod if you want to take some nice pics inside the cave.  Fairly dark in spaces.  The walk should take about 1.5 hours.

Jusangjeolli are stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju Island. Jusangjeolli Cliff was formed when the lava from Hallasan Mountain erupted into the sea of Jungmun. There is a admission fee and parking fee to enter this place. We reached there by car the other day and it was an hour journey from Seogwipo city.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

It was hot at the cave entrance at 32 degrees.  There is notice at entrance on temperature drop to 10 degrees as we continued the walk.  It is a 1 hour to and fro walk along the dark and slippery caveт囹. Good for those who like trekking.

It was a lovely place where you can enjoy boarding transparent canoes in a small clear river. Actually even we had to wait nearly for 2 hours to get a canoe and the trip is not long more than 30 min. But I liked it a lot the scenery was a piece of heaven.

If you just wan to spend for few hours while waiting for your flight. Here the good place. Entrance 8000KRW.  A small area block up for your big luggage you will have locker for your shoe. Once you enter inside you will find a long locker to store your belonging. It can fit in a small backpack.  Take a spa relax and rejuvenate before go for rest room. There are a lot ppl go there for overnight stay even it is weekday perhaps just their culture. The living hall area and sleep place rather to say it's hot I will say is steaming. If you kind of person can't stay for hot this might not be a good place to sleep for you unless you are very tired. You can take blanket from the counter you pay for your entrance fee. Where the pillow just look it from any empty room

A beautiful island and it was nice to travel around in an ATV along the coastline although 2.5 hours wasn't quite enough after taking a break at a cafe. It might be a good idea to stay overnight at Udo too.

Yongmeori Beach is a great place to visit, the erosions along the coast is just amazing. The place is just located along the coast, there are no fences or anything to keep you off. The place may not be open to public every day because if the winds are too strong they do not allow entry, so you may want to check before you come. It gets quite windy and there is not much shelter so remember to wear a jacket and bring a hat. I recommend spending around 1.5 to 2 hours here, it will make a great walk.

Weather was not perfect, but the park was still well worth the visit, the walk through the caves is really fun too. Give yourself at least 2 hours there, we budgeted for one and no where near long enough

We were looking for a good place to shop and buy souvenirs and we found this place in Jungang area. Lot of cheap items from clothes, bags, shoes and beauty products.Tips:- GPS: 752-8776- There is a public parking in front of Jeju Bank along Ohyeon-gil. 3-4 hours cost us 3700Krw.- Jejumok Gwana is just on the West exit (exit 11). You might want to drop by if you got time.- There are Korean food in the middle section. Cheap but taste good.

We hired bicycles at a shop adjacent the pier and cycled around the whole island. Along country roods, there were many scenic spots, mostly adjacent to the sea,  where we could take pictures. Besides, there were many cafes and kiosks where we could dine and rest.  Cycling around the island in a relaxing pace took about 3 to 4 hours. It was a very good experience.

Visited at about 4pm, 2 hours before its closing time, however everything was still available. We tried out the DIY soap making and bath bomb making, which cost 15 000 won each. Do remember to bring along your passport, as you can get a tax refund too. The DIY sessions were very fun, and a great experience for children.The Innisfree House was although small, it is very well-maintained and therapeutic. It sells a range of Innisfree products, mostly for face and skin care. The cafe drinks and desserts were great as well, and definitely worth a shot if you?셱e there for tea break.

Udo, which means cow island because of its shape, has been a popular island trip from the island of Jeju.  Taking about three to four hour to circle on an electric bike, it?s a great day trip (there are plenty of lodgings for those who want to stay longer).  With only a handful of full size cars on its road, it?s a fantastic place to ride a bike around.  Also, for a small island, the amount of dining and cafe options are impressive. Just going around to sample some cafes and restaurants can easily fill up a full day on Udo.  As the island is famous for peanuts, there are lots of peanut flavored products available ranging from ice cream to makgeolli (Korean traditional wine).

Udo island is a small island at east of Jeju Island. It is named after cow because of its cow alike shape. Once you reached the island, you are able to find few bike rental shop. You can rent a electrical scooter with roof or normal scooter to tour around the island. Bare in mind the speed limit is 30 km/h. Most of the rental shop offer two hours rental only. Generally, it should be sufficient if you don't linger at each place too long. Do try the peanut ice-cream as the island is famous for peanut plantation. Get your camera ready as there are many beautiful scenaries to take photos.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.
Not bad, interesting, but didn't really stayed for longer than necessary. It took us around and hour or less, I think.

Manjanggul cave is world historic place of volcanic lava formation! The cave path is very unsmooth with bumpy small rock patches and wet so we had to walk steps by steps very slowly to the end! All along to the main attraction, there are small lamps and lamppost to guide us along.Took us one and a half hours to reach the main attraction of lava formation.We spent a few minutes taking some picture there and proceeded back out of the cave.I think I won't be going there again because I'm not interested in geography.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.
Long, impressive and well maintained. It has good English explanations. Surly worth  the visit. About 1.5 hours all in all

It took us more than an hour to get there. The wind was so chilly that you could feel your fingers freezing up when you take your gloves off to take photo.  But it is absolutely worth it !  The rock formation,formed layer by layer from lava erupted long long ago is so mystic & original. It's like touching rocks that are a million years ago.  Come dressed warmly in comfortable shoes  if you plan to walk along the coast as it is very very cold, wet & slippery. Nevertheless, not to be missed if you are travelling to Jeju!

I thoroughly enjoyed the Castle. I got to try my hand at glass blowing  (I'm not very good) and found the detail in the pieces amazing. You can wander around at leisure, take as long as you like (I was there for 2 hours). There's a short 500m walk at the back you should do if able, there's all sorts of surprising pieces hidden in the woods.

I found this museum really interesting. I knew a little about Hanyeo beforehand but this gave me a much more detailed understanding. The exhibits (consisting of genuine Haenyeo clothing, tools and equipment alongside dioramas, videos and various documents) are well laid out and the accompanying explanations and labels almost all have high-quality English translations. I read every word and it took me a little under 2 hours to complete my visit, which considering the entrance fee is only 1100 won is excellent value for money. Recommended, especially if you are already on the east side of the island.

Four young entertaining painters give a 2-hour long show of slap-dash painting, sketches, dance and pop to enthrall groups of teenagers and school kids. Audience participation is strongly encouraged!!

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.
Cave is big and long, take around 1 hour to come and back. Nothing much to see and it's dark so it's hard to take photo. Average compare to other caves

Bring your swimming gear along, it has a sea swimming pool during low tides, basically daytime. Seeing ppl drives and swimming. There is life-jacket rental available for snorkelling. No entrance ticket required. But the carpark attendance charged us W2K which seem only W1K per hour. No proper carpark control. See ppl park along road side.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

At first, I did not see the point of going to a Teddy Bear Museum. I could not imaging myself checking all teddy bears dressed as popular celebrities and personalities. But I was suprised that I loved every minute of it and I was totally entertained. Me and my friend stayed in the museum for over an hour, longer than what we expected. Highly recommended.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.
Walking along the coastal and climb up to the lighthouse is not a bad idea. Horse riding course nearby. Relaxing and enjoyed the cool wind blow .

It's worth our climb n walk to the fall. Please wear warm enough to prevent same thing as us. I just wear a sweater and T-shirt inside yet the wind breeze can make you freeze. Worth the long walk and stairs taken to reach the destination.

I?ve visited many waterfalls during my travels but this one is unique as it is not located within a lagoon or by a river or along a forest but this is one that goes out to the ocean!! A unique experience for me :)Definitely no swimming here but you can actually walk up close to the foot of the waterfalls for pictures and such. Wear comfortable shoes as there is a significant amount of steps to climb up and down.

Unlike Hallasan and Ilchulbong, the shape of the crater is not very obvious. Moreover, there are less climbing and walking involved here. The main attraction here is actually the field along the path to the observation point of the crater. Make sure your camera fully charged and enough memory because it is a good photography location.

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

This is a UNESCO site and I find it quite awesome, how Mother Nature made these underground caves. Do note that you'll have to climb steep stairs up and down to the caves, so I wouldn't recommend the elderly folks to go in. Do bring along a jacket as it can get chilly down in the caves. Also bring along a torch and have good anti-slip walking shoes as it can be a little wet and slippery.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

There are statues of the Future Buddha, Maitreya; Bodhisattva of Compassion,? an outdoor huge Golden statue of Buddha, hundreds of miniature green Buddhas.? If you climb up the 471 steps, you will reach a cave with a statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion. The tears that she constantly cries for all the pain of this   ocean of suffering   world collects in pools up the stairs below the altar.? Visitors drink it and make prayers before it. If you drink 3 sips of the water, you will enjoy longevity in good health. Great temple to visit.

The sea woman's show and horse riding beach are all inside the park.Climb up takes 20 min. Then you are at the edge of the volcano.Must go place beautiful volcano peak.you can hear sea woman sing and eat their harvest. you can ride pony along the seashore.As you know, every scenery place cost 2,000.

One of the 3 major waterfalls in Jeju, the water falls from a height of around 22 meters and thus named Cheonjiyeon ? meaning Sky connected with Land. Though not as majestic as Cheonjeyeon , this water falls is as beautiful when it comes to its natural surroundings . A very well laid out path ensures one can enjoy the long walk from main entrance to the waterfalls. As there is not much climbing to do, tourists of all ages can visit this place.

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

If you only see one waterfall in Jeju, I would see this one. It is beautiful how it goes into the see. We visited it during a taxi tour along with Cheonjiyeon Falls. They are very close to each other so there is no need to see just one but if you are short on time I would go to Jeongbang. For 2000 won each it is a bargin. Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet and can climb over rocks in, if you want to get close to the waterfall.

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

Went there in the morning. Was windy but filled with tourists. They have some photo locations that will look good on a photo graph.not a place you can stay for long but a good place to drop by if u have some spare time.

We did only this folk village with my family and friends. This recreated the feeling of living a long time ago in korea it communicates well the differences of different backgrounds. We did not hire the audio guide and we had two korean speakers with us who were able to read everything. It was fabulous for my kids to see and touch most of the displays plenty to keep them occupied. We saw a dance and others getting photos taken in wedding costumes and a Korean Drama being filmed. Overall the experience was a good cultural morning out. We did not eat there as we were meeting friends for lunch but it looked very traditional
This UNESCO cave is well worth it. It's a long walk through the black lava cave but fascinating. Leave plenty of time if you are a slow walker because of uneven surfaces.

This rock formation was spotted on the eastern side of Jeju island. I was lucky enough to see this attraction having not spotted one a long time ago.The water present in these area is crystal clear where you can see different fishes swimming in the ocean breeze.
There's a section where you can take photos and I think they're pretty cool. Wanted to try their tea icecream but queue were too long and we didn't have much time :(

thank you so much for your lovely comment and also the visit. you mentioned exactly what i want to explain about our museum. we wish you might keep a nice memories of teddy bears for a long long time. have a wonderful day ^^

Some of the mini structures in the land look like not taken good care for a long time and  most of the painting had faded. If you are travelling with kids and have extra time can go for a short visit .

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.

One of my all time favourite brand of tea! Great to finally step foot into the museum. There are specialty teas that is only available at the museum eg the freshly roasted green tea and the herbal tea lines coupled with a few award winning teas!There are set options at the cafe and the weather was beautiful so we took our order outside and it was great sitting amongst the trees and enjoying a fine cup of tea and dessert! Highly recommend the green tea roll and green tea cheesecake! Do bring your passport along so that you can do the tax rebate once you spend 30000 won and above! Right across the street you can also take photos amongst the rows of luscious greens!
No trip to jeju should be without a visit to this amazing cave. Comfortable walk inside the cave as long as one has suitable shoes.  Take the time to enjoy this cave. Last entry should be at 5:10 pm.
nice place for strolling if you have spare time on hand.  quite a few nice spots for picture taking.  bring along a brolly for occasional drizzle.

My friend had completed the maze shorter time by instinct and not following the map.  Me and my partner collected all the marking stamp but takes a longer time to end.  But it was a great fun. Worth visit!

It's pretty went on May around 3pm. So cloudy and cold because of the light rain. But must visit. School students trip also arrived at the same time. Got to taste free hot green tea. Long lines at the cafe but worth trying. Yes must try the cake and ice cream. Very nice. Got to make own postcards at innisfree museum for souvenirs. If you're good at photography i mean insta moments the pictures will be very great for that!
It?s a once in a lifetime opportunity to visit this maze considering it is the world?s longest. Young and old alike will enjoy the adventure it brings.
It would worth your time to visit if you have kids along or yourself personally fancy about all these bears. The collection of bear is alright though. But they are really cute

I was lucky enough to be given the first hand visit to a mega tourist attraction project open progressively in September 2017. The Jeju Shinhwa World  is the first premium resort in Jeju Island. It's really a resort for everyone . With different choices of hotels catering for all ages. It's just so enticing that I hope I don't need to wait that long but ....everything here is done to perfection. There will be 7 theme parks(three of these theme with TUBAn)4 hotels  villas Asian Food street YG Town all these within this 2.5 million square feet  . It is really going to be so much fun staying here the happening place. I only have time to snap photos on the theme park. Sooooooo excited to go back again to have fun in this Resort.

I walked along the garden path together with my best  friends during our trip to korea.each plant has their own story and some piece of advice regarding life that we can learnt from tree.The garden well kept and all the staff very friendly and can speak englishWe had a great time hereWe even get free tea.KamsahammidaⅠ

I visited this place because is part of the Route 10 of Jeju Olle Walking Festival. Walking here was the most refreshing feeling. Everywhere you look is beautiful and is hard to fight the temptation of taking pictures all the time. I wanted to enjoy the walk instead of taking pictures so I tried to don't use the phone that must. Still couldn't help it. So I will share some pictures too. I hope you have the chance to visit this place. Even better if you can do the full Route 10. Is long but is worth it. I came here during corona times and it was super safe. Max of 15 people per group and mandatory mask (and they give you one for free btw)

I visited Soesokkak Estuary during October after reading about it online.I went there sometime in the afternoon approximately around 2pm or so after lunch. There was a huge crowd (mostly locals) and lines were formed to book the activities.I had wanted to try out the transparent canoe but to my dismay it was sold out fully till late evening. Instead I tried out the aqua bicycle (I suppose that's what it's called?) where you get to paddle with a partner around the river. It requires quite a level of coordination with your partner in order to steer it in the right direction. I can't remember the exact prices but it wasn't too expensive.Bring along an extra set of apparel in case you get wet in the water and do go early if you interested in the transparent canoe!In conclusion great place to visit for enjoyable bonding time for family and friends!

I visited in the past many caves but this is the first time for a lava cave. It is not so beautiful and interesting as a natural cave but it is something new for me. Three stars only because it is not the best place I ever visited but it is interesting.The entrance is really cheap and the cave is long 1 Km so the visit is really fast.

I initially wasn't too keen on visiting this attraction as it was a hot day and inside the village it looked even hotter but via peer pressure I went in.I ended up really enjoying myself and although all the houses look the same it was still a very nice walk and large enough that it keeps you occupied for sometime.If you're into Korean Drama's you would most likely really like this place along with killing some time.

I am 6 years old and I love horses. I like the horse show and now I really want to go to horse school. I liked to feed the horses carrots. I really liked riding horse and I can't wait to do it again. I especially liked the little ponies. They were funny. I was in Korea for a long time and this is the bestest thing we did. If you have children you should come here so they will love you more. Goodbye

Don't waste your time or money here. It's a pure tourist trap and totally overrated for what it is. Long lines to buy silly overrated green tea lattes and soft serve ice cream that don't even taste that great. It's just a giant shop selling the same teas you can buy all over the city. The innisfree shop next door was even worst! Sorry but will not be recommending this place to anyone. That's why it's hard to believe what trip advisor says these days. Everyone seems so happy to come here but once you're here it's a big fat disappointment.

Dec 2019 My husband and I (in our 40s) went on a free & easy to Jeju Island in Dec 2019 and engaged Mr Kim Choong Kun for 4 days from 14th to 17th. We touch base with him via what's app and listed the activities & food we wished to try and places of interest we wished to visit prior to our travelling. He could text in English converse in Mandarin & English. He planned our itinerary in an organised manner which ensured travelling time efficiency. He did such a good job in planning our itinerary that we could visit so many places of interest plus completing all our intended activities such as horse riding shooting Go karting and catching a NANTA show. Mr Kim not only drives us to destinations he was knowledgable and could enlighten us with historic information to the various places of interest. This was a big bonus to us as he served as a good tour guide and doubled up in helping us take photographs. He brought us to places for meals which are patronised by locals (not touristy places) for instance we had a yummy authentic ginseng chicken soup pork knuckles sashimi and other Korean local dishes. If you are willing he is able to join in for meals and personally we liked the arrangement as he was able to communicate on our behalf when placing ordersand even suggested to us which food goes well with which sauces. His sensitivity and personality made dining together very comfortable. He is patient and accommodating to our preferences and needs. He is friendly and we enjoyed conversations with him along our rides. He is also sensitive hence for travellers who are introverts I am sure he is able to gauge his involvement in conversations accordingly. He definitely made our stay in Jeju enjoyable and memorable. These are his info/ contact: Mr Kim Choong Kun Taxi licence plate: 2984 +82-10-63425688 Highly recommended. Good Value.

At the entrance of the plaza there is tourist information center where you can get any info related to the area. From this plaza there are occasional festival from time to time this time I just went to see sunset on the ocean. Above the big waves sunset was pretty. There is long sea-side walk which leads to Dragon head rock.

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

A nice stroll along a coastline that is inspiring. Take the time to enjoy this place - don?t just blow past it.  Look at the years of nature carvings and imagine what it was like when first inhabited.

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We love exploring caves, and we've been to quite a few worldwide. However, Manjanggul isn't really one of the best. The problem is, there isn't much special,. By the time you walk in half a kilometre, what you see becomes a little unchanging. Not bad for a short visit however. Tips: 1. It is a long walk and can be slippery. Wear comfortable shoes with grippy soles.2. A small torch may be useful

We enjoy shopping underground. We were able walk from one end to another. Just remember where you enter. There is a number so you will not get lost.There were beauty products, children clothing, adult clothing, bags, shoes, restaurants, etc. They are not your designer stuff but cheap items. Since winter, they sell winter wear. We bought some face masks, cleanser for less than $10. We also bought bags for $15. The lady said made in korea so we think ok. The backpack is great cos very spacous. Good for traveling. Quality is just ok. Then at one exit near to the wet market, we found a shop called bang bang. It belongs to a friend of the korean actor who starred in the famous korean drama   my love from the star   we were able to buy simple T shirts, socks. They are less than $10. Socks about $3. We actually shop here 2 times when we were staying in ocean suites hotel. It was just 10 to 15 minutes walk to this underground shopping area.There are restaurants here too. We found a good korean restaurant here. It was good food and affordable.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

This is one of the must see in Jeju. The most beautiful rocky beach in Jeju. Hamel ship (copy) is on beachside. You can check some pics on TripAdvisor. Spring season is high season.  Summer season is also high season, but check if typhoon is near. Check the typhoon, you cannot go close beach if there is typhoon. It is not normal beach, waves carved this beach for long time, hundreds of thousands of years.

This is a big park where you get to sample the attractions seen in Jeju . We enjoyed visiting the folk museum, flower and bonsai garden, Jeju stone park as well as the place where they have big palm trees. Our time was limited so we didn't really stay here for long.

There is a secret bunker at on Jeju Island, which once housed old national communication facility and had remained unknown to the public for a long time. This large structure is covered with soil and trees, thus disguised to look like a mountain. This old national facility will be reborn as “Bunker de Lumieres”, a media art exhibition hall that will become Jeju's new landmark for culture and art.

The park is big and have many to see, especially for people who don't know the culture of Jeju. It would be also good for family but since it requires lots of walks I wouldn't recommend elder people who can't walk for a long time. The weather of the day we went wasn't quite good, but the drizzle and fog made that place more mysterious which is quite special because we saw different type of scenery from those pictures you can find from the Internet.

The market mainly consists of two parts: a fruit market (mostly for visitors) and a fish market (mostly for local, as visitors basically can?t do anything with the raw fishes). In night time, there is also food stalls near Gate 8 but the number is limited (I think there?s about 20) so the queue is often long - mostly Korean youngsters. My Korean friend told me that Jeju is unique with its rice cake (similar to Japanese mochi) and orange that even Koreans ?have to? purchase as gifts when visiting Jeju thus their prices are not cheap.

The lack of literature on the Seongeup Folk village was compensated by the cheerful caretaker who gave informative, colourful and refreshing description of their well preserved ancient village.The village revealed a period of time when peace and security were prevailing, and privacy was highly respected. No one would enter the village when the two horizontal portable poles placed across the main entrance were not removed.Visitors would learn about the social structure of the days gone by, when men were out-numbered by women, when men stayed home and were pampered, while the women became the   work-horses   of the family.  Apart from becoming skilled divers, many womenfolk had to travel long distance daily, carrying heavy loads of water supply or agricultural products back to their homes.One would be surprised to learn that rudimentary recycling system was already being practiced. The caretaker must be congratulated for so cleverly circumvented the description the   grand father   stone status, which was in the shape of a male organ.  She described the statue as a god that offered protection against the demons, and promoted fertility for the living.

The beach is nice, clean and not too crowded but a bit small. Many hotels and villas are located along this beach. Therefore, if you want to be stick on it, just take one hotel here, normally just 5 minutes walking. A good place to relax and have romantic time.
thank you so much for visiting , we are so afraid to hear you haven't taken your time long at the garden .  however we believe that you had wonerful time at the teddy bear museum. have a nice day ^^

Parking is free, next to Osulloc. The ajusshi will be there to direct you in the carpark. Lovely place. I love Innisfree products and im happy to be there. However, there are only skincare products, no makeup items. There is an area for soap-making but we didnt do it. During the time we visited, noone did it too, so i cant comment how interesting it is.There is also an area which you could do ink stamping on paper. If you like ink stamping, do remember to bring some paper along. Its free.The food is organic and took quite some time to prepare. So the best is to find a table first, order your food and then do your retail shopping. We ordered 4 drinks & 2 meals, it took about 20-30 mins to be done. Yes, its that long.There are also desserts and they are made beautifully. How i wish i still have the stomach space for them. I would just come back to have tea and dessert at the place. Dont forget to look at their   Jeju only   products. There is innisfree Hallabong jam and strawberry jam. Yup, jam for bread. So look closely at the retails. One of the benefits of being an island is all the beaches. One of the drawbacks is that beaches usually draw tourists, and where there are tourists, the shallow villainy of tourist industries inevitably follows. Sehwa has not yet been targeted for development. As of this writing, the long, open expanse of Sehwa beach is still a beach in its rawest form. When the tide goes out, the volcanic rock formations nearer to the road are exposed, leaving tidal pools to explore, thriving with an over abundance of flora and fauna. The beach at low tide is enormous, and rarely crowded. There are no lifeguards. No music. No lights. Just a beautiful beach, minor waves, clean sand, and decent swimming. When the tide comes in, you can continue swimming, or you can visit some of the restaurants in the area that cater to the locals rather than skimp for the tourists. I had some shabu shabu (??\대＿?) very near Sehwa which was like a kick to the pleasure center of my brain.  Sometimes there's even a local crafts market right next to Sehwa beach, but you have to get lucky to catch it.   Basically, Sehwa is a beach that is still Jeju. It's part of a local community, part of a local ecosystem, as yet only mildly disturbed by ideas of profitability or development.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

Mind your step! The cave is long, dark and slippery. This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience.The price is reasonable. A number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing.

It's my favourite place in Jeju! It's not just an island as we thought it would be! Rmb to bring along your international license if you are planning to ride any motorised vehicles. We biked around the island which in my opinion allows you to see more attractions. Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.
A very long cave made from lava tube. Cold and dark, no bat dung smell though  as claimed. Kids having good time despite being city boys. Good new experience for us

A great museum in Jeju with all its collection of computers and video games. World heritage Site. 13km long lava tube under Jeju Island. Formed by successive eruptions. The section that can be visited is about 1km long - first descending down two levels into the lava tube where the roof has collapsed and then walking up the tube under the mountain and ending at a lava pillar where the lave cascaded down from a parallel tube running above.  There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.

This was not part of my original plans but I'm so glad this was suggested to me!!! The mountain is gorgeous along with the temples inside. If you walk further down the base of the mountain there are some different food places/cafes. ALSO  at the bottom of the mountain is Yongmeori cliffs!! I had no idea they were there. Such a pleasant surprise. I'm not sure why this place isn't more popular! Gorgeous.

This canyon was created by lava flows.When it rains water can flow down from the mountain in to the estuary. We were there during a rainy period and saw water cascading down. Our guide said in a week or two the upper area might be completely dry and sea water would fill in much of the now being filled by fresh water. Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. This little folk village was located right next to our hotel (Haevachi) so we figured we should check it out.  We were spoiled because we had just gone to the folk village and that is the bomb!It is only about $8 for admission and then we opted for the audio tours.  Most of the written signs are not in English so I'm glad we had the audio tours but they didn't work very well.  They are tripped by some sort of sensor when you go by but mine kept skipping back to the original message ugggg.It's a very large complex but somehow unauthentic feeling.  I thought the neatest part was the artisans that sell their crafts.  That was cool and they do have a nice gift shop.  It was very hot out so we went through fairly quickly.  If it hadn't been so hot we might have spent much longer just exploring.If this is your only opportunity to see such a thing then I would visit but if you have the chance to see the folk village in Seoul then I would wait for that one!
Spectacular experience whereby you got to walk one kilometer in and walk back the same distance. It is the longest lava tube in the world. Very interesting experience.

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

I recommend this tour and also in the same town you can go out in a boat for sightseeing or fishing cheaply.

Jeju National Museum is set almost in the middle of nowhere -- well it's beside an adult theme park but otherwise literally nowhere. Had a car so it wasn't tough to find but would be extremely tough using public transport.The museum and the garden that surrounds it is well sterile... for the lack of a better term. Beautiful but seems to lack any personality... it's quiet laid back and perfect for a long walk... but not much action.

We gave a 4 stars owing to its mysterious element.The 100m stretch of road appears to be uphill but it is actually and in fact downhill. This can be done by several experiments. E.g. pour water on the road, put a bottle of water and it will roll towards the   uphill  , walk or run backward along this road; you will feel the difference whether it's uphill or downhill.There are a few stalls selling food so you can eat and think how this is possible.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

Interesting cave, for someone who has stayed in a city for the whole of her life. We went in winter and what is interesting is that the cave is considered warm for winter. Be prepared for the long walk to and back and the path would be too rocky for strollers or wheelchairs

The quality of products are better here.

It is an ideal place to buy souveniors and see/taste the local food.  Rather clean even we went inside the fish and vegetable market.  Along we found few food stalls and restaurants to offer seafood, we were hesitated but decided to go for fish and cuttle fish sushimi in one with rather good environment, it's food and service were up to standard, price was not high compared to those in restaurant.  Interested to see local Kimchi, fish, fruits, herds, snacks from the stores

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

Crowded with a good mix of locals and tourists; jostling along for something.But the items on offer are common, with lots of seasonal clothing on display. Snacks are plentiful, so you have lots of choice. It's an interesting market, with old hands working at street food corners.

Basically a market place that sells the usual basic seafood and fruits. Practically all the fruit stalls sell the same things; mango, Jeju mandarin orange, peaches, etc. Do try the peaches if they are in season. They are huge, soft and fragrant.A lot of stalls are selling the same Jeju chocolate, mandarin or Hallabong tea & jam, etc.There are several stores that sell street food like oden, teokbokki, sundae, etc. In fact there is one particular stall that seems to be very famous due to the Korean variety show 'Running Man'. There is a long queue by 5pm; with people waiting to get a table to try all their Korean snack food. The teokbokki, sundae and fried fritters are really good.Do try the Jeju orange ice cream on a stick if you come across them. They are really nice and fragrant; especially on a warm day.

*Firstly, don't go here. Instead, go to the 5 Day Market (誘쇱ㅼ쇱 Minsok O-il Jang) in Jeju-si. It is open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27th.*As for Dongmun, the best part is the 몃 (Hoddeok). Along one of the side alleys are these beautiful grandmas (癒몃 Halmeoni) who sell fried rice pastries filled with cinnamon, brown sugar, and nuts (Hoddeok). This is some of the best I've had in Korea. SO delicious. There are three of these stalls in this alley. The best, and oldest one, is furthest inside the market.The bad: vendors are rude and over priced. Their goods are not the highest quality and they know that the tourists don't know how to find better quality.

Visited during Dec. The place is nice and cool. Do put on some thick coat or rain coat before there as there will be water dripping on your head. There is bat in the cave. Do not bring a stroller as the road inside the cave is very uneven. Do bring touch light along during your visit as the light inside the cave is not so bright.

Very popular tourist attraction (you know its popular when they have those cheesy fast speedboat tours on the water) but still worth the visit to see these unique shaped cliffs in the ocean if you are already in the area. Just a short simple walk along their boardwalk to see them so quite a short visit. Only 2000 Krw per adult to visit with kids under 4 free.
This is a beautiful beach! It was peacfecul to look out over the water and watch the families enjoy themselves. It was also great to drive along the coast and forget about the worries of the day.
The waterfall is very close to the ticketing booth so there isn't a need to walk for a long distance to get to it. It is generally quite nice but not super impressive.
The park around the waterfall area was simple and not too long and tedious for a walk with your family. Waterfall was nice too for a photoshoot. Overall was great!

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water
The beach was super pretty.. not a long walk.. Very clean.. it was amazing.. And the water was super clean which was really nice!! Love it!

Nothing that fantastic unless you are the one driving. The road is also only approximately 150metres long. Difficult to feel the gravity on human body/walking. Test using a vehicle or can/bottle/water poured on the road. The better deviation is Black pork stall manned by samurai-looking chefs. Mouth-watering black pork BBQ. Nice ice ball dessert nearby as well.

My wife and I went to this place all of a sudden as We had no plan to cover this area. it is located in Jungmoon Resort area. the environment is like slience is spekaing everything. alongside the three water falls are awesome. Go and see.
Long lava tube and if you are into stones and caves you will find it interesting. Inside was cold and some water drops coming from ceiling. Once you reach the end that it just take a picture then go.

Less crowded than many other attractions somehow. A beautiful temple and big! Small cave behind temple worth checking out. Don't forget to drink of the water legend has it you will live a longer life!

It?s does appears that the law of gravity is defied! Haha. Big ample car park available at site if u drive. Nice lady at the stalls along the road facilitated my science experiment by lending me a water bottle to roll on the road. And yes! It does appears that the water bottle was rolling uphill against the law of physics. Its worth a visit if u are in town!

I think this is the better of the two main waterfalls in the area.  It is more natural and a little less touristy. There is a second waterfall shown on the map around 1km along the coast path but this is not worth going to.

Had a long bikecycle trip from Jeju-do city to which I ended at this beach.It's like a small bay with white sand beach. was pretty crowded although it wasn't the season. water sport wasn't operational

Emerald color water with a beautiful long beach and white sand!!  a great place for families with children to play together and enjoy a quiet. It makes a beautiful scenery photo with Biyangdo Island is located directly in front of the beach.

Came with my 80-year old dad and we had a slow walk along the uneven ground. Would recommend wearing waterproof as water drips fr the ceiling. It's is also a little chilly inside the tube (abt 8 degrees C) The place is also dim so some agility is needed to prevent slipping but it is generally safe. Just walk slowly. Overall it's an enjoyable experience as we marveled at the forces of nature that made the tube possible.

Best visit in summer or late spring when there's more water in the river. It would have been more magnificant. Historical evidence shows that the entourage sent by the Emperor Qin to search for the longivity medicine passed by this place.
About 5mins down the long flight of stairs and you get upclose with the waterfall. Helpful to come with proper shoes as you can walk closer the the waterfall on the rocks to get a good photo.
A lovely natural cliffs along the western side of the island which has granit made from direct touch of laba and water.
A long walk although only 1km. Inside cave at low temperature and water keep dripping. Experience the nature of the lava cave formed since 20000-30000 years ago would be something not to miss.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: yes we took that long but it was definitely a highlight of our trip...start early, 630 to 7am would be good... as it was nov, we ended trekking the last part in the dark... a torchlight would be a good idea...there's a shelter 3/4 up that sells water and instant noodles...still some snacks as you trek might be a good idea

What I like about this waterfall is that you can either admire it from a distance or if you prefer, you can literally walk along the rocks and take a closeup shot right next to the falls. What a thrill.

We went with my 63 year old mom, husband, and 15 and 6 year olds. It was great! It's waaaay longer, wider, taller and more interesting of a lava tube than at Volcanos national park in Hawaii! The largest accessible in the world. Bring a waterproof camera, hiking shoes or at least tennis goes, a raincoat or jacket. Won't wear white. I still can't get the ash stain out of my sons sleeve after he fell in a puddle. It's only a few dollars to get in. Do the quick museum first, if you want to know more about it. Cold, wet, dark, tired but Loved it!

We visited a total of 3 waterfalls (including Jeongbang Waterfall) for our recent trip to Jeju Island.  This was my favourite among the 3 waterfalls visited, as it was rather unique, flowing directly into the sea.  However, when we were there on a weekday afternoon, it was nice and quiet for only a few minutes, then a huge group of teenagers / students arrived and filled up the whole place.  It was too crowded and we had difficulty finding space to walk on the rocks and to take a good picture was nearly impossible.We would have stayed longer if it didn't get so crowded.

We only managed to visit at night. The street food location is at gate 8. Some of the stalls have long long queue. The watermellon drink stall seems to be a hit... A bit pricey at KRW9000 for one watermellon drinks (2 cups equivalent).Other food is spaghetti, korean fried chicken etc. Grab the food you want and there are sitting area to eat.There are also few restaurants selling raw fish and sashimi at the same place
