Very good exercise, the longest route takes about 6 hrs if you walk fast (as it says 8 hrs) but u need to go in the morning so that u should return before dark.Lot of locals doing this but don't forget to bring water n packed lunch!

Too fascinating when seeing all the traits of massive lava flow in the cave, which is actually part of the lava tube. Must bring along a powerful torch if you want to enjoy from the ceiling to the ground. Relying just on the phone torch or the lights inside will hinder your enjoyment and appreciation of this natural masterpiece as you will be only focusing on your steps. Do walk the entire 1 km so you can see the big massive lava lumps which stretches from the ground to the ceiling. Water drippings and water patches are common, wear a cap and windbreaker will help. In fact the temperature inside is a few degrees lower than the outside

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

This is quite an interesting place to visit. Do remember it's a long lava tube cave.Take note:1) Stairs to the cave can be steep.2) The floor of the cave is in its natural form. It's wet, slippery, jagged and uneven. There are large puddles everywhere so watch where you step.3) When we went, there isn't really any special colorful lighting in it. It was quite dim. We used our cellphone as our flashlight in some of the darker and very uneven floor areas.4) It's cold so wear some warm clothing. There may be water dripping from the ceiling as well. Overall we enjoyed the lava cave.

This is a very interesting place to visit. Our driver put his car in neutral gear, turned off the engine and put his keys on the dashboard, and the car rolled uphill! We got off and watched other people put bottles of water on the road and they rolled uphill as well! It is actually an optical illusion, but still a strange sight to behold. You don't have to stay here for long - maybe 30 minutes will do.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

The beautiful white color of the sand comes from the large amounts of crushed seashells that have been mixed in with the sand. The long seashore stretches for 9 km and has cobalt colored seawater and evergreen forests scattered around the vicinity, making the scenery very beautiful. Just off the beach is Biyangdo Island. The white sandy beach is about 20 meters long, and the water is 1.2 meters deep with no sudden drops. In the evergreen groves, there are plenty of convenient facilities and campgrounds for visitors to use.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.

it was just a super long cave that is really cold, perfect when you are visiting during the hot summers. Wear comfortable shoes because you will be avoiding water puddles, trekking on uneven rocky floors. Its just a super long walk in and out.

I expected a longer walk for this, given that this is what Mother Nature had blessed us with, but this cave is only opened for the first 1km to the public. Still, it was an amazing sight (with the turtle-like rock formation and the various lava formations). Wear comfortably with a cap or hoodie as the cave will be chilly and the water will drip from above! Also, bring flash lights as it can get quite dark!

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. A good thing we visited this Dragon Head Coast while doing the west coast route.The canola flowers site is a paid visitor spot (should be around KRW2K each adult). There is a Viking ride @ the base for the young ones to try. You can see many interesting lines and grains on the side of the rocks' walls. You get to see women divers selling fresh seafoods along the coast, youngest are already in their 50s and oldest are in their 70s (still diving)...they are simply amazing.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.
Beautiful blue/green water  with white sand beach. We didn't get in the water since it was chilly, but it looks very shallow with some rocks.   Can park and walk along the beach shore.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It?s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn?t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.

1st falls was kinda disappointing cos there was no water coming down. Perhaps dry season? On the + side, the still water surface made excellent photo opp. After more staircases, we had the option to descend a long staircase to 2nd falls. Which we skipped and proceeded on. We crossed the bridge of the 7 nymphs - indeed an odd architecture with such a curved surface to near centre of bridge. Easiest is to walk in reverse to give the hamstrings some relief. Later on, there was a lookout point for 2nd falls. Yay. All done, we rewarded ourselves with icecream :)
Visited on 17th October 2019.If you going with friend it would be great.A relax mini hiking walk along the breezy turquoise sea.It's a must go. Nice place to take photo too.

Wasn't planning to do any hiking, so just drove to Eorimok base station to experience the snow and took some photographs, as we came from a tropical country and never had any snow experience before. Turns out the drive up to the station is very beautiful with the snow covered trees along the road. The base station itself is also nice for a leisure walk especially for family with kids.
I enjoyed it more than the group.  It's geared for those who are used to hiking.  Long lava tube - you don't have to walk the whole thing, but why not?  It is just 1 KM in and 1 KM out.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

Loved my visit here. It is one of the most relaxing islands that I've visited. Food's great and driving around the island is a pleasant experience. They have nice cafes and sceneries along the coastal road. getting around is easy with a car.

I heard about Udo Island from a few of the other ladies I was traveling with. They had seen pictures and couldn't wait to visit. I tagged a long for some good fashion outdoor fun. We rented bikes for the afternoon and took a ride around the island. The weather was perfect and we were able to see some great scenery. We visited a couple of the beach places and were able to take incredible pictures. We took a ferry ride over and it was amazing. Getting tickets and filling out paper work to take the ferry was incredibly easy and everyone was very helpful on the island. We were able to eat some great seafood and awesome ice-cream. Great spot to visit!

You need to bring jacket that day we went even if its summer still cold inside, wear rubber shoes easy for you to walk, though there's not much inside to see, young kids will not enjoy for sure they will just be tired walking very long cave.

We thought we're going to be at the base only because we brought along our 3 years old son.To our surprise, our son can complete the route going up and down by himself (he refused for me to carry him). The steps were quite easy and it's really worth it.If you miss this, your visit to Jeju-do is incomplete.

This is one location where you do not have to worry about bad weather, actually I would recommend going here on a day with rain and wind since then you can actually experience the force of nature when the waves hit the cliffs.Easy access, parking (for a fee) and you can walk along the shore line on a board walk (sort of).

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.
Cool scenic cliffs at the ocean, easy path to get to them, not a very long walk, highly recommend it.

A pretty long walk over some decent grounds and some stairs to get through the entire cave. Its a little chilly down there so bring some easy to shed clothing. Really a vast and large cave, not something you get to see very often elsewhere and for the small entry fee... you cant beat it.
We were here to hunt local foods and it didn?t disappoint us. We followed the locals for those long queue at Gate 8 zone. Get yourself be patient and enjoy the delicious foodie here.

There has a long line up food area even they only have simple menu. The food is good. Must try their mandarin drink. Lot of different kind of tea you can pick. I bought it for gift and its little bit pricey.

The cliffs here have odd and somerimes beautiful formations.  It's where you can put your creative photography skills to work! It costs 2000 won admission and it is very close to the edge.  Strong wind or waves can be a little dangerous i thought.Along the coast are also older men and women selling freshly caught seafood and you can eat it there as well.
Nothing much here. The place that local playing skateboard long board basketball on the street. If you are a seafood lover this is the right place to find.
It is near to the famous Nolman seafood ramen soup location. One can take a leisurely stroll along the coast and take great pictures

I am a green tea lover. Highly recommended for tea lover. There is cafe there the food was good. But you possibly will que up longer to have your meal order. There are shop selling tea's merchandise and Innisfree cosmetic shop.

great icecream and the cakes are pretty good too but seats inside the cafe are very limited due to the crowds and long queue to purchase the food adds to the delay.families with young kid may want to avoid bringing in stroller in as it extremely crowded inside

With the help of Mr. Jang, our experience of Jeju local food has also been very exciting. Grilled Mackerel, Sundubu, Oysters soup rice, Samgyetang, black pork barbeque, abalone hot pot rice etc. We wish we could stay longer in Jeju.

We stayed nearby and went in to find dinner. There's gate no 8 which is full of people selling food and those with long queue usually means It's nice. We tried some of it but it will be quite pricy as in the end, both of us not full.

The stacked cliffs of Yongmeori are beautiful! This was one of my favorite sites in Jeju. It's a very windy walk but in the summer, this provided respite from the humid heat. The rocks are uneven and bumpy, so it is a good idea to wear sturdy shoes.You have to pay a small fee but it's very much worth it. Along the walk, there are women selling raw seafood meals for 10,000 a pop. It's a very simple set-up: plastic stools and chairs, some garlic, gochujang, and soju if you wish.

Innisfree is a well-known brand with numerous outlets throughout Korea and Asia. As it originated from Jeju, this is their main outlet in Korea. It was much smaller than expected, with only a single long building housing both the shop and cafe.The shop stocked quiet a good range of their toiletries and cosmetics, with an natural soap-making activity available. You can purchase a pack from the counter, choose the scent of soap you want, and there are stations with a screen to guide you through the soap-making process step-by-step. Shop staff are on hand for assistance as well. At the end of it, you can pack the soap into an eco-bag as a gift.The organic green cafe had ample seating and a good range of food, compared to the adjacent O Sulloc tea museum. Their drinks are served in funky bottles with interesting tastes, and make a pretty picture.If in the area, the soap-making is interesting and wouldn't take too long.

Yongmeori is an excellent beauty but one has to walk along the coast during low tide to see its true beauty. The rock formation is unique n a city dweller like me walk each step with awe looking at the formations. I believe anyone who enjoys nature but is brought up in a concrete jungle will love this place.
Went on a rainy day but most importantly wear comfortable clothing and walking shoes that won't slip on rocks.. Also bring a sweater or wear long sleeve as it gets colder further inside.
Well maintained. It is basically a km long walk into a cave (which is created by lava). Some structures inside from the lava. But otherwise nothing interesting. It is cold in there so be prepared.

We went there with a tour group as part of a package.  It's basically a long walk in the park with a bunch of photo ops.If we had kids with us I would think it was OK.  But not for a couple of retired folks.

We arrived early morning but a crowd had already built up with a school trip group from Seoul. All the rides were prebooked and the earliest rides available was after 2pm that day. We took a walk on the boardwalk alongside and that was nice too.

Visited this amazing cave recently with the kids. Aged between 7-13 years old. We all enjoyed it. Remember to bring along a jacket as the cave can be quite cold. It?s about 11 degree Celsius. Wear a pair of good shoes too as the walking surface is uneven and wet.
This place is huge. And the walk til the end is a very long walk. It's very dark and very cold. I was all prepared with sneaker and jacket with scarf.
This place is a gorgeous volcanic cave which has been presented beautifully. It is not too long in length and not a difficult walk.
This is the longest tunnel with very dim light and the temperature is 13 deg C.You will need a proper shoe/sneaker not slippers to walk safely on the uneven ground
This cave is just ok. It's a long walk in the dark for a nice photo of a buddhist altar at the end of it. It was cold when I went so I didn't enjoy it all that much
There really isn't much to it. You walk down a long flight of stairs into a large cool dark cave which is lit enough to see.
The Jusangjeolli Cliff is a beautiful geographical site with lava rock formations against the beautiful ocean. Great scenery for pictures and a relaxing stroll along the boardwalk.

The cab driver brought us to this place. This bridge was near to the harbour.Nice place to walk along the bridge where you can enjoy the surrounding. It was very windy where you able the enjoy the breeze. Indeed just a normal bridge but with nice surrounding.

The art is so real and creativity is the most appreciated from this museum. Long walk through the hall with many art picture along side you. At the end there's cozy cafe and beautiful garden. Unfortunately when we visited there it was raining so we can't play and took photo at the garden.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.
Really the Tubes are fascinating but a little redundant. Was a long walk in the dark for a six (6) year old BUT the park is well equipped w/ Toilets and a Local Resto & Taxi Cabs!!! Enjoy.

Place is very clean and beautiful. No thrash bins around so do bring extra plastic bag to throw your unwanted things or drinks in it. It is a long walk up to the entrance. Choose the path wisely. Not advisable for those with joint pain and old injuries.

Nice place to visit but must be extra careful with your steps. Not a huge rock but worth a look. Loved the wind on my face and the plane landings every 7-8 minutes. The walk along the coast to Ramada Plaza was great.

Lava flows which are cool-you walk along about 20mins or so then see the large lave flow at the end which i think is one of the largest in the world. The walk is in semi darkness but there are enough lights to see by without ruining the ambiance. No need for a torch. Bring good shoes as the ground is super uneven. It can get cold too so bring a jumper.
it's a long walk through the end..but it feels great when you are actually walking in where the lava used to pass.the fee is not expensive and this is a place not to miss when you are in jeju

It was a short walk of about 10 min but we took longer than usual as we were distracted by the locals selling raw abalone... decided to try out the raw abalone... Dont really know how to appreciate them... Too hard and chewy for me... But the locals are very kind... They even offered us soju...

It only costs about $2 to visit (separate from transportation costs).  Very well maintained site but still a rough surface that requires suitable footwear and it can be wet and slippery in some spots; also quite cool.  This is a very impressive channel to walk through and imagine the lava flowing and leaving the characteristic marks and artifacts along it path.  Dim lighting gives a neat eerieness that somehow makes it even more exciting to explore.  Various well constructed boardwalks with built in floor lights improve access.  The entire tour is about 1 km in each direction.  Very interesting experience.
It is dark and cooling walk and some part of the floor can be a bit rocky. Bring along a small torch light as some part can be quite dark.

Being Australian  we had never heard of All In but were taken here on our tour. We didn't go into the museum but did walk by it along the coast track to the lighthouse. Scenery was very nice. This area is called Seopjikoji on the Jeju maps.
An eye opening experience to walk along a real lava flow cave! Bring along a small touch light; as well as a warm jacket as it can get a little chilly inside the cave.
A little scary and very dark inside the cave and the ground is uneven making walking rather tiring and it was a long walk but overall a good experience for me.
You can walk along the shore and admire the nature artist who created wonderful coastline and statue made from stone. It's very scenic, photogenic and good exercise for your body.

Yes, it's just a cave. Nothing much there besides a long, large, cool and dark cave with uneven walking path. The walk path is uneven and wet. Please wear good walking shoes and that will be good if you have flashlight. I will not recon to bring kids or old folks to this attraction. I saw only 1 security camera at the entrance but none in the cave and no workers in the cave. So, if someone injured or any emergency help, I guess no one can help you except other tourist.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. Although the path throught the three sections of the cave are shorter, you can see much more. Go to Halim Park and skip Manjang Cave.

Well worth the visit, especially if geology is your interest.Plenty of stairs in and out of the cave so not too advisable for elderly, or families with babies/ toddlers. (though i did bring both!) Being a lava tube, the flooring can be uneven and slippery within the cave so wear proper footwear.It will be cold and dimly lit down in the lava tube, so bring your sweaters if chill is a concern.The walk long to and fro the end, so be prepared.After the first half to the end, it can get boring for some especially the kids. That said it is still a unique experience for many.

We didn't go on a tour; we just walked through the caves at our own pace reading all the signs. It was a pretty neat place to visit, unlike an other place I'd been before. It gets cool down in the cave, even in hot July weather so bring a long sleeve shirt or light jacket.

Very interesting cave, which has been created by the vulcano. 1km long tunnel available for tourists inside of old not active  vulcano. Not difficult to reach and walk. Little dark, but lamps inside are giving sufficient light. Very good level of safety. Info how long to walk, communication system with support team,  stairs, bridges, walking paths. Information boards describing what you can see in cave. Even young children like 3-6y can easily enjoy this trip.

Unique maze park where maps of the maze are provided.  If you follow the map, it will take you about 5 minutes to complete it.  But try it on your own, and you may take longer or get lost!!   Along the maze, the plant is high, so you can't see over into other areas.  There are three skywalks where you can stand and observe the entire maze and take pictures of it.  Fun for the entire family.

This place is a must-visit if you visit Jeju. It was a pretty long walk from one end to another end. Inside the cave, it was quite dark and you have to be extremely careful while inside as the floor might be slippery. It was a magnificient cave and if you are a nature/cave lover, you will definitely love it!

This lava cave is interesting if you are into nature and ok to walk in the dark on uneven rocks for 2km. I like the experience but my elderly parents didn't really appreciate the dark long walk, especially with the steep stairs. So unless your elderly members are physically fit, it will be much better if they skipped this.

This is the longest lava tube in the world.  It's 7kms long and only 1km is open to the public.  It's rather spectacular to be in it, to appreciate the wonders of Nature.  For the cynics, you would probably ask yourself why you want to part with money to walk in almost darkness, through a wet and uneven surface, just to affirm yourself that you are visiting one of the UNESCO's accredited natural wonders of the world.  For me, it's a been there, done that experience.  Enough said!

This is one of the longest lava tubes in the world and a World Heritage Site. You are able to walk for about 1km and return. We enjoyed the walk, especially as it was so hot outside and nice and cool inside.

This is a seriously big lava tube. In fact, as lava tubes go I think it's one of the biggest. Definitely a whopper! The whole thing is almost 8km long, but the section open to the public is just 1km. You descend steps and walk along the dimly lit tube. There are some things to look at like lava 'rafts' (lumps of lava that have floated along) and lava stalactites (lumps of lava that have dripped from the ceiling) and at the end a lava column (where lava has poured in through a hole in the ceiling and formed a column). In short, it's lava-ly!

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.

There are many beautiful walks along this southern side of Jeju and this is another one. As it was so hot when we visited, our driver took us to a swimming hole among the rocks, down some steep steps at the opposite end of the walk to Oedolgae itself. Our families loved this very much.
The place defitinely not suitable for elder people. Is too long walk for them and the long stair case. However, is an amazing place to visit.

The dragon head rock is a good place to visit, if your wanting to stay close to jeju si. It doesnt take long to look at the rock and there are many tourists but the costal road is a nice relaxing walk.
The cave is dark and cold especially nearing winter. If you are into cave exploration, then be sure to bring along a flashlight to brighten up. Be careful walking in the cave.

the cave is 1 km long you walk mostly in dark.not too.kuch to seeat the end there is a pillar but if you have been to.caves in the world before, it's not as fascinating as you see on the pictures not a real must

The beach itself could do with some TLC from the council.   There is a lot of debris which washes up daily onto the beach and along the coastal walk. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.

Stayed by Hyeopjae beach two nights, wish we stayed longer.Lovely place with a real local feeling, many caf챕s and restaurants around.Large and free car park.Don?t miss the beer battered chicken with beer by the walk down to the beach, opposite to the foot cleaning bath

Place for everyone who like caves, volcanos or geology. The cave is long, but the one kilometre available for tourists is enough. There are many interesting lava formations, described in English. Beside that the cave is just beautiful. The temperature inside is around 10째C, humidity close to 100%. If you are not very fond of caves, stones or walking, probably you should skip it. :-)

Perfect for couples to take a romantic walk through the woods. Be sure to take the shortcut if you just want to get to the end of it quickly and see the oldest tree around, or if you're a romantic be sure to take the long route and walk hand in hand with your beloved. Enjoyed the refreshing walk and highly recommended.
Nothing too spectacular, but it's a nice walk along the coast. Restaurants nearby for dinner and a drink. If you're in the area, check it out!

Not many such places are open to public visit, so I will say this is something interesting to explore if you visit Jeju. Temperature is lower than outside, so do bring a jacket or wear long sleeves if you are scare of cold. Physical mobility is required as there are steep steps to walk down to the entrance and paths are uneven.There is a restaurant and convenient store on site. We had lunch at the restaurant after the visit. Pretty decent Korean meals. Have translation app ready if you do not read Korean as menu is in Korean .
Nice walk along the shore and take a few photos near the airport, tourist information, gift shops and casino.

Never been to lava cave before..it's fascinating..the colour led lighting makes the cave more beautifull..to reach the end of a cave you had to walk for about 1km..maybe because it's rain outside,the temperature inside the cave is more colder..you should wear a long shirt and a long pants..

Manjanggul Cave came to me as a surprise. To walk in a lava tube is an enchanting experience. There are steep stairs and long walk so be prepared. Don't bring heavy bags. Wear jacket because its cold inside the cave. Bring good camera. As you enter the cave, you will see the limestone that looks like lava flow (see picture attached). The path is dim that completes the enchanting atmosphere. By the end of the road, you can see the lava column.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world. It is one of the UNESCO heritage. There's a good 1km walk from the entrance of the cave til you get to the end of the tunnel to sight the beautiful stalactites.  The tunnel is of course much longer than that however access is only allowed up to the 1km mark. The path is dark, chilly,  rocky and slippery. Please wear good shoes and bring a jumper and mini torchlight if you wish.

Love love love. Everything was beautiful. If you like just seeing different glass art works this is the place for you. It was between $11-12 for entry but of the   museums   in korea  this one is my favorite (lived in korea for 4 years). The jungle walk through that starts with some dinosaurs is kind of long but very gorgeous
It's quite a long walk to the end and return but I enjoy myself. wear suitable shoes, its rocky, wet and limited light source.
It's definitely a different weather from the above, pls bring along jacket if you enter. The attraction is really worth for a kilometre walk.

It's a nice bridge, and takes you across to the little island on the other side. Not really a lot to see apart from passing through the quaint port and adjacent coastline. Would suit you if you just wanted to go out for a relaxing walk along a peaceful area.

It was an interesting experience to walk through the 1km long tunnel if you enjoy understanding and seeing the various structures and rock formations formed from the lava flow. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!

It is really long cave. Pls wear sensible shoes and high heels are NO NO there.I think it is nice for the first 15 min but after 15min it all looks the same. So unless you really knows you rocks well, or else it will be just a walking trip
It is just a long, dark, unending walk in a tunnel and nothing to see.Just a nice temperature inside. Don't bother and not suitable for older people...

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

In my opinion, there are two world heritage sites that visitors to Jeju must visit. One is Manjanggul Cave and the other one is Seongsan Illchubong. Manjanggul Cave is unique as it was formed by lava movement thousands of years ago. It provides an insight into Jeju's geographical structure. The temperature in the cave could be chilly, so bring a jacket along. Visitors to the cave usually walked for about 2 km to reach the end, where photos with a large stalactite pillar could be taken. Other features in the cave include lava formations that look like elephant feet, turtles and book shelves.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

I was staying at the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun and decided to go for an out door walk to enjoy the beautiful weather. I was walking along the coastline and it eventually lead me to this attraction. Although it is wonderful to see these unique rock formation, this attraction is rather small.

I find walking in this lava cave is interesting as it is so cool inside and surprisingly there is no bad smell as it is rather wet. The cave produces it's on air conditioning as the temperature inside is around 15-17 Celsius. Some areas are well lighted and some are not, proper walking shoes are needed as there are many uneven areas along the path provided. Good experience for the ones who loves outdoor!

I find this cave beautiful as it is made by nature. It is just 1km long, it is good for a short trip. The place is cold, that's why Koreans go here in the summer. If you get bored easily, this place is not for you as the cave doesn't have a variety of rock formations.Furthermore, if you do not like to walk in rocky paths, you may not appreciate this. This place is dimly lit to preserve the cave, so you have to be careful. Overall, a good place to visit if you appreciate nature.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.
Be prepared to walk a lot. Stores selling similar items tend to cluster together. Traffic and parking can be a harrowing experience. From what we observed at the taxi queue, it can be a long wait.
An interesting walk underground in a 1 km long cave. Some people would find fascinating, others might get abit claustrophobic.Very cheap, about 90 pence per person. Beautiful grounds on the outside.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.
A wonderful place to visit a regular place to visit whether for a walk along the shore to relax or to camp out for the weekend in summer,it is really just great!

A very wide (23m), high (18m) and long cave (7+ km) one can walk along by yourself (about 1km is open to the public). The temperature inside is perfect, when there is a heatwave outside (which was the case in August 2016). It is doable with a small kid, however you can't bring a stroller as the surface is too uneven in the cave. Also bring solid shoes, it is slippery. Some visiters had flipflops or even some kind of high heals - truly not recommended.

A nice park where you can walk up easily to see the crater. The crater is long dried up with vegetation growing and on my visit, there was a excavation truck at the bottom working! Wonder how the truck and worker get down there.Recommend to all age group.

Woke up early hoping to catch the sunrise. We stayed at a pension just 5 min walk from the entrance to Seongsan ilchulbong. It was a wonderful experience to climb in the darkness of the predawn hour. We were surprised to see so many people waiting the start the climb when we reached?? it was raining the night before so the ground was rather slippery. Thankfully the rain had stopped when we started the climb. According to a local there are 500 steps to the peak. It's  doable though it does require a good amount stamina / more time (we were pressed as we wanted to catch the sunrise). The route is easy to follow - steps all the way; there're toilets along the trail too. It was cloudy on the day we climbed so the sunrise wasn't as we'd hoped but still spectacular regardless. On the way down we took a short detour down a flight of steps to a lagoon-like region where the haenyeon dive for seafood. The view there is spectacular especially before the tide rises in the morning. There is a restaurant that sells seafood caught by the haenyeon that was very yummy  we actually took some really nice pictures there. Would return in a heartbeat just for the refreshing climb!!

Well worth the hike even on a cloudy day. If you go to see the sunrise like we did and it's dark don't forget to read the signs! We totally missed the sign that said no eating at the top...Oops! We were going full speed on the way up to make sure we did not miss the view. Be advised....trail up and down is not the same. If you want to enjoy both make sure you give yourself enough time. Both trails are beautiful and I wish we had enjoyed the trail going up a little slower. If you are active this should be easy although expect stairs as with any Korean hike! Plenty of parking and bathrooms at the bottom.

We went to see the beautiful rock formations but also enjoyed the natural swimming pools at the left side of the fork in the trail.  So much fun to enjoy the water on a hot day.  GORGEOUS views and just an awesome stop on your way around the island!
We went this trail up and can recommend it surely for everyone who is in doubt of their stamina. It was a steady elevation with nice stops on the way

We walked to Oedolgae from Seogwipo on one of the Olle trails. It was a beautiful coastal walk between route 6 and route 7. There were lots of small cafes and stalls selling refreshments along the way and the rock itself was very picturesque. We went out of season so plenty of opportunities for photos

We walked from our hotel located at the Arang Joeul Street to the Saeyeongyo bridge for almost 30 minutes. There were many locals visited and walking leisurely there. There many restaurants and the Seogwipo Submarine was located on the way there. You can see the beautiful ocean wave along the way to the bridge. The bridge connected to the Saesom island. The island was brighted by light and old korean song music at night. We visited the bridge twice in the evening to see the colourful light and daytime to observe the surrounding scenery. The trail to Cheonjiyeon waterfall can be found? on the way to the Saesom bridge. The entrance to the waterfall was after Chilsimnigyo bridge.

We hiked the trail at Seogwipo Recreation Area.   The cost is 1.00 US per person and 2.00 per car.The trails are very well marked in english with plenty of stopping stops along the way.   There are also a number of bathroom faculties along the way.   be sure to get the trail map when paying admission.

We hiked the mountain a bit late but still was very interesting. There are many trails to hike just make sure to be back to the bus station before 5:30. We missed throats bus and a Korean guy who works there showed his hospitality. He took me and 4 others to the next station and civilization ( 30 Klm away). Be light when hiking you will get some portable water and a shelter to get God about 3 Klm from the beginning. It was a very nice experience It an be very foggy

We hiked down to Jungmun Beach from the Lotto Resort and had a  great time.  The schlep was a little strenuous for a 70 year old especially on the way up.  We went pretty early in the morning on a grey and rainy day at the end of June.  There we no crowds but the water was rough and dangerous for swimming.  This made the whole scene romantic and enjoyable.  The trip was worth the effort but how worth it for you will depend on the weather and the crowds. We walked the beach as part of Olle Trail #8.  We got lost a couple of times.

We climbed to the top of Mt.  Hallasan via the seongpanak trail. We are in just above average shape and we had no issues getting to the top with not stops in 2hrs 40 mins. There are three rest areas along the way that you can stop at if you need a good break. The last 1.5k to the top is the real shocker. We did not do our homework and went up real early on the morning and it was so windy and cold we did not stay long at the top. It was cloudy at the top anyway so we were not able to see 20 feet off the mountain so we headed back down. There is little to no people climbing the mountain at 6am but I'm out way down there was more people ascending to the top. Overall it was a good trip but I recommend bringing a windbreaker and not starting until around 7 on a clear day.

We choose Yeongsil Trail as it's the easiest but too bad in less than 1km we had to turn back. We were there in early April 2014 and the wind was blowing like crazy and it was very cold. Reason for turning back? We spotted ice and in no way wearing the suitable clothes for the climb. We even saw the waterfall freezes. Astounding and beautiful. The trees were all bare and yellowish. Don't expect greenery at this time of year.

Took the longest trail to Mount Hallasan peak (Seongpanak Trail) - 9.6 km - but started a bit late and did not make the cut-off time at the Jindalrae shelter (7km). However it was a great walk and I visited the Saraoream peak on a side tril on the way back.  This was well worth it as there is great view and also a beautiful crater lake.  It is key that you start early and take enough water with you.  Also need good shoes. Although it was August - most of the trail is in the forest - so not so hot.

Today I hired a car and drove to Hallasan National Park. Only 1000 won to enter and park.Plenty of clean toilets. An excellent Visitor center who gave me an informative map. I did not have time to do Eorimok Trail today but will do tomorrow.I climbed the Eoseungsaengak Trail which is only 1.3km and has wooden steps all the way up so no problem with any fitness level.30 minutes up to the top. Great 360 deg.view of the surrounding mountains and a small Japanese bunker to see too. Friendly Jackdoor birds wanting a scrap of food..

This waterfall was a 15 min walk away from where we were staying. The trail which led to this waterfall is amazing with great views of the ocean. Waterfall itself is pretty amazing and great opportunity for few pics.

There are 7 trails that you can climbs the mountainBut there are 2trails  only to reach to the top.Since i took 4courses i will explain where i visited that is also most people goTo SummitTrails : If you want to go to the top there are 2trails Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa  trail. Normally people go up by Seongpanak and go down by Gwaneumsa since Gwaneumsa is more difficult to go upTaking time : round trip takes 9 to 10hours so you better start your day early otherwise they will stop you to go up in some area Especially Jindalrea shelter will close at 1230pm or 1pm which can be vary depends on seasonAlso on your way to Jindalrea shelter there is another short trail Sara oreum which is really beautiful and takes only 40min. so it is YOU MUST VISIT place unless you are not hurry by time.How to get to : from Jeju bus terminal there is a bus that ofpen goes every 15min and takes 30min For beautiful viewTrail : Yeonsil trail and Eorimok Trail People normally go up by Eorimok and go down by Yeongsil but for me the opposit is betterTaking time : round trip takes 5hours and easy to walk if you like climbingHow to get to : there is only one time every hour so you better check in the termimalEorimok takes 35min from terminal and Yeonsil is 2stops more from EorimokPersonally i prefer Eorimok and Yeongsil trails.Also i highly recommend you to have climbing shoes otherwise your feet will be beaton up by rocks and enough waterall trail has shelters that sell food and drink but you better bring your own water Even it rains it is another feeling climbing mountain very attractive to go with lots of fogI never thought it is good to climbs when raining but i liked it a lotHowever prepare a nylon raincoat  from jeju bus terminal since it is very windy Poly raincoat would be ripped It is double price from the entranceThis is the best montain among i have visited in Korea

The wonder of nature in Jeju!Take note that there are a few visitor centers around Hallasan National Park.  Decide the trail you want to hike before heading to the visitor center.Info extract from VisitKorea website:Hiking Course - Seongpanak Trail: Seongpanak  Dongneung Peak9.6 km / 4 hrs 30 mins each way- Eorimok Trail:Eorimok  Nambyeok Bungijeom 6.8 km / 3 hrs each way- Eoseungsaengak Trail: Eorimok  Eoseungsangak Peak1.3 km / 30 min each way- Yeongsil Trail: Yeongsil - Nambyeok Bungijeom5.8 km / 2 hrs 30 mins each way- Gwaneumsa Trail:Gwaneumsa Temple - Dongneung Peak8.7 km / 5 hrs each way

Oh my GOD!! The hiking to the top was a BIG challenge for just an average walker.... You definitely need to be fit to be able to hike with an ease... as the name suggests it is a hike to the peak! The trail was very well built with stairs and was well supported with a railing all the way to the top. I was certainly glad that I nearly killed myself to get to the top!

Me and family went to Halla Park. I was 7month pregnant so I could not attempt the long Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trail to the summit. We picked the shortest hike Yeongsil Trail. It is about a 3.7k trail from Yeongsil Rest Area to the Witsae ?Oreum Shelter one way which took me about 2 hours of gentle walk to get to the turnaround point. The trail was well signed and marked. It was a busy day on the tail with a whole school of high school kids out for an organized hike. But the view of the trail is still very nice. The steps were all well maintained so I had no issue of going up and down by myself. I will definitely come back to attempt the longer trail to the summit in the future.
Located along Olle 7 (I believe) Oedolgae is a gorgeous coastline and certainly worth a visit! Spend the day walking the Olle trail and stopping for drinks and snacks along the way. Recommended!

It takes 45-60 minutes to hike around the whole trail. The trail is diverse in the scenes that it presents along different coastal views. Brace yourself for high wind speeds during the colder months. There are a lot of inclines/declines on the trail so be wary of that on the way. There are a couple of restaurants/eateries spotted along mid-trail but I have no comment on those establishments. Before the trail officially begins there is a little rest-stop with coffee shops convenience stores and restrooms so I would recommend using the facilities before you embark on your hike.

It is away from the main city but easily accessable.  It is a sand beach which is rare for this volcanic island.  You can rent kayaks and paddleboats on the beach and there is a nice mountain overlooking the ocean which has nice trails and views.
It is 1 km trail one way and nothing much. The ground is uneven so a good footwear is essential and can be a bit cool.

If you like to visit beautiful scenery this should definitely be one of the places you go in Jeju. If you start near the beach it'll only take you a few minutes to see the best parts. If you're like me and you enjoy seeing a bit more you can walk for about 10-15 minutes along a boardwalk trail up the estuary. The trail (and river) are next to the road the whole time so it's a very easy walk. I'd probably recommend starting up the river a bit and walking to the beach that way the scenery gets nicer and nicer as you go.As for the kayaks I had no expectation of being able to go on one since the reviews all suggest you have to come early and wait for a long time. It was a pleasant surprise then that the kayaks were not operating. There were none to be seen anywhere. This was great because it meant there weren't too many people and the river looked serene with no one paddling around in it.If you're keen on doing the kayaks people have told me that they're stopped for good  and other people have told me that they're just stopped temporarily. I would recommend calling a tourist office or tour agency to find out the latest news.
I revisited this place after being away for 1.5 yrs. Still love the hike. Do visit the cafe along the trail.My wife loves to take photos along this trail. Worth the visit if you like to hike.

I have spent years reading about WW2 history so it's a sobering experience to walk the same places as the men and women who fought and died in that conflict. Altteureu Airfield was a WW2 Japanese airbase that sits in a strategic corner of Jeju Island  midway between China and Japan. In the 1930s bombing missions were launched from here to Shanghai  later it was a training base. There are 19 remaining concrete hardened shelters sized for a Zero fighter and Jeju has done a good job with preserving the site (even though most of it is active farmland)  adding a large parking lot and bathroom  and placards to explain the history and locate the structures. It's right on the Olle trail so there are many hikers passing through and it's easy to find from the shore road by car.

I go here every day to walk up the steep hill to the right of the beach for exercise.  It's the start of the No. 19 Olle Trail.  I usually always see bride and grooms having their photos taken on the beach and in the fields of rapeseed.  Views from the top of the hill are amazing.  Sometimes if there are horses around I'll pick grass and feed them in exchange for a little pat and nuzzle from them.  If you look carefully there are quite a few different flowers around.  If you pick a green rapeseed that hasn't yet flowered and peel the stalk you can eat the stalk.  It tastes like sweet brocalli.  The cherry blossoms are lovely there too if you happen to be there in early April.  The water is clear.  I like to feed and water some of the stray dogs.  It kills me that I can't give them a home.  They appreciate a bit of a cuddle too but you can see their priority is getting food.  There are some very good restaurants in Hamdeok as well.  Ive put a pic of one of the ones on the main street of Hamdeok. .its a local one that serves a set menu at lunch time and its very good.  The sunsets are spectacular.

I did the Seongpanak trail on my own and it's pretty manageable. There are many koreans hiking along with you (there was rarely any moment that i was completely alone) even on a normal weekday. The climb gets tough towards the top but the view and sense of achievement will be worth it. Do start early and pack some food as you probably will get super hungry on the way down. It gets windy at the top so a jacket would be handy to avoid catching a cold as you would have sweat a lot on the way up.

Hiked up from Yeongsil trail. The trail is amazing and full of surprises. The trail starts out as a forested path then opens up to a breathtaking and liberating view of the surrounding. Can see as far as Seowipo city in the south of Jeju. The hike up is long and can be challenging for elderly visitors. There are sufficient rest areas along the way. Cater around 4 to 5 hrs for a return trip.

Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

Gwaneumsa Temple is close to Jeju National University and about 1 KM from the Gwaneumsa trail head to go to the top of Halla-san (the tallest mountain in South Korea).  I've been to the temple many times and always found it peaceful and beautiful.  Usually there were not many people here either so you can enjoy some quiet time.

A wonderful way to enjoy beautiful Udo is actually by walking the Olle Trail 1-1. There's a total of 26 trails totaling 425kms round Jeju. Website jejuolle.org. Distance is 11.2km which covers the major places on the island. Trail starts & finishes at Cheonjin-hang(port) where you arrive by ferry from Seongsan Harbour. Its a relatively easy & flat trail taking 3-4hrs. Only slight challenge is Udo Peak. There is a century old lighthouse at the peak with a Lighthouse Park with miniature lighthouses in Korea & around the world as you make you descent. Need to watch out for scooters & buses while walking.

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.

Yeongsil was a wonderful trail leading up along the mountain to see clouds pass through you while you're near the top of the trail. It had a wonderful view of the island, and looks like it came from a k-drama.Eorimok trail on the otherhand is boring, 1 km longer then Yeongsil. We wanted to go back a different way and regretted it. Skip this trail.

Wow. Just wow. We're beginners climbing up Seongpanak trail (longest trail, 9.6km). I thought I was never going to make it! But the people going down were very encouraging. Try to go early, as the carpark will be full by 9. Entrance is free, but you have to pay for the parking. Take note - you gotta reach the peak by 1.30. They'll start chasing people down by then, because you don't want to get stuck up there in the dark (trek takes approximately 4.5 hours one way) Oh, the weather was really good; it was sunny and not a cloud to be seen. It gets pretty hot up there so wear sunscreen. The lake was quite dry though.

Wow! I'm glad I saw this before leaving! Jeju is full of surprises and this is one of them. We were extremely lucky this was a foggy day because seeing this place in fog was really special.  The amazing display of wood carvings etc at the wood exhibition place was amazing as we're all the large insects carved out of cedar wood. It's a 20 min drive from Jeju City. Apparently in summer you have to protect your lunch from the crows! A nice easy walk and an oreum (hill) trail if you want something a bit harder. There are lots of carved statues all along the way and one of those stone paths which you can walk on with your shoes off.  I manage about 2 feet, too hard for me! Haha!

When you get to the top theres the most beautiful view you will ever see. Im not an adult so if you are planning to go with your family just go, Jeju itself is really pretty but this mountain is exceptional, if you have the kind of teens/children that like challenges and adventures it is a must. I believe it is SO much better on spring or summer, cause i went on winter and the landscape is beautiful with all the snow but at the top its super cold and windy and the lake is freezed of course so you can not really appreciate it at all and it may make you think like you hiked all that enormous mountain(trust me the journey to the top is HUGE)  for just a freezed lake. Anyway its really amazing amazing, but i personally hated the way down, theres a trail for the way down opened all the year except from winter, so you have to go down the same way you went up and im just gonna say i fell 4 times. Go on spring or summer.

When we arrived at the Peak, the hiking trail appeared quite intimidating because of the height and length of the trail.  However, once we started up the trail, we were presently surprised that the trail was quite easy actually - only a lot of steps on a very well maintained trail.  The views on the way up and at the top were fantastic (see photos)!  This is a must place to see in Jeju.

What a way to experience another side of Korea on an extinct volcano. The view at the summit was amazing. Suitable for ages, but a certain level of fitness is definitely required. The park is well maintained and well kept by the government. However, if you are looking for something more unpaved or natural this might not be the right trail as everything is already nicely laid out. (You will never get lost)

Went on a day hike up and down the Seongpanak trail! It was a gorgeous day, about 18C and I couldn't have asked for better weather. It took about 10 hours round trip. Started around 8:30am and made it down by 6:30pm. Luckily the sun didn't go down until 7:15ish so I had plenty of light to guide me.Now, I am not a hiker by any means and this was one of the toughest hikes I've been on. To be honest, it wasn't because the trails were all that difficult - it was actually quite pleasant through the woods and there were 2 rest stops along the way. The first stop is basically a bathroom break and the 2nd had some food available before heading up the last (somewhat steeper) trail to the lake up top. Oh, by   food   I mean some cup ramen and snacks. They also sold water and sports drinks. It would be helpful for you to bring food of your own. They also have no garbage cans so you need to carry and dispose of your own trash once you get back down.The reason why this trail was difficult for me was because I simply wasn't ready for a 20km hike! By the last 5km of the descent, I felt my feet and legs were going to fall off or give in to becoming jelly due to all the stairs and rocks. Make sure you have proper shoes! All in all, I'm glad I did this hike - it was worth it when I got to the top and was able to experience amazing views and clean air. And the flowers!! It was simply beautiful. Just expect to have sore calves for a few days following :)

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long? It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

we were definitely not prepared for this - in terms of experience and equipment!started off at about 9am on the Eorimok route. the entrance was a 10 min walk from the bus stop. then, it was off on the hike!initially the trail was straightforward. then it gradually went into a steep ascent. the path was quite rocky and unstable. but there were sufficient rest stops along the way. also people going in the same and opposite direction to you so you will not be alone (unless you hike in the middle of the night)there were also multiple signboards along the route providing interesting facts about Hallasan and also maps showing your current location and remaining distances to go to the next point.there was almost a natural portable water point where you can refill your bottles. remember to stay hydrated throughout and take breaks when needed.needless to say, the views along the route were truly breathtaking but the higher elevation you reach, the colder it becomes. also, the winds were very strong!we reached the Witseoreum shelter at about 12pm and had lunch there. The locals actually brought hot water in their thermos flasks and had cup ramen there!after lunch, we started our descent on the Yeongsil trail and reached the entrance of Yeongsil at about 2pm and there was a 2km walk out of the entrance to the bus stop.by then our legs were aching and heavy, but we pushed on. overall the hike took about 5 hrs.in summary, we should have worn more proper hiking footwear, wear thicker clothing (as higher you go, the colder it gets) and more food and snacks!we decided we will come back to attempt the summit next time.

We went with our boys for a short hiking. Jeomul Oreum trail is shady and only takes 45min. There are few junctions at the top of the trail which might be confusing. The maps say one big round trail, ultimately it is the same way up and down. If you took the wrong trail, it will lead to 5km trail. Overall good and short trail for the kids.

We went up the Gwaneumsa Trail and down Seongpanak and thought it was a great route.
