Will try it again one day.P/S: it is a natural place so not clean bathroom. A very natural way of toiletry but I really don't like it but can't blame!!

I am a complete beginner to mountain climbing but was there thankfully with an experienced climber. We took a taxi from jeju city to Seongpanak visitor centre and the journey costs around 20,000 krw and approx 40 min. I was there on 7 December after a snowy night, and the trails were covered in snow. Poles, proper hiking shoes and crampons are absolute necessity as the snowy paths were hard to walk.  Gwaneumsa, the popular trail for descent after reaching the crater summit, was closed that day as the snowy trail was too dangerous, so it was pretty rough to get up while people are trying to get down. Especially since the trail was already made quite narrow by the snow. However, the view is great and it's like a winter wonderland all the way up. The last stretch to the crater summit was hard for a complete beginner like me. It was however considered easy for seasoned hiker like my friend. On the whole a great experience and certainly worth the trouble for the views but would recommend complete beginners like me to do some training before getting up. The rest stops are well stocked and constant announcements were made (in Korean only) to keep the hikers moving up before the gate closes at 12 pm and down before it's gets dark. Note: we were staying in Jeju city before the climb and the weather was grim with lots of rain. The weather on Hallasan was however completely different. Sunny and pleasant for climbing.  Be sure to check the weather forecast on Hallasan and not Jeju!

Hiking up Mt Hallasan was such an incredible adventure - you really can't experience the island for what it is without giving it a go. The vegetation on the volcano changes as you get higher, ranging from lush dark-green forests and pines, to beautifully unusual flowers and scrub as you get closer to the summit. There are several trails up the mountain, but only two reach the summit - Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa. Seongpanak is the easiest, but is a long trail (19.2km return), whereas Gwaneumsa is one of the most scenic. The views from the summit really are breathtaking, and quite unusual if you have never hiked up a volcano before. Hiking up Hallasan was a great way to experience South Korea's natural beauty.

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

Highly recommend everyone to do at least one of the Jeju Olle trail routes. We chose route 6 as it?s being classified as the easiest route. The route is filled with beautiful sceneries. Some part of the route takes you onto the roads, into the bush, along the coastal and up some hilly roads. We meet a lot of locals along all way and they are helpful & friendly. Lot of cafes for one to take a rest too.

Hallasan was a good challenging climb, with the hike splits into 3 parts. The first 2 hour or so, we were hiking through mostly level ground, some rocks and little steps. As we reach the middle ground, the trail gets steeper, more rocky and almost half are made up of steps, mostly made of rocks. Using a hiking stick at this time really helps in making the climb easier. When it rains, which happened the entire day when we went, the ground gets covered with puddles and pools of water, so it was extra effort trying to choose the rocks to step on to avoid getting our feet wet. Towards the top, there are flights and flights of steps, followed by a trail made of rocks where u have to use a rope to climb up the steep rocky surface. It was challenging but overall, felt good.As it was raining, we didn't manage to get any view of the crater or lake at the summit. But the sense of accomplishment making it up was great!The way down was more challenging as after a day of rain, the trail became wetter and what used to be steps, some were submerged in water. Hence, even with a good waterproof shoes, ur feet could still get wet. Also, note that the sky turns dark at around 5pm in winter and there's no lighting in the reserve. Hence, make sure u buffer enough time to reach the foot of the mountain before that time. Otherwise, u would be hiking in the dark. Nevertheless, there would be a ranger moving down the rail lines in a cabin moving on a rail line, looking for stranded hikers. So no need to panic. However, I would still recommend planning well, checking the weather and choosing a clear day to climb. Start early so as to buffer enough time to reach the 3rd rest station by 12pm, as anytime after that, they do not allow hikers to go up to the top. Think it is for safety reason to buffer enough time for the ascend and descend. Also, to wear waterproof shoes and if available, bring a hiking stick along. Do standby a raincoat in case of light drizzle. Also bring some food along. Though they sell instant ramen and some bento at the resting stations, it closes by 2pm or so and you don't want to end up hungry.  Lastly, enjoy the climb!

Halla Mountain or Hallasan is one sadistic hike. For the month of May 2018, Gwaneumsa Trail is the only trail open that summits Halla. Seongpanak is having maintenance done.We did Gwaneumsa Trail... with one slow hiker... we got to parking at about 7:30am and we were walking by 8:06am. It is beautiful and green, especially in Spring. There is one restroom stop about 1/4 way and another 3/4 way at Samgakbong shelter. There was no other support. Take water, take food, take toilet paper just in case.READ: There is only one potable water stop. It is after Samgakbong about 3.5 hours into the hike at the last downhill before the bridge and start of final red part of trail. There is a hose at the corner at bottom os stairs before the bridge. Fill up here both going up and down.Also wear good walking or hiking shoes. We witnessed two people's shoes rip up and one guy had to walk back 2.5 hours with no shoe. There is no rescue for small issues. There is a supply cart that goes up once or twice a day but only for serious rescue. There is AED in Samgakbong shelter too. No food for sale when we went in April 2018.The reason for the difficulty is the climb and distance... mostly on volcanic rocks... large ones... and lots of stairs of wood and of stone.We left at 8:06 and back in the parking lot at about 5:30. All day event. 9.5 hours going slow up Gwaneumsa Trail.

Halla mountain can be hiked in 3-5 hours easily. I have hiked the Seongpanak Trail (on the east side)  and the Gwaneumsa Trail (on the north side). These are the two trails that go all the way up to the summit. If you are fit, these runnable, but Geaneumsa trail especially gets very steep at the end. Get to your trail of choice early to miss the crowds, and also note that the half way points of each trail close around 12 (depending on the time of year it is sometimes 12:30). Een when it is foggy it is beautiful, but, of course, it is best when you can see clearly down to the crater lake and across off of Jeju to the ocean. Pack a lunch and enjoy it on top of the mountain! (Or instant ramen is the traditional food to pack).My favorite time to go is in winter when the top of the mountain is covered in a few feet of snow! Make sure to bring crampons for your shoes (simple ones are OK, you aren't hiking K2!)

Great and easy trails! The trails were well marked and well planned.  Yeongsil and Eorimok trails are shorter and varied in difficulty in different stretches.  Some stretches are as easy as flat wooden planks and some are uphill, climbing up small-midsize rocks.  It's a good half-day hike anyway!

Good, peaceful trail, starts slowly, then is quite steep for a while, then flattens out, nice views of a dome on its side. The path is well maintained, steps or planks lead almost all the way to the top. How to get there? By a taxi from Jungmun Beach (approx. 30,0000 Won). There also is a public bus. We went up on an overcast day, it was quite windy and chilly on top.

Good driving views.  You will be blown away. Should visit this place in the morning before 9am to avoid the crowd especially during weekend. There are so many trails.  Please ensure you know which trail you are taking as the mountain is so huge.  Must wear proper trekking clothes and shoes. If you are driving, please ensure you go down the same way as you climb up or else, you need to get a cab to bring you back to your car. Bring water, snacks and plastic bag to throw your rubbish. You must bring down your rubbish with you.

Fun hike that faces easy to difficult terrain.  Footing can be slippery at points and trail narrow at times.  Really crowded trail when we went!  Standing in line to hike at times isn't my thing, but still a fun hike.  It was not crowded on the way up because we hit it really early in the morning, but lots of people on the way down.Be prepared with good shoes and jacket as it can be really windy!There is a cutoff time to when you can hit a certain point.   There is a little snack place about 1/4 to half way up.

From the Jejusi bus terminal we took bus 201 to Udo. It took about 1 1/2 hours. Definitely download the app Naver to navigate your way around the island, as Google Maps does not have any results for public transportation. We spent 4 hours on the island. Ferry ride from the port is only about 15 minutes each way. Buying a ticket can be a little chaotic as there are no signs in English but we just held up 2 fingers for two passengers and were given 2 round-trip tickets. Upon arrival in Udo expect to be bombarded with shop owners yelling at you to rent bicycles, ebikes, motorcycles, or 3-wheeled cars (for 2 people). 2 people renting 2 ebikes for 4 hours cost us 40,000 won. Need int?l drivers license for the latter 2. I definitely recommend the ebike over the bicycle unless you really want to get strenuous exercise. Lots of hills and 11.4 km of trail to follow. Lots of little mini-towns where you can buy food, have coffee or peanut ice cream (recommend). Tons of photo opps so take your time. We finished in 3 hours, 40 mins (and my hubby wanted to stop A. LOT. Last ferry back to Jeju is at at 5 pm this time of year. Plan accordingly.

For hiking enthusiasts, this is a must do!  The Seongpanak (9.6km) trail has an average hiking time of 4.5 hours and Guaneumsa (8.7km) trail has an average hiking time of 5 hours.  One must reach the Jindallaebat Shelter by 1pm to be permitted an attempt at the Baekrokdam summit.  My husband and I completed the hike in 7hrs 35mins but were perplexed to understand how it took us 5 minutes longer to descend, given that we did not take breaks while descending. Guaneumsa has the reputation of being the roughest trail on the crater, but does live up to its reputation for breathtaking views.  - There was one potable water area on each trail where nature provided delicious water refills.  - Emergency posts appear through the trails, each with its own number, so keep track of the number in case you need assistance, rescue workers can narrow down your location.  - There are incredibly handy signs along the way to pinpoint your progress and identify the level of difficulty along the trail.  Paths are well maintained and varied; wooden, rocky, skree, etc. - If you take the bus to there is no fee for hiking.- Although we did not have cell phones with us, many folks seemed to be talking an walking throughout the trails.- We chose to end at the Guaneumsa trail head because it was the closest in proximity to our hotel.  Cabs are available at the trailhead.

For 1st time hikers climbing Mount Hallasan, take note of the different hike trails AND the closing time for each trail. This is especially if you drove on your own and parked at 1 of the 5 (one of the locals told me there are 5 different car parks at different foot of the mountain)If you are climbing Mt Hallasan to reach Baengnokdam (the crater top), do not take the Eorimok trail as it does not lead there. I made the 1st mistake taking this trail and the trail ended 3 quarters way up the mountain and you only get to see the side of the mountain top. I made the 2nd mistake not watching my time and could not descend Hallasan from the trail (Eorimok) where I came as apparently it closes at 2pm, and there was a park warden stopping me from taking the trail back and kept ushering me to take the other way (towards Donnaeko trail) to descend. The descend took 4 hours and the trail was treacherously full of rocks. You could tell that it was a trail less taken as there were over-grown bushes covering parts of the trail. Your only guidance of where to go was a      thin cord string tied from tree to tree and red strips of cloth tied on the string. If you weren't too careful and lost sight of the guiding string, you may actually go off tangent of the trail. There are no lights, very few signage and are all in Korean, so if you are like me with no understanding of Korean, good luck. And that wasn't the end. Donnaeko trail actually ends up at Donnaeko cemetery. So when I got to the foot of Hallasan, it was pitch dark (6pm+ and no street lamps), by myself, and I had to walk for 1 hour through the cemetery to get to Donnaeko car park (which was 30 mins driving distance away from Eorimok car park where my car was T-T).

First of all ensure you hike on a non rain day.  We were worried all week because it was raining.  We got a non rain day but cloudy. When got pass 1 km up it was beautiful sunny weather.Know there are 6 trails and they start in different places and not all go to the top. We took the Eorimok Trail (Northwest). It was one of the shortest. We didn't do good research and started too late to do a longer trail.I'm moderately fit. The trail was steep! I was definitely challenged for the first 2km. It was balance of even and uneven ground. Anyone can make it up but it might take you a bit longer if you were unfit. There isn't a drone restrictions and was able to take some great video. Bring water and food.  There are places near the top to grab instant noodles and water. There is no washroom on the way up.  Bring some tissue and wet wipes just in case.Although we didnt get to go to the summit, it is a must do while visiting. Jeju.

fascinating  view from bottom until top. but we went on saturday, pack with local hikers. the path is quite easy. about 18km back and forth using seongpanak trail. on the way back we tag along with the person incharge/worker of mt. hallasan, and being offered to use the little train to the way down. best of all, there is no entrence fee charge to hike the  national park.

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Easy access by bus 240 from Jeju Intercity bus station (about 45mins). Beautiful wet walk of about 4 hours, fairly tough Hike for us city dwellers as we were not equipped for the hike. Missed the bus stop on our way back and walk 20 mins in the wrong direction. A helpful bus driver stop to give us free lift to the correct bus stop so that we could catch the correct bus back to Jeju. Will be back during Spring or Summer next time to do the other trails.

Driving from the city to the Seongpanak trail is the most convenient way to do it, it's only 20 minutes away from the busy area of Jeju.I hiked the mountain at early morning January 01 and when i reached the Seongpanak trail the parking was crazy long that it goes as far as 1km from the side of the road. If you want to save time in walking you should be at the trail around 3am at Jan01. Anyway, the trail was relatively easy on the first 7km, it was cold around -1 to 5C that time, still manageable but the trail was slippery due to ice forming on rocks and the trail was covered with snow. So, to prevent accidents wear a mini crampons or a Yaktrak coil underneath your shoes.Don't worry hiking alone, you can do this without a guide, you probably are blind if you get lost out there. Also, the trail was properly maintained that hiking at the peak was a breeze except the last 2km of the hike. When you reached the final kilometers it starts to get steep, so take your time and avoid slippery rocks and you should be fine. Finally, the peak was amazing, you would be able to see sea of clouds if the weather permits. Overall not bad for a hike.

Don't forget to drive past the ticket booths to the real start of the trail, we some some poor gits having to hike up the twisty road which takes 5 - 10 minutes in a car.  Wear layers as it gets cool up high.  First part is through bush trail, we had a roe deer come across 10 m. away.  Then trails steepens to get to ridgeline, a little tough.  Nice views and steps on the ridge, then another transition to a boardwalk through a tundra like alpine area.  Go past WitseOreum to the 1700m. junction where there's a toilet and snack bar, hot cup noodles are the best.  You can go another 2 km closer to the crater but why bother? Pack out your garbage.  The man made plank trail is kind of artificial but keeps the humans on a defined path and generally keeps them out of trouble, all in all a good way to get the masses of all ages into the outdoors.

Disclaimer: Not a seasoned/experienced hiker. Was done on a cloudy day with a scattered drizzles.I had high expectations for the highest point in South Korea and a highly rated tourist attraction on TripAdvisor but was greatly disappointed by the experience.The reason I am giving a score of 1/5 is because there is a long hike (approximately 3-4 hours one way) with very little to see along the way, with ultimately what I would consider an   okay   view of a   crater lake   up the top. In addition, whilst walking the unpaved bits of the trail (rocks, which account for about half of the trails we walked) you will need to focus hard on walking to ensure you don't slip as it can be quite slippery. This means you don't have the luxury of looking around at the scenery/surroundings while doing the hike.It is not that the view up the top is objectively poor. It is actually decent. it is simply that the effort (3-4 hours one way) to reward (the view up top) ratio is terrible.The group of us hiked up the East trail (Seongpanak) and went down the North trail (Gwaneumsa). The hike down along the North trail provided a handful of views that were decent - better than the East trail.My experience at Mount Hallasan was preceded by Seongsan Ilchulbong the day before which to me provided a much much better experience. The hike was a lot easier and the view was much superior, offering a beautiful view of the Jeju City skyline. I personally would highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong over Mt Hallasan and would recommend against doing Mt Hallasan, unless you are someone that personally loves hiking as an activity anyway.Summary: Long 3-4 hour one-way hike (7-8 hours return) to the summit rewarded with a decent view, with a lot unpaved trail which can be slippery. Not good for people with bad knees, those expecting plenty of beautiful views, and those wanting to enjoy scenery while hiking.

Climbing Mt. Halla was a highlight of our trip to South Korea! We climbed up the Eorimok trail and then down the Yeongsil trail. I would recommend going this way because Yeongsil was a lot of stairs - I'd rather do that on the way down than up. Going up probably took us a little over two hours and wasn't too strenuous (though we are in good shape). The trails are very well kept and there are signs all along (in English) showing how far you've gone and how far you have left, and how easy/difficult the next stretch is. The view from the top (even though it wasn't even the top) was unbelievably beautiful! To get there, we hailed a cab from Jeju city. We just told him we wanted to start at Eorimok trail. I would recommend a cab because if you take the bus, you have a pretty large hill to walk up before you even get to the mountain because of where it drops you off. I think the cab cost about 15,000 won. The way home, we were waiting for a bus and then saw a cab so we hailed him. This guy charged us 30,000 won, I think because Jeju city was out of his way. Make sure to bring plenty of water - at least two bottles per person - and snacks.

Climbing Hallasan Mt. Is one of my bucket list and It's in jeju island thats why i love jeju. The climb is so worth it and really something you can achieve even choosing the most difficult trail. You get close to the nature as you walk through the vast rich forest with different species of trees, Hear the birds singing harmonizing with the crickets chirping, Colorful flowers & sighted a roe deer along the way. The sweats you get from those steep rocky path is nothing when you reach the summit, it was so awesome! witnessing the wonders of nature & learnt some historical events happened many years ago. It is well preserved and well managed. Definitely will come back again to try another trail to see more what hallasan Has to offer. RockNroll!P.S. Going there must wear proper hiking attire that suits the weather condition.You can still try to hike even though you're not that hiking type of person as the trail has pretty nice part. Just be pro and you're good to reach the summit! Have fun!

Certainly a must-visit destination in Jeju! Soak yourself in the impressive view of this UNESCO heritage site. We came on the first Monday of the month, and unfortunately the paid trail to the peak is closed. Blessing in disguise is that portion of the trail is open free to the public though it only brings us to mid-way - perfect for those who find it too challenging to climb to the top. Don?t miss the women divers show which is on the left trail, at the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Showtimes are 1.30 and 3pm. It?s complimentary. And you can choose to buy and eat fresh abalone at the little restaurant. Overall a truly relaxing and uplifting experience!

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Beautiful landscape, the trek is relatively easy to manage. Weather on the way up is was just perfect too, except it gets very chilly at the peak, so make sure you pack enough warm clothing up. The trail gets very slippery during wet days, make sure you have a pair of shoes with good grip. The route I did that morning - Seongpanak > Peak - Baengnokdam > Gwaneumsa.

Beautiful hike, I went up the Seongpanak trail and down Gwaneumsa. Hardly anyone around on the way down, was nice and peaceful. Contrary to what some info says online there is a public bus to/from Gwaneumsa during the week - the 475. The column in red of the picture below are the times to depart on this bus from the trail car park.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

An amazing scenic spot with stunning view. Try to hike along the trail for panoramic view of jeju island and the ocean. If you have limited time, it is not necessary to hike up the peak since the best scenery is blocked by the fences. The descending path has much better scenery that the ascending one! p.s. Try out the hanrabong ice-cream! One of the best way to recharge after hiking

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After hiking the Sunrise Peak, I was delighted by the fact that Jeongbang Waterfalls requires no rigorous hiking. We drove with our rental call and entered the phone number (7331530) into the GPS to get there. Parking is free. You just walk a short distance down a stairway and navigate through a few rocks to get closer to the waterfall. Overall, it is not difficult at all. The waterfall itself was so beautiful with the water flowing directly out to the ocean. If you've been to Yosemite, it kind of reminds me of the Vernal Falls/Mist trail without the heavy hiking up the steep steps. There were couples, seniors, and children sitting by the rocks enjoying the view. Of the three main waterfalls in the area, I would say Jeongbang is the best one.

Abu Oreum was a great easy hike.? Took about 45 minutes to get to the top, hike all the way around the crater, and get back down with a 5-year-old and 7-year-old walking.? There is a trail into the crater that we didn’t take.? The climb itself from the parking lot to the top is less than 10 minutes. Has beautiful views of the countryside around it and a very pleasant walk past some cows and a small forest. It was also very easy to find and park.

Absolutely hike Oedolgae, it's a beautiful coastal walk that is part of an Olle trail. You wind all around a part of the southern coast of Jeju, and can walk as long as you please. Lots of shops and restaurants along the way. The Jeju trails are my favorite attraction on Jeju, definitely walk one! And they're free!

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.
A counterpart of Giant?s Causeway. It?s part or along the Olle trail of Jeju. The viewing place is not that big, but if you are visiting Jeju, it is worth visiting.

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.

You want free entrance? Then go to this place and plunge into warm sea water in a cold weather.You will love the view and be amazed how the nature formed these rocks.The place is not so crowded by the time I visited this place.Going solo into this place. I met a kind Ajussi who lives in Jeju. He guided me to reach the top of the rock formation. He always come to this place to see dolphins and observe sunset.

You should go there. Lovely view. Great for riding a bike around the island. It takes only 1-2h only but the view is so stunning. You should not eat at restaurants at the dock. There is a lot of places to eat along the way. Food is a bit more expensive but acceptable.

You need a certain level of fitness to be able to climb the many steps to the top. Great views along the way but the view from the top is spectacular. Very popular destination so prepare for the crowds.

Would have been nice to visit for sunrise but we were reliant on public transport. Still glad we did it in the morning. Jeju is alot larger than we thought and it was more than an hour to get there on the bus from the bus station. It's less than 200m high but it felt like a struggle to get to the top! I think we took about half an hour for the climb. The pathways are very well laid out and it was very busy with visitors. Nice view while climbing. Right at the top it's more the crater you see so it was a sea of green when we were there. Defo worth a visit when in Jeju. From there we travelled to Seogwipo

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.
we're always trying to give a satisfaction to the visitor. thank  you so much for the review and have a nice day .

Went to this as part of a tour. The view from the coach as your ?defying gravity? is of a coach full of people craning their necks not straight ahead which you need to get the perspective. This is something thats maybe worth doing on the way to somewhere else but don?t go out of your way for it.

Went there as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It is a great walk and views. Avoid if raining or cloudy. The walk to the top of what is known in English as Sunrise Peak is quite strenuous and involves a lot of stairs. There are rest stops along the way. There are no lifts. It can get quite windy so jackets are required. There is a town centre area at the base with restaurants and shops.
We were wondering near our hotel and found the falls it was a great way to spend afternoon.  Lots of stairs so wear good shoes...but every step is rewarded with a beautiful view ?

We went to the beach after hallim park. It was a nice place for my little one to run around as the sand is very soft. Must be a lovely place to relax in summer. The view was beautiful. Lovely cafes along the way and we had nice pizza.
We went there on our way back after U-do. It offers such a gorgeous view of Jeju-do and it was a short hike - return trip of less than 1 hour. Definitely worth the hike!

We went there and reach to the top at noon time. So it's pretty hot! So I'd like to suggest you to come early in the morning. The view from the top is very nice. The way to go up is not that tough and you will reach to the top sooner than you expect.

We stopped by Wolijeongri Beach for about 30 min. on the way to UDO; the water was very clear.  There were kids playing sand on the beach. The view was peaceful. We enjoyed our short walk along the beach. You can get some snacks and a good coffee from a caf챕 or a convenient store nearby. There is a restroom facility too.

We started at 9am before the busloads Of tourist started arriving. It was a tough hike because the flights of stairs were literally endless. There were many resting areas along the way and I was not shy about just sitting on the stone benches to catch my breathe. Many reviewers shared that they took between 20 to 40 mins to reach the summit. I took 1 full hour. The stairs and tracks were well maintained and most stretches had handrails. The views at mid point and the summit were superb and makes this hike so rewarding! Don?t miss visiting this UNESCO world heritage site!

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

We made a wrong turn and found this place by chance.? Amazing view. The bridge connects you to bird Birds Island. It's 1.2km walking path. Best to visit before the Sunset and you will be blown away with the views around this area. A good place to stroll and relax.

We Enjoyed a leisure walk amidst the lovely silver grass swaying with the wind blowing :) reaching at the top ud be surprised to see swings  perched on top of the hill with piped in music. Love to just sit  there and enjoying the view and wind.the climb is not too hard as compared to other attractions.

We drove to check this Estuary out and we werent disappointed at all.Love the scenic view especially when the Estuary meets the Ocean half way....u have to see it for yourself... Good place to chill and there are cafes to while some time away too...

We drove down here on our way around the Island and I'm glad we did.It was a Spectacular view with a Deep Blue Ocean and clean fresh air.It was only a short hike to the top but worth every minute of it

We came to this museum based on the previous reviews and came away extremely disappointed. The displays are very average and there's really not too much to see inside the display hall. The tunnel with the dioramas (which looked to be the most interesting one) was locked while we were there. There were no signs to indicate why it was closed or when it would re-open.The other tunnels were OK but once you've seen one tunnel you've seen them all - and the fairy lighting in the tunnels did seem a little out of place considering their history. There is a lot of painful history in this area but the museum fails to capture and relay it.It would have been better to see more of the human history alluded to in the video display in the other displays.Note that a lot of the pictures for this Trip Advisor listing may not actually be of this museum - we were quite confused trying to find it based on these pictures and they make it seem a lot grander than it really is.Overall wouldn't recommend and wouldn't go back.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

Was there during winter  thus not much water can be seen under the bridge. Can see far away on the bridge  and the view was nice. Other than that  nothing much at the attraction. There was one fountain of various animals heads  and supposedly you are to face any one of them to throw in a coin and make a wish according to what you wanted.

Walk to the top is quite easy with good views.Don't miss the signpost to the women divers near the bottom on the way down.  They do a few shows a day and you don't have to pay extra to see it.Lot's of parking and eateries in the area

Walk about 5 minutes from the parking lot to arrive at wide open grass field that showcases a cliff side view out to sea.There are tall columns of rock formation that are the site's main attraction.You can also peer down the cliff side walkways down to the waves crashing against the bottom of cliffs.Pathway consist of some stairs and portions just muddy... May be rectified as they were doing some renovation work on paving those sections.

Visited Sangumburi Crater as our first stop from Jeju city centre. It was in the morning and was rather cooling and relaxing. Not much visitors at the time. Sangumburi Crater was one of my favorite attractions of Jeju (the other being Udo-bong). It was a short stroll along the way and viewing of the greenery and flowers.

View is beautiful but too crowded It pretty amazing that such nature formation is almost perfect for taking beautiful shots which make the place looks so big in actual it is quite small Perhaps should have more viewing point or benches along the way  so can just seat n enjoy the serene  view
Thoroughly enjoyed this gallery. Visually spectacular especially with accompanying music. A very different way to view art.

This waterfall is beautiful in that the water falls all the way to the rocks in the ocean unimpeded.  You have to scramble on rocks to get closer or you can remain on the landing at the bottom of the steps and get a pretty good view.

This stadium had an awesome design. I wouldn't travel far to see it but it was on the way so I popped it. I couldn't go inside so viewed from behind the gate. I can imagine watching a game their would be great

This site explains everything one needs to know about the island's historical past.  It has a long walkway leading one through outdoor exhibit areas each section with attendants who can give information.  There also was a traditional musical performance available to view.  It was chilly when we were there so we left earlier than desired but if we had known there was a cafe in which to warm up and perhaps have lunch we could have made a day of it.  One perk of going in February was that the crowds were very very small here and at other locations.

This place was way beyond my expectations.We visited most of aquariums in north east america since we have a little child and live near by new york city but this aquarium is one of the best compares to those in america.2yr old facility has lots of displays and shows.Very clean and up close displays so children can find interests.You should watch aqua aerobic and sea animal show. It is fun and amazing.The view from the building is spectacular.We found great deal with 20% off admission on internet so it was worthy for about $30.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: This place still exists as of April 2019. It's an amazing place for kids and they have so many toys and so much equipment. If your kids know about Tayo the little bus the place is magic and if they don't well it is still a pretty good kids play cafe. There's a cafe selling drinks and food. While as noted in the previous review the staffs English isn't good but is sufficient and they try to help. We have been to this Tayo cafe and some in Seoul as well. This one is much bigger and has more and better play equipment overall. It was also way less busy than the ones in Seoul and slightly cheaper @ 12k won per child and 3k won per adult compared to 15kw won per child and 5k won per adult in Seoul. Note: Visits are capped at 2 hours (or I'm sure the kids can play there all day)Tip: Ask the staff about riding the Tayo car ride as they are not always on but when you request a staff member will assist with it. Also the pork cutlet and rice were pretty decent for the kids (and adults) to eat.

This place has great views  beautiful falls  and a cool folk tale about the nymphs or fairies that visit the falls. Not a particularly difficult walk  but if you have trouble with stairs  pace yourself. Only gave it 4 of 5  because the biggest and best falls are not always running. Best views require a visit after the rains. Definitely still a must do while in Jeju. Only need about 1-1.5 hours here.

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

THis Maze Park is located between Manjanggul Cave and Gimnyeongsagul Cave. It was designed by the world famous company and jeju National University. The Park contains a maze that has 7 view incorporated in it. and here are three skywalks called ?gureum dari? and an observatory. There are four ways to get through the maze from the entrance. We had funny and enjoyable time!

This is one of my wife's favourite walks. A lovely circular amble around the Songaksan peninsula mostly on boardwalks and steps. Lovely views of the unique geology of the cliffs. Can see pheasants cormorants peregrine falcons and occasionally dolphins if you're lucky. You can walk up to the summit which affords stunning views back to Sangbansan and Hallasan (clear day required). If you are that way inclined there's a Starbucks at the start/finish too.

This is a world heritage site where a pathway leads to the peak of a long dead volcano. There are great views along the way. On the path leading downstairs to the ocean beach- they have the women divers show-at 1:30 and 3 pm as well as a seafood restaurant.

This is a must-do! You get to the peak using staircases which allows any age group to do this activity also. There are also toilets along the way. The view of the peak as well as Jeju Island is amazing.There are shops where you can buy souvenirs. You should try the tangerine ice cream 'cuz it's yummy!
This is a must visit here in jeju island. The climb is much easier than it looks.Take some beautiful pictures along the way and more at the summit.Enjoy the view and breeze at the top.

This being my first time in Jeju Island it was an unforgettable experience riding around the circumference of the island. The view of the ocean was breathtaking and being on a bicycle allowed me to experience the island in a very tangible way. Honestly it was physically very challenging for me. The first day we were riding wasn’t so bad but on the second day the path was constantly switching between big uphills and big downhills. On the third day it was pouring rain and the winds were so strong! But even though it was hard this experience was very empowering.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!

There are places in Jeju that convince you that you made the right decision to go there -- they're just really beautiful. Oedolgae is one of those places. It's just a photo spot that will take about 15 minutes of your time. The rock formation is interesting and the place is just lovely in a natural way. I gave this a 4/5 because it's not difficult to get there from the entrance of the park -- no steep mountains and such to climb in order to see the view.There's not much to do here -- just check it out and move on.
The view from the bridge is really pretty but we wanted to see the fall and you could barely see it because it was so far away.

The scenery is definitely beautiful and you feel achievement and reward once you make it to the top but the journey up is steep. If you are not in shape like me it can take a while but stopping along the way to look down and enjoy the view is nice.

The road to this temple is a single carriage way and you drive carefully.  Parking is free. Before I reached the temple I can hear the chanting and is was so soothing.  It just calm a city travellers. I didn't take any pictures inside the temple only the surrounding. It would be great to have a audio or a translator/guide to explain more of this historical and majestic temple.  The sea view from the temple is stunning. Do check out the temple second floor.

The most memorable thing was rather on the ferry to Udo Island.The seagulls were hovering over those who had Calbee prawn crackers ready to feed them. They followed the ferry from Jeju all the way to Udo. That was a sight!Udo generally has good scenic views and interesting coral beach with clear blue waters.

The hike up to the crater is quite easy with elevation gain of less than 100m and even my elderly mother can do it. There are several routes to choose from and we took the easy route that winds through fields of thatch grass. The view along the way was just beautiful. At the top you can look down into the huge crater which has a circumference of 2km.

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.

The cliffs are carved by the sea and you can walk the pillars of these cliffs all the way around the small outlet. Be careful not to slip and fall as it is very wet and very rocky. But the view and the scene and the smell of the sea are all worthwhile. There is also some small nearby attractions and food stalls

The beach's sand is actually volcanic sand/ash which is why it's black and on a good sunny day the view is marvelous. I'm not sure if it's a lucky occurrence but we spotted jumping fish a distance away from the shore line. I didn't have time to but you can rent transparent kayaks to explore the river which apparently has a whirlpool (not that dangerous according to my guide) at the head. The water is quite clear so you may actually be able to see fishes under the kayak. Otherwise enjoy the picturesque view of the estuary.
thank you so much for the visit and a good review. we always try to give our visitors good memories during the travel. we hope to see you again someday ^^

Temple is nice design and along our walk we found many tangerines tree which I believe during the spring season the temple view will be good. Since It's FOC do drop by if you have time. It's along the way to Teddy Bear Museum and Cheonjeyon Fall Yeomiji Botanical Garden

Sunrise Peak. Sunset PeakWe travelled as part of a tour and on arriving were given the usual coach departure time. 1hour in this instance! Not sure of the entrance fee as it was included in our tourNot hanging around we set off immediately for the top with several good rests in between. The pathway is steep in places but in good order with plenty of resting/passing places. Separate paths up and down. Quite a climb but well worth it. Half way up is a little stall/shop for soft drinks and snacks (they have to manhandle everything up!)Once at the top there are plenty of viewing spots. Really worth the climb. We witnessed a superb sunset over the island and took some wonderful photosOn the path down there is a WC.We made the round journey just about in time with 15mins at the peak and a wander around the cliff edge on the way downFrom what I?ve heard the sunset is equally as breathtaking as the sunrise but not as crowded. Sunset was at approx 7.30 and on the way down the path is fairly well lit

Steep climb up the hill but the view worth every step. The stair halfway up is quite steep and a bit of a challenge if u have a bad knee. The best time to go is either for sunset or sunrise. There is only 1 shop to buy water up there. Make sure you have your water with you for the climb.

Songaksan was one of the places that had actually a very small crowd of tourists so it make the hike a bit more enjoyable. At the foot of the mountain is a large parking lot with some coffee shops and restaurants from there it is a light hike up the mountain. Lots of greenery and nice views along the way. The center which I believe is a crate is closed right now I think for recovery from too many tourists. it is still a good destination to visit the hike is easy and relaxing peaceful and enjoyable.

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!
Simply amazing. From the moment you start the climb up till you reach the submit the views wqs just out of this world. Once on top it is just wow all the way. A must do.

Seongsan Ilchulbong also called as Sunrise Peak! It's located on the Eastern end of Jeju do Island. There is a huge crater at the top of the peak!  The place is really wonderful with magnificent view. Strong wind. Cooling. The way up are well prepared and safety. Suitable for children  so no worried.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

read reviews on this place and thought should visit and ee all the hype. To start of with there is an entrance fee of 12000 KW its not worth it for the exhibits and it was all in Korean so really didn't get it at all. Anyways since I was already there just make the most of it. nothing so special so you can give this a miss if you have spare time enjoy the beach view is much better than wasting time here.

Place where you can consider one of the exercise from steps and all the way to the end to view the nature of Lava.You can learn about the Manjanggul Cave as there's information along the way. Cool weather as we went during the winter. Not sure if you go during any other season.Must come as you might not get it from your own country.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.
One of the pit stop along the way to Yongmeori Coast via halim park route. Offer a great view. Ample prking space is available.

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). The only down side is that the area as well as the park have limited street lights so you'll be needing a torchlight to walk either early in the morning or at night.

One of my best spot in Jeju. We went in July end and the climate was very very hot. We were sweating like anything and in the mid way my wife said lets go back but i was like we have to go. But when we reached at the top it was so beautiful around. I forgot the stairs and all our exertion was gone. The view is so astonishing and it definitely looks like a world heritage.Tip: Do keep lot of water if visiting in summer.This peak has lot of stairs (not advisable old person or for heart patient).
not too bad to climb up as it looks. definately top 5 things to do in Jeju.I go there everytime I go to Jeju island.Always nice view and great feeling on the top.
Not have to hike too much. Look peaceful but nothing much to see and the view is not too impressive. Can see autumn leaves far away. Can spend less than one hour here.

Normally as everyone is aware that the aquarium always be busy and crowd with people. Here also crowd but it's not too tight since the space is very big. At the end of tunnel you will see the souvenir shop which I think the items are not too expensive.I think it's better than other place I have been since some places you may see people more than sea animals.At the exit of aquarium you can see the nice scenic view of Hallasan Mountain

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My friend and I enjoyed the hike up the stairs to the top and the view of Jejudo was worth the hike up. Took roughly 10-15 minutes to get up. There are rest stops on the way to the top. There are shops on the bottom if you need some energy before or after the walk :)

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Moonlight is a great walking activity to do with your friends or family. It's pretty easy and the view is awesome. We walked on a golf felid for about 30min until arriving at a cliff with a great ocean view. Walking barefoot on the grass felt fresh and was pretty fun! After watching the sunset we head to watch a mini-concert just for us! this was the perfect getaway to feel relaxed again!

Many steps to reach the grotto mid way up. Have to stop to rest many times but view is quite good. Also can make wishes and prayers as lots of altars for different things such as eternal love and to be blessed with a baby.

Magnificent views even I only managed to climb half way. Here you can see people mountain people sea. Young and old. No wonder it's declared as another 7 Wonders of heritage of South Korea. A very worthy place to visit.
Magic road which can run car without engine. Always full with tourist but safe. Actually the othe side of the road have spectaculare view. Also can have chance to try local food from stall around it.

It?s a must visit place in Jeju. The time I went there was in Winter but surprisingly all trees along with the side walk bloomed so much. The walk in the forest and a big fall blew my stress away. Enjoy the view!

It was quite a strenuous climb up to the shrine in the cave at the top. Although it was a very hot afternoon. The views on the way up are beautiful and you can see for miles. Lots of great photos. Places to eat and souvenirs at the bottom near the car park.

It takes a little effort climbing  up the peak but the fascinating view to Jeju from the top worth the climb. Do enjoy the view along the way & suggest to make an early morning trip to enjoy the stunning sunrise view from the top . There is haenyeo show beside the walking path which worth to explore how this great diving skill passing down the generation to women only divers can dive into the sea to pick up abalone & others sea produce without an oxygen tank

It is listed as a Unesco World Heritage and definetly a place to stop. Highway 1132 will bring you there and you cannot miss it. Be prepared that parking might not be easy and you may have to spend some time. The place is quite busy and many tourist buses are coming too. We had a cloudy day and it was very windy. Entrance fee is 2000 adult and 1000 child. Couple of shops at the entrance where you can buy each and everything. Please keep in mind that waste management is terrible as everywhere in Korea. If you buy something keep in mind that no any trash beans are available. The way up and down is quite crowded and loud. Obviously many tourists are rushing on top to get the selfies done to rush down again. The walk is definetly nothing for stroller or wheel chair. We went up slowly enjoying the view and getting some pictures. On top it is quite nice to look into the volvano and rest. Sure some pictures not to forget. But again very busy place and loud. Again our day was cloudy and windy but as long as it is not raining worth to visit the peak. So conclusion would be to visit the place very early.

In five visits to South Korea in four years I have not come across a museum palace or historical building I did not like.They are all well-maintained offer good information in Englishoften have multilingual guides and free tours and are free or cheap to get in.The Jeju National Museum is no exception. Our hotel was about 4km away and we walked to and from there seeing many interesting sights on the way and eating lot of local food.I am an unabashed fan of the curating skills of the Koreans; they do a very good job.Here they provided a great overview from prehistoric to modern times offering interesting exhibits and information.There was also a special exhibition on Canopus a star of great significance to the people who lived here.Entry is free. There are buses from the city and taxi fares are reasonable. We like eating so we need to walk.

Have to climb down the stairs with 3 kids. Very challenging task & we need slowly go down the stairs. It?s not that far. But the view & surrounding is worth it. Hallasan the 2nd highest mountain in South Korea is a fantastic hiking place!! You can choose to hike from two different easy routes to enjoy different scenery. If this is your first hike after a long hiatus do be mindful that it's better to take the easy route. Cos at some points it's huge boulders that require some stamina to step up.Take the first bus from the bus interchange cos it's advisable for tourists to reach midpoint by noon so that you have adequate time to trek back and catch the last bus from the bus stop which is still 20 min from the start of trekking point. Alternatively there's taxi if you are a group or pair. There's only a hut at midpoint which sells cup noodles which is not cheap.  Thus advisable to bring along dry food and plenty of water for recovery. Along the way you would meet seasoned hikers and some are so friendly that they offer you a ginseng sweet if they see you resting.  There's a water point and the water taste so good! The viewing points offer such fantastic view and it's so breezy that we forgot ourselves!  Definitely a place to visit.
Free entry. Just a rock that doesn't seem to resemble a dragon as claimed. Nice view of the sea though. Not very worth to go out of the way to visit. Spent maybe 5 minutes there in total.
