The path down takes a slightly different route too, which is nice.

This place is the signature sightseeing here. So every tourists would be here. It's crowd with people. There're many shops, kiosk, snack bar and food shops at the front of the sightseeing. So there are large space for parking. You need to buy ticket to get in there. Once you get ticket, you walk straight on the walk way till you see the junction. There's the highlight signage for photo shooting. And you need to choose either way to go. If you go to the right, you need to walk up to the hill and you will see the good view from there. The way to go up the mountain is fine, not too rough. But not recommend during rainy day.If you go to the left, you will see fisherman Village, sea sand sun and fresh seafood from local people. The highlight is the lady from the village dive deep into sea to get the seafood stuffs.

This place is easily accessible by bus. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about more than an hour to get to Seongsan Ilchulbong. After you get off at Ilchulbong entrance station, walk right into the small alley and continue straight until the end to the Main Street, you will see sign leading to Ilchulbong. It was a nice hike but a lot of stairs. The view is beautiful up at the top. There are plenty rest stop along the way so no need to worry. When you come down, you can go to the beach where you?ll find the house of women divers. There are performances at certain time slot but since I visited in the winter, there was none. They also sell fresh seafood where you can have right at the restaurant. It was quite expensive but It?s fresh and also to support the women divers.

This place is accessible (1.5 hours away from Jeju Bus Terminal/Airport by bus 101.  It was too cold to swim in october (and I didn't bring my trunks) but I hope to swim here another time!  Cafe Delmoondo is just next to the beach - I went there cos I needed to use the toilet (and bought an ice-cream just to be a customer), but food was so good there I ended up having lunch!  This is a nice place to hang out if you are staying in N Jeju because it was not too crowded (at least not in october), and because the view was really nice (the sea was emerald green, as the blogs say, and quite breathtaking)

This park is on the mountain above the Jeju main ship port.The way up can be done with a car, then the entrance to the park is near the large white lighthouse with a great view over the coastline.you'll have their wide green areas. good for to chilling out but can be skip after the lighthouse.

This mountain (aka Sunrise Peak) is located to the eastern seaboard of the island and is not accessible easily if you are staying in one of the hotels in Jeju-ri (city area) in the north. You need to take public transport which can take you more than 1 hr (Blue intercity bus, flat rate 1200 W) or 50+ min by express bus (Red, flat rate 2000 W). It is advisable to put up overnight in one of the many hotels or guest houses in Seongsan itself so that you can wake up early and start your ascend to watch the sunrise.This will take about 25-40 min to climb up the well laid out steps if you do not stop along the way to take pictures. However it is advisable to stop along the numerous rest areas and take your own time to ascend. Certain parts can be quite steep so come with a good pair of canvas sneakers or hiking shoes, sunglasses, sun screen, bottles of water. The climb up is worth the effort as you will be rewarded with the fantastic views from the peak. Going down is much easier and you can stop at the foothill to watch the women divers putting up a demo at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. At the foothill is a public toilet and a McDonald and cafe apart from stalls selling souvenirs and cold drinks.
This is the most attractive place in jeju. The view from the peak was good but not breathtaking. Anyway, it is still better than the waterfalls which are just little falls.

This is the largest waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea, and one of the only ones that is not fenced up at the bottom. Usually, when you visit waterfalls, it's always staring at it from a distance, where a viewing platform has been built. This is different, you get to walk ALL THE WAY to below that waterfall, and if you are open to wading through knee deep water, go touch that waterfall.The spray of water is refreshing, and the scenery rocks. You'll feel one with nature.

This is the highlight of our trip. For only KRW2,000, it's worth every won! A must visit. The hike to the top can be very tiring especially if you are not fit. That said, the air is fresh and invigorating, so take your time and pace yourself and you will reach there eventually. If ahjummas can make it up there, so can you! (what I was telling myself on my way up). When you finally reach the top, you get to see the crater, although I do prefer the view on the way up of the town and the surrounding areas. Even if you don't hike to the top, there is still much to see. If you take the scenic route, you can have a great view of the ocean and the cliffs. Great photo opportunities.

This is the climb for the unfit too. It is relatively easy compared to Hallasan or Elephant Mountain in Taipei (not even half as difficult) and the views all the way up and down is amazing. We did the sunrise climb as we stayed overnight at Illchubong Hotel. From the hotel, it is about 20mins walk to the base - we had a car. There are many public buses that come to this spot. If you have 4of you, you can cheaply get a taxi to the spot for the morning climb.At the top, we did not see the amazing postcard view (aerial view?). If you wanted to take the sunrise with the illchubong Seongsan, you actually do not have to climb up the mountain. There is a huge area to view it as you drive up the highway.There are public buses to the entrance/ base of the mountain. There are 2 women divers performance which we missed due to the timing. It's 11 and 1 or 3pm. You can probably go to Udo island and be back for the late performance.Highly recommended to visit.

This is sunrise peak at Jeju island you should to add in your travel list. Before go to Seongsan pls check the sunrise time. You will see a very fantastic view point here. Anaway, pls prepare your cloths for strong windy and cold. Along the walking platform the view is beautiful also. Do not miss it.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is one of my favourite places to visit in Jeju. No matter which angle you are taking photos from, the views are gorgeous. You can hike up Seongsan as well, if you are up for it. Or you could go down nearer the shoreline to catch a glimpse of the women divers. Past that area, and you can make out Udo Island in the distance. It has gotten extremely crowded over the years though, with tons of tour groups making their way here. It still remains a must-see area in Jeju, in my opinion.

This is one of my favorite places in Jeju.? Walking up the steps to the temple you experience one enlightenment after the next.? The temple and the grounds are in immaculate condition, and clearly there is a lot of love and respect which goes into every section.? This is a wonderful hour or two to spend as you are wandering around the island - take your time, don't rush it, enjoy both the temple and its attractions, and the stunning views toward the ocean and the rest of the island.? BTW, this is not an easy stroll up the hill, but not that taxing either - if you have elders, perhaps you settle for mid-way.? if you're young - do the entire journey, you'll never know when you'll be back.

This is like a must-see attraction according to the reviews and the crowds there.... so despite there is nothing much to see when you reach the summit.... just some balding green on a small concave patch of land  .. it is probably still worth the 20 odd minutes climb up , for health sake.. .   Some cardio exercise is always good after all the black pig meals ! If you arrive at the right time at the foot of the hill, you may be lucky to  catch some women divers performing there..

This is a tough stair climb up to the top, especially on a hot and humid day in August.  It is a gorgeous view all the way up and especially at the top.  It is a new 7 Natural Wonders of the World, voted in 2011.  I'd been wanting to visit since then and was not disappointed.  You won't regret the view.

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a long way up but it only takes about 40 minutes.  It's worth it, the view is amazing and I didn't want to leave.  It's so relaxing, the only downside is, it's full of tourist so croissant are unavoidable, and it's always crowded

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This is a beautiful volcanic crater well worth visiting. It doesn?t take too long to reach the top from the entrance (despite the sometimes steep stairs). The views are magnificent as you ascend, from the summit, as well as when you descend. Plus there are various volcanic rock formations that you can appreciate along the way, both ascending and descending (the two paths are different). The crater is full of trees and grass of a very unique shade of green (I?ve seen this shade of green only in the vegetation of other extinct volcanic craters such as the ones in Tanzania). There are platforms to sit on at the summit from where you can appreciate the view. After descending, make sure to visit the cove where you can meet the Haenyeo or the traditional fisher women of Jejudo. The way to the cove is clearly marked with signboards and it?s only a couple of staircases down to the beach. The Haenyeo put up a performance twice a day, which is very touristy but interesting nevertheless. You can buy all kinds of fresh seafood from them and ask them to prepare it for you to eat at the restaurant. But it?s mostly eaten raw / semi-raw with various sauces and the typical side dishes. The sea weed is particularly good, which you get as a side dish. There is unfortunately no English menu. If you don?t want to eat raw seafood, after picking your seafood portion at the entrance, take it to the counter inside the restaurant and ask that it be stir-fried (?pokkum? in Korean). Beware that even when it?s stir-fried, it?ll still be more on the raw side than the fried side. The black sand beach in the cove is also a treat. If you look closely and attentively, you?ll find all sorts of marine life among the rocks, in the pools and on the sides of the mini cliffs facing the beach.

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

They have everything here from hiking, go karts, horseback riding, sky diving to airsoft. Buses traverse every half hour in one of the safest highways all over the world amidst a back drop of awesome scenic views.

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don?t need to linger. It?s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.

There's a lot to try and absorb in this open air museum. Maybe too much for your average tourist. I mean the somewhat authentic reproductions were cool for the first three or four structures. I enjoyed having a window into what life was like for peasants 100 - 300 years ago and/or the actors who currently play them in historical television dramas. However the minutia became simply overwhelming especially since there was a tendency to focus on the details as if everyone lived and breathed Korean archaeology. There was also a fairly obvious and persistent attempt to commercialize on cheesy trinkets. Some of the   traditional wares   were okay but I think you can get better quality at lower prices elsewhere. The same can be said for the food. The reenactments of wedding ceremonies and shaman rituals were entertaining and the kids could ride ponies. All in all I was glad to end my tour of this facility. It was a rather pricey way to spend an hour or two. If you were in the area or you have a passion for such things maybe give it a try. However I think there are far better ways to spend your time on Jeju. *You can catch bus 720 at the Bus Terminal for 3300 Won. The trip takes a little over an hour:http://www.rome2rio.com/s/Jeju-si/Jeju-Folk-Village-Museum*Here's a Jeju Weekly piece that might give you a better idea of what this place is all about:http://www.jejuweekly.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=4196

There were sooo many people  and the view was also not that great. I couldn't even take a proper picture. First i wasn't even sure if this is the right place, because it didn't look like the pictures i saw online.Go there if you want to have a walk at the cost (2000 won admission fee) and en passant you can look at the cliffs.Going there by bus is not really convenient. The bus station is a bit far and the bus comes about every hour (timetable not reliable).By the way this kind of view you can also have at the Phoenix island (near ilchulbong).

There was no sun in a June afternoon, the temperature was pleasant and the air was clear. I climbed up to the top to view the crater which is covered by lush green.  The climb was pleasant along with the gorgeous views.  The views on the way up were lovely, there were many places for great photo op. I appreciated the views from the top, views to the city and views to the sea without interruptions. It was one of the most memorable experiences I recorded in Jeju.

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...
There is a good view at 1100m streetway of hanla mountain.in Winter day, you can see the snowflowers at hereby

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

The western name for this is Sunrise Peak, and it is an extinct volcano. The walk/hike to the top rim is quite tiring and the last 50 metres is quite steep.  Having said this, there are good steps/stairs all the way up and even older people can make it with a little effort.  The views from the top make the trip very worthwhile.

The waterfalls was nice and a real up close look was possible as the access allowed visitors to go all the way to the base of the waterfall. I like the views just before sunset, as there are haneyeo serving sashimi on the rocks nearby, giving it an additional local touch.In addition, the kids liked the fun and adventure of walking on the rocks up to the waterfall.

The walk up was easy but definitely gets you sweating, even on a cool day.  The weather was not on our side when we went up and it was cloudy at the top.  We still had good views on the way up and down.

The walk up sunrise mountain was  windy and relatively easy. Steps all the way up with many spots for you to rest and take in the beautiful view. Don't miss out on this mountain if you are going to Jeju. Entrance fee is 2000W. They charge for everything here, waterfalls and parks all have an entrance fee.

The volcano look really scenic when looking from far away. This is also a part of UNESCO world heritage site too. There are about 500 steps to the peak of volcano which is not that tired though because step are well built. The view from the top also worth climbing. The weather is great even it was winter, it is not too cold, about 5c.
the view was great!  we climbed our way up to the top and when you looked across, it is just like a endless sea boundary view. the wind was relatively strong but stilll it is worth the walk

The view was amazing even if you did not make it up to the top. From halfway point onwards, you could see the awesome seaview. We went in the afternoon so that we could catch the divers' performance at 3pm. What impressed me the most about the performance was that the Ajumma actually went into the cold waters in winter! For that, it was worth my time standing out in the cold to show them our support.

the view of the waterfall is great! however, many will get closer to the waterfall by walking through the very rocky area from the stairway. kids and elderly need to be careful and also to secure your belongings, if things were to drop into the rocks, may be hard to retrieve. ensure you wear proper footwear!

The trip up and down the 1.95km tall mountain took me the entire day but experience and view was really worth it. It would have been better if I had been properly equipped as I was in normal walking shoes and a small bottle of water while everyone else had their trekking shoes and stick with them which made going up and down more quickly and safe. There are alot of routes but not all the routes will lead you to the peak. Spoke to a few people on my way up and they shared that this is most tedious route as its the longest. There is only one way up and down which makes trekking easy for solo traveller like me.It'd be good if you can bring some food and lots of water with you where you can picnic with many korean families when you reach the peak. Do prepare to start early as you will have to reach a certain checkpoint before they allow you to continue your way up the peak. It was a heartwarming experience for me when all the korean people who walked past me would encourage me to press on and they would share they food around at the peak. Korean families usually do this as a family activity where the grandmother, grandfather, parents and kids would climb leisurely. If a grandparent can do it, so can you. Thats all :)

The ticket office was still not opened, cold and windy and we could not find the signs. We just follow 2 guys, there were more people coming along but not in tourist buses. So going this early is best to avoid the hordes of tourists we saw after we had our sunrise view and breakfast. It is steps all the way but it goes up and up and up and up ... bring your gloves windproof type!The crater is in front of you and then the sea and in the horizon, the egg yolk getting cook and rising up into the sky. Cloudy and initially disappointed but we waited and finally it emerged from behind the clouds and the rays and appearance became much more dramatic!One of the best sunrise I have experienced!

The temple complex is structurally interesting because it is spread out on the foot of the mountain. It's not actually very big and not of the structures are magnificient compared to other temples elsewhere, but very nice overall. But the view is really amazing. Look South and you'll see green slopes going down to the sea, look the other way and you'll see behind the temple rocky mountains that almost look like a cliff. This place captures perfectly the contrast between the sea and the mountain, and is very relaxing.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The sun was shining though not really hot this time (last time 9 years ago was rainy).  I wasn't sure how far up I wanted to climb but started off with the family anyway.  Personally I preferred slopes to stairs.  I saw these signs which showed the distance to the peak (caldera): 274m, 180m, etc. I almost decided to turn back because I thought I would be late if I continued to the top when suddenly I reached the top.   Turned out that those were distance markers and not altitude markers.  The view at the top was really good.  The grass in the crater was lush green.  No steam here.  The walk back down was very manageable, and had some good photo spots.  Towards the bottom, the vast patches of perfect green grass were really pretty.

The stand-alone rock wasn't as impressive as say the Twelve Apostles in Melbourne, but it was nice to walk and take in the sights in the area.If you are a fan of Korean drama serial, Da Changjin (鸚㏝룝), you'll see that they filmed some scenes here (marked by some cut-out boards)On the way out, we saw a store selling black or red volcanic rocks (plus drinks and a really yummy grape ice bar). These rocks float cos of the air trapped in the holes. We bought some home as souvenirs to remember Jeju.I'll recommend taking a walk in the area. The views were great and it was most enjoyable.

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak has 2 main attractions. The first is obviously the climb to the peak itself. The second is the Woman Divers at the black sand beach at the bottom. We spent about 3 hours here and it was just barely enough. The climb is actually not that bad for the physically fit. The steps are steady and most are stone paved or have wooden stairs. There were quite a few elderly ladies/gents climbing too. Rest areas with benches are plentiful, so there really is no reason why you would not try for the top if you have the time. :-) Two thirds of the way up, you will see a big resting area with a marvelous view of the city below. Once you are up at the peak, you will also be able to see the city view AND into the crater. The climb back down is very safe with well made wooden staircases. Regarding the Woman Diver show at the bottom, I found the show to be a little underwhelming and a bit too touristy. However, it was still an interesting experience to see divers selling fresh seafood off the beach. If you have limited time, I would recommend that you focus on the hike/view, and just spend a couple of minutes to browse through the woman diver area. I think the Seongsan Iichulbong is a must-see in Jeju.

The previous review states that the climb was in 20 minutes but for a relatively unfit person like myself, it took me 30 to 40 minutes with numerous stops beginning from halfway till the top. Much to your agitation, we see older citizens and children alike happily and easily climbing the steps and overtook you to the top. Nevertheless, the view on the top was well worth the tough climb (according to my unfit status). Managed to take some photo shots of the surrounding and the crater itself. As it was just beginning spring, the crater floor was covered with brownish grass and vegetation, not the greenish color you would expect in summer. What I most remembered was the real cold buffeting wind of 2 Degrees Celsius blowing and you could really feel it even with winter jackets and caps worn while climbing the steps. But it was most memorable. Wife did not want to climb the steps but decided to go shopping for the famous Jeju orange chocolates in the shops at the foot of the park.

The period I went was very windy, the surrounding was very refreshing with patches of green. Very relaxing, peaceful  and is a good place for photography. A typical k-drama filming location for kfans to visit! Once you reach the highest point, you will see endless of   green    and can even spot mountains that is far away. You can actually relax and enjoy this view by sitting at this cute wooden swing. Very nice place which you probably won't want to miss it.However, to visit this place, you need an entrance fee of  6,000won, But if you booked a experience tour driver with your own group of friends, he can help you bargain it to a even cheaper price which is like 3,000won per person! So, afterall, it was pretty worth it for both the price and this exquisite experience! Recommended to rent a car there, inaccessible by public transport!

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don?t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

The island was recommended by a friend, it’s fairly small with gorgeous ocean views. You can hire bikes to ride around the island, we chose not to and just took a slow stroll around stopping at one of the many pavilions facing out to sea for some lunch with a view. If you are a seafood lover you’ll be in heaven with several places to eat freshly prepared food however if you don’t eat seafood I’d recommend taking something with you (we had been warned). The green barley festival was on while we were there so lots of fields to see and take photos in. A perfect way to spend 3 hours in the sun (be warned there is no shady spots except for the pavilions so take a hat or buy one from the locals like I did)
The GPS lead us to a wrong car park and that's a 20mom walk to the cliff, when there's another carpark just a few minutes away from the cliff. View is aweson but very crowded in the afternoon.
The climb was relatively easy as it had well build steps all the way to the top. The view from the top of the crater, overlooking Jeju Island is what makes it all worth while.

The climb to the top is relatively easy and there are several lookout points along the way. The view isn't spectacular, but it is pleasant. After your descent, don't miss the haenyo (women divers), who perform daily at 1:30 and 3 pm. After catching fish with minimal equipment, they sell it and serve it right there.

The climb is not too bad with stairs going all the way up. The view from the top is amazing and definitely worth the climb.  Below there is also a show put on by the women free divers, as well as a short boat tour to see the other side.

The cliff is located on the southern side of Jeju Island in the township of Seogwipo. A well-laid stair-way/boardwalk has been constructed for visitors to view and appreciate the natural rock formations of hexagonal lave tubes. These make great photo shots when framed with overhanging pine trees, crashing waves, clear blue skies and setting sun. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry and hordes of tourists, especially students on excursion. What an incredible place to spend an hour or two!

The best time to go is early in the morning, to see the sun rise. I had gone a little after the sunrise and many people were already on their way down. The views are spectacular and the way up is very safe, and good for all ages. This was probably the most memorable part of Jeju Island.

Sunrise is at 615 am . The entrance fee is free if you arrive before 7 am . Free Car park to the viewing points a short  8-10 minutes walk away , very doable and you get one of the most memorable sunrise sights . A most do except the getting there so early in the morning is hard .

Summary: You have to go here if you're on Jeju. But what can I add to the many reviews already here?The signs to the women's diving show are very clear. From the ticket office, just follow the signs down to the beach to the left of the peak. If the only way to make the show is to sacrifice something else on your itinerary, I wouldn't do it. But it was pretty cool if you happen to be there at the right time. You see the divers actually catch live octopus right in front of you.I recommend taking a snack up to the top and enjoying it there. There are plenty of places to sit down at the top and relax before you head back down. Also, definitely take at least one bottle of water if it's a hot day. You might even want two.If you plan to catch a taxi from this site to somewhere else, you'll have to walk just a little ways. We asked a taxi driver who was waiting on another family where we could get a taxi, and he told us where to walk. We had to wait about 10-15 minutes for one to show up that didn't already have people in it, but they always drive by eventually.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Spectacular views from the bottom, the side, the peak and everywhere else. I couldn't put down my camera. After two rainy, cloudy days at Jeju, the morning of our visit to Sunrise Peak we were blessed with blue skies.The ticket booth (2000 won for adults, 1000 for youth) listed the roundtrip time as 50 minutes, but we spent 2+ hours climbing and descending the tuff cone, followed by checking out the 1:30 p.m. Haenyo woman diver performance. (There is a second performance at 3:00 p.m.)The tuff cone at the peak is something else, and the climb itself is not that bad, especially if you take it slow. The descent is arguably just as good, with cooling breezes and more picture opportunities. One Con: It can get fairly crowded. Dozens of tour buses are parked at the base, carrying mainly Chinese tourists. It get can a bit competitive at times waiting out the best picture spots, but luckily they like taking pictures by signs. Overall it's not that bad, though it was funny watching the korean couples' responses to the crowds, with the girl posing for the picture and giving the side eye while the guy patiently crouched several feet away.But hey, it's a UNESCO heritage site and definitely worth a trip!

Some of the reviews say it's a quick photo spot and that's all, but if you walk up the street just a little way, there's another path down where you can get some great pictures.  The main photo spot is kind of small and crowded, but this other area isn't, and you can still see the rock and more surrounding formations.I didn't really see the dragon, but it depends on your impression of what a dragon should look like.  This is definitely an Asian dragon, not a European one. :-)

So we saw great reviews and some great pictures online. Thought this was a must see place. To be fair, the island has some real potential to be fantastic, however it was a hot August day, it was getting very crowded.Highlights:- some really nice sights to take in and you can tour the whole island in about 4hrs (including stops along the way)- one let we went for a walk and ran into some people camping. Very pleasant and offered us coffee. We hadn?t encountered too many people willing to go out of their way, so was a nice touch. - took a high speed boat ride around the cliff that looks like the cow laying down (hence the name cow island). That was great and worth the 30k KRW for two adults.Low points:- way too much garbage around. Just about every beautiful sight is ruined by plastic bottles and litter. - a lot of areas were closed like it was low season (or maybe we were just early in the day)- lots people standing around endlessly. Got a little frustrating at times. Advice if you do go:- we took the bus. It was good, but we were on a bus schedule. If I did it again, I would have rented a small electric vehicle (which needs an international driving license to rent). Not sure if the cost, but they looked fun and you control your own timeline then.

Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. At first blush it may not seem too nice but Udo kind of grows on you. I'd recommend renting a moped or bicycle and bopping around the backroads; that would be the best way to see and enjoy Udo.

Skip this and head for Dodubong Peak, especially if you're on the Jeju Golden Bus day tour. This place is unremarkable and is honestly one of the dirtiest parts of the area; I attempted to have my photo taken and a rat scurried out from between the rocks. If you walk up the road (away from the site) about a half mile, maybe less, the photo ops are much nicer. The area near Dodubong Peak is also nicer and you can see great views of of Jeju from the summit.

Since their official website is unclear about opening hours in June, I called the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline and was informed that the museum was indeed open late under summer hours. So after spending 45 minutes in and 30,000+ ?? on a taxi to visit the area with my girlfriend, who absolutely loves teddy bears, we arrived at 6:10pm. With doors still open and people still inside, we were told the museum closed at 6pm. After asking politely to let us enter the gallery and   No, no, no   being the only response, I asked the non-English speaking employee for management and soon they found someone who spoke English. I calmly explained the situation and again asked for an exception, that we were only here for a day, it would be doing us a great favor and that we would finish with the other guests and not prevent them from going home late. We were again met   No, no, no   To her credit, the English speaking manager(?) did include a   sorry   with her   no's   and did genuinely want to know how I received wrong information about their hours (and yes,if I can find a way to review the Korea Travel Hotline, they too will receive a poor rating). But ultimately, we were turned away. The only positive I could take from this experience is that, from what we could see from the lobby, the gallery looked small and over-rated. So I guess we saved ourselves the 20,000?? entrance fee.

Seongsan Sunrise Peak is one of the seven wonders of Nature, a Unesco Heritage sight not to missed while in Jeju. From the peak, you see the remains of an erupted volcano.From the entrance, you can see the green mountain  view. From one angle you can see rock of the mountain going all the way to the sea. All in all an awesome sight. All of these accompanied by strong wind from the sea that is a trademark of Jeju. The park has two main path, one that leads to the peak and another that leads to the sea. There is also a show featuring the diving women of Jeju. By the way, there is also a place where you can see Jeju Horses, smaller than usual horses.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of Jejudo's famous icon.  I'm so glad i was able to climb this famous icon on one sunny mid day. When you reach this attraction, you will see so many shops for souvenirs and food just before the entrance and there is even a Starbucks nearby. Upon entering, you will see a ridge where you can go horseback riding or just do some leisurely walk.  The climb going up was quite a challenge for me but because of the magnificent and awesome views on the way up, i was able to make it to the top. At the middle part of the climb, there is a stall ( the only one there) selling some refreshments and souvenirs.  There is a resting area nearby to enjoy some refreshing drinks before you continue your climb.  Upon reaching the top, i enjoyed the cool breeze and the awesome view of the dried crater covered with grass.  Sharp  rocks around the crater makes it looks like a giant crown.  Coming down was a lot easier as there is a wooden stairs provided and the steps are even, not like the going up where the stone steps are uneven.  i would recommend this attraction to the physically fit only.  When you go down, you might be able to catch their scheduled show of divers and there are also boat rentals.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seongsan Ilchulbong greets us in drizzled rain with fog everywhere making the place look mystic. However we put on raincoat and keep hiking. Halfway we stopped when all of us already looking dreadful.Since nobody want to keep climbing we make way to see the hanyeo. Eventho we didnt climb up to the peak, it was already so worth it. The view is something u cant get else where. Someday will come back to hike again!

Sangumburi Crater is our 1st stop after we got a rental car.It's 40 mins drive from Jeju city.Entrance fee cost KRW6,000. There are several small souvenir & coffee shops.It quite unfortunate for us because that day is raining. We're freezing because of the cold weather.We didn't prepare any umbrella or raincoat. So from the parking to the entrance, we soak under the rain.Thankfully the souvenir shop inside sell raincoat with the cost of KRW4,000.From the entrance, you have to hike up to the crater.The path up to the crater was breathtakingly beautiful.What makes this place looks so gorgeous is because of the vast flame grass field along the way to the crater.Sadly, when we arrive at the top, we couldn't see the crater at all.It was cloudy all over.  However we still enjoy the view.The walk down is as beautiful as it was on the way up.

Sagumburi Crater was one of the highlights of my trip in Jeju Island. The view and scenery was breathtaking. The hike to the top was easy and you get to take pictures along the way. It is really relaxing when you get to the top, you get to feel the wind and appreciate nature.

Rent a car when u r in Jeju & make yr way to Hamdeok beach. There's lots of parking space available along the beach & behind the convenience store (just as you enter the area). Toilet facilities are easily available along this beach. The view is awesome & when the wind blows, make sure you cover yourself with a thicker jacket (if you are afraid of the cold). We were there in end April; not advisable for sunbathing.
Really worth it. Only one way up and one way down, no u-turn. It's pretty steep Nd take energy to climb. Amazing view.

Our hotel in old sity side. But from there use local bus( from bus terminal) W3000 one way,when we back was W1600..So cheep.Anyway,this place was 1hour round trip. quite steps has but some of them points has so nice views!!! 1 thing , this place is very windy spot.. When you go must check your clothing and hat or cap...

One of the more outstanding attractions on Jeju Island. It was raining almost everyday while we were on Jeju Island, but the day we visited this cliff, the clouds lifted and we had a beautiful view of the cliff. The entrance and the rest of the park (the area surrounding this cliff) were very unassuming though, and to a certain extent, poorly maintained. Don?t waste time hanging around those areas, just head for the cliffs straight away!

One of the best views on Jeju island. The climb is not that hard, my 7 year old daughter and 65 year old mom managed to do it in 25 minutes. 15 minutes to go down. Its all stairs, plenty of places to rest. There is a small shop with regular prices (yes they could have charged 5 times for a bottle of water but they do not do that so hurray for the owner) half the way. There is no shade at the top but the view is really, really great.

One of the best stops we made in Jeju. This rock formation is pretty cool and the stop is more worth it since it's a good hour's worth of walking and snapping photos (as opposed to a number of the really touristy places where it's just one kodak moment).Check the tides. The rock formation that people walk on are really close to the water, so if the tides are high, it gets slippery. Actually, some parts are slippery as it is.You have two options: going counter-clockwise, which ends up being an upward movement OR going clockwise, a downward movement.  The views are nice-ish both ways (personally the counter-clockwise views were nicer). More than that though, going counter-clockwise is a lot easier as the steps are easier to deal with moving up. Many of the people coming down were cursing the steep rocks and were tired even before it began for them. Might not recommend this if walking is difficult for you as climbing and hoping around is a must. Little children were around and they seemed to be enjoying themselves, but none of them were younger than 3 years of age.No bathrooms once you enter the formations, but ladies will sell you food and drink (mostly alcohol) if you're interested in a seaside meal.

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area

On the way to the site, we took pictures from afar by the beach.We hiked a bit but mostly sat down and admired the scenic view spread at the foot of Seongsan. Haenyo divers may be found in their area below where they made a performance for the audience. It was cloudy and vey cold but do bring sunblock!

Okay judging by the other reviewers, I must have been there on a great day. The water was crystal clear and the experience was amazing. There is a convenient store located right on the beach for all your necessities (i.e. beer etc) and convenient ice cream and restaurants. While it was a little far away from where I was staying, it was an unforgettable experience and was my favorite part of my trip to Jeju.

Not a difficult climb, but if you haven't worked out in awhile, your legs will definitely feel like jelly on the way down. It took about 20 minutes to hike up the stairs to the top and another 20 minutes to get down. The volcanic cone and the view are totally worth visiting the top for.

Nice views, nice place to take pictures, not a lot of beach front to relax or swim. Most of the area people relax and sunbath are away from the beach since most of the coast has lava rock. Fun place for kids to find stuff in the rocks.
Nice view while walking along the way to the top, view of the sea and mountains, cold wind gets to blow away all worries and agony. Enjoying walk up the mountain, it is a place where you must visit.

Nice getaway island. We drove to the passenger terminal, park our car and take the ferry. The ferry ride there was fantastic. We fed the seagulls flying around the boat. it was a spectacular view!To travel within the island, take a bus or pay for a bike..it is a covered bike really cute. Or you can ride a bicycle.We took the bus, need to pay 6k won. There is a ticket office for shuttle bus. Buses numbered k1,k2,k3,rtc..there were 4 stops.the first stop has many actuvities, cafes, restaurants.You can spend an hour or more here. Second stop is lighthouse so we stop too.   The 3rd and 4th stops are the beaches. We did  not get off the  bus  l
natural cliff formation like steps, very much similar to giant causeway in belfast. good ocean view, cheap entrance ticket. a vert worthwhile visit

My 'poetic' side has always loved gardens. Used to dream and draw secret gardens all the time. My heart and gut was somehow curious about this place, especially after reading reviews from travellers all over the world. Was made to understand that not many young people from our country like myself come to visit which intrigued the caretaker enough to see someone such as myself wandering around the garden and I was therefore approached with such warmth. Even had the pleasure of sipping tea and being in the company of the very welcoming founder owner himself Mr. Bum-Young Sung, who transformed, built and developed this garden over 40 years ago with his own bare hands when nobody but his wife believed that he could turn a wasteland into what is known and recognised now to be   The most beautiful garden in the world  . Like a poetic art carefully, passionately, calmly and beautifully crafted, Spirited Garden indeed does justice to its name. Even in winter where the trees and plants don't bloom as much, I could still feel the garden's spirit that it's almost like nature is speaking to you which gives you a sense of serenity. For a moment, Felt like I was in Edward Scissorhands's world ㅿ Learned so much about the bonsai tree, as well as the philosophical and wisdom in gardening. Thank you Spirited Garden for the beautiful inspiration.

My mum and i took about one hour plus to reach the top. but not to worry if you aren't that physically fit, you can always take a break at seats along the way and enjoy the nice scenery. we went around sept therefore the weather is very good though we are sweated a lot too. However once you are up at the peak, you can enjoy the full panoramic view of the sea and the eastern coastline.A place not to be missed when you go Jeju

My kids request for it & quite excited at 1st. The excitement last for the 1st train ride & once we got off the 1st station & need to walk nearly 1km the kids mood just went sour. Then it becomes a more sour when you need to wait for the next train & need to fight for a seat. They're several trains runs every 15-20m if i'm not mistaken. If you missed one you need to wait till the next train. There is no ticket system while waiting for the train & one must grab the seats. So for me with a 2 kids & a baby it was just very hard. Luckily we stayed at the far front of the track station. We managed to get the train & never get off till the end of the station. We went during end of spring. Nothing much to see. Some flowers & i think it will be a great view during summer. Pro's : A great way to relax while enjoying the ride. Con's : You need to walk a lot. The truth is the train tracks was just goes around the same land. 1st come 1st serve basic when taking on the trains. Not stroller friendly.  Tip's : If you have a tight schedule, just stay on the train. Don't go off.

My husband and I walked here from Jeju-si (not recommended, unless you just really like to walk) so it's not far from the big hotel district. It's free to get in, but is mostly just trees and bushes, the wildflower garden was completely bare, of course, we didn't really come at the right time for that anyway. Follow the signs for   Green Shower   and you'll go up a pretty steep climb (especially for us in our flip-flops) to a nice view of the city and the ocean beyond. There's a nice lily-pad pond and a nice green   lawn   for anyone wanting a place to sit in nature. Although, the entire island of Jeju is about nature, so this wasn't a must-see for us. Just behind the Arboretum (on the left as you drive out and behind a group of concrete apartment buildings) is the ＿?由쇱?? Buddhist Temple. It has a really gorgeous campus and nice view of the city and sea, as well. If you got to the Arboretum, take the time to visit the temple, too.

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My family walked from our hotel to the top of Ilchulbong and down. From the entrance, the mountain(?) looked formidable and it looked to be a painful hike, but it turned out to be rather a short hike. I wish I had taken more time on the way up and enjoyed the views more. On the way down, we saw a restaurant by the rocky shore.  I believe this is where mermaids do their demonstrations and sell raw oyster dishes.  I wanted to go down but my 10 & 12 yr olds won't have it.  So I missed out.         The guy who took the tickets at the entrance surprising had a good nack for taking pictures.  If he is not too busy, ask him to take your group photo.         After the hike, we went to a bakery just by the entrance.  From the second floor, we had a nice view of the Ilchulbong and enjoyed cup of coffee with various breads.  The owner was very kind and let us wait out the rain in the store.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Mount Hallasan is the tallest mountain in South Korea, so expect this hike not to be an easy one. For the less trained hikers, you can go half way and stop at the first crater, which also offers beautiful views.

Most of Udo island except the attractions are rural farms. We went to Udo island with a few local Koreans from jeju island. We took a 15mins ferry. I was surprised that there are no seats on the ferry, people sit on the floor instead, korean style. Interesting experience. As I went with locals, I thought they would know the way. No! They didn't and we walked 1h around the island before reaching the peak. It was beautiful. The grass was green n the sea view was nice. Though it was really windy. And thus very cold even though it was summer. Be sure to wear enough clothes.

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Lots of people, but it's expected.  Climb was not too bad but my wife did need a rest in the middle.  Provides great view on a clear day.  Take some pics of it when you are far away if you are driving.  There are places on the side of the road where you can park and take a few pictures of the entire thing.

Long long route indeed ! Best is to go via one route and come down via another. Scenery could be a bit monotonous but at the end being surrounded by nature is always more rewarding. Ensure to be on the checkpoint by 1pm else one can be very close yet so far to the summit - since you won't be allowed to climb up the remaining 2.5 kms of stretch. If its a brighter day, view is what makes the climb worthwhile.. if its not, aaah bummer, bummer... !

Located next to   Loveland   this museum is small modern place with beautiful outdoor features such as a reflecting pool sculptures and a small surrounding forest. There was a little bit of everything from an exhibit about a famous national artist who lived for decades on Jeju to an interesting video and poetry collaboration of Korean rappers talking about social issues. The upstairs is currently showcasing drawings and sculptures made by Korean schoolchildren in a surprisingly cheeky cheerful exhibit. Much of the museum was in English but others were only in Korean. The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.

Like other traveller's review, this is not a place that worth the effort to purposely come by to visit. As it is really just a peace of rock that stood by the sea... It seems more attractive when the spot light is on at night.We dropby this place when we are on the way back to Yeha Guesthouse, surprisingly lots of tour buses stopping by! And you need to walk all the way down the staircase to have a better view of the rock, so old folks with knee problem would suggest to skip this sight seeing point.We couldn't identify which portion is the 'dragon head' until we over heard a tour guide's explanation to their guests @@

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.
