The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.

About 35 - 1hr hike to reach up the hill. The view at the top is amazing, it's worth to hike. Halfway through the hike there will be 1 pit stop if you would like to purchase any drink and some resting point. There are 2 points where you can U-turn if you feel that you are unable to complete the hike. Once you miss the last turn, you have to complete it hike as it's one way direction.

A way to escape from daily hectic life. You can walk at your own pace and choose the route and scenery you like (coastal road, hiking). I completed Route 1, 1-1, 20, part of route 6 & 7. Just choose the route and follow the olle sign, relax and enjoy the view Olle wanna show you. Is quite safe, I am a girl and I walked alone.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A very long and tiring climb if you are not used to climbing. There's lots of people both locals and tourists climbing along so you will definitely be motivated to continue climbing. Tip: bring sunglasses, pack light, grab a snack and bring a bottle of water, most importantly wear comfortable sports shoes. Just climb slowly and take a break along the way as you need so that you are not overly tired out. If you are thinking of combining this attraction with other nature sites that require ample walking or climbing, do take note that this attraction may already be rather tiring... the view and wind at the top is worth it, in my opinion. You do not see the bird's eye view you see online but nonetheless you see the vast greenery and top down view of the scenery below.

A very beautiful and peaceful, cooling place. Full of natural trees.  I went after rain,vision not clear from hill top. But I love this natural scenery. It is money back guarantee for Korean people if can not view anything from hill top with heavy mist. Anyway announcement were made if there is heavy mist during rain.

A must go place when visiting Jeju-do. Although it was slightly drizzling on that day, there was still quite alot of local and tourists taking the hike. The climb was a smooth one with well laid pathway. Good exercise and a closer touch with nature.View was awesome and air was fresh, really heavenly and relaxing.

A hike to the top is quite challenging especially for the elderly and family with young children as there are heaps of steps. Make sure to bring something to hydrate you as there were no drinking fountains available on your way to the top. Enjoy the views of the sea and cityscape once you're at the top. Also, there are a number of restaurants, coffee shops and food stalls at the bottom of the peak.

A great way to enjoy the view and burn off a few calories at the same time. It's a lovely coastline with a spectacular panorama of the area, definitely a nice little hike. You can easily spend a couple of hours here. Very enjoyable.

A good place to start your visit to Jeju, the place is very accessible to people of all ages.  There is a decent spot for photo taking though there is also a stairway down to the beach to marvel at the eroded stones as well as a view of the   Dragon Head   from the other side.  Stairs to the beach not recommended for young kids and elderly with movement issues.  There are cafes nearby like Dunkin Donuts and some hot local titbits.

A cheap half-day activity. Udo Island was the perfect little get-away. We took a nice little ferry ride over to the island and rented peddle bikes to ride around. (You must have an international driver's license, however they took just our American driver's license.. depends on who you talk to) Took us about 3 hours to loop the whole thing (with stopping for icecream, a snack, a drink, etc) Beautiful views around very corner. Make sure to stop and get a burger at HAHA HOHO (located on the left around the bend from ferry drop off) it was definitely an Udo highlight as well as their local icecream. Pack some snacks and have a picnic, great spots to stop and enjoy! Friendly NOTE: Bring sunscreen! The sun is brutal!

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!
You pass the Maze Park when you head towards the Lava Cave. My mum and I went to the park after the cave on our way back up to the main road to catch the bus. It was a fun way to kill some time.

Yakchunsa temple was built in late 14th or early 15th century and is located between Jungmun Tourism Complex and World Cup Stadium. The temple is on the coastal road so people can overlook the sea from the temple in clear days. The 600 Airport Limousine Bus might be the only public transportation here. The architecture style of Yakchunsa temple was probably influenced by Chinese Buddhism. The similarity can be noted from the styles of Buddha statue and the sculptures in the temple as well as how the main structure bell tower and drum tower have been arranged. The golden Buddha statue is probably 3 or 4 stories high and looks magnificent. There are also relief sculptures next to the Buddha statue. In addition to the main hall of the temple there is a smaller hall of 500 arahans 100 meters away. This small arahan hal is also worth to visit. Faces and poses of the 500 arahans are different and full of meaning. Perhaps you can realize some philosophy of life from these arahans.

We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy

We took the bus to get to this location and was dropped off at the bus stop.  There were no signs how to get to the destination so we went to the nearest hotel to inquire.  They pointed us the way and we forgot to ask how far it was.   We still did not find any signs how to get there but after walking 15-20 min found the entrance.  The scenery is beautiful and we took several pictures.

We took bus 600 from the World Cup Stadium. This bus is also the Airport Limousine. We got off at Jeju ICC and walked from there towards the sea. The geometrical volcanic rock formation simply took our breath away!  Who cut/shaped the rocks this way? A fantastic work of art created by the Master Craftsman. Another wonder of nature. The geometrical shapes were amazing! This is - must-visit site!

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

Very beautiful and serene temple. there is also an option for temple stay here. it's tucked away from the hustle and bustle of city life so it will be a good retreat. There were prayers ongoing when we were there which was very relaxing to listen to. you can enter the temple through the side doors (not through the centre) make offerings of rice (you can get this at the counter inside) or donations. it may be a little difficult to get there by public transport. we hired a driver Mr Yang (+82 10-3639-7469) to help us get around - he was most helpful quite humorous and very easy to get along with even taking photos for us and giving short descriptions of the sights at the attractions.

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This is so amazing beach to walking around and relax even 11 pm we still walk and feel so peaceful and good food and good clean bar I always stay here when ever come to jeju and you can take the bus anywhere you want to go around jeju it?s beautiful island and I am from Hawaii tham you know what I mean alright

This is located in the southwest quadrant of the island and can be a chore to get to without a car. The highlight of the building is the tea drinking experience that you need to make a reservation for(I'm pretty sure) that is entirely in Korean though so bear that in mind. There are tea fields in different directions for quite a ways the ones next to the museum are setup for visitors and picture but the further away fields aren't meant for tourists. We arrived around 10:30 and it wasnt busy at all but when we were getting ready to leave at 12:30 it was quite full.

This is a great volcanic cave with very interesting information cards dotted around to teach the novice geologist more about how it was formed and the story of the cave. Its a bit out the way but you can get the 101 circle route to nearby then one of the 7xx buses up to it

the ticket price is cheap but place a bit far away from city..sculptures are not well kept so looked run down.but there are many beautiful world buildings which make good photo spots.i am very disappointed there is not even a small cafe for us to take a snack.there is a drink vending machine though..i checked the surrounding for staff.think less than 6staff..this can be a very good attraction place if jeju govt can pump in some money to repaint the buildings open a cafe and make the bus stop nearer so we do not have to walk so long.

Suitable for anyone who can walk without aid as there were steep stairs leading in/out of cave. Floors were uneven as can be expected. We entered just after the rain so the place was literally dripping from the ceiling. One way in and out from the same entrance. Midpoint (the deepest part of the cave) was a formation that was supposedly the highlight. Lighting was sufficient to find your way around but not for taking pictures unless you are equipt with an SLR and a tripod. My 10yr old couldn't wait to get out as he was rather bored. No thanks to his father(me) who was busy taking pictures with long exposure :-)

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

On a 3 day trip to jeju we needed more indoor activities due to the daily snowy conditions and found Jeju National Museum. With low expectations and dampened spirits as we were expecting to visit more outdoor activities we were pleasantly happy with our choice.This museum was easily accessible from our hotel as it was only a 28 minutes bus ride (costs us 1150krw). The bus stop just outside the museum.The museum itself is quite out of the way from the city centre but so was all the other places we wanted to visit and therefore was not an issue for us.Highly recommend you taking your time to read and inspect each exhibit. It is quite amazing how history laid out the changes made due to advancement through discovery. Although for a quick browser it may only take you half an hour (it took us more than 1 hour).Entry was free and I'm not sure if this is the norm but surely worth a visit even if just as a time filler.

Not so much a museum as much as a gift shop on a tea field. I live right next door and it's always super busy (not sure why). The land is really beautiful with rolling tea fields but it is not a museum just an insanely overpriced gift shop. But if you're in the area it's definitely worth a visit.

Jeju has many beautiful bushland and park areas that are truely outstanding at all seasons of the year. Bijarim Forest is yet another one of these and can be different in each of the seasons. Take water if in summer and a coat if in winter!! Enjoy wandering the pathways and seating areas provided to take in the beauty.
it's a bit off the beat but still quite a few tourists find their way but mainly by car or bus tour. Went there by bus which is still pretty easy.

It?s a very busy beach but it has lots of lifeguards which is always a good thing to know. The only reason why I am rating this beach a 4 is because there?s a lot of trash which is very sad. Other than that it is fun to play at(they also rent out tubes).

It isn't worth travelling all the way but if you are passing by it is an interesting stop. The optical illusion is really amazing. It looks like we are climbing uphill without any help. You can even try by placing a can or bottle or even water. Place is rather crowded though. Seem to be a common tourist stop for most with lots of buses.
I love their tea but I rarely come to the cafe because it's always so uncomfortably busy.  I would recommend visiting though especially to purchase things from their shop.

I live just down the road from O'Sulloc and pass it on a nearly daily basis it's always busy always!.I have visited once get past standing next to a tea plant and a big tea pot and your pretty much done there is a collection of crockery and quite a nice cafe you need to like green tea though...It takes about half an hour to see and do everything.

I like Greek history. So when I heard about this place I decided to visit. My wife was not ready but I persuaded her. Although this place is bit off way bus service is limited so I booked a taxi for to-fro. When we reached there it was foggy weather so could not see much from outside.I come to know that it is combo Greek+Trick eye museum.When we enter Greek Museum I was surprised on white environment cleaniness....really a good place. We end up taking lots of pics.Wouls recommend to go there.

I have to say going to the Alive Museum was not on my 짢to see짢list but it was on the Yeha West tour.And I was dying of laughter after I left.It쨈s like the Laguna Pageant of Masters if you쨈re ever gone to Laguna California.At the Alive Museum you take your picture and you become part of the painting.  It쨈s hysterically funny. I have one of my best pictures taken at the museum.We were only halfway through the museum and the tour guide came in to chase us back onto the bus.  It쨈s a hoot and even funnier if you watch the kids and their parents interact.

I found about this temple while looking for things to do around the waterfalls. It's quite a drive from them and I'm not pretty sure if by bus it's possible to get there but since it was my first temple we drove there anyway. It's a nice big temple though some of its decorations seem to be amateur. Nevertheless it was a nice experience. It's not very crowded so that's also a bonus. I don't recommend this temple for people who are disabled or have a hard time walking since there's a fare amount of stairs till you get to the temple.

I ate here on two of my four nights in Jeju. Excellent food stalls at night and it was busy but to me a buzz. It is always interesting to wander round and see what is available before choosing. I know little Korean but the signs are self explanatory and most of the stall holders help

Fun half day out !  Green tea everything from tea to face cream and our 8 year looked the GT icecream which is truly delicious. The plantation and site is is sleek spotless and well maintained but we found the prices a trifle steep. (The Euro was a bit wobbly in Aug 2010!) We got a taxi there and hitched our way back to the mainroad to pick up the bus back to Jeju Si.

First of all the cave is not accessible by public transportation. We got dropped off the main road by public bus but it is still a long way in by foot.  My expectation was we will be dropped very close to it but it wasn't. The cave was ok.  Nothing special.

Although most of the board and model displays are in Korean language some are in English. It stresses on different cultures of sex ranging from western SE asian chinese and japanese Peru and Indian societies. Different sculptures from ancient to modern ages show the impact of sex to human life. Some erotic sceneries are shown but good to our sex education of adults and even kids! It tells us the pyschology diseases economical values and romantic features of sex even the sex of the elderly people. It costs W12000 each for entry taking you about 1 to 2 hours walk in the 2-storey hall. It is easy to get there by taxi or Jungmun Express Bus (JEB)from Jeju intercity bus terminal (or from Jeju Grand Hotel in Yeon-dong) of Jeju-si. If taking JEB it costs W2500 for 45 minutes. You can take transit at Changcheon-ri and then take western round bus (towards Hwasun-ri direction away from Jungmun Resort). Only soft creams and drinks are provided. The lovers are welcome to enjoy the sex knowledge there.If the museum has translations into English or Chinese I'd give her 5 points!

Actually I didn't know about this road until the Jeju Golden Bus City Tour ticket lady excitedly explained this strange phenomenon about the bus being able to move on its own while on neutral gear.So those on the Jeju Golden Bus Tour don't really have to go out of the way to see this mysterious road. It's just before the Jeju Museum of Art stop.

A grand n majestic temple. Upon entering the temple vicinity you can feel truly blessed n at ease.Even though the history of the temple aint long the architecture of the temple n beautiful landscaping are truly marvellousThe airport limousine bus from airport/ jeju city stops in front of the temple on the way to Seogwipo.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

With only one full day in Jeju and a list of places to visit, there was no way we can go see it all by ourselves in one day. So when we ran across this tour that included almost all of our must see places in Jeju we had to book it. Jin was our tour guide for the day and was very prompt with the pickup and was very knowledgeable of the sites that he took us to. Each stop of the tour was ??. And the option to go tangerine picking checked off one of activity that I wanted to do myself. The price for this tour is very reasonable considering that we didn’t have to figure out how to get place to place by bus or taxi. The cherry on top is the food and activity recommendations that Jin gave us as the tour ended so it felt like our tour continued on through the night even after the tour ended. Thanks Jin for the awesome tour!

What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

Went there twice. Once on a rainy day and on a sunny day. Do not go on rainy days! We went on the bus tour which told us that English tour will be provided but the guide spoke korean throughout instead. Bus tour took us to a few attractions which were pretty scenic and impressive. However, the wind was too strong and it was freaking cold. Always have a poncho/raincoat prepared in case of rain! Went on a sunny day the next day and rented the ATV for 15,000 won for an hour. Managed to explore and rode the ATV round half of the island. Fantastic experience, would definitely recommend it and do it again! Also, try the peanut ice cream!

Well it's a big cave and you are surrounded by lava rocks- which are basically... Rocks.So if you like caves or rocks you will love this!It was very quiet.. Just a few people walked past us... Very different from Ichulbong..You don't need walking shoes or even a torch really, but do care where you walk..It is about 2km from the main road if you take a bus that drops you off on the main road.. Taxis often wait in the main road and charge 4000 one way to the caves..I think entry to the caves was just 1500..The Maze garden is a few hundred metres away too but I didn't go

We wrer stayed call KAL hotel. From here about 25min walk.We went here at lunch time after Tonmunsijan?? Is the food markets.We done this, first we went Tonmunsijan( food markets) eat street foods, look around here then went to Black pork street.In Korea is bit hard,coz no English...But these peoples were very kind,they always to try understand.So YOU!!!  Must go and try some this street's Black pork restaurants!!!You can choose from 5 of them. 1 was no many but others were quite all busy at lunch time.

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We went there with a bus group, they organized a lot of activities and Mysterious road was one of these. We found out it's too crowded and there's nothing to see and to do, it's normal street, they said that the cars will move without a driver, but you can't see it or feel it, just the driver feels that. overall don't go there if specially for the street if it's on your way or you are with a group it's okay.

We went there on July 17, 2016. We asked the hotel front desk how to get there by public bus, 2 bus numbers to take to the destination. There are plenty of bus for the first leg, but the 2nd bus no. 990 there are only 2 or 3 available in a day and the next one for us like 2 hours away, so the few people/tourists that was there with us decided to walk to the destination for about 3 kilometers. When we got there sweaty and tired we pay the cheap fare of KW2,000 (mind you cheap attraction). The good thing is the cool breeze inside the cave, mind your steps because its wet and some puddle of waters in there. Many people in there, mostly Korean tourists. The few inside the dimly lighted cave is not impressive neither beautiful as I thought. When we got out at about 4:30 pm. we happened to catch the bus no. 990, to our surprise the bus driver told us to get out of the bus while he let the Korean passengers in. We asked why and he keep telling us taxi..taxi..taxi.. So apparently, he does not take foreigners to go to the next bus stop and forced us to take taxi, sure enough, a taxi driver in the area approached us. I felt so discriminated by the bus driver, we didn't even want to negotiate with the taxi driver (because, I believe they do this on purpose). We decided to walk back 3 km. to the next bus stop. It was a waste of almost a day of our time, definitely not recommended to visit this place, NOW I KNOW WHY IT'S CHEAP!

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We went on a cloudy day and the driver drove us all the way to the entrance at Yeongsil.  Having a hot afternoon the day before, we thought it would be warmer thN the day before as we Han to walk uphill. The driver saw us in our thin layer, offered me a rain and wind breaker and a pair of gloves. I reluctantly accepted them out of courtesy but later genuinely thanked him after four hours.On a windy and cloudy October morning, the temperature actually dropped as we ascended. Two hours later it got even much colder with strong gusts, as we approached near to split of the main road to either continue uphil to the top, or to go downhill to the other parking lot. I had to use my gloves and another layer there. My husband regretted not bring his hat on a cloudy day to protect his cold ears (anyway later I found his nose sunburnt even on a cloudy day)We used our walking sticks and wore our hiking shoes, which I found very helpful. We saw some people who really had difficulty completing the loop.  I suggest tourists first decide whether you physically can complete the four hour trip (adults) to the other parking lot. If not, better discuss with your driver (if using one) to meet in the starting point, or decide where to park your car, if not taking the bus.Pack your bag reasonably and don't take any unnecessary items. Some snacks are helpful though as there are no snack bar at all. I suggest also try to bring your garbage downhill as I don't think there will be regular cleaner everyday up/downhill for hours'hike.

We traveled here by public transport. The bus stop turned out to be quite a bit away from the cave itself, but we were lucky enough to get a lift from a friendly lady. The cave itself is nice, with lights everywhere. It's not a long walk through, nor is it a difficult one. I would recommend wearing shoes, rather than sandals or flipflops, as the rocky surface isn't easy in the low light. Also recommend a jacket/vest because it gets cold and drops fall from the ceiling.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took the ferry to Udo island, the ferry trip was fun with many seagulls flying around us. We booked 5 electric bicycles for 2 hours (need to bargain with the price). Electric bicycle no need international driving license. Think 2 hours is very rush as we don't have enough time to slowly explore the beautiful island. Halfway we go lost and need to rush back to return the bicycles to avoid the penalty. Need to exercise caution while cycling as the roads are shared with cars, buses, other mobile vehicles. No separate road for bicycles. It's a nice island to explore

We took bus 701 to the foot of the hill. We thought we had got off at the wrong stop as it was very quiet at the bus stop. We walked a little uphill and saw that we were on the right track. Admission was W2,000. The stairs made it a very easy climb.  One direction up and one direction down.  Very scenic along the way and at the peak. Very windy though.

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We took a cab from Ramada Plaza for 30,000 wan. It took about half an hour. The bus home 710 was great and took an hour. 3000 wan. The island was good fun. We cycled the island stopping along the way to see things. The elder diving women were really cool. Sad to see the garbage around from the sea :( Udo is in such a highly populated area of the world garbage is a big problem. It makes me want to really try to become green at home in Canada.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

We originally got the bus here to go to hallim park. we noticed this beautiful beach and decided to check it out. anyway we ended up staying here all day. Was so nice to be on such soft, yellow sand with clear waters. There was quite a few families with young children which was nice to see all the children playing. Unfortunately there was a digger truck digging the sand while we were there for a few hours and a man kept blowing his whistle at everyone walking near the truck. if it wasnt for this it would have been excellent. Theres shops and restaurants close by and toilet blocks that provide flowing water to wash off but this is cut off around 5 or 6 pm. Sunset here was amazing.

We made a quick little stop here on our way back to the airport. We came in the morning and it was fairly easy to get parking and not too busy for taking pictures. It's a nice spot if it's on your way somewhere, but it's not a super must-see attraction.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We felt peacefulness in this place even if it is next to a main road. The entry fee is only 1000 won and clean facilities.From Seogwipo bus station take bus 700 for 1500 won each way.The building in the Korean style are well maintain and the climb all the way to the grotto is a good exercise. The golden Buddha sit up there under the dripping mountain. People collect the water for? believe of power, may be like Christian for Easter water..Well! Each are different, Friday for the Jews, Saturday the Muslim, Sunday the Christians, everyday for Buddhas...

We didn't have great weather when we were on the island so couldn't climb the mountain. This was an alternative activity and glad we did it as it was really interesting. Make sure you go all the way to the end as you don't want to miss the lava flow. The ground is slippy in places and not suitable for small children, strollers or wheelchairs. If you're using public transport get the bus 900. Not the 701 as we did! The 701 has a stop called 'Manjamggul Cave entrance' but it's 2km walk away from the entrance!!

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

We decided to get off the bus on the way to Jeju city and walking towards the sea it looked like a really quiet place... When we arrived on the beach front we were pleasantly surprised by all the quaint little cafes that dotted the shoreline. There's a surf school on the beach and parasols everywhere. It is a smaller beach, but clear and shallow water. You are not short for choice for lunch or snacks. We had a lovely day!

We could not come here to enjoy the famous sunrise, but we had the chance to see the sunset from the top. AMAZING! If you come with bus #701, you should get off at the bus stop called   Entrance to the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak  . from there, the entrance is only two blocks away. Climbing up to the top is takes around 20 mins. NOTE --> If you would not take your luggage or bag with you to the top, but leave the in the number coded lockers downstairs, don't forget to check the opening hours of the luggage store!!! When we were there it closed at 6 pm, we got there only 4 mins past 6, and despite the place was still open, the lockers could not be opened anymore even with the right codes after 6 pm. We had to call the emergency number shown on the locker side, to unlock it for us and retrieve our bags.

We chance upon this on our drive from Seogwipo to Hyeopjae.  The pink building is big and visible from the highway. They should have repainted it as it looks washout and faded pink. But once I step in, it?s totally new! Infact it is even newer than Sanrio Puroland which I visited in Tokyo and bigger than there! I am a true blue HK fan since 40 years ago. Once HK fan steps in, I am sure you will be transformed to a little princess at heart and you?ll be so excited again! There are a lot of Instagram worthy area to take photos. As others pointed out, it has a section that talks about the evolution of HK from 1970s till now.  There are HK rooms, dining room, bus, living room, wardrobe, dressing room etc. Even the toilets are so pretty! Level 2 offers some purikura area, a restaurant and some other HK displays.  There is a 3D dancing room too. On the 3rd floor, there is a open air rooftop HK small maze. On level 1, you go through the souvenirs shop to exit and a notice states that once u exit, u can?t go in again. So it?s best that u buy yr souvenirs when u are ready to leave. I swear I could stay there for 3 hours but as my husband is with me, it only took us about 1.5 hrs to complete our visit. Overall this place is small and not much for non Kitty fans. For us Kitty fans, it is definitely a must visit.

We caught the 7:30 am ferry from Seongshan Port to Udo.  The ferry left a bit early so we actually arrived at the island by 7:35.  The ferry ride should be about 15 minutes.  Cost was 17,000 kwr for 2 adults for round-trip tickets.  We struggled with whether we should have brought our car on board and immediately regretted not doing so once we landed.  Seems it is off season so not busy at all.  The first place we stopped at was the mango shop, where they also have a shop In the back for vehicle rentals.  Stopped there and tried to rent a mini-car/scooter but the staff said no rentals today because of the festival (seems it is the seashell festival).  Anyway, with no other option, we just took the hop-on and hop-off bus (5000 krw per person).  It?s about 21,000 krw round trip for a small car.  First stop was the lighthouse, got there at 7:45 and went back down to catch the next bus at 8:30.  The next stop after was the black sand beach.  Then to the other lighthouse on the northern tip of the island.  We concluded our trip at the stop after that which is the other ferry port.  We caught the 10 am ferry.  We skipped the white sand beach which is probably the most popular site as a lot of Korean dramas were shot there.  Some tips:- bring your car if you have one so you can visit the island on your own schedule - try the peanut ice cream at Jimmy?s Natural Ice Cream- most of the food places may be closed on a Sunday

Visiting Manjanggul Cave is one of the main reason I visited Jeju. I and my family were not disappointed at all. We visited during late June 2015. The cave is a little bit cooler inside even in a hot summer day so remember to bring a jacket especially for kids. There was rain before our visit so the cave inside was a little bit wet but we could go inside and visit. There is a steep stair in the beginning of the tunnel/cave so one must walk very carefully. After entering the cave, there is no more stair and on flat level mainly.The whole cave is well lit so you should be able to see inside without bringing your own flashlight torches. (You can still bring it if you want to see everything in detail!)Only 1km of the cave is accessible by visitors. You go inside and walk to the end of the tunnel and then walk back the same way you go in. I suggest you riding a taxi to this place since public bus is not easily accessible to this tourist spot. There is a bathroom outside the cave only. So if you need to go to bathroom, you have to go before entering the cave.

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Visited the cave as a part of a bus tour. We entered through the 2nd section and were given 40 mins to walk to end of the cave and back. Grounds are uneven and slippery due to water dripping from the ceiling, hence proper shoes are necessary. The lighting was quite dim and there were only a couple of descriptions along the way. I didn't come out with a full appreciation of the lava cave. The cave wasn't very spectacular but it's worth a visit if you are in the area.

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Udo is like a big kids playground. You rent an electric scooter and scoot around this fun little island. We looped it in about an hour and a half, stopping for iced cream. The rental was 3 hours and so we explored the middle of the island off the beaten path. You cant really get lost and apple maps or navient works great (so does cell phone data). Some expert tips:Get the ?Harley Davidson? 2 man bike.Its rain covered, and you wont get too hot like the enclosed units. Adjust the seat forward (lever under your leg) to free up some space behind your seat for your bagOnce you get your scooter, scoot scoot! Everyone follows the same clockwise loop around the island. Open that throttle and pass those dottling tourists. Udo Awaits!Use your horn, and folks let you pass. Beep Beep!Skip the first two big pulloffs where everyone stops. Its way too crowded and you may have to pay to park! Watch for the big bus! It runs opposite motorcycle traffic and takes up most of the narrow roadway. So dont drive in the middle of the motorway. The bus driver is very safe and watches for confused motorcyclists. It was very safe.Otherwise, beep beep, scoot scoot, and enjoy the Electric Scooterland of Udo!

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

Took a bus from Seogwipo early morning and it takes around 1 hour 40 minutes to get there as the bus stops on all stops along the way. Once there, it is a short 10 to 15 min hike up to the top where you will be met with a green crater. Unless you have a drone, its not possible to capture the beauty of the place unfortunately. On the way down, we waited to see the women diving show, but it got cancelled which was a let down as we only got to know after the show was supposed to start.

Took a bus from Jeju bus terminal (1.5hrs) and arrived at the port. Ferry to Udo island is just 15 mins away. Arrived at Udo, we join the hop on & off bus that takes us to 4 destinations. Bus interval is every 30 mins. It is a beautiful island not to be misssed out. Spent at least half a day or more at the island.

This was the first place to visit before we headed to other place in Jeju Island.O?셎ulloc Tea Museum is also located here and we just stopped by there for lunch and check out the products at Innisfree Jeju House. The lunch was not cheap , it's organic, There were also some visitors who were learning how to make soap, I think we need to pay for that course. I just bought a box of mini masks and move on to other places.Not too bad for a short lunch time and for photos maybe. To go about Jeju Island is best with to rent a car as it's more convenient to go for one places to another unlike in Seoul or Busan where subway are available.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This place will be good for nature lovers and those who are in Jeju to relax and get away from busy city life. It only takes 1hour to cover the area at a slow pace. You may get a chance to see autumn foliage here from mid to late Nov as there are quite a number of maple trees in the forest. (Note: Autumn is mild in Jeju, while northern parts of Korea are having colourful autumn foliage, we hardly see any colourful trees in Jeju till we came to Bijarim forest)

This island is 15min away from seongsan ferry terminal. You just have to fill in the passenger particular and show yourpassport. The island is full of atv for rent, do look out for the bus as the road are quite tight.  I shipped my car over at the price of 21000wonDo try their seafood ramen and peanut ice cream!

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.

This is the best track if you are planning to climb mount hallasan. From Jeju you take bus number 780 to Mount hallasan. Cost of taxi is around KRW17,000. To reach on the top of the mountain, it takes 4 hours. There are a lot of facilities on the way to Mount Hallasan such as toilet and place to sleep.

This is NOT really a museum. I mean having a teeny tiny collection and a small display of tea sets and tea cups and tea.... doesn't make a  museum. Honestly. Didn't help that it was drizzling and had a constant stream of tour buses... making it perpetually crowded. It's like 20 steps worth of   tea museum   followed by a cafe that sold some o'sulloc products. Stuff ranging from facial wash to flavoured tea and green tea milk spread. Since we were there we decided - oh hey let's try their apparently awesome green tea ice cream green tea latte & green tea roll. Meh. Nothing special. I've had better green tea food.Please just go buy a 2000 won green tea milk latte drink from any 7-11 or convenience store. A convenience store green tea latte is better than their caf챕's green tea latte. (Cost 6000 won)Their green tea ice cream(4500won) and roll(5000won) were equally disappointing. Nothing special. No harm dropping by this place if it's on the way - as it's free entry. BUT... Dont go out of your way to go here. It's nothing special and food's not worth it.
This is also a very nice site in Seogwipo, you can get there by bus, and then go down all the way to see the falls as close as you like, it is impressive.

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue.
