It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

This cave was decent but the caves in Jeju were much better. It was a nice get-away from the heat since the cave is nice and cool but when I went it was super busy so I was constantly wading through crowds while inside the cave. If you have  a chance to go, try in the off-season or go early in the day to avoid the crowds.

These lava columns are a must to visit when staying on Jeju.  They are basalt hexagonal columns similar to The Giants Causeway in Ireland, though not as big.  We got the bus to the Conference Centre and walked through to the entrance.  They were amazing and were our favourite sight on the island, although you can't actually get down to them and walk on them.

The world's largest nutmeg forest can be found on Jeju Island, South Korea.  A beautiful, old growth forest with a gigantic nutmeg tree as the central attraction, this forest offers quiet beauty to stroll through in a relaxed and rejuvenating atmosphere. The smell of nutmeg is distinct immediately upon entering.  Parts of the forest have beautiful red crushed stone walking paths and other parts have very well maintained wooden pathways.  To do the whole forest takes about 60 minutes at a comfortable pace.  Picture opportunities abound, and you'll likely be able to see wedding couples posing for their formal pictures amidst the beauty of the forest surroundings.  A great break from the hustle-bustle of other attractions, this forest offers the opportunity to enjoy nature in a very unique way.

The trip ti Mt Halla is great and do not miss it. Youu really should start early, and it takes a little less than recommended times, about one hour less if you walk clow but continuously.We walked three 15, 30 and 55, two males - my son and me and one female accompanied us.We traveled by bus from Seogwipo, busses go every 15-30 minutes since early morning to Seongpanak - busstop.Back we walked to Gwaneumsa and there is no direct bus connection, but take a taxi (for 5 thous WON) or walk about 5 km. We finaly shared taxi with very kind Korean directly to Seogwipo, thank again to the kind man. It was good and exhausting and we slept nicely after all. The next day we were ready to walk again. Unfortunatelly was very cloudy and walked upon clouds finally, however it was June, it was not too hot. There are two springs along the way - one up and nexd on the way down. Recommended to every who travels with teenagers:) Normal hiking shoes like trainers were OK, dont worry.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The mountain is extremely busy with tons of people and older koreans are not always very friendly toward foreigners, but the rude people are exceptions. In general the hike is wonderful, just very long. There is beautiful scenery and forests to enjoy. Take a jacket for the top as its cold and start early.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.
The beach by bus is easy to get to the bus stop is located about 1 or 2 minutes away, the beach is clean and the water is lovely and blue

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

So we went to Hallasan but didn't have much time, so we've decided to do the yeongsil train until the shelter and then go back the other way (eorekon? Haha). It was about 2hours each ways so 4 hours total. The mountain is free but to get there it's either a bus from Jeju city hall or a taxi (about 27.000 won - 25???). You have to be there before 12:00 pm otherwise it's closed. Really good activity, winter time so there was snow, pretty cool!!But wear good shoes and some coat because it's super windy there !I recommend it 100 times.

Really....it is just another rock with a legend.  It seems that everyone turns into rock while waiting for someone....story line is always the same.  If you are a big fan of Korean drama - Daejeonggeum, then this is the place for you.  A lot of tourist stops here....maybe becos it has no admissions fees.  Try and come early in the morning as the tour buses start coming in late morning.

quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.

Our plans to visit Hallasan were foiled by a typhoon the night before (we luckily still got to go, though), and we were all excited to do a nice hike. We came here probably 2 or 3 hours before the park closed (we did some other sightseeing instead of Hallasan, this happened to be close by), and the admission was free because the typhoon had caused some damage. Anyways, because of the typhoon and the time of day, the park wasn't very busy. It felt like we had the walking paths to ourselves most of the time (we chose one of the shorter routes because we didn't want to run out of time). It was a nice, easy, relaxing walk. It was also dead quiet except for the occasional group of ladies walking by with music playing on their phone's speaker. Oh and the crows going off every now and then, but that was kind of amusing since their call is funny to me (and different from North American crows). A good alternative if you can't go up some of the steeper stairs and stuff like in Hallasan. We got plenty of beautiful photos because the typhoon the night before gave all the woods a nice, moody atmosphere. If you like going for walks in the woods (even though these are all wooden paths), just being outdoors enjoying the fresh air, and you have enough time, this is worth a visit. If you are short on time and can only do one park or something, then make sure you try to at least go to Hallasan. I would definitely recommend this park over Hallasan though if you have any mobility issues, because the wooden paths are very easy to walk on and there doesn't seem to be a lot of uphill/stairs.

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

on the way it seems that the road is upward - the bus moving on  on its own without the gas but upon reaching a certain point it did stop & looking back to where you've been, it seems that the road is leveled.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Of all the waterfalls we visited, which included all the major ones, this waterfall takes the cake. How to get there:It is easy to reach, a quick walk from anywhere in Seogwipo to the shore. Taxi's help.Once you get there you pay entrance and climb down the steps to the beach.What we liked:Waterfall falling into the sea.Nice way to cool down in the summer heat (water spraying everywhere, cold sea water).Busy, but not too busy.There are much appreciated ice creams and cold drinks at the top of the stairs.What we didn't like:The idea that we looked as silly as everyone else with our selfie stick. Would we recommend others to go?Yes

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

Near the Osulloc Tea Museum, the Innisfree Jeju House has a cafe and a store. The selection isn't great, and they don't give you free samples, though you could score some Jeju only products. Admittedly, there weren't at lot of these products though. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store, so you can do it on your own), it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.I like Innisfree products, so I didn't stopping by, but if you're not into that or soap making, you may want to give it a miss.

review: Markets have always been interesting to me. They show so much about how the locals eat, shop, trade and work. Dongmun Market is pretty laidback. The folks there are not pushy. It's hardly touristy but still attracts a fair number of tourists. You mainly get to see seafood, fruits and vegetables as you explore the many lanes at the market. Aside from the market itself, the businesses nearby are also colourful and pix-worthy.For me, the highlight of the visit is lunch at one of the several restaurants within a zone at the market. They specialise in seafood, of course, and offer sets (featuring sashimi, a grilled fish, fish stew and banchan) that are value for money.Also don't miss some snack stalls there. My favourite is operated by an old lady (probably in her 70s)  who makes hatteok, sort of a pancake filled with cinnamon sugar, on the spot. It's a sweet, hot treat.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

I've visited many caves but by far this is the first lava tube that I have experienced. It is interesting to know the science and geography behind this magnificent tube. However, only 1 km deep into the tube is open to tourists. You can take a public bus directly from the Jeju bus station if you opt to travel on a budget. The bus fare is less than KRW 2000 compared to very pricey tours with taxi. The bus ride is only slightly more than an hour away from Jeju City.

It's pretty difficult using public transportation in Jeju to getting around expect using car. But this one is ok because there is bus stop in the highway, but you need to take a taxi or walking 3km from bus stop to get this place

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Hair and beauty treatment was the first thingwe went for. it was just awesome,. they made us feel us like superstars. One my friend spent all her time in the casino. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

It was along the way to Manjanggul Cave. As we had missed the bus 990 which could take us to the Cave, we had to walk the 2.5km way. About 1.4km's walk, we came to the Gimnyeong Maze Park. It was a fun place even for adults. We did not follow the map so that it would be exciting. Indeed it was, and the more lost we were, the more exciting it got.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It took me a long time to get there. All those folks with cars would have no problems. But I am on a budget, and I am bussing it all the way. I came here from the Seongsan Ilchulbong crater thing, and I took the 701 bus to the stop that said it was for the cave. Then I walked 2.5km to the cave. The cave was gloriously cold inside, as I was a hot sweaty mess by then (Korean people staring at the fat, sweaty American haah!). I took my time through the cave, it was nice and worth the trip for me, even though it took me almost 2 hours to get back after I was finished. I think you could take a cab for a reasonable price... but I am cheap.

It took a little over 2 hours by bus to get here. I feel conflicted with it, as a part of me liked the place but another part of me thought there was (yet again!) nothing special here. Plus the journey to get there was already exhausting so probably my feet were already asleep halfway into my walk.So only go if you can rent a car, it will take much less time to get here. All in all a relaxing place to take a stroll or read in.

It is quite windy here. Lots of people visiting this beach. The beach are covered by a beautiful black stones all the way. The most memorable experience i have here is to taste the grill squid! It was so fresh and nice until i almost left by the bus just because i want to buy the squid again..haha..if i ever come to Jeju again, i'll definitely come here and looks for this nice squid.

It is just a vision trick. The road appears going up when it is really going down, so cars and buses can glide down when put in neutral. The way the trees at the side of the road is planted tricks your vision. Coming from Canada, we have seen it similar to the one in Moncton, New Brunswick.

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the   jimjilbang   (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you   foreigners   out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called   Orum   in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I happened to notice a separate entrance desk that had pictures of SCUBA divers on it. I asked an attendant nearby in simple English sentences if they had any SCUBA diving and how much was it? It was only 119000 KWon and they happened to have availability right away! I've dove in other aquariums but this was the cheapest and didn't even require a reservation on a busy day! Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids. They loved it!I still had to pay the separate entrance fee for the aquarium (about $40 but I received a 20% off coupon at the airport) but it was worth it. The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Would definitely go back.Note: A lot of the aquarium features the image of a whale shark. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.

review: I had heard about these women from NatGeo. Being able to see how important these women are to the local community was impressive. The museum provides a detailed panorama of these women's lives. From when they are children to when they give birth to late into their lives. It provides some real size replicas of boats, costumes, and even foods. A must see. A little out of the way if you are not staying in the area but well worth the drive or the bus ride(bus stop is named after the museum). Price is reasonable and the gift shop has some out of the normal options.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.
I always loved this market. Everything you need from household appliances to fresh produce, chocolates and souvenirs can be found here. Accessible by bus and convenient aa it is close to city centre.

Highest mountain in Korea.  Beautiful area.  The wife and I went in midweek hoping to beat the crowds.  Forget it.  masses of cars, buses and people.  At 10 am on a weekday we sat in a line of cars for approx. 80 minutes just to get a place to park.  Once in, the hike was pretty strenuous.  Bring a hat and sunscreen.  We got approx. 2/3 of the way up (in a horde of people) before the park employees turned everyone back saying there was a   big wind coming  .  It was a nice sunny day and no visible weather to be seen.  Oh well.  I will probably try again when I come back.  But I will be sure and get here at daybreak and try to beat the crowds.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Great photo spot, many people use this beach for camping. Hard to find eating place or restaurant. The public transport also quite hard here! We wait so long for bus and finally we use taxi for way back hotel

For the ones who believe they are in good shape:Why struggle, why do it the hard way? because it is much more scenic and maybe only one tenth of climbers going that way. Taxi from town to starting point (approx 20 min) was 11.000 won on taximeter from my hotel in Nohyung-dong (near the int. airport) or take the bus but only on sat and sundays). Bus stop at Seongpanak when you come down from the mountain on the road. Check schedule and bus no. Taxi back 20.000 won (not on meter..)This is by far the most important place to look before you set out. THE WEATHER! http://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Hallasan/forecasts/1950 I wouldn't call my self an experienced climber but I did it in 3h10min up and 2h down. This is in a pace where I overtook and was not overtaken, and very short breaks, maybe only 2 min in total 5 times. The track is changes between rocks or stairs, I think it's well kept. Two toilet stations up and two down. None at the top. Bring 3-4L of liquids minimum, no passport nor entry is needed for the mountain (aug 2013). A windbreaker for the summit can be nice to have. The weather can change every minute so rain is likely. I did it in old worn-out runners. Bring food and nutrition - no shops. Good luck and enjoy

For the adventurous and those seeking a different experience. This place is located quite out of the way, however close enough to Halla arboretum as well. Quite challenging to find as Naver and googlemaps does not have this location up to date. If you are looking to find it, look for a bus that will take you to Halla arboretum stop and you could find it by following the street direction towards the arboretum. When you see a building with   playbox  , you've found it!There's an ice sculpture display area with an ice slide you can experience. Next level on is your VR experience that you could choose to experience (cost of entry varies depending on what experiences you would like to add on).As reference we chose the Basic A experience which provides us entry into the ice sculpture, Trick art area, 5D movie experience and 1 VR experience of our choice - cost 22000krw per person.You could spend at least an hour here and rest at the cafeteria before moving on.

Easily accessible via 15min ferry from Jeju Seongsanpo harbour, Udo is ideal for a short day trip or sorta those places in Korean dramas whereby couples miss the last ferry and have to wing it for the night). Anyways we made sure to check the ferry schedule. We had 2 hours and decided to walk instead of renting motorised vehicles (didn't have IDL), bicycles (too hot) or tourist hop-on-hop-off bus (too rushed). Other than tourists nearly running down pedestrians and into other vehicles, it's a nice place to explore & hike for nature lovers. Ferry return is a little pricey at ??8500 but should be ok if staying over. We tried the peanut icecream but didn't think it was that great. Basically vanilla soft serve with sprinkled peanuts. Perhaps the wrong shop.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.

review: C1 ( 2016.07.15 ) I visited there on my way to Psyche World, because there was located beside this one. But Psyche World was close and out of business. So I visited this Teseum Safari. But there was under my expectation for price, and many tourist was crowded by bus. If visited Teddy's museum in Jungmun, no need to visit there, I think.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Bangju Church is a picturesque little church that?s unmissable on the way to Bonte Museum.  It?s the unique ark-shaped exterior along with the surrounding water that makes it photogenic and there isn?t much inside (which is off limits most of the time anyway).  Despite being a short stop, there were always a half dozen cars in the parking lot with people busy taking photos around the church.

Awesome cave! The ticket price was 2,000KRW.  The transportation is a bit tricky as the bus stop isn't that close to the caves (additional 2.5 km walk).  You can take a taxi from the bus stop (4,000 KRW one way).

As with everything on Jeju, this is built for tourists. The cave itself is interesting but understand there is nothing but this one section of one cave that you can access. This is not in the least bit adventurous - the cave is lit well all along its length. It's the kindergarten of caves but if you haven't been in a lava tube before then it may be for you. Beware that if you take the bus to the caves, you still have 2.5 km on foot to the cave entrance, though you can flag a cab down if one happens past.  Overall ok, but don't expect to be blown away.

As a part of our school's field trip program, we went to the one of the known attraction in Jeju-do which is the Jeju mysterious road. While inside of the bus, our tour guide asked the driver to turn the engine off. Our tour guide pointed out that even though the engine is turned off, the bus still continues to move   way up  . But in reality, our bus moved downwards. It was like an optical illusion. For me, this attraction is not that amazing, just a normal road. On a positive note, if you have a lot of time to spend in the island, give it a try and experience the illusion.

Apart from walking 2.5km in the extreme summer heat from the bus stop outside (pls find alternative routes), the cave was unique and pretty interesting to see. Love the temperature inside to cool us down and be away from the heat too.

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

After visiting the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, we proceeded to head to the ferry terminal for Udo Island. We were surprised we couldn?t get a cab during winter. Hence, we ended up walking to the ferry terminal instead.Note you need to show your passport and fill up a boarding form in order to take the ferry, at 30 mins interval. We took the 1400hr ferry. A 2-way ferry ticket costs 8,500 won. Upon arriving the island, one has the option of renting an electric scooter, manual bicycle or take the bus. For us, we took the round island bus. Bus fare is 5,00 won, which you can hop in and out at any attraction stops.  We headed to Udo-bond Peak stop and hiked up. Unfortunately, it was drizzling the whole day. We spent about an hour before returning to the ferry terminal.I suggest you allocate an entire day for Udo island. If the weather is fine, it is worthwhile to stop by all the attractions, enjoy the beach and food there.

A group of 22 of us went to South Korea from 13 - 20 April 2014.  We visited Ecoland Theme Park after our flight from Jeju Island. If you have seern Disneyland  in California, you wil;l; have some idea of what to expect from Ecoland.  However, when we were there, there was this tulip festival.  So we got to see tulips of various colours in a number of places, particularly  near the entrance. Overall, the theme park is an exciting place to visit.  I have one grouse to make.  We lined up like everyone else for the safari park ride on the bus.  Guess what? Instead of our turn to get on the bus, the ushers pushed us aside and gave some other tourists (locals I think) preference to get onto the bus.  In all my life, I have never been humiliated this way.  Come on South Korea, especially Ecoland.  You are developed country.  Civilsed society don't treat tourists to your country like that. There were not  many animals in the park.  Safari Park Indonesia beats you flat.  I like tthough the bus driver got the bears to stand to get food thrown to them.

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

You're given a map at the beginning but it's much more fun to try and find your way without it! We got there pretty early so it wasn't very crowded. It didn't take us very long to walk through it but it was definitely worth the stop.

you should read the story of this museum.it comes to live cos there is a dream.it has a sharp appearance a vibrant red exterior in jeju when comparing with those surrounding buildings.the art pieces in the museum is nice but i do appreciate the way that the owner makes this museum as an art piece more.To renovate rather than destroy and rebuild keeping the scratches of time and inject the modern art atmosphere into this old building.although you may think the entry free maybe a bit high but it still worth to visit.the cafe and souvenir shop at top floor also nice to stay awhile.

We stopped by this museum at the end of a long day because my daughter  who loves science  was begging us to go. We were all pleasantly surprised. There were quite a few hands on displays like static balls  using bikes to light up a display  a few trick eye displays  plasma globes  and of course Tesla coils. The staff were incredibly friendly and although they didn't speak much English they went out of their way to show us around. The Tesla coil music show was quite cool - the coils were used to create different pitches and played both classical and modern music. It took about an hour to go through everything and cost ??0000 for 2 adults and 2 kids. My kids loved it! Great hands on science.
We stop here on the way to the airport. It's quiet interesting experience when the car moves. Can't help laughing inside the car as the power is off but it still moves.

We made a short stopover at the Mysterious Road on the way back from the south side of the island - just a quick 20 minute one would suffice. You can start the experience from either lane - there's a marker to demarcate where the Mysterious Road starts and stops.Basic Procedure: 1) Switch on your hazard lights; 2) Slowly come to a complete stop; 3) Prepare your video recording device; 4) Be mildly amused at how something like this can happen!You're done!

We had no intention of going to the top as it is a long day long activity . However how could we have missed seeing the HallaSan from up close. So we asked our driver to take us as far as he could . There is a driving spot till 1.1km where the driver took us . But it was nothing much than a regular hilly drive .So my personal reco if not going up there you can also avoid going to the 1100m point . See the Hallasan from far away. It's beautiful .

We decide to go up the mountain on foot. It was a long way but worth it. The scene from the this mountain top is unforgetable and undeniably great. We could have stayed here all day seeing the nature changed if the weather weren?t cold. Walking the way up was exhausting but the fresh air and the sights we saw at different heights really cooled us down.
Waterfalls have always been interesting to me and this one certainly was among the top 10 I have visited.

Waterfall is easily accessible from seogwipo town and surrounded by lovely parks. Entrance fee is 2000 krw but no one was collecting fares when I was there. There is a stairway down to water fall but you can see it from the top easily. Nothing spectacular if you have seen other water falls.

Very large temple with beautiful surroundings. Other than that it was a bit boring compared to other temples I've been to in Korea. If you're in the area it's worth the stop but I wouldn't go out of my way to see it.

This place is quite far from the main city so we hired a driver to take us there because you need to start early to be able to make it in time for sunrise.  When we got there it was still really dark since it was barely 5.  We started hiking up and there were few people along the way but once you got up to the top there's already a bunch of people sitting around waiting for the sunrise.

This is a very beautiful location and in a good location. You can visit here for any length of time that you would like. It is great for a quick stop on the way to other attractions on the south side of the island. Don't miss this one. Even if you have many other things to do there is time to put this on the list.

These cliffs reminded me of the hexagonal volcanic blocks forming Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland except with much nicer weather. Worth a short stopover while travelling the southern coast of Jeju.

There is nothing much here at the museum but the green tea ice cream and the green tea cake roll are fabulous! The green tea cake roll sold out in a very short period of time! We reached there at around noon time and we were so lucky that we took the second last roll! I guess the cake roll is pretty popular among the locals too as we saw a lot of locals stopping by at the cafe. I saw an O'Sulloc Cafe at Myeongdong too. We went in the morning and there were still quite a few of green tea cake rolls there. I wanted to get a cake roll the night before I flew back to Singapore (in order to maintain the freshness) but the staff told us that it has been sold out! The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. Other than food you can go all the way to the third floor to take some photos. Personally I feel that the scenery outside of the building is much more nicer. There's a big park right in front of the tea museum there are people who lie down and chill on the grass. There's tea plantation located opposite of the tea museum. We are allowed to wander around there for more pretty photos.
There are a lot of streets food here selling all types of local korean delicacies.  I love fried black pork with toppoki. Food are rather expensive here. Anyway worth a try!
The weather wasn't the best. It rained on the way up and was very cloudy. Would have been great if the cloud had lifted. Still was an easy walk to the top and a must do.

The trick worked for the car but not for other objects that we kept on the road. Not worth the trip unless on your way. There are a few cafes around that place so can be a stopover. Was not very crowded.

The top of Sunrise Mountain was obscured by clouds when we were there.      We climbed up.    It?s somewhat steep but there are benches for stopping along the way along with one restroom area about 1/3 of the way up.    Signage also in English.   It was extremely windy up at the top and we were in the clouds.   We had some visibility downward but very little outward.

The temple is very impressive and is worth stopping at for an hour if you're passing the general area - that said I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to visit.No charge for entrance but a donation box on entry/exit.

The scenery is absolutely stunning at the top. We brought our 4-years old kid along and we were initially worried if the hike is too tiring for him. We were so wrong! He loves the hike and has lots of fun along the way. Just make sure that you have sufficient time to finish the hike before it closes. Would strongly recommend this place for families even with young children!
The routes to the top can be hard one route with lots of steps up is very steep most of the way. Both routes are uneven and it does take 5/6 hours to do. Make sure you carry water.

The Joanne Bear Museum is one of the stops in the package tour that we availed of. It is basically a collection of stuffed bears that Joanne Oh has created  each bear hand made. There are three buildings where all the bears are housed. We were there in winter and the place was well-heated. The pathway between the buildings were open air  though. The bears came in different sizes  colors and variations. There are some depict historical or cultural scenes  others depict pop culture. The bears are all finely crafted. Unfortunately though  many of the signage are in Korean only.There are several displays where guests can pose with the bears. One of those bears  a polar bear  was featured in a Korean drama  ?쏱aradise Ranch.??I especially loved the displays that feature the acronym of the place (JB) because it is my initial as well. There is a souvenir shop which sell?봸ou guessed it right?봲tuffed bears. I wanted to have one as a souvenir so I was settling for the least expensive keychain bear when I saw a much larger 8-inch plushie being sold at a discounted rate; it was only 2 000 won more expensive than the keychain so I got it instead. As with many of the Joanne bears  it an embroidery of Joanne Oh's signature.

The cliff is formed from lava flow. Hexagonal basalt columns like those in Ireland. It is interesting if you have not seen this kind of formation. It will be interesting if you could visit during high tide and high waves as the crashing waves may reach all the way to the top.

Stopped here on the way to Segwipo from Jeju City. Had an incredible lunch at Innisfree House walked the gardens and then had dessert and tea at the tea museum. Highly suggest this site to anyone who enjoys serene landscapes and healthy/energizing food!

Stop by Alive museum on the way to visit other places spend an hour inside the optical illusion museum and play kart outside.  Karing part is fun with the two seater. (Kids can sit next to parent) and it is 4 times faster than the ones in Disney.

So we did minimum research on this thinking that the trip up would be somewhat difficult but we were way off that. We made it to the top but we had to push through it. Highly recommend bringing lots of water and snacks.
Optical illusion on this road.  looks to slope in one direction but actually flows the other way.  Pretty cool spot to check out if nothing else but for a photo op.  Should be done in 15-20 mins tops
Nothing spectacular but wouldn't mind a stop by as its along the way to nearby restaurants. Should try the hot rice cake and fish cake though.

Made a quick stop here and found it mostly overrated and not that special. There were an abundance of tourists around. One thing I did enjoy is the green tea ice-cream. Also taste tested the Jeju mandarin flavoured tea which you can buy from the gift/tea shop. Overall a good place to stop at for a quick break if you are on the way to other attractions around the island.

Love this natural rock formations along the coastal beach walk ... definitely not your usual sandy beach ... lots of opportunities for great photosThere are ladies selling fresh seafood catches along the way ... we didn't have time to stop for that though ...

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

It's a good stop if you're in the area. I get the feeling there's much more to do around but it was raining. Anyways it's cheap and easy to access. It's also right in the city so ot won't require you to travel far. Really nice spot for photos.

It was so quiet.  No one was there which made us think that we werent suppose to be there.  The monks were setting up for Buddha's birthday.  We didnt bother going into the buildings and i am sure we didnt see everything.  Overall it was a nice peaceful little stop away from some of the more crowded places in jeju

It takes entrance fee to enter the museum  but that's okay as there are three venues in total. With lots of different appearances bears  such as dressing up like students and wedding. The most memorial teddy bear is the president Obama  it is similar to the real Obama but in bear form. The top floor of the second venue is about wedding and relationships between lovers  so it is a great place for lovers to take pictures and have memories with the teddy bear couples. Although I am not a teddy bear fan  I took lots of photos in that first two venues. And in the third venue  bears are for sell  so please remember not to photo bears in the third venue as it is subjected to copy right. Finally  my father bought me a bear which I think is the cutest as a present of graduation. It takes about 40k-80k unequally per bear  but I think it is valuable as all bears are made in Jeju.So  if you think you don't have any way to spend your money  you can go to this teddy bear museum and buy your favorite bear as an emblem of stepping on Jeju.
Interesting on a rainy day and only if you have visited all of the important sights on Jeju. Worth a stop if you are on your way to Sanbangsan but not worth a special trip just to visit.
if u have time to come here..climb all those stairs on the way is definitely worth to do..the niew from the top is breath taking

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is 9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is  9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

I visited this aquarium with my family on New Year?셲. I had high hopes for it since it was rated as one of the top 10 world?셲 best aquariums in the world. I was impressed with the way the animals were kept and could tell that they put a lot of effort into maintaining this aquarium. The only complaint I had was with their Touch Tanks. It had starfish and sharks but there was no staff to guard it and guide people how to handle the animals. I saw a lot of kids grabbing the sharks by the tail grabbing them out of the water to carry them across the room and throw them into another tank. I was disappointed that such a conservation-based aquarium did not place staff at the touch tanks to make sure the visitors learn how to respectfully handle animals. However besides that a great place to learn about marine life and support Jeju tourism & conservation.
