review: I think the best way to enjoy the island is to rent the electric bike. We moved at our own pace and did many photo stops. There are many nice corners and colourful restaurants for photo taking. Great place!

I stopped by here on my way to the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak from the Seogwipo area.  It was nice but the waterfall was not eye popping as it was quite small.  Nonetheless if you are also travelling from the Seogwipo area to the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak then a short stopover for a stretch might not be a bad idea.

I rented a car near from the airport so this is the best way to get the chills up your back in this place. Dive up here. Leave your gear in NWhen you were clearly moving forward in a downhill.... Your car just slows... Stops then moves backwards!!!! What the hill????? LolI did it like 5 time still fled funny in a very great way. I recommend visiting this place just for the heck of it!

I have seen all the a lot of Aquariums in Asia and America. Comparatively this is not big as that with big shows but it makes use of its space and is a natural stop over from Seongsan sunrise peak. 10 minutes away. There are amphibians like exotic frogs iguana and Lizzard from all over the world Penguins and Pelikans Walrus seals and sealion. You can also sea them during feeding time.There is also a big aquarium with fishes sharps and stingrays. What I liked most were the small aquariums with exotic fish variety. It did not have whale shark which require big space and are usually in the wild. This I have seen in the open sea while swimming near it. Overall the place is cool although smaller by comparison but spacious inside. It is recommended because it is part of the it is on the way to or from Seongsan and educational especially for children.

review: Hike this 19.2km return path *9.6km one way on a rainy and cloudy day is definitely an unforgettable experience. Rocky paths have turn into flowing streams. Took  9 hours non stop to reach the peak and return. Thick fog on the peak most of the time and only manage to get a glance at the lake. Great sense of achievement when reaching the top
Good trekking course in great nature. But no confusion that there is only one way to see the lake on the top called Baekrokdam.
Don't go out of your way to stop here.  Takes less than 5 minutes to take a picture of the Dragon's Head Rick.

Another UNESCO World Heritage you should visit!This place is a peak form from previous volcanic eruption!I was allocated about 1 hour by the driver to went up all the way to the top hill and come down. Feel little bit rush. This place definitely should spend about 2-3 hours to enjoy the natural scenery in this place!

After I toke all photos then hurry up to the musuem and walked around. And I stopped at the bakery shop! You must to order Green Tea ice cream Green Tea Latte. Guide always cheer about Green Tea roll I think it is not delicious.
A nice venue to visit along your way - didn't see the divers but a pleasant stop off along the way as part of an overall tour.

A mountain with beautiful scenery. I did not manage to climb all the way up to the top as I was having knee problem but my friend did. It was really beautiful even when I was only half way up the mountain. I also enjoyed the nice cooling breeze that made me want to stay longer if possible. Worth the visit. Probably will visit this mountain and climb up again next time.

A great place for new travellers who want to explore or have an interest in Korea's traditional culture. This place is huge and there are many things for you to explore. It was raining heavily when I was there but it did not stop other people there to explore this place. There are some rest stops along the way to take shelter in case it rains. Ticket price for adult is 10000won.

You have to get up early to be on time.Around 20minutes to go to the top of the mountain, so it's not that difficult.But it's really cold at the top, and really many people are waiting for the sunrise there, so if u wanna take a seat, you must reach there early.If the weather allow, u can see the beautiful sunrise.It's really up to your luck whetherr u can watch a beautiful sunrise or not.Anyway it's wothty to go.If u are enjoying yourself in Jeju Island, u must stop by this fabulous Mt.

Yep, there are a lot of stairs here. It honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting it to be, seeing as how stairs are my natural enemy. You will probably be tired when you get to the top, but little kids and elderly people are doing it, so it's not crazy. It's over a lot faster than it feels like it's going to be as you're ascending. We were there in the late afternoon, and it was a little crowded, but not too much trouble. Most people move along at a pretty good pace and don't stand in the way too much when taking pictures. It's a bit more difficult to get good pictures at the top though, because everyone stops up there to rest and take tons of photos. It's worth the climb and you'll get some good pictures out of it if the weather permits. Even if you think you are unable to go up to the top, it's worth coming out here just for the landscape.
Worth a brief stopover on the way to other attractions on the south coast of Jeju but if you've seen stacks before, this is just another one. Accessibility is excellent though.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

Went to the 1100m point where the wetland reserve is. Didn?t occur to me that wetland exists on mountain top. A round trip takes about 20mins and was quite scenic. It was foggy when we were there, which adds to the ambience. Our guide pointed out some of the edible leaves and tree sap. Very interesting stopover on the way to the south.

We where on the way to the Love Park, then suddenly our driver passed it by some 20 metres. He stopped the car with the 5 of us in it, we were facing up hill, he turned of the engine, took the handbrake off, put the car in neutral and I kid you not we rolled UP the hill???I am told it's obvious its an optical illusion but amazed us!! It's free by the way, it's just a normal road

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

We were attracted by the promise from the literature that this was the only waterfall in Asia with 'debouches' into the ocean. Hmmm, you almost get the impression from above that some channel engineering has helped this along. Anyway, Wikipedia tells me that this claim is not quite correct. Anyway, we arrived as then had to purchase entry tickets. The stressed out man next to the ticket gate then seemed to think that we have not purchased the correct amount of tickets. We had. It was all the more puzzling because he was only 2 feet from where we bought the tickets. Maybe he was so bored he was asleep at the wheel. Or maybe it was because we were foreigners. Anyway, once that nonsense was resolved we headed down the steps, only to be stopped half-way down at yer another ticket check! Ridiculous, three check for a 1000-or-so won entry ticket. We thought we must be in for something very special. Alas not. Said waterfall falls a few score metres, generates a modest amount of spray and attracts thousands of people taking selfies of themselves and said insipid attraction. There are some older folk selling ghastly looking octopus slices by the rocks - poor animals (the octopus that is). We were not stopped for more ticket checks on the way out, thankfully. I suggest you just look at the photo on the web and go and do something more interesting instead.

We visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on two separate days - the first was in the afternoon to see the women free-divers' performance (1pm/3pm) and the second was in the wee hours of the morning (5+am) to see the sunrise. The free-divers were all middle-aged women who looked old enough to be our mothers. Despite their age, it was amazing how they managed to hold their breath so long underwater to harvest the seafood which you could buy from them and eat on the spot (they'll prepare/cook it in whichever way you want). The way they sang prior to the dive and the way they chatted and swam out to sea together reminded us of the friendly grannies in our neighborhood enjoying a nice chit-chat over tea. To see the sunrise at the peak, we started our climb at 4+am (it helps to stay in a hotel within walking distance to Ilchulbong). It was pitch-dark and torchlight was a must. The climb was shorter than expected and we reached the top before 5am. Thankfully the sky was clear that morning and we managed to catch a beautiful sunrise (around 5:30am) that was nothing short of amazing.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

We thoroughly enjoyed our day on Udo. We hired manual bikes and stopped at the little beached and cafes along the way. It was cold and really windy so I think it was quite quiet in terms of people compared to a normal day which is why I think we enjoyed it so much. The bigger beaches (especially the black sand beach at the end) are a terrible example of sympathetic tourism and are blights against the beautiful natural landscape. Blaring music, ugly buildings and structures detract from the stunning island itself. We chose to eat at a cute little cafe which had character and that was away from the others.

We stopped by the mysterious road on the way back to the hotel, Our guide did the customary demonstrations- car in neutral brakes, water bottle and measuring tape. Interesting to see if you happen to be in the vicinity but don't go out of your way.

We hired a taxi for the day but this wasn't one of the place we wanted to go. The driver, Charles Cho, unilaterally decided we should stop at Sangumburi anyway. We're glad he did. We've been to Kintamani in Bali, but this crater is smaller and within a more scenic and lonely area. The surrounding mountains and farmland are serenely beautiful. One of the attractions here is a patch of tall reeds, but at this time of the year, they have not sprouted yet.The crater itself is supposedly valuable because of the unique plants and animals there, but for us casual visitors, it's a nice, green geographical feature.There are remains of tombs there, but no information on them.
We had a taxi tour and this just happened to be on the way to a museum. It was neat to experience and see, but I wouldn't stop by if it was out of the way.

We drove our rented car onto the ferry which took us to Udo in 15 minutes. If the weather hadnt been so cold, we would have tried the fun looking electric scooters. We stumbled into a seafood restaurant to the left of the ferry terminal and enjoyed a sumptuous seafood kimchi hotpot. Ordering was not a problem as the service staff spoke mandarin. The place was an obvious favourite with locals. We spent 4 hours exploring various sites and even got lost. A friendly local policeman kindly pointed us the right way. We stopped by quaint coffeeshops and hugged their cute puppies. We were reluctant to leave this idyllic tiny island.

We did a back to back sunset/sunrise hike. Sunset was great because it wasn't hot and it was really nice and breezy up there after 20 minutes of stomping up stairs. You get to see the sunset on one side of the peak while you see the moon rise over the crater at the top. Pretty awesome. There is a water/coffee stand about halfway up in case you forget water, but the it wasn't open when we hiked it in the morning (big fail). We camped on the beach nearby, not the greatest...Garbage EVERYWHERE! Not just your typical beach garbage (cups, bags, broken plastic boxes) but long fluorescent light bulbs, peices of boats, clothing... The water had lots of debris in it and despite the sweltering heat, we just couldn't get ourselves to wade past the trash into the deeper areas so we left for Udo Island instead. It was also pretty tricky finding a good spot to post our tent. The tide comes up REALLY high there and the garbageless, flat tide-safe spots are pretty much non existant. Pretty uncomfortable night/morning, but at least we didn't have to get up until 5am to hike the peak. There are washrooms in the village which is about 10 min from the beach, but bring a flashnight cause the lights and water turns off at night.

We came just after the rain stopped. Love the layout of the whole place. Instantly brings you back to the past there are real people - Craftsmen Painter Potter man on the respective   villages   with living animals - chicken black pigs goats horses. It is a nice experience. There are old   games   for you to try on. Saw traditional drummers along the way. You can have greater understanding on how the past Koreans houses based on their occupations - fisherman farmer locksmith painter. There are school police station & court house too. Few of the famous Korean dramas been shot here namely Jewel In The Palace.  A worker told us if we came on a non rainy day there will be more activities. Entrance fee is on higher side - 8000 Won/ Person but it is worth a visit.

This was the last stop on our vacation. Unfortunately it was also the only grey/cloudy/cold day. The island was still a must see for us. The ferry ticketing area can be very confusing, so be prepared if you don't know any Korean. We figured it out after about 5 minutes of standing around, staring in confusion. Once we reached the island, we rented an electric car (from Gulliver's Travels) with side-by-side seating for 占35,000 for 2.5 hours and cruised around the island following the path. The beaches were incredible. White sand, crystal clear water at the shore, turning into turquoise water a little farther out. Even with the grey sky, it still looked amazing. We didn't climb out to the lighthouse (if you climb to the top of Hallasan on your visit, you'll understand why. Ow.) but we got some great photos of it. Peanut ice cream is way overrated in my opinion, but it was still a must since we were on Udo! My husband got the hallabong ice cream. We liked that one more, but the stuff they put on it tastes like mashed up hallabong peel, so it was bitter and we just scraped it off. There is a restaurant that serves (I forget the name, I am guessing) Hallasan fried rice. They make it look like a volcano! We really wanted to go, but needed to catch the ferry back. Overall, if it had been warmer and the we could actually see the sun, it would have been much more enjoyable. We talk about going back and spending a night on the island so we have the time to walk around it, instead of having to drive/rent a bike.

This was defiantly a must do event for Jeju! We thought it would be easier than it was. Towards the top it gets very steep and with all the snow and ice it can be quite challenging, especially since we were only wearing regular footwear and no crampons or even hiking shoes!We made it and 3 days later our legs still hurt but was worth the struggle! It took us 3.5 hours each way including stops but not including the time at the very top, which was almost an hour. So 8 hours total!

This was a terrific little museum. Excellent, helpful staff. Fantastic introductory film that they played in English for us, and top class exhibits. We came away with a deep admiration for the women divers of Jeju, they are tough, proud and awesome achievers :)

This tiny, delightful island feels miles away from anything familiar and mundane.  I highly recommend renting an electric scooter (for about 25 bucks for 2 hours) and driving around the entire island.  Driving around the island only takes about an hour, but give yourself extra time to stop for photo ops.  The place is dreamy and laid back - you can even spot the famous haenyeo (women divers) at work, and see their   dressing stations.    There is no   one particular amazing   thing to see on Udo, but rather it's about the whole experience of exploring this off-beat place and losing track of time.

This place was the first on my list of place-to-go in Jeju. We were quite rushing as we don't want to miss the Haenyeo show (I totally adore them since years ago while watching documentary!). We would love to go for hiking to the peak, but we are pretty much time-constrained. Make sure to wear comfy shoes as there are lots of stairs. Go downstairs (it's really tiring to go upstairs later) to the Haenyeo house for the show and be there early as those ahjumma (auntie) in diver suit will perform their Haenyeo song and dance before going to the sea (this is so much fun!). There is boat service provided if you'd like a tour. You may enjoy fresh raw seafood (abalones, octopus etc.) from their catch, approx. from KRW10000 for a plate. If you love horse-riding, give it a try!The area is surrounded with souvenir shops. Try Hallabong (citrus fruit), one of Jeju specialities! The sight is way too gorgeous to be missed. MUST-GO-PLACE!Haenyeo (women diver) show: 1.30 pm & 3.00 pmAdmission fee for adult: KRW2000Boat ride: KRW10000Horse-riding: approx. KRW5000++Hallabong: KRW2000 each

This looks like any regular road.  However, due to an optical illusion, your car without any power will seemingly roll uphill.  This was discovered by a taxi driver by accident.  If you?re there, why not stop by.  It only takes a few minutes.  You?ll see other cars as well testing it out.  This was the first stop of our taxi tour that day and it only takes a few minutes.   There?s an English sign explaining the road.  If on the way, why not. A bit of fun!

This is worth a trip to Jeju all by itself!  Going up to the peak looks intimidating, but it was pretty easy and we saw a woman in her 70s at the top.  It's hundreds of stairs and took about 35 minutes, but they have benches and a lot of shade on the way up.  There's a path designated for ascending and another for descending, and I recommend following them as intended.  We saw some people trying to beat the crowd by going up the 'down' path, but there aren't benches to rest on and not much shade on that path; also, the ascending path is a LOT steeper and the stairs are kind of narrow (like a typical home staircase), so if you go down the 'up' path, you'll be going down very steep stairs and shuffling around people, while the designated 'descending' path is a very gradual slope and much wider.  We went on a hot & humid day, but I unquestionably would do it again.

This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. When i visit Jeju, i stayed in a hotel nearby, so i can see the sunrise from the top of seonsan Ilchulbong. To see the beautiful sunrise, i walk from my hotel at 4.30 am. You need to buy an entrance ticket to this place.You need to walk the stair path, uphill, and soon you arrive on top, you'll find so many people already setting up the camera to capture the sunrise. after enjoying the beautiful scene from top, on our way down, my eyes can't stop admiring the beauty scene of Jeju City. Everything is taking your breath away in this place.You also can ride a horse or watch the mermaid show (lady divers). If you want to buy some goods for your family from Jeju (orange, souvenirs, cake, snacks), you have to buy it in Jeju, because you can't find any of these goods in Seoul. If you want to give a second thought on it, your last chance to shop is in the Jeju International airport (price is the same everywhere in Jeju).This is a very highly recommended place to visit in Jeju Island!

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This is just another roadside attraction that many people visiting Jeju stop by to see only because it is in the city proper. It is just a rock that could appear to look like any number of different animals.If your tour guide takes you out of your way to see this then you need a new tour guide because this rock is typical of any of the millions of rocks you run into along the seashore in Jeju.There are a lot of interesting things to see and fun places to go in Jeju but, this isn't one of them.

This is a very long beach along the south Jeju coast near the south-western end.  You can bike (there's trial, do segway, or a long walk) or drive and stop along places to take beautiful photos. At the end of the beach is Songacsan where you can hike for an hour or so - very easy.

This hill looks rather spectacular from a distance and the approach to its foot is thru a pretty green field. The pathway is well maintained and it's an easy hike up to the top, at only 180 meters. It's mostly a broad stairway to the top and makes for a pleasant evening walk. At the peak it would be a great place to watch the stars on a clear moonless night. Admission is free after   closing time   -- there's no gate.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

This could be an amazing place to visit provided you have good weather and great friends. Scootering around the tiny island can be fun if you stop off at the beaches, swim along the way and explore the caves and tunnels by the black sand beach. Definitely keep an eye out for the giant burger restaurant and the peanut Makgeolli stand (留嫄몃━, it's alcoholic rice wine!), both are delicious! Don't over-hype it or expect too much, just go to have fun and you'll be happy you went.

This beach was a short stopover point for us. We were on the way to another place.It was mid afternoon & the sun was very very hot, probably that's why there were so few people then. My guess is that those who are here came for the same reasonThe roaring sounds of the waves & the deep blue sea always gives one a nice relaxed feeling. In countries like Korea, there are lots of similar beaches & seas. So although it is nice, there is no need to make a special trip unless you are on the way to another place & passes through here for a short stop. Or for toilet breaks.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The Dragon Head Rock was rather disappointing since the shape was difficult to visualize as a dragon head no matter which ever way we looked at it.  However for a brief stop, it is worthwhile for first time visitors.

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

Take a ferry from Seongsan, jump on a bicycle for the day and peddle round stopping at all the attractions. It's only 1.5hrs to cycle at a slow pace round the entire island so easily done via a day trip from Seongsan or even Jeju City if you got up early. We stayed on the island itself but truth be told there's not much added value, just do a great fun day trip / cycle - and we are very much NOT cyclists by the way!

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

So happy we took the time to make the climb.  It's a lot of stairs to the top, so I would suggest you take along some water, and possibly some snacks, so you can take a rest part way up.There is one way up, and another down, which keeps things moving quickly.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. Toilets are unfortunately not clean, so you may want to bring some disinfectant lotion and/or toilet paper.The first part of the hike is easily accessible, the latter part less so. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!
Prepare yourself for climbing up to the top of the hill. Stairway is excellent, you just need extra breath, but it is a must. Once you find yourself you are at the top, it is so relieving!!!

People still live here!     There was no admission fee.   We drove right in and walked around.     Obviously, the biggest thing is the roofs which are replaced every year.     You still have the stone walls and the entry gate.     We saw several people who still live here but didn?t interact with any of them.    The village was a convenient stop on our way back from the eastern side of the island.     I wouldn?t make a special trip to see it but it?s certainly worth 20-30 minutes if it?s on your way.

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.

One of Jeju Island attraction, the rock formations that looks more like a horse head to me. Well, legendary it was a head of a dragon. We stop by for a photo stop on our way to airport.A good nice photographing platform for visitor to take picture. There is a stairway leading down to the rocky beach, down there you can see many locals selling fresh seafood.  It is not a wheelchair friendly place. Be there before sunset otherwise you will not able to take a clear photo.

On a trip to Halla mountain we came across this road. Our taxi driver was very excited about stopping to show us this local 'phenomenon'. It's just a bit of fun really where your eye plays tricks on you :)I wouldnt go out of my way to go here, but if your on a taxi tour its fun to watch other people here!
Near to Halla mountain, a beautiful stop on the way between the north and south coast, little taril around a pond

My son live and work teaching English  in Jeju , I spent 10 days with him in his apartment and this trip to  Seogwipo and the hike will always be in my heart.  We stayed in nearby hotel and woke up 4am started walking and climbing the steps to see the sunrise on the top and its all worth it .. Indeed Jeju has teh rightful name - the island of the Gods.

My mother-in-law bought my husband and I entry to this   museum   and I went in expecting ultra-hokey and a waste of time. I was really pleasantly surprised!There are a few   galleries  . The highlights for me were the Teddy Bear History gallery - where they use teddy bears to display historical dioramas including a Teddy Moon Landing, teddy bears knocking down the Berlin Wall, Teddy Disney World and more. These are pretty creative and well made. Some even include music.There's also an   art   gallery, with some famous paintings or sculptures reenacted with teddy bears. This gallery extends into more dioramas such as the   runway   and a Korean wedding scene. Not always logical in where they put things, but fun anyway. There are a few honestly significant teddies in the museum - a Louis Voittan teddy that cost millions at auction, and a small side gallery of Teddies combined with historical memorabilia from Teddy Roosevelt, with some brief English descriptions of where the teddy bear came from.It's not a top attraction if you're here for a short visit, but if you're around a while and want something cute and fun, it's worth an hour or two!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Along the Mysterious Road, have a few food stall, try out the grilled black pork sausage and many delicious food. For those driving, key in the number 7126988 (yup.. heading to Loveland, you will reach Mysterious Road first), most people stop by here on the way to airport.

It's not that high from what I thought that we need to climb. There are many rest place that you can have a rest on the way up to the top. It's really worth it, the scene is so beautiful. At the foot of the mountain on the way climb down, there are lady divers who sells seafoods which can have a try.
It's about 1.3km from the bottom to the top. Along the way to the top, u can really enjoy the fresh air and the woods. From the top, u can see hills and jeju town.

It's a hedge maze straight out of the movies, except with nothing popping up to scare you. It is only the hedge.  It takes about 20 minutes to find your way out and costs 3,300 for an adult. It's 500m down the road from Manjanggul cave, so if you're going to the cave you could stop by, but not worth the trip otherwise.

It was the best decision to travel around the beautiful island of Jeju with Jeju Taxi Tour Samchoon Kim! He brought us to all the places in our itinerary that we intended to visit and he even checked the weather prior to that so that we would not be caught in the rain. The whole trip was very comfortable and it was not in a rush. We took our time to see and soaked in all the goodness of Jeju! Samchoon Kim is also very kind and polite, I remembered one of the day he stopped by a morning market and ran down coming back with 6 freshly made Bungeo ppang (a Korean dessert) for us. That act really warm our hearts =) Not to forget, he also always offered to snap pictures for us so we do not need a selfie stick! Thank you for being a great tour guide and driver!

It was raining and our driver decided to start with this attraction first. Although before getting into the caves, we got a bit wet, but once inside we lost track of the rain. This is a lava cave and quite different from the usual limestone caves. The only problem is that we have to backtrack all the way out. When we came out, the rain has stopped and the sun was out. Just Nice.

It was Autumn, when I visited this place. I enjoy playing indoor coz its very cold outside. Upon entrance, I enjoyed already the music that u will listen to from generation to generariion, it was fun to guess them until u reached the dance floor whic you can see yourself dancing in the platform also, after that u will experience also, to sing and play some music instrument. Beside that corner, u can also have a chance to hear top 100 music alonh the way, u can play and take photo with all ur favorite k-pop star on the stage! While enjoying inside, they will give u a call if their hologram concert starts, everybody will run to watch this. The best part is to shop items, with our favorite k-pop star logo/dasigns. See you there!

It was a rainy and foggy day when I visited. It was very hard to drive, but went there anyway. As it is very famous place, not an attraction, for its artistic figure, it was a Must-See place.It is an actual church, so we had to respect the environment and the rules of the church.Do not wear sleeveless top, flip flops, mini shorts if you want to go in and pray or have a service.They seemed very conservative. :)

It took everything in me to make this climb.  But at the end of the day, my legs wobbling, I could say,   I hiked Korea's tallest mountain  Make sure to bring your food as the only thing available for sail will be ramen noodle, a favorite among Koreans.One tip, push through till you get to the area set up for sitting and eating.  Doing this instead of many stops along the way will definitely save you some time.

It this is on the way to your other destination, then no harm dropping by. We just drove past by the road, then came down to take some picture. A 10 min pit stop. Nothing fanciful. Not a big deal to give this a miss.

It takes about 6 hrs for hiking up and go back. The way back is rock path half of the way, so quite tough for me. But it's worth to hiking up. The scenery on the top is breathtaking and unique. I visited there on late May, which there were still some pink azalea blooming and it was very beautiful.Please beware of the weather and strong wind on the top.I'd rate it for No.1 attraction site to visit in Jeju-do.

It takes 10 min tops to actually enjoy the rock.  Its unique and pretty but that's all folks!  You have to pay for parking (500 won every 30 min) and believe me, it doesn't even take that long to see all there is to see.  We had extra time before rental car needed to be returned so we stopped.  But I wouldn't have otherwise gone out of my way to see this rock formation.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

In my opinion the best way to go around the island is a bicycle. About 16km. Took us 4h to make it, with stop in every single possible place, including a lunch brake, rest on a beach, etc. Most interesting for us were diving women, we had a chance to see at work in few places. Probably the island is crowded in a season. In May we had good time and enjoy the trip very much.

I'm coming from a developing country and would expect more from the markets in developed country such as South Korea. The market is as dirty as my country's wet markets. Generally the country is not tourist friend enough. A lot of interesting consumable   seafood   types in the market that I haven't seen in my country and wished to try. However, I couldn't find any label of the seafood stated in English or han zi (chinese character). The shop owners too couldn't communicate in any languages that I know. A lot of times my desire to try was stopped upon not knowing the best way to eat, eating raw? Deep fried or stir fried is better?Frankly, I would expect the overall standard close to the markets in Japan or other western countries.

If you have time along the way and want to stop for some black fur pig, you can learn about the history about the pigs from this village. It was great to learn and appreciate the culture first before we ate at a local black fur pork place nearby. Plus you get to taste some tasty tea where you can apparently taste all 5 different flavors, and horse placenta which makes a funny story to tell that it tastes like almonds.

If you have no knowledge of the K-pop industry, this may not be the place for you. But, we love it. For the ticket price, things it offers is beyond our expectation. If you have a personal preference of 'which' pop star you wanna watch for the hologram show, you should check its schedule online. The ticket has a 3-hour validity (I think it's a bit short, if you really try all the stations/ experience) There are 3 levels where you could see lots of displays (music, costumes) and to try lots of fun interactive games with cutting edge technology. For instance, to dance with the stars, to shoot a picture with them, where you could actually scan your ticket and choose from the list, which star you want to pick. We stopped half way to watch the scheduled hologram show, which lasted for about 30 mins, and it was fabulous because that is the singer we really adore. After the show, we continued with our visit for a while. You can print whatever photos you snapped (if you like it) on the spot with a small fee. Likewise, you may download all the funny photos you have snapped from their website later that day. We enjoyed ourselves tremendously.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.

If there is nothing else you do go see this temple. It is a sprawling complex that goes all up to the base of the mountain. Along the way if you do hike all the way up to the top, there are signs to explain the legends behind the names of the places you walk and why there is a temple there. But even if you don't it is still an sight to see

I was staying last week at the Shilla in Seogwigpo, and this was just a short cab ride away. Despite the slight morning drizzle, it held the attention of my 20 year old son! There were enough wow moments - spider web, Jack's beanstalk, mushrooms, football, dinosaur eggs, slippers... all made of glass, of course. I'm sure they would have looked even more impressive at night with the lights on. The cafe was worth a stopover -- you must have the freshly squeezed tangerine juice there. The souvenir shop sells some nice pieces of glass jewelry and ornaments.

I really feel sorry for those went earlier this year and totally missed the beauty of the silvery purple grass we have not seen elsewhere. It is such an easy walk so even you push baby strollers, or having a baby buggy, it shouldn't be too difficult. Anyway, you probably stop Sao many times on the way to take photos so it is not a tiring climb.There's only one small snack place at the bottom but a few nice wooden picnic booth for people to rest.  We saw some Korean families enjoying their homemade kimba at the top enjoying the scenery. I think it's a great family trip for about one to two hours depending on the age difference in your group.Selfie stick is quite useful here if you want to post in from too the unique grass.  Obviously don't dress in silver (autumn time).After this we went on another 20~30 min to the world's biggest nutmeg forest which is on the way to the east coast (5 Day Market and Haenyeo Women Diver Museum) to,follow in the afternoon.

I really did enjoy working my way through this maze. The entire area is beautifully put together and is the kind of place you just want to spend time in and enjoy. Unfortunately, uniqueness comes with a price. I thought nearly $5 per person was a little steep but it isn't every day you get to walk through a hedge maze. The maze itself is a lot of fun and is large enough to actually be a bit of a challenge. We met the owner and he is very friendly and interesting to talk to. I am glad we stopped here but, because of the price, I don't think I would do it again.

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I hiked for 14 hours (amateur hiker) because I'm slow and also have not been doing any exercise for years... It was raining and windy quarterway through. Then it was sunny on the hike back. Since it was misty at the peak, so I didn't see the lake. Go prepared with water and food. Two bottles of water to last you to the top. When you come down, refill water at portable water spot. When I said food, like actual kimbap, bento or even cup noodles. In fact, bring all three. If one of the guy I bumped into did not give me his kimbap, I'd have starved for sure cause all I brought was three bananas and protein bar. Some people even offered me mini chocolate bars and tangerines. Bring isotonic drink if you want to. Bring Hiking stick(s) if you're uncoordinated like me. Bring windbreaker for sure and make sure it's waterproof. Get a good hiking shoes tha can grip because I slipped a lot on the way down. Because of my lack of preparation, I've suffered for sure coupled with my lack of exercise lol. So really, go prepared. And if you're like me with determination, and don't mind 14 hours hike, please go early like 5am. Though they do have transportation to bring you down should you really need it. I just missed it...

Here is the best was to try the experience of climbing up the hill Come from the loveland (from the north) and stop at what seems to the bottom of the hill (there will be a sign on the other sign of the road)Stop your car, go in neutral put you warning signals on.Make sure there is no pedestrian and car behind you and release the break The car will start climbing the hill in reverse mode It is a bit dangerous as there are lot of pedestrian and potential drivers that dont understand what you are doing but really the best way to experience the illusion

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Great day out doors. Many options of travel within the island (drive from mainland, rent bicycles, various motorized vehicles) making it really easy.Roads are narrow so personally would avoid driving. Further the ferries can only hold that many cars which means expect long wait times during peak periods.Many nice small eateries for coffee or ice cream along the way. Beaches are really pretty too and water clear though I didn't see anyone swimming in dec (winter).Only thing that I didn't quite like was the rentals were pricey at 70000 won for 3 hrs (two motorized bicycles and one two seater). And that was after some bargaining . The guy mentioned that it takes 45 min to go around the island without stops

For us it was a bit of a disappointment that we would need international driver's licence to rent 50-125cc scooter/motorbikes/small car like vehicles on the island. So it is a good thing that they have the electronic scooters, which don't require the licence. They are way cooler to cruise around the island with.It was a clear sunny day, and we spent 2 hours driving around the island, stopping every now and then to enjoy the scenery. There are a few places to visit on the tour so no need to rush around the place. Be sure to make it to the last boat back to the mainland in time (for us it was 5:30pm, but people kept coming there late so it left just before 6pm). From the boat we were able to enjoy the setting sun, which was a great finish for the trip. The boat ride there and back was reasonably priced, and the scooters we got were 25,000KRW for 2 hours. We went there a bit late so the only minus was that the place available for us was with no insurance for the scooters. Still, if you visit Jeju and have extra time on the east side of the island, be sure to visit udo!

Few hundred feet of road that makes you feel like your rolling uphill with the car in neutral.  Best is to begin at the start point from a full stop place the car in neutral and release the brake, the car will begin to roll very slowly and it appears that you are going up a slight incline.   I would not go out of my way for this... although I did.  If you have plenty of time or nothing to do because of rain then why not.

Fall season would be dull here. We made a stop on the way to lunch. A few exhibition halls to cater for vegetation from different temperate and climate.? Otherwise, nothing spectacular in this huge park. The train ride requires a special ticket.

Don't talk, just feel yourself on the walk way to clim to the top. Open your eyes and record the scene to your soul. It will treat your mind, very well. Don't forget your water bottle. Be careful when taking your selfie.

Dived back to those nostalgic childhood moments when teddy bears once played as friends in your life. This Teddy Bear Museum has a wide array of collection of teddy bears, dressed beautifully in different costumes. The most popular bear will probably be the one dressed in Louis Vuitton clothes.What particularly caught my attention was the exhibition which actually used famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa, and the Teddy Bear was dressed to depict her. A creative way to carry out this exhibition. However, those expect to see a wide range of   depiction  .Overall, I felt that this was only an average stop-over, but will be good for families traveling with their young children. There's a souvenir shop on site too, where I'll be expecting young children to be bugging their parents to get them a teddy bear each!

Didn't think there was anything special about this as compared to other jeju attractions. Mainly a maze which could be completed in an hour, then u ring the bell at the top before making your way out. The kids would probably like that, I saw quite a number of teenagers and families with young children.

Did a solo hike in the hot summer of July, and wasn't disappointed.It was a long, easy hike up with some steep steps near the end of the hike. 10KM up and down, in total 20KMThere are some stops along the way, especially the 'base camp' where you can purchase ramen to eat.There are no railings or ropes to hold on to a few metres close to the peak, so this would be harder to do on a winter's day.Was kinda sad that the peak was shrouded by a large cloud, but nonetheless satisfied with the easy hike.Public transport starts as early as 6AM, so if you drive and want to end early, it would be better.

Cruise stop. Jeju tour. On the way back we walked through both this and the underground mall. A million oranges and fish stores. Neat to be among the Jeju people going about their day. Try some of the food! But watch out for the guys DRIVING up and down the aisles on mopeds!I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Couldn't believe that a car museum of such excellence would be found on Jeju Island in South Korea.the large number of cars covered all makes, types and brands and we just loved all the old advertising posters around the museum.The displays outside were also a delight and the museum was not hard to get to by public transport.? We stopped off to watch some of the races on the way back and that is also worth a visit.? They use descendants of the Mongolian ponies, and with their colourful jockeys they made a wonderful display.? The extensive grounds have lots to entertain children as well as a mini golf course in the centre of the race track.? Would definately recommend both destinations.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: Completely worth the early morning waking up to see the sunrise. It looks completely difference bathed in the early morning light than after the sun has arisen, so check when the sun rises and wake up early!Is it easy to climb up? My wife doesn't work out, and we took about 40 minutes to walk up the stairs, with occasional stops along the way. I do work out, and even I had to pause a little here and there - bring some water, you'll be glad you did. Otherwise, it's not really difficult, just takes a bit of stamina.

Circumnavigated this little island on a bike in an afternoon, and it was a lovely excursion. The older culture is still somewhat alive (weeding through the tourist stops), but even the bitsy coffee shops are endearing. Bicycle is the way to see this place, for sure!

As I can clearly assure that you wont be regret if you visit this place. This is my second visit to Seongsan Ilchulbong. We went there to catch a majestic sunset.  We reached the parking area around 5 o'clock in the morning then we straight away climbed to the highest peak. For us, it took roughly 30-40 minutes to reached the top of the observatory area. It is indeed quite challenging but its worth it. Just bare in mind to wear the most comfortable shoes and jacket, plus dont forget to bring a mineral water.

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.

Arrived in the morning parked easily, cost for parking at the entrance was 1800 WON and picked up a map.  Make sure you wear good shoes -- preferably with good ankle support and walking sticks.  The path is well layer out but does take some effort.  We did not get all the way to the top as it was closed due to a slide but it's nice walk.  Suggest an early start and bring water too.
all the ways up the top is basically stairs ,the design has quite a lot of resting places along the way ,if you are fast,half an hr can reach the top

A little bit hard and tired for people who don't exercise so much to climb up this height but worth it. Trust me, you can see almost of the island from the top of the mountain, feel the sea breeze and hear the wave sound. If you don't familiar with climbing mountain just try to go with the way down. There will be stair so you can walk easily. This way should be fit for handicap and elderly people too.

500 steps to the summit, take your time to climb those steps if you are not physically fit. The scenery from halfway on is beautiful and the highlight of the climb. Once at the top, we expected something nicer than what we saw of the crater but photographs are actually nicer. Enjoy the climb and scenery awaiting you though.

2 days in Jeju, this was probably the highlight of our trip. We didn't for the sunrise/sunset, but came in the middle of the day.  The place was packed with tourist, but it didn't take away from the beauty of the place.  The is a fairly long climb of a series of stairs to get to the top.  But totally worth it.  On our way down, we were able to catch the women divers head out, which was a nice treat.

180m to the top but more then worth it in the end. Taking the hike up the steps was quite a workout, so I highly suggest, prepare to break a sweat. My favorite part was taking pictures on the way down, there are many great picture opportunities. One thing I recommend is to take the extra steps down to the ocean, take your shoes off and enjoy the cool refreshing water. It is well worth it after after walking down.

You can get right up to the falls even as it empties into the sea. Where sneaks that day because there are a lot of rocks. Be careful and take lots of pictures. A taxi or bike ride is preferable but you can easily walk to the entrance it is just out of the way of the town
Yes! From far away it looks like a gigant clam!. No touring was available when we where there  but we parked near by and walked close and took pictures. It is huge  it is worth seeing!

Wow wow wow!! This beach is absolutely stunning!! We enjoyed it while staying at the Hyatt Regency. It wasn't packed at all on the side of the hotels side but there was an area roped away that had more people. It was so beautiful and although the water was cold it was still enjoyable. Must go if in Jeju!

With a minimal fee of KRW10k one gets to kayak along the stream for 20 mins. The water is clear and deep. Each wooden kayak can only take 2 passenger with only one person rowing. The catch is the ticket counter is a distance away from the port. And the best time to go is on a weekdays. Weekends are usually crowded.
Who knew seeing tall weeds used as native house roofs would be very picturesque against the clear blue October sky? Only in Jeju and only on the way to the Sangumburi Crater!

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)

well. this fashion street was near with my hotel & i've walked here quite many times in a week. not so special for me as i don't do shopping but i ate 2times in this street that was impressivefirst time i reached here at 1st day no any breakfast shop near around*(they are opened at 9-10am at least) quite hungry & finally i stepped in one of traditional shop that only served 3 types of food all was hangover soup ha. seem that for drunken. price not so expensive(but not cheap) and quite many stuffs. tasty but full. lady boss also quite nice although she can't well communicate with meanother times with fds that was in a quiet corridor seem quite expensive restaurant with old & korean deco. however price was acceptable & serve sausage stew. well we ate traditional sausage stew in korean style house(boss always walk out from his room & overall style was house instead of restaurant). he was quite concern do we know how to eat & taking care of our table. maybe it has no many tourist but only korean or japanese while we having dinner moment.
Well worth climbing up. Lots of selfie sticks in evidence. Music and commentary on the way up a bonus. Legs hurt for a couple of days afterwards - do your stretches!

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..
Well made wooden stairs lead you all the way along with the cliff line. Octagon shaped stones are amazing over the clean blue ocean. You?ll be taking tens of pictures over there!!

Well i get there by accident - really - i didnt plan to visit this park but good thing happened. I had so much fun back there. All labyrinths(maze) are great adventure. Just try to get lost and find way between tries without any map of maze! :P. Tickets are bit expensive but still it worth to go especially if you have kids! Well for grow ups it is also fun ( but make it harder- dont use  map)

We wwnt here because it was on the way to the airport.  It isnt really special but a good place to pick up some last minute souvenirs like chocolates and jeju oranges.  We looked around for 15 minutes then headed off because most of the venders were all selling the same items
We were lucky that the lady of the house was both detail and funny when explaing about the old jeju ways. A good place to visit and get to know abit of the culture.

We went up at 6am in the morning to see the sunrise. With cold rainy weather the event was less romantic than expected but well worth and good fun for us. We went up with our 3yr old boy. The way up is very well prepared and suitable for children who like walking/climbing a bit. We carried out son partly and party he walked. Well Organised tourist attraction.Entrance fee is only W2000.Have fun!

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.
