We went to the memorial hall to see the exhibition on Kim Manduk after we visited a recreation of her travellers' in that is about 150m away.I have always admired Korea's efforts to recreate buildings and scenes fron the past that are both infirmative and interesting.The exhibit at the hall added to what we had learnt at the inn.What comes across from the information cards and exhibits was a woman dedicated to the service of others.Profit was never her main motive. Nor self-aggrandizement.We need more people like her today.

We went there on our way back after a day of sightseeing. It is good to just drive pass that stretch. But not worth if it is not on the way. You could just spend a brief less than 5mins there while staying in the car.

We went on a Sunday at about 10+AM and it was crowded. Transparent kayaks have to be reserved in advance so we opted for a floating water bike. When we bought our tickets we were told to come back at 12PM (the time was handwritten on the ticket). There are shade and chairs at the waiting area close to the rides where you get called out when your turn comes. Since we had more than an hour to spare we headed to Jeongbang Waterfalls (about 10 mins drive away) and made it back on time. The bike was easy to maneuver and unlike bicycles the handles do not steer. Overall an enjoyable 20 mins experience for 15000KRW.
We went here to see the waterfall. The stones were very slippery but otherwise it was okey. The easiest way to get here is by taxi I think.

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We visited this last for the day at Jungmun Resort since this opened till rather late (~8+pm). Last entry should be around 7pm since it would take you around 1 1/2 - 2 hours if you're gonna snap alot of the photos inside. If you are already inside Jungmun Resort and are travelling in groups you can take a cab to this place since it would not cost much and you can save the hassle of walking. The paintings inside are really cool and we had a fun time snapping photos away. Effects came out rather cool on the photos. There are several sections in the museum and each sections has its own theme. Definitely worth a visit and we really didn't regret it. Initially we intended to spend only 1 hour in the museum since we really rushing off to other places in the night. We ended up spending 2 hours there. So do equip yourself with a camera and of course have someone with you to take photos for you.
We visited Songaksan on an extremely windy day... The winds were so strong we felt like we were gonna get blown away any second! The scenery is beautiful and there are no crowds. Serene and peaceful.

We visited here as part of a ships tour. The 8 minute film was very interesting. There are three exhibit halls. The first two were the best. You can see the whole thing in less than an hour. I wouldn?t go out of my way to come here
We tried putting our water bottle down to see if the bottle roll up downhill.. errmmmm... Yeahhh.. not disappointed anyway

We took VIP tickets from Jungmun Tourist centre  at 50 percent off. The show is very entertaining and involves lots of interaction with the crowd. The place is a bit far away and close to Jeju university. If you are going for 8:00pm show booking a taxi is recommended. The show is value for money for the deal we got from the tourist office. Apparently there is a rush pass which is available for discounts on shows for the same day.

We took many amazing pictures here against the camellia flowers. The walkways around the park were arranged nicely so we spent a few hours here easily. Overall one of the best spots we visited in Jeju this is a place you definitely have to include in your travel plans!

We stumbled upon this place whilst walking about but didn't regret it.I would be careful if you are accompanying very young children or old people as the stairs are made of rock and quite difficult to negotiate. Our 5 year old made it ok but required assistance.A nice place to visit but not much in the way of a waterfall when we were there. Perhaps they take the water in during the day? (that was a joke by the way!)

We stumbled upon this market while walking around Jeju. It was very vibrant inside with many vendors selling their products. The vendors were very friendly and tried to speak English to us. Some even gave us samples of their products. We bought some local chocolates. It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend some time.

We spent the night at a Pension at the base so it was easy to get to to catch the sunrise. From the base we could already see people making their way up. We were prepared to spend at least 40 mins to climb the stairs but surprisingly we got there within 20 mins. I would not say it was a breeze as we (and most people there) were panting and had a good sweat. Regardless of your fitness level just go at your pace with comfortable shoes and attire - the beautiful sunrise against the ocean is definitely worth it (unless it's bad weather)

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We rented a car. We reached the Tea Museum just after 12 noon. The car park was already full and we had to park by the side road. The museum is more of an exhibition of tea cups with write-ups on a brief history of tea and the origins of the Osulloc tea. Easy reading for a morning activity. There is a tea merchandise section and a cafe.We ordered the green tea ice-cream and black tea ice-cream. Both were good. The tea was very intense on both the ice cream. The green tea roll was just passable for us. Drop by if you are on the way. I think at certain times of the day there maybe some demonstration on tea but nothing was written in English so not sure of the timing.
We really enjoyed visiting this place! I recommend you to bring your car with you. but any way you will enjoy there

We reached in late afternoon and the place is not crowded. Very quiet and peaceful. Suitable for kids.There's a few restaurants 3 min drive away from the entrance that serves nice traditional korean food in decent price.

We manage to visit this Mysterious Road while on our way going to Hallasan but we are unable to try the road on our own. The road is really mysterious but the length of the road is not that long. We just try the road by using a mineral bootleg water and it is really awesome. You can try Visit it if you are curious about the road.
We loved the Alive museum. It was so much fun!!!So many funny poses you could make and was a lovely way to spend the day out.

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.

We had an old Korean man who has lived there for all his life guiding us around his own house in English. He was very humorous and a very friendly guide. It was an interesting and refreshing experience of learning about the old village way of living in Jeju!

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.

We drove around Jeju and decided to give this thing a go cos we didn't believe it would be possible. So we reached the road and there were signs that told you that its the starting. So all you have to do is to put your car in neutral gear and release the accelerator at the starting point and watch your friend's jaw drop. Recommended to visit together with Jeju Loveland as its just 3 minutes driave away. Admission at 8000 won per pax. pricey but its a pretty interesting visit XD
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

We came on a cloudy day so the water didn't look as turquoise. So if you're opting for a blue-green picture for your Instagram do come here on a sunny day. I like how it is connected to a black sand beach and the way how Koreans pile stones to make a wish tower makes me happy. 30 mins is enough for this place.
Way too many rules. Can't take off masks for photos  there are 3 small waterfalls that you have to pay to see. Don't waste your money. See a waterfall somewhere else in Jeju for free.

Was very crowded the day/time we were there.  There's a tiny museum which leads to shop and cafe.At the cafe we had the trio of  green tea cake/roll smoothie and ice cream which were very good.Then we headed next door to the Innisfree Jeju house.A nice way to spend a couple of hours.  There's a couple of very uncrowded O'sulloc cafes in Seoul too.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Was curious and it was on our way. We drove it twice to be sure we didnt miss something. It was also difficult to tell if we were in the right place. Then we saw a large group in the middle of the road and figured it out.

Walk thru a corridor of two rows of Buddha leading you all the way to tis great big golden gwaneusmsa Buddha. This golden Buddha backdrop contains many small Lohan buddhas in rows....there is also a small temple for you to pray

Visited this park on my way back from Manjanggul Caves. There were a lot of cats there as it seems the owner is pretty fond of them. They provided me with the map but could finish in about 8 minutes without using it. Nothing thrilling about the place though and one can skip it if short of time..

Visited on a rainy day.  Limited parking - so had to park along the road and take a muddy path through the team garden.  Tea shop was very crowded to went to the Innisfree jeju House about 60 m away - great food and can make your own soap.
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.

Very well manicured plantations and garden areas. Museum is professional and store was well laid out with all their delicious teas with samples in bottles for customers to smell.Limited parking space though. Could see people parking by the sides of roads all over the vicinity.Cashier staff was very helpful combining our global tax refund receipts when we made two purchases separately.Ice cream was good. Cream roll would prefer it like a Swiss roll where cream is well spread around the roll. Current style has too much dry cake at the sides.Beautiful packaging as always.

Very interesting maze. First 2 are fairly easy but the 3rd one gets a little tricky. Water mist kept getting in the way as you try to navigate so it gets a little more complicated. The kids and adults had a fun time. Should do it without the maps given so you just have to rely on sense of direction.
Very cute themepark to while away a good 1-2 hours. Good for summer when it's too hot outside. The rooms are separated into various different themes. Particularly good for silly selfies!!
very cool. a cave that was chilling yet interesting always cool to have a look into the past as it is.

Use your 3D imagination and spend a couple of fun hours. Where you can become part of each scenario from hungry dinosaurs to a VanGong painting from an explosive mine to be on a boat in Venice. Great museum best recommendation don't go alone to enjoy it more. Although other tourists are always kind to take some pic for you.

Understand that the day we went weather was harsh as there?셲 typhoon warning ; the parking escort/attendant wasn?셳 helpful at all is was raining and very windy we were traveling with a 2yr old baby  ask him nicely to let us ?쁃rop off??only but he insisted that we go to the other carpark to park our cars (the carpark has open lots and a few cars are coming out) ; I don?셳 know his against foreign or what but after we parked our car Far far away carrying the baby  pram  umbrella diaper bag we saw he letting the locals go in and park . We were so piss ; and it ruin our trip in jeju as my toddler felt sick after. His now down with flu thanks to them and I still got 12 more days in Korea . Very disappointed  will not recommend any of my friends and family period

Udo island is perfect for short day trip where you can enjoy the peaceful ambiance of the ocean while aboard a ferry.It may seem so plain and simple but for me it is perfect for a qucik romantic get away with a breeze of fresh air..It feels like the ocean is all yours...

Today is the last day in Jeju but since the plane is evening time so we went to Jeju folk village museum.It's worth visiting there! Every one of us really enjoyed ourselves going to learn their traditional style and ways of living! Furthermore the place is very beautifully designedmaking us just want to know what that's waiting ahead of us as we go along!I'll visit this place again if ever to go to Jeju again!

To experience something different something unique not know how the car keeps going with the Engine turned off.  We did it on our way over and our way back to the hotel.  It was fun to see all the tourist on the roads waiting to see each car going without the start of the engine.

This was seriously one of the coolest things I've ever seen. The waves crashing against the rocks was incredible. I went on a rainy day and that didn't take away from how amazing it was. Since it was rainy it wasn't that crowded. I stayed longer than many people though. I just couldn't believe it. Stay longer if you want. Definitely try to see this in Jeju.

This was really a nice long walk. Will advise to wear good walking shoe. The route was easy to walk just that when the wind come you can feel the wind blowing at you. You have to walk all the way up and you will be able to see the nice surrounding. It was really nice and we really enjoyed it.

This was just like Legoland in California just on a much smaller scale (no pun intended). It looks like it was once a better place and has gone to the wayside. My first visit was around December then again in June. December was really rundown then June the grass and greenery covered up the poor parts from the winter. Kids will enjoy it you will be wondering why you gave KRW to see it!

This was a great way to spend an hour!  It would have been more fun had I been able to navigate alone.  My friend was not interested in using the map and just wanted to finish for the photo op as quickly as possible.  We did go back into the maze to each of the six stations and stamped our cards.
This was a disappointing visit. There was not much in the way of information and it seemed like a gimmick if anything. Many buildings were under renovation.

This place were providing some information about teas making and how korean history about tea production and cultures. They also provide a cafe that served tea of course and some tempting Deli. If you visit the place on winter it actually perfect to spent time to get warm up and stuff your stomach. On Summer or Spring would be great for afternoon tea or take away for your picnic basket. And once more as this place is all about teas there is cosmetic and some supplies product made from tea essence. You could also find some fun activities at the creation counter at the third building near the tea plantation. Come and have look!!

This place was a little bit out of the way but we had a rental car so it didn?셳 really matter. The aquarium itself was very clean and well organized but I agree with the others that it is a bit overpriced. The touch tank like others said was unmanned and I can only imagine what those poor creatures go through with all the handsy kids that were around. The main tank was neat and they had a lot of variety.

This place is ok if you have some spare time and want a peaceful walk.As long as you don't meet any tours because they can me noisy.Its nothing special just trees and very little else.Not worth it if you have to come out of your way.

This place is considered clean for a local market. Mixture of raw fresh food and cooked food stores. We came here at around 10am and a number of cooked food stores are already open. Nice experience walking around and eating street food along the way. There are benches around for you to sit and have your food. Market closes at 8.30pm.

this place is a two story building tuck far away from anything however there are carnivals outside with loads of kiddie stuff. you will be greeted by man-sized teddy bears every great picture taking all the time had a fabulous time there.however if u are in korea for a party pumping time. skip this place.
This park was a five minute walk from the beach and the perfect way to pass the afternoon. It's huge! Such a great deal for the ticket price.

This natural attraction isn't that remarkable (rock that looks like a dragon) but it would have been nice except it is PACKED with tourists. It is way too crowded for my liking and most photos taken will include a bunch of other random tourists in it as well. My boyfriend and I were far more interested in the little food stalls set up around this tourist attraction - as you can try some local snacks. We came here as a part of a tour from Hong Kong.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is located a short distance from the city center. However a taxi ride from our centrally located hotel only cost about 6000 Korean won. On the day that we went to the museum we were able to get free admittance because they had some special promotion though I think that the admission fee is very inexpensive anyway. We enjoyed the museum very much especially the special exhibit entitled ?쏞hoe Bu`s Diary: An Unexpected Encounter with China.??This exhibition will run from July 21 to October 4 2015. This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.

This museum displays many clay artwork and handicrafted items from ages. The tour guide and the ticket booth employee cannot speak English anyway. However the souvenir shop in the museum sells many wonderful things that we could buy home as gifts.

This market is small compared to many others in bigger Korean cities.Anyway  Seogwipo is just a small part of Jeju Island. Can't expect too much.However  the markets in Korea are all too familiar & very similar. In every city  you will never fail to find such markets - supposed it's a culture thing.

This lava tube is different from a cave. it is as big as the new york subway in headroom and width. runs for 7 over km but tourist are allowed to see over 1 km in a safe environment. The ground is most and uneven in some locations so wear comfortable hiking shoes. Entrance is very reasonable for this UNESCO world heritage site!

This island is only about 10 mins away by ferry from Jeju Island. The environment is very clean and very beautiful. You can either take your own car or hire a scooter to go around the island. It only takes less than 2hrs to complete a full circle. I seriously recommend you to spend a least a day or two.

this is the only white sand blue water beach in Korea. So i was pretty excited to see it. Its quite shallow and you can easily play around. Its well maintained just like alll other beaches in korea. there is life guard always on duty. Careful while walking near the stones.
This is not a cave that was slowly worn away.  It is a tube that was created in a speck of time.  The unique conditions needed to make a lava tube of this size and length is pretty impressive.
This is located in the eastern part of Jeju Island. Taxi fare is around 30KRW one way. The place is well maintained and lots of Cats running around the park.
This is just a regular museum with a small collection of glass from different parts of the world. It is far away from everything and not worth the trip. I would skip it.

This is an excellent play place for teenagers. If you are a child 120 cm and under you must go with an adult. I recommend that if you’re really tall or big you might not want to go because this place has narrow tunnels. I almost got stuck in one of the hammock tunnels... haha.We saw this place on a pamphlet we got from the airport and really wanted to go right away and it was totally worth going.Remember to wear something comfortable because you’ll be moving around a lot so clothing with shenanigans hanging off from it probably won’t be a good idea. Or excessive jewelry. The price was 12000 per person for the Maze ep.3 and the Level 2 (harder level with timer) was around 5000?? But as a package it was 16000 per person. We had so much fun here!

This is a well put together museum. It has all of the explanations in English. The museum includes an outside area as well as the inside. It covers the history of the island as well as the way of life of the islanders. There's a wildlife and fish exhibit.
This is a nice waterfall to see going in to the sea. The walk down is all steps about 130 each way. The rocks at the bottom can be difficult to walk over.
This is a great place to visit on your way to somewhere. Worth about 30 mins of your schedule. See the formation and learn how they are formed.

This is a farm for Green Tea. First and foremost it is near the Glass park 5 mins drive away. So if you are planning to visit this place and have no budget constraints and have lots of time you can consider to spend 30mins at the glass park as well.The Tea farm sells tea (of course) and remember to try the green tea ice cream in the building. You can walk around the farm but be careful of the snakes. We seen one there.Nice place to visit whether alone in a group or with your family and kids.

This is a cool place to take the family. It fun and easy way to walk through mazes. With stream for kids to play in. A amusing part for me was U given a picture of maze so can solve easily. The inside exhibition is worth a walk through with more puzzles and games.

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!

This collection of old houses and replication of villages was fascinating. One could really understand the way of living in the old times when getting up close to the stone construction and thatched roofs and garden plots. This is a perfect walking area for anyone and especially families. As an added bonus the little restaurant on site was reasonable for local dishes.
This attraction is located minutes drive away from Jungmun Beach. Slow down your pace as you admire this amazing natural cliff formation.
There are three connected mazes.  You can go through one or all.  A great way to spend a few hours.  There is also a museum/exhibit maze in the building.

There are many stone carvings statues in the garden. They make the place looks cool as well as creepy at night. There?셲 not much to see and do here anyway though the stones look funny. But the staff can?셳 speak English.

The water park is ok. It would have been way better if you didn't have to pay extra for swim vests and extra for sun beds. So practically paying entrance fee doesn't mean you go and have fun. You are forced to spend good amount of money to have a good time.

The tea museum is not a muesum at all but instead a huge store selling tea. Other then that the tea fields are nice to look it. You can make some green tea soup and eat green tea ice cream. Be warned this place is always packed with tourists.
The taxi driver is punctual. He is always in the taxi waiting for you. He will lead you to the tourist spots if you do not have any plan.

The five-day markets in Jeju Island are fascinating places where locals converge for their everyday needs. Mostly under cover - it was a wonderful way to explore despite a rainstorm!What struck us the most was the incredible friendliness of the Korean merchants - knowing that we were not Korean - they were patient and was very open for us to try some of their foods! One vendor offered me some Kimchi and when she saw my reaction to the spicy-ness - she handed me a piece of pickled lotus root to help cool my mouth followed by a big smile!

The car drives  up the road by itself! Great fun. ( visual effect)It only works one way. You need to drive in neutral towards the shops. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

Similar to other markets i have visited in korea. anyway markets always attract me and I must go. I could find some sea stuff  which haven't seen in other markets. Sometimes I wonder whether it can be eaten :-)

Shinhwa Theme Park is unique in many ways.  First it tries to make its own characters seems as popular as Mickey Mouse and Spider Man - it doesn’t work but it’s great fun just trying to figure out who is who.  Second everything seems brand new - so it’s spotless and at the same standards as a Disneyland or Universal Studios.  Third - the rides are small but oh so knock out fun.  And there is rarely anyone there.  I don’t know if they sell a fast pass but there is no need for one because i don’t ever imagine it getting that crowded.  The food was quite delicious too - great offerings at multiple locations.  You can easily do this park in a half day and not feel like your exhausted or missing anything.  Like everything in Jeju I think they think they are expanding but who knows..  and as i remember the entry price is super affordable. Don’t go in thinking it’s Disneyland though and get picky - just enjoy it for what it is...a bold effort to start something special and first class and doing very well right from the start.  It was a great day for me and my daughter and her two cousins.  Enjoy!
Romantic place to strolling with beautiful grass/weed around along the way to the crater. Took lots of nice foto :) Heard every season the grass have different colours. Entrance Fee : KRW2000
rock formation. nothing particularly special about it. visit if along the way or have time to do so.

Rent a bicycle or ATV to enjoy the scenery here. In spring rape flowers are all over the island. The cliff by the sea are amazingly nice. Good place to go with your love ones if two of you want a short getaway by yourselves.

Reduced scaled of world famous known buildings like great wall of china and many more that I cannot name of all... PS - do pray that after u came in u can find your way out as there is no transport at the area

Really nice calming atmosphere and was not crowded with too many tourists. Beautiful estuary connecting to the ocean. Nice walkway with not too many steps running alongside the estuary.

Quite interesting maze. It took us a bit more time than expected to find the way out and it was funny. If you plan to take a brake in this area I would certainly recommend spend about hour to play in the maze.

Put your vehicle on neutral and it will seemingly be rolling uphill. Very intriguing.Unable to figure out how it happened but definitely have something to do with the way the trees were planted along the road.

Plenty of interesting glass installations in the park and museum. Really worth to see. Very nice and friendly owner. Many beautiful things and funny toys in the shop. The best way to get there is by taxi  it's about $15 from Seogwipo city center.
Perhaps it may be because that I am staying in a cityarea and hardly have the opportunity to see natural scenery. Oedolgae really takes my breathe away. Its beautiful!

Past by Wolijeongri beach on my way to other attractions. The beach is very beautiful. Good to spend 15 mins of your time there to take some nice shots.
Paid a 1000 (or 2000?) won entrance fee and my breath was taken away by the beautiful sight! There was even a rainbow at the end of the waterfall... simply beautiful :)

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

Our taxi driver took us here after going to Horseland (by the way there are better horse places).  The driver switched the ignition off placed it in neutral and it rolled up hill rather than down.  A very odd experience.  If you are passing by it is definitely worth the experience.

Our hotel room overlooks this sea. Don't think there is a way to get down but the waterfront makes for a nice breezy walk. I suppose the reason for the decoration on the barrier is to make the walk interesting and photo worthy.
Our guide June gave us a detailed explanation of all the places we went to. She was also helpful in many ways and answered our queries. She even recommended a good dinner place for us!

We also have a little chat with the tea-picker ajumma. one of the smaller waterfalls of he two but very well kept. shades of water can be seen along with a wishing well and a few picture spots on the bridge and walk way
One of the nice places to get fresh air from the ocean. Anyway I don't see how this mountain is different from the others. You can get fresh air from the edge of the island anyway.

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.

One of the best waterfalls in Jeju that flows all the way to sea... Spent a wonderful time in our free and easy trip around Jeju island with a rented car! Will go to Jeju again for the third time again!
one of Main tourist object. You must use your image to get the head. A lot shop on the way which attract tourist to spend more time than the main object.

Mr. Jang was very kind and extremely helpful within our two days in Jeju. He went out of his way to help us with everything. His car is very comfortable and spacious. He provided us with water bottles every time we entered his car.

Magpie Brewery is one of the handful of craft breweries in Jeju with a great selection of seasonal and year round selections. Little walk down pathway along the cliff on the seaside.Something to see while in the area.May be difficult for elderly or those with weak walking abilities as walk to the waterfall from parking lot consist of lots of stairs and wet floors.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.
Learning the culture of early Korean way of life early development of Korea. The weather is fine we enjoyed it.

review: Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

Jeju Beer Company is the biggest of the microbreweries in Jeju.  They are now the fourth biggest brewery in Korea even though the gap between the third brewery (Lotte) and the fourth is quite large.  Despite chagrin 12000 won for a brewery tour the slots filled up pretty quickly and we had to reserve well ahead of time.  The factory is a bit out of the way from the main road and in the middle of a rather stinky industrial area.  The pub area inside the factory is nicely decorated and a cool spot to enjoy a few drinks straight from the source even though not a lot of food is served.  The tour is well run but only includes one beer without any opportunity to taste more than one beer type.  They charge for everything like pens and coasters which I thought was a bit petty when people are driving out of the way to visit the brewery and paying a rather steep price for the tour.

Interesting but not a must. The village tries to explore the way of life in the past. Not to impressive.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

If you are a fan of green tea you should pass by here if it's on the way of where you are going. The museum itself doesn't offer too much information. If anyways in Jeju you will most likely walk this street. It's rather boring. I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

I love this place and how I wish that there were a film shooting there....poor me?. It was a long way to go there but as always it was worth it. If you like Korean Historical Drama Films that this place is must to visit.

I love open-water swimming and just plain jumping off rocks. This spot is ideal for both and is also a good way of interacting with locals. you don't even need to speak Korean to get along with folks here!

I know it is soon tiring waking up at least an hour before the sun is even up and then be driven all the way there. It could take an hour for some as it did for me but MAAAN WAS IT WORTH IT! I have visited half a dozen Buddhist temples in Korea and so far this is my favorite! This temple is simply gorgeous. We arrived just as the monks started ring the outside bell. We were greeted with open arms and encouraged to come inside the main temple building and to go upstairs to see it all. I have always been hesitant to venture into the temples to take pictures because I do not want to offend anyone but we were invited in to explore it was fantastic. so ornate. The three gold Buddhist statues were very large and beautiful. The monks where in the middle of chanting it was a mesmerizing experience so peaceful and relaxing. The grounds of the temple were just as lovely.

I have seen many Korean Markets in the course of my 18 days in korea. To be honest  no market have truly captured my attention. You can go to any traditional market in any state of S.K and you wouldn't be missing out. My advice for any Korean Traditional Market in general:- Go to any market that is decently sized that is convenient to travel to from your accomodation. - Take note that they do not have rubbish bins there most of the time and you'd have to return your trash to the store which you have bought the food from. - Be very clear in the number of portions you order as I had a rather awful experience ordering one portion and receiving three person quantity since I had three people.- Go in the morning/day time since most markets will be closing shop by 6pm- The fishcake skewers and the broth are great to enjoy on a cold day. You grab a cup from the stall to get the broth and start eating the oden. Payment will come after you return the sticks to the owner.Lastly  enjoy yourselves in Korea. Learn some basic Korean before you come as you will definitely elevate your experience in Korea. Koreans will always treat you better if they see you making an effort to speak some Korean as all other countries.

I have always wanted to visit a maze.  This one was lots of fun.  Just when we thought we found our way out  we were at a dead end.  The Korean people who were actually at the end were up on the platform laughing at us and cheered when we arrived. No translation was needed.

I had never seen dried lava before (other than when hiking hallasan which was only the day before) so I thought this was super cool. There are tons of informative signs along the way too. Oh and it's cool inside--not humid!

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

I didn't come to pray but to take pictures -- and this place did not disappoint. The carvings statues and paintings inside the massive temple were really beautiful. There was a dignity about the place; it was peaceful and solemn. We spent more time here than we planned (about 30 minutes) since we made our way down from the temple to the fields covered in canola flowers. There were paths to run in it! There were cherry blossoms and tangerines. It was a beautiful place and I would come back if I have the chance.

I come here first time. And the local guide will explaining about Korean folk life.She tought us about  how to choose real honey by easy way. And we know already why Old girl who is 65yearsold still stronger than 30 yearold people. (They eat calcium from horse and Golgi berry with honey!!!

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

While this is  just of the roadway, it?s fairly free of visitors.   The path goes alongside running water (or not - depending on rainfall).    There was about a 30m section where the path ended and we had to walk from rock to rock before the path restarted.    On the other side was a cave - Rock Shade Residence - which olden people used as shelter.   Entire area is a beautiful evergreen valley, well worth a visit.

While the hike was long it was definitely worth it. It wasn't too difficult, it was beautiful the whole way, and knowing I reached South Korea's highest peak felt like an achievement.It never felt too steep and even in the middle of summer the brutal heat didn't diminish the experience much. The only complaint I have is that parts of the path are covered with large, randomly distributed volcanic rocks that are a pain especially during the decent and my feat were pretty sore for quite a while afterwards.

While it is not spectacular like other caves around the world that are open to tourists, they are worth visiting due to their geographical nature.They are easy for families to visit, no bending over or crawling necessary.The temperature inside stays around 16-18c all year round. It is always damp, and most areas are dimly lit.

While climbing to the summit, please look back on. Scenery really beautiful. On the way to the summit three or four beautiful rocks, there are. It will take 1 hour for normal people of in their forties to take a round trip, on foot. There are many stairs. Enjoy the 'Haenyeoeuijip'  on the beach, too.

When you visit JEJU island, UDO is a must-visit spot, especially in summer.UDO is a small island next to Jeju island.You can go to UDO by taking a ferry.It takes about 20 minutes and you can load your rent car on a ferry as well.A ferry back and forth between jeju and UDO frequently.The best thing in UDO is to enjoy the swimming in the shell beach.Instead of sand, the beach in UDO has  small stone and shell. Due to the small, round stone and small shell particles, the color of the sea is wonderful.Also you can rent a bike or small 4-wheel motorcycle and enjoy the scene around the island.I visited UDO twice and it was always above my expectation.

When you are in Jeju, South Korea a visit to the Folk Village is a must.  during our trip to South Korea from 13 - 20 April, 2014, we visited the Folk Village in Jeju. In my opinion, the place is well set up. It's worth every cent that you pay.  The place gives you a glimpse of what South Korea looks like sometime in the past.  The houses built reflect that time in history.  And the houses in the village were authentically reconstructed.  Anyway, most of us in our group were impressed.  We give rating to the place.

When we arrived i thought it looked boring, then u step in and u find lots of nice standees and   stations   for you to take selfies and wefies (they even set up the wefie stand for you) ! After you flood yrselves silly with pics, you can try the maze. Its interesting walking in and out and along the way you can look out for cats that are just chillin by the greenery. Overall a good experience especially for families !

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

When my group and I first went to this market I assumed it would be small like a on the side of the road market where they sell fruits, veggies, and jams. This market was that times ten and the market even had the kitchen sink. When we first walked through they had fresh picked flowers, potted plants, fresh spices, 15 different types of kimchi. As we walked around it wasnt just food and plants they had housewares to clothes even puppies, rabbits and chickens. then we realized that they even had a fish market. This market of cousre smelled of fish we consumers selling squid, shrimp, and tilapia. This market is such a good way to imerse oneself into a the korean culture on the island. This was one of the places on my wish list to see while my group and I were in Korea and it was much more than I expected and I am so glad I went.

What WERE they thinking of! The   museum   is a few glass cases with examples of bars/boxes of chocolates. The   factory   is a table where you can buy cooking chocolate and make your own. The only good news is that your (HUGE) entrance fee is refunded in the way of a coupon to use at the (VERY OVERPRICED) chocolate shop. There is NOTHING here. It's AWFUL.Buy your choccies in the supermarket and give this place a wide berth.

what made this place interesting besides the dragon head was the locals selling their wares.  We also bought our first hallabong here.  I can tell you prices are pretty much the same all over for those hallabongs.  If you walk down there are a lot of ajjumas selling I think sea food, I did not walk all the way down since I did not have the right foot wear but it seemed like fresh sea food.It is a very touristy place, we just took a look few pictures and left.  Its one of those places we dont have to go see again once you seen it thats good enough.  But were are glad we did see it.  Again I would have walked down to the ocean side but opted not to might have been interesting, so make sure you have the right footwear, it is rocky and maybe a little wet.

What a great place to visit especially on a rainy dayIt traces the history of computing from the 50s to the present day in a very informative wayHowever of somewhat more interest to particularly children is the very interactive history of computer gaming. This includes the ability to play the old games like tv tennis and space invaders to more modern gamesA great way to spend a couple of hours , it certainly kept me and the grandchildren entertained

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

Went up and down seongpanak. Went with my parents who are in their early 50s. The way up gets a little tough after the 12:30 point. We started at 6:30 and got to that area by 11:00. On the way down gets very boring. Bring lots of water and wear shoes. You'll see old Korean people wearing stuff you'd wear to summit some crazy mountain but just good shoes with good grip (not converse) will be good for the hike. Of course hiking boots would help. Things to bring: hand sanitizer, water, sunscreen, gatorade/pocari sweat if it's very hot. Bring some food and bags for trash as you have to take it all with you. Overall probably 4/5 experience but nice to experience with family. Probably not good for young kids - people with health problems die each year per locals.

went there with my sister joining a local tour and met some new friends. strongly suggest NOT doing it alone... would be soooooooooo boring, but with someone else you can fight on which way to go.Learn more about your sense of direction,bring pen for easy remembering which way did you go.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

went there on a rainy day. Was't hard to get down to the waterfall but it was a little difficult trying to balance myself on the rocks while holding on to a camera. Was crowded but still manageable. On my way down, I found the lady divers selling fresh catch of the day and it was awesomely fresh!

Went there in the morning via taxi. Not many people. Admission: 2000 won each.There are flights of stairs to climb down when you first reach, so imagine the climb back up once you are done. To get nearer to the waterfall, you have walk over many many many rocks. Not recommended to go after rain as it will be super slippery. However, I love this waterfall more than Cheongjiyeon waterfall. It is nicer actually and you can get closer to the waterfall (of coz getting passed the obstacles of rocks).Love it actually but no way near magnificent.

Went there during peak of autumn season, how it blew my mind away. guess i mustve been so lucky to come about at the right time! The pampas grass/ silver grass leading the way up to the crater really makes a beautiful , breath-taking landscapes. With the windblows, and the clear blue sky, this place could give you that romantic vibe and really picturesque too. But I guess if I were to come during the summer, nothing will spark my interest. As for the craters ? nothing much to shout about. Its just a shape of crater, with greens covering it.

Went there after visiting the Manjanggul caves, fairly close by. Not necessarily a tourist attraction, but if you're looking to spend an hour or two in a nice forest away from all the coach visitors, this is a great spot. All we saw were Koreans out for a Sunday walk. There is a circuit path through the forest, all level, well maintained, took us maybe an hour to complete. Totally relaxing and peaceful.

Went here with a tour package bought from Klook. Entering caves experience feels great however, for it requires like 30 minutes walk to the Lava Coloum and you have to walk back (there is no other way out) so you need to make sure to wear comfortable shoes because the floor is uneven.

Wear your sport shoes, warm jacket, bring light snacks, a bottle of water, and of course..a determination. Dont forget camera as you will blown away by the scenery from the peak. Early morning is a good time to climb

We would have never imagined that you can make so much out of a teddy bear. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and I would suggest it for any bear lover but especially for families with young kids. As for the Alive Museum, I would strongly advice to go there either in the morning or early in the afternoon. We visited it in the morning and it was a bliss, but my guts' feeling tells me the crowds in the afternoon must be a little bit more stressful to deal with.PS: Don't forget the Elvis Presley Show. Yes, it is kind of tacky but really cute anyway!

We were there with a tour group and this itinary was compulsory.  Interesting to understand the history and a better understanding of the culture.  The guide of the village was obviously a Chinese but they spin it to say she is Korean (didn't see any)!  Sold products after the talk and items were not cheap.  360,000 Won for the Horse Bone Powder.  50,000 Won for the Horse Oil.  Saw at other shops away from the village, selling at 30,000 Won for the Horse oil.  Bought the Horse Bone powder and realized everything was in Korean!  If this is a State product and only sold in the village, pamplets of it should be in multi - languages as it is targeted at tourists.

We were staying in Jungmun so it was a long drive to the peak. It was a rainy day so the steps were slippery. I made it up half way but turned back when the rain came. It was not a very difficult climb as there are steps and signs to guide you. I saw the older local people climbing up with no problem. There are many foreign and local tour groups there. On the left at the base of the mountain, you could see the female divers diving at specific time. There are many restaurants at the base for you to reward yourself after the climb.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We were brought to this house with an old man waiting for us. He gave us a tour around his house and then started selling us omjia tea, honey, horse bones pill, horse oil products. And they range from 45,000KRW to 140,000KRW. I'm not sure if there was any way you could avoid this.

We were a little disappointed after walking all the way down the hill at Sunrise Peak to see the women divers, only to find out that because of the holiday, they wouldn't be diving today.So as a consolation, our tour guide took us to the Haenyeo Museum.  This museum was dedicated to the Haenyeo women divers of Jeju and Japan.  It's a very nice museum with excellent displays, and you will learn a lot about the divers.I recommend seeing the video show before you start wandering around.

We went with 3 children (aged 5,7 and 10) and two seniors, and they enjoyed the maze park. It was a smaller maze park compared to maze land, so it's not too difficult for kids. We spilt into two groups, one group managed to find out way out and rang the bell in 5 mins, while the other got lost in the maze and required rescue.  We spent about an hour or so, going through the maze thrice, and it was a fun experience.

We went to this folks village on tour. For me, this village is very nice and i learn a lot of their culture. For example, as a Chinese, we celebrate Chinese New Year. The elderly will give red packets to us as a sign of good fortune. Everything comes in red during Chinese New Year. But in Korea, they will use White packets and everything comes in Black and White during Chinese New Year. This is because in old era of Korea, when they have wars, the man will be wearing white colour war costume and when they come back to their own house, their clothes is full of Red Colour Blood, that's the reason why they thinks that Red Colour is not a fortunate colour to them. More and more stories you can learn from this place, especially from the statue, you can see usually man is eating always and woman is the one who always do everything. That's their culture. This place is really worth a visit, and by the way, we are not being brought to those shop which sells local specialty. Hence, i felt that this place is nice to visit and nice place to take photos.

We went to this cave as friends want to visit even it was not on my bucket list. It was impressive to see volcanic layers and massive path inside. We walked down all way to the end i.e. 1 km away and walk back again. Personally, I don't find it interesting.
We went to this area by a taxi. jusangjeolli cliff. this is not as beautiful as cliffs of moher in Galway, Ireland but a must see place

We went to the one at T 724-0228, mainly after the ferry landed and we were hungry, 'tween lunch and dinner parking wS available out front.  Staff were a little underworked so we go the full service treatment, good thing not tips expected (?);  we had the less fatty pork neck.  Served with a nice crab soup and nangymun noodles as a dessert.  Can't seem to get away from grilled fatty pork in Korea, have they heard of lean tenderloin here? Marinated  Pork skin was also served,

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went there because closest hotel, we driving to there and saw that is not to much visitor maybe was late evening, we try to going up, however in the middle of the path have 1 counter ask us to buy a ticket, we only want to walk around so we haven't paid and plan to leave, but we saw some of people can go up on the other way, actually is the same road but one for entrance and one for exit, you can go inside in the exit way but only have limited area you can visit. if you want to go up, you must need to paid

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

We went in summer, so the waterfall was less impressive (due to less rainfall in summer months) especially the 1st waterfall... the water was beautifully clear... be aware the the are plenty of steps up and down... my mum gave up after the first waterfall... the second waterfall is really pretty but there is no way to get access to the water below (unlike the 1st) as the observation platform was rise high from the river below... everyone including the fit and young gave up on the third fall due to the tough & long steps and punishing summer heat... its definitely worth going if you are in the area... fees for admission

We went here straight away. Had some street foods,some of them so good ,some of them so spicy!!!But quite huge market so look around first then try some foods.so many sea foods,veges,fruits and Korean foods.One thing... normal streets has bins but when I been 4-5 markets dose not have bins..I wonder... How or where these peoples throw away the rubbish...
We went here right as we landed, it was a fun way to get moving after sitting on the plane for a couple of hours.  Really enjoyed this cave experience.

We went here on our way to south jeju.It was a nice place where we can see the various art forms possible with glass.A sculpture of a horse made with glass was displayed, which was really looking cool...

We went as a couple  not expecting much  but this place was really fun! Lots of little experiments to do with electricity  plasma  light.
