The Manjang Cave was one of the   must-dos   in my itinerary. I can only say it was somewhat a disappointment. It was not quite as spectacular as I have thought it would be. I was with my mum and dad both 60. My mum did not take the walk well and headed back halfway. My dad stayed behind to do some photo-taking, Here's the bottomline:- If you have never ever been in a lava cave before - go for it!- If you are traveling with young children / older folks / people with bad knees and weak ankles - give this a miss. The initial flight of stairs can be quite a walk. The floor of the cave can be wet and uneven- If you have been to lava caves before and if you do not have a mental benchmark - go for it if you have time- If you have seen the most wondrous lava caves and already formed expectations - skip it... more than likely this might underperform

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The lava cave which need you to walk about one km in and walk back the same distance. You can walk with/ without a torchlight as there are lights in the cave as well, wear jacket as it's quite cooling in the cave. Better wear sport shoes since walkway is wet and slippery and uneven too. Overall its a nice attraction to visit :)

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The Jeju Mysterious Road, also known as Dokkaebi Road, lies on a hill at the foot of a mountain, and connects two major highways on Jejudo Island. It has earned its name, as objects and liquid appear to roll and flow up the hill instead of down, when, in fact, such image of gravity defiance is an optical illusion rendered by the seemingly high surroundings.

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of   impressive historical sites   compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The day was dark, cloudy, windy with heavy drizzle. It gave a rustic feel to the little fishing village by the beach. There were two families there and a couple who were taking pre-wedding photos. If the above was a normal situation, then it would be a perfect gateway for writers and people who want to get away from the rat race.
The day before we visit Mt Hallasan, it rained. Therefore, we had the chance to hike with snow. Very important to have proper gadgets as slipped a few times on the way down....

The crater itself is nothing to crow about. As they say, see one see all. However the area around the crater is fantastic. A few nice pathways up to the crater sight. Not much colour although it is autumn but fresh air and the waving pampas grass made our day.

The concept of the Innisfree Jeju House is nice. Good brand extension. However, don't expect great bargains on cosmetics. As a matter of fact, the range is limited. Best to buy from Seoul or other major cities. The cafe is a nice place to rest with some interesting food choices. However, it's always crowded and thus the ambience is not too conducive for a nice tea session. Overall, it's a nice short introduction to the use of tea in Innisfree product range.

The Cave was very different to other caves I have been to. It was like a Subway train tunnel. You can way approx 1 km of the reported 7km+ lava tube tunnel. Did have much of the usual Stalagmite and stalactite and crystal formations. The Lava tracks /grooves where interesting to me. But I was not a   Wow   experience.

The cave is really nice, and amazing as it was created by the lava tunnel, thus the floor is the original ground where the lava froze. The journey is 1km one way, butnthe cave is lit, so you dont need torchlight or guide inside. There's interactive exhibitions too inside about the structure of the cave that was created by lava, unlike any other limestone cave.

The building looks a bit old. There re space for parking. Inside the castle, there's hello kitty tree at the middle for photo shooting. When you walk inside, there're few theme of hello kitty for photo shooting and walk up the stair to the 2nd floor you will see a few rooms theme of hello kitty including the kitty cafe which sell drinks,Desserts and cakes. The restroom also there. The price is not high. The restaurant decorated in cute seating with hello kitty design. On the way back on ground floor you need to pass the souvenir shop. The price is not cheap for stuffs but if you are hello kitty fan it may worth.

The bridge is beautiful to look at, and provides a nice walk to an island that provides more opportunity to stroll near the water.? Big tourist attraction, and if you prefer staying away from the crowds, you may not enjoy this.? Great picture taking venue, and it doesn't cost anything, except a little workout for your feet and legs.
The black pork was really good. I love BBQ pork belly, but the black pork was a tad different -in a good way. It had more flavor and was more tender. I would go here again to eat!

The best way to experience nature and the beauty of Udo Island is not necessarily by being seperated by metal and a loud motor, but it sure is fun!  One of our best days while on vacation was riding the ferry to Udo and renting ATV's to tour around the island.

the best thing to do in jeju, it wasnt that attractive for me while i search udo online, my friend made me go with her, when i got there, im so glad i did it, it was so laid back, so nice, the circle island bike was awesome, the sunset, nice people. we enjoyed it a lot and forgot the boat time. we were late for the boat back to jeju, so we have to paid for personal boat, was way so expensive.

The best part of this is all the nature surrounding you while on the train (which takes you everywhere) , the river, just the pretty landscape. I'm a teen and I definitely wouldn't go there again, it was boring for me except for the nice pictures of the landscape tbh. There's a windmill, a big pirate ship, picnic side. If you have kids they are gonna love it, trust me. I went with other families with kids and they completely enjoyed it. If you want to have a picnic, I suggest this place also cause even when it's crowded the picnic side is literally huge so you have all the space you need anyway.
The bears are adorable! It is also a 10 min walk from the cheonjeyeon waterfalls, alive museum and 3100w away from the cliffs!

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans

The 1 star is not a reflection of Gapado but of the ferry company's bureaucracy.? Travelled all the way to Moseulpo to get ferry across to Gapado this morning only to be told at the ticket office, after we completed the registration forms, that we must also show our passports before they sell us tickets. Can't understand the logic of this - it's only a 20 minute domestic journey- and very frustrating as no mention anywhere of this requirement. Even Seogwipo tourist office staff made no mention when we enquired on timings etc. Very disappointed....

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

thank you for your visit. actually there are several ways getting discount benefit for the admission, such as discount coupon in the tour ad magazine, contracted certain air line boarding pass or on-line selling tickets. however we'll try to give another discount benefit to foreign guests who visit our museum.

Taking a quick ferry ride will bring you to a breathtaking place called Udo Island. Rocky coasts, beautiful beaches, and crystal clear waters are what you will find on this little farming and fishing island. I decided to rent a bike on my trip and wander around the coastline. In my opinion, it was the best way to see the island. Amazing photo opportunities and tons of places to get some fresh seafood along the way. The clear and shallow water is great for children to play in. Tons of little tidal pools as well. Biking allowed you to be outside and experience the people and the culture of the island. It is probably not a place for people that do not enjoy the outdoors or those that are afraid of a little bit of exercise!
Take the afternoon and walk around this beautiful park and zoo. All different kind of plants, trees, flowers, and animals, this park is way better than it seems. Don't miss it!

Such an awesome excursion. Doesn?t take too long and there are cool explanation signs along the way. Highly recommend and is super fun. Gets chilly so make sure you bring a sweater, it?s a nice escape from the hot humid jeju weather. Easy to park and easy to find.

Such a beautiful place where I experienced peace of mind and heart. Reading how Bunjae and our lives are quite parallel really made me think twice about nature and how we should cherish it as if it was our own lives. The quote that I will keep with me forever is   Potted plants wither when their roots are not trimmed, and people age when they do not change their ways of thinking  . Thank you for providing a space for people to learn and reflect on life amongst nature. God bless.

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Spent about 3 hours here one afternoon and was very happy with the overall visit. A full display of buildings, traditional way of life, farm areas, gardens and other typical tourist information, shops and food areas give the whole village a unique attraction for everyone. A little pricey in the shops, but as you walk through the areas you get a real sense of tranquility with the how things were. Very enjoyable and if you are there - make sure you visit.

Spend a couple hours here walking through the village and seeing traditional Korean way of life.  There isn?t much interaction with anything outside of the performance they have, which is 2-3 times a day and with the vendors.  They do offer horse back riding here and you can also have photos taken in a hanbok.
Spectacular waterfall! Definitely worth a visit. If you are staying in Tae Gong Gak Guesthouse, the waterfall is just a 10-15 minute walk away :)
Special geographical zone & it is interesting to visit.  But, if you have been to other bigger lava column sites such as The Giant Causeway, you may skip this one.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.

Small island - the main road that goes around the island is around 13,8 km. A good way to explore is to rent a vehicle - electric scooter, electric motor cycle, electric bike, or bike - and go as you like. But all the electric is required international driving license.
Since when did it became samsung ? The place spelling is wrong.! Anyway.. Nice to visit, entrance fee for adults 2500krw only and nearby is the folklore and natural history museum.
Several nice waterfalls around here. This is one of the nicest. Swimming is not allowed, but you can cool down anyway, so nice for kids as well!

Seongeup Folk Village of Jeju Island is the place that the past resident live in. The tour guide told us this place can keep well mostly because of the government. The government funds the residents to live here, let them to keep the old building and the culture well. When there have visitor like us, the resident will become a tour guide or shop assistant. It is a good way to spread the culture. Because the residents must know more about the culture than other tour guides. They will show the old tools and teach you how to use it, it is funny and you must be proud of their wisdom.If you like to watch the episode that comes from Korea. You must go here, because most of the building had appeared in the episode, such as ?Dae Janggeum?, if you are lucky, you will see the actor here.

Seems the name of the road has some psychological effect on the tourists. Is it mystery or reality? Hope anyone who is a land surveyor can throw some light on this with the appropriate surveying equipment or we need a long specially made spirit level to verify the inclination of the road. Without it, the so-called 'mysterious' is purely perception. By the way, there is a grave-yard nearby which adds to its spookiness.

Saw the show with a group of friends, one of whom was selected for the audience participation segment.  This increased the enjoyment for us, but the show was entertaining anyway even for non-Korean speaking people.

Sangumburi crater is a designated Natural Monument touted as the world's only flatland crater. The car park entrance showcases several large rocks from the crater such as the volcanic bomb and lava tree mold. During the eruption, molten rock flew from the volcano into the air and cooled into many exotic shapes. The area near the crater also contain several traditional Jeju graves - wide, trapezoidal stone walls surrounding the burial mounds. Visitors can walk around the extinct volcano crater rim, peer into it but cannot venture inside the crater pit covered with lush vegetation. The hills and Hallasan surrounding the crater is a picture of serenity and rustic greenery. Sangumburi is especially popular in autumn when the slopes are covered in Jeju?s famous Eulalia. Crowds and couples will be lining up for photos among the tall plume-like, silver grass swaying in the breeze. At a quiet spot, listen to the whispers of the eulalia dancing against the blue sky to add a pensive mood to the autumn romance.  Note: KRW6000 entry fee is quite expensive. Closes at 6 pm, except Nov-Feb closing at 5 pm.

Rushed to watch the sunrise. Starts around 5am and everybody walk as fast as they can but once reach the stairway, mostly starts to b exhausted. Took some rest by snapping some pictures. Suddenly reached at 530am and already some crowd booked their best location for taking the sunrise. Anyway its a must do activity once you are in jeju island.

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

Rather interesting show about the life of Genghis Khan. But a lot of dialogs on Korean, so it is better to speak Korean or know history a bit. Anyway, there was beautiful and spectacular stunts on horseback. We were glad we visited this show.

Put your rented car on neutral going   uphill   and experience it. Mysterious probably because for most it?s a baffling experience having your car in neutral but going uphill, backwards or forward ? hands off the wheel and feet off that pedal. The place is on the way to Jusangjeolli by way of the Mount Halla route from Jeju town. 5-10 minutes (no crowd here) and you have covered one of the ?touristy? sites in Jeju. A woman attempted to see what would happen with a plastic water bottle placed on the road, nothing did.  Why would any vehicle with so much metals built into it got pulled but not a plastic bottle? Go figure. I have encountered a similar experience at a site in Saudi Arabia near Madinah which has a longer stretch for that ?mysterious? experience.

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street ? you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

Perhaps I've been in Asia too long, but I feel like a lot of these markets start to look, feel and smell the same. It was fun to walk through but I didn't feel like it had a whole lot to offer that felt special. If you're new to Asia, certainly worth a walk though I wouldn't go out of my way to come here.

overrated spot with overcrowded visitors and cars trying to test out the slope. but in fact it is just some form of landscape optical illusion. So unless you are popping by the sex museum too, there's no point going all the way to see this small stretch of road.

Our guide was very knowledgeable about the history and culture of Jeju, and he recommended some wonderful food and activity options that we hadn't thought of, despite doing some research. Highly recommend this way of experiencing this place!

Our guide brought us here to understand the striking cultural lifestyle of the local folks of Jeju.  The unique and exquisite architectural design of the `primitive'' huts and cottages of the natives was impressive. The pair of well carved and exotic Jeju deities statues that were made from volcanic lava stood spiritually on guard at the entrance. The sculptures matched harmoniously with the decorative Kimchi clay vases left unattended in the manicured lush green lawn compound displaying a special cultural taste that reminded me of the unique Hindu traditions on the island of Bali. I always think that it is the vibrancy and dynamism of the native folk culture that made certain attractions so special. The unique Alisan native lifestyle in Taiwan is just remarkably outstanding and different from that of the Maori in New Zealand and again, distinctively unique from the Dayaks longhouse traditions. It is thus a pleasure and a must thing to do to visit a folk village in Jeju to look at how the culture of the natives and how it is being preserved here.  We were introduced to a guide speaker who showed us the many agricultural tools used by the local natives but the real commercialized promotion began when we were `lured' into a room with seats and the speaker started marketing a type of drinks made from `Wuweiji' traditional herb that grew in abundance in Jeju and is believed to strengthen and invigorates the mind and body. It looks like another `tourist trap' and on the pretext of going to the toilet, I escaped the aggressiveness of the marketing talk. I wandered around the cottage compound admiring the foliage and the surrounding native architectural designs until my group of friends came out from the promotion. One of my group members was anxious to purchase the `elixir' drinks to enhance her youthfulness and she shared the drinks with the rest in the group.   I came out from the cottage and saw there were many similar cottages around the village and there were many sales talk going on in the other cottages. The admission to this folk village was free but I am not sure if my guide earned any commission from the purchase of the herbal bottled drinks by my friend.Except for the commercialized promotion, it is interesting to visit a folk village in Jeju.

Our family visited   Cheonjiyeon Falls   on June 8th, 2019. To get to the waterfall, you have to walk a lot. There were a lot of small markets that sold simple snacks, which was sweet, but the way to the waterfall was not worth it. Although the way to the waterfall was harsh, still the waterfall was beautiful. I recommend this waterfall to whom that likes walking. If your stamina is poor, you will be tired . I don't think the waterfall was worth walking a lot.

Our family really enjoyed this walk.? It was nice to see the lighthouse and islands around this area.? And when we were there, the brushes were full of beautiful spiders and webs.? Of course, they were far enough away to not bother you.? It was really cool to see.

Our driver/tour guide took us here on the way back to the hotel. Actually, he said it was his first time there as well. My 17-year old son and I felt the uphill rolling and it was a weird feeling. Not sure why it was doing it, but we saw some tourists pouring water on the pavement and watching the water rolling uphill. Many years ago, I took my son to a similar   mystery road   in Manzanillo, Mexico. Back then, may be he was too young to feel it, or may be I was a terrible tour guide, but this time he finally got it. So, it was fun for us to take the quick detour and had some laughs.  Oh, and it was free and there are road signs tell you how to experience the   mystery  .

Our children really wanted to spend time on the ocean. This was a great introduction to the power of the sea. Big waves. Rocky coast. Perfect for sea shell collecting, sand castle building, and glimpses of aquatic life. We managed to watch the Haenyo divers bobbing their way across Jungmun Beach and later walked the length of the beach to see their catch.
Our cab driver brought us there on the way to loveland! Quite an interesting sight, no fees required! Do drop by if you're in the area :)

one of the many trick art museums in Korea. The first bit has the usual pose-with-renaissance-paintings stuff but if you don't have that much time skip that stuff and make your way through to the end where there's a pretty cool arabian nights themed room where you pretend to run from giants climb into the sky or escape over burning bridges. the station where you pretend to skydive while strapped to a backpack on the floor is quite special. warning : wear pants when visiting this museum if you wish to avoid inadvertently flashing other tourists. the sculpture garden is nothing fantastic and   little provence   is a bunch of stuffed dogs dressed in french peasant outfits in a lackluster room.

One of our favorite places! We practically ate at every stall! Best place to bargain for souvenirs plus a underground mall is just steps away....Nice place to walk around, food trip and people watch...

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

one of a kind museum... and it was weirdly funny in it's own way.. thankfully my son was asleep all the time... Sells kinky and   bachelor party   stuff... it was quite funny when you are with your friends!!
On the way to the mountain, you can see some horses, the kind that can only be raised in the mountain. There is some snow but not enough yet.
On the second day when i gave her my feedback about how she always silence and not really guiding throughout the tour, she snapped and her answer is “ this is my style “.

on reaching the car park ., Go and grab a J - Shape ice cream before you buy the entrance ticket to this Unesco Sights . To those who is not so fit you will be able to rest on the way uphills with the friendly stools provided at different stage of the climb upwards . Wonderful Sight await you on reaching the peak and you will want to catch up on your breadth as you soak in the sights . Never to be missed !!

Ok it?s a road that looks like up hill but your car can move forward. In my opinion you can skip this unless you are on the way. While we were on this road, one car started honing us for being slow. He later turn in to love museum rushingly!!

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Nothing spectacular, but I would recommend watching the sunset from the bridge if you just so happen to be in the area. It is also a short bike ride away from Cheonjiyeon Falls which is a nice site to visit during the evening.

Not suitable for old folks, because is full with rocks.. Better prepare a torch light or you handphone torch light. Inside very dark. The lights not that bright enough. Prevent any injury. Walking distance to the end about 1km, one way. Winter season, very fresh air inside the cave.

Not spectacular but unusual that it flows into the sea. You can walk across the rocks to get really close and many did for pictures. Be careful though. Some women selling freshly cut abalone, sea cucumber, snails - raw! Just 200m away from the base of the fall. Ticket is affordable at 2000 won even for foreigner which is the good part about most of the sights unlike some countries which cost double or more for foreigners.Don't see any restaurant so drive into the city seogwipo food street for plenty of choices.

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.
Not much to see, looked a little bit worn out to me. Any way its nice if you have extra time on your hands
Not a must visit, though a spot of fun if you have 15 minutes free as your vehicle seemingly rolls its way 'up' a hill.

No trip to Jeju Island would be complete without a trip to climb Seongsan Ilchubong (sunrise peak).  A relatively easy climb that our 4 year old was able to do herself with only a little complaining, it's mainly just lots of stairs. Round trip takes about 50min they say.  We didn't go at sunrise (we would have it we didn't have kids with us) which I imagine would be really pretty but still worth the climb up.  There is a shop selling snacks and drinks half way up if you need to, as well as many at the base car park area. There is also horse-riding for 5000krw and you can go down to the water on the other side.  Not easy to get to unless you have planned transportation or a car as not close to Jeju City, Segowipo or Jungmun.

No point come to this fall, not even if you are nearby. Not worth your time. I walked all the way in just to find out that The waterfall is so small. I don?t see how they made an attraction out of this.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.
Nice couple explaining their way of living in their own old house with their old fashioned habits. If you have ever visited some other folk villages in other Asian countries, it is not worth it.
Nice beach not far away from the airport. Too overcrowded during the swimming season in Korea, you can find stores and places to eat around the beach.

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.

Nevertheless, people always recommend us to visit this cave when we're in Jeju. what we found is around 2km long cave with cold temperature all the way. if you quite a fan for geology and similar, this cave is exactly for you.the 'main' attraction is located at the very end of the cave. nothing more , nothing less...come if you have free time.. but not suitable for older people due to steep stair and slippery.

My own experience was during dark, and I loved it. There was a spotlight highlighting the rock. Relax listening to the waves coming from the sea to the shore. On the way here I recommend walking through Yongyeon bridge.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.

My biggest regret, if there was one for Jeju, would be to miss this attraction. The crater may not seem much to some but this site was truly amazing. The natural occurrence was a sight to behold. It may be hard for some to imagine the significance of this crater but for me, I could relate to it and blessed to witness it. A not to be missed attraction albeit out of the way. The pampas grass fields were so scenic during fall that one just cannot miss this picture taking opportunity. The were so well grown here.

Must do if you enjoy hiking! We climbed to the peak of Mt Hallasan, South Korea's highest mountain.  Took us 3.5 hours up and 2 hrs down at a reasonable pace hike.  Beautiful autumn/fall leaves starting to changing colour (we hiked on the 13th Oct).  Despite what is advertised, there is a water station on the way up so you don't have to overload on water.
museum, full of teddy bears, so nice. we seem so much of different types of teddy bears with different way of presenting, cute way, rock way, lovely way and so and soooo...

Mr Kim, also affectionately known to us as Samchoon was introduced to us by a friend. Even before we arrived in Jeju, he was so ever helpful whenever I had questions about planning the day. He would offer the best ideas and try to accommodate to your requests as much as possible so that your day would be a breeze and convenient. He didn?셳 mind that we stayed almost an hour away from Jeju city and arrives early at our hotel to make sure our day starts off well. He actually does research and make calls for you and made sure that attractions and restaurants are open when you get there. He really goes to the extra mile to put a smile on your face! Not to mention showering our family with little treats and souvenirs. He also made sure my mum who wasn?셳 feeling well is okay and offered to get us some medicine. That really warmed our hearts. As a bonus, he?셲 always ready to take the best photos for you without you asking!
