There is one or two bathroom points on the way and a place to refill your water bottle. Entrance is free

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..

Definitely worth a visit, even if you only have a few hours to spare. This attraction my husband and I completed in just over an hour, there is no audio guide but there are informative signs throughout the cave. You return to the start of the cave the same way you came in, so take your time reading the signs but if you are tight on time you can read some of it on the way back. Being a natural cave/tube the floor of the cave is pretty rocky, must wear comfortable shoes. If you are driving around Jeju, and using the rental GPS, the telephone number to type into the gps system is: 7834818

Could not expect that it is so huge, need a lot of time to visit all the places. So many different plants, birds, even caves. cool experience and worth to visit if you on the way to visit other attraction because its on the way to other place, But if you just come and just for  visit this mysterious way its not worth because its nothing to do there just an empty road.

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. Climbing Hallasan will really take your breath away, both literally and figuratively. We did this in the middle of autumn and the colors around were so beautiful, it was worth all the effort. Be sure to start early and allow yourself 5-6 hours for the entire return trip up and down the mount.

Chose to visit this attraction because it is UNESCO world heritage site. I and my kids went into the cave, make our way to the lava column, took some photos, then u-turn to make our way out. Nothing to see unless you are a geological fan. It is OK, just another   for the experience   trip.

Cheonjeyeon Falls are very near to the Booyoung hotel and the ICC (International Convention Center), an easy 5 minutes walk takes you to the bottom of a very steep flight of wooden steps. If you chance to go up there (no English signs, and as far as I could judge, they do not mention the fall even in Korean) you will find the falls, only to climb down - and then up again. I found it very exhaustive. The falls had very little water, so were somewhat disappointing. Apparently there is an easier, but somewhat longer, way to get there from Booyoung, going to the Botanic Gardens along the main road.
Check the weather forecast, it was raining and very foggy mid way up the mountain, we went back another day after the sky cleared. Prepare warmer outer wear as it get very cold.

Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.? The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.? The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.? The calm music playing enhanced the experience.? The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.? Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

Best way is to go to the starting point (where it's steepest and most deceptive).  Make sure that there's no car or people behind you, put car in N, then release your brake too, to see you and your car going backwards UP the hill.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

Before we arrive, the tour guide told us the story of the dragon and how the mark of the dragon landed create all the cracks on ground. At night with spot lights, it added some mysteries of the legend and when we climb all the way down hill at the dragon head,. it complete the story itself. A good trip full of imagination
Beautifully maintained and a real variety of landscapes, from the swaying pampas grass fields to the almost perfectly symmetrical crater to the birdsong-filled woodland. Very reviving and peaceful.

Be sure to wear good shoes for the somewhat uneven - but not particularly slippery - walk and a raincoat for the dripping water.    There is only 1km of the lava tube which is open to tourists, so the entire walk is 2km roundtrip.   There are a number of informational plaques along the way as well as before you even enter.    There are restrooms and a restaurant by the parking lot.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

At eye level, the short stretch looked like an upward sloping road, but it was actually a 3 degrees downhill slant. A bit out of the way, would not recommend making a trip there unless you're from Jeju-si enroute to Hallasan National Park. Many of the 'mysterious bottle rolling uphill' videos have been posted on youtube in case you want to see the mystery! The real attraction here was the huge iconic black pig family statue. It was detailed and incredible. LOL

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini   jungle   that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.

Aside of the rock on the photos, if you follow the way out sign, there's also a place for you to swim in the sea. Unfortunately, I don't have much time to swim there. But I saw lots of people are having fun there.
As the only show in Jeju (while in Seoul have 3 theatre) so always full. Interesting, Fun & a Must see Show.

As the name implies, this is a street of restaurants offering black pork that is cooked in front of you. Basically, same offerings per restaurant with a lot of free side dishes (fish cake is a staple). Pork ranges fro thinly sliced to a little bit thicker. Flavorful, smoky but surprisingly, when you get out of the restaurant, the smell of cooking does not stick with you (unlike our experience back home). Way so much better than what we have in our home country as this is authenticity in the real sense of the word. We only tried 2 restaurants since we were only there for 2 nights, Dombedon and Donhyanggi. Both were ok. But I like Donhyanggi better.

As someone who loves walking on rocky surfaces (yes it does sound weird when I type it like that), I really enjoyed walking down to the base of the waterfall. You don't have to walk the rocky part to get you to the waterfall though - the steps from the carpark down to the base will take you close enough. Someone the rocks are slippery so be careful. Along the way I think there were haenyeon with their very freshly caught seafood. Loved this place; would come back in a heartbeat.

As it is UNESCO heritage site which I had planned to pay a visit. The temperature starts to drop slightly when you walk further in. There's low dim light installed along the walk however, the pathway full of small rocks, uneven ground and wet with little bit slippery. So might not be suitable for elderly or young kids. Wear comfortable shoes although i did see some ladies wear heels which i wondered how are they going to survive for the 2km walk. Worth visit if you are interested to know more on lava tube formation.

As I made my way to the waterfall, I noticed some divers swimming towards the rocky beach. Two older ladies were selling freash seafood for 30000 won. The divers were women in their 60's and 70's. I dined on the seafood al fresco while taking in the the vista and clean air. Well worth the 2000 won admission price.

As a bear lover, I enjoy this museum & appreciate all the hard work put into each & individual presentation & its theme. Be warn that its really for the young & young at heart. My only regret is that I missed the outdoor cafe. Didnt realised after I exited & look down thru the windows. Must have missed the signages? Overall , a good way to spend 1-2 hours

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Arrived around 4pm and bought 4 tickets...2,000?? for adults and 1,000?? for children. That's about $5-6 USD. It was 90 degrees outside but cool and refreshing inside. At the start it was 50F and got colder as we got deeper. If you get cold easily, you should bring a light jacket. I would wear shoes because it's a bit wet and rocky but I saw many people walk through with sandals and slippers. It's about a 25 minutes one way. It is pretty well lit for a  tunnel/cave. There's no climbing or steep terrain except for the way down but there are handrails. You will enjoy the experience. It's informative as well.
Approximately 2km walk all the way in then back out. Cooling inside the cave. If I were to go again, I would bring a torch so I can take better pictures and videos inside.

Another UNESCO site in Jeju, hence there are always a lot of people there. But the climb is actually not that difficult, as the way is nicely paved with stairs, and there are quite a few resting places along the way. Took us around 1 hour to climb up to the peak and down again, but other than climbing up to the peak you can also go down to the seaside to see the diver's performance! Unfortunately, when we were there the sea was rough, so there was no performance.

Another spectacular volcanic rock. Is a beautiful nature creation. Cold and Windy when you visit this place during winter. Nice places for photography. Is also the filming scene of the famous Korean drama   Dae Jang Geum  , where Lady Han of Dae Jang Geum passed away.

An interesting melding of pop dance and painting with 4 eccentric young painters creating unique pieces. that is when they are not vamping, dancing or goofing their way on the stage. I think a worthwhile show for kids to give them some appreciation for painting and for adults who have just had a sochu laden dinner.It's entertaining enough, but seriously, a bit weird.

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.

Amazing beachside for prewedding photos as there are this colorful chairs that are always available there as props. The beach was clean and there are cafes and the famous colorful candle gel gift shop. Great visit with family, couples or for photoshoots!

Always you can see from Korean drama movies of their house. Now you can see from your eyes. How the house split in few session. Such as, toilet and bath area. Quite interesting. Do not miss it.. must go and visit.

Although this place was packed with tourists, it was my favorite site in jejudo. The rock formations are like Giant's causeway in Ireland with the hexagonal rock formations at different levels. Since we visited right after the hurricane, the waves would cover the lower level of rocks but it was amazing when the water subsided and the rocks were revealed in those amazing shapes!
Although the weather wasn't perfect for a visit this afternoon, however, it hasn't spoiled a positive impression. Lots of tourists anyways, and it leaves a good feeling of connectedness with nature.
Although the area seems small, but quite interesting. It took 30 minutes for us to find out the way out and we had great fun with lots of pictures. Well recommended for visiting.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

After being in the cave, this is a good way to warm your body under the sun (well, at least during this season).So, it took 10 minutes to work out the right direction with the map, then we tried without the map and again it was ten minutes, then we left our 5 years old daughter to find the way out...still 10 minutes.I cannot define it challenging but fun for sure and super-rewarding to see your kid beaming with light every time she play the bell!Definitely worth combining cave and maze!

After all the hype about Manjanggul Cave, our expectations were high but were disappointed. Nothing spectacular to see unless you are interested in the stones that you will walk on in the dim, damp cave. You will come out the same way you went in.

After a 1.5-hour drive in the wee hours of a beautiful night, we finally got to the ticket office at 5:50am.... we didn't expect to see this crowd (well, we thought we alone were the crazy ones).... we embarked on the trek saying... not bad!!! After 5 minutes, if was like... pooff!!!! After  another 10 minutes, we were exhausted.. after yet another 5 minutes, it was a killer.... anyways, we made it to the peak at 6:18am and imagine our shock... there was a sea of people up there all set with their cameras...At precisely 6:28, it was there... flaming orange and rising at a speed unmatched (in sunrise). Spectacular!!! Fabulous!!!! Breath-taking!!! Start of a new day... a new way... new hopes... everything positive. It was so worth that strenuous climb.. If you are in Jeju, you gotta do this! Yes, the steps are high and tough, but so doable. We saw some people in ballerina shoes, with their fancy skirts and stockings.. keep the dressing for the yatch tours.. for this one, be ready for a mini hike.

Actually originally didn't think to visit this place. But coincidence have the chance, me and my travel partners was shock to see with our own eyes for the water and bottle both run to the upfront road which its was suppose to be opposite way....Make youself drop by to see this amazing effect while you around in Jeju. This place is just very nearby the Sex Museum which we didn't go but passby~

A quiet valley in an evergreen forest, the place is almost free of foreign tourists and allows one to capture the most tranquil moments of nature. Where cliffs and reflective pools of crystal clear water meet, lined by stones, guarded by trees and filled with crisp air. The sunlight peeking through the trees permeates a serene and mesmerising ambience in the valley. Look out for the stone wells and Rock Shade Residence along the way. The Rock Shade Residence formed from volcanic lava were used by ancient inhabitants of Jeju Island as shelter. It is said that Andeok Valley has water flowing all seasons long.  With such charming beauty, its no wonder Chusa Kim Jeong-hee, a renowned Joseon-era scholar, used to visit here for contemplation and perhaps, inspiration. Spring and fall would be great for light trekking while the cool forest provides the ultimate summer shade. Nearby attractions: O'Sulloc Tea Museum, Camellia Hill and Jungmun Resorts.Trivia: Andeok Valley was also the filming location of historical K-drama   Slave Hunter   (Chuno in Korean)

A pleasant park that protects the 3 holes in the ground from which sprang the demigods who founded the Kingdom of Tamna. It also houses a small museum which tells the story of the founding of Tamna, as well as buildings for the clan rituals that are held each year to mark the anniversary. Although in the city it is a fairly quiet and reflective place where you can get away from the city noise under the tall trees which provided some much needed shade during our visit.

A long lava tube with about 1km opened to public.  Very easy to walk as perfectly level all the way apart from the initial steps, and wide and spacious (up to 23m high and 18m wide). Lots of interesting volcanic geology, features, etc. Well worth visiting.

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

A bit out of the way so had to take a taxi. The bar gives you your taxi fee x2 in free drinks which is great. We arrived early so wasn?셳 many people but didn?셳 matter as were so many bar games to play for free.Filled up later on and ended up being packed. Lots of entertainment and games with prizes. Jump rope, dance competitions etc

50 minutes show. Is definitely worth for money as both my kids enjoyed it. There are Chinese subtitle shown on the side screen, thus I am able to understand. Perhaps we are the only foreigner there. I presumed they know we understand Chinese thus provided Chinese subtitle? I sat in the middle of the stage, in another way sometime this may not be the best place as some show like throwing basketball I can see the back of the elephant only. The ticket price is reasonable. Adult 15k, youth 12k and child 10k. There is elephant ride 18k per pax which I do not pay for it. After the show can take photo with the elephant. Do not need to come early to this place as there's nothing to do here except the elephant ride. The performance of the show is at 1030, 130, 3pm,450pm. While waiting, there have 3 little elephant trojan to ride for the kids. There has a little cafe selling pop corn and snacks.

2 maze garden which worth to explore, test your capability to overcome the obstacle in finding your way out. There is 2 giant mazes within the park come with easy & challenging route to explore. RM has make this place popular

- Jeju is also known for it's high quality green tea. And here O'Sulloc Tea Museum you can taste many green tea-flavored foods.- Though this place has a   Museum   on its name it's more like tea shop & garden observatory.- Good place for spending time and chat.- Various kinds of  flavored-tea-products are so attractive. you can smell them before you buyTIP:   Innisfree house  (cosmetics shop) is just 1-min away by it's walk.
